title: feat(agents): distribute gentle-ai-security subagent across runtimes
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area
Agent Detection

### 💡 Problem Statement
Gentle AI has package-owned generic ODD subagents such as `gentle-ai-explore`, `gentle-ai-worker`, and `gentle-ai-verify`, and OpenCode receives those background subagents during install/sync. Security-sensitive work currently has a parent-orchestrator routing rule, but the dedicated `gentle-ai-security` subagent is not distributed consistently through the same runtime asset paths. That leaves runtimes such as OpenCode without a native security/Sec-TDD worker that can accept Gentle AI package context and perform focused attack-surface analysis.

### 📦 Proposed Solution
Add `gentle-ai-security` as a package-owned subagent asset and install/sync target for every supported runtime with managed subagent assets, including OpenCode.

Implementation plan:
- Add a concise `gentle-ai-security` prompt for OpenCode and native file-subagent runtimes managed by Gentle AI.
- Make the prompt explicitly accept Gentle AI package/orchestrator context while staying separate from RDD review lenses.
- Route OpenCode security/Sec-TDD delegation to `gentle-ai-security` from the orchestrator instructions.
- Include `gentle-ai-security` in OpenCode parity/config generation and managed-agent detection.
- Include `gentle-ai-security` in native agent manifests for supported file-subagent runtimes without reviving retired RDD review agents.
- Add tests for embedded asset layout, OpenCode parity install, and native asset manifest behavior.
- Keep PR slices under 400 changed lines where possible; if the final diff exceeds the budget, split into reviewable PR slices and link each PR back to this issue.

Acceptance criteria:
- Fresh installs/syncs include `gentle-ai-security` where the runtime supports managed subagents.
- OpenCode can delegate to `gentle-ai-security` alongside the existing Gentle AI generic agents.
- The security prompt covers threat modeling, auth/authz/session/crypto/untrusted-input/dependency security work, and Sec-TDD negative regression test design.
- Focused tests verify asset inclusion and install/config output.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered
- Reuse `review-risk`: rejected because it is an RDD review lens and should remain read-only/review-lifecycle-specific rather than a general ODD security/Sec-TDD worker.
- Keep security work in parent orchestrator prose only: rejected because OpenCode and other runtimes need a concrete managed subagent entry for consistent delegation.

### 📎 Additional Context
The implementation branch is expected to be `feat/security-subagent-compat`. The delivery plan is to link the resulting PR(s) to this issue; if the changed-line count exceeds 400, the work should be split into chained PR slices instead of one oversized review.

title: bug(engram): sync overwrites a user-customized Claude Code mcpServers.engram wrapper on every run (3.7.0)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

`gentle-ai sync` (component `engram`) overwrites a user-customized Claude Code `mcpServers.engram` entry in `~/.claude.json` with the managed default on every run, including `gentle-ai sync --agent claude-code`. A user who launches Engram through a custom stdio wrapper (for example a script that reaches a remote shared Engram over SSH and rejects unknown extra arguments) loses the wrapper on each sync. New Claude Code sessions then show the `engram` MCP server failing (the wrapper exits 2 on the injected `mcp --tools=agent` arguments; client reports `CONNECTION_CLOSED`).

Observed 4 times across native Windows and WSL on gentle-ai 3.7.0. `gentle-ai sync --help` offers no flag to skip or preserve the component (only `--include-permissions` / `--include-theme`), and sync is also triggered by the `managed_assets_outdated` continuation after upgrades.

Read from source (v3.7.0, observed evidence, not asserted as the only mechanism):
- `internal/components/engram/inject.go` `injectClaudeUserConfig` (~L581) runs when the Engram Claude plugin is not enabled. It resolves the command via `stableEngramCommandForMergedConfig`, which preserves an existing command only if its executable is an engram binary (`isEngramCommand`), otherwise falls back to the resolved engram path.
- It then merges `engramOverlayJSON` (~L134-146) via `claude.MergeUserConfig`, which sets `{"command": <resolved engram>, "args": ["mcp","--tools=agent"]}`. A wrapper script is replaced in both `command` and `args`.
- The same pattern exists for OpenCode (~L111-114) and OpenClaw (~L122-127).
- Related but distinct: #3146 (OpenCode two-part wrapper command rewritten) and #4933 (Context7 custom launchers replaced; its "Expected" cites the Engram injector as the model for keeping user entries).

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Use Claude Code with the Engram plugin not enabled in `~/.claude/settings.json`, and set a custom wrapper as the Engram MCP server in `~/.claude.json`, e.g. on Windows `claude mcp add-json --scope user engram '{"type":"stdio","command":"C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe","args":["<wrapper-script>"]}'` (the wrapper exits non-zero if it receives extra arguments).
2. Confirm `~/.claude.json` has `mcpServers.engram.args = ["<wrapper-script>"]`.
3. Run `gentle-ai sync --agent claude-code` (a bare `gentle-ai sync` behaves the same).
4. Inspect `mcpServers.engram` again: observed `args` is now `["mcp","--tools=agent"]` (on Windows the `command` stayed the Git Bash path, so the client runs `bash mcp --tools=agent`).
5. Start a new Claude Code session: the `engram` MCP server fails to connect.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Sync should not overwrite an existing `mcpServers.engram` entry that it did not write. Either preserve any non-managed entry (for example when `command` is not an engram binary), or provide a supported opt-out (a sync flag, or a config marker) so users can keep the Engram MCP wiring user-managed.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The entry is replaced with the managed default on every sync. No flag skips it. The only workaround is to re-register the wrapper with `claude mcp add-json` after each sync.

### Gentle AI Version

3.7.0

### Operating System

Windows

### AI Agent / Client

Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

_No response_

### Additional Context

Also reproduced on Windows (WSL), same version. Before/after of the relevant entry (placeholders, no real paths):

```json
// before sync (observed, Windows)
"engram": { "type": "stdio", "command": "C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe", "args": ["<wrapper-script>"] }
// after sync (observed, Windows)
"engram": { "type": "stdio", "command": "C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe", "args": ["mcp", "--tools=agent"], "env": {} }
```

title: Tests can overwrite external OpenCode configuration when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is inherited
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

On source commit `b388eb31e9d39f81bea8ab0e439a6c70848d84bc`, two uninstall tests can pass while permanently replacing OpenCode configuration outside their temporary HOME:

- `TestUninstallOpenCodeFamilyManagedAgents`
- `TestCompleteUninstallLegacyOpenCodeDefaultOwnership`

The tests mock HOME but inherit an absolute `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. On Linux, mocking HOME changes `os.UserHomeDir()`, satisfying the current-home predicate in `opencode.ConfigPath`. Consequently, `adapter.SettingsPath(home)` resolves into the inherited XDG directory, where the test writes its fixture and performs uninstall operations.

The existing `testenv.Isolate()` helper explicitly excludes XDG because it assumes a temporary home cannot equal `os.UserHomeDir()`. HOME mocking invalidates that assumption.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

**Use synthetic configuration only. Do not run this reproduction with live user directories exposed.**

1. Prepare a read-only snapshot of the source commit above inside an isolated Linux namespace. Hide live user directories, disable networking, and use private writable directories for temporary files and caches.
2. Create a synthetic XDG directory outside the test HOME but inside the sandbox. Seed `opencode/opencode.json` with `{"sentinel":"synthetic-v1"}`, mode `0600`, and set `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` to that directory.
3. Record the sentinel hash and directory inventory. Inside that namespace, run:

   ```shell
   go test ./internal/components/uninstall \
     -run '^TestUninstallOpenCodeFamilyManagedAgents/opencode$' \
     -count=1 -timeout=90s -v
   ```

4. Compare the sentinel afterward: the test passes, but the file has been replaced.
5. Repeat with a fresh sentinel and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` unset. The external OpenCode sentinel remains unchanged.

The ownership test reproduces a second persistent-write variant. Separate file-event monitoring also detects transient external writes in the CLI persistence-failure tests, even though rollback restores their final OpenCode state.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Tests must not read or modify ambient user configuration, including temporary writes later restored by rollback. Explicit XDG-path tests should continue to work with directories owned by those tests.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Both uninstall tests pass while persistently modifying the synthetic external OpenCode configuration. The ownership test also leaves an external ownership record.

Two CLI persistence-failure tests perform transient external writes before restoring state. `TestResolveEffectiveConfigUsesBaseURLFallback` reads ambient configuration and fails with a deliberately malformed external sentinel, while passing with XDG unset.

### Gentle AI Version

Source checkout: `b388eb31e9d39f81bea8ab0e439a6c70848d84bc` (`main` at audit time). No release-binary reproduction is claimed.

### Operating System

Linux (Arch/Manjaro)

### AI Agent / Client

OpenCode

### 📋 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
# Controlled synthetic-XDG reproduction, independently repeated:
TestUninstallOpenCodeFamilyManagedAgents/opencode: PASS
Exit code: 0

Sentinel before: 27 bytes
SHA-256: 7ac619e20392fabd22a09e332bd1ac537c0ed5ac5df7a38b10072eeaaef9c68a

Sentinel after: 321 bytes
SHA-256: cdda6c2f75ccc017e302ed6803fd44484a805de74c653fb94d79610423f379c6
```

### Additional Context

Reproduced on Arch-based Omarchy with Go 1.27.1 and `bwrap`, without exposing live user configuration.

Relevant source:
- [`service_test.go:37–163`](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/b388eb31e9d39f81bea8ab0e439a6c70848d84bc/internal/components/uninstall/service_test.go#L37-L163)
- [`testenv/isolate.go:14–35`](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/b388eb31e9d39f81bea8ab0e439a6c70848d84bc/internal/testenv/isolate.go#L14-L35)

[#5039](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/5039) and [PR #5012](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/5012) addressed the related Pi/runtime-directory override vector, not this inherited-XDG variant. No equivalent tracker was identified in the completed bounded open-and-closed lookup.

Suggested repair: extend the existing isolation boundary and its unit/subprocess sentinel regressions, correcting the inaccurate assumption rather than adding another helper or restricting production XDG paths.

Windows behavior and the full repository test suite were not verified.

title: docs(sdd): remove retired SDD references from living docs
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

Documentation

### 💡 Problem Statement

SDD/OpenSpec was retired on `main` (#4959, #4967), but living docs still describe it as current behavior. This is wave C of the docs re-audit tracked in #4556.

- `internal/components/sdd/`, the `sdd-*` skills, the Kiro `sdd-{phase}` agents and `sdd-orchestrator.md` no longer exist, and presets install no SDD component (`internal/model/presets.go:19-40`).
- `docs/components.md`, `docs/trigger-rules.md` and `docs/kiro.md` still document the SDD component, its skills, an "Optional SDD" route and an SDD execution model.
- `docs/trigger-rules.md:92` links `internal/assets/skills/_shared/sdd-status-contract.md`, which no longer exists.
- `docs/architecture/organic-rdd.md` describes FINALIZE as the closing step (lines 28-55), while line 121 of the same file says FINALIZE is retired. `finalize` is an unknown command; `review acknowledge-approved` burns approved authority.
- `docs/testing-agents-deterministically.md:58,121` points to `internal/assets/opencode/sdd-orchestrator.md`; the asset is now `opencode/orchestrator.md`.
- Smaller stale mentions: `platforms.md:82-83`, `architecture.md:26`, `docker-e2e-testing.md:34`, `community-roadmap.md:81`, `review-authority-threat-model.md:10,20`, `gga-powershell-shim.md:70`, `skill-registry.md:126-128`, `telemetry.md:496,542,584`.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

- Remove or rewrite stale SDD content to describe current ODD behavior, and add a short "Since v4 (unreleased)" note where v3.7.0 users still see SDD (`components.md`, `kiro.md`, `trigger-rules.md`).
- Rewrite the FINALIZE lifecycle in `organic-rdd.md` as STATUS → START → collection → `acknowledge-approved` burn.
- Remove the `.kiro/specs` section from `kiro.md`; keep `.kiro/steering`, which the Kiro orchestrator asset still uses.
- Keep the mentions that remain accurate:
  - legacy compatibility (`ComponentSDD`, `--sdd-mode`, `sdd-runtime` cleanup), labeled as legacy;
  - the negative controls ("creates no SDD artifacts");
  - the `bind-sdd` retirement sentence, which `review_capabilities_test.go:694` asserts;
  - legacy telemetry values that v3.7.0 clients still send.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- Deleting every SDD mention: rejected, because some describe guards and legacy-compatibility paths that still exist.
- Leaving SDD docs until the v4 tag: rejected, because docs on `main` describe `main` (baseline policy in #4556).

### 📎 Additional Context

- Out of scope: `docs/engram.md:159`, which mirrors the Engram protocol text (`internal/components/engram/testdata/protocol-full.md:52`). The CLI reference and the telemetry docs beyond SDD belong to wave D.
- Expected diff: about 150 lines, within the 400-line budget.

title: bug(review): a lens admitted a CRITICAL TS6306 "missing composite" build failure that the frozen candidate disproves, making fix_finding_ids unsatisfiable and dead-ending the lineage
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

A high-risk review lens admitted a candidate-caused **CRITICAL** asserting that the candidate's TypeScript solution build is broken: that a project referenced by the solution root does not declare `composite: true`, so `tsc -b` fails with `TS6306` and the build cannot start.

The claim is false in a way that is checkable **without any project-specific knowledge**, and it became the *only* fixable ID in the lineage — so the correction contract then required an edit that could not be made.

The already-shipped shape (a multi-project solution where no project sets `composite`) is a valid, build-passing configuration. Asserting otherwise is a false blocker.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a negotiated compact v2 review, `--committed-only`, on a TypeScript candidate: 9 paths, 1014 original changed lines → high risk, four lenses, correction budget `min(200, ceil(1014/2)) = 200`.
2. All four lenses capture. Lens R4 reports CRITICAL `R4-001`: a `tsconfig` referenced by the solution root lacks `composite: true`, therefore the build fails with `TS6306` and cannot start.
3. Run the candidate's build. It **succeeds, exit 0**.
4. Delete the build caches and run again: still exit 0. No `TS6306` in any output form, in either invocation.
5. Inspect the solution graph: **no** project in it declares `composite` — including the two projects that predate the candidate under review. The shape is not introduced by the change.
6. Negotiated STATUS → `collect` / `correction_plan_required`, with `fix_finding_ids: ["R4-001"]` and no other admitted finding ID.
7. Author a bounded correction that fixes three other *real* findings (188 lines, inside the 200 budget) and documents `R4-001` as disproven with the evidence above.
8. Negotiated STATUS → `stop` / `manual_intervention_required`.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

A lens must ground a build-breaking CRITICAL in either an actually observed failure or an authoritative signal available in the frozen trees. A `TS6306` claim in particular is *testable*: the referenced project either declares `composite` or it does not, and the build either emits `TS6306` or it does not.

If the claim cannot be verified from the immutable candidate, it must not survive as the sole admitted CRITICAL — because `fix_finding_ids` becomes a mandatory edit target that no truthful correction can satisfy.

Equivalently: a finding whose premise is disproven should carry an evidence-bound non-issue disposition *before* `correction_plan_required`, so a truthful "no change needed" does not dead-end the lineage.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The CRITICAL is admitted without verification and is pinned as `fix_finding_ids`. Because a build-breaking claim was fabricated, no truthful correction can target it, and there is no disposition at this stage that says "investigated and confirmed non-issue". The lineage dead-ends in `manual_intervention_required` with the three genuine fixes stranded.

Note the reviewer is *not* given partial credit here for noticing a real reference in the solution graph — the referenced project genuinely does not declare `composite`. The failure is asserting that this configuration *cannot build*, which is false, and it is checkable from the frozen candidate alone.

### 🖥️ Environment

- Gentle AI Version: **3.7.0**
- Operating System: Linux (Ubuntu/Debian), x86_64
- AI Agent / Client: OpenCode

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
# candidate build, caches cleared, twice
$ rm -rf node_modules/.tmp && npx tsc -b ; echo "exit=$?"
exit=0
$ npm run build >/dev/null 2>&1 ; echo "exit=$?"
exit=0

# no TS6306 in any output form
$ npx tsc -b 2>&1 | grep -c "TS6306"
0

# solution graph: no project declares composite, including the two pre-existing ones
$ grep -l composite tsconfig*.json || echo "none"
none

# lineage authority after the bounded correction
state:             "correction_required"
fix_finding_ids:   ["R4-001"]
correction_budget: 200
correction_lines:  188
next_transition:   {"kind":"stop","reason_code":"manual_intervention_required"}
```

Opaque reproduction identifiers:

```text
lineage:            review-5a9b1bb05048fb9d
target identity:    sha256:c3cf189f…
repository context: rctx2_248e42db…
```

### 💡 Additional Context

The immediate terminal condition is reported separately in #3805, which reproduces on 3.7.0 rather than 2.5.0-rc. The missing non-issue disposition at the *later* targeted-validator stage is #4806. This issue covers the distinct root cause that produced the unsatisfiable finding: a lens asserting a build failure that the frozen candidate disproves.

Node v26.5.1, git 2.53.0. Consumer state preserved and pushed; nothing reset, forced, or hand-edited under `.git/gentle-ai`. No secrets, absolute paths, credentials, environment values, diffs, source contents, hostnames or private project identifiers included in this report.

title: bug(review 3.7.0): capture-result refuses a schema-valid completed result with repository_context_preserve_failed on Linux/OpenCode; same opaque binding then admitted
body:
## Summary

`review.capture-result` refused two reviewer results that native had itself relayed as complete and schema-valid, reporting `repository_context_capture_failed` followed by `repository_context_preserve_failed`, while the raw result text was returned "for manual recovery". Retrying the **same opaque binding** then admitted the identical result. No schema defect was observable in either refused result.

## Environment
- gentle-ai 3.7.0
- OS/arch: Linux x86_64
- Client: OpenCode, negotiated contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, `--agent claude-code` reported in the START envelope
- Frozen tier: high, 4-lens canonical selection, 9 changed paths

## Operation shape
`capture-result` invoked per negotiated `collect` input with exactly the returned argument tokens: `--lineage`, `--expected-revision`, `--target`, `--repository-context`, `--lens`, `--order`, `--subject-hash`. No argument was added, removed, reordered, or retyped. The `revision` token was the provider-issued `expected-revision` from the collection input, and `subject_hash` was copied verbatim from `artifact_subject.subject_hash`.

## Bounded attempts and outcomes

| order | lens | attempt 1 | attempt 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | review-risk | `repository_context_capture_failed` + `repository_context_preserve_failed` | admitted |
| 1 | review-resilience | `native admission rejected the reviewer result as incomplete` | admitted |
| 2 | review-readability | admitted | — |
| 3 | review-reliability | `repository_context_preserve_failed` + incomplete verdict | admitted |

Mutation outcome: after the retries all four lenses were admitted and the lineage reached `approved_acknowledgement_required`, then `review.acknowledge-approved` returned `acknowledged`.

## Actual vs expected

**Actual.** For orders 0 and 3 the reviewer returned `inspection.status: "completed"` with the full ordered manifest, and every `findings[]` entry carried `location`, `severity`, `claim`, `evidence_class`, `causal_disposition`, and non-placeholder `proof_refs`. Every `evidence_class` was one of `deterministic` / `inferential` and every `causal_disposition` was `introduced` — all inside the documented enums. Native nevertheless declined to preserve the result and returned no `admission_decision`.

**Expected.** A completed inspection with in-enum values is admitted on the first attempt, or the refusal names the specific offending field.

## Is the incomplete verdict trustworthy?

No — this is the sharper half of the report. The `preserve_failed` errors were accompanied by `repository_context_capture_failed`, and in both orders the reviewer result was schema-valid on its face. Compare order 1, where the `incomplete` verdict was **correct and actionable**: two `SUGGESTION` findings genuinely omitted `evidence_class` and `causal_disposition`. A caller cannot currently distinguish a real schema rejection from a transport failure, because both surface as "incomplete" plus a preserve failure.

## Minimal reproduction (shape)
1. Reach a high-risk candidate so the canonical 4-lens selection is returned.
2. Complete `review.start` and consume the consent envelope.
3. Launch each lens with the provider-injected binding and capture the result for the exact returned `collect` input.
4. Observe: with identical reviewer output shape, some first attempts are refused with `preserve_failed` while others are admitted, and a retry of the unchanged binding succeeds.

## Preserved-state evidence
No repository evidence was accepted or mutated as part of these refusals. The refused reviewer results were relaid by native for manual recovery only; they were not written to any committed store path, and no correction budget was consumed.

## Opaque identifiers (sanitized)
- lineage: `review-99d771d02b5233b1`
- target identity: `sha256:499eba8d8b98010bb9f3bebd85cc530600f140f8ea0fba56c2bdf7cba8fb3166`
- authority revision: `sha256:e2b40c3a9daff79670bdf40b41dc01a12ab490697c7ca8095c4dd494074f33db`
- refused subjects: order 0 `sha256:e6c9c55bed8fda36d4ecc6372134f4369a89b6341ce29225375e60e36fb11dd7`, order 3 `sha256:08965371ceed968bdbabaa4d7a73278e73aacc28569f6775f301c65d0dbfdf57`
- store revision after closing capture: `sha256:54f09494dfb1320ae8e9068c757f5cbb11063ab83af15b06bf6a056e652f7f82`

## Closest existing reports
#4705 and #4993 cover `repository_context_capture_failed` on Windows; #4972 covers a validator-scoped refusal on 3.7.0. None covers a `preserve_failed` refusal on Linux where the reviewer result is schema-valid and a same-binding retry succeeds.

Separately, the same session hit the authority-store/gate blockage tracked in #4964; the pre-commit gate there reported `allowed: false` with `sanctioned_exits: []`.

title: feat(claude): configure models per ODD organic role (explorer, writer, verifier) like Codex
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

TUI (terminal UI)

### 💡 Problem Statement

On Claude Code, ODD organic delegation roles (explorer/mapper, writer, verifier, research collector) cannot be assigned different models through Gentle AI. Since #4062 (closes #4054), every organic delegation reads the single `default` row of `## Model Assignments`. The Claude model picker offers no per-role entries for ODD, and `~/.gentle-ai/state.json` only persists `claude_phase_assignments` for `default` plus the `sdd-*` and `jd-*` roles.

This makes it impossible to, for example, run the explorer on a cheaper model and the writer or verifier on a stronger one. The only workaround is hand-editing the managed `<!-- gentle-ai:sdd-model-assignments -->` block in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, which the next `gentle-ai sync` overwrites.

Codex already has this: #4911 added Custom assignments for ODD Explorer, Worker and Verify. Claude Code has no equivalent.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

- Add ODD role entries (at least Explorer, Writer/Worker, Verifier, matching the Codex set from #4911) to the Claude model picker.
- Persist them in `claude_phase_assignments` and render them as named rows in `## Model Assignments`, with the orchestrator rule mapping each organic role to its row and falling back to `default` when unset.
- Keep current behavior unchanged when no ODD role assignment is saved.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- Editing `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` by hand: overwritten by `sync`.
- A user-owned section outside the managed blocks: works only as prose that competes with the managed table, and is not visible in the TUI.
- `sync --profile` / `--profile-phase`: appear to target OpenCode SDD profiles, not Claude ODD roles.

### 📎 Additional Context

Related: #4911 (Codex ODD role models), #4054 / #4062 (organic delegation uses `default`), #4928 (`default` row effort never applies to organic delegation — per-role effort would hit the same carrier limit), #2914 (Claude review role models).

Gentle AI 3.7.0, Linux, Claude Code.

title: bug(engram): Pi provisioning misses an incompatible core behind the current companion
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

A current Pi `gentle-engram` companion can coexist with an Engram core that does not provide the capabilities the companion requires. Gentle AI's Engram verification checks executable presence, but does not detect this incompatibility at the managed installation/update boundary. The failure is deferred until the user tries to use persistent memory.

Observed combination: `gentle-engram` 0.1.16 with the effective `engram` executable at 1.20.0. Native `mem_*` tools could not initialize because that core lacks `instance-id`, introduced in 2.0.0-rc.11.

The reporter encountered this while using the update offer shown on entering the Gentle AI TUI, not by running a dedicated Engram upgrade. This is a compatibility-validation/recovery report, not proof that the Engram downloader failed. The companion's installation time and the pre-update Gentle AI version were not captured; we do not claim that self-update installed the companion in that same event.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

Observed user journey and environment; the entire upgrade journey was not replayed in a fresh isolated installation:

1. Use a Pi installation where an Engram 1.20.0 executable is resolved from `PATH` and the installed `gentle-engram` companion is 0.1.16. `ENGRAM_BIN` and `ENGRAM_URL` were unset in the observed environment.
2. Enter the Gentle AI TUI and use its startup update offer. No dedicated `gentle-ai upgrade engram` was reported.
3. Open/resume Pi and invoke a native memory operation such as `mem_save` or `mem_session_summary`.
4. Observe initialization refusal for the missing `instance-id` capability rather than a compatibility warning/recovery handoff at the managed integration boundary.

The original bad runtime was directly observed. Static inspection of the exact installed Gentle AI module confirmed the presence-only Engram verifier; no updater/install/sync command was executed for this diagnosis.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

When provisioning or refreshing the managed Pi memory integration, validate the effective Engram runtime against the installed companion's requirements, rather than treating executable presence as compatibility.

For an incompatible runtime, clearly identify the active runtime/version and requirement, and offer an explicit supported upgrade/recovery path before the integration is presented as ready. Preserve user consent and the existing memory store; self-updating Gentle AI need not silently update every component.

Honor existing `ENGRAM_BIN`/`ENGRAM_URL` configuration so a compatible external provider is not incorrectly rejected because an unrelated local binary is old. Reuse the existing verification/upgrade paths rather than introducing a parallel configuration authority.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The active core remained 1.20.0 while the Pi companion required instance identity support. Native memory operations repeatedly failed initialization. A second executable was also an old 1.20.x development build, so selecting another existing copy would not have resolved the mismatch.

After taking a consistent backup and replacing the effective executable with the official Engram 2.2.1 release, native `mem_save`, `mem_get_observation`, and `mem_search` succeeded without changing the companion version. The HTTP health identity matched the CLI identity, and the original observations and sessions were preserved.

This confirms the runtime incompatibility and the repair, not a fresh end-to-end reproduction of the TUI upgrade sequence.

### Gentle AI Version

4.0.0-20260930194056-30ff0afd88cc (observed after the reported update; pre-update version unknown)

### Operating System

Windows (WSL)

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
# Relevant native memory diagnostic; the local server endpoint is omitted.
The Engram binary "engram" does not support "instance-id" and predates v2.0.0-rc.11. Upgrade the binary, or point ENGRAM_BIN at the current one.
```

### Additional Context

- Client: Pi with `gentle-engram` 0.1.16; global Gentle Shell package 3.7.0.
- Environment: Ubuntu 26.04 under WSL2, Linux amd64.
- Evidence comes from the exact installed Go module build, not an unrelated local checkout.
- [Engram verification only checks executable presence](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/30ff0afd88cccc89ec7ae133f8f0b3d725cabf3b/internal/components/engram/verify.go#L14-L18).
- [Pi provisioning installs the companion](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/30ff0afd88cccc89ec7ae133f8f0b3d725cabf3b/internal/agents/pi/adapter.go#L58-L62) and [runs its initialization command](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/30ff0afd88cccc89ec7ae133f8f0b3d725cabf3b/internal/agents/pi/adapter.go#L272-L284).
- [Self-update filters Gentle AI itself](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/30ff0afd88cccc89ec7ae133f8f0b3d725cabf3b/internal/app/selfupdate.go#L115-L120), with [the self-upgrade flow](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/30ff0afd88cccc89ec7ae133f8f0b3d725cabf3b/internal/app/selfupdate.go#L152-L159) separate from component upgrades.
- [Dedicated core upgrade replaces the executable resolved from PATH](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/30ff0afd88cccc89ec7ae133f8f0b3d725cabf3b/internal/update/upgrade/download.go#L152-L165).

Related but distinct reports: #4712 concerns release-tarball detection/Homebrew version lag; #4354 concerns beta/RC selection and the non-brew install path; closed #872 covered broader update-experience improvements. This report targets the missing companion/core compatibility check, not those upgrade mechanisms.

Regression coverage should exercise an old effective core with a current companion, a compatible core, and configured runtime overrides. No automated regression tests or upgrade replay were run for this report.

title: bug(sync): SDD retirement leaves stale sdd-preflight-hook and SDD assets after sync on main
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description
After moving from v3.7.0 to `main` (which includes `e219644b feat(workflow)!: retire SDD and OpenSpec in favor of ODD`), `gentle-ai sync` does not migrate the SDD artifacts that earlier versions installed.

The most visible effect: the Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook (matcher `Agent`) that earlier versions wrote still runs `gentle-ai sdd-preflight-hook --agent claude-code`. That command no longer exists on `main` (`Error: unknown command "sdd-preflight-hook"`, exit 1), so every subagent launch reports a hook error. On `main`, `sdd-preflight-hook` is referenced only in `internal/components/uninstall/service_test.go`, so neither sync nor upgrade prunes the hook.

Other SDD artifacts are also left in place after sync on `main`:
- Claude Code: 11 `sdd-*` skills, 11 `sdd-*` agents, 11 `gentle-sdd-*` commands, and `_shared/sdd-*.md` / `openspec-convention.md`.
- Codex: 11 `sdd-*` skills, `_shared/sdd-*` files, and `sdd-{cheap,mid,strong}.config.toml`.
- OpenCode: `opencode.json` still defines `sdd-*-fallback` agents loading `prompts/sdd/*.md`, and `gentle-orchestrator-auto` keeps an SDD orchestrator prompt.

These artifacts keep advertising SDD skills, agents and commands that the new instructions no longer use.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce
1. Install gentle-ai v3.7.0 (or earlier) with Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode, and run `gentle-ai sync`.
2. Install `main`: `GENTLE_AI_CHANNEL=beta go install github.com/gentleman-programming/gentle-ai/v4/cmd/gentle-ai@main`
3. Run `gentle-ai sync`.
4. Launch any subagent in Claude Code, or check `~/.claude/settings.json` and the skills/agents/commands directories.

### ✅ Expected Behavior
Sync (or upgrade) on a build that retired SDD removes or migrates the hooks, agents, skills, commands and OpenCode agent entries it previously owned, at least the hook that calls a removed CLI command.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
The stale `PreToolUse` hook fails on every `Agent` call with `unknown command "sdd-preflight-hook"`. The SDD assets listed above remain installed. `gentle-ai sync` reports success without warning about them.

### Gentle AI Version
4.0.0-20260930215115-b388eb31e9d3 (`main`)

### Operating System
Windows

### AI Agent / Client
Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area
Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Logs / Error Output
```
$ gentle-ai sdd-preflight-hook --agent claude-code
Error: unknown command "sdd-preflight-hook" — run 'gentle-ai help' for available commands
(exit 1)
```

### Additional Context
Claude Code 2.1.286, Codex CLI 0.159.2, Windows 11 Home (build 26200). Workaround: remove the stale hook entry from `settings.json` and move the leftover `sdd-*` assets out manually. Codex and OpenCode are also affected; the dropdown allows only one client.

title: feat(odd): offer task close as an optional session boundary with a short printed brief
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Problem Statement

ODD already has a checkpoint with state saved: every task ends with at least one work-unit commit, and the commit identity is recorded in the feature document ([routing.go#L43](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/b388eb31e9d39f81bea8ab0e439a6c70848d84bc/internal/components/agentguidance/routing.go#L43)). It also has a resume procedure: `mem_context`, scoped `mem_search`, `mem_get_observation` for the full document, then the task file ([routing.go#L49](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/b388eb31e9d39f81bea8ab0e439a6c70848d84bc/internal/components/agentguidance/routing.go#L49)).

What I could not find is task close used as a place where a session can end. A case-insensitive search for `session` in `routing.go` and `odd-orchestrator-sections.md` at this commit returns six lines:

- "The parent session orchestrates" ([sections#L76](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/b388eb31e9d39f81bea8ab0e439a6c70848d84bc/internal/assets/skills/_shared/odd-orchestrator-sections.md#L76));
- skills resolved "once per session" ([sections#L184](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/b388eb31e9d39f81bea8ab0e439a6c70848d84bc/internal/assets/skills/_shared/odd-orchestrator-sections.md#L184));
- the long-session backstop, which pauses at approximately 150k parent-context tokens and is "advisory context guidance, not mechanically observed or enforced" ([routing.go#L82](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/b388eb31e9d39f81bea8ab0e439a6c70848d84bc/internal/components/agentguidance/routing.go#L82));
- "long-session mapping" as a reason to delegate an explorer ([routing.go#L61](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/b388eb31e9d39f81bea8ab0e439a6c70848d84bc/internal/components/agentguidance/routing.go#L61), [#L78](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/b388eb31e9d39f81bea8ab0e439a6c70848d84bc/internal/components/agentguidance/routing.go#L78), [sections#L98](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/b388eb31e9d39f81bea8ab0e439a6c70848d84bc/internal/assets/skills/_shared/odd-orchestrator-sections.md#L98)).

None of these six ties a session to task close. There is also no `odd` case in either command dispatch switch in `app.go` ([#L103](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/b388eb31e9d39f81bea8ab0e439a6c70848d84bc/internal/app/app.go#L103), [#L301](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/b388eb31e9d39f81bea8ab0e439a6c70848d84bc/internal/app/app.go#L301)).

Inference, not measured: a feature with several tasks can keep running in one parent session that grows task after task, although each task close is already a recoverable checkpoint.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

1. At task close (work-unit commit recorded in the feature document), gentle-ai prints a short brief derived from the feature document: the feature, the task just closed and its commit, the next unfinished task, and open decisions or blockers. Name for illustration: `gentle-ai odd brief <feature>`.
2. The ODD Close step mentions the brief as an option: continue in the same session, or start the next task in a fresh session from the brief plus the existing resume procedure.
3. Optional and advisory. No gate, and no change to the delegation triggers or evidence budget shipped in #5147.

This builds on Gentleman-Programming/gentle-shell#1160, which proposes a derived, deterministic feature index (`odd/state.jsonl` with `status`, `tasks_done`, `tasks_total`, `last_commit`, `open_decisions`, `blockers`) and explicitly rules out summary chains and compacting or rewriting the feature documents. The brief could be read from that index rather than written as a summary.

Inference, not measured: starting the next task in a fresh session resets the parent context at a point ODD already defines, instead of waiting for the size-based backstop.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- **Backstop alone.** It is size-based and advisory, and it delegates the next unit inside the same parent session ([routing.go#L82](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/b388eb31e9d39f81bea8ab0e439a6c70848d84bc/internal/components/agentguidance/routing.go#L82)).
- **Guidance text without a brief.** The resume procedure works today, but it reads the full document and then the task file ([routing.go#L49](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/b388eb31e9d39f81bea8ab0e439a6c70848d84bc/internal/components/agentguidance/routing.go#L49)); gentle-shell#1160 measured two feature documents in one repository at 32.6 KB and 22.4 KB, averaging about 27.5 KB.
- **A mandatory new session at task close.** Not proposed; this should stay a user choice.

### 📎 Additional Context

This came from point 2 of a comment on #5139. PR #5147, merged for #5139, lists its out-of-scope follow-ups as mechanical context-size telemetry, cross-file managed-block deduplication, and executor context isolation for non-Pi runtimes; task close as a session boundary is not among them.

title: bug(pi-packages): host-provided pi-tui and typebox declared as runtime dependencies
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

The checklist above is the reporting agent's evidence-backed attestation, not a statement attributed to the user. This automated report was explicitly authorized by the user. No implementation or PR is proposed.

### 📝 Bug Description

Pi emits extension-package warnings for installed `gentle-pi 3.3.0` and `gentle-engram 0.1.16`. Their installed manifests declare host-provided modules in `dependencies`, contrary to the installed Pi package documentation's requirement to declare those modules in `peerDependencies` with a `"*"` range.

Observed manifest declarations:
- `gentle-pi 3.3.0`: `@earendil-works/pi-tui` is in `dependencies` with range `0.85.1`.
- `gentle-engram 0.1.16`: `typebox` is in `dependencies` with range `^1.1.38`.

The loader warns that installed copies can bypass extension module mapping and create duplicate runtime modules. Actual duplication, a crash, or behavioral corruption has not been demonstrated in this occurrence.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Use Pi `0.99.2` with installed extension packages `gentle-pi 3.3.0` and `gentle-engram 0.1.16`.
2. Start a Pi session that loads those extensions.
3. Observe the host-provided dependency warnings.
4. Inspect the installed packages' manifests to confirm the declarations above.

Steps 1–3 describe the user's reported occurrence. The reporting agent inspected both installed manifests once and read the installed Pi package documentation; it did not launch another Pi session or reinstall packages.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Host-provided Pi modules are declared as peers using `"*"` and not bundled/installed as ordinary runtime dependencies. Loading the extension packages does not produce these manifest warnings.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Both manifests place a host-provided module in `dependencies`, and Pi reports the warnings below.

### Gentle AI Version

`3.7.0` (installed CLI); affected packages: `gentle-pi 3.3.0`, `gentle-engram 0.1.16`; Pi host: `0.99.2`.

### Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

Other

Other

```shell
Warning: Extension package "<extension-package>/gentle-engram/package.json": Host-provided extension packages must be declared in peerDependencies with a "*" range, not dependencies: typebox. Installed copies can bypass the extension loader and create duplicate runtime modules.
```

### Additional Context

- Client: Pi interactive session; affected area: extension package manifests/startup loading. The form does not offer Pi as a client option, so `Other` is used.
- Verified environment: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, Linux x86_64.
- Installed Pi `docs/packages.md`, section "Declare dependencies", lists both modules as host-provided and requires `peerDependencies` with range `"*"`.
- Duplicate lookup completed across open and closed issues using peerDependencies, host-provided, package/module names, and the exact warning terminology. No equivalent issue was found in the returned non-saturated result sets; the peerDependencies hits concerned CodeGraph onboarding and an unrelated OpenCode upgrade dependency conflict.
- Bounded diagnostic attempts: one inspection per affected manifest; one installed documentation read; one read-only version/environment collection. No package edit, install, update, source repair, Git mutation, or review-authority operation was performed.
