title: bug(community-tool): Pi is permanently reported missing — the pending adapter-health sentinel is consumed as a failed status check, so CodeGraphReconcileSatisfied() can never be true when Pi is detected
body:
## Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

---

## 📝 Bug Description

On a machine where the Pi CodeGraph integration is fully installed and its direct MCP capability has been verified **by Gentle AI itself**, the CodeGraph status still reports `- Pi: missing`, and `Status.CodeGraphReconcileSatisfied()` can never return true — so the already-reconciled install shortcut is unreachable.

The cause is that a discriminated probe result is flattened into a bare `error` and that error is then consumed as a "not configured" signal.

`verifyPiMCPWithProbe` (`internal/components/communitytool/pi_codegraph.go:476`) distinguishes two outcomes through its `(PiCodeGraphMCPVerification, error)` pair:

- **genuine failure** → a wrapped error, no verification;
- **validated capability whose activation health is not machine-verifiable** → a fully populated verification, plus the sentinel `ErrPiCodeGraphAdapterHealthUnavailable` (`:501`), which is exactly what the shipped probe returns on success (`:599`).

The project's own test asserts that the second outcome is a success-with-pending, not a failure — `pi_codegraph_test.go:476` (`"validated capability with unavailable adapter health becomes pending"`) requires both the sentinel **and** a populated verification:

```go
if !verification.Adapter || !verification.ReadOnlyExplore || len(verification.Tools) != 1 || verification.Tools[0] != "codegraph_explore" {
    t.Fatalf("verification = %#v, want validated capability evidence", verification)
}
```

The install/reconcile path preserves that distinction: `PreservePiCodeGraphPending` only converts the result into the pending manual action when the error chain is **exclusively** the sentinel (`pi_codegraph.go:106`, `isExclusivePiCodeGraphPending`).

The status path does not. `verifyPiCodeGraphWithProbe` returns only `error`, so the populated verification is dropped, and `inspectPiCodeGraph` maps **any** non-nil error to `false`:

```go
if err := verifyPiCodeGraph(paths.MCPConfig, nil); err != nil {
    return false, err.Error(), nil      // pi_codegraph.go:678
}
// ...
if err := verifyPiCodeGraph(paths.MCPConfig, reports); err != nil {
    return false, err.Error(), reports  // pi_codegraph.go:703
}
```

That `false` flows through `PiCodeGraphConfigured` (`:662`) → `hasCodeGraphWiring` (`tool.go:453`, Pi branch at `:456`) → `detectCodeGraphAgents` (`tool.go:427`) → `AgentStatusMissing` (`tool.go:435`). No input can make it return true, because the probe's success path always carries the sentinel.

The rest of the module already knows Pi is special — but only in two of the three places that read the same flag:

```go
// tool.go:297 validateCodeGraphInstallStatus — Pi excluded
for _, agent := range status.Agents {
    if agent.Agent == model.AgentPi {
        continue
    }
    // ...
}

// tool.go:257 codeGraphCanRepairWithoutFullInstall — Pi excluded
if !agent.Detected || agent.Configured || agent.Agent == model.AgentPi {
    continue
}

// tool.go:369 CodeGraphReconcileSatisfied — Pi NOT excluded
for _, agent := range s.Agents {
    if agent.Detected && !agent.Configured {
        return false
    }
}
```

Two consequences, both observable:

1. The Community Tools pane reports a healthy machine as broken: `CodeGraph: CLI available • 9 detected agents • 8 configured • 1 missing`, with `- Pi: missing`.
2. `CodeGraphReconcileSatisfied()` is permanently `false` whenever Pi is detected, so `InstallWithHome` can never take the *"CodeGraph is already available and configured for all detected supported agents. No changes were needed."* branch for that user. The existing test for that branch — `TestInstallSkipsWhenCodeGraphAlreadyReconciled` (`tool_test.go:1182`) — builds a home directory with **no Pi at all**; that is the only combination in which the shortcut is reachable, and it is not covered with Pi detected. This is the direct cause of the *"CodeGraph CLI was installed and supported agents were connected…"* note reappearing on every rerun.

---

## 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Gentle AI 3.7.0 with the `pi` agent and the `codegraph` community tool selected, on a machine that has a Pi agent directory and the Pi MCP adapter present.
2. Confirm the direct capability probe passed. The pending note is itself the evidence: it is only produced when the error chain is *exclusively* the sentinel, so `initialize`, `tools/list`, and the read-only `codegraph_explore` schema all had to pass. A schema or guidance failure would instead be a fatal `FAILED` step:
   > Pi CodeGraph integration remains pending: CodeGraph configuration was installed and preserved, and direct MCP capability was verified. Pi adapter activation health cannot be machine-verified on the detected Pi version.
3. Open **Community Tools/Plugins**, or call `DetectStatus(model.CommunityToolCodeGraph, home, detector)` from a test.
4. Observe `Pi: missing` (`AgentStatusMissing`) while every other detected agent reports `configured`, and while the ownership manifest, the expected MCP entry, and the child guidance/tool markers all exist.
5. Observe that `Status.CodeGraphReconcileSatisfied()` is `false`, and that a rerun never takes the no-changes-needed path.

---

## ✅ Expected Behavior

The status path should preserve the distinction its own install path preserves, and apply the same Pi exclusion that `validateCodeGraphInstallStatus` and `codeGraphCanRepairWithoutFullInstall` already apply:

- Pi with a verified direct capability but unverifiable adapter activation health should not be `AgentStatusMissing`. Either exclude Pi from the configured/missing counters, or give it a third state (`pending` / `unverifiable`).
- `Status.CodeGraphReconcileSatisfied()` should apply the same Pi exclusion, so a machine whose Pi integration was successfully reconciled can reach the already-reconciled branch.
- Optionally, surface the populated `PiCodeGraphMCPVerification` — currently discarded for Pi — so the status reason can state what was actually verified.

---

## ❌ Actual Behavior

```text
║  Community Tools/Plugins
║  ✓ Community tools configured
║  1 selected.
║  CodeGraph: CLI available • 9 detected agents • 8 configured • 1 missing
║    - Google Antigravity: configured
║    - Claude Code: configured
║    - Codex: configured
║    - Cursor: configured
║    - Gemini CLI: configured
║    - Hermes: configured
║    - Kiro IDE: configured
║    - OpenCode: configured
║    - Pi: missing
║  Next: Pi CodeGraph integration remains pending: CodeGraph configuration was installed and preserved, and direct MCP capability was verified. Pi adapter activation health cannot be machine-verified on the detected Pi version.
```

`hasCodeGraphWiring` returns `(false, <ownership manifest path>, "Pi MCP adapter health is not machine-verifiable")`; the reason string is not shown by the counter, so a *pending/unverifiable* state renders as the same `missing` label used for an agent that is not wired at all.

---

## 🖥️ Environment

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Gentle AI Version** | 3.7.0 (stable, Homebrew) |
| **Operating System** | macOS (arm64) |
| **Pi Version** | 0.99.1 |
| **CodeGraph CLI** | 1.4.1 |
| **AI Agent / Client** | Other (Pi) |
| **📋 Affected Area** | Agent Detection |

---

## 💡 Logs / Error Output

Capability evidence from the live Pi MCP adapter's `tools/list` cache — this is what the probe validated before returning the sentinel:

```json
{
  "name": "codegraph_explore",
  "inputSchema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "query":       { "type": "string" },
      "maxFiles":    { "type": "number" },
      "projectPath": { "type": "string" }
    },
    "required": ["query", "projectPath"]
  }
}
```

This passes `isReadOnlyCodeGraphExploreSchema()` exactly (single tool, exactly three properties, `query` required, only `query`/`projectPath` admitted as required).

---

## Additional Context

Verified against the tagged source of `v3.7.0`. `main` (v4) still returns the same sentinel from the probe (`pi_codegraph.go:592`) and keeps the same `inspectPiCodeGraph` body, so this is not fixed on main.

Related, and deliberately out of scope for this report:

- **#1159 (closed)** fixed the wording of the pending action and set its non-goals ("Do not treat unavailable Pi adapter evidence as success"). This report does not ask for that. It asks only that a capability Gentle AI *did* verify stop being reported as `missing`, and that the third Pi exclusion be applied consistently.
- **#5108** claims a broader common root for the Pi CodeGraph symptom cluster (dual ownership between gentle-pi's native tool and Gentle AI's MCP projection) and may supersede the projection entirely. If that lands by removing the Pi MCP projection, this status path presumably goes with it; the inconsistency described here still holds for every release in the meantime.
- **#3763 (closed)** shows the same `Pi: missing` label, but from a genuine probe failure, which is why it is not this issue.

**Separate observation (not part of this defect — happy to file separately if useful).** `pi-codegraph.json` records file ownership as a whole-file sha256 (`afterHash`). Any later unrelated edit to a managed child — for example adding a `model:` line to its frontmatter — makes `UninstallPiCodeGraph` classify that file as drifted and preserve it (`"Pi CodeGraph child drifted; preserved: …"`) instead of restoring it, and the manifest entry is never refreshed because reconcile only writes entries that do not already exist. On this machine 10 of 21 owned children are in that state.

title: review: status --next-transition runs git init on a non-repository --cwd
body:
## Summary

`gentle-ai review status --next-transition` runs `git init` on its `--cwd` when that directory is not a Git repository. When `--cwd` is the user's home directory, this silently creates `~/.git`, which turns the whole home directory into a worktree and then breaks other tools (see Impact).

## Environment

- gentle-ai version: 3.7.0 (`~/.local/bin/gentle-ai`)
- gentle-pi (Pi extension) version: 3.7.0
- pi version: 0.99.1
- OS: Linux 7.2.7-arch1-1 x86_64 (Arch Linux)
- Shell: /usr/bin/fish
- Terminal: TERM_PROGRAM=herdr, TERM=xterm-256color
- Install/channel: release binary installed at `~/.local/bin/gentle-ai`
- Review mode: `receipt-driven development: off (decided by global)` — the switch is already OFF and this still happens

## Reproduction

1. Make sure the target directory is not a Git repository, and that `~/.git` does not exist:

   ```sh
   rm -rf ~/.git
   ```

2. Run the negotiated STATUS preflight with `--cwd` set to the home directory:

   ```sh
   export GENTLE_PI_REVIEW_RELAY_CONTRACT=gentle-pi.review-relay/v1
   gentle-ai review status \
     --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 \
     --cwd "$HOME" \
     --projection workspace \
     --agent pi \
     --next-transition
   ```

3. Observe that `~/.git` now exists, and that the command itself fails:

   ```sh
   ls -d ~/.git
   ```

Actual output of step 2:

```json
{
  "schema": "gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2",
  "contract": "gentle-ai.review-integration/v2",
  "operation": "review.status",
  "phase": "preflight",
  "code": "invalid_request",
  "message": "The negotiated review request is invalid.",
  "mutation_outcome": "not_started",
  "next_action": "correct_request",
  "cause": "git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z output exceeds deterministic 8388608-byte limit (377563 NUL-terminated entries)"
}
```

Bisect notes: the creation only happens when `--cwd` is the real home directory. An empty `/tmp` directory, a `/tmp` directory with files, and a fully isolated `HOME=/tmp/...` sandbox (even after copying `~/.gentle-ai`, `~/.config` and `~/.pi` into it) all complete without creating `.git`. So the home directory appears to be resolved independently of the `HOME` environment variable — possibly via the passwd database — which is what makes this unavoidable for a user who runs an agent from `~`.

The creation is repeatable and deterministic: the sequence is `git init <cwd>` followed by `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z`, and the second step is what then fails. `git rev-list --all --count` on the result is `0`, so the created repository has no commits, no objects and no remote.

## Expected Behavior

`review status` should refuse a `--cwd` that is not inside a Git repository with a clear error (something in the shape of "not a git repository: use --cwd <repo>"), the way the SDD edit-authority path already does when it reports that authority lives in the Git common directory. It must never create a repository as a side effect of a read-only status/preflight operation — especially not in the user's home directory.

## Actual Behavior

1. `git init` is executed on `--cwd`, leaving an empty repository behind.
2. The command then aborts with `invalid_request` because `git ls-files` over the new worktree exceeds the deterministic 8 MiB limit.
3. The empty `~/.git` survives the failure and affects every other tool that inspects the home directory.

## Impact

- **opencode** (v2.0.18) treats `$HOME` as a worktree and its snapshotter enumerates every untracked file in the home directory — 431k files in my case — which makes `opencode` hang indefinitely when started from `~`.
- **starship** switches from the path format to `repo_root_format` and renders the directory name plus a branch for every prompt.
- Other Git-aware tooling in the home directory now resolves to the wrong repository root.
- `gentle-ai review mode disable --scope global` does not prevent it, and neither does `--scope clone` being unset.
- Deleting `~/.git` only helps until the next agent run from `~`, which is what makes this recur.

## Additional Context

- The offending `git init` is not visible in the shell history and there is no `git init` call site in the gentle-pi npm package — the invocation lives in the Go binary, so the creation is entirely in-process from the user's point of view.
- Workaround used on my side: a `systemd --user` path unit that removes `~/.git` when it appears, plus never starting an agent with `cwd=$HOME`.
- Version where this was observed: gentle-ai 3.7.0 / gentle-pi 3.7.0 on Arch Linux.

title: fix(review): granular rctx2 error codes instead of generic repository_context_unavailable
body:
## 📝 Bug Description

`gentle-ai review capture-result` returns the generic `repository_context_unavailable` code for every rctx2 resolution failure — malformed binding, absent authority record, and identity mismatch are all lumped under the same opaque error. Community reporters (#2227, #2411, #2461) cannot distinguish the root cause.

## 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `gentle-ai review start` and note the returned repository context handle
2. **Scenario A** — Delete the compact authority file, then run `capture-result` with that handle
3. **Scenario B** — Pass a structurally invalid handle (`rctx2_not-base64`)
4. **Scenario C** — Run `capture-result` from a different repository than the one the binding commits to
5. All three scenarios return the same generic error: `repository_context_unavailable`

## ✅ Expected Behavior

The error system should return one of three distinct sub-codes:

- **`rctx2_binding_unusable`** — the binding is structurally invalid (malformed base64, invalid revision format, missing fields)
- **`rctx2_resolution_failed`** — binding was valid when issued but the underlying repository has changed (authority record removed, repository relocated, commit lost)
- **`rctx2_identity_mismatch`** — binding commits to a different repository than the one named by `--cwd`

Each sub-code should include specific remediation in the action text so users know exactly what to do.

## ❌ Actual Behavior

All three scenarios return the opaque `repository_context_unavailable` code with no actionable hint.

## 🖥️ Environment

### Gentle AI Version

`v4.x.x` (commit range: 717087b1..HEAD)

### Operating System

All

### AI Agent / Client

Any — this affects the CLI regardless of agent

title: fix(review): START commits authority with empty base_tree/candidate_tree then fails on capture
body:
## 📝 Bug Description

`gentle-ai review start` returns `action: created` (authority committed) even when the frozen candidate context has null or empty `base_tree` / `candidate_tree`. Subsequent `capture-result` fails with `repository_context_unavailable` and agents are left with an authority that cannot be reviewed.

## 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `gentle-ai review start` against a repository where the worktree has no pending changes (all files committed) or where the base resolution produces empty trees
2. Command returns successfully with `action: created` and a lineage ID
3. Run `gentle-ai review capture-result` with the returned lineage
4. Observation: failure with `repository_context_unavailable` or `base_tree: None` / `candidate_tree: None`

## ✅ Expected Behavior

`review start` should refuse to create authority when `base_tree` or `candidate_tree` resolve to empty strings. It should return a clear error explaining the candidate context is incomplete and what the user must do (provide a valid `--base-ref` or stage changes).

## ❌ Actual Behavior

Authority is committed with null trees. All downstream captures fail. The agent must manually clean up the authority record.

## 🖥️ Environment

### Gentle AI Version

`v4.x.x` (commit range: 717087b1..HEAD)

### Operating System

macOS (darwin/arm64)

### AI Agent / Client

Pi (earendil-works)

title: [Automated provider defect] bug(sync): Pi CodeGraph probe deadline aborts sync on Windows, even with --agent claude-code, leaving review stuck on managed_assets_outdated (3.7.0)
body:
### Bug Description

On Windows, `gentle-ai sync` aborts the whole sync pipeline when the Pi CodeGraph MCP capability probe times out on `tools/list`. The same abort happens when sync is explicitly scoped to another agent (`--agent claude-code`), so a Claude Code user cannot clear the review `managed_assets_outdated` stop.

### Environment

- gentle-ai 3.7.0 (stable channel)
- Windows 11 x64, build 26200
- Client: Claude Code
- CodeGraph MCP server 1.4.1 (the MCP server reports that 1.6.1 is available)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. With receipt-driven review enabled globally, run `gentle-ai review status --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --next-transition --base-ref <empty-tree> --committed-only` on a repository.
2. STATUS returns `next_transition.kind: stop`, `reason_code: managed_assets_outdated`, with the continuation `gentle-ai sync`.
3. Run `gentle-ai sync`.
4. Run `gentle-ai sync --agent claude-code --strict-tdd`.

### Expected Behavior

- A Pi CodeGraph probe deadline is classified as pending or unverifiable adapter health, in line with the intent of #1149, instead of failing the entire sync.
- Or, at minimum, `sync --agent claude-code` does not run the Pi CodeGraph sync step at all.
- The review `managed_assets_outdated` stop can be cleared for the agent that is actually in use.

### Actual Behavior

Both sync invocations exit non-zero with:

```
Error: execute sync pipeline: sync Pi CodeGraph: Pi CodeGraph MCP capability probe failed: MCP tools/list: context deadline exceeded
```

A later STATUS still returns `stop` / `managed_assets_outdated` with the same single stale asset, so the review lifecycle stays blocked.

### Attempts

- 2 sync attempts, 1 unscoped and 1 scoped to `--agent claude-code`. Both failed identically, with no retry loop.
- Mutation outcome: unknown whether any managed assets were partially written before the abort. The STATUS readback afterwards still reported them as stale.
- Consumer workaround: disable review for the clone with `gentle-ai review mode disable --scope clone`. Delivery then falls under ordinary repository policy.

### Related (not duplicates)

- #1149 (closed): the probe self-times out; the fix intent was to classify a deadline as pending.
- #4508: the probe fails on Ubuntu with a different message (adapter unavailable).
- #3902: Pi CodeGraph MCP registration on Windows.
- #2146: treat MCP initialize EOF during Pi CodeGraph sync as non-fatal.

title: bug(install): explicit --component selection is dropped when state.json already exists (update-check stub); sync then applies the full default set
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

A first `install --agent X --component … --preset …` can silently fail to persist the explicit
selection when `~/.gentle-ai/state.json` already exists without a previously configured selection —
for example the stub that a successful update check writes (`{"last_update_check": …}`).

The merge in `internal/cli/run.go` (`mergeExplicitAgentInstallState`) only applies the fresh
selection when the **existing** state already has one (`if merged.SelectionConfigured {`), and
`internal/state/state.go` (`MergeAgents`) copies `selection_configured` / `components` / `skills`
from the existing state. When the existing file is a stub, the fresh selection is dropped and a
later `gentle-ai sync` falls back to the full default component set — provisioning more than the
user asked for.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Point `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` at a scratch directory (no `~/.gentle-ai/state.json` yet).
2. Emulate the state file the update check leaves behind after a successful check:

   ```sh
   mkdir -p ~/.gentle-ai
   printf '{"last_update_check":"2026-09-30T09:00:00Z"}' > ~/.gentle-ai/state.json
   ```

   In real first runs this stub is written by `internal/app/selfupdate.go` →
   `internal/update/cooldown.go` when the check succeeds before the install state is persisted.
   Source builds reporting `dev` skip the check entirely (guard), which makes this easy to miss
   locally. Set `HTTP(S)_PROXY` to an unreachable address if you want the check deterministic.
3. Run:

   ```sh
   gentle-ai install --agent claude-code --component persona,skills,context7 --preset minimal
   ```
4. Inspect `~/.gentle-ai/state.json`.
5. (Optional consequence) Run `gentle-ai sync` and look at the reported components/files.


### ✅ Expected Behavior

The explicit selection is persisted:

```json
{
  "selection_configured": true,
  "components": ["persona", "skills", "context7"],
  "preset": "minimal"
}
```

### ❌ Actual Behavior


The selection fields are absent; the fresh selection is discarded:

```json
{
  "installed_agents": ["claude-code"],
  "managed_asset_digest": "sha256:…",
  "persona": "gentleman",
  "last_update_check": "2026-09-30T09:00:00Z"
}
```

A following `sync` provisions the full default set instead of the recorded selection:

```text
Managed components synced: persona, engram, context7, gga, skills
Sync actions executed: 15 files changed
```

…including Engram, GGA (`gga/config`, `gga/AGENTS.md`) and 7 default skills beyond the minimal
install. Control: with **no** pre-existing `state.json` (and the update check blocked), the very
same command persists the selection correctly — so the trigger is the pre-existing file, not the
flags.


### Gentle AI Version

 built from source at main @ 5bf23ad9 (binary reports dev)             

### Operating System

Windows

### AI Agent / Client

Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area

Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
- **Gentle AI version:** built from source at `main` @ `5bf23ad9` (binary reports `dev`); the same
  code is present in the `v3.7.0` tag (`internal/cli/run.go:401`,
  `internal/state/state.go:236`).
- **OS:** Windows (the merge logic is OS-independent).
- **Agent/Client:** Claude Code (the affected state-merge path is agent-agnostic).
- **Affected area:** Installation Pipeline.
```

### Additional Context

  Root-cause pointers on `main` @ `5bf23ad9`:
  
  - `internal/cli/run.go`: `persistInstallState` (~line 350) → `mergeExplicitAgentInstallState`
    (~line 402); the guard `if merged.SelectionConfigured {` (~line 437) reads the **existing**
    state's flag, so a fresh selection is dropped when the existing file has none.
  - `internal/state/state.go`: `MergeAgents` (~line 231) copies
    `SelectionConfigured`/`Components`/`Skills` from the existing state (~line 253).
  - Stub source: `internal/app/selfupdate.go:116` → `internal/update/cooldown.go:97` (persists
    `last_update_check` only on a successful check).
  
  Possible direction: when the existing state has no configured selection and the fresh install
  brings one, take the fresh selection (or treat a stub-only state as absent). Maintainers own the
  call, of course.
  
  I'm not opening a PR: happy to prepare a fix + regression test if this gets `status:approved`.

title: bug(opencode): SDD profile writes the coordinator model to sdd-orchestrator-<profile> instead of the default gentle-orchestrator, and its phase agents are undelegable
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate (checked #4382, #4465, #4467, #4781, #4088, #4292, #3026 — related family, none cover the coordinator/allowlist wiring below)
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

## 📝 Bug Description

Applying an OpenCode SDD profile from the TUI reports success and renders the coordinator row as `gentle-orchestrator (coordinator)`, but the model assignment is never written to the `gentle-orchestrator` agent. It is written to a different, generated agent named `sdd-orchestrator-<profile>`.

That generated agent is not the one OpenCode runs. The config sets `default_agent: "gentle-orchestrator"`, so the profile's coordinator model is dead on arrival. Separately, the generated phase agents `sdd-<phase>-<profile>` are never added to the orchestrator's `permission.task` allowlist, which ships with `"*": "deny"`. So the phase agents the profile just created are undelegable.

Two distinct symptoms, one root cause: the profile writes into its own `<profile>`-suffixed agent namespace without wiring that namespace into the agent OpenCode actually executes.

### Observed shape

`~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` after `gentle-ai sync --profile "<name>:<provider/model>"` (installed build `3.7.0`):

```jsonc
"gentle-orchestrator": {
  "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5",   // <-- untouched by the profile
  // no "variant" key
  "permission": { "task": { "*": "deny", /* ...sdd-<phase> entries only... */ } }
},
"sdd-orchestrator-<name>": { "model": "<provider/model>", "variant": "medium" },
"sdd-<phase>-<name>":      { "model": "<provider/model>", "variant": "medium" }
```

The TUI reports `gentle-orchestrator (coordinator)  <provider/model> [medium]`, but the only agent holding that model is `sdd-orchestrator-<name>`.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. In the TUI, open **OpenCode SDD Profiles** and apply a profile with a coordinator model and a set of phase models.
2. Let the sync finish. It reports success and shows `gentle-orchestrator (coordinator)` bound to the chosen model with an effort level.
3. Inspect `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`:
   - `default_agent` is `gentle-orchestrator`.
   - `agent["gentle-orchestrator"].model` still holds the pre-profile value, and no `variant` key is present.
   - The chosen model appears only on `agent["sdd-orchestrator-<profile>"]`.
4. Inspect `agent["gentle-orchestrator"].permission.task`: it contains `"*": "deny"` and only the unsuffixed `sdd-<phase>` names. No `sdd-<phase>-<profile>` entry exists.
5. From the orchestrator, delegate any SDD phase to the profile agent name. The delegation is refused by the permission gate.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Either of:

- the profile's coordinator assignment is written to the agent named by `default_agent` (`gentle-orchestrator`), so the displayed coordinator row reflects the running agent; **or**
- the generated `sdd-<phase>-<profile>` agents are added to the orchestrator's `permission.task` allowlist, so a profile that created them also makes them reachable.

The TUI label and the written agent name should refer to the same agent.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

- The coordinator model assignment lands on an agent that is never executed. The profile is a silent no-op for the coordinator.
- The generated phase agents are created outside every allowlist and remain undelegable.
- The reported success is false: nothing about the running agent changed.

### 💡 Impact

A user who configures a profile to move the orchestrator to a different model/effort gets no change at all, with no warning. The failure is silent because the sync genuinely writes the files it says it writes.

## 🔗 Related (not duplicates)

- #4382 — `sync --profile` regenerates the profile orchestrator and wipes a manually-set `variant`. Same family, narrower: that one is about losing the effort key on `sdd-orchestrator-<profile>`; this one is about the assignment never reaching the executed agent at all.
- #4465 — deleted profile assignments are restored by sync. Different failure mode in the delete path.
- #4088 — generated SDD authority disconnected from runtime grants. Related class (generated assets not wired into runtime), different subsystem.

## 🧾 Environment

- `gentle-ai 3.7.0` (stable build; no `-rc.`/`-main.` suffix)
- macOS 26.1, arm64
- OpenCode
- Anthropic provider authenticated via OAuth

title: bug(review): rctx2 host resolution denies a review bound to a registered submodule, and a dead worktree denies every review
body:
## Bug Description

A negotiated review whose repository is a **registered submodule** of the session host is refused at every reviewer capture. When the host also carries a stale `git worktree list` registration, the resolution aborts before the submodule is even considered:

```
opencode_review_transport_binding_invalid: Task repository context does not
match the repository and binding it commits to
```

Frozen reviewer slots become ungrantable even though the `rctx2_…` handle and the
compact authority are both valid, so the lineage has to be recovered by hand.

## Relationship to existing issues

Sibling of #4516, which reports the same error and the same relay mechanism from a
**git-less parent directory**. That topology fails earlier, at
`OpenRepositoryIdentityLease` → `ResolveRepositoryRoot`, and is a different
mechanism. This issue is for the **registered-submodule host** and the
**dead-worktree denial** on the same code path, one step later. #4516 stays open
for its own topology; the two may deserve to be tracked separately.

Fix: #5096

## Environment

- Gentle AI: current `main` (`d96a5d4f`) — the defects below are present there
- Client: OpenCode (managed review-transport plugin)
- Platform: Linux x86_64
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`

## Observed evidence

- A high-risk negotiated review was started and granted consent; the lineage
  entered `reviewing`.
- Native STATUS returned a reviewer collect input with a complete provider-issued
  binding.
- Every reviewer Task was refused at the relay with the error above, before model
  execution.
- The host was a git superproject holding 34 registered submodules.
- The host's worktree registry also contained a stale entry for a directory that
  no longer opened as a Git repository.
- No reviewer result, receipt, source mutation, commit, push, or PR was produced.

## Root cause

Two independent defects; a real occurrence needed both.

**1. A dead registered worktree denies every review.** `ResolveReviewRepositoryContextBindingFromHost`
builds its candidate set from `git worktree list` only. For each candidate it
opens an identity lease, and on the first failure it returns
`errInvalidReviewRepositoryContextV2` immediately (main, lines ~454-458). A
registered worktree that no longer opens — a recreated or pruned checkout — kills
the whole resolution before any candidate has been probed.

**2. A registered submodule is never a candidate.** A submodule is a gitlink
(mode `160000`) named in `.gitmodules`. It is not a linked worktree, so it never
appears in `git worktree list`, and the sibling
`GitCommonDir == hostIdentity.GitCommonDir` filter drops it too, because its
common directory is `<host>/.git/modules/<name>`. A review bound to a submodule
is therefore indistinguishable from a review bound to a repository the host never
registered.

## Why probing candidates is safe here

`rctx2` handles are opaque digests (`rctx2_` plus a hash over repository
identity, lineage, target, and revision). The resolver cannot read a target root
out of the handle, so it must search, and matching recomputes that digest in
constant time. A wrong candidate cannot match. The common-directory assertion is
a search-narrowing heuristic, not a security boundary.

## Expected behavior

A review bound to a registered submodule should resolve to that submodule, and a
stale worktree registration elsewhere on the host should not prevent it.

## Actual behavior

Every reviewer Task is refused with `binding_invalid`; the review cannot proceed.

## Minimal reproduction

1. Create a superproject `H` with at least one registered submodule `S`, and
   open the agent session rooted at `H`.
2. Start a negotiated review in `S`; grant consent; the lineage enters
   `reviewing`.
3. Query native status until it returns a reviewer collect input.
4. Launch the reviewer with the exact provider-issued binding.
5. Observe: the transport refuses with `binding_invalid` before model execution.

The dead-worktree denial reproduces independently: register a worktree in `H`,
remove or repoint that directory, then attempt a review bound to any healthy
target of `H`.

## Proposed fix

Skip a registered candidate that no longer opens instead of aborting the whole
resolution, and admit the host's registered, in-place submodules as their own
candidate class, read from the host's own Git registry rather than any
host-authored path.

This admits nothing: the host lease gate, the closing host revalidation, the
digest match against a live authority, and the exactly-one-match fail-closed
rule are all unchanged. Pinned refusals — an unrelated clone of the host, a moved
registered worktree, tamper, and confinement — are preserved and verified.

title: Review integration blocks on undocumented intended-untracked capture
body:
## Observed provider-integration defect

### Environment
- Gentle AI: 3.7.0
- OpenCode: 1.18.33
- OpenCode plugin: `@opencode-ai/plugin` 1.18.33
- Engram: 2.2.1
- Client: OpenCode on Linux x86_64

### Operation shape
A selectorless native review status was requested for a current workspace-changes candidate through the documented review integration contract. The candidate contained two tracked documentation paths and one eligible untracked task document. The intended scope was the two documentation paths; the untracked task document was not intended for the review candidate.

### Expected behavior
The runtime should expose the provider-bound `external.select_intended_untracked` capture for schema `gentle-ai.review-intended-untracked-selection/v1`, or provide its exact supported adapter/schema so the intended untracked scope can be submitted safely.

### Actual behavior
Status returned `action: start` and a `collect` transition with reason `intended_untracked_selection_required`, but the installed CLI, OpenCode integration, and schema help expose no capture UI, command, JSON schema, or relay-frame contract for that provider-bound input. The command help exposes an `--intended-untracked-selection` flag without defining its accepted value format. The transport help requires strict relay frames but does not document a frame for this capture.

### Bounded attempts and outcomes
1. Initial status: returned the collect transition; no capture interface was available.
2. Read-only CLI/help and local integration inspection: no intended-untracked schema or capture operation was documented.
3. Updated Gentle AI and managed tools to current versions, aligned the OpenCode plugin, and restarted the client: health checks passed, but status returned the same collect transition.
4. No guessed payload, relay frame, lifecycle mutation, repository mutation, deployment, or production operation was performed.

### Safe reproduction
1. Have a workspace with a current-changes candidate and at least one eligible untracked file.
2. Request selectorless status using the review integration contract and next-transition output.
3. Observe `intended_untracked_selection_required` and the schema-bound collect input.
4. Consult the installed CLI help and integration surface: no supported capture contract is available.

### Preserved state and impact
The candidate, repository files, review authority, and user work remain preserved. The expected review cannot progress to candidate consent/collection, so the documentation change cannot safely reach its normal terminal review outcome.

### Opaque identifiers
- Target identity: `sha256:39b6dbbaac3e0b011b25a8efade564a73870e79f0e8bf2eb0e366a96c968081e`
- Eligible-untracked inventory: `sha256:e0037b89ca02f288d3892dec9280d4555a96a937074b5345acd8c25e5e3dfd70`
- Reason code: `intended_untracked_selection_required`
- Input schema: `gentle-ai.review-intended-untracked-selection/v1`

Please document or expose the exact provider-bound capture path and schema, including how a client submits an explicit exclude or select decision, without requiring adapters to reconstruct provider input from prose.

title: bug(doctor): tool: checks report [ok] for an executable that cannot run
body:
## Summary

`gentle-ai doctor` reports `[ok]` for a `tool:` entry whose binary exists and is executable but **cannot actually run**, so the health check reports a healthy tool while the tool is unusable.

## Environment

- `gentle-ai` 3.7.0, stable channel (no prerelease tag).
- Linux inside WSL2 (Ubuntu 24.04, x86_64, kernel 6.x).

## Observed

A `gga` entry was present on `PATH` as an executable shim whose target path does not exist. Invoking it fails:

```
<shim path>: line 2: <nonexistent target>: No such file or directory
```

`gentle-ai doctor` nevertheless reported:

```
[ok]  tool:gga    gga found at <shim path>
```

So the check accepted a binary that cannot execute, and the diagnostic surface that is documented as the read-only health check gave a green result for an unusable tool.

## Expected

A `tool:` check on the health surface should verify the tool actually runs (e.g. a bounded version/probe invocation), or report a warning, rather than reporting `[ok]` on existence and the executable bit alone. An `[ok]` for a binary that cannot execute makes the whole check untrustworthy, because the same pattern hides a genuinely broken toolchain.

## Minimal reproduction

1. Put an executable shim named `gga` on `PATH` whose target does not exist.
2. Run `gentle-ai doctor`.
3. The `tool:gga` line reports `[ok]`.

## Preserved state

Read-only diagnostic; nothing was mutated.

## Related

Not the same defect as the open `tool:gga` report about a hardcoded check producing a permanent false *unhealthy* — this one is the opposite direction (false `ok`), and it is about not verifying execution rather than about which components are inspected.

title: [Automated provider defect] bug(opencode): all four 4R lens Tasks rejected with opencode_review_transport_binding_invalid on 3.7.0 stable when the session root is the review repository root
body:
## Automated provider-defect report

Filed by an agent with explicit operator consent. Only observed evidence is below; the root cause is **not** confirmed and is **not** claimed. No repository identifiers, absolute paths, project or organization names, usernames, hostnames, credentials, environment values, diffs, source contents, or raw argv are included.

## Summary

On a stable `3.7.0` build, a canonical 4R native review freezes successfully and every one of its four reviewer Tasks is rejected before model execution by the OpenCode transport with the identical error envelope. The review can therefore never reach a terminal state, even though START, the consent grant, and the bound STATUS re-entry all succeed.

The distinguishing condition: the OpenCode session root **is** the review repository root (a real git worktree, single worktree, not nested, not a registered sibling worktree).

## Environment

- Gentle AI: `3.7.0` (no `-rc.` / `-main.` suffix; evidence channel is the stable channel)
- Client runtime: OpenCode
- OS/architecture: Windows / X64
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`
- Review tier: `high`, one changed file, 22 changed lines
- Risk reason: `shell_source` (a file that executes shell)
- Safe lineage: `review-c1d052e97f01ecab`
- Safe target: `sha256:939a814740e0fd4c4b60f98dced43d3a52e08ba6d6bcd78ae415175cedb476a8`
- Safe revision: `sha256:836f14a0fc1773a6e42661cc949279c68bdf8e1a3205b744f39e308ebcaacea9`
- Safe repository context: `rctx2_3175ce7ed16f1075baa33f40d6c09dee70712a4517db2bed00a14eb061e50a56`

## Operation shape

1. `review assess` on a committed base-diff candidate returns `risk: high`, `review_due: true`, `review_due_reason: high_risk`.
2. The returned preflight STATUS offers exactly one fresh START for the current worktree.
3. START returns the typed `gentle-ai.review-integration.consent/v3` envelope; the candidate is granted.
4. The granted START returns `action: created`, `state: reviewing`, `lenses_required: true`, `selected_lenses: [review-risk, review-resilience, review-readability, review-reliability]`, `correction_budget: 11`.
5. The reviewing START returns a bound re-entry STATUS, executed verbatim.
6. That STATUS returns `action: collect`, `reason_code: reviewer_results_required`, with four `review.capture-result` inputs, each carrying an exact `provider_task.agent` and `provider_task.prompt`.
7. Four OpenCode Tasks are launched, one per input, in provider order, copying `provider_task.agent` into the subagent type and `provider_task.prompt` into the prompt byte-for-byte, with no parsing, reconstruction, fencing, or appended text.
8. All four are rejected before reviewer execution.

## Failure envelope

```
opencode_review_transport_binding_invalid: Task repository context does not match
the repository and binding it commits to
```

Identical string for all four lenses.

## Bounded attempts and outcomes

| Round | Lenses | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4 | 4/4 rejected, identical envelope |
| 2 | 4 | 4/4 rejected, identical envelope |
| 3 | 4 | 4/4 rejected, identical envelope |

Total: 12 of 12 rejections, byte-identical prompts, same process cwd, one bound lineage. No prompt was ever modified, rebuilt, or supplemented.

A bound lineage-scoped STATUS was re-queried after the failures. It returned the same `collect` / `reviewer_results_required` transition re-offering the same four bound slots, so the failure is not a consumed-slot or replayability condition.

## Expected

Each exact provider-issued reviewer Task is accepted by the transport and executes against the provider-bound immutable trees named by the binding, so the four lens results can be captured and the review reaches a terminal state.

## Actual

Transport binding validation rejects every Task before reviewer execution. `inspection.status` is never produced, so no lens result is ever admitted, and the lineage stays in `reviewing` with no path to `approved`.

## Minimal reproduction

1. Take any valid committed base-diff candidate that `assess` rates `high` because it contains a shell-executing file.
2. Pass `--agent=opencode` to `assess`, to the preflight `status`, and to `start` — omitting it makes the provider fall back to a different runtime, which is a different defect.
3. Start the native v2 review and grant the returned consent envelope.
4. Execute the bound re-entry STATUS returned by the reviewing START, unchanged.
5. Launch the four returned `provider_task` entries unchanged, one foreground Task per slot, in the order `review-risk`, `review-resilience`, `review-readability`, `review-reliability`.
6. All four fail with the envelope above, from the OpenCode session root that is the review repository root.

## Preserved state

No receipt, tombstone, witness, mirror, sidecar, or delivery authority was created. The lineage remains `reviewing` with an unchanged authority revision, and the frozen candidate trees are intact. Consumer state is fully preserved and the transaction is not consumed.

## Differentiation from related reports

A lookup across open and closed issues found reports that share either the error string or the build, but none that owns this exact combination:

- Same error string, different condition: an earlier report covers a session rooted in a **git-less parent** of the review repository. This report's session root **is** the git repository root.
- Same build and client, different error: another automated report covers `immutable_review_transport_unsupported`, where the same binding succeeds over a different transport route.
- A third report uses a different error variant entirely (`prompt has no provider-issued review binding`).
- Two further reports cover a registered sibling worktree and a lineage that rematerializes its artifact subject; neither applies to a fresh single-worktree START.
- The earlier report for this exact error string was closed on 2026-09-27 without an identified fix.

Please confirm or correct this differentiation before any deduplication decision.

title: bug(communitytool): shell-centric CodeGraph guidance injected into bash-less Pi agents causes retry loops
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

`gentle-ai sync` unconditionally injects the shell-centric `CodeGraphGuidanceMarkdown()` block into every installed Pi subagent definition (`internal/components/communitytool/pi_codegraph.go:renderPiChild`), including subagents whose declared tool allowlist has no shell access (`bash`), such as `gentle-ai-explore`.

The injected checklist mandates:
1. Resolving project root via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel || pwd`
2. Running `gentle-ai codegraph init --cwd <project-root>` once
3. Invoking upstream CLI commands directly (`codegraph status`, `codegraph query`)
4. Forbidding fallback to normal filesystem tools before CodeGraph initialization or use fails ("Do not fall back just because `.codegraph/` is missing...").

When an instruction-following model without `bash` attempts structural questions, it cannot execute the required shell commands, cannot abandon the checklist, and enters an infinite tool-call retry loop.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable the CodeGraph community tool and run `gentle-ai sync`.
2. Inspect installed Pi subagents under `~/.pi/agent/agents/` whose frontmatter tools lack `bash` (e.g. `gentle-ai-explore.md` with `tools: read, grep, find, codegraph`).
3. Delegate a codebase structural question to that subagent.
4. Observe the subagent attempt to execute shell commands it does not have, get refused, and enter an infinite retry loop attempting to satisfy the mandatory checklist.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

`renderPiChild` renders tool-aware guidance when a subagent lacks `bash`. The guidance routes structural exploration through Pi's native `codegraph` tool (`operation: "init"`, `query`, `explore`) or `mcp`, and permits clean fallback to standard filesystem tools (`read`, `grep`, `find`) when CodeGraph tools or indexes are unavailable.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

All Pi subagents unconditionally receive shell-centric guidance demanding `git rev-parse` and CLI invocations while forbidding fallback, causing retry loops on bash-less agents.

### Gentle AI Version

v3.7.0 / v4.0.0-dev (commit d96a5d4f)

### Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

Other

_No response_

### Additional Context
