Path shown relative to the installed skills directory; no project-specific content involved.

title: feat(cli): resolve multi-repository workspaces explicitly instead of git-init or refusing
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Problem Statement

Gentle AI assumes **one directory = one project = one Git repository**. That assumption is baked into project-root resolution, and it has no expression for a directory that exists only to *contain* several independent repositories.

This is not a hypothetical layout. Splitting a system into independently-owned frontend and backend repositories, each with its own history, tags, and release cadence, under one working directory is common. The parent directory is a convenience, not a repository — it has no `.git` and should never acquire one.

When the cwd is such a parent, Gentle AI has exactly two behaviours, and both are wrong:

1. **It mutates the directory.** `gentle-ai review status` runs `git init --quiet` on a directory that is not a repository, creating an unintended parent repository. This happens on the passive discovery path, from a read-only-looking command, with no flag to disable it. Reported in #4466 and #4830.
2. **It refuses.** Because the directory is now a repository containing nested repositories, untracked-scope discovery refuses with `invalid_request` and a message that names a path the user cannot act on, because the layout change it prescribes is not one any Gentle AI command can perform. Reported in #4603.

Measured behaviour on this layout (locally built binary from `main`, see environment below):

| Umbrella layout | Result |
|---|---|
| No root `.git`, 3 nested independent repos | `invalid_request` — and a `.git` is created at the umbrella |
| Root `.git`, nested repos untracked | `invalid_request` |
| Root `.git`, proper submodules | works |
| No root `.git`, nested repos listed in `.gitignore`, one commit | works |
| No root `.git`, nested repos as linked worktrees | works |
| An individual member repository, or any subdirectory of one | works |

Note the last row. **Per-repository operation works correctly.** The defect is confined to the umbrella, and only because the umbrella has no way to declare what it is.

The same assumption appears in four other places, each with its own observable failure:

- `internal/opencode/config.go` (`candidateConfigDirs`) walks ancestor by ancestor and stops at the first `.git`. In a directory with no `.git` anywhere up to `/`, it keeps appending ancestors and can select an unrelated ancestor's `opencode.json` as the project configuration. A member repository correctly stops. This asymmetry was observed directly.
- `internal/cli/codegraph.go` (`canonicalCodeGraphProjectRoot`) requires the cwd to be **exactly** the Git top-level. A subdirectory is rejected as `unsafe CodeGraph root`, and a `.git`-less umbrella is rejected as `not a recognized project`.
- `internal/skillregistry/guard.go` treats `.git` as the canonical project marker, and `internal/app/app.go` skips the refresh silently (status 0, no message under `--quiet`) when it is absent. There is no project-level skill index for such a workspace.
- The Engram component resolves its project from the git remote, then the Git root, then **direct child repositories**. For an umbrella with several direct child repositories it refuses to write with `ambiguous project: multiple git repos found in cwd`. For an umbrella with a `services/` grouping directory it detects nothing and silently resolves to the umbrella's own directory name — so every member repository's memories land in one shared bucket. `docs/engram.md` documents only the "outside a git repo, fall back to the directory name" case.

What is missing is not a feature. It is a decision the product never had to make and never made: **when the cwd is not a repository, what is it, and who says so?** Today the answer is inferred — from a `.git` found by walking upward, or manufactured by running `git init`.

I am **not** asking for atomic cross-repository review. That is a different problem with its own history (#2540, #2849) and it should not be bundled here.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Make the project root an **explicit, single, typed resolution** with named outcomes, and delete the two silent behaviours.

**1. A declared workspace.** An opt-in manifest at the umbrella, for example `.gentle-ai/workspace.json`, listing member repositories:

```json
{
  "workspaces": [
    { "name": "frontend", "path": "web" },
    { "name": "backend",  "path": "services/api" }
  ]
}
```

Absent the manifest, nothing changes. Present, the umbrella is a first-class project root and members are addressable by name. This is opt-in and creates nothing on disk by itself.

**2. One typed root predicate, replacing every independent guess.** Every consumer — review, skill registry, CodeGraph, the OpenCode config layer — resolves its root through the same function, which returns exactly one of:

| Outcome | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `exact_repo_root` | cwd is the Git top-level of a member repository |
| `member_subdir` | cwd is inside a member repository, resolved to that member's root |
| `declared_workspace_root` | cwd is a declared workspace root |
| `not_a_project` | none of the above — a typed, non-mutating outcome |

`not_a_project` is a legitimate answer, not an error. It must never be resolved by mutating the filesystem.

**3. Remove the implicit `git init` from the passive path.** This is the change #4466 and #4830 both ask for, and it is a prerequisite for anything else: until a read-only command cannot mutate the workspace, every other guarantee in this issue is unverifiable. Greenfield bootstrap stays supported behind an explicit mutating command with explicit intent — which is what #3880 originally asked for.

**4. Stop the ancestor walk in the OpenCode config layer.** Apply the same predicate. A directory with no repository must not silently adopt an ancestor's configuration. The existing parity test for this behaviour is `TestResolveEffectiveConfigStopsProjectSearchAtGitRoot`; the new cases belong beside it.

**5. Make the nested-repository refusal actionable and honest.** The message at `internal/reviewtransaction/snapshot.go` currently prescribes a repository-layout change it explicitly declares out of scope, and the path it prints is redacted even when the directory exists. If a refusal is still the right answer for an undeclared layout, it should name the real path and the exact declaration that would make it work.

Deliberately out of scope: submodules, worktree registries, and cross-repository authority transfer. The refusals at `internal/reviewtransaction/snapshot.go` are defensible on their own terms — Git reports an embedded repository as a bare directory and refuses to enumerate it, so a snapshot could never hash those bytes. This issue does not dispute that reasoning. It asks that the *undeclared* case have a supported answer, so the refusal is reached only after the user declined to declare.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

**Use submodules.** Verified working on this layout. Rejected: it changes the user's repositories and their workflows, and a frontend/backend split is usually independent by design, not nested by intent. Gentle AI should not require that.

**Use linked worktrees.** Verified working. Rejected for the same reason — a worktree is another checkout of one repository, which is a different relationship from "two independent repositories that happen to sit together".

**List the member repositories in the umbrella `.gitignore` and commit the umbrella.** Verified working. Rejected: it produces exactly the artifact #4466 and #4830 are reporting. It is a workaround that adopts the bug, and it is not discoverable by anyone who did not already know it.

**Give every member repository a `.engram/config.json` with an explicit `project_name`.** Verified working, and it correctly prevents the memory-mixing problem. Worth documenting regardless. It does not address root resolution in review, CodeGraph, the skill registry, or the OpenCode config layer — only Engram's own project identity.

**Open each member repository as its own agent root.** This is what I do today, and it works. Its cost is that the umbrella remains unusable, cross-repository context is lost, and the silent skips are invisible. It is a mitigation, not a resolution.

### 📎 Additional Context

**Environment.** Local binary built from `main` at `61692e5` (`3.0.0-20260928192733-61692e5ff953`), Linux, Go 1.26. This is a source build, not a released version; I did not verify any published release. Commands exercised: `review status --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --agent claude-code`, `codegraph init --cwd`, `skill-registry refresh --cwd`. No real project, path, hostname, or credential is included; the layout below is a synthetic fixture.

**Observed behaviour, verbatim, at the umbrella with three nested repositories:**

```
"code": "invalid_request",
"cause": "untracked directory \"libs<redacted>\" holds another Git repository that is
 not a linked worktree of this one, so it cannot enter the review candidate: add it
 to .gitignore, move it outside this repository, or register it as a linked worktree"
```

and, in the same run, a new `.git` directory created at the umbrella with no output mentioning it.

**Anchors in the current code:**

| Location | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `internal/reviewtransaction/repository_bootstrap.go:44` | `git init --quiet` on the passive discovery path |
| `internal/reviewtransaction/snapshot.go:899` | nested-repository refusal, marked `refusal:by-design` |
| `internal/opencode/config.go:154-175` | ancestor walk that only stops at `.git` |
| `internal/cli/codegraph.go:54-68` | requires cwd to be exactly the Git top-level |
| `internal/skillregistry/guard.go:56-69` | `.git` as the canonical project marker |
| `internal/app/app.go:433-438` | silent skip when the marker is absent |
| `internal/cli/scope.go:50`, `internal/cli/run.go:755` | workspace scope is `os.Getwd()`, which is the one place no root is inferred at all — evidence the ambiguity is unresolved rather than settled |

**Related, and how this differs from each:**

- #4466, #4830 — the implicit `git init`. A prerequisite here, not a duplicate.
- #4603 — the same refusal, plus a redacted path. Same refusal, narrower report.
- #4516 — OpenCode transport rejects reviewer Tasks when the session root is a `.git`-less parent. Same topology, different observable; the deepest-discussed thread on this family.
- #4331 — the skill-registry startup refresh never runs in `.git`-less workspaces. Same family, different plugin.
- #4962 — initialization resolves the enclosing repository instead of cwd. The inverse mistake, from the same assumption.
- #3927 — ambiguous worktree placement guidance for nested layouts. The only item in this family already carrying `status:approved`.
- #2540, #2849 — multi-repository SDD authority. Adjacent, and explicitly out of scope above.

**Duplicate search.** Completed across open and closed issues. #2214, #3128 and #4656 also use "workspace", for MCP manifest reconciliation, `--scope workspace` install placement, and Pi CodeGraph allowed roots respectively. No open or closed issue requests a declared multi-repository workspace as a project-root concept.

**On root cause.** I am reporting observed behaviour and the anchors I verified by reading the code and running the binary. I have not confirmed whether the maintainers consider the embedded-repository refusal a deliberate product boundary, and I am not claiming the anchors above are the responsible cause. If that boundary is intentional and correct, the useful question this issue still leaves open is whether an *undeclared* container directory can be told apart from a non-project directory at all — today it cannot, and the two silent behaviours are what fill the gap.

**AI assistance disclosure.** Per `AI_POLICY.md`: the investigation, code reading, fixture construction, binary builds, command runs, and this draft were produced with material AI assistance. I reviewed every claim above, reproduced each result myself, and own the submission. No result is reported that I did not observe.

title: [provider defect] Pi host relay: targeted validation result refused as not binding the provider-owned correction request (3.7.0 stable, clean worktree)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description
On `3.7.0` stable, a Pi host-relayed targeted-validator result for an **accepted** bounded correction plan is refused at admission with a binding error, twice, while the bound STATUS keeps reoffering the identical slot. No validator verdict is admitted and the slot is never consumed.

The refusal is the retained guard string `compact targeted validation does not bind the provider-owned correction request` (present on `main`, `internal/reviewtransaction/compact.go`), so the guard is intentional. What is unproven is **which side is expected to bind**: the relay produced a result for the exact provider-issued request and the provider's own STATUS reissued the same request after the refusal.

Observed shape differs from the already-filed reports of this family:
- stage is `submit` (not `materialize`), ~150 ms, no `rctx2`/`repository_context_unavailable` text;
- the reviewed worktree was **clean** at the corrected HEAD (no dirty tracked file inside the frozen scope);
- the lineage was **retained** afterwards (`correction_required`, same slot, same `request_hash`) with no `unrelated` downgrade and no terminal escalation.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce
1. Call bound STATUS with `--committed-only --base-ref <tree>`, projection `workspace`, compact-v2. Admit a high-tier review with four lenses.
2. Bound STATUS → `collect` / `reviewer_results_required`. Run the exact provider-issued lens binds; admit all four.
3. Provide the provider refuter: one severe inferential and one severe deterministic finding confirmed.
4. Bound STATUS → `collect` / `correction_plan_required`. Submit the exact binding once with `correction-lines` within the frozen budget → accepted, closure `correction_required`.
5. Author the correction inside the frozen path scope and the budget, then commit it as the stop reason instructs (candidate tree changes; base unchanged). Worktree clean at the new HEAD.
6. Bound STATUS → `collect` / `targeted_validation_required`, one `provider_targeted_validator` slot (`review.capture-validation --materialize=true`), carrying a new target identity.
7. Request the one-run forecast, acknowledge it, and submit that exact slot verbatim through the host relay.
8. Observe the refusal. Query bound STATUS again; it reoffers the same slot with the same request hash and the same target identity. Submit the identical bytes once more.

### ✅ Expected Behavior
A validator result produced for the exact provider-issued correction request should be admitted exactly once and produce a verdict for the accepted correction plan. If the result genuinely cannot bind, the diagnostic should name the actionable side (result materialization vs provider request derivation) instead of returning an opaque `invalid_request` for a request that STATUS still reissues as current.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
Both submissions are refused before admission:

```
Error: targeted validation result does not bind the provider-owned correction request [invalid_request]
```

Host-relay envelope: `stage: submit`, `exit_code: 1`, `elapsed_ms: 154`, `mutation_performed: false`, `mutation_outcome: none`, `next_action`: call fresh STATUS and run only the exact reoffered slot. The fresh STATUS reoffers the identical slot, and the identical submission reproduces the identical refusal. No third attempt was made.

### Gentle AI Version
3.7.0 (stable build; no `-rc.` or `-main.` tag)

### Operating System
Linux (x86_64)

### AI Agent / Client
Other — Pi host relay (`--agent=pi`, contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`)

### 📋 Affected Area
CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output
```text
attempt 1: review.capture-validation refused at admission
           - targeted validation result does not bind the provider-owned correction request [invalid_request]
           - mutation_performed: false, mutation_outcome: none, slot not consumed
fresh status: collect / targeted_validation_required, identical slot, identical request_hash
attempt 2: identical submission, identical refusal
```

### Additional Context
Operation shape: compact-v2 bounded correction on a committed range, provider-owned targeted validation after an admitted correction.

Safe opaque identifiers:
- Retained lineage: `review-2561b1cdcc7a1d57`
- Correction request hash: `sha256:f99c7fb3bda86a2815d4cfbc50b5a2cdd8439723aebd6331a1e6dd4b056f957f`
- Accepted correction plan: 90 diff lines; correction committed at 88 diff lines
- Original target: `sha256:62ef9641f69572ab43303b97c27eea3fda68b8477c3ba4411865980020b14645`
- Corrected target: `sha256:cd375c9145b0ed084ba9fe40822b843afa35ac45f11cdead2a97cf797fa6b0b3`

Preserved-state evidence: convergent worktree unchanged at the corrected commit; lineage retained in `correction_required` with the same offered slot; no reset/reclaim/recover; no delivery operation; the refused bytes were not replayed again after the second refusal; an earlier bound review in the same run reached `approved` and completed its acknowledgement.

title: feat(agents): integrate a defensive Sec-TDD worker through native client delegation
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Problem Statement

Gentle AI supports 17 clients, but has no managed, verified test-authoring security worker. Existing read-only review lenses do not write defensive regression tests. Agent integration differs by client: native files, configuration agents, dynamic workers, inherited configuration, and clients with no established delegation contract. Copying a universal Markdown prompt would advertise support that does not execute.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Add a bounded Sec-TDD role only through each viable client-native mechanism. It maps trust boundaries, challenges vulnerability hypotheses against existing controls, writes local negative regressions using synthetic identities, records observed RED/GREEN, and hands production fixes to the implementation worker. Authorization matrices, property tests, static rules and LLM-boundary tests apply only when the project supports them. Test installation, upgrade, ownership, preservation of user overrides, uninstall, dispatch, model selection and tool boundaries per client. Stop and document each unsupported client rather than marking it compatible. Do not add a Go RDD reviewer role or treat prompt text as a sandbox. No live attacks or real credentials.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

Reuse `review-risk` (wrong role); distribute one prompt to all clients (no native dispatch/ownership proof); claim support from `FileSubAgents` alone (the manifest explicitly does not guarantee delegation).

### 📎 Additional Context

Deliver as independent review slices of roughly 400 authored changed lines or less, with tests and documentation in each unit. Coordinate Pi runtime ownership through a separate gentle-shell issue. Candidate blockers include Cursor's retired assets, Kimi's legacy format, Windsurf's solo contract and Conductor's Claude inheritance.

title: [Automated provider defect] opencode: re-registering a resumed session hits POST /sessions 409, collapsed into a false server-availability error and blocking all attributed writes (3.7.0)
body:
### Summary

On OpenCode, session-attributed memory writes (`mem_save`, `mem_save_prompt`, `mem_session_summary`, `mem_capture_passive`) fail permanently with:

```
gentle-engram could not confirm Engram session registration for engram_mem_save; verify that the Engram server is available and retry
```

The Engram server was **available and healthy** throughout: `/health` returned 200, `engram doctor` was clean, CLI writes landed, and read tools kept working. The blocking condition is a **`409 Conflict`** from `POST /sessions` when the adapter re-registers a session that Engram already closed. `engramFetch()` collapses every non-2xx status into `null`, so the 409 is indistinguishable from an outage and is reported as server unavailability.

Because the adapter closes the session on `dispose` and OpenCode resumes the same session id after a restart, the failure is **permanent and self-inflicted on every resumed session**.

### Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| gentle-ai | 3.7.0 (stable build string, no `-rc.`/`-main.` tag) |
| engram binary | 2.2.1 |
| Client | OpenCode 1.18.33 |
| OS / arch | Windows amd64 |
| Component | OpenCode plugin adapter — `tool.execute.before` attributed-write guard + `ensureSession()` |

### Evidence

Read-only HTTP measurements against the same local Engram server the adapter talks to:

| Request | Result |
|---|---|
| `POST /sessions` with a **new** session id | `201 {"status":"created"}` |
| `POST /sessions` with a session id Engram has already closed | **`409`**, empty body |
| `GET /sessions/{closed id}` | `200`, `ended_at` set |
| `POST /sessions/{id}/end` | `200` |
| `POST /sessions/{id}/reopen`, `/start`, `/resume` | `404` — no reopen path exists |
| `POST /observations` against the **closed** session | `201 {"status":"saved"}` |
| `GET /health` | `200`, instance id matches `engram instance-id` |
| `GET /project/current` | `200`, project resolved |
| `engram delete session {closed id}` | refused: "session still has observations" |

Instrumenting the adapter's `tool.execute.before` to dump in-process state at the throw site showed every suspected guard clean:

```
disposed: False          localReady: True        projectResolutionError: ''
known: False             invalid: False          closeRequested: False
closed: False            subAgent: False         parentHas: True
registrationAttempts: True
```

So the refusal is not `disposed`, not the invalid / close-requested / closed / sub-agent sets, and not project resolution. The only unreachable step is registration: `POST /sessions` answers 409 and can never succeed for that id, so `knownSessions` is never populated.

### Root cause (observed in the adapter)

1. `dispose` ends the session's Engram lifecycle via `POST /sessions/{id}/end`.
2. OpenCode resumes the same session id on the next start.
3. `ensureSession()` re-registers it with `POST /sessions`; Engram replies **409** because the row exists and is closed.
4. `engramFetch()` returns `null` for *any* non-2xx status, so the 409 reaches the caller as `null` — indistinguishable from a connection failure.
5. The hook throws the server-availability message.

Confirmed by intervention: the 409 is the only blocker. Treating 409 as "already registered" restores every attributed write immediately, with no change to Engram.

### Distinct from the existing reports

- **#5007** — same error string, different causal class. There the client is offered a reduced tool set, `mem_session_start` is unreachable, and *every* write fails across all projects. Here the tool set was complete (`mem_session_start` was callable), the attribution diagnostic reported `ok` with no ambiguity, and only the resumed session failed.
- **#5056** — same guard, same error string, but that report explicitly bounds its class to "a session the store still reports **open**" (`ended_at` NULL) with the blocking state in the adapter's in-memory lifecycle. Here the store reports the session **closed** (`ended_at` set) and every in-memory set listed above is clean — the blocking condition is server-side and API-level.

### Reproduction

1. Run OpenCode with the engram plugin adapter on a session, then stop OpenCode (the adapter ends the Engram session).
2. Start OpenCode and **resume the same session**.
3. Call any attributed write tool, e.g. `mem_save`.
4. Observe: `could not confirm Engram session registration`.
5. `GET /sessions/{id}` shows `ended_at` set; `POST /sessions` with that id returns 409; `POST /sessions` with a fresh id returns 201.
6. Read-only tools and `engram doctor` still report a healthy store.

### Expected

- A write to a session Engram has closed either lands, or the failure names the actual condition (closed session, no reopen path) instead of server availability.
- A resumed session is not permanently un-writable.

### Actual

- The error names server availability as the cause; the server answered every request correctly.
- All attributed writes for the resumed session fail for the lifetime of that session, with no recovery path.

### Suggested direction (not a diagnosis)

- Preserve the response status through `engramFetch()` so a 409 is not reported as an outage.
- Treat `POST /sessions` 409 as "already registered" — a closed session still accepts observations (measured above), so registration state is the only gate.
- Alternatively, give sessions a reopen path, or avoid closing a session whose client id may be resumed.

### Related

- #5007 — same error string, different causal class (reduced tool set / attribution ambiguity).
- #5056 — same guard and error string, different blocking condition (store reports the session open).

### Evidence limits

The adapter's internal state was captured in-process at the throw site, so the guard state above is measured rather than inferred. This report does not claim Engram's intended 409 semantics; it claims only that the 409 is what blocks registration, and that collapsing it into `null` is what produces the misleading message. No upstream repository was inspected or modified as part of this report.

title: feat(odd): critique substantial feature intent with fresh context before implementation
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Problem Statement

ODD creates a feature document for substantial implementation after exploration, capturing scope, constraints, tasks, and acceptance criteria. The same context that shaped that document also drives implementation. A missed scenario, unsupported assumption, contradiction, or unclear acceptance criterion can therefore survive until code and tests have already been written. Users cannot be expected to review every feature document themselves. ODD permits one scoped assumption challenge for a high-consequence premise, but it does not provide a fresh-context critique of the feature intent as a whole before implementation.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

For substantial authorized features, after the feature document and Engram mirror have been created but before the first source change, request one bounded read-only critique from a fresh-context reviewer. Give it the feature document, relevant requirements and code context, and a narrow question: which material gaps in scope, scenarios, constraints, assumptions, or acceptance criteria would change the implementation or its verification? Require concrete evidence and suggested corrections rather than a generic approval verdict.

The orchestrator reconciles findings with existing evidence, updates the feature document and mirror for accepted in-scope corrections, and asks the user only when a genuine product or scope decision remains. Findings must not silently expand authorized scope. The critique is advisory: it creates no new approval state, user consent prompt, native review receipt, or blocking gate for ordinary work. Keep small, understood changes on the current direct route; retain the existing targeted assumption challenge for high-consequence premises without duplicating it. Native RDD continues to review implemented commit/PR candidates under its existing policy.

Acceptance criteria:
- A substantial feature's documented intent receives one bounded independent critique before the first source write; small, understood work does not acquire a mandatory review step.
- The reviewer checks for material missing scenarios, conflicting requirements, unsupported assumptions, and untestable or incomplete acceptance criteria, citing the document or repository evidence.
- The orchestrator incorporates justified in-scope changes into both feature-document copies; unresolved product decisions return to the user, and critique alone does not authorize scope expansion.
- A reviewer finding, absence of findings, or unavailable reviewer is reported honestly without manufacturing an approval, receipt, or new hard gate.
- Guidance and focused tests demonstrate the ordering, the small-work bypass, and preservation of existing assumption-challenge and RDD boundaries.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

Ask the user to review every feature document: unreliable when users do not read generated artifacts and adds a manual interruption. Run native RDD earlier: RDD evaluates a frozen implementation candidate, not the unimplemented feature intent. Reuse only the existing one-premise assumption challenge: useful for a named high-consequence premise, but it does not systematically examine missing scenarios and acceptance criteria across a substantial feature. A mandatory spec-approval gate would add friction and duplicate human authority.

### 📎 Additional Context

The current ODD protocol describes feature-document creation before source changes and native review of a later work-unit commit or PR slice (`docs/usage.md`, "The ODD protocol"). Related issue #3986 proposes a design-minimality pass between exploration and implementation; this request instead targets missing or contradictory feature intent and acceptance criteria, and should be coordinated with that pass rather than adding redundant reviewer machinery.

title: bug(cursor): generated global rule lacks alwaysApply frontmatter
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

Gentle AI installs its global Cursor guidance at `~/.cursor/rules/gentle-ai.mdc`, but the generated `.mdc` file has no YAML frontmatter. It begins directly with `## Rules` and does not declare `alwaysApply: true`.

Cursor's rule format uses YAML frontmatter to control activation, and its bundled rule-authoring guidance states that `alwaysApply: true` applies a rule to every session. As generated, the Gentle AI rule is present on disk but is not automatically loaded into new Cursor Agent conversations.

This also reproduces from the current `main` branch, not only the released 3.7.0 binary. Install verification still reports success because it checks that the file exists, not that it contains valid activation metadata.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Ensure Cursor is installed and `~/.cursor/` exists.
2. Run `gentle-ai install --agent cursor --preset minimal --scope global`.
3. Inspect the beginning of `~/.cursor/rules/gentle-ai.mdc`.
4. Observe that the first line is `## Rules`; there is no YAML frontmatter and no `alwaysApply: true`.
5. Start a new Cursor Agent conversation in a workspace that has no project-local copy of the rule.
6. Observe that the Gentle AI persona and orchestration instructions are not automatically present.

The generation result was also reproduced with a binary built from `main` commit `b424e4b725e817fb5f0320a65de8b3e0bdd6805c` in an isolated `HOME`.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The generated Cursor rule should include valid MDC frontmatter that makes the global Gentle AI guidance apply to every conversation, for example:

```yaml
---
description: Gentle AI global rules
alwaysApply: true
---
```

Installation verification and regression tests should assert the activation metadata, not only the file's existence and body fragments.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The generated file begins directly with Markdown content:

```markdown
## Rules

- Never add "Co-Authored-By" or AI attribution to commits. Use conventional commits only.
```

There is no YAML frontmatter or `alwaysApply: true`. The install command nevertheless reports that verification passed because the required file exists. Cursor does not automatically apply the managed Gentle AI rule in new Agent conversations.

### Gentle AI Version

3.7.0; also reproduced from `main` at `b424e4b725e817fb5f0320a65de8b3e0bdd6805c`

### Operating System

macOS

### AI Agent / Client

Cursor

### 📋 Affected Area

Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
$ gentle-ai version
gentle-ai 3.7.0

$ gentle-ai install --agent cursor --preset minimal --scope global
Verification checks: 4 passed, 0 failed, 0 warnings, 0 skipped
[ok] verify:file:<home>/.cursor/rules/gentle-ai.mdc - required file exists

$ first lines of <home>/.cursor/rules/gentle-ai.mdc
## Rules

- Never add "Co-Authored-By" or AI attribution to commits. Use conventional commits only.
```

### Additional Context

- Cursor version used for the observed behavior: 3.22.7, arm64.
- `internal/agents/cursor/adapter.go` maps the system prompt to `.cursor/rules/gentle-ai.mdc` using `StrategyFileReplace`.
- `internal/components/persona/inject.go` writes the persona body directly for Cursor without wrapping it in MDC frontmatter.
- `TestInjectCursorGentlemanWritesRulesFileWithRealContent` checks body fragments such as `Senior Architect` and `Contextual Skill Loading`, but does not check frontmatter or `alwaysApply`.
- The repository currently contains no `alwaysApply` handling for generated Cursor rules.
- #5009 is not a duplicate: it covered `sync` ordering that deleted managed sections and was fixed on `main`.
- #2123 is not a duplicate: it requests preservation of user customizations during sync.

A minimal regression test could assert that a freshly generated Cursor rules file starts with YAML frontmatter and contains exactly one `alwaysApply: true` declaration while retaining the existing managed body.

title: bug(opencode-plugin): OpenCode V2 community-plugin refusal is classified as a failed apply step, so install runs end in error and roll back
body:
## 📋 Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate. Closest matches are #4729 (managed plugins fail to load on OpenCode v2.0.5+, V1 SDK content) and #4940 (post-apply verification requires V2-skipped logo files). This is neither: no plugin ever loads here, and no verification check is involved. What this reports is that a **documented, intentional refusal** is surfaced as a failed apply step, so the run cannot complete successfully.
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

## 📝 Bug Description

`docs/opencode-compatibility.md` declares the V2 posture for community TUI plugins as an intentional refusal, not a defect:

| Surface | V1 | V2 (tested release: 2.0.4) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Community TUI plugins | Existing integration retained | Compatibility unproven; installation/update refuses, not silently omitted |

That refusal is implemented in `internal/components/opencodeplugin/plugin.go` → `Install()` (v3.7.0, lines 174-184):

```go
if major == opencode.RuntimeV2 {
    if id == model.OpenCodePluginGentleLogo {
        return Result{}, UnsupportedLogoError{}
    }
    return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("OpenCode community plugin V2 compatibility is unverified; existing configuration preserved")
}
```

The asymmetry is the bug: `gentle-logo` returns `UnsupportedLogoError`, which implements `SkipReason()` and is therefore classified as **skipped**; every other community plugin returns a plain `fmt.Errorf`, which the pipeline classifies as **failed** (`internal/pipeline/runner.go:31-40` — only errors carrying a nonempty `SkipReason()` are nonfatal).

The install plan turns each selected community plugin into a step that returns that raw error (`internal/cli/run.go:791-795`, `openCodePluginInstallStep.Run()` at `internal/cli/run.go:1326-1329`), so on an OpenCode V2 host every selected community plugin becomes a failed step:

```
FAILED: opencode-plugin:sub-agent-statusline — OpenCode community plugin V2 compatibility is unverified; existing configuration preserved
FAILED: opencode-plugin:sdd-engram-plugin — OpenCode community plugin V2 compatibility is unverified; existing configuration preserved
pipeline completed with errors
```

In v3.7.0 both entries are still offered by the TUI catalog (`opencodeplugin.Definitions()`, lines 42-61), so a V2 user is invited to check a plugin that can never be installed, and any install run that has either one checked can never finish cleanly.

### Consequences

1. The run is reported as an error even though nothing broke. `internal/tui/model.go:1451-1452` logs `pipeline completed with errors` and returns before `persistInstallReviewMode()`, so the selected global RDD mode is not persisted either.
2. `RunInstall` uses `pipeline.DefaultRollbackPolicy()` (`OnApplyFailure: true`), and `Execute` rolls back every succeeded apply step of the stage when `applyResult.Err != nil` (`internal/pipeline/orchestrator.go:52-63`). A documented refusal therefore triggers the same rollback path as a real installation failure — the refusal can undo an otherwise successful run.
3. The documented reason never reaches the user as a skip: it appears only as `FAILED: ...`, indistinguishable from a broken install.

(On `main` the legacy `sdd-engram-plugin` entry was removed from the install catalog and is retained only for uninstall identification. That narrows the trigger to the remaining catalog entry, but the classification gap is unchanged: any community plugin id in `Selection.OpenCodePlugins` on V2 still produces a hard failure.)

## 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Install OpenCode V2 — reproduced with `opencode v2.0.18`.
2. Install gentle-ai v3.7.0.
3. Launch the TUI (`gentle-ai`) and walk the install flow with OpenCode among the selected agents (preset `full-gentleman` works).
4. On the "Optional OpenCode Community Plugins" screen, check one or both catalog entries (`sub-agent-statusline`, `sdd-engram-plugin`).
5. Run the install.
6. Observe the `FAILED: opencode-plugin:...` lines and `pipeline completed with errors`, while the refusing step writes nothing to `~/.config/opencode`.

## ✅ Expected Behavior

The intentional V2 refusal should be nonfatal and self-describing, exactly like the accepted logo omission:

- The V2 branch returns an error implementing `SkipReason()` (same shape as `UnsupportedLogoError`) for community plugins instead of a bare `fmt.Errorf`, or `openCodePluginInstallStep.Run()` translates it before returning.
- The pipeline records `StepStatusSkipped` and the TUI logs `skipped: opencode-plugin:<id> — OpenCode community plugin V2 compatibility is unverified ...` (`internal/tui/model.go:1383-1389` already handles that path).
- The run ends with `pipeline completed successfully`, post-success work (RDD-mode persist) still runs, and no rollback is triggered by a documented refusal.
- Optionally, the catalog screen annotates/omits entries that cannot be installed on the detected runtime, so the user is not invited to select them in the first place.

## ❌ Actual Behavior

```
running: community-tool:pi-codegraph-reconcile
done: community-tool:pi-codegraph-reconcile
FAILED: opencode-plugin:sub-agent-statusline — OpenCode community plugin V2 compatibility is unverified; existing configuration preserved
FAILED: opencode-plugin:sdd-engram-plugin — OpenCode community plugin V2 compatibility is unverified; existing configuration preserved
pipeline completed with errors
```

No file is written by the failing steps, but the run is reported as failed, the apply stage takes the rollback path, and the persisted post-install work is skipped. Re-running the install reproduces the same result as long as a community plugin stays selected.

## Gentle AI Version

3.7.0 (release binary; the same binary ships inside `gentle-pi` 3.7.0)

## Operating System

Windows (10.0.26200)

## AI Agent / Client

OpenCode (`opencode v2.0.18`)

## 📋 Affected Area

- [ ] CLI (commands, flags)
- [x] TUI (terminal UI)
- [x] Installation Pipeline
- [ ] Agent Detection
- [ ] System Detection
- [ ] Catalog/Steps
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Other

## 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
running: community-tool:pi-codegraph-reconcile
done: community-tool:pi-codegraph-reconcile
FAILED: opencode-plugin:sub-agent-statusline — OpenCode community plugin V2 compatibility is unverified; existing configuration preserved
FAILED: opencode-plugin:sdd-engram-plugin — OpenCode community plugin V2 compatibility is unverified; existing configuration preserved
pipeline completed with errors
```

## Additional Context

Code map at tag `v3.7.0`:

| File | Lines | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `internal/components/opencodeplugin/plugin.go` | 174-184 (`Install`), 28-35 (`UnsupportedLogoError`) | V2 branch: skip-classified error for the logo, bare error for every other plugin |
| `internal/cli/run.go` | 791-795, 1326-1329 | One `opencode-plugin:<id>` apply step per selected community plugin; returns the error unchanged |
| `internal/pipeline/runner.go` | 31-40 | Only `SkipReason()`-carrying errors become `StepStatusSkipped` |
| `internal/pipeline/orchestrator.go` | 52-63 | Failed apply stage → `ExecuteRollback` under `DefaultRollbackPolicy()` |
| `internal/tui/model.go` | 1383-1389, 1443-1444, 1451-1455 | `skipped:` vs `FAILED:` logging, `pipeline completed with errors`, early return before `persistInstallReviewMode()` |
| `docs/opencode-compatibility.md` | "Community TUI plugins" row | Declares the refusal intentional |

This report does not ask for V2 community-plugin support. It asks that the refusal the documentation already promises be classified as a skip, so that a V2 host can complete an install by design rather than by removing the plugin selection.

title: review recover rejects an escalated corrected candidate with base-ref mismatch
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description
An ordinary compact-v2 review was escalated when its targeted validator rejected the first bounded correction. After committing a second correction, lineage-bound STATUS for the corrected candidate offers `action: recover` with `action_disposition: escalated`, but the native `review recover` invocation exits with `Error: recovery base-ref does not match predecessor base`. No actionable correction to the six-input recovery contract is offered. The escalated review remains unresolved; a new review must not bypass its findings.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce
1. Start an ordinary review on a workspace candidate based on commit B. The initial candidate C is reviewed and receives a deterministic blocker.
2. Apply the bounded fix F1. Its targeted validator passes the original criterion but detects a regression and escalates the lineage.
3. Commit a subsequent correction F2. In the **same worktree where the lineage began**, temporarily check out F2 while keeping the historical review store intact. B, C, F1, and F2 are distinct reachable commits/trees; the original review snapshot is B -> C and the rejected fix-diff snapshot is C -> F1.
4. Query bound `review.status` for the escalated lineage. It reports the original three changed paths, base tree B, current candidate tree F2, `action: recover`, provider-selected `action_disposition: escalated`, and a current target identity distinct from F1.
5. Supply the six exact `review recover` fields (`predecessorLineage`, `expectedPredecessorRevision`, fresh `successorLineage`, provider-selected `disposition`, `actor`, `reason`) through the interactive Pi facade. Do not supply a caller-authored authorization binding.
6. Re-query bound STATUS after the failure; restore the worktree's original branch.

### ✅ Expected Behavior
The provider should either recover this corrected candidate through its issued transition, preserving the prior findings, or fail with a typed, actionable explanation of the exact incompatible base/selector and a supported continuation. A recovery command with no `baseRef` input should not be offered when its hidden base-ref precondition cannot be met.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
The native process exits 1 with `recovery base-ref does not match predecessor base`; the Pi facade reports `native-operation-failed`, `mutation_outcome: unknown`, and `status_required`. The immediate bound STATUS still reports the same escalated predecessor revision and recovery action; no successor was observed. A blind retry was not attempted. The original worktree and separate feature branch were left clean and unchanged.

### Gentle AI Version
3.7.0

### Operating System
Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client
Other

### 📋 Affected Area
CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output
```shell
review.status: state=escalated action=recover action_disposition=escalated
projection: kind=base-diff base_tree=<B> initial_review_tree=<C> current_candidate_tree=<F2>
review recover: exit_code=1 stderr="Error: recovery base-ref does not match predecessor base"
facade: outcome=native-operation-failed mutation_outcome=unknown next_action=review.status
review.status (after failure): state=escalated revision=<same predecessor revision> action=recover
```

### Additional Context
The agent/client is Pi via gentle-pi. The review was originally started in the principal worktree; implementation subsequently continued on a sibling feature worktree. The recovery attempt deliberately used the original lineage-bound worktree at F2, not the sibling worktree or the unrelated default-branch candidate. `ABANDON` is documented for non-terminal compact-v2 lineages, while this one is escalated, so it was not attempted. Related but non-equivalent reports: #4504 concerns a committed-range correction representation, and #4433 concerns terminal escalation being re-offered as START/abandon. Neither contains this native base-ref refusal on the workspace recovery route. No source repository names, local paths, usernames, tokens, or private hostnames are included.

title: test(app): the documented-invocation sandbox is not hermetic — a concurrent Go toolchain write fails t.TempDir cleanup
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

`TestDocumentedInvocationsRunAsDocumented` (`internal/app/documented_invocation_test.go`) flakily fails its own `t.TempDir` cleanup on a developer machine, with no assertion failure anywhere in the test:

```text
testing.go:1369: TempDir RemoveAll cleanup: unlinkat /tmp/TestDocumentedInvocationsRunAsDocumentedexecutedsync_#4189739437/001: directory not empty
--- FAIL: TestDocumentedInvocationsRunAsDocumented/executed/sync_#
--- FAIL: TestDocumentedInvocationsRunAsDocumented/executed/sync_--dry-run
--- FAIL: TestDocumentedInvocationsRunAsDocumented/executed/restore_latest
```

The corpus passes its assertions and reports its summary line; only the framework's cleanup step fails. CI is green on the same commit, so this is timing/path sensitive rather than deterministic.

The sandbox is built by `newDocumentedInvocationSandbox` (`internal/app/documented_invocation_test.go:313-326`), which points `HOME`, `USERPROFILE`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `XDG_STATE_HOME` at a `t.TempDir()`, and the corpus runs the documented verbs **in-process** (`app.RunArgs`, line 477). Anything the verb reaches that writes into that home therefore writes into the directory the framework is about to delete.

**The artifact that loses the race**, left on disk after a failing run, is the Go toolchain's own telemetry counter:

```text
/001/home/.config/go/telemetry/local/go@go1.25.10-go1.25.10-linux-amd64-2026-09-28.v1.count
/001/home/.config/go/telemetry/upload/
```

Only that counter survives cleanup — `repo/` and the rest of `home/` are removed — so a Go toolchain process is writing there after the subtest body returns.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

On a Linux host with Go on `PATH` and a normal (non-CI) environment:

```sh
for i in $(seq 1 12); do
  go test -count=1 -run 'TestDocumentedInvocationsRunAsDocumented' ./internal/app/ || echo "run $i FAILED"
done
```

Observed here: **9 to 11 failures out of 12**, always the same three subtests.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The corpus sandbox should be hermetic: neither the developer's environment nor Go's own bookkeeping should be able to write into a `t.TempDir()` after the subtest that owns it has returned. Either the sandbox should not redirect the Go toolchain's config/state root, or the executed tier should own a scratch directory whose removal cannot race a concurrent writer.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

`t.TempDir` reports `directory not empty` and the package fails, with no product assertion failing and no product defect indicated.

Causes I could **rule out** by experiment (all on `main` @ `e2cb2bf2`, same command, 12 iterations each):

| Hypothesis | Result |
|---|---|
| gentle-ai's own telemetry | `GENTLE_AI_TELEMETRY=0` → still **11/12** fail |
| Go toolchain telemetry disabled | `GOTELEMETRY=off` → **10/12** fail (the `go` command still creates `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/go/telemetry/{local,upload}`) |
| A `go` child resolved from the ambient `PATH` | `PATH` without `go` → **7/8**; a logging `go` wrapper placed first on `PATH` recorded **zero** invocations |

So the writer is a Go toolchain process that this sandbox's environment reaches some other way, and I could not identify the exact spawn site without tracing tools (`strace` is unavailable here, and installing it needs root). I am reporting the artifact, the chain and the refutations rather than guessing the last link.

### 🖥️ Environment

**Gentle AI Version:** dev build `3.0.0-20260927195256-e2cb2bf25193` (`main` @ `e2cb2bf2`)

**Operating System:** Windows (WSL) — Ubuntu 24.04, Go 1.25.10 installed natively

**AI Agent / Client:** Other

**📋 Affected Area:** Other (test infrastructure)

### Additional Context

- Related in the same family, not duplicates: #4678 (`test(cli): stabilize TempDir cleanup after Windows atomic renames`, open, different package and cause), #4843 and #5039 (closed, test/environment leakage).
- One adjacent hazard worth a look while investigating: `internal/system/path.go` mutates the **process** `PATH` with `os.Setenv` (`addToProcessPath`, `prioritizeProcessPath`) and never restores it, and `internal/cli/run.go:86` wires it as `addUserPath`. Any test that exercises an install path therefore changes the `PATH` every later test in that binary sees. That is exactly the kind of ambient leak this sandbox is trying to avoid.

*Filing note: created through the GitHub API, so the bug-report form's labels were not applied — a contributor cannot add them afterwards either (`AddLabelsToLabelable` is refused). A maintainer adding `bug` and `status:needs-review` would put it in the normal triage queue.*

---

Every command and count quoted above was run and verified by the human contributor against `main` @ `e2cb2bf2` before posting.*

title: test(cli): install and sync tests inherit the host codex binary and fail when its version probe fails
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

The `internal/cli` install and sync tests are not hermetic with respect to the host's `codex` binary: they fail on any machine where a `codex` is resolvable on `PATH` and its `--version` probe fails. CI stays green only because CI has no `codex` installed.

The test helpers already isolate the analogous OpenCode probe. `installTestHome` (`internal/cli/opencode_background_test.go:311-328`) stubs `osUserHomeDir`, `runCommand`, `cmdLookPath` (to a missing-binary helper), `runOpenCodeVersion` and `resolveOpenCodeTarget`. Its own comment describes the intent: an isolated home "where every runtime binary resolves as installed".

The Codex runtime-version probe is not stubbed, and it does not go through the stubbed `cmdLookPath`:

- `internal/agents/codex/runtime_version.go:32` — `runVersionCommand = func() ([]byte, error) { return exec.Command("codex", "--version").CombinedOutput() }`
- reached from the engram injection step: `internal/components/engram/inject.go:437` — `codex.ValidateGPT56Runtime()`

So the real host `codex` executes, and any error other than `exec.ErrNotFound` becomes a hard install/sync failure:

```text
execute install pipeline: inject engram for "codex": Codex >=0.144.0 is required for GPT-5.6 profiles.
Update Codex with: npm install -g --ignore-scripts @openai/codex@latest
(codex --version failed: exit status 1: ...)
```

This is the same class of defect as #5041 (a host `opencode` binary leaking into a hostile-environment test, fixed by #5045), one binary over.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Put a resolvable `codex` on `PATH` whose `--version` fails:

   ```sh
   mkdir -p /tmp/codexstub
   printf '#!/bin/sh\necho "Error: Missing optional dependency @openai/codex-linux-x64" >&2\nexit 1\n' > /tmp/codexstub/codex
   chmod +x /tmp/codexstub/codex
   ```

2. Run the package with that directory first on `PATH`:

   ```sh
   PATH=/tmp/codexstub:$PATH go test -count=1 ./internal/cli/
   ```

3. Observe the failures below. Remove the stub from `PATH` and the same command passes.

   ```sh
   PATH=/tmp/codexstub:$PATH go test -count=1 ./internal/cli/   # FAIL
   go test -count=1 ./internal/cli/                             # ok
   ```

### ✅ Expected Behavior

`internal/cli` tests should be hermetic against the host toolchain. The same helper that already stubs the OpenCode version probe should stub the Codex one, since a seam already exists for it: `codex.SetRuntimeVersionCommandForTest` / `codex.SetRuntimeVersionProbeForTest` (`internal/agents/codex/runtime_version.go:188-197`). A broken, foreign, or older `codex` on the developer's machine should not change the outcome of tests unrelated to it.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Five tests fail whenever the host `codex` version probe fails:

```text
--- FAIL: TestInstallThenSyncConverges (0.99s)
    --- FAIL: TestInstallThenSyncConverges/codex (0.01s)
--- FAIL: TestCodexReinstallKeepsConfigTOML (0.01s)
--- FAIL: TestCodeGraphInstallThenSyncConverges (0.89s)
    --- FAIL: TestCodeGraphInstallThenSyncConverges/codex (0.07s)
--- FAIL: TestInstallLeavesNoDanglingSharedReferences (1.13s)
    --- FAIL: TestInstallLeavesNoDanglingSharedReferences/codex (0.01s)
--- FAIL: TestSyncCodexGentlemanConvergesWithHooksJSON (0.02s)
FAIL	github.com/gentleman-programming/gentle-ai/v3/internal/cli	3.066s
```

Measured on the same commit, full suite both ways:

| `codex` on PATH | result |
|---|---|
| resolvable but `--version` fails | 78 packages ok, **5 tests FAIL** in `internal/cli` |
| absent | **79 packages ok, 0 FAIL** |

### 🖥️ Environment

**Gentle AI Version:** dev build `3.0.0-20260927195256-e2cb2bf25193` (`main` @ `e2cb2bf2`)

**Operating System:** Windows (WSL) — but the reproduction above is platform independent; any host with a failing `codex` reproduces it. I originally hit it because WSL interop exposes the Windows npm Codex (`/mnt/c/Users/Willy/AppData/Roaming/npm/node_modules/@openai/codex/bin/codex.js`), which cannot run under Linux:

```text
Error: Missing optional dependency @openai/codex-linux-x64. Reinstall Codex: npm install -g @openai/codex@latest
    at findCodexExecutable (file:///mnt/c/.../node_modules/@openai/codex/bin/codex.js:105:9)
```

**AI Agent / Client:** Other

**📋 Affected Area:** Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
RunInstall() error = execute install pipeline: inject engram for "codex": Codex >=0.144.0 is required for GPT-5.6 profiles. Update Codex with: npm install -g --ignore-scripts @openai/codex@latest (codex --version failed: exit status 1: file:///mnt/c/Users/Willy/AppData/Roaming/npm/node_modules/@openai/codex/bin/codex.js:105
      throw new Error(
            ^

        Error: Missing optional dependency @openai/codex-linux-x64. Reinstall Codex: npm install -g @openai/codex@latest
            at findCodexExecutable (file:///mnt/c/Users/Willy/AppData/Roaming/npm/node_modules/@openai/codex/bin/codex.js:105:9)
            at file:///mnt/c/Users/Willy/AppData/Roaming/npm/node_modules/@openai/codex/bin/codex.js:110:20
            at ModuleJob.run (node:internal/modules/esm/module_job:561:25)
```

### Additional Context

- The same `--version` probe also decides a real product behavior (`ValidateGPT56Runtime` gates GPT-5.6 profile configuration), so making it injectable here is a test-isolation change only; I am not proposing to change what the product does when a user's Codex is genuinely too old or broken.
- Related but distinct: #4678 (`test(cli): stabilize TempDir cleanup after Windows atomic renames`) is another `internal/cli` hermeticity issue in the same package, with a different cause.
- A second, unrelated hermeticity defect turned up during the same investigation: the `internal/app` documented-invocation sandbox (`newDocumentedInvocationSandbox`, `internal/app/documented_invocation_test.go:313-326`) redirects `HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`XDG_STATE_HOME` into a `t.TempDir()`, and `t.TempDir` cleanup intermittently fails with `directory not empty` because the Go toolchain's own telemetry counters land there (`home/.config/go/telemetry/local/go@go1.25.10-...v1.count`). I have not filed it yet; I can do so separately if that is useful.

---

*Disclosure: the reproduction, the code reading, and this report were produced with material AI assistance (el Gentleman harness on Pi; provider `nan`, model `deepseek-v4-flash`). Every command and result quoted above was run and verified by the human contributor against `main` @ `e2cb2bf2` before posting.*

title: bug(review): negotiated OpenCode review.start fails with invalid consent question identity before consent envelope is shown (3.7.0)
body:
### Pre-flight Checks
- [x] Explicit user consent was obtained to report this apparent provider defect.
- [x] Open and closed issues were searched for the exact error code (`invalid consent question identity`); none found. Related open reports describe other START failures (#2196, #4749, #4952, #5032) but not this exact consent-identity failure.
- [x] This report contains observed evidence only and does not assert a root cause.
- [x] Final privacy scan completed immediately before creation: no raw argv, absolute paths, private project names, usernames, hostnames, credentials, diffs, source contents, or environment values are included. Identifiers are SHA, lineage id, and one sanitized WASM size only.

### Bug Description
On the OpenCode host, negotiated `review start` is rejected before any review mutation with `mutation_outcome: unknown`, citing `validate consent question: invalid consent question identity`. The provider-issued START transition, when run once, returned no `gentle-ai.review-integration.consent/v3` envelope, so the human consent decision point becomes unreachable. The defensive local diagnostic file was written to `.git/gentle-ai/defect-reports/operation-outcome-unknown-<hash>.md`, but no lineage, receipt, authority, or delivery mutation was created, and the candidate bytes remained unchanged.

### Environment
- Gentle AI: 3.7.0 (unknown install channel)
- OS/architecture: Windows 11 x86_64
- Client: OpenCode via the gentle-orchestrator primary agent
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`
- Projection: `workspace`
- Negotiation path: selectorless `review.status` returned `fresh_target_ready`; exact provider-issued `review.start` was run verbatim.

### Observed Sequence
1. Native assess: `risk: medium`, `review_due: true`, reason `slice_budget_reached`.
2. Selectorless STATUS (exact provider command, `--committed-only`, `--base-ref` set to the candidate base SHA): returned `next_transition.execute.review.start` with a fresh lineage token and target-evidence matching the prepared committed-only candidate (13 paths).
3. START executed verbatim from the STATUS return with `--consent=relay`, `--lineage=<fresh>`, `--agent=opencode`, `--target` and `--target-evidence` copied unchanged:
   - `schema: gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2`
   - `operation: review.start`
   - `phase: native_running`
   - `code: operation_outcome_unknown`
   - `mutation_outcome: unknown`
   - `lineage_id: <fresh>`
   - `cause: validate consent question: invalid consent question identity`
4. As a documented side effect, a local failure file was written at `.git/gentle-ai/defect-reports/operation-outcome-unknown-<hash>.md`.
5. No `gentle-ai.review-integration.consent/v3` envelope was ever produced; no exact decline invocation was offered; the candidate state remained unchanged.

### Expected Behavior
A provider-relay START on a non-empty committed-only candidate should either reach native admission and surface a v3 consent envelope (or exact decline invocation) for the consumer, or return a typed actionable stop with the exact recovery transition. It should not silently fail at `validate consent question`, mark `mutation_outcome: unknown`, and leave the consumer without an envelope or a recoverable continuation.

### Actual Behavior
- Operative failure: `operation_outcome_unknown` with cause `validate consent question: invalid consent question identity`.
- Side effect: a local failure file written under `.git/gentle-ai/defect-reports/` (documented behavior, but should not be the only signal).
- Mutation outcome: `unknown`; lineage created: false; no authority was evaluated; the candidate bytes are unchanged.
- Recovery: STATUS offered the same `next_transition.execute.review.start` again with no provider-owning change, so re-invoking risks an identical unknown outcome; the consumer cannot choose between admit and decline without an envelope.

### Minimal Reproduction
- A Git workspace with a committed-only candidate (no untracked files).
- Provide a client/runtime that registers the gentle-orchestrator agent with `task` permissions for the v2 review contracts.
- Run native assess; then run selectorless STATUS with `--committed-only --base-ref=<HEAD after candidate>`; then run the exact provider-issued `review.start` with `--consent=relay`, unchanged `--target` and `--target-evidence`.
- Observe `operation_outcome_unknown` cause `invalid consent question identity` and the local defect-report file; no consent envelope is ever returned.

### Bounded Attempts and Preserved State
- 1 selectorless STATUS, 1 exact provider-issued START.
- Both ran against the same target identity and target-evidence tokens as the prior STATUS; no client-rebuilt flags.
- No lineage, receipt, authority, commit, push, PR, or delivery mutation was created. The candidate remains preserved locally.

### Safety Impact
The reviewer/consent decision point is unreachable for this candidate. The consumer must either stop or carry the candidate forward under ordinary repository policy without native reviewer authority.

### Related But Not Duplicate
- #2196, #4749, #4952, #5032 — describe other pre-START or post-START review defects; the literal error code and the missing consent envelope differ.
- #1856, #2872, #3143, #3551 — closed issues for older version ranges covering related but distinct START rejection modes.

title: feat(sdd): keep Strict TDD suites lean — reuse tests, prune in REFACTOR, quiet scoped test runs
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

Other (SDD skills: `sdd-apply/strict-tdd.md`, `sdd-verify/strict-tdd-verify.md`)

### 💡 Problem Statement

With Strict TDD enabled, test suites grow monotonically and token usage snowballs over time. One user reports a suite of 1000+ tests that is re-run constantly, and another community user reports the same.

Observed causes (gentle-ai 3.7.0):

1. **Triangulation is mandatory by default** (`strict-tdd.md`: "DEFAULT: triangulation is REQUIRED"), and the skill never says *where* triangulation cases should live, so agents usually add new test functions instead of extending existing ones.
2. **The contract is additive only.** No rule tells the agent to look for existing tests of the same behavior, update or delete tests that a change invalidates, or merge duplicates during REFACTOR.
3. **Test output is read in full.** Running tests costs no tokens, but reading per-test `PASS` lines does. The skills say to run only the relevant file during the cycle, but they never ask for a quiet reporter (failures + summary only), so full-suite runs at task closure and in `sdd-verify` add the whole suite output to the context.

These feed each other: more tests → more output → more failures to fix after each change → more rework → more tests.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Keep RED → GREEN → TRIANGULATE → REFACTOR unchanged, and add three rules to `strict-tdd.md` (and matching checks in `strict-tdd-verify.md`):

1. **Reuse before create:** before RED, search for existing tests of the same behavior. Triangulate by adding cases to an existing table-driven or parametrized test, and create a new test function only for new behavior.
2. **Prune as part of REFACTOR:** update or delete tests that a change invalidates, and merge tests that assert the same outcome. Report `reused | extended | new | deleted` per test in the TDD evidence table.
3. **Quiet, scoped execution:** run affected tests only while iterating and the full suite once per task closure, always with a quiet reporter (e.g. `vitest --reporter=dot`, `jest --silent`, `pytest -q -rf`, filtered `go test`). Always read failure output in full.

Optionally, `sdd-init` could detect the stack and store the quiet/affected test commands next to the test runner it already records.

I have a working user-level skill (in `~/.agents/skills`, loaded through global user instructions for Claude Code, Pi, and gentle-shell) that implements this without modifying managed files, and I'm happy to share it or open a PR if this gets approved.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- **Disable Strict TDD:** this loses the safety net; the problem is growth and output noise, not TDD itself.
- **Edit the managed `strict-tdd.md` locally:** this is likely overwritten by `gentle-ai sync`.
- **User-level skill (current workaround):** this works, but every user has to rediscover it, and it sits next to a contract that still says "triangulation REQUIRED" without saying how.

### 📎 Additional Context

This came up in the Gentle AI users' Discord, where another user had hit the same problem and worked around it with a custom skill.

title: [Automated provider defect] opencode: attributed-write guard refuses a session the store still reports open, and the compaction hook mandates the refused call (3.7.0)
body:
### Summary

On OpenCode, `engram_mem_session_summary` and `engram_mem_save` fail with:

```
gentle-engram could not confirm Engram session registration for engram_mem_session_summary; verify that the Engram server is available and retry
```

The Engram server was **available and healthy the whole time**. Only **one** session was affected; writes in other sessions of the same runtime succeeded. The failure is session-scoped, not server-scoped, and the suggested remedy in the message is wrong for this case.

### Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| gentle-ai | 3.7.0 (stable build string, no `-rc.`/`-main.` tag) |
| engram binary | 2.1.0 |
| Client | OpenCode 1.18.30 |
| OS / arch | Linux x86_64 |
| Component | OpenCode plugin adapter, `experimental.session.compacting` hook + `tool.execute.before` attributed-write guard |

### Evidence

Session under test: a long-lived interactive root session, healthy for hours, whose last user turn was a close-out message. Per-project and per-session facts, all from local read-only inspection:

| Observation | Result |
|---|---|
| User prompt captured by the store, same session | succeeded, ~27 s **before** the failure |
| `mem_save` in a *different* session, same runtime, same moment | succeeded |
| `engram doctor` after the failure | 9/9 checks `ok`, 0 warnings, 0 errors |
| `ambiguous_active_runtime_sessions` diagnostic | `ok` — "No issues detected" |
| Store row for the affected session | present, `ended_at` **NULL** (no closure was ever processed) |

The prompt-capture hook (`chat.message`) and the attributed-write guard (`tool.execute.before`) both depend on the same session-resolution path. The capture succeeded 27 s earlier, so the session was resolvable and registerable at that moment; the write guard refused it seconds later.

### Root cause (observed in the adapter)

`tool.execute.before` reaches the "could not confirm" throw only when an authoritative session ID *was* resolved and `ensureSession()` then returned `false`. `ensureSession()` returns `false` when the in-memory session is in `invalidSessions`, `closeRequestedSessions`, `closedSessions`, `subAgentSessions`, or when the plugin instance was `disposed`.

The store row still shows `ended_at = NULL`, so no closure was ever acknowledged by the server. Two shapes of this are reachable in the adapter:

1. **Unrecoverable in-memory poison on a failed close.** `closeKnownSession()` adds the session to `closeRequestedSessions` *before* attempting `POST /sessions/{id}/end`, and `endSessionInEngram()` removes it from that set only on a successful acknowledgement. A close that is requested but not acknowledged therefore leaves the session permanently un-writable for the lifetime of the plugin process, while the server still lists it as open — exactly the observed state.
2. **Plugin reload / dispose.** `ensureSession()` returns `false` for *all* sessions once the plugin instance is `disposed`; the in-memory sets do not survive a reload, so the poisoned state is invisible after restart.

The sets are process-local, so the exact condition that fired cannot be proven after the process exits. Observed behaviour is consistent with (1) and inconsistent with a server outage, an ambiguous-registration condition, or a sub-agent session.

### Second finding: the compaction hook mandates a call the guard can refuse

`experimental.session.compacting` gates the compaction-context fetch on `ensureSession(sessionId, true)`, but the block pushed to `output.context` is **not** gated:

> CRITICAL INSTRUCTION FOR COMPACTED SUMMARY: ... You MUST include the following instruction at the TOP of the compacted summary: "FIRST ACTION REQUIRED: Call mem_session_summary ..."

So when `ensureSession()` fails, the adapter skips the safe path and still instructs the agent to call `mem_session_summary` as its first action — a call that `tool.execute.before` will then reject with the error above. Immediately adjacent to the reported failure, OpenCode ran an automatic compaction in the same session (~0.4 s later), so this path re-arms the same refusal.

### Expected

- A write either resolves to an unambiguous, writable session and lands, or the failure names the actual condition that blocked it (closed / invalidated / sub-agent / plugin disposed) instead of a server-availability remedy.
- A session that the store still reports as open is not silently un-writable.
- The compaction hook does not inject a mandatory instruction whose target call the same adapter can refuse.

### Actual

- The error names server availability as the cause; the server was healthy.
- The affected session's end-of-session writes were all rejected, so the session summary and final `mem_save` never persisted.
- The store row for that session is still open with `ended_at = NULL`, and gives no signal that it is unwritable.
- No client-side remedy exists for this shape: the remedy is a plugin/session-lifecycle condition, not a missing tool or an argument.

### Reproduction

1. Run OpenCode with the engram plugin adapter on a session that stays open long enough to accumulate context.
2. Let the session reach its end-of-session close-out, where the agent runs its memory-write protocol.
3. Attempt `mem_session_summary` and `mem_save` on that session.
4. Observe: `could not confirm Engram session registration`.
5. `engram doctor` still reports healthy, and writes on other sessions still succeed.

### Impact

End-of-session memory is silently lost exactly at the moment it matters most — session boundaries. The store looks healthy, so nothing surfaces the loss. Reported severity: medium (data loss, no crash, narrow trigger).

### Related

- #5007 — same error string, **different causal class**: there the client is offered a reduced tool set so the registration remedy is unreachable, and *every* write fails across all projects. Here every write succeeds except one session's, the tool set is complete, and the blocking state is the adapter's in-memory session lifecycle.
- #4475 — delegated sub-agents leaking unclosed Engram sessions; a related lifecycle leak with the opposite failure direction (ambiguity rather than refusal).

### Note on evidence limits

The blocking state is process-local, so this report does not claim a confirmed internal branch. The externally observable facts — healthy server, successful capture 27 s prior, successful writes in a sibling session, `ended_at` still NULL, doctor clean — are reproducible and rule out the server-outage and ambiguous-registration explanations.

title: bug(review): lens_context_inspection_failed on every fresh Claude Code slot for a candidate with a ~2.6 MB binary-attributed path; refresh-and-retry reoffers the same failing slots (3.7.0)
body:
## Automated provider-defect report

### Environment
- Gentle AI: `3.7.0` (stable channel)
- Client: Claude Code `2.1.283`, in-process capture (`review.capture-result` tokens carry `--agent=claude-code`, no `--input`)
- OS/architecture: Windows 11, x86_64 (Git Bash)
- Review contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`

### Operation shape
1. `review assess --committed-only --base-ref <last reviewed commit>` → `risk: high`, `review_due: true`.
2. Exact returned preflight STATUS → exact START with `--consent=relay` → consent envelope → exact `granted` invocation.
3. START `created`, state `reviewing`, 4 lenses (risk, resilience, readability, reliability), correction budget 200.
4. Bound STATUS → `collect / reviewer_results_required` with 4 `review.capture-result` slots.
5. The 4 exact capture invocations launched concurrently, tokens unchanged.

Candidate: committed base-diff, 8 paths, 846 insertions / 55 deletions. One path is a ~2.6 MB JSON file marked `binary` in `.gitattributes` (numstat `- -`); the rest are text (JS, JSON, Markdown).

### Observed evidence
Every capture failed in preflight, no mutation:

```text
code: invalid_request
phase: preflight
mutation_outcome: not_started
retry_safe: true
cause: lens_context_inspection_failed: provider-owned reviewer lens context was not produced; ask the parent orchestrator to refresh the exact native next transition ... then run this operation again with the tokens it returns
```

Following the remediation: bound STATUS was re-queried, it reoffered the same 4 slots at the same expected revision, and all 4 were relaunched with the new tokens. All 4 failed again with the identical cause. Total: 2 bounded attempts per slot (7 captures executed), 0 admitted results.

### Controlled comparison (same machine, same build, same session)
- An earlier 4-lens review on the same repository completed and was acknowledged normally. Its candidate: 3 paths, ~2,088 changed lines, including an ~87 KB JSON file that was also marked `binary` at the time.
- Several 1-lens reviews on text-only candidates completed normally.
- The failing candidate is the only one containing the ~2.6 MB binary-attributed path. Unverified hypothesis: that path prevents lens-context materialization and surfaces as `inspection_failed` rather than `lens_context_budget_exceeded`.

### Expected
Either a lens context is produced, or a terminal, actionable refusal (e.g. `lens_context_budget_exceeded` with a split that can succeed). A `retry_safe: true` remediation should not reoffer the same slot to fail identically.

### Actual
Deterministic `lens_context_inspection_failed` on fresh slots. The prescribed "refresh and retry" reoffers the same slots and fails the same way.

### Related (not established as the same root cause)
- #3078: same code on fresh Claude Code slots (2.3.0), closed.
- #3338: binary assets preventing lens context (reported as `lens_context_budget_exceeded`), closed as not reproducible on 2.5.0-rc.2.
- #3389: single path > 4 MiB (this path is ~2.6 MB), open.

### Preserved state
Lineage left in `reviewing`, then declined for this candidate through the provider-issued decline invocation. No repository mutation by the review.

title: [Automated provider defect] sdd-status resolves no Engram changes when store detection and project scoping succeed (3.4.0)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
