### 📝 Bug Description

`gentle-ai sync` — and applying a Pi model profile from the TUI Model Configuration menu — rewrites `~/.pi/agent/subagents.json` with gentle-ai's own default, deleting every `model_profiles` entry configured for Pi subagents. The same write re-materialises `~/.pi/agent/agents/*.md` from embedded templates that carry no `model:` / `thinking:` frontmatter.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Pi subagent routing so `~/.pi/agent/subagents.json` holds N `model_profiles` entries.
2. Run `gentle-ai sync`, or open the TUI and apply a Pi model profile.
3. Read `~/.pi/agent/subagents.json`.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The configured `model_profiles` survive a sync, or gentle-ai backs the file up and asks before overwriting it.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

`subagents.json` is reduced to a single entry (`review-refuter`). Every other `model_profiles` entry is gone, with no backup of that file, and all `agents/*.md` lose their `model:` / `thinking:` frontmatter.

### Gentle AI Version

3.7.0

### Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

TUI (terminal UI)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
# observed timestamps on one machine, same day
07:29:53  backup upgrade-<ts>      (binary upgraded)
07:30:10  last_synced_at
07:30:34  settings.json rewritten
07:31:46  subagents.json rewritten
07:38:50  subagents.json restored by hand (23 entries)
07:39:59  subagents.json wiped again after using the model-profile menu

# pre-change backup manifest
grep -c subagents.json <snapshot>/manifest.json   # -> 0
grep -c '\.pi/agent/agents/' <snapshot>/manifest.json  # -> 23
```

### Additional Context

Workaround: keep a copy of `subagents.json` outside `~/.pi` and re-apply it after any sync or menu use. Restoring the `.md` frontmatter is pointless because the next sync re-materialises those files, so `subagents.json` is the only file worth restoring.

The pre-change backup covers `~/.pi/agent/agents/*.md` but not `subagents.json`, so the lost routing is only recoverable indirectly by rebuilding `model_profiles` from the agent frontmatter in the backup.

Related: #2123 (preserve customizations in managed agent files during sync), #4397 (Pi model presets menu), #3430 (config not persisted).

title: perf(gentle-pi): extensions add ~3.4 s to every pi/gentle-shell start; personalization appears seconds after the TUI
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Problem Statement

`gentle-pi` adds roughly 3.4 s to every `pi` / `gentle-shell` start on Windows, and the Gentle AI personalization (theme, banner, runtime panel, todo sidebar) only appears once that load finishes, so the user sees a bare pi TUI for a few seconds before the Gentle look lands.

Measured on Windows 11, pi 0.87.1, gentle-pi 3.7.0, Node 22, warm jiti transpile cache (8 MB under `%TEMP%\jiti`, not rewritten between runs), each command run twice and the second run reported:

```
pi -ne --list-models x                                   805 ms   (no extensions)
pi -ne -e <13 gentle-pi extensions/*.ts> --list-models x 4160 ms  (+3.4 s)
pi -ne -e pi-web-access/dist/index.js --list-models x   3921 ms  (+3.1 s, for comparison)
pi -ne -e @schuettc/pi-claude-bridge/src/index.ts       1639 ms  (+0.8 s)
pi --list-models x  (all packages as installed)         6096 ms
```

pi loads extensions through jiti with `moduleCache: false`, so the cost is not transpilation but evaluating the 13 extension entry points (304 TS files, about 6 MB of source) and their startup work (git child processes for the repository identity, skill registry, banner, sidebar, codegraph tools, SDD init) on every launch, before the first prompt is shown.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Make gentle-pi's startup lazy and observable:

1. Register only the hooks and tool stubs at load time and defer the heavy module imports (gentle-agents, codegraph-tools, sdd-init, skill-registry, runtime-metrics) to first use or to `session_start` after the TUI is up, so the theme/banner extension runs first and the user sees the Gentle look immediately.
2. Run the startup git identity probes asynchronously and render the banner with a placeholder until they resolve, instead of blocking extension load.
3. Print per-extension load timings when `PI_TIMING=1` (pi already exposes the hook) so regressions in gentle-pi startup can be caught in CI.

Target: gentle-pi adding well under 1 s to `pi -ne` on a warm cache.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- Removing packages from `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`: not acceptable, the user wants the full Gentle setup and `web_search` from pi-web-access.
- Bundling gentle-pi into a single prebuilt JS file: reduces file resolution overhead but not the eager startup work, and loses the "edit extension, restart, see change" workflow that `moduleCache: false` exists for.
- A pi-side extension cache: out of gentle-ai's control (upstream pi design decision).

### 📎 Additional Context

The delay is proportional and consistent (6.1 s and 6.7 s on back-to-back full starts), so it is a design cost, not an intermittent hang. Related but different: #4554 (child sessions mutate files on startup) and #3434 (skills flagged on every startup) show that gentle-pi already does non-trivial work at every launch.

title: bug(gentle-pi): Gentle Todo list is lost on a new session, cleared silently when finished, and the sidebar goes stale after subagent todo calls
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

Gentle Todo (`gentle-pi/extensions/gentle-todo.ts`) keeps its list only in an in-memory `Map<sessionId, TodoSession>` and rebuilds it on `session_start` by replaying the `todo` tool results already stored in the current pi session transcript (`lib/shell-todo.ts` `replayTodo`). Nothing is written to disk under `~/.pi` or `~/.gentle-ai`, and there is no project-scoped store.

Consequences observed on a daily basis:

1. Closing the terminal and opening a **new** pi/Gentle Shell session in the same project loses the list entirely. Asking the agent to "recover what we were doing" cannot bring it back: the new session has no `todo` tool results to replay, and no other artifact holds the list.
2. `session_start` replay discards the list when every task was already done (`gentle-todo.ts` treats it as history), and `agent_end` sets `clearOnNextTurn` when the last task closes, so on the next turn the list vanishes. From the user's point of view the todo list "disappears" without an explicit action.
3. The sidebar sometimes stays stale. The widget is refreshed only on `tool_execution_end` for the parent session's `todo` tool, so `todo` calls made inside a Gentle Agents subagent (keyed by the child session in the same `Map`) never refresh the parent's sidebar, and the parent's system-prompt block keeps the old state.

Item 3 is reproduced less reliably than 1 and 2; the mechanism above is derived from the code, not from a deterministic repro.

Related: #4190 retired `@juicesharp/rpiv-todo` in favour of Gentle Todo, but the shipped replacement is still transcript-scoped.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Start `pi` (or `gentle-shell`) in a project, ask the agent for a multi-step task so Gentle Todo shows 4 to 5 tasks, let it complete 2 of them.
2. Close the terminal (do not use `pi -r` / `--continue`).
3. Open a new `pi` session in the same project and ask: "recover what we were doing and continue the pending tasks".
4. Observe the sidebar and the agent's answer.
5. Variant for the stale sidebar: in a session with an open list, have a Gentle Agents subagent run a task that calls the `todo` tool; watch the parent sidebar.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

- The open todo list survives a terminal restart for the same project (or at least the ODD feature document under `odd/tasks/` is offered as the recovery source when the list cannot be replayed).
- A finished list is cleared visibly, with a hint, not silently on the next turn.
- The parent sidebar reflects every `todo` update, including those made by subagents, or subagents are prevented from mutating a list they do not display.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

- Step 4: the sidebar is empty and the agent answers from memory only (Engram/ODD document if one exists); the Gentle Todo list is gone.
- Finished lists disappear on the next turn without any notice.
- Step 5: the parent sidebar keeps the pre-subagent state until the parent itself calls `todo` again.

### Gentle AI Version

v3.7.0 (gentle-pi 3.7.0, pi 0.87.1)

### Operating System

Windows

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
# pi session transcript of the affected project: todo state exists only as tool results
$ rg -o '"name":"todo"' <session>.jsonl | wc -l
20
$ rg -o '"customType":"[^"]+"' <session>.jsonl | sort | uniq -c
   1 "customType":"gentle-pi.review-preflight"
  25 "customType":"gentle-pi.review-reminder-receipt/v1"
  24 "customType":"gentle-pi.session-change/v1"
   1 "customType":"gentle-pi.session-worktree/v1"
# no todo custom entry, no file under ~/.pi or ~/.gentle-ai
$ rg -l "todo" ~/.pi/agent ~/.gentle-ai --glob '!sessions/**' --glob '!npm/**'
(no results)
```

### Additional Context

Client: Gentle Shell / pi 0.87.1 with `gentle-pi@3.7.0`, provider `claude-bridge`, `tuiMode: fullscreen`. Code references: `extensions/gentle-todo.ts` (`session_start`, `tool_execution_end`, `agent_end` handlers) and `lib/shell-todo.ts` (`replayTodo`).

title: bug(installer): post-apply verification requires V2-skipped logo files (tui.json, gentle-logo.tsx), so install can never pass on OpenCode V2
body:
---
name: Bug Report
about: File a bug report for Gentle AI
title: "bug(installer): post-apply verification requires V2-skipped logo files (tui.json, gentle-logo.tsx), so install can never pass on OpenCode V2"
labels: ["bug", "status:needs-review"]
---

### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

On OpenCode V2, the `opencode-gentle-logo` component install is **intentionally skipped** with `UnsupportedLogoError` (writes nothing, per `docs/opencode-compatibility.md`: "Gentle logo — V2: Explicitly skipped; no equivalent `home_logo` slot, no relocation or config writes"). That skip is correct.

But `runPostApplyVerification` in `internal/cli/run.go` unconditionally registers both logo paths as hard "required file exists" checks whenever the component is in `Resolved.OrderedComponents`, **without applying the same V2 skip condition**:

```go
case model.ComponentOpenCodeGentleLogo:
    if adapter.Agent() == model.AgentOpenCode {
        paths = append(paths,
            filepath.Join(homeDir, ".config", "opencode", "tui-plugins", "gentle-logo.tsx"),
            filepath.Join(homeDir, ".config", "opencode", "tui.json"),
        )
    }
```

The writer that produces these files (`opencodeplugin.Install` in `internal/components/opencodeplugin/plugin.go`) returns `UnsupportedLogoError` for `RuntimeV2` and never writes them. So on any OpenCode V2 host these two checks are unsatisfiable by design: apply reports `skipped`, verification reports `failed`, and the install always ends with "post-apply verification failed".

Knock-on effect: the failed verification prevents `state.json` from recording `installed_agents` (it stayed `null`), so `gentle-ai doctor` also reports `[!!] state:json — no installed agents` even though every component applied successfully. Re-running `gentle-ai install` cannot recover; the run fails at the same two checks every time.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Install OpenCode V2 (reproduced on `opencode v2.0.14`) on a Linux host.
2. Install gentle-ai v3.7.0 (linux_amd64 release binary).
3. Run `gentle-ai install --agent opencode,gemini-cli,antigravity` with the `opencode-gentle-logo` component in the selection (default preset `full-gentleman` includes it).
4. Observe the apply step for the logo report `− component:opencode-gentle-logo (skipped)`.
5. Observe post-apply verification fail on the two file checks.
6. Inspect `~/.gentle-ai/state.json` → `installed_agents` is still `null`.
7. Re-run the same install command → identical failure (no recovery path).

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Post-apply verification should honor the V2 logo omission: either exclude those two paths from the check list when `opencode.DetectRuntimeMajor()` returns `RuntimeV2` (the same condition `opencodeplugin.Install` uses), or register them as `CheckStatusSkipped` with the `UnsupportedLogoError` reason instead of `CheckStatusFailed`. The install should report success and write `installed_agents` to `state.json`.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

```
Error: post-apply verification failed:
Verification checks: 114 passed, 2 failed, 1 warnings, 0 skipped
[!!] verify:file:/home/alkon/.config/opencode/tui-plugins/gentle-logo.tsx - required file exists (stat ...: no such file or directory)
[!!] verify:file:/home/alkon/.config/opencode/tui.json - required file exists (stat ...: no such file or directory)
Installation completed with verification issues.
```

`state.json` never receives `installed_agents`, so `gentle-ai doctor` stays degraded. Retry suggested by the tool itself (`gentle-ai install --agent opencode,gemini-cli,antigravity`) fails identically.

### Gentle AI Version

3.7.0 (release binary `gentle-ai_3.7.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz`, sha256 verified against `checksums.txt`)

### Operating System

Linux (Arch/Manjaro)

### AI Agent / Client

OpenCode

### 📋 Affected Area

Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

Apply phase (logo correctly skipped):

```
[7/9] ...
  − component:opencode-gentle-logo (skipped)
  ✓ component:permissions
  ✓ component:sdd
  ✓ component:skills
```

Verification phase (fails on the files the skip never writes):

```
Error: post-apply verification failed:
Verification checks: 114 passed, 2 failed, 1 warnings, 0 skipped
[!!] verify:file:/home/alkon/.config/opencode/tui-plugins/gentle-logo.tsx - required file exists (stat /home/alkon/.config/opencode/tui-plugins/gentle-logo.tsx: no such file or directory)
[!!] verify:file:/home/alkon/.config/opencode/tui.json - required file exists (stat /home/alkon/.config/opencode/tui.json: no such file or directory)
[??] verify:antigravity:rules-collision - (expected, warning)
[ok] verify:opencode:config-layers - OpenCode model write authority
Installation completed with verification issues. Run `gentle-ai install --agent opencode,gemini-cli,antigravity` to retry the failed checks.
```

State never recorded:

```json
{
  "installed_agents": null,
  "installed_binary_version": "3.7.0",
  "last_synced_at": "2026-09-24T05:46:43.974383564Z"
}
```

`gentle-ai doctor`:

```
[!!] state:json  state file found ... with no installed agents
     Remedy: Run 'gentle-ai install' to configure agents
```

### Additional Context

- Source references (v3.7.0): `internal/cli/run.go` — `componentPathsWithWorkspaceScoped` (`case model.ComponentOpenCodeGentleLogo`, adds both paths with no V2 guard) vs `internal/components/opencodeplugin/plugin.go` — `Install()` (`if major == opencode.RuntimeV2 { ... return UnsupportedLogoError }`). The verification path list never consults the runtime major, so writer and verifier disagree on V2.
- Test coverage gap: `TestOpenCodeV2LogoSkippedWithoutWrites` (`internal/cli/opencode_logo_v2_test.go`) asserts the apply step skips and mutates no files — the correct V2 behavior — but there is no companion test asserting post-apply verification passes after that skip.
- Doc contract: `docs/opencode-compatibility.md` states the V2 logo omission is "accepted". Verification failing the install contradicts that documented acceptance.
- Workaround we used (not a fix): re-run with the logo component removed from the selection — `gentle-ai install --agent opencode,gemini-cli,antigravity --component claude-theme,context7,persona,engram,gga,permissions,sdd,skills` — then verification passes (0 failed) and `state.json` is written correctly. This only masks the bug for users who know to deselect the component.

title: bug(review): acknowledged workspace candidate reoffers consent after exact commit (3.5.0)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

On Gentle AI 3.5.0 with Pi, a workspace `current-changes` candidate completed four-lens review and the exact approved acknowledgement (`authority: burned`). Committing the already-reviewed bytes changed its representation to a committed `base-diff`, but the base tree, candidate tree, changed paths, and paths digest remained identical. The next selectorless inspect classified that range as `unrelated` / `fresh_target_ready` and offered another START. START returned a new consent request for the same content (`lineage_created: false`); no second review ran.

This is post-acknowledgement cross-kind deduplication, not a request to equate arbitrary projections, changed bases, modes, paths, or content. It creates another human prompt and could spend a second four-lens budget on bytes just approved.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. In a disposable Git worktree with RDD on, modify tracked files so the workspace candidate is high risk. Keep its integration base fixed.
2. Inspect the `current-changes` target, grant consent, complete the lenses, and execute the exact acknowledgement. Record `authority: burned`, base tree, candidate tree, paths digest, and complete changed-path set.
3. Commit precisely those reviewed bytes without changing modes; verify HEAD tree equals the reviewed candidate and the worktree is clean.
4. Inspect the committed base-to-HEAD candidate against the same integration base. Observe `kind: base-diff`, equal base/candidate trees and path digest, but a different target identity and a fresh START.
5. Execute only that provider-issued START. Observe consent required; in this run `lineage_created: false` and no second reviewer was launched.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

An exact acknowledged A-to-B range should not automatically demand another review solely because the same complete paths, bytes, and modes are represented as a committed `base-diff` rather than workspace `current-changes`. Either narrowly proven cross-kind terminal-consumption equivalence should suppress the fresh offer, or STATUS should provide a reasoned actionable stop if that equivalence cannot safely be established. Genuine drift and deliberately independent reviews remain eligible.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The exact committed candidate was treated as fresh and START re-presented consent for a high-risk four-lens review despite matching reviewed content boundaries. The first acknowledgement had already burned authority. The second START stopped at consent; this report does not claim a duplicate review completed.

### Gentle AI Version

3.5.0 (stable)

### Operating System

Windows

### AI Agent / Client

Other

Pi coding agent through the Gentle Pi review integration.

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
initial: kind=current-changes, projection=workspace, base_tree=86cc60be…, candidate_tree=4380b3c1…, paths_digest=sha256:b01677af…
acknowledgement: authority=burned, target=sha256:5d5bf14c…
after exact commit: kind=base-diff, projection=workspace, base_tree=86cc60be…, candidate_tree=4380b3c1…, paths_digest=sha256:b01677af…
inspect: applicability=unrelated, reason_code=fresh_target_ready, offered_target=sha256:b338ab5a…
subsequent START: consent_required, lineage_created=false, mutation_performed=false
```

### Additional Context

Related but not equivalent: #2688 fixed an active approved receipt across staged-to-committed representation; here approval was acknowledged and burned. #4405 was closed by #4737, which suppresses the exact consumed target identity, while this case changes only the representation identity. #4737 is an ancestor of the 3.5.0 release. #4624 reports a post-acknowledgement re-offer of the same target without a commit on an older build. #4815 concerns Stop-hook disagreement with `review_due` on later changed commits.

In 3.5.0, terminal-consumption lookup is keyed by exact target identity and STATUS checks the live identity. This is a code-path hypothesis consistent with the observation, not proof that globally relaxing identity is safe. Preserve fail-closed checks for base, full path/mode set, policy, provenance, and live authority. No private repository data, raw command arguments, or source content is included.

title: bug(review 3.6.1): pi host-relay materialize reviewer replays a byte-identical truncated JSON payload across capture attempts; admission refuses it and the lineage stalls in reviewing
body:
## Environment

- gentle-ai **3.6.1** (stable channel)
- Review executed from an interactive Pi host (`--agent=pi`), **pi host-relay** transport, materialize reviewer slot
- Contract: gentle-ai.review-integration/v2; lens: `review-reliability`, order 0
- macOS (arm64); private multi-tenant Next.js repository (details withheld)

## Observed behavior

1. Ordinary START created a lineage (risk medium, one materialize reviewer slot). Forecast acknowledged; the host-relay reviewer run was authorized exactly once per attempt.
2. The capture was refused at admission **three consecutive times** with the same admission error:

```
lens provider result admission incomplete: reviewer payload contains no
complete JSON object: 5 objects opened, 4 closed; 6 arrays opened, 5
closed; scan ended at byte 2797  [invalid_request]
```

3. The rejected reviewer payload was preserved at admission each time under the repository's gentle-ai rejected-results store. **The preserved file's content identifier was byte-for-byte identical across all three refusals** (short id `ce34bf67e34f`, 2797 bytes), i.e. the relay resubmitted the same truncated payload instead of producing a fresh reviewer run per acknowledged capture.
4. The lens slot was never consumed and no terminal outcome was reached: the lineage remained in `state=reviewing` with STATUS reoffering the same collect slot, so the candidate could not reach any terminal review state (approved, declined, or a typed stop) across three acknowledged attempts.

## Expected behavior

Either each acknowledged materialize capture produces a fresh reviewer result (admissible or typed-unavailable), or the contract surfaces a typed terminal stop for an unproducible reviewer output — in both cases letting the lineage leave `reviewing` instead of stalling on a replayed rejected payload.

## Notes for triage

- Possibly the same payload-truncation class as closed #3942 (native `--agent` reviewer, 2.5.0-main) and closed #4061 (in-process claude-code targeted validator) — this occurrence is the **pi host-relay materialize reviewer** on 3.6.1 stable, and adds the deterministic **replay of the identical rejected bytes** across attempts, which neither predecessor describes.
- Reported from one occurrence only; no reproduction outside this repository. Happy to run a probe build or provide additional sanitized relay logs on request.

title: feat(installer): verify Gentle-Shell route and private diagnostics on macOS and Windows
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area
Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Problem Statement
Gentle AI's proposed Gentle-Shell installer has separate `pi` and `gentle-shell` terminal routes and an optional private failure report. Source-only work exists outside the canonical branch, but the Gentle-Shell route is still disabled. The private report writer currently supports Linux only; macOS and Windows intentionally return unsupported. A Linux build or a cross-compile cannot establish native filesystem security, launcher readiness, or end-to-end behavior on either OS. The upstream external-ready marker also deliberately refuses Windows authoring until reparse-point safety is solved.

### 📦 Proposed Solution
- Land small, reviewed work units that bind an immutable launcher source and its effective executable, home and Pi context, keep approval separate from inspection, create needed config directories only after approval, and verify Ready before managed-state persistence. Keep the Pi route intact.
- Preserve explicit pre-Apply capture consent and separate post-failure destination consent. Implement owner-only, exclusive local report storage on macOS and Windows only with documented filesystem, ACL and reparse guarantees and native tests; fail closed where those guarantees cannot be demonstrated.
- Exercise focused tests in pull-request CI on actual macOS and Windows runners, alongside Linux. Verify refusal/no-write cases and positive behavior separately, report skipped coverage honestly, and keep PR slices at most 400 changed lines.
- Keep PRs draft and independent of release: no upstream merge, Stable publication, preview replacement, global installation, or real Apply follows from CI.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered
A workflow-only smoke step on a clean main branch cannot test untracked source-only packages. Treating a successful cross-compile or a `bin.gentle-shell` manifest entry as proof of native Ready would be misleading. Shipping a generic 0600/Node path check without verified platform semantics would weaken the privacy and path-safety contract.

### 📎 Additional Context
The dependent upstream fork PRs for the external-ready marker are drafts; the first has an escalated native review, and the second passed focused macOS/Windows CI while keeping Windows marker authoring fail-closed. The Gentle AI native CI work must not claim a fully functional cross-platform installer until the upstream contract and runtime/Ready proof are available.

title: bug(sync): Context7 component replaces user-customized MCP server entries (custom launcher command/args/env) in all agents on every sync (3.6.1, unchanged in 3.7.0)
body:
## Summary

The Context7 sync step rewrites the `context7` MCP entry for every synced agent and discards a user-configured launcher. Some users run Context7 through a local stdio wrapper, for example one that injects `CONTEXT7_API_KEY` from the OS keychain and fails closed when the key is missing. On the next sync, that wrapper is replaced by the default configuration, with no warning that a customized entry was overwritten.

The Engram injector already preserves an existing custom command (`stableEngramCommandForMergedConfig`, `buildSeparateMCPContent`). Context7 has no equivalent.

## Environment

- gentle-ai 3.6.1 installed. The involved code paths are unchanged in v3.7.0 (tag commit `6dee8f8`).
- macOS arm64. Agents: codex, opencode, pi and claude-code. Each one has a custom local stdio launcher configured for `context7`.

## Behavior per agent

Source: v3.7.0, `internal/components/mcp/inject.go`.

| Agent | What sync does | Effect on a custom launcher |
|---|---|---|
| Codex | `injectTOMLFile` calls `UpsertCodexRemoteMCPServerBlock` (`internal/components/filemerge/toml.go:116`), which deletes `[mcp_servers.context7]` and appends only `url = "https://mcp.context7.com/mcp"` | command, args and environment removed |
| OpenCode | `injectOpenCodeMergeIntoSettings` writes an atomic `__replace__` remote entry; only string `headers` survive | local command and environment removed |
| Claude Code | `injectClaudeUserConfig` merges `DefaultContext7OverlayJSON` (npx plus the pinned package) | custom command replaced |
| Pi | `StrategyMCPConfigFile` merges the same default stdio payload into the agent `mcp.json` | custom command replaced |

## How it gets triggered

- Any `gentle-ai sync`, from the CLI or the TUI "Sync configs" option.
- After a self-upgrade: `PendingSync` makes the next TUI launch sync automatically.
- After a binary upgrade: review START stops with `managed_assets_outdated`, and its continuation is `gentle-ai sync --agent ...`. The managed orchestrator instructions tell agents to run that continuation.

## Expected

Keep a user-customized `context7` entry intact, as the Engram injector does, or provide a supported way to keep Context7 user-managed. Two possible shapes:

- a sync option to skip the component;
- leaving an entry alone when its command differs from the managed default.

## Actual

On every sync, the custom launcher is replaced in all four agents.

## Reproduction

1. Configure a custom entry in `~/.codex/config.toml`:

   ```toml
   [mcp_servers.context7]
   command = "/path/to/custom-launcher"
   args = []
   ```

2. Run `gentle-ai sync --agent codex` with the `context7` component in the persisted selection.
3. The table is replaced by `url = "https://mcp.context7.com/mcp"`.

This was traced from the v3.7.0 source; it was not executed separately in an isolated HOME.

## Related

#1186 (closed) fixed OpenCode `mcp.context7` headers being wiped on sync. This request extends the same preservation principle to the launcher itself (command, args and environment) in all agents.

title: feat(skill-registry): stop instructing agents to edit project .gitignore
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Problem Statement

The shipped `skill-registry` skill instructs agents to add `.atl/` to the project's root `.gitignore` when possible. That file may be tracked and shared by a team even when only one contributor uses Gentle AI. Following the skill can introduce an unrelated change into a pull request.

In a team repository, only I use Gentle AI. The instruction to add `.atl/` to the root `.gitignore` led to an unrelated change being included in a PR, for which I received review feedback. A local tool's runtime state should not require a change to a shared project file.

The generated OpenCode startup hook already uses `--no-gitignore`, but the skill instruction can still direct an agent to make the root-file change.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Update the shipped `skill-registry` skill so it no longer instructs agents to create or edit the project's root `.gitignore` for local registry state. Direct agents to keep generated `.atl/` content ignored using `.atl/.gitignore` containing `*`, without claiming that this untracks files already committed to Git.

Keep registry generation available. The separate Pi startup implementation is tracked in [gentle-shell #1387](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-shell/issues/1387).

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- `.git/info/exclude` avoids a tracked-file change, but applies only to Git repositories and needs worktree-aware handling.
- Editing the root `.gitignore` risks unrelated changes entering commits.

### 📎 Additional Context

The instruction appears at `internal/assets/skills/skill-registry/SKILL.md:21`: “Add `.atl/` to `.gitignore` when possible unless explicitly disabled.” Related reports: #4554 and #4409 concern startup workspace mutations in different circumstances.

title: bug(review): the in-process Claude reviewer drops the assigned effort, so every review role runs at one unassigned effort
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description
Gentle AI assigns a model and an effort to each review role (`risk`, `readability`, `reliability`, `resilience`, `refuter`, `validator`). The in-process Claude reviewer (`review capture-result --agent claude-code`) applies the model and discards the effort:

- `savedClaudeReviewModel` (`internal/cli/review_provider_runtime.go:82`) reads the effort, uses it only to validate the assignment, and returns `configured.Model`.
- `ClaudeAdapter` (`internal/reviewerprovider/claude_adapter.go:37-67`) runs `claude --print ... --setting-sources "" ...` and appends only `--model`.
- `claude_adapter_test.go:108` fails if `--effort` is passed: "reviewer must not pass unverified effort flags".

Because of `--setting-sources ""`, the reviewer does not read the user's `effortLevel` either. Every role runs at the effort Claude Code resolves without the flag (`high` in the test below), whatever the TUI says. The same roles launched as `review-*` sub-agents through the Agent tool do honor the effort frontmatter. The two surfaces disagree, as they did for the model in #4275.

This was deferred on purpose. The task document of #4912 (`odd/tasks/claude-native-rdd-models.md:9`) says: "CLI help locally advertises `--model <model>` and `--effort <level>`; model selection is in scope, and any effort wiring requires verified applicability." This report supplies that verification.

The flag is documented: `claude --help` (Claude Code 2.1.281) lists `--effort <level>  Effort level for the current session (low, medium, high, xhigh, max)`, and the settings docs name `--effort` as the flag for `effortLevel` (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings). It also applies under the reviewer's isolation flags. I ran `claude --print --output-format text --tools "" --permission-mode dontAsk --setting-sources "" --model sonnet` on a one-line prompt, three times, and read the `effort` field that Claude Code records in each session transcript:

| Extra flag | Recorded effort |
|---|---|
| none | `high` |
| `--effort low` | `low` |
| `--effort max` | `max` |

The model stayed `claude-sonnet-5` in all three runs. The test kept session persistence on only so that a transcript exists; the adapter's `--no-session-persistence` does not change how the flag is parsed.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce
1. In the TUI, assign `risk` → `opus` + `low` (any non-default effort).
2. Sync, then run a native review on a medium-risk candidate so that `review-risk` is captured in process.
3. Compare with the argv that `ClaudeAdapter` builds: `--model opus` is there, and no `--effort`.

### ✅ Expected Behavior
The in-process reviewer runs each role with the effort that Gentle AI assigns to it, the same as the `review-*` sub-agent files declare. `--effort <value>` is appended when the assignment has a non-default effort that is valid for the model (`ClaudeEffortAllowedForModel`), and omitted for `default`.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
The effort assignment is persisted and rendered into the `review-*` agent files, but the in-process capture never passes it. Every role runs at the effort Claude Code resolves without the flag, and a test forbids the flag.

### Gentle AI Version
gentle-ai 3.7.0 (latest release). Code references are from `main` @ `c5da5fd0f5`.

### Operating System
Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client
Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area
Other

### 💡 Logs / Error Output
```shell
# gentle-ai state (review roles)
claude_phase_assignments.risk        = {"model":"opus","effort":"low"}
claude_phase_assignments.refuter     = {"model":"opus","effort":"medium"}
claude_phase_assignments.validator   = {"model":"opus","effort":"medium"}

# rendered agent file (Agent-tool path honors it)
review-risk.md: model: opus / effort: low

# internal/reviewerprovider/claude_adapter_test.go:108
t.Fatal("reviewer must not pass unverified effort flags")

# claude --help (Claude Code 2.1.281)
--effort <level>   Effort level for the current session (low, medium, high, xhigh, max)
```

### Additional Context
**Proposed fix (mirror of the #4275 model fix):**
1. `savedClaudeReviewModel` returns the whole `ClaudePhaseAssignment`, not only the model.
2. `ClaudeAdapter` gains an `Effort` field and appends `--effort <value>` only when `renderClaudeEffortFrontmatter` would emit a line for the same assignment. One rule then governs both surfaces.
3. The test at `claude_adapter_test.go:108` asserts that `--effort` is present exactly when the assignment has a valid non-default effort, and absent otherwise.

Related: #4912 (added `--model` to this adapter and deferred effort), #4275 (model half of the same command), #4469 (the same defect for the Codex reviewer), #2914 (exposing review rows in the Claude picker), #817 (effort frontmatter for generated agents).

title: bug(claude): the `default` model-assignment row accepts an effort that organic delegation can never apply
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description
The Claude model picker offers an effort for the `default` row ("General delegation"). Gentle AI saves it and renders it in the always-on `## Model Assignments` table. Since #4062 (closes #4054), that row governs every organic delegation (explorer, mapper, writer, verifier). The effort half of the row never takes effect, and nothing says so.

Named roles get their effort through generated frontmatter (`renderClaudeEffortFrontmatter`, `internal/components/sdd/inject.go:3429`, from #817). Organic delegation uses Claude Code's built-in agents (`general-purpose`, `Explore`). Gentle AI generates no file for them, so the effort has no carrier:

- The Agent tool accepts a per-call `model` but no `effort`. The rendered gate (`inject.go:3441`) can only require `model`.
- Claude Code documents that a subagent without `effort` frontmatter "inherits from session" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents, frontmatter reference).
- Claude Code has no subagent-specific effort variable (only `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` for the model).

The organic workers therefore run at the session effort. The chosen value affects only one path: the fallback for a named role without an assignment (`inject.go:3412`).

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce
1. In Claude Code, set the session effort to `high` (`effortLevel` in `~/.claude/settings.json`).
2. In the Gentle AI TUI, set the Claude `default` row to `opus` + `medium`, then sync. `~/.gentle-ai/state.json` holds `claude_phase_assignments.default.effort = "medium"`, and `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` renders `| default | opus | medium | ... |`.
3. Start a Claude Code session and ask for work that makes the orchestrator delegate to `general-purpose` (for example an exploration over 4+ files).
4. Inspect the sub-agent transcript.

### ✅ Expected Behavior
The TUI offers only settings that Gentle AI can apply, and the rendered table shows what each delegation will really use. For the `default` row on Claude Code, that means the model, and an effort shown as inherited from the session.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
The sub-agent transcripts record `"effort":"high"` (the session value) on every turn of two `general-purpose` explorers that the orchestrator launched with `model: opus` under a `default` row of `opus` + `medium`. The configured `medium` is saved, rendered and silently ignored.

### Gentle AI Version
gentle-ai 3.7.0 (latest release). Code references are from `main` @ `c5da5fd0f5`.

### Operating System
Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client
Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area
TUI (terminal UI)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output
```shell
# gentle-ai state
claude_phase_assignments.default.model = opus
claude_phase_assignments.default.effort = medium

# rendered ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
| default | opus | medium | Generic and SDD/JD delegation fallback |

# claude settings
"effortLevel": "high"

# the two general-purpose sub-agent transcripts (count of effort values)
73  "effort":"high"
110 "effort":"high"
```

### Additional Context
**Proposed fix (smallest, removes a false promise):**
1. In the Claude picker, the `default` row offers a model only. Its effort choice is removed or fixed to `default`.
2. The rendered table shows `session` in the Effort column of the `default` row, plus one line: organic delegation inherits the Claude Code session effort, because the Agent tool has no per-call effort.
3. A persisted `default.effort` stays readable for backward compatibility. It keeps its only live meaning, the fallback for a named role without an assignment, or it is dropped. The maintainer decides which one.

**Out of scope, a separate product decision:** make the effort enforceable. The only documented channel is a user agent file with the same name as a built-in agent. Claude Code documents that "a user or project subagent named `Explore` overrides the built-in and keeps its own `model` field". Gentle AI could generate managed `general-purpose.md` and `Explore.md` files with the `default` row's model and effort. Cost: Gentle AI would then own a copy of each built-in agent's system prompt and tool list, and it could overwrite a user's own file. A new `gentle-worker` agent is the other route. It repeats what #1099 rejected for OpenCode: duplicating native agents.

Related: #4054 / #4062 (model half of the same row), #817 (effort for generated agents), #2914 (review rows in the Claude picker).

title: fix(cli): STATUS replaces explicit commit base-ref with tree hash before START
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description
In Gentle AI 3.7.0, a clean, committed-only base-diff review negotiated with an explicit full commit `--base-ref=<BASE_COMMIT>` cannot enter START. `review assess` preserves the commit and `review status` identifies the intended candidate, but STATUS emits a START transition with `--base-ref=<BASE_TREE>`, the Git tree of that commit. Executing the emitted transition literally is rejected as `native-start-base-ref-unresolvable`. No lineage is created and no mutation occurs. This report records the observed transition mismatch, not a presumed implementation cause.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce
1. Use a clean detached worktree `<WORKTREE>` at `<HEAD_COMMIT>`, directly above `<BASE_COMMIT>` (a full 40-character commit SHA). In the observed case the committed-only diff contained exactly six changed paths.
2. Run `gentle-ai review assess --cwd <WORKTREE> --agent pi --base-ref <BASE_COMMIT> --committed-only --json`. Its `candidate` has `kind: "base-diff"`, `base_ref: "<BASE_COMMIT>"`, `consumed: false`, and `changed_paths: 6`. Its emitted `review.status` continuation retains `--base-ref=<BASE_COMMIT> --committed-only=true`.
3. Execute that emitted STATUS continuation literally. It preserves the six-path candidate and reports `base_tree=<BASE_TREE>` and `current_candidate_tree=<CANDIDATE_TREE>`.
4. Inspect its emitted `next_transition` for `review.start`: the command contains `--base-ref=<BASE_TREE> --committed-only=true`, not `--base-ref=<BASE_COMMIT>`. Confirm `git cat-file -t <BASE_TREE>` returns `tree`, and `git rev-parse <BASE_COMMIT>^{tree}` returns exactly `<BASE_TREE>`.
5. Execute the emitted START transition literally, without substituting or reconstructing any provider argument. Observe `native-start-base-ref-unresolvable` before authority creation.

### ✅ Expected Behavior
STATUS should issue an executable START continuation for the negotiated candidate, preserving a resolvable commit/ref boundary when its caller supplied `--base-ref=<BASE_COMMIT>`. No consumer-side reconstruction of provider-owned arguments should be necessary.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
`review assess --base-ref=<BASE_COMMIT> --committed-only` preserves `<BASE_COMMIT>` → `review status ... --base-ref=<BASE_COMMIT> --committed-only` preserves the candidate → STATUS's START transition substitutes `<BASE_TREE> == git rev-parse <BASE_COMMIT>^{tree}` as `--base-ref` → native START rejects that tree object. This is fail-closed: `lineage_created=false`, `mutation_performed=false`, `mutation_outcome=none`.

### Gentle AI Version
3.7.0

### Operating System
Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client
Other (Pi)

### 📋 Affected Area
CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output
```shell
$ git cat-file -t <BASE_TREE>
tree
$ git rev-parse <BASE_COMMIT>^{tree}
<BASE_TREE>

# STATUS-generated START includes --base-ref=<BASE_TREE> --committed-only=true
{
  "operation": "start",
  "status": "blocked",
  "outcome": "native-start-base-ref-unresolvable",
  "reason": "base-ref-unresolvable",
  "lineage_created": false,
  "mutation_performed": false,
  "mutation_outcome": "none",
  "reset_eligible": false
}
```

### Additional Context
Related, not exact duplicates: #3203 emits a tree as a base-ref in START remediation but silently widens scope; #2756 is a STATUS→START disagreement about staged projection ambiguity; #4250 concerns a stale committed-range candidate view/rev-parse failure; #4639 selects the wrong default-branch commit as base. Here an explicitly supplied full commit boundary survives assess/STATUS, but the generated START substitutes its tree and is rejected before lineage creation. No workaround by manually rewriting the generated transition was attempted.

title: Bug: Judgment Day fix agent rejects confirmed HIGH dispatch
body:
## Summary
A user-authorized Judgment Day correction batch containing one confirmed CRITICAL finding and one confirmed HIGH finding is rejected before the fix agent begins.

## Observed behavior
The dispatcher reports that only BLOCKER/CRITICAL open Judgment Day rows are accepted. No source files, tests, or external systems were changed.

## Expected behavior
The Judgment Day workflow classifies severe findings confirmed by both judges as correction-eligible. A confirmed HIGH finding included in an otherwise canonical bounded batch should be accepted, or the workflow documentation should state that HIGH findings cannot be corrected.

## Minimal reproduction
1. Freeze a Judgment Day ledger with a confirmed CRITICAL finding and a confirmed HIGH finding.
2. Submit one round-one correction batch containing exactly those two authorized rows and narrow edit surfaces.
3. Observe rejection before the fix actor starts.

## Environment
- Pi 0.87.1
- Darwin 24.5, arm64

## Impact
The bounded correction and required re-judgment cannot proceed, leaving a confirmed HIGH reliability defect unresolved.

## Preserved state
No candidate source mutation, test execution, deployment, or delivery action occurred.

title: Gentle AI 3.7.0: Correction-plan capture rejected despite current STATUS binding
body:
## 1. Summary

A native review remains in `correction_required`. STATUS continues to offer `correction_plan_required` with a binding for `review.capture-correction-plan / correction_lines`, but two capture attempts using the then-current binding were rejected with:

```text
collectBinding is unknown, expired, or belongs to a different session route
```

Both responses reported:

```text
mutation_performed=false
```

Subsequent STATUS continued to recognize the same lineage and authority revision and re-emitted the same binding.

No root cause is established. The behavior is consistent with a capture relay/session-route binding failure, but that remains an inference.

## 2. Environment

- Gentle AI / Gentle Pi: `3.7.0`
- Review/lineage: `review-5efabb4d0d586111`
- Candidate identity: `sha256:ee303ab8c93575c47aebbe2ba44f9cde4d24422dbbddad95c66238d914eea6ef`
- Authority revision: `sha256:3421d06cddc27efe7cee0aaa685052413ccff5fa52eaca462c9a376b97b2726e`
- Recognized repository-context handle: `rctx2_443bd0cd739f716c1b85a23ddabf80427a0ad111f9a5ea76eac3c876a210979b`
- Repository-context revision: `sha256:6ad6ddbb89db64c4faea361dd704f57df0dcb8244153816468536c882dcb3b19`

## 3. Preconditions

Confirmed facts:

- STATUS recognized the lineage in `correction_required`.
- `next_transition` was `collect`, with reason `correction_plan_required`.
- The offered capture operation was `review.capture-correction-plan` for `correction_lines`.
- STATUS recognized the repository-context handle.
- `repair.status` was `unsupported`.
- STATUS listed `review/complete-fix` and `review/validate-fix`; neither replaced the current correction-plan transition.

## 4. Exact reproduction steps

1. Query STATUS for the existing lineage in its owning context.
2. Confirm `correction_required` and `correction_plan_required`.
3. Submit the currently offered correction-plan capture binding through the supported capture facade.
4. Observe the binding rejection.
5. Query STATUS again; it recognizes the same lineage and reoffers the same correction-plan capture binding.
6. Submit the reoffered binding once more; observe the same rejection.

The opaque binding and tokens are intentionally omitted.

## 5. Expected behavior

A current provider-issued correction-plan binding should be accepted by the supported capture facade for its intended session route, or the system should return a diagnostic that identifies the actionable route/session mismatch without changing authority.

## 6. Actual behavior

Both capture attempts returned the same binding-rejection message.

Afterward, STATUS still reported the same lineage, state, and authority revision, and re-emitted the correction-plan capture binding.

## 7. Evidence that provider authority remains intact

- STATUS continued to recognize `review-5efabb4d0d586111`.
- State remained `correction_required`.
- Authority revision remained `sha256:3421d06cddc27efe7cee0aaa685052413ccff5fa52eaca462c9a376b97b2726e`.
- The correction-plan transition and repository context remained recognized.
- No authority mutation was reported.

## 8. Evidence that mutation_performed=false

Both capture error responses explicitly reported:

```text
mutation_performed=false
```

No correction plan was admitted.

## 9. Why this appears to be a relay/session-route failure

Strong inference: the provider kept recognizing and reissuing the correction-plan binding, while the capture facade rejected that binding as unknown, expired, or belonging to another session route.

This points toward a mismatch between binding issuance and capture routing.

Unknown: whether the cause is session routing, binding lifetime, relay state, or another validation issue. No root cause is confirmed.

## 10. Impact

The review lineage cannot proceed through its currently offered correction-plan step.

No correction plan was admitted into this lineage and no acknowledgement was produced.

Corrective development may exist separately, but it is not associated with or admitted by this review authority.

## 11. Safe workaround status

None known.

No alternate transition or recovery route was used. Do not substitute another operation for the currently offered correction-plan transition without maintainer guidance.

## 12. Minimal logs/identifiers useful to maintainer

- Gentle AI / Gentle Pi version: `3.7.0`
- Review/lineage ID: `review-5efabb4d0d586111`
- Candidate identity: `sha256:ee303ab8c93575c47aebbe2ba44f9cde4d24422dbbddad95c66238d914eea6ef`
- Authority revision: `sha256:3421d06cddc27efe7cee0aaa685052413ccff5fa52eaca462c9a376b97b2726e`
- Transition: `collect / correction_plan_required`
- Capture operation and slot: `review.capture-correction-plan / correction_lines`
- Repository-context handle and revision: listed above
- Exact error string and `mutation_performed=false`
- `repair.status: unsupported`
- Number of failed attempts: two

Do not attach the full opaque binding or its tokens to a public issue.

## 13. Information intentionally omitted for privacy

- Full collect binding and opaque tokens
- Customer, invoice, supplier, or other business data
- SQL, database contents, backups, and backup paths
- Credentials, secrets, and `.env` contents
- Local absolute filesystem paths and unrelated repository details
- Candidate source contents not required to describe the failure

title: feat(bench): compare coding-agent outcomes, cost, and cache under controlled baselines
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area
Other

### 💡 Problem Statement
The existing `bench/` journeys verify Gentle AI lifecycle and recovery behavior, but they do not establish whether using Gentle AI improves coding-task outcomes over the same host agent without it. Likewise, a Gentle Shell claim needs a controlled comparison against plain Pi. Public coding-agent scores are easy to misread: they depend on the underlying model, agent harness, task set, benchmark revision, tool permissions, infrastructure, retries, and budget. Comparing different models or environments would not isolate the effect of our integration. Cache reuse, token cost, and latency matter to users, but a cache-read token share is not automatically a provider-defined cache-hit or cache-miss rate.

We need a reproducible, evidence-backed way to answer: on the same coding tasks and with the same model, does Gentle AI or Gentle Shell improve success, cost per solved task, or time to completion, and at what review/interaction overhead?

### 📦 Proposed Solution
Build a separate outcome-oriented benchmark lane in Gentle AI; keep the existing driven lifecycle journeys rather than presenting them as task-quality scores. Start with two paired comparisons:

1. Claude Code alone vs. the same Claude Code version with Gentle AI enabled; where supported, repeat the design for OpenCode and Codex.
2. Plain Pi vs. the same Pi version with Gentle Shell (`gentle-pi`) enabled. Define and freeze exactly which features are on in each arm.

Use a small, version-pinned real-repository task set first, then add an explicitly versioned public suite such as SWE-bench Verified and/or Terminal-Bench 2.1 where the agent interface and execution budget fit. Consider Hermes Agent and other agents only as additional independently configured competitors; do not treat another model's published score as a direct comparison. Publish task selection criteria and known exclusions, and retain a held-out slice so changes to the harness or prompts cannot silently optimize for the evaluation set.

For each task, restore the same repository snapshot and container/tool environment. Match provider/model version, credentials tier, context and tool access, CPU/RAM/network policy, time limit, maximum spend/tokens, retry policy, and test oracle. Randomize arm order, repeat tasks enough to show uncertainty, and record failures and unsupported cases rather than dropping them. Pin the benchmark dataset, agent versions, harness commit, model ID, environment, and scoring code in a reproducible run manifest. Run a cold-cache pass and a warm-cache pass separately; do not compare one arm's warm cache against the other's cold cache.

Report task-level solved/not solved with oracle evidence, pass@1 and uncertainty interval, wall-clock time, model requests, total spend and spend per solved task, input/output tokens, provider-reported cache-read/write tokens, and any unavailable fields. Define a token-weighted cache-reuse ratio only where the provider's accounting makes its denominator valid; label request-level cache-hit/miss percentage unavailable unless the provider actually exposes comparable request-level evidence. Break results down by task class and host, rather than compressing everything into a single 'best agent' number. Publish a sanitized per-task artifact and the exact rerun command, with a CI smoke subset and an opt-in full/expensive run.

Acceptance criteria:
- A contributor can reproduce a paired comparison locally from pinned inputs without relying on a manually assembled prompt or unpublished environment.
- The two arms differ only by the declared integration, and the run manifest validates that invariant before scoring.
- At least one public benchmark subset and one real-repository task subset produce task-level outcome, cost, latency, and cache-accounting results, including unsupported/missing-evidence counts.
- The result explains benchmark version, harness/model/budget, repetitions, uncertainty, cold/warm-cache policy, and which claims the evidence does **not** support.
- A CI smoke run checks corpus/scorer integrity; the full benchmark is explicitly invoked and never inferred from unit tests alone.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered
- Reuse lifecycle journey counts as evidence of coding quality: rejected because those journeys measure workflow behavior, not whether a repository task was solved.
- Compare vendor leaderboard headlines directly: rejected because agent, model, dataset revision, infrastructure, and budgets vary.
- Use only token or cache-read totals: rejected because low usage can mean failure, short tasks, or missing observations; cost must be paired with correctness, and cache-hit/miss needs a defined denominator.

### 📎 Additional Context
Related but non-equivalent work: #2026 (outcome-quality direction), #3912 (foreground live-agent SDD/RDD bench), and #1866 (binding benchmark results to exact inputs). This issue specifies the controlled cross-agent baseline, reproducible task-quality scorecard, and cache/cost methodology rather than replacing those scopes.

Benchmark-version caution: Terminal-Bench 2.1 corrected 28 of 89 tasks from 2.0; cross-version percentages should not be compared. Sources: https://www.tbench.ai/news/terminal-bench-2-1 ; https://www.swebench.com/ ; https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/infrastructure-noise ; https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching ; https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/prompt-caching .
