title: Design: classification is a single point of failure with no reclassification path, and everything traceable depends on it
body:
Cuarto y último de la revisión (#4915, #4916, #4917). Este no es un bug: es una observación de diseño, y la mando porque creo que explica *por qué* la delegación fue difícil de hacer obligatoria.

## La clasificación es un punto de fallo único, y es irreversible

El protocolo tiene siete pasos. El 4 decide si el trabajo es substancial:

> **4. Classify.** The work is substantial when exploration yields two or more meaningful implementation steps, or progress worth recovering after an interruption. Small, understood work stays small and **creates no durable task artifacts**.

Todo lo que viene después cuelga de esa decisión:

- **Paso 5** — `Track before the first write` aplica a *"substantial authorized implementation"*.
- **Paso 6** — `Route declaration` registra la ruta *"in the feature document"*.
- **Paso 7** — `Close` reporta el resultado verificado.

Si el paso 4 dice "small", no hay feature document. Y sin feature document, la declaración de ruta del paso 6 no tiene dónde escribirse. El mecanismo que `odd-mandatory-delegation.md` introdujo para hacer observable la no-delegación —*"so skipped delegation is observable instead of silent"*— depende de un artefacto que la clasificación pudo no haber creado.

## Lo que no encontré

Busqué en `routing.go`, en `docs/` y en `internal/assets/` alguna forma de **reclasificar**: qué hacer cuando un trabajo clasificado como pequeño resulta grande a mitad de camino. No hay ninguna mención (`reclassif`, `revisit the classification`, `grew into substantial`). Los únicos hits en el repo son de `reviewtransaction`, sobre otra cosa.

El long-session backstop es lo más cerca que hay, y manda a delegar:

> after about 20 tool calls, 5 exploratory reads, or 2 non-mechanical edits without any delegation, pause and delegate the next bounded unit of work.

Pero no dice que se cree el feature document que falta. Un trabajo mal clasificado que dispara el backstop delega — y sigue sin tener dónde registrar que delegó.

## Por qué creo que esto es la causa, y no un síntoma

La clasificación es el único paso que es **juicio puro y a la vez determina qué se registra**. Los demás juicios de ODD (cuánto explorar, qué es "mechanical") afectan la calidad del trabajo pero no su trazabilidad. Este define si existe evidencia.

Cuando lo medí para NODD lo marqué como fila mixta: la *decisión* es juicio irreducible, pero la *declaración* sí es mecanizable. Terminé separándolas — se exige declarar una ruta antes de la primera escritura, sin opinar sobre si la clasificación fue correcta. Un trabajo pequeño declara `inline` y sigue; lo que no puede es escribir sin declarar nada. La clasificación sigue siendo del modelo; lo que deja de ser opcional es dejar rastro de ella.

No digo que ODD deba hacer eso — es prosa, y la prosa no puede exigir. Pero si en algún momento se agrega enforcement, creo que **este es el punto donde más rinde**: un solo gate ahí hace observables los pasos 5, 6 y 7, mientras que atacarlos por separado no alcanza si el 4 ya decidió que no hay documento.

## Lo más chico que se me ocurre, sin enforcement

Una regla de reclasificación en el paso 4: *"si trabajo clasificado como pequeño cruza un trigger de delegación o llega a N archivos, reclasificar a substancial y crear el feature document en ese momento, antes de continuar."*

No lo hace obligatorio —sigue siendo texto— pero cierra el caso donde hoy la prosa no dice nada, y le da al backstop algo que hacer más allá de delegar.

---

Con este cierro la revisión. Gracias por bancar los cuatro; si prefieren que los consolide en uno, o que cierre alguno, díganme.

title: A corrupt custom-agents.json silently drops the registry entry of a successful install
body:
Tercero de la revisión (viene de #4915 y #4916). Este es de código, no de prosa.

## Un registro corrupto hace que una instalación exitosa no se registre, en silencio

**`internal/tui/model.go:5717-5749`**, tras `agentbuilder.Install`:

```go
registryPath := filepath.Join(homeDir(), ".config", "gentle-ai", "custom-agents.json")
_ = os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(registryPath), 0755)
if reg, loadErr := agentbuilder.LoadRegistry(registryPath); loadErr == nil {
    ...
    _ = agentbuilder.SaveRegistry(registryPath, reg)
}
```

Si `LoadRegistry` falla, el bloque entero se saltea. No hay `else`, no se propaga el error, y `AgentBuilderInstallDoneMsg` ya se devolvió con los resultados de la instalación: **el usuario ve "instalado" y el registro nunca se escribe.**

`LoadRegistry` es tolerante con el archivo ausente (devuelve un registro vacío), así que el primer install funciona. Falla con un archivo **corrupto**: un JSON truncado por un crash, un disco lleno a mitad de escritura, o una edición a mano.

Verificado con su propio código, en un test temporal dentro de `internal/agentbuilder`:

```
JSON corrupto → reg==nil:true err:unexpected end of JSON input
```

Con ese error, `loadErr == nil` es falso y no se registra nada.

## Por qué no es sólo cosmético

El agente **sí** quedó instalado en disco: `agentbuilder.Install` ya corrió y escribió los assets. Lo que queda inconsistente es el registro que dice qué agentes custom existen. A partir de ahí el estado en disco y el registro divergen permanentemente, y nada vuelve a intentarlo: cada install siguiente encuentra el mismo archivo corrupto y también se saltea.

El `_ = os.MkdirAll` de la línea anterior tiene el mismo patrón: si falla la creación del directorio, `SaveRegistry` va a fallar igual, y ese error también está descartado.

## Lo que sugeriría

No propagar el error hasta romper la instalación — el agente ya está instalado y fallar ahí sería peor. Alcanzaría con que el usuario se entere:

- Si `LoadRegistry` falla por corrupción (no por ausencia), mover el archivo a `custom-agents.json.corrupt-<ts>` y arrancar uno nuevo, que es recuperable y deja rastro.
- O incluir una advertencia en `AgentBuilderInstallDoneMsg` para que la TUI la muestre: "instalado, pero el registro no se pudo actualizar".

El comentario dice *"Best-effort save — ignore save errors"*, así que entiendo que la tolerancia es deliberada. Lo que creo que no es deliberado es que **el usuario no se entere**.

Feliz de mandar el PR si les parece, con un test que fije el caso del registro corrupto.

title: docs/intended-usage.md and routing.go describe the long-session backstop with different conditions
body:
Siguiendo con la revisión (viene de #4915). Este es concreto y chico.

## La docs y el bloque canónico describen el long-session backstop con condiciones distintas

**`internal/components/agentguidance/routing.go:82`** (lo que el agente recibe):

> after about 20 tool calls, 5 exploratory reads, or 2 non-mechanical edits **without any delegation**, pause and delegate the next bounded unit of work.

**`docs/intended-usage.md:124`** (lo que lee una persona):

> after roughly 20 tool calls, 5 exploratory reads, or 2 non-mechanical edits **with growing complexity**, pause and delegate, re-plan, or justify why not.

Son dos reglas diferentes, no dos redacciones de la misma:

| | canónico | docs |
|---|---|---|
| condición | sin ninguna delegación previa | con complejidad creciente |
| acción | delegar | delegar, replanear **o justificar por qué no** |

La condición del canónico es observable (¿hubo una delegación o no?). La de la docs es un juicio del modelo. Y la salida "justify why not" existe sólo en la docs: el canónico no ofrece escape.

El caso que las separa: 25 tool calls en una tarea simple y sin delegar. Por el canónico el backstop dispara; por la docs no, porque la complejidad no creció.

## Por qué creo que importa acá más que en otro repo

`docs/intended-usage.md` es lo que una persona lee para entender qué esperar del agente. Si describe un escape que el bloque real no da, la expectativa y el comportamiento divergen — y justamente en el trigger que `odd-mandatory-delegation.md` identificó como el más fácil de saltear en silencio.

## Contexto de por qué lo encontré

Al medir paridad para NODD tomé estas condiciones como especificación y me topé con las dos versiones. Terminé implementando la del canónico (sin delegación previa, sin escape), porque es la única de las dos que se puede verificar con eventos de herramientas.

No hay ningún test que ate `docs/intended-usage.md` al render de `RenderRouting` — busqué referencias al archivo en los `_test.go` y no aparece. Si les sirve, un test que compare los umbrales de la docs contra las constantes de `capabilitymanifest` evitaría que vuelvan a separarse.

Feliz de mandar el PR si me dicen cuál de las dos versiones es la correcta.

---

Nota: corrí `go build ./...` y la suite completa. Todo pasa salvo `internal/releaseprovenancecmd`, que falla **sólo en mi entorno**: mi toolchain reporta `go1.27.0-X:nodwarf5` y `goPattern` (`provenance.go:33`) espera `^go1\.[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$`. Con el Go de `go.mod` (1.25.10) pasa. Lo menciono para que no se lea como un bug suyo.

title: ODD parity matrix from an enforcement implementation: 44 of 56 clauses are mechanizable, 10 are irreducibly prose
body:
Hola 👋 Soy el autor de [NODD](https://github.com/gonzalonicolasr/nodd), una extensión de pi que implementa ODD como gates que bloquean en `tool_call`. Vengo de una charla en X con @G_Programming y @juan_barbat, donde quedamos en compartir por acá lo que salió de construirla.

Antes que nada: el README y el LICENSE de NODD ya acreditan ODD y su autoría. Toda regla que NODD impone es de ustedes; lo único que agrega el proyecto es que dejen de ser opcionales.

## Qué hice

Para construir NODD medí ODD cláusula por cláusula contra `routing.go` y los assets, y clasifiqué cada una en tres categorías:

- **M (mecanizable)** — se puede verificar con eventos de herramientas reales
- **P (prosa)** — juicio irreducible sobre lenguaje natural
- **F (forge)** — depende del binario `gentle-ai`

El resultado sobre **56 cláusulas**: **44 contienen algo mecanizable**, **10 son prosa pura**, 1 es F, 1 mixta.

La matriz completa, con cita de línea por cláusula, está en [`.sdd/nodd/requirements.md`](https://github.com/gonzalonicolasr/nodd/blob/master/.sdd/nodd/requirements.md). Es de ustedes si les sirve.

## Lo que me parece que vale la pena

**1. Las 10 cláusulas P no son deuda técnica.**

Es el hallazgo que más me sorprendió. Cosas como *"explorá proporcionalmente al pedido"* o *"lo chico se queda chico"* no son observables: el mismo `read` se ve idéntico si precede a un edit o si cierra la sesión. Intenté mecanizarlas y desistí — ponerle un número a "¿exploré lo suficiente?" convierte una guía en un techo arbitrario. Creo que marcarlas explícitamente como juicio, en vez de dejarlas como aspiracionales, las hace más fuertes.

**2. `odd-mandatory-delegation.md` diagnostica algo que el propio documento no puede resolver.**

Leí el task file y el diagnóstico es exacto:

> ODD routing is pure model judgment: nothing requires the route decision to be stated, recorded, or checked, so non-delegation is invisible

El fix de `6ad6843a` fortalece mucho el texto — "these triggers are mandatory, not advisory", la declaración de ruta, el backstop. Pero `RenderRouting` sigue emitiendo un string: 53 `WriteString` y ningún punto donde el código pueda frenar una llamada. Si el modelo decide no delegar, el resultado es el mismo que antes del fix.

No lo digo como crítica — es una limitación estructural de cualquier cosa que viva en el prompt, y por eso NODD existe. Pero significa que "mandatory" describe una intención, no un mecanismo.

**3. Dónde sí se puede cerrar, si les interesa.**

Los runtimes que soportan hooks de pre-tool-call (pi con extensiones, Claude Code con `PreToolUse`) permiten rechazar la escritura antes de que ocurra. En NODD son 6 gates que miden observaciones reales: sin ruta declarada no hay primer write; a los 2 archivos sin delegar, corta; una tarea no se marca hecha hasta observar el runner declarado pasar.

Lo interesante: el 44/56 sugiere que buena parte de ODD **es** mecanizable. No hace falta tocar `routing.go` — puede vivir como una capa opcional para los runtimes que lo soporten, degradando a prosa en los que no.

## Ofrecimiento

Feliz de aportar lo que sirva: la matriz, los casos de test, o lo que salga de charlarlo. Si prefieren que esto sea un PR en vez de un issue, díganme dónde encajaría.

Y gracias por ODD — sin el workflow no había nada que hacer cumplir.

title: [Automated provider defect] bug(opencode): possible regression of #3987 on 3.5.0 — reviewer Tasks rejected for a target in a registered sibling worktree
body:
## Summary

OpenCode reviewer Tasks are still rejected with `opencode_review_transport_binding_invalid` when the review target is a **registered sibling worktree of the same Git repository** as the OpenCode session root. This is the topology reported in #3987 and fixed by #3992. The installed build demonstrably contains that fix, so this looks like a **possible regression**.

Filed as an automated provider-defect report, with explicit consent from the operator. Only the observed evidence below is included; the root cause is not confirmed.

## Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Gentle AI | 3.5.0 (stable channel) |
| Fix contained? | Yes. GitHub compare `cd4ab336...v3.5.0` (merge commit of #3992) reports `status=ahead, behind_by=0` |
| Client | OpenCode 1.18.32, managed review-transport plugin |
| Platform | macOS (Darwin) arm64 |
| Contract | `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2` |

## Topology

- The OpenCode session is rooted at the **primary checkout A** of a Git repository.
- The review target is a **linked worktree B** of the same repository, created with `git worktree add`:
  - B lives outside A's directory tree;
  - `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` in B resolves to A's `.git`.

## Operation shape

No argv or paths, in order:

1. `review assess --committed-only` → `risk: high`, `review_due: true`, `review_due_reason: high_risk`.
2. Returned preflight `review status --next-transition` → `execute review.start`, reason `fresh_target_ready`.
3. `review start --consent=relay` → typed `consent/v3` envelope. The human answered **granted**.
4. Exact `granted` invocation → `action: created`, next `execute review.status`, reason `review_status_required`.
5. Exact-lineage `review status` → `collect`, reason `reviewer_results_required`, with 4 reviewer inputs: risk, resilience, readability, reliability.
6. One grouped launch of 4 foreground OpenCode Tasks. Each copied `provider_task.agent` as `subagent_type` and `provider_task.prompt` verbatim.

## Observed

All 4 Tasks were rejected before model execution with:

```
opencode_review_transport_binding_invalid: Task repository context does not match the repository and binding it commits to
```

## Bounded attempts

- 1 grouped launch of 4 Tasks. All 4 were rejected identically.
- 1 exact-lineage STATUS re-query. It reoffered the same 4 bound slots, with byte-identical prompts.
- No relaunch: the failure is deterministic for this topology.

## Expected

Per #3987 and #3992, the transport should resolve the opaque provider-issued repository context against the uniquely matching registered worktree that shares the host's Git common directory. It should then launch the reviewers against the immutable candidate in B and keep every lifecycle mutation bound to B.

If the host cannot launch the Task in the target worktree, #3980 says the preflight should refuse **before** START freezes authority.

## Actual

- START froze a reviewing lineage; the preflight did not refuse.
- Every reviewer Task was then rejected, leaving an unrunnable `collect` step. This is the #3980 symptom.

## Minimal reproduction

1. In checkout A: `git worktree add ../wt-b -b fix/x origin/main`. Commit a small high-risk change in B.
2. Open OpenCode rooted at A.
3. Run `gentle-ai review assess --cwd <B> --agent opencode --base-ref origin/main --committed-only --json`.
4. Run the returned STATUS, then START with `--consent=relay`, and grant.
5. Run the bound STATUS and launch the provider-issued reviewer Tasks from the A session.
6. Observe the rejection above.

## Mutation outcome and preserved state

- A reviewing lineage was created.
- No capture was admitted, and no receipt or acknowledgement was produced.
- No source file was mutated by the review attempt.
- The consumer will decline this candidate through the provider-issued decline invocation, which is candidate-scoped. Review mode stays enabled.

## Safe identifiers

- Reason codes: `fresh_target_ready`, `review_status_required`, `reviewer_results_required`.
- Frozen revision: `sha256:e6bafaba980bd8e0e47f4403d6fb2e77471eeb1a323802ebb767cff70b408a0c`.

## Related

- #3987 and #3992: the same topology, fixed on the 2.5 line. The fix is contained in 3.5.0.
- #3980: preflight before freezing an unrunnable Task lineage.
- #4516: same error code, different topology (git-less parent directory).

title: bug(review): claude-code reviewer transport deterministically refuses with 'claude: executable file not found in %PATH%' when running as a VS Code extension (3.5.0, Windows)
body:
## Environment
- gentle-ai version: 3.5.0 (stable channel, no `-rc.`/`-main.` tag)
- OS: Windows
- Agent: claude-code
- Client context: Claude Code running as a VS Code native extension (not the standalone terminal CLI install)

## Observed behavior

Ran the standard receipt-driven-review flow end to end:

1. `gentle-ai review status --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --agent claude-code --next-transition` → returned a fresh-target `review.start` command.
2. Ran the exact returned `review.start` invocation → returned a `gentle-ai.review-integration.consent/v3` envelope (risk_level: high).
3. Relayed consent to the human, who granted it. Ran the exact `granted` invocation from the envelope → `action: "created"`, `state: "reviewing"`, 4 lenses selected (review-risk, review-resilience, review-readability, review-reliability), `next_transition` pointed to `review.status`.
4. Ran the returned `review.status` → got a `collect` transition with 4 `review.capture-result` inputs (one per lens), each carrying `--agent=claude-code` and no `--input` (in-process capture per the v2 contract).
5. Launched all 4 `review.capture-result` commands concurrently, in lens order, exactly as instructed by the contract.

**All 4 failed identically**, each returning:

```json
{
  "schema": "gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2",
  "operation": "review.capture-result",
  "phase": "preflight",
  "code": "invalid_request",
  "message": "The negotiated review request is invalid.",
  "mutation_outcome": "not_started",
  "retry_safe": true,
  "next_action": "correct_request",
  "cause": "invoke provider reviewer: claude reviewer transport unavailable: exec: \"claude\": executable file not found in %PATH%"
}
```

6. Per the contract's recovery rule ("relaunch only if fresh STATUS reoffers the same bound slot"), re-ran `review.status` — it reoffered the identical 4-input collect slot (same subject hashes, same revision).
7. Retried one lens (`review-risk`) once, per `retry_safe: true` — **identical failure**, same cause string. Not transient.

## Expected behavior
Either the in-process `claude-code` capture path should not shell out to a separate `claude` binary at all (since the agent invoking `gentle-ai` already *is* Claude Code, just embedded in a VS Code extension host rather than a standalone terminal CLI install), or `review.start`/`review.status` should detect the missing transport during preflight (before freezing a high-risk candidate and burning a consent round-trip) and report a clear, actionable `blockedReasons` entry instead of a generic `invalid_request` surfaced only at the capture step.

## Mutation outcome / state preserved
`mutation_outcome: "not_started"` on every failed capture — no partial state was written. The lineage remains parked in `state: "reviewing"` with all 4 lens slots still uncollected. No workaround was attempted from the consumer side (no synthesized reviewer prompt, no `--input` added) per the contract's explicit prohibition on reconstructing the relay form.

## Minimal repro shape
- Any repository with RDD enabled.
- Agent = `claude-code`, but the actual process is Claude Code running inside a host that does not expose a `claude` executable on `PATH` (e.g., the VS Code extension host, as opposed to a terminal where the `claude` CLI was installed globally).
- Trigger any `review.start` → `review.capture-result` cycle.

title: feat(tui): add provider search filter in OpenCode model picker
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

TUI (terminal UI)

### 💡 Problem Statement

When configuring OpenCode models in the TUI (`Configure models` -> `Configure OpenCode models` -> select an SDD/JD/custom phase), the user enters `Select provider:`.

In the initial two-step picker implementation (commit `c606dca4`, March 14, 2026), this screen was designed under the assumption of a "short list" of 2–3 static providers (`auth.json`). Since then, the runtime catalog and discovery pipeline expanded dramatically (support for custom JSON/JSONC endpoints, LM Studio, streaming catalog discovery via `opencode models`), turning the provider list into 30+ dynamic entries (see #3004).

However, unlike `Select model:` which features real-time search filtering via `ModelSearch`, `Select provider:` lacks any filtering capability and forces item-by-item vertical scrolling.

Furthermore, several critical UX and technical debts exist in the current picker:
1. **Application termination on 'q':** In `Select provider:`, typing `q` (e.g. attempting to search for `qwen`) returns `handled = false` from `handleProviderNav`, falling through to `model.go:1830` (`case "ctrl+c", "q": return m, tea.Quit`). Gentle AI quits immediately without confirmation.
2. **Search key hijacking (`j`/`k`):** In `isModelSearchInput` (`model_picker.go` and `codex_model_picker.go`), lowercase `j` and `k` are intercepted for list navigation, preventing users from typing terms containing those letters (e.g. `deepseek`, `json`). Because string comparison is case-sensitive, pressing `Shift+K` (`"K"`) bypasses navigation and types `"K"`, creating erratic behavior.
3. **Cursor clamping on value receiver:** In `renderModelSelect`, cursor clamping operates on a value receiver copy of `ModelPickerState`. The underlying pointer state is not clamped, creating a potential `panic: runtime error: index out of range` on `Enter` if the model catalog shrinks. Codex already fixed this defensive clamping in commit `eac1a4b9`, but it was never backported to `model_picker.go`.
4. **Lack of test coverage:** Neither `handleProviderNav` nor `renderProviderSelect` currently have dedicated unit tests.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

1. Add `ProviderSearch string` to `ModelPickerState` in `internal/tui/screens/model_picker.go`.
2. Implement case-insensitive substring filtering in `FilteredProviderEntries` matching against both provider `Name` and `ID`.
3. Render `Search: <query>_` and empty-state warning (`No providers match your search.`) in `renderProviderSelect`.
4. Fix navigation and key handling: reserve Up/Down arrow keys (and `ctrl+j`/`ctrl+k`) for list navigation so all printable characters (including `j`, `k`, and `q`) can be typed into the search buffer without triggering application termination or unwanted jumps.
5. Apply this navigation pattern consistently to both `ProviderSearch` and `ModelSearch` within `model_picker.go`.
6. Add defensive clamping (`min(max(0, cursor), max(0, len-1))`) before indexing slices.
7. Clear `ProviderSearch` when pressing `esc` (returning to phase list) or `enter` (advancing to model select).
8. Add thorough unit tests in `internal/tui/screens/model_picker_test.go` covering provider filtering, search typing, backspace, clear (`ctrl+u`), empty states, and cursor clamping.
9. Keep changes strictly within the 400 changed lines budget.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- Extracting a generic `SearchableList` component across OpenCode and Codex: deferred to avoid exceeding the 400 changed-line PR budget and touching stable pickers simultaneously.
- Vim-style modal search (`/` to search, `esc` to navigate): rejected in favor of the immediate typing model established across Gentle AI.

### 📎 Additional Context

- Historical commits: `c606dca4` (March 14, 2026: original "short list" assumption) and `56bfc6c9` (May 25, 2026: model search introduction).
- Profile creation (`internal/tui/screens/profile_create.go`) reuses `ModelPickerState` and will automatically inherit `ProviderSearch`.
- Related issues: #3004 (paging and position indicators for long lists), #2301 / PR #4502 (adaptive viewport height).

title: feat(pi): add audited exceptions for sensitive-path false positives
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

The submission agent searched open and closed issues before publishing; the requester explicitly affirmed the second checklist item.

### 🔍 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Problem Statement

Pi's sensitive-path guard rejects direct read/write/edit for any path containing a `/secrets/` segment before inspecting its contents. A non-secret UI component in a directory named `secrets` is therefore blocked even after the human explains its purpose. The refusal asks for a safer plan, but the installed integration exposes no supported path-specific authorization. This shares the false-positive class of #3976; this request proposes a general authorization mechanism rather than a fix limited to that example.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Provide an opt-in, auditable authorization table for false-positive path guards. Each entry should bind a canonical repository identity, an exact path by default, permitted operations, the approving human, and a bounded lifetime. An optional justification can record why the exception is safe. Require explicit UI approval to create or renew an entry, show its effective scope, and support revocation. Keep unmatched paths denied and preserve non-overridable protections for genuinely sensitive material. Chat text alone must not create authority.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

Renaming directories merely to avoid the match would evade the policy and risk breaking references. A broad allowlist or disabling the guard would weaken protection. Manually editing the blocked file leaves the agent workflow incomplete.

### 📎 Additional Context

The installed guard matches the `/secrets/` path segment and blocks direct read/write/edit. The example concerns an OAuth client-secrets UI component, not stored credentials. No private repository path, file contents, or credentials are included. Related: #3976.

title: bug(review): capture-validation reports no mutation after terminal validator escalation
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

On the stable `gentle-ai 3.5.1-0.20260922125209-7a1af77f0fd3` build, an exact provider-issued targeted-validation capture for a bounded correction returned `native-operation-failed`, `mutation_performed:false`, `mutation_outcome:none`. A fresh STATUS for the same lineage immediately showed terminal `escalated`, `targeted_validator_rejected`, `stop`. The two reports disagree about whether review authority changed. No validator verdict or diagnostic explanation appeared in the capture result or STATUS; no root cause is asserted.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Reach `correction_required` in a high-tier native review with one finding and a committed, in-budget correction.
2. Read native STATUS and use its exact current `provider_targeted_validator` collect binding.
3. Request the host-relay one-run forecast, then acknowledge and execute that same binding once. Do not replay it.
4. Compare the returned capture outcome with a fresh STATUS for that lineage.

Observed once in Pi's native review controller. The reviewed application code and repository identity are private; the operation shape above contains no private source or arguments.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

A capture that changes authority must not report `mutation_performed:false` and `mutation_outcome:none`. If the native mutation result is uncertain, provide an honest unknown outcome requiring STATUS reconciliation; if terminal validator rejection is conclusive, expose an auditable and actionable diagnostic without offering replay. Either way, preserve the terminal lifecycle and never fabricate a receipt.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The capture response asserted no mutation and advised `resolve-native-operation-failure`. Fresh STATUS showed a changed terminal authority state with `targeted_validator_rejected` and `native_stop_required`. No receipt was issued, no retry was attempted, and the user cannot determine from the surfaced evidence why the validator rejected the correction.

### Gentle AI Version

3.5.1-0.20260922125209-7a1af77f0fd3 (stable build string; no `-rc.` or `-main.` tag)

### Operating System

Linux (Fedora/RHEL)

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
capture: {status: blocked, outcome: native-operation-failed, lineage_created: false, mutation_performed: false, mutation_outcome: none, next_action: resolve-native-operation-failure}
fresh STATUS: {authority.state: escalated, action: stop, next_transition.reason_code: native_stop_required, escalation.cause: targeted_validator_rejected, escalation.finding_ids: [<redacted>]}
```

### Additional Context

The local correction passed focused and full tests, and separate process-exit probes recovered before and after a real atomic replacement; neither establishes the validator's verdict or power-loss behavior. This report is about contradictory authority/mutation reporting, not a claim that the validator should have approved.

Related but not equivalent on the observed contract: #4223 documents a last-event schema incompatibility with an **unknown** mutation outcome; #4006 documents an **unknown** capture outcome and subsequent escalation; #3799 concerns inspectability of an admitted failed validator result. Here the capture explicitly claimed **none/false** while subsequent STATUS showed a changed terminal lineage. No specific schema, model, or transport fault is inferred.

title: bug(review): intended-untracked selection submission drops the committed-only --base-ref selector, widening a slice to the whole branch until lens_context_budget_exceeded (3.5.0 stable)
body:
### Pre-flight checks
- [x] Explicit user consent was obtained to report this apparent provider defect.
- [x] Open and closed issues were searched (intended-untracked selection, `intended_untracked_selection_required`, base-ref / committed-only with untracked files, `lens_context_budget_exceeded`, `selector_arguments`). No equivalent was found; related reports are listed below.
- [x] This report contains observed evidence only and does not assert a root cause.
- [x] Final privacy scan completed immediately before creation: no raw argv with local paths, absolute paths, private project names, usernames, hostnames, credentials, diffs, source contents or environment values.

### Summary
When a committed-only slice is selected with an explicit `--base-ref`, the `intended_untracked_selection_required` collect step returns `submission.argument_tokens` that carry neither `--base-ref` nor `--committed-only`. Submitting exactly those tokens makes STATUS re-derive the target from the branch point on the default branch. The resulting START covers the whole feature branch instead of the requested slice, including a range that was already acknowledged. On a large branch it then stops with `lens_context_budget_exceeded`. While the worktree keeps any untracked file, every later slice on the branch hits the same wall.

### Environment
- gentle-ai `3.5.0` (no `-rc.` or `-main.` tag, so stable evidence channel; latest published release at the time of the report)
- Windows 11, x86_64
- Client: claude-code, in-process capture
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`
- Projection: `workspace`, `--committed-only`
- RDD mode: on (global)

### Repository state
- A feature branch with three commits (C1, C2, C3) on top of the branch point B0 on the default branch.
- The slice B0..C2 was already reviewed through the same flow, approved, acknowledged and burned. In that first cycle the dropped selector could not be seen, because the requested base was B0 anyway.
- The worktree has three untracked files, all generated by tooling and none intended for review: two tool registry files and one task-tracking document.

### Observed sequence (one attempt)
1. `gentle-ai review assess --cwd <repo> --agent claude-code --base-ref <C2> --committed-only --untracked-scope=exclude --expected-untracked-inventory=<inv> --json` returned:
   - `risk: medium`, `changed_paths: 17`, `changed_lines: 2763` (C3 only);
   - `review_due: true`, `review_due_reason: slice_budget_reached`;
   - `next_transition.command = gentle-ai review status --cwd=<repo> --contract=gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --agent=claude-code --next-transition=true --base-ref=<C2> --committed-only=true`.
2. That exact STATUS returned target **T1**:
   - `projection.base_tree` = tree of C2, and 17 paths (C3 only);
   - `next_transition.kind: collect`, `reason_code: intended_untracked_selection_required`;
   - `submission.argument_tokens` = `--contract=gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --next-transition=true --agent=claude-code --projection=workspace --intended-untracked-selection={{value}}`. There is no `--base-ref`, no `--committed-only` and no `--cwd`.
3. Those exact tokens were run with the process cwd at the repository, with this value: `{"schema":"gentle-ai.review-intended-untracked-selection/v1","untracked_scope":"exclude","expected_untracked_inventory":"<inv>","intended_untracked":[]}`. STATUS returned a **different** target **T2**:
   - `projection.base_tree` = tree of B0, and 21 paths (C1 + C2 + C3);
   - `next_transition` = `execute review.start … --base-ref=<B0> --committed-only=true … --untracked-scope=exclude --expected-untracked-inventory=<inv> --consent=relay`.
4. The exact START returned a `consent/v3` envelope for 21 files and 4274 lines. The human answered `granted`, and the exact granted invocation returned `gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2`:
   - `code: lens_context_budget_exceeded`, `phase: preflight`;
   - `mutation_outcome: not_started`, `next_action: stop`, `retry_safe: true`.

### Expected
The selection submission keeps the selector negotiated in step 1 and step 2. After the untracked selection, the target stays T1 (base C2, C3 only, 2763 lines). Alternatively, the selection gate is skipped for a committed-only selector, as proposed in #4339.

### Actual
The selector is dropped. The target widens from the requested slice to B0..C3, including the already-acknowledged range B0..C2, and START refuses it with `lens_context_budget_exceeded`. The failure text recommends splitting into smaller commits, but the slice as requested was already a single commit; what widened it was the selection step.

### Minimal reproduction
1. On a feature branch, leave at least one untracked, non-intended file in the worktree.
2. Make commit C1, then run `assess --base-ref <branch point> --committed-only` and review and acknowledge that slice.
3. Make commit C2, then run `assess --base-ref <C1> --committed-only --untracked-scope=exclude --expected-untracked-inventory=<inv>`, and run the returned STATUS.
4. Submit the `intended_untracked_selection` collect with `untracked_scope: exclude` and the exact submission tokens.
5. Observe that the next target's `base_tree` is the branch point, not C1.

### Preserved state
- No lineage was created for the failed START (`mutation_outcome: not_started`).
- The earlier lineage for B0..C2 remains acknowledged and burned.
- Nothing in the repository was changed by gentle-ai.
- The next step on the consumer side is the candidate-scoped decline invocation from the `consent/v3` envelope.

### Related
- #4339: skip the intended-untracked gate for committed-only or empty inventory. If implemented, it would avoid this path.
- #4639: committed-candidate base derived from the default branch. That report is about a different trigger, with a well-formed selector.
- #4790: the frozen-evidence budget is validated only after consent.

title: [Automated provider defect] Claude Code: a correction_required lineage opened by an unrefuted inferential blocker is reoffered as a fresh START that refuses candidate_context_unavailable (3.5.0)
body:
## Summary

A compact lineage in `correction_required` — opened by a single **inferential** CRITICAL finding that went straight to `correction_plan_required` without a refuter batch — is reoffered by the selectorless preflight / Claude Code stop hook as a `fresh_target_ready` START for the **same lineage id**. That START relays a normal `consent/v3` envelope; executing its exact `granted` invocation refuses with `candidate_context_unavailable` (`retry_safe: false`, `mutation_outcome: unknown`). The bound STATUS then returns `collect / correction_plan_required` again. The only offered continuation is a correction plan (`positive_correction_lines`, min 1), and the only other exit is `review abandon` with maintainer authorization.

Adjacent, on the evidence not the same observable defect:

- #4704 — reoffered START refuses `candidate_context_unavailable`, but there the lineage is terminal `corrupted_or_unverifiable_authority`. Here the lineage is live in `correction_required` and its bound STATUS still returns a `collect`.
- #1856 (closed) — STATUS repeating a non-retry-safe START after a candidate-context failure. Here the repetition comes from the stop hook / selectorless preflight offering START for a lineage that is already bound and awaiting a correction plan.

This report asserts no root cause.

## Observed evidence

- Gentle AI `3.5.0` (stable channel), contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, agent `claude-code`, Linux x86_64.
- Candidate: committed-only, projection `workspace`, 25 paths, 3514 changed lines, risk `medium`, one selected lens (`review-reliability`), correction budget 200.
- Lineage `review-c1fa08e88d4f8188`, target identity `sha256:65725835b5b5ff295ca6e2147494f0e2e10e8da9a5b518dfba1379d132a1b41d`, base tree `0e4a1f52cdcd6ec42ba23f6bfa1008e832795b0d`.

Sequence, each step running only the exact provider-issued operation and ordered tokens returned by the previous one:

1. Selectorless preflight STATUS → `execute / review.start / fresh_target_ready`.
2. Exact START with `--consent=relay` → `consent/v3`, human answered `granted`.
3. Exact `granted` invocation → `action: created`, `state: reviewing`.
4. Bound STATUS → `collect / reviewer_results_required`, one in-process `review.capture-result` slot.
5. Exact capture (in-process, `--agent`, no `--input`) → `state: correction_required` with a `status_continuation`; no `advisory_findings`, no `reviewer_results` in the capture output.
6. Exact `status_continuation` → `collect / correction_plan_required`, forecast `horizon: partial`, one `review.capture-correction-plan` input.
7. The only frozen finding (found in the STATUS body) is `severity: CRITICAL`, `evidence_class: inferential`, `causal_disposition: introduced`. Its claim is that APIs the candidate calls are absent from the base. The operator verified they are present in the base tree above (same tree as the remote default branch), so the claim is false. No refuter ran.
8. Claude Code stop hook then reported the same target as unreviewed and printed the exact selectorless START for lineage `review-c1fa08e88d4f8188` (`fresh_target_ready`, `--consent=relay`).
9. That exact START → `consent/v3` envelope again; human answered `granted`.
10. Exact `granted` invocation → exit 1, `gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2`:
    - `phase: native_committed`, `code: candidate_context_unavailable`
    - `mutation_outcome: unknown`, `retry_safe: false`, `replayability: status_required`, `next_action: review.status`
    - cause: `render frozen context for selected durable START authority "review-c1fa08e88d4f8188" at revision sha256:c09d2991…: validate negotiated START response: negotiated START repository context does not match the active reviewing authority`
11. Exact bound STATUS for the lineage → `collect / correction_plan_required` (unchanged).

## Expected vs actual

- Expected: a lineage awaiting a correction plan is not reoffered as a fresh START (by the preflight or the stop hook); an inferential blocker goes through the refuter batch before opening `correction_required`; a false inferential blocker has a sanctioned non-maintainer exit.
- Actual: the reoffered START is refused, the lineage stays in `correction_plan_required`, and the only exits are a correction plan for a finding that does not exist, `review abandon` with maintainer authorization, or disabling review.

## Minimal reproduction shape

Committed-only candidate whose diff calls APIs that exist only in the base (not in the diff); medium risk, one reliability lens. Grant review, capture. If the reviewer emits an inferential CRITICAL about the base, observe steps 5–11.

## Preserved state

No correction plan was submitted, nothing was abandoned, review mode was not changed. The lineage is left in `correction_required` / `correction_plan_required`. After filing, the operator runs the exact `declined` invocation from the step-9 envelope once for this candidate.

title: bug(installcmd): engram and gga component installs fail on Homebrew 7 because the formula is never trusted
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

On Homebrew 7 the install pipeline cannot install `engram` or `gga` from the tap. Both component steps run `brew tap Gentleman-Programming/homebrew-tap` (which succeeds) and then `brew install engram` / `brew reinstall gga`, and Homebrew refuses to load the formula because the tap is not trusted.

This is the Go side of the same Homebrew 7 change reported in #4573. That issue is about `scripts/install.sh` failing on the first `brew tap`; here the tap is already there and `gentle-ai` itself is fine (I installed it with `brew install gentleman-programming/tap/gentle-ai`, which trusted only the `gentle-ai` formula). The component installs in `internal/installcmd/resolver.go` never trust the formula they are about to install, and `brew tap` alone does not grant trust on Homebrew 7.

`brew trust` did not exist on older Homebrew, so the fix has to emit the trust step only when the subcommand is there. The upgrade path in `internal/update/upgrade/strategy.go` already trusts the single formula being upgraded before running `brew upgrade`; the component install path should do the same before `brew install` / `brew reinstall`.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Fedora 44 Workstation (kernel 7.2.5, x86_64) with Linuxbrew, Homebrew 7.0.6.
2. `brew install gentleman-programming/tap/gentle-ai` (gentle-ai 3.5.0). Homebrew prompts to trust the `gentle-ai` formula only.
3. Run `gentle-ai`, select any agent plus the Engram and GGA components.
4. Watch `component:engram` and `component:gga` fail.

Same thing from a shell, with nothing trusted:

```
brew untrust --tap gentleman-programming/tap
brew tap Gentleman-Programming/homebrew-tap      # exit 0
brew reinstall gga                                # refuses
brew trust --formula gentleman-programming/tap/gga
brew reinstall gga                                # works
```

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Selecting Engram or GGA on a Homebrew 7 machine installs them. The pipeline should trust the one formula it is about to install (the same scope the upgrade path already uses) before `brew install` / `brew reinstall`, and skip that step on Homebrew versions without `brew trust`.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Both component steps fail and the install ends with errors. Engram and GGA are not installed until the user runs `brew trust` by hand and reruns.

### Gentle AI Version

3.5.0

### Operating System

Linux (Fedora/RHEL)

### AI Agent / Client

Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area

Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
FAILED: component:engram — run command "<user-home>/.local/bin/brew install engram": exit status 1
output:
Error: Refusing to load formula gentleman-programming/tap/engram from untrusted tap gentleman-programming/tap.
Run `brew trust --formula gentleman-programming/tap/engram` or `brew trust gentleman-programming/tap` to trust it.
FAILED: component:gga — run command "brew reinstall gga": exit status 1
output:
Error: Refusing to load formula gentleman-programming/tap/gga from untrusted tap gentleman-programming/tap.
Run `brew trust --formula gentleman-programming/tap/gga` or `brew trust gentleman-programming/tap` to trust it.
```

### Additional Context

Workaround that got me through: `brew trust --formula gentleman-programming/tap/engram` and the same for `gga`, then rerun `gentle-ai`.

I have a branch with the resolver change and tests, and I verified it end to end on this machine: with `gga` uninstalled and nothing trusted, the patched binary emitted `brew trust --formula gentleman-programming/tap/gga`, then tapped and reinstalled, and `brew trust --json=v1` showed only that formula afterwards. I will open the PR once this is approved.

title: bug(review): a generated ORM migration designer consumes 99% of the lens context budget, making the authored change unreviewable
body:
Automated provider-defect report. Observed evidence only; no root cause asserted beyond what the shipped source states. Filed with the operator's explicit consent.

## Summary

A single work-unit commit that adds one ORM migration is **unreviewable**: `review start` refuses with `lens_context_budget_exceeded`, and the refusal is caused almost entirely by the migration's **generated designer file**, not by the authored change.

The authored change is 246 insertions across 9 files. The generated file is 27,159 insertions — **99.1 % of the candidate**. It is deterministic tool output (a full snapshot of the data model, regenerated verbatim by the ORM's CLI), and it carries no review value.

The refusal advises reviewing "this change as smaller candidates". That advice cannot be followed here: the candidate is already one work unit, and the only available split would separate the migration from its generated designer — which is where the migration-registration attribute lives, so the resulting commit would not stand on its own.

## Environment

- gentle-ai 3.4.0 (no `-rc.` / `-main.` tag → stable evidence channel; latest published release)
- Windows 11 x64 (Git Bash), client `claude-code`, in-process capture
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, projection `workspace`, `--committed-only=true`
- Candidate scoped deliberately to the last acknowledged boundary via `--base-ref`, so this is **not** the accumulated-branch mis-scope of #4639.

## Observed

`review assess` on the correctly scoped candidate:

```json
{
  "risk": "medium",
  "reasons": [{ "code": "executable_change", "path": "<a controller>" }],
  "changed_paths": 10,
  "changed_lines": 27411,
  "review_due": true,
  "review_due_reason": "slice_budget_reached"
}
```

Per-file breakdown of the same candidate (`git show --numstat`):

| Insertions | Deletions | Kind |
| ---: | ---: | --- |
| 27,159 | 0 | **generated** ORM migration designer |
| 120 | 0 | tests |
| 38 | 0 | domain model |
| 31 | 3 | documentation |
| 28 | 0 | migration (authored) |
| 8 / 8 / 8 | 0 | three DTOs |
| 5 | 0 | controller |
| 3 | 0 | generated model snapshot |

Authored total: **246 insertions, 3 deletions**.

`review start … --consent granted` then returned:

```
schema: gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2
operation: review.start
phase: preflight
code: lens_context_budget_exceeded
message: The candidate's complete reviewer evidence exceeds the native context budget,
         so no review authority was created; review this change as smaller candidates
         that each fit under it.
mutation_outcome: not_started
authority_applicability: not_evaluated
retry_safe: true
next_action: stop
```

No authority was created, so nothing needed abandoning or repairing. The refusal itself is clean and correctly classified — the problem is that it is unavoidable.

## Why the usual escape hatches do not apply

**Marking the file as generated cannot work, by design.** `internal/reviewtransaction/frozen_candidate_context.go` states that the inspector installs "an empty attributes file plus `GIT_ATTR_NOSYSTEM`, so neither the repository's `.gitattributes` nor the machine's can move the classification." That determinism guarantee is sound, but it also means a repository has no way to declare that a path is derived.

**Splitting the commit breaks a stronger rule.** The migration-registration attribute lives in the generated designer, so a commit holding the migration without it leaves the migration unregistered. Splitting trades an unreviewable commit for a commit that does not stand alone.

**There is precedent for excluding non-substantive content from this budget.** #3208 (closed, approved) charges a git-detected rename as one small change-inside-the-moved-file patch specifically so that "a candidate dominated by pure moves stays inside the reviewer context byte budget". A candidate dominated by regenerated tool output is the same class of problem, unaddressed.

## Why this is not a one-off

Any commit containing an ORM migration is affected, because the designer file is regenerated in full on every migration regardless of how small the schema change is. In the repository where this was observed, four more planned work units each add a migration; all four are expected to hit the identical refusal.

The severity is not "a review was skipped": it is that **the authored 246 lines — which include a domain model change and a controller change — cannot be reviewed at all**, while a file nobody wrote consumes the entire budget.

## Related but not equivalent

- **#3208** (closed) — rename-driven budget inflation. Same budget, same shape of fix, different trigger; the rename path was solved specifically and generated artifacts were not.
- **#3389** (open) — a single path over 4 MiB starts and then loops on an unresolvable refusal. Different: here nothing starts, the refusal is terminal and clean at preflight, and no loop occurs.
- **#4680** (closed) — START accepted a candidate the reviewer later rejected as too long. Opposite ordering: this refusal correctly happens before any authority exists.
- **#4790** (open) — budget validated only after consent and lineage creation. Partially adjacent: here the refusal did arrive at `phase: preflight` with `mutation_outcome: not_started`, so no lineage was created; the cost was the consent round, not a stuck lineage.
- **#4639** (open) — mis-scoped base-ref. Explicitly ruled out: this candidate was scoped to the last acknowledged boundary on purpose.

## Suggested direction (not a prescription)

Either of these would unblock the class without weakening the determinism guarantee:

1. Charge provably-derived content the way #3208 charges renames — by marker rather than by full content — using a signal the tool derives itself rather than one the repository asserts.
2. Let the `--policy` file declare derived path globs, so the exclusion is explicit, auditable, and still part of the frozen candidate identity.

Both keep the candidate's byte identity intact; only what the reviewer lens is asked to read changes.

## Privacy

No credentials, absolute paths, private repository or project names, usernames, hostnames, source contents, diffs, raw argv, or environment values are included. Files are described by role rather than named.

title: feat(review): add a session-scoped RDD mode override for interactive agents
body:
## Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

## 🔍 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

## 💡 Problem Statement

`gentle-ai review mode status` exposes exactly two policy scopes — global and clone-local — and both are persistent. After a single candidate-specific terminal review failure (for example, a lineage that stops with `native_stop_required`), the only way to keep working interactively in that clone is `gentle-ai review mode disable --scope clone`, which changes policy for every future session in the clone. There is no way to authorize a temporary, session-only exception.

## 📦 Proposed Solution

Add a session-scoped RDD mode override for interactive agents:

- granted only by explicit human authorization, scoped to one session;
- bound to the current session manager instance (for example, one interactive Pi session) and the repository identity;
- expires on session reload, replacement, quit, or process exit (or a documented equivalent);
- never implies approval of any review candidate or finding;
- never persistently alters global or clone-local policy — after the session ends, the effective mode resolves from the existing scopes again;
- `review mode status` identifies the effective source, including when the session override is deciding;
- unrelated repositories require separate authorization.

## 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- `disable --scope clone`: works today, but persists for every future session in the clone — over-broad for a one-candidate failure.
- Worktree-scoped override (#1973): useful, but it is a persistent scope stored with the worktree; it does not expire with the session.
- Clone-local opt-in when global is off (#4410): addresses opt-in direction, not ephemeral session-scoped exceptions.

## 📎 Additional Context

Motivation: continue one interactive session after a terminal candidate-specific review failure without disabling RDD for every future session in the clone. Complementary to #1973 (worktree scope) and #4410 (clone-local opt-in); this request is specifically an ephemeral, session-expiring override that leaves persistent policy untouched.

title: [Automated provider defect] bug(sync): gentle-ai.exe missing from go/bin after 'sync' reports success (Windows)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] Searched existing issues (open + closed) before filing.
- [x] Understand PRs are rejected without `status:approved` on the linked issue.

### Environment

- OS: Windows 10, Git Bash (MSYS) as the shell.
- Install method: `go install` under the user's `go/bin`, which is on `PATH`.
- Agent: `claude-code`.
- Installed build/version: could not be determined post-incident — the binary that would report `--version` is the artifact that went missing.

### Bug Description

Mid-way through a native review lifecycle (several successful `gentle-ai review status/start/capture-result` calls in the same session), `review status --next-transition` returned a `stop` transition with `reason_code: "managed_assets_outdated"` and a `continuation` naming `gentle-ai sync --agent claude-code` as the recovery command.

Running that exact sync command reported full success:

```
gentle-ai sync — managed sync executed
Agents synced: claude-code
Managed components synced: persona, sdd, engram, context7, gga, skills
Sync actions executed: 4 files changed
  - <user home>\.claude\CLAUDE.md
  - <user home>\.claude\settings.json
  - <user home>\.claude.json
  - <user home>\AppData\Roaming\gga\config
```

Immediately afterward, every subsequent `gentle-ai` invocation failed:

- Bare `gentle-ai <cmd>` (relying on `PATH`) → `command not found` (exit 127).
- Fully-qualified Windows path (`"C:\...\go\bin\gentle-ai.exe" <cmd>`) → `No such file or directory` (exit 127).

Inspecting the install directory (still correctly present on `PATH`) showed the expected `gentle-ai.exe` absent; only `gentle-ai.exe~` remained (~26.5 MB, executable bit set, mtime predating the session — consistent with `os.Rename` preserving the original file's mtime when a live binary is renamed aside).

### Expected vs Actual

- Expected: `sync` either leaves a working `gentle-ai.exe` in place (atomic self-replace that actually completes), or reports the replacement failure instead of "managed sync executed" success.
- Actual: `sync` reports unqualified success, but the CLI it is part of is left non-functional — no `gentle-ai.exe`, only a renamed-aside `.exe~`.

### Impact / preserved state

This left an in-flight native review lineage stuck: the review had already reached `state: "approved"` with a pending `acknowledge-approved` step (lineage id, expected-revision, and a one-time token already issued), but that acknowledgement command could not be run because the CLI itself was gone. No further `gentle-ai` operations (including recovery ones) were possible until the binary is restored some other way. Lineage id, revision, and token were preserved client-side but are not included here since they're single-use, session-scoped, and irreversible if disclosed alongside instructions to use them.

### Bounded attempts

- Bare `gentle-ai <cmd>` — fails (exit 127).
- Fully-qualified absolute path invocation — fails identically (exit 127).
- Confirmed `go/bin` is still listed on `PATH` (checked via `which`/`PATH` inspection).
- Confirmed no other `gentle-ai.exe`-named file exists elsewhere under that same directory — only the `.exe~`.

### Related issues (not duplicates)

- #2216 — binary installs rename without `fsync` and can corrupt/revert on crash, but its own text scopes the **self-update** path to Linux/macOS only (`Download` explicitly refuses Windows). This occurrence is on Windows and was triggered by `sync`, not `upgrade`/self-update, so the causal site is likely different even if the symptom class (unsynced rename leaving a broken binary) rhymes.
- #3774 — Windows atomic-rename denial during install/sync aborting the pipeline, but scoped to the `skills` component leaving empty directories, not the binary itself, and that report describes the pipeline *aborting* rather than reporting success.

This looks like a related-but-distinct causal path: the **binary component's own atomic replace**, on Windows, during `gentle-ai sync` specifically (not `upgrade`), silently leaves the binary missing while the rest of the sync still reports full success.

title: Windows Full Suite: telemetry state lock intermittently loses a concurrent counter update (TestIncrementSyncsConcurrentDoesNotLoseUpdates)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

`TestIncrementSyncsConcurrentDoesNotLoseUpdates` in `internal/telemetry/counters_test.go` intermittently loses one of twenty concurrent counter increments on the `windows-latest` runner. The test exists precisely to guard this (`// Guards R4-state-lost-update`), and its comment states the intent that each goroutine "opens its own lock fd, so this exercises real flock/LockFileEx contention, not an in-process mutex". A lost update therefore means the exclusive file lock did not provide mutual exclusion on that run.

This is a product-side defect in the Windows telemetry state lock, not a test defect. The test is well formed: twenty goroutines each call `IncrementSyncs(home)`, `wg.Wait()` joins all of them, and only then is the state loaded and asserted.

Observed intermittency, which is what makes this a race rather than a deterministic break:

| Head | Windows Full Suite run | `internal/telemetry` |
|---|---|---|
| `bc4b36e5` | `35681974704` (push) | ok |
| `bc4b36e5` | `35683674455` (schedule) | ok |
| `0b335e43` | `35698925392` (first attempt) | **FAIL** |
| `0b335e43` | `35698925392` (`gh run rerun --failed`) | ok |

The four commits between the green head `bc4b36e5` and the failing head `0b335e43` are all documentation-only (PR #4871), so they cannot have introduced this.

The `Windows Full Suite` shard invokes `go test <packages> -count=1 -timeout=30m` with **no `-race`**, so the race detector never observes this path on any platform.

Suspect area, stated as a hypothesis to check and not as a confirmed root cause: `internal/telemetry/state_lock_windows.go` calls `windows.LockFileEx(windows.Handle(f.Fd()), windows.LOCKFILE_EXCLUSIVE_LOCK, 0, ^uint32(0), ^uint32(0), overlapped)` with `overlapped := new(windows.Overlapped)`. Go's `os` package opens files with `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED` on Windows, and for an overlapped handle whose `OVERLAPPED.hEvent` is nil a lock that cannot be granted immediately is documented to return `FALSE` with `ERROR_IO_PENDING` rather than blocking, requiring a `GetOverlappedResult` wait. Whether that is what happens here, or whether the lost update comes from elsewhere in the lock/`EnsureState`/`Save` sequence, needs to be established with the race detector and a targeted Windows repro.

Impact is bounded: `IncrementCounter` documents that "callers treat a returned error as non-fatal: recording telemetry must never fail the operation that triggered it", so no user-facing operation breaks. The consequence is silently undercounted adoption and review-outcome telemetry on Windows hosts that run concurrent `gentle-ai sync` or review activity.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the `Windows Full Suite` run `35698925392`, job `Windows Full Suite (rest)`, job id `106652040477`.
2. Observe the single failing test and its count.
3. Rerun the failed jobs on the identical head with `gh run rerun 35698925392 --failed`; the shard goes green, which is the intermittency evidence.
4. To reproduce deliberately, run the test repeatedly on Windows and under the race detector:

```bash
go test ./internal/telemetry -run TestIncrementSyncsConcurrentDoesNotLoseUpdates -count=200
go test -race ./internal/telemetry -run TestIncrementSyncsConcurrentDoesNotLoseUpdates -count=50
```

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Twenty concurrent `IncrementSyncs` calls against the same home always produce `Counters.Syncs == 20` on every platform, deterministically, because `Update` holds an exclusive state lock across the load-mutate-save sequence.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

On `windows-latest` the count intermittently lands one short:

```
--- FAIL: TestIncrementSyncsConcurrentDoesNotLoseUpdates (1.16s)
    counters_test.go:70: Counters.Syncs = 19, want 20
FAIL	github.com/gentleman-programming/gentle-ai/v3/internal/telemetry	11.317s
```

No goroutine reported an error from `IncrementSyncs`, so the lost increment did not surface as a failed lock acquisition to the caller.

Because `Windows Full Suite` is part of the release gate, this intermittently blocks releases on heads that changed nothing relevant. It did so on `0b335e43`, whose only delta from the previously green head was documentation.

### Gentle AI Version

main at 0b335e43 (tagged v3.5.0)

### Operating System

Windows

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
Windows Full Suite (rest)	Run shard	2026-09-22T07:30:18.2607807Z --- FAIL: TestIncrementSyncsConcurrentDoesNotLoseUpdates (1.16s)
Windows Full Suite (rest)	Run shard	2026-09-22T07:30:18.2609498Z     counters_test.go:70: Counters.Syncs = 19, want 20
Windows Full Suite (rest)	Run shard	2026-09-22T07:30:18.2610428Z FAIL	github.com/gentleman-programming/gentle-ai/v3/internal/telemetry	11.317s
```

### Additional Context

AI Agent / Client is answered "Other" and Affected Area "Other" because this was found by inspecting CI runs, not by using `gga` with an interactive AI client, and `internal/telemetry` maps to none of the declared areas.

Found while clearing the v3.5.0 release gate. Two related but distinct follow-ups are worth considering separately from the fix itself:

1. No shard of `Windows Full Suite` runs with `-race`, so this class of defect is invisible to the race detector on the platform where it manifests. Adding `-race` to at least the `rest` shard would surface it deterministically instead of as a rare lost update.
2. Because this lane is part of the release gate but fails intermittently on unrelated heads, the release procedure currently needs a `gh run rerun --failed` to proceed. That is the documented flake path, but a genuine product race should not be living in the flake lane.

title: [Automated provider defect] bug(opencode): review-reliability lens yields no capturable result on 3.4.0 — possible regression of #3477 / #4545
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I searched open and closed issues for the exact failure shape and observable mechanism.
- [x] I understand PRs require a linked issue carrying maintainer approval.

### Regression of
- Canonical/equivalent: **#3477** (closed, `COMPLETED`) — `bug(opencode): Reliability transport hits completion safety bound and reoffers the same slot`.
- Associated fix: **#4545** `fix(review): classify OpenCode reviewer task outcomes explicitly` (merged).
- The installed build **demonstrably contains** #4545: the failure code `opencode_task_output_empty` only exists after it, and it is emitted here. Reproduction therefore happens on a build proven to contain that fix.

### Bug Description
On Gentle AI `3.4.0` with OpenCode, contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, one selected lens — **`review-reliability`** — never yields a capturable reviewer result, while sibling lenses of the *same* frozen candidate are captured and admitted normally. The lineage stays `reviewing` on `reviewer_results_required`, reoffering the identical bound slot with no typed, actionable transition.

This is the same observable as #3477, unfixed on a build that contains #4545. Observable behavior only; no root cause is asserted.

### Environment
- Gentle AI: `3.4.0`
- Client: OpenCode `1.18.31` (plugin `opencode-review-transport.ts`)
- OS / architecture: Linux / x86_64
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`
- Reviewer model on the failing agent: `deepseek/deepseek-flash`; also attempted with `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` — identical outcome

### Failure envelopes observed
```text
opencode_task_output_empty: the reviewer Task completed without producing a result
```
```text
opencode_reviewer_result_refused: OpenCode Task transport did not produce a capturable reviewer result; run 'gentle-ai review status --cwd <repo> --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --next-transition' before retrying
```

### Bounded attempts and outcomes
- Candidate A — four-lens review, lineage `review-80c664cf6f4c0fef`, target `sha256:077348f9a9ea4fdff5d13714ba7adfcce9330c5c3a86f52ba7e05ea0eee91929`:
  - `review-risk`, `review-resilience`, `review-readability` → captured and admitted (`admission_decision: completed`).
  - `review-reliability` (order 3) → **5 consecutive failures**, each preceded by a fresh exact-lineage STATUS confirming the same slot, revision, context, subject, lens and order were reoffered.
- Candidate B — medium tier, whose *only* selected lens is `review-reliability`, lineage `review-b78579119b6db3bb`, target `sha256:b575ceb7b9dd64592a89ae8188405c68f5d54788eff53d7130aec06c7af9caf7`:
  - **3 consecutive failures** on the single lens, so the review cannot reach an admitted closure at all.
- Total: **9/9 failures** for this lens across two candidates, two models, and after restarting the client.
- Control: a different candidate of the same session (lineage `review-e80b3038073d59c5`) completed a four-lens review to `approved` and burnt its authority on exact acknowledgement — so the transport is not broken for every lens.

### Expected behavior
Each selected lens slot should produce one schema-valid result that native capture can admit, or a typed, actionable transition that preserves authority without indefinitely reoffering a slot that cannot complete (the clause already stated in #3477).

### Actual behavior
`review-reliability` repeatedly completes with no capturable result; the frozen candidate is preserved and the identical slot is reoffered. For medium-tier candidates where this lens is the only selected lens, review is impossible.

### Minimal reproduction
1. Enable receipt-driven review (`gentle-ai review mode enable`), OpenCode, contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`.
2. Start a review whose selected lenses include `review-reliability` (four-lens candidate, or a medium candidate where it is the sole lens).
3. Satisfy the provider-issued collect transition for that slot.
4. Observe `opencode_task_output_empty` / `opencode_reviewer_result_refused` while sibling lenses on the same candidate are admitted.
5. Re-query exact-lineage STATUS: the identical bound slot is reoffered.

### Mutation outcome
No mutation reached GitHub on the reporter's side, and no destructive operation was performed. Reviewer launches only; no commit, push, bypass, store reset, abandonment, or new lineage.

### Preserved state
- Candidate A: `reviewing`, three admitted lens artifacts, `review-reliability` missing; no receipt, no acknowledgement.
- Candidate B: `reviewing`, single lens missing; no receipt, no acknowledgement.
- Candidate bytes unchanged across every attempt; target identity stable.

### Privacy
This report excludes private repository and project names, usernames, hostnames, absolute paths, raw arguments, credentials, environment values, source code and diffs. Identifiers included are opaque lineage/target hashes only.

title: bug(review): worker refuses explicitly unreviewed candidate
body:
## Observed behavior
A bounded  task was given an exact candidate that the user explicitly left unreviewed after an audited abandonment. The worker acknowledged that disposition, then returned without executing its assigned test-only task.

## Expected behavior
When the user explicitly leaves the exact candidate unreviewed, the worker should follow ordinary policy and execute its scoped task without attempting or requiring native review.

## Evidence
- RDD was enabled.
- The user explicitly requested ordinary continuation after abandoning the lineage.
- The worker stated it would not invoke review, but performed no requested work.
- No source, configuration, dependency, or delivery mutation occurred from the worker invocation.

## Reproduction
1. Start an RDD candidate.
2. Explicitly abandon it with an operator disposition.
3. Instruct a bounded worker that the exact candidate is intentionally unreviewed and ask it to perform a scoped task.
4. Observe the worker return only the review disposition rather than execute the task.

title: fix(telemetry): custom endpoint subpath is stripped when resolving runtime-events path
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

When configuring a custom self-hosted telemetry collector via `GENTLE_AI_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT` that resides behind a reverse proxy or API gateway with a subpath (e.g. `https://example.com/telemetry-api/v1/events`), `SendRuntimeWithDeliveryID` strips the subpath prefix when resolving the runtime events URL:

```go
endpoint, err := url.Parse(Endpoint(getenv))
if err != nil || ... {
    return "discarded"
}
endpoint.Path = "/v1/runtime-events"
```

Assigning `endpoint.Path = "/v1/runtime-events"` unconditionally overwrites `endpoint.Path`, changing `https://example.com/telemetry-api/v1/events` to `https://example.com/v1/runtime-events`. This results in HTTP 404 errors for self-hosted instances that rely on URL prefixes/path routing.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Set `GENTLE_AI_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT` to an HTTPS endpoint with a path prefix:
   `export GENTLE_AI_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT="https://proxy.internal.corp/gateway/v1/events"`
2. Trigger runtime telemetry (e.g. via an agent run using OpenCode/Claude Code/Pi).
3. Observe the outbound request URL target: it hits `https://proxy.internal.corp/v1/runtime-events` instead of `https://proxy.internal.corp/gateway/v1/runtime-events`.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The endpoint resolution should preserve existing path prefixes/base paths, transforming:
- `https://proxy.internal.corp/gateway/v1/events` -> `https://proxy.internal.corp/gateway/v1/runtime-events`
- `https://telemetry.gentlemanprogramming.com/v1/events` -> `https://telemetry.gentlemanprogramming.com/v1/runtime-events`

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The existing subpath prefix is discarded, causing requests to hit the root `\/v1\/runtime-events` and fail on path-based reverse proxies.

### 🖥️ Environment

- **Gentle AI Version:** 3.4.0
- **Operating System:** Linux
- **AI Agent / Client:** Other
- **Affected Area:** CLI (commands, flags)

### Additional Context

title: fix(telemetry): GENTLE_AI_TELEMETRY opt-out silently fails when value has whitespace
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

When setting `GENTLE_AI_TELEMETRY=0` to opt out of usage telemetry, any surrounding whitespace (e.g. `export GENTLE_AI_TELEMETRY=" 0"` or `"0 "`) causes the opt-out to silently fail, leaving telemetry enabled by default (`source: default`).

Other kill-switch variables like `DO_NOT_TRACK`, `CI`, and `GITHUB_ACTIONS` trim whitespace via `strings.TrimSpace(...)`, but `internal/telemetry/killswitch.go` uses strict string equality:
```go
if getenv("GENTLE_AI_TELEMETRY") == "0" {
    return Decision{Enabled: false, Source: SourceEnvOptOut}
}
```

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. In a shell, export the opt-out variable with whitespace: `export GENTLE_AI_TELEMETRY=" 0 "`
2. Check telemetry status: `gentle-ai telemetry status`
3. Observe that telemetry reports enabled (`telemetry: enabled (source: default)`) instead of disabled (`source: GENTLE_AI_TELEMETRY`).

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The `GENTLE_AI_TELEMETRY` value should be trimmed with `strings.TrimSpace`, recognizing `" 0 "` as a valid opt-out, matching the behavior of `DO_NOT_TRACK`.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Telemetry remains enabled because the strict comparison `== "0"` fails against `" 0 "`.

### 🖥️ Environment

- **Gentle AI Version:** 3.4.0
- **Operating System:** Linux
- **AI Agent / Client:** Other
- **Affected Area:** CLI (commands, flags)

### Additional Context

A fix with unit tests is already implemented locally: wrapping `getenv("GENTLE_AI_TELEMETRY")` with `strings.TrimSpace(...)` in `internal/telemetry/killswitch.go`.
