title: bug(gga): a provider failure exits 0, so the pre-commit gate passes commits it never reviewed (v2.10.1)
body:
## Summary

`gga run` exits `0` when the configured provider fails, so the pre-commit hook `gga run || exit 1` commits code that was never reviewed. A gate that reports success without a verdict is worse than no gate, because it advertises coverage that does not exist.

## Environment

- GGA: `gga v2.10.1`
- Host: Debian 13, root, no TTY on the review path
- Providers tried: `opencode:opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `opencode:opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro`, `codex`
- `.gga`: `FILE_PATTERNS="*.sh,*.ps1,*.mjs,*.js"`, `TIMEOUT="900"`, `STRICT_MODE="false"`

## Observed behaviour

Reproduced in a scratch repository that contains only a copy of `.gga`, a copy of the rules file, and one staged shell file, so nothing about the surrounding project is involved. `gga run` was executed directly and its exit code captured after the pipeline, not through `tail`.

| Provider | Output | `gga run` exit |
|---|---|---|
| `opencode:opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | `❌ Provider execution failed (exit code: 1)` then `UnknownError: Unexpected server error. Check server logs for details.` (`ref: err_6ab911f9`) | **0** |
| `opencode:opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro` | same shape, `ref: err_d23e34f6` | **0** |
| `codex` | `❌ Provider execution failed (exit code: 1)`, `(provider returned no output)` | **0** |

The same thing happens on a real pre-commit path. With the hook installed as it ships:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ======== GGA START ========
gga run || exit 1
# ======== GGA END ========
```

several commits in a real repository succeeded while the hook printed `Provider execution failed` / `Unexpected server error` (`ref: err_f96ef0a5`, `ref: err_460f50a3`). No review verdict was produced for any of them, and nothing in the commit output says so.

## Expected behaviour

`gga run` should exit non-zero whenever it did not produce a review verdict, so that the shipped hook actually gates. At minimum:

1. A provider execution failure is a failure: exit non-zero, as it already does for a timeout.
2. A run that produces no verdict is distinguishable from a run that produced an approving verdict, in the exit code and not only in prose.

## Why this is not #2625

#2625 reports a provider timeout on the pre-commit review and states "Hook exited non-zero and the commit did not happen". That is the behaviour a gate should have. This issue is the opposite outcome from the same code path: the provider fails fast with an error rather than hanging, and the hook exits `0`, so the commit proceeds unreviewed. Both are silent-failure complaints, but only one of them blocks.

## Why this is not #3019

#3019 reported the OpenCode provider failing with the generic `Unexpected server error` and is closed. The same error string reproduces here on v2.10.1, for both `deepseek-v4.1-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro`, so if the fix was provider-side it does not hold for these two model ids. That is the trigger; this issue is about the exit status the trigger produces.

## Impact

Silent loss of the review gate. Any repository that installs the hook believes commits are reviewed, and on this host none of them were. The only signal is a line of prose on stdout, which `|| exit 1` ignores.

## Minimal repro shape

1. Create an empty git repository and copy a valid `.gga` into it, with a provider that will fail.
2. Stage one file matching `FILE_PATTERNS`.
3. Run `gga run; echo $?`.
4. Observe the provider error on stdout and exit status `0`.

title: bug(review): candidate-view materializes a full 5.2 GB worktree copy for a 16-path candidate, times out at a 10s git add budget, and leaks the partial view as candidate-view-invalid (3.4.0)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

On a large repository, `candidate-view` materializes a **full copy of the worktree as a Git worktree**, regardless of how small the candidate is. For a 16-path candidate this writes ~260,000 files and 5.2 GB.

The materialization does not finish within its own budget. Two consequences, both observed deterministically:

1. START fails with a `candidate-view` Git `add` timeout of **10000 ms**, while the repository's own full scan costs ~22 s. The budget is unsatisfiable by construction, not under load.
2. When it fails, the partial view is **left behind on disk** and the next START rejects it with `candidate-view-invalid`. Two consecutive attempts produced views with **different file counts** (262,852 and 259,383), neither containing a `.git` entry, and `git worktree list` marks them `prunable`. So `candidate-view-invalid` here is not inherited corruption — it is the incomplete materialization being rejected.

Every attempt costs 5.2 GB that is never reclaimed. With 37 GiB free, that is about seven attempts before the volume fills.

This is the same root cause as #4850 seen one phase later: work proportional to the repository instead of to the candidate. #4850 covers the 25 s `pre_native` budget; this issue covers the materialization step and the disk leak.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a repository with a large worktree (here: 297,509 tracked files, ~196k source files, APFS on local SSD, macOS).
2. Commit a small candidate — 16 files, 800 changed lines.
3. Run preflight: `review status` with `--committed-only=true --base-ref=<sha>`. It returns `action: start`, `next_transition.kind: execute`, `reason_code: fresh_target_ready`.
4. Run the offered START.
5. Observe the `candidate-view` failure, then inspect `.git/gentle-ai/candidate-views/`.
6. Re-run START. It now fails with `candidate-view-invalid`.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The candidate view should be scoped to the candidate's paths, or be materialized by a mechanism whose cost does not scale with the repository. A failed materialization should be cleaned up rather than left as a 5.2 GB orphan that poisons the next attempt.

Where the index is already resolved, the narrow Git operation would suffice: `git add -u` costs **0.22 s** in this repository against **22 s** for `git add -A` — a factor of ~100.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

```
outcome:          native-operation-failed
diagnostics.code: candidate-view timeout / candidate-view-invalid
git_subcommand:   add
timeout_ms:       10000
lineage_created:  false
mutation_performed: false
next_action:      resolve-native-operation-failure
```

Measurements on this repository:

| Operation | Cost |
|---|---:|
| `git status --porcelain` | 0.70 s |
| `git add -u` (tracked only) | 0.22 s |
| `git add -A` (full worktree scan) | 22.0 s |
| `pre_native` aggregate budget | 25 s |
| `candidate-view` Git `add` budget | 10 s |
| One candidate view on disk | 5.2 GB / ~260k files |
| `rm -rf` of one view | 1m54s |

Ruled out with evidence: default model resolution (the phase is pure Git/FS), harness (Pi and Claude Code behave identically), provider 429s (reproduced with the provider healthy), cold FS cache (`git status` is 0.7 s), Spotlight (0.2 % CPU), and accumulated state (deleting the 5.2 GB view changed nothing — the next START failed the same way and immediately created a new 5.2 GB view).

Side effect worth noting: creating the view registers a Git worktree, which makes Git LFS reinstall its four hooks into the repository's configured `core.hooksPath`. Those appear as untracked files in the user's working tree after every attempt.

### Gentle AI Version

3.4.0

### Operating System

macOS

### AI Agent / Client

Pi

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
$ git worktree list
/path/to/repo                                                  7bda5e4aad3e [feat/…]
/path/to/repo/.git/gentle-ai/candidate-views/4c8c9f0f-…        7bda5e4aad3e (detached HEAD) prunable

$ ls -a .git/gentle-ai/candidate-views/4c8c9f0f-…/
.  ..  pkg  pnpm-workspace.yaml          # no .git entry

$ du -sh .git/gentle-ai/*
5.2G    candidate-views
932K    sdd-runtime
164K    review-transactions
 72K    rejected-results
```

title: bug(review): selectorless STATUS succeeds at 21s but the intended-untracked selection path exhausts a fixed 25s pre_native budget on a ~297k-file repository (3.4.0 stable)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I searched open and closed issues for an equivalent report. The closest reports in this class were compared and excluded on evidence, not title similarity — see "Why this is not a duplicate" below.
- [x] This automated provider-defect report contains privacy-scrubbed diagnostics only.

### Bug Description

On a very large repository (~297k tracked files), the selectorless negotiated preflight **succeeds** — but the `intended_untracked_selection` path that its own `next_transition` requires **always fails**, exhausting an aggregate time budget in `pre_native` at a hard **25.00 s**.

The two invocations run against the identical frozen candidate, seconds apart:

| Invocation | Wall time | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Selectorless STATUS `--next-transition` | 20.43 s / 21.05 s / 20.83 s | **exit 0**, full `status/v9`, `action: start` |
| STATUS satisfying the untracked selection | **25.00 s / 25.00 s** | `operation_timeout`, `phase: pre_native` |

Two consecutive failing runs landing on `real 25.00` to the centisecond indicate a fixed deadline being hit, not variable latency. The successful path consumes **21 s of that same budget — roughly 84 %** — purely to freeze the candidate. The selection path appears to redo that work and cross the line.

**The failure is not proportional to the untracked selection.** Reducing the selection from four untracked paths to **a single path** reproduces the identical envelope at the identical 25.00 s. The trigger is the code path, not the amount of work the operator asked for.

This reports observed evidence only; the root cause is unconfirmed. The hypothesis that the selection path re-freezes the candidate rather than reusing the inventory the preceding STATUS already computed is inference, not verified.

### Environment

- Gentle AI: `3.4.0` (stable channel — build string carries neither `-rc.` nor `-main.`)
- Client: Claude Code
- OS / architecture: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0), arm64
- Filesystem: **local APFS on internal NVMe** — low latency, which distinguishes this from the high-latency-filesystem class
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, agent binding `claude-code`
- Projection: `workspace`
- Repository shape: **single worktree**, ~297k tracked files, no linked worktrees, no foreign untracked inventory
- Candidate: 12 tracked modified paths + 4 untracked paths, no commits of its own on the branch
- Review authority store: empty (no lineage exists; every invocation reported `mutation_outcome: not_started`)

### Evidence

Selectorless STATUS returns a complete, correct envelope — the candidate freezes fine, and the untracked inventory is computed and accurate (all four eligible paths are exactly the four real untracked files):

```
schema:        gentle-ai.review-integration.status/v9
action:        start
applicability: unrelated
projection:    workspace (base_tree + candidate_tree both resolved)
next_transition.kind:        collect
next_transition.reason_code: intended_untracked_selection_required
```

Satisfying that collect step — using the first-class flags documented by `gentle-ai review status --help` (`--untracked-scope=select`, `--intended-untracked=<path>`, `--expected-untracked-inventory=<digest from the preceding STATUS>`) — returns:

```
schema:              gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2
operation:           review.status
phase:               pre_native
code:                operation_timeout
message:             The negotiated review operation exceeded its aggregate time budget.
cause:               context deadline exceeded
mutation_outcome:    not_started
retry_safe:          false
next_action:         stop
```

`retry_safe: false` and `next_action: stop` were honored — the pairs above are a deliberate two-run measurement, not a retry loop.

**No configuration escape exists.** The installed binary exposes no environment variable matching `GENTLE_AI_*(TIMEOUT|BUDGET|DEADLINE)`, so the 25 s budget cannot be raised by the operator.

### Minimal Reproduction

1. Use a repository with a very large tracked-file count (~300k) on a local low-latency filesystem, with review mode enabled and an empty authority store.
2. Produce a candidate that contains **at least one untracked file** alongside tracked modifications.
3. Run the selectorless preflight: `gentle-ai review status --cwd <repo> --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --agent claude-code --next-transition`. Observe success in ~21 s and a `collect` transition with `reason_code: intended_untracked_selection_required`.
4. Satisfy that transition by supplying the untracked selection.
5. Observe `operation_timeout` in `pre_native` at 25.00 s, regardless of whether one path or four are selected.

### Why this is not a duplicate

- **#4208** (selectorless preflight STATUS times out `pre_native` on its first call, empty authority store): the observable is the opposite here. With an equally empty store, the selectorless preflight **succeeds** and returns a complete `status/v9`. Only the subsequent selection path fails.
- **#4441** (START exhausts the 120 s deadline on a 16-path candidate, high-latency filesystem): different operation (`review start` in `native_running`, not STATUS in `pre_native`), different budget (120 s vs 25 s), and the distinguishing trigger there — per-operation I/O latency — is absent here: this filesystem is local NVMe APFS. Its closing discussion of per-path subprocess amplification may well name the same underlying cost, which is why the 21 s baseline is reported above as evidence.
- **#4655** (bound STATUS times out `pre_native` after a granted START, 3-path candidate): that failure occurs **after** a consent-granted START, against an existing lineage. Here no lineage exists and START is never reached.
- **#4617** (cross-worktree untracked inventory blocks a medium review + `pre_native` status timeout): its trigger is multiple linked worktrees sharing one Git common dir, where the advertised inventory belongs to a foreign worktree. This repository has a **single** worktree and the advertised inventory is correct. Its symptom 1 also has the selectorless STATUS failing, which does not happen here.
- The `intended-untracked` schema-rejection family (**#4311**, #4370, #4488) reports `invalid_request` on the JSON selection. That is a separate defect, encountered here as well and reported as an occurrence on #4311; this report is about the **timeout**, which is reached through the documented first-class flags and therefore does not depend on that schema at all.

What no existing report contains is the differential measurement: the same frozen candidate, seconds apart, succeeding at 21 s and failing at a fixed 25.00 s, with the failure independent of the selection size.

### Expected Behavior

Having successfully frozen the candidate and computed the untracked inventory in the preceding call, satisfying the `collect` transition it advertised should advance the lifecycle — not exhaust a budget that the freeze alone already consumed 84 % of.

### Actual Behavior

The lifecycle is unreachable. The preflight advertises a `collect` transition that cannot be satisfied within the budget, and the failure envelope says `next_action: stop`, so there is no legal continuation. Every candidate in this repository that contains a new file is therefore unreviewable, with no operator-side configuration to work around it.

title: bug(community-tool): install fails on a Pi CodeGraph MCP entry that is the expected package and answers MCP
body:
### Summary

`gentle-ai install` fails two steps and reports `pipeline completed with errors` because it refuses to manage a Pi CodeGraph MCP entry that is **already correct and already working**. The refusal is reasonable in intent — do not clobber a user's entry — but it is reported as a step failure, which makes the whole install look broken and, combined with #4509, leaves later steps pending.

### Observed

```
✗ community-tool:codegraph
✗ community-tool:pi-codegraph-reconcile

FAILED: community-tool:pi-codegraph-reconcile — misconfigured Pi CodeGraph MCP entry at "<pi mcp config>"
FAILED: community-tool:codegraph — install community tool "codegraph": misconfigured Pi CodeGraph MCP entry at "<pi mcp config>"
pipeline completed with errors
```

The string in the binary is `misconfigured Pi CodeGraph MCP entry at %q; Gentle AI will not overwrite it`.

### Why this looks wrong

The entry it calls misconfigured is the expected package and it works:

- The configured command resolves through a global npm install to `@colbymchenry/codegraph/npm-shim.js`, which is the same package the binary references as `@colbymchenry/codegraph@latest`.
- A real MCP handshake against that exact command succeeds:

```
$ printf '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize",...}' | <configured command> serve --mcp
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{"tools":{}},
 "serverInfo":{"name":"codegraph","version":"1.4.1"},...}}
```

So the package is right and the server answers. The only thing that differs from what Gentle AI writes appears to be the **shape**: an absolute path to the npm shim rather than the managed form.

### Impact

1. The install pipeline reports failure for a non-failure.
2. A user reasonably concludes the environment did not install. In this case `gentle-ai doctor` reported `11 passed, 0 failed, 0 warnings, healthy` with 4 agents installed, while the installer said it errored.
3. Combined with #4509, the steps after the failure stay pending and never run.
4. There is no CLI flag for community tools (`--component` rejects `codegraph`), so recovering requires removing the entry by hand and re-running the interactive TUI.

### Expected

When the configured entry resolves to the expected CodeGraph package and answers an MCP initialize, treat it as already satisfied: skip with an informational note rather than failing the step. Reserve the hard failure for entries that genuinely do not resolve or do not answer.

### Environment

- Gentle AI 3.4.0 (stable), macOS arm64
- Pi installed and configured; CodeGraph installed globally via npm and exposed on PATH through a symlink
- Verified: removing the entry and running `gentle-ai sync` does not restore it, because this is an install-time community tool rather than a sync-managed asset

### Related

- #4509 — pipeline stalls with pending steps after a step fails

title: bug(pi): pi-host-relay reviewer completion fails deterministically with JSON parse error on one lens while sibling lens captures succeed (3.4.0)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

In an ordinary review lineage on contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, the `gentle_review_capture` host relay (`transport: pi_host_relay`, `captureOperation: review.capture-result`, result schema `https://gentle-ai.dev/schema/review/reviewer/v1`) fails deterministically for one lens while three sibling lenses capture successfully in the same session.

The failure envelope is a transport failure, but the reason shows the reviewer ran and produced output that failed JSON parsing:

```
outcome: pi-host-relay-transport-failure
failure.kind: pi-failed
failure.stage: pi
failure.exit_code: null
failure.timed_out: false
failure.elapsed_ms: ~58000-65000 (timeout_ms 939448)
mutation_performed: false
reason: Reviewer completion failed for review-reliability: Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1 (line 1 column 2)
```

Observable sequence (single session, high tier, 4 lenses):

1. Group capture (`gentle_review_capture_group`, 4 materialize slots) failed on `review-risk` with the same JSON parse error; 0 reviewers prepared, 0 submitted.
2. After a fresh STATUS, single-slot captures succeeded: `review-risk` (order 0), `review-resilience` (order 1), `review-reliability`... correction: `review-readability` (order 2) — each admitted as `native-reviewer-result-captured` with non-empty result bytes (1272 / 5629 / 2846 bytes).
3. `review-reliability` (order 3) then failed with the identical parse error on 3 consecutive attempts, each following a fresh bound STATUS that reoffered the exact same slot. Every attempt ran ~60 s before failing, so the reviewer model actually executed and produced a completion each time.

So the defect is not a dead subprocess (different from #4337) and not empty stdout `pi-empty-output` (different from #4611): the relayed reviewer completion is produced but the relay cannot parse it as JSON for this lens, deterministically, while sibling lenses parse fine. Because the final reviewer lens owns closure, the lineage cannot reach acknowledgement.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. START an ordinary workspace-projection lineage (9 paths, high tier, correction budget 200, four lenses).
2. Capture lenses one by one: three succeed, the fourth (`review-reliability`) fails with the parse error above.
3. Call bound STATUS; it reoffers the same slot; resubmit the exact reoffered binding with the run acknowledged; the same parse error reproduces (3/3).

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Either the reviewer completion is parsed/admitted like the sibling lenses, or the failure envelope distinguishes a reviewer-completion parse failure from a subprocess transport failure (typed reason, e.g. a parse-class outcome instead of `pi-failed`/`stage: pi`), ideally with a bounded diagnostic of where parsing failed, so callers can distinguish transient relay death from deterministic output-format defects.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The deterministic parse failure is reported as a generic `pi-host-relay-transport-failure` with `kind: pi-failed`, `stage: pi`, and no diagnostic; retries are identical, and the slot stays pending without a way to close the lineage.

### Gentle AI Version

3.4.0 (stable channel; managed bundle under gentle-pi)

### Operating System

macOS (arm64)

### AI Agent / Client

pi coding agent host relay

### 📋 Affected Area

review capture (pi host relay)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

Full failure envelopes preserved session-side; omitted here to keep the report free of repository-identifying content. Safe opaque identifiers available on request: lineage id and artifact subject hashes of the three admitted results.

### Additional Context

Related: #4337 (transport failure leaves slot pending without retry semantics — same outer envelope, but there the subprocess dies with no output), #4611 (pi-empty-output with models.json providers — closed). This report adds the distinct causal class: reviewer completion produced but unparseable, deterministic per lens.

title: bug(engram): Claude Code MCP entry is written without "type": "stdio" and, on Linuxbrew, with a PATH-dependent command
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

When registering Engram's MCP server for Claude Code, Gentle AI writes the `mcpServers.engram` entry in `~/.claude.json` through a direct JSON merge. The resulting shape is:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "engram": { "command": "engram", "args": ["mcp", "--tools=agent"] } } }
```

Two properties of that shape do not match the contract that `engram` 2.0.0 enforces on the **same key** in the **same file**:

1. **It omits `"type": "stdio"`.** `engram` requires that field explicitly and treats any other shape as a conflict it refuses to overwrite (fail-closed):
   - `internal/setup/setup.go`, `inspectClaudeCodeUserMCP` (~L1158): `if server.Type == "stdio" && server.Command == command && slices.Equal(server.Args, []string{"mcp", "--tools=agent"})`
   - `EnsureClaudeCodeUserMCP` (~L1188) returns: *"claude Code MCP conflict at <path>: mcpServers.engram differs from Engram's expected stdio command; resolve it manually"*.

2. **The command is the bare `engram` name on Linuxbrew.** `isStableHomebrewEngramPath` (`internal/components/engram/inject.go`, L1028) only recognizes two paths, both macOS:

   ```go
   return (clean == "/opt/homebrew/bin/engram" || clean == "/usr/local/bin/engram") && isEngramCommand(clean)
   ```

   On a WSL2 + Ubuntu + Linuxbrew host (canonical prefix `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew`, binary `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/engram`) neither matches, so `preferredStableEngramCommand()` (L768) falls back to `return "engram"`. Verified with gentle-ai 3.4.1 (build `134409f6a9d5`): this is current behavior, not a legacy artifact — the writer either produces that bare command or preserves an existing one.

   This contradicts the stated purpose of that helper (to write a stable command that does not depend on PATH) and Engram's own contract, which documents that the durable Claude Code user MCP config *"must never persist a PATH-dependent command"* (`claudeCodeEngramCommand`, `engram/internal/setup/setup.go` ~L1451). It matters more on WSL, where the inherited PATH may not include the Linuxbrew prefix.

**Observable effect:** on every Claude Code session start, the Engram plugin's SessionStart hook runs `engram setup claude-code --mcp-only`, which exits 1 and prints a permanent warning; the registration is never repaired, even though the MCP server itself is connected and works. In other words, the self-healing path introduced by engram PR #959 is inert on these hosts.

**How the state is reached (context):** `injectClaudeUserConfig` (`internal/components/engram/inject.go` L581) skips its own write when the plugin is enabled (`claudeEngramPluginEnabled`, L621, reading `enabledPlugins["engram@engram"]` from `~/.claude/settings.json`), but it does **not** delete a pre-existing entry. An entry written while the plugin was disabled survives, and once the plugin is enabled the hook reports it as a conflict on every session.

Scope note: this is independent of the duplicate-registration defect fixed by engram PR #959 (which is resolved by updating the plugin package). It was found while investigating that issue and remains after updating the plugin to 0.1.3.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Linux (here: WSL2, Ubuntu 24.04.4) with Homebrew (Linuxbrew), Claude Code and the `engram` 2.0.0 binary installed, the `engram@engram` plugin **disabled**, and no pre-existing `mcpServers.engram` entry in `~/.claude.json`.
2. Run `gentle-ai install` (or `gentle-ai sync`) and inspect the entry that was written:

   ```json
   { "mcpServers": { "engram": { "command": "engram", "args": ["mcp", "--tools=agent"] } } }
   ```

   (no `"type"`, and on Linuxbrew the command is the bare name).
3. Enable the plugin: `claude plugin enable engram@engram` (0.1.3).
4. Open a Claude Code session. The SessionStart hook runs `engram setup claude-code --mcp-only`, which fails with exit 1 and prints the warning. The entry is left untouched and the warning repeats on every subsequent session.

Minimal, isolated verification of the shape mismatch, **without touching the real configuration** (`engram` honors `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`):

```shell
$ probe=$(mktemp -d)
$ printf '%s' '{"mcpServers":{"engram":{"command":"engram","args":["mcp","--tools=agent"]}}}' > "$probe/.claude.json"
$ CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="$probe" engram setup claude-code --mcp-only; echo "exit $?"
engram: claude Code MCP conflict at .../.claude.json: mcpServers.engram differs from Engram's expected stdio command; resolve it manually
exit 1

# The same entry with type + an absolute command is accepted idempotently:
$ printf '%s' '{"mcpServers":{"engram":{"type":"stdio","command":"/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/engram","args":["mcp","--tools=agent"]}}}' > "$probe/.claude.json"
$ CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="$probe" engram setup claude-code --mcp-only; echo "exit $?"
exit 0
```

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The entry Gentle AI writes for Engram's MCP server should be exactly one of:

- the shape the consuming component validates and produces: `"type": "stdio"` with an absolute command and `args: ["mcp", "--tools=agent"]`; or
- the shape produced by the supported Claude Code CLI, by delegating the registration to `claude mcp add --transport stdio --scope user engram -- <absolute-path> mcp --tools=agent`.

Either way, Engram's self-healing should end with exit 0 and no warning, and `isStableHomebrewEngramPath` should recognize the Homebrew prefix actually installed.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

- Gentle AI writes `mcpServers.engram` without `"type"` and, on Linuxbrew, with the PATH-dependent `"engram"` command.
- `engram setup claude-code --mcp-only` (run by the plugin's SessionStart hook on every session) exits 1 with the conflict message and does not modify the entry.
- The warning repeats on every session indefinitely while the MCP server is connected and working: `claude mcp get engram` → `Status: ✔ Connected`.
- There is no automatic repair path, and the message only says *"resolve it manually"*.

### Gentle AI Version

3.4.1 (build 134409f6a9d5)

### Operating System

Windows (WSL) — Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS on WSL2, kernel 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2, Linuxbrew at /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew

### AI Agent / Client

Claude Code 2.1.278

### 📋 Affected Area

Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
# Entry written by Gentle AI (Linuxbrew)
$ jq -c '.mcpServers.engram' ~/.claude.json
{"args":["mcp","--tools=agent"],"command":"engram"}

# Plugin SessionStart hook, on every session
$ engram setup claude-code --mcp-only
engram: claude Code MCP conflict at ~/.claude.json: mcpServers.engram differs from Engram's expected stdio command; resolve it manually
$ echo $?
1

# The server still works with the rejected shape
$ claude mcp get engram
engram:
  Scope: User config (available in all your projects)
  Status: ✔ Connected

# Plugin 0.1.3 registers no MCP server of its own (0.1.0 did; see related)
$ claude plugin details engram@engram
  MCP servers (0)

$ gentle-ai version
gentle-ai 3.4.1-0.20260921051030-134409f6a9d5
```

### Additional Context

Useful comparison: `engram` solves the same Homebrew problem prefix-agnostically, by locating the `/Cellar/engram/` marker in the path and deriving `<prefix>/bin/engram` (`stableHomebrewEngramCommand`, `engram/internal/setup/setup.go` ~L1468; that function's comment explicitly mentions both `/opt/homebrew` **and** `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew`). On the reporting host that derivation yields `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/engram`, which exists (a symlink to `Cellar/engram/2.0.0/bin/engram`). Gentle AI instead hardcodes two macOS paths.

Fix options (the decision belongs to the maintainer):

1. Add `"type": "stdio"` to the Claude Code overlay in `engramOverlayJSON`.
2. Derive the stable path with the `/Cellar/engram/` marker instead of comparing fixed prefixes, covering macOS and Linuxbrew with a single rule.
3. Delegate the registration to `claude mcp add --transport stdio --scope user`, which is what Engram itself does and guarantees the expected shape.

Related: gentle-ai #4532 (the inverse failure: `sync` skips `mcpServers.engram` when the enabled plugin declares no MCP server), gentle-ai #4188 / PR #4278 (origin of the plugin-detection guard); engram #933 / PR #959 (duplicate registration; origin of the single-owner registration contract), engram #1153 (follow-up regression from the same PR), engram #1323 (companion report on the consuming side: the entry is rejected while the server keeps working, and the self-healing path stays inert).

Environment: gentle-ai 3.4.1 (build 134409f6a9d5), engram 2.0.0 (Homebrew/Linuxbrew), plugin `engram@engram` 0.1.3, Claude Code 2.1.278 inside WSL2 (Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS).

title: bug(review 3.1.0): stop-hook START picks a --base-ref that is neither merge-base, default branch nor newest tag, offering a 1453-file candidate for an 81-file branch
body:
## Automated provider-defect report

### Environment

- Gentle AI: `3.1.0` (stable channel)
- Client: Claude Code
- OS/architecture: Windows x86_64 (MINGW64 shell)
- Review contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`

### Operation shape

A feature branch with four commits of real work, each one reviewed and
acknowledged **before** it was committed, through the ordinary flow: selectorless
STATUS with no `--base-ref`, the returned START, capture, acknowledge, burn. All
four receipts are terminal and their authority is burned.

After each of those commits, the stop hook reported an unreviewed candidate and
returned a START invocation carrying `--committed-only=true` and a `--base-ref`
that is **not** the branch point.

### Expected vs actual

Expected: the committed-only candidate the stop hook offers spans the branch's
own work — the commits between the branch point and `HEAD`.

Actual: the offered candidate spans roughly a month of already-merged upstream
history. Measured on the same tree, four times in one session:

| Stop-hook occurrence | Candidate offered | Real branch diff vs integration branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| after commit 1 | 1446 files / 246 606 lines | 10 files / 289 lines |
| after commit 2 | 1446 files / 246 704 lines | 12 files / 384 lines |
| after commit 3 | 1450 files / 247 412 lines | 68 files / 1153 lines |
| after commit 4 | 1453 files / 247 804 lines | 81 files / 1579 lines |

Every occurrence carried the **same** `--base-ref` commit. The risk evidence
attached to the consent envelope names files that are not in the branch at all
(a lockfile, CI workflow YAML, an auth spec, an unrelated DTO), which is the
clearest symptom: the candidate is not the branch's work.

### What the base-ref is not

The offered base is a commit roughly one month behind the branch point. It was
checked against every selector that could plausibly produce it:

- **Not the merge-base** with the integration branch. The correct branch point is
  a different commit, and the selectorless preflight (no `--base-ref`) computes a
  correct candidate from it in the very same tree.
- **Not the repository default branch.** The default branch here *is* the
  integration branch, so #4639 does not apply.
- **Not the last release tag.** The only tag in the repository points at a
  different commit, so the #4628 selector does not apply either.
- It is an ordinary merge commit, contained in 462 of the repository's 1090
  remote branches.

No root cause is claimed. Only the observation that the selector is neither
merge-base, nor default-branch head, nor newest tag.

### Reproduction

1. A repository with many long-lived remote branches (≈1000) whose default
   branch is the integration branch.
2. Branch off the integration branch and make a commit.
3. Review it through selectorless STATUS → START → capture → acknowledge, and let
   the authority burn.
4. Let the session end. The stop hook reports an unreviewed candidate whose START
   carries a `--base-ref` far behind the branch point.

Selectorless STATUS run by hand, with no `--base-ref`, returns a correct
candidate for the same tree — so the two paths disagree about the same state.

### Preserved state

No repository or authority state was mutated by any of the four occurrences. Each
consent envelope was relayed to the human, who answered `declined` every time;
each decline returned `action: "declined"` with an empty lineage and created no
receipt. The four legitimate receipts from the ordinary flow are untouched.

### Related, but not the same

- #4628 — same shape (stop hook offering a candidate spanning everything since a
  point far behind the branch), but there the base is a release tag, the tree is
  clean and level with upstream, and preflight **refuses** afterwards. Here the
  base is not a tag, the branch carries real work, and preflight does not refuse:
  it produces a consent envelope for a 1453-file candidate.
- #4639 — committed-candidate base-ref derived from the default branch. Does not
  apply here, since the default branch is the integration branch.
- #4739 — proposes scoping risk classification to the delta since the last
  acknowledged candidate. That would mask this symptom, but the defect is the
  base-ref selection itself, not the classification over it.

title: [Automated provider defect] bug(pi): review relay session-less lane cannot route any opencode-go model (400 MissingSessionID), and zen free tier rejects non-OpenCode clients — no config-reachable model remains (3.4.0)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

The gentle-pi review relay's in-process reviewer completion is documented as session-less by design ("no systemPrompt, no tools, no session"). The `opencode-go` provider endpoint rejects **every** request that lacks the `x-opencode-session` header with `HTTP 400 MissingSessionID`. The combination makes **every model on `opencode-go` unusable for the review relay** — the failure is transport-level and model-independent, so switching to "similar models within the same subscription" cannot fix it. Meanwhile the sibling `opencode` (zen) provider's **free-tier models return `403 FreeTierError`** ("OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode") when called from outside the OpenCode client. Net effect: a user whose only funded provider is the `opencode-go` subscription **cannot run the review gate at all** without additionally funding pay-per-use zen. Nothing in the model-routing config or documentation surfaces this incompatibility; it is discovered per-run, after START and capture authorization.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Authenticate a `opencode-go` subscription; point the review routing entries (`review-risk`, `review-resilience`, `review-readability`, `review-reliability`, `review-refuter`, `review-validator`) at `opencode-go/<model>`.
2. START an ordinary native review; capture the materialize forecast; resubmit with the reviewer run acknowledged.
3. Every reviewer run fails with the upstream `400 MissingSessionID`; the slot is left pending with `mutation_performed: false` (same slot-pending behavior as #4337, different root cause).

Minimal transport-level reproduction (model-independent, verified live with a real key):

| Request | Result |
|---|---|
| `POST zen-go/v1/chat/completions`, no `x-opencode-session` | `HTTP 400 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"MissingSessionID","message":"Request is missing x-opencode-session and cannot be routed efficiently."}}` |
| Same request **with** the header | `HTTP 200` |
| `POST zen/v1/chat/completions` (zen provider), any of the six free models | `HTTP 403 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"FreeTierError","message":"OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode"}}` (not User-Agent based; spoofing does not bypass it) |

### ✅ Expected Behavior

One of:

1. The in-process lane can supply a session identity for providers that require one (e.g. a per-provider transport adapter adds `x-opencode-session` from the host's session), **or**
2. Capture preflight validates the lens routing entries against provider transport requirements and fails fast typed (`reviewer-config-invalid`-style, naming the routing key and the incompatibility) instead of discovering it per-run, **or**
3. The documented compatibility table states that `opencode-go` is unusable for the pi review relay so users do not burn a frozen lineage discovering it.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Per-run failures: each acknowledged reviewer run fails with the upstream `400 MissingSessionID`, the reviewer slot stays pending, the lineage stays frozen, and the only workaround is re-routing the six entries to a different (funded) provider after the fact. A secondary dead end: zen free-tier models cannot serve as the fallback because they are client-locked to OpenCode itself (`403 FreeTierError` from outside the OpenCode client).

### Gentle AI Version

gentle-ai 3.4.0, gentle-pi 3.3.0, Pi 0.86.1

### Operating System

macOS (arm64)

### AI Agent / Client

Pi

### 📋 Affected Area

Review (host relay / reviewer transport)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

{"type":"error","error":{"type":"MissingSessionID","message":"Request is missing x-opencode-session and cannot be routed efficiently. Please see https://opencode.ai/docs/go/#where-can-i-use-it"}}

title: feat(pi): support opt-in community plugin discovery and installation
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

Catalog/Steps

### 💡 Problem Statement

Gentle AI currently has no supported discovery or installation path for independently maintained Pi community plugins. Pi users can install external packages directly, but Gentle AI cannot present an optional community plugin without either treating it as a built-in managed dependency or leaving it undiscoverable.

Gentle Live Observer is an independently developed, opt-in Pi plugin that exposes a local-only browser observer and an embedded Pi workspace. Its implementation and visual acceptance coverage already live in the public `Maicololiveras/flugo-gentle` repository. Copying its source into Gentle AI would duplicate ownership, exceed the repository's review budget, and would not be included by the current release packaging.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Add a small, explicit community Pi-plugin catalog/listing mechanism that:

1. Keeps plugin implementation and releases in the independent upstream repository/package.
2. Presents community plugins as optional and clearly marks their external maintainer and trust boundary.
3. Installs a selected plugin through Pi's supported package command rather than vendoring plugin source into Gentle AI.
4. Does not add the plugin to Gentle AI's default Pi support stack or silently install it.
5. Documents installation, activation, stopping, local-network behavior, and removal.

The first catalog entry would be Gentle Live Observer. If maintainers prefer a smaller first step, the approved scope could be limited to a discoverability section in `docs/pi.md` that links to the independently versioned package and its verified installation instructions.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- Vendor the complete plugin under `plugins/`: rejected because the current release archive does not ship that directory, it duplicates ownership, and the candidate is above the 400-line review budget.
- Add the package directly to the built-in Pi adapter: rejected because a community plugin should remain opt-in and should not become a default managed dependency.
- Documentation only in the external repository: works for existing users but provides no Gentle AI discovery path.

### 📎 Additional Context

The independent implementation has been validated on Windows and WSL2 with observer startup, local browser connection, embedded PTY startup, English/Spanish switching without extra model calls, reconnect behavior, and shutdown coverage. Native Linux and macOS acceptance remain explicitly unverified.

Proposed implementation should begin only after maintainers choose the supported community-plugin ownership and installation model and apply `status:approved`.

title: bug(contracts): intended-untracked-selection.schema.json has a non-absolute $id, so the cross-lane schema lane cannot compile it
body:
## Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

## 📝 Bug Description

The `schema` lane of the cross-lane battery fails at its first step, compiling the published schemas
under `contracts/`. Exactly one schema breaks it:
`contracts/review-integration/v2/schemas/intended-untracked-selection.schema.json`.

That file is the only schema under `contracts/` with a non-absolute `$id`:

```json
{
  "$id": "gentle-ai.review-intended-untracked-selection/v1",
  ...
  "properties": {
    "expected_untracked_inventory": {"$ref": "status-v5.schema.json#/$defs/sha256"},
    "intended_untracked": {"$ref": "start.schema.json#/$defs/changed_path"}
  }
}
```

Every sibling uses an absolute `$id`, and so do the product's own schema constants
(`ReviewIntegrationConsentSchemaID = "https://gentle-ai.dev/contracts/review-integration/v1/schemas/consent.schema.json"`).
Because this `$id` is a relative URI reference, the base URI becomes the schema's directory plus
`gentle-ai.review-intended-untracked-selection/`, so the file-relative refs resolve against that base
instead of the directory and fabricate a doubled path.

## 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Check out `2336d09a` (`origin/main` at the time of writing).
2. `./scripts/cross-lane-battery.sh --binary /tmp/gentle-ai` (any real binary works).

No binary is needed to see the failure: the lane globs
`contracts/review-integration/{v1,v2}/schemas/*.schema.json` from the repository tree
(`scripts/crosslane/schema.go:92`), so it reproduces from the tree alone, for any build.

## ✅ Expected Behavior

The `schema` lane compiles every published schema, as it does for the other 30-odd files.

## ❌ Actual Behavior

```
schema  compile published schemas  FAIL  compile gentle-ai.review-intended-untracked-selection/v1:
failing loading "file://<repo>/gentle-ai.review-intended-untracked-selection/gentle-ai.review-intended-untracked-selection/status-v5.schema.json":
open <repo>/gentle-ai.review-intended-untracked-selection/gentle-ai.review-intended-untracked-selection/status-v5.schema.json: no such file or directory
```

The failure also short-circuits the lane's later rows: with the broken `$id` the battery reports 24
checks, and with it fixed the battery reports 31.

## 🖥️ Environment

- **Gentle AI Version:** `3.4.1-0.20260920211654-2336d09aefe2` (commit `2336d09a`)
- **Operating System:** Linux (Arch/Manjaro)
- **AI Agent / Client:** Other (Pi)
- **📋 Affected Area:** Other (published `contracts/` schemas and the cross-lane battery)

## 💡 Logs / Error Output

See the Actual Behavior block.

## Additional Context

Scope, stated honestly: I could not find any path by which this reaches a user. The only reader of
`contracts/**/*.schema.json` from the tree is this battery; the product serves embedded schema
constants that already use absolute IDs. So the impact is limited to the out-of-CI regression net
reporting a red in its first step, which reads as "the binary under test is broken" when the binary is
fine. That misattribution is the whole cost.

Causality is confirmed by mutation rather than inspection. Changing only the `$id` to the absolute
form its siblings use:

```diff
-  "$id": "gentle-ai.review-intended-untracked-selection/v1",
+  "$id": "https://gentle-ai.dev/contracts/review-integration/v2/schemas/intended-untracked-selection.schema.json",
```

makes the compile step pass and advances the battery from 24 to 31 checks. Reverting restores the
failure exactly. The file was introduced by `bb43f9a7` ("fix(review): execute intended untracked
selection handoff", #3998).

Distinct from #3346 and #3347. That pair covered published schemas diverging from live emitters and
two envelopes with no schema at all, and it is closed. This is a schema that exists and cannot be
compiled, which that fix did not address.

Why the guard missed it, verified in the tree. The two consumers key schemas differently:

- The battery registers each file under **its own `$id`** and then compiles every entry that carries a
  `properties.schema.const` identity (`scripts/crosslane/schema.go:104-127`). A relative `$id`
  therefore becomes the resolution base and the sibling refs break.
- The Go guard synthesizes a location from the path instead of the `$id`
  (`internal/cli/review_published_schema_conformance_test.go:31`, `AddResource("https://gentle-ai.dev/..." + entry.Name(), document)`),
  and compiles only the schemas its tests name: `failure`, `gate-result`, `assess`,
  `capabilities-v1.5`, `last-event-closure`, `start-v4` and the transition pair. Nothing compiles
  `intended-untracked-selection.schema.json`, so its refs are registered but never resolved.

The same file also walks every published schema and asserts each local `$ref` resolves to a real file
(`review_transition_schema_drift_test.go:115-127`), which this file's refs do. They are valid file
paths; the problem is only that a relative `$id` redefines the base they resolve against. That is
likely why the file reads as fine to inspection and only the battery disagrees.

Happy to open the one-line PR if the issue gets `status:approved`.

title: [Automated provider defect] bug(opencode): orchestrator calls unavailable tools (question, task) — TypeError crashes session before work begins
body:
## Observed Behavior

The OpenCode orchestrator (`gentle-orchestrator` agent) attempts to call `question` and `task` tools that are unavailable in the current runtime, causing an immediate `TypeError: Unknown tool: question` crash. The session never reaches the user request.

## Expected Behavior

The orchestrator should either:
1. Gracefully handle unavailable tools and continue without them, or
2. Detect tool availability at startup and adjust its workflow accordingly

## Reproduction

1. Start a session with the `gentle-orchestrator` agent
2. Send any request
3. The orchestrator immediately crashes with `TypeError: Unknown tool: question`

## Evidence

- Error: `TypeError: Unknown tool: question`
- Error: `Something went wrong, please try again`
- Error: `Model tried to call unavailable tool task`
- Version: Built-in orchestrator agent (not a specific version)
- Runtime: Linux

## Impact

This is a **session-blocking defect**: the orchestrator cannot function at all when `question` and `task` tools are unavailable, preventing any work from being done.

## Suggested Fix

The orchestrator should check tool availability before attempting to use them, and fall back to alternative approaches (e.g., inline prompts, direct actions) when tools are unavailable.

title: bug(review): the Stop hook forces a consent + review round for every commit, ignoring review_due: false / under_budget from review assess
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

In an ODD session with RDD enabled, the Stop hook forces a full consent + review lifecycle for **every** unreviewed candidate, contradicting the `review_due` decision that `gentle-ai review assess` returns for the same commit, and contradicting the ODD contract text the installer writes into the agent instructions.

The installed ODD contract says:

> After each work-unit commit, when RDD is enabled, run `gentle-ai review assess ... --committed-only --json` on that commit and read `review_due` and `review_due_reason`. When `review_due` is true (`high_risk`, or `slice_budget_reached` ...), execute the returned `next_transition.command` verbatim. **When `review_due` is false, record `review_due_reason` and continue**: ... `under_budget` stays pending in the slice until a later commit reaches the budget.

In practice `assess` said `review_due: false` / `under_budget` for the first work-unit commit, and the Stop hook demanded a full review of that same commit anyway. The two mechanisms disagree about the same candidate.

Compounding this, every Stop-hook-generated START carried the branch point as `--base-ref`, so each successive review re-read the whole accumulated diff. Across one feature branch this produced 7 consent prompts and 6 full reviews whose candidate grew monotonically: 388 → 515 → 759 → 923 → 1116 → 1171 → 1228 changed lines. The same module was re-reviewed 6 times, and each pass surfaced new advisory findings in code that an earlier pass had already approved and acknowledged (`authority: burned`).

The scoping half of this is the same causal class as #4739 (risk classification computed over the full base-diff rather than the delta since the last acknowledged candidate). What that issue does not cover, and what this report is about, is the **Stop hook ignoring `review_due` entirely** — #4739's proposal explicitly keeps the full base-diff as the thing reviewed, so even with its fix the Stop hook would still force a review that `assess` said was not due.

The net effect is that ODD — documented as the lighter, less bureaucratic route — cost substantially more human interaction than the SDD cycle it replaced, because human consent is requested per commit instead of per slice.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable RDD globally (`gentle-ai review mode enable --scope global`) on a repository whose integration branch is not the default branch.
2. Create a feature branch and make a work-unit commit of roughly 370 changed lines (below the 400-line slice budget).
3. Run `gentle-ai review assess --cwd <repo> --agent claude-code --base-ref <branch point> --committed-only --json`. Observe `review_due: false`, `review_due_reason: "under_budget"`.
4. End the agent turn. The Stop hook reports an unreviewed candidate and requires the selectorless STATUS preflight plus the returned START, which returns a blocking `gentle-ai.review-integration.consent/v3` envelope for that same commit.
5. Grant consent, let the single lens run, acknowledge (`authority: burned`).
6. Make another work-unit commit and end the turn again. Observe that the new candidate's `--base-ref` is still the branch point, and `changed_lines` includes everything from step 2.
7. Repeat. Each round re-reviews all prior approved content and asks for consent again.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

- The Stop hook honours the same `review_due` / `review_due_reason` decision that `gentle-ai review assess` returns for the candidate, so an `under_budget` commit stays pending in the slice instead of forcing a consent round.
- Once a candidate is approved and acknowledged, the reviewed boundary advances, so the next candidate is scoped to the delta since that acknowledgement — as the installed ODD contract states: *"the reviewed boundary advances to this commit once that review is acknowledged ... every reviewed boundary becomes the next base."*
- Consent is requested per slice, matching the delivery budget ODD already defines, not per commit.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

- The Stop hook requires a review for every unreviewed candidate regardless of `review_due`.
- `--base-ref` stays pinned to the branch point across all rounds; acknowledgement burns authority but does not advance the boundary.
- Candidate size grows monotonically and already-approved code is re-reviewed on every round, producing fresh advisory findings on content a previous receipt already covered.
- `risk_evidence` keeps naming an executable file from an early commit even for later commits that touch only documentation or tests, because the candidate spans the whole branch. Documentation-only commits are therefore reported as `medium` risk with the stale executable-change reason.

### Gentle AI Version

3.4.0

### Operating System

Windows

### AI Agent / Client

Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
# Step 3 - assess says the commit is not due for review
gentle-ai review assess --cwd <repo> --agent claude-code --base-ref <branch-point> --committed-only --json
{
  "schema": "gentle-ai.review-assessment/v1",
  "risk": "medium",
  "reasons": [{ "code": "executable_change", "path": "<src-file>.ts" }],
  "changed_paths": 5,
  "changed_lines": 372,
  "candidate": { "kind": "base-diff", "base_ref": "<branch-point>", "consumed": false },
  "review_due": false,
  "review_due_reason": "under_budget"
}

# Step 4 - the Stop hook demands a review of that same commit anyway
Receipt-driven development is enabled for this repository, and it holds an unreviewed
candidate (target_identity sha256:<redacted>).
By the review contract entry rule, you must run the selectorless STATUS preflight below
and route only from its returned next_transition before reporting completion.

# Step 6 onward - base-ref never advances after acknowledgement.
# Every START across the whole branch carried the same base-ref:
--base-ref=<branch-point> --committed-only=true

# Candidate size per consent round, same branch, same base-ref:
#   round 1: changed_files  5, changed_lines  388   -> approved, acknowledged (authority burned)
#   round 2: changed_files 19, changed_lines  515   -> approved, acknowledged
#   round 3: changed_files 19, changed_lines  759   -> approved, acknowledged
#   round 4: changed_files 19, changed_lines  923   -> declined (candidate-scoped)
#   round 5: changed_files 21, changed_lines 1116   -> approved, acknowledged
#   round 6: changed_files 21, changed_lines 1171   -> approved, acknowledged
#   round 7: changed_files 21, changed_lines 1228   -> approved, acknowledged
```

### Additional Context

Rounds 5, 6 and 7 covered commits that changed no source file at all (documentation corrections and test hardening), yet each was classified `medium` with `risk_evidence` naming an executable change from round 2's commit.

Because each pass re-read already-approved files with a fresh reviewer, findings did not converge: round 5 surfaced a stale-verification-record finding, round 6 surfaced a round-trip coverage gap in a module round 1 had already approved. Those findings were genuinely useful, which makes the point sharper — they were reachable only by paying for a full re-review of approved content, rather than by scoping the pass to what was new.

Related: #4739 covers the risk-classification half of the scoping problem, from a different reporter and a different repository. #4783 introduced the `review_due` contract that the Stop hook does not consult.

title: fix(install): gentle-pi postinstall always fails on Windows — lstat/fstat dev mismatch rejects every settings.json read
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues (open and closed) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

Automated provider-defect report, filed with the operator's explicit consent.

### 📝 Bug Description

On Windows, `gentle-pi`'s `postinstall` always fails. The failing step is `installTuiModeSetting()` in `scripts/install-tui-mode-setting.mjs`, which sets `process.exitCode = 1`, so npm treats the whole install as failed and rolls the package back to the previously installed version.

Net effect: **gentle-pi cannot be installed or upgraded on Windows** through `pi install`, `pi update --extension npm:gentle-pi`, or a plain `npm install gentle-pi@latest`. The package silently stays on whatever version was already present, and the reported error does not point at the real cause.

The first half of the postinstall succeeds: the package-local Gentle AI v3.4.0 binary is built and published correctly via the Go SumDB source path. Only the settings step fails, and that is enough to fail the install.

**Root cause.** `readSettings()` guards against a swapped file between `lstat` and `open` by comparing the two stat results:

```js
const before = inspect(path);              // lstatSync
const fd = openSync(path, constants.O_RDONLY | (constants.O_NOFOLLOW ?? 0));
if (!sameFile(before, fstatSync(fd))) throw new Error("settings.json changed while opening");
```

with

```js
function sameFile(left, right) {
    return left && right && left.dev === right.dev && left.ino === right.ino;
}
```

On Windows with Node 22, `lstatSync(path).dev` is `0`, while `fstatSync(fd).dev` returns the volume serial number. `ino` matches on both sides. `sameFile()` therefore returns `false` on every call, and the guard rejects a file that never changed.

Two further Windows notes on this guard:

- `constants.O_NOFOLLOW` is `undefined` on Windows, so the `?? 0` fallback means the open carries no symlink protection there anyway — the `dev`/`ino` comparison is the only real check, and it is the one that misfires.
- The same `sameFile()` helper backs the lock-ownership check later in the same function, so that check is affected by the same platform behavior.

**Suggested direction.** Treat `dev` as non-comparable when either side reports `0`, or compare on `ino` alone where the platform does not provide a stable `dev` across `lstat` and `fstat`. Separately, a failure of this cosmetic settings step arguably should not fail the whole package install, given the binary install that precedes it has already succeeded.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

Minimal, no gentle-pi needed — on any Windows machine with Node 22, against any existing regular file:

```js
const fs = require("node:fs");
const p = "<path to any existing file>";
const before = fs.lstatSync(p);
const fd = fs.openSync(p, fs.constants.O_RDONLY);
const after = fs.fstatSync(fd);
fs.closeSync(fd);
console.log("lstat dev:", before.dev, "fstat dev:", after.dev, "ino equal:", before.ino === after.ino);
```

End to end:

1. On Windows, with a Pi agent home that already has an older gentle-pi installed.
2. Run `npm install gentle-pi@latest --prefix <agent-npm-dir> --legacy-peer-deps`.
3. Observe the postinstall failure and the rollback.
4. Check the installed version — it is unchanged.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

`sameFile()` treats an unchanged file as the same file, `installTuiModeSetting()` completes, the postinstall exits `0`, and gentle-pi installs or upgrades normally on Windows.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

`dev` differs between `lstat` and `fstat`, so the file is always treated as changed. The postinstall exits `1` and npm rolls the package back.

Observed on the affected machine:

```
lstat dev: 0   fstat dev: <volume serial>   ino equal: true
```

### Gentle AI Version

3.4.0 (stable, Go SumDB source build). gentle-pi 3.3.0, pi 0.86.0.

### Operating System

Windows

### AI Agent / Client

Other (Pi)

### 📋 Affected Area

Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```
npm error command failed
npm error command <shell> /d /s /c node scripts/install-gentle-ai.mjs
npm error Gentle AI v3.4.0 installed at <package-root>\.gentle-ai\v3.4.0\gentle-ai.exe
npm error gentle-pi could not enable fullscreen: settings.json changed while opening
```

### Additional Context

Environment: gentle-pi 3.3.0 (npm, stable channel), gentle-ai 3.4.0 (stable), pi 0.86.0 with its bundled Node v22.14.0 and npm 10.9.2, Windows 11 x64, Go toolchain 1.26.0 present.

**Workaround in use:**

1. `npm install gentle-pi@latest --prefix <agent-npm-dir> --legacy-peer-deps --ignore-scripts`
2. Run the useful half of the postinstall by hand from the package directory:
   `node -e "import('./scripts/gentle-ai-installer.mjs').then(m => m.installGentleAi()).then(r => console.log(JSON.stringify(r)))"`
   This builds and publishes the package-local Gentle AI binary correctly.
3. Skip the `tuiMode` step, or set `"tuiMode": "fullscreen"` in the agent settings file by hand.

**Secondary observation (separate, likely transient).** Running the same postinstall through `pi update --extension npm:gentle-pi` additionally raced Pi's own write to the agent settings file, and on two attempts produced:

```
EPERM: operation not permitted, rename '<package-root>\.gentle-ai\.v3.4.0.staging-XXXXXX'
  -> '<package-root>\.gentle-ai\v3.4.0'
```

Invoking npm directly, with no Pi process running, made the staging publication succeed every time. Noted only as an observation; the deterministic blocker is the `dev` comparison above.

title: bug(community-tool): injected codegraph-guidance claims the CLI auto-syncs, so CLI reads serve stale results silently
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

The `codegraph-guidance` block injected into every detected agent states that CodeGraph's index stays fresh through the watcher, and authorizes agents to fall back to the upstream CLI's read-only intelligence commands when the MCP tool is unavailable. That conflates two different surfaces:

- MCP (`codegraph serve --mcp`): runs a daemon with a file watcher and catches up on connect. Auto-sync works.
- CLI (`codegraph status|query|explore|node|files|callers|callees|impact|affected`): reads the index as-is. It does not start a daemon and does not auto-sync.

So an agent doing exactly what the guidance tells it to do can read a stale index and get silently wrong structural answers, with no warning from the tool.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a scratch project, run `codegraph init <project-root>`, then make sure no daemon is running (no `daemon.sock` under `<project-root>/.codegraph/`), so no file watcher is active.
2. Add a new method with a distinctive name to a source file, without running `codegraph sync`.
3. Run `codegraph query "<new-symbol>"`, and also read the index directly with `select count(*) from nodes where name='<new-symbol>'`.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Either the injected guidance states that CLI reads do not auto-sync and requires an explicit `codegraph sync -q <project-root>` first, or the CLI refuses or warns when the index is stale. `codegraph status` already reports the information: a `Pending Changes:` section plus `Run "codegraph sync" to update the index`.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The guidance asserts the opposite:

```
7. After edits, rely on watcher auto-sync by default. Run `codegraph sync` only when the
watcher is disabled or CodeGraph reports stale files that do not refresh normally.
```

And the CLI returns stale data with no warning:

```
$ codegraph query "metodoNuevo"
ℹ No results found for "metodoNuevo"
```

### Gentle AI Version

3.2.1

### Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client

Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
# MCP surface, working as designed (catch-up on connect):
[CodeGraph daemon] Listening on <project-root>/.codegraph/daemon.sock (pid 1581491, v1.3.1). Idle timeout 300000ms.
[CodeGraph MCP] File watcher active — graph will auto-sync on changes
[CodeGraph MCP] Caught up 1 file(s) changed since last run

# CLI surface, same tree, stale index served silently:
$ codegraph query "metodoNuevo"
ℹ No results found for "metodoNuevo"
$ sqlite3 -readonly <project-root>/.codegraph/codegraph.db "select count(*) from nodes where name='metodoNuevo';"
0
```

### Additional Context

- Single shared source, so it affects every agent that receives the block (Pi, Claude Code, Codex, opencode): `internal/components/communitytool/codegraph_guidance.go` (lines 46 and 58 on current `main`). `docs/pi.md` (Intelligence / Indexes rows) documents the same assumption.
- Verified against CodeGraph v1.3.1. Two related facts: `codegraph serve --help` exposes `--no-watch` ("Disable the file watcher (no auto-sync...)"), and the daemon shuts down after a 5-minute idle timeout, so nothing watches between agent sessions.
- A local 3-file fix (guidance + `tool_test.go` assertions + `docs/pi.md`) already passes `go test ./internal/components/communitytool/...`. Happy to open the PR from a fork once the issue is approved.

title: fix(odd): clarify work-unit commit authorization boundary
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

The installed Pi orchestrator guidance contains conflicting commit-authorization rules.

The mandatory ODD workflow says that every substantial task closes with at least one work-unit commit on the feature branch. The Safety section separately says: “Never commit unless the user explicitly asks.”

During an ordinary ODD continuation, the user said “continue with WU5.” After exploration established that WU5 should close as a documentation-only N/A decision, the agent stopped before writing because it could not determine whether continuing the work unit implicitly authorized its required work-unit commit. This adds an unnecessary confirmation step and makes the newly introduced automatic ODD commit contract ambiguous.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a Pi session with the current Gentle AI orchestrator guidance and ODD enabled.
2. Continue an existing substantial work unit using wording such as “continue with WU5,” without separately saying “commit.”
3. Complete read-only exploration and reach a clear implementation or documentation decision.
4. Observe the conflict between the ODD requirement to close the task with a commit and the Safety requirement not to commit without an explicit request.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The guidance should define one unambiguous authorization boundary. For example, explicit authorization to implement or continue a substantial ODD work unit should include its required local work-unit commits, while push, pull-request creation, merge, publication, and destructive operations remain separate user decisions.

If that is not the intended policy, ODD should not state that every task automatically closes with a commit; it should explicitly require a commit confirmation at the task boundary.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The agent conservatively stops and asks for commit authorization after the work unit was already authorized, because both instructions apply and neither defines which one governs this case.

### Gentle AI Version

3.3.0

### Operating System

Linux (Other)

### AI Agent / Client

Other

A delegated `gentle-ai-worker` blocks before performing an authorized multi-file merge because receipt-driven review is enabled, but the worker runtime does not expose the native `gentle_review` tool.
