title: bug(review 3.0.2): inferential CRITICAL goes straight to correction_required with no refuter step
body:
## Summary
On **3.0.2 stable**, a single-lens native review routed an **inferential** CRITICAL straight to `correction_required` with **no refuter step**, although the contract says inferential blockers share one read-only refuter batch. The finding is falsifiable in seconds and is false, so the only ways forward are a correction for a non-defect or declining the candidate.

Related, not the same cause: #4548 (false CRITICALs from dependencies the reviewer cannot see). Here nothing is hidden from the reviewer — it inferred the runtime behaviour wrongly — but the routing symptom is identical: no refuter between an inferential severe finding and a mandatory correction.

## Environment
- gentle-ai **3.0.2** (stable, built with `go install`), agent `claude-code`, Windows 10 x64.
- Candidate: committed base-diff (`--base-ref <base> --committed-only`), untracked excluded, 11 paths, 301 lines, risk `medium`, consent granted. Native plan: one lens, `review-reliability`.

## What happened
1. START (granted) → STATUS → one `review.capture-result` (in-process) → closure `state: correction_required`, `action: "candidate-caused severe findings require one bounded correction"`. The closure envelope carried no findings, only `status_continuation`.
2. STATUS (after resubmitting the intended-untracked selection) → `collect correction_plan_required` with `fix_finding_ids: ["R3-001"]`.
3. R3-001: `severity: CRITICAL`, `evidence_class: inferential`, `causal_disposition: introduced`. Claim: a new `.mjs` test importing a sibling `.ts` module "will be rejected with ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION … no test() callback is ever registered and all six assertions are silently skipped".
4. No refuter transition was offered at any point.

## Why the finding is false (observed, not argued)
- Emulating a Node without type stripping (`node --no-experimental-strip-types --test <file>`) makes the run **fail loudly**: `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION`, `pass 0`, exit code 1. Nothing is skipped silently.
- With the repository's CI runtime (Node 24) the same file passes 6/6.
- 84 other test files in the same repository import `.ts` siblings the same way.
- An earlier review of a different candidate in the same repository reported the **same claim as a non-blocking WARNING** — the severity is not stable across runs.

## Expected
An inferential severe finding goes to the read-only refuter batch before any correction is required; with the refuter's verdict this one would be rejected by the evidence above.

## Actual
`correction_required` with a mandatory correction for a non-defect; no refuter slot offered.

## Minimal reproduction
1. Candidate that adds `x.ts` and `x.test.mjs` importing `./x.ts`, in a repo whose CI runs Node ≥ 22.18 / 24.
2. Native review at `medium` risk (single `review-reliability` lens).
3. If the lens rates the import as CRITICAL/inferential, STATUS goes to `correction_plan_required` without a refuter.

## State
Lineage `review-6e3477511bf87a39` left at `correction_plan_required`; the candidate is being declined via the provider's own decline invocation. No correction plan was submitted.

title: feat(installation): renew managed opencode.json format for OpenCode 2.x strict-schema conformance
body:
## 🎯 How this works

1. **Submit** this feature request → it gets the `status:needs-review` label automatically
2. A **maintainer reviews** it and adds `status:approved` (or closes it as out-of-scope/duplicate)
3. **Only then** should you (or anyone) open a PR to implement it

PRs that implement features without `status:approved` on the linked issue will be automatically rejected.

## ✅ Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate. The closest match is #4729 (managed plugins fail to load on OpenCode v2.0.5+), but #4729 is a bug report about V1 SDK imports in plugin source; this issue is an RFC for a holistic renewal of the managed `opencode.json` shape itself, which is the structural root cause behind #4729 and several other V2-vs-gentle mismatches.
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

## 🛠 Affected Area

- [ ] CLI (commands, flags)
- [ ] TUI (terminal UI)
- [x] Installation Pipeline
- [ ] Agent Detection
- [ ] System Detection
- [ ] Catalog/Steps
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Other

## 🤔 Problem Statement

After upgrading to `gentle-ai 3.3.0` (which adds support for OpenCode 2.x), a user's `~/.dotfiles/opencode/opencode.json` ends up as a **~500 KB hybrid** that violates `additionalProperties: false` of the official OpenCode 2.x config schema (`https://opencode.ai/config.json`, which the file's own `$schema` declares). Specifically, gentle's managed content writes:

| Top-level key gentle emits | Status per official schema (`additionalProperties:false`) |
| --- | --- |
| `agent` (singular, 23 entries, `prompt`+`permission`) | ✅ Valid |
| `agents` (plural, 23 entries, `system`+`permissions` array) | ❌ Foreign |
| `permission` (singular map: `bash`, `read`) | ✅ Valid |
| `permissions` (plural array, 29 rules) | ❌ Foreign |
| `theme` | ❌ Not in `Config` schema (belongs in `cli.json`) |
| `mcp.servers.<name>.disabled` | ❌ Schema requires `enabled` (boolean) |
| `plugin` (missing entirely) | ❌ Missing — managed plugins don't register |

Per-agent in the singular `agent` block, gentle also emits a duplicated per-agent `system` field plus a `permissions` array alongside the canonical `prompt` + `permission`. The result is roughly 2× file size, divergent content (the singular `prompt` and the plural `system` differ by ~600 chars in `gentle-orchestrator`), and a `gentle-ai sync` cycle that re-introduces the residue on every run, so a user-side cleanup is immediately undone.

The official OpenCode 2.x config schema uses **singular** keys (`agent`, `permission`, `plugin`) and per-agent `prompt`/`permission`. Gentle's managed template instead emits the **plural** shapes that the opencode.ai/config.json schema does not list. The runtime currently tolerates this through a "configuration normalization diagnostic" (retained native value over legacy value), but that is a runtime compatibility shim, not a real schema match — and the compatibility layer is undocumented surface area.

The downstream effects already visible in the wild: #4729 (managed plugins fail to load with `SchemaError(Expected object at ["default"])`), MCP servers emitting `disabled` instead of `enabled` (silently treated as legacy), `plugin` array missing so `opencode plugin list` returns "No plugins found" even though the plugin files exist on disk, and `theme` being written at the wrong level (opencode.json instead of cli.json).

## 💡 Proposed Solution

Adopt a single canonical shape for the **managed portion** of `opencode.json` that strictly matches the official OpenCode 2.x schema. The shape should be:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "default_agent": "<name>",
  "share": "disabled" | "enabled",
  "agent": {
    "<name>": {
      "mode": "subagent" | "primary" | "all",
      "prompt": "<string>",
      "permission": { "<tool>": { "<pattern>": "allow|deny|ask" } },
      "model": "<provider/model>",
      "description": "<string>",
      "hidden": <boolean>
    }
  },
  "permission": { "<tool>": { "<pattern>": "allow|deny|ask" } },
  "plugin": [
    "/absolute/path/to/plugin.ts",
    ["path/to/plugin-with-config.ts", { /* opaque config object */ }]
  ],
  "mcp": {
    "<serverName>": {
      "type": "local" | "remote",
      "command": ["node", "..."],  // local
      "url": "https://...",         // remote
      "enabled": true,
      "timeout": 30000
    }
  },
  "formatter": { "<name>": {} },
  "lsp": true | { "<language>": {} }
}
```

Concrete changes gentle should make to its managed emission:

1. **Singular `agent` only** — drop the plural `agents` block. Per-agent fields: `prompt`, `permission` (map), `mode`, `model`, `description`, `hidden`. Never emit `system` or `permissions` array per agent.
2. **Singular `permission` only** — drop the plural `permissions` array from both top level and per-agent. Permission rules are always the map shape `{tool: {pattern: effect}}`.
3. **No `theme` in opencode.json.** Move/keep theme in `cli.json` where the official cli.json schema lives.
4. **MCP servers: `enabled` (not `disabled`).** Invert semantics; current `disabled: false` becomes `enabled: true`.
5. **Top-level `plugin` array** must be present and complete, listing every managed plugin file. Each entry is a bare path string or a `[path, config-object]` tuple per the schema's `anyOf`.
6. **Per-agent IDs and version markers** (`__managed_by`, etc.) must use schema-allowed fields only — for fields not in `AgentConfig`, store metadata in a `gentle-ai` extension file (e.g., `~/.gentle-ai/state/opencode-managed.json`) instead of inlining into agent blocks.
7. **`subagent_depth` at top level** (not under `experimental`) — schema-correct location for nested subagent depth.
8. **Strict pre-sync validation**: before writing, `gentle-ai sync` should dry-run the produced file against the official schema and fail with a clear error if any unknown key would be written. This makes the "managed template emits non-schema shapes" class of bug structurally impossible.

For users who currently rely on the dual-shape file, ship a one-shot migration script (`gentle-ai migrate opencode-v2-shape`) that:
- Reads the existing dual file,
- Selects the schema-conformant block (`agent` singular + `permission` singular) per-agent per-field (preferring `prompt` over `system`, `permission` map over `permissions` array),
- Drops the non-schema blocks,
- Writes back a single-shape file,
- Updates the `plugin` array with all managed plugin paths,
- Emits a before/after diff for review.

This makes the renewal opt-in and reversible.

## 🤔 Alternatives Considered

- **Comment on #4729 instead of opening a new issue.** Rejected: #4729 is a specific bug report about plugin SDK content (`@opencode-ai/plugin` vs `@opencode/plugin`); it does not cover the broader shape mismatch in the surrounding opencode.json emission. A separate RFC is the right surface for a renewal proposal. I have cited #4729 as related in the context.
- **Ship a user-side post-processing step** (e.g. a `~/.config/opencode/post-sync-hook.sh`) that strips the non-schema blocks after every `gentle-ai sync`. Rejected: this defeats the purpose of `gentle-ai sync` (managed reconciliation) and silently masks the underlying schema mismatch from view. The correct fix is upstream.
- **Document the legacy normalization layer** in `docs/codebase/integrations.md` and tell users to ignore the dual emission. Rejected: the runtime diagnostics surface only on conflicts, not on every read, which makes behavior hard to reason about across `gentle-ai sync` cycles. The cleanest contract is one shape.
- **Adopt the plural `agents`/`permissions` shape as the new canonical and document it as gentle's "V2 managed extension".** Rejected: this would diverge from the opencode.ai/config.json schema that the file itself declares via `$schema`, multiplying the drift between gentle-managed files and what the OpenCode runtime prefers natively. The schema already provides everything gentle needs in singular form.

## 📎 Additional Context

Reproduction on a clean `gentle-ai 3.3.0` install with `opencode` agent selected:

1. `pacman -S opencode` (Arch; equivalent: `brew install opencode` on macOS, `npm i -g opencode-ai` elsewhere) — installed version `2.0.5-1.1`.
2. `gentle-ai init` and select the `opencode` agent.
3. `gentle-ai sync` — populates `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` from managed components (opencode, sdd, engram, context7, permissions, theme, opencode-gentle-logo).
4. `python3 -c "import json; print(sorted(json.load(open('/home/josel/.dotfiles/opencode/opencode.json')).keys()))"` →
   `['$schema', 'agent', 'agents', 'default_agent', 'formatter', 'lsp', 'mcp', 'permission', 'permissions', 'share', 'theme']`
5. Fetch the official schema: `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/config.json -o /tmp/opencode/config-v2.json` (39,039 bytes).
6. Compare file keys to `$defs.Config.properties` — three violations (`agents`, `permissions`, `theme`).
7. Apply manual cleanup: remove top-level `agents`/`permissions`/`theme`, remove per-agent `system`/`permissions`, invert MCP `disabled` → `enabled`, add `plugin` array of 5 managed plugin paths.
8. File size: `502,111 B → 166,146 B` (-67%), schema check returns 0 unknown keys.
9. `gentle-ai sync` again — 4 files changed, including `opencode.json`. Post-sync the residue (`agents`, `theme`) is back. The `plugin` array is preserved, but the surrounding shape is clobbered.

The runtime currently runs despite the shape mismatch because the opencode 2.0.5 runtime applies a legacy normalization for MCP (`disabled` vs `enabled`) and tolerates unknown top-level keys. That tolerance is what hides the bug from view but does not make it correct.

Related issues / context:
- #4729 — managed plugins fail to load because plugin source imports the V1 SDK. A strict-shape renewal is the structural prerequisite for fixing #4729 cleanly: once the shape is canonical, the SDK-compat work in plugin source can be tracked independently.
- The repo's `docs/codebase/integrations.md` defines a "thin plugin principle" — gentle manages registration, OpenCode owns runtime. This proposal extends that principle to "and gentle's emitted content is schema-conformant" so registration never points at non-loading content.

A purely shape-level fix (no SDK change) already removes 2 of the 3 user-visible symptoms (file bloat + sync-undoes-cleanup); the SDK migration in #4729 removes the third (load failures). The two are complementary; neither subsumes the other.

Environment for the reproduction above:
- gentle-ai v3.3.0 (`gga version` → `3.3.0`)
- opencode v2.0.5-1.1 (Arch package)
- OS: Arch Linux (kernel Zen, GNOME, Nushell)
- engram v2.0.0 (diagnostic context only; engram reports a related ERROR on `sync_target_closed_space` from the v2.0.0 migration — separate issue)

Privacy note: this issue does not include user-specific credentials, secrets, or local path material beyond the public locations documented in `docs/codebase/integrations.md`.

title: feat(review): add audited retention for terminal escalated authorities
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Problem Statement

Terminal `escalated` compact-v2 authorities accumulate indefinitely. `review abandon` rejects terminal lineages, while `review recover` creates a successor without changing the predecessor. Even after abandoning that empty successor, the original terminal authority remains in `review status`. Operators cannot keep the active inventory bounded without manually deleting authority data and breaking auditability.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Add an audited retention/prune operation for terminal authorities. It should dry-run by default, explicitly bind lineage IDs and revisions, preserve durable audit evidence in quarantine or a compact tombstone, and remove retired terminal entries from normal active inventory. It must refuse current/nonterminal authority and fail closed on drift.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

Manual deletion is unsafe. Recovery preserves the predecessor. Leaving entries forever creates unbounded operational noise.

### 📎 Additional Context

Observed on Gentle AI 3.2.1. Related: #4433, #1529, #2423. #1529 explicitly excluded terminal history; this request covers that remaining lifecycle gap.

title: review capture-result: operation_outcome_unknown after 'managed reviewer assets are outdated'
body:
## Bug Description

Running `gentle-ai review capture-result` (also via the `gentle_review_capture` facade) repeatedly fails with `operation_outcome_unknown`. The typed classification falls back to "managed reviewer assets are outdated; run `gentle-ai sync`" — but `gentle-ai sync` does NOT resolve the issue. The reviewer's expected digest appears stale relative to the local install.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `gentle-ai install --agent pi` (fresh install or sync).
2. `gentle-ai sync --agent pi` (assets updated; digest visible in `~/.gentle-ai/state.json` as `managed_asset_digest`).
3. `gentle-ai review start --contract=gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 ...` (succeeds, returns `lineage_id`).
4. `gentle-ai review capture-result --lineage=<id> --expected-revision=... ...` (or via `gentle_review_capture` with `reviewerRunAcknowledged: true`).
5. Native capture execution fails with stderr `managed reviewer assets are outdated; run gentle-ai sync`.
6. Defect report saved at `.git/gentle-ai/defect-reports/operation-outcome-unknown-*.md`.
7. `gentle-ai sync` again — reports `no managed sync actions needed`.
8. Re-attempt capture — same failure with a NEW defect report.

## Expected Behavior

Either:
- The reviewer asset digest check is satisfied after `gentle-ai sync`, OR
- The error message names the specific asset path/digest that is stale and the exact command to refresh it.

## Actual Behavior

Capture repeatedly fails with the same generic message even after multiple syncs. In one session I generated **4 identical defect reports**:

- `operation-outcome-unknown-01580c46742f.md`
- `operation-outcome-unknown-0ead75ac2a27.md`
- `operation-outcome-unknown-ccef9e91e9df.md`
- `operation-outcome-unknown-fc20c6c346b6.md`

Local `~/.gentle-ai/state.json` after sync shows:

```
managed_asset_digest: sha256:51d6e0033fc0df10b9f07a4bbdd9c6ea156455d7f024644be61df369604cf177
```

Stale digest reported by the reviewer (from the FIRST inspect's continuation):

```
sha256:54ae22f8501cdb55d834b1b16a92ddab7e4b28b2c57332291d38490c025a389a
```

The sync DID change the digest, but the reviewer session keeps using the previous one. Possibly the reviewer's expected digest is cached at START time and not refreshed when sync runs in parallel with an active review.

## Environment

- **Gentle AI Version**: 3.1.0 (`cfc415ce4d330ada53ff6ece99f9f11b63956f51`)
- **Operating System**: darwin/arm64
- **AI Agent / Client**: Pi (gentle-pi) calling via `gentle_review_capture` MCP facade and `gentle-ai` CLI.
- **Repository**: `cjguajardo/tronco`, branch `feat/latam-mercadopago-routing`, base `444c357`, candidate `8d81e9a`.
- **Lens**: `review-reliability` (R3)
- **Risk level**: `medium` (16 files, 913 changed lines)

## Defect Reports

All four files contain the same content template (no automatic capture):
- `reason_code: operation_outcome_unknown`
- `operation: review.capture-result`
- `phase: native_running`

## Workaround Used

`gentle-ai review mode disable --scope clone` — disables RDD for the specific clone so delivery can proceed via ordinary repository policy. Review authority for the lineage stays in `state: reviewing` (unclosed). Global RDD remains `on`.

## Hypothesis

The reviewer's expected asset digest appears to be frozen at START time. Subsequent `gentle-ai sync` updates the global asset digest in `state.json` but does not refresh the bound authority's expected digest on the active lineage. So the reviewer always compares against a digest that no longer matches the installed assets, even though they are effectively equivalent.

A fix might be: when `gentle-ai sync` runs, walk all open lineages and update their bound expected asset digest, OR run `gentle-ai sync` automatically before each capture execution.

title: bug(review): fresh Pi START immediately reports consent binding expired on 3.1.0
body:
## Summary

On Gentle AI 3.1.0, a fresh ordinary Pi review START immediately returns `consent-binding-expired` after a negotiated fresh-target status. No valid consent envelope is returned for a human answer.

## Environment

- Gentle AI: 3.1.0 stable
- Client: Pi coding agent
- Contract: review integration v2
- OS: Linux x86_64

## Reproduction

1. Prepare a committed-only candidate and inspect review status.
2. Confirm the native transition is fresh `review.start`.
3. Start ordinary review through the Pi controller.
4. Observe an immediate `consent-binding-expired` outcome.
5. Confirm `native_invocation_attempted: false`, `lineage_created: false`, and no repository mutation.
6. Fresh inspection still reports the candidate ready for review.
7. Repeat once with a new START request; observe the same immediate expiration.

## Expected

A fresh START should either create review authority or return a valid candidate-scoped consent envelope that can be answered exactly once.

## Actual

Fresh START returns an already-expired consent binding before native invocation. The candidate stays unreviewed and review cannot begin.

## Relation to prior report

Related to #2135, but this is a distinct later symptom on 3.1.0: expiration occurs immediately at START, before any consent answer is available.

## Privacy

This report intentionally excludes repository names, paths, user names, host names, source contents, diffs, credentials, environment values, opaque bindings, target identities, and raw command arguments.

title: bug(update): multiline GitHub token output breaks all update checks
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

`gentle-ai update` fails every GitHub-backed update check when the token source contains more than one line. The immediate error is:

```
net/http: invalid header field value for "Authorization"
```

`resolveGitHubToken()` in `internal/update/github.go` applies `strings.TrimSpace()` to `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`, and the stdout of `gh auth token`. This removes surrounding whitespace but preserves internal newlines. `doGitHubRequest()` then uses the complete value in the `Authorization` header, which Go rejects before sending the request.

This was observed on Omarchy, where a stale stock wrapper generated by `omarchy-mise-install` runs `mise use -g "gh"` before the real command. That mise invocation writes a status line to stdout, so `gh auth token` returns the mise status plus the token. Omarchy tracks the wrapper behavior in [basecamp/omarchy#7426](https://github.com/basecamp/omarchy/issues/7426), and corrected its current wrapper generator with `mise use -g --quiet` in [basecamp/omarchy#6940](https://github.com/basecamp/omarchy/pull/6940). Existing generated wrappers can remain stale.

Although Omarchy exposed the problem, the same failure can be produced by any multiline `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `GH_TOKEN`. The missing invariant is that values used in HTTP headers must be validated as single-line, header-safe tokens.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Place a `gh` wrapper earlier in the effective `PATH` that prints a line before delegating:

   ```sh
   #!/bin/sh
   echo "wrapper notice: resolved toolchain"
   exec /usr/bin/gh "$@"
   ```

2. Confirm that `gh auth token` now produces the notice and token on separate lines.
3. Run `gentle-ai update`.
4. Observe that every GitHub-backed check fails with `invalid header field value for "Authorization"`.
5. Remove the wrapper from the effective `PATH`, or provide a valid single-line `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and rerun the command. The update checks work again.

The same class can be reproduced directly with a multiline environment variable:

```sh
export GITHUB_TOKEN='invalid
second-line'
gentle-ai update
```

### ✅ Expected Behavior

An unusable token source should not break update discovery. `gentle-ai` should only use a single-line, header-safe token. If a candidate token is unsafe, it should be ignored and the existing unauthenticated request path should continue, as it already does when `gh` is unavailable.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The multiline value is inserted verbatim into the `Authorization` header. Go rejects the header before sending the request, all checked tools report `latest: -`, and no available update can be offered.

### Gentle AI Version

v3.0.0 installed; defective code confirmed on `main` at `e7729359fd9d`

### Operating System

Linux (Arch/Manjaro)

### AI Agent / Client

Other — Pi

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
$ gentle-ai update
Update Check
============

  [!!] gentle-ai     installed: 3.0.0    latest: -    check failed: github API request failed: Get "https://api.github.com/repos/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/releases/latest": net/http: invalid header field value for "Authorization"
  [!!] engram        installed: 1.20.0   latest: -    check failed: github API request failed: Get "https://api.github.com/repos/Gentleman-Programming/engram/releases?per_page=100": net/http: invalid header field value for "Authorization"

Update check incomplete: 5 tool(s) failed to check.
Error: update check failed for: gentle-ai, engram, gga, opencode-subagent-statusline, opencode-sdd-engram-manage
```

### Additional Context

The defect is present in `resolveGitHubToken()` and `doGitHubRequest()` in `internal/update/github.go`.

A strict fix would validate all three token sources (`GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`, and `gh auth token`) before header construction. Empty, multiline, whitespace-containing, control-character, or non-ASCII candidates should be treated as unavailable so the request proceeds unauthenticated. Selecting the last non-empty line would be less safe because it guesses which line is the credential.

Suggested regression coverage:

1. Reject multiline stdout from a stubbed successful `gh auth token` invocation.
2. Reject unsafe values from both token environment variables.
3. Verify that an unsafe token still permits the request without an `Authorization` header.

title: gentle-pi 3.2.0 facade: START consent/v3 undecodable + capture rejects CLI-started lineage bindings
body:
## Summary

Pure-facade RDD review flow (`gentle-pi` Pi tools) dead-ends on native `3.2.1`: facade `START` cannot decode the `consent/v3` envelope (`schema-incompatible`, no `consentBinding` issued), and after completing `START` via the exact CLI invocation from the `inspect` binding, facade `status` works but both capture tools reject the returned `collectBindings` ("unknown, expired, or belongs to a different session route"). A third, smaller finding: the facade masks the typed `managed_assets_outdated` failure envelope as `schema-incompatible` instead of surfacing its `next_action`/`continuation`.

## Environment

- `gentle-ai 3.2.1` (homebrew `gentleman-programming/tap/gentle-ai`, linux amd64)
- `gentle-pi 3.2.0` (npm latest at time of writing)
- Pi `0.85.1`, agent `pi`
- Worktree review: `--base-ref <40-hex>` + `--committed-only`, `--projection workspace`, contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, 20 files / 1381 lines, tier medium, 1 lens (`review-reliability`)

## Bug 1 — facade START cannot decode `consent/v3`

1. `gentle_review { operation: inspect, workspaceRoot }` → `ready`, `action: start`, `reason_code: fresh_target_ready`, lineage `review-529472b638c60b55`.
2. `gentle_review { operation: start, input: {"mode":"ordinary","baseRef":"<40-hex>","committedOnly":true}, idempotencyKey }` → `blocked`, `native-operation-failed`, `schema-incompatible`, `lineage_created: false`.
3. Same native START via CLI (exact tokens from the `inspect` `next_transition.execute`, `--consent relay`) exits 0 with a well-formed `gentle-ai.review-integration.consent/v3` envelope (`action: consent_required`, `risk_level: medium`, two choices `granted`/`declined`, `off_path` note).

Expected: facade relays the consent envelope with a `consentBinding` so `answer-consent` can proceed. Actual: `schema-incompatible` with no binding — pure-facade flow cannot pass consent on native 3.2.1. (Note: the envelope carries `choices[].invocation` but no top-level opaque consent binding field; possibly the decoder expects a shape native no longer emits.)

## Bug 2 — facade capture rejects bindings for a CLI-started lineage

After answering `granted` via the envelope's exact CLI invocation, native `review.start` returns `start/v4`, `action: created`, `state: reviewing` (same lineage id). Facade `status` then works and returns one `collectBinding` (`review-reliability`, materialize reviewer). But:

- `gentle_review_capture_group { lineageId, collectBindings: [<exact status binding>] }` → `capture-group-rejected`: "collectBindings are unknown, expired, or belong to different session routes".
- `gentle_review_capture { lineageId, collectBinding: <exact status binding> }` (fresh binding from a new `status`) → `capture-binding-rejected`, same reason.

The repository-context handle was stable across calls (not a single-use rotation issue). Hypothesis: the facade capture route requires the lineage to have been started through the facade session, but facade START can never succeed while Bug 1 exists — a Catch-22 for this candidate.

Expected: either capture accepts provider-issued bindings for a live lineage regardless of which surface performed START, or `status` clearly marks the lineage as foreign to the facade session with the supported migration path.

## Bug 3 — typed `managed_assets_outdated` failure masked as `schema-incompatible`

Before `gentle-ai sync --agent pi`, the same CLI START exited 1 with a typed `gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2` envelope: `code: managed_assets_outdated`, `retry_safe: true`, `next_action: stop`, `continuation: { operation: sync, command: "gentle-ai sync --agent pi", stale_assets: [...] }`. The facade reported only `schema-incompatible` for the same operation, hiding the actionable `sync` continuation (which resolved it — sync changed 3 skill files and the next native START reached consent).

Expected: facade surfaces typed failure envelopes (code, `retry_safe`, `continuation`) instead of generic `schema-incompatible`.

## Repro

```bash
# 1. outdated assets (or fresh install pre-sync) + base-ref review:
gentle-ai review start --cwd=<worktree> --contract=gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 \
  --target=<sha256> --target-evidence=<v1:...> --projection=workspace \
  --base-ref=<40-hex> --committed-only=true --lineage=<id> --agent=pi --consent=relay
# → failure/v2 managed_assets_outdated (facade: schema-incompatible)
gentle-ai sync --agent pi
# → same START now returns consent/v3 (facade: still schema-incompatible)
# → answer granted via CLI → start/v4 created
# → facade status OK, facade capture / capture_group reject bindings
```

## Impact

Any Pi user on `gentle-ai ≥ 3.2.1` + `gentle-pi 3.2.0` doing a base-ref (`committedOnly`) ordinary review cannot complete RDD purely through the facade: consent is undecodable, and the CLI fallback produces a lineage the facade won't capture for.

title: bug(review): negotiated OpenCode review.start target evidence mismatches target identity on 3.1.0 stable
body:
### 📝 Bug Description
Gentle AI 3.1.0 stable rejects its own provider-negotiated review.start request during preflight for a current OpenCode workspace candidate. The selectorless status operation returns a target identity and target-evidence token intended for the exact next transition; invoking that exact transition with the granted candidate-scoped consent returns invalid_request before review mutation or authority evaluation because the target-evidence does not hash to the negotiated target identity. Review cannot start for this candidate, despite the candidate being unchanged and the request being provider-issued.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce
1. On macOS arm64 with Gentle AI 3.1.0 stable and OpenCode, prepare a current workspace candidate with three modified frontend files.
2. Run the selectorless native status operation for `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2` with `--agent opencode --next-transition`.
3. Execute the exact provider-issued `review.start` command returned by `next_transition`, selecting candidate-scoped review consent `granted`.
4. Observe preflight rejection before the review transaction starts.

### ✅ Expected Behavior
The exact provider-negotiated `review.start` invocation should accept its matching target identity and target-evidence, create the review transaction, and return the next provider-owned review transition.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
The exact provider-issued invocation is rejected with:
`The negotiated review request is invalid. [invalid_request]`
Cause:
`review start --target-evidence does not hash to --target; the token and the identity come from different negotiations`
Mutation outcome is `not_started`; authority applicability is `not_evaluated`.

### Gentle AI Version
3.1.0 stable

### Operating System
macOS

### AI Agent / Client
OpenCode

### Affected Area
CLI (commands, flags)

### Logs / Error Output
```shell
schema: gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2
contract: gentle-ai.review-integration/v2
operation: review.start
phase: preflight
code: invalid_request
mutation_outcome: not_started
authority_applicability: not_evaluated
cause: review start --target-evidence does not hash to --target; the token and the identity come from different negotiations
```

### Additional Context
Candidate-local checks passed before this attempt: focused tests (3 files, 27 tests), typecheck, lint, and diff check. Candidate state was preserved and no review mutation, authority, receipt, or delivery action was created. The failure is reproducible at the negotiated start boundary; no source content, credentials, private paths, account names, or environment values are included here.

title: [Automated provider defect] Claude Code: the four collect-returned capture-result slots refuse when launched concurrently as the contract mandates, and admit when serialized; one empty capture then strands the lineage on a fieldless native_stop_required (3.0.1 stable)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues, open and closed. Closest prior art is listed under "Relationship to prior art"; none covers this observable defect.
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### Bug Description

Automated provider-defect report filed after the operator consented. **Observed behavior only; no root cause is asserted.**

On `gentle-ai 3.0.1` (stable channel — the build string carries no `-rc.` or `-main.` tag), a negotiated high-risk workspace review on the `claude-code` runtime selected four lenses. The bound STATUS returned a `collect` transition with four independent `review.capture-result` slots.

**The four captures refuse when launched concurrently, and admit when the identical operations are run one at a time.** The contract's Concurrent Reviewer Group rule instructs the adapter to launch every returned capture operation concurrently in provider order, so following it deterministically refuses.

### Environment

- gentle-ai: `3.0.1` (stable channel)
- OS/architecture: macOS (Darwin) arm64
- Client: Claude Code, in-process reviewer transport (`--agent claude-code`, no `--input`)
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`
- Projection: `workspace`, `current-changes`, 10 changed files / 334 changed lines
- Risk tier: `high`; lenses `review-risk`, `review-resilience`, `review-readability`, `review-reliability`
- Correction budget: 167

### Observed behavior

**Observation 1 — concurrent capture refuses; sequential capture admits.**

Four attempts, same lineage, same frozen revision:

| # | Form | `--cwd` passed | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4 captures launched concurrently | no (process cwd was the repository root, verified) | all 4 refused |
| 2 | 1 capture, sequential | yes | **admitted** (`admission_decision: completed`) |
| 3 | 3 captures launched concurrently | yes | all 3 refused |
| 4 | 3 captures, sequential | yes | 2 admitted, 1 returned empty stdout + exit 1 |

Every refusal was byte-identical in shape:

```json
{
  "schema": "gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2",
  "operation": "review.capture-result",
  "phase": "preflight",
  "code": "invalid_request",
  "message": "The negotiated review request is invalid.",
  "mutation_outcome": "not_started",
  "authority_applicability": "not_evaluated",
  "retry_safe": true,
  "replayability": "not_replayable",
  "required_inputs": [],
  "next_action": "correct_request",
  "cause": "review capture-result requires an exact repository context, --lineage, --target, --lens, --order, and either --input or --agent (or --preflight); ..."
}
```

The cause names flags that **were all supplied**. `gentle-ai review capture-result --preflight` on the same binding (same lineage, revision, target, repository-context, lens, order, subject-hash) returned a valid `gentle-ai.review-capture-preflight/v1` envelope with the full changed-path manifest, confirming the binding itself is well-formed.

Attempts 1 and 3 differ only in whether `--cwd` was passed explicitly; both refused. Attempt 2 used the same flags as attempt 3 and admitted. The only variable that tracks the outcome is concurrent vs. sequential launch.

**Observation 2 — one sequential capture returned empty stdout and exit 1.**

The fourth lens (`review-reliability`, order 3) produced **no output at all** and exited 1. No typed envelope, no failure schema, nothing on stdout or stderr.

**Observation 3 — the lineage then went terminal with no diagnostic, discarding three admitted lens results.**

Re-querying the bound STATUS after the empty capture, exactly as the contract prescribes, returned:

```json
{ "kind": "stop", "reason_code": "native_stop_required" }
```

The transition carries **no other fields** — no message, no cause, no state, no lineage id, no continuation. Per the contract's stop table, `native_stop_required` is terminal: "maintainer inspects authority/lineage, or disable review for the clone."

Three lens results had already been admitted (`review-risk`, `review-resilience`, `review-readability`). They are discarded with no sanctioned exit for the candidate short of disabling review for the clone.

### Expected behavior

1. Either the four returned capture slots can be executed concurrently as the Concurrent Reviewer Group rule instructs, or the returned transition declares that they must be serialized.
2. A refusal whose `cause` lists required flags should not fire when every listed flag is supplied and `--preflight` validates the same binding.
3. A capture that fails should emit its typed failure envelope rather than empty output with exit 1.
4. A terminal stop should carry enough diagnostic to act on, and should not silently discard already-admitted lens results.

### Actual behavior

Following the contract's mandated concurrent launch deterministically refuses (7 refusals across 2 batches, 0 successes). Serializing works until one capture returns empty, after which the lineage goes terminal with an empty `native_stop_required` and the admitted results are unrecoverable.

### Minimal reproduction

1. Enable receipt-driven review; stage a change that classifies `high` with 4 lenses selected.
2. Run the selectorless STATUS preflight, then the returned START with `--consent granted`.
3. From the returned `collect` transition, launch all four `review.capture-result` operations **concurrently** with `--agent claude-code`.
4. Observe all four refuse with `invalid_request` / `phase: preflight` / `mutation_outcome: not_started`.
5. Run the same operations one at a time; observe they admit.
6. If any sequential capture returns empty with exit 1, re-query the bound STATUS and observe terminal `native_stop_required` with no other fields.

### Evidence

- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`
- Failure schema: `gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2`
- Preflight schema that validated the same binding: `gentle-ai.review-capture-preflight/v1`
- Result artifact schema on the admitted captures: `gentle-ai.review-result-artifact/v2`, `admission_decision: "completed"`
- Mutation outcome on every refusal: `not_started` (no repository or authority mutation occurred)
- No source mutation, no receipt, no acknowledgement, and no delivery authority were created.

### Relationship to prior art

Searched open and closed issues. Adjacent but, on the evidence, **not the same observable defect**:

- **#4696** — `claude-code` capture-result rejects the provider-issued rctx2 context on initial lens collection. There the refusal is `repository_context_unavailable` / `invalid rctx2 repository context`, and STATUS reissues a handle capture-result rejects. Here the repository context is accepted (`--preflight` validates it and sequential captures admit with it); the refusal is `invalid_request` naming flags that were supplied, and it tracks concurrency.
- **#4708** — capture-result refuses with the same envelope shape (`invalid_request` / `preflight` / `not_started` / `retry_safe: true`), but its `cause` is a claude reviewer transport permission refusal (`CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB`). Here the reviewer transport is reached and succeeds when serialized.
- **#4746** — in-process capture admits and advances the lineage yet exits with a failure envelope. Here the refusing captures never started (`mutation_outcome: not_started`).
- **#4704** — reviewing lineage goes terminal `corrupted_or_unverifiable_authority` after an admitted capture, with the reoffered START refusing `candidate_context_unavailable`. Here the terminal reason code is `native_stop_required`, the stop carries no fields at all, and it follows an **empty** capture rather than an admitted one.

title: [Automated provider defect] Claude Code: in-process capture-result admits the result and advances the lineage to approved, yet exits with invalid_request / repository_context_capture_failed "capture binding does not match the current reviewing authority" (3.1.0 stable)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate (closest family: #2411 and #4027, both closed; there the capture genuinely failed before persisting — here the result **was** admitted and the lineage advanced, but the command still exited with a failure envelope)
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

Automated provider-defect report, privacy-scrubbed (no paths, project names or hosts).

### Environment

- gentle-ai: `3.1.0` (stable channel, `gentle-ai --version`)
- OS/architecture: macOS (Darwin) arm64
- Client: Claude Code `2.1.276`, in-process reviewer transport (`--agent claude-code`, no `--input`)
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`
- Projection: `workspace`, candidate `base-diff` with `--committed-only=true`
- Review risk: `medium`, one selected lens (`review-reliability`)
- Lineage (opaque): `review-123a331a28296487`

### Operation shape and observed outcomes (all commands run verbatim as issued by the provider)

1. Selectorless STATUS → `next_transition.execute` = START (`--consent=relay`).
2. START → `gentle-ai.review-integration.consent/v3`; the human answered `granted`; the granted invocation returned `start/v4` `replayed` / `reviewing`, `selected_lenses: ["review-reliability"]`, with a bound `review.status` continuation.
3. Bound STATUS → `collect` / `reviewer_results_required` with one `review.capture-result` input (`--lens=review-reliability --order=0`, exact `--expected-revision`, `--target`, `--subject-hash`, `--repository-context`, `--agent=claude-code`).
4. `review.capture-result` run once with exactly those tokens. Wall time consistent with a full reviewer run. **Exit: failure envelope**:

```json
{
  "schema": "gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2",
  "operation": "review.capture-result",
  "phase": "preflight",
  "code": "invalid_request",
  "message": "The negotiated review request is invalid.",
  "mutation_outcome": "not_started",
  "authority_applicability": "not_evaluated",
  "retry_safe": true,
  "next_action": "correct_request",
  "cause": "repository_context_capture_failed: provider-issued review repository context operation failed; cause: capture binding does not match the current reviewing authority; retry capture-result with the same exact binding or refresh status"
}
```

5. Following the contract (refresh the exact-lineage STATUS after a failed capture, relaunch only if the same slot is reoffered): the bound STATUS returned `execute` / `approved_acknowledgement_required` with a `review.acknowledge-approved` command carrying a **new** `--expected-revision` and a token. The slot was **not** reoffered.
6. The acknowledgement ran once and returned `gentle-ai.review-acknowledged/v1` `acknowledged`, `authority: burned`.

Earlier in the same session, an identical lifecycle on a different lineage (same build, same client, same lens) returned `gentle-ai.review-last-event-closure/v1` with `state: approved` and the acknowledgement command directly from `capture-result`, i.e. the success path exists and worked minutes before.

### Expected

`capture-result` either persists/admits the result and returns the success/closure envelope, or fails without admitting. Its reported outcome should match the lineage state.

### Actual

The reviewer ran, the result was admitted and the lineage advanced to `approved` (the very next bound STATUS offered the acknowledgement and the acknowledgement burned the authority), but the command reported `phase: preflight`, `mutation_outcome: not_started`, `code: invalid_request` with a binding-mismatch cause. `retry_safe: true` and `next_action: correct_request` would have led a host that trusts the envelope to retry a capture against a lineage that was already approved. The mismatch message looks like a post-admission repository-context step comparing against the revision that the admission itself had just rotated.

### Minimal reproduction (as observed; not deterministic in one attempt)

1. `gentle-ai review status --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --agent claude-code --next-transition` on a committed-only, single-lens (`medium`) workspace candidate.
2. Run the returned START, answer the consent with `granted`, run the bound STATUS.
3. Run the single offered `review.capture-result` verbatim (in-process, `--agent claude-code`).
4. Compare the command's envelope with the next bound STATUS.

### Preserved state

No retry was attempted; no substitute command; the lineage closed through the provider-issued acknowledgement. No data loss observed.

title: [Automated provider defect] Claude Code: review finding + targeted validator both misread a template literal's fixed segment as conditionally derived, rejecting a verified-passing correction (3.1.0)
body:
## Summary

A `review-reliability` lens finding, and the subsequent `review.capture-validation` targeted validator, both asserted a factually incorrect claim about how a helper function's output filename is constructed, and rejected a verified-passing correction on that basis.

## Environment

- gentle-ai 3.1.0 (stable channel, no `-rc.`/`-main.` tag)
- OS/arch: macOS (Darwin), arm64
- Client: Claude Code (`--agent claude-code`)
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`

## Operation shape

1. A `review.capture-result` (lens `review-reliability`) raised a `BLOCKER` finding claiming that a JS helper's output filename "cannot contain" a specific hardcoded literal prefix once a caller starts passing an already-normalized string instead of a raw string that the helper itself normalizes internally (a no-op for already-normalized input).
2. In reality, the helper builds its filename with a template literal where that prefix is a **fixed string constant**, independent of the input's own shape — e.g. `` `PREFIX_${normalize(input)}_SUFFIX.csv` ``. The prefix always appears regardless of whether `input` was raw or pre-normalized.
3. I submitted a `review.capture-correction-plan` that added an equivalence test proving both call shapes (raw vs. pre-normalized input) produce identical output filenames.
4. `review.capture-validation` (`--execute=true`) rejected the correction (`state: "escalated"`, `escalation.cause: "targeted_validator_rejected"`), repeating the same incorrect claim: that a *pre-existing* assertion in the same test file "cannot produce a filename containing the \[prefix\]" and that the test suite "would already fail" before reaching the new lines.

## Actual vs. expected

- **Actual**: the targeted validator's `original_criteria.passed: false` rests entirely on the claim that the pre-existing assertion is unsatisfiable.
- **Expected**: the validator should evaluate the claim against the real, executable behavior of the code, not restate an unverified premise from the original finding as settled fact.

## Independent verification (minimal repro shape)

I ran the exact test file the validator's evidence cites, against the exact committed HEAD the validator was scoped to, multiple times:

```
30 passed, 30 total
```

including the specific test the validator says "would already fail first." This was reproduced consistently across repeated runs, not a flake.

## Mutation outcome

No regression: the submitted correction was purely additive (new test lines appended after existing ones, no deletion/weakening of any existing assertion, mock, or production code — confirmed by the validator's own `correction_regression.passed: true` block, which contradicts its own `original_criteria.passed: false` conclusion).

## Preserved state

- `lineage_id`: opaque, session-scoped (available on request through the reporting session if needed)
- `state`: `escalated`
- `escalation.cause`: `targeted_validator_rejected`
- `original_criteria.passed`: `false`
- `correction_regression.passed`: `true`

## Suspected root cause (unconfirmed)

The reviewing lens and/or the targeted validator appear to reason about string-template construction as if every segment of the output were conditionally derived from the input's own prefix, rather than distinguishing a template's fixed literal segments from its interpolated segments. This would produce false-positive "naming scheme regression" claims for any helper that hardcodes part of its output format.

title: [Automated provider defect] Claude Code: capture-validation refuses the provider's own targeted validator output on both admission attempts — json: unknown field "proof_refs" (3.0.2 stable, contains #4058 and #4076)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues, open and closed, and this is not a duplicate. The closest prior art is listed under "Relationship to prior art" below; none covers a `capture-validation` run on a build containing both #4058 and #4076 where **both** admission attempts fail and the lineage is left with no exit.
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

Automated provider-defect report filed after the operator consented. Observed behavior only; no root cause is asserted.

On `gentle-ai 3.0.2` (stable channel — the build string carries no `-rc.` or `-main.` tag), a compact-v2 review on the `claude-code` runtime reached `targeted_validation_required` after a bounded correction. The exact provider-issued command was run verbatim:

```
gentle-ai review capture-validation --lineage=<id> --expected-revision=<sha> --target=<sha> \
  --repository-context=<rctx2> --request-hash=<sha> --agent=claude-code --execute=true
```

Native admission refused the in-process targeted validator's own output on **both** attempts of a single invocation:

```
provider reviewer result was refused on both admission attempts:
  attempt 1: targeted-validator provider result admission incomplete:
             reviewer payload contains no complete JSON object:
             no object start was found in 45 bytes
  corrective attempt 2: decode provider targeted validator result:
             json: unknown field "proof_refs"
[provider_capture_result_refused]
```

Both rejected payloads were preserved under `<repo>/gentle-ai/rejected-results/<lineage>/targeted-validator-{1,2}-<hash>.json`, as #4076 intends.

### Why this is filed against a build that already contains the prior fixes

The two closed issues in this area were both fixed and published well before this build:

| Issue | Closing PR | Merged | First stable release containing it |
|---|---|---|---|
| #4053 — validator output refused on a stray field (`passed_note_unused`) | #4058 `fix(review): harden targeted validator admission` | 2026-09-02 | v2.6.0 (2026-09-04) |
| #4061 — validator returns a truncated JSON payload | #4076 `fix(review): retry a malformed targeted validator result once with admission feedback and preserve the refused payloads` | 2026-09-02 | v2.6.0 (2026-09-04) |

The installed build (3.0.2, released 2026-09-16) therefore demonstrably contains both. The #4076 retry mechanism is visibly working — the corrective second attempt ran and both payloads were preserved — but it did not recover the run, because the second attempt failed on a *different* cause than the first.

### Expected vs actual

**Expected:** either the provider constrains its own targeted validator to the wire schema, or admission tolerates unknown top-level fields it does not need, so that a completed validator run is not discarded. Failing that, the lineage should offer an exit rather than an indefinitely reoffered slot.

**Actual:** the strict decoder rejects the provider's own validator output on an unknown top-level field (`proof_refs`), the one corrective retry lands on the other failure mode, and the bound STATUS then reoffers the identical `capture-validation` slot indefinitely with nothing for the operator to correct — the request tokens were the exact provider-issued ones and the rejected bytes were produced in-process by the provider's own validator.

### Minimal reproduction shape

1. `claude-code` runtime, stable 3.0.2, `--projection=workspace`.
2. Medium-risk candidate, single lens (`review-reliability`), one `CRITICAL` inferential finding.
3. Grant consent, capture the lens result; the transaction opens `correction_required`.
4. Apply the bounded correction, then `capture-correction-plan` with `--correction-lines`.
5. STATUS returns `targeted_validation_required`; run the returned `capture-validation` tokens verbatim.
6. Observed: `provider_capture_result_refused` with the two attempt causes above. Re-querying STATUS reoffers the identical slot; a verbatim relaunch reproduces it.

### Observed evidence

- Build: `gentle-ai 3.0.2`, stable channel.
- OS / architecture: Darwin, arm64.
- Runtime / agent: `claude-code`, in-process capture (tokens carried `--agent`, no `--input`).
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`.
- Operation: `review.capture-validation`, `--execute=true`.
- Failure envelope: `code: provider_capture_result_refused`, `phase: preflight`, `mutation_outcome: not_started`, `authority_applicability: not_evaluated`, `retry_safe: true`, `next_action: review.status`, `required_inputs: []`.
- Preceding attempt on the same slot returned `code: invalid_request`, `cause: admitted targeted-validator evidence does not match its request and digests`, `next_action: correct_request`.
- Attempts and outcomes: STATUS → reoffered identical slot → verbatim relaunch → refused again. No blind retry beyond the single contract-sanctioned relaunch.
- Preserved-state evidence: both refused validator payloads written under the lineage's `rejected-results/` directory; no mutation, no receipt, no tombstone created.

### Relationship to prior art

- **#4053** (closed, fixed by #4058) — same operation, same contract, same observable defect class: the strict decoder refuses the provider's own validator output on an unknown top-level field. Different field (`passed_note_unused` vs `proof_refs`), and there the reoffered retry recovered the run. Filed as a possible regression rather than reopening.
- **#4061** (closed, fixed by #4076) — same operation, truncated-payload variant, matching attempt 1 here. There the retry recovered; here the retry itself is what fails.
- **#4596** (open) — same strict-decoder / unknown-field class on `capture-refuter` rather than `capture-validation`, on 2.9.0, where the re-offered retry was admitted. Sibling class on a different operation.
- **#4386** (open) — `capture-validation` unadmittable on claude-code 2.7.0, but because the validator emitted prose instead of JSON; different cause.

### Privacy note

Repository identity, paths, project names, account names and all candidate source content are deliberately omitted. Version, platform, contract, operation shape, typed envelope fields and opaque lineage identifiers are included as observed.

title: feat(review): scope risk classification to the delta since the last acknowledged candidate, not the full base-diff
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate (closest related: #4390, but that one is about an *unchanged* candidate being re-reminded after acknowledgement in the same session — this report is about a candidate that *did* change, trivially, and still re-triggers full high-risk review)
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags) — specifically `gentle-ai review status` / `review start` risk classification for `base-diff` projections.

### 💡 Problem Statement

`review status`/`review start`'s risk classification for a `projection: workspace`, `kind: base-diff` candidate is computed over the **entire diff since the branch point** (`base_ref`), not over the delta since the last *approved and acknowledged* candidate on that same lineage. This means that once a large, high-risk change has already been reviewed and acknowledged (`authority: burned`), adding one more commit that only touches an unrelated, low-risk file (in our case, a passive markdown progress-tracking doc) causes the *entire accumulated diff* to be re-classified from scratch — including files that were already reviewed and approved — and it lands back on `high` risk with 4 lenses required, because an already-approved file (an auth-related test) is still part of the cumulative diff.

Concretely: every already-reviewed byte gets re-judged again, for no reason other than an unrelated 2-line addition to a project-tracking file.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

When a lineage has an `approved` + `acknowledge-approved` (`authority: burned`) event for a given `target_identity` on a `base-diff` projection, and a *later* commit changes the candidate identity, consider computing risk (and, if the diff qualifies as low-risk, skipping the consent/lens cycle) over the **delta between the last acknowledged target_identity's tree and the new candidate tree**, rather than over the full `base_ref..candidate` diff every time.

Concretely, something like:
- Track, per lineage, the tree of the last acknowledged `target_identity`.
- On a new STATUS/START call for that same lineage, if a prior acknowledgement exists, compute `risk_evidence` and the low/passive fast-path from `last_acknowledged_tree..candidate_tree` instead of `base_ref..candidate_tree`.
- The full `base_ref..candidate_tree` diff would still be the one actually reviewed/recorded for provenance, but the *risk classification that decides whether a human even gets asked* should reflect what's actually new since the last acknowledgement.

I don't have visibility into the internal architecture (how lineages/authority/base-diff projections are actually modeled in the Go core), so this is a suggestion from the observed behavior, not a prescribed implementation.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- A narrower fix scoped just to our trigger: exclude project-tracking/task files (e.g. a configurable glob like `odd/tasks/**`) from risk classification entirely, so edits to them never re-trigger a review on their own. This would help our specific case but wouldn't fix the general problem (any trivial addition to *any* already-low-risk file re-triggers full re-classification of the whole accumulated diff).
- Doing nothing and just declining the review each time it re-triggers on a doc-only commit (what we did) — works, but means real signal (an actually-changed high-risk file) and no-signal (an unrelated doc tweak) look identical to the person being asked, session after session.

### 📎 Additional Context

**Environment:** Windows 11, Claude Code, `gentle-ai review` with RDD (Receipt-Driven Development) enabled, `contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`.

**Steps that led to this:**

1. Branch `feature/us-11-api-client`, diverged from `main` at commit `e601a886...`.
2. Multiple commits accumulated on the branch implementing a feature (HTTP client + error handling, ~30 files, ~1000 lines).
3. Ran the full review lifecycle: selectorless STATUS → provider-issued START → consent `granted` (risk `high`, 32 files, 1010 lines) → 4 lenses captured (`review-risk`, `review-resilience`, `review-readability`, `review-reliability`) → `state: approved` → ran the exact `review.acknowledge-approved` command returned → `"authority": "burned"`.
4. Made **one more commit** on the same branch, changing **only** a single markdown progress-tracking file (`odd/tasks/us-11-api-client.md`) — 2 lines added, a link to the just-opened PR. No source, test, or config file touched.
5. On the next turn, the `Stop` hook fired again: `review stop-hook` reported an "unreviewed candidate" and returned a new provider-issued START for a *new* `target_identity` (expected — the tree did change).
6. Ran that START. It came back `risk_level: high`, `changed_files: 32`, `changed_lines: 1012` (1010 + the 2 new lines), with `risk_evidence: ["authentication in src/features/auth/cambiarClave.test.ts"]` — **the exact same file already reviewed and approved two steps earlier**, now re-flagged as the reason for a fresh high-risk, 4-lens review cycle.

We ended up declining that second review, since the only actual new content was the 2-line doc addition, and everything else had already gone through a full 4-lens approved review moments earlier.

**Illustrative excerpt from the second START's consent response:**

```json
{
  "risk_level": "high",
  "changed_files": 32,
  "changed_lines": 1012,
  "risk_evidence": [
    "authentication in src/features/auth/cambiarClave.test.ts"
  ]
}
```

That `src/features/auth/cambiarClave.test.ts` file was untouched by the new commit — it was part of the diff approved and acknowledged in the *previous* review cycle on the very same lineage family.

### Gentle AI Version / Agent

Observed on the current stable release as of 2026-09-17, with Claude Code as the driving agent, `contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, `projection: workspace` / `kind: base-diff`.

title: bug(review): foreground Pi sessions have no automatic RDD-status visibility, and Engram proactive saves never trigger unless asked
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

During a real Pi coding session (not a background/orchestrator flow — a single foreground agent doing direct implementation work), the agent implemented, tested, committed, opened a PR for, and **merged** a non-trivial change to a private application repository entirely without ever invoking the RDD review gate (`gentle_review` / the native `gentle-ai review …` CLI), even though **global RDD is `on`** for this machine.

When asked directly afterwards ("did you use RDD?"), the agent reported it had not, and explained why: it had looked for a **repository-local** `openspec/config.yaml` (there was none) and concluded RDD was "not configured for this repo" — it never checked the **global** native CLI state (`gentle-ai review mode status --json`) at all. Only after the user pushed further ("is it RDD?") did the agent run that command and discover:

```json
{
  "schema": "gentle-ai.rdd-mode-status/v1",
  "global": "on",
  "clone_local": "",
  "effective": "on",
  "source": "global"
}
```

Tracing this in `gentle-pi`'s own extension source (`extensions/gentle-ai.ts`) shows the likely root cause: `resolveRddStatusLine`/`renderRddStatusLine` (the mechanism that renders the current RDD line into a prompt) is only wired into **background-subagent orchestrator prompts** (`getOrchestratorPrompt`). There is no equivalent injection into a **foreground/primary** session's own system prompt or any session-start hook. So a foreground agent doing direct work — exactly the case where the commit/PR/merge gate matters most — has **zero automatic visibility** into the effective RDD line and must proactively think to shell out and check it itself. This directly contradicts the shipped skill text (`gentle-ai-rdd-defect-workflow` / the `gentle-ai` skill's "Gentle AI RDD Ownership" section), which states: *"Gentle AI dynamically supplies runtime-specific RDD instructions at runtime. Treat them as the sole lifecycle authority."* In practice, nothing was dynamically supplied to the foreground session at all.

A second, related gap surfaced in the same session: **Engram was never used proactively**. The agent made at least two non-trivial decisions mid-session (a design workaround for a third-party library's missing per-record delete filter, and a merge-blocking bug fix surfaced by an independent post-merge review) and called `mem_save` **zero times** for either, despite:
- Engram (`gentle-engram`) being installed and reporting healthy (`mem_doctor` → `status: ok`, 0 warnings/errors).
- The very same project's memory history (visible in the session's own `SessionStart` recall) showing this exact kind of proactive `[decision]`/`[discovery]` capture happening routinely in prior sessions.

This overlaps with #1907 ("mandatory protocols are not self-enforcing — agent skips proactive saves and searches unless reminded"), which already tracks the general design problem. I'm filing this as a concrete, evidenced incident (with the RDD finding from the same session, since both share the same underlying pattern: guidance that exists in skills/docs is not actually surfaced or enforced to the agent at the moment it matters) — happy to have it linked/merged into that root-cause tracking rather than treated as a separate fix if maintainers prefer.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. On a machine with **global RDD enabled** (`gentle-ai review mode status --json` → `"effective": "on", "source": "global"`) and **no** `openspec/config.yaml` in the target repository.
2. Start a Pi session (via `gentle-pi`) in that repository and ask the agent to implement a real feature end-to-end: write code + tests, run the test suite, `git commit`, push a branch, open a PR, and merge it — without explicitly telling the agent to "run RDD" or "check review mode".
3. Observe whether the agent proactively calls `gentle_review` / `gentle-ai review …` at any point before the merge.
4. In the same session, have the agent make 1–2 non-trivial architecture or bug-fix decisions, with Engram installed and healthy. Observe whether the agent proactively calls `mem_save` for any of them without being asked.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

- The effective RDD line (`on`/`off`/`unknown`, and its source: global vs. clone-local) should be surfaced to the **foreground** agent automatically — the same way it is already rendered for background-orchestrator prompts — so the agent does not need to independently discover that global RDD exists and applies here, and does not mistake "no repo-local `openspec/config.yaml`" for "RDD is off".
- Given the skill's own wording ("Gentle AI dynamically supplies runtime-specific RDD instructions at runtime. Treat them as the sole lifecycle authority"), the agent should have had that instruction available before its first commit, not only after being asked twice by the user.
- The agent should proactively persist non-trivial decisions to Engram as they happen (or the harness should more strongly nudge/enforce this), consistent with how prior sessions on the same project actually behaved.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

- The agent committed, opened a PR (#17 in the target repo), and merged it with **zero** RDD gate invocations.
- Only a direct, repeated user challenge ("did you use RDD?" → "why not?" → "is it RDD?") led the agent to run the global status check and discover RDD was `on` all along, sourced from global config, with no per-repo override needed or present.
- A follow-up native `gentle-ai review assess` run against the merged range reported `risk: "high"` (`process_boundary` on a test file) — meaning, per the harness's own risk-gated plan, an independent verifier should have run **before** merge and did not.
- Across the whole session, the agent called `mem_search` exactly once (early, no results) and `mem_save` **zero** times, despite making decisions worth capturing and Engram being fully operational.

---

## 🖥️ Environment

### Gentle AI Version

gentle-ai 3.1.0 (the `gentle-ai` CLI binary that `gentle-pi`'s native review integration shells out to — `gentle-ai review mode status --json`, `gentle-ai review assess --json`). Note: the repo's own issue template asks for `gga version`; `gga` on this machine resolves to a different, unrelated tool ("Gentleman Guardian Angel", a pre-commit-hook code reviewer, v2.10.1) — not the same binary this report is about. Flagging that mismatch in case the template question is stale.

### Operating System

macOS

### AI Agent / Client

Other

_(Pi, via the `gentle-pi` npm package, model `claude-bridge/claude-sonnet-5`, persona mode `gentleman`. None of the listed options — Claude Code, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Windsurf — accurately describe this runtime, hence "Other".)_

### 📋 Affected Area

Other

_(Spans the native review CLI's status/assess surfacing (`CLI (commands, flags)`), the `gentle-pi` extension's prompt-injection logic for foreground vs. background sessions, and Engram's proactive-capture guidance — no single listed area covers it.)_

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
$ gentle-ai review mode status --json
{
  "schema": "gentle-ai.review-mode/v1",
  "operation": "status",
  "scope": "both",
  "status": {
    "schema": "gentle-ai.rdd-mode-status/v1",
    "global": "on",
    "clone_local": "",
    "effective": "on",
    "source": "global"
  }
}

$ gentle-ai review assess --base-ref <full-commit-sha> --committed-only \
    --untracked-scope=exclude --expected-untracked-inventory=sha256:<redacted> --json
{
  "schema": "gentle-ai.review-assessment/v1",
  "risk": "high",
  "reasons": [
    { "code": "process_boundary", "path": "<app>/tests.py", "detail": "signal: shell_process" }
  ],
  "changed_paths": 4,
  "changed_lines": 305,
  "candidate": { "kind": "base-diff", "base_ref": "<full-commit-sha>" }
}

$ mem_doctor
{
  "status": "ok",
  "summary": { "total": 4, "ok": 4, "warnings": 0, "blocked": 0, "errors": 0 }
}
```

### Additional Context

- Target repository: a private client application repository (Django/Python), not open-source — paths and repo-specific identifiers have been redacted/generalized above.
- No `openspec/config.yaml` exists in that repository; this is what led the agent to (incorrectly) conclude RDD did not apply.
- `~/.pi/gentle-ai/*.json` (global config) has no explicit RDD toggle file of its own visible to the agent — the only authoritative source found was the native `gentle-ai review mode status` CLI call, which nothing prompted the agent to run proactively.
- The MCP-wrapped `gentle_review` tool's own `assess` operation, when invoked without first resolving intended-untracked/base-ref selection through its multi-step protocol, silently fails closed with `"native-assess-unavailable" / "native command returned empty output"` rather than surfacing the same clear error the raw CLI gives (`untracked files require an explicit declaration; run gentle-ai review status ...`). That mismatch made initial troubleshooting harder than it needed to be — worth a look independently of the main issue here.
- Related: #1907 (mandatory protocols are not self-enforcing).

title: feat(claude-code): emit omitClaudeMd on generated executor agents so SDD/review/JD phases stop loading the orchestrator CLAUDE.md
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Problem Statement

Every agent that `gentle-ai sync` generates for Claude Code loads the managed global `CLAUDE.md` into its own context window, including the phase executors that the managed block itself declares out of scope.

The managed orchestrator block states, verbatim:

> Bind this to the Claude Code orchestrator rule only. Do NOT apply it to executor phase agents such as `sdd-apply` or `sdd-verify`.

The instructions declare that executors must not apply them, and the executors load all of them anyway.

**Measured on gentle-ai 3.1.0 with Claude Code 2.1.270:**

| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Managed global `CLAUDE.md` | 69,185 chars / ~17,296 tokens |
| Generated agents installed | 19 (`sdd-*` x11, `review-*` x5, `jd-*` x3) |
| Generated agents carrying `omitClaudeMd` | 0 |
| All loaded skill descriptions, combined | ~1,103 tokens |

The managed `CLAUDE.md` is roughly **15.7x** the combined weight of every skill description loaded in the session, so it is the dominant always-on cost, and every subagent pays it again.

Cost measured over one user's local session history (232 sessions), counting only invocations of gentle-ai-generated agents:

```
review-reliability  26    sdd-verify           9
sdd-apply           16    sdd-archive          9
sdd-tasks           11    review-readability   9
sdd-propose         11    sdd-init             2
review-risk         11    jd-judge-a           2
review-resilience   11    jd-judge-b           2
sdd-spec            10    jd-fix-agent         2
sdd-explore         10
sdd-design          10
-------------------------------------------------
151 invocations x ~17,296 tokens = ~2.6M tokens of preamble
```

A single four-lens review pays ~69k tokens of orchestrator preamble before any lens reads a line of the candidate.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Claude Code 2.1.271 added `omitClaudeMd` to agent frontmatter, which skips the user and project `CLAUDE.md` files for that agent.

Emit it on the generated agents whose contract already excludes them from the orchestrator rules:

```yaml
---
name: sdd-apply
description: >
  Implement code changes from task definitions. ...
model: sonnet
omitClaudeMd: true
tools: Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep, Bash, ...
---
```

Suggested scope:

- **Emit `omitClaudeMd: true`**: `sdd-apply`, `sdd-verify`, `sdd-spec`, `sdd-tasks`, `sdd-design`, `sdd-propose`, `sdd-explore`, `sdd-research`, `sdd-archive`, `review-risk`, `review-resilience`, `review-readability`, `review-reliability`, `review-refuter`, `jd-judge-a`, `jd-judge-b`, `jd-fix-agent`.
- **Keep inheriting**: any agent that genuinely needs user or project conventions. `sdd-init` and `sdd-onboard` are the plausible exceptions, since they inspect and bootstrap the user's project.

Because executors lose the project conventions they legitimately need (language, stack, test runner), the phase context the orchestrator already forwards becomes the carrier for them. That forwarding is explicitly part of the current contract, which tells the orchestrator to pass the authorized scope, the resolved TDD mode, its source, and the exact test runner on every implementation delegation.

Two details worth deciding in the design:

1. **Version gate.** `omitClaudeMd` requires Claude Code >= 2.1.271. On an older client the unknown frontmatter key should be inert, but emitting it conditionally on the detected client version is safer.
2. **Opt-out.** A `sync` flag or config key for users who deliberately want executors to inherit their `CLAUDE.md` would avoid a one-way door.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

**Shrink the managed `CLAUDE.md` itself.** This is what #4241, #259, #4036, #720 and #1213 already pursue (dedup, lazy-loading, `--exclude`, `@import`). Those are worth doing and they reduce the per-load cost, but they are orthogonal: they make the block smaller, while this makes the executors stop loading it at all. Whatever size the block converges to, 151 invocations still pay it 151 times. The two compose.

**Edit the generated agent files by hand.** Not durable. `gentle-ai sync` rewrites them, so the field is lost on the next sync. This is precisely why it needs to come from the generator.

**Move the orchestrator block to a lazy-loaded skill.** Partly done already for the SDD workflow surface. It helps the orchestrator's own context, but a skill that the executor never invokes still does not explain why the executor loads the orchestrator's rules today.

### 📎 Additional Context

Verified on the reporting machine:

- `gentle-ai 3.1.0`; `strings` over the installed binary returns **0** occurrences of `omitClaudeMd`.
- Generated frontmatter for `sdd-apply` currently emits only `name`, `description`, `model`, `tools`.
- Claude Code `2.1.270` (the reporting client) predates the field; upstream is at `v2.1.274`.
- Client changelog, 2.1.271: *"Added `omitClaudeMd` to agent frontmatter to skip user/project CLAUDE.md files."*

The token figures above come from one user's local history on a single machine and are offered as an order-of-magnitude signal, not as a benchmark. The structural facts (0 of 19 agents carry the field; the managed block excludes executors in its own words) are independent of that sample.
