title: fix(doctor): mise shims and Omarchy launcher stubs are counted as duplicate copies of the same tool
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

`gentle-ai doctor` reports `tool:pi` and `tool:claude` as degraded on a mise host because every PATH entry whose basename matches the tool is counted as an independent installation. Two of those entries are dispatchers, not installations:

1. **mise shim** — `<user-home>/.local/share/mise/shims/pi` is a symlink to the mise binary itself. It dispatches into the same install directory that is also on PATH, so both entries execute the identical binary.
2. **Omarchy launcher stub** — `<user-home>/.local/bin/claude` is a generated wrapper (`omarchy-mise-install`) that runs `mise use -g <pkg>` and then `exec mise x <pkg> -- <bin> "$@"`. It is the fallback for contexts where mise never populated PATH, and Omarchy migrations recreate it.

`doctorToolCopies` dedupes copies by `filepath.EvalSymlinks` of the PATH entry. A dispatcher resolves to the dispatcher, not to the tool it dispatches to, so the dedupe cannot collapse them: the shim resolves into the mise binary and the stub resolves to itself. The result is a false duplicate report plus `Status: degraded`, even though the tool resolves to the same version through every entry.

The fix for #4141 recognizes gentle-ai's own managed launcher through its ownership marker. That does not cover third-party dispatchers such as mise shims and Omarchy wrappers, which carry no gentle-ai marker.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. On Linux, install a tool with mise (`mise use -g pi`, `mise use -g claude`). With `activate_shims = true` (the default), mise puts both the real tool bin directory and `<user-home>/.local/share/mise/shims` on PATH.
2. On Arch/Omarchy, let `omarchy-mise-install` generate `<user-home>/.local/bin/claude` (called from `install/user/mise.sh`; migrations 1784909971, 1785617047, 1785846769, 1788577553 and 1788724825 create or regenerate these wrappers).
3. Confirm that every entry runs the same version: `mise which pi`, `shims/pi --version`, `installs/pi/latest/pi/pi --version`.
4. Run `gentle-ai doctor`.
5. Observe `tool:pi` reporting 2 copies and `tool:claude` reporting 3 copies, with the overall status degraded.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Doctor should count one installation per tool when the extra PATH entries are dispatchers that resolve to the same tool: a mise shim, and a managed launcher stub that `exec`s through mise. It should either ignore those entries or report them informationally, without degrading the check and without proposing binary removal as the remedy.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Every matching PATH entry is counted as an independent copy, the health status becomes degraded, and the remedy instructs the user to delete entries that are load-bearing. Removing the shim or the stub breaks version resolution and the non-mise fallback respectively; Omarchy also recreates the stubs on later migrations.

### Gentle AI Version

3.1.0

### Operating System

Linux (Arch/Manjaro)

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

System Detection

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
[!!]  tool:pi      pi resolved to <user-home>/.local/share/mise/installs/pi/latest/pi/pi but 2 copies found in PATH: <user-home>/.local/share/mise/installs/pi/latest/pi/pi, <user-home>/.local/share/mise/shims/pi
      Remedy: Remove duplicate binaries; keep only one copy of pi in PATH
[!!]  tool:claude  claude resolved to <user-home>/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/latest/claude but 3 copies found in PATH: <user-home>/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/latest/claude, <user-home>/.local/share/mise/shims/claude, <user-home>/.local/bin/claude
      Remedy: Remove duplicate binaries; keep only one copy of claude in PATH

Summary: 7 passed, 0 failed, 2 warnings
Status:  degraded

# Every entry resolves to the same version
$ mise which pi
<user-home>/.local/share/mise/installs/pi/latest/pi/pi
$ <user-home>/.local/share/mise/shims/pi --version
0.85.1
$ <user-home>/.local/share/mise/installs/pi/0.85.1/pi/pi --version
0.85.1
$ <user-home>/.local/share/mise/installs/pi/latest/pi/pi --version
0.85.1
```

### Additional Context

- `gentle-ai doctor` exits 0 and nothing is functionally broken; the impact is a permanently `degraded` status plus a remedy that would break the toolchain.
- Root cause in `internal/cli/doctor.go`: `doctorToolCopies` scans PATH directories and dedupes by `filepath.EvalSymlinks(p)`. A shim symlink points at the dispatcher (`mise`), not at the tool, so it survives the dedupe; a shell wrapper resolves to itself.
- The Omarchy stubs are written by `<user-home>/.local/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-mise-install`, which emits a fixed template and is invoked from `install/user/mise.sh`. They are managed artifacts, and its migrations recreate them, so deletion is neither durable nor correct.
- Related, but distinct: #4141 (closed; gentle-ai's own managed OpenCode launcher, recognized by its `gentle-ai:managed-opencode-launcher/v1` marker), #1664 (closed; usrmerge symlink false positive — the `EvalSymlinks` dedupe fixes aliases pointing at the same binary, which is why dispatchers are the remaining gap), #924 (closed; Windows gga shim reporting "3 copies"), #709 (closed; ignoring non-executable PATH entries), #4706 (open; mise shim resolution, different defect).
- Suggested direction: count a PATH entry as a duplicate only when its effective target is a different tool binary. Practical options: skip entries that are mise shims (they resolve into the mise binary or live in the shims directory) and managed launcher stubs whose content `exec`s the resolved tool; keep the existing symlink dedupe for real aliases.

title: bug(review): active reviewing STATUS offers collect before stale managed assets are preflighted
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`.

### 📝 Bug Description

On released Gentle AI `v3.0.1`, the negotiated transition code checks stale managed reviewer assets while classifying a fresh/unrelated target before it offers `review.start`, but not while it classifies an active `current_target` lineage in `reviewing`. The latter path can therefore offer `collect`; capture admission then rejects that provider-offered work because the managed reviewer assets are outdated.

This is an offer-versus-admission inconsistency. No reviewer result was admitted, and the lineage was preserved for inspection.

Relevant immutable source links at the `v3.0.1` commit:

- Fresh/unrelated-target stale-asset check before `review.start`: https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/2594581e1ca227b6dea85a2861dd03e6d427974a/internal/cli/review_next_transition.go#L244-L253
- Active `StateReviewing` branch that projects missing capture work: https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/2594581e1ca227b6dea85a2861dd03e6d427974a/internal/cli/review_next_transition.go#L304-L326

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Use released `v3.0.1` with receipt-driven review enabled and an active ordinary-review lineage whose target is `current_target` and whose authority state is `reviewing`.
2. Arrange for the managed reviewer asset provenance to be stale for the running binary.
3. Query bound negotiated STATUS for that lineage.
4. Observe STATUS offer `collect` reviewer slots rather than `stop / managed_assets_outdated` with a provider-owned sync continuation.
5. Submit one offered capture through the supported host route.
6. Observe capture reject before any reviewer execution with `managed reviewer assets are outdated; run gentle-ai sync`.
7. Re-query bound STATUS; the lineage remains active and still projects collection work.

No additional capture was attempted for this report.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

For an active `current_target` / `reviewing` lineage, STATUS should perform the same managed-asset freshness preflight before offering collection work. If assets are stale, it should return `stop / managed_assets_outdated` with the exact provider-owned sync continuation; after that continuation succeeds, bound STATUS can decide whether collection is eligible.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

STATUS offers `collect` even though the later capture admission rejects the offered operation for stale managed reviewer assets. The actionable recovery is not supplied by the read-only transition that offered the work.

### Gentle AI Version

v3.0.1 (release commit `2594581e1ca227b6dea85a2861dd03e6d427974a`)

### Operating System

Linux (Other)

### AI Agent / Client

Other (Pi host relay)

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
managed reviewer assets are outdated; run gentle-ai sync
```

### Additional Context

Related but not equivalent:

- #4379 reports a capture-time stale-asset failure caused by its reporter's global-vs-pinned binary digest mismatch, with a workaround that closed that reporter's review. It does not establish that bound STATUS for an active `current_target` / `reviewing` lineage must preflight assets before offering `collect`: https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/4379
- PR #4242 / #3299 / #4170 added a STATUS-time continuation for the fresh/selectorless `review.start` route. Its own summary scopes the check to STATUS before offering `review.start`; the `v3.0.1` active-review branch above still lacks the analogous check before `collect`: https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/4242

The candidate contents, repository identity, opaque bindings, authority files, credentials, and local paths are intentionally omitted. No sync, reset, recovery, candidate mutation, or launch/review result was performed after the observed rejection.

title: bug(review): capture-result deterministically refuses claude reviewer transport with 'Permission mode forced to default — CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB is set'
body:
## Summary
`gentle-ai review capture-result` for a `claude-code` agent fails deterministically (2/2 attempts, same slot, no variation) when invoking the claude reviewer transport, with a permission-hardening refusal rather than a review verdict.

## Observed
- Operation: `review.capture-result`
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`
- Schema: `gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2`
- `phase`: `preflight`
- `code`: `invalid_request`
- `retry_safe`: `true` (but retrying the identical capture-result invocation reproduced the same failure both times)
- `mutation_outcome`: `not_started`
- `cause`: `invoke provider reviewer: claude reviewer transport failed: exit status 1: ⚠ Permission mode forced to default — CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB is set (allowed_non_write_users hardening). Declare allowedTools explicitly, or set <redacted> to opt out.`

## Context
- Review tier: `high` (4-lens plan: review-risk, review-resilience, review-readability, review-reliability), selected via a granted consent envelope on a fresh `review start`.
- The other 3 lenses (review-risk order=0, review-resilience order=1, review-readability order=2) captured successfully in the same lineage/session.
- Only `review-reliability` (order=3) hit this refusal, on both the first attempt and a relaunch after `review status --next-transition` reoffered the same bound slot.
- No `required_inputs` were listed in the failure envelope, and `next_action` was `correct_request` with nothing further specified.

## Expected
Either the reviewer transport should not be blocked by this permission-mode/env-scrub hardening in a normal `claude-code` agent capture flow, or the failure envelope should give an actionable `required_inputs`/`next_action` (e.g. which `allowedTools` to declare, or which env var to opt out with) instead of a generic `correct_request` with an empty `required_inputs` list.

## Repro shape
1. Enable RDD, grant consent on a high-risk 4-lens `review start`.
2. Capture review-risk, review-resilience, review-readability lenses — succeed.
3. Capture review-reliability lens with the exact provider-issued `capture-result` command from `next_transition` — fails with the above every time.

## Environment
- Agent: `claude-code`
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, schema versions `status/v7`, `start/v4`, `failure/v2`

title: bug(gentle-pi installer): Windows source-build Go resolution picks the first where.exe match, which fails under shim-based version managers (mise)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate (searched "mise", "where.exe go.exe", "Windows source installation requires local Go", "GENTLE_AI_GO_TOOLCHAIN_UNAVAILABLE" across open+closed issues; #3743 is about mise as an install method for gentle-ai itself, a different contract)

### Affected Area

`gentle-pi` npm package's Windows source-build installer (`scripts/gentle-ai-installer.mjs`, `resolveWindowsGoExecutable` / `assertGoToolchain`), used to build the package-local `gentle-ai` binary from source on Windows.

### Environment

- OS: Windows 10/11 (build 26200), x64
- `gentle-pi` npm package: 3.1.1 (installing package-local `gentle-ai` v3.0.1 via the Windows source-build path)
- Go: 1.26.1, installed and managed via [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) (shim-based version manager)

### Problem Statement

`npm install gentle-pi` (via `pi install npm:gentle-pi`) fails on Windows with:

```
gentle-pi could not install its package-local Gentle AI v3.0.1 binary: Windows source installation requires local Go 1.25.10 or newer; install Go and retry (automatic Go toolchain download is disabled).
```

...even though a valid Go 1.26.1 toolchain is installed and resolvable on `PATH` (`go version` works fine in an interactive shell).

### Root cause

Traced in `scripts/gentle-ai-installer.mjs`:

- `resolveWindowsGoExecutable()` shells out to `where.exe go.exe` and takes the **first** absolute-path line from the output, validating only that it is a regular, non-symlink file.
- When Go is managed by a shim-based version manager (mise, asdf, volta, etc.), the shims directory commonly precedes the real toolchain's install directory on `PATH`. The first match is then the shim executable — a genuine, non-symlink file, so it passes validation.
- `assertGoToolchain()` then runs `<resolved> version` inside `sealedGoEnvironment()`, which sets `PATH` to only `[dirname(resolved), System32, WinDir]` plus a small fixed set of env vars (no `HOME`/`USERPROFILE`/`APPDATA`/version-manager-specific vars).
- A version-manager shim needs those stripped PATH entries/env vars to locate its real manager binary and delegate to the actual toolchain. Without them it fails, and that failure is caught and re-reported as the generic "install Go and retry" message — masking that a perfectly valid Go toolchain is present and on `PATH`.

### Minimal repro

1. Install Go via mise: `mise use -g go@latest` (or any version), so both `<mise-shims>/go.exe` and `<mise-installs>/go/<version>/bin/go.exe` end up on `PATH`, with the shims directory first.
2. On Windows, run `npm install gentle-pi` (or otherwise trigger gentle-ai's Windows source-build path).
3. Observe the "install Go and retry" failure despite a working Go toolchain.

Directly confirmed the mechanism: executing the mise shim under an environment restricted to `[shimsDir, System32, WinDir]` (no `HOME`/`USERPROFILE`) reproduces the exact failure (`mise-shim: failed to execute mise: program not found`), while executing the real `go.exe` from the mise-managed install directory under the same restricted environment succeeds and prints the version correctly.

### Suggested direction (not prescriptive)

- Iterate all `where.exe go.exe` candidates and accept the first one that actually succeeds running `go version` inside the sealed environment, instead of trusting the first non-symlink match.
- Alternatively, perform the initial version probe with an inherited (or broader) environment, and only apply the fully sealed environment to the actual build step once a working toolchain path is confirmed.

### Workaround

Temporarily prepend the real Go install's `bin` directory to `PATH` ahead of the version manager's shims directory for the one command, e.g.:

```powershell
$env:Path = "<mise-installs>\go\<version>\bin;$env:Path"
pi install npm:gentle-pi
```

title: bug(review): capture-result fails with repository_context_capture_failed "Access is denied" on Windows (2.9.1 stable)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] Searched open and closed issues for the failure code and the "Access is denied" cause text. Nearest neighbour is #4329 (capture-result / repository_context_capture_failed, also lineage becomes unresolvable), but its cause is a missing-file error on Darwin arm64, and its follow-up STATUS fails with "lineage not held by repository" — a different symptom from what is reported here. #3103 and #2411 share the same failure code but document different causes (occupied reviewer slot; DrvFS/9p EXDEV or a binding_mismatch variant). None matches this occurrence's cause text or platform.
- [x] This report contains observed evidence only and does not assert an unconfirmed root cause.
- [x] Privacy review removed private project/repository names, paths, users, hosts, credentials, raw arguments, source, diffs, and environment values beyond OS/version.

### Environment

- Gentle AI: `2.9.1` (stable channel — no `-rc.`/`-main.` in build string)
- Client: Claude Code
- OS/arch: Windows
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`
- Agent binding: `claude-code`
- Projection: `workspace`
- Risk tier: medium (3 changed paths, `changed_lines: 136`) — two JSON/Markdown metadata files plus one small `.gitignore` edit
- Review authority store: not empty; a prior lineage in the same session had already completed and been acknowledged/burned successfully.

### Bug Description

A negotiated medium-risk review starts successfully (`state: reviewing`, one selected lens `review-reliability`, opaque `repository_context` handle) and the first bound `review.status` correctly returns the `collect` transition naming the `review.capture-result` input. Running that exact provider-issued `capture-result` invocation, unchanged, fails at `phase: "preflight"` with:

```
code: invalid_request
message: "The negotiated review request is invalid."
cause: "repository_context_capture_failed: provider-issued review repository context operation failed; cause: Access is denied.; retry capture-result with the same exact binding or refresh status"
mutation_outcome: not_started
authority_applicability: not_evaluated
retry_safe: true
replayability: not_replayable
next_action: correct_request
```

Following the contract's recovery rule, the same exact bound `review.status` (identical lineage/repository-context tokens) was re-run once to reconcile. It did not reproduce the same failure; instead it timed out (`operation_timeout`, `phase: pre_native`, `next_action: stop`) — reported separately as an occurrence of #4655, since that symptom matches an existing open report. This issue is filed only for the initial "Access is denied" `capture-result` failure, which has no existing equivalent.

Observed evidence only; no root cause is asserted. In particular, this report does not assert what resource the OS-level "Access is denied" refers to.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. On Windows, in an ordinary local Git checkout, with receipt-driven review enabled and at least one prior lineage in the same session already completed/acknowledged.
2. Leave a small non-passive workspace candidate uncommitted (here: 3 changed metadata/config paths, 136 changed lines).
3. Run the selectorless STATUS preflight for contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2` with `--next-transition`.
4. Run the returned `review start` unchanged; it returns the typed consent envelope.
5. Run the envelope's exact `granted` invocation; it returns `state: reviewing` with one selected lens and a `repository_context` handle.
6. Run the returned bound `review.status`; it returns a `collect` transition naming one `review.capture-result` input.
7. Run that `review.capture-result` with its returned argument tokens exactly, unchanged, from the repository as process cwd.
8. Observe the `repository_context_capture_failed` / "Access is denied" failure above.

### Expected vs Actual

- Expected: `capture-result` either admits the reviewer result or returns a typed failure whose named recovery ("retry capture-result with the same exact binding or refresh status") actually succeeds.
- Actual: capture fails before persisting anything with an OS-level "Access is denied" cause, and the documented recovery path (re-running the same bound STATUS) does not recover — it times out instead (tracked separately under #4655).

### Impact

The consumer cannot finalize, correct, or safely relaunch the review under this lineage. The contract forbids inventing a binding or retrying from prose, so the lifecycle had no executable continuation left. All consumer state was preserved; no receipt, tombstone, or delivery authority was created for this lineage.

### Safe identifiers

- lineage: `review-273dae4d8a711275`
- target identity: `sha256:e2b302c1b625916db97e52cce5d2ef76c67797779f14117975a8fbf2b654c4b1`
- authority revision at start: `sha256:b4bc390efe360e41413bce437ac74172b83cf5be1565eff14bec4c54e00df893`
- selected lens: `review-reliability`, `selected_order: 0`
- correction budget: 68

title: [Automated provider defect] Claude Code: reviewing lineage goes terminal corrupted_or_unverifiable_authority after an admitted capture; the reoffered fresh START refuses candidate_context_unavailable (3.0.2)
body:
## Summary

A `reviewing` compact lineage that had already admitted a reviewer capture is classified by its own bound STATUS as terminal `corrupted_or_unverifiable_authority`. The selectorless preflight then reoffers the **same** lineage id as `fresh_target_ready` with a repair assessment of all-zero counts, but executing that exact provider-issued START refuses with `candidate_context_unavailable` (`retry_safe: false`), and the bound STATUS stops the same way again. There is no sanctioned exit for the candidate short of disabling review for the clone.

Adjacent but, on the evidence, not the same observable defect:

- #4606 — START reports `created` while the store stays at zero bytes. There the lineage never progresses and a lineage-scoped STATUS still returns `collect`; here the lineage progressed through an admitted capture before going terminal.
- #4433 — terminal lineage reoffered as a fresh START, but refusing `atomic_start_conflict` on an `escalated` state (2.7.0). Here the state is `corrupted_or_unverifiable_authority` and the refusal is `candidate_context_unavailable`.
- #1856 (closed) — STATUS repeating a non-retry-safe START after a candidate-context failure. That repetition no longer happens; STATUS stops instead, which is why the loop terminates without an exit rather than spinning.
- #3373 — contention reported as authority corruption. Possibly the causal class given the concurrency noted below, but this report deliberately asserts no root cause.

## Observed evidence

- Gentle AI `3.0.2` (stable channel), contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, agent `claude-code`, Darwin arm64.
- Candidate: 10 paths, 539 changed lines, risk `medium`, projection `workspace`, one selected lens (`review-reliability`).
- Lineage `review-1791a1f67fe1e55d`, target identity `sha256:5392986ea4111c88584c9ea0ff9fe2a676d97710deb9bcb75bc6b8d533e4fc59`.

Sequence, each step running only the exact provider-issued operation and ordered tokens returned by the previous one:

1. Selectorless preflight STATUS → `execute / review.start / fresh_target_ready`.
2. Exact returned START with `--consent=relay` → typed `consent/v3` envelope, `risk_level: medium`.
3. Exact `granted` invocation from that envelope → `action: created`, `state: reviewing`, `selected_lenses: ["review-reliability"]`.
4. Its `next_transition` bound STATUS → `collect / reviewer_results_required`, one `review.capture-result` input.
5. Exact `review capture-result` (in-process, `--agent`, no `--input`) → returned without a usable transition.
6. Bound STATUS for the same lineage → `stop / corrupted_or_unverifiable_authority`, with no `cause` and no `code`.
7. Selectorless preflight STATUS again → `action: start`, `applicability: unrelated`, `candidates: []`, `repair.status: unsupported` with **every count zero** (`lineages: 0`, `events: 0`, `bytes: 0`, `conflicts: 0`), and `next_transition: execute / review.start / fresh_target_ready` carrying the **same** lineage id.
8. Exact returned START from step 7 → `gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2`, `phase: native_committed`, `code: candidate_context_unavailable`, `mutation_outcome: unknown`, `authority_applicability: current_target`, `retry_safe: false`, `replayability: status_required`, `next_action: review.status`. Cause text: `render frozen context for selected durable START authority "review-1791a1f67fe1e55d" at revision sha256:e0bbe28ec069e547841f35c57576db3f1006fc36b49149e7038cdd8d0ab18e38: validate negotiated START response: negotiated START repository context do…` (truncated as received).
9. Bound STATUS again → `stop / corrupted_or_unverifiable_authority`.

Steps 7–9 reproduce on repeat.

## Possibly relevant: concurrency

Three review lifecycles were driven in parallel in the same session, each in its own git worktree. **Two of those worktrees belong to the same clone**; the third is an unrelated repository. Outcomes:

- unrelated repository, lineage `review-96d3af8e1a9bfdbe` — reached `approved` and acknowledged normally;
- same-clone worktree A, lineage `review-fed10cee21dc3258` — reached `correction_required` with a corroborated finding, normally;
- same-clone worktree B, lineage `review-1791a1f67fe1e55d` — the failure above.

Whether the shared per-clone authority store under concurrent lifecycles is the trigger is not established here; it is reported as an observation, not a diagnosis. A single earlier lineage in worktree B had already completed and been acknowledged in the same session.

## Expected behavior

Either of these would be a sanctioned outcome:

- a lineage whose authority cannot be verified is not reoffered by the selectorless preflight as `fresh_target_ready`, and STATUS names an exit (repair, abandon, or recover) that actually applies to it; or
- the reoffered START succeeds, since the preflight reported nothing held in the store.

Today the preflight and START disagree about whether anything is held, and the only remaining exit is turning review off for the clone.

## Impact

The candidate cannot be reviewed at all. Delivery proceeds under ordinary repository policy with the review recorded as unavailable, which is the correct fallback, but the candidate silently loses its independent check.

title: bug(persona): "extend the existing project's language" escape hatch licenses regional register leakage into artifacts (residual of #1702)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

The shipped persona asset still licenses extending a project's **regional register**, so an agent writes Rioplatense voseo into the artifacts of a project whose existing files are already Rioplatense. The anti-voseo contract sits two lines below the sentence that permits it, and in practice the permission wins.

This is the residual mechanism of #1702 ("executor artifacts leak conversation dialect"), reproduced on **2.9.1**, a build that already contains that issue's fix.

The offending sentence, in the assets that get installed into the global instruction file — `internal/assets/opencode/persona-gentleman.md:29`, and the same block in `internal/assets/generic/persona-gentleman.md` and the other generated variants:

> Default to English. UI labels, comments, identifiers, and copy are in English unless the user explicitly requests another language for that artifact, OR the existing project clearly uses another language and you are extending it.

Two lines later, the same file says:

> Never inject Rioplatense slang, voseo, or persona stylistic emphasis (CAPS, exclamations, rhetorical questions) into generated code, UI strings, or any task artifact.

An agent reading line 29 as "match the project's language" has a documented licence to extend the project's *register*. That reading dominates in practice because the project's own `AGENTS.md` is the strongest in-context signal the agent has, and the contract on line 30 reads as a rule about the *conversation* rather than about the repository's existing voice.

Line 34 opens the same gap from the other side:

> Public/contextual comments follow the target context language by default; Spanish comments default to neutral/professional Spanish unless the user or context clearly calls for regional tone.

An existing Rioplatense codebase is exactly the kind of context that reads as calling for regional tone, so the exception swallows the rule.

**Self-reinforcing loop.** Because the escape hatch keys off the project's existing language, a project that acquires voseo once keeps licensing more of it. The first leak is not self-correcting; it becomes the justification for the next one.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Take a project whose existing `AGENTS.md`, docs and source strings are already written in Rioplatense Spanish. (A project can arrive in that state from earlier agent sessions — that is step 1 of the loop.)
2. Confirm the persona is installed: check the managed `<!-- gentle-ai:persona -->` block in the global instruction file, or list it with `gentle-ai sync --dry-run`, which reports `persona` among the managed components.
3. Ask the agent to add user-facing text to that project: an admin UI label, an error message, a documentation paragraph.
4. Inspect what it wrote, and scan the repository for voseo forms afterwards.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Artifacts follow the project's **locale** (Spanish vs English) but never its **regional register**. A project written in Rioplatense Spanish is extended in neutral/professional Spanish. That is precisely what line 30 already promises, and what #1702 was closed to deliver.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The agent extends the project's register. New voseo appears in the artifacts it writes: admin UI copy, public-site copy, empty-state and error strings, and documentation.

Observed on a real project: a single pass produced new voseo strings in component copy, error boundaries and docs. None of them were written by the human operator — the operator's own messages are consistently neutral Spanish, so the voseo is not the operator's voice being preserved. It is the agent's output, licensed by line 29 and primed by the repository's existing files.

**Second, independent consequence: there is no supported way for a user to correct the shipped text locally.**

- Editing the managed persona block in the global instruction file is reverted by the next sync. `gentle-ai sync --dry-run` lists `persona` among the managed components, so the block is owned by gentle-ai and a hand edit is not durable.
- The `instructions` config key is not a workaround: OpenCode V2 accepts the array but does not resolve its entries, so it adds no instructions.
- The only sync-proof correction available to a user is a per-repository `AGENTS.md` override, which fixes one repository and no other.

So the escape hatch cannot be tightened by the person who hit it. It has to be fixed in the assets.

### Gentle AI Version

2.9.1

(Stable channel. The leak reproduces on this build even though it already contains the #1702 fixes.)

### Operating System

Linux (Arch/Manjaro)

### AI Agent / Client

OpenCode

### 📋 Affected Area

Documentation

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

Evidence that the block is owned by gentle-ai and that a hand edit is not durable:

```text
$ gentle-ai sync --dry-run
gentle-ai sync — dry-run
Managed components: engram, sdd, skills, context7, permissions, gga, claude-theme, opencode-gentle-logo, persona
Apply steps: 20

$ gentle-ai sync --help
  sync         Sync agent configs and skills to current version
```

The exact sentence is still present in the current sources, next to the contract that is supposed to prevent it:

```text
26: - Any string literal inside source code
27:
28: For those artifacts:
29: - Default to English. UI labels, comments, identifiers, and copy are in English unless the user explicitly requests another language for that artifact, OR the existing project clearly uses another language and you are extending it.
30: - Never inject Rioplatense slang, voseo, or persona stylistic emphasis (CAPS, exclamations, rhetorical questions) into generated code, UI strings, or any task artifact.
31: - The persona styles HOW YOU TALK, not WHAT YOU BUILD.
32: - Generated technical artifacts default to English regardless of the active persona or conversation language.
```

### Additional Context

**Relationship to existing issues — read before classifying this as a duplicate.**

- **#1702** (closed, COMPLETED) is the class: "executor artifacts leak conversation dialect (misleading alias, sync revert loop, unforced component, contract-less agents)". Its fix is present in this build — the anti-voseo contract on line 30 — and the leak still reproduces. This report is the residual/regression of that class, not a new class.
- **Not filed as a comment on #1702** because that issue is closed as COMPLETED and the specific mechanism has no issue of its own. Exact-phrase searches for `"clearly uses another language"`, `"existing project clearly uses"` and the surrounding wording return nothing on open or closed issues. I did not reopen #1702, and I did not add, remove or change any labels.
- **#912** (open) is the structural fix: decoupling persona style from language/region, with a curated region list and an artifacts-language toggle. This report is evidence for it — the coupling is what makes line 29 ambiguous in the first place.
- **#2123** (open) covers the sync-reverts-user-customizations half of the second consequence.

**Suggested minimal change.** Make the escape hatch defer to the locale rather than to the project's voice:

> ...OR the existing project clearly uses another **locale** (e.g. Spanish rather than English) and you are extending that **locale**. Extend the project's locale, never its regional register: a repository written in Rioplatense Spanish is extended in neutral/professional Spanish.

and close the "regional tone" exception on line 34 the same way, so that an existing Rioplatense codebase is explicitly *not* context that calls for regional tone.

**Scope note.** This is reported from an OpenCode install, but the same block is generated into the other variants under `internal/assets/`, so the wording change belongs in the shared source rather than in the OpenCode asset only.

title: bug(repo): contributor-filed issues never receive the form-declared status:needs-review label — triage gate never starts
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description
Both YAML issue forms declare automatic labels — `bug_report.yml` declares `labels: ["bug", "status:needs-review"]` and `feature_request.yml` declares `labels: ["enhancement", "status:needs-review"]` — and the form's own instructions document the workflow as "Submit this bug report → it gets the `status:needs-review` label automatically". In practice, issues filed by external contributors never receive those labels: 22 of the 25 most recent open issues (filed by at least 6 different users) have zero labels.

Reproduced directly while filing https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/4700 through the GitHub CLI with `--label "bug" --label "status:needs-review"` (both labels exist in the repository): the create succeeded and returned the issue URL, but the target-host read-back showed `labels: []`. The labels were silently dropped because the creating actor has no `triage` permission (`{"admin":false,"maintain":false,"pull":true,"push":false,"triage":false}`), and the repository ships no labeling workflow (`.github/workflows/` contains no labeler/triage automation) that would apply the form-declared labels after creation.

The consequence is that the documented triage gate never starts: `status:needs-review` — the entry point of the "maintainer reviews it and adds `status:approved`" flow — is never present on contributor-filed issues.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce
1. As a contributor without `triage` permission, file an issue against the repository via `gh issue create` (or any API route) with `--label "bug" --label "status:needs-review"`.
2. Note that the create succeeds and returns the issue URL with no error.
3. Read the issue back from the target host: `labels` is empty; the form-declared labels were dropped silently.
4. List the 25 most recent open issues: 22 have zero labels despite both forms declaring automatic labels.

### ✅ Expected Behavior
Every declared label of a YAML issue form should end up applied to the created issue — either GitHub applies them at creation, or the repository provides an automation (e.g. a `label` workflow) that applies the form-declared labels to issues created outside the web form. A create that cannot honor `--label` should fail loudly instead of silently dropping the labels.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
Labels are silently dropped for API/CLI-created issues by actors without `triage` permission, and no automation compensates. Most recent contributor issues land unlabeled, so the documented "submit → `status:needs-review`" step of the triage workflow does not happen.

### Gentle AI Version
3.0.2 (the defect is repository-side — `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE` configuration — and version-independent)

### Operating System
Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client
Other

### 📋 Affected Area
Other

### 💡 Logs / Error Output
```shell
$ gh api --paginate "repos/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/labels?per_page=100" --jq '.[].name' | grep '^status:'
status:approved
status:needs-design
status:needs-info
status:needs-review

$ gh issue view 4700 --repo Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai --json labels
{"labels":[]}

$ gh api repos/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai --jq '.permissions'
{"admin":false,"maintain":false,"pull":true,"push":false,"triage":false}
```

### Additional Context
- Related, docs-side and closed: #2631 ("issue-creation skill promises labels that CLI filing does not apply") — this issue covers the repository-side gap that remained after that fix.
- Direct reproduction artifact: https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/4700 (created with `--label`, read back with zero labels).
- Candidate fixes: a labeler workflow that applies form-declared labels to issues created via API (matching on the first markdown/heading signature of each form), or documenting that contributors must not pass `--label` and maintainers apply labels at triage.

title: bug(review): claude-code capture-result rejects provider-issued rctx2 context on initial lens collection (3.0.2 stable)
body:
## Observed behavior

On stable Gentle AI 3.0.2 with the claude-code runtime, a negotiated high-risk workspace review (4 lenses: risk, resilience, readability, reliability) was started with granted candidate-scoped consent. Three of the four initial `review.capture-result` lens captures (risk, readability, reliability) admitted successfully. The fourth (resilience) refused on its first attempt with an admission-side error unrelated to repository context (reviewer evidence claimed inspection could not occur while reporting `inspection.status: "completed"`), then on a corrective retry refused as `out_of_scope` (evidence referencing a path outside the frozen repository).

Following the error's own instruction, the bound STATUS was re-queried. It reoffered the identical resilience lens slot with a `--repository-context` token. Executing the exact provider-issued `review.capture-result` operation with that token refuses before admission:

`repository_context_unavailable: provider-issued review repository context operation failed; cause: invalid rctx2 repository context; refresh the exact native next_transition before retrying`

Re-querying the bound STATUS again and re-running the exact reoffered command reproduces the identical typed refusal with a byte-identical `--repository-context` token (confirmed twice).

No source mutation occurred. No reviewer verdict, receipt, acknowledgement, or delivery authority was created for the resilience lens. The other three lenses (risk, readability, reliability) hold admitted results.

## Expected behavior

Either the `--repository-context` token issued by the bound STATUS is consumable by the exact `review.capture-result` operation it was issued for, or the bound STATUS issues a **replacement** token that can advance the same lens slot — so the remediation named in the error message is actually followable.

## Actual behavior

The prescribed remediation ("refresh the exact native next_transition before retrying") is a no-op: STATUS reissues the same handle that capture-result rejects as invalid, so the lineage cannot admit the resilience lens through any provider-issued transition.

## Minimal reproduction

1. Enable receipt-driven review.
2. Start a negotiated high-risk workspace review (4-lens: risk/resilience/readability/reliability) as claude-code and grant candidate-scoped consent.
3. Run the returned `review.capture-result` for all four lenses concurrently, in provider order.
4. One lens's first capture attempt admits successfully; observe whether any other lens instead first refuses on an unrelated admission-side cause (inspection-status/out-of-scope), then, after the STATUS-directed retry, hits `repository_context_unavailable` on its reissued `--repository-context` token.
5. Re-query the bound STATUS; compare the reoffered `--repository-context` value against the one that failed: byte-identical.
6. Re-run the exact reoffered `review.capture-result` command: identical typed refusal.

## Environment

- Gentle AI: 3.0.2 stable
- Runtime: claude-code
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`
- Projection: workspace, current-changes
- Risk: high (4-lens: review-risk, review-resilience, review-readability, review-reliability)
- Selected lens affected: review-resilience (order 1 of 4)
- Phase: initial lens collection (`review.status` action `collect`, reason `reviewer_results_required`) — not post-correction targeted validation
- Attempts: one unrelated admission refusal + two `repository_context_unavailable` refusals on the reissued token

## Search

Searched open and closed issues for `repository_context_unavailable`, `rctx2`, `capture-result`, `3.0.2 rctx2`, and `capture-result claude-code repository_context_unavailable`.

Closest existing reports, none equivalent:

- #4664 (open, 2.9.1) — same typed `invalid rctx2` refusal and claude-code runtime, but `capture-validation` operation during post-correction `targeted_validation_required` phase, not `capture-result` during initial lens collection. Different operation, different phase, older version.
- #4605 (open, 2.9.1) — same typed refusal and `capture-result` operation, but Codex runtime (not claude-code) and a different preceding sequence (first attempt empty at the host boundary, not an unrelated admission-side refusal). Older version.
- #4012, #3194, #4019 (closed, 2.3.0-2.4.0) — repository-context failures on much older versions and different phases.

No exact match for claude-code + `capture-result` + initial lens-collection phase + 3.0.2 was found, so this is filed as a new report rather than assumed equivalent to #4664 or #4605.

## Privacy

This report intentionally excludes repository identity, absolute paths, source contents, environment values, and any project-specific details. All identifiers above (lineage id omitted, tree hashes omitted) are omitted or generic; only the reproduction shape, typed causes, and version/runtime/phase facts are included.

title: bug(review 2.9.2): capture-correction-plan rejects the rctx2 repository-context its own lineage STATUS reissues; Pi facade rejects the verbatim correction-plan binding
body:
## Observed evidence (not a confirmed root cause)

- Build: gentle-ai 2.9.2-0.20260915231333-5383ee5bbaec, Linux amd64.
- Contract: gentle-ai.review-integration/v2, compact-v2 lineage, agent=pi, workspace projection, untracked-scope=select.
- Lineage reached correction_required through the normal route: 4-lens reviewer-result group captured successfully, then the provider refuter captured successfully and closed with correction_required plus a correction_request (request-hash and repository-context handle rctx2_H rendered by that same STATUS output).

## Defect A — native CLI preflight refuses its own issued context

`review capture-correction-plan` invoked with the exact provider-issued tokens (lineage, expected-revision, target, request-hash, repository-context=rctx2_H) fails in preflight:

- schema: gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2
- phase: preflight, code: invalid_request, retry_safe: true, mutation_outcome: not_started
- cause: `repository_context_unavailable: provider-issued review repository context operation failed; cause: invalid rctx2 repository context; refresh the exact native next_transition before retrying`

Re-running lineage-bound native STATUS with --next-transition re-issues the same rctx2_H and the same collect input; an immediate retry with those fresh tokens fails identically (2 attempts total).

## Defect B — Pi compact facade rejects the verbatim binding

The compact capture facade rejects the byte-exact `collectBindings[].collectBinding` string for the correction-plan slot with `capture-binding-rejected: "collectBinding is unknown, expired, or belongs to a different session route"` (3 attempts, each immediately preceded by a fresh bound STATUS rendering that same binding). The same facade accepted the reviewer-result group binding and the provider-refuter binding on this same lineage, which isolates the failure to the correction-plan collect route's repository-context validation.

## Expected / actual

- Expected: the repository-context handle issued by lineage STATUS is accepted by its own capture-correction-plan preflight (or STATUS issues a context the capture accepts), so the one bounded correction can proceed.
- Actual: the correction-plan capture is unusable from both routes; the lineage cannot leave correction_required through the offered transition.

## Minimal reproduction

On any compact-v2 lineage in correction_required: read the correction_request from STATUS with --next-transition, then call capture-correction-plan with exactly those tokens (including the repository-context handle from that same output). Preflight fails with repository_context_unavailable; refreshing native next_transition re-issues the identical handle and the failure repeats.

## Provenance / scope

- Opaque identifiers (safe prefixes): lineage `review-7035c3…`, request-hash `sha256:653e42…`, expected-revision `sha256:4d06af…`.
- No repository paths, diffs, source contents, or environment values are included.
- Related-but-not-equivalent issues reviewed before filing (different operation and/or agent): #4605 (capture-result/Codex/2.9.1), #4664 (capture-validation/claude-code/2.9.1), #4498 (pi facade, later lens slots), closed #3194 (correction-lines finalize, 2.3.0).

title: bug(review): Pi compact START returns schema-incompatible and never creates a lineage (empty workspace candidate)
body:
### Pre-flight Checks
- [x] Explicit user consent was obtained to report this apparent provider defect.
- [x] Open and closed issues were searched (`schema-incompatible`, `review start`, Pi facade). Closest reports are not equivalent: #4332 (empty native START output, tracked-only candidate, 2.6.1); #4488/#4370 (`schema-incompatible` on intended-untracked selection, not START); #4243 (repair preflight).
- [x] This report contains observed evidence only and does not assert a root cause.
- [x] Final privacy scan completed immediately before creation: no raw argv, absolute paths, private project names, usernames, hostnames, credentials, diffs, source contents, or environment values are included.

### Bug Description
On the Pi compact review facade, negotiated `inspect` offers `review.start` for an empty workspace candidate (`paths: []`, current tree equals base tree, `applicability: unrelated`). Executing START through `gentle_review` with the documented compact input fails immediately with `error_code: schema-incompatible`. Native reports `lineage_created: false`. No consent envelope is produced. Inspect continues to re-offer START.

The inspect `next_transition.execute` reconstruction includes CLI-only tokens (`--consent=relay`, a lineage id, `--committed-only=true`, an explicit base ref) and a **different** target identity than `inspect.result.target_identity` / snapshot identity. The compact START input cannot carry those CLI tokens; both compact encodings that were attempted were rejected as schema-incompatible.

### Environment
- Gentle AI: `local-5383ee5bbaec` (local/source build string; not treated as published-fix evidence)
- OS/architecture: Windows 11 x86_64
- Client: Pi `0.85.1` via the gentle-pi `gentle_review` tool facade
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`
- Projection: `workspace`
- Candidate shape: empty current-changes (`paths: []`); inspect `applicability: unrelated`

### Observed Sequence
1. RDD reminder named snapshot identity `08a95d21…`.
2. `inspect`: `action: start`, `reason_code: fresh_target_ready`, empty `paths`, snapshot identity `08a95d21…`.
3. Reconstructed execute target identity: `fb2dfa0e…` (does not match the snapshot identity). Reconstructed command also carried `--consent=relay`, a lineage token, `--committed-only=true`, and `--base-ref`.
4. START attempt A (fresh idempotency key) with compact input encoding `mode` plus explicit `baseRef` and `committedOnly: true`: `blocked`, `outcome: native-operation-failed`, `error_code: schema-incompatible`, `lineage_created: false`, `reset_eligible: false`.
5. `inspect` again: same START offer, still no lineage.
6. START attempt B (fresh idempotency key) with compact input `{"mode":"ordinary"}` only: identical `schema-incompatible` / `lineage_created: false`.
7. No consent/v3 envelope was returned. `candidates: []` remained.

### Expected Behavior
For an empty or unrelated workspace candidate, inspect should either:
- refuse START with a typed empty-diff / unrelated-target reason, or
- offer a compact START input that the Pi facade can submit unchanged and that either creates a lineage or returns a typed actionable failure.

A documented compact START (`{"mode":"ordinary"}`) should not fail `schema-incompatible` when inspect just classified the target as ready.

### Actual Behavior
Inspect advertises START. Compact START cannot represent the reconstructed CLI command and is rejected as schema-incompatible. No lineage, consent, or review progress occurs. The same START route is re-offered.

### Minimal Reproduction
- Clean workspace (no unstaged/untracked review paths).
- RDD enabled; Pi `gentle_review` `inspect` offers `review.start`.
- Call `gentle_review` `start` with a fresh idempotency key and input `{"mode":"ordinary"}`.
- Observe `schema-incompatible` and `lineage_created: false`.

### Bounded Attempts and Preserved State
- 2 START attempts; both `schema-incompatible`; both `lineage_created: false`.
- Inspect re-checked after the first failure; still `action: start`.
- No lineage, receipt, commit, push, PR, or authority mutation occurred.
- Consumer working tree was already clean before the review reminder.

### Safety Impact
The consumer cannot start or decline review for this candidate through the Pi facade. Exits are defect reporting or clone-scope review-mode disable.

### Related But Not Duplicate
- #4332: Pi START never creates a lineage, but via empty native output on a tracked-only candidate (2.6.1), not `schema-incompatible` on an empty workspace.
- #4488 / #4370: `schema-incompatible` on intended-untracked *selection*, not START.
- #4243: `schema-incompatible` on repair preflight inventory.

title: fix: add Kilo Code support to RTK community tool
body:
## Summary

The `community-tool:rtk` sync step fails with `RTK has no selected supported detected agents; select an installed supported agent before setup` when Kilo Code is the selected agent.

## Root cause

`rtkDetectedAgents()` in `internal/components/communitytool/rtk_runtime.go` only checks for Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, and Pi — Kilo Code is excluded. When gentle-ai runs `sync:community-tool:rtk` with Kilo Code in `s.agents`, `rtkScopedDetectedAgents` returns empty, triggering the error at line 152.

RTK itself supports Kilo Code via `rtk init --agent kilocode` (writes `.kilocode/rules/rtk-rules.md`), but gentle-ai's setup contracts and detection logic never included it.

## Fix

Added Kilo Code to the RTK setup contracts, managed paths, detected agent ordering, and status checking:

- `rtk_source.go`: Added `{model.AgentKilocode, "init --agent kilocode", ...}` contract
- `rtk_runtime.go`: Added Kilo Code to `rtkManagedPaths`, `rtkDetectedAgents` order, and `rtkAgentConfigured`

## Files changed

- `internal/components/communitytool/rtk_source.go`
- `internal/components/communitytool/rtk_runtime.go`
- `internal/components/communitytool/rtk_source_test.go`
- `internal/components/communitytool/rtk_runtime_test.go`

## Tests

All existing tests pass plus two new tests:
- `TestRTKScopedInstallConfiguresKiloCodeOnly`
- `TestRTKStatusDetectsKiloCode`

title: Windows installer hard-codes the Go module major across source revisions
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

The Windows source installer in `scripts/install.ps1` still hard-codes `/v3` in its Go package target, stable source command, and beta Go environment patterns instead of deriving the module path from the selected source revision.

This is a follow-up to the resolved installer migration in #4685 and merged #4686, not a report that current v3 installation is broken. At source revision `9bf454d4d40803635bd302451ec8ed08d78bd1f4`, the `/v3` literals agree with the current `go.mod`. They would become inconsistent if a selected future source revision declared a different major module path without another manual installer edit.

The root class is shared with #4687. This issue covers only the PowerShell installer and its regression tests. It excludes #4687's internal Go updater, registry, upgrade strategy, and printed instructions, and excludes the separately proposed Unix installer slice.

Windows is the target platform. The local fixture environment was PowerShell 7 on macOS; native Windows behavior is unverified.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Inspect `scripts/install.ps1` at `9bf454d4d40803635bd302451ec8ed08d78bd1f4`, especially the literal `/v3` Go package target, stable source command, and beta Go environment patterns. Compare them with the module declaration in that revision's `go.mod`.
2. For a deterministic recurrence fixture, provide a controlled selected-source `go.mod` declaring `/v4` or `/v5`, with network responses and installation commands mocked. Record the selected tag or commit and the Go install arguments; do not execute a downloaded installer or perform a real installation.
3. Verify that module path, selected revision, and beta Go environment patterns agree. The unchanged current source still constructs `/v3`; a future-major source fixture would therefore expose a mismatch unless the literal is edited.

Evidence boundary: the current-base recurrence is a static deduction, not a newly executed failing test or a production outage. title: bug(cli): bare `gentle-ai` invocation crashes with Go runtime panic (traceback did not unwind completely) during startup dependency detection on Windows
body:
## Automated provider-defect report

### Summary
On Windows, Gentle AI v2.9.1 (stable channel) aborts with a Go runtime fatal error during ordinary startup, before any subcommand is dispatched, instead of printing its normal CLI output.

### Environment
- Gentle AI build: v2.9.1 (stable channel, module `github.com/gentleman-programming/gentle-ai/v2`)
- OS / architecture: Windows amd64
- Client: interactive terminal (PowerShell), invoking the `gentle-ai` binary directly with no arguments
- Go runtime: matches the toolchain used to build v2.9.1 (stack trace references `C:/Program Files/Go/src/runtime`)

### Operation shape
1. Invoke `gentle-ai` with no subcommand/arguments from an ordinary repository working directory.
2. `main.main` → `internal/app.Run` → `internal/app.RunArgs` → `internal/system.Detect` → `internal/system.DetectDependencies` → `internal/system.detectDeps`.
3. `detectDeps` fans out several concurrent goroutines, each resolving a dependency executable via `os/exec.LookPath` (Windows `syscall.GetFileAttributesEx` stat calls).
4. While those goroutines are mid-syscall, a background GC mark cycle attempts to scan goroutine 1's stack (`runtime.scanstack` inside `gcBgMarkWorker` → `gcDrain` → `markroot`) and fails to unwind it completely.

### Expected behavior
The bare `gentle-ai` invocation should complete dependency detection and print its normal output without crashing.

### Actual behavior
The process aborts with:
```
runtime: g 3: frame.sp=0x... top=0x...
fatal error: traceback did not unwind completely
```
followed by a full goroutine stack dump, then exits. No typed failure envelope is emitted — this is a raw Go runtime fatal error, not a CLI-level error path.

### Bounded observed evidence
- Crash occurs inside `runtime.scanstack` / `runtime.(*unwinder).next`, called from `runtime.gcBgMarkWorker` → `runtime.gcDrain` → `runtime.markroot`, i.e. during concurrent GC mark-phase stack scanning.
- The scanned goroutine (goroutine 1, the main goroutine) is executing `internal/system.detectDeps` (`internal/system/deps.go:110`) → `internal/system.DetectDependencies` (`deps.go:94`) → `internal/system.Detect` (`detect.go:106`) → `internal/app.RunArgs` (`app.go:172`) → `internal/app.Run` (`app.go:62`) → `main.main` (`cmd/gentle-ai/main.go:16`).
- Several worker goroutines are concurrently inside `internal/system.detectSingleDep` (`deps.go:138`/`145`) → `os/exec.LookPath` → `os/exec.lookPathExts` / `findExecutable` → `os.Stat` → `syscall.GetFileAttributesEx`, each resolving a different dependency executable on `PATH`.
- No repository mutation, review transaction, or delivery gate was in progress — the crash happens before any subcommand logic runs, during the earliest startup dependency probe.
- No typed failure envelope was emitted; the process exited via Go's fatal-error path (uncatchable by the caller).

### Minimal reproduction
Not yet isolated to a fully deterministic trigger. Observed once when invoking the bare `gentle-ai` command (no arguments) from an ordinary Git repository working directory on Windows amd64. The crash is timing-dependent (GC racing concurrent dependency-detection goroutines mid-syscall), consistent with the class of crash described below.

### Related reports
- #4081, #4128, #4152, and #4316 report the same family of Go runtime crash signatures (`unexpected return pc for runtime.gopark` / `fatal error: unknown caller pc`) on Windows during `runtime.scanstack`, each in a different CLI contract (`sdd-status` artifact resolution, `review status` negotiated preflight, `sdd-attempt` acquire, `review stop-hook` RDD-mode resolution respectively). #4081 and #4128 were closed by #4218 ("harden the Windows git process tree launch"); #4316 remains open on a later build (v2.6.0), indicating that fix did not eliminate the underlying crash class. This report adds a fifth distinct contract — bare CLI startup / dependency detection (`internal/system.detectDeps`) — with a related but distinct fatal-error message (`traceback did not unwind completely` vs. `unknown caller pc`), both originating in `runtime.scanstack`/`runtime.(*unwinder).next` during concurrent GC. Per those reports' own framing, this is a related observation on a shared crash-signature family, not an asserted duplicate or confirmed shared root cause.

title: bug(review): stop-hook and mode status fail on a Windows SMB share while RDD is off (2.9.1)
body:
## Automated provider-defect report

### Summary

The Claude Code `review stop-hook` fails at the end of every turn when the repository's Git common directory is hosted on a Windows SMB network share. RAR authority validation classifies the share as an unknown filesystem and refuses fail-closed, so the hook reports an error on each turn.

The refusal itself is the behavior requested in #1918 (fail closed on unknown or remote filesystems rather than assuming NTFS commands are valid). The defect is that it also fires when receipt-driven development is **off**, where the hook has no authority work to do and no review can run.

### Environment

- Gentle AI: `2.9.1` (stable channel)
- Client: Claude Code
- OS: Windows `10.0.19045`, 64-bit
- Shell: PowerShell 5.1 / Git Bash
- Repository topology: Git worktree and Git common directory on a Windows SMB network share, reached through a mapped drive letter and resolved to its UNC form

### Operation shape

```text
gentle-ai review stop-hook            # end-of-turn preflight, Claude Code
gentle-ai review mode status          # same refusal, read-only path
```

### Minimal reproduction

1. On Windows, place a Git repository on an SMB network share and map it to a drive letter.
2. Leave receipt-driven development unset, so the effective mode is `off`.
3. Run `gentle-ai review mode status` with the repository as process cwd, or complete any Claude Code turn with the stop hook installed.
4. Observe the refusal.

### Observed evidence

`gentle-ai review mode status` prints the resolved mode and then fails:

```text
receipt-driven development: off (decided by clone_local)
  global:      unset
  clone-local: unset
Error: validate RAR Git common directory "<UNC-repo>\.git": RAR authority
parent "<UNC-repo>\.git" is on an unknown filesystem; cannot assume NTFS
semantics; check the path and rerun
```

The stop hook surfaces the same cause, prefixed by its own operation:

```text
Stop hook error: Failed with non-blocking status code: Error: review stop-hook:
resolve review mode: validate RAR Git common directory "<UNC-repo>\.git": RAR
authority parent "<UNC-repo>\.git" is on an unknown filesystem; cannot assume
NTFS semantics; check the path and rerun
```

- Phase: RDD-mode resolution, before any authority mutation
- `mutation_outcome`: `not_started`
- Non-blocking for the client: the turn completes, the error is appended to every turn
- Reproduces on every turn; no bounded retry changes the outcome

### Expected behavior

Two separable expectations:

1. When the effective RDD mode is `off`, mode resolution should complete without validating the RAR authority path. There is no authority to establish, so an unsupported-filesystem classification should not be reached and the stop hook should be a no-op.
2. For a genuinely remote SMB/UNC Git common directory, the refusal should carry a typed unsupported-filesystem result with a documented continuation, rather than a bare error whose remediation text ("check the path and rerun") cannot resolve a correct path.

### Actual behavior

The stop hook errors on every turn in a repository where review can never run, and `review mode status` — documented as read-only and non-mutating — exits non-zero after having already printed the correct mode. The only caller-side remedy is to stop using the hook.

### Relationship to existing issues

- #1918 (closed, approved) specified this fail-closed classification; this report is about it being reached while RDD is off, not about the classification being wrong.
- #3497 (closed) also involves a Windows UNC repository, but fails earlier with `git_command_failed` from a dubious-ownership rejection.
- #4316 (open) is the same command and phase, but the observable failure is a Go runtime panic.

### Privacy

This report intentionally omits raw argv, absolute paths, repository and organization names, usernames, hostnames, credentials, source content, diffs, hashes, and environment values.

title: bug(review): negotiated status regressed to git_command_failed on an unborn repository (2.9.1)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

On `2.9.1`, negotiated v2 `review status` fails during `pre_native` on a repository with zero commits (unborn branch) and an all-untracked candidate. The typed envelope names the failing Git subprocess directly:

`git rev-list --max-count=1 --skip=1 HEAD` exits `128` with `fatal: ambiguous argument 'HEAD': unknown revision or path not in the working tree`.

The envelope reports `retry_safe: false`, `replayability: manual_action_required`, and `next_action: stop`, so there is no consumer-side continuation. The review lifecycle cannot be entered at all on a greenfield repository until a commit exists.

**This appears to be a regression, reported as observed evidence rather than an asserted root cause.**

The initial-STATUS cohort of the unborn-repository defect was root-scoped to #2843 and fixed by PR #2926 (merged `2026-08-10`, commit `8c2cbd80a354258e5e1b315633110e832144249d`). That commit is an ancestor of tag `v2.9.1`: `compare/v2.9.1...8c2cbd8` returns `status: behind`, `ahead_by: 0`. The installed build therefore demonstrably contains the fix, and the defect still reproduces.

The failure signature differs from the earlier reports, which returned a generic `operation_failed` with `retry_safe: true` and `next_action: retry` (see #3204, closed as a duplicate aggregate, and its occurrence comments). Here the code is `git_command_failed` and the operation is terminal. The improved Git diagnostics from #1618 / #2718 make the underlying subprocess visible.

No authority, lineage, receipt, staging change, commit, source mutation, push, or PR was created. Candidate state was preserved throughout.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Create an empty directory and initialise a Git repository in it, making no commits:

   ```shell
   git init
   echo hello > a.txt
   ```

2. Run negotiated review status against it:

   ```shell
   gentle-ai review status --cwd <repo> --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --agent claude-code
   ```

3. Observe the `pre_native` failure below. It reproduces with and without `--next-transition`.

4. For contrast, repeat in a repository that has exactly one commit plus an uncommitted change. Status succeeds and returns `action: start`.

Observed across three freshly created unborn repositories: 3/3 failed. The single-commit contrast repository succeeded.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Status on an unborn repository with an all-untracked candidate should return a provider-owned transition that can identify or collect that candidate, as the initial-STATUS cohort fix intended. If the shape is genuinely unsupported on this path, it should return a typed stop reason carrying an executable continuation, rather than surfacing a raw Git subprocess failure with `next_action: stop` and no remedy.

A `--skip=1` predecessor lookup has no meaning on a repository with zero commits and should not be reached before the unborn case is classified.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Both the flagged and unflagged invocations exit `1` and return the envelope below before native evaluation. Because `retry_safe` is `false` and `next_action` is `stop`, the consumer has no in-contract path forward: the lifecycle is unreachable on a greenfield repository.

Note that an earlier call in the same session, on the same repository, had returned a valid `status/v7` envelope with a `collect` transition. Attempting the returned `review start` tokens failed twice with `stale_target_identity` (`candidate_tree` and `paths_digest` drifting between negotiation and answer), after which status returned the Git failure consistently. The isolated reproduction above does not depend on that sequence.

### Gentle AI Version

2.9.1

### Operating System

Windows

### AI Agent / Client

Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
{
  "schema": "gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2",
  "contract": "gentle-ai.review-integration/v2",
  "operation": "review.status",
  "phase": "pre_native",
  "code": "git_command_failed",
  "message": "A Git subprocess failed before review authority mutation.",
  "mutation_outcome": "not_started",
  "authority_applicability": "not_evaluated",
  "retry_safe": false,
  "replayability": "manual_action_required",
  "required_inputs": [],
  "next_action": "stop",
  "cause": "git rev-list --max-count=1 --skip=1 HEAD failed with exit code 128: fatal: ambiguous argument 'HEAD': unknown revision or path not in the working tree."
}
```

### Additional Context

Environment:

- Gentle AI: `2.9.1` (latest published stable at time of report; no `-rc.` or `-main.` suffix)
- OS/architecture: Windows 11 x64
- Client/runtime: Claude Code
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`
- Agent binding: `claude-code`
- Effective receipt-driven mode: enabled, decided by global scope

Candidate shape: a greenfield project scaffold. Zero commits, zero tracked paths, roughly 44 intended untracked files. No base selector was supplied.

Related history, for triage convenience:

- #2843 — canonical root for the initial-STATUS cohort, closed as completed by PR #2926
- #3204 — duplicate aggregate whose comment thread split the cohorts
- #3307 — canonical root for the post-approval cohort (distinct from this report)
- #1618, #2718 — Git diagnostics work that makes this subprocess failure visible

This report was filed with the user's explicit consent. Diagnostics were privacy-scrubbed before submission: no absolute paths, project names, usernames, hostnames, credentials, diffs, source contents, or environment values are included.

title: bug(review): claude-code capture-validation refuses the rctx2 context that bound STATUS keeps reissuing, so the prescribed refresh is unfollowable (2.9.1 stable)
body:
## Observed behavior

On stable Gentle AI 2.9.1 with the claude-code runtime, a negotiated medium-risk workspace review reached `correction_required`, an accepted correction plan was submitted, the correction was applied, and the bound STATUS advanced to `targeted_validation_required` with one `review.capture-validation` slot.

Executing the exact provider-issued `review.capture-validation` operation refuses before admission:

`repository_context_unavailable: provider-issued review repository context operation failed; cause: invalid rctx2 repository context; refresh the exact native next_transition before retrying`

The refusal message instructs refreshing the exact native next_transition. Doing so does not help: the bound STATUS reoffers the identical slot **with the identical rctx2 handle**, which the capture then refuses again with the same typed cause. Two executions, same outcome.

No source mutation occurred as part of the capture. No validator verdict, receipt, acknowledgement, or delivery authority was created.

## Expected behavior

Either the context issued by the bound STATUS is consumable by the exact `review.capture-validation` operation it was issued for, or the bound STATUS issues a **replacement** context that can advance the same candidate — so that the remediation the error message prescribes is actually followable.

## Actual behavior

The prescribed remediation is a no-op. STATUS reissues the same handle that capture-validation rejects as invalid, so the lineage cannot leave `targeted_validation_required` through any provider-issued transition.

## Minimal reproduction

1. Enable receipt-driven review.
2. Start a negotiated workspace review as claude-code and grant candidate-scoped consent.
3. Let the reliability lens return `correction_required`.
4. Submit a correction plan via the exact `review.capture-correction-plan` operation.
5. Apply the correction in the working tree.
6. Run the exact bound STATUS; it advances to `targeted_validation_required` and offers one `review.capture-validation` slot.
7. Run that exact operation with the provider-issued tokens. Observe `repository_context_unavailable` / invalid rctx2 context.
8. Re-run only the bound STATUS as instructed, and compare the reoffered `--repository-context` token with the previous one: it is byte-identical. Re-running the capture refuses identically.

## Environment

- Gentle AI: 2.9.1 stable
- Runtime: claude-code
- Contract: review integration v2
- Projection: workspace, committed-only
- Risk: medium
- Selected lens: reliability
- Phase: targeted validation, after an accepted and applied bounded correction
- Attempts: two capture executions, both typed refusals with the same cause

## Search

Searched open and closed issues for `repository_context_unavailable`, `rctx2`, `capture-validation`, and `invalid rctx2 repository context`.

Closest existing reports, none equivalent:

- #4605 (open, 2.9.1) — same version and same typed `invalid rctx2` refusal, but Codex runtime, `capture-result` operation, initial capture phase, and a different preceding sequence (first attempt empty at the host boundary). This report is claude-code, `capture-validation`, post-correction targeted-validation phase, with the first attempt already refusing. Possibly the same causal class; filed separately rather than assumed equivalent.
- #4496 (open, 2.7.0) — capture-validation preflight refusal, but a different typed cause (admitted targeted-validator evidence mismatch), not a repository-context failure.
- #4012, #3194, #4019 (closed, 2.3.0-2.4.0) — repository-context failures on older versions and different phases.

The distinguishing observation here is that the remediation named in the error message is unfollowable, because STATUS reoffers the identical rejected handle rather than a replacement.

## Privacy

This report intentionally excludes repository identity, absolute paths, source contents, diffs, credentials, raw environment values, and opaque target/context/revision/lineage identifiers.
