9. The medium review cannot proceed.

### Related but distinct

The intended-untracked selection failure surface has several existing reports. This one is distinct because the eligible/expected inventory is populated from a **sibling worktree sharing the Git common dir** rather than the reviewed worktree, so no valid selection can exist for worktree A (its untracked set is empty):

- #4311 (invalid_request on selection) and #4488 / #4370 (schema-incompatible): in those the candidate contains real eligible untracked files — the inventory is correct and only the submission is rejected. Here the inventory itself points at another worktree.
- #4320 (no executable CLI path / no serializable schema for the selection): overlaps with the missing `review schema` entry, but is OpenCode-specific and does not involve a cross-worktree inventory.
- #4603 (STATUS invalid_request cites an untracked nested-git dir not in cwd): a different preflight check (nested Git repo among sibling repos under a non-git parent), not the intended-untracked selection inventory.
- #3260 (status timeout after a rejected capture): same `pre_native` / `operation_timeout` envelope class, but that timeout follows a rejected reviewer capture; here it occurs on the first status call under the default model and is worked around by pinning the reviewer model.
- #3741 / #2470 touch cross-worktree state, but neither concerns the intended-untracked selection inventory.

### Privacy

This report excludes repository/project/brand/domain names, usernames, hostnames, absolute paths, real file/branch names, credentials, environment values, diffs, and source contents. Worktrees and files are referred to generically.

title: bug(review): capture-result preflight rejects published v2 envelope fields while the canonicalizer demands terms the decoder rejects (2.7.0 stable, codex, windows/amd64)
body:
Automated provider-defect report filed after operator consent. Privacy-scrubbed: observed behavior only; no root cause is asserted; raw argv, absolute paths, private project/repo names, usernames, hostnames, credentials, environment values, source/diffs, and reviewer finding content are excluded.

### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] A definitive open+closed lookup was completed. Closest prior art: #2227 (closed; decode-cause part fixed per #3942's note; there the rejected field was a stray top-level `inspection_note` plus an opaque `repository_context_capture_failed` on 2.2.4), #2630 D1 (closed; orchestrator-contract reviewer prose `inspection_completed` vs native reviewer schema field names), #3942 (closed; nested `inspection` object rejecting `lens`/`paths_note`, main-channel 2.5.0-main, claude-code), #4288 (open; six preflight preconditions folded into one indistinguishable refusal). None covers this observable: at stable 2.7.0 the top-level fields of the published v2 result envelope are themselves rejected, and the canonicalizer's demanded terms never appear as accepted field names in any decoder output. Filed as a new report, not a reopening.
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

On stable Gentle AI `2.7.0` (windows/amd64, client `codex`), a negotiated review lifecycle (contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, medium risk, single lens `review-reliability`, order 0) reached the bound `reviewer_result` collect slot correctly. `review status --next-transition` re-offered the exact same slot before and after every attempt.

`review capture-result` was attempted 17 times with payload shapes derived from the published `contracts/review-integration/v2/schemas/admitted-result.schema.json` and from the decoder/canonicalizer error text itself. Every attempt failed in preflight decode or canonicalization with `mutation_outcome: not_started` (zero side effects per attempt; authority remained `state: reviewing`, generation 1, unburned).

Observed contradiction between stages, within the bounded attempt space:

- The strict decoder rejects the published envelope's top-level fields: `result`, `admission`, `subject`, `schema`, and top-level `summary` -> each yields `json: unknown field "<name>"`.
- Finding-level names documented or implied by the contract surface are also rejected: `title` -> `unknown field "title"`; `evidence` as an array of objects -> `cannot unmarshal object into Go struct field facadeReviewerResult.evidence of type string`; the same field as a string -> `cannot unmarshal string into Go struct field facadeReviewerResult.evidence of type []string`.
- The only shapes that pass decode (`findings` with just `severity`/`id`, plus `evidence` as `[]string`) are then refused by the post-decode canonicalizer with requirements `id, lens, location, severity, and neutral claim are required` and, after satisfying the claim part, `at least one proof reference is required`.
- Every field name tried for those canonicalizer demands is rejected by the decoder: `neutral_claim`, `proof`, `references`, `proofs` -> `unknown field ...`.

Within the 17 bounded, contract- and error-text-derived shapes, no payload advanced past preflight. The capture step of the lifecycle could not be completed on this build; the re-offered slot remains open.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. On Gentle AI stable 2.7.0 (windows/amd64), enable receipt-driven review and open a negotiated workspace review; grant candidate-scoped consent.
2. Obtain the bound `reviewer_result` collect slot via the exact `review status --next-transition` output.
3. Run the inspect recipe against the provider-bound immutable candidate (unchanged from provider output).
4. Compose a reviewer-result payload whose envelope follows the published v2 admitted-result schema (`schema`/`subject`/`admission`/`result`).
5. Run the exact provider-issued `review capture-result` tokens against the live lineage.
6. Observe `json: unknown field "result"`; iterate field names as shown in the matrix below.

Attempt matrix (operation shape and rejection class only):

| Attempt | Shape tried | Rejection |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `schema`+`subject`+`admission`+`result` (published envelope) | `unknown field "result"` |
| 2 | top-level `summary`+`findings` | `unknown field "summary"` |
| 3 | `schema`+`subject`+`admission`+`findings`+`summary` | `unknown field "admission"` |
| 4 | same without `summary`; finding with `title` | `unknown field "title"` |
| 5 | `subject`+`admission`+`findings` | `unknown field "admission"` |
| 6 | `schema`+`admission`+`subject`+`findings` | `unknown field "schema"` |
| 7 | `subject`+`findings`+`admission` (reordered) | `unknown field "subject"` |
| 8 | `findings` with `severity`,`id`,`evidence` (objects) | `unknown field "evidence"` |
| 9 | `findings` with `severity`,`id` | requires explicit findings and evidence arrays |
| 10 | + `evidence` array of objects | unmarshal object -> string (`facadeReviewerResult.evidence`) |
| 11 | + `evidence` single string | unmarshal string -> []string |
| 12 | + `evidence` []string | finding: id, lens, location, severity, neutral claim required |
| 13 | + `neutral_claim` | `unknown field "neutral_claim"` |
| 14 | + `claim` | at least one proof reference required |
| 15 | + `proof` []string | `unknown field "proof"` |
| 16 | + `references` []string | `unknown field "references"` |
| 17 | + `proofs` []string | `unknown field "proofs"` |

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Either a payload following the published v2 result-contract surface passes `capture-result` preflight, or the decoder/canonicalizer error output names the exact accepted field names so the caller can converge without guessing.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Preflight rejects every published-envelope field name; the canonicalizer then demands terms ("neutral claim", "proof reference") for which none of the corresponding plausible field names is accepted by the decoder, and the error text does not disclose the accepted names. All 17 attempts ended `mutation_outcome: not_started`; the slot was re-offered unchanged each time.

### Gentle AI Version

2.7.0 (stable channel; build string carries neither `-rc.` nor `-main.`). Newer releases (2.8.x/2.9.x) were not tested by this consumer; no regression claim against them is made.

### Operating System

Windows 11, amd64

### AI Agent / Client

Codex (negotiated review lifecycle, `review.capture-result`, external payload assembly from published contract documents)

### 🎯 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags) — `gentle-ai review capture-result` preflight decoder/canonicalizer vs published `contracts/review-integration/v2` result schema

### 📋 Logs / Error Output

```
decode reviewer result: json: unknown field "result"
decode reviewer result: json: unknown field "admission"
decode reviewer result: json: unknown field "subject"
decode reviewer result: json: unknown field "schema"
decode reviewer result: json: unknown field "summary"
decode reviewer result: json: unknown field "title"
json: cannot unmarshal object into Go struct field facadeReviewerResult.evidence of type string
json: cannot unmarshal string into Go struct field facadeReviewerResult.evidence of type []string
lens result finding[0]: id, lens, location, severity, and neutral claim are required
at least one proof reference is required
decode reviewer result: json: unknown field "neutral_claim"
decode reviewer result: json: unknown field "proof"
decode reviewer result: json: unknown field "references"
decode reviewer result: json: unknown field "proofs"
```

### Additional Context

- Deterministic: identical shapes produced identical rejection classes; STATUS re-queried between every attempt always re-offered the same target/revision/lens/order.
- Authority state after the sequence: `reviewing`, generation 1, unburned; no recovery, reset, or manual authority edit was attempted.
- This report does not assert which stage is wrong (decoder, canonicalizer, or the published schema). It records that the three surfaces disagree on field names within a bounded attempt space, so the consumer cannot complete capture using only provider-published guidance.
- Related class reports searched: #2227, #2630, #3942, #4288, #4596, #4605, #4526 — each documents a different rejected field set, channel, or mechanism.
- No opaque repository-context handles, lineage ids, target hashes, project names, paths, or finding content are included.

title: bug(updater): gentle-ai can't detect engram installed from the release tarball — Homebrew tap lags at 1.20.0 vs 2.0.0-rc.11
body:
### 📝 Bug Description

`gentle-ai update` and `gentle-ai upgrade` abort with `update check failed for: engram` because the active engram binary is not Homebrew-managed. The Homebrew tap (`gentleman-programming/tap/engram`) only publishes stable `1.20.0`, while the latest release is `2.0.0-rc.11`, which is installed via the GitHub release tarball through engram's own install/setup flow. That mismatch blocks the gentle-ai updater, which requires a Homebrew-installed engram to verify and update it.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Install engram `2.0.0-rc.11` from the release tarball (`engram_2.0.0-rc.11_darwin_arm64.tar.gz`) and run `engram setup` so it adds `~/.pi/agent/bin/engram` → `~/.engram/bin/v2.0.0-rc.11/engram` to the agent PATH.
2. Also have engram installed via Homebrew at `/opt/homebrew/opt/engram/bin/engram` (formula `gentleman-programming/tap/engram`, version `1.20.0`).
3. Run `gentle-ai update` (or `gentle-ai upgrade`).
4. Observe the error below; gentle-ai stays on the older version.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

One of:
- The engram Homebrew formula tracks the current release line (so `brew upgrade engram` yields `2.0.0-rc.11`), letting the gentle-ai updater detect the Homebrew-managed engram.
- Or, for the tarball/setup install path, there is a documented, consistent distribution story so `gentle-ai update` does not fail to detect engram.

At minimum, a single engram version/distribution mismatch should not make the gentle-ai update command fail entirely.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

`Error: update check failed for: engram` — the updater aborts, so gentle-ai can only upgrade to `2.9.1` (from `2.8.2`) if engram's Homebrew ownership is resolvable. Because the active engram is `2.0.0-rc.11` installed outside Homebrew paths, and the tap only has `1.20.0`, the update cannot proceed without a workaround.

### Operating System

macOS

### Engram Version

`2.0.0-rc.11` (active, tarball install); Homebrew formula at `1.20.0`

### Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Relevant Logs

```shell
[!!] engram        installed: -           latest: -           check failed: detect Homebrew ownership for engram: active executable "~/.pi/agent/bin/engram" is outside installed Homebrew paths; inspect `brew list --formula --full-name`, `brew list --cask --full-name`, and `command -v engram`

1 update(s) available. 1 check(s) failed.
Error: update check failed for: engram
```

### 💡 Additional Context

Verified root cause (read-only):
- Two engram installs coexist. The ACTIVE one is `~/.pi/agent/bin/engram` → symlink → `~/.engram/bin/v2.0.0-rc.11/engram` (version `2.0.0-rc.11`), created by extracting `~/.engram/downloads/v2.0.0-rc.11/engram_2.0.0-rc.11_darwin_arm64.tar.gz` and adding the PATH symlink via `engram setup`. `~/.pi/agent/bin` precedes `/opt/homebrew/bin` in PATH.
- The Homebrew formula publishes stable `1.20.0` (no HEAD, no cask), so `2.0.0-rc.11` is not obtainable via brew; `brew upgrade engram` cannot produce the active version.
- gentle-ai's updater requires the active executable to be inside an installed Homebrew path, so it errors on the manually installed `2.0.0-rc.11`.
- Related prior issues, none a conforming duplicate: Gentleman-Programming/engram#885 (gentle-ai RC/prerelease install support), Gentleman-Programming/engram#498/#461/#143 (engram setup writing versioned Homebrew Cellar paths — the inverse direction). This issue is that the tap lags releases and the tarball/setup install is detected as non-Homebrew, blocking a third-party updater.
- No downgrade workaround is acceptable: pointing the symlink at the `1.20.0` brew binary would regress the memory runtime. A clean fix should either publish the current release (or a stable `--HEAD`) to the tap, or make the tarball/setup install verifiable by gentle-ai.

title: bug(pi): CodeGraph injection into sdd-remediate.md makes gentle-pi managed remediation refuse the actor ("Unsupported remediation actor content")
body:
## Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

## Bug Description
Gentle AI's optional Pi CodeGraph integration rewrites `~/.pi/agent/agents/sdd-remediate.md`, appending the `<!-- gentle-ai:pi-codegraph-tool -->` and `<!-- gentle-ai:pi-codegraph-guidance -->` blocks and adding `mcp` to the `tools` list. gentle-pi's managed remediation admission (`extensions/gentle-agents.ts`, `admitManagedRemediation`) requires the installed `sdd-remediate` body and tools to equal the packaged `assets/agents/sdd-remediate.md` exactly. The two components contradict each other, so every managed `sdd-remediate` launch is refused before acquire on a machine where CodeGraph for Pi is configured.

This is reported as observed evidence; the internal root cause is not asserted.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Install Gentle AI with Pi as a client and enable the CodeGraph community tool for Pi.
2. Confirm `~/.pi/agent/agents/sdd-remediate.md` ends with the two `gentle-ai:pi-codegraph-*` marker blocks and lists `mcp` in `tools` (all 24 installed Pi child agents carry the same injection).
3. Have an SDD change whose native status selects `nextRecommended: remediate` for a bound failed evidence revision.
4. From a gentle-pi session, submit one managed `sdd-remediate` launch with a valid plan and attempt intent.

## Expected Behavior
Either the Pi CodeGraph integration leaves `sdd-remediate.md` in a shape the managed remediation validator accepts (for example by excluding it from injection, or by comparing only the canonical region), or the validator tolerates Gentle AI's own owned marker blocks. Managed remediation should be launchable on a machine where both features are enabled.

## Actual Behavior
```text
Unsupported remediation actor content; install matching managed assets
```
The refusal happens before acquire; no actor starts and no attempt budget is spent. Native `sdd-attempt status` afterwards shows the same evidence revision, no active attempt and the next ordinal still available.

Local comparison with gentle-pi's own `parseAgentDefinition`:
- installed body starts with the canonical body, then 3230 extra characters of injected CodeGraph guidance (3414 vs 6644 chars);
- installed tools are the canonical 10 plus `mcp` (11 vs 10);
- `model` and `thinking` are not compared and are not the cause.

Removing the two marker blocks and `mcp` from `sdd-remediate.md` only makes the validator's `instructions` and `tools` comparisons pass. This is a per-launch workaround: the injection was observed being re-applied in five separate write batches on the same day during ordinary use, so the file drifts back.

`~/.pi/agent/gentle-ai/managed-assets.json` (schemaVersion 1) has no `agents/*` ownership entries, but the validator does not consult the manifest.

## Environment
- **Gentle AI Version:** 2.9.1 (stable; no `-rc.`/`-main.` tag)
- **gentle-pi Version:** 2.7.0 (npm package on disk)
- **Operating System:** macOS (Darwin arm64)
- **AI Agent / Client:** Pi (gentle-pi managed subagents)
- **Affected Area:** Pi CodeGraph community-tool integration / gentle-pi managed SDD remediation admission

## Additional Context
- #4451 reports `gentle-ai sync` failing on a Pi child CodeGraph tool-block/allowlist conflict; that is a different failure surface (sync exits non-zero). Here sync is not involved: the injected file is on disk and the consumer's remediation validator rejects it.
- #1094 (closed) covers Pi children lacking CodeGraph capability. This is the inverse: the capability injection itself breaks a consumer contract that requires byte-identical managed content.
- gentle-pi re-reads agent definitions from disk on every launch (`lib/agents-config.ts`, `discoverAgents`), so no runtime reload is needed after a disk fix; the problem is that Gentle AI rewrites the file again.

title: bug(review): review start reports created but the authority store stays at zero bytes
body:
### Pre-flight Checks
- [x] I have searched existing issues, including open and closed results, and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I understand this issue needs maintainer approval before any PR can be opened.

### Bug Description

`review start` returns `action: created` with a distinct `lineage_id` and a full lens selection, but the authority store is never written. `review status` then reports `repair.counts` all zero — `lineages: 0`, `events: 0`, **`bytes: 0`** — `candidates: []`, and a `next_transition` of `execute / review.start / fresh_target_ready`, as though no review had ever been started.

Six starts were issued across one session, each returning `created` with its own lineage id. After all six, `bytes` was still `0`.

The effect is a loop with no exit: every commit re-triggers the stop hook, each `review start` reports success, nothing is persisted, and no reviewer result can ever be captured because there is no lineage to capture into.

This is **not** #2700. There, native admission *rejects* the frozen target with a typed stale-target failure and no lineage is created, on 2.2.4 via a different agent. Here the start *succeeds*, a lineage id is returned, and the loss is silent. They may share a cause; the observable outcomes differ.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Gentle AI 2.8.1, `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, agent `claude-code`, Darwin arm64.
2. Run the selectorless status preflight and take the returned `review.start`.
3. Answer the consent envelope with the exact `granted` invocation it carries.
4. Observe `action: created`, a `lineage_id`, `selected_lenses` of four, `correction_budget: 200`.
5. Run the selectorless status preflight again.
6. Observe `repair.counts.bytes: 0`, `candidates: []`, and `next_transition` back at `fresh_target_ready`.
7. Repeat from 2. Each iteration yields a new lineage id and `bytes` stays `0`.

A lineage-scoped status (`--lineage <id>`) *does* return `collect / reviewer_results_required` with the four lens inputs, so the transition is derivable from the id while nothing backs it in the store.

### Expected Behavior

A `review start` that answers `created` has committed authority: a subsequent selectorless status should discover that lineage rather than offering a fresh start, and `repair.counts` should reflect it. If the start cannot persist, it should fail with a typed envelope instead of reporting success.

### Second observation, possibly the same root

The `--base-ref` carried by the provider-issued START stayed pinned to a merge commit six days and 122 commits behind the branch under review, so every candidate was 238 changed files and ~21k lines — almost all of it already merged. Passing `--base-ref <current>` to status instead yields 24 paths for the same working state, a tenfold reduction.

Because the authority store never advances, the recorded base appears unable to move forward on its own. Worth checking whether the stale base and the zero-byte store are the same defect seen from two sides.

The practical cost is that a lens context rendered for the wide candidate is ~1.09 MB per lens, which is not deliverable through a prompt-carried reviewer; scoped to the real change it is around a tenth of that.

### Environment

- gentle-ai 2.8.1, stable, `go1.25.10`
- OS: Darwin arm64
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, protocol 2.x
- Agent: `claude-code`
- `repair.status: unsupported`, `supported_operations: [review/complete-fix, review/validate-fix]`

title: bug(review): Codex capture-result rejects provider-issued rctx2 context on 2.9.1
body:
## Observed behavior

On stable Gentle AI 2.9.1, a negotiated medium-risk review starts successfully and the bound STATUS returns one Codex in-process `review.capture-result` slot. The first exact capture attempt returns no result within the host window. A fresh bound STATUS reoffers the identical slot. The second execution of the exact provider-issued capture then refuses before admission:

`repository_context_unavailable: provider-issued review repository context operation failed; cause: invalid rctx2 repository context; refresh the exact native next_transition before retrying`

No source mutation occurred after START. No reviewer result, receipt, acknowledgement, GitHub mutation, or delivery was created by the review lifecycle.

## Expected behavior

A context issued by the successful START/STATUS binding should be consumable by the exact in-process Codex capture operation, or the bound STATUS should issue a replacement context that can advance the same candidate.

## Actual behavior

The exact slot is reoffered, but the provider-issued context is rejected as invalid. Re-executing the reoffered exact slot refuses before any result can be admitted, leaving the lineage reviewing.

## Minimal reproduction

1. Enable receipt-driven review.
2. Start a negotiated workspace review as Codex and grant candidate-scoped consent.
3. Run the exact bound STATUS operation.
4. Run the exact `review.capture-result` operation with the provider-issued tokens (`--agent`, no relayed input).
5. Re-run only the bound STATUS after the empty result; it reoffers the same slot.
6. Run that exact reoffered capture operation and observe `repository_context_unavailable` with invalid rctx2 context.

## Environment

- Gentle AI: 2.9.1 stable
- Runtime: Codex
- Contract: review integration v2
- Risk: medium
- Selected lens: reliability
- Attempts: two capture executions; first empty at the host boundary, second typed refusal

## Search

Searched open and closed issues for `repository_context_unavailable`, `capture-result`, and Codex repository-context combinations. Existing reports cover older versions, other runtimes, or different failure phases; none established an equivalent 2.9.1 Codex in-process capture failure.

## Privacy

This report intentionally excludes repository identity, absolute paths, source contents, diffs, credentials, raw environment values, and opaque target/context/revision identifiers.

title: Review relay timeout permanently stops valid RDD candidate
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description
A Pi-host-relayed RDD review can exceed the relay timeout for a materialized reviewer prompt. Retrying the exact provider-issued slot then declares the lens unachievable and leaves the candidate in a terminal `stop` state, even though earlier lenses completed successfully.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce
1. Enable Receipt-driven development in an interactive Pi session.
2. Start an ordinary review for a high-risk working-tree candidate (observed: 13 files, 334 changed lines, four lenses).
3. Capture the first lenses successfully.
4. Capture a remaining materialized lens through `pi_host_relay` and acknowledge the forecast.
5. Wait for the reviewer subprocess to reach the relay timeout.
6. Retry only the exact reoffered one-slot binding from a fresh STATUS.

### ✅ Expected Behavior
The reviewer completes within the configured bound, or a transport timeout remains recoverable without permanently stopping the review. The system should distinguish a transient model runtime timeout from an intrinsically unachievable lens.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
The reviewer was killed after 948741 ms against a 948701 ms relay limit for a 56740-byte prompt. The provider committed `unachievable_lens_slot` with `relay_transport_bound_exceeded` and transitioned the review to terminal `stop`. A previous grouped attempt also timed out after approximately the same bound without submitting reviewers.

### Gentle AI Version
2.9.0

### Operating System
Linux (Arch/Manjaro)

### AI Agent / Client
Other

### 📋 Affected Area
CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output
```shell
outcome: unachievable-lens-slot-declared
reason: pi reviewer subprocess exceeded the relay bound
failure.kind: pi-timed-out
elapsed_ms: 948741
timeout_ms: 948701
prompt_bytes: 56740
provider_action: stop
stop reason: unachievable_lens_slot
slot reason: relay_transport_bound_exceeded
```

### Additional Context
The AI client was Pi. Two earlier lenses (`review-risk` and `review-resilience`) completed. A grouped capture of the two remaining lenses first timed out with zero submitted reviewers and instructed the caller to request fresh STATUS. The exact reoffered readability slot then timed out again and became permanently unachievable. The suggested workaround is to raise `GENTLE_PI_REVIEW_RELAY_PI_TIMEOUT_MS` (up to 7200000 ms) or reduce candidate scope, but neither addresses whether timeout classification should be recoverable.

title: bug(review): STATUS invalid_request cites untracked nested-git dir that does not exist in cwd (2.7.0)
body:
## Summary
`gentle-ai review status` (with `--next-transition`) fails deterministically in the `preflight` phase with `invalid_request`, citing an untracked directory inside the review cwd that allegedly holds another (non-worktree) Git repository — but no such nested `.git` exists anywhere under that cwd.

## Environment
- gentle-ai 2.7.0
- OS: Linux
- Runtime: Claude Code, contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, agent `claude-code`

## Repro shape
1. `gentle-ai review status --cwd <repo> --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --agent claude-code --next-transition` → returns a fresh `review.start` transition (normal).
2. Ran the returned `review start ... --consent=granted` → succeeds, returns `state: reviewing`, one lens selected, and a `next_transition` pointing to `review.status` with `--repository-context=<handle>` and `--lineage=<id>`.
3. Running that exact returned `review status --contract=... --next-transition=true --lineage=<id> --repository-context=<handle> --agent=claude-code --projection=workspace` fails every time with:
```json
{
  "schema": "gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2",
  "phase": "preflight",
  "code": "invalid_request",
  "mutation_outcome": "not_started",
  "retry_safe": true,
  "cause": "untracked directory \"src<redacted>\" holds another Git repository that is not a linked worktree of this one, so it cannot enter the review candidate: add it to .gitignore, move it outside this repository, or register it as a linked worktree"
}
```
4. Retried the identical command a second time (per the retry_safe hint) — same failure, byte-identical shape.

## Investigation done client-side
- `find <repo-root> -maxdepth 8 -name ".git"` inside the target repo cwd returns exactly one hit: the repo's own `.git`. No nested `.git` directory or file exists anywhere under the cwd.
- `git status --porcelain -uall` at the repo root shows no untracked top-level directory matching a `src...`-shaped path.
- Repo layout context: this is a workspace where several independent Git repositories exist as **sibling** directories under a common parent that is itself not a Git repo (documented, intentional layout — a monorepo-style workspace, not a single repo with nested submodules). The repo passed as `--cwd` for review is one such sibling; other sibling repos live outside that cwd's directory tree entirely, not underneath it. It's unclear why the untracked-nested-git-repo check appears to be firing against something that isn't actually inside the reviewed repo's worktree.

## Expected
Either the preflight correctly detects no nested-repo condition (matching what `find`/`git status` show), or, if it is intentionally scanning outside the given `--cwd`, the error message should name the actual offending path so it can be diagnosed and fixed, rather than a path that doesn't correspond to any real nested `.git`.

## Actual
Deterministic `invalid_request` at `review.status` preflight, blocking the frozen `reviewing` lineage from progressing past its first `next_transition`, with no way to locate or resolve the cited path.

title: feat(sync): list the files sync --dry-run would touch instead of only step counts
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Problem Statement

`sync --dry-run` is documented as `preview plan without executing`, but its report only prints aggregate pipeline step counts. It never names the files the run would write, and its output does not change with the state of the system.

Measured on **v2.9.1**, macOS arm64 (Homebrew), same machine, same flags, two consecutive runs:

| run | system state | `--dry-run` reported | the following real `sync` wrote |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | after upgrading 2.7.0 → 2.9.1, managed assets stale | `Prepare steps: 1` / `Apply steps: 9` | **38 files** |
| 2 | immediately after run 1, assets current | `Prepare steps: 1` / `Apply steps: 9` — byte-identical | **2 files** |

The preview is identical while the real work differs by an order of magnitude, so an operator cannot use it to decide whether to proceed. In run 1 the rewritten files included `~/.claude/settings.json`, `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.claude.json`, `~/.config/gga/config` and 19 agent definitions — exactly the blast radius a preview exists to disclose.

To learn what the sync would touch, I had to back up the config tree, run the real sync, and diff. That is the operation `--dry-run` exists to make unnecessary.

**This is not a counting bug.** `Plan.Prepare` / `Plan.Apply` are pipeline units and `ChangedFiles` are written paths; they are different magnitudes by design, and `9` is not a wrong version of `38`. The request is for the **list**, not for a corrected number.

**The doctrine is already stated in this repo, inside the same function.** `RenderSyncReport` (`internal/cli/sync.go`), executed branch:

```go
// Report actual files changed — not the count of successful pipeline steps.
fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Sync actions executed: %d files changed\n", result.FilesChanged)

if len(result.ChangedFiles) > 0 {
	for _, path := range result.ChangedFiles {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  - %s\n", path)
	}
}
```

The `result.DryRun` branch ~10 lines above prints `len(result.Plan.Prepare)` and `len(result.Plan.Apply)` instead.

There is a second consequence. The `result.NoOp` branch can conclude `All managed assets are already up to date. No files changed.`, but a dry-run never reaches that conclusion: run 2 above printed 9 apply steps on an already-current system. So `--dry-run` cannot currently answer "is there anything to do at all?".

**Relationship to existing issues** (checked open and closed):

- **#198 → PR #498** (merged 2026-05-28) added precisely this for the executed sync. The dry-run branch never received it. This issue asks for symmetry with that decision.
- **#1273** (open, `status:approved`) lists this as point 2 of its proposed solution. While implementing it, @ardelperal wrote: *"Skipping the `sync --dry-run` UX improvement (point #2 of the issue's proposed solution) — it's nice-to-have, not the must-have the issue's first paragraph demands. Can be a follow-up issue/PR if reviewers want it."* This issue is that follow-up.
- **PR #3906** (open) declares `Closes #1273` while covering only `last_synced_at`. If it merges, #1273 closes and point 2 is left without a home — which is why this is filed separately rather than as a comment there.
- **#3984** asks the `install --dry-run` plan to report the effective SDD mode: same principle (a dry run should be a trustworthy read path), different command and different datum.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

In the `result.DryRun` branch of `RenderSyncReport`, report the planned paths, mirroring the executed branch:

```
gentle-ai sync — dry-run
Agents: claude-code
Managed components: persona, sdd, engram, context7, gga, skills
Sync actions planned: 38 files would change
  - /Users/me/.claude/settings.json
  - /Users/me/.claude/CLAUDE.md
  ...
```

Two properties matter more than the exact formatting:

1. **The planned set is derived from the same comparison the apply path uses**, so that "what dry-run listed" and "what sync wrote" cannot drift.
2. **An already-current system reports that it is current**, i.e. a dry-run on a synced machine states there is nothing to do instead of printing a fixed step count.

If the plan cannot be resolved to paths before execution without restructuring, printing the per-step managed component and target agent for each of the `Apply` steps would already be a large improvement over a bare integer, and could be an incremental first slice.

I am happy to implement this and open the PR if the issue gets `status:approved` — I would follow whatever shape the maintainers prefer between the full path list and the incremental slice above.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

1. **Back up, run the real sync, diff.** What I do today. It requires mutating the system to learn what the mutation would have been, and it needs an out-of-band backup to be reversible.
2. **A new `--verbose` or `--json` flag.** Adds CLI surface for something the existing flag already promises; `sync --help` documents `--dry-run` as `preview plan without executing`.
3. **Infer scope from `--exclude` (#4036).** Orthogonal: that controls what is synced, not what is disclosed beforehand.
4. **Do nothing, and document that the dry-run reports pipeline shape rather than file impact.** Cheapest, but it leaves `--dry-run` unable to answer the question operators actually ask before a sync.

### 📎 Additional Context

- **Version:** `gentle-ai 2.9.1` · **OS:** macOS (Darwin 25.5.0, arm64) · **Install:** Homebrew, `gentleman-programming/tap` · **Agent:** claude-code
- Verified against `main` at the time of filing: the dry-run branch still prints only the two counts.
- **How I hit it:** we keep a pinned manifest of the base-layer assets gentle-ai manages, and our upgrade protocol says to preview the sync plan before applying it. That step could not be carried out, so the upgrade proceeded on a manual backup instead.
- Exit code was `0` in both runs; nothing here is a crash or a failure, only a preview that cannot be acted upon.
- **AI assistance disclosure** (per `AI_POLICY.md`): the measurements above were produced and the text drafted with AI assistance on my machine, from a real 2.7.0 → 2.9.1 upgrade. I reviewed the report and the cited source before filing, and the numbers are from actual runs rather than estimates.

title: bug(provider): opencode-go gateway route deepseek-v4.1-flash hangs / fails at transport layer — GLM route on same gateway healthy
body:
## Summary

On the `opencode-go` managed provider in OpenCode (gateway reported in errors as "Console Go"), the `deepseek-v4.1-flash` route fails at the network/transport layer while a GLM model on the same gateway and same client works. User-facing reproducible since after a laptop sleep, and reproducible in a cold test today.

## Environment (scrubbed)

- gentle-ai build: `2.9.1` (stable, no prerelease suffix)
- Client: OpenCode 1.18.30/1.18.31
- OS/arch: macOS (Apple Silicon), darwin
- Provider: `opencode-go` (key auth present and valid; GLM calls bill and respond normally)
- Model: `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` (ID confirmed present in `opencode models` catalog)

## Observed behavior

1. Session traffic to `deepseek-v4.1-flash` fails with:
   `AI_APICallError: Cannot connect to API: Unable to connect. Is the computer able to access the url?` (transport error, not a 4xx model-name error)
2. A retry attempt logged the alternate cause wording: `Cannot connect to API: Was there a typo in the url or port?`
3. Cold `opencode run -m 'opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash' 'Reply with the single word OK.'` hangs with no output for 90+ seconds and must be killed.
4. Control test on same gateway, same client, same moment: a GLM model route completes a round trip normally (reacts with an upstream response).
5. Reboot of the machine and restart of the client did not clear it; network to the general internet is fine (web searches succeed).

## Expected behavior

`deepseek-v4.1-flash` on the `opencode-go` gateway should stream a completion like GLM routes on the same gateway.

## Timeline note

Observed on Sep 14, 2026 (UTC-3), the same day DeepSeek began serving `deepseek-v4-pro` requests with V4.1 Flash (first-party routing migration announced by DeepSeek). Possibly related gateway-side route configuration.

## Reproduction

- From an OpenCode session: select `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` as primary model, send any message → transport error.
- CLI: `opencode run -m 'opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash' 'Reply with the single word OK.'` → hangs ≥90 s.

No reproduction depends on specific network conditions beyond ordinary connectivity; both a sleeping-and-woken laptop and a fully rebooted machine show it, and the same machine reaches the gateway fine with other model routes.

## Workaround observed

Model routes whose non-DeepSeek IDs share the same gateway remain usable; switching primary model off `deepseek-v4.1-flash` restores the session.

title: bug(review 2.9.0): in-process claude-code refuter result refused by the strict decoder — json: unknown field "name" (capture-refuter), admitted on the re-offered retry
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues, open and closed, and this is not a duplicate. Closest reports are listed under "Relationship to prior art" below; none covers the provider refuter decoder on the claude-code runtime rejecting an unknown top-level field.
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

Automated provider-defect report filed after the operator consented. Observed behavior only; no root cause is asserted.

On `gentle-ai 2.9.0` (stable channel; the build string carries no `-rc.` or `-main.` tag), a compact-v2 review on the `claude-code` runtime reached `provider_refuter_required` after its single lens (`review-reliability`) was admitted with one `CRITICAL` finding of `evidence_class: inferential`. The exact provider-issued `review capture-refuter --agent=claude-code` command was run verbatim. The in-process refuter produced a result that native admission refused with:

```
decode provider refuter result: json: unknown field "name"
```

The bound STATUS re-offered the identical refuter slot. The second run of the same command, tokens unchanged, was admitted (`role: refuter`, verdict upholding the finding) and the lineage moved to `correction_required`. So on this build the stray field is not deterministic, the same shape reported for the targeted validator in #4053.

Two further observations from the same lineage, recorded here because they belong to the same run:

1. The admitted refuter result's `proof` text states that its review workspace directory was empty ("no checkout, not a git repository"), so it adjudicated from the supplied diff hunks alone and marked the conftest/module-mark question "unverifiable". The refuter therefore upheld a CRITICAL it could not inspect.
2. The very next bound STATUS after `correction_required` returned `stop` / `corrupted_or_unverifiable_authority`. That half is reported as an occurrence on #4571, which already tracks it.

The store preserves no rejected payload for the first attempt (the gap #1867 names), so the error string above is quoted from the operator's session record, not from an artifact on disk.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. With receipt-driven development enabled, run the selectorless STATUS preflight for `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2` with `--agent claude-code` on a committed feature-branch candidate (`--committed-only`, explicit `--base-ref`, `workspace` projection).
2. Run the returned START with `--consent=relay`, answer the consent/v3 envelope with the `granted` invocation. Candidate here: medium risk, 2 changed files, 141 changed lines, one selected lens `review-reliability`, correction budget 71.
3. Run the bound STATUS, then the single returned `review.capture-result` (`--agent=claude-code`, no `--input`). The lens returns one inferential CRITICAL; admission accepts it.
4. Bound STATUS returns `collect` / `provider_refuter_required`. Run the returned `review.capture-refuter` verbatim.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The in-process refuter's own output is admissible by its own decoder, or an unknown top-level field is tolerated or stripped so a completed refuter run is never turned into an operator-facing refusal. If the provider must fail closed, the failure should say the provider's own refuter output was malformed rather than that the operator's request needs correction.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

- Attempt 1: `capture-refuter` refused, cause `decode provider refuter result: json: unknown field "name"`.
- Bound STATUS: identical refuter slot re-offered.
- Attempt 2 (same tokens): admitted; lineage state `correction_required`, `fix_finding_ids` carries the one CRITICAL.
- Refuter `proof` on the admitted result reports an empty, non-git reviewer workspace, so the adjudication never inspected the frozen trees.

### Relationship to prior art (open and closed)

- #4053 (closed): the same decoder class, `json: unknown field "passed_note_unused"`, on the **targeted validator**; the occurrence comment there also notes the field was non-deterministic across two byte-identical runs. Here the role is the **provider refuter** and the field is `name`.
- #3942 (closed): the same class on the **reviewer lens** decoder (`unknown field "lens"`, `"paths_note"`), claude-code in-process. Its archaeology comment names the strict facade decoding (`DisallowUnknownFields`).
- #4439 (open): provider refuter on claude-code returning **no JSON object at all** (tool-use narration). Here a JSON object was returned and rejected on one field.
- #4422 (open): refuter admission rejecting **truncated** JSON on the Pi relay. Different payload shape and runtime.
- #1867 (open): rejected payload preservation; applies here, since the refused bytes are not on disk.
- #4571 (open): the `corrupted_or_unverifiable_authority` stop right after `correction_required`; the second half of this run is filed there as an occurrence.

No published release notes for `v2.9.0` or `v2.9.1` (latest stable at filing time) mention the refuter decoder, so no relevant published fix is known for this class on the stable channel.

### 🧾 Observed evidence

- Gentle AI version: `2.9.0` (stable). Latest published stable at report time: `2.9.1` (2026-09-14).
- OS/arch: `Darwin arm64`
- Client: Claude Code, in-process capture (`--agent=claude-code`, no `--input`)
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, projection `workspace`, `--committed-only` with explicit `--base-ref`
- Lineage: `review-a36a8cfd114b3997` · target identity `sha256:f7e5a225483adfd5b7360b8a6ae4c1536343bec787e137a91a340bb6f99814e4`
- Store record after the admitted retry: schema `gentle-ai.review-state-record/v2`, revision `sha256:f060741977aa099d59523194fe0a712fd0d39848027219a2427b73c798355f45`, `state: correction_required`, `selected_lenses: [review-reliability]`, `original_changed_lines: 141`, `correction_budget: 71`
- Bounded attempts: two `capture-refuter` runs on the same re-offered slot (1 refused, 1 admitted); no other retry.
- Date: 2026-09-14

### 🔒 Preserved state

No source change, reset, push, delivery action or `review mode` change was made as part of this failure. The candidate was later superseded by a corrected candidate under a new lineage; this lineage remains in the store as history. No labels were touched on any issue.

title: bug(tui): fresh cooldown results contradict the current release advisory
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

The TUI can show a current release advisory while simultaneously labeling `Upgrade tools` as `(up to date)`. This happens when an earlier successful update check leaves `LastUpdateCheck` inside the six-hour cooldown across a release publication. The advisory is fetched independently and reflects the new release, while the cooldown-suppressed update check returns no results and the welcome menu treats that absence as authoritative proof that every tool is current.

This is a false status, not a Homebrew publication delay. For v2.9.1, the release and tap formula were already published when the contradiction was observed.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch the Gentle AI TUI before a new release and allow its update check to complete, which records `LastUpdateCheck`.
2. Publish a new release and update the release advisory before the six-hour cooldown expires.
3. Launch the TUI again within that cooldown window.
4. Observe that the advisory names the new release while the menu says `Upgrade tools (up to date)`.
5. Open `Upgrade tools` and observe that the TUI offers no upgrade from the suppressed result set.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The advisory and updater must not present contradictory release state. If a fresh remote update check was skipped, the TUI must not claim that all tools are up to date. It should either refresh when the advisory indicates a newer release or represent the check as cached/skipped/unknown without a false success claim.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The uncached advisory announces the newly published version, but the shared cooldown returns no update results. The TUI marks the check complete and renders `Upgrade tools (up to date)`, leaving the user unable to initiate the advertised upgrade from that screen.

### Gentle AI Version

Observed while the installed binary was older than v2.9.1 and v2.9.1 was the upgrade target. The current environment is now v2.9.1, and the same timestamp-only cooldown behavior remains in the v2.9.1 source.

### Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client

OpenCode

### 📋 Affected Area

TUI (terminal UI)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
_No response_
```

### Additional Context

Source-path evidence:

- `internal/app/app.go` intentionally skips pre-dispatch self-update for direct TUI entry.
- `internal/tui/model.go` independently starts the update check and advisory fetch.
- `internal/update/cooldown.go` caches only `LastUpdateCheck`; during the six-hour TTL it returns no result set.
- `internal/tui/screens/welcome.go` maps a completed check with no detected updates to `Upgrade tools (up to date)`.
- `internal/update/advisory.go` fetches the advisory independently, so it can reflect a release published after the cached update timestamp.

Related but non-duplicate issues:

- #872 introduced the broader update-experience design, including the separate cooldown and advisory paths.
- #4111 tracks false up-to-date behavior caused by update-check timeouts, not cooldown suppression.
- #157 fixed stale positive results after an upgrade, the inverse state problem.
- #4086 fixed concurrent install-state clobbering during cooldown persistence, not result authority.

A regression test should combine a fresh `LastUpdateCheck`, an advisory naming a newer release, and the welcome menu rendering. Existing tests exercise these states separately and therefore do not catch the contradiction.

title: bug(claude-code): jd-fix-agent/jd-judge-a/jd-judge-b hardcode mcp__plugin_engram_engram__* prefix, unlike sdd-* agents
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

After `gentle-ai sync --agent claude-code` on gentle-ai 2.9.0, the managed Claude Code agent files `jd-fix-agent.md`, `jd-judge-a.md`, and `jd-judge-b.md` declare their Engram memory tools only with the plugin-namespaced prefix `mcp__plugin_engram_engram__*` (`mem_search`, `mem_get_observation`, `mem_save`, `mem_update`), while the managed `sdd-*` agents declare both `mcp__engram__*` and `mcp__plugin_engram_engram__*` for every Engram tool.

This is the same defect class reported and fixed in #2698 and #3778, but that fix was scoped only to the `sdd-*` agent templates. In the source repository, `internal/components/sdd/inject.go` documents the fix: asset templates carry a `{{ENGRAM_TOOL_PREFIX}}<tool>` placeholder that `expandEngramToolNames` expands to both `mcp__engram__$1, mcp__plugin_engram_engram__$1` at sync time (see the `#2698/#3778` comment above that function). The `jd-*` source templates (`internal/assets/claude/agents/jd-fix-agent.md`, `jd-judge-a.md`, `jd-judge-b.md`) do not use that placeholder — they hardcode `mcp__plugin_engram_engram__*` directly in their `tools:` frontmatter, so the earlier fix never reached them.

Separately, the Engram Claude Code plugin (`engram@engram` 0.1.2, marketplace `Gentleman-Programming/engram`) no longer ships a `.mcp.json`. Its session-start hook now delegates to `engram setup claude-code --mcp-only`, which registers a direct user-scope MCP server named `engram`. At runtime this exposes only `mcp__engram__*` tools (verified this session: `claude mcp list` shows a plain `engram: engram mcp --tools=agent` entry, no plugin-scoped entry). Under this now-current plugin behavior, the three `jd-*` agents' Engram tool grants are dead — the declared tool names never resolve, while `sdd-*` agents still work via their `mcp__engram__*` declarations.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. On gentle-ai 2.9.0, with Claude Code as the target agent and the Engram Claude Code plugin (`engram@engram` 0.1.2) installed via the marketplace, run `gentle-ai sync --agent claude-code`.
2. Inspect the generated `tools:` frontmatter line in each managed agent file: `jd-fix-agent.md`, `jd-judge-a.md`, `jd-judge-b.md`, and any `sdd-*.md` agent (e.g. `sdd-apply.md`).
3. Observe the three `jd-*` files declare Engram tools only under `mcp__plugin_engram_engram__*`, while the `sdd-*` file declares both `mcp__engram__*` and `mcp__plugin_engram_engram__*` for the same tool names.
4. Confirm the plugin's current runtime registration with `claude mcp list` — it registers a direct `engram` MCP server exposing only `mcp__engram__*` tools in the session, not `mcp__plugin_engram_engram__*`.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The `jd-fix-agent`, `jd-judge-a`, and `jd-judge-b` templates use the same `{{ENGRAM_TOOL_PREFIX}}` placeholder mechanism already used by the `sdd-*` agents (or otherwise emit a single prefix consistent with the Engram plugin's current registration, `mcp__engram__*`), so their Engram tool grants actually resolve at runtime — bringing them in line with the fix already applied to `sdd-*` agents in #2698 and #3778.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

`jd-fix-agent.md`, `jd-judge-a.md`, and `jd-judge-b.md` declare Engram tools only as `mcp__plugin_engram_engram__*`, which does not match the Engram plugin's current direct-route registration. Engram tools never resolve for these three agents, so `jd-fix-agent`, `jd-judge-a`, and `jd-judge-b` run judgment-day review/fix work with no working memory tools despite declaring the grants, while `sdd-*` agents remain functional through their `mcp__engram__*` declarations.

---
## 🖥️ Environment

### Gentle AI Version

2.9.0

### Operating System

Linux (Arch/Manjaro)

### AI Agent / Client

Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area

Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
tools: Read, Glob, Grep, mcp__plugin_engram_engram__mem_search, mcp__plugin_engram_engram__mem_get_observation, mcp__codegraph__codegraph_explore
# ^ jd-judge-a.md / jd-judge-b.md (identical shape)

tools: Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep, Bash, mcp__plugin_engram_engram__mem_search, mcp__plugin_engram_engram__mem_get_observation, mcp__plugin_engram_engram__mem_save, mcp__plugin_engram_engram__mem_update, mcp__codegraph__codegraph_explore
# ^ jd-fix-agent.md

tools: Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep, Bash, mcp__engram__mem_search, mcp__plugin_engram_engram__mem_search, mcp__engram__mem_get_observation, mcp__plugin_engram_engram__mem_get_observation, mcp__engram__mem_save, mcp__plugin_engram_engram__mem_save, mcp__engram__mem_update, mcp__plugin_engram_engram__mem_update, mcp__codegraph__codegraph_explore
# ^ sdd-apply.md, for comparison — both prefixes present
```

### Additional Context

- Engram: 2.0.0-rc.11. Engram Claude Code plugin: `engram@engram` 0.1.2 (marketplace `Gentleman-Programming/engram`, commit `a2199d9`, 2026-09-14). This plugin version no longer ships a `.mcp.json`; its session-start hook delegates to `engram setup claude-code --mcp-only`, which registers Engram as a direct user-scope MCP server (`engram: engram mcp --tools=agent` per `claude mcp list`), not a plugin-scoped one.
- Not a duplicate of #2698 or #3778: both are closed and scoped explicitly to `sdd-*` agents; neither mentions `jd-fix-agent`, `jd-judge-a`, or `jd-judge-b`. This report is the same root-cause class recurring in agent templates the earlier fix did not cover.
- Not a duplicate of #4532: that issue is about `gentle-ai sync` skipping the `mcpServers.engram` *registration* entry for a plugin that declares no MCP server (a sync-time registration bug). This report is about the *tool-name prefix* declared in already-generated agent frontmatter being wrong for three specific agents, independent of registration.

title: gentle-pi postinstall masks recoverable Go module fetch failure as SumDB error
body:
## Problem
`gentle-pi@2.6.4` fails during its postinstall while installing the package-local Gentle AI v2.9.0 binary. The surfaced message classifies the failure as a Go SumDB source-install failure, but it omits the underlying Go stderr needed to diagnose the actual network/module error.

## Environment
- Windows 10.0.22631, amd64
- Node.js 24.14.1
- npm 11.11.0
- Go 1.26.1
- Pi 0.85.1
- gentle-pi 2.6.4
- Gentle AI target 2.9.0

## Observed evidence
- Two bounded extension-update attempts reached the `gentle-pi` postinstall and failed with the same generic SumDB message.
- Before the second attempt, direct installation of the exact public Gentle AI module/version completed successfully.
- The default public Go module proxy returned HTTP 403 for transitive modules; direct module fetching succeeded.
- Pi core updated successfully, but extension mutation remained incomplete because npm rolled back after the postinstall failure.
- npm also emitted non-fatal Windows `EPERM` cleanup warnings after rollback.

## Minimal reproduction
1. On Windows with the versions above, update Pi extensions so npm installs `gentle-pi@2.6.4`.
2. Observe the `install-gentle-ai.mjs` postinstall failure.
3. Compare with a direct Go installation of `github.com/gentleman-programming/gentle-ai/v2/cmd/gentle-ai@v2.9.0` using a reachable module-fetch path.

## Expected behavior
The postinstall should either complete when the exact module can be installed, or preserve bounded underlying Go stderr and identify the failed network stage accurately.

## Actual behavior
The postinstall exits with only: `Gentle AI Go SumDB source installation failed for github.com/gentleman-programming/gentle-ai/v2/cmd/gentle-ai@v2.9.0.` This prevents distinguishing a SumDB integrity failure from a module-proxy/network failure.

## Scope
This report records observed behavior only; it does not assert an unverified root cause.

title: bug(review 2.9.0): correction_required still exposes no corroborated findings — collect/correction_plan_required omits correction_request on a build containing #4224 (possible regression of #4087)
body:
Automated provider-defect report. Observed evidence only; no root cause asserted.

Filed as a **possible regression** of #4087, per its closing condition ("Re-open with the STATUS envelope if a current build returns `correction_required` without `correction_request`"). Not reopening automatically — filing a linked report instead, because the installed build is three stable releases newer than the one that closed it.

## Environment

- Build: `gentle-ai 2.9.0` (no `-rc.` / `-main.` tag → stable evidence channel)
- OS / arch: Windows 10 / x86_64 (MINGW64 shell)
- Client: claude-code (in-process reviewer capture, `--agent`, no `--input`)
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`
- Projection: `workspace` (uncommitted working-tree candidate, no `--committed-only`)
- Candidate: medium tier, 2 changed files, 201 changed lines, frozen correction budget 101
- Selected lenses: `review-reliability` (single lens)

## Fix-containment evidence

The remediation named in #4087's closure is #4224 (merged 2026-09-05T22:35Z). Its merge commit is **contained** in the installed release:

- `compare/v2.9.0...<#4224 merge commit>` → `status: behind`, `ahead_by: 0`, `behind_by: 313`
- `compare/v2.7.0...<#4224 merge commit>` → `status: behind`, `ahead_by: 0`, `behind_by: 112`

So this is not release-gap evidence: the installed stable build demonstrably contains the fix and the defect still reproduces.

## Expected

Per #4087's closure: after a reviewer capture closes `correction_required`, the bound STATUS answers `collect` / `correction_plan_required` and its `next_transition.correction_request.findings` carries every corroborated finding with id, severity, location, claim, proof references and evidence — so the orchestrator can author the one bounded in-budget correction the contract permits.

## Actual

The lifecycle reaches `collect` / `correction_plan_required` as promised, but **no `correction_request` and no findings are present on that envelope**, so the bounded correction remains unauthorable.

Observed sequence:

1. `review capture-result` (in-process, `--agent`, lens `review-reliability`) returned `gentle-ai.review-last-event-closure/v1` with `state: correction_required`, `action: "candidate-caused severe findings require one bounded correction"`. Top-level keys were exactly: `schema`, `operation`, `lineage_id`, `state`, `action`, `status_continuation`, `store_revision`. No finding content on any of them.
2. Ran the returned `status_continuation` verbatim. It answered `next_transition.kind: collect`, `reason_code: correction_plan_required`. `next_transition.collect.inputs` contained exactly one input, `correction_lines`, whose keys were `name`, `schema`, `capture_operation`, `arguments`, `submission`. **There is no `correction_request` key anywhere on the envelope**, and no `findings` on the input. Sibling fields: `candidates: []`, `frozen: {tier, original_changed_lines, correction_budget}` only.
3. Submitted `review capture-correction-plan` with `--correction-lines` at the budget maximum (the only value slot offered; `domain: positive_correction_lines`, min 1, max 101). Accepted; `state` stayed `correction_required`.
4. Re-queried the bound STATUS. It returned `next_transition.kind: stop`, `reason_code: corrected_candidate_unavailable`.

The documented continuation for `corrected_candidate_unavailable` is to change the correction candidate and re-query. That is unreachable here: the contract permits edits to map only to corroborated frozen findings, and no surface ever named them.

## Non-determinism

In the same session, same host, same client, same contract and the same single `review-reliability` lens, a **larger** medium-tier candidate in a different repository (7 changed files, 428 changed lines) completed normally: `approved` → exact `acknowledge-approved` → `authority: burned`. Only the 2-file / 201-line candidate dead-ended. Both were `workspace` projection, both in-process capture.

## Minimal reproduction

1. On `gentle-ai 2.9.0` stable with review mode enabled, produce an uncommitted working-tree candidate that a single `review-reliability` lens will close as `correction_required`.
2. Run the selectorless STATUS preflight, then the exact returned START with `--consent granted`.
3. Run the returned `review capture-result` with `--agent` (in-process capture).
4. On `correction_required`, run the returned `status_continuation` verbatim and inspect the envelope for `correction_request`.

Observed: `collect` / `correction_plan_required` with a `correction_lines` slot and no `correction_request`.

## Preserved state

The lineage remains in `correction_required`. No reset, recover, delete or reopen was performed, and no labels were changed on #4087. Its corroborated findings were never exposed, so no claim is made that they were resolved.

## Possibly related

#4571 reports a different failure on the same transition (`correction_required` capture's own `status_continuation` classifying the just-minted authority `corrupted_or_unverifiable_authority` on 2.8.2). The reason code observed here is `corrected_candidate_unavailable`, and the authority was never reported corrupt, so these look distinct.

title: feat(hermes): first-class native integration through a profile-scoped plugin
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues and PRs; this updates the existing tracker rather than opening a duplicate.
- [x] I understand implementation requires the repository's `status:approved` process. This issue does not authorize a PR on its own.

### 🔍 Affected Area

Hermes adapter, installation/sync lifecycle, managed methodology assets, and optional native Hermes plugin. Native RDD is a separate capability requiring its own proof.

### 💡 Problem

I use Hermes as the central agent environment. I want one selected coding profile (for example `coder`) to use Gentle AI's current methodology while Hermes executes the work. Other profiles should remain unchanged. Updates should arrive through Gentle AI without a private fork, manually copied prompts, or a second coding runtime.

The existing Hermes adapter and native `delegate_task` integration remain useful. This issue asks for a supported profile-scoped integration and plugin lifecycle, not a rewrite of Hermes.

**Update (2026-09-29):** The original September 14 proposal described SDD and OpenSpec as live workflows. [#4967](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/4967) merged on September 25 and retired them from `main` in favor of **ODD**. Independent RDD and Strict TDD remain. This proposal now targets ODD. Historical SDD names may still appear in compatibility code or installed assets; they are migration inputs, not new integration targets.

### 📍 Current state and remaining gaps

| Area | Verified on 2026-09-29 | Consequence for this issue |
|---|---|---|
| Workflow | [#4967](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/4967) merged: ODD replaces live SDD/OpenSpec on `main`. | Render and test the current ODD guidance and artifacts. Do not rebuild retired SDD phases, commands, or OpenSpec integration. |
| Scoped sync | [#5080](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/5080) merged `sync --scope=workspace`, isolating workspace-managed writes from global state. | Reuse that machinery where applicable. **Workspace scope is not Hermes profile selection**; a profile target still needs resolution and persistence. |
| Hermes home | [`adapter.go`](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/main/internal/agents/hermes/adapter.go) still returns `homeDir/.hermes`. [#4079](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/4079) is open and unmerged; [#4901](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/4901) closed without merge. | Coordinate the existing path issue [#2094](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/2094) and PR instead of submitting a competing path-only fix. Account for native Windows defaults and `HERMES_HOME`. |
| Native review | The current [capability manifest](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/main/internal/agents/capabilitymanifest/manifest.go) does not advertise Hermes for review transport or immutable review execution. | A plugin with ODD does **not** imply native RDD. Prove transport and reviewer isolation before advertising it. |
| Strict TDD | Independent, selectable behavior remains after the ODD migration. | Preserve the selected policy and actual RED/GREEN evidence where applicable; do not turn every change into a mandatory TDD ceremony. |

These findings describe current `main` and PR state, not proof that any proposed Hermes plugin runs.

### 🎯 Proposed boundary

```text
Gentle AI (source of truth)
  ├─ ODD instructions, skills, Strict TDD policy, RDD contracts
  ├─ adapter and managed install/sync/doctor/uninstall
  └─ optional Hermes plugin bundle
            ↓
Selected HERMES_HOME profile
  ├─ native plugin: bounded context, skills, useful lifecycle hooks
  └─ Hermes: execution, delegate_task, tools, models, worktrees, state
```

Keep the adapter thin and the methodology generated from Gentle's canonical assets. The plugin is an optional Hermes-native delivery and runtime layer, **not** an independent copy of Gentle or another worker engine. Native Hermes features remain owned by Hermes.

### 🧩 Design work

#### 1. Resolve the selected profile throughout the lifecycle

Use the effective Hermes home (including `HERMES_HOME`) for install, sync, doctor, backup/restore and uninstall. The adapter currently hardcodes `.hermes`. Coordinate the shared resolver with #2094/#4079, including Windows behavior.

Persist the minimum selected target in Gentle's installation state. If a later shell lacks the original environment setting, `sync` must use the recorded target or stop on ambiguity; it must not silently write to `default`. Installing into `coder` must not alter `default`, `ops`, or another profile.

Keep **workspace** and **profile** as distinct axes: #5080 prevents unwanted global writes during workspace sync but does not select a Hermes home.

#### 2. Evaluate a Gentle-managed Hermes plugin

Proposed package, subject to Hermes' actual packaging contract:

```text
<HERMES_HOME>/plugins/gentle-ai/
  plugin.yaml
  __init__.py
  managed assets
```

Use public plugin APIs for a short ODD entry point, namespaced skills, and hooks only where they offer a measurable guarantee. Normal Hermes skills can remain outside the plugin when native discovery works better. Plugin skills are not automatically listed with ordinary skills, so show the exact entry skill and hand it explicitly to workers. Test relative asset references, fresh sessions, children, and a different working directory.

Keep `SOUL.md` as the user's identity unless a Gentle persona is explicitly selected. Preserve memory, unrelated skills/plugins, MCP, auth, models, permission choices, and the user's disabled plugin state. Context7/Engram remain optional through the existing integration.

The installer should reuse Gentle's rendering and ownership rules, not copy raw templates. Migrate only provably managed legacy sections/assets, with backup or a reported conflict for user edits. Do not leave old and new orchestrator instructions active together. Document whether a new Hermes session/reload is needed after enable, disable, or update.

#### 3. Run ODD with native Hermes delegation

Keep small work proportional. For substantial work, follow the current ODD authorization, durable artifact, implementation and checking guidance rather than retired SDD phases.

Use `delegate_task` for ordinary bounded workers. If the plugin truly needs programmatic lifecycle control, use Hermes' public lifecycle API, never private delegation internals. Give each worker a self-contained goal, authorized workspace, exact skill, constraints, expected evidence and cancellation behavior. Do not assume it inherits the parent's conversation, memory, identity or policy.

Use Hermes' existing concurrency, worktrees, model/auth configuration, budgets and approvals. Do not add a Gentle-owned model registry, credentials store, scheduler or Kanban mirror. Model/provider overrides per task can improve routing later but are not a prerequisite for the first usable slice. For remote/container/SSH execution, establish that Gentle's artifacts and Hermes workers refer to the same authorized workspace before claiming support.

Record evidence against the code revision checked: command, exit status and relevant output. A worker summary or `completed` status is not test evidence. For Strict TDD when selected and applicable, preserve RED/GREEN evidence. Report absent runners, timeouts, known baseline failures and partial results honestly. A generic hook is not an unbypassable test gate or filesystem sandbox.

#### 4. Keep native RDD as a separately proven slice

The Hermes capability manifest currently leaves review transport and immutable review execution dormant. Do not flip those claims when the ODD plugin starts working.

A later RDD slice must demonstrate the shared review contract on the real host: frozen candidate and exact bindings, complete inspection, human consent choices, provider-owned transitions, bounded correction, and canonical closure. A prompt saying “read only,” a summarized diff, or a child report is insufficient proof of an immutable reviewer. If public Hermes primitives cannot provide the required boundary, document a minimal reproduction and open a narrowly scoped Hermes issue. Review does not itself authorize a commit, push, PR or release.

### 🔄 Managed lifecycle

- **Install:** target the explicit/selected Hermes profile and provision only Gentle-owned assets. Activation must follow Hermes' native consent/configuration behavior.
- **Sync:** update the same recorded target, reuse applicable scoped-sync machinery, preserve user edits and disabled state, and be idempotent.
- **Doctor:** report the selected home, plugin loadability, discovered skills, rendered asset consistency and unsupported host capabilities without spending model tokens.
- **Disable/uninstall:** remove or disable only Gentle-owned assets; keep user state, config, sessions, plugins, skills and credentials.
- **Upgrade/migration:** handle old managed SDD/OpenSpec files safely without reviving retired flows. Pin and document tested Gentle/Hermes releases or commits; `main` alone is not a release contract.

### ✅ Acceptance criteria (pending implementation)

- [ ] A named Hermes profile can be installed, synced, diagnosed, disabled and uninstalled without changing another profile; retargeting ambiguity stops safely.
- [ ] Profile path resolution covers POSIX, custom paths/spaces and native Windows with/without `LOCALAPPDATA`, coordinating #2094/#4079.
- [ ] The plugin loads through supported Hermes APIs, can be enabled/disabled normally, and repeated sync is idempotent. User-owned configuration and legacy migration conflicts are preserved or reported.
- [ ] A fresh parent and child discover/load the exact current ODD entry skills and their relative references without unresolved placeholders or duplicate legacy instructions.
- [ ] A real fixture shows a proportional direct edit and a substantial ODD task executed with Hermes workers, coherent artifacts, code changes and verified checks; no Pi/OpenCode worker runtime is required.
- [ ] Strict TDD applies only when selected and applicable; failures, interrupted jobs and missing evidence never become false success.
- [ ] CLI and noninteractive behavior are verified separately; gateway and remote backends are claimed only after direct tests. Human decisions block clearly in unattended runs.
- [ ] Hermes RDD remains unadvertised until real transport and immutable-review contract tests pass. A documented blocker is a blocker, not completed parity.
- [ ] No private Hermes imports, duplicate Gentle workflow engine, unexpected model spending, profile leakage or permission escalation.

Separate deterministic asset/contract tests from actual host/model tests. Report commands, versions and PASS/FAIL/SKIP accurately. A static inspection is not an end-to-end plugin test.

### 🪜 Suggested delivery

| Slice | Reviewable outcome |
|---|---|
| A | Coordinate profile home fix with #2094/#4079; add target persistence and lifecycle coverage missing from existing work. |
| B | Minimal managed plugin plus current ODD entry/skills; one native Hermes coding workflow with evidence. **First usable scope: A+B.** |
| C | Native RDD only after its transport and immutable boundary are proved; otherwise publish the precise Hermes prerequisite. |
| D | Versioned compatibility, migration and documentation alongside each shipped slice. |

Follow the repository's approved-issue and review-size process. Intermediate PRs should reference this tracker without closing it prematurely. The tracker closes when the approved scope has end-to-end evidence and documented limits; a path fix or an installed skill bundle alone is insufficient.

### 🔄 Alternatives

| Alternative | Tradeoff |
|---|---|
| Keep only file-based Hermes setup | A useful baseline, but lacks a managed native plugin lifecycle and per-profile activation. |
| Run Pi/OpenCode from Hermes | Possible for immediate use, but adds another coding runtime and does not meet this native Hermes goal. |
| Separate Gentle-Hermes fork | Creates another methodology source and update burden. |
| Port Gentle Pi or reimplement Hermes delegation | Duplicates engines owned by Gentle/Hermes. |

### 📎 Related work and disclosure

Original Hermes support: [#569](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/569), [#774](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/774), and native delegation [#868](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/868). Current changes: [ODD retirement #4967](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/4967), [workspace sync #5080](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/5080), [Hermes path #2094](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/2094) / [#4079](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/4079), and [Hermes adapter source](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/main/internal/agents/hermes/adapter.go).

Material assistance: **ChatGPT** researched public repository code/PR state and drafted this revision. The verification here was static code and PR inspection on 2026-09-29; no plugin was built, installed or tested, and no end-to-end Hermes+Gentle result is claimed.

**Maintainer decision requested:** Is this ownership boundary and A+B first usable slice appropriate for this tracker? If so, should the managed plugin live in the existing Gentle Hermes adapter/release pipeline? RDD remains independently scoped and requires its own contract evidence.

title: bug(sync/upgrade): backup snapshot directory created with mode 0600 (no execute bit) on Linux, "permission denied" creating archive file
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

`gentle-ai sync` (and separately, the self-upgrade backup step, e.g. via `brew upgrade gentle-ai`) creates its timestamped backup-snapshot directory under `~/.gentle-ai/backups/<timestamp>/` with mode `0600` (`drw-------`) instead of an executable mode. Since a directory needs its execute bit to be traversed/written into, the very next step — creating `snapshot.tar.gz` inside that same directory — fails with `permission denied`, even though the directory is owned by the invoking user and the parent `backups/` directory itself is `drwxr-xr-x`.

This reproduces on every `sync` run: each fresh timestamped directory is created with the same broken mode, so it is not a one-off leftover — it looks baked into the directory-creation call itself (as if a literal `0600` were used where an executable mode like `0700`/`0755` was intended).

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. On Linux, run `gentle-ai sync` in a project with SDD/engram already initialized.
2. Observe the "permission denied" error on `create archive file ".../snapshot.tar.gz"`.
3. Manually `chmod 755` the freshly-created backup directory named in the error and re-run `sync` — it gets past that step, but the *next* `sync` invocation creates a brand-new timestamped directory with the same broken `0600` mode and fails the same way.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The backup-snapshot directory is created with a mode that includes execute permission for the owner (e.g. `0700` or `0755`), so `sync` can write `snapshot.tar.gz` into it without manual intervention.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

```
Error: execute sync pipeline: create backup snapshot: create archive "~/.gentle-ai/backups/<timestamp>/snapshot.tar.gz": create archive file "~/.gentle-ai/backups/<timestamp>/snapshot.tar.gz": open ~/.gentle-ai/backups/<timestamp>/snapshot.tar.gz: permission denied
```

`ls -la ~/.gentle-ai/backups/` on the affected directories shows entries like:

```
drw------- 2 <user> <user> 4096 <date> <time>  <timestamp-dir>
```

instead of `drwxr-xr-x`, seen on older/working backup directories in the very same folder.

Also observed the identical `drw-------` mode on several `upgrade-<timestamp>` directories under the same `~/.gentle-ai/backups/` path, from a recent self-upgrade run — suggesting the same underlying directory-creation helper is shared between the `sync` and self-upgrade backup-snapshot code paths, and the bug affects both.

### Gentle AI Version
