2.9.0 (also reproduced immediately after upgrading from 2.8.2 via Homebrew — not specific to 2.8.2)

### Operating System

Linux

### AI Agent / Client

Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (sync / self-upgrade backup pipeline)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

(see Actual Behavior above — full error text and `ls -la` output included there)

title: bug(review): explicit lineage STATUS loses committed correction without frozen selector
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

An explicit historical lineage does not recover its committed correction candidate when STATUS is called without the frozen `baseRef` and `committedOnly` selector. The same retained lineage succeeds when those selectors are supplied explicitly.

This is a current-main recurrence of #3551 after the atomic lifecycle migration. It reproduces in native Gentle AI itself, not only in the Gentle Pi adapter. After HEAD advances with a valid committed correction, the public Pi-shaped STATUS request falls through to an unrelated empty/current workspace and offers a fresh START instead of targeted validation.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Build native Gentle AI from current main at `be49554794917ae92a6dc9dbfa2eb3db5cf70084`.
2. In a disposable HOME and Git repository, start a committed-only review with an explicit frozen base reference.
3. Capture a candidate-caused blocker so the lineage reaches `correction_required`, then capture an in-budget correction plan.
4. Apply and commit the valid correction so HEAD advances beyond the reviewed candidate.
5. Run STATUS with the retained lineage, frozen `baseRef`, and `committedOnly`. Observe that it returns the same lineage with `applicability: current_target` and `targeted_validation_required`.
6. From a fresh process context, run STATUS with the same retained lineage but without `baseRef` or `committedOnly`, matching the public Pi request shape.
7. Observe that STATUS reports `applicability: unrelated`, `action: start`, and an empty/current `current-changes` projection.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

When STATUS explicitly names an existing open committed-correction lineage, native Gentle AI should reconstruct that lineage's frozen committed candidate or return a lineage-specific safe stop. It must preserve predecessor, scope, cleanliness, budget, and repository-binding checks and must not select a sibling lineage.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The explicit lineage skips durable committed-correction reconstruction when the frozen selectors are absent. STATUS evaluates the clean current workspace instead, loses the selected lineage, and offers an unrelated fresh-start/base-selection route.

### Gentle AI Version

2.9.0 and current main `be49554794917ae92a6dc9dbfa2eb3db5cf70084`

### Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
# Control: explicit frozen selector
applicability=current_target
action=collect
state=correction_required
projection.kind=base-diff
next_transition.reason_code=targeted_validation_required

# Public Pi-shaped STATUS: same lineage, selectors omitted
applicability=unrelated
action=start
state=absent
projection.kind=current-changes
initial_review_tree == current_candidate_tree == corrected_HEAD_tree
next_transition.reason_code=empty_candidate_base_ref_required
```

### Additional Context

Native binary SHA-256: `c9c79ad917429692ca6325fd81726c09d54d4c331ac7514e43b4323cad75792b`.

Both STATUS variants left the authority-store aggregate hash unchanged. The existing baseline `TestCommittedCorrectionStatusAfterCommitAnswersTheTransitionItBinds` passed, and the source worktree remained clean.

The current cause is scoped to `internal/reviewtransaction/target_status.go`: durable committed-correction reconstruction is entered only when `request.LineageID == ""`. An explicit lineage therefore skips the reconstruction path before target classification.

Related history:
- #3551 was closed as obsolete with an explicit request to file a fresh report if the behavior remained reachable on current main.
- #4212 / #4213 cover STATUS that retains `baseRef` and `committedOnly` after HEAD moves.
- #3748 covers selector transport in nonterminal closures.
- #4239 scopes STATUS inventory by lineage but does not reconstruct this missing-selector candidate.
- Consumer report: Gentleman-Programming/gentle-pi#1014.

No source correction, authority repair, reset, installation change, delivery action, or PR was performed during this reproduction.

title: bug(review): a declined candidate is re-offered by STATUS, producing an unterminating consent re-ask loop
body:
### Automated provider-defect report

#### Pre-flight checks
- [x] Explicit user consent was obtained before reporting.
- [x] A final privacy review removed raw argv, absolute paths, private project names, usernames, hostnames, credentials, diffs, source contents, and environment values.
- [x] Open and closed issues were searched with exact, broad, and symptom-shaped queries.
- [x] Closest reports #2045 (declined candidate leaves no lineage, so delivery gates stay blocked), #2984 (consent-bound committed START moves detached HEAD) and #2172 (START freezes an empty candidate) cover adjacent areas but none reports the re-offer loop described here.
- [x] This report states observed evidence only; the root cause is unconfirmed.

#### Environment
- Build: `2.8.2` (stable channel — build string carries neither `-rc.` nor `-main.`)
- OS / architecture: Linux x86_64
- Client: Claude Code
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`
- Receipt-driven development: `on` (decided by global)

#### Observed behavior

A medium-risk candidate reached `review start --consent=relay`, which returned a
`gentle-ai.review-integration.consent/v3` envelope. The envelope was relayed losslessly; the
human answered `declined`. The exact provider-issued decline invocation was executed once and
succeeded:

```
action:     declined
consent:    declined_this_candidate
lineage_id: ""
state:      ""
```

The stop hook then fired again for the same session, stating it "reminds once per session and
candidate". The selectorless STATUS preflight was re-run as the contract requires, and it
returned `action: start`, `reason_code: fresh_target_ready`, whose `next_transition.execute`
names **the same lineage and the same target that were just declined**. Executing that exact
returned START produced a byte-identical `consent/v3` envelope — same headline, reason,
risk evidence, choices and answer tokens.

The cycle has no terminating branch: declining is documented as creating no review record
(`"no review record is created"`), so the candidate never stops qualifying as unreviewed, and
every subsequent preflight re-offers it.

#### Identity mismatch observed in the same STATUS payload

The STATUS response carries a top-level `target_identity` that differs from the `--target`
token inside the START command it returns:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| STATUS `target_identity` | `sha256:3f448f3a…` |
| returned START `--target` | `sha256:4f051e0a…` |
| returned START `--lineage` | `review-a76aa09e…` (the lineage already declined) |

Whether this mismatch causes the re-offer or is a second symptom is unconfirmed.

#### Expected behavior

After a decline is recorded for a candidate, the lifecycle should reach a terminal state for
that candidate: either the preflight stops offering that lineage for the remainder of the
session, or the envelope is not re-presented for an answer the human already gave. The relay
contract instructs the agent to return a valid answer to the same blocked actor exactly once,
so a re-presented identical envelope leaves the agent with no admissible move.

#### Minimal reproduction

1. Enable receipt-driven development.
2. Produce a candidate that classifies as medium risk (here: a documentation-only change plus
   one edit to a `CLAUDE.md`, which the envelope classified as "an executable change", so the
   candidate is "not purely passive documentation").
3. Commit it.
4. Run the selectorless STATUS preflight, then the exact returned START carrying `--consent=relay`.
5. Answer the consent envelope with `declined` and run the exact returned decline invocation once.
6. Let the stop hook fire again, then re-run the selectorless STATUS preflight.
7. Observe the same lineage re-offered and the identical envelope returned.

#### Candidate shape

`changed_files: 10`, `changed_lines: 716`, `projection: workspace`, `committed-only: true`,
`risk_level: medium`, `lenses_required: false`, `correction_budget: 0`.

#### Preserved state

No further GitHub mutation was performed beyond this report. Consumer state was preserved; the
captured provider-owned decline invocation is executed once after this report, per the
report-and-continue path.

title: bug(install): first install fails on Homebrew 7.0.0 (tap trust required before brew tap)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

`scripts/install.sh` establishes Homebrew tap-trust **after** running `brew tap`, but Homebrew 7.0.0 requires third-party taps to be trusted **before** their formulae/casks can be loaded — and `brew tap` itself now evaluates the whole tap and refuses to load every untrusted formula/cask it contains. As a result, the brew install method can never complete a **first** install on Homebrew 7.0.0: `brew tap` fails, the script hits `fatal "Failed to tap $BREW_TAP"` and aborts before ever reaching `brew install`. The `untrusted tap` guidance in `print_homebrew_failure_help` is unreachable for this path, because it only runs after a `brew install`/`brew upgrade` failure.

The ordering in `install_brew()` (main @ `be49554794`, 2026-09-14):

```bash
233:    brew untap "$BREW_TAP" 2>/dev/null || true
234:    if ! brew tap "$BREW_TAP"; then
235:        fatal "Failed to tap $BREW_TAP"
236:    fi
237:
238:    homebrew_trust_gentle_ai_formula   # <- too late on Homebrew 7: `brew tap` already failed
```

`homebrew_trust_gentle_ai_formula()` (line 53) calls `brew trust --formula gentleman-programming/tap/gentle-ai`, which is fine for older Homebrew but cannot help here: the tap-level refusal happens during `brew tap`, before that call is ever reached.

This affects macOS and Linux alike: the Homebrew error output shows the same refusal repeated for every platform stanza (`golden_gate`, `arm64_golden_gate`, `tahoe`, `sequoia`, `sonoma`, `ventura`, `monterey`, `big_sur`, their `arm64_` variants, `x86_64_linux`, `arm64_linux`), so any fresh machine running Homebrew 7.0.0 hits this, not only Linuxbrew.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. On a machine with Homebrew 7.0.0 and no prior gentle-ai installation, run:
   `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/main/scripts/install.sh | bash`
2. Watch the `Installing via Homebrew` step.
3. `brew tap gentleman-programming/tap` clones the tap, then Homebrew refuses to load every formula and cask in it as untrusted, and the tap command itself fails; the installer aborts with `Failed to tap Gentleman-Programming/homebrew-tap`.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The installer anticipates Homebrew >= 7 tap-trust enforcement (it already ships a `homebrew_trust_gentle_ai_formula` helper and untrusted-tap error guidance) and completes a first-time brew install without manual intervention.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

`brew tap` aborts with untrusted-tap load errors for all 5 formulae and the cask (`Error: Cannot tap gentleman-programming/tap: invalid syntax in tap!`), the installer exits with `[error] Failed to tap Gentleman-Programming/homebrew-tap`, and gentle-ai is not installed.

### Gentle AI Version

Not applicable — the failure occurs before any gentle-ai version is installed. Script: `scripts/install.sh` from `main` @ `be49554794` (2026-09-14). After applying the workaround below, gentle-ai 2.9.0 installed cleanly via the same script, confirming the rest of the brew path is sound.

### Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
==> Tapping gentleman-programming/tap
Clonando en '/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/Homebrew/Library/Taps/gentleman-programming/homebrew-tap'...
Error: Invalid formula (golden_gate): /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/Homebrew/Library/Taps/gentleman-programming/homebrew-tap/Formula/engram.rb
Refusing to load formula gentleman-programming/tap/engram from untrusted tap gentleman-programming/tap.
Run `brew trust --formula gentleman-programming/tap/engram` or `brew trust gentleman-programming/tap` to trust it.
Error: Invalid formula (golden_gate): /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/Homebrew/Library/Taps/gentleman-programming/homebrew-tap/Formula/gentle-ai.rb
Refusing to load formula gentleman-programming/tap/gentle-ai from untrusted tap gentleman-programming/tap.
...
Error: Invalid cask (Linux on Intel x86_64): /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/Homebrew/Library/Taps/gentleman-programming/homebrew-tap/Casks/engram.rb
Refusing to load cask gentleman-programming/tap/engram from untrusted tap gentleman-programming/tap.
...
Error: Cannot tap gentleman-programming/tap: invalid syntax in tap!
[error]   Failed to tap Gentleman-Programming/homebrew-tap
```

The same `Refusing to load ...` block repeats for `engram`, `gentle-ai`, `gentle-creation`, `gentleman-dots` and `gga` across every platform stanza listed above (60+ refusals in total) before the final `Cannot tap` error.

### Additional Context

**Verified workaround** (run before the script; completes the install):

```bash
brew trust --tap gentleman-programming/tap   # persisted in ~/.homebrew/trust.json
# then re-run install.sh -> success, gentle-ai 2.9.0
```

**Proposed fix**: trust the tap **before** `brew tap`, e.g. in `install_brew()`:

```bash
# before: if ! brew tap "$BREW_TAP"; then
if brew help trust &>/dev/null; then
    info "Pre-trusting ${BREW_TAP} for Homebrew tap-trust enforcement"
    brew trust --tap "$BREW_TAP" &>/dev/null || true
fi
```

Notes from verifying this locally against Homebrew 7.0.0:

- `brew trust --tap` works **before** the tap exists (it only writes the trust store), and tap-level trust is the right granularity here because `brew tap` evaluates **all** formulae/casks in the tap — trusting only `gentle-ai` (the current helper's `--formula` target) would still leave the other four formulae and the cask refused.
- `Tap.fetch("Gentleman-Programming/homebrew-tap").reference` normalizes to `gentleman-programming/tap` even when the tap is not installed, so passing the existing `$BREW_TAP` variable to `brew trust --tap` stores the correct trusted reference.
- The existing post-tap `homebrew_trust_gentle_ai_formula` call can stay as a harmless no-op for older brew versions, or be folded into the pre-tap step.

title: bug(review 2.8.2): correction_required capture's own status_continuation classifies the just-minted authority corrupted_or_unverifiable_authority, so the bounded correction is unreachable
body:
Automated provider-defect report. Observed evidence only; no root cause asserted.

## Environment

- Build: `gentle-ai 2.8.2` (no `-rc.` / `-main.` tag → stable evidence channel)
- OS / arch: darwin / arm64
- Client: claude-code (in-process reviewer capture, `--agent`, no `--input`)
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`
- Projection: `workspace`, `--committed-only=true` with an explicit `--base-ref` (candidate already committed on a feature branch)
- Candidate: medium tier, 5 changed files, 148 changed lines, frozen correction budget 74
- Lineage: `review-903e2e8ed39ad4ce`

## Expected

After a capture closes a lineage in `correction_required`, the `status_continuation` the capture itself returns is the contract's prescribed re-entry. Running it verbatim should report the correction phase for that binding — the corroborated findings, a `correction_lines` transition, or a stop reason describing the correction state.

## Actual

The lineage was created, driven, and corrupted entirely within a single session on one build. The very next operation after the capture — the exact `status_continuation` command the capture returned, run unchanged — classifies the just-minted authority as damaged.

Sequence, each command exactly as the previous transition returned it:

1. Selectorless STATUS → `action: start`, `fresh_target_ready`, one START invocation.
2. Exact START (`--consent=relay`) → `gentle-ai.review-integration.consent/v3`, medium risk.
3. Exact `granted` invocation → `action: created`, `state: reviewing`, one lens (`review-reliability`), `authority_revision: sha256:540442…`-class value for this lineage, opaque `repository_context` handle issued.
4. Bound STATUS → `action: collect`, `reviewer_results_required`, one `review.capture-result` input.
5. Exact `capture-result` (in-process, `--agent`, no `--input`) → `gentle-ai.review-last-event-closure/v1`, `state: correction_required`, `action: "candidate-caused severe findings require one bounded correction"`, plus a `status_continuation` block binding revision `sha256:085cf18a…`.
6. That exact `status_continuation` command, run unchanged → `state: correction_required` in `authority`, but `action: stop`, `forecast.horizon: terminal`, and:

```
"next_transition": { "kind": "stop", "reason_code": "corrupted_or_unverifiable_authority" }
```

The finding content is never exposed. Step 5 returns no finding bodies on this path, and step 6 is terminal, so the bounded correction the state demands cannot be authored. `repair.status` is `unsupported` with all counts zero; `candidates` is empty.

## What makes this distinct from prior art

Checked open and closed issues before filing:

- **#4087** — same "findings unreachable" half, but its terminal stop is `corrected_candidate_unavailable`. Here the stop is `corrupted_or_unverifiable_authority`.
- **#3647** — the stuck `correction_required` lineage there blocks every subsequent review with `sanctioned_exits: []`. Here nothing else is blocked; the selectorless STATUS still offers ordinary fresh starts.
- **#3306** — `corrupted_or_unverifiable_authority` for lineages frozen under a retired snapshot-identity formula, i.e. prior-schema inert history. This lineage was minted minutes earlier by the same binary that then rejected it.

Evidence that the store itself was healthy: two earlier lineages in the same session, same repository and same build, each completed `start → status → capture-result → acknowledge-approved` and burned cleanly. This was the third.

## Reproduction shape

1. On a feature branch whose changes are already committed, run the selectorless STATUS preflight for `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2` with `--agent claude-code`.
2. Follow only the returned transitions: exact START with `--consent=relay`, then the `granted` invocation, then the bound STATUS, then the single returned `review.capture-result` with `--agent` and no `--input`.
3. Have the lens close the lineage in `correction_required` (medium tier, candidate-caused severe findings).
4. Run the `status_continuation` command from that capture, unchanged.

Observed: terminal `corrupted_or_unverifiable_authority` instead of a correction transition.

## Impact

The stop reason's documented continuation is "maintainer inspects authority/lineage, or disable receipt-driven development for the clone". Neither surfaces the findings, so a candidate the reviewer judged to need a bounded correction cannot be corrected through the lifecycle, and no receipt is produced for it. Delivery is unaffected — it was never gated on the review — but the correction the contract promises is unreachable.

title: bug(pi): gentle-agents child never emits a first event — stall watchdog re-armed by protocol acks, and the task surfaces raw ENOENT
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

A `gentle-agents` Pi child task can reach a permanently wedged state that nothing in the runner can bound: the child process starts, answers the `get_state` RPC round-trip, then never begins a turn — no provider call, no thread event, no session file — while the host keeps reporting it as `running` indefinitely.

Two independent defects in `gentle-pi` combine to make this unrecoverable and undiagnosable:

**1. The stall watchdog is re-armed by non-progress protocol frames, and no total-runtime bound exists.**

`AgentsRunner.receive()` re-arms the stall timer on *every* inbound line from the child, before classifying it:

```ts
// lib/agents-runner.ts (receive)
private receive(id: string, request: TaskRequest, value: unknown): void {
    const live = this.live.get(id);
    if (!live || live.terminal || !value || typeof value !== "object") return;
    const raw = value as Record<string, unknown>;
    const remediation = this.store.get(id)?.sddRemediation;
    if (remediation) observeRemediationTool(remediation, raw);
    this.armStall(id, live);                      // <-- re-armed before any progress check
    if (raw.type === "response") {
        ...
        return;                                   // protocol ack: zero progress, clock reset
    }
```

`type: "response"` frames are pure protocol acks. Frames that `normalizeRpcEvent` maps to nothing are equally inert. Either resets the silence clock.

This is load-bearing because `timeout_ms` was deliberately retired and is now inert — `lib/agents-config.ts` states it outright:

```ts
// `timeout_ms` remains accepted as an inert legacy key so existing JSON
// files load normally; only silence is bounded by `stall_timeout_ms`.
stallTimeoutMs: positiveInteger(merged.stall_timeout_ms, DEFAULT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS),
```

So `stall_timeout_ms` is the *only* bound in the system, and a child that emits any periodic byte stream — without ever producing a task event — resets it forever. There is no wall-clock ceiling left to catch it. Existing `subagents.json` files still carrying `timeout_ms` provide no protection and give a false sense of one.

**2. A task whose child never started a turn surfaces a raw `ENOENT` instead of a typed state.**

The host records the child's session path from the `get_state` response:

```ts
// lib/agents-runner.ts (launch)
if (typeof data.sessionFile === "string" && data.sessionFile) resolved.sessionPath = data.sessionFile;
```

That is the path the child *intends* to use. Pi creates the session JSONL lazily, on the first persisted turn. When no turn ever starts, the path is recorded but the file never exists.

The overlay's open path guards only on emptiness, not existence:

```ts
// extensions/gentle-agents.ts (open selected task)
if (!chosen.sessionPath) {
    ctx.ui.notify("This task has no session file yet.", "warning");
    return;
}
...
ctx.ui.notify(`Could not read the task's session: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`, "warning");
```

The correct branch — "this task has no session file yet" — is unreachable for exactly the case it describes, because `sessionPath` is populated. The user gets a raw filesystem error naming a path that was never created.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. On Pi 0.85.1 with the `gentle-pi` package installed, configure `~/.pi/agent/subagents.json` with `"stall_timeout_ms": 600000` and `"timeout_ms": 3600000`.
2. From a session whose cwd is a large repository, launch an `sdd-apply` task through `gentle-agents`.
3. Observe the task reach `running` and remain at `waiting for the first event`.
4. Wait past `stall_timeout_ms`. The task is not timed out, not signalled, and not finished; the elapsed counter keeps climbing (observed past 18 minutes against a 10-minute bound).
5. Open the task from the agents overlay. Instead of a typed "not started" state, a warning reports `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '~/.pi/agent/gentle-agents/sessions/<timestamp>_<uuid>.jsonl'`.
6. Inspect the child process: it is alive, sleeping in `ep_poll`, holds zero TCP sockets, and has no child processes.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

1. The stall watchdog should be re-armed only by frames that represent task progress. A `type: "response"` protocol ack, and any frame that normalizes to zero events, must not reset the silence clock. Alternatively (or additionally), restore a real total-runtime ceiling so `stall_timeout_ms` is not the single point of failure — an "alive but producing nothing" child must become terminal on its own.
2. A task whose child never persisted a turn should surface a typed, actionable state ("the child has not started a turn yet"), not a raw `ENOENT` naming a path the runtime chose but never created. Existence should be checked before `readFile`, or the recorded `sessionPath` should stay unset until the child confirms the file exists.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The child never starts a turn, the host cannot tell, no bound applies, and the only diagnostic offered is a filesystem error about a missing file. Recovery requires killing the detached process group by hand from outside Pi; the concurrency slot stays occupied until then.

### Gentle AI Version

gentle-ai `2.8.3-0.20260913211349-266574b0ec43`; client package gentle-pi `2.6.2`

### Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
# Host warning when opening the task from the agents overlay
Warning: Could not read the task's session: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open
  '~/.pi/agent/gentle-agents/sessions/<timestamp>_<uuid>.jsonl'

# Agents overlay row, well past the configured 10-minute stall bound
sdd-apply · running · <provider>/<model> · 16m37s
  waiting for the first event

# Child process state (alive, idle, never called the provider)
State:    S (sleeping)
Threads:  26
wchan:    ep_poll
children: <none>
open TCP sockets: 0
open unix sockets: 5   (stdin/stdout/stderr/permission-fd/ipc, all to the host)

# Child thread CPU (ticks), highest first
885  fff-bg-0            futex_do_wait
193  pi                  ep_poll
104  notify-rs debounce  hrtimer_nanosleep
 17  V8Worker            futex_do_wait

# Child I/O over a 20s window: reads a lot, writes a trickle to the host pipe,
# writes nothing to disk (write_bytes flat => the trickle is protocol traffic)
rchar       +1,155,008
wchar           +984
write_bytes       +0
```

### Additional Context

- **Why the watchdog provably did not fire, rather than firing and failing:** the host TUI kept rendering a live elapsed counter throughout, so the host event loop was running and `setTimeout` was being serviced. `requestStop` sends `SIGTERM` immediately and escalates to `SIGKILL` after the grace window; the child was still alive 18+ minutes in, so `requestStop` was never called. Combined with the measured trickle of child-to-host bytes (`wchar` rising while `write_bytes` stays flat — pipe traffic, not disk), the only consistent explanation is repeated re-arming by inert frames.
- **Why the child never started the turn is NOT established here.** Zero TCP sockets proves no provider call was ever attempted; the main thread idle in `ep_poll` proves it was not CPU-wedged. The trigger is unidentified and may well be upstream of gentle-pi. The defects reported above are the ones that made an unknown startup wedge *unbounded and undiagnosable*, which is what this issue asks to fix.
- Notable in the thread dump: the `pi-pretty` `fff` background indexer and its `notify-rs` watchers are the dominant CPU consumers inside a headless `--mode rpc` child, continuously scanning the caller's repository. Whether a headless child should run that indexer at all may be worth separating into its own issue.
- Ruled out during investigation: #4373 (the affected agent definition carries `thinking: xhigh`, not `max`) and #4554 (the worktree was clean; `.atl` was last written by the parent session at startup, not by the child).
- Related but distinct, neither an equivalent defect nor a canonical tracker for this class: #4047 (worker-result admission for endless-pending SDD results — a different layer, the SDD task result rather than the Pi child runner) and #4337 (pi-host-relay reviewer slot left pending — the review relay transport, a different component).
- Privacy: this report excludes raw argv, absolute paths, private project or repository names, branch names, usernames, hostnames, credentials, diffs, source contents of private repositories, and environment variable values. Environment variables are named by key only where relevant.

title: bug(opencode): review-transport plugin-side lens-context rejects every reviewer launch; identical host-CLI call succeeds (2.8.1, macOS)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description
Negotiated v2.1 review on `gentle-ai 2.8.1` with OpenCode wedges at reviewer launch: the orchestrator launches each of the four canonical 4R reviewer lenses (`review-risk`, `review-resilience`, `review-readability`, `review-reliability`) as OpenCode Task agents carrying the exact `GENTLE_AI_REVIEW_BINDING` line assembled from the provider-returned collect input. The OpenCode review-transport plugin intercepts each Task and fails at its internal lens-context step before any model invocation:

```
review lens context failed for lens review-risk: gentle-ai review lens-context failed (1): Error: review lens-context requires the exact provider-issued repository context, lineage, target, expected revision, and lens carried by the collect transition; run `gentle-ai review lens-context --help` for the closed command form.
```

The exact same `gentle-ai review lens-context` invocation with the same handle/cwd/binding tokens succeeds from the orchestrator session and renders the full binding + patches. So the handle matches the repository; the defect is that the transport-side lens-context call inside the plugin runtime is rejected, while the identical call from the host CLI is accepted. Nine reviewer launches across three bounded rounds (4 + 4 + 1 sequential) failed identically and deterministically; the authority stays `reviewing` with `reviewer_results_required` and reoffers the same bound collect slots.

Duplicate search covered open+closed issues for `lens-context`, `reviewer lens`, `lens capture`, and the failure phrase. Closest are #4030 (opencode-transport rejects binding after lens-context succeeds — different failure surface: transport validation, not plugin-side lens-context), #4302 (plugin fails to load on OpenCode 1.18.x — not this: the plugin loads and intercepts, then its lens-context call fails), #4491 (captures reject after two admissions — none happened here), #3343/#2946 (closed, older forms). None covers this 2.8.1 deterministic plugin-side lens-context rejection on every lens.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce
1. On `gentle-ai 2.8.1`, OpenCode (macOS, arm64), RDD enabled globally.
2. Stage a 2-file, 226-line high-risk candidate; run the negotiated route: `gentle-ai review status --cwd <repo> --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --agent opencode --next-transition` → `fresh_target_ready` → `gentle-ai review start ... --consent granted` → created, high risk, canonical 4R lenses selected.
3. Launch each lens as an OpenCode Task with the prompt prefix `GENTLE_AI_REVIEW_BINDING ` followed by the one-line JSON assembled from the collect input (`lineage`, `target`, `lens`, `order`, `revision`, `repository_context`, `subject_hash`).
4. Observe every Task fail at the plugin's lens-context step with the error above, before model invocation.

### ✅ Expected Behavior
The plugin's transport resolves the provider-issued `repository_context` handle (the same handle `lens-context` accepts from the host CLI), materializes the frozen candidate, and launches each lens exactly once, offering a capturable `review.capture-result` slot.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
All four lenses (and a bounded sequential retry of one, then two more full rounds) fail identically at the plugin-side lens-context step with the "requires the exact provider-issued repository context..." error. No reviewer result is captured; `review status` remains `reviewing` / `reviewer_results_required` with the identical bound slots reoffered. The orchestrator-session `lens-context` call with identical tokens succeeds, proving handle validity.

### Gentle AI Version
2.8.1

### Operating System
macOS (arm64)

### AI Agent / Client
OpenCode

### 📋 Affected Area
CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output
```text
# Every reviewer Task (canonical 4R: review-risk, review-resilience, review-readability, review-reliability):
review lens context failed for lens <lens>: gentle-ai review lens-context failed (1): Error: review lens-context requires the exact provider-issued repository context, lineage, target, expected revision, and lens carried by the collect transition; run `gentle-ai review lens-context --help` for the closed command form. The reviewer was not launched, so its exactly-once invocation is preserved.

# Host CLI with the same tokens succeeds and renders the full context:
gentle-ai review lens-context --cwd <repo> --repository-context rctx2_<handle> --lineage review-<id> --target sha256:<target> --expected-revision sha256:<rev> --lens review-risk
# → GENTLE_AI_REVIEW_BINDING + GENTLE_AI_REVIEW_CONTEXT + GENTLE_AI_REVIEW_INSTRUCTION + GENTLE_AI_REVIEW_RESULT_SCHEMA

# capture-result --materialize probe (host CLI) reports the runtime transport:
review capture-result --materialize is unavailable for "opencode": printing the Go-materialized provider task is the host-relay form, and this runtime's compiled transport is "opencode_provider_injected"; collect its reviewer result through that live host transport instead

# status stays wedged, reoffering the same collect slots:
state: reviewing, action: collect, reason_code: reviewer_results_required
```

### Additional Context
- No candidate, lineage, or authority state was mutated by the retries; no reviewer result was captured; the review authority remains open (`reviewing`).
- Bounded attempts: 9 reviewer launches across 3 rounds, all identical failures, deterministic.
- The consumer workflow is preserved and awaiting either a fix or the documented `review mode disable --scope clone` exit.

title: bug(review): Pi candidate-view selection fails at checkout-index without stderr on Windows
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description
On Windows, Pi native review preflight cannot materialize a candidate view during intended-untracked selection. The native integration reports a `checkout-index` failure but does not expose the Git stderr needed to diagnose it. The operation fails before lineage creation or authority mutation.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce
1. Use Pi with Gentle AI 2.8.1 on Windows.
2. Prepare a workspace review candidate and run native review preflight.
3. Select the candidate's intended untracked paths, or stage those paths and exclude unrelated local tooling.
4. Observe the intended-untracked selection fail in `candidate-view` with `checkout-index`.

### ✅ Expected Behavior
The native integration should materialize the candidate view and continue to START, or return the Git subprocess stderr and an actionable failure reason.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
The selection fails repeatedly with `git-failure` for `checkout-index`. No lineage is created and no mutation is performed. The same outcome persists after native asset sync reports all assets current and after the intended paths are staged.

### Gentle AI Version
2.8.1

### Operating System
Windows

### AI Agent / Client
Other

### 📋 Affected Area
CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output
```shell
phase: candidate-view
category: git-failure
git_subcommand: checkout-index
timeout_ms: 10000
message: candidate-view Git command checkout-index failed; inspect the candidate state before any new START
lineage_created: false
mutation_performed: false
```

### Additional Context
A disposable local clone successfully ran `checkout-index` against the same base tree and after adding all selected path names to a temporary index. No Git index lock, linked worktree, reserved path, or custom filter was found. The native materializer is the only failing path.

title: meta(docs): documentation triage and PR execution tracker
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

Documentation

### 💡 Problem Statement

Documentation triage needs a bounded operational tracker to coordinate priorities, blockers, and existing PRs without maintaining another mutable copy of the general audit in #3841.

This tracker brings together **36 selected issues: 22 documentation issues and 14 related functional or safety issues**. Its technical baseline is the **13 September 2026** assessment against [`main@7aad6a5`](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/tree/7aad6a51064beef17299e59b6a59bb232238654a). It is a snapshot of that analysis, not a fresh technical validation of every issue at publication time.

Duplicate searches covered open and closed issues. #538 and #2178 concern historical work; #2236 proposes triage automation; #2471 and #3841 are general trackers, not equivalents of this documentation queue.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Use this issue for **operational coordination**, keeping diagnosis, specific decisions, and closure evidence in each original issue; implementation and validation remain in their PRs.

**This is neither an implementation PR nor blanket authorization.** Priorities are recommendations, not label changes. Revalidate each work unit before acting. Creating this tracker does not close issues or establish that work is complete.

#### Initial operational status

Owner of each work unit: **unassigned**. “Open PR” means existing work identified during the assessment, not that it is approved or ready to merge. Pending checks are not marked as completed.

| Wave | Work unit | Operational status | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | #2975, #2999 | Closure verification pending | Revalidate the fix and record evidence. |
| 0 | #3187 → #3186 | Consolidation pending | Confirm duplication and preserve any unique information. |
| 0 | #1792 | Current reproduction pending | Check the scenario before proposing closure. |
| 1 | #3273 → #3286 | Existing PR; administrative blocker | Enable and verify the private channel before publishing its policy. |
| 1 | #4520 | Approval and scope pending | Correct references per runtime, not through a global replacement. |
| 1 | #2886 | Decision pending | Define ownership of index exclusion. |
| 1 | #2470 | Investigation pending | Attribute the incident without assuming its cause. |
| 2 | #2998 → #4176 | Existing PR; incomplete scope | Complete the retirement of current references. |
| 2 | #3738 → #4154; #3739 → #4126; #3297 → #4127; #3160 → #4122 | Existing PRs; review pending | Revalidate and continue each PR independently. |
| 2 | #4428 | Approval and update pending | Check the current release when executing. |
| 3 | #4136 → #4178 | Preparatory correction; evidence pending | Do not confuse correcting claims with proving wrappers work. |
| 3 | #3292 | Approval pending | Align documentation with current ownership and configuration. |
| 3 | #966 → #3579 | Existing PR; review pending | Verify capabilities and address feedback. |
| 4 | #1021 → #4115 / #1070 | Selection and validation pending | Prefer #4115 as the starting point; do not integrate both. |
| 4 | #1017 → #1080 | Existing PR; Windows validation pending | Correct guarantees about windows and tabs. |
| 4 | #2732 | Approval pending | Derive help and errors from canonical values. |
| 5 | #3490, #1863 | Decision/design pending | Resolve ownership and boundaries before implementation. |
| 5 | #3339, #3186 | Information pending | Obtain original artifacts and provenance. |

The other 11 adjacent functional issues in section 4 remain in their original tracking threads; this tracker does not create a second functional queue.

### 1. Documentation: work to execute

| Priority | Cluster | Issue | Diagnosis | Action and PR | Closure criteria |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P1** | Vulnerability disclosure | **[#3273](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/3273)** | The policy is missing and private reporting is disabled. | An administrator enables the channel; then update [#3286](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/3286). | A working private channel and accurate documentation. |
| **P1** | Generated CodeGraph state | **[#2886](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/2886)** | Guidance does not establish how to exclude the generated index from the Git candidate. | Approve the scope and decide who owns exclusion. Separate PR. | Index, WAL, and SHM excluded without modifying unrelated files. |
| **P2** | Retired interfaces | **[#2998](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/2998)** | A removed switch is still presented as operational. | Correct [#4176](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/4176): retire the guide and current references while preserving history. | No current document recommends the retired switch. |
| **P2** | Copilot capabilities | **[#4136](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/4136)** | Current claims are not supported by the installed capability; the requested proof is missing. | Correct documentation through [#4178](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/4178), **without automatically closing #4136**. | The required Windows + POSIX evidence, or an explicit change to the approved scope. |
| **P2** | Pi capabilities | **[#3292](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/3292)** | The background policy is missing and references to a retired package contradict each other. | Approve and prepare a bounded Pi documentation PR. | Flags, precedence, configuration, and ownership match the implementation. |
| **P2** | Current versions | **[#4428](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/4428)** | Documentation presents v2.6.0 as current; the issue's v2.7.0 target is also outdated. | Approve and update against the release published at execution time; at the cutoff it was **v2.8.0**. | Consistent current references; historical versions preserved. |
| **P2** | Candidate review | **[#3738](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/3738)** | Overly broad guidance can trigger another review of the same approved, unchanged candidate. | Reuse [#4154](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/4154). | An exception limited to the exact candidate; no general bypass. |
| **P2** | PR diff scope | **[#3739](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/3739)** | The recipe does not use the merge-base corresponding to GitHub's diff. | Reuse [#4126](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/4126). | A recipe using `<base>...<head>` with an accurate explanation. |
| **P2** | Template links | **[#3297](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/3297)** | Relative links break when copied into the PR body. | Reuse [#4127](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/4127). | Both URLs work from the rendered PR. |
| **P3** | Hermes capabilities | **[#966](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/966)** | Documentation is partial and needs to distinguish installed capabilities from native delegation. | Update and review [#3579](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/3579). | Claims verified against the adapter/manifest; feedback addressed. |
| **P3** | Engram Cloud | **[#1021](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/1021)** | A validated recipe is missing; two PRs compete. | Prefer [#4115](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/4115) as the starting point; do not also merge [#1070](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/1070). | Enrollment, synchronization, and verification tested on an identified Engram version. |
| **P3** | Windows Terminal | **[#1017](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/1017)** | The recipe confuses reusing a window with reusing a tab/pane. | Correct [#1080](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/1080) and validate on Windows. | The command provides exactly the documented guarantees. |
| **P3** | Persona help | **[#2732](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/2732)** | Help omits valid values; the issue mixes canonical values with an alias. | Approve a help/error PR with tests. | Exposes `gentleman`, `neutral`, `custom`; treats the alias as an alias. |
| **P3** | Code comments | **[#3160](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/3160)** | A comment attributes another function's responsibility to this function. Behavior is correct. | Adjust and reuse [#4122](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/4122). **Comment only.** | Accurate permissions rationale, with no functional changes. |

---

### 2. Documentation: do not implement until the blocker is resolved

| Cluster | Issue | Missing prerequisite | Triage decision | Next step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Skill contributions | **[#3490](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/3490)** | Canonical location and ownership of new skills. | **Decision pending.** | Agree on destination and responsibility; then document it by linking the existing guide. |
| Architecture | **[#3339](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/3339)** | The referenced artifacts are not on `main`. | **Information pending.** | Obtain originals and revalidate them against current code. |

### 📝 Bug Description
`gentle-ai sync` derives the Pi persona configuration path from an executable/install location when it runs inside an FHS environment. It attempts to create `/usr/bin/.pi/gentle-ai/persona.json` instead of using the user's home directory.

Sync stores persona configuration under `$HOME/.pi/gentle-ai/` (or the documented configuration override) and succeeds independently of the executable's FHS-visible path.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
Sync fails while trying to create `/usr/bin/.pi/gentle-ai/persona.json`, where `/usr` is read-only in the FHS namespace.

2.6.0

Linux (Other)

Other (Pi)

CLI (commands, flags)

execute sync pipeline: sync persona for "pi": create parent directories for "/usr/bin/.pi/gentle-ai/persona.json": mkdir /usr/

title: bug(pi): child sessions mutate .atl and .gitignore on startup
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

Package-owned Pi child sessions implicitly modify the caller's Git worktree during session startup. The skill-registry integration writes `.atl/skill-registry.md` and changes `.gitignore`, even when the delegated task is read-only or its allowed edit surfaces exclude both paths.

This contaminates governed worktrees, changes native review scope, consumes changed-line budget, and makes otherwise valid SDD candidates fail closed. Child sessions already carry a child-process marker, but the skill-registry startup path does not appear to suppress repository writes for those children.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a clean Git worktree and confirm an empty short status.
2. Launch a package-owned Pi subagent or an SDD continuation that starts a Pi child session.
3. Do not authorize `.atl/**` or `.gitignore` as edit surfaces.
4. Inspect Git status after the child starts or finishes.
5. Observe modifications to `.atl/skill-registry.md` and `.gitignore`.
6. Repeat in a second clean worktree. The same path pair is modified again.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Package-owned child sessions must not perform implicit repository writes outside their authorized edit surfaces. Skill-registry discovery for a child should be read-only, externally cached, explicitly opted in, or disabled automatically when the child-process marker is present.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Starting package-owned child work reproducibly dirties `.atl/skill-registry.md` and `.gitignore`. A read-only SDD status operation leaves the worktree clean, while the subsequent child-backed mutable lifecycle route introduces the two modifications. The implementation may otherwise pass focused and full offline tests, but the candidate cannot proceed to verification or review because forbidden runtime paths entered the ambient diff.

### Gentle AI Version

2.8.0 stable; client package gentle-pi 2.6.0

### Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
# Before child startup
## <feature-branch>

# After child-backed work
 M .atl/skill-registry.md
 M .gitignore
 M <authorized-sdd-artifact>
 M <authorized-product-files>
```

### Additional Context

- Reproduced in two newly created clean worktrees from the same pinned commit.
- The first occurrence followed SDD continuation; the second followed package-owned SDD apply.
- A read-only native SDD status between creation and apply did not dirty the second worktree.
- The implementation report showed passing focused and full offline tests, but it was retained only as incident telemetry because the worktree was contaminated.
- A known safe process-level mitigation is to start the parent Pi process with `GENTLE_PI_NO_SKILL_REGISTRY=1`, which child processes inherit. A child-aware guard in the extension plus runner defense-in-depth would avoid requiring repository-specific cleanup.
- Both contaminated worktrees were preserved. No forbidden payload was opened, diffed, cleaned, staged, committed, or published.
- Privacy: this report excludes raw argv, absolute paths, private project or repository names, usernames, hostnames, credentials, diffs, source contents, environment values, and private data.

title: bug(tui): Claude model picker always reopens as Custom — preset tables include "orchestrator" but persistence strips it
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

The Claude model picker (`Configure models` → Claude) always reopens showing `Custom`, no matter which preset was selected. Selecting `Performance` and syncing works — the assignments are written and applied correctly — but reopening the picker shows `Custom` again. The same happens for every preset (`Balanced`, `Performance`, `Economy`, `Diversity`), so preset detection never succeeds after the first sync.

This is a defect in the detection added by #675, not a persistence failure: `~/.gentle-ai/state.json` holds the correct table.

**Root cause** (read from `main`):

1. Every preset constructor in `internal/model/claude_model.go` returns **15** entries, including `"orchestrator"`.
2. `claudePhaseAssignmentsToState()` in `internal/app/app.go` deliberately skips `"orchestrator"` when persisting, because Claude Code owns the main session model. **14** entries reach `state.json`. `claudeAliasesToStrings()` and the CLI-sync loaders in `internal/cli/sync.go` drop it too, so the key can never come back.
3. On reopen, `NewClaudeModelPickerStateFromPhaseAssignments()` in `internal/tui/screens/claude_model_picker.go` compares the persisted map against each preset with `phaseAssignmentsEqual`, which begins with:

```go
func phaseAssignmentsEqual(a, b map[string]model.ClaudePhaseAssignment) bool {
	if len(a) != len(b) {
		return false
	}
```

15 vs 14 → no preset ever matches → the function falls through to `ClaudePresetCustom`.

A minimal fix is to compare against the same filtered view that persistence produces (drop `"orchestrator"` from the preset table before comparing), or to exclude that key in `phaseAssignmentsEqual`.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `gentle-ai` with Claude Code installed and open `Configure models` → Claude models.
2. Select the `Performance` preset and let the sync finish.
3. Run `gentle-ai` again and open `Configure models` → Claude models.
4. The preset list shows `Custom` selected instead of `Performance`. Repeating steps 2-3 any number of times never changes the result.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Reopening the picker preselects the preset that was saved (`Performance`), because the persisted assignments are exactly that preset's table.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The picker always preselects `Custom`, which reads as if the selection had been lost. The assignments themselves are correct and applied, so the impact is a misleading label plus repeated re-selection by the user.

### Gentle AI Version

2.8.1

### Operating System

Windows (WSL)

### AI Agent / Client

Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area

TUI (terminal UI)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
# ~/.gentle-ai/state.json — claude_phase_assignments (14 keys, no "orchestrator")
{
  "default":      {"model": "sonnet"},
  "jd-fix-agent": {"model": "opus"},
  "jd-judge-a":   {"model": "opus"},
  "jd-judge-b":   {"model": "opus"},
  "sdd-apply":    {"model": "sonnet"},
  "sdd-archive":  {"model": "haiku"},
  "sdd-design":   {"model": "opus"},
  "sdd-explore":  {"model": "sonnet"},
  "sdd-onboard":  {"model": "haiku"},
  "sdd-propose":  {"model": "opus"},
  "sdd-research": {"model": "sonnet"},
  "sdd-spec":     {"model": "sonnet"},
  "sdd-tasks":    {"model": "sonnet"},
  "sdd-verify":   {"model": "opus"}
}

# Compared against ClaudeModelPresetPerformance():
len(preset) = 15   len(state) = 14
state == performance-minus-orchestrator: True
only difference: orchestrator -> ("opus", absent)
```

### Additional Context

Related: #675 introduced preselecting the saved preset. The detection it added cannot match once the assignments round-trip through `state.json`, because persistence and the preset tables disagree on whether `"orchestrator"` belongs in the map.

title: Per-unit review of a work-unit split cannot complete: cross-unit dependencies escalate as unknown causality (false CRITICALs)
body:

### 📝 Bug Description

Per-unit review of a work-unit split cannot complete honestly: when unit k consumes an API implemented in an earlier unit of the same split, the frozen candidate view hides the implementation, the reviewer cannot verify the contract, and unknown causality escalates — producing terminal escalations and false CRITICAL corrections for code that is provably correct on the combined branch.

Observed in an 11-unit split of a ~37k-line working tree (RDD on, all commits green: typecheck + 820 tests):

- U9 (review-127286611b3862e0): CRITICAL R3-001 claimed the RPC model-override path was broken because model-resolver.ts (unit 1) was outside the changed-path manifest; in-candidate witnesses (removed `typeof resolved === "string"` branch + stale in-file comment) described the obsolete contract. Unknown causality → escalated (`native_stop_required`, terminal). HEAD: the typed ResolvedModel union exists exactly as consumed; the only real defect was the stale comment.
- U10 (review-a3341db19d4b9ad7): refuter-corroborated CRITICAL R3-01 claimed call sites might mismatch the manager signature because agent-manager.ts (unit 5) was outside the tree and in-candidate tests mock the manager → correction_required. 5. U9: unknown causality → escalated, terminal. U10: correction_required with no honest correction available (the code is correct at HEAD).

Per-unit review of a split can complete: the engine lets a transaction declare "context commits" (read-only reviewer context from dependency units), or offers first-class committed-range candidates (cf. #4336), so cross-unit contracts are verifiable in view instead of escalating as unknown causality.

title: RDD review re-offers the full candidate after approval — post-approval edits should re-review only the modified files
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

RDD review scope is not atomic across post-approval edits. After a candidate is reviewed and its authority is burned, ANY later modification to one file of that candidate causes the next review preflight (`review status` → inspect → START offer) to re-offer a full review of the ENTIRE candidate again — including files that are byte-identical to the already-approved revision. There is no per-file receipt consultation: approved-and-unchanged files are re-frozen and re-reviewed as if never reviewed.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Run an RDD review over a candidate of 5 changed files; it completes `approved` and the acknowledgement burns the authority.
2. Modify one of those 5 files (still uncommitted, same worktree).
3. Run the review preflight again (`gentle-ai review status --next-transition ...` / the agent-side inspect).
4. The preflight offers a brand-new full review over the same 5 files — all 5 paths re-freeze and all lenses re-run over them.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Review units should be atomic per file: a post-approval modification should scope the next review offer to ONLY the file(s) changed since the last approved revision (the delta). Files already covered by an approved, burned lineage and unchanged since the burn should be excluded from the new candidate, so the new offer covers exactly the modified file(s).

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The next preflight offers `review.start` over the full 5-file projection again. All 5 files re-freeze into the new candidate and every lens re-runs over all of them (a full reviewer group cost) even though 4 of the 5 files are byte-identical to the approved revision.

### Gentle AI Version

main @ 21d9ffa6 (source build; `gentle-ai version` prints `gentle-ai main`)

### Operating System

macOS

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

_No response_

### Additional Context

Suggested direction: consult prior lineage receipts for the same target when scoping a new review — files already covered by an approved, acknowledged (burned) lineage and unchanged since that burn form the "already approved" set; the new candidate should contain only files modified since (or new files). At minimum, the review offer could surface which paths were already approved and offer a delta-scoped alternative. Related but distinct reports: #551 (review session cost report) and #4031 (lifecycle/receipt visibility after burn). Reproduced through the Pi host integration (gentle-pi facade), but the scoping decision belongs to the native review lifecycle.

title: bug(engram): regression from #4278 — sync skips mcpServers.engram for a Claude Code plugin that declares no MCP server, leaving zero registrations
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

Possible regression from #4188 / PR #4278 (`fix(engram): skip direct Claude MCP when plugin is enabled`, commit `8d45521`, contained in the `v2.6.0...v2.7.0` range).

That fix makes `sync` skip writing `mcpServers.engram` when `engram@engram` is enabled in `settings.json`, on the premise that the plugin registration already exposes the same tools under the `mcp__plugin_engram_engram__*` prefix.

**The Claude Code plugin package does not declare an MCP server.** Plugin `engram@engram` v0.1.2 (`source: ./plugin/claude-code`) ships `hooks/` and `skills/` only:

- no `.mcp.json` in the plugin root — only the sibling `plugin/codex/.mcp.json` exists
- no `mcpServers` key in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`
- no reference to `engram mcp` anywhere in the installed plugin tree

So on a plugin-enabled Claude Code host the fix does not deduplicate two registrations — it removes the only one that existed. The result is **zero** Engram MCP registrations: no `mem_*` tools under either prefix, and `gentle-ai doctor` stuck at `degraded` with a remedy that cannot converge.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Claude Code host with the Engram plugin enabled: `"enabledPlugins": { "engram@engram": true }` in `settings.json`, plugin version 0.1.2.
2. Run `gentle-ai doctor` — `engram:reachable` warns, remedy says run `gentle-ai sync`.
3. Run `gentle-ai sync`. It reports `Managed components synced: engram, sdd, skills, context7, permissions, gga, claude-theme, opencode-gentle-logo, persona`.
4. Run `gentle-ai doctor` again.
5. Inspect `mcpServers` in the Claude Code user config, and run `claude mcp list`.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

After `sync`, exactly one working Engram MCP registration exists and `engram:reachable` passes.

Concretely, one of:

- `sync` skips the direct entry only when the plugin actually declares an MCP server, and writes `mcpServers.engram` otherwise; or
- the Claude Code plugin package declares the MCP server, making the skip correct; or
- `doctor`'s `engram:reachable` recognizes the plugin path as a valid registration, so the check stops prescribing a remedy that cannot change the outcome.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

`sync` skips the direct registration, the plugin supplies none, and nothing registers Engram.

- `mcpServers` contains only `context7` — no `engram` entry, before or after `sync`. Confirmed identical in the pre-sync config snapshots `sync` itself took (today's and one from three days earlier), so the entry was never present on this host.
- `claude mcp list` reports only the two unrelated servers as connected; no `engram`.
- No `mem_*` tools resolve in-session under either `mcp__engram__*` or `mcp__plugin_engram_engram__*`.
- `doctor` reports `engram:reachable` → `engram MCP not probed: no persisted MCP configuration found for installed agents`, remedy `Run 'gentle-ai sync' to restore the Engram MCP configuration`. Status stays `degraded` across repeated sync/doctor cycles.

The remedy `doctor` prescribes is the exact command whose current behavior produces the state, so the check can never clear by following its own guidance.

### Gentle AI Version

gentle-ai 2.7.0 (stable channel — build string carries neither `-rc.` nor `-main.`), managed assets 2.7.0, engram 1.20.0, plugin `engram@engram` 0.1.2

### Operating System

Windows 10 (build 19045), amd64

### AI Agent / Client

Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area

Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
# doctor, before and after sync — identical
  [!!]  engram:reachable   engram MCP not probed: no persisted MCP configuration found for installed agents
       Remedy: Run 'gentle-ai sync' to restore the Engram MCP configuration
Summary: 7 passed, 0 failed, 1 warnings
Status:  degraded

# sync reports success for the engram component
gentle-ai sync — managed sync executed
Agents synced: claude-code
Managed components synced: engram, sdd, skills, context7, permissions, gga, ...
Sync actions executed: 3 files changed

# registered MCP servers after sync — engram absent
$ claude mcp list
claude.ai Mobbin: ... - Connected
context7: npx -y --package=@upstash/context7-mcp@2.2.5 -- context7-mcp - Connected

# installed plugin tree — hooks and skills only, no MCP declaration
plugin/claude-code/.claude-plugin/plugin.json   # no mcpServers key
plugin/claude-code/hooks/hooks.json
plugin/claude-code/scripts/*.sh, user-prompt-submit.ps1
plugin/claude-code/skills/memory/SKILL.md
# compare: plugin/codex/.mcp.json exists
```

### Additional Context

Reported by an agent session after `doctor` returned `degraded` and the prescribed remedy did not change the result.

Not reopening #4188: its scope and delivered fix are the opposite direction (removing a duplicate registration), and this is the inverse failure the fix introduces on hosts where the plugin supplies no MCP server. Filing separately and linking rather than commenting on a closed, delivered issue.

Related but distinct:

- #4282 — `engram:reachable` mis-counting persisted configs. Same check, different defect: that one is about which configs are named, this one is about the plugin path not being a persisted config at all.
- #3778 — `sdd-*` agents declaring plugin-scoped Engram tools that never resolve for a non-plugin install. Same prefix mismatch, opposite install shape.
- #2762 — `engram:reachable` false positive on `opencode.json`. Different agent.

Duplicate search performed over open and closed issues for `engram mcp`, `engram registration`, `sync mcpServers`, `engram mcp missing`, `no persisted MCP configuration`, `plugin enabled no mcp registration`, and `4278 regression`; no equivalent report found.
