title: bug(review): admission honesty scan false-positives on out-of-manifest scope phrasing while inspection.status=completed, forcing a full lens re-run
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

`review capture-result` rejects an otherwise-valid reviewer result as a **false completion** when the `evidence` prose contains phrases like "could not be verified" or "could not be inspected" **about modules outside the candidate's frozen manifest**, even though `inspection.status` is correctly `"completed"` and `inspection.paths` covers the full manifest.

Standard reviewer practice on multi-lens external reviews is to state scope limits for out-of-manifest collaborators ("the agent-manager module ... could not be verified from the candidate alone"). The admission prose scan cannot distinguish "the **candidate** could not be inspected" (the honesty violation the scan exists for) from "an **opaque collaborator** could not be verified" (correct, expected phrasing). The only remedy is re-running the entire lens with reworded evidence — substance identical, only wording changed — after which admission accepts the same findings.

Cost observed: one full reviewer re-dispatch plus transport on a 4-lens, 5,748-line candidate.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a multi-lens external review whose candidate imports modules outside the changed-path manifest (any refactor unit over an extracted module graph).
2. Have the reviewer complete the inspection honestly: `inspection.status = "completed"`, full `inspection.paths`, and an evidence array that includes a sentence like "the callee module is outside this candidate, so its return contract could not be verified here".
3. Submit via `gentle-ai review capture-result --input ...` with the slot's exact binding tokens.
4. Admission rejects with `invalid_request` / "reviewer artifact admission incomplete: reviewer evidence reports the candidate could not be inspected even though inspection.status is 'completed'; declare inspection.status: 'unavailable' ...".
5. Re-run the same lens with the identical findings and the only change being that evidence phrases about out-of-manifest modules are reworded to "lies outside this candidate's frozen manifest and was therefore treated as an opaque collaborator".
6. Admission accepts.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

- The prose scan for false completions should be scoped to statements about the **candidate itself** (the manifest paths / the inspection), not to any occurrence of "could not be verified" anywhere in the evidence array; or
- scope limits for out-of-manifest collaborators should be a typed field (e.g. `inspection.opaque_collaborators`) instead of free prose that a string scan then misreads.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

A completed, honest result with correct typed inspection fields is rejected as a false completion; the prescribed "fix" (flipping to `inspection.status: "unavailable"`) would be wrong (the candidate WAS fully inspected), and the only working remedy is a cosmetic rewording that wastes a full reviewer run.

### Gentle AI Version

main (brew `main` channel)

### Operating System

macOS

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
$ gentle-ai review capture-result --lineage=<id> --expected-revision=... --target=... \
    --repository-context=... --lens=review-resilience --order=1 \
    --subject-hash=sha256:<task-binding-subject> --agent=pi --input=<answer-file>

{
  "schema": "gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2",
  "operation": "review.capture-result",
  "phase": "preflight",
  "code": "invalid_request",
  "mutation_outcome": "not_started",
  "retry_safe": true,
  "cause": "reviewer artifact admission incomplete: reviewer evidence reports the
           candidate could not be inspected even though inspection.status is
           \"completed\"; declare inspection.status: \"unavailable\" with a non-empty
           inspection.reason instead of describing the failure only in evidence:
           the rejected admission did not consume the lens slot, so re-run the lens
           and invoke gentle-ai review capture-result again ..."
}

# rejected evidence phrasing (triggered the false positive):
#   "... the callee module is outside this candidate, so its return contract
#    could not be verified here ..."
# accepted evidence phrasing (same findings, same subject, admitted):
#   "... the callee module lies outside this candidate's frozen manifest and was
#    therefore treated as an opaque collaborator whose internals belong to other
#    units ..."
```

### Additional Context

The working mitigation for other agents hitting this: instruct reviewer dispatches to use the "opaque collaborator" formula for any out-of-manifest scope statement and to reserve "could not (be inspected/verified)" phrasing strictly for the candidate itself. That convention is invisible to new users and undocumented; the scanner making it load-bearing is the defect.

title: bug(review): rejected capture-result rotates the collect subject while the failure message quotes the old value — admission becomes unsatisfiable and a fresh start is blocked
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

A rejected `review capture-result` can leave a reviewer slot in a state that **no payload can satisfy**, and the lineage then cannot be replaced. Four defects chain into this on the external CLI route (Pi host, `agent=pi`):

1. **Rejection rotates the collect subject, but the failure message quotes the old value.** After a `binding_mismatch` rejection (which explicitly says "the rejected admission did not consume the lens slot"), the next lineage-scoped STATUS offers the same slot with a *different* `subject-hash`, while the rejection message keeps demanding the old one.
2. **The task materializer binds the authority revision as the task's subject.** `capture-result --materialize=true` emits a `GENTLE_AI_REVIEW_BINDING` whose `subject_hash` equals the lineage's `expected-revision` value, not the current artifact subject. A reviewer that faithfully echoes the binding (as instructed) therefore produces a result that mismatches the live collect binding.
3. **The failure message does not render the value admission actually compares.** The rejection says the expected subject is `sha256:2bf68…` while a byte-identical copy of that exact value in the payload is still rejected.
4. **A stuck lineage blocks fresh starts.** Pre-start negotiation (`review status … --next-transition`) keeps re-emitting the same stuck lineage id, so the only exit is the destructive `review abandon`.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Start an ordinary negotiated review (`review start … --consent granted`); here a 4-lens, 35-changed-line candidate.
2. `review status --lineage <L> --next-transition` → collect slot for `review-risk`, subject `sha256:2bf68…`.
3. `review capture-result … --materialize=true` → task whose `GENTLE_AI_REVIEW_BINDING.subject_hash` is `sha256:2bf68…`.
4. Run the reviewer; it returns a schema-valid result echoing `subject_hash: sha256:2bf68…`.
5. `review capture-result … --input <result>` → **rejected**: `binding_mismatch … re-run the lens … with a result that echoes the binding's top-level subject_hash, which is sha256:2bf68…` — the same value the payload contains.
6. `review status --lineage <L> --next-transition` → the same slot now carries subject `sha256:06c4…` and `expected-revision sha256:2bf68…` (the old subject and the revision have swapped roles).
7. Re-materialize → the task **still** binds `sha256:2bf68…` as its subject (the revision value).
8. Retry the capture with every combination — old payload + old tokens, new payload + new tokens, old payload + new tokens — all three are rejected with the identical message quoting `sha256:2bf68…`.
9. `review status --cwd <repo> --contract … --agent pi --next-transition` (pre-start negotiation) → re-offers the **same** lineage id, so no fresh lineage can be started for the target.

Caveat noted for honesty: between steps 5 and 7 a second `--materialize` was issued on the same slot before the rotation was understood; the double-materialize may have aggravated the state, but step 5's rejection already showed the contradictory message on a clean single-materialize attempt.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

- A rejected admission that "does not consume the lens slot" leaves the binding unchanged, or the failure message and the re-offered binding agree on one subject value.
- The materialized task's `GENTLE_AI_REVIEW_BINDING.subject_hash` is the artifact subject the next capture will compare against.
- The rejection message renders the value admission actually compares.
- An unsatisfiable lineage does not block minting a fresh lineage for the same target.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The slot becomes unsatisfiable (three payload×token combinations rejected while the message demands a value the payload already contains), the preserved rejected-result file proves the payload was received byte-intact, and the negotiation re-offers the stuck lineage so the review cannot be restarted without a destructive abandon. In the live session the lineage was left open as drift and the candidate went unreviewed.

### Gentle AI Version

`gentle-ai main` (brew main channel, update notice to 1.20.0 pending)

### Operating System

macOS

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
# attempt 1: payload subject == token subject == message-expected, still rejected
$ shasum -a 256 answer.txt
fe1360cdfcfd2deea79b7775b0adbc0b154a436aa1a048e36a12fa37c8afa172  answer.txt
# .git/gentle-ai/rejected-results/<L>/review-risk-1-fe1360cdfcfd.json
#   "raw_sha256": "fe1360cdfcfd2deea79b7775b0adbc0b154a436aa1a048e36a12fa37c8afa172"  (byte-intact)
#   "reason": "... echoes the binding's top-level subject_hash, which is sha256:2bf68...
#              the rejected admission did not consume the lens slot ..."

# status BEFORE the rejection (slot subject):
subject-hash    = sha256:2bf68ca9…   expected-revision = (different)

# status AFTER the rejection (same slot, "not consumed"):
subject-hash    = sha256:06c4273f…   expected-revision = sha256:2bf68ca9…

# re-materialized task binding (step 7):
GENTLE_AI_REVIEW_BINDING {"subject_hash":"sha256:2bf68ca9…", "revision":"sha256:…"}
#   ^ subject_hash field carries the revision-shaped value, not sha256:06c4273f…

# all three retries rejected with the identical cause quoting sha256:2bf68ca9…
# pre-start negotiation afterwards:
#   next_transition.execute.command … --lineage=<same stuck id> … (fresh start blocked)
```

### Additional Context

Route: external native CLI (`gentle-ai review … --agent pi`) driven by the Pi host; the in-process host relay is known-broken for this setup (gentle-pi#919), so the CLI path is the de-facto integration.

Related but distinct: #4421 (OpenCode transport rematerializes a v1 artifact subject as v2 and rejects it — different component, same subject-desync family), #4027 (reviewer echoed target_identity as subject_hash — reviewer-side cause), #2028 (recovery path for rejected reviewer results), #2442 (twelve causes behind one message).

Secondary observations from the same session, offered for triage context:

- Provider-rendered refuter (`capture-refuter --execute=true`) hit `operation_timeout` ("pi reviewer transport failed: context deadline exceeded") twice on a 4-lens lineage; the third attempt succeeded only when given a >900s window. `mutation_outcome: unknown` + `retry_safe: false` on a timeout makes the safe continuation non-obvious.
- Tier/lens selection assigned 4 lenses (risk/resilience/readability/reliability) to a 35-changed-line whitespace-only reformat candidate.
- Each `--materialize` task re-embeds the full patch plus schema (~580 lines per lens; ~2.3k lines of identical boilerplate for one 4-lens unit), which is heavy for relayed reviewer transports.

Full sanitized artifacts (STATUS dumps, the three rejected outputs, the preserved rejected-result JSON, task bindings) are available on request.

title: bug(opencode): opencode-transport rejects reviewer Tasks when the session root is a git-less parent of the review repository (2.6.0)
body:
## Bug Description

A negotiated OpenCode review freezes its lineage, then every reviewer Task is rejected before model execution with:

`opencode_review_transport_binding_invalid: Task repository context does not match the repository and binding it commits to`

when the OpenCode session is rooted in a **git-less parent directory that contains the review repository** (nested repo layout). The managed relay starts `gentle-ai review opencode-transport` with the session context (`worktree || directory`), which resolves outside the repository the review commits to, so the fail-closed Go validation refuses and the frozen reviewer slots remain ungrantable. No typed actionable continuation is offered for this topology.

## Environment

- Gentle AI: 2.6.0 (stable channel; latest published at report time: 2.7.0, not yet verified against this defect)
- Client: OpenCode (managed review-transport plugin)
- Platform: Linux x86_64
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`

## Observed evidence

- A high-risk negotiated review was created via `review start` (consent granted); the lineage entered `reviewing`.
- Native STATUS returned a canonical 4-lens collect set (review-risk, review-resilience, review-readability, review-reliability) with complete provider-issued bindings.
- Four foreground reviewer Tasks were launched with the exact provider-issued `GENTLE_AI_REVIEW_BINDING` payloads; **all four were rejected before reviewer execution** with the envelope above.
- Manual transport probes with the same binding frame:
  - run from **inside** the repository (root and a nested subdirectory): materializes the reviewer prompt successfully;
  - run from the **git-less parent** and from the session root: refused with the same envelope.
- No reviewer result, capture, receipt, source mutation, commit, push, or PR was created by the failed launches.

## Expected behavior

Either:

- the relay resolves the repository context to the repository its binding commits to and launches the reviewer exactly once against the immutable candidate; or
- the lifecycle returns a typed, actionable continuation before or instead of wedging an already-frozen lineage (the preflight-guard direction was declined in #3980; the slot here is unreachable and re-offered with no sanctioned retry).

## Actual behavior

After consent and freeze, every reviewer Task for this topology is refused by the transport validation; the lineage remains in `reviewing` with `reviewer_results_required`. The refusal is deterministic and correlates with the relay spawn directory, not with the binding contents.

## Minimal reproduction (sanitized)

1. Have repository R reachable at `<parent-workspace>/<subdir>/R`, where `<parent-workspace>` is not a Git repository; open the OpenCode session rooted at `<parent-workspace>`.
2. Run the negotiated lifecycle with cwd R: STATUS → START (consent granted) → STATUS until it returns a reviewer collect input.
3. Launch the published reviewer Task with the exact provider-issued binding.
4. Observe the transport refusal before reviewer execution.
5. Control: run `gentle-ai review opencode-transport` manually with the same binding frame from inside R → succeeds; from `<parent-workspace>` → refused.

## Related

- #3980 (closed, not planned): cross-worktree wedge and the declined preflight guard.
- #3987 (closed, completed): registered-worktree target resolution (does not cover a git-less parent that merely contains the repository).
- #2946 (closed, completed): opaque repository-context launch.
- #4030 (open): same envelope on a single worktree (2.5.0) — the control probe above (in-repo transport succeeds on 2.6.0) distinguishes this report from that divergence.
- #4331 (open): git-less workspace worktree resolution in another plugin (skill registry) — related family, different observable.

## Preserved-state evidence

- Lineage: `review-03d5ffad6f43805f` (still `reviewing`; slots re-offered, unconsumed)
- Target identity: `sha256:5b34d89ff55ddd94331b768c7c6171f0d82304ec97a448d3dc29bd220cbb8488`
- Authority revision: `sha256:c1a55b040230ebc0a8e29ded40225585856893160c3065df1b8654840e9bc274`
- Bounded attempts: 4 Task launches + 4 manual transport probes; no retry storm.

## Privacy

This report excludes repository identifiers, project names, absolute paths, usernames, hostnames, credentials, environment values, source contents, diffs, and raw command arguments.

title: bug(review): claude-code reviewer transport fails intermittently with invalid_request and an empty cause, then the identical slot completes on retry (2.4.0, Windows)
body:
## Observed

`gentle-ai review capture-result` for a reviewer lens slot fails intermittently within 3–6 s with admission code `invalid_request`, and the same bound slot later succeeds on retry without any change to the candidate or the arguments.

## Environment

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| gentle-ai | 2.4.0 |
| OS / arch | Windows 11 (10.0.26200), x64 |
| Agent / client | `claude-code` |
| Contract | `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2` |
| Review tier | high (4 lenses), workspace projection, 8 files / 292 changed lines |

## Operation shape

STATUS `--next-transition` → `kind=collect`, `capture_operation=review.capture-result` → `gentle-ai review capture-result <provider-returned tokens>` (lineage, expected-revision, lens, order, repository-context, artifact_subject), executed exactly as returned, in the foreground, once per provider-returned collection attempt.

## Attempts and outcomes (same lineage, same bound slot for lens 2)

| Run | Attempt | Elapsed | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | lens 1 | 16 s | completed |
| 1 | lens 2, #1 | 5 s | `invalid_request` |
| 1 | lens 2, #2 | 6 s | `invalid_request` |
| 1 | lens 2, #3 | 6 s | `invalid_request` |
| 2 (fresh STATUS reoffered the identical slot) | lens 2, #1 | 3 s | `invalid_request` |
| 2 | lens 2, #2 | 4 s | `invalid_request` |
| 2 | lens 2, #3 | 92 s | completed |
| 2 | lenses 3–4 | 71 s / 68 s | completed |

Two later high-tier lineages on the same machine the same day completed 4/4 lenses on the first attempt each.

## Failure envelope

```
admission_decision: invalid_request
Error: invoke provider reviewer: claude reviewer transport failed: exit status 1:  [invalid_request]
```

Note the double space before `[invalid_request]`: the child process stderr that would normally sit there is empty, so the message carries no diagnostic from the reviewer runtime.

## Expected vs actual

- Expected: a transient transport failure of the reviewer child process to be classified as retryable/transient (or at least distinguishable from a malformed request), with the child's stderr or exit reason surfaced.
- Actual: the same code (`invalid_request`) that signals a caller-side malformed request, for a failure that is not reproducible with identical inputs and clears itself on retry, with no diagnostic payload.

## Mutation outcome / preserved state

No lifecycle mutation was lost: STATUS kept reoffering the exact same bound slot (`lineage`, `target`, `expected-revision`, `artifact_subject`, `lens`, `order`), the retry completed, and the lineage went on to `approved` and `pre-commit` / `pre-pr` `allow`.

## Minimal reproduction

1. Start a high-tier review with `--agent claude-code` (four lenses).
2. Follow STATUS `--next-transition`, running each `review.capture-result` as returned.
3. Intermittently, a lens capture exits in 3–6 s with the envelope above; re-querying STATUS reoffers the slot and a later attempt completes.

Not deterministic; observed 5 consecutive failures on one slot, then success.

## Opaque identifiers

Lineage `review-2a03fb3c09317217`.

## Related, not equivalent

- #4306 has the same envelope shape but a named cause (`[claude-code:unrecognized_model]`) and is deterministic; here the bracket is empty and the same slot succeeds later.
- #4275 (lenses refused on the account default model) is content-dependent per its reports; here the identical content and tokens completed on the sixth attempt, which reads as a transient transport failure rather than a refusal. It may still be the same underlying child-process path; reported separately because the classification (`invalid_request` with no cause) is what a routing consumer sees.

_Automated provider-defect report, filed with the repository owner's explicit consent; observed evidence only._

title: feat(cli): built-in AI router that dispatches prompts to the best local tool
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Problem Statement

Users who combine several AI tools (Pi, OpenCode, Claude CLI, local Ollama models) must manually decide which tool handles each prompt, weighing cost, speed, complexity, specialization, and privacy. The binary has no built-in dispatch: every prompt starts with a manual tool choice, and private prompts risk being sent to a cloud tool by habit. I validated the concept with a standalone local router CLI: deterministic precedence (explicit tool flag, then private/local provider, then task rule, then default provider), one adapter per provider type (local CLI execution, local HTTP model runtime, safe echo mock), YAML configuration, and a JSONL decision log used for later tuning.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Add a native router command to the binary, e.g. `gentle-ai router ask "<prompt>"`, that:

- reads provider adapters from configuration (local agent CLIs, local model runtimes, echo mock for dry runs);
- selects the provider by an explicit, explainable rule order: `--tool <name>`, then `--private`, then `--task <name>`, then default;
- supports fallback chains when the selected provider is missing or fails;
- appends each routing decision (provider, reason, latency, error) to a local JSONL log;
- ships with `gentle-ai router providers` to list configured providers and their roles.

Example usage:

```
gentle-ai router ask "summarize this note" --private
gentle-ai router ask --task code "refactor this function"
gentle-ai router ask --tool pi "apply the SDD change"
```

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- Keep the router as a standalone external CLI (works today, but every user re-solves config, adapters, and logging).
- Shell aliases per tool (no policy, no fallback, no decision log).
- Cloud-side model routing such as Kilo Gateway routing (#851) — solves model selection inside one platform, not dispatch across local tools/agents with privacy boundaries.

### 📎 Additional Context

Personal, local-first use case. A zero-dependency reference implementation exists with an adapter contract, a routing precedence spec, and an architecture doc; happy to share the design to shape the native implementation. No PR will be opened until/unless this issue is approved.

title: [provider defect] Targeted validation binding loses correction lineage during reconciliation
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

### 📝 Bug Description
A provider-issued targeted correction-validation binding was rejected immediately after fresh status produced it. Fresh target-scoped status then reoffered the exact same slot, but the single permitted relaunch failed during status reconciliation. The next bound status classified the corrected target as unrelated to the retained correction lineage and offered a fresh review start, leaving the validation mutation outcome unprovable.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce
1. Start a high-risk compact review, capture its correction plan, and apply a correction only within the admitted paths and line budget.
2. Request bound status and submit the exact targeted-validator collect binding returned by that status.
3. If the binding is rejected, request fresh bound status and resubmit only when it reoffers the exact same bound slot.
4. Observe status reconciliation fail and a later bound status classify the corrected target as unrelated while offering a fresh start.

### ✅ Expected Behavior
The fresh provider-issued validator binding should be accepted exactly once. If capture or reconciliation is uncertain, subsequent bound status should authoritatively report whether validation committed and preserve the correction lineage association. It should not offer a fresh review while the prior mutation outcome is unknown.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
The first fresh binding was reported as unknown or expired. Fresh status reoffered the same slot. Its single permitted relaunch failed reconciliation with a schema incompatibility and unknown mutation outcome. Final bound status treated the corrected target as unrelated and proposed a new review lineage.


title: bug(review): provider_refuter_required transition emits --execute=true, a flag capture-result does not define (claude-code, 2.7.0 stable)
body:
## Summary

After a reviewer lens capture, `review status` moves the lineage to `collect` / `provider_refuter_required` and returns, as its exact `next_transition`, a `review capture-result` invocation carrying `--execute=true`.

`review capture-result` does not define `--execute`. Running the provider-issued command verbatim is refused by the CLI itself, so the lineage cannot reach a terminal outcome.

Re-querying the bound `review status` reoffers the identical slot with the identical token, so this is not transient.

## Environment

- gentle-ai **2.7.0** (stable channel — build string carries no `-rc.` or `-main.` tag)
- OS/arch: darwin/arm64
- Client/runtime: Claude Code (in-process capture, `--agent=claude-code`)
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`
- Projection: `workspace`, `--untracked-scope=exclude`
- Lineage: `review-a8a5a593b8ea2790`

## Reproduction

1. `review status --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --agent claude-code --next-transition` → `action: start`, exact START returned.
2. Run the returned START with `--consent granted` → `action: created`.
3. Re-enter with the returned bound `review status` → `collect` / `reviewer_results_required`, one `review-reliability` slot.
4. Run that slot's exact `review capture-result … --lens=review-reliability --order=0 --agent=claude-code` verbatim.
5. Re-enter the bound `review status` → now `collect` / `provider_refuter_required`, with this exact command:

```
gentle-ai review capture-result \
  --lineage=review-a8a5a593b8ea2790 \
  --expected-revision=sha256:<redacted> \
  --target=sha256:<redacted> \
  --repository-context=rctx2_<redacted> \
  --agent=claude-code \
  --execute=true
```

6. Run it verbatim.

## Expected

The provider-issued command runs, the refuter batch is captured, and the lineage advances toward a terminal outcome.

## Actual

```json
{
  "schema": "gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2",
  "contract": "gentle-ai.review-integration/v2",
  "operation": "review.capture-result",
  "phase": "preflight",
  "code": "invalid_request",
  "message": "The negotiated review request is invalid.",
  "mutation_outcome": "not_started",
  "authority_applicability": "not_evaluated",
  "retry_safe": true,
  "replayability": "not_replayable",
  "required_inputs": [],
  "next_action": "correct_request",
  "cause": "flag provided but not defined: -execute"
}
```

`gentle-ai review capture-result --help` lists only:

```
--agent --cwd --expected-revision --input --lens --lineage
--materialize --order --preflight --repository-context --subject-hash --target
```

`--execute` is absent.

## Bounded attempts and outcomes

| # | Operation | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `capture-result --lens=review-reliability --order=0 --agent=claude-code` (verbatim) | `invalid_request`, cause `refuter provider result admission incomplete: reviewer payload contains no complete JSON object: no object start was found in 391 bytes` |
| 2 | bound `review status` (recovery rule after an incomplete capture) | advanced to `collect` / `provider_refuter_required` |
| 3 | reoffered `capture-result … --execute=true` (verbatim) | `invalid_request`, cause `flag provided but not defined: -execute` |
| 4 | bound `review status` again | reoffers the identical slot and the identical `--execute=true` token |

No blind retries were issued beyond the contract's recovery rule (re-query bound STATUS, relaunch only on an identically reoffered slot).

## Preserved state

- `mutation_outcome: not_started` on both refusals.
- The lineage remains in `collect` / `provider_refuter_required`; no receipt, no tombstone, no acknowledgement.
- No other lineage was touched.

## Related, not duplicate

- #4439 — same run also hit the in-process claude-code refuter returning no JSON object (attempt 1 above). That one reproduces here on 2.7.0 stable; commenting there separately.
- #4388 — same causal class (a transition emitting a provider-issued command the CLI rejects) but a different transition (`correction_plan_required`) and the opposite shape (a flag **omitted** rather than an **undefined** flag emitted).

title: bug(pi): capture facade rejects collect bindings it just rendered (later slots after first two lens captures)
body:
## Summary

The Pi review capture facade rejects collect bindings that its own negotiated STATUS render just issued, for later slots in a multi-lens review, while the same mechanics succeeded for the first slots of the same lineage.

- Affected: `gentle-pi@2.5.0` facade (`gentle_review_capture` / `gentle_review_capture_group`) over `gentle-ai@2.7.0` (stable channel), contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, negotiated high-risk ordinary review, 4 lenses, transport `pi_host_relay`.
- Contract followed: `{"operation":"inspect"}` → `select-intended-untracked` (empty selection, eligible untracked excluded) → lineage created → facade STATUS → capture.

## Observed behavior

| Slot | Flow | Result |
|---|---|---|
| lens order 0 (single capture) | STATUS render → capture → forecast → capture with `reviewerRunAcknowledged: true` | ✅ captured + admitted (`completed`) |
| lens order 1 (same flow, same session) | same | ✅ captured + admitted (`completed`) |
| lens order 2 (STATUS re-render → capture, binding from that render) | ×3 attempts (2 immediately after fresh renders, 1 after managed `gentle-ai sync --agents pi`) | ❌ `capture-binding-rejected` |
| capture-group with the two bindings from the same fresh render | ×2 attempts (once pre-sync, once post-sync) | ❌ `capture-group-rejected` |

Rejection envelope (both tools, every attempt):

```
{"status":"blocked","outcome":"capture-binding-rejected","reason":"collectBinding is unknown, expired, or belongs to a different session route","mutation_performed":false,"mutation_outcome":"none"}
```

## Expected behavior

A collect binding returned by the facade's own `status` render for the current revision should be accepted by the immediately following `gentle_review_capture`/`gentle_review_capture_group` call, as it was for the first two lens slots in the same lineage.

## Bounded evidence

1. Bindings were submitted immediately after the STATUS render that issued them; no intermediate facade/CLI status calls between render and capture.
2. The authority revision and frozen manifest stayed identical across renders; the lineage stayed `reviewing` with the same two admitted lens results throughout (state preserved; no additional authority burn).
3. The single-slot forecast for the failing slot itself validated at first attempt on an earlier render (returned the cost forecast), but the subsequent acknowledged submission was rejected — the same shape that succeeded for orders 0 and 1.
4. Persists after managed component sync (`gentle-ai sync --agents pi`, "3 files changed", components list incl. engram/sdd/skills).
5. No mutation occurred on any rejection (`mutation_outcome: none`); 2 of 4 lens results remain captured/admitted; consumer state preserved.

## Adjacent issues (not equivalent)

- #2442 (closed; OpenCode plugin generic message, different surface and text) and #1599/#1610/#2972/#2630 (OpenCode managed dispatcher / rc-era native contract) — adjacent capture-binding failures, but this occurrence is the **Pi facade** route (`pi_host_relay`) refusing bindings from its **own** render for later slots, which none of them document.

## Environment

- `gentle-pi 2.5.0` (package-local facade), `gentle-ai 2.7.0` (published stable binary), Linux x86_64, Pi runtime, negotiated `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2` status v7.
- Lineage state at report time: `reviewing`, 2/4 lens results admitted, 2 lenses blocked, consumer state preserved (no reset/recover attempted).

title: bug(review): capture-validation refused in preflight with "admitted targeted-validator evidence does not match its request and digests" although no validator tuple was ever admitted (workspace, select, 2.7.0)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

Automated provider defect report, filed with the operator's explicit consent. Observed behavior only; no root cause is asserted.

On `2.7.0` stable (build string carries no `-rc.` or `-main.` tag), `claude-code` runtime, contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, projection `workspace`, `--untracked-scope=select`: a bounded compact-v2 correction that edits only files already inside the frozen candidate cannot be validated. The bound STATUS after the edit correctly stays in-lineage and offers `collect` / `targeted_validation_required` with a `review.capture-validation` slot, but running that slot with its exact returned tokens is refused in **preflight** (`mutation_outcome: not_started`, `retry_safe: true`, `next_action: correct_request`) with:

```
cause: admitted targeted-validator evidence does not match its request and digests
```

STATUS then reoffers the identical slot (same `--expected-revision`, `--target`, `--request-hash`, `--repository-context`), and the single contract-permitted relaunch fails with the same envelope. The lineage is left in `correction_required` with no runnable exit.

Two details that may help a maintainer:

- The store for the lineage (`review-state.json`) contains exactly **one** admitted role tuple (`role: lens`, `review-reliability`, `decision: completed`). There is no `targeted_validator` tuple at all, and no `rejected-results/<lineage>/` directory was written — so the refusal text names "admitted targeted-validator evidence" for a lineage in which the validator was never executed or admitted.
- The same store shows `fix_delta_hash: sha256:e3b0c442…b855`, which is the SHA-256 of the empty string, and `current_snapshot.candidate_tree` still equal to the initial candidate tree, while the bound STATUS reports a different `current_candidate_tree` and a `validation_request.correction_candidate_tree` / `correction_target_identity` for the corrected tree. `capture_phase_epoch` is `2`.

**Relationship to the closest existing issues** (searched open and closed, including the exact phrases `"does not match its request"` and `"targeted-validator evidence"`):

- #4386 (open, 2.7.0) — same phase, different observable: there the validator runs and returns prose with no JSON object (`reviewer payload contains no complete JSON object`). Here the validator is never launched; the refusal is a preflight digest check.
- #4473 (open, 2.7.0) — workspace + select, but the correction there *adds* a new untracked file and STATUS reroutes to a fresh target. Here no file is added, and STATUS correctly stays bound and offers validation.
- #4318 (open) — `--committed-only` projection; refusal text is `captured reviewer result slot conflicts with different canonical bytes`. Different projection and different cause.
- #4094 / #4080 / #4061 (closed) — different refusal causes (`correction submission descriptor is not provider-bound`, over-budget admission then wedge, truncated validator JSON).

A contrasting data point from the same session and the same build: an earlier lineage on the same repository followed the identical sequence (plan → edit two already-candidate files, one of them intended-untracked → bound STATUS → `capture-validation --execute=true`) and validated, approved, and acknowledged without incident. The only notable difference in the failing candidate is its size: ~9,800 changed lines, of which ~8,400 are one generated JSON snapshot file included as intended-untracked.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Selectorless STATUS (`review status --cwd <repo> --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --agent claude-code --next-transition`) → `collect` / `intended_untracked_selection_required`.
2. STATUS with `--untracked-scope=select --expected-untracked-inventory=<digest> --intended-untracked=<path>` (seven new files, one of them a ~8,400-line generated JSON) → `execute` / `fresh_target_ready` with an exact START.
3. Run the exact START (`--consent=relay`), then the exact `granted` invocation from the consent envelope → `action: created`, `state: reviewing`, tier `medium`, one lens (`review-reliability`), `changed_lines: 9773`, `correction_budget: 200`.
4. Bound STATUS → `collect` / `reviewer_results_required`; run the exact `review.capture-result … --agent=claude-code` token list → admitted, `state: correction_required`, one candidate-caused CRITICAL.
5. Run the `status_continuation` → `collect` / `correction_plan_required`; run the exact `capture-correction-plan … --correction-lines=80` → `correction_required`, `correction_lines: 80`.
6. Apply the bounded correction in the worktree: edit one intended-untracked test file (the finding's location) and one tracked markdown file, both already inside the frozen candidate. No file added or removed. Run the focused tests (green).
7. Bound STATUS → `collect` / `targeted_validation_required` with a `review.capture-validation` slot (`--lineage`, `--expected-revision`, `--target`, `--repository-context`, `--request-hash`, `--agent=claude-code`, `--execute=true`).
8. Run that slot with the exact returned tokens → failure envelope below. Bound STATUS again → identical slot (byte-for-byte same tokens). Relaunch once → identical failure.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

`capture-validation --execute=true` runs the provider-owned targeted validator on the corrected candidate and admits its verdict (as it did on an earlier lineage of the same build and session), or the refusal names a state that actually exists in the lineage store and offers a runnable continuation.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Preflight refusal, twice, on the identical reoffered slot; no validator execution, no admitted or rejected validator evidence in the store; lineage stuck in `correction_required`. Recovered by declining the candidate through the captured v3 consent envelope and continuing under ordinary repository policy.

### Gentle AI Version

gentle-ai 2.7.0

### Operating System

Windows

### AI Agent / Client

Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
$ gentle-ai review capture-validation --lineage=review-dac4b2e19dd5fb64 --expected-revision=sha256:6b9236a0c4a8b6addb20a108ef46e169690ff85fc46cb34c5ea96525d63652a5 --target=sha256:f5d3136d9094a5f071ac966e13a4a4313bb158af2ea1f9e019cb93127eb62588 --repository-context=<rctx2 handle from STATUS> --request-hash=sha256:c853fb0ca83ce81f26b9621ed8c6213a80ac1a20d98fb7cb62e227d86d5e79f2 --agent=claude-code --execute=true
{
  "schema": "gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2",
  "contract": "gentle-ai.review-integration/v2",
  "operation": "review.capture-validation",
  "phase": "preflight",
  "code": "invalid_request",
  "message": "The negotiated review request is invalid.",
  "mutation_outcome": "not_started",
  "authority_applicability": "not_evaluated",
  "retry_safe": true,
  "replayability": "not_replayable",
  "lineage_id": "review-dac4b2e19dd5fb64",
  "required_inputs": [],
  "next_action": "correct_request",
  "cause": "admitted targeted-validator evidence does not match its request and digests"
}
Error: admitted targeted-validator evidence does not match its request and digests [invalid_request]

# Bound STATUS between the two attempts (excerpt of validation_request):
#   schema: gentle-ai.review-targeted-validation-request/v1
#   request_hash: sha256:c853fb0c…5e79f2
#   expected_revision: sha256:6b9236a0…652a5
#   target_identity: sha256:b44ed129…ea74e   (initial candidate)
#   correction_candidate_tree: e2a67fbff850a574089816dbae3bdc03a8c8da57
#   correction_target_identity: sha256:f5d3136d…62588
#   correction_paths: 2 entries; correction_paths_digest: sha256:0aac82d2…d9226
#   fix_finding_ids: 1

# review-state.json (store) for the lineage after both attempts:
#   state: correction_required, generation 1, capture_phase_epoch 2
#   capture_phase_revision: sha256:6b9236a0…652a5
#   proposed_correction_lines: 80
#   fix_delta_hash: sha256:e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855  (SHA-256 of "")
#   admitted_role_results: [ {role: lens, lens: review-reliability, decision: completed} ]  — no targeted_validator tuple
#   current_snapshot.candidate_tree: 9e576d4d28774313e12ea45a97e817366a31ba6c (initial tree, unchanged)
#   no .git/gentle-ai/rejected-results/review-dac4b2e19dd5fb64/ directory
```

### Additional Context

- Host: Windows 11 (10.0.26200), x86-64. Commands were run from Git Bash (MSYS) inside Claude Code 2.1.268; the primary shell is PowerShell. `gentle-ai` installed as the release binary under the Go bin directory.
- Bounded attempts: 2 (the contract-permitted single relaunch after STATUS reoffered the same slot). No blind retries, no store reset, no repair command run. Consumer state preserved; the lineage was left untouched for inspection.
- Same session, same build, same repository, an earlier lineage with a 1,327-line candidate went plan → edit → STATUS → `capture-validation --execute=true` → `approved` → acknowledged, so the sequence itself is known-good on this host. The failing candidate differs mainly in size (9,773 lines, one ~8,400-line generated JSON file among the intended-untracked paths).
- Not asserting a cause. Two things a maintainer might want to check given the store evidence: whether the preflight digest check reads a validator tuple that was never written, and whether `fix_delta_hash` being the empty-string hash at validation time is expected for a plan captured before the edit.

title: bug(review): lens captures reject as different session route after two admissions; START replay then fails candidate-view-invalid (2.7.1-dev)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

A negotiated high-risk ordinary review (4 lenses) became permanently stranded after two successful reviewer captures. The remaining two lens captures are rejected with `capture-binding-rejected: collectBinding is unknown, expired, or belongs to a different session route` even though bound STATUS re-offers the exact same collect bindings every time, and the failure survives a full client restart. The offered recovery (inspect re-offers START on the same lineage, reporting the target as unreviewed) then fails natively with `candidate-view-invalid: candidate view lineage binding is missing or ambiguous`, leaving the lineage wedged in `reviewing` with 2/4 lenses admitted and no sanctioned continuation.

Same stranding shape as #3871 (closed; STATUS timeout in `pre_native`) but a different failure mechanism: here STATUS stays healthy and keeps deriving bindings, while the capture path rejects them on session-route grounds. Same terminal error code as #4085 (closed) but a different path (no consent envelope, no intended-untracked selection).

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. On gentle-ai 2.7.1-dev (4a5315127ca7) with the Pi integration, in a Git worktree of a public repo with a small uncommitted 2-file candidate (~67 changed lines, no intended-untracked paths), run `gentle_review inspect` then `start` (ordinary mode, workspace projection). Tier resolves high with 4 lenses (risk, resilience, readability, reliability).
2. STATUS routes to `collect` with 4 materialize collectBindings.
3. Capture lens order 0 (`review-risk`): first call returns the model-run forecast, resubmit with `reviewerRunAcknowledged: true` → `native-reviewer-result-captured`, admission completed.
4. Fresh STATUS, capture lens order 1 (`review-resilience`) with acknowledged submission → captured, admission completed.
5. Fresh STATUS (still offers orders 2 and 3), capture lens order 2 (`review-readability`) → `capture-binding-rejected ... belongs to a different session route`. Retrying after another STATUS rejects identically. Lens order 3 rejects identically.
6. Full client restart (`/reload`, new session route): STATUS offers the same two bindings; both captures still reject with the same session-route reason.
7. `inspect` now reports `applicability: unrelated`, `fresh_target_ready`, and offers a START replay pinned to the SAME lineage.
8. START replay (same idempotency key, `{"mode":"ordinary"}`) → native failure `candidate-view-invalid: candidate view lineage binding is missing or ambiguous`, `lineage_created: false`.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

One of:

- the remaining collect bindings remain capturable after earlier admissions (the route that issued them stays valid through the collect phase); or
- when the binding route is no longer valid, STATUS stops re-offering stale bindings and returns a typed stop with a sanctioned continuation instead of an unactionable rejection loop; and
- the START replay offered by inspect on an existing lineage either re-binds the candidate view or fails before offering, never `candidate-view-invalid` after the lineage already holds admitted artifacts.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

- Lens captures 3 and 4 are permanently rejected as belonging to a different session route, across a client restart, while STATUS keeps offering the identical bindings.
- `gentle_review_capture_group` with the complete current 4-binding set also rejects with `capture-group-rejected` (same reason) before any capture.
- The START replay offered by inspect fails with `candidate-view-invalid`; the lineage stays in `reviewing` (generation 1) with 2/4 lenses admitted and no reachable continuation, finalize, or terminal state.

### Gentle AI Version

title: bug(opencode): orchestrator omits phase summary in chat before invoking interactive question tool
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

OpenCode SDD Orchestration (`internal/assets/opencode/`, `gentle-orchestrator`, SDD Interactive Mode)

### 💡 Bug Description

In SDD **Interactive Mode**, after a delegated sub-agent (e.g. `sdd-explore`, `sdd-propose`, `sdd-spec`) completes successfully and returns its structured task result, the orchestrator is instructed to:
1. Wait for the delegated phase to return.
2. Show a concise phase result summary (status, artifact path(s), key decisions, risks, and next recommended phase).
3. Present the interactive confirmation choice before proceeding to the next phase via the native `question` tool.

However, in practice with OpenCode, the orchestrator invokes the native `question` tool call without first emitting the conversational message containing the phase summary. 

Because OpenCode immediately mounts and renders the interactive `question` modal UI when the tool call arrives, the turn concludes with zero visible assistant text in the conversation history. The user is presented with a blocking decision prompt ("Continue / Adjust / Stop") without having been shown the executive summary or technical achievements of the completed phase. If the user dismisses the prompt to see what happened, the chat contains no summary.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Initialize an SDD change in OpenCode with **Interactive Mode** (`interactive`) selected in session preflight.
2. Run `/sdd-new <change>` or delegate an initial planning phase (e.g., `sdd-explore`).
3. Allow the sub-agent to complete its work and return its task result payload to the orchestrator.
4. Observe the orchestrator's response:
   - It issues the `question` tool call (`question: "¿Continuamos con la fase de Propuesta...?"`).
   - It emits **no assistant text message** before or alongside the tool call.
5. In the client TUI, the user only sees the question options with no context or summary of the completed phase.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The orchestrator must reliably deliver the concise phase summary (status, artifacts created, key decisions, risks, next steps) as visible chat text **before** or **within** the interactive blocking prompt, ensuring the human reviewer has full context before being asked to approve, adjust, or stop.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The assistant text is completely empty/omitted. The orchestrator jumps directly into the `question` tool call, forcing the user to approve a phase blind or dismiss the prompt to ask what was actually done.

### 📋 Proposed Solution

1. In the `gentle-orchestrator` instruction prompt for OpenCode, add an explicit structural enforcement:
   - When using the `question` tool between SDD phases, the phase result summary MUST either be rendered in the assistant message body before calling the tool, or formatted inside the `question`'s context/description field.
   - Instruct the orchestrator that invoking `question` with an empty assistant message is a contract violation in interactive mode.

title: bug(review): approved closure lists advisory findings without their claim text, and the acknowledgement deletes the only store that had it (2.7.0)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues, open and closed ("advisory_findings", "advisory findings without claim", "informational findings text", "acknowledge burns state", "receipt findings after burn"), and this is not a duplicate. #4031 mentions "receipt invisible after burn" on Pi as one item of a broader UX report; this report isolates one concrete data loss on the `claude-code` runtime with the store evidence.
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

Automated provider defect report filed with the operator's consent. Observed behavior only; no root cause is asserted.

On `2.7.0` stable, when a compact-v2 review closes `approved`, the final `gentle-ai.review-last-event-closure/v1` envelope carries an `advisory_findings` block whose `statement` says the findings are non-blocking and should be treated "as separate later work". Each finding in that block has only five fields: `id`, `lens`, `location`, `severity`, `disposition`. There is no `claim`, `evidence`, `proof_refs` or any text describing what the reviewer found. In this transaction the block listed **24 findings** (14 `WARNING`, 10 `SUGGESTION`), all `disposition: informational`.

The text does exist while the lineage is alive: the sibling lineage from the same session that is still in `correction_required` keeps 27 `claim` fields in `review-transactions/v2/<lineage>/review-state.json`, including the full claims of its severe findings and of the findings that later became advisory. But the exact `review.acknowledge-approved` invocation removes the approved lineage's directory under `review-transactions/v2/` entirely (verified: the directory of the acknowledged lineage is absent while eight other lineage directories remain). After the burn, no `review` subcommand listed in `--help` exposes the admitted reviewer results or the advisory text, and the only per-lineage artifact left on disk is `rejected-results/<lineage>/` (a refused validator payload).

Net effect: the operator is told to file 24 items of "separate later work" and is left with identifiers such as `R3-frozen-fallback-priority-inversion` or `R4-silent-safety-net-fallback` plus a `file:line` range, with no way to recover what the reviewer actually claimed. The identifiers are descriptive, but they are not the finding.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Workspace projection, tier `high`, four lenses. Selectorless STATUS, exact START, `consent/v3` relayed, exact `granted`: `created` / `reviewing`.
2. Four exact `capture-result --agent=claude-code`. Final capture: `correction_required` with one CRITICAL finding; the `status_continuation` STATUS shows its full `claim`.
3. Exact `capture-correction-plan`, bounded edit, bound STATUS: `collect` / `targeted_validation_required`. Exact `capture-validation --agent=claude-code --execute=true`: closure `state: approved` with `advisory_findings.findings[]` of 24 entries, each with only `id`, `lens`, `location`, `severity`, `disposition`.
4. Restart the bound STATUS: `execute` / `approved_acknowledgement_required` with the same acknowledgement tokens; the STATUS output carries no advisory text either.
5. Run the exact `review.acknowledge-approved`: `gentle-ai.review-acknowledged/v1`, `action: acknowledged`.
6. List `review-transactions/v2/`: the acknowledged lineage's directory is gone; other lineages' `review-state.json` remain and contain `claim` text.
7. Look for the advisory text: not in the closure envelope, not in any remaining file, not in any `review` subcommand.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Either the `advisory_findings` entries in the approved closure carry the same `claim` (and ideally `proof_refs`) that the finding had while the lineage was alive, or the acknowledgement leaves a readable receipt or artifact with that text, or a read-only `review` command exposes the admitted results of an acknowledged lineage. Any of the three would let the operator author the "separate later work" the statement asks for.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

24 advisory findings reduced to identifiers and locations; the only store that had their text is deleted by the acknowledgement; no command reads it back.

### 🖥️ Environment

- gentle-ai `2.7.0` (stable; build string has no `-rc.` or `-main.` tag), release binary.
- Linux (WSL2, x86-64), Claude Code 2.1.268, runtime `claude-code`, in-process capture, RDD enabled globally.
- Candidate: NestJS 11 + Prisma 6 backend, 11 changed files / 451 changed lines, workspace projection, `--untracked-scope=select` with three intended untracked files.

title: bug(review): a bounded correction that adds a new untracked file is rerouted to a fresh target instead of validated in-lineage (workspace projection, 2.7.0)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues, open and closed ("corrected_candidate_unavailable", "intended_untracked_selection_required", "correction adds new file", "correction new untracked path", "lineage recover", "fresh_target_ready after correction"), and this is not a duplicate. Closest are #4318 (committed-only projection: the corrected candidate is refused by targeted validation) and #3961 (closed, committed-only: bound STATUS refuses its own repository context after a committed correction). This report is workspace projection and fails one stage earlier: the lineage never reaches validation because STATUS reroutes the corrected candidate to a fresh target.
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

Automated provider defect report filed with the operator's consent. Observed behavior only; no root cause is asserted.

On `2.7.0` stable, `claude-code` runtime, contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, projection `workspace`, `--untracked-scope=select`: when a corroborated finding's remedy requires **adding a new untracked file** (here: splitting one hand-written Prisma migration into two, so a second migration directory appears), the bounded correction cannot be validated inside its lineage.

After the correction plan is admitted (`correction_required`) and the edit is applied, the bound STATUS returns `action: recover` with `collect` / `intended_untracked_selection_required` whose submission tokens carry no `--lineage`. Submitting that selection yields `action: start` / `execute` / `fresh_target_ready` with a **new lineage id**. Running that START asks for consent again and re-runs all four lenses from scratch. The four admitted reviewer results and the captured correction plan of the original lineage are never used, and the original lineage remains in `recover` / `intended_untracked_selection_required` with no runnable exit (still the case hours later, after the fresh lineage was approved and acknowledged).

In the same session, a second bounded correction on the fresh lineage that touched **only tracked files** was accepted in-lineage: bound STATUS went straight to `collect` / `targeted_validation_required`, the validator approved, the acknowledgement burned. So the divergence is specifically the new untracked path introduced by the correction.

The contradiction: the corroborated finding (four-lens reduction, `CRITICAL`, `causal_disposition: introduced`) told the operator to split the migration into two files. The lifecycle then treats the file that split produces as a different candidate rather than as the bounded correction it requested.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Workspace projection with at least one intended untracked file (a new migration directory). Selectorless STATUS, untracked selection, exact START, `consent/v3` relayed, exact `granted` invocation: `created` / `reviewing`, tier `high`, four lenses.
2. Bound STATUS: `collect` / `reviewer_results_required`. Four exact `capture-result --agent=claude-code` in provider order. Final capture: `correction_required` with `status_continuation`.
3. `status_continuation` STATUS: `collect` / `correction_plan_required`, four findings, one of them requiring the migration to be split into two files. Exact `capture-correction-plan --correction-lines 150` (budget 200): closure `correction_required`.
4. Bound STATUS before editing: `stop` / `corrected_candidate_unavailable` (expected).
5. Apply the correction: edit tracked files inside the frozen paths, rewrite the first migration file, and add the second migration directory (new untracked path).
6. Bound STATUS (same tokens): `action: recover`, `collect` / `intended_untracked_selection_required`. The eligible paths now list three untracked files; the submission `argument_tokens` are `--contract`, `--next-transition`, `--agent`, `--projection`, `--intended-untracked-selection`, with no `--lineage`.
7. Submit the selection exactly as returned: `action: start`, `execute` / `fresh_target_ready`, START command with a new `--lineage`.
8. Re-query the original lineage's bound STATUS at any later time: still `recover` / `intended_untracked_selection_required`.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Either the corrected candidate that adds the new path is accepted for `targeted_validation_required` inside the original lineage (the finding it corrects asked for that file), or STATUS returns a typed `stop` naming the reason (for example that a correction may not add paths under `--untracked-scope=select`) with a runnable exit for the original lineage, instead of an untyped reroute to a fresh target that silently abandons the admitted lenses and the correction plan.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

`recover` / `intended_untracked_selection_required` with no `--lineage` in the submission, then `fresh_target_ready` on a new lineage; the original lineage stays in `recover` indefinitely. The operator pays four reviewer runs and a consent round twice for one candidate.

### 🖥️ Environment

- gentle-ai `2.7.0` (stable; build string has no `-rc.` or `-main.` tag), installed via the release binary.
- Linux (WSL2, x86-64), Claude Code 2.1.268, runtime `claude-code`, in-process capture, RDD enabled globally.
- Candidate: NestJS 11 + Prisma 6 backend, 8 to 11 changed files / 357 to 451 changed lines, workspace projection, `--untracked-scope=select` with two, then three, intended untracked files.
- Original lineage: `review-b38280495c7bba74`. Fresh lineage created by the reroute: `review-71aba8f5fb239555` (later `approved` and acknowledged).

title: bug(review): Codex reviewer runs `codex exec --ignore-user-config` without model/effort routing, so lenses reason at minimal effort and inherit the global AGENTS.md
body:
## Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate (closest: #4426 — Pi relay, closed as local configuration; #2914 / #4461 / #3468 — same routing gap for Claude / Pi / OpenCode; #2418 superseded by #3138; #2208 closed with no effort/model scope).
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

## 📝 Bug Description
`internal/reviewerprovider/codex_adapter.go` (`codexReviewerArguments`, present on `main` @ b0fe284 and in v2.6.0/v2.7.0) launches the reviewer as:

```
codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --ignore-user-config --sandbox read-only -C <scratch> --output-last-message <path>
```

with no `-m`/`--config model=` and no `--config model_reasoning_effort=`. Because `--ignore-user-config` discards `~/.codex/config.toml`, the reviewer cannot pick up the user's model or reasoning effort by any supported means. The lens then runs on the Codex CLI built-in default model with **no reasoning effort configured**.

A second effect of the same invocation: Codex still loads the global `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` (the SDD orchestrator guidance gentle-ai installs for the host session, ~77 KB) into the reviewer subprocess as `<INSTRUCTIONS>`, on top of the CLI's plugin/skills boilerplate. The lens prompt itself (GENTLE_AI_REVIEW_INSTRUCTION, schema, full patches) is correct and complete — the problem is routing and context pollution, not the materialized task.

## 🔄 Steps to Reproduce
1. `codex-cli 0.153.4` logged in (ChatGPT). `~/.codex/config.toml` with `model = "gpt-6-astra"` and `model_reasoning_effort = "xhigh"`.
2. Enable RDD; in any repo stage a small change; run the v2 lifecycle with `--agent codex` (preflight STATUS → START → bound STATUS → `review capture-result` for one lens).
3. Open the Codex rollout for that capture (`~/.codex/sessions/<date>/rollout-*.jsonl`, `originator: codex_exec`).
4. Observe `turn_context` has **no `effort` key** and `token_count.total_token_usage.reasoning_output_tokens` is in the tens (43–115 observed) for 37k–110k input tokens. Control: an interactive Codex session on the same machine with the same model shows `effort: xhigh` and 900–10 000+ reasoning tokens.
5. Set `model = "gpt-5.6-terra"` (or `gpt-5.6-sol`), add `review_model`, `model_supports_reasoning_summaries = true`, `include_apps_instructions = false` — repeat step 2: the reviewer still runs the CLI default model with `effort` absent (config is ignored as designed by the flag).

## ✅ Expected Behavior
The Codex reviewer honors an explicit, provider-owned model + reasoning-effort routing (as requested for Claude in #2914, Pi in #4461 and OpenCode in #3468), e.g. `--config model="…"` / `--config model_reasoning_effort="…"` from gentle-ai state or environment, and does not inherit the host session's orchestrator `AGENTS.md` into the lens context (e.g. `--config project_doc_max_bytes=0` for the reviewer subprocess).

## ❌ Actual Behavior
Lens, refuter and targeted validator run at the CLI default model with no reasoning effort and ~35k tokens of unrelated instructions per lens. On a 15-file candidate all four lenses returned zero findings; in a scratch candidate the reliability lens did not flag an unguarded division by zero. The same candidates reviewed via the Claude runtime produced CRITICAL findings.

## Gentle AI Version
2.6.0 (adapter unchanged on `main` b0fe284 / v2.7.0)

## Operating System
macOS (Darwin arm64)

## AI Agent / Client
Codex (codex-cli 0.153.4) — host session Claude Code, reviews run with `--agent codex`

## 📋 Affected Area
Review (native RDD reviewer provider / Codex adapter)

## 💡 Logs / Error Output
Sanitized rollout excerpts (one lens capture):
```
session_meta: originator=codex_exec cli_version=0.153.4 model_provider=openai
turn_context: model=gpt-6-astra  (no "effort" key)  sandbox_policy=read-only
token_count.total_token_usage: input_tokens=110518 output_tokens=833 reasoning_output_tokens=115
developer[0] 17 600 chars <skills_instructions>; user[0] 80 823 chars = <recommended_plugins> + <INSTRUCTIONS> (global AGENTS.md ≈ 77 KB); user[1] 292 529 chars = GENTLE_AI_REVIEW_BINDING/CONTEXT/INSTRUCTION/RESULT_SCHEMA/PATCH…
```
Control (interactive session, same model): `turn_context.effort=xhigh`, `reasoning_output_tokens=5195`.

## Additional Context
Verified fix for the routing half (happy to open the PR once approved): in `codexReviewerArguments`, append `--config model=%q` and `--config model_reasoning_effort=%q` from provider-owned routing (`GENTLE_AI_CODEX_REVIEWER_MODEL` / `GENTLE_AI_CODEX_REVIEWER_EFFORT`, effort validated against minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh; no-op when unset). Keeps `--ignore-user-config` and the loopback provider untouched. With this patch built on v2.6.0 the same scratch candidate shows `turn_context.effort=xhigh` and `reasoning_output_tokens` 574–913 (vs 43–86), and the reliability lens now reports WARNING findings it previously missed.

The AGENTS.md / plugins leak is a separate Codex-side behavior: passing `--config project_doc_max_bytes=1` and `--config include_apps_instructions=false` through the same invocation did **not** remove the ~77 KB `<INSTRUCTIONS>` block nor `<recommended_plugins>` on codex-cli 0.153.4, so that half likely needs a different mechanism (e.g. an isolated `CODEX_HOME` for the reviewer, or an upstream Codex flag).

title: bug(pi): `install --agent pi` writes a runtime-derived pinned duplicate of npm:gentle-engram into Pi's settings.json, and `pi remove` deletes both entries
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

`gentle-ai install --agent pi` (2.7.0) writes **two** entries for the same package into
`~/.pi/agent/settings.json`:

```json
"npm:gentle-engram",
"npm:gentle-engram@0.1.12"
```

The pinned one is **derived at runtime from whatever version was just installed** — it is not read
from a template. Searching the 2.7.0 binary for the pinned version string returns nothing, while a
control search for the binary's own version string hits:

```
$ grep -c -o --binary-files=text '2\.7\.0'   gentle-ai.exe   → 3   (positive control)
$ grep -c -o --binary-files=text '0\.1\.11'  gentle-ai.exe   → 0
$ grep -c -o --binary-files=text '0\.1\.12'  gentle-ai.exe   → 0
```

What the binary *does* embed is the **unpinned** form plus `@latest`:

```
npm:gentle-engram
gentle-engram@latest
pi install npm:gentle-engram
npm exec --yes --package gentle-engram@latest -- pi-engram init
```

So the pin follows the installed version across runs — observed `@0.1.8` → `@0.1.11` → `@0.1.12`
on the same machine — and is re-added on every install, which makes manual cleanup non-durable.

#### Why this is not cosmetic — two concrete consequences

**1. Pi skips pinned entries during package updates.** Pi's own documentation (`docs/packages.md`)
describes npm sources with a version specification as *"pinned and skipped during package
updates"*. The duplicate therefore creates a declaration that `pi update --all` will not advance.

**2. There is no safe way to remove the duplicate — `pi remove` deletes both entries.**
Pi matches packages by **name only**; the version in the argument is parsed and then discarded.
From the installed Pi 0.85.1 (`dist/core/package-manager.js`):

```javascript
    getSourceMatchKeyForInput(source) {
        const parsed = this.parseSource(source);
        if (parsed.type === "npm") {
            return `npm:${parsed.name}`;      // version dropped
        }
        ...
    }
    removeSourceFromSettings(source, options) {
        ...
        const nextPackages = currentPackages.filter((existing) => !this.packageSourcesMatch(existing, source, scope));
```

Measured in an isolated Pi agent directory (`PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`), starting from
`["npm:gentle-pi","npm:gentle-engram","npm:gentle-engram@0.1.12","npm:pi-btw"]`:

| command | stdout | resulting `packages` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pi remove npm:gentle-engram@0.1.12` | `Removed npm:gentle-engram@0.1.12` | `["npm:gentle-pi","npm:pi-btw"]` |
| `pi remove npm:gentle-engram` | `Removed npm:gentle-engram` | `["npm:gentle-pi","npm:pi-btw"]` |
| `pi remove npm:gentle-engram@9.9.9` (version never installed) | `Removed npm:gentle-engram@9.9.9` | `["npm:gentle-pi","npm:pi-btw"]` |

All three exit `0` and report removing a single source, while removing **both** entries. The user
is left with **no Engram declaration at all**, which is a worse state than the duplicate.

#### The duplicate cannot be produced by `pi install`, so it is written outside Pi's CLI

`pi install` de-duplicates by name: installing a pinned source on top of an unpinned one
**replaces** the existing entry rather than appending. Measured in the same isolated directory:

```
before: ["npm:gentle-pi", "npm:gentle-engram", "npm:pi-btw"]
$ pi install npm:gentle-engram@0.1.12
Installed npm:gentle-engram@0.1.12
after:  ["npm:gentle-pi", "npm:gentle-engram@0.1.12", "npm:pi-btw"]     # ONE entry, not two
```

Confirmed in `addSourceToSettings` (same file), which finds an existing match by name and
overwrites it in place instead of appending.

Since `pi install` is structurally incapable of leaving two entries for one package, the observed
duplicate must be written into `settings.json` by gentle-ai directly. gentle-ai's own output on the
two runs supports this — it reports the write in its own words, not Pi's:

```
Kept  npm:gentle-engram@0.1.11 in settings.json      # first run
Added npm:gentle-engram@0.1.12 in settings.json      # second run, after the package updated
```

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Have Pi installed with `npm:gentle-engram` declared (unpinned) in `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`.
2. Run `gentle-ai install --agent pi`.
3. Inspect `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`.
4. Let `gentle-engram` publish a newer version, run `gentle-ai install --agent pi` again, and
   inspect the file: the pinned entry now carries the new version.
5. Try to clean up with `pi remove npm:gentle-engram@<version>` — both entries disappear.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

`gentle-ai install --agent pi` declares `npm:gentle-engram` **without a version**, matching the
unpinned form the binary already embeds and the `@latest` policy it uses to execute
`pi-engram init`. One entry per package.

If a pin is intentional, it should **replace** the unpinned entry rather than sit beside it, so
the file never carries two declarations of the same package — and the choice should survive
re-install rather than being re-derived from the currently installed version each time.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The install adds a second, version-pinned entry next to the unpinned one. The pin tracks whatever
version happens to be installed at that moment, so it changes on every install that updates the
package. Removing it with Pi's own CLI removes the good entry too, so the only workaround is
hand-editing `settings.json` after every install.

### Gentle AI Version

gentle-ai 2.7.0

### Operating System

Windows 11

### AI Agent / Client

Pi (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 0.85.1)

### 📋 Affected Area

Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
# gentle-ai install --agent pi — run 1 (pre-existing pin kept)
Pi agent dir: ~/.pi/agent
Kept npm:pi-mcp-adapter in settings.json
Kept npm:gentle-engram@0.1.11 in settings.json
Kept existing Engram MCP server in mcp.json

# gentle-ai install --agent pi — run 2, after gentle-engram updated 0.1.11 -> 0.1.12
Installing npm:gentle-engram...   changed 1 package
Pi agent dir: ~/.pi/agent
Kept npm:pi-mcp-adapter in settings.json
Added npm:gentle-engram@0.1.12 in settings.json
Verification checks: 5 passed, 0 failed, 0 warnings, 0 skipped

# resulting diff of ~/.pi/agent/settings.json across run 2
 1a2
 >   "lastChangelogVersion": "0.84.4",
 10c11
 <     "npm:gentle-engram@0.1.11",
 ---
 >     "npm:gentle-engram@0.1.12",

# final state — two entries, one package, both resolving to the same directory
$ pi list
  npm:gentle-engram          ~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/gentle-engram
  npm:gentle-engram@0.1.12   ~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/gentle-engram
```

Possibly related, different mechanism and already closed: #4188 (`sync` registering Engram twice
for Claude Code via `mcpServers`). This one is the Pi package-declaration path and still reproduces
on 2.7.0.

The selected assignments are persisted to `state.json`, and the sync generates matching agent entries in `opencode.json`. After restart, Configure OpenCode Models and OpenCode both show the selected values.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
Sync runs and rewrites `opencode.json`, but `state.json` retains the previous assignments. The generated agent configuration therefore returns to the old values after sync and restart.

### Gentle AI Version
2.7.0

### Operating System
Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

OpenCode

TUI (terminal UI)
