title: bug(review): review status initializes a Git repository in a non-repository cwd
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

`gentle-ai review status` mutates a directory that is not a Git repository by initializing a new repository in it. This can happen indirectly during Pi startup because `gentle-pi` calls negotiated review status from its `session_start` handler.

A status query is expected to be read-only. Instead, the native process launches `git init --quiet`, creating `<cwd>/.git` without an explicit bootstrap command or user confirmation. In a directory used only as a container for several independent repositories, this silently creates an unintended parent repository and changes Git discovery and workspace scope.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Start with review mode enabled and create a temporary directory that is not inside a Git worktree.
2. Run the negotiated status command against that directory:

   ```shell
   tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
   gentle-ai review status \
     --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 \
     --cwd "$tmp" \
     --projection workspace \
     --agent pi \
     --next-transition
   ```

3. Inspect the directory:

   ```shell
   test ! -e "$tmp/.git"
   ```

4. The assertion fails because status created `$tmp/.git`.

The same behavior is reached when Pi starts in the non-Git directory with `gentle-pi` enabled. An equivalent Pi launch with `--no-extensions` does not create `.git`.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

`review status` should remain read-only. For a cwd outside a Git repository, it should return a typed non-repository/unsupported outcome without creating files or invoking `git init`.

If bootstrapping an unversioned workspace is supported, it should require an explicit mutating command and user intent rather than occur as a side effect of a startup status check.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The status process launches:

```shell
git --no-replace-objects -C <cwd> init --quiet
```

This creates `<cwd>/.git` and turns the containing directory into an unintended parent repository.

### Gentle AI Version

v2.7.0

### Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
execve("<gentle-ai-binary>", ["gentle-ai", "review", "status", "--contract", "gentle-ai.review-integration/v2", "--cwd", "<empty-directory>", "--projection", "workspace", "--agent", "pi", "--next-transition"], ...) = 0
execve("/usr/bin/git", ["git", "--no-replace-objects", "-C", "<empty-directory>", "init", "--quiet"], ...) = 0
mkdir("<empty-directory>/.git", 0777) = 0
```

### Additional Context

The causal chain was captured with a bounded `strace` reproduction in an isolated temporary directory:

```text
Pi -> gentle-pi session_start -> gentle-ai review status -> git init -> mkdir(<cwd>/.git)
```

Versions in the reproduced host path were `gentle-pi` 2.5.0 and Pi 0.85.1.

A control using the same Pi binary with `--no-extensions` neither executed Git nor created `.git`, isolating the trigger to the extension path rather than Pi core.

Related issue #3880 requested a way to bootstrap an unversioned workspace. This report concerns bootstrap occurring implicitly inside a read-only `status` operation during host startup. Explicit greenfield initialization can remain supported without allowing passive status discovery to mutate the cwd.

title: feat(skills): branch-pr needs a repo-detection gate before enforcing Gentle AI's own governance elsewhere
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Problem Statement

The `branch-pr` skill's own "When to Use" section says to use it for "creating a pull request for any change" / "any project" — it's clearly intended to be installed as a personal skill across projects, not scoped to this repo. But its body hardcodes Gentle AI's own governance (the `status:approved` issue gate, `type:*` labels, the shellcheck requirement, the strict branch/commit regexes) with no check for which repo it's actually running in. When invoked in an unrelated project — say, a Laravel app with its own `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, its own git workflow (documented in that project's own CLAUDE.md), and none of Gentle AI's labels or CI checks — the agent tries to impose Gentle AI's specific rules there instead of that project's real conventions. This isn't user error; it's exactly the skill's advertised install-anywhere use case breaking.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Add a repo-detection gate at the very top of the skill, before any other rule: check `git remote get-url origin` against `Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai`. If it matches, apply the skill exactly as written today — no behavior change for this repo. If it doesn't, fall back to reading that project's own conventions instead of enforcing Gentle AI's specific mechanics: use its own `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` if one exists, only touch labels discovered via `gh label list` (never invent a `type:*` label the project doesn't have), and follow that project's own documented git workflow (base branch, reviewer policy) instead of the branch-name/commit regexes below. Universal good practice (conventional-style commits, linking a related issue when one exists) can stay as a soft default, just not a hard gate outside this repo.

I patched a local copy with exactly this gate as a stopgap (happy to share as a reference diff if useful) — but a local patch gets silently overwritten on the next `gentle-ai sync`, so flagging it here for the maintainers to decide how to fold it in properly.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

Splitting into two skills (a Gentle-AI-specific one plus a generic `branch-pr` for other projects) — rejected as more maintenance surface for what's really one conditional check.

### 📎 Additional Context

_No response_

title: Windows: nested Gentle AI Git launch can show a console window during gentle-pi use
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

On Windows, a visible console window was observed while using gentle-pi normally. The user did not invoke a Gentle AI command directly. Procmon associated the popup with `conhost.exe` descended from a package-local Gentle AI Git invocation triggered during the interaction.

The current Windows Git launcher sets `CreationFlags: windows.CREATE_SUSPENDED` in `internal/reviewtransaction/git_process_windows.go`; it does not include `windows.CREATE_NO_WINDOW`.

This report is limited to the Gentle AI nested-Git route. It does not claim that gentle-pi itself was changed or proven causal.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. On Windows, run Pi `0.85.1` with official Gentle AI `2.7.0` and Engram `1.20.0`.
2. Use gentle-pi normally and send the first message.
3. Observe the visible console window.
4. Capture process creation with Procmon filtered to `Operation is Process Create`.

This describes one recorded run, not a measured reproduction rate. Personal paths and transient process IDs are redacted.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Using gentle-pi should not cause Gentle AI's nested Git process to create a visible Windows console window.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

A visible console window was observed. The redacted Procmon chain was:

```text
Pi node.exe
└─ package-local gentle-ai.exe 2.7.0 review mode status --cwd <workspace>
   └─ git.exe --no-replace-objects -C <workspace> rev-parse --show-toplevel
      └─ conhost.exe
```

This associates the captured popup with a console host descended from Gentle AI's nested Git launch. It does not establish universal causality.

### Gentle AI Version

`2.7.0`

Official baseline artifact SHA-256:
`4b1ef51a96412a0e3f5d49c5417389a646034d328a3122f06a5a271ef5396073`

### Operating System

Windows

### AI Agent / Client

Other — Pi / gentle-pi. Pi version: `0.85.1`.

The exact installed gentle-pi package version used in the recorded run was not retained.

### 📋 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
No application error output was retained.

Procmon filter: Operation is Process Create

Pi node.exe
└─ package-local gentle-ai.exe 2.7.0 review mode status --cwd <workspace>
   └─ git.exe --no-replace-objects -C <workspace> rev-parse --show-toplevel
      └─ conhost.exe
```

### Additional Context

#### Recorded comparison

These are three single runs, not a statistical study:

| Engram runtime | Gentle AI state | Startup window | First-message window |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Engram `1.20.0` | Gentle AI `2.7.0` official baseline | Observed | Observed |
| Engram `1.20.0` | Experimental Gentle AI `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` build | Observed | Not observed |
| Engram RC10 (`v2.0.0-rc.10`) | Experimental Gentle AI build | Not observed | Not observed |

“Not observed” applies only to each recorded run and does not prove a universal fix.

#### Focused local experiment

A temporary one-line experiment in `gentle-ai/internal/reviewtransaction/git_process_windows.go` changed:

```go
windows.CREATE_SUSPENDED
```

to:

```go
windows.CREATE_SUSPENDED | windows.CREATE_NO_WINDOW
```

The focused test passed, but the exact test command and test name were not retained. The source change was restored afterward and no Gentle AI patch was committed.

Experimental artifact SHA-256:
`565e7d3a28fc0da1c8e940cde32636988ae9a19d02282e8fd32ede209b111cce`

#### Separate Engram route

Engram RC10 contains the fixes for the separate Engram startup/subprocess route:

- [Engram issue #599](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/599) and [PR #604](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/604)
- [Engram issue #641](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues/641) and [PR #643](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/643)

[Gentle AI #543](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/543) describes Pi opening CMD windows while querying Engram. That Engram route is resolved in RC10 and is not the nested Gentle AI Git route reported here.

[Gentle AI #197](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/197) is an older Cursor-specific report and is not treated as the same incident.

#### Evidence limitations

- Windows edition, build number, and architecture were not retained.
- The exact installed gentle-pi package version was not retained.
- The exact first-message input and repeatable reproduction rate were not retained.
- Procmon screenshots and PML remain private because they contain sensitive local metadata.
- The exact focused-test command and test name were not retained.

body:

### 📝 Bug Description
On Gentle AI 2.7.0 with OpenCode 1.18.29, the parent orchestrator can load installed skills under `<opencode-config>/skills/.../SKILL.md`, but delegated Task agents receive a permission denial for the same required skill files. This blocks canonical workflows because workers must load their contracts before starting, while the parent is not allowed to bypass that gate.

1. Install Gentle AI skills for OpenCode.
2. From a parent OpenCode session, verify that the required global skills load successfully.
3. Delegate a Task to a specialized agent such as `general-sol` or `explore`, and require it to read two installed `SKILL.md` contracts before repository work.
4. Observe that the delegated agent reports a tool-permission denial and stops before reading files, changing code, or running tests.

### ✅ Expected Behavior
A delegated agent can read installed global skill contracts that the parent is permitted to load. If the provider cannot grant that access, it should return a native, actionable recovery path before the workflow starts.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
The delegated agent cannot read the exact required skill paths even though the parent can load them. The workflow stops before any implementation or verification, and retrying with another delegated profile reproduces the same denial.

2.7.0

### Operating System
Linux (Other)

OpenCode

Other

<opencode-config>/skills/<required-skill>/SKILL.md

title: bug(gga): Codex provider asks for review mode instead of returning strict status
body:
## Automated provider-defect report

### Observed evidence

- Gentle AI: `2.4.0`
- Gentleman Guardian Angel: `2.10.1`
- Codex CLI: `0.153.4`
- Platform: macOS arm64
- Operation shape: strict pre-commit review of a staged TypeScript candidate using the Codex provider
- Bounded attempts: one occurrence of this response shape
- Mutation outcome: the commit was blocked; the staged candidate remained preserved

The Codex provider returned this interaction request instead of the required verdict:

```text
Which review should I run: Bugbot (correctness and coding standards) or Security Review (security-focused)?
```

GGA then rejected the output because it contained no unambiguous `STATUS: PASSED` or `STATUS: FAILED` line in the strict parsing window.

### Expected behavior

The GGA Codex provider should execute the configured review contract and return exactly one machine-readable strict status without asking the pre-commit caller to select a different review workflow.

### Actual behavior

The provider interpreted the review request as an interactive choice between two review modes. Strict mode correctly failed closed, but a verified candidate could not be committed.

### Minimal reproduction shape

1. Configure GGA `2.10.1` with the Codex provider and strict mode.
2. Stage a non-trivial TypeScript candidate.
3. Run the normal pre-commit GGA review.
4. Observe the provider ask which review mode to run instead of emitting the strict status contract.
5. Observe the commit abort while the staged candidate remains intact.

### Scope and classification

This differs from the already-closed strict-parser reports where a valid status existed later in provider output. In this occurrence, the provider's final message contained no status at all; it returned an interactive review-selection prompt.

No credentials, source content, repository names, private project names, usernames, hostnames, absolute paths, raw arguments, diffs, or environment values are included.

title: bug(review): Codex Desktop sandbox blocks RDD owner validation
body:
## Summary
On native Windows Codex Desktop, RAR rejects an ordinary Git common directory owned by the interactive user because Codex executes commands under a distinct Windows sandbox principal.

## Reproduction
1. Use Codex Desktop on native Windows with a normal local Git repository.
2. Confirm the Git common directory is an ordinary directory owned by the interactive user and is not a reparse point.
3. From Codex Desktop, run:

   gentle-ai review mode status --cwd <repo>

4. Observe that RDD mode is projected, then the command exits non-zero with an unsafe RAR authority-path ownership rejection.

## Expected
A supported Codex Desktop sandbox should have a secure RDD path, such as an authenticated owner-context broker or a typed client-sandbox diagnostic with actionable guidance.

It must retain fail-closed ownership, ACL, filesystem, and reparse-point validation. It must not require changing Git metadata ownership to the sandbox identity.

## Actual
RAR compares Git metadata ownership with the sandbox process identity, so RDD commands are blocked before lifecycle execution.

## Impact
RDD cannot be used from Codex Desktop for an otherwise normal user-owned repository.

## Related issues reviewed
- #1918: unsupported filesystem ownership semantics; not equivalent.
- #4048: local NTFS classification; not equivalent.
- #3416: authority directory unsafe after repair despite current-process ownership; not equivalent.

## Privacy
No repository path, account name, hostname, SID, credential, source content, or environment value is included.

title: bug(review): START still exhausts the 120s deadline on a 16-path candidate when the worktree is on a high-latency filesystem (2.7.0 stable)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I searched open and closed issues for an equivalent report. The closest is #1778 (START timing out on valid large workspaces), closed on 2026-07-29 with "Current review START uses the expanded 120-second deadline with deterministic coverage". That fix is in my build and the deadline is demonstrably active (see timings), yet START still exhausts it. Its closing comment explicitly left the underlying per-path subprocess amplification alive, and the trackers for that class (#1957, #1963, #1965) are all closed. #3314 and #4208 are `pre_native` STATUS failures, not `native_running` START. Detailed comparison below.
- [x] This automated provider-defect report contains privacy-scrubbed diagnostics only.

### Bug Description

Negotiated `review start` exhausts its aggregate time budget in `native_running` on a **small** candidate (16 paths, +196/−14) when the worktree sits on a **high-latency filesystem**. Two consecutive attempts failed at ~111 s, consistent with the 120 s START deadline from #1778 being active and still insufficient.

The distinguishing factor against every prior report in this class is the trigger: not candidate size, not workspace size alone, but **per-operation I/O latency**. The process spends essentially no CPU and all of its time in system calls, which matches the per-path subprocess amplification described in #1778's closing discussion (reported there as ~15k subprocesses for a single START). On a filesystem where each subprocess costs milliseconds instead of microseconds, the expanded deadline is consumed by fork/stat overhead alone.

This reports observed evidence only; root cause is unconfirmed.

### Environment

- Gentle AI: `2.7.0` (stable channel; build string carries no prerelease tag)
- Client: Claude Code (agent binding `claude-code`)
- OS/architecture: Linux x86_64 (WSL2)
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`
- Receipt-driven development: on (global)
- Candidate: `kind: base-diff`, `projection: workspace`, `committed-only`, 16 paths, +196/−14
- Workspace: TypeScript monorepo, ~7,120 tracked files in the checkout
- Filesystem: worktree on a 9p mount (WSL2 drive mount). An ext4 mount is available on the same machine for contrast but was not yet used for a comparison run.
- Review authority store: empty before the first attempt (`lineages: 0`, `events: 0`, `bytes: 0`)

### Operation Shape

```text
# Step 1 — preflight, succeeded in 5.8s, returned fresh_target_ready
gentle-ai review status --cwd <worktree> \
  --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --agent claude-code \
  --base-ref <merge-base> --committed-only --next-transition

# Step 2 — the exact START it emitted; failed at ~111s, twice
gentle-ai review start --cwd=<worktree> \
  --contract=gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --target=<identity> \
  --projection=workspace --base-ref=<base-tree> --committed-only=true \
  --lineage=<lineage> --agent=claude-code --consent=relay

# Step 3 — reconciliation STATUS bound to the same lineage; also timed out
gentle-ai review status --cwd <worktree> \
  --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --agent claude-code \
  --lineage <lineage> --next-transition
```

### Attempts and Outcomes

| # | Operation | Duration | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `review start` | not measured | `operation_timeout`, `phase: native_running`, `mutation_outcome: unknown` |
| 2 | `review status --lineage` | not measured | `operation_timeout`, `phase: pre_native`, `mutation_outcome: not_started`, `next_action: stop` |
| 3 | `review status` (preflight, no lineage) | **5.8 s** | success, `fresh_target_ready`, same lineage reoffered |
| 4 | `review start` (relaunched only because step 3 reoffered the same bound slot) | **111 s** (`real 1m51.020s`) | `operation_timeout`, `phase: native_running`, `mutation_outcome: unknown` |

Timing breakdown of attempt 4:

```text
real  1m51.020s
user  0m0.634s
sys   0m14.267s
```

Under 1 s of user CPU across 111 s of wall clock. The remainder is system time and I/O wait, not computation.

### Failure Envelopes

START (attempts 1 and 4, identical):

```json
{
  "schema": "gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2",
  "contract": "gentle-ai.review-integration/v2",
  "operation": "review.start",
  "phase": "native_running",
  "code": "operation_timeout",
  "message": "The negotiated review operation exceeded its aggregate time budget.",
  "mutation_outcome": "unknown",
  "authority_applicability": "not_evaluated",
  "retry_safe": false,
  "replayability": "status_required",
  "next_action": "review.status",
  "cause": "context deadline exceeded"
}
```

Lineage-bound STATUS (attempt 2):

```json
{
  "schema": "gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2",
  "operation": "review.status",
  "phase": "pre_native",
  "code": "operation_timeout",
  "mutation_outcome": "not_started",
  "authority_applicability": "not_evaluated",
  "retry_safe": false,
  "replayability": "manual_action_required",
  "next_action": "stop",
  "cause": "context deadline exceeded"
}
```

### Expected Behavior

A candidate of 16 paths and ~210 changed lines should freeze well inside the START deadline regardless of the filesystem backing the worktree. Failing that, the timeout should be classifiable and actionable: either a typed error naming I/O latency or workspace scan cost as the limiting factor, or a deadline derived from measured throughput rather than a fixed wall-clock budget.

The current behaviour is a dead end for the consumer. The preflight STATUS keeps returning `fresh_target_ready` for the same lineage, so the contract permits relaunching the same bound slot, but the relaunch reproduces the timeout. Meanwhile the lineage-bound STATUS, which is the prescribed reconciliation path after an `unknown` mutation outcome, times out as well and returns `next_action: stop` with `manual_action_required`.

### Minimal Reproduction

1. Place a Git worktree of a repository with several thousand tracked files on a high-latency filesystem (a WSL2 `/mnt/<drive>` 9p mount reproduces this; a network mount should too).
2. Produce a small committed-only candidate against a base ref (16 files is enough).
3. Run the negotiated preflight STATUS with `--base-ref <merge-base> --committed-only --next-transition`. It returns promptly with `fresh_target_ready`.
4. Execute the emitted START verbatim. Observe `operation_timeout` in `native_running` after ~111 s.
5. Run the lineage-bound STATUS. Observe `operation_timeout` in `pre_native` with `next_action: stop`.
6. Re-run the selectorless preflight. It still returns `fresh_target_ready` for the same lineage, and a relaunched START reproduces step 4.

### Why This Is Not A Duplicate

| Issue | State | Why it does not cover this |
|---|---|---|
| #1778 | closed | Same operation and same failure envelope, but its trigger is candidate size (87 paths, 165 KB diff) and it was closed by expanding the START deadline to 120 s. That deadline is active in this build and is still exhausted by a 16-path candidate, which is the regression being reported. Its closing comment left the per-path amplification cause explicitly unresolved. |
| #1957, #1963, #1965 | closed / merged | Address per-path git amplification and batching for large workspaces. All predate this build, so whatever they fixed is present here. |
| #3314 | closed | STATUS with `--base-ref --committed-only` timing out in `pre_native`. Matches only the secondary symptom (attempt 2); the primary failure here is START in `native_running`. |
| #4208 | open | Selectorless preflight STATUS timing out in `pre_native` on its first call. Does not match: the selectorless preflight here succeeds in 5.8 s and does so repeatedly. |
| #3260, #3733, #3871 | open / closed | Require an existing lineage, a prior capture, or a rejected capture. The authority store here was empty before the first attempt. |

### Additional Note

A comparison run with the same repository on an ext4 mount on the same machine would isolate filesystem latency as the trigger. Happy to add that measurement as a follow-up comment if useful.

title: bug(review): in-process claude-code refuter returns tool-use narration with no JSON object, so capture-refuter is unadmittable and the lineage escalates (2.6.0)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues), including open and closed results, and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

Automated provider defect report. Observed behavior only; no root cause is asserted.

On `2.6.0` (stable channel — build string carries no `-rc.` or `-main.` tag), a compact-v2 review on the `claude-code` runtime that reaches `provider_refuter_required` cannot complete. The exact provider-issued `review capture-refuter --agent=claude-code --execute=true` runs the in-process refuter, and native admission rejects its payload because it contains **no JSON object at all**. The lineage then closes as `escalated` and STATUS returns the terminal `stop` / `native_stop_required`.

The rejected payload preserved under `rejected-results/<lineage>/refuter-1-*.json` shows what the refuter returned: 224 bytes of prose narrating an inspection it intended to perform, never a verdict. Its three paragraphs begin "I'll inspect the candidate snapshot to determine whether …", "I need to check the working directory for the hook definition." and "Let me examine the available files." Admission reason recorded verbatim: `refuter provider result admission incomplete: reviewer payload contains no complete JSON object: no object start was found in 224 bytes`.

This is the second occurrence on the same build in two days (first on 2026-09-09, a different lineage and candidate, same observable payload shape: tool-use narration instead of JSON).

**Relationship to the closest existing issues** (searched, open and closed):

- **#4386** (open) — same causal class on the same runtime, different role and contract: the *targeted validator* emits its `inspect-candidate` command as prose, so `capture-validation` is unadmittable. Here it is the *provider refuter* and `capture-refuter`; the payload is narration of an intended inspection rather than a rendered command.
- **#4422** (open) — same affected contract (refuter admission), different payload shape and runtime: a *truncated* JSON object on the Pi host relay. Here there is no object start at all, on `claude-code`.
- **#3482** (closed 2026-08-31, reported on 2.4.0) — compiled `claude-code` refuter batch could only return `inconclusive` and always escalated. Here the refuter does not return an `inconclusive` verdict; it returns no verdict.
- **#4226** (closed) — inconclusive refuter verdict escalates to a terminal stop and STATUS names no cause. That is the precondition of the resulting state here, not the defect being reported; STATUS after escalation still exposes no findings and no cause.
- **#4433** (open, 2.7.0) — escalated terminal lineage has no sanctioned exit. Not yet exercised for this lineage; noted because it is the state this defect leaves behind.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. With RDD enabled, drive a negotiated v2 `workspace` review to `reviewing` on a medium-risk candidate (2 changed files, 40 changed lines, one selected lens `review-reliability`) via the exact provider-issued START (`--consent=relay` → consent/v3 → `granted` invocation).
2. Run the exact bound `review.capture-result` for the lens (`--agent=claude-code`, no `--input`). The reviewer returns 1 `CRITICAL` with `evidence_class: inferential` and `causal_disposition: introduced`, plus 5 `WARNING`; admission accepts it.
3. Bound STATUS returns `collect` / `provider_refuter_required` with one `review.capture-refuter` input carrying `--agent=claude-code --execute=true`.
4. Run that exact capture verbatim.

### ✅ Expected

The refuter adjudicates the inferential finding against the frozen immutable trees and returns an admissible JSON verdict (`refuted` / `upheld` / `inconclusive`), or a typed recoverable result that re-offers the bound slot.

### ❌ Actual

`capture-refuter` returns `state: escalated`, action `review completed with inconclusive severe findings; maintainer action is informational`. The rejected payload is prose with no JSON object. Bound STATUS afterwards: `action: stop`, authority `state: escalated`, forecast `terminal` / `native_stop_required`, `candidates: []`, no findings and no cause surfaced. The reviewer's findings are only readable from the transaction's `review-state.json` under the git common dir.

### 🧾 Observed evidence

- Gentle AI version: `2.6.0` (stable). Latest published stable at report time: `2.7.0` (2026-09-08); #4386 and #4422 report the neighbouring defects on 2.7.0, so no published release is known to contain a fix for this class.
- OS/arch: `Darwin arm64`
- Client: Claude Code `2.1.267`
- Agent contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, agent binding `claude-code`, projection `workspace`
- Lineage: `review-17bad7d1551ab678` · target identity `sha256:7cf49b9ca66c11e673f911e53a9093609b17f5e5e88a20ab7f73ea0d709f1494`
- Refuter attempt: 1, captured at `2026-09-10T13:38:06Z`, raw payload sha256 `a1e2338b0ac64390de66957bffc599ae83cf12992f5a02421b19ef4a32083315`, 224 bytes
- Prior occurrence: 2026-09-09, lineage `review-51dd967b…`, same build, same payload shape (tool-use narration, no JSON). Exit used then: new candidate, new lineage.
- Bounded attempts: one capture-refuter, no retry (STATUS did not reoffer the slot).

### 🔒 Preserved state

No source change, reset, push, delivery action or `review mode` change was made as part of this failure. The candidate stays staged and uncommitted on its branch; the lineage remains `escalated` in the store. The reviewer's one `CRITICAL` was inspected manually and is contradicted by a module outside the candidate scope, which is exactly what the refuter was needed to adjudicate.

title: Regular (non-fullscreen) TUI: viewport jumps to the top when output updates while scrolled up
body:
## Summary

In the **regular** (non-fullscreen) TUI, the viewport jumps back to the top when new output arrives
while the user has scrolled up to read earlier content.

## Environment

- `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`: **0.85.1**
- `@earendil-works/pi-tui`: **0.85.1**
- macOS, stock Terminal, `tuiMode` unset (regular mode)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start a turn that keeps producing output (any long agent run).
2. Scroll up to read earlier output.
3. Wait for the next output update.

## Expected

The viewport stays where the user scrolled to. Reading history should not be interrupted by new output.

## Actual

On the next output update the viewport jumps to the top of the transcript, so the text the user was
reading disappears. Reproducible consistently while an agent is streaming.

## Notes and workaround

- The problem does **not** appear in `fullscreen` / alt-screen mode: that pane owns its own scroll
  offset and exposes `tui.altScreen.*` navigation keys (`pageUp`, `pageDown`, `lineUp`, `lineDown`,
  jump to latest).
- Workaround for users hitting this: set `"tuiMode": "fullscreen"` in `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`.
- The cause appears to be in the client's regular-mode renderer rather than in this repository, but it
  is reported here because that is where the reporter was asked to file it.

## Suggestion

In regular mode, avoid resetting the viewport when the user has scrolled away from the bottom: only
auto-follow while the user is already at the bottom (sticky-bottom behaviour), and otherwise leave the
viewport untouched.

title: feat: add reusable model configuration profiles with quick switching
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

TUI (terminal UI)

### 💡 Problem Statement

Gentle AI is gaining support for configuring models across Pi agents and SDD phases, but users still lack a first-class way to define and switch between complete model configurations.

Related work such as #3522 (editing Pi agent models), #4397 (subscription-oriented presets), and #838 (per-phase SDD model configuration) addresses important parts of the problem. However, these efforts do not provide reusable, named profiles that capture the full routing matrix and can be activated as a unit.

Today, a user who wants to switch between setups such as "Quality", "Balanced", and "Budget" must revisit agents and phases individually or manually coordinate several configuration surfaces. This is slow, error-prone, and makes it difficult to keep a consistent model strategy across SDD phases, reviewers, executors, and Judgment Day agents.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Add first-class, reusable model configuration profiles for supported agent runtimes, starting with Pi where the need is especially visible.

A profile should be a named configuration that can define, for each supported agent or workflow phase:

- Provider and model ID.
- Reasoning/thinking effort when supported.
- Inheritance or fallback behavior where an explicit assignment is not needed.

The user should be able to:

- Create, rename, duplicate, edit, and delete profiles.
- Select a profile and activate it with one action instead of editing agents one by one.
- See a preview or summary of the assignments before applying it.
- Preserve existing assignments and unrelated configuration when profiles are edited or switched.
- Validate unavailable models and unsupported effort levels before activation, with actionable errors.
- Use a canonical, runtime-compatible persistence format so profiles do not create competing sources of truth.
- Keep a safe default profile and make switching reversible.

The design should build on and integrate with the related per-agent, per-phase, and subscription-preset work rather than replacing it. A preset can be treated as a profile template, while advanced users can customize every agent/phase assignment before saving.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Users can create and persist multiple named model configuration profiles.
- [ ] A profile can contain model and supported effort assignments for each configurable agent and/or workflow phase.
- [ ] Users can activate a complete profile in one action and switch back to another profile without manually editing each assignment.
- [ ] The UI shows the active profile and provides a clear assignment preview before activation.
- [ ] Profiles support inheritance/fallback and do not require every role to have an explicit model.
- [ ] Invalid or unavailable model assignments are detected before activation and reported clearly.
- [ ] Switching profiles preserves unrelated runtime configuration and does not silently discard user-managed fields.
- [ ] Existing per-agent/per-phase configuration flows and native runtime selectors remain compatible.
- [ ] Focused tests cover profile persistence, activation, switching, validation, inheritance, cancellation, and preservation behavior.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

**Continue editing every agent or phase individually.** Rejected because it is repetitive, error-prone, and makes common quality/cost switches impractical.

**Provide only fixed subscription presets.** Useful as a starting point, but insufficient for users who need custom model assignments or different strategies per workflow phase.

**Maintain separate configuration files for each runtime.** Rejected unless the format remains canonical and runtime-compatible; otherwise it would introduce drift and competing sources of truth.

### 📎 Additional Context

This issue intentionally goes one step beyond the related open work:

- #3522 provides a central TUI editor for Pi's per-agent assignments.
- #4397 proposes subscription-based Pi presets.
- #838 tracks per-phase model configuration for the SDD orchestrator.

The requested feature should provide the profile layer that composes these capabilities into reusable configurations, while preserving their individual editing and synchronization behavior. The implementation can be phased: shared profile data model and persistence first, then activation/switching, followed by TUI management and integration with existing presets.

title: bug(pi): resumed general worker loops terminal activity and returns no result
body:
## Summary

A foreground Pi workflow using the package-owned `gentle-ai-worker` repeatedly entered a terminal loop when `subagent_continue` resumed a completed worker after a bounded scope response. The continuation returned no usable result until the human stopped it.

## Environment

- Client: Pi 0.85.1
- Gentle AI: 2.7.0
- Mirrored provider bundle: 1.2.0
- OS/architecture: Windows x64
- Node.js: 24.11.1
- pnpm: 11.19.0

## Operation shape

- Foreground package-owned worker; no background workers or parallel writers.
- The worker first returned a bounded partial or `interaction_required` result.
- The host sent exactly one continuation with narrow repository-relative edit surfaces and explicit instructions to avoid concurrent commands and polling.
- No raw command arguments, source contents, or candidate diff are included here.

## Attempts and outcomes

1. A continuation resumed a completed partial worker. The tool returned `No result provided`; the human stopped a terminal loop.
2. After confirming no worker remained, a fresh bounded worker returned `interaction_required` for one missing allowed schema path. The host supplied that one parent-derived path through a single continuation. The tool again returned `No result provided`; the human stopped the recurring terminal loop.

## Minimal reproduction

1. Start one foreground package-owned `gentle-ai-worker` against an existing Git worktree.
2. Let the worker finish with a bounded partial or `interaction_required` result.
3. Call `subagent_continue` exactly once for that completed task, with a narrow continuation and valid allowed edit surfaces.
4. Observe repeated terminal activity without a usable terminal result until the human stops execution.

## Expected behavior

The continuation should execute once and return one bounded completed, partial, blocked, or failed result. It should not repeatedly open or recycle terminal activity.

## Actual behavior

The continuation produced no usable result (`No result provided`) and terminal activity repeated until manual intervention. The symptom reproduced twice through two independently bounded continuation attempts.

## Mutation and preserved-state evidence

- The failed continuation attempts made no observed source mutation.
- The pre-existing partial candidate remained preserved.
- After each manual stop, the host found no active subagent task.
- No commit, push, migration, dependency installation, or destructive Git action occurred.

## Impact

The consumer workflow cannot safely resume the bounded writer and must preserve state rather than retry indefinitely. Root cause is unknown; this report describes observed behavior only.

title: docs: quickstart and trigger-rules still name v2.6.0 as the current stable release (2.7.0)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

`docs/` still names **`v2.6.0`** as the current stable release, but `v2.7.0` has been the `Latest` (non-prerelease) release since 2026-09-08. `README.md` was already updated to `v2.7.0`; the files under `docs/` were not, so the repository now contradicts itself about which version `@latest` installs.

Five occurrences across three files still assert the old stable channel:

| File | Line | Current text |
|------|------|--------------|
| `docs/quickstart.md` | 54 | ``# Stable channel (`@latest`, currently v2.6.0)`` |
| `docs/quickstart.md` | 65 | ``The current stable release is [`v2.6.0`](...)`` |
| `docs/trigger-rules.md` | 87 | ``In stable [`v2.6.0`](...) and unreleased `main`...`` |
| `docs/testing/organic-rdd-testing-guide.md` | 7 | ``...not current guidance for stable [`v2.6.0`](...)`` |
| `docs/testing/organic-rdd-testing-guide.md` | 668 | ``...first reproduce it against stable [`v2.6.0`](...)`` |

The remaining `v2.x` references under `docs/` are historical (audits, ledgers, closure reports) and are correct as written — they must stay pinned. Only the five above assert the *current* channel.

This is a recurring class rather than a one-off: #2836, #3213, and #3424 were the same defect at earlier version boundaries, each fixed by hand for that release only.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Confirm the current stable release: `gh release view -R Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai --json tagName,isPrerelease` → `v2.7.0`, `isPrerelease: false`.
2. Open `docs/quickstart.md` at the [Version policy](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/main/docs/quickstart.md) section on `main`.
3. Compare it with the stable version stated in `README.md` on the same commit.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Documentation that asserts the current stable channel names the release that `@latest` actually resolves to — `v2.7.0` — and stays consistent with `README.md` on the same commit.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

`docs/` states that the current stable release is `v2.6.0` and that `@latest` tracks it, while `README.md` on the same commit states `v2.7.0` and `@latest` resolves to `v2.7.0`. A reader following the Quickstart version policy is told to expect a version one minor behind what they receive.

### Gentle AI Version

2.7.0

### Operating System

macOS

### AI Agent / Client

Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area

Documentation

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
$ gentle-ai --version
gentle-ai 2.7.0

$ gh release view -R Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai --json tagName,isPrerelease
{"isPrerelease":false,"tagName":"v2.7.0"}

$ rg -n 'currently v2|current stable release is|In stable \[|against stable \[' docs/ README.md
README.md:454:> **In stable `v2.7.0`, a review does not end when it is approved.**
docs/quickstart.md:54:# Stable channel (`@latest`, currently v2.6.0)
docs/quickstart.md:65:The current stable release is [`v2.6.0`](...)
docs/trigger-rules.md:87:In stable [`v2.6.0`](...) and unreleased `main`
docs/testing/organic-rdd-testing-guide.md:7:...stable [`v2.6.0`](...)
docs/testing/organic-rdd-testing-guide.md:668:...against stable [`v2.6.0`](...)
```

### Additional Context

The fix is a five-line documentation bump and is ready to submit as a PR once this issue carries `status:approved`.

Worth noting for triage, though intentionally **out of scope** for that PR: nothing in CI verifies that these five assertions still hold after a release, which is why the same defect has now recurred at four version boundaries. A follow-up could mark the current-channel occurrences and check them against a single source of truth, leaving the historical references untouched. Happy to open that as a separate issue if it is wanted.

title: feat(review): stop-hook criterion should be task completion, not turn-end, to avoid reviewing stale in-progress candidates
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Problem Statement

With receipt-driven development enabled, the Claude Code `Stop` hook (`gentle-ai review stop-hook`, introduced in #4064) reminds the agent whenever the repository holds an unreviewed candidate at the end of a turn. That criterion is "a turn ended and a diff exists," not "the requested work is finished."

During a multi-step implementation spanning several assistant turns, each additional edit produces a new target identity. The hook fires its reminder at the end of every turn where that target is unreviewed, so the agent (following the contract, as it's supposed to) opens the STATUS → START preflight against a still-in-progress, partial diff. By the time the agent keeps editing in the next turn, that reviewed candidate is already stale — the review effort is spent on a snapshot of unfinished work rather than on the actual deliverable.

Observed on a private local repository, CLI Claude Code session, receipt-driven development enabled (`global: on`), `gentle-ai 2.7.1-0.<dev pseudo-version>`, during a multi-turn implementation task: the reminder fired repeatedly across turns before the task was complete, each time against a candidate that a later turn immediately superseded.

This is not a violation of the hook's documented contract (it does exactly what #4064 specified: reminds once per session and target identity, at turn end). The gap is that "unreviewed candidate exists" and "the requested work is finished" are being treated as the same signal, and they aren't.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Give the hook (or the STATUS/START contract behind it) a way to gate on completion instead of merely on turn-end + unreviewed-diff. Some directions, not prescriptive:

- Let the agent declare intent explicitly (e.g., a marker the agent writes only when it considers the current request fully implemented) and have the hook check that marker before nudging.
- Defer the reminder while there is open SDD task state (e.g., an active change under `openspec/changes/` with unchecked tasks) and only nudge once that state closes.
- Debounce reminders across a run of consecutive turns that keep touching the same file(s)/task, so only the turn where no further pending work is detected triggers the nudge, instead of every turn that happens to end with a diff present.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

Relying on agent-side instructions ("finish the whole task before running the preflight, ignore the hook until then") to filter out premature nudges. This is the status quo, and it doesn't work reliably: the hook fires unconditionally on every Stop with an unreviewed target identity, so it depends entirely on the agent choosing to disregard a reminder that is, per its own text, framed as something to act on before reporting completion.

### 📎 Additional Context

- AI Agent / Client: Claude Code, used via CLI.
- Related: #4064 (introduced the Stop hook; established the current "once per session + target identity, at turn end" criterion). #4390 (different bug: the hook re-reminds for a candidate already acknowledged and burned earlier in the same session). This report is about firing cadence relative to task completion, not about re-firing on an unchanged candidate.

title: bug(opencode): transport rejects a complete provider-issued binding after rematerializing its artifact subject
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description
An existing review lineage in `reviewing` can recover a `review-reliability` collect transition through lineage-scoped STATUS, but OpenCode rejects the provider-issued binding before launching the reviewer.

The collect input contains all seven binding values: `lineage`, `target`, `lens`, `order`, `revision`, `repository_context`, and `subject_hash`. The Task copies all seven values literally, and the OpenCode plugin forwards the prompt unchanged.

The provider-issued subject uses schema `gentle-ai.review-artifact-subject/v1`, whose hash is based on the candidate diff and changed-path manifest. During initial transport validation, OpenCode rematerializes the subject through `NewArtifactSubject`, producing the v2 tree-based representation, and compares the hashes before canonical binding. This rejects the unchanged provider-issued v1 hash.

Compatibility handling exists later in result admission, but it is not applied to this initial transport comparison.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce
1. Have an existing review lineage in `reviewing` with an outstanding `review-reliability` result.
2. Request lineage-scoped negotiated STATUS and obtain its `collect` transition.
3. Verify that the provider-owned collect input contains `lineage`, `target`, `lens`, `order`, `revision`, `repository_context`, and `subject_hash`.
4. Launch the OpenCode reviewer Task using those seven values literally.
5. Observe that the OpenCode plugin forwards the prompt unchanged.
6. Observe that transport validation rejects the binding before the reviewer runs.

### ✅ Expected Behavior
The OpenCode transport should accept the complete provider-issued binding and launch the requested reviewer.

If multiple artifact-subject schema generations are supported, initial transport validation should compare them using compatible canonical semantics rather than rejecting a valid provider-issued v1 subject after rematerializing it as v2.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
The Task is rejected before reviewer execution with:

`opencode_review_transport_binding_invalid: Task subject hash does not match the provider-issued artifact subject`

The candidate, index, and authority remain unchanged. No reviewer result, correction, receipt, or new lineage is produced.

### Gentle AI Version
`gentle-ai 2.6.0-local-opencode-untracked-selection`

### Operating System
Windows

### AI Agent / Client
OpenCode

### 📋 Affected Area
CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output
```shell
opencode_review_transport_binding_invalid: Task subject hash does not match the provider-issued artifact subject
```

### Additional Context
Runtime:

- Windows 10
- OpenCode 1.18.29
- Custom Gentle AI binary SHA-256: `126b7b2aea68e610b869fe71c841208b5a634897931c0be930e9390af0241b34`
- OpenCode plugin SHA-256: `486013282380d0a0ef3358f3c5ed3ad1b6ed54c4d890a04b1f89e710fc9b55e5`

The relevant causal files were verified as byte-identical or causally unchanged in official v2.7.0. However, this was not reproduced at runtime with the official v2.7.0 binary, and Linux was not tested.

Related but not duplicate: #2047, #2064, #4030, and #4293.

A full lineage-scoped STATUS artifact and the Task records are available locally, but they contain private paths and repository content. Minimal sanitized evidence is included here; fuller sanitized artifacts can be provided if maintainers request them.

title: bug(review): consent/v3 omits granted invocation for OpenCode
body:
## Automated provider-defect report

### Environment
- Gentle AI: `2.7.0` (stable channel)
- Platform: Windows
- Client: OpenCode
- Review contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`

### Operation shape
1. Selectorless negotiated STATUS returned one exact START transition for a workspace candidate.
2. The exact provider-owned START invocation was executed once with consent relay.
3. START returned a blocking `gentle-ai.review-integration.consent/v3` envelope at high risk.
4. The envelope contained an exact invocation only for the declined choice; the granted choice had a label and effect but no invocation.
5. The human selected granted once, but the client could not safely execute it without synthesizing a command.

### Expected behavior
Every selectable consent choice exposes the exact provider-owned invocation required to submit that human answer without reconstructing lifecycle tokens.

### Actual behavior
The granted choice omits its invocation. The declined choice contains one. The client therefore cannot honor a granted answer under the exact-invocation contract.

### Bounded evidence
- Candidate: workspace projection, 2 changed files, 12 changed lines, high risk
- Risk evidence: security workflow and shell-process workflow
- Consent schema: `gentle-ai.review-integration.consent/v3`
- Action: `consent_required`
- Human answer: granted, selected once but not executed
- Mutation after consent answer: none
- Candidate state: preserved

### Minimal reproduction
1. Create a high-risk workspace candidate in OpenCode.
2. Run negotiated review STATUS and execute its exact consent-relay START transition.
3. Inspect the returned consent/v3 choices.
4. Observe that declined includes an invocation while granted does not.
5. Select granted and observe that the host has no exact provider-owned invocation it can execute.

### Duplicate lookup
Open and closed issues were searched. Issue #4124 is not equivalent: it reports a missing opaque consent binding in a Pi intended-untracked flow while explicitly stating that both granted and declined invocations were present. title: feat(tui): offer the current GPT-6 Astra models in the Codex model assignment presets
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

TUI (terminal UI)

### 💡 Problem Statement

During installation, the **Codex Model Assignments** screen ("Choose the reasoning_effort tier for Codex SDD phases") only offers the previous GPT-5.6 generation. All three presets are built from `gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-5.6-terra` and `gpt-5.6-luna`:

```
( ) Low-cost   — Orquestador gpt-5.6-terra/medium · Razonamiento gpt-5.6-sol/medium  · Código gpt-5.6-terra/medium · Liviano gpt-5.6-luna/high
(*) Recommended — Orquestador gpt-5.6-sol/medium  · Razonamiento gpt-5.6-sol/medium  · Código gpt-5.6-terra/high   · Liviano gpt-5.6-luna/high
( ) Powerful   — Orquestador gpt-5.6-sol/medium  · Razonamiento gpt-5.6-sol/xhigh   · Código gpt-5.6-sol/high     · Liviano gpt-5.6-luna/high
```

The current Codex CLI has already moved to the GPT-6 Astra family. On this machine:

- `codex-cli 0.153.4`
- `~/.codex/config.toml` → `model = "gpt-6-astra"`
- `~/.gentle-ai/cache/model-variants.json` already knows the family across many providers: `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6-astra-fast`, `gpt-6-astra-pro`

So the presets install a routing that is one generation behind what Codex itself defaults to, and the user has to go through **Custom — per-phase model + effort** and retype the model for all 13 SDD phases to get the current one.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Update the Codex preset catalog so the three tiers are expressed in the GPT-6 Astra family, mapping each old role to its current equivalent, e.g.:

```
( ) Low-cost   — Orchestrator gpt-6-astra-fast · Reasoning gpt-6-astra      · Code gpt-6-astra-fast · Light gpt-6-astra-fast
(*) Recommended — Orchestrator gpt-6-astra     · Reasoning gpt-6-astra      · Code gpt-6-astra      · Light gpt-6-astra-fast
( ) Powerful   — Orchestrator gpt-6-astra      · Reasoning gpt-6-astra-pro  · Code gpt-6-astra-pro  · Light gpt-6-astra
```

(exact tiering is up to the maintainers — the point is the family, not the specific split)

Ideally the list is not hardcoded at all: `~/.gentle-ai/cache/model-variants.json` is already fetched and already contains the Astra entries, so the presets could be resolved against that cache with a static fallback, and the screen would stop going stale on every OpenAI model generation.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- **Custom — per-phase model + effort**: works, but it means typing the model and effort for all 13 SDD phases by hand on every install, just to avoid an outdated default.
- **Editing `~/.codex/config.toml` after install**: only fixes the CLI default, not the per-phase SDD routing that gentle-ai writes.

### 📎 Additional Context

Screenshot of the current screen (gentle-ai install, Codex Model Assignments):

- Header: `Codex Model Assignments`
- Subtitle: `Choose the reasoning_effort tier for Codex SDD phases (tied to your ChatGPT plan)`
- The three visible presets are the GPT-5.6 ones quoted above.

Possibly related: #3693 (automated review hook selects an unsupported Codex model for a ChatGPT account) — both come from Codex model data that no longer matches what the account/CLI actually serves.

title: feat(review): allow clone-local opt-in for receipt-driven development when global is off
body:
## Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

## 🔍 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

## 💡 Problem Statement

Currently, receipt-driven development (RDD) cannot be enabled selectively for a single repository or clone when the global switch is off or unset.

Running:
```bash
gentle-ai review mode enable --scope clone
```
outputs:
```text
receipt-driven development: off (decided by default)
  global:      unset
  clone-local: unset
  note:        a clone-local override can only disable, so this cleared the clone's off opinion and the global switch still decides; run `gentle-ai review mode enable --scope global` to turn receipt-driven development on
```

Under the current `ResolveRDDMode` precedence, the clone-local override is strictly "off-only" (`any off wins, a repository can never force on`). This creates significant friction for developers who want to experiment with or adopt RDD in a specific, isolated project without turning it on globally across every repository on their machine.

## 📦 Proposed Solution

Support an explicit opt-in at the clone scope, allowing a repository to enable RDD locally even when the global switch is `unset` or `off`.

Expected behavior:
```bash
gentle-ai review mode enable --scope clone
```
Result:
```text
receipt-driven development: on (decided by clone-local)
  global:      unset (or off)
  clone-local: on
```

Precedence could allow `clone-local: on` to govern the repository when `global` is unset or explicitly allow repository-level opt-in.

## 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- Enabling RDD globally via `gentle-ai review mode enable --scope global` and manually running `disable --scope clone` on all other existing repositories, which is invasive and error-prone.
- Forgoing RDD entirely on experimental repositories due to reluctance to enable it system-wide.

## 📎 Additional Context

Verified on `gentle-ai 2.7.0` on Windows / PowerShell.

title: bug(opencode): startup skill registry refresh mutates workspace after review freeze
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I searched existing open and closed issues and found no equivalent report of startup registry writes after review freeze.
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`.

### 📝 Bug Description

Launching the installed OpenCode runtime to run a provider-bound reviewer created two skill-registry files in the consumer workspace after native review START had frozen its candidate. The files appeared before the OpenCode session was created and before any assistant or tool execution. The next normal negotiated STATUS discovered a different workspace target instead of the original pending reviewer slots.

This report concerns the startup mutation. The same single launch also failed with a generic server error, but the evidence does **not** establish that the registry mutation caused that error.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

Observed once on the installed versions below:

1. Prepare a Git workspace where `.atl/skill-registry.md` and `.atl/.skill-registry.cache.json` are absent and would participate in workspace candidate discovery if created. Keep the managed OpenCode skill-registry startup plugin installed.
2. Through another orchestration client, follow negotiated workspace review STATUS, grant candidate-scoped consent, and execute the returned START. Retain the frozen candidate (Candidate A) and the provider-issued pending lens bindings.
3. Confirm normal unscoped STATUS discovers the reviewing lineage and pending slots. Complete the native preflight for the returned risk capture.
4. Launch the installed OpenCode runtime once in the same workspace to execute the exact bound risk task through its managed orchestrator. Allow normal plugin initialization.
5. Before any reviewer result exists, compare workspace file inventory and native candidate identity with the frozen state. Query normal unscoped negotiated STATUS again.

These are abstract reproduction steps; private paths, raw arguments, source contents, and provider configuration values are omitted.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Starting the reviewer transport for an already-frozen candidate should not create or rewrite candidate-visible workspace files as a startup side effect. Required registry preparation should complete before freeze, or the launch should leave the frozen workspace unchanged.

The original review authority, selected lenses, pending slots, and budget should remain usable. An unrelated runtime failure must not become a completed inspection or a fabricated reviewer result.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

START succeeded for Candidate A with four lenses, high risk, and a frozen correction budget of 200 lines. Risk-capture preflight also succeeded.

During the single OpenCode launch, two previously absent files appeared:

| Repository-relative path | Size | Recorded appearance time (UTC) |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `.atl/skill-registry.md` | 23,537 bytes | 2026-09-09 12:32:53.398 |
| `.atl/.skill-registry.cache.json` | 64 bytes | 2026-09-09 12:32:53.405 |

The OpenCode session was created at 12:32:53.453 UTC, after both files. Its runtime database records one user message and no assistant message or tool execution.

Read-only inspection of the installed `plugins/skill-registry.ts` found automatic registry refresh during plugin initialization, with quiet and no-gitignore semantics, before the requested task.

The candidate comparison contained only these two added files, totaling 98 added lines; application source remained unchanged. Normal unscoped STATUS then reported `applicability: unrelated` and an executable `fresh_target_ready` transition for Candidate B instead of the pending slots for Candidate A. This report does not claim that an explicitly lineage-scoped STATUS was tested.

After preserving only the two generated files outside the candidate, normal STATUS rediscovered the exact original target and authority revision: `state: reviewing`, generation 1, `reviewer_results_required`, four pending slots, and receipt `expected_missing`.

### Gentle AI Version

`gentle-ai 2.2.4`

This occurrence was not retested on a newer release and is not asserted to be a regression from a later fix.

### Operating System

macOS 26.6.2, build 25G83, arm64; zsh.

### AI Agent / Client

OpenCode 1.18.4 as the attempted reviewer transport; Codex CLI 0.153.4 as the parent orchestration client.

### 📋 Affected Area

Other — installed OpenCode skill-registry startup plugin interacting with negotiated workspace review.

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

The single OpenCode launch ended before any assistant, tool, or reviewer result:

```text
name: UnknownError
message: Unexpected server error. Check server logs for details.
ref: err_d6b861ee
```

No detailed server log was available for this occurrence. The underlying server-error cause is unverified and is separate from the evidenced startup workspace mutation.

### Additional Context

- One foreground OpenCode launch; no retry. Existing configured provider/model settings were unchanged.
- No reviewer result, correction, receipt, commit, or deployment was produced. The original review authority and consumer work remain preserved, and review is paused.
- Related #2016 covers continuation of an explicitly selected frozen lineage after workspace drift. Here the primary defect is that reviewer-runtime startup itself creates the drift; only normal unscoped STATUS was observed.
- Related #1986 covers pre-inspection exact-slot recovery with an unchanged live candidate. Its comments mention registry generation before START, whereas these files appeared after START.
- #1731 and #3350 concern startup refresh at an incorrect or non-project location; this occurrence is in the intended Git workspace.
- #4302 reports a concrete plugin-loader SchemaError, which was not observed here. #3019 reports the same generic server-error wording through GGA, but matching wording does not establish a shared cause.
