title: feat(orchestration): evaluate firstmate-style worker mechanics + lavish visual design gate (SDD/RDD-compatible)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Problem Statement

Gentle AI orchestrates via SDD phases plus RDD review gates. The delegation mechanics underneath are mostly prompt-driven per agent (`sdd-orchestrator.md` + phase skills over native subagent primitives, inline fallback in solo agents).

Limits when parallel work grows:

1. Workers are not visible/isolated by default — no separate session endpoint per task, no disposable worktree, so parallel writers risk colliding.
2. The orchestrator↔worker contract lives mostly in prompt prose — no explicit handoff (identity, allowed roots, acceptance criteria, verification commands) aligned with RDD lineage/receipts.
3. No resumable, event-driven supervision — recovery and supervision cost more tokens/attention than needed.
4. Design-phase Q&A is text-only — architecture tradeoffs are harder to review than in a visual artifact with diagrams + pinpoint questions.

Reference: `https://youtu.be/kPN564Kol14?t=2073`, https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate, https://github.com/kunchenguid/lavish-axi.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Evaluate and adapt worker **mechanics only**. SDD (`propose → spec → design → tasks → apply → verify`) and RDD (lineage, receipts, gates, delivery authority) stay unchanged and normative.

**1. Visible, isolated workers within SDD/RDD**

- One session endpoint per delegated task where the host supports it (tmux/Herdr/cmux/Orca-style), graceful fallback otherwise.
- Disposable worktree per task so parallel SDD work on one repo never collides.
- Every worker still runs its assigned SDD phase(s); every candidate still passes RDD gates. No new lifecycle.

**2. Explicit orchestrator↔worker handoff, RDD-aligned**

- Parent owns routing, handoff identity, user decisions, commits, delivery, all mutations.
- Handoff carries: opaque identity, allowed edit roots, target behavior, acceptance criteria, exact verification commands. Missing/mismatched handoff fails closed.
- Worker returns changed paths + verification evidence + blockers; never claims approval/delivery. Reviewer passes use fresh context over worker output.
- Handoff identity is independent of but compatible with RDD lineages/receipts; it never impersonates them.

**3. Resumable supervision, hybrid disk + Engram**

- Coordination source of truth on disk (project-scoped store, exclusive `flock` via the existing `AcquireAuthorityFileLock` pattern): claims, handoffs, locks. Crash-safe by kernel release, synchronously visible across sessions.
- Engram as semantic mirror only (decisions, session summaries, learnings across phases/sessions via `mem_save`/`mem_session_summary`), never as lock manager. Rationale: Engram today is SQLite+FTS5 curated memory with search previews and manual git sync — no CAS, leases, or fencing — so using it as claim authority risks races and stale reads.

**4. Opt-in visual design gate inside `design` (lavish-style)**

- Orchestrator optionally renders a local HTML artifact with diagrams + structured questions.
- Human annotates elements/text, answers, queues feedback; answers return as structured input to continue the SDD cycle.
- Local-first, never blocks non-interactive runs.

**Non-goals (explicit):**

- No change to SDD/RDD semantics or authority.
- No `project modes` (`no-mistakes` / `direct-PR` / `local-only`).
- No `ship` vs `scout` task types.
- No Engram-as-lock-manager; no new Engram coordination primitives in this issue.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- Keep prompt-only delegation; document limits.
- Adopt only worktree isolation.
- Adopt only the visual design gate in `design`.
- Full firstmate adoption (rejected: different goals — firstmate is an agent distro, gentle-ai is a multi-agent SDD/RDD installer; borrow mechanics only).

### 📎 Additional Context

- https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate (MIT) — crew/session/worktree/supervision mechanics only
- https://github.com/kunchenguid/lavish-axi (MIT) — local HTML annotate → poll → agent-continues loop
- Related but not duplicates: #3026 (reviewer/worker roles), #3600 (backbone + claiming), #1302 (work queue), #4004 (bound context)

title: bug(gga+review): the managed Claude Code Stop hook fires inside gga's own provider subprocess, so gga's review never runs and its strict mode blocks the commit (2.7.0 / gga 2.10.1)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing open and closed issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs require `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

Automated sanitized provider-defect report. It states observed behavior only and does not assert a root cause.

On `gentle-ai 2.7.0` (stable channel) with `gga v2.10.1` and `PROVIDER=claude`, the managed Claude Code `Stop` hook (`gentle-ai review stop-hook --agent claude-code`, shipped in 2.6.0 via #4071) fires **inside gga's own provider subprocess**. That subprocess is a non-interactive Claude Code session, so the blocking `gentle-ai.review-integration.consent/v3` envelope it receives cannot be answered by anyone.

The observed result is that gga's provider spends its entire turn relaying the consent envelope instead of producing a review. No review body is emitted. gga's own `STRICT_MODE=true` parser then rejects that output as ambiguous and exits non-zero, so the pre-commit gate blocks the commit — while the review it blocked on never ran.

Both actors here are Gentle AI: the hook that fires is `gentle-ai review stop-hook`, and the invocation that fails is `gga run`.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Windows (`MINGW64_NT-10.0 x86_64`), `gentle-ai 2.7.0`, `gga v2.10.1`, Claude Code `2.1.265`.
2. Review mode enabled; managed `SessionStart` and `Stop` hooks installed.
3. gga configured with `PROVIDER="claude"`, `STRICT_MODE="true"`, `TIMEOUT="900"`, `RULES_FILE` set.
4. Stage a medium-risk candidate containing at least one executable source file, so the consent envelope is required rather than skipped.
5. With that candidate **unreviewed** by RDD, run `gga run` (directly, or via the pre-commit hook).
6. Observe gga's provider output: it contains the consent envelope, its choice list, its two invocations, and a closing line asking for an answer — and no review.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

A reviewer subprocess launched by another Gentle AI tool should not be handed a blocking consent prompt it structurally cannot answer. Either the stop hook recognizes a non-interactive provider subprocess and stays silent, or the invoking tool marks its subprocess as exempt, so `gga run` can complete its own review.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

`gga run` produced 97 lines of provider output with no review body, then failed with its own strict-mode refusal:

```
⚠️  Could not determine review status
❌ STRICT MODE: Failing due to ambiguous response

Expected exactly one line starting with 'STATUS: PASSED' or 'STATUS: FAILED'
in the first 30 lines of provider output
```

The provider's own closing line was `Waiting on your answer — granted or declined.` The wall-clock cost was roughly five minutes per occurrence, with no reviewer work performed.

### 🩹 Observed workaround, and why it is fragile

Completing the RDD lifecycle for the current candidate to `authority: burned` **before** invoking gga makes the next `gga run` produce a full review. Re-running the identical gga invocation after that burn returned a normal `STATUS: FAILED` with substantive findings, which is the same command that had returned nothing minutes earlier.

That workaround interacts badly with #4390: after a burn, any index or worktree change re-arms the reminder, so a review-fix-review cycle has to re-run the whole RDD lifecycle — START, consent envelope, lens capture, acknowledgement — before **every** gga round. Over eight gga rounds on one changeset, that was eight complete RDD cycles, each requiring a human answer to the consent envelope, purely to keep the other reviewer able to run.

### 📎 Additional context

- `gentle-ai 2.7.0` carries no `-rc.` or `-main.` tag, so this occurrence is on the stable evidence channel.
- Related but distinct: #4390 (stop hook reminds for a candidate already acknowledged and burned), #2625 (claude provider times out silently on pre-commit review), #4098 (disjoint finding sets for byte-identical staged content), #1352 (a pre-commit actor invalidating a receipt and re-triggering review — same causal class, different actor).
- No source contents, diffs, paths, or repository identity are included in this report.

title: feat(tui): configure Pi agent model presets by subscription
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

TUI (terminal UI)

### 💡 Problem Statement

Gentle AI supports Pi as an AI coding agent target, and its TUI provides a Model Configuration screen (ScreenModelConfig) with quick configuration options for Claude, OpenCode, Kiro, and Codex.

However, configuring model routing for Pi is currently missing from this menu. Pi users who have gentle-pi installed and authenticated through Codex (native Pi login) or Claude (via extension) must manually configure more than 17 subagents (SDD phases, Judgment Day judges, reviewers) one by one in Pi's interactive /gentle:models prompt (~34 individual selections).

Existing issue #3522 proposed a per-agent manual editor relying on an external CLI (gentle-pi-models from gentle-pi #381) that is currently stalled. It does not provide subscription-based presets (e.g., Claude, Codex, Kiro, Budget) with economic, balanced, and premium tiers that automatically map the best model and reasoning effort to all 17+ subagents according to their capability tier.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Add a "Configure Pi models" entry to the Model Configuration menu (internal/tui/screens/model_config.go).

When selected, open a single-screen tiered preset picker (ScreenPiModelPicker) grouped by provider:

- Claude (Anthropic):
  - Claude — Balanced (Recommended): Sonnet for reasoning & code, Haiku for light work.
  - Claude — Premium (Max Quality / Opus): Opus for architecture & verification, Sonnet for code.
  - Claude — Economy (Token Saver / Haiku): Sonnet for architecture, Haiku for code & maintenance.
- Codex (OpenAI):
  - Codex — Balanced (Recommended): Sol for reasoning, Terra for code, Luna for light work.
  - Codex — Premium (Max Quality / Sol): Sol with high effort across architecture & code.
  - Codex — Economy (Token Saver / Luna): Terra for code, Luna for light tasks with minimal effort.
- Kiro (Frontier):
  - Kiro — Balanced (Recommended): Claude 4.8 for reasoning, Sonnet 4.6 for code, Haiku 4.5 for light work.
  - Kiro — Premium (Max Quality / 4.8): Claude 4.8 across all critical architecture and coding phases.
  - Kiro — Economy (Token Saver / 4.5): Sonnet 4.6 for architecture, Haiku 4.5 for code & maintenance.
- Budget / Open Source:
  - Budget — Open Source (DeepSeek Reasoner & Chat): High quality at minimal token cost.

Configuration Preview:
As the user navigates the options, a live preview box displays the concrete model IDs and thinking levels assigned to Reasoning, Execution, and Light work tiers before confirming.

Execution & Sync Flow:
When confirmed:
- Selection is staged in PendingSyncOverrides and applied during sync.
- During sync, Gentle AI writes the canonical configuration to ~/.pi/gentle-ai/models.json and updates ~/.pi/agent/subagents.json (model_profiles).
- When Pi starts, gentle-pi automatically consumes ~/.pi/gentle-ai/models.json on session_start and updates agent frontmatters.

Acceptance Criteria:
- [x] "Configure Pi models" appears in the Model Configuration screen (ScreenModelConfig).
- [x] Selecting it opens ScreenPiModelPicker displaying the tiered presets in a single view with live configuration preview.
- [x] Selecting a preset stages the full 17+ agent routing matrix into PendingSyncOverrides.
- [x] Running sync persists the routing to ~/.pi/gentle-ai/models.json and mirrors it to ~/.pi/agent/subagents.json (model_profiles).
- [x] Existing non-model properties in subagents.json are preserved without loss.
- [x] Comprehensive unit tests cover presets generation, file serialization, and TUI navigation.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- Relying solely on #3522: Rejected because #3522 is tied to an unreleased IPC binary (gentle-pi-models) and requires configuring 17+ agents individually rather than selecting a one-click subscription preset.
- Configuring only inside Pi /gentle:models: Rejected because Gentle AI's ecosystem mission is unified configuration across all supported agents from one central CLI/TUI.

### 📎 Additional Context

Gentle Pi already consumes ~/.pi/gentle-ai/models.json on session startup via applySavedModelConfig(ctx) in extensions/gentle-ai.ts. This allows Gentle AI to directly configure Pi without requiring external CLI binary dependencies.

Implementation Status — Ready for PR Submission:
The implementation is already completed, tested, and verified locally (100% test pass rate). To respect the repository's strict <400 LOC review limit, the code is prepared as a clean, sequential 4-PR chain (<270 LOC each):

1. PR 1 — Core Models & Presets: internal/model/pi_model.go and tests (~220 LOC).
2. PR 2 — File Persistence: internal/agents/pi/model_config.go and tests (~217 LOC).
3. PR 3 — Sync Engine & State: internal/model/selection.go, internal/state/state.go, internal/app/app.go, internal/cli/sync.go and integration tests (~237 LOC).
4. PR 4 — TUI Integration: internal/tui/screens/model_config.go, internal/tui/screens/pi_model_picker.go, internal/tui/model.go, internal/tui/router.go and tests (~270 LOC).

Awaiting maintainer triage and status:approved to dispatch the PR chain.

title: Idea: integración opcional de voz/TTS con secretos runtime vía Bitwarden
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area
Documentation

### 💡 Problem Statement
Me gustaría compartir con la comunidad una integración local que resultó útil: ejecutar Pi/Gentle AI con salida de voz y secretos cargados desde Bitwarden/Vaultwarden sólo en tiempo de ejecución.

El problema que resuelve es doble:

1. Accesibilidad y experiencia: escuchar respuestas finales del agente mediante TTS puede ser útil para sesiones largas, revisión asistida, multitarea o flujos donde la terminal no está siempre en primer plano.
2. Seguridad operativa: muchas integraciones de voz necesitan API keys. La forma segura debería evitar guardar secretos en el repositorio, en archivos de configuración planos o en logs.

Actualmente esto puede resolverse con wrappers locales, pero no vi una receta oficial o recomendada para hacerlo de manera reproducible y segura.

### 📦 Proposed Solution
Propongo empezar como documentación/ejemplo comunitario, no necesariamente como cambio del core:

- Un ejemplo de wrapper opcional, por ejemplo `pi-voz` o `gentle-voice`, que:
  - desbloquee Bitwarden/Vaultwarden usando `bw`,
  - lea la API key necesaria para TTS,
  - exporte el secreto sólo como variable de entorno del proceso,
  - lance Pi/Gentle AI con una extensión o hook de voz,
  - no escriba secretos en disco ni los imprima.
- Una pequeña guía de seguridad para integraciones con secret managers:
  - no hardcodear tokens,
  - no guardar API keys en el repo,
  - evitar logs con secretos,
  - documentar cómo desactivar la voz.
- Un ejemplo de integración TTS opcional:
  - backend inicial: Deepgram/Aura, aunque el diseño podría permitir otros proveedores,
  - hablar sólo respuestas finales del asistente,
  - evitar hablar mensajes de subagentes o eventos internos,
  - deduplicar eventos para no repetir audio.

La intención sería validar primero si esto encaja mejor como:

- receta oficial en docs,
- ejemplo en `examples/`,
- paquete comunitario separado,
- o una futura API de hooks/plugins para integraciones opcionales.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered
- Mantenerlo sólo como wrapper privado local: funciona, pero no ayuda a otros usuarios que podrían necesitar el mismo patrón.
- Integrarlo directamente en el core: parece prematuro hasta que los mantenedores definan si voz y secret managers pertenecen al proyecto principal.
- Crear un fork con cambios internos: posible, pero aumentaría el mantenimiento y podría separar innecesariamente una idea que quizás sólo necesita documentación o una API pequeña.

### 📎 Additional Context
Ya existe un prototipo local funcionando con esta arquitectura general:

- wrapper de lanzamiento,
- Bitwarden/Vaultwarden para recuperar el secreto en runtime,
- variable de entorno sólo en memoria,
- extensión/hook que reproduce con voz las respuestas finales,
- control separado para activar/desactivar la voz.

No estoy proponiendo publicar secretos, rutas locales ni detalles privados. La propuesta es compartir el patrón de integración y convertirlo en una receta segura para la comunidad si los mantenedores lo ven útil.

title: bug(review): Claude Code stop-hook reminds for a candidate already acknowledged and burned in the same session, forcing a second review of an unchanged candidate (2.7.0)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing open and closed issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs require `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

Automated sanitized provider-defect report. It states observed behavior only and does not assert a root cause.

On `gentle-ai 2.7.0` (stable channel) with Claude Code, the managed `Stop` hook (`gentle-ai review stop-hook --agent claude-code`, shipped in 2.6.0 via #4071) fired its "unreviewed candidate" reminder for a candidate that had already been reviewed, approved, and acknowledged (`authority: burned`) earlier in the same session, with no repository mutation in between. The agent followed the reminder as the contract requires, and the same unchanged candidate went through a second complete START/acknowledgement cycle.

The STATUS side of this is documented as designed: after the burn, negotiated STATUS reports the unchanged target as `fresh_target_ready` (#3638, closed not-planned under the atomic model of #3417). The hook, however, appears to derive "unreviewed" from the absence of authority, which after a burn is indistinguishable from "never reviewed". Within one session the hook itself has the information to tell them apart: the acknowledgement burned the exact target identity the hook later named.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Linux amd64, `gentle-ai 2.7.0`, Claude Code 2.1.x, review mode enabled, managed `SessionStart` and `Stop` hooks installed.
2. In an interactive session, edit one documentation file in a repository (low-risk, `non_executable_only` candidate).
3. Before ending the turn, run the selectorless STATUS preflight; run the returned START verbatim. START returns `action: closed`, `state: approved`, `lenses_required: false`, with an exact acknowledgement.
4. Run that acknowledgement verbatim once. It returns `gentle-ai.review-acknowledged/v1`, `action: acknowledged`, `authority: burned`.
5. End the turn without touching the worktree.
6. Observe the `Stop` hook block the stop with a `gentle-ai.review-stop-hook/v1` reminder naming the same `target_identity` that was just acknowledged and burned, and offering the same START command with the same `--lineage`.
7. Following the contract, run STATUS again (`applicability: unrelated`, `fresh_target_ready`), START again (`closed`/`approved` again, new revision), acknowledgement again (`burned` again).
8. End the turn. The hook does not fire a third time for this candidate.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Within a session, a candidate whose exact target identity was acknowledged and burned should count as reviewed for the hook's "once per session candidate" rule, so the reminder stays silent and the unchanged candidate is not reviewed twice.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The reminder fired once for the already-burned candidate and caused one redundant review cycle on an unchanged candidate. It fired exactly once, so the once-per-candidate suppression held after the second acknowledgement; the gap is that the first acknowledgement did not count.

### Gentle AI Version

2.7.0 (stable; build string carries neither `-rc.` nor `-main.`)

### Operating System

Linux x86_64

### AI Agent / Client

Claude Code 2.1.265

### 📋 Affected Area

Review (receipt-driven development), Claude Code stop-hook

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

Safe opaque identifiers, one candidate, workspace projection, one documentation file:

- Lineage: `review-563e12597ffe8b64`
- Target identity: `sha256:45af00e4668752d4a004a4eaf2b05119a6705b02a467eaadbbce4a8c029acfff`
- First acknowledgement consumed revision: `sha256:30c5fa81b54938fceccd91fa74ef9f1364338860fb1d1455f0e9a9b2e453537a`
- Second acknowledgement consumed revision: `sha256:f6233d05cda96c30beb4eeaf03ce31ecd59b79ccd1598e504f2f493cd22b7a2e`

Hook reminder text after the first burn (verbatim, identifiers as above):

```
Receipt-driven development is enabled for this repository, and it holds an unreviewed candidate (target_identity sha256:45af00e4…).
[...] STATUS returned this exact provider-issued START (carrying --consent=relay); run it unchanged: gentle-ai review start [...] --target=sha256:45af00e4… --projection=workspace --lineage=review-563e12597ffe8b64 --agent=claude-code --consent=relay
[...] This hook never runs review start itself, and it reminds once per session and candidate.
```

Both START responses:

```
action: closed · state: approved · risk_level: low · selected_lenses: [] · risk_reasons: [{code: non_executable_only}]
```

Both acknowledgements:

```
{"action":"acknowledged","authority":"burned"}
```

### Additional Context

- Earlier in the same session, on a different candidate in the same repository (a two-line edit to the same file), the hook fired once, the review closed and burned, and the hook stayed silent afterwards. That candidate was acknowledged in response to the hook, not before it. The difference in the failing case is only that the acknowledgement happened before the turn ended.
- Related: gentle-pi#568 records a session baseline so the `agent_end` reminder ignores pre-session work. This report is the complementary case: work reviewed and burned inside the session.
- No source or index mutation between the first acknowledgement and the hook firing; the second review reported the same target identity.

title: bug(review): correction_plan_required transition omits --correction-lines, so capture-correction-plan rejects its own provider-issued command (2.7.0)
body:
## Automated provider-defect report

### Summary

A bounded review reached `correction_required` after the refuter corroborated two candidate-caused severe findings. Negotiated STATUS then returns a `collect` transition with `reason_code: correction_plan_required` and a single input whose `capture_operation` is `review.capture-correction-plan`.

The input's `arguments` array publishes exactly five tokens:

```
lineage, expected-revision, target, repository-context, request-hash
```

Running that operation with exactly those five tokens, unchanged, is refused by the same CLI:

```json
{
  "schema": "gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2",
  "operation": "review.capture-correction-plan",
  "phase": "preflight",
  "code": "invalid_request",
  "message": "The negotiated review request is invalid.",
  "mutation_outcome": "not_started",
  "authority_applicability": "not_evaluated",
  "retry_safe": true,
  "replayability": "not_replayable",
  "next_action": "correct_request",
  "cause": "review capture-correction-plan requires --lineage, --target, --expected-revision, --request-hash, and positive --correction-lines"
}
```

`gentle-ai review capture-correction-plan --help` confirms the CLI accepts **six** flags — the five published plus `--correction-lines <value>`, which STATUS never emits, in `arguments` or anywhere else in the transition.

The consumer cannot proceed by following `next_transition` alone: the integration contract requires executing the provider-issued operation and its ordered arguments unchanged and explicitly forbids synthesizing an invocation from prose, so adding `--correction-lines=<n>` is not an available remedy. The lineage is left in `correction_required` with no executable route forward.

### Environment

- Gentle AI: **2.7.0** (stable channel — no `-rc.` / `-main.` tag)
- OS: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, Linux x86_64
- Client: claude-code
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`
- Projection: `workspace`
- Lineage: `review-9efa0b6434628bdb`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a medium-risk compact review on a workspace projection and grant consent.
2. Capture the reviewer lens result; STATUS then requests `provider_refuter`.
3. Run the exact `review.capture-refuter` operation. It returns `state: correction_required`, `action: "candidate-caused severe findings require one bounded correction"`.
4. Follow its `status_continuation` and run the returned `review.status`.
5. STATUS returns `kind: collect`, `reason_code: correction_plan_required`, `capture_operation: review.capture-correction-plan`, with the five arguments above.
6. Run that operation with exactly those arguments.

**Expected:** the correction-plan input is captured and the lineage advances to the bounded correction.
**Actual:** `invalid_request` at preflight, because the CLI requires a sixth flag the transition never publishes.

### Bounded attempts and outcomes

| # | Operation | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `review.capture-result` (lens slot, exact tokens) | `invalid_request` — `cause: "refuter provider result admission incomplete: reviewer payload contains no complete JSON object: no object start was found in 495 bytes"` |
| 2 | exact-lineage STATUS | reoffered a **different** slot: `provider_refuter_required` |
| 3 | `review.capture-refuter` (exact tokens) | success — `state: correction_required` |
| 4 | exact-lineage STATUS via `status_continuation` | `correction_plan_required`, five arguments |
| 5 | `review.capture-correction-plan` (exact tokens) | `invalid_request`, envelope above |

No further GitHub or lifecycle mutation was attempted after the refusal. All consumer state is preserved; the lineage was not abandoned, recovered or reset.

Attempt 1 may be a separate matter and is reported here only as observed context, not as a claim about its cause.

### Same causal class, already closed on older builds

- **#3319** (2.3.0) — *finalized v2 binding omits request-hash, finalize preflight rejects as invalid_request*. Same shape: STATUS publishes a transition whose command omits a token its own preflight requires, and the consumer cannot supply it by following the contract.
- **#1745** (2.1.11) — *next_transition emits non-executable captured_results argument*. Same class, different operation.

Both are closed. This occurrence is on **2.7.0**, on a **different operation** (`capture-correction-plan`) and a **different missing flag** (`--correction-lines`), so it is filed as a new observable defect rather than an occurrence comment on either. If maintainers consider one of them the canonical tracker for the causal class, this can be folded in.

### Notes

- Observed evidence only; no root cause is asserted.
- The `--correction-lines` value is a count the consumer cannot derive from the contract: the transition publishes no budget, and the contract states the correction budget is frozen and owned natively.

title: bug(review): targeted validator emits its inspect-candidate command as prose on claude-code 2.7.0, so capture-validation is unadmittable (regression of #3787)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues), including open and closed results, and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

Automated provider defect report. Observed behavior only; no root cause is asserted.

On `2.7.0` (stable channel), a bounded compact-v2 review that reaches `targeted_validation_required` after a successful bounded correction cannot be completed on the `claude-code` runtime. `review capture-validation --agent=claude-code --execute=true` runs the provider validator, and native admission rejects the returned payload because it contains no JSON object at all.

The rejected payloads preserved under `rejected-results/<lineage>/targeted-validator-*.json` show what the validator actually returned: the exact `gentle-ai review inspect-candidate --purpose targeted-validation ... --operation name-status` command it was asked to run, rendered as prose. The first attempt emitted it as a tool-call block; the corrective attempt and a later relaunch emitted it inside a fenced `bash` block. In every case the payload is the command text, never a verdict.

**Relationship to the closest existing issues** (searched, open and closed):

- **#3380** (closed, 2026-08-17) — the targeted validator was never told how to inspect the frozen candidate. That fix appears to be present: the validator now names `inspect-candidate` with arguments derived from its own binding. What it does not appear to have is any way to execute it, so it returns the recipe instead of a verdict.
- **#3787** (closed, 2026-08-27, reported on `2.5.0-rc.1`) — same observable defect and the same affected contract: `capture-validation --execute` on `claude-code` dead-ends a corrected lineage because admission rejects the provider's own result, and `capture-validation` exposes no `--input` route. Closed by #3789, merged 2026-08-27 as commit `1143761`, which `v2.5.0` (2026-09-01, stable) already contains and `v2.7.0` therefore contains too. This report is a reproduction on a build proven to contain that fix, so it is filed as a linked regression rather than a reopen.
- **#4061** (closed) — in-process targeted validator returns a *truncated* JSON payload. Here the payload has no object start at all.
- **#3427** (closed) — same lifecycle stage on the OpenCode runtime, different adapter.
- **#4355** (open) — every capture refused on a Pi host relay, including verbatim forecasts. Different runtime and different surface: here the correction plan and the correction itself were both admitted without incident, and only the validator capture fails.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. With RDD enabled, drive a negotiated v2 `workspace` review to `reviewing` on a medium-risk candidate (5 changed files, 340 changed lines, one selected lens).
2. Let the lens return a candidate-caused `CRITICAL`; `review status --next-transition` offers `collect correction_plan_required`.
3. Submit the bound `capture-correction-plan` with a positive `--correction-lines` forecast, then apply the correction in the worktree.
4. `review status --next-transition` advances to `collect targeted_validation_required`, offering `review.capture-validation` with `--execute=true`.
5. Run that reoffered capture verbatim.

### ✅ Expected

The validator inspects the frozen corrected candidate through `inspect-candidate` and returns the validator JSON, so the corrected lineage can converge to a receipt.

### ❌ Actual

Both internal admission attempts are refused and the operation exits with the typed failure envelope:

```
"schema": "gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2"
"operation": "review.capture-validation"
"phase": "preflight"
"code": "provider_capture_result_refused"
"mutation_outcome": "not_started"
"retry_safe": true
```

cause: `targeted-validator provider result admission incomplete: reviewer payload contains no complete JSON object: no object start was found in N bytes` — N was 695 and 682 on the first run, and 487 on the relaunch.

Re-querying `review status --next-transition` reoffers the identical bound slot: same `expected-revision`, same correction target, same `request-hash`. Running that reoffered capture verbatim produced one further rejected payload and then exited with `"code": "invalid_request"`, `"mutation_outcome": "not_started"`, `"retry_safe": true`.

### 🧾 Preserved state

Three refused attempts, no mutation. `mutation_outcome` is `not_started` on every failure and the lineage remains at `targeted_validation_required` with identical binding tokens, so the single bounded correction attempt was not consumed. No verdict was submitted: recording an inconclusive check as a failed one would consume that attempt irreversibly.

### 🖥️ Environment

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Build | `2.7.0` |
| Evidence channel | stable (no `-rc.` or `-main.` tag) |
| OS / arch | macOS / arm64 |
| Runtime | `claude-code` |
| Contract | `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2` |
| Projection | `workspace` |
| Risk / lenses | medium / one lens |

title: bug(orchestrator): post-compaction continuation prompt treated as consent for an option the user never chose
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description


While presenting two implementation options (B1/B2) to the user with an explicit question
("¿vamos con B1?"), automatic context compaction triggered before the user answered. After compaction resumed, a generic continuation message ("Continue if you have next steps...")
was interpreted by the orchestrator as approval, and it delegated implementation of the
RECOMMENDED option (B1) without the user ever choosing it.

This is a consent failure: a pending decision with explicit options is not unblocked by a
generic continuation prompt. The orchestrator must re-ask open questions after compaction
instead of inferring the recommended default.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce


1. In an interactive session, present two or more implementation options (A vs B) and
   recommend one, ending with an explicit question the user has NOT answered.
2. Wait for automatic context compaction to trigger.
3. After compaction, a generic continuation prompt like "Continue if you have next steps,
   or stop and ask for clarification if you are unsure how to proceed" arrives.
4. The orchestrator interprets this as approval and immediately implements the recommended
   option.


### ✅ Expected Behavior

After compaction, the orchestrator should detect there was an OPEN user decision (recover
via mem_context / mem_session_summary / pending-question tracking) and RE-ASK the question before implementing. Implementation only happens after an explicit user choice — never an inferred default from a non-committal continuation prompt.


### ❌ Actual Behavior


The orchestrator launched a full implementation (backend getter + frontend typeahead +
tests) of the recommended option B1 without user consent. The user had to interrupt and
point out they had never chosen an option.

### Gentle AI Version

1.34.0

### Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client

OpenCode

### 📋 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
[orchestrator]: Mi recomendación: arrancar con B1 ... ¿Vamos con B1?   [compaction triggered]
[system]: Continue if you have next steps, or stop and ask for clarification...
[orchestrator]: interpreted as approval -> delegated B1 implementation (5 files, tests green)
```

### Additional Context

_No response_

title: [bug] operation_outcome_unknown: managed reviewer assets are outdated — digest mismatch global dev vs pinned relay
body:
## Symptom

4x `operation_outcome_unknown` on `review capture-result` (lineage `review-ef219a0b81685504`), all with:

> managed reviewer assets are outdated; run `gentle-ai sync`

Repeated `gentle-ai sync`, extension update + `/reload`, and full Pi restart did NOT clear it. Forecast passed (4 lenses OK), submit failed every time.

Defect reports generated (all `operation_outcome_unknown`, `native_running` phase):
- `operation-outcome-unknown-b1236e202637.md` — 2026-09-08T17:37:47Z, v2.6.0, windows/amd64
- `operation-outcome-unknown-d0adee162ada.md` — 2026-09-08T18:55:11Z, v2.6.0, windows/amd64
- `operation-outcome-unknown-3a462feefb35.md` — 2026-09-08T18:58:03Z, v2.6.0, windows/amd64
- `operation-outcome-unknown-07ab414a6bca.md` — 2026-09-08T19:25:54Z, v2.7.0, windows/amd64

Each report's reproduction command: `review capture-result --agent --expected-revision --input --lens --lineage --order --repository-context --subject-hash --target`. Full texts available on request (all four identical except timestamp/version).

## Root cause (user-diagnosed)

Not a sync bug: `sync` was executed by the global dev binary while `capture` was executed by the gentle-pi pinned relay (2.7.0). Without an override, the digest check declares them enemies forever — no amount of re-sync fixes it.

## Workaround that closed the loop

1. Backed up the +dirty binary (`go/bin/gentle-ai.exe.bak-2.7.1-dev-dirty-20260908`).
2. Clean rebuild from the installer (`0924ebcb`): `2.7.1-0.20260908182451-0924ebcbda31`, no +dirty, installed globally. Repo untracked files restored, forks untouched.
3. Registered the dev override (`~/.pi/gentle-ai/dev-binary.json`) — verified the relay now resolves to the dev binary. (Pi uses the pinned relay unless overridden; Zed uses the global from PATH.)
4. Re-sync with the same binary + STATUS resumed the old lineage (current_target, 4 slots).
5. Captures 1+3 admitted, review closed APPROVED, authority burned (acknowledge-approved, no STATUS after).

## Useful data point

The digest covers only embedded assets: the dirty build and the clean build produced the SAME digest. The +dirty suffix was cosmetic. Future rebuilds of the same source should not require re-sync — only asset changes should.

## Environment

- OS: windows/amd64
- gentle-ai: 2.6.0 (first 3 reports) → 2.7.0/2.7.1-0.20260908182451-0924ebcbda31
- Client: Pi host relay (forecast OK, capture failed); Zed via global PATH binary
- Review: high tier, 26 files, ~2042 lines, 4 lenses (risk/resilience/readability/reliability)

## Suggested fix

When sync and capture resolve to different binaries (global vs pinned relay), either warn with both resolved paths + digests, or make the error message name the two digests so the mismatch is diagnosable instead of looping on `run gentle-ai sync`.

title: bug(install): Windows compatibility skills refusal names no exit when .agents/skills is a reparse point
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

On Windows, when `%USERPROFILE%\.agents\skills` is a reparse point, `gentle-ai install` and `gentle-ai sync` fail the compatibility skills step with `compatibility target is not a physical directory`, wrapped as `open compatibility skills root directory "<path>": compatibility target is not a physical directory`. This is a by-design containment refusal; a comment next to the check says the physical-directory requirement exists so the opened handle does not target a reparse point.

The failure ends an interactive run (gentle-ai's default TUI) with the pipeline's generic recovery block:

```
What to do
  1. Check the error messages above
  2. Fix the underlying issue (missing deps, permissions, etc.)
  3. Run gentle-ai again to retry
```

That block names no runnable continuation for this specific failure. Running the same failing case through the direct CLI subcommand form (`gentle-ai install ...` / `gentle-ai sync ...`, not the interactive wizard) shows the same refusal is just as silent about a continuation there: it ends the run with a bare `Error: ...` line and no further recovery guidance. A sibling check in the same feature, for a symlinked or non-directory compatibility destination ancestor, already names a continuation when it hits an analogous condition: `compatibility destination ancestor %q must be a physical directory; replace it with a physical directory, then rerun gentle-ai install or gentle-ai sync`. Neither the TUI's generic block nor the CLI's bare error line names one for this refusal.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a throwaway home directory, e.g. `C:\gentle-repro\home`, and a real target directory, e.g. `C:\gentle-repro\target-skills`.
2. Create `C:\gentle-repro\home\.agents` as a real directory, then make `C:\gentle-repro\home\.agents\skills` a directory junction to `target-skills`:
   ```
   mkdir C:\gentle-repro\home\.agents
   mklink /J "C:\gentle-repro\home\.agents\skills" "C:\gentle-repro\target-skills"
   ```
3. Point the environment at that throwaway home and run install with the skills component:
   ```
   set USERPROFILE=C:\gentle-repro\home
   set HOME=C:\gentle-repro\home
   gentle-ai install --agents claude-code --components skills
   ```
   This reproduces on gentle-ai 2.7.0: the command exits 1 and prints `Error: open compatibility skills root directory "C:\\gentle-repro\\home\\.agents\\skills": compatibility target is not a physical directory` with no further guidance. `gentle-ai sync --agents claude-code` against the same throwaway home fails identically.
4. To see the boxed "Installation completed with errors" / "What to do" form quoted in Actual Behavior below (the form shown in the report that prompted this issue), run bare `gentle-ai` (the interactive TUI) instead of step 3 and walk through the wizard with the same throwaway home; the wizard reaches the same refusal and renders it through its completion screen instead of a plain CLI error line.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The refusal should name the same runnable continuation the sibling ancestor check already names for its analogous condition: tell the user to replace the compatibility skills root with a physical directory, then rerun `gentle-ai install` or `gentle-ai sync`, the way the ancestor check's message already does. That applies whether the refusal surfaces through the interactive wizard's completion screen or through the plain CLI subcommand's error line.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Direct CLI subcommand (`gentle-ai install --agents claude-code --components skills` against a throwaway home with `.agents\skills` set up as in Steps to Reproduce, gentle-ai 2.7.0, exit code 1):

```
Error: open compatibility skills root directory "C:\\gentle-repro\\home\\.agents\\skills": compatibility target is not a physical directory
```

No "What to do" text or other continuation follows; the process simply exits.

The interactive TUI (the form in which the report that prompted this issue was filed) reaches the same refusal but renders it through its completion screen, which does add a recovery block, just a generic one that does not name a continuation for this failure; see the screenshot transcript in Additional Context.

### Gentle AI Version

2.7.0 (the version the direct-CLI reproduction above ran on; the version behind the screenshot in Additional Context is not visible in it).

### Operating System

Windows

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

Paths below are shortened to the example location used in Steps to Reproduce; the captured text is otherwise verbatim.

```shell
# gentle-ai install --agents claude-code --components skills   (exit code 1)
WARNING: installing with --scope=global (default). Agent config files (system prompts, skills/, agents/, etc.)
will be written to each selected agent's global config directory and will affect ALL workspaces for those agents on this machine.
To install only into the current workspace, rerun with --scope=workspace.

Error: open compatibility skills root directory "C:\\gentle-repro\\home\\.agents\\skills": compatibility target is not a physical directory

# gentle-ai sync --agents claude-code   (exit code 1)
Error: open compatibility skills root directory "C:\\gentle-repro\\home\\.agents\\skills": compatibility target is not a physical directory
```

### Additional Context

The direct-CLI transcript above is from running gentle-ai 2.7.0 against a throwaway `.agents\skills` junction set up as in Steps to Reproduce. The boxed "Installation completed with errors" transcript below is a second occurrence of the same underlying refusal, from the interactive TUI form, and comes from a screenshot together with an Explorer view of a 23 item `.agents\skills` directory:

```
Installation completed with errors.

Failed steps
  X install
    open compatibility skills root directory "C:\\Users\\patri\\.agents\\skills": compatibility target is not a physical directory

What to do
  1. Check the error messages above
  2. Fix the underlying issue (missing deps, permissions, etc.)
  3. Run gentle-ai again to retry

Press Enter to exit.
```

Which kind of reparse point the reporter's directory is was not established; the screenshot shows a reparse point that Explorer lists as a populated directory. The refusal that names no continuation is raised in `internal/cli/compatibility_transaction_windows.go` at line 466 and reached through the wrapping call at line 238 (the interactive TUI's generic recovery block that also names no continuation is rendered separately, in `internal/tui/screens/complete.go`); the sibling check that already names a continuation for an analogous condition is in `internal/cli/compatibility_skills.go` at line 149.

title: bug(pi): facade inspect refuses immutable transport before offering a review route
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

title: doctor: tool:gga PATH check is hardcoded (coreTools) and ignores state.json components → permanent false "unhealthy" after deregistration
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

`doctor`'s tool-existence checks are built from a hardcoded `coreTools` constant, not from the user's persisted component selection. Once a user removes a component (e.g. `gga`) from `state.json.components`, `sync` and `update` respect the choice, but `doctor` keeps emitting `[xx] tool:gga → unhealthy` unconditionally. There is no supported non-interactive way to reconcile the two sources of truth (`uninstall --components` removes files and prunes `installed_agents`, but never touches the `components` array).

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. On a machine where `gga` is no longer on PATH, remove `"gga"` from `components` in `~/.gentle-ai/state.json` (manually — no supported command prunes that field)
2. `gentle-ai sync` → reports no managed actions; gga is not re-added
3. `gentle-ai update` → gga is neutral: `[--] gga installed: -`
4. `gentle-ai doctor` → `[xx] tool:gga not found in PATH`, `Status: unhealthy` persists

### ✅ Expected Behavior

`doctor` derives per-component `tool:` checks from `state.json.components` (gated by `selection_configured`, with a fallback to checking all core tools when no state exists, preserving first-install contracts). A tool the user deselected → check omitted, never a hard `[xx]`.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

`requiredDoctorTools` unconditionally appends `coreTools = {"gentle-ai","gga","engram"}` (`internal/cli/doctor.go:32-36,140-159`). `RunDoctor` reads only `InstalledAgents` from state (`internal/cli/doctor.go:128-134`) and never `Components`, so `exec.LookPath("gga")` failure is unconditional. The only ways to silence it are reinstalling a binary the user explicitly opted out of, or changing the preset via the interactive TUI / full `install` run (which rewrites agent configs).

### Gentle AI Version

gentle-ai 2.7.0

### Operating System

Windows

### AI Agent / Client

OpenCode

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
[xx]  tool:gga            gga not found in PATH
     Remedy: Install gga or add its directory to PATH
Summary: 9 passed, 1 failed — Status: unhealthy
```

### Additional Context

Consumer divergence observed on 2.7.0 (all verified against current main):

- `sync` restores persisted `Components` verbatim (`internal/state/state.go:193-200`, `internal/cli/sync.go:411-416`) — respects the removal
- `update` reads a static registry (`internal/update/registry.go`) and renders not-detected as neutral `[--]` (`internal/update/render.go:79-80`) — looks like it respects state, actually a different severity policy
- `doctor` ignores `Components` entirely — hardcoded `coreTools`
- `uninstall --components --yes` (requires `--agent`) deletes managed files and prunes `installed_agents` only (`components/uninstall/service.go:1714-1753`), never `state.components`; `install --components` is whole-list replacement and a live run rewrites configs

Minimal fix shape: gate `gga`/`engram` (keep `gentle-ai` always) in `requiredDoctorTools` on `state.Components` gated by `SelectionConfigured`; omitting the check is preferred over introducing a new doctor status. Do NOT re-derive from `state.preset` — `ComponentsForPreset` hardcodes gga in `full-gentleman`/`ecosystem-only` (`internal/model/presets.go:28-36`), which would resurface the bug. Fallback (no/unreadable state) must keep checking all core tools.

Tests pinning current behavior: `internal/cli/doctor_test.go:1003-1020` (byte-exact golden incl. `[ok] tool:gga` with no-components state), `:1225-1239`, `:1246-1267` (`TestCheckToolBinaries_StateMissing_ChecksCoreOnly`).

title: bug(review): intended-untracked selection rejects exact binding as schema-incompatible
body:
## Observed behavior

A Pi compact-review controller can discover an intended-untracked selection for a normal workspace candidate, but submitting the exact provider-issued selection fails before a review lineage starts with a typed `schema-incompatible` native operation failure.

No source mutation, commit, push, review lineage, receipt, or review capture was created.

## Sanitized environment

- Gentle AI: 2.6.0 (stable)
- Pi client: 0.85.1
- Node.js: 22.22.2
- Platform: Linux x86_64
- Review mode: globally enabled
- Review integration: negotiated v2 / Pi compact controller

## Minimal reproduction

1. In a disposable Git workspace, create a candidate containing intended untracked files plus ordinary tracked changes.
2. Enable receipt-driven development.
3. Call the Pi controller's read-only `inspect` operation with the selected workspace root.
4. Observe a current-changes projection whose next transition requests intended-untracked selection and supplies a provider-owned selection binding plus an eligible ordered path list.
5. Submit that exact binding and the complete ordered eligible path list through `select-intended-untracked`.
6. Observe the typed result: native operation failed, `schema-incompatible`, no lineage created, and no mutation performed.

## Expected behavior

The exact provider-issued intended-untracked selection should be accepted when its target, projection, inventory and ordered eligible path list still match. The controller should then provide the normal next transition, or return a precise selection-validation failure when the caller-provided selection is invalid.

## Actual behavior

The exact binding plus full ordered path list was rejected as `schema-incompatible` before review start. The result reported `lineage_created: false` and `mutation_outcome: none`, so the required RDD review cannot begin.

## Preserved state

- Candidate source state preserved.
- No review lineage or receipt.
- No commit, push, PR, or source mutation performed by the review operation.
- The integration was reinstalled after an extension update; binary installation then succeeded. The schema failure remained after repair.

## Related reports checked

- #2981: status discovery fails before lifecycle start; not equivalent because this status discovery succeeds and the failure is at intended-untracked selection.
- #2013: managed OpenCode capture preflight schema mismatch; related schema-bound integration class but different controller, operation and stage.

## Acceptance criteria

- An exact current selection binding with its complete ordered eligible list succeeds when unchanged.
- Invalid or reordered selections fail with an actionable, schema-specific validation explanation.
- A failure before review start preserves candidate state and creates no lineage or receipt.
- Regression coverage exercises inspect -> intended-untracked selection using untracked app files and tracked companion changes.

title: bug(2.7.0): capture-result refuses a canonical proof path containing spaces — admission tokenizes evidence on whitespace and adjudicates the trailing fragment
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

Automated provider defect report.

`review capture-result` refuses a reviewer artifact as `out_of_scope` when the cited path **is** a changed path of the frozen candidate, because that path **contains spaces**. Admission tokenizes free-text evidence on whitespace, so a canonical repository-relative path is split and only its trailing fragment is adjudicated against the base∪candidate trees.

The reviewer emitted a correct, fully-qualified path:

```
docs/Changelog/<note title with spaces> (08-09-2026).md:6
```

Admission reported the offending token as:

```
(08-09-2026).md:6   reason: unknown_or_malformed_repository_path
```

The trailing fragment is what remains after splitting on the last space. It contains `.`, so it matches the `X:NNN` citation shape, is adjudicated as a repository path, is absent from the manifest, and the whole artifact is refused.

This is the mechanism already mapped in #3042 by a maintainer comment against `v2.3.0`: `referenceOutsideRepository` (`internal/reviewtransaction/artifact_admission.go`) "tokenizes free text on whitespace/quotes and adjudicates every token shaped `X:NNN` where `X` contains `/` or `.`". #3042 was closed as completed, but its fix addressed a **different** sub-cause of that class — a reviewer citing a bare basename instead of the repository-relative path (see the `transition-binding.schema.json:12` occurrence). That sub-cause is caller-correctable; **this one is not**: the reviewer's citation is already canonical, and the only way for a caller to avoid it is to have no spaces anywhere in the repository's paths.

Impact scales with how a repository names files. In the affected repository 135 of 139 tracked files under `docs/` contain a space, so no Markdown-bearing candidate can reach a terminal receipt.

Related, none equivalent:
- #3042 (closed) — same causal class and the source of the mechanism map; fixed sub-cause is bare-basename citation, not whitespace splitting of a canonical path.
- #2029 (open) — the inverse case: the reviewer abbreviates the path and admission is correct to reject it.
- #3044, #4039 (closed) — spaces in `cwd`/client-binary paths on Windows; a different surface (invocation quoting, not evidence adjudication).

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. In a repository whose tracked paths contain spaces, stage a Markdown-only change including at least one file whose repository-relative path contains a space followed by a parenthesized token, e.g. `docs/Changelog/<note title with spaces> (08-09-2026).md`.
2. Run the selectorless preflight, select the untracked paths if prompted, and run the returned `review start` with `--consent granted`. Risk resolves to `medium`; one lens (`review-reliability`) is selected.
3. Run the exact `review capture-result` tokens returned by the bound `review status` (in-process capture: tokens carry `--agent` and no `--input`).
4. Observe the refusal. Re-query the bound `review status`; it re-offers the identical slot. Relaunch the re-offered capture once.
5. Observe the identical refusal. Four admission attempts total (two per capture invocation, each retried once internally as a "corrective attempt").

### ✅ Expected Behavior

An artifact whose every cited path is a changed path of the frozen candidate is admitted, regardless of whether those paths contain spaces.

Path adjudication should resolve citations against the frozen changed-path manifest by longest match rather than by whitespace tokenization, so that a canonical repository-relative path containing spaces is recognized as the manifest entry it exactly matches.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Every capture attempt is refused. The lineage cannot reach a terminal receipt and stays in `reviewing` with zero admitted results.

The refusal names as the offending token a fragment that the reviewer never emitted — it is produced by admission's own tokenizer — so the diagnostic points at a string that does not exist in the artifact.

All three findings in the refused artifact were severity `SUGGESTION`; none were blocking. The candidate is refused on citation grammar alone, not on review outcome.

### Gentle AI Version

v2.7.0 (stable)

### Operating System

macOS

### AI Agent / Client

Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
# capture-result, both admission attempts, both invocations
{
  "schema": "gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2",
  "contract": "gentle-ai.review-integration/v2",
  "operation": "review.capture-result",
  "phase": "preflight",
  "code": "invalid_request",
  "message": "The negotiated review request is invalid.",
  "mutation_outcome": "not_started",
  "authority_applicability": "not_evaluated",
  "retry_safe": true,
  "replayability": "not_replayable",
  "required_inputs": [],
  "next_action": "correct_request",
  "cause": "provider reviewer result was refused on both admission attempts:
    attempt 1: reviewer artifact admission out_of_scope: reviewer proof references
    a path outside the frozen repository;
    admission_diagnostic={\"code\":\"proof_path_out_of_scope\",
                          \"finding_id\":\"R3-001\",
                          \"location\":\"(08-09-2026).md:6\",
                          \"reason\":\"unknown_or_malformed_repository_path\"};
    corrective attempt 2: reviewer artifact admission out_of_scope: reviewer evidence
    references a path outside the frozen repository;
    admission_diagnostic={\"code\":\"evidence_path_out_of_scope\",
                          \"location\":\"(08-09-2026).md:6\",
                          \"reason\":\"unknown_or_malformed_repository_path\"}"
}

# what the reviewer actually emitted (from the preserved rejected payload)
"location": "docs/Changelog/<note title with spaces> (08-09-2026).md:6",
"proof_refs": ["docs/Changelog/<note title with spaces> (08-09-2026).md:6"]

# every finding location in the refused artifact — all four paths contain spaces
docs/Changelog/<note title with spaces> (08-09-2026).md:6
docs/analisis/<note title with spaces> (2026-09-08).md:114
docs/<two word name>.md:10-11
docs/Changelog/<note title with spaces> (08-09-2026).md:1
```

### Additional Context

**Operation shape:** selectorless `review status` → `--untracked-scope=select` with two `--intended-untracked` paths → `review start --consent granted` → bound `review status` → `review capture-result` (in-process, `--agent`, no `--input`).

**Candidate:** projection `workspace`, 3 changed files, 138 changed lines, risk `medium`, one selected lens `review-reliability` at order 0, correction budget 69. Changed-path manifest: 1 modified tracked Markdown file, 2 added intended-untracked Markdown files. All three paths contain spaces.

**Opaque identifiers:** lineage `review-d9e722c6c12b258e`, authority revision `sha256:4de8d530…`, target identity `sha256:dc75720a…`, subject hash `sha256:4217179f…`.

**Bounded attempts:** 2 `capture-result` invocations, each refused on both its admission attempts (4 total). Between them, the bound `review status` was re-queried and re-offered the identical slot (same lineage, expected-revision, target, repository-context, lens, order, subject-hash), which is why exactly one relaunch was made. No blind retry beyond the re-offered slot.

**Mutation outcome:** `not_started` on every attempt. Rejected payloads preserved by the tool under `.git/gentle-ai/rejected-results/<lineage>/`.

**Preserved state:** nothing was forced, reset, or worked around. The kill switch was not touched and receipt-driven development remains enabled. The lineage remains in `reviewing` with zero admitted results. Delivery for this candidate follows ordinary repository policy.

**Note on the obvious workaround:** renaming the affected files is not a targeted fix here — every finding in the artifact cites a path with spaces, including a pre-existing tracked file, so renaming would mean renaming the repository's documentation tree and rewriting its relative links to accommodate the tokenizer.

title: bug(engram): sync exports relations whose scope-filtered endpoints are missing, stalling --import for the whole store
body:
## Problem

`engram sync` filters observations by scope when exporting a chunk, but does not apply
the same filter to relation mutations. A chunk can therefore carry a relation whose
endpoint observation was withheld by the scope filter. That chunk is valid on the machine
that wrote it and permanently unimportable anywhere else.

Because `engram sync --import` stops at the first chunk it cannot apply, one such chunk
freezes the whole team's shared memory: every later chunk stays pending behind it
indefinitely.

This report records observed integration evidence only; it does not claim a confirmed
root cause beyond the export/import asymmetry described below.

## Environment

- `gentle-ai 2.6.0` (stable channel), `engram 1.20.0`
- Platform: macOS Darwin arm64
- Transport: local git-committed chunk store (`engram sync` / `engram sync --import`).
  **No Engram Cloud involved** — this deployment is deliberately cloud-free.
- Scope model: a shared store holding only `project`-scope observations for one project;
  contributors also hold `personal`-scope observations locally.

## Expected behavior

A chunk that `engram sync` produces is importable by `engram sync --import` on any other
machine. If a relation's endpoint cannot be exported because the scope filter excludes
it, the relation should be excluded too, rather than exported without its endpoint.

## Actual behavior

One chunk in the store carries:

- 2 observations
- 71 relation mutations, referencing 29 distinct observation ids
- 27 of those 29 ids exist in **no chunk of the store** — they are endpoints the scope
  filter withheld (personal scope or another project)

Import stalls on it and never advances:

```text
engram: dependency-safe local import stalled after 1 pass(es); chunk <chunk-id>:
apply chunk mutation 8: relation FK precondition not met: referenced observation
missing; pending session dependencies: <session-id>
```

`engram sync --status` then reports a pending count that never drains:

```text
Local chunks:    46
Remote chunks:   29
Pending import:  1
```

The failure is not transient: it reproduces on every import, on every machine that pulls
the store, because the missing endpoints were never in the store to begin with.

## Minimal reproduction

1. On machine A, hold observations in two scopes for the same project: at least one
   `project`-scope observation and one `personal`-scope observation.
2. Create a relation between them (for example, by resolving a `judgment_required`
   candidate where the candidate is the personal-scope observation).
3. Run `engram sync` and commit the resulting chunk to the shared store.
4. On machine B, pull the store and run `engram sync --import`.
5. The import stalls on that chunk with the FK precondition above, and every chunk
   created after it stays pending.

## Why this is hard to recover from downstream

The asymmetry is the operational problem: machine A can still enumerate which
observations exist, so it could detect the inconsistency at export time. Machine B can
only fail — the endpoint is not merely unapplied, it was never transmitted. So the broken
chunk cannot be repaired from the consuming side, and editing chunk files by hand is not
a supported operation.

A consumer-side mitigation is possible but only prevents *new* damage: validating, before
publishing, that every relation endpoint in a new chunk resolves somewhere in the store,
and refusing to publish otherwise. It cannot heal a chunk already in the store.

## Suggested direction

Apply the export scope filter transitively: a relation is exportable only when both of
its endpoints are. Alternatively, make `--import` skip an unappliable relation mutation
and continue, so one unresolvable relation degrades to a missing edge instead of halting
the entire import queue.

## Relationship to existing reports

- #2669 — also an FK failure on applying a relation, but on the **Engram Cloud autosync
  pull** path, and it explicitly reports `Pending import: 0` with converged chunk state.
  This report is the cloud-free chunk transport, where the chunk itself is internally
  inconsistent at export time.
- #2389 (closed) — pending mutations **missing required fields** (`session.id`,
  `prompt.content`, `observation.title`) blocking a cloud replication health check. Here
  the mutations are well-formed; the problem is a referenced entity that was filtered out.

No credentials, absolute paths, host names, user names, project names, environment
values, memory contents, or source contents are included in this report. Counts and
shapes only; identifiers are redacted.

title: bug(review): provider refuses every capture including verbatim forecasts seconds after STATUS; two lineages stuck in correction_required
body:

### 📝 Bug Description

On two ordinary review lineages, the provider refuses every capture, including materialize forecasts resubmitted verbatim seconds after the STATUS that issued them. Reads (inspect, START, STATUS) keep working. Both lineages are stuck in `correction_required` (generation 1). One lineage captured its correction plan (4 lines, epoch 2) but never converged; the other never admitted the plan (epoch 1, two verbatim refusals after worktree edits). No convergent transition is ever offered. This report describes observed behavior only; no root cause is asserted.

2. Drive captures to `correction_required`.
3. Run any bound capture verbatim, including a forecast resubmitted with acknowledgement seconds after STATUS.
4. Observe refusal; re-query STATUS and retry, refusal repeats identically; lineage stays `correction_required`.

Captures run verbatim within their horizon, or a typed recoverable failure names a caller-actionable exit (recover, abandon, or fresh START route).
