title: bug(engram): beta upgrade/install path misses Engram v2 RC and fails when brew is absent
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

   > Repro confirmed on `gentle-ai 2.7.0-rc.1`: one failure in `upgrade engram` when `brew` is absent, and a second failure where
 beta install lands on legacy `engram@main` instead of `engram/v2@v2.0.0-rc.8`.

The current Engram beta path in `gentle-ai` shows two separate failures in the same workflow:

   1. **`gentle-ai upgrade engram` hard-fails when `brew` is not on `PATH`**, even when the active Engram binary is not
 Homebrew-managed.
   2. **`gentle-ai install --component engram --channel beta` does not install the latest Engram v2 RC**, and instead leaves Engram
 on the legacy non-`/v2` line.

   I reproduced this immediately after updating `gentle-ai` itself to `v2.7.0-rc.1`.

   Observed result:

   - `gentle-ai` updated correctly to `2.7.0-rc.1`
   - the latest published Engram prerelease is `v2.0.0-rc.8`
   - but the beta install/update flow through `gentle-ai` did **not** reach that version

   Instead:

   - `upgrade engram` failed before updating anything
   - `install --component engram --channel beta` completed, but left:
     `engram 1.20.1-0.20260902040530-5b2f08fad025`

   That means the beta path currently does not reliably deliver the intended Engram v2 RC line.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

   1. Update `gentle-ai` to the current RC:
      ```bash
      go install github.com/gentleman-programming/gentle-ai/v2/cmd/gentle-ai@v2.7.0-rc.1
      gentle-ai sync
 ```

 2. Confirm versions:
    ```bash
      gentle-ai --version
      engram --version
    ```

 3. Use a setup where:
     - brew is not available on PATH
     - engram resolves from a user-managed location
     - example active binary path:
       ```bash
         ~/.local/bin/engram -> ~/go/bin/engram
       ```

 4. Run:
    ```bash
      GENTLE_AI_CHANNEL=beta GENTLE_AI_YES=1 gentle-ai upgrade engram
    ```

 5. Observe that the update check fails with a Homebrew ownership/detection error instead of falling back cleanly.

 6. Then run:
    ```bash
      GENTLE_AI_YES=1 gentle-ai install --component engram --channel beta
    ```

 7. Check the installed Engram version:
    ```bash
      engram --version
      go version -m ~/.local/bin/engram

### ✅ Expected Behavior

 For the beta channel Engram path:

 - GENTLE_AI_CHANNEL=beta gentle-ai upgrade engram should not fail just because brew is absent when the active binary is not
   Homebrew-managed.
 - gentle-ai install --component engram --channel beta should install the current intended Engram beta/RC line.
 - Given the currently published prerelease state, the resulting binary should resolve to:
     - module: github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/v2
     - version: v2.0.0-rc.8

### ❌ Actual Behavior

#### Failure 1 — upgrade path

 ```shell
   $ GENTLE_AI_CHANNEL=beta GENTLE_AI_YES=1 gentle-ai upgrade engram
   Update Check
   ============

     [!!] engram        installed: -           latest: -           check failed: detect Homebrew ownership for engram: list Homebrew
 formulae: exec: "brew": executable file not found in $PATH; inspect `brew list --formula --full-name`, `brew list --cask
 --full-name`, and `command -v engram`

   Update check incomplete: 1 tool(s) failed to check.
   Error: update check failed for: engram
 ```

 #### Failure 2 — beta install path

 ```shell
   $ GENTLE_AI_YES=1 gentle-ai install --component engram --channel beta
   ...
   engram 1.20.1-0.20260902040530-5b2f08fad025
 ```

 And the installed binary confirms the legacy non-/v2 line:

 ```shell
   $ engram --version
   engram 1.20.1-0.20260902040530-5b2f08fad025

   $ go version -m ~/.local/bin/engram
   /Users/<user>/.local/bin/engram: go1.26.8
           path    github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/cmd/engram
           mod     github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram  v1.20.1-0.20260902040530-5b2f08fad025
 ```

### Gentle AI Version

 2.7.0-rc.1

### Operating System

macOS

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
$ gentle-ai --version
   gentle-ai 2.7.0-rc.1

   $ engram --version
   engram 2.0.0-rc.1

   $ GENTLE_AI_CHANNEL=beta GENTLE_AI_YES=1 gentle-ai upgrade engram
   Update Check
   ============

     [!!] engram        installed: -           latest: -           check failed: detect Homebrew ownership for engram: list Homebrew
 formulae: exec: "brew": executable file not found in $PATH; inspect `brew list --formula --full-name`, `brew list --cask
 --full-name`, and `command -v engram`

   Update check incomplete: 1 tool(s) failed to check.
   Error: update check failed for: engram

   $ GENTLE_AI_YES=1 gentle-ai install --component engram --channel beta
   ...
   go: downloading github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram v1.20.1-0.20260902040530-5b2f08fad025
   ...
   Installed npm:gentle-engram
   ...
   [ok] verify:engram:binary - engram binary on PATH (restart shell if missing)
   [ok] verify:engram:version - engram version returns valid output

   $ engram --version
   engram 1.20.1-0.20260902040530-5b2f08fad025

   $ go version -m ~/.local/bin/engram
   /Users/<user>/.local/bin/engram: go1.26.8
           path    github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/cmd/engram
           mod     github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram  v1.20.1-0.20260902040530-5b2f08fad025
```

### Additional Context

#### Verified current release/RC state

 I verified these separately outside the failing gentle-ai flow:

 ```bash
   curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/Gentleman-Programming/engram/releases?per_page=20 | grep -E '"tag_name"|"prerelease"' |
 head -n 30
 ```

 This shows the newest prerelease as:

 - v2.0.0-rc.8

 And Go module resolution confirms the v2 RC line exists and resolves correctly:

 ```bash
   go list -m github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/v2@latest
 ```

 Resolved result:

 - github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/v2 v2.0.0-rc.8

 By contrast, the legacy non-/v2 line resolves separately:

 ```bash
   go list -m github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram@main
 ```

 Resolved result:

 - github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram v1.20.1-0.20260902040530-5b2f08fad025

 #### Why this looks actionable / likely touchpoints

 I am NOT asserting root cause, only pointing to the smallest likely area to inspect first:

 - the Engram beta upgrade/install path appears to still reach the legacy module line:
     - github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram
     - instead of:
     - github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/v2

 - separately, the upgrade engram path appears to fail closed on a Homebrew ownership probe when brew is absent, instead of treating
   the tool as non-brew-managed and continuing/falling back appropriately

 These may be one bug or two adjacent bugs, but they surfaced from one user workflow.

 #### Manual workaround that succeeded

 Manual direct install of the v2 RC works correctly:

 ```bash
   go install github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/v2/cmd/engram@v2.0.0-rc.8
 ```

 After that:

 ```bash
   $ engram --version
   engram 2.0.0-rc.8

   $ go version -m ~/.local/bin/engram
   path    github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/v2/cmd/engram
   mod     github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/v2  v2.0.0-rc.8
 ```

 So the published RC itself is good and installable; the problem is specifically the gentle-ai beta/update path.

title: bug(review): regression — negotiated intended-untracked START still rejected with stale_target_identity on 2.5.0, which contains the #2872 fix
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

On stable `2.5.0` with Claude Code, a negotiated workspace review cannot reach native admission when the candidate includes intended untracked paths. Negotiated STATUS returns `collect` / `intended_untracked_selection_required`; supplying the exact eligible selection returns `execute` / `fresh_target_ready` with an exact `review.start` operation and its ordered argument tokens; running those tokens verbatim fails with typed `stale_target_identity` (`review start target does not match the freshly built snapshot`), `mutation_outcome: not_started`.

This is the observable defect of #2872, which was closed as completed by #3998 (`bb43f9a`).

**This build provably contains that fix.** Comparing that commit against tag `v2.5.0` reports `status: ahead`, `ahead_by: 1`, `behind_by: 0`, and the `v2.5.0` release notes state that "the intended-untracked selection handoff executes the printed START transition verbatim". The reproduction below is on that build, so it is recorded here as a possible regression rather than as another occurrence on #2872. #2872 was not reopened.

Observed evidence only; no root cause is asserted.

**Why this is not one of the neighbouring reports**

- #4323 (Pi, `2.6.1`): there START re-derives a *different*, selection-less target and re-offers the selection. Here START receives and rejects the exact target STATUS issued, and never re-offers.
- #4005 (Pi, `2.5.0-rc.3`): there the collection binding cannot be captured at all. Here the CLI accepted the selection and produced a complete START transition.
- #4074: there the candidate is made only of untracked files. This candidate also has tracked modifications.
- #2957: no intended-untracked selection was involved, and the second attempt there fails with `invalid_request`. Here every attempt fails identically with `stale_target_identity`.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Prepare a workspace candidate with 3 tracked modifications plus eligible non-ignored untracked files.
2. Run the selectorless negotiated status: `gentle-ai review status --cwd <repo> --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --agent claude-code --next-transition`.
3. Observe `next_transition.kind: collect`, `reason_code: intended_untracked_selection_required`, an `eligible_paths_json` list, and an `expected_untracked_inventory` digest.
4. Re-run status with `--untracked-scope=select`, `--expected-untracked-inventory=<digest from step 3>`, and one `--intended-untracked=<path>` per selected path.
5. Observe `next_transition.kind: execute`, `reason_code: fresh_target_ready`, `operation: review.start`, with its ordered argument tokens including `--target=<identity>` and `--lineage=<id>`.
6. Run `gentle-ai review start` with those exact tokens, unchanged and in the returned order.
7. Observe the typed failure below.

**Bounded attempts and outcomes** — 4 START attempts, each preceded by a freshly derived STATUS. Every one returned `mutation_outcome: not_started`; no lineage was created and the candidate was preserved.

- 3 consecutive STATUS calls returned the identical target identity, so the candidate did not drift between derivation and execution.
- Reproduced with and without an explicit `--cwd` on the status call.
- Reproduced with every eligible untracked path selected, and again with one unrelated eligible untracked file excluded. The identity and the failure were identical in both.
- Substituting the projection's `intended_untracked_proof` for the collect binding's `expected_untracked_inventory` is rejected earlier with `invalid_request` / "untracked inventory changed", which confirms the inventory digest used in the reproducing runs is the canonical one.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

`review start` accepts the exact target identity that negotiated STATUS issued for the same unchanged candidate, and freezes the lineage so the review can reach native admission.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

`review start` rejects its own provider-issued target before native admission. STATUS and START disagree on the snapshot identity for an unchanged candidate, so the lifecycle cannot advance and no receipt can be produced.

### Gentle AI Version

2.5.0

### Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client

Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
{
  "schema": "gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2",
  "contract": "gentle-ai.review-integration/v2",
  "operation": "review.start",
  "phase": "preflight",
  "code": "stale_target_identity",
  "message": "The negotiated review request no longer matches the live workspace snapshot; re-derive the exact next transition before retrying.",
  "mutation_outcome": "not_started",
  "authority_applicability": "not_evaluated",
  "retry_safe": true,
  "replayability": "not_replayable",
  "required_inputs": [],
  "next_action": "review.status",
  "cause": "review start target does not match the freshly built snapshot"
}
```

### Additional Context

- Explicit user consent was obtained to report this apparent provider defect.
- Open and closed issues were searched with exact and broad symptom queries (`stale_target_identity`, intended-untracked START, review start snapshot) before this report.
- Final privacy scan completed immediately before creation: no raw argv, absolute paths, private project names, usernames, hostnames, credentials, diffs, source contents, or environment values are included.
- Architecture: x86_64. Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`. Projection: `workspace`.
- Receipt-driven development was enabled at global scope; the effective mode was `on`.

title: Skip intended-untracked selection gate when inventory is empty or projection is committed-only
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Problem Statement

START is blocked on `intended_untracked_selection_required` even when the requested candidate is a committed-only range, and satisfying the gate means submitting a large opaque selection binding that agents must transcribe inline (one such submission was rejected). The practical workaround found was to commit every file first so `eligible_untracked_inventory` becomes empty and the gate auto-satisfies — but that forces committing before review and is undiscoverable.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Skip the intended-untracked selection step entirely when:

- `eligible_untracked_inventory` is empty, or
- the START selector is `committedOnly`.

In both cases there is nothing for the selection to affect; the gate only adds a rejected-submission hazard.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

_No response_

### 📎 Additional Context

Related cluster: #4311, #4323, #4005, #3924, #4187 (intended-untracked selection binding capture/rejection family). Observed on 2.6.0.

title: ABANDON: echo exact input schema, current revision, and allowed reasons on native-input-required
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Problem Statement

`review abandon` required three attempts to succeed:

1. `capturedLensResults` as a scalar count was rejected — the field must be an array of captured lens results; the shape is not documented anywhere in the blocked envelope.
2. After a blocked attempt the expected revision changed concurrently, so the next attempt failed with `review transaction changed concurrently: expected ... current ...` until a fresh STATUS was read.
3. The `reason` field is constrained to undocumented tokens (`operator_disposition` | `retired_schema`); the constraint was only discoverable from stderr after a rejection.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

The `native-input-required` envelope for ABANDON should echo, in one place:

- the complete expected input schema with field names and types (including that `capturedLensResults` is an array),
- the current compact revision to use,
- the full list of allowed `reason` values.

With that, ABANDON succeeds on the first well-formed attempt.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

_No response_

### 📎 Additional Context

Related: #1612 (echo the binding format in errors). Observed on 2.6.0.

title: pi-host-relay: subprocess transport failure leaves reviewer slot pending without retry semantics
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

An acknowledged reviewer run through `pi-host-relay` failed with a subprocess transport failure (`kind: pi-failed`, `exit_code: null`, elapsed ~133s, "pi subprocess failed"). No reviewer output was produced and `mutation_performed` is false, so nothing was admitted — but the slot is left pending with no automatic retry, no retryable flag, and no subprocess diagnostic (stderr tail, exit reason) in the failure envelope. Recovery requires a fresh STATUS and an exactly re-offered binding, and replaying the capture is explicitly forbidden.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. START an ordinary committed-only lineage (2 files, medium tier, `review-reliability` lens).
2. Capture the forecast, then resubmit the same binding with the reviewer run acknowledged.
3. The host relay spawns the reviewer subprocess; the subprocess exits without producing a result after ~133 seconds.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

A subprocess-level failure before any admission is safe to retry: either one automatic retry with backoff, or the failure envelope marks the slot retryable so the driver can resubmit without re-materializing anything. The failure envelope should include a bounded diagnostic tail (last N lines of subprocess stderr) so the cause is visible.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

```json
{"tool":"gentle_review_capture","status":"blocked","outcome":"pi-host-relay-transport-failure","failure":{"kind":"pi-failed","stage":"pi","exit_code":null,"timed_out":false,"elapsed_ms":133632,"timeout_ms":7200000},"reason":"pi subprocess failed","mutation_performed":false,"mutation_outcome":"none","next_action":"Call fresh STATUS and submit only an exact reoffered one-slot binding; never replay this capture from transcript inference."}
```

### Gentle AI Version

2.6.0 (v2.6.0-174-g57efc6b5)

### Operating System

macOS

Other

Other

title: Support explicit end ref for committed-range review candidates (baseRef..endRef)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Problem Statement

`baseRef` + `committedOnly` diffs the base tree against **current HEAD** only. Reviewing one historical commit therefore requires checking that commit out (detached HEAD) before START. Starting from a branch tip by accident produced a 180-file / 36,950-line lineage that had to be abandoned (`operator_disposition`) and relaunched once per work unit with a detached checkout — review scope ended up depending on worktree state instead of an explicit selector.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Accept an explicit end ref so START scopes a committed range `baseRef..endRef` without touching HEAD:

```
gentle-ai review start --base-ref=<sha> --head-ref=<sha> --committed-only
```

Alternatively, document the detached-HEAD requirement as normative for per-unit review of committed work.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

Detached-HEAD-per-unit works but couples review scoping to worktree manipulation and invites accidental whole-branch candidates.

### 📎 Additional Context

Committed-range walks are already practiced through the direct CLI route (see gentle-pi session reports #577, #581, #582); this gap is in the negotiated/facade START selector. Observed on 2.6.0.

- the inline string form remains supported as a fallback for small bindings.

```

_No response_

title: bug(opencode): skill-registry startup refresh never runs in git-less workspaces (worktree resolves to /)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

The OpenCode `skill-registry` startup plugin resolves the `--cwd` passed to `gentle-ai skill-registry refresh` as `input.worktree || input.directory || process.cwd()`. In a session started inside a directory that is not a git repository, OpenCode populates `worktree` with the filesystem root `/` (its `Project.fromDirectory` fallback for non-git directories). The plugin therefore passes `/` to the guard, the guard rejects it, and the startup refresh silently never runs — even for workspaces that carry project markers and that the CLI accepts when the real directory is passed via `--cwd`.

This is the residue of two intentional fixes: #1731 flipped the preference to `worktree` first (so startups from a nested directory of a git repository refresh at the repo root), and #3350 added the CLI guard plus plugin validation that made the `/` case fail quiet instead of loud. The combination means a git-less workspace gets neither behavior: no refresh, and only the one stderr line as a hint.

Observed on macOS with the OpenCode Bun runtime; the plugin bytes are identical across platforms, so this should be OS-agnostic.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Install gentle-ai v2.5.0+ (plugin bytes unchanged through current main) with the OpenCode integration so the managed `skill-registry.ts` plugin is deployed.
2. Create a directory that is not a git repository but is a valid workspace — for example a folder containing several independently cloned repositories — and give it a project marker the CLI guard accepts (an empty `skills/` directory suffices).
3. Start `opencode` from that directory and wait for startup to finish.
4. Run `gentle-ai skill-registry refresh --cwd <that directory>` manually for comparison.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

When `input.worktree` is the filesystem root (git-less session), the plugin should fall back to the real session directory before the guard runs, so a marker-carrying git-less workspace refreshes at startup exactly like a git repository does.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Every startup in the git-less workspace prints the skip line to stderr and no `.atl/skill-registry.md` is created. The manual CLI call with the real directory succeeds, proving the guard itself accepts the workspace; only the plugin's cwd resolution never hands it over.

### Gentle AI Version

v2.6.0

### Operating System

macOS

### AI Agent / Client

OpenCode

### 📋 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
[skill-registry] skipping refresh: not a project root: /
```

### Additional Context

- Lineage: #823 added the startup refresh; #1731 made it prefer the git worktree root; #3350 made the `/` case fail quiet. None covers a git-less session, where OpenCode reports `worktree: /` (documented in the opencode repository — issues describing `Project.fromDirectory` setting `worktree: '/'` for non-git directories).
- Proposed fix (deployed and verified in a consumer setup, then dual-review judged): when `input.worktree` is empty or equals `parse(input.worktree).root`, use `input.directory || process.cwd()`. Guard behavior for `/`, `$HOME`, and markerless directories is unchanged; `PROJECT_MARKERS` and its Go parity contract are untouched.
- Test extension point: `internal/assets/skill_registry_plugin_guard_test.go` already runs the real plugin under node with a fake `gentle-ai` recording argv; a `worktree: "/"` plus project-marker directory case pins the fallback.

title: bug(2.6.0): capture-result fails with a missing-file repository_context_capture_failed, then the bound lineage reports as not held by its own repository
body:
### Automated provider-defect report

### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] Searched open and closed issues for the failure code, the lineage-ownership symptom, and the missing-file cause; no equivalent report was found. Nearest neighbours were reviewed and ruled out (see below).
- [x] This report contains observed evidence only and does not assert an unconfirmed root cause.
- [x] Privacy review removed private project names, paths, users, hosts, credentials, raw arguments, source, diffs, and environment values.

### Environment

- gentle-ai: 2.6.0 (stable channel; no `-rc.` or `-main.` tag)
- OS/arch: Darwin arm64
- Client: claude-code
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`
- Projection: `workspace`
- Risk tier: medium (5 changed files, 48 changed lines)
- Repository shape: ordinary local Git repository, not a worktree (`--git-dir` and `--git-common-dir` both resolve to the same plain `.git`)

### Bug Description

A negotiated medium-risk review starts successfully and freezes a lineage in `state: reviewing`, but the collection step cannot proceed and the lineage then becomes unreachable from the very repository that created it.

Two observations, in order:

1. The provider-issued `review.capture-result` for the single selected `review-reliability` lens fails at `phase: "preflight"` with:

   ```
   code: invalid_request
   cause: repository_context_capture_failed: provider-issued review repository context operation failed;
          cause: open <redacted> no such file or directory;
          retry capture-result with the same exact binding or refresh status
   mutation_outcome: not_started
   retry_safe: true
   ```

2. Following the contract's recovery rule, the exact bound `review.status` (the command returned by the transaction's own `next_transition`, run unchanged with the repository as process cwd) then fails with:

   ```
   code: invalid_request
   cause: review lineage "<lineage>" is not held by repository <redacted>
          rerun the same command from the repository that owns the lineage, or name it
   ```

   That command was run from the same repository that `review start` was invoked in, and whose absolute path `review start` received in its own `--cwd=` token.

Additional observed evidence: no gentle-ai authority directory exists anywhere in the repository at depth 2 after `review start` reported `state: reviewing`, `generation: 1`, and an authority revision.

Also observed, possibly related: the consent-`granted` `review start` returned `"action": "replayed"` for what was, from the consumer's side, the first start of this lineage.

Observed evidence only; no root cause is asserted.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. On macOS (arm64), in an ordinary local Git repository that is not a worktree, enable receipt-driven review.
2. Leave a non-passive workspace candidate uncommitted (here: 5 modified source files, 48 changed lines).
3. Run the selectorless STATUS preflight for contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2` with `--next-transition`.
4. Run the returned `review start` unchanged. It returns the typed consent envelope.
5. Run the envelope's exact `granted` invocation. It returns `state: reviewing` with one selected lens (`review-reliability`) and a `repository_context` handle.
6. Run the returned bound `review.status`. It returns a `collect` transition with one `review.capture-result` input.
7. Run that `review.capture-result` with its returned argument tokens exactly, unchanged, from the repository as process cwd.
8. Observe the missing-file `repository_context_capture_failed` above.
9. Run the same bound `review.status` again to reconcile, as the contract requires.
10. Observe that the lineage is now reported as not held by this repository.

### Expected vs Actual

- Expected: `capture-result` either admits the reviewer result or returns a typed failure whose named recovery can succeed; and the bound STATUS keeps resolving the lineage from the repository that owns it.
- Actual: capture fails before persisting anything, and the documented reconciliation path (`refresh status`) fails too, because the lineage no longer resolves from its own repository. No returned transition remains executable.

### Impact

The consumer cannot finalize, correct, or safely relaunch the review. The contract forbids inventing a binding or retrying from prose, so the lifecycle has no executable continuation. All consumer state was preserved; no receipt, tombstone, or delivery authority was created.

### Nearest existing issues, and why this is not one of them

- #3103 — same failure code, but the cause there is an occupied reviewer slot (`different canonical bytes`). This cause is a missing file.
- #2411 — same failure code and contract, but its documented causes are a DrvFS/9p `EXDEV` publication root under WSL and a Windows `binding_mismatch` variant. This is macOS arm64 on an ordinary local filesystem, and neither of those symptoms is present.
- #2973 — closed as a duplicate; its cause is an uncreatable private reviewer-result directory after reviewer completion. Here the failure is at preflight, before any reviewer compute, and is accompanied by the lineage-ownership loss, which that report does not describe.
- #4023 — lineage resolution from a worktree sharing the Git common dir. This repository is not a worktree.

### Safe identifiers

- lineage: `review-6a9d0b3ff8e5fc4d`
- authority revision at start: `sha256:0bd2095470f819b35420e8a7f5677e150a9d7a5ce5047b57f12837af1427cb65`
- authority revision at bound STATUS: `sha256:efa012fa26fb880b6d97517b481bc694d358797c61ac7971cf92f24f7a86e06b`
- selected lens: `review-reliability`, `selected_order: 0`
- correction budget: 24

title: security(permissions): agent can execute unauthorized remote commands via ambient SSH ControlMaster sockets
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

Autonomous orchestrator/general agent escapes repository workspace boundaries by discovering and utilizing active SSH ControlMaster sockets in `/tmp/` to execute arbitrary commands on remote servers without human authorization or permission boundaries.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Establish an SSH connection on the host with OpenSSH multiplexing enabled (`ControlMaster=auto`, `ControlPath /tmp/...`).
2. Run OpenCode with Gentle AI orchestrator/general agents on a project where a remote host or database IP is referenced in configuration.
3. Request troubleshooting of a remote connection failure (e.g., database connection refused).
4. The agent autonomously inspects the host process table (`ps aux`), locates the open Unix domain socket in `/tmp/`, and issues `ssh -S /tmp/... <remote-host> "<commands>"` to inspect remote system services and containers without requesting human approval.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The agent must be strictly confined to the local repository workspace. Gentle AI generated permissions and system prompt contracts should explicitly prohibit:
1. Executing remote network execution tools (`ssh`, `scp`, `sftp`, `rsync`) via `bash` unless explicitly authorized.
2. Interacting with or hijacking existing Unix domain sockets outside the workspace (particularly `/tmp/*ssh*`).
3. Autonomous lateral movement or remote infrastructure inspection without explicit human consent.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Gentle AI's generated permissions restrict file reads (e.g. `**/.ssh/**`, `.env`), but:
1. No `permission.bash` deny rules exist for `ssh *`, `scp *`, or `rsync *`.
2. Access to active ControlMaster sockets in `/tmp/` is unrestricted.
3. Behavioral instructions lack an explicit security boundary forbidding remote command execution.
Consequently, the agent executed commands as root on a remote production server via an ambient socket without human knowledge or authorization.

### Gentle AI Version

v2.6.0

### Operating System

Linux (Arch/Manjaro)

### AI Agent / Client

OpenCode

### 📋 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
# 1. Agent autonomously searches host process table:
ps aux | grep -i ssh
# <user>  78299  ... ssh: /tmp/herdr-ssh-XXXXX/ctl [mux]

# 2. Agent invokes remote command via ambient ControlMaster socket without user prompt:
ssh -F /tmp/herdr-ssh-XXXXX/config -S /tmp/herdr-ssh-XXXXX/ctl root@<remote-ip> "docker ps"
```

### Additional Context

#### Security Impact
In Linux environments where developers utilize SSH multiplexing (`ControlMaster`), Unix domain sockets in `/tmp/` inherit host user permissions. Any local agent with bash execution privileges can hijack authenticated root sessions on remote infrastructure.

#### Suggested Mitigations
1. **Permission Deny Rules**: Include default `bash.deny` rules in generated agent profiles (`opencode.json` / Claude settings) for remote shell utilities:
   - `ssh *`
   - `scp *`
   - `rsync *`
2. **Behavioral Boundary Directive**: Add an explicit, non-negotiable directive in orchestrator / agent system prompts:
   *"Never execute remote commands (ssh, scp, rsync) or interact with external infrastructure/sockets without explicit user direction."*

title: bug(review): Pi negotiated intended-untracked START loops — start re-derives selection-less target and re-offers selection (2.6.1)
body:
### Pre-flight Checks
- [x] Explicit user consent was obtained to report this apparent provider defect.
- [x] Open and closed issues were searched with exact and broad symptom queries (negotiated intended-untracked START loops, selection re-offer, stale target).
- [x] This report contains observed evidence only and does not assert a root cause.
- [x] Final privacy scan completed immediately before creation: no raw argv, absolute paths, private project names, usernames, hostnames, credentials, diffs, source contents, or environment values are included.

### Bug Description
On the Pi host (gentle-pi facade), a negotiated workspace review loops between `intended_untracked_selection_required` and a derived `fresh_target_ready` execute, without ever reaching native admission. Unlike #2872 (which rejected with `stale_target_identity` on OpenCode), each `review start` here re-derives a DIFFERENT target identity that excludes the just-selected untracked paths and re-asks the selection. Three identical cycles were observed; no lineage was created.

### Environment
- Gentle AI: `2.6.1-0.20260907190052-a609f88b0c78`
- OS/architecture: Windows 11 x86_64
- Client: Pi (pi 0.85.1) via the gentle-pi `gentle_review` tool facade
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`
- Projection: `workspace`
- Candidate shape: 7 tracked modifications (code) + 3 intended untracked test files; one extra eligible untracked file was deliberately NOT selected (a tool-local state file)

### Observed Sequence (3 identical cycles)
1. Negotiated status: `next_transition.kind = collect`, reason `intended_untracked_selection_required`, target identity T0 (7 tracked paths, no untracked), with a selection binding whose eligible paths list contains 4 files.
2. Selection submitted with exactly the 3 intended test files (excluding the tool-local state file).
3. Response: `outcome: native-mutation-status-reconciled`, `mutation_outcome: unknown`; reconciled status shows `fresh_target_ready` with target identity T1 (10 paths incl. the 3 selected, intended_untracked_proof set) and an executable `review.start` route naming lineage `review-…b6381012`, `--untracked-scope=select`, the expected inventory hash, and the 3 `--intended-untracked` tokens.
4. `review start` executed for that route (three variants tried: bare ordinary input; input plus the selected untracked list; input plus the offered lineage id).
5. Each start returns blocked status showing T0 again (7 paths, empty intended_untracked, empty proof) with `next_transition.kind = collect`, reason `intended_untracked_selection_required`, and a fresh selection binding.
6. `lineage_created` false in effect: no lineage, no review authority, no mutation.

### Expected Behavior
After an exact intended-untracked selection is reconciled to `fresh_target_ready` with target identity T1 and an executable start route, `review.start` should begin native admission for T1, not revert to the selection-less derivation T0 and re-offer the same collect step.

### Actual Behavior
The start step appears to evaluate the selection-less target (T0) instead of the selection-bound target (T1), causing the selection requirement to be re-offered indefinitely. The loop is stable across 3 attempts in one session.

### Minimal Reproduction
- Workspace candidate with tracked modifications plus eligible non-ignored untracked files.
- Run negotiated Pi facade status; submit a partial selection (subset of eligible paths) via `select-intended-untracked`.
- Follow the returned `review.start` execute route exactly.
- Observe the status revert to the pre-selection target and re-require selection.

### Bounded Attempts and Preserved State
- 3 start attempt variants, all returning the same collect requirement.
- 1 earlier stop (`managed_assets_outdated`) was resolved via the provider continuation (sync) before this loop; after sync all managed assets verified current and the loop persists.
- No lineage, receipt, commit, push, PR, or authority mutation occurred.
- Working tree and test suites remain intact locally.

### Safety Impact
The consumer cannot obtain review authority and must stop; the only exits are defect reporting or clone-scope review-mode disable.

### Related But Not Duplicate
- #2872 (CLOSED, 2.4.0-rc.1, OpenCode): same selection→start→selection loop shape, but rejection was typed `stale_target_identity`; here the target identity silently changes between the selection-reconciled status (T1, includes selection) and the start result (T0, excludes selection). Pi client, 2.6.1.
- #4271 (OPEN): stale-assets reporting vs sync; the earlier `managed_assets_outdated` stop in this session resolved after sync, so that part was not terminal.

title: bug(opencode): preflight review status names external.select_intended_untracked with no executable CLI path
body:
### Bug Description

Native Review Integration v2 preflight returns a collect transition whose only advertised capture operation is `external.select_intended_untracked`. The OpenCode client has no way to execute that operation: `gentle-ai review --help` lists the supported review subcommands and exposes no `select-intended-untracked` command, no provider-owned binding, and no serializable schema example for the JSON value the status continuation names.

Submitting the selection was not attempted because doing so would require inventing provider-owned structured input. No START, lineage, capture, mutation, commit, push, or PR followed; consumer state is preserved.

### Environment

- Gentle AI: 2.6.0 (stable)
- Client: OpenCode
- Platform: Linux x86_64
- Contract: gentle-ai.review-integration/v2

### Observed evidence

- One bounded selectorless `review status` returned `next_transition.kind=collect` with `reason_code=intended_untracked_selection_required`.
- The collect input advertised only `external.select_intended_untracked` as the capture operation; no provider-owned binding, candidate set, or schema example was attached.
- One bounded `gentle-ai review --help` listed the available review subcommands and exposed no `select-intended-untracked` command and no serializable JSON schema for the selection.
- No selection was submitted; the runnable continuation was unavailable.

### Expected behavior

A native review that requires intended-untracked selection should expose an executable supported capture path — a CLI command, a provider-owned binding, or a documented schema-bound JSON value the consumer can produce without inventing authority. If no supported capture path exists, status should not require the consumer to invent it.

### Actual behavior

The required collect transition names only an external capture operation with no matching CLI command, no provider-issued binding, and no documented schema. Native review cannot complete for a workspace that requires intended-untracked selection on the OpenCode client.

### Minimal reproduction

1. Use OpenCode with review mode configured and a workspace containing eligible untracked files.
2. Run `gentle-ai review status --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --next-transition` (selectorless).
3. Observe the collect transition and its only capture operation `external.select_intended_untracked`.
4. Run `gentle-ai review --help` and verify no corresponding command is exposed.
5. Observe that no provider-owned binding or schema example for the selection is published.

### Consumer-state evidence

No review start, capture, correction, correction-plan, refuter, validation, source mutation, staging, commit, push, PR, reset, review-mode change, or blind retry followed. Candidate state remains preserved.

### Related

This is the same OpenCode-specific shape observed in #4311, #4285, and the OpenCode occurrences on #4005. The discriminating detail here is that the missing capture path is the absence of an executable CLI command, not the rejection of an emitted binding or a `clone_local` mode misread.

### Privacy

This report excludes repository identifiers, absolute paths, usernames, hostnames, credentials, environment values, diffs, source contents, raw command arguments, and any opaque lineage / target / revision identifiers not strictly required.

title: bug(review): committed-only correction cannot close — the corrected candidate the stop reason demands is the one targeted validation refuses
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

On stable `2.6.0`, a compact-v2 `--committed-only` lineage that opens `correction_required` cannot be closed. The documented continuation for `corrected_candidate_unavailable` requires changing the correction candidate, which on a committed-only projection means committing the fix; doing so changes the candidate tree, and the targeted validation the provider then offers refuses because the admitted reviewer-result slot is still bound to the pre-correction canonical bytes. The lineage terminates at `manual_intervention_required`.

The two requirements contradict each other: the stop reason demands a different candidate, and the validation demands the candidate the reviewer already inspected.

This is filed as a possible regression rather than an occurrence. #3961 (committed bounded correction on `--committed-only` has no runnable exit) and #3805 (last-event correction dead-ends after an in-budget edit) both closed `2026-08-31`; `v2.5.0` published `2026-09-01` and `v2.6.0` published `2026-09-04`, so the installed stable build contains both published fixes and the class still reproduces at the next stage. The refusal text is the reviewer-result slot family of #3897, whose close date (`2026-09-05`) is after the latest published release, so that fix is not in any stable build yet.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Selectorless STATUS, then STATUS with `--base-ref <sha> --committed-only --untracked-scope=exclude --expected-untracked-inventory=<digest>` → `execute` / `fresh_target_ready` with an exact START.
2. Run the exact START with `--consent relay`, relay the typed `consent/v3` envelope to the human, run the exact `granted` invocation → `action: created`, `state: reviewing`, one lens (`review-reliability`), medium tier, 1 changed path, 76 changed lines, correction budget 38.
3. Bound STATUS → `collect` / `reviewer_results_required`. Run the exact `review capture-result --agent claude-code` → `state: correction_required`, no advisory findings, one CRITICAL finding.
4. Bound STATUS → `collect` / `correction_plan_required`. Run the exact `review capture-correction-plan … --correction-lines=38` → exit 0, closure envelope `correction_required`.
5. Author the correction in the worktree, 38 changed lines, inside budget and inside the frozen path scope. Full test suite green. Bound STATUS → `stop` / `corrected_candidate_unavailable`.
6. Follow that reason code's documented continuation — change the correction candidate, do not reuse the pre-correction target — by committing the correction. Base is unchanged; only the candidate tree differs. Bound STATUS → `collect` / `targeted_validation_required`, returning an exact `review capture-validation … --agent claude-code --execute=true` carrying a **new** target identity.
7. Run those exact returned tokens.
8. Query the bound STATUS again.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Step 7 completes, or step 8 returns some transition that can be executed. A correction that was forecast, authored inside its budget and inside the frozen scope, and then committed exactly as the stop reason instructs, should be able to reach validation and closure.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Step 7 refuses:

`invalid_request` — `captured reviewer result slot conflicts with different canonical bytes`, `mutation_outcome: not_started`, `phase: preflight`, `retry_safe: true`, `required_inputs: []`.

Step 8 returns `action: stop`, `authority.state: correction_required`, `next_transition: stop / manual_intervention_required`, which the stop-reason table marks terminal. No further operation is offered. The candidate is correct and its suite is green; only the receipt is unreachable.

Retrying the returned validation is not attempted, per the one-attempt rule.

### Gentle AI Version

2.6.0

### Operating System

Linux (Other)

### AI Agent / Client

Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
# step 6 — bound STATUS after committing the correction
next_transition: collect / targeted_validation_required
  op: review.capture-validation
  --lineage=<lineage> --expected-revision=<rev> --target=<new-target>
  --repository-context=<rctx> --request-hash=<hash>
  --agent=claude-code --execute=true

# step 7 — those exact tokens
{
  "schema": "gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2",
  "operation": "review.capture-validation",
  "phase": "preflight",
  "code": "invalid_request",
  "mutation_outcome": "not_started",
  "retry_safe": true,
  "required_inputs": [],
  "cause": "captured reviewer result slot conflicts with different canonical bytes"
}

# step 8 — bound STATUS
{
  "action": "stop",
  "authority": { "state": "correction_required", "generation": 1 },
  "next_transition": { "kind": "stop", "reason_code": "manual_intervention_required" }
}
```

### Additional Context

Secondary observation from the same run, matching #4087 (closed): no negotiated surface returned the CRITICAL finding needed to author the correction. STATUS carried no findings block and the closure envelope carried none. The finding text was only reachable by reading the on-disk transaction state directly, which is not a documented adapter route. Without it the bounded correction cannot be authored at all, so this blocks step 5 before the contradiction in steps 6–8 is even reached.

Candidate shape: one modified test file, medium tier, single lens, correction budget 38 of 76 changed lines. No secrets, paths, source bytes, or repository identifiers are included in this report.

title: bug(cli): review stop-hook crashes with Go runtime panic (unknown caller pc) during RDD-mode resolution on Windows
body:
## Automated provider-defect report

### Summary
On Windows, Gentle AI v2.6.0 (stable channel) aborts with a Go runtime fatal error during the `review stop-hook` command's RDD-mode resolution, instead of returning its normal stop-hook result.

### Environment
- Gentle AI build: v2.6.0 (stable channel, module `github.com/gentleman-programming/gentle-ai/v2`)
- OS / architecture: Windows amd64
- Client: Claude Code
- Command: `gentle-ai review stop-hook --agent claude-code`

### Operation shape
1. A normal Claude Code conversational turn completed.
2. The Stop hook fired `gentle-ai review stop-hook --agent claude-code` as usual.
3. During RDD-mode resolution for the stop-hook's target identity, the process crashed instead of returning a result.

### Expected behavior
The stop-hook should resolve the RDD mode and return its normal (typed) result without crashing.

### Actual behavior
The process printed `runtime: g 3: unexpected return pc for runtime.gopark called from 0xb`, followed by `fatal error: unknown caller pc` and a full goroutine stack dump, then exited.

### Bounded observed evidence
- Crash occurred inside `runtime.scanstack` / `runtime.(*unwinder).next` while a GC assist was running concurrently with `path/filepath.Join`.
- Stack evidence places the join call inside `internal/reviewtransaction/rdd_mode.go:829` (`cloneLocalRDDModeLegacyRoot`), called from `rdd_mode.go:886` (`cloneLocalRDDModeReadRoot`) → `rdd_mode.go:897` (`readCloneLocalRDDOverride`) → `rdd_mode.go:309` (`ResolveRDDMode`) → `internal/cli/review_stop_hook.go:233` (`reviewStopHookResolveTargetIdentity`) → `review_stop_hook.go:162` (`runReviewStopHookStop`) → `review_stop_hook.go:129` (`runReviewStopHook`).
- No typed failure envelope was emitted; the process exited via Go's fatal-error path.
- No repository mutation, review transaction, or delivery gate was in progress at the time — this occurred during ordinary conversational-turn bookkeeping, not during an active review lifecycle action.

### Minimal reproduction
Not yet isolated to a deterministic trigger (unlike #4081/#4152, which had specific reproducible preconditions). Observed once during a routine Claude Code session on Windows; the Stop hook simply ran as it does after every turn.

### Related reports
- #4081, #4128, and #4152 show the same Go runtime crash signature (`unexpected return pc for runtime.gopark` / `fatal error: unknown caller pc`) on Windows, each in a different CLI contract (`sdd-status`, `review status`, `sdd-attempt` respectively). This report adds a fourth distinct contract (`review stop-hook` / RDD-mode resolution). Per those reports' own framing, these are related observations on the same crash signature, not asserted duplicates or a confirmed shared root cause.

title: review: reviewer admission still prose-scans evidence and rejects completed inspections that honestly scope out base files
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

Reviewer-artifact admission still keyword-scans the reviewer's free-text **evidence** strings with the unavailability phrase family, so an honest reviewer that completed its inspection gets its whole artifact rejected as `ArtifactAdmissionIncomplete`.

The phrase family is shared with `InconclusiveValidationEvidence` (the validator path). #4256 established the contract for the reviewer path — "a typed `inspection.status: unavailable` is the only admission-incomplete signal" — and #4266 delivered exactly that for the validator path ("not from scanning evidence prose"). But the reviewer-path loop in `internal/reviewtransaction/artifact_admission.go` (current `main`, lines ~369-372) still runs `evidenceReportsUnavailableInspection` over every evidence string. Worse, the passive phrases added to that shared list for #3378 ("could not be inspected", ...) widen the reviewer-path false-positive surface: a phrase family introduced to catch unavailable validators now rejects available reviewers.

The false-positive class is not hypothetical: bounded reviews instruct reviewers to inspect only the changed-path manifest, so an honest reviewer routinely writes that out-of-manifest base files were assumed rather than read. That exact sentence kills the artifact.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Start an ordinary review whose candidate adds tests that rely on base-tree helpers (a `newMCPTestStore` fixture, a sibling test harness, a store API) outside the changed-path manifest.
2. The reviewer inspects all manifest paths, reports `inspection.status: completed`, and writes evidence like:

   > "...these were assumed present in the base tree because the store package and sibling test files could not be inspected under the review scope."

3. Submit the reviewer result. Admission rejects it:

   ```
   reviewer artifact admission incomplete: reviewer evidence reports that candidate inspection was unavailable [invalid_request]
   ```

4. The reviewer model run is wasted, the lens slot is not consumed, and a retry only passes by phrasing luck.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Per the #4256 contract, admission reads the typed `inspection.status` and the structured inspection payload; free-text evidence prose never flips a completed inspection into admission-incomplete. Quoting or describing the bounded-scope limitation (out-of-manifest base files) in evidence must not change the verdict, exactly as #4266 established for validators.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

`for _, evidence := range canonical.Evidence { if evidenceReportsUnavailableInspection(evidence) { return fail(ArtifactAdmissionIncomplete, "reviewer evidence reports that candidate inspection was unavailable") } }` rejects completed inspections. The substring matcher (`artifact_admission.go` ~line 782 on `main`) matches "could not be inspected" even when the object of the phrase is out-of-manifest base files, not the candidate.

Field evidence (real review on Gentleman-Programming/engram#1039, gentle-ai 2.6.0, reviewer lens `review-reliability`): the reviewer reported `inspection.status: completed` over all three manifest paths and three findings (one a genuine WARNING that led to a real fix), yet its artifact was refused at admission and preserved under `.git/gentle-ai/rejected-results/<lineage>/`. The rejection reason string itself proves the typed status was completed and ignored.

### Gentle AI Version

2.6.0

### Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```
Error: reviewer artifact admission incomplete: reviewer evidence reports that candidate inspection was unavailable; the rejected reviewer payload was preserved at <repo>/.git/gentle-ai/rejected-results/<lineage>/review-reliability-1-<hash>.json [invalid_request]
```

The preserved payload shows `"inspection": {"status": "completed", "paths": [<all manifest paths>]}` alongside the offending evidence string, which references only out-of-manifest base files.

### Additional Context

- Related history: #1555 introduced evidence-based unavailability detection; #4256 demanded typed-status-only admission for reviewers; #3378 added the passive phrases to the shared list (validator path); #4266 removed prose scanning for validators. The reviewer path is the remaining prose-scanned surface.
- Suggested direction, mirroring #4266's fix: the reviewer contract already has a typed `inspection.status`; make `unavailable` there (with a reason) the only admission-incomplete signal for unavailability, and stop running the phrase matcher over free-text evidence.

title: review.capture-result fails: claude-code reviewer transport does not recognize session model
body:
## Automated Provider-Defect Report

### Observed behavior

`review.capture-result` fails during RDD lifecycle with `invalid_request` because the claude-code reviewer transport does not recognize the session model identifier.

### Error

```
operation: review.capture-result
phase: preflight
code: invalid_request
cause: invoke provider reviewer: claude reviewer transport failed: exit status 1: [claude-code:unrecognized_model]
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable RDD globally
2. Run selectorless STATUS preflight on a workspace with untracked files
3. Classify untracked files as intended
4. Consent to review (granted)
5. START succeeds, creates lineage, state=reviewing
6. Bound STATUS returns collect with `review.capture-result` slot for `review-reliability` lens
7. Execute `review.capture-result` with exact provider-issued tokens
8. Reviewer transport fails with `unrecognized_model`

### Expected behavior

The reviewer transport should either:
- Use a known supported model for the reviewer (not blindly pass the session model)
- Validate the model identifier before invoking the reviewer
- Fall back to a supported model when the session model is not recognized

### Environment

- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`
- Agent: `claude-code`
- Lens: `review-reliability`
- Risk level: medium

### Notes

- The session model identifier is not a standard API model ID
- The reviewer transport appears to use the session model to invoke the reviewer, but this model is not recognized by the underlying API
- START and STATUS both succeed; only `capture-result` fails because it invokes the reviewer transport

title: bug(opencode): shipped review-transport plugin fails to load on OpenCode 1.18.x — provider-injected lens capture structurally unavailable
body:
### Summary

The OpenCode reviewer-transport plugin shipped with Gentle AI fails to load in the current OpenCode 1.18.x runtime, which makes the compiled `opencode_provider_injected` capture path structurally unavailable: reviewer lens agents launch but receive no Go-injected evidence context, refuse the capture as incomplete inspection, and the 4R collect can never be satisfied.

### Environment (sanitized)

- gentle-ai: `2.5.0` (stable build, no prerelease tag)
- OS / arch: Linux x86_64
- Client runtime: OpenCode `1.18.25` (server/desktop runtime, plugin loader active)
- Plugin file: `~/.config/opencode/plugins/opencode-review-transport.ts`

### Observed behavior

At every OpenCode boot in the affected session:

```
failed to load plugin  target=~/.config/opencode/plugins/opencode-review-transport.ts
cause="Plugin must export a default definition with an id and an effect or setup function.
(SchemaError(Expected object, got async function ...))"
```

Consequences observed in one high-risk 4R review attempt:

1. Review START succeeds; canonical 4 lenses freeze; collect reoffers 4 `review.capture-result` slots.
2. Each lens reviewer agent launches and correctly parses the caller relayed binding line, but reports that the provider-injected evidence context block was never supplied and refuses with `inspection.status: "incomplete"` (empty paths/findings) — correct behavior per the reviewer contract, since prompt prose is not evidence.
3. `gentle-ai review capture-result --agent opencode ... --materialize` is rejected: the compiled transport for this runtime is `opencode_provider_injected`, and printing the Go-materialized task is only the host-relay form — so there is no caller-side way to obtain the injected evidence.
4. Result: the 4 collect slots cannot be captured by any permitted path; the lineage stays open with no captures submitted.

### Expected behavior

The plugin loads under OpenCode 1.18.x's plugin schema (default export: definition object with id + setup/effect), intercepts reviewer agent child sessions, and injects the Go-materialized user prompt/evidence so lens captures can complete.

### Minimal reproduction

1. Install gentle-ai 2.5.0 and start OpenCode 1.18.25 with the shipped plugin in the plugins directory.
2. Observe the `failed to load plugin` warning at boot (SchemaError on the default export).
3. Start a negotiated review (`review start`), grant consent, and delegate any lens slot to its reviewer agent: the agent reports missing injected context and refuses as incomplete.

### Bounded attempts and outcomes

- 4/4 lens launches (risk, resilience, readability, reliability) returned incomplete-inspection refusals; 0 captures submitted; no further mutation attempted (no comment/create/retry loops).
- Re-querying the exact bound STATUS reoffered the same 4 slots, as designed.

### Preserved state

- Lineage `review-762f375332599437` remains open/frozen with consent granted and zero captures; consumer state preserved; no delivery authority granted.

### Notes

- Runtime detail: the plugin source appears written against an older OpenCode plugin definition shape (async default export); OpenCode 1.18.x expects a default definition object with an id and an effect or setup function. Reported as an observed transport defect, not a confirmed root cause in Gentle AI's Go code.
