title: RDD as audit vs enforcement — a case for optional "teeth"
body:
Thanks for gentle-ai — I've used it daily on production systems for months, and RDD reshaped how I work. This isn't a bug report; it's feedback from a use case that v2.6 moves away from, in case it's useful.

## What I read in v2.6

> "Review never governs delivery. Commit, push, PR and release stay separate human decisions under your ordinary repository policy."

And that compact receipts / FINALIZE / delivery gates are retired. I understand the philosophy: review **informs**, the human **decides**. For mature teams and low-risk changes, that's the right default.

## My case

I run production pipelines where part of the work is done by an AI agent and where a bad commit has real downstream cost. There, I've found I need review to have **teeth** — to *block* a commit, not just log it. A control that informs but doesn't block tends to get skipped the day there's time pressure, and in production there's always a day with time pressure.

## A technical note that may help others

The RDD flow **does** close on 2.3.0:

```
start (negotiated: --contract …/v2 --agent <runtime> --target <sha> --projection workspace)
  → capture-result → capture-evidence → finalize --captured-results --captured-evidence
  → validate --gate pre-commit : allow
```

The piece that's easy to miss: the **negotiated** `start` is what returns the per-lens `subject_hash` (and the changed-path manifest). Running `start` "bare" never does, so `capture-result` has nothing to bind to. Sharing in case others coming from 2.3.0 hit the same wall — the closed #3939 has the surrounding context.

## What I'm proposing, concretely

An **opt-in enforcement mode** — one flag that restores teeth for those who want them:

- **Review governs delivery when enabled.** A commit is blocked unless a valid terminal receipt covers exactly that change.
- **Approval requires evidence that was actually run**, not just asserted — the receipt binds to executed verification, so "it works" can't ship without the command behind it.
- **Off by default.** Your audit model stays the default and nothing changes for teams who want the human sovereign. It only turns on for those who deliberately choose it.

That one option covers the whole enforcement use case without touching your current direction — the gate becomes a *choice*, not a removed capability.

Honestly, I'd love to see an opt-in enforcement mode land in gentle-ai — it's the one piece that would let those of us who need teeth keep building on your work as it evolves, instead of pinning to an old version for it. Even if it doesn't fit your roadmap, I wanted to make the case plainly.

Either way — thank you for building in the open.

title: feat(review): emit a runnable command on native capture collect inputs so hosts stop assembling the invocation
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Problem Statement

An `execute` transition ships a fully-formed `command` string. A `collect` input for a native capture operation does not: it ships `arguments[]` whose entries carry runnable `token` values, but no `command`. Every host must therefore compose `gentle-ai review <verb> <tokens>` itself and decide the process working directory.

That composition step is where invocations break, and the repository already records it happening twice. The `reviewCollectTransition` doc comment in `internal/cli/review_next_transition.go` states that tokenizing the arguments exists because a hand-assembled invocation "twice dropped or mispaired `--repository-context`".

#4288 is the third occurrence. A host mis-assembled a `review.capture-result` invocation, and because the preflight refusal folded six independent preconditions into one enumerating sentence, an assembly bug and a genuine contract fault were byte-identical from outside. The result was an irreproducible report whose own isolation table read as self-contradictory.

This is the unfinished half of a principle this repository already ratified:

- **#1745** established that a native next transition must be directly executable without consumer inference. It was applied to `execute` transitions.
- **#1879** established that collect inputs must carry runnable `token` values rather than only `name`/`value`. That delivered the `token` field.

So hosts no longer reconstruct individual flags, but they still reconstruct the whole invocation. The remaining gap is the command line itself.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Emit a `command` on collect inputs whose `capture_operation` begins with `review.`, so a host runs it verbatim exactly as it already does for `execute`.

The rendering helper already exists and is already used for the sibling operation: `reviewTransitionCommandLine` produces the command for the `capture-unachievable` withdraw descriptor in `reviewUnachievableLensSlotEntry`. `reviewNativeCaptureVerb` already resolves the runnable verb from the operation name.

**This requires a new schema version and must not be an in-place edit.**

`$defs/transition_input` in `contracts/review-integration/v2/schemas/status-v5.schema.json` is `"additionalProperties": false`, and it is defined exactly once: `status-v6.schema.json` and `status-v7.schema.json` both `$ref` that same definition. A payload carrying an undeclared `command` property is therefore rejected, not ignored, by a conforming consumer of v5, v6 and v7 alike. Adding the field in place breaks three published envelope versions at once.

Ship it as the repository already ships envelope changes:

- new `contracts/review-integration/v2/schemas/status-v8.schema.json`
- new `contracts/review-integration/v2/schemas/capabilities-v2.6.schema.json` (v2.5 enumerates status v5/v6/v7)
- new `gentle-ai.review-integration.status/v8` schema ID and its constant in `internal/cli/review_status_contract.go`
- bench pins updated

Two constraints the design must respect:

1. **Do not serialize the repository root.** Three written invariants forbid a `--cwd` token (`RepositoryRoot` is never serialized; `reviewStartStatusContinuation` deliberately carries no `--cwd`; submission descriptors refuse a `--cwd` token outright). The command should run with the repository as process cwd, exactly as the `execute` rule already states.
2. **The field cannot be universal.** The host-relay (`--input`) form genuinely cannot have a complete command up front, because `--input` points at a reviewer result that does not exist until the host produces it. That form already carries the `submission` descriptor. The `command` should be conditional on the compiled in-process (`--agent`) form, where the token list is complete and runnable today.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

**Do nothing beyond documenting the assembly rule.** The shipped host contract can be made explicit about how a native capture collect input composes its invocation, matching what the `execute` rule already says ("run that provider-issued command verbatim, with the repository as process cwd"). That removes the ambiguity at zero contract cost and is worth doing regardless. It does not remove the assembly step itself, so it reduces the chance of the mistake rather than eliminating it.

**Edit `transition_input` in place.** Rejected: `additionalProperties: false` means a conforming consumer pinned to status v5, v6 or v7 rejects the entire status payload, so its review lifecycle stops rather than degrades.

**Let hosts derive the command from `capture_operation`.** That is what hosts do today, and it is the thing being removed. Note that deriving the verb by splitting the operation name on `.` is unsafe: `bench/journeys.go` records that a dot-split yields a runnable verb only by coincidence, since operations such as `review.retry_final_verification` do not spell their verbs that way.

### 📎 Additional Context

Verified on 2.6.0 stable:

- The exact provider-issued token list does work. Driving the full lifecycle (selectorless STATUS, then `--base-ref` with `--committed-only`, START, granted START, bound STATUS, then the returned tokens verbatim with the repository as process cwd) admits successfully and returns `admission_decision: completed`. The tokens were never the problem; the assembly step is.
- No native capture collect input emits a `command` today: `review.capture-result`, `review.capture-refuter`, `review.capture-validation` and `review.capture-correction-plan` all omit it. `review.capture-unachievable` carries one only on its stop-transition withdraw descriptor, which is a separate type.
- `ReviewTransitionInput` in `internal/cli/review_next_transition.go` has no `Command` field, so the Go type needs one alongside the schema work.
- The omission is a documented decision in `reviewCollectTransition`, whose stated rationale is that `capture-result` "also requires `--input` pointing at a reviewer-result artifact that does not exist yet". That rationale holds for the host-relay form and is stale for the compiled `--agent` form, where `providerExecution` requires no `--input` at all.

This is hardening rather than a bug fix, and it is not urgent: it removes the opportunity for the mistake rather than making the failure legible. Priority should be judged accordingly.

title: bug(review): capture-result folds six preflight preconditions into one refusal, so a host assembly error is indistinguishable from a contract fault
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

#3441 established the standard for this exact command: two opposite `capture-result` refusals shared byte-identical text, so a report quoting one could not be traced to either branch. That fix closed it, and the test comment in `internal/cli/review_capture_result_refusal_distinct_test.go` records the resulting rule:

> Each refusal now names the flag the caller passed, the runtime's compiled transport, and the one accepted form.

That rule was applied to the two host-mediated branches only. The preflight guard in the same command still does not meet it, and neither do four sibling verbs.

`review capture-result` folds six independent preconditions into one refusal that enumerates requirements instead of naming the violated one. Four distinct mis-assembled invocations produce a byte-identical `cause`.

The consequence is worse than a vague error. The message lists requirements the caller did supply, and names none of the ones it did not. A host reading it verifies every item on the list, finds them all present, and reaches the only conclusion the message allows: that the product is refusing its own provider-issued tokens. That conclusion is false. The exact token list returned by `review status` works, and driving the full lifecycle on 2.6.0 stable admits successfully with `admission_decision: completed`.

So the defect is not that a bad invocation is refused. It is that the refusal makes a host's own assembly error indistinguishable from a genuine contract fault, so the host cannot self-correct and instead reports a defect that does not exist. This is the same harm #3441 named, one layer down.

Two secondary defects live in the same sentence:

- It cites contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v1` on stderr while the live negotiated contract is v2. A wrong named exit is worse than a missing one, because it sends the reader somewhere confidently.
- The JSON `cause` renders that same citation as `gentle-ai.review-integration<redacted>`, so a machine consumer cannot even see the wrong pointer to know it is wrong.

Four more call sites share the same root:

| Site | Preconditions folded into one message |
| --- | --- |
| `internal/cli/review_artifact.go` | 6 |
| `internal/cli/review_provider_role_capture.go` | 5 (shared by `capture-refuter` and `capture-validation`) |
| `internal/cli/review_correction_plan_capture.go` | 6 |
| `internal/cli/review_capture_unachievable.go` | 5 |
| `internal/cli/review_last_event_closure.go` | 4 (`acknowledge-approved`) |

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

No review lineage, consent, or lens selection is required. The guard fires at preflight before any authority lookup, so dummy values reproduce it. In any git repository, on 2.6.0 stable:

1. Operation name leaked as a positional argument:

   gentle-ai review capture-result review.capture-result --lineage=L --target=T --lens=review-risk --order=0 --agent=claude-code

2. `--agent` supplied with an empty value:

   gentle-ai review capture-result --lineage=L --target=T --lens=review-risk --order=0 --agent=

3. `--agent` omitted entirely:

   gentle-ai review capture-result --lineage=L --target=T --lens=review-risk --order=0

4. A trailing stray positional after all flags:

   gentle-ai review capture-result --lineage=L --target=T --lens=review-risk --order=0 --agent=claude-code stray

5. Compare the `cause` field across all four.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Each refusal names the one precondition that was violated, the value it observed, and a continuation that actually leads somewhere. Four different mistakes should read as four different messages, so a host can correct itself instead of concluding the product is broken.

The cited contract should be the live negotiated one (v2), and it should be visible on both the human and the machine surface.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

All four invocations produce a byte-identical `cause`. The message enumerates requirements that are present in the invocation, and names none of the ones that are not.

A related symptom that looks like evidence but is not: replacing `--agent` with `--preflight` on the same binding is accepted. That reads as proof that the binding is valid and the `--agent` path is broken. It proves neither. `--preflight` is one of three disjuncts in the same clause, so it never needed `--agent` at all. Because the refusal never says which disjunct failed, this acceptance actively misleads whoever is isolating the problem.

### Gentle AI Version

2.6.0

### Operating System

macOS

### AI Agent / Client

Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
$ gentle-ai review capture-result --lineage=L --target=T --lens=review-risk --order=0

{
  "schema": "gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2",
  "operation": "review.capture-result",
  "phase": "preflight",
  "code": "invalid_request",
  "mutation_outcome": "not_started",
  "authority_applicability": "not_evaluated",
  "retry_safe": true,
  "next_action": "correct_request",
  "cause": "review capture-result requires an exact repository context, --lineage, --target, --lens, --order, and either --input or --agent (or --preflight); `gentle-ai review status --contract gentle-ai.review-integration<redacted> --next-transition` prints the exact bindings and `gentle-ai review schema reviewer` emits the result schema with a working example"
}

The stderr line for the same run shows the citation the JSON redacts:

Error: review capture-result requires an exact repository context, --lineage, --target, --lens, --order, and either --input or --agent (or --preflight); `gentle-ai review status --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v1 --next-transition` prints the exact bindings and `gentle-ai review schema reviewer` emits the result schema with a working example [invalid_request]

All four reproduction commands emit the same cause, byte for byte.
```

### Additional Context

Proof that the provider-issued tokens themselves are correct, so this is a diagnostics defect and not a binding defect: the full lifecycle was driven end to end on 2.6.0 stable in a throwaway repository (selectorless STATUS, then STATUS with `--base-ref` and `--committed-only`, START, granted START, bound STATUS, then the returned `review.capture-result` tokens verbatim with the repository as process cwd). The capture admitted and returned `gentle-ai.review-result-artifact/v2` with `admission_decision: completed`. Nothing about the binding is broken.

A contributing factor worth fixing alongside: the shipped host contract is explicit for `execute` transitions ("run that provider-issued command verbatim, with the repository as process cwd") but says nothing about how a `collect` input composes its invocation, so every host assembles that command line by hand. The `reviewCollectTransition` doc comment in `internal/cli/review_next_transition.go` records that hand assembly "twice dropped or mispaired `--repository-context`", so this class has bitten before. Making that rule explicit costs nothing and closes the gap that lets a host build the wrong command in the first place.

Emitting a ready-to-run `command` on collect inputs would remove the assembly step entirely, but it requires a new status envelope version and is out of scope here.

title: fix(skills): permit a bounded first Issue Form bootstrap PR
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

`issue-creation` v1.4 enforces \"YAML Issue Forms are the single format authority\" for any repo operation. The contract is silent on a separate concern observable in the wild.

A repository that has **never had** any `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.yml` cannot legally open its first issue, and it cannot legally open its first PR introducing such a form, because the PR body has no `Closes #N` link to any previously-approved issue. The two rules deadlock each other.

The defect is not in `issue-creation` itself. `issue-creation` does what it says. The defect is that the **bootstrap** of a no-form repo is unrepresented in the `branch-pr` contract surface — the place where the first PR introducing forms ought to be authorised.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Pick any repository that has zero `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.yml`.
2. Apply the `branch-pr` contract to that repository (try to authorise a PR).
3. Observe: `branch-pr` requires every PR to link an approved issue. No issue exists. The PR cannot be authorised.
4. Try to publish the first issue: `issue-creation` runs discovery, finds zero forms, returns \"Failed or ambiguous discovery stops publication\".
5. No mutation has occurred. The publisher has refused before any write.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

`branch-pr` authorises the first PR introducing forms into a formless repo when **all** of the following hold simultaneously:

- The repository has zero valid `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.yml` on the PR's base.
- The actor's `viewerPermission` against the target host is `ADMIN` (strict — `MAINTAIN` and `TRIAGE` are not sufficient).
- The PR's diff adds only `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.yml` (or `.yaml`) and, as an optional accompaniment, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml`. Other paths are not allowed.
- The PR carries exactly one `type:chore` label. Other labels outside the `type:*` namespace are permitted.
- `branch-pr` searches for other open PRs that add files under `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.yml` to the same base branch (e.g. `main`) — not only to the same base commit — and treats any competitor as a fail. While a competitor exists, the second PR is **not eligible** for the bootstrap exception. After the first PR merges and the form lands on `main`, the bootstrap exception closes (no bootstrap PR remains eligible) and the second PR, if any, must follow the default issue-first flow on the form path.
- The classification is fail-closed: any unexpected state (failed API call, paginated truncation, malformed YAML, no `viewerPermission` read) returns invalid and blocks the PR.
- When the first form reaches the consumer's main, `branch-pr` classifies any subsequent bootstrap-form PR as **ordinary** and the default YAML-only flow re-engages.

`issue-creation` is **not changed** by this issue. The exception belongs exclusively to `branch-pr`.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

No compliant first-form bootstrap route exists today. `issue-creation` cannot publish an issue (no form). `branch-pr` does not authorise the bootstrap PR. The path closes correctly only after a form lands on `main` — which it cannot, because of the deadlock.

v2.6.0

### Operating System

Linux (Other)

Other

_No response_

title: bug(opencode): reviewer transport misreads clone-local review mode after START
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

On Gentle AI `2.6.0` stable with OpenCode `1.18.29`, native review mode status reported receipt-driven development enabled globally with no clone-local override. A consented high-risk workspace START then succeeded and froze one candidate. Native bound STATUS returned four independent `review.capture-result` slots.

Each OpenCode reviewer Task transport failed before producing a capturable result with `opencode_review_transport_authority_unavailable`, stating that receipt-driven development was disabled because the `clone_local` mode source kept it off. The exact bound STATUS afterward still showed the lineage in `reviewing` and reoffered the same four slots.

This report records the observed mode-resolution mismatch only. The internal root cause is not confirmed.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Use Gentle AI `2.6.0` stable with OpenCode `1.18.29` on Windows x64.
2. Enable receipt-driven development globally and leave clone-local mode unset.
3. Confirm native mode status reports effective mode on, decided globally.
4. Start and consent to a high-risk workspace review; confirm START creates a frozen lineage.
5. Run the exact bound STATUS and receive multiple `review.capture-result` slots.
6. Launch the provider-bound OpenCode reviewer Tasks with their exact bindings.
7. Observe each transport reject capture because it resolves `clone_local` mode as off.
8. Re-enter exact bound STATUS and observe the unchanged reviewing lineage and reoffered slots.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The OpenCode reviewer transport should resolve the same effective review mode as native mode status and the successful START. With global mode on and clone-local mode unset, each bound reviewer Task should produce a capturable result or a terminal native continuation.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

All four independent reviewer Task launches returned `opencode_review_transport_authority_unavailable` before producing results, claiming clone-local mode disabled review despite native status and START treating review as enabled. The frozen review could not advance.

### Gentle AI Version

2.6.0

### Operating System

Windows

### AI Agent / Client

OpenCode

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
opencode_review_transport_authority_unavailable: OpenCode Task transport did not produce a capturable reviewer result; receipt-driven development is disabled: advancing an existing review is rejected because the clone_local mode source keeps it off; the review is frozen, not discarded
```

### Additional Context

- OS/architecture: Windows x64.
- Client: OpenCode `1.18.29`.
- Candidate shape: seven files and 115 changed lines.
- Bounded attempts: four independent provider-issued reviewer slots were launched once; no slot was blindly retried.
- Native STATUS after the failures reoffered the same bound slots.
- Safe opaque identifiers: lineage `review-2d98e83d6fe662d4`; target `sha256:5ed4ced403cbd723c7e17b71a2d01286c00794a00ba02e4eddf371435ae22d76`; authority revision `sha256:f1f855c501368c8469a280449c333b42eb792463c392e9a2e2fc25a2e2bbfc07`.
- No reviewer result, correction, receipt, source mutation, staging, commit, push, pull request, reset, review-mode change, or blind retry followed.
- Candidate bytes and frozen identity remained unchanged.
- Raw arguments, absolute paths, repository/project names, usernames, hostnames, credentials, diffs, source contents, and environment values are omitted.

title: bug(doctor): engram:reachable names only two persisted configs and reports healthy when three declare Engram
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

`gentle-ai doctor` reports `engram:reachable` as `[ok]` while naming only **two** persisted configurations, even when **three** agent configs declare an Engram MCP entry. One config silently drops out of the reported set, and which one drops depends on the others present.

The check message claims the handshake answered "for persisted configuration: `<list>`". With three eligible configs on disk, the list is two entries long. From outside it is not observable whether the third config was probed and omitted from the message, or never probed at all — but either way the summary reports `healthy` without accounting for it.

This matters because `doctor` is the command users are pointed at to confirm their install. A config that is never named is a config the user cannot tell was checked.

This is **not** #2762. That issue is a false *negative* — `engram:reachable` fails on a valid `opencode.json` because a top-level `command` key is misread. This report is the opposite direction: the check *passes* while under-reporting its own coverage.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

Starting state: `opencode.json` and `.codex/config.toml` both declare Engram; `~/.claude.json` does not.

1. Run `gentle-ai doctor` and read the `engram:reachable` line.
   Reported: `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json, ~/.codex/config.toml` — two configs, both correct.
2. Add a third Engram registration for Claude Code:
   ```
   claude mcp add engram <engram-path> -s user -- mcp --tools=agent
   ```
   Confirm `mcpServers` in `~/.claude.json` now contains `engram`.
3. Run `gentle-ai doctor` again and read the same line.
   Reported: `~/.claude.json, ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` — still two configs. **`~/.codex/config.toml` is gone**, although nothing about the Codex config changed between the two runs.
4. Remove the Claude registration (`claude mcp remove engram -s user`) and re-run.
   Reported: back to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json, ~/.codex/config.toml`.

A/B verified on the same machine within one session; only step 2 changed between runs.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

`engram:reachable` accounts for every persisted Engram configuration it found. Either name all of them in the message, or report per-config results so an unreachable or unprobed config is visible instead of being absorbed into a single `[ok]`. The summary line should not read `healthy` for a set the check did not fully cover.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The check names exactly two persisted configurations regardless of how many declare Engram, and returns `[ok]`. With three configs present, one is silently absent from the message. The run still summarizes as `11 passed, 0 failed, 0 warnings — healthy`.

### Gentle AI Version

gentle-ai 2.6.0 (Homebrew) · gga v2.10.1 · engram 1.20.0

### Operating System

macOS

### AI Agent / Client

Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
# A) two configs declare engram (claude.json does not)
$ gentle-ai doctor | grep engram:reachable
  [ok]  engram:reachable   engram MCP (stdio) answered the initialize handshake for persisted configuration: ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json, ~/.codex/config.toml

# B) after adding a third registration in ~/.claude.json — codex drops out
$ gentle-ai doctor | grep engram:reachable
  [ok]  engram:reachable   engram MCP (stdio) answered the initialize handshake for persisted configuration: ~/.claude.json, ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json

# summary in both cases
Summary: 11 passed, 0 failed, 0 warnings
Status:  healthy
```

### Additional Context

Installed agents in `~/.gentle-ai/state.json`: `claude-code`, `opencode`, `vscode-copilot`, `codex` (4 agents, `installed_binary_version: 2.6.0`).

Found while auditing why the same Engram server was registered twice for Claude Code (#4188, fixed in #4278 but not yet in a published release — v2.6.0 predates that merge). `doctor` reported `healthy` both with the duplicate registration active and after it was removed, which is what prompted a closer look at what this check actually covers.

title: bug(review): compiled Claude reviewer launches `claude --print --setting-sources ""` without `--model`, so lenses run on the account default model instead of the assigned one (Opus 5 1M safeguards refuse lens contexts; any lens can be hit)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched existing issues (open and closed: "reviewer model", "setting-sources", "safeguards", "ANTHROPIC_MODEL", "--model", "claude_adapter", "flagged this message") and this is not a duplicate. Closest is #2286 (OpenCode: an invalid model ID cannot be resolved); this report is the opposite case: the model resolves, but it is not the one gentle-ai assigns.
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### Status (updated 2026-09-10)
Reproduced independently by four other users in the comments below (thanks @IP-Mattos, @Torresric, @TinMon11, @lockder), all on Windows with the `claude-code` runtime and an Opus 5 (1M) account default:

- **Versions:** 2.5.0, 2.6.0 and **2.7.0 stable** (published 2026-09-08). `internal/reviewerprovider/claude_adapter.go` is unchanged on `main` since `9a27cd5` (2026-09-05), so the current stable still passes no `--model`.
- **Any lens can be refused.** The original report saw resilience and reliability fail while risk and readability passed. Later reports saw risk refused too, readability as the only surviving lens, and single-lens medium-risk candidates where the only offered lens (reliability) is refused on every attempt, so the review can never close. The refusal is content-dependent; the model fallback is what makes it reachable.
- **Workaround confirmed twice more**, independently: the exact provider-issued `capture-result` tokens, unchanged, with `ANTHROPIC_MODEL=<sonnet id>` in the process environment, capture on the first attempt and the transaction reaches `approved` (in one case the targeted validator approved as well). Same context, same tokens, only the model changes.
- **No supported way to route the model from outside** on the compiled runtime: `review capture-result --materialize --agent claude-code` is refused ("a compiled runtime materializes internally"). The adapter's argument list is the only path.
- A related request from the thread: when the provider refuses a lens, surface a typed provider-refusal outcome that can reach a human decision, instead of `invalid_request` plus an indefinitely re-offered slot.

The patch for option (a) below is still applicable and waits for `status:approved`.

### 📝 Bug Description
`internal/reviewerprovider/claude_adapter.go` launches the in-process Claude reviewer with a fixed argument list:

```text
--print --output-format text --tools "" --permission-mode dontAsk --no-session-persistence --setting-sources "" --system-prompt "You are an isolated code reviewer process. ..."
```

`--setting-sources ""` is there to drop hooks, plugins and permissions, but it also drops the `model` the user configured in `settings.json`, and no `--model` is passed. Claude Code then runs the reviewer on the **account default model**. On this account that is `claude-opus-5[1m]`, and its safeguards reject provider-issued lens contexts on ordinary candidates (in the original reproduction, `review-resilience` and `review-reliability` on shell-hook candidates; other reporters saw other lenses refused, see Status above):

```text
API Error: Opus 5 (1M context)'s safeguards flagged this message (https://www.anthropic.com/legal/aup). This sometimes happens with safe, normal conversations. Claude Code can't respond to this message with Opus 5 (1M co…
```

The same context, same flags, plus `--model sonnet` produces a valid reviewer result. gentle-ai already assigns a model per review role: the installed `review-*` sub-agents render `model: {{CLAUDE_MODEL}}` through the Claude phase-assignment table (sonnet by default), but the compiled transport never consults that table, so the two surfaces disagree and the model choice is decided by the account, not by gentle-ai or the user.

Checked against `main` at `84d36d4` (after 2.6.0) and again on 2026-09-10 (after 2.7.0, adapter unchanged since `9a27cd5`): the adapter still passes no `--model`.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce
1. Claude Code account whose default model is Opus 5 (1M). User `settings.json` sets a different model (here a non-Opus one); receipt-driven development enabled globally.
2. In a scratch git repository, add a small bash PreToolUse hook (`hooks/guard.sh`, ~25 lines: reads stdin, greps for a commit command, refuses a bypass flag, checks a pinned reviewer model in `hooks/guard.conf`, exits 2 on missing marker file) and stage it.
3. `gentle-ai review status --cwd <repo> --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --agent claude-code --next-transition` → START → consent `granted`. Native selection returns four lenses (risk, resilience, readability, reliability).
4. For each lens, emit the exact provider context: `gentle-ai review lens-context --cwd <repo> --repository-context <handle> --lineage <id> --target <sha256> --expected-revision <sha256> --lens <lens>` (about 10 KB each).
5. Pipe that context into the adapter's exact command (with `--output-format json` only to read `modelUsage`), once without `--model` and once with `--model sonnet`, from an empty scratch directory and with `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` unset.

Model fallback alone reproduces with a one-line prompt (`Reply with the single word OK.`):

| flags | `modelUsage` |
| --- | --- |
| adapter flags without `--setting-sources ""` | the model configured in `settings.json` |
| adapter flags (with `--setting-sources ""`) | `claude-opus-5[1m]` (account default) |
| adapter flags + `--model sonnet` | `claude-sonnet-5` |

### ✅ Expected Behavior
The fresh reviewer runs on the model gentle-ai assigns to review roles (the same table the installed `review-*` sub-agents resolve from: persisted phase assignment → `default` → sonnet), or at least on the user's configured model. The account default should never decide which model reviews a candidate, and a lens should not fail closed because of a model the user did not choose.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
Shell-hook candidate, four lenses, adapter flags verbatim (Windows, Claude Code 2.1.261):

| lens | without `--model` (account default `claude-opus-5[1m]`) | with `--model sonnet` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| review-risk | exit 0, valid result (65 s) | exit 0, valid result (115 s) |
| review-resilience | **exit 1 after 3 s, `is_error: true`, safeguards refusal** | exit 0, valid result (140 s) |
| review-readability | exit 0, valid result (59 s) | exit 0, valid result (115 s) |
| review-reliability | **exit 1 after 3 s, `is_error: true`, safeguards refusal** | exit 0, valid result (157 s) |

Inside gentle-ai the failure surfaces as `claude reviewer transport failed: exit status 1: API Error: Opus 5 (1M context)'s safeguards flagged this message …`; the lineage stays `reviewing` with `reviewer_results_required`, and STATUS re-offers the same slot, which fails the same way every time. Previously observed three times in real sessions on hook/guard candidates; a minimal JavaScript candidate (one function) does not trigger the refusal, so the refusal is content-dependent, while the model fallback is deterministic.

Workaround in use: a local PreToolUse guard that requires every `gentle-ai review capture-result|capture-refuter|capture-validation` invocation to carry an `ANTHROPIC_MODEL=<model>` prefix (Claude Code honours the env var over settings). It works but pins the model outside gentle-ai, must be replicated per repository, and is invisible to the orchestrator contract.

### Gentle AI Version
2.6.0 (stable) in the original report; reproduced by others on 2.5.0 and 2.7.0 (stable, 2026-09-08). Adapter unchanged on `main` since `9a27cd5`.

### Operating System
Windows (11, x64)

### AI Agent / Client
Claude Code 2.1.261 (original report); others on 2.1.219 and 2.1.263

### 📋 Affected Area
Review / RDD (reviewer provider transport)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output
```text
API Error: Opus 5 (1M context)'s safeguards flagged this message (https://www.anthropic.com/legal/aup). This sometimes happens with safe, normal conversations. Claude Code can't respond to this message with Opus 5 (1M context).
```

### Additional Context
Two ways to fix it; either one resolves this report:

**(a) Pass `--model` from gentle-ai's own model assignment.** `ClaudeAdapter` gains a `Model` field appended as `--model <value>`; the CLI resolves it in `reviewProviderAdapterFor` for `AgentClaudeCode` through the same resolution the `review-*` sub-agents use (`resolveClaudePhaseAssignment`: persisted `claude_phase_assignments` → `default` → sonnet), with an environment override `GENTLE_AI_CLAUDE_REVIEWER_MODEL` as an escape hatch for one machine or CI. Configure Models could later expose an explicit slot for review lenses. I have a working patch for this (6 files, +219/−3, adapter minimality guard and package tests green, `go build ./...` clean) and can open a PR once the issue is approved.

**(b) Keep the user's configured model despite `--setting-sources ""`.** Read `model` from the user's `settings.json` and pass it as `--model`. Simpler, but it still lets an account or user setting override gentle-ai's per-role assignment and diverges from what the installed `review-*` agents declare.

(a) keeps the model decision where gentle-ai already makes it; (b) only restores the user's choice. Both remove the dependency on the account default.

title: bug(doctor): state:json remedy tells users to delete state.json on a permission error
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

When `state.Read` fails with any error other than "file not found", `checkStateJSON` (`internal/cli/doctor.go`) renders the same remedy regardless of error class:

> Delete or repair <state.json>, then re-run 'gentle-ai install'

For a **permission error** (`open ...: permission denied`) the actionable problem is file permissions or ownership, not corruption. Deleting `state.json` is destructive advice that loses the user's agent registrations and does not fix the underlying access problem — the recreated file will hit the same EACCES on the next run if the environment is the issue.

The same branch also labels every failure as "failed to parse", which is inaccurate for read errors.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

Non-destructive sandbox repro (verified on 2.6.0):

1. `SANDBOX=$(mktemp -d)`
2. `mkdir -p "$SANDBOX/.gentle-ai"`
3. `echo '{"installed_agents":["pi"]}' > "$SANDBOX/.gentle-ai/state.json"`
4. `chmod 000 "$SANDBOX/.gentle-ai/state.json"`
5. `HOME="$SANDBOX" gentle-ai doctor`

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The remedy for a permission-denied read distinguishes it from genuine corruption: advise inspecting the file's permissions/ownership (or moving it aside intentionally), keeping doctor's read-only mandate.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

```shell
[xx]  state:json   failed to parse .../state.json: open .../state.json: permission denied
     Remedy: Delete or repair .../state.json, then re-run 'gentle-ai install'
```

### Gentle AI Version

2.6.0

### Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
$ HOME="$SANDBOX" gentle-ai doctor | grep -A1 state:json
  [xx]  state:json                     failed to parse /tmp/…/.gentle-ai/state.json: open /tmp/…/.gentle-ai/state.json: permission denied
       Remedy: Delete or repair /tmp/…/.gentle-ai/state.json, then re-run 'gentle-ai install'
```

### Additional Context

- Fix is scoped to the non-`IsNotExist` branch of `checkStateJSON`: classify with `os.IsPermission` (and arguably `errors.Is(err, fs.PathError{})` unwrapping) before choosing remedy text; "failed to parse" wording could also distinguish read vs parse failures.
- Related: #3512 / #1197 want remedies to become executable — remedy text should be accurate per error class before that happens.

title: bug(doctor): state:json skips config-dir verification for most agents — agentConfigDir uses drifted agent IDs
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

`gentle-ai doctor`'s `state:json` check is supposed to verify that each installed agent's managed config directory exists. The lookup table that decides which dir to check (`agentConfigDir` in `internal/cli/doctor.go`) has drifted from the real agent ID vocabulary in `internal/model/types.go`:

- **Dead branches**: the map keys `vscode` and `kiro` match no real `AgentID` (the real IDs are `vscode-copilot` and `kiro-ide`), so those branches can never fire. The stale `vscode` branch even points at `~/.config/Code`, while the catalog manages `~/.copilot` for `vscode-copilot`.
- **Silently skipped agents**: `pi`, `gemini-cli`, `kilocode`, `kimi`, `qwen-code`, `openclaw`, `trae-ide`, `hermes`, and `antigravity` return `""` from `agentConfigDir`, so their managed config dirs are never verified. If `~/.pi` or `~/.gemini` disappears, doctor still reports `state file OK` and `Status: healthy`.

`internal/catalog/agents.go` already carries `ConfigPath` for every agent, so the hand-maintained switch duplicates — and now contradicts — the source of truth. This is the same registry-rot risk that the `agentToolBinaries` comment in the same file already warns about.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

Non-destructive sandbox repro (verified on 2.6.0):

1. `SANDBOX=$(mktemp -d)`
2. `mkdir -p "$SANDBOX/.gentle-ai" "$SANDBOX/.config/opencode"`
3. Copy your `~/.gentle-ai/state.json` into `$SANDBOX/.gentle-ai/` (with `installed_agents` containing `pi`, or any of the skipped IDs)
4. Do **not** create `$SANDBOX/.pi`
5. `HOME="$SANDBOX" gentle-ai doctor`

### ✅ Expected Behavior

`state:json` warns that the managed config dir for `pi` (`~/.pi`) is missing, with the sync remedy — the same way it behaves today for `claude-code`, `opencode`, or `codex` when their config dirs are absent.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

`state:json` passes: `state file OK — 2 agent(s) installed: opencode, pi` — even though `~/.pi` does not exist in the sandboxed HOME. The `pi` entry is silently skipped because `agentConfigDir` has no `pi` key.

### Gentle AI Version

2.6.0

### Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
$ HOME="$SANDBOX" gentle-ai doctor | grep state:json
  [ok]  state:json                     state file OK — 2 agent(s) installed: opencode, pi
# ~/.pi does not exist in $SANDBOX — the check never looked at it
```

### Additional Context

- Evidence in code: `agentConfigDir` (`internal/cli/doctor.go`) vs `AgentID` constants (`internal/model/types.go`) and `ConfigPath` (`internal/catalog/agents.go`).
- Fix direction: derive the per-agent config dirs from the catalog's `ConfigPath` (expanding `~`) instead of a second hand-maintained registry, so new agents are covered automatically.
- Related but different: #1623 covers the reverse drift (managed configs on disk for agents *missing* from `installed_agents`); #709 is why doctor derives checks from `installed_agents`.

title: bug(review): committed-range START selects stale candidate view and fails rev-parse
body:
## Summary

A committed-range ordinary review cannot start because the native candidate view appears tied to stale worktree metadata rather than the current review target.

## Environment

- Gentle AI CLI: `2.6.0` stable
- Client: Pi native review facade
- OS / architecture: Linux x86_64
- Review contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`

## Observed sequence

1. A workspace review was not applicable because only planning metadata and an unrelated local change remained in the working tree.
2. A committed-range ordinary START was requested with `committedOnly: true` and a verified immutable base commit.
3. The short base reference returned `native-start-base-ref-unresolvable`; this matches the separately tracked short-SHA behavior.
4. Retrying once with the full immutable object ID returned `native-operation-failed` before lineage creation, with candidate-view phase `git-failure` and `git_subcommand: rev-parse`.
5. Read-only inspection confirmed that the full base object resolves locally, while existing candidate-view worktrees point to older unrelated HEAD commits.

## Expected behavior

START should construct or select a candidate view bound to the requested committed range, or return a typed actionable failure that identifies the unresolved reference and candidate-view context.

## Actual behavior

The full immutable base object is available, but candidate-view construction fails during `git rev-parse`. No lineage or review authority is created, and the review cannot proceed.

## Minimal reproduction

1. In Pi, use a branch containing committed changes while the workspace has only unrelated/planning metadata changes.
2. Inspect the candidate and request ordinary START for an explicit committed range using a full immutable base object ID and `committedOnly: true`.
3. Observe `native-operation-failed` in candidate-view phase with `git_subcommand: rev-parse`, despite the base object resolving locally.

## Preserved state

No source changes, Git references, review lineage, authority, reviewer result, receipt, commit, push, pull request, or deployment were created by the failed START attempts.

Privacy scan completed before submission: this report excludes repository/project identity, paths, usernames, hostnames, credentials, source, diffs, raw arguments, environment values, and opaque bindings.

title: fix(review): publish targeted validator evidence in last-event closure schema
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

A rejected targeted-validator capture emits a `gentle-ai.review-last-event-closure/v1` document containing `targeted_validator_evidence`, but the published last-event closure schema sets `additionalProperties: false` and does not declare that property.

The producer therefore emits a document that is invalid against its own advertised schema. Strict Pi carriers reject the mutating capture as `schema-incompatible`, leaving the mutation outcome unknown and requiring fail-closed STATUS reconciliation.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Check out clean `main` at `e5ddebcef9bfb2f9e90db4ef8af16797d770c122`.
2. Build `./cmd/gentle-ai` and the benchmark runner.
3. Run `j123-rejected-provider-validator-starts-fresh-high-risk-review`.
4. Observe the rejected targeted-validator path emit an escalated `gentle-ai.review-last-event-closure/v1` containing `targeted_validator_evidence`.
5. Inspect `contracts/review-integration/v2/schemas/last-event-closure.schema.json`.
6. Observe that the schema has `additionalProperties: false` but no `targeted_validator_evidence` property.
7. Run `TestTargetedValidatorCaptureEscalatesRejectedCorrectionWithoutFinalize`; it passes because it unmarshals the runtime JSON but does not validate it against the published schema.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Every emitted `gentle-ai.review-last-event-closure/v1` document must validate against the published schema.

The schema should strictly declare the optional native-emitted `targeted_validator_evidence` shape without weakening `additionalProperties`, version checks, authority binding, replay rules, or terminal lifecycle semantics.

Published-schema conformance coverage must include the rejected/escalated targeted-validator closure.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The native emitter adds `targeted_validator_evidence` for rejected targeted validation, while the published schema forbids the field.

A strict carrier reports:

`review/capture-provider-role: schema-incompatible`

Because the operation is mutating, the carrier must treat the outcome as unknown, perform one STATUS reconciliation, and never replay the capture. In the observed Pi flow, no recoverable authority candidate remained available.

### Gentle AI Version

`dev` at `e5ddebcef9bfb2f9e90db4ef8af16797d770c122`

--- PASS: TestTargetedValidatorCaptureEscalatesRejectedCorrectionWithoutFinalize

  targeted_validator_evidence property: absent

native rejected-validator closure:

title: bug(review): selectorless preflight STATUS times out pre_native on its first call with an empty review authority store (2.6.0 stable)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I searched open and closed issues for an equivalent report. Related `operation_timeout` reports exist (#3871, #3733, #3260, #3314) and one related `pre_native` preflight failure (#4021), but each requires an existing lineage, a prior capture, an extra selector, or a nested worktree. None covers the plain selectorless preflight failing on its **first** call with an empty review authority store. Detailed comparison below.
- [x] This automated provider-defect report contains privacy-scrubbed diagnostics only.

### Bug Description

The selectorless negotiated preflight — the exact entry point the Claude Code Stop hook names — exhausts its aggregate time budget in `pre_native` on its first invocation. No selectors are passed: no `--base-ref`, no `--committed-only`, no lineage, no target.

The review authority store is empty: `.git/gentle-ai` contains only the SDD runtime subtree and no review lineages, so the failure happens before any transaction could exist. The envelope reports `retry_safe: false` and `next_action: stop`, so it was not retried.

This is consequential in 2.6.0 specifically because of the new Stop hook (#4071). The hook makes preflight mandatory before reporting completion and prints both the STATUS command and a START invocation. The orchestrator contract forbids running a command inferred from prose or a stale reply — a START must come from a live STATUS `next_transition`. With STATUS returning `next_action: stop`, the consumer has **no legal continuation at all**: the candidate can neither be reviewed nor legally released from the entry rule, and the hook re-arms the same requirement.

This reports observed evidence only; the root cause is unconfirmed.

### Environment

- Gentle AI: `2.6.0` (stable channel)
- Client: Claude Code
- OS/architecture: Linux x86_64 (WSL2)
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`
- Agent binding: `claude-code`
- RDD mode: on (decided by global; clone-local unset)
- Repository: TypeScript/React, ~16,200 tracked files
- Candidate: one modified tracked Markdown file, +9 lines, workspace projection, worktree otherwise clean
- Review authority before the call: no review lineages present

### Operation Shape

1. The session ends with an unreviewed candidate. The Stop hook fires and prints the `gentle-ai.review-stop-hook/v1` reminder naming the STATUS command and a START transition.
2. The consumer runs the named selectorless preflight verbatim, with the repository as process cwd:

```
gentle-ai review status --cwd <repo> \
  --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --agent claude-code --next-transition
```

3. It times out.

No START was run, because the contract requires routing only from a live STATUS `next_transition` and never from a command that appeared in prose.

### Actual Behaviour

```json
{
  "schema": "gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2",
  "contract": "gentle-ai.review-integration/v2",
  "operation": "review.status",
  "phase": "pre_native",
  "code": "operation_timeout",
  "message": "The negotiated review operation exceeded its aggregate time budget.",
  "mutation_outcome": "not_started",
  "authority_applicability": "not_evaluated",
  "retry_safe": false,
  "replayability": "manual_action_required",
  "required_inputs": [],
  "next_action": "stop",
  "cause": "context deadline exceeded"
}
```

Exit status is non-zero.

### Expected Behaviour

The selectorless preflight returns a status envelope with a `next_transition` naming exactly one START invocation for the current worktree candidate, as the Stop hook's own reminder presupposes.

If a candidate exceeds a supported operational limit, the failure should name that limit rather than returning a generic aggregate timeout — and a one-file, nine-line candidate is not near any such limit.

Failing that, `next_action: stop` with `retry_safe: false` should carry a documented continuation from the reason-code table. It carries none, which is what strands the consumer.

### Attempts and Outcomes

- STATUS attempts: 1. One bounded attempt, not retried, because the envelope reports `retry_safe: false` and `next_action: stop`.
- START attempts: 0. No START was run.
- Capture, correction, validation, acknowledgement, recovery, reset, or manual authority edit: none attempted.

### Negative Controls

- **Not a nested worktree.** `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` is `true`, there is no `.git` file, and the checkout is an ordinary repository — the exact shape #4021 records as returning a well-formed envelope. So worktree placement is not the variable here.
- **No selectors involved.** The failing call passes no `--base-ref` and no `--committed-only`, so the base-ref collect round of #3314 is not on this path.
- **Authority store empty.** No review lineage exists, so no prior capture, correction, or admitted result is present.

### Minimal Reproduction

1. Enable RDD globally and install the 2.6.0 Claude Code hooks.
2. In an ordinary repository (not a worktree) with no review transactions, modify a single tracked text file by a few lines and leave the worktree otherwise clean.
3. Let a Claude Code session end so the Stop hook fires with an unreviewed candidate.
4. Run the selectorless preflight the hook names, with no selectors.
5. Observe `operation_timeout` during `pre_native`, mutation not started, applicability not evaluated, automatic replay prohibited, and no continuation.

### Preserved-State Evidence

- The operation is read-only; `mutation_outcome` is `not_started`.
- No review authority was created; the review transaction store remained empty.
- Candidate bytes, paths, modes, and index intent are unchanged.
- No commit, push, or pull request resulted from the failed operation.
- Lineage named by the hook's START text: `review-f2dcfd39e28df055`. No transaction was created under it.

### Relationship to Existing Reports

The envelope is byte-identical across several of these; what differs is the operation shape and the lifecycle state, which is how the existing reports are already distinguished from one another (see the comparison table in #3871).

| Report | State | Why it does not cover this |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #3871 | open | Requires an active lineage with two admitted reviewer captures. Here: zero lineages, zero captures. |
| #3733 | open | Requires an active high-risk START. Here: no START was run. |
| #3260 | open | Requires a capture invocation rejected during local argument validation. Here: no capture was attempted. |
| #3314 | closed (completed) | Nearest match, and the same envelope, but its failing call carries `--base-ref <default-branch> --committed-only`; its plain step-1 selectorless call **succeeded**. Here the plain call is the one that fails, and this is stable `2.6.0` rather than prerelease `2.4.0-rc.8`. |
| #4021 | open | Different code (`operation_failed`, `retry_safe: true`, `next_action: retry`) and its distinguishing variable is a repository-nested worktree, which this checkout is not. |

On #3314 specifically: it is closed as completed, but I could not establish a **verifiable relevant published fix** for it in this build's evidence channel. It has no linked closing pull request, and neither the v2.5.0 nor the v2.6.0 stable release notes reference it or any fix for a `pre_native` STATUS aggregate timeout. So this is filed as a new report rather than as a regression occurrence against it. If maintainers know the #3314 fix did ship in 2.5.0 or 2.6.0, then this should be reclassified as a regression on stable and I am happy to have it closed as such.

### Privacy

This report excludes raw argv, absolute paths, private repository and project names, usernames, hostnames, credentials, diffs, source contents, and environment values.

Git aborts the fetch because `V1.25.3` and `v1.25.3` require the same filesystem lock name.

Other

Installation Pipeline

title: bug(bench): engram-download journeys j2138/j3043 flake on CI with GitHub API 403 from the shared-runner rate limit
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

The two core-corpus journeys whose install steps download the engram binary — `j2138-opencode-native-fallback-boundary` and `j3043-opencode-managed-background-activation` — flake intermittently in the CI `Unit Tests` job's `Run benchmark evidence` step. Their `gentle-ai install` step fails with `fetch latest engram version: GitHub API returned HTTP 403`, both journeys record `failed` across every dimension ("the run measured nothing for those rows"), and the step exits nonzero — putting a red `Unit Tests` check on unrelated PRs.

Mechanism, from `internal/components/engram/download.go`:

1. `DownloadLatestBinary` → `fetchLatestEngramVersion()` → GET `https://api.github.com/repos/<engram>/releases/latest`.
2. When `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN` is present, GitHub Actions injects a repository-scoped one; against a different repository's releases endpoint it can respond 401/403, and the code already retries anonymously (`fetchLatestEngramVersion` handles that case).
3. On shared `ubuntu-latest` runners the anonymous retry lands on a runner-pool IP that has exhausted GitHub's 60 req/hr unauthenticated quota → HTTP 403 → the install pipeline fails closed.

Only 2 of the 61 core journeys exercise the engram download path, which is why the flake always names exactly this pair. This also contradicts `bench/README.md`'s core-corpus contract — "It is **deterministic and offline**" — for these two journeys: their outcome depends on live GitHub API availability from the runner's IP.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Open any PR (observed on a message-text-only change; nothing in the diff needs to touch the install path).
2. Wait for the `Unit Tests` job, step `Run benchmark evidence` (`gentle-ai-bench run --binary … --out …`, full core corpus).
3. Intermittently — rate-limit windows on the runner IP — j2138 and j3043 fail together at their install step.

Selecting just the affected pair locally:

```bash
cd bench && go build -o gentle-ai-bench .
./gentle-ai-bench run --binary <path-to-built-gentle-ai> \
  --only j2138-opencode-native-fallback-boundary,j3043-opencode-managed-background-activation
```

This passes locally with network headroom; reproducing the failure needs an egress IP whose anonymous GitHub API quota is exhausted (shared CI runners hit it regularly; a 403-stub egress reproduces it deterministically).

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The bench core corpus outcome should not depend on live GitHub API reachability or the runner IP's rate-limit budget, per its own documented offline/deterministic contract. A red `Unit Tests` check on an unrelated PR should indicate a product or bench defect, not GitHub's quota for a shared IP.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Intermittent CI failure: 2/61 journeys fail with `GitHub API returned HTTP 403`, the step exits nonzero because "the run measured nothing for those rows", and unrelated PRs show a red `Unit Tests` check that a re-run clears without any code change.

### Gentle AI Version

main @ 4db804e5 (bench built from source in the CI job)

### Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
# CI run 33979100739, job 101341009933 (PR #4198):
failed: step "public multi-mode install" after: public multi install failed: …
Error: execute install pipeline: download engram binary: fetch latest engram version: GitHub API returned HTTP 403

failed: step "install reports managed activation" after: OpenCode background install failed: …
Error: execute install pipeline: download engram binary: fetch latest engram version: GitHub API returned HTTP 403

journeys: 59 completed, 0 unsupported, 2 failed
2 journey(s) FAILED: the run measured nothing for those rows, so it exits nonzero rather than letting a gate read it as success.
```

- Failed run: https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/actions/runs/33979100739 (PR #4198)
- Same code, passed on retrigger minutes later: https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/actions/runs/33980292791

title: bug(gga config): generated EXCLUDE_PATTERNS use mid-string wildcards that never match — every test/spec file is reviewed
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

The `~/.config/gga/config` generated by `gentle-ai sync` sets:

```
EXCLUDE_PATTERNS="*.test.*,*.spec.*,*.d.ts,dist/*,build/*,node_modules/*"
```

`*.test.*` and `*.spec.*` **match nothing** in gga 2.10.1, so every test and spec file is sent to the AI reviewer on every commit. The failure is silent: `gga config` prints the patterns as configured, and `gga run` echoes them in `Exclude patterns:`, so nothing signals that two of the six are inert.

**Root cause** — gga's matcher (`bin/gga`, exclude branch at lines 1102-1107, identical to the include branch at 1081-1085):

```bash
if [[ "$pattern" == \** ]]; then
  local suffix="${pattern#\*}"        # strips ONLY the leading '*'
  if [[ "$file" == *"$suffix" ]]; then  # "$suffix" is QUOTED -> no globbing
```

Stripping only the leading `*` and then comparing against a **quoted** suffix makes every remaining `*` literal. For `*.test.*` the suffix is `.test.*`, so a file would have to end with a literal asterisk to match. Only patterns whose wildcard is strictly leading (`*.test.ts`) work.

**gga's own default is the working form.** `bin/gga:441` ships:

```bash
EXCLUDE_PATTERNS="*.test.ts,*.spec.ts,*.test.tsx,*.spec.tsx,*.d.ts"
```

and the documented examples above it (`bin/gga:439-440`) use the same enumerated style. So the config generated by gentle-ai contradicts the default of the tool it configures.

`*.d.ts`, `dist/*`, `build/*` and `node_modules/*` are unaffected — the first has a leading wildcard, the rest take the non-`*` branch.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `gentle-ai sync --agents claude-code` and confirm the generated `~/.config/gga/config` contains `EXCLUDE_PATTERNS="*.test.*,*.spec.*,..."`.
2. Reproduce gga's matcher exactly (verbatim from `bin/gga:1102-1107`):

   ```bash
   matches() {
     local pattern="$1" file="$2"
     if [[ "$pattern" == \** ]]; then
       local suffix="${pattern#\*}"
       [[ "$file" == *"$suffix" ]] && return 0
     fi
     return 1
   }
   for p in '*.spec.*' '*.spec.ts'; do
     matches "$p" src/auth.service.spec.ts && echo "$p -> EXCLUDED" || echo "$p -> not excluded"
   done
   ```
3. Or end-to-end: stage a `*.spec.ts` file in a repo with the generated config and run `gga run`.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The generated config excludes test and spec files. `EXCLUDE_PATTERNS` should use the enumerated leading-wildcard form that gga's own default already uses:

```
EXCLUDE_PATTERNS="*.test.ts,*.test.tsx,*.spec.ts,*.spec.tsx,*.test.js,*.test.jsx,*.spec.js,*.spec.jsx,*.d.ts"
```

Secondarily, an unmatchable pattern should not be silently accepted — either gga supports mid-string wildcards, or it warns when a pattern contains a non-leading `*`.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

```
p='*.spec.*'   file=src/auth.service.spec.ts   -> not excluded
p='*.test.*'   file=src/user.test.ts           -> not excluded
p='*.spec.ts'  file=src/auth.service.spec.ts   -> EXCLUDED
p='*.test.ts'  file=src/user.test.ts           -> EXCLUDED
```

Every test and spec file reaches the reviewer on every commit: extra provider cost and latency on files the configuration explicitly meant to skip, plus review noise on test code. Because `gentle-ai sync` regenerates the file, a manual fix is reverted by the next sync or upgrade.

### Gentle AI Version

gentle-ai 2.5.0 (Homebrew) · gga v2.10.1

### Operating System

Windows (WSL)

### AI Agent / Client

Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area

Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
# generated by gentle-ai sync
$ grep EXCLUDE_PATTERNS ~/.config/gga/config
EXCLUDE_PATTERNS="*.test.*,*.spec.*,*.d.ts,dist/*,build/*,node_modules/*"

# gga reports them as configured — no warning that two are inert
$ gga config
  EXCLUDE_PATTERNS:  *.test.*,*.spec.*,*.d.ts,dist/*,build/*,node_modules/*

# gga's own shipped default, which does work
$ sed -n '441p' "$(readlink -f "$(command -v gga)")"
EXCLUDE_PATTERNS="*.test.ts,*.spec.ts,*.test.tsx,*.spec.tsx,*.d.ts"
```

### Additional Context

Checked against nearby reports; this is a distinct root cause:

- #3090 — config found but no values applied. **Does not reproduce here**: on this machine `gga config` shows every value correctly loaded (`PROVIDER: claude`, patterns, `RULES_FILE`). The config *is* applied; the pattern syntax is what cannot match.
- #2465 — staged Java files skipped by `FILE_PATTERNS`. Same matcher, opposite direction (include failing), different file type.
- #3079 — reviewer reports missing tests *when specs are excluded*, i.e. exclusion working as intended.

The one-line fix on the gentle-ai side is to generate the same enumerated form gga already defaults to.

title: fix(tui): explicit Upgrade and sync is suppressed by update-check cooldown
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] Searched open and closed issues; no equivalent report was found.
- [x] Verified the behavior remains present in the published `v2.6.0` source.
- [x] I understand implementation requires maintainer approval under the repository issue-first workflow.

### Bug description

The TUI action **Upgrade and sync** can silently skip an available `gentle-ai` upgrade and run only synchronization when the six-hour background update-check cooldown is active.

An explicit user-requested upgrade should not be treated like a passive launch-time update check. The current behavior makes the action appear successful while leaving the executable on the previous version.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install `gentle-ai` through the official Homebrew formula.
2. Have version `2.5.0` installed while release `2.6.0` is available.
3. Ensure `state.json` contains a successful `last_update_check` within the previous six hours.
4. Launch the `gentle-ai` TUI.
5. Select **Upgrade and sync**.
6. Observe that synchronization runs, but `gentle-ai version` remains `2.5.0`.
7. Run `brew upgrade gentle-ai` manually and observe that Homebrew upgrades to `2.6.0`.

### Expected behavior

Selecting **Upgrade and sync** should perform a fresh update check, apply every available managed upgrade, and then synchronize as permitted by the existing self-upgrade safety rules.

The six-hour cooldown may remain appropriate for passive checks during TUI initialization, but it should not suppress an explicit user action.

### Actual behavior

The explicit action reuses the launch-time results. When the cooldown is fresh, `CheckAllWithCooldown` returns no results. `startUpgradeSync()` passes that empty result set to the upgrade executor, which has nothing to execute, and synchronization proceeds.

The user receives a sync result without the available executable upgrade being applied.

### Source evidence (`v2.6.0`)

- `internal/tui/model.go`: `Model.Init()` calls `update.CheckAllWithCooldown(...)` using `update.UpdateCheckTTL`.
- `internal/update/cooldown.go`: the TTL remains six hours and a fresh timestamp returns `nil` without a network check.
- `internal/tui/model.go`: `startUpgradeSync()` passes `m.UpdateResults` directly to the upgrade function and then continues to sync when Gentle AI was not upgraded.
- Comparing `v2.5.0...v2.6.0` shows that the cooldown change in `v2.6.0` concerns reconciled timestamp persistence; it does not bypass the cooldown for explicit upgrade actions.

### Environment

- Gentle AI: `2.5.0`
- Available release: `2.6.0`
- OS: Linux x86_64
- Installation method: official Homebrew formula
- Channel: stable

### Workaround

```bash
brew upgrade gentle-ai
gentle-ai sync
```

### Suggested regression coverage

Add a TUI test where `last_update_check` is inside the cooldown window but an explicit **Upgrade and sync** selection still performs a fresh update check and receives an `UpdateAvailable` result. Keep the existing cooldown behavior for passive initialization checks.

title: bug(review): Codex safety rejects exact consent-relay START transition

### Pre-flight Checklist

### Bug Description

On Gentle AI 2.5.0 with Codex, negotiated review status returns a fresh executable START transition containing the provider-owned consent-relay binding. Submitting that exact transition once is rejected by the Codex command-safety layer as unacceptable risk because it interprets the same consent-relay binding as forbidden.

This report records observed behavior only. The apparent contract mismatch is an inference, not a confirmed root cause.

### Steps to Reproduce

5. Submit that exact returned transition once, without adding, removing, or changing any argument.
6. Observe the command-safety layer reject it before native execution, stating that starting review with consent relay is unacceptable because the governing contract forbids appending it.

### Expected Behavior

An exact executable transition returned by negotiated status should be admissible to the Codex execution layer. If consent is required, native START should return the typed consent envelope. If the transition is unsafe, status should return a typed stop or collect transition rather than an executable command that the consumer must reject.

### Actual Behavior

One exact START attempt was rejected before the Gentle AI operation ran. The rejection classified the provider-returned consent-relay binding as an impermissibly appended argument even though it was part of the exact native transition.

title: test(engram): TestStdioHandshake_GarbageOutput races the helper exit and reports broken pipe instead of invalid MCP stdout
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

`TestStdioHandshake_GarbageOutput` in `internal/components/engram/healthprobe_test.go` is racy. The `garbage` helper mode prints one non-JSON-RPC line and exits immediately. When the child exits before `stdioHandshake` writes the `initialize` request to its stdin, the write fails with `EPIPE` and the probe returns `write engram mcp initialize request: write |1: broken pipe` instead of the expected `invalid MCP stdout` classification.

It failed the `release.yml` preflight unit-test step for `v2.6.0` on `c24a724a` while `ci.yml` had passed the same package on the same commit minutes earlier. A re-run of the preflight passed.

The race also has a production-facing consequence: an `engram mcp` binary that prints garbage and exits would be diagnosed by `doctor` as a broken pipe rather than as invalid MCP stdout, depending on scheduling. The handshake should classify a child that exited after emitting non-protocol stdout as invalid stdout regardless of whether the stdin write or the stdout read loses the race.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `go test ./internal/components/engram/ -run TestStdioHandshake_GarbageOutput -count=200` on a loaded machine (or with `GOMAXPROCS=1`).
2. Observe occasional failures with `write |1: broken pipe`.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

`stdioHandshake` returns an `invalid MCP stdout` error whenever the child emits a non-JSON-RPC line, even if the child exits before the initialize request is written. The test passes deterministically.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The write to stdin occasionally loses the race with the child's exit and the error is `write engram mcp initialize request: write |1: broken pipe`.

### Gentle AI Version

main @ c24a724a (v2.6.0)

### Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
--- FAIL: TestStdioHandshake_GarbageOutput (0.00s)
    healthprobe_test.go:440: stdioHandshake() error = write engram mcp initialize request: write |1: broken pipe, want invalid stdout error
FAIL
FAIL	github.com/gentleman-programming/gentle-ai/v2/internal/components/engram	1.425s
```

### Additional Context

- Failing preflight: https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/actions/runs/33917408534 (first attempt).
- Possible fix: when the stdin write returns `EPIPE`, drain whatever the child already wrote to stdout and run it through the same validation path, so garbage output is classified as invalid stdout; otherwise surface the child's exit. The test helper could also block on stdin before printing so the ordering is deterministic, but that only hides the production race.

### 💡 Problem Statement
Google Antigravity configurations are currently fragmented. Global skills and MCP configurations are written to `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/`, which prevents Antigravity 2.0 (Desktop) and IDE from discovering them, while leaving `~/.gemini/config/` stale. Additionally, `skill-registry` does not discover skills residing under the canonical `~/.gemini/config/skills/` root.

Unify the global configuration root of Google Antigravity to `~/.gemini/config/` across Desktop, CLI (`agy`), and IDE:
1. **Adapter Path Unification (`internal/agents/antigravity/adapter.go`)**:
   - `GlobalConfigDir(homeDir)` resolves to `~/.gemini/config`.
   - `SkillsDir(homeDir)` resolves to `~/.gemini/config/skills`.
   - `MCPConfigPath(homeDir, _)` resolves to `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json`.
   - `SettingsPath(homeDir)` preserves variant-specific isolation via `antigravityVariantDir`: resolves to `~/.gemini/antigravity-desktop/settings.json` if that directory exists, otherwise falling back to `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json`.
2. **Skill Registry Discovery (`internal/skillregistry/registry.go`)**:
