title: feat(testing): add foreground live-agent SDD and RDD bench
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Problem Statement

Gentle AI has deterministic CLI journeys and synthetic organic-runtime coverage, but it has no directly executable manual harness that launches the real Claude Code, Codex, Pi, and OpenCode clients in an attached terminal and follows an implementation from task prompt through SDD/RDD completion.

This leaves a critical integration gap: client startup, interactive consent, runtime-owned SDD routing, native RDD transitions, bounded correction, and final evidence can each work in isolation while the complete human-facing workflow still fails. These failures are currently discovered only during ad hoc maintainer sessions.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Add a manual live-agent bench under `scripts/` with documentation under `docs/testing/`.

The harness should:

- select Claude Code, Codex, Pi, or OpenCode;
- launch the selected client in the foreground with the controlling TTY inherited, never as a background process;
- create a fresh temporary Git fixture while preserving the user's existing authenticated runtime configuration;
- exercise four scenarios: direct/correct, direct/defective, SDD/correct, and SDD/post-verify-defective;
- leave SDD and RDD lifecycle decisions entirely to the selected runtime and Gentle AI rather than synthesizing transitions in shell;
- plant the defective direct implementation before review and inject the defective SDD candidate only after `sdd-verify`, so the latter honestly tests RDD over a post-SDD mutation rather than pretending SDD verification missed an organic defect;
- record actual `gentle-ai` command invocations without intercepting prompts or model output;
- run read-only post-exit assertions for fixture tests, SDD artifacts, review activity, unintended commits/remotes, and cleanup;
- support retaining the isolated workspace for manual inspection.

The harness is intentionally manual and nondeterministic. A missed planted defect is a failed live-agent bench run, not a condition to hide with synthetic reviewer output.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- Extending the deterministic Go journey corpus: rejected because that corpus intentionally synthesizes reviewer results and does not launch real agents or models.
- Extending organic-runtime CI tests: rejected because they use scripted model responses and cannot represent human consent prompts safely.
- Running clients noninteractively or in the background: rejected because native consent and other runtime prompts require an attached human-capable terminal.
- Capturing full terminal transcripts by default: rejected because interactive sessions may expose sensitive user input; the harness should record bounded command evidence and use an operator checklist instead.

### 📎 Additional Context

The implementation should remain outside `bench/` and `e2e/` so their deterministic contracts remain unchanged. Existing cross-lane host helpers and the transparent command-recording shim are useful precedents, but the new harness must drive complete user-agent workflows.

Expected first target is a POSIX shell host with preinstalled and authenticated `claude`, `codex`, `pi`, and/or `opencode` executables. Each run selects one runtime and one scenario; an aggregate mode may execute the matrix sequentially while keeping every client attached to the terminal.

title: bug(community-tool): Pi CodeGraph MCP registration fails on Windows without shell
body:
### Bug Description

Pi's CodeGraph MCP entry in `mcp.json` is written as `{command: "codegraph", args: ["serve", "--mcp"]}`. On Windows the npm global shim is only `codegraph.cmd`/`.ps1`, which agents that spawn without shell semantics cannot launch (Node `execFile('codegraph')` → `ENOENT`/EINVAL on win32). Pi therefore never starts the CodeGraph MCP server on Windows.

The fix `e904983b` (codegraph_native.go) resolves the vendored bundle `<shimDir>/node_modules/@colbymchenry/codegraph/node_modules/@colbymchenry/codegraph-win32-<arch>/node.exe + codegraph.js` and writes absolute native paths `{command: "<abs node.exe>", args: ["--liftoff-only", "<abs codegraph.js>", "serve", "--mcp"]}` on Windows, with graceful bare-name fallback.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. On Windows, `npm install -g @colbymchenry/codegraph`
2. Run `gentle-ai` TUI and install CodeGraph for Pi
3. Check `.pi/mcp.json` → bare `codegraph` entry
4. Pi tries to spawn `codegraph serve --mcp` without shell → ENOENT, CodeGraph unavailable

### Expected
On win32 with vendored bundle present, Pi's mcp.json contains absolute native entry and probe spawns it directly.

### Actual
Bare entry, probe fails, CodeGraph unavailable for Pi sub-agents.

### Environment
Windows 11, Node 24, codegraph 1.4.1

## 🔗 Tracking branch (fork)

Work in progress lives at [`Seinra/gentle-ai:fix/codegraph-windows`](https://github.com/Seinra/gentle-ai/tree/fix/codegraph-windows) (currently based on upstream v2.7.0, `go test ./internal/components/communitytool/` green). This branch is kept current via merges, so this pointer stays fresh — no PR until `status:approved`, per the issues-first rule. Note: this is the gentle-ai registration-side fix (absolute command paths in Pi's `mcp.json`), complementary to the merged gentle-pi#553 tool-side fix.

title: OpenCode review capture repeats stale managed-assets error after sync
body:
## Summary

OpenCode review capture transport repeatedly reports `opencode_review_transport_authority_unavailable` with `managed reviewer assets are outdated; run gentle-ai sync` even after managed sync completes and native STATUS reoffers the same reviewer slot.

## Sanitized environment

- gentle-ai: `2.5.0-rc.1`
- Evidence channel from build string: release candidate (`-rc.`)
- OS: `Darwin`
- Architecture: `arm64`
- Client/runtime: OpenCode `1.18.25`

## Operation shape

1. A medium-risk base-to-workspace-overlay review started successfully for a committed branch candidate.
2. Native STATUS returned one `review.capture-result` input for lens `review-reliability`.
3. OpenCode Task transport was launched with the provider-issued `GENTLE_AI_REVIEW_BINDING` prefix and the exact reviewer slot fields.
4. The transport failed with `opencode_review_transport_authority_unavailable` and instructed the caller to run native STATUS before retrying: `managed reviewer assets are outdated; run gentle-ai sync`.
5. `gentle-ai sync --agent opencode` completed successfully and reported managed components synced, with no runtime restart required.
6. Native STATUS reoffered the same bound reviewer slot.
7. Relaunching the same bound reviewer slot failed with the same `opencode_review_transport_authority_unavailable` / managed-assets-outdated message.

## Expected behavior

After sync completes and STATUS reoffers the same bound reviewer slot, the OpenCode review transport should produce a capturable reviewer result or return a terminal native state that does not repeat the stale-assets instruction.

## Actual behavior

The transport repeats the stale managed-assets failure after a completed sync and a STATUS-sanctioned retry.

## Bounded attempts and outcomes

- START: succeeded; lineage created.
- First reviewer capture launch: failed with `opencode_review_transport_authority_unavailable`.
- Managed sync: completed successfully.
- STATUS: reoffered the same reviewer slot.
- Second reviewer capture launch: failed with the same `opencode_review_transport_authority_unavailable` message.

## Safe opaque identifiers

- Lineage: `review-bf58dff3ab443054`
- Target identity: `sha256:61184c79257b1084b68292d49df261482f3cc3e25b9057dedae15ca30aaa6cde`
- Authority revision: `sha256:6e247eaed237722f50ae4f7a8b18444e98fd8c4783676f406bf16ead4788b32f`
- Subject hash: `sha256:514ef0de312932d5c45c64bbaf55a034ed605ae247c9d59599ccabdb5f88e82b`

## Minimal reproduction outline

1. Start a medium-risk review in OpenCode for a committed candidate using base-to-workspace-overlay mode.
2. Let native STATUS return a single `review.capture-result` slot.
3. Launch the OpenCode bound reviewer task.
4. If it reports managed assets outdated, run `gentle-ai sync --agent opencode`.
5. Re-enter STATUS and retry only when the same reviewer slot is reoffered.
6. Observe whether the same stale-assets transport error repeats.

## Privacy notes

This report omits raw argv, absolute paths, private project names, usernames, hostnames, credentials, diffs, source contents, and environment values.

title: feat(review): add immutable receipt-review transport for Cursor
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Problem Statement

Cursor is a first-class Gentle AI adapter (SDD, skills, MCP, personas), but it cannot participate in native immutable receipt-review.
  `gentle-ai review status|start --agent cursor` fails in preflight with `immutable_review_transport_unsupported` before any repository, target, or authority work. The same
  disposable candidate is startable with `--agent opencode`.
  This is policy, not an accident. #2209 limited native/bundled immutable RDD to OpenCode, Claude Code, and Codex (Pi via gentle-pi). Cursor is in the "every other built-in
  runtime" set. I re-checked `v2.5.0-rc.1`: `reviewTransportV1` and `ImmutableReviewExecutorV1` still advertise only `claude-code`, `opencode`, `codex`, and `pi`. Cursor
  remains dormant.
  Cursor users can implement in Cursor, then must hop to another runtime to run native review. That split is the problem.
  Reproduction (disposable git repo, one small workspace edit, RDD mode on):
  ```bash
  gentle-ai review status \
    --cwd <repo> \
    --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 \
    --agent cursor \
    --next-transition
  ```
  Actual: `immutable_review_transport_unsupported`, `next_action: stop`, `mutation_outcome: not_started`.
  Control with `--agent opencode` on the same candidate: `next_transition.execute` is `review.start` (`fresh_target_ready`).


### 📦 Proposed Solution

Admit Cursor as an immutable review runtime only after it owns a real fresh-reviewer boundary. Do not flip Eligible / capability bits first.
  The compiled contract already says what counts: a new constrained reviewer, Go-owned prompt materialization and admission, raw bytes back through the exact capture
  operation. Cursor subagents, skills, and prompt prose are not that boundary (#2209 non-goals).
  I am willing to implement and maintain this adapter after `status:approved` (and after any `status:needs-design` decision). Proposed direction, not a claim that it already
  works:
  - host-relay or scratch-process using `cursor-agent` (same class as Codex `exec` / Pi print-mode / OpenCode Task relay)
  - empty scratch directory, discovery surfaces disabled
  - Go keeps binding, capture, retry, correction, and closure
  - negotiated `review status|start --agent cursor` reaches repository validation instead of the current preflight refusal
  - no RDD parity claims until a native E2E matrix passes, same bar as #2208 for Codex
  I will not open a PR until this issue has `status:approved`.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- Keep Cursor as TierFull / SDD-only and keep reviewing in OpenCode, Claude Code, or Codex. This is the current workaround. It works, but it is not Cursor-native review.
 - Treat existing Cursor reviewer agents as transport. Rejected by #2209: generic subagents are not an immutable executor.
 - File this as a bug. Incorrect: the refusal is the intended #2207/#2209 gate.

### 📎 Additional Context

Sibling, not a duplicate: #3485 asks for the same class of adapter for Antigravity. This issue is Cursor-specific.
Related: #2209 (matrix), #2207 (pre-mutation gate), #2208 (Codex proof bar).
Offer: I can own the Cursor transport after approval, including follow-up breakage and the E2E proof the matrix requires. I already have a local fork and can reproduce the current refusal on demand.

I understand this may land as `status:needs-design` first. I want that decision before writing code.

title: bug(installer): published RC cannot be selected by the official binary installer
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I searched existing open and closed issues and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`.

### Bug Description

The published release candidate `v2.5.0-rc.1` cannot be installed unambiguously through the official installer from the same tag using its documented binary method.

The installer does not expose an explicit version or tag selector for this path. Its binary flow resolves `releases/latest`, which excludes prereleases, and expects a `.tar.gz` archive plus `checksums.txt`. The published RC instead provides a direct Linux amd64 binary plus `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

This report records the observed compatibility gap only. It does not assert an unconfirmed root cause.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. On Linux amd64 under WSL, inspect the official installer distributed from tag `v2.5.0-rc.1` and select its documented binary method.
2. Attempt to identify an option that pins the installation to the exact published tag.
3. Observe that the path has no explicit version or tag selector and resolves the stable `releases/latest` endpoint.
4. Compare the installer asset shape, `.tar.gz` plus `checksums.txt`, with the published RC assets, the direct `gentle-ai_2.5.0-rc.1_linux_amd64` binary plus `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
5. Stop before execution because the target cannot be proven to be the RC and the flow could reinstall the stable release.

### Expected Behavior

A published release candidate should be selectable by exact tag through the official installer from that tag, and the documented binary method should consume the asset and checksum names published for that candidate.

### Actual Behavior

The binary method cannot identify `v2.5.0-rc.1` as its target and expects a different release-asset shape. Running it would not prove that the RC is being installed, so the attempt must stop before mutation.

### Gentle AI Version

Installed: `2.4.0`. Target: `v2.5.0-rc.1`.

### Operating System

Windows (WSL), Ubuntu 26.04, Linux amd64.

### AI Agent / Client

Other: Gentle AI CLI.

### Affected Area

Installation Pipeline.

### Logs / Error Output

```text
target release: cannot be pinned to v2.5.0-rc.1
resolution surface: releases/latest (stable releases)
installer asset shape: .tar.gz + checksums.txt
published RC asset shape: direct linux_amd64 binary + SHA256SUMS.txt
mutation result: stopped before execution; no mutation
```

### Additional Context

- `v2.5.0-rc.1` is a public, non-draft prerelease published on 2026-08-26.
- The compatible public asset is `gentle-ai_2.5.0-rc.1_linux_amd64`.
- The existing `gentle-ai` installation remains healthy at `2.4.0`.
- No installation, configuration, repository, or RDD state changed during the bounded attempt.

title: OpenCode task delegation interrupted without result
body:
## Observed behavior

A delegated OpenCode `task` operation was interrupted before returning a verifiable result. Retrying the same task through its existing task handle was also interrupted.

## Expected behavior

A task should either complete with its declared result or return a structured, actionable failure that lets the consumer determine mutation state.

## Actual behavior

Both bounded attempts ended with the failure envelope: `[Tool execution was interrupted]`. No task result or mutation outcome was returned, so the consumer workflow halted and preserved state.

## Environment

- Client: OpenCode
- OS: Linux
- Operation shape: delegated general-agent task, then one resume attempt
- Attempts: 2
- Secrets, paths, project identifiers, command arguments, source contents, diffs, and environment values omitted intentionally.

## Minimal reproduction

1. In an active OpenCode session, invoke a permitted delegated general-agent task for a bounded code change.
2. Observe the task interruption envelope before a result is returned.
3. Resume the same task once using its returned task handle.
4. Observe the same interruption envelope.

## Impact

The caller cannot safely tell whether source mutation occurred, cannot verify the work, and cannot retry indefinitely.

## Preserved state

No Git staging, commit, push, installation, or external service invocation was performed by the consumer after the interruptions.

title: chore(lint): adopt golangci-lint for Go linting
body:
## Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

## Problem Statement

Gentle AI is a Go CLI/TUI project with existing CI checks for formatting, `go vet`, unit tests, and benchmark validation, but it has no repository-wide `golangci-lint` configuration or lint CI job. This leaves static-analysis debt to accumulate between releases.

A fresh local scan of the current repository at commit `7cd3e0ef` using `golangci-lint v2.13.1` found:

- Root module: **145 issues** — `errcheck` 50, `staticcheck` 40, `unused` 50, `ineffassign` 5.
- `bench/` module: **61 issues** — `errcheck` 6, `staticcheck` 5, `unused` 50.
- Total inventory: **206 issues** across both Go modules.

These counts are an inventory, not proof that every diagnostic is a product defect; test helpers, benchmark journeys, build-tagged code, and platform-specific code need explicit policy decisions.

## Affected Area

Other — repository tooling and CI.

## Proposed Solution

Adopt `golangci-lint` as the project's standard Go linter and add a staged lint gate:

1. Add a committed `.golangci.yml` or `.golangci.yaml` with a pinned, documented version and rules appropriate for the root module and test-heavy benchmark code.
2. Add a reproducible local lint command that covers both modules (`./...` at the repository root and `./...` from `bench/`).
3. Run the same checks in GitHub Actions as a required CI job, without replacing the existing `gofmt` or `go vet` checks until overlap is evaluated.
4. Record the current diagnostic inventory and ratchet down from it instead of attempting to fix all 206 findings in one change. Prefer new-issue gating first, then reduce existing debt in focused, independently reviewable slices.
5. Document exclusions and handling for generated files, tests, benchmark fixtures, build tags, and Windows-specific code.

## Alternatives Considered

- Keep only `gofmt` and `go vet`: lower setup cost, but less static-analysis coverage.
- Add `staticcheck` directly: narrower and simpler, but does not provide one configured gate for the project's lint policy.
- Fix all current findings before adding a gate: does not prevent the debt from returning and creates an oversized review.

## Additional Context

- This is the Go-focused adaptation of [gentle-pi issue #438](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-pi/issues/438), which proposed linter adoption for that TypeScript project.
- Current CI already runs `go run ./internal/gofmtcheck`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...`, and separate benchmark-module validation.
- `bench/` is a separate Go module and must be linted separately.
- No existing matching `golangci-lint` issue was found in this repository.

title: feat(install): configure global RDD mode during installation
body:
## Related work

Issue #3766 owns the post-install TUI controls for global Receipt-Driven Development (RDD) state. Issue #3772 and PR #3775 provide the shared status and global-mutation API required by that TUI work.

This issue covers a separate installation adapter: choosing the global RDD mode while running `gentle-ai install`. It must reuse the same persistence and precedence authority rather than expand the active TUI scope or create another representation.

## Problem

RDD is user-owned and opt-in, with an unconfigured installation resolving to `off`. Users can currently change the global setting after installation with `gentle-ai review mode enable|disable`, but the installer has no explicit option for declaring that choice.

This matters during reinstall and automation: an existing global `on` value is preserved unless the user knows and runs a separate review-mode command. Installation therefore cannot fully express the desired machine-wide Gentle AI configuration in one invocation.

## Required change

Add a documented installer option that accepts an explicit global RDD mode (`on` or `off`).

The implementation must:

- write only the existing global RDD setting and recorded timestamp;
- preserve the current global value when the installer option is omitted;
- keep a fresh, previously unconfigured installation effectively `off`;
- apply the explicit mode only after a successful installation;
- reuse the existing review-mode mutation and resolution boundary where practical;
- reject invalid values before installation begins;
- report the selected value in installer help and installation review/output where applicable;
- preserve clone-local overrides and truthful effective-mode precedence.

## Non-goals

- Adding or changing TUI controls already owned by #3766.
- Mutating clone-local RDD mode from the installer.
- Changing the opt-in default or `off`-wins precedence.
- Modifying review receipts, lineages, authority, consent, or delivery behavior.
- Replacing `gentle-ai review mode enable|disable|status`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An explicit installer `on` selection persists global RDD as `on`, and a subsequent `gentle-ai review mode status --json` reports the global source truthfully.
- [ ] An explicit installer `off` selection persists global RDD as `off`, including when a previous installation stored `on`.
- [ ] Omitting the option preserves an existing global setting and does not create mode state for a fresh unconfigured installation.
- [ ] Invalid or missing option values fail before any installation mutation.
- [ ] Installation failure does not change the previously persisted RDD mode.
- [ ] Clone-local overrides remain untouched and continue to determine the effective result when applicable.
- [ ] Installer help and user-facing documentation describe the option, accepted values, global scope, and default-preservation behavior.
- [ ] Focused tests cover fresh install, reinstall preservation, explicit `on`, explicit `off`, invalid input, and failed-install rollback behavior.
- [ ] Existing review-mode and installer tests continue to pass.
- [ ] Each PR stays below 400 additions plus deletions.
- [ ] Applicable Go, vet, formatting, deadcode, refusal, cross-platform runtime, and E2E checks pass.

## Delivery

Implement this as an installer-only work unit. Keep #3766 and its active TUI chain independent; consume the shared RDD API after it lands if that avoids duplicating persistence or precedence logic.

title: feat(memory): add privacy-preserving community problem memory
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist - [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate - [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved` ### 🔍 Affected Area Other ### 💡 Problem Statement ## Executive summary Gentle AI users can independently encounter the same technical failure, but the useful evidence remains fragmented across local sessions, GitHub Issues, versions, runtimes, attempted workarounds, and later regressions. This proposal introduces an optional, privacy-preserving community problem memory with a strict ownership boundary: - **A GitHub Issue is canonical for human workflow:** prioritization, discussion, implementation, pull requests, publication decisions, and closure. - **Community memory is canonical only for aggregated technical evidence:** sanitized occurrences, affected versions and runtimes, workaround outcomes, versioned fingerprints, and regression signals. Community memory must not become a second issue tracker. It does not own issue status, priority, discussion, assignments, implementation decisions, or closure. Today, maintainers repeatedly reconstruct whether reports describe the same problem, which versions are affected, whether a workaround is compatible, and whether a closed issue may have regressed. Users cannot safely benefit from prior occurrences without risking disclosure of raw logs, prompts, source code, local paths, project names, credentials, or other private context. The system needs deterministic local recall, privacy-preserving aggregation, and an explainable maintainer review surface without automatic GitHub mutations, semantic clustering, raw telemetry, or hidden scoring. ### 📦 Proposed Solution Add an optional community problem memory built around sanitized, versioned technical evidence and explicit human authority. ## End-to-end flow The intended flow is: 1. A Gentle AI operation fails or produces a recognizable technical problem. 2. A local Observation Builder creates a structured candidate occurrence. 3. A local Privacy Guard applies a strict field allowlist and secondary secret/PII detection. 4. The user decides whether to contribute the sanitized observation to community memory. 5. The ingestion service validates the schema, size, provenance, and rate limits. 6. Deterministic matching returns one of: - `exact` - `candidate` - `none` 7. Gentle AI may show a known issue or compatible workaround from the local catalog. 8. Compatible independent occurrences are aggregated into a problem pattern. 9. Maintainers review patterns through a private, explainable inbox. 10. A maintainer may link a canonical GitHub Issue or prepare a public summary for human approval. 11. Workaround attempts and released fixes produce structured feedback events. 12. Post-fix occurrences become regression candidates for human review; they never reopen GitHub Issues automatically. No stage may automatically create, edit, comment on, label, close, or reopen a GitHub Issue. ## Ownership and authority | Concern | Canonical authority | |---|---| | Human discussion, prioritization, assignment, implementation, PRs, and closure | GitHub Issue | | Sanitized occurrence aggregation | Community memory | | Affected versions and runtimes | Community memory, subject to reviewed evidence | | Workaround outcomes | Community memory, compatibility-bounded | | Public problem statement and public updates | GitHub Issue | | Pattern classification and catalog curation | Audited maintainer decisions | | Local private evidence | User's local memory | A pattern may reference one canonical GitHub Issue. It may also retain explicit related or duplicate issue links, but those links do not create competing canonical trackers. ## Three-plane architecture | Plane | Responsibility | Privacy boundary | |---|---|---| | **Private local memory** | Structured capture, allowlist sanitization, consent, deterministic local matching, and private history | Raw diagnostic context never leaves the machine | | **Ingestion and aggregation service** | Validate sanitized events, perform deterministic matching, aggregate compatible occurrences, and serve the maintainer inbox | Accepts only versioned schemas and approved fields | | **Curated community catalog** | Cacheable, versioned patterns, compatibility constraints, verified issue links, and reviewed workarounds | Contains no raw reports or project identity | Gentle AI must continue operating normally when either remote plane is unavailable. ## Local components The client-side MVP consists of: - **Observation Builder:** converts a failure into a bounded structured occurrence. - **Privacy Guard:** enforces the allowed-field schema and performs secondary secret/PII detection. - **Consent Controller:** keeps community contribution consent separate from GitHub publication consent. - **Catalog Cache:** stores a versioned static or downloaded catalog for local matching. - **Deterministic Matcher:** returns `exact`, `candidate`, or `none` with explicit reasons and compatibility checks. Raw logs, prompts, source code, filesystem paths, usernames, hostnames, project names, repository names, credentials, private network addresses, and project identity are prohibited from transmission. ## Consent model Two separate decisions are required: 1. **Community-contribution consent:** permission to transmit a sanitized technical observation. 2. **GitHub-publication consent:** permission to publish selected information in a public GitHub Issue or comment. Community-contribution consent never implies GitHub-publication consent. A maintainer may review aggregated private evidence and prepare a proposed GitHub summary, but publication still requires explicit human approval through the repository's normal workflow. ## Deterministic matching Matching must be versioned, explainable, and compatibility-aware: | Result | Meaning | |---|---| | `exact` | Fingerprint version, normalized fields, runtime constraints, and affected-version constraints match | | `candidate` | One or more bounded rules suggest a possible match, but evidence or compatibility is incomplete | | `none` | No catalog pattern satisfies the deterministic rules | Every match response must include the rules that matched or failed. A candidate must never be presented as a confirmed known issue. The initial implementation must not use embeddings, LLM clustering, semantic similarity, opaque confidence scores, or cross-device human identity.
Core data model ### ProblemPattern Represents one reviewed technical problem. Suggested fields include: - stable pattern identifier; - fingerprint schema version; - normalized deterministic fingerprint; - lifecycle state; - severity classification; - affected version and runtime constraints; - first and last observed timestamps; - aggregate independent-installation count; - reviewed workaround summaries; - one canonical GitHub Issue link when available; - related and duplicate pattern aliases; - catalog revision and maintainer-decision references. ### Occurrence Represents one sanitized observation from one installation. Suggested fields include: - event identifier and idempotency key; - rotating random installation identifier; - pattern fingerprint and schema version; - Gentle AI version and release channel; - runtime, agent, operating-system family, and architecture where allowed; - bounded error category or normalized failure code; - sanitized reproduction attributes from the strict allowlist; - observation timestamp; - match result and reasons. An Occurrence must not contain raw diagnostic material or stable human identity. ### WorkaroundEvidence Represents one consented workaround outcome. Suggested fields include: - pattern identifier; - workaround identifier and revision; - attempted, succeeded, or failed outcome; - applicable Gentle AI version range; - applicable runtime and operating-system constraints; - sanitized failure category when unsuccessful; - timestamp and idempotency key. Workaround evidence is valid only within its declared compatibility bounds. A workaround observed on one runtime or version must not be recommended outside those bounds without reviewed evidence. ### IssueLink Represents a reviewed relationship between a pattern and GitHub. Suggested fields include: - repository identity; - issue number and URL; - relationship type: `canonical`, `related`, or `duplicate`; - verified issue state and last synchronization timestamp; - maintainer decision reference. Each pattern may have at most one canonical issue. Related and duplicate links remain available for lineage and search.
Pattern lifecycle and event synchronization ## Pattern lifecycle | State | Meaning | |---|---| | `observed` | One sanitized occurrence exists | | `recurring` | Compatible occurrences exist from at least two independent installations | | `tracked` | A maintainer linked one canonical GitHub Issue | | `fix_available` | A reviewed fix is available in an identified version | | `resolved_pending_observation` | The canonical issue is closed or the fix is released, but post-fix observation time is still required | | `resolved` | Reviewed evidence indicates the affected range is no longer reproducing | | `regression_candidate` | A compatible post-fix occurrence requires maintainer review | A new post-fix occurrence must not reopen a GitHub Issue or mark a regression automatically. It transitions the pattern to `regression_candidate` or creates a review candidate, depending on compatibility and evidence. ## Event-based synchronization Synchronization should use idempotent events rather than full bidirectional record copies. Initial event types: - `occurrence_observed` - `issue_linked` - `issue_closed` - `fix_released` - `workaround_attempted` - `workaround_succeeded` - `workaround_failed` - `post_fix_occurrence_observed` Each event carries a stable event identifier, schema version, timestamp, bounded payload, and idempotency key. Reprocessing the same event must not increment occurrence counts twice, duplicate workaround evidence, or repeat a maintainer decision. Conflicting or out-of-order events must be retained for review rather than silently overwriting newer authority.
## Maintainer inbox and operations The private maintainer inbox must explain why each pattern or candidate is present. Impact information may include: - severity; - number of compatible independent installations; - recent occurrence growth; - affected Gentle AI versions; - affected runtimes and operating-system families; - availability and success rate of compatible workarounds; - evidence confidence; - whether a canonical issue exists; - whether occurrences continue after a reviewed fix. These are explainable impact factors, not one opaque score. Maintainers may: - confirm or reject a proposed pattern; - classify severity and affected scope; - link one canonical GitHub Issue; - add related or duplicate issue links; - merge patterns; - split a pattern; - confirm a regression; - mark evidence insufficient; - review a proposed public GitHub summary. A merge preserves old pattern identifiers as aliases so clients and historical events still resolve correctly. A split requires explicit, reproducible rules describing which fingerprint fields or compatibility constraints separate the new patterns. Existing occurrences must be reassigned deterministically from those rules. Maintainer decisions must be durable, attributable, auditable, and reversible. Reversal should use compensating events rather than deleting history. ## Governance and security - Installation identity uses a rotating random identifier generated locally. - The identifier must not be derived from hardware, usernames, paths, account identity, repository identity, or other stable fingerprints. - Detailed sanitized events and rotating installation identifiers should be retained for approximately 90 days. - Identifier-free aggregates may remain while the pattern exists. - Audited maintainer decisions and versioned catalog releases are durable. - Maintainer access requires verified identity and repository-scoped permissions. - Ingestion enforces rate limits, schema validation, payload-size limits, and accepted-enum validation. - Invalid, suspicious, or conflicting events enter quarantine rather than aggregation. - Secondary secret and PII detection runs after allowlist serialization. - If secret-like or disallowed material is detected, the event exits the community path and remains local. - Security-sensitive, privacy-sensitive, credential-exposure, or severe data-loss reports must be routed to a private responsible-disclosure path rather than the public catalog or GitHub publication flow. - No service component receives permission for automatic GitHub writes. ## Safe degradation | Condition | Required behavior | |---|---| | Privacy Guard is uncertain | Do not transmit; retain locally with an explanation | | Community consent is absent | Keep the observation local | | Remote service is unavailable | Continue Gentle AI normally; optionally use the cached catalog | | Request times out | Report an uncertain delivery outcome and do not blind-retry | | Match is ambiguous | Show only a `candidate` with reasons | | Workaround compatibility does not match | Do not recommend the workaround | | Potential secret or PII is detected | Remove the event from the community path | | Catalog is stale or unavailable | Identify its revision or omit community guidance | | GitHub state cannot be verified | Keep the existing reviewed link but mark synchronization unavailable | | Post-fix occurrence is observed | Create a regression candidate; never reopen automatically | Community memory failures must never block installation, configuration, review, delivery, or any existing Gentle AI command. ## Minimal service surface The initial conceptual API may remain small: | Endpoint | Purpose | |---|---| | `POST /v1/occurrences` | Submit one consented, sanitized occurrence event | | `POST /v1/workaround-results` | Submit one consented workaround outcome | | `GET /v1/catalog` | Retrieve a versioned, cacheable community catalog | | `GET /v1/maintainer/inbox` | Retrieve explainable patterns and review candidates | | `POST /v1/maintainer/decisions` | Record an audited maintainer decision | These endpoints describe capability boundaries, not a commitment to a particular deployment technology. ## Initial thresholds | Evidence | Initial behavior | |---|---| | First sanitized occurrence | Record it without generating a maintainer alert | | At least two compatible occurrences from independent installations | Mark the pattern `recurring` and create a private inbox alert | | Recurring pattern without a canonical issue | Propose issue preparation only after a complete duplicate search and human approval | | Existing tracked pattern with materially changed evidence | Prepare a GitHub summary proposal for human review | | Severe privacy, security, credential, or data-loss signal | Route privately; do not propose public publication | | Post-fix compatible occurrence | Create a regression candidate for maintainer review | “Record silently” means no maintainer alert or public action; it does not bypass community-contribution consent. Only material evidence changes should produce GitHub summary proposals. Event volume alone must not create public noise. ## MVP stages ### Stage 1: local recall - Observation Builder - Privacy Guard - Consent Controller - Catalog Cache - deterministic matching against a static versioned catalog - explainable `exact`, `candidate`, and `none` results - no ingestion service required for normal local operation ### Stage 2: ingestion, aggregation, and inbox - consented sanitized occurrence submission; - idempotent event processing; - deterministic server-side matching; - aggregation across compatible independent installations; - basic private maintainer inbox; - merge, split, classify, and insufficient-evidence decisions; - quarantine and abuse controls. ### Stage 3: verified GitHub linkage and workaround evidence - reviewed canonical, related, and duplicate issue links; - verified issue-state synchronization; - compatibility-bounded workaround outcomes; - fix-release and post-fix observation events; - human-reviewed GitHub summary proposals; - regression confirmation without automatic reopening. ## Acceptance criteria The proposal is successful only if: - outbound community data is limited to an explicit, versioned allowlist; - secondary detection prevents suspected secrets or PII from entering the community path; - no raw logs, prompts, source code, paths, hostnames, project names, repository identity, or credentials are transmitted; - community contribution and GitHub publication require separate consent; - matching is deterministic, explainable, and constrained by compatible versions and runtimes; - idempotent event replay does not duplicate aggregates or decisions; - every pattern has at most one canonical GitHub Issue; - merge aliases and split rules preserve deterministic lineage; - maintainer decisions are audited and reversible through compensating events; - incompatible workarounds are not recommended; - post-fix occurrences do not automatically reopen issues; - no component automatically creates, comments on, labels, edits, closes, or reopens GitHub Issues; - service failures and privacy uncertainty degrade safely without blocking Gentle AI. ## Pilot metrics Measure: - percentage of matches users find useful; - false-match rate; - candidate-to-exact confirmation rate; - compatible workaround attempts, successes, and failures; - duplicate GitHub Issues avoided; - maintainer classification time; - percentage of patterns marked insufficient evidence; - ingestion rejection and quarantine rates; - privacy incidents, with a target of zero. Raw event volume is not a success metric. A system that collects many observations but produces unsafe, misleading, or unactionable results has failed. ### 🔄 Alternatives Considered - **Use GitHub Issues alone.** GitHub remains the correct workflow authority, but issue threads do not provide deterministic local recall or structured aggregation of privacy-scrubbed independent occurrences. - **Send raw telemetry or diagnostic bundles.** Rejected because raw logs, prompts, source code, paths, credentials, and project identity cross an unacceptable privacy boundary. - **Use LLM or embedding-based clustering.** Rejected because matching would be non-deterministic, difficult to explain, vulnerable to false merges, and likely to ignore strict version compatibility. - **Keep all problem memory local.** This preserves privacy but cannot establish independent occurrence counts, shared workaround outcomes, or community regression signals. - **Synchronize full records bidirectionally.** Rejected because competing mutable copies create ownership conflicts and make replay, audit, and recovery harder than idempotent events. - **Automatically publish or update GitHub Issues.** Rejected because community contribution consent is not public-publication consent and automation could override maintainer judgment. - **Automatically execute suggested workarounds.** Rejected because compatibility evidence cannot prove that a mutation is safe for an individual environment. - **Track stable cross-device user identity.** Rejected because the system needs independent-installation evidence, not human tracking. ### 📎 Additional Context ## Explicit non-goals This proposal does not include: - automatic GitHub issue creation; - automatic GitHub comments, labels, edits, closure, reopening, or prioritization; - a second public issue tracker; - LLM clustering, embeddings, or semantic matching; - raw telemetry or diagnostic-bundle upload; - transmission of logs, prompts, source code, paths, project identity, or credentials; - automatic workaround execution; - opaque impact or confidence scoring; - cross-device human tracking; - automatic root-cause attribution; - automatic regression confirmation; - automatic publication of community observations; - replacing maintainer review or responsible disclosure. The community catalog provides reviewed technical evidence. GitHub remains authoritative for public workflow and human decisions.

title: bug(install/sync): transient atomic-rename denial on Windows aborts the pipeline before 'skills' (last component) and leaves empty skill directories
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

**Not a duplicate of #293** (closed, fixed in v1.20.1): that one was `sync parent directory ... Access is denied` — a *directory fsync*. This one is `replace ... atomically: rename <tmp> <dest>: Access is denied` — the *file rename*. Different primitive, and the amplifying factors below are new.

### 📝 Bug Description

On Windows, `install`/`sync` abort when the atomic file rename hits a **transient** lock held by the very AI sessions gentle-ai serves. Three properties turn one transient lock into total, quiet data loss:

**1. `skills` is the LAST component in the pipeline order.** From `--dry-run`:

```
Components order: claude-theme,context7,persona,engram,gga,opencode-gentle-logo,permissions,sdd,skills
```

The pipeline is fail-fast, so **any** earlier component failing means `skills` never executes. Skills are not failing — they never get their turn.

**2. The atomic rename does not retry.** The denial is transient, not a permission problem. Performing the *same* rename by hand on the *same* file succeeds, with a positive control in a neutral directory:

```
CONTROL MOVE OK     (neutral temp dir)
SUBJECT MOVE OK     (~/.claude/agents/sdd-apply.md)
```

The lock holders are live agent sessions: 62 `node.exe` processes reading `~/.claude/agents/*.md`, an on-access AV scanning newly created `.tmp` files, and 2 running `engram` processes — which gentle-ai itself reports it could not stop:

```
gentle-ai: engram stop: WARNING: 2 engram process(es) could not be stopped (access denied or still running).
```

**3. The rollback uses the same non-retrying primitive**, so the rollback fails too and leaves mixed-version state (see attempts 2 and 3 below).

**The dangerous residue:** directories are created *before* the file is written, leaving `~/.claude/skills/<name>/` **empty**. To a human browsing the folder it looks installed; to the runtime the skill does not exist. The CLI does print the error and exit 1 — but nobody re-reads the exit code of an install that "finished", and the empty directories persist silently.

Measured on this machine after one such run: **32 files that the pre-install backup manifest declared with `existed=false` — i.e. gentle-ai's own declaration of files it would create — were all absent afterwards.**

```
output: entries with existed=false (declared to be created) = 32
output: PRESENT=0  MISSING=32
positive control: 0 of 148 entries with existed=true are missing  (nothing was deleted; creation failed)
```

Five skill directories were left with no `SKILL.md`: `gentle-ai-bench`, `rdd-defect-workflow`, `skill-registry`, `systemic-issue-triage`, `skill-creator`.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Windows 11, gentle-ai 2.4.0, with AI agent sessions actively running (Claude Code sessions reading `~/.claude/agents/`, engram MCP running).
2. Run `gentle-ai sync --agent claude-code --skills gentle-ai-bench`.
3. Repeat 3 times.

Reproduced 4/4, failing at three different lock points:

```
ATTEMPT 1  EXIT=1
Error: execute sync pipeline: sync sdd for "claude-code": write agent sdd-apply.md:
  replace "...\.claude\agents\sdd-apply.md" atomically:
  rename ....gentle-ai-1074093341.tmp -> sdd-apply.md: Access is denied.

ATTEMPT 2  EXIT=1
Error: ... rollback step "apply:rollback-restore": restore path "...sdd-archive.md":
  ... Access is denied.

ATTEMPT 3  EXIT=1
Error: ... rollback step "apply:rollback-restore": restore path "...jd-fix-agent.md":
  ... Access is denied.
```

Narrowing the scope to a single component does not help — it pulls `engram` in anyway (same root class as #3554, which reports this for `sdd`):

```
$ gentle-ai install --agent claude-code --components skills
Error: execute install pipeline: refresh shadowed engram binary: extract engram zip:
  write ...\engram\bin\engram.exe: replace ... atomically:
  rename ....gentle-ai-4138936696.tmp -> engram.exe: Access is denied.
EXIT=1
```

### ✅ Expected Behavior

- The atomic rename retries with a short backoff on Windows before failing (`ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` / `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION` from a transient scanner or reader handle is expected on Windows, not exceptional).
- A component that cannot be written does not silently take down every component ordered after it — in particular `skills`, which is last and therefore the first casualty of anything.
- A failed write does not leave an empty skill directory behind. Either the directory is created only alongside a successful write, or the failure path removes the directory it created.
- Rollback does not depend on the same primitive that just failed.
- `--components skills` installs skills.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

One transient rename denial aborts the whole pipeline, `skills` never runs, rollback fails on the same primitive leaving mixed-version state, and empty skill directories are left on disk that look installed and are invisible to the runtime.

### Gentle AI Version

2.4.0

### Operating System

Windows 11 (10.0.26200), amd64. On-access antivirus active; 62 `node.exe` agent processes and 2 `engram` processes live during the run.

### AI Agent / Client

claude-code (also affects gemini-cli, vscode-copilot, codex — the same 26 files are missing across those homes)

### 📋 Affected Area

`install` / `sync` pipeline, `filemerge` atomic write layer, component ordering, rollback.

### Suggested fixes, in order of impact

1. **Retry the atomic rename** with bounded backoff on Windows. Highest value per line changed — it addresses the trigger directly.
2. **Never leave an empty skill directory.** Create the directory as part of the successful write, or remove it on the failure path. This alone converts a silent failure into a visible one.
3. **Reconsider `skills` being last** in the component order, or make component failures isolable so one component cannot cancel the rest.
4. **Make rollback resilient** — it should not fail on the same primitive that triggered it.

title: bug(pi): verifier ignores requested worktree and runs session checkout
body:
## Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I searched existing open and closed issues; no equivalent report was found.
- [x] I understand this report requires maintainer review before implementation.

## 📝 Bug Description

A Pi verifier subagent can execute a requested repository validation in the session checkout instead of the explicitly requested existing Git worktree. The requested candidate then has no validation evidence, while unrelated checks can run in the session checkout.

## 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a second Git worktree for a repository.
2. Ask a fresh Pi verifier subagent to run one non-destructive validation from that named worktree.
3. Inspect the verifier-reported working directory.

## ✅ Expected Behavior

The verifier executes in the requested worktree. If it cannot establish that directory, it stops before launching the validation.

## ❌ Actual Behavior

Across two bounded attempts, the verifier reported executing the validation in the session checkout instead of the requested worktree. The requested candidate remained unverified. No consumer source mutations, commits, pushes, or pull requests were performed by either attempt.

## 🖥️ Environment

- Gentle AI version: 2.4.0
- Operating system: macOS (Darwin), arm64
- AI agent/client: Other — Pi coding agent
- Affected area: Other — subagent verification worktree selection

## 💡 Logs / Error Output

No raw logs included. Observed outcome: requested worktree was not used; the session checkout was used instead.

## Additional Context

This is an automated, privacy-scrubbed provider-defect report. It excludes paths, repository names, usernames, credentials, source contents, diffs, raw argv, and environment values. The operation shape was a fresh verifier subagent asked to run one repository validation against a named existing worktree.

title: fix(issue-creation): require causal ownership before upstream reporting
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

The canonical Gentle AI issue-creation workflow can offer the official `Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai` repository as a new-issue target without first establishing that the reported failure is causally owned by Gentle AI. A symptom observed while Gentle AI participates in a workflow may instead belong to the user's project, repository configuration, a dependency, host agent/tooling, or the environment. This can route unrelated reports to Gentle AI maintainers.

The workflow needs a narrow, deterministic ownership gate for new issue creation targeting the official Gentle AI repository. Existing comments, triage, approval, and explicit third-party targets must remain unchanged.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Report a failure encountered while working in a user repository.
2. Let the agent observe that Gentle AI participates somewhere in the workflow.
3. Enter the issue-creation flow before isolating the causal owner.
4. Observe that the official Gentle AI repository can be offered or selected without evidence that a Gentle AI change is independently actionable, necessary, or behavior-worsening.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

For new issue creation targeting exactly `github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai`, the workflow must classify scope and ownership before offering that target, materializing Issue Form answers, or publishing.

The ordered decision must be:

1. Proceed for a confirmed Gentle AI defect only when concrete evidence identifies reproducible Gentle AI causality, an independently necessary Gentle AI change, behavior worsening, or a Gentle AI contract violation. Gentle AI merely being present is insufficient.
2. Proceed for an explicit Gentle AI feature or policy request without misclassifying it as a defect.
3. Otherwise, route away only when evidence supports exactly one external destination: user project, repository configuration, dependency, or host agent/tooling/environment.
4. Fail closed and request the smallest missing evidence when ownership is insufficient, tied, or mixed without a decisive Gentle AI responsibility.

Comments, triage, approvals, and explicit non-Gentle-AI targets must retain their current behavior.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The current contract validates exact target resolution, repository policy, YAML Issue Forms, duplicates, privacy, labels, one-attempt mutation, and read-back, but it does not require causal ownership classification before the official Gentle AI target is offered or before new-issue materialization/publication begins.

`main @ cabd0afb544b3f45e004436949a4862054cf4b1a`

### Operating System

Linux (Other)

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

### Additional Context

- `internal/assets/skills/issue-creation/SKILL.md`

Acceptance criteria:

- The gate applies only to official Gentle AI new-issue creation.
- Tests cover target and mutation-kind specificity, confirmed defects, legitimate feature/policy requests, each external routing destination, mixed causes, ambiguous ties, and ordering before offer/materialization/publication.
- Existing target-policy, Issue Form, duplicate, privacy, label, mutation, and read-back guarantees remain unchanged.

title: Add mise (mise-en-place) install support
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Problem Statement

`gentle-ai` has no supported install path through [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) (the polyglot dev-tool version manager): no `mise.toml`, no registry entry, no mention in `README.md`/`docs/`/`CONTRIBUTING.md`. Users who already manage their toolchain with mise have to fall back to `go install` or Homebrew, and contributors reconstruct the Go/Node toolchain by hand — `CONTRIBUTING.md` doesn't even name Node as a prerequisite today, despite CI needing Node 24 and `gentle-ai install` requiring Node 18+ at runtime.

Separately, `gentle-ai upgrade`'s self-updater has no awareness of mise-managed installs: if a user installs `gentle-ai` via mise and later runs `gentle-ai upgrade`, the self-updater would overwrite the binary in place, desyncing it from the version mise thinks it manages.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Add first-class mise support end-to-end, split into 4 chained, independently-revertible PRs (already implemented and open, `stacked-to-main` per this repo's chained-PR delivery strategy):

- **PR 1** — [#3734](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/3734): repo-root `mise.toml` pinning Go `1.25.10` (mirrors `go.mod`) and Node `24` (mirrors `ci.yml`), plus `scripts/verify-mise-pins.sh` wired into CI as a fail-closed drift guard.
- **PR 2** — [#3735](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/3735): `internal/update/upgrade/mise.go`, a detector answering whether the running `gentle-ai` binary lives under mise's resolved install root, with full table-driven test coverage.
- **PR 3** — [#3737](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/3737): wires the detector into the upgrade executor's preflight chain, so a mise-managed `gentle-ai` is skipped during self-upgrade with a `mise upgrade gentle-ai` hint instead of being overwritten in place.
- **PR 4** — [#3742](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/3742): documents mise as an install method (README, quickstart, platforms matrix) and closes the CONTRIBUTING.md Node-prerequisite gap.

Two sibling registry PRs make `mise install`/`mise use -g` actually resolve `gentle-ai` by name: [aquaproj/aqua-registry#59466](https://github.com/aquaproj/aqua-registry/pull/59466) and [jdx/mise#12444](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/12444) are both **merged** now. The short name still won't resolve until a mise release ships after `v2026.8.16` (the release cut a few hours before the jdx/mise merge). Neither blocks this chain — the documented bridge command `mise use -g github:Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai@latest` works today regardless.

Full design rationale lives in this repo's own SDD artifacts: `openspec/changes/mise-install-support/{proposal.md,design.md,specs/,tasks.md}` (included in PR 1).

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- Reading `MISE_*` environment variables to detect a mise-managed install — rejected: produces false positives in any shell where mise happens to be activated, regardless of how `gentle-ai` itself was installed.
- Shelling out to `mise which` for detection — rejected: adds an external-process dependency to a pure path-containment check that doesn't need one.

### 📎 Additional Context

**Process note**: this issue is being opened retroactively — the 4 PRs above were already implemented and opened before I (external contributor, read-only permission on this repo) found `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s issue-first requirement. Apologies for the out-of-order workflow. Filing this now so each PR can link back to an approved issue as required.

Because I don't have push access to create intermediate base branches in this repo, all 4 PRs target `main` directly (GitHub requires a PR's base to exist in the base repository). Each PR's diff therefore shows the cumulative changeset of every earlier, still-open PR in the chain until they merge in order — real added/removed lines per work unit are noted in each PR body and are well within this repo's 400-line review budget individually. I've asked for `size:exception` on each PR that needs it, and for the appropriate `type:*` label, since I can't self-apply either as a non-collaborator.

title: bug(docs): use merge-base scope when recounting GitHub PR changes
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

`skills/gentle-ai-collab-perfect/SKILL.md` teaches contributors to recount GitHub pull-request scope with:

```bash
git diff --stat <base>..<head>
```

That two-dot comparison compares the endpoint trees. When the base advances independently, it includes upstream-only changes as reverse deletions or modifications and therefore inflates or misrepresents the changes introduced by the pull request.

GitHub pull-request scope is merge-base based. The contributor guidance should use:

```bash
git diff --stat <base>...<head>
```

or an explicit merge-base comparison that preserves `<head>` as the compared side. This is a contributor-facing documentation defect, independent of the implementation of native review authority.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Check out the current `main` branch.
2. Inspect `skills/gentle-ai-collab-perfect/SKILL.md` and locate its PR recount guidance.
3. Create a scratch Git repository with a common base `B`.
4. Create a feature branch from `B`.
5. Advance the main branch with `upstream-only.txt`.
6. Advance the feature branch with `feature-only.txt`.
7. Run:

   ```bash
   git diff --stat main..feature
   git diff --stat main...feature
   ```

8. Compare the output with the files actually introduced by the feature branch.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The contributor skill teaches merge-base PR scope:

```bash
git diff --stat <base>...<head>
```

or an equivalent explicit merge-base comparison. The documentation explains that two-dot compares endpoint trees, while three-dot reports the changes from the merge base to `<head>`, preserving `<head>` as the compared side.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The skill currently recommends two-dot endpoint-tree comparison for GitHub PR scope. With upstream-only drift, the result reports both the feature addition and the upstream-only file as a deletion, even though the upstream-only file was not introduced or deleted by the feature branch.

### Gentle AI Version

`main@cabd0afb544b3f45e004436949a4862054cf4b1a` (latest audited main)

### Operating System

macOS

### AI Agent / Client

OpenCode

### 📋 Affected Area

Documentation

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```text
Real temporary Git object-tree reproduction of the two endpoint-tree states:

TWO_DOT (equivalent endpoint-tree comparison, main..feature):
 feature-only.txt  | 1 +
 upstream-only.txt | 1 -
 2 files changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

THREE_DOT (equivalent merge-base-to-head comparison, main...feature):
 feature-only.txt | 1 +
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+)

Affected guidance:
skills/gentle-ai-collab-perfect/SKILL.md:149
Numbers and file counts must match the API. If you can't trust the API, recount locally: git diff --stat <base>..<head>
```

### Additional Context

This issue is limited to the contributor-facing command and explanation in `skills/gentle-ai-collab-perfect/SKILL.md`. It does not claim that native review, pre-PR authority, or GitHub's own changed-file API is incorrect.

Related history was reviewed but does not correct this exact contributor command: #1170, #1605, and PR #2876. Those reports and changes concern adjacent review/base-binding behavior, whereas this remaining defect is the command taught by the collaboration skill itself. No exact duplicate issue or pull request was found for this proposed title or behavior.

title: bug(docs): exclude terminally approved unchanged candidates from fresh PR-readiness review
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

`docs/intended-usage.md` gives a broad instruction to use fresh-context adversarial review for diffs, conflicts, PR readiness, and incidents. The shipped review contracts establish a narrower terminal boundary: native approval burns the exact review authority, and unchanged content must not be reviewed again merely because delivery preparation begins.

This is an instruction-layer contradiction. A contributor or orchestrator following the broad PR-readiness wording can start another review after an unchanged candidate has already received terminal approval, recreating review and correction loops. The issue is not a request to restore durable review receipts, delivery gates, or reusable review authority.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Check out the current `main` branch.
2. Read the fresh-review rule in `docs/intended-usage.md`.
3. Read the corresponding shipped boundaries in:
   - `README.md`
   - `internal/assets/opencode/sdd-orchestrator.md`
   - `internal/assets/skills/_shared/review-ledger-contract.md`
4. Observe that the contextual PR-readiness guidance does not exclude a candidate whose terminal review authority has already been burned.
5. Complete terminal native review for an unchanged candidate in OpenCode.
6. Start PR preparation.
7. Observe that the broad contextual rule permits another review despite terminal unchanged-content approval.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

- Terminal approval burns its native review authority.
- An unchanged approved candidate is not reviewed again solely because PR preparation begins.
- Changed candidates may enter a new review transaction.
- Commit, push, PR, and release remain ordinary repository-policy decisions.
- The documentation and shipped orchestrator/review-ledger guidance describe these boundaries consistently.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The contextual documentation instructs agents to use fresh adversarial review for PR readiness without excluding candidates that already reached terminal approval with unchanged content. The shipped contracts separately state that the review authority is burned and that delivery operations never reopen review for unchanged content.

### Gentle AI Version

`main@cabd0afb544b3f45e004436949a4862054cf4b1a` (latest audited main)

### Operating System

macOS

### AI Agent / Client

OpenCode

### 📋 Affected Area

Documentation

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```text
docs/intended-usage.md:123
Fresh review rule: use fresh context for adversarial review of diffs, conflicts, PR readiness, and incidents when the agent platform supports it.

README.md:243
Once you enable it, both implementation routes can converge on RDD: a bounded native review freezes the candidate and reports an informational outcome — review is never reopened for unchanged content.

internal/assets/opencode/sdd-orchestrator.md:102
Commit, push, PR, direct-main, emergency, and release gates are informational and unmanaged; ordinary repository policy decides delivery and they never reopen review for unchanged content.

internal/assets/skills/_shared/review-ledger-contract.md:11-15,82
Every later STATUS and collection call for that transaction passes the exact captured lineage, revision, and target tokens. ... Do not start another lineage, reuse a burned lineage, or perform ambient recovery.
Native Go ... reads back successful approval, then burns that exact authority and its artifacts before returning approved.
After terminal approved burn, the review lifecycle stops. Commit, push, PR, and release remain separate human decisions under ordinary repository policy.
```

### Additional Context

This is a documentation/instruction-only defect unless another shipped asset contains the same stale wording. It does not propose restoring review authority or making review a delivery gate.

Related history was reviewed but does not own this remaining contradiction: #1293, #3417, #3587, #3357, #3330 / PR #3331, and #2295. No exact duplicate issue or pull request was found for this proposed title or behavior. The correction should align the contextual PR-readiness guidance with the existing terminal unchanged-content boundary while preserving fresh review for genuinely changed candidates.

title: feat(harness): reuse host-provided worktrees instead of provisioning twice
body:
## Problem

Gentle AI currently contains several correct but incomplete worktree rules:

- RDD defect work asks for a dedicated worktree.
- Parallel writers require isolated worktrees.
- CodeGraph-aware workers require a checkout-local index and safe worktree placement.

These rules protect repository state, but they do not consistently define **who owns workspace provisioning**.

Agent orchestration hosts may already create and manage the session worktree. If Gentle AI creates another worktree instead of reusing the host-provided workspace, the host can lose its mapping to the active branch, diff, terminal, ports, setup lifecycle, and session UI.

The compatibility risk is therefore double provisioning—not worktree support itself.

## External interoperability evidence

Worktree-based hosts are already common:

- Superset documents each workspace as an isolated Git worktree with its own branch, directory, terminal, and ports: https://docs.superset.sh/workspaces
- VS Code Agent Host supports both folder isolation and worktree isolation for local agent sessions: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/concepts/agent-harnesses
- T3 Code exposes current-checkout and new-worktree execution flows in its public repository: https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code

This issue does not claim those hosts are currently broken. It records the missing ownership contract before host-specific edge cases become accidental policy.

## Root cause

The harness conflates two separate responsibilities:

1. **Isolation and identity:** determine the canonical workspace/worktree root and bind work to it.
2. **Provisioning:** create, switch, import, or remove a worktree.

Gentle AI needs the first responsibility. The active orchestration host should own the second whenever it already provides an isolated workspace.

## Required behavior

- Treat the invocation workspace root as host-supplied authority.
- Detect and reuse an existing linked worktree without creating a second one.
- Keep ordinary current-checkout execution supported when the host chooses folder isolation.
- Create a fallback worktree only when no host-provided isolation exists and the parent workflow explicitly owns provisioning.
- Keep worktree creation/removal parent- or host-owned; delegated workers must not provision or destroy worktrees.
- Preserve canonical Git common-directory identity, review/attempt stores, selected-untracked accounting, and explicit handoff when work genuinely moves between worktrees.
- Derive this behavior from the current workspace and invocation context; do not add durable ownership state, a second workspace registry, or GUI-specific truth.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Harness instructions distinguish workspace isolation from workspace provisioning.
- [ ] RDD and generic writer guidance say to reuse a host-provided worktree before considering fallback creation.
- [ ] Parallel writer guidance accepts host-created isolated workspaces and never nests another worktree beneath them.
- [ ] The worker contract requires an exact workspace root, branch/base identity when applicable, and refuses to write in a different checkout.
- [ ] Tests cover an ordinary checkout, an existing linked worktree, and a host-provided sibling worktree.
- [ ] Tests prove no second worktree is created when the invocation already targets an isolated worktree.
- [ ] Tests preserve Git common-directory state and require explicit handoff when execution changes worktrees.
- [ ] Documentation explains compatibility with host-managed workspaces such as Superset, VS Code Agent Host, and T3 Code without adding host-specific adapters.

## Non-goals

- Removing worktree support.
- Requiring every delegated task to use a worktree.
- Managing host terminals, ports, setup scripts, or GUI session state.
- Adding separate Superset, VS Code, or T3 Code runtime integrations.
- Treating a worktree as a security sandbox.

title: bug(opencode): AGENTS.md instructs mem_save to pass content as object — MCP tool expects string
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

The AGENTS.md system prompt for OpenCode instructs agents to pass `content` as a structured object to `mem_save`, but the engram MCP tool expects `content` as a plain string. This causes every `mem_save` call to fail with:

"content is required for mem_save (use content, or observation for backward-compatible clients)"

The AGENTS.md format section shows:
- content:
  - What: One sentence — what was done
  - Why: What motivated it
  - Where: Files or paths affected
  - Learned: Gotchas, edge cases

This is interpreted by agents as `content: { what: "...", why: "...", where: "...", learned: "..." }` (an object), when the engram MCP schema expects `content: "What: ...\nWhy: ..."` (a string).

Verified on engram 1.16.1 AND 1.20.0 — the bug persists across versions.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Install gentle-ai with OpenCode agent
2. Sync: gentle-ai sync
3. From OpenCode, call mem_save via MCP with content as object:
   { "title": "Test", "type": "discovery", "content": { "what": "test", "why": "test", "where": "N/A", "learned": "N/A" } }
4. Observe error: "content is required for mem_save"
5. Call mem_save with content as string:
   { "title": "Test", "type": "discovery", "content": "What: test\nWhy: test" }
6. Observe: succeeds


### ✅ Expected Behavior

AGENTS.md should document `content` as a string format, or engram MCP should accept structured objects. Either fix the prompt or fix the tool.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

AGENTS.md still shows the object format in v2.4.0. Every mem_save call from OpenCode agents fails unless the agent independently discovers that content must be a string.

### Gentle AI Version

2.4.0

### Operating System

Windows

### AI Agent / Client

Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area

TUI (terminal UI)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
"content is required for mem_save (use content, or observation for backward-compatible clients)"
```

### Additional Context

Related issues: #827 (closed, same root cause but for Windsurf/Devin Desktop). That issue was closed as "schema mismatch lives in the Devin client and Engram, not in gentle-ai code" — but in this case the mismatch IS in gentle-ai's AGENTS.md prompt, which instructs OpenCode agents to use the wrong format. Engram MCP tool schema and AGENTS.md need to agree on whether `content` is a string or an object.

Engram version tested: 1.16.1 (original) and 1.20.0 (after upgrade) — both reject object content.

title: bug(opencode): commit amendment can rewrite an unauthorized HEAD commit
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing open and closed issues and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`.

### Bug Description

An automated OpenCode commit workflow was authorized to amend one specific non-HEAD local revision. Instead, it executed an ordinary amend against the current HEAD and rewrote that different commit. The intended target was left unchanged.

This report records observed behavior only; it does not assert the underlying cause.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Prepare a local commit sequence where the explicitly authorized amendment target is not HEAD.
2. Request a commit workflow constrained to amend only that named target, while preserving all other commits.
3. Let the automated executor perform its amendment step.
4. Inspect the resulting local history.

### Expected Behavior

The workflow validates that its target is the authorized revision before mutating history. If the requested target is not safely amendable by the selected operation, it stops without changing any commit and asks for an explicit recovery decision.

### Actual Behavior

The executor amended the then-current HEAD rather than the authorized target. In the observed event, intended revision `0cfa3e8e` was not amended; then-HEAD `9343ae0d` was rewritten as `5bd48af9`.

### Environment

- Gentle AI: 2.4.0
- Client: OpenCode
- Operating system / architecture: Linux x86_64
- Build revision: not captured
- Operation shape: automated local commit amendment with an explicitly named non-HEAD target

### Bounded Evidence and Mutation Outcome

- Attempts: 1
- Outcome: a local commit other than the authorized target was rewritten.
- Remote outcome: no push or pull request occurred.
- Preserved state: the workflow stopped after detecting the incorrect rewrite; no automated repair or further history mutation was attempted.

### Minimal Reproduction

Use any disposable local repository with at least two commits. Authorize an automated workflow to amend only the older commit, leave a later commit at HEAD, and run the amendment step. Observe whether it mutates the named older revision or unconditionally rewrites HEAD.

### Additional Context
