title: design(review): one store load per STATUS call — make negotiated STATUS a pure reader over the runtime's bytes
body:
## 📝 Problem / Proposal

This is a continuation of the accepted `rdd-root-simplification` architecture line, not a new direction. That program's own goal statement (`docs/architecture/rdd-root-simplification-design.md:77`) is *"expose status as a read-only view, not a second planner"*, and its root-cause table (:110-121) names this proposal's exact target as **"Replicated contract truth"** and split transition ownership. The recent #3587 wave closed most of the historical dual-truth territory: the FINALIZE verb is retired behind last-event atomic closure (`internal/cli/review_last_event_closure.go`), deciding gates collapsed into the non-deciding delivery surface (`runNonDecidingReviewGate`, `review_facade.go:2440-2457`), and SDD attempt accounting no longer consults RDD state at all (`runtime_ledger.go:801-804`). The STATUS-vs-START scope-divergence family is pinned property-test green (`TestNegotiatedStatusNeverOffersAStartItsOwnPreflightRefuses`).

What remains is narrower and structural: **the negotiated STATUS command itself still reads authority state twice, through two unrelated readers, and answers identity with two different policies.** This issue asks for a design that closes those three seams as one increment.

## Seam 1 — two store loads inside one STATUS call

The contract branch of `review status --contract … --next-transition` first classifies via `AssessTargetStatusWithSnapshot` (`internal/reviewtransaction/target_status.go:127-165`), then performs a **second, independent** store load to assemble envelope facts (`CompactAuthoritativeStore` + `LoadContext` at `internal/cli/review_facade.go:926-931`). Nothing binds the two loads to the same revision; the envelope can be assembled from bytes the classifier did not see. Today the only mitigation is post-hoc revalidation (`validateWithCompactAuthority`, `review_status_contract.go:338-363`) — detection after the fact rather than construction from one snapshot.

## Seam 2 — two identity policies without a stated contract

The store publishes frozen identity from persisted bytes alone ("a stale lineage still publishes the identity its own authority was frozen at"), while the negotiated target status "recomputes the identity from the worktree and withholds the authority block entirely once the target drifts" (`internal/reviewtransaction/status.go:67-74`; mirrored in `review_status_contract.go:66,204-207`). Both behaviors are individually defensible — archaeology wants the frozen value, negotiation wants the live check — but no document states which question each policy answers, so every new consumer guesses.

## Seam 3 — two projections, no shared reader

Plain `review status` walks `InventoryAuthority` (`status.go:111-181`); negotiated STATUS builds `TargetStatusDecision` via `AssessTargetStatusWithSnapshot`. They answer different questions today, but nothing owns their agreement: there is no shared read-model from which both views project. The ownership table of the design doc (:151-158) already assigns transitions to `ReviewCore` and rendering to adapters; the read side lacks its equivalent statement.

## Adjacent, explicitly out of scope

#3442's residual (no host-declared "this slot cannot be produced" channel; only the lens-context budget probe stops re-offering, `review_lens_context.go:308-325`) touches the same reader but requires a contract-surface decision, so it should be designed separately once seams 1-3 settle what the reader even is.

## What the design must decide

1. **Single load**: the classification pass either accepts an already-loaded compact context or returns its revision-stamped record for reuse, so envelope facts derive from exactly the classified revision. No wire/schema changes expected — envelopes stay byte-compatible; this is an internal reader refactor plus tests.
2. **Identity policy table**: one written table mapping question → policy (frozen vs live-recomputed), placed next to `SnapshotIdentity`'s doc comment so future consumers stop guessing.
3. **Shared projection core**: one read-model function over the compact record from which both `InventoryAuthority` entries and `TargetStatusDecision` project; existing property tests (the STATUS↔START convergence suite) extended to pin inventory/negotiated agreement the same way.

## Hygiene residuals observed during the audit (separate small fixes, listed only for completeness)

- Test files gated behind `//go:build legacy_compact_receipt` reference production symbols deleted in the #3587 wave (`bindPreparedReview`, `RecordReceiptRequest`, `applyReviewGateEvaluation` have no definitions anywhere); building with that tag should currently fail to compile.
- `docs/architecture/organic-rdd.md` still describes the retired FINALIZE verb at :22, :29, :35, :47.

## Why now

Every historical contradiction this design would prevent has already cost users a report (#3476, #3429, #3529 among them), and all three were closed by *removing* a competing truth source rather than reconciling readers after the fact. Seams 1-3 are the remaining places where the same pattern can regrow. The wave-7 openspec change (`openspec/changes/rdd-root-simplification-wave7/proposal.md:100-113`) documents deferred switch removal and an open re-entry condition; a defined pure-reader contract is the natural prerequisite for that next step.

title: bug(orchestration): injected OpenCode dispatch is revoked before first heartbeat
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I searched existing open and closed issues and found no equivalent report.
- [x] I understand that a PR must not be opened until the issue has `status:approved`.

### 📝 Bug Description

A coordinated Orca dispatch to a visible OpenCode TUI delivers the injected TASK successfully, but the dispatch operation returns `agent_prompt_stalled` and revokes its capability before the worker can send its first lifecycle signal.

The worker receives the complete coordinator preamble and TASK. When its first action is the required heartbeat using the exact injected task ID, dispatch ID, sender handle, and capability, Orca rejects it because the capability is already revoked.

This creates an authority/execution split: a worker may have actionable task content while lifecycle authority already considers the dispatch invalid. In earlier bounded attempts, workers continued, mutated files, passed tests, and then had `worker_done` rejected for the same revoked capability.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Create an orchestration Run and a ready task.
2. Create a visible OpenCode TUI terminal and wait for its TUI-idle condition.
3. Dispatch the task to that terminal using injected delivery.
4. Confirm the TUI received the full preamble and TASK.
5. Make the worker's first action a heartbeat using the exact lifecycle identifiers and capability injected by the dispatch.
6. Observe that the dispatch reports a stalled prompt and the heartbeat is rejected because the capability is already revoked.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

After injected delivery reaches the worker, the dispatch capability should remain valid for the worker's first lifecycle signal and subsequent bounded task execution.

If the dispatch cannot establish lifecycle authority, the worker should not receive an actionable TASK, or it should be stopped before any mutation can occur. Prompt delivery and dispatch authority should not disagree.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The TASK is visibly delivered, but the coordinator receives:

```text
agent_prompt_stalled
```

The worker's first heartbeat then receives:

```text
Dispatch capability is revoked.
```

A later `worker_done` is rejected for the same reason.

### Gentle AI Version

2.4.0

### Operating System

Windows 11, x64

### AI Agent / Client

OpenCode 1.18.21 through Orca 1.4.188 visible terminals

### 📋 Affected Area

Other — Orca orchestration Dispatch lifecycle

### 💡 Bounded Attempts and Outcomes

- Attempt group 1: two injected tasks were visibly delivered. Both dispatch calls reported the stalled-prompt outcome. A read-only worker completed verification and a writer completed a two-file TDD change, but both final lifecycle messages were rejected because their capabilities had been revoked.
- Attempt group 2: two fresh visible TUI workers were launched. Each TASK explicitly required the heartbeat as the first action. Both exact first heartbeats were rejected because their capabilities were already revoked. One writer stopped before inspection or mutation as instructed.
- No additional dispatch retry was attempted after confirming the same behavior with the first-action heartbeat.

Safe opaque evidence identifiers:

- Run: `run_7a5a2eed28bc`
- Earlier dispatches: `ctx_0b27199b68f3`, `ctx_1758d306de0c`
- First-action heartbeat dispatches: `ctx_fa768145ae36`, `ctx_db5c66398c5d`

### Mutation and Preserved State

- The latest writer reported no file mutation and remained blocked pending fresh authority.
- The current tasks and visible terminals remain preserved.
- Earlier attempts demonstrate that the injected worker can continue executing after authority is revoked, so the lifecycle result cannot safely be treated as equivalent to cancellation.

### Additional Context

This report records observed behavior only and does not assume whether the defect is in prompt-delivery acknowledgment, capability lease timing, dispatch settlement, or the OpenCode/Orca integration boundary.

Privacy review completed immediately before submission: no credentials, capability tokens, usernames, hostnames, absolute paths, private project names, environment values, source contents, or diffs are included.

title: fix(antigravity): unify global skills and MCP paths under ~/.gemini/config and update skill-registry
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

When running `gentle-ai sync` or `gentle-ai install --agent antigravity`, skills and MCP configurations are written to `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/`, which Antigravity 2.0 Desktop never discovers:

1. **`SkillsDir` Hardcoded to CLI Path**: In `internal/agents/antigravity/adapter.go` (lines 104-106), `SkillsDir(homeDir)` resolves to `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills/` (via `antigravityVariantDir`).
2. **Official Discovery Hierarchy**: According to Google Antigravity's official Customization Architecture (`agy-customizations`), the canonical Single Source of Truth for global customizations across both Antigravity 2.0 (Desktop) and CLI (`agy`) is:
   - **Global Customization Root**: `~/.gemini/config/`
     - Global Skills: `~/.gemini/config/skills/<skill_name>/SKILL.md`
     - Global MCP Servers: `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json`
     - Global Hooks: `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json`
     - Global Plugins: `~/.gemini/config/plugins/`
   - **Terminal Scope (CLI only)**: `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/` is isolated solely for terminal preferences (`settings.json`) and CLI session state.
3. **Silent Stale Skill Execution**: Running `gentle-ai sync` updates skills in `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills/`, leaving `~/.gemini/config/skills/` untouched. As a result, Antigravity 2.0 Desktop sessions silently continue executing outdated skills left in `~/.gemini/config/skills/`.
4. **Skill Registry Gap**: `internal/skillregistry/registry.go` in `UserSkillDirs()` (lines 57-82) scans `~/.gemini/skills/`, `~/.gemini/antigravity/skills/`, and `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills/`, but omits `~/.gemini/config/skills/`.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce
1. Install or sync Gentle AI with Antigravity target: `gentle-ai sync`.
2. Inspect modified files in `~/.gemini/`:
   - `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills/` receives updated files.
   - `~/.gemini/config/skills/` remains unchanged.
3. Open Antigravity 2.0 Desktop. The agent prompt lists skills discovered only from `~/.gemini/config/skills/` (the outdated copy).

### ✅ Expected Behavior
- `gentle-ai sync` and `gentle-ai install` should write global skills to `~/.gemini/config/skills/` and MCP configurations to `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json`.
- Both Antigravity 2.0 (Desktop) and Antigravity CLI (`agy`) automatically discover customizations from `~/.gemini/config/`.
- `skill-registry` should index `~/.gemini/config/skills/`.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
Skills are written to `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills/`, causing Antigravity 2.0 Desktop to silently execute stale skills from `~/.gemini/config/skills/`.

---
## 🖥️ Environment

**Gentle AI Version**: `2.4.0` (commit `51a0d60`)
**Operating System**: `Windows` (reproduces identically on macOS and Linux)
**AI Agent / Client**: `Other` (Google Antigravity 2.0 / Antigravity CLI)
**Affected Area**: `Installation Pipeline`

### 💡 Logs / Error Output
```shell
# Observed file modification times after 'gentle-ai sync':
LastWriteTime             FullName
23/08/2026 12:15:57 a. m. ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md
23/08/2026 12:15:56 a. m. ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills/sdd-apply/SKILL.md
23/08/2026 12:15:55 a. m. ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills/_shared/sdd-phase-common.md

# ~/.gemini/config/skills remains frozen at previous install timestamp:
15/07/2026 10:42:22 p. m. ~/.gemini/config/skills/graphify/SKILL.md
```

### Additional Context

#### Antigravity Path Taxonomy
To clarify the purpose of each directory under `~/.gemini/`:
- **Canonical Global Base**: `~/.gemini/config/` (Single Source of Truth for Skills, MCPs, Hooks, Plugins, Rules across Desktop 2.0, CLI `agy`, and IDE).
- **Specialized Terminal Scope**: `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/` (for CLI-specific overrides, TUI settings, history, and CLI-exclusive skills/hooks/MCPs if a user explicitly wants terminal-only behavior).
- **Runtime App Data**: `~/.gemini/antigravity/` (internal application data, session logs, and SQLite DBs managed internally by Antigravity; untouched by external installers).

*Note*: While placing skills, hooks, or MCPs in `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/` works when running the CLI tool directly, global customizations (which is what `gentle-ai install` and `gentle-ai sync` provide) should be located in `~/.gemini/config/` so they are universally available to Antigravity Desktop, CLI, and IDE without duplication or synchronization drift.

#### Official Google Antigravity Precedence Order
From the official Antigravity customization specification:
1. **Workspace Project**: `.agents/skills/` or `.gemini/skills/` (CWD up to repo root)
2. **Declared Configurations**: `skills.json` or `plugins.json` in workspace
3. **Global Discovery**: `~/.gemini/config/skills/` and `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json`
4. **Built-in Customizations**: Default platform skills in `~/.gemini/antigravity/builtin/skills/`

#### Proposed Solution
1. **Update Antigravity Adapter (`internal/agents/antigravity/adapter.go`)**:
   - Route `SkillsDir()` to `filepath.Join(homeDir, ".gemini", "config", "skills")`.
   - Route `MCPConfigPath()` to `filepath.Join(homeDir, ".gemini", "config", "mcp_config.json")`.
   - Keep `SettingsPath()` returning `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` for CLI-exclusive options.
2. **Update Skill Registry Scanner (`internal/skillregistry/registry.go`)**:
   - Add `filepath.Join(home, ".gemini", "config", "skills")` to `UserSkillDirs()`.
   - *(Optional maintainer decision)*: Add `filepath.Join(home, ".gemini", "antigravity", "builtin", "skills")` if indexing built-in platform skills in `.atl/skill-registry.md` is desired.
3. **Update E2E Tests & Docs**:
   - Update `e2e/e2e_test.sh` (`test_antigravity_sdd_skills_path`) to assert `~/.gemini/config/skills/`.
   - Update `docs/agents.md` references.

title: feat(pi): parse typed model-routing apply responses
body:
## Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`.

## 🔍 Affected Area

Other — Pi model-routing protocol parsing.

## 💡 Problem Statement

The apply operation can persist configuration and still return a failed envelope with exit 6, `outcome: "partial"`, and `saved: true`. Its typed result and strict materialization evidence must be validated independently before the bounded process client interprets exits or reports mutation state.

Combining strict apply parsing with request construction, transport mapping, and mutation-aware exit consistency would repeat the oversized client pattern already measured for inspect and validate.

## 📦 Proposed Solution

Add a pure typed parser for `gentle-pi.model-routing/v1` apply responses using #3599's shared strict operation envelope.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A public parser returns a typed apply response containing version, contract, operation, envelope `ok`, exit class, and typed apply result.
- [ ] Apply outcomes are constrained to success, validation-failure, unavailable-runtime, persistence-failure, or partial.
- [ ] Result contract, result `ok`, outcome, saved flag, and non-null diagnostics are presence-aware required fields.
- [ ] Optional target and config path preserve omission, reject null, and target is constrained to global/project.
- [ ] Optional materialization requires non-null affected/succeeded/failed arrays; every failure entry requires target and message.
- [ ] Diagnostics reuse the canonical strict code/message/severity/path rules.
- [ ] Envelope/result `ok`, outcome, saved, and exit-class consistency is preserved as parsed data for #3580; the parser does not normalize or interpret process exits.

title: fix(cli): make the refusal-resolution ratchet enforce the runnable-command grammar the benchmark already classifies
body:
## 📝 Bug Description

Two grammars in this repository define what counts as a "runnable continuation" for a refusal message, and they disagree today:

1. **The static ratchet** (`internal/cli/refusal_resolution_ratchet_test.go`, `refusalRatchetNamedContinuationRegexp`, ~line 151) matches only `gentle-ai [a-z][a-z-]*` — product name plus one verb, nothing after. A refusal printing `gentle-ai review status --cwd <repo>` **passes** this check.
2. **The benchmark classifier** (`bench/classify.go`, `HasRunnableCommand` with `placeholderRun = <[^>\s]*>`) requires at least one real argument and **rejects unfilled `<placeholder>` tokens**. The same message is classified *not runnable* there.

So a message the benchmark classifies out-of-band satisfies the ratchet that CI runs as a required merge check. The ratchet's own header states the limitation plainly: *"it cannot catch a WRONG named continuation — one that parses, runs, and does not help."*

This seam is the shared root of a recurring class of reports where printed guidance cannot be executed as printed:

- #3443 (scrubber destroys contract identifiers) — fix in flight via PR #3456
- #3440 (pi transport refusal never names the handshake)
- #3557 (doctor sync remedy unrunnable for dangling symlinks) — fix in flight via PR #3561
- #1997 (escalated abandon refusal names an unusable continuation) — related fix in flight via PR #3268
- #2790, #2895 (further continuations awaiting design/review)

And per #2834's measurement, `internal/sddstatus/runtime_ledger.go` alone declares 36 refusals with no runnable exit.

## 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Observe `refusalRatchetNamedContinuationRegexp = regexp.MustCompile(`gentle-ai [a-z][a-z-]*`)` in `internal/cli/refusal_resolution_ratchet_test.go`.
2. Evaluate it against a refusal text such as `run `gentle-ai review status --cwd <repo>`` — it matches (`gentle-ai review`), so the site passes the ratchet.
3. Run the same text through `bench/classify.go` `HasRunnableCommand`: `placeholderRun` finds `<repo>` and the classifier returns false.
4. Result: the two enforcement layers disagree about the same emitted sentence, and CI's required check is the weaker of the two.

## ✅ Expected Behavior

The static ratchet enforces the same printed-command grammar the benchmark already enforces:

- a named continuation must carry real arguments, not stop at the verb;
- an unfilled `<placeholder>` tail is accepted only when the site explicitly declares operator knowledge via the existing `refusal:by-design operator-knowledge:` marker (or holds a baseline row);
- the baseline regenerates once at the switch and may only shrink afterwards;
- existing CI (already a required merge check) then enforces the stronger grammar going forward — no new CI lane needed.

Both command splitters needed already exist and are deliberately mirrored (`internal/cli/review_printed_command.go` `SplitPrintedCommandWords` and its bench twin); no third splitter should be written.

## ❌ Actual Behavior

The ratchet accepts verb-only matches regardless of what follows, including tails the benchmark classes as not runnable. Wrong or dead-end continuations therefore pass the required merge check until someone files a per-instance report.

## 🌍 Environment

- Current `main` (verified against source on 2026-08-22)
- Evidence gathered on Windows; the grammar seam itself is platform-independent

## 💡 Proposed Scope

Static unification slice only: swap the ratchet's continuation grammar to the shared printed-command grammar, add the operator-knowledge marker path, regenerate the baseline once. Estimated ~150–250 changed lines including tests; one revertible PR from current `main`. The dynamic half ("follow the printed recipe until the block clears") already has a canonical pattern (`internal/cli/review_abandon_message_test.go`) and grows case-by-case afterwards.

**Non-goals**: no execution sandbox in the unit lane, no new wire vocabulary, no parallel command splitter, no change to bench classification semantics.

title: bug(pi): same-version reinstall leaves package-private runtime missing
body:
## Automated provider-defect report

This report contains observed evidence only. The root cause is not confirmed.

## Observed behavior

`gentle-pi` cannot launch native bounded review because its verified package-private Gentle AI runtime is absent. A supported reinstall of the exact configured package version exits successfully and reports that the package is already current, but it does not restore the missing runtime.

## Environment

- OS/architecture: macOS arm64
- Client: Pi 0.84.2
- Package: gentle-pi 2.2.0
- Expected private runtime: Gentle AI 2.4.0

## Operation shape and bounded attempts

1. Native read-only review inspection was requested from a Git repository.
2. The controller failed closed before launching a native process.
3. The exact configured `gentle-pi` version was reinstalled through Pi with the documented skip-install override unset.
4. One reinstall attempt completed with exit status 0 and reported the package already up to date.
5. The package-private runtime remained absent. No repair retries were attempted.

## Failure envelope

```json
{
  "operation": "inspect",
  "status": "blocked",
  "outcome": "native-status-package-binary-missing",
  "lineage_created": false,
  "mutation_performed": false,
  "mutation_outcome": "none",
  "inventory_complete": false,
  "next_action": "reinstall-package-local-gentle-ai"
}
```

## Expected behavior

A normal reinstall of the exact configured package version should execute the package installation lifecycle needed to restore and verify the pinned package-private runtime, or return an actionable non-success result explaining why it was not restored.

## Actual behavior

The reinstall succeeds as an up-to-date no-op while the package-private runtime remains absent. The next native review inspection therefore returns the same fail-closed missing-runtime result.

## Minimal reproduction

1. Install `gentle-pi` 2.2.0 through Pi.
2. Start from a state where its package-private Gentle AI runtime is absent.
3. Reinstall the same package version normally, without the documented skip-install override.
4. Observe a successful up-to-date result.
5. Request native review inspection and observe that it remains blocked because the package-private runtime is still absent.

## Preserved-state evidence

- No review lineage was created.
- Native process launch did not begin.
- Repository HEAD and the staged candidate hash remained identical across the reinstall attempt.

## Duplicate search

Open and closed issues were searched using exact and broader terms for the missing package-local runtime, package-private runtime, postinstall, reinstall, and `gentle-pi` installer behavior. No equivalent report was found. Closed issue #1896 concerns a different historical `native-status-unavailable` inventory failure, not a successful same-version reinstall that leaves the private runtime absent.

title: feat(filesystem): add cooperative no-follow file mutation
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`.

### 🔍 Affected Area

Other

Shared cross-platform filesystem coordination and OpenCode shell-profile mutation.

### 💡 Problem Statement

PR #3460 must identify and update only the exact Gentle-managed block inside a user-owned shell profile. Current point-in-time checks are insufficient:

- `Lstat -> Open` can follow a final-component symlink installed between calls.
- `revalidate -> atomic rename` detects many stale snapshots but is not an identity-bound compare-and-swap.
- `filemerge.WriteFileAtomic` provides atomic pathname publication and durability checks, not a predicate against a previously observed destination file ID.

POSIX and Windows do not expose one portable operation that atomically replaces a destination only when it is still the same previously observed filesystem object. This issue therefore MUST NOT claim portable CAS or protection against arbitrary non-cooperating writers.

The required product behavior is a cooperative optimistic mutation contract that is honest about this boundary and fails closed when its declared guarantees cannot be established.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Add one shared mutation pipeline for Gentle-managed edits to user-owned files:

```text
acquire Gentle lock
  -> open/read without following the final symlink or reparse point
  -> capture exact bytes, mode, and point-in-time identity
  -> compute replacement
  -> revalidate while the Gentle lock is held
  -> atomically publish by pathname
  -> read back and report durability
  -> release lock
```

#### Threat model

| Actor or failure | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Concurrent Gentle AI process using this API | Serialized by the shared cross-process lock. |
| Ordinary external edit completed before final revalidation | Detected as a typed conflict; no publication. |
| Final-component symlink or Windows reparse point at observation | Refused without following the target. |
| Missing, non-regular, wrong-mode, malformed, or unowned input | Typed no-change/conflict/unsupported result; no mutation. |
| Process failure before publication | Temporary artifacts are cleaned according to the existing atomic-writer contract. |
| Successful publication | Pathname replacement is atomic and read back; reported durability reflects the platform. |
| Malicious or non-cooperating writer racing after final revalidation | **Not prevented portably.** This residual window is explicit and must never be described as CAS. |
| Lost or ambiguous mutation output | No blind retry; inspect current bytes/state before any next action. |

A caller that requires protection against arbitrary non-cooperating writers must receive `unsupported` and perform no automatic mutation.

#### Typed outcomes

The shared API must distinguish:

- `no_change`: semantic no-op; no publication;
- `committed`: replacement was atomically published and read back under the cooperative contract;
- `conflict`: snapshot/topology/content changed before publication; no publication by this operation;
- `unsupported`: required lock or no-follow capability is unavailable; no mutation attempted;
- `failed`: definite operational failure with no success claim.

Results must include whether bytes changed, the observed conflict reason, and the platform durability level. `committed` MUST NOT imply arbitrary-writer identity CAS.

#### Work unit 1 — lock API and fail-closed contract

Define the reusable API, privacy-preserving lock identity, typed errors, idempotent lease release, and an all-platform `unsupported` backend.

- `LockPath` must be side-effect free.
- `Acquire` must fail before filesystem mutation until a platform backend exists.
- API comments must state the cooperative, non-CAS boundary.
- Maximum: 400 authored changed lines.

#### Work unit 2 — secure POSIX lock backend

Implement bounded POSIX acquisition with descriptor-relative, no-follow traversal and private lock files.

- Use kernel `flock`; never infer ownership from lock-file residue.
- Reject symlinked or non-regular roots and lock paths.
- Add real subprocess contention tests.
- Maximum: 400 authored changed lines.

#### Work unit 3 — secure Windows lock backend

Implement Windows acquisition with reparse-safe root/file handling, private ACLs, and `LockFileEx`.

- Add real Windows subprocess contention tests.
- Keep unsupported platforms fail closed.
- Maximum: 400 authored changed lines.

#### Work unit 4 — no-follow snapshot authority

Add a shared, side-effect-free snapshot API:

- POSIX: parent-directory-relative open with final-component no-follow semantics.
- Windows: handle-based open with reparse-point-safe semantics.
- Capture bytes, mode/attributes, and point-in-time identity from the opened object.
- Reject symlinks/reparse points and non-regular files without reading their targets.
- Maximum: 400 authored changed lines.

#### Work unit 5 — cooperative optimistic rewrite

Compose lock + snapshot + existing atomic writer:

- hold the Gentle lock across observation, revalidation, publication, and read-back;
- compare exact bytes, topology, mode, and point-in-time identity before publication;
- return typed conflict/unsupported outcomes;
- retain existing same-directory staging and durability behavior;
- document the residual non-cooperating-writer race in code and public API comments;
- never silently downgrade or retry.
- Maximum: 400 authored changed lines.

#### Work unit 6 — OpenCode D10 integration

Update #3460 to use the shared API:

- backup and mutate only a regular profile containing the exact current canonical Gentle-managed block;
- exclude nonexistent, unrelated, stale, malformed, multiple, symlinked/reparse, wrong-mode, or read-only profiles;
- preserve surrounding user bytes, line endings, and mode;
- surface conflict/unsupported results with exact manual-cleanup guidance;
- never claim cleanup when no mutation committed.
- Maximum: 400 authored changed lines.

### ✅ Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The public contract explicitly states that it is cooperative optimistic mutation, not portable CAS.
- [ ] Concurrent Gentle AI writers serialize through one shared lock authority.
- [ ] POSIX observation cannot follow a final-component symlink.
- [ ] Windows observation cannot follow a final-component reparse point.
- [ ] Exact bytes, mode/attributes, and point-in-time identity are captured from the opened object.
- [ ] Changes completed before final revalidation return `conflict` without publication.
- [ ] Successful publication remains atomic by pathname and is read back before reporting `committed`.
- [ ] Unsupported lock/no-follow capabilities fail closed without mutation.
- [ ] No code, docs, or UI describes the operation as identity-bound CAS against arbitrary writers.
- [ ] Deterministic seams cover symlink/reparse swaps, stale bytes/identity, lock contention, publication errors, ambiguous output, and cleanup.
- [ ] Platform CI executes real POSIX and Windows behavior, not compile-only proof.
- [ ] #3460 uses typed outcomes and provides manual cleanup instructions for conflict/unsupported states.
- [ ] Every work unit stays at or below 400 authored changed lines.

### 🚫 Non-goals

- Portable prevention of a malicious or non-cooperating writer racing pathname replacement.
- A general crash-recoverable quarantine or filesystem transaction engine.
- Automatic recovery after ambiguous output.
- Weakening existing launcher ownership, rollback, or profile-topology safeguards.
- Expanding #3460's supported shell/profile policy.
- Merging any branch into `main`; merge decisions remain human-owned.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- **Portable identity-bound CAS.** Rejected because documented POSIX and Windows replacement APIs select by pathname/existence, not by a previously observed destination identity.
- **Check then rename described as CAS.** Rejected because a non-cooperating writer can still race the final publication window.
- **Quarantine/recovery engine inside #3460.** Rejected as disproportionate and incomplete without a new durable recovery authority.
- **Manual-only cleanup for every profile.** Rejected because it makes the approved profile feature unnecessarily unusable when all cooperating Gentle writers can be serialized safely.

### 📎 Additional Context

Related work:

- #3460 — blocked OpenCode D10 integration
- #3452 — approved POSIX launcher-profile behavior
- #3043 — parent OpenCode background-subagent feature
- #1121 — related but non-duplicate journal/configuration CAS work

Current `main` at the original triage point: `ec3b1db7aa6deaace75fd8c05f217de64bd25b28`.

feat(agents): add Zed IDE agent support
body:
## 💡 Problem Statement

Zed IDE (zed.dev) is a high-performance, Rust-based code editor with a built-in AI assistant panel that supports MCP servers, custom agent instructions via `AGENTS.md`, a shared skill system (`~/.agents/skills/`), and a native **sub-agent runtime** (`spawn_agent`). These capabilities make it a good candidate for gentle-ai integration.

Currently, Zed has no first-class support in gentle-ai. Users who prefer Zed — especially those learning to program with AI assistance — must manually configure MCP servers, skills, and system prompts instead of getting the full gentle-ai stack out of the box.

The PRD already lists Zed as **P2 with partial support**, but no adapter exists yet.

## 📦 Proposed Solution

Add Zed as a supported agent in gentle-ai's agent catalog. Based on Zed's architecture, the integration would need to handle:

- **MCP config**: Zed has no dedicated `mcp.json`. MCP servers live inside `settings.json` under `context_servers` with a stdio shape (`{ enabled, command, args, env }`). The installer would need a strategy to merge into that structure.
- **System prompt**: Zed supports a user-global `AGENTS.md` at the config root (`~/.config/zed/` on Linux/macOS, `%APPDATA%\Zed\` on Windows). It live-watches this file and treats empty files as absent.
- **Skills**: Zed scans `~/.agents/skills/` natively on startup (project `.agents/skills` > global > built-in), so the shared cross-agent skills directory should work without registry changes.
- **Agent profile**: Zed supports named agent profiles in `settings.json` (`agent.profiles.*`), which could hold the Gentleman persona config.
- **Sub-agents**: Zed exposes a native `spawn_agent` tool from the Agent Panel: each call creates a fully isolated sub-agent session (own context window + own tools) that runs independently and returns only its final message plus a `session_id`. Follow-up calls reusing the `session_id` resume that session with its own accumulated history. Multiple spawns issued together run in parallel. Messages must be self-contained (the sub-agent never sees the parent's conversation).
- **Detection**: Desktop app, no binary on PATH — detect by config directory presence.

Component support estimate:

| Component | Feasible | Notes |
| ----------- | ---------- | ------- |
| Engram | Yes | MCP server injected into `context_servers` |
| SDD Orchestrator | Yes | Multi-agent variant — Zed has a native sub-agent runtime via `spawn_agent` |
| Skills | Yes | Shared `~/.agents/skills/`, Zed scans natively |
| Persona | Yes | Via agent profile in `settings.json` |
| MCP | Yes | Merge into `context_servers` (no `mcp.json`) |
| System Prompt | Yes | `AGENTS.md` at config root |
| Sub-agents | Yes | Native `spawn_agent` sessions (isolated context, parallel spawns, `session_id` resume) |
| Auto-install | No | Desktop app only |

## 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- **Manual configuration**: Users can set up MCP servers and skills by hand, but this defeats the purpose of gentle-ai as an ecosystem configurator.
- **Waiting for Zed to add `mcp.json` support**: Unlikely to happen — `context_servers` is their established config pattern.

## 📎 Additional Context

- Zed config paths: `%APPDATA%\Zed\` (Windows), `~/.config/zed/` (Linux AND macOS — macOS does NOT use `~/Library/Application Support` for config)
- Zed validates skill frontmatter names against `[a-z0-9-]`, which may reject directories like `_shared`
- Zed's `settings.json` supports JSONC (JSON with comments), which the filemerge strategy would need to handle gracefully
- Zed `spawn_agent` behavior verified empirically (2026-08-22): sub-agents start with a clean slate (no parent history), branches never see each other's output unless the parent relays it, results return as final message only (no intermediate reasoning/tool streaming), and error results may still carry a usable `session_id` for retry/resume
- Related closed issues for reference: #136 (Trae IDE), #166 (Kiro)


## 🔗 Tracking branch (fork)

Work in progress lives at [`Seinra/gentle-ai:feat/zed-support`](https://github.com/Seinra/gentle-ai/tree/feat/zed-support) (currently based on upstream v2.7.0, test suite green). This branch is kept current via merges, so this pointer stays fresh — no PR until `status:approved`, per the issues-first rule.

title: bug(skills): skill-registry misclassifies project skills when --cwd is relative
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description


  `gentle-ai skill-registry list --json --cwd .` treats project-local skills as
 `scope: "user"` and emits relative paths, while the same command with an absolute
 cwd correctly reports `scope: "project"` and absolute paths.

 This makes explicit relative `--cwd` behave differently from the default cwd or
 an absolute `--cwd`, even though `--cwd .` is a natural CLI usage.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

   1. Check out `Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai`.
   2. From the repository root, run:

      ```bash
      gentle-ai skill-registry list --json --cwd . | grep -A3
 'cognitive-doc-design'
 ```

 3. Run the equivalent command with an absolute cwd:

    ```bash
      gentle-ai skill-registry list --json --cwd "$PWD" | grep -A3
    'cognitive-doc-design'
    ```

 4. Compare the scope and path fields.

### ✅ Expected Behavior


   `--cwd .` and `--cwd "$PWD"` should resolve to the same project identity.

   Project-local skills should be reported as:

   ```json
   {
     "scope": "project",
     "path": "<repo>/skills/cognitive-doc-design/SKILL.md"
   }
 ```

### ❌ Actual Behavior

 With relative `--cwd .`, project-local skills can be reported as:

   ```json
   {
     "scope": "user",
     "path": "skills/cognitive-doc-design/SKILL.md"
   }
 ```

 With absolute --cwd "$PWD", the same skill is correctly reported as
 project-scoped.

### Gentle AI Version

gentle-ai 2.3.0

### Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
$ gentle-ai skill-registry list --json --cwd . | grep -A3 'cognitive-doc-design'
       "name": "cognitive-doc-design",
       "scope": "user",
       "description": "Design docs that reduce cognitive load. Trigger: writing
 guides, READMEs, RFCs, onboarding, architecture, or review-facing docs.",
       "path": "skills/cognitive-doc-design/SKILL.md"

   $ gentle-ai skill-registry list --json --cwd "$PWD" | grep -A3
 'cognitive-doc-design'
       "name": "cognitive-doc-design",
       "scope": "project",
       "description": "Design docs that reduce cognitive load. Trigger: writing
 guides, READMEs, RFCs, onboarding, architecture, or review-facing docs.",
       "path": "<repo>/skills/cognitive-doc-design/SKILL.md"
```

### Additional Context

 Likely cause:

   - `internal/app/app.go`: `resolveSkillRegistryDirs` returns explicit `--cwd`
 unchanged.
   - `internal/skillregistry/registry.go`: `List`, `Regenerate`, and `ScopeForPath`
 use `filepath.Clean(cwd)` but do not canonicalize relative cwd values to absolute
 paths.
   - `ScopeForPath` checks whether the cleaned skill path has the cleaned cwd as a
 prefix. With `cwd="."`, project-local paths such as `skills/...` do not match the
 expected `./` prefix and are classified as user-scoped.

   Nearby but not duplicate issues:

   - #1731 fixed OpenCode refreshing from a nested directory instead of the Git
 worktree root.
   - #3350 fixed refresh initializing non-project directories / filesystem root.

   This issue is narrower: explicit relative `--cwd` should be normalized before
 skill registry list/refresh scope calculation.

title: bug(tui): Reset Review Store is offered outside a Git repository and fails with a raw git rev-parse error (2.4.0, macOS)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and found no duplicate for the TUI "Reset Review Store" entry outside a Git repository.
- [x] I understand that PRs require `status:approved` before implementation.

### Bug Description

The interactive TUI (`gentle-ai` with no arguments) lists the **Reset Review Store** entry unconditionally, regardless of whether the current working directory resolves to a Git repository.

The review store is repository-scoped: it lives under the repository's Git common directory (the successful run below reports `<repo>/.git/gentle-ai`). When the TUI is launched from a directory that is not inside a Git repository, the entry is still offered and selectable. Selecting it fails, and the failure is surfaced as the raw Git plumbing error rather than an actionable message:

```
Reset Review Store

✗ Could not read the review store

  git rev-parse --show-toplevel failed with exit code 128: fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git

▸ Back
```

The underlying command behaves identically:

```
$ gentle-ai review store-reset --cwd .
Error: git rev-parse --show-toplevel failed with exit code 128: fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
```

Two separable problems:

1. **Unconditional affordance.** A repository-scoped maintenance action is presented as available in a context where it can never succeed. The precondition is only discovered after selection.
2. **Non-actionable failure text.** `git rev-parse --show-toplevel failed with exit code 128` describes an internal implementation detail. It does not tell the operator what the entry requires or what to do next. Nothing in the message states that the TUI must be launched from inside a Git repository.

This is a discoverability defect, not a lifecycle or authority defect. No lineage, receipt, or store state is involved, since none can exist outside a repository.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `cd` to any directory that is not inside a Git repository (a user home directory with no `.git` at or above it reproduces this).
2. Confirm the precondition is absent: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` exits 128.
3. Launch the interactive TUI: `gentle-ai`
4. Open the **Reset Review Store** entry.

### Expected Behavior

Any of the following would resolve it:

- Omit the entry when the working directory does not resolve to a Git repository, or
- Render it disabled with a stated precondition (for example, "requires a Git repository"), or
- Keep it selectable but fail with an actionable message naming the precondition and the remedy (launch `gentle-ai` from inside a Git repository), instead of propagating the `git rev-parse` subprocess error.

The precondition should be legible before selection, not only after failure.

### Actual Behavior

The entry is always listed and selectable. Selecting it outside a repository renders the raw `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` exit-128 output with no guidance.

### Contrast: same command inside a repository

Run against a directory that does resolve to a repository root, the command succeeds and reports the store location:

```
$ gentle-ai review store-reset --cwd <repo>
review store: <repo>/.git/gentle-ai

nothing to remove: this clone holds no review lineage state.

0 settled review(s)
```

Same binary, same session. The only variable is whether the working directory resolves to a repository root, which confirms the failure is a missing precondition rather than a damaged store.

### Environment

- gentle-ai: `2.4.0` (stable channel; build string carries no `-rc.` or `-main.` tag)
- OS: macOS (Darwin)
- Architecture: arm64
- Client: interactive TUI (`gentle-ai` with no arguments), and `gentle-ai review store-reset --cwd .`
- Git: available and functioning; exit 128 is the correct Git response for the directory, not a Git fault

### Additional Context

Reported through the automated provider-defect handoff with the operator's explicit consent. Paths, usernames, hostnames, repository names, and command arguments beyond the flags shown have been excluded.

Other repository-scoped TUI entries may share the same unconditional-affordance pattern; this report covers only the entry that was observed.

title: feat(pi): resolve npm and local package roots
body:
## Parent tracker

Foundation slice for #3533 and #3531.

Resolve npm and local/file Pi package declarations into one absolute package root without rereading settings, executing the package, or implementing git transport grammar.

title: feat(opencode): enable background subagents by default with post-install controls
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`.

### 🔍 Affected Area

Other

OpenCode post-install controls and orchestration policy.

### 💡 Problem Statement

Issue [#3043](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/3043) and merged PR [#3179](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/3179) established native OpenCode background subagents, managed `auto|on|off` intent, install/sync flags, environment activation, safe foreground fallback, and an OpenCode-only routing addendum. #3043 is currently reopened for a POSIX launcher-persistence/readiness defect and has active repair slices; that defect remains in #3043.

A separate product gap remains on current `main` at audit commit `35deba324046c0687d38b1da66638da952e290ab`:

- unresolved non-interactive `auto` resolves to foreground `off`, even when a supported OpenCode runtime can be safely managed;
- users can change the policy only by re-entering install or sync flags, while the TUI choice exists only inside the unresolved interactive installer flow;
- the OpenCode routing addendum limits background work to independent read-only exploration, audit, or review, which leaves eligible independent verification and planning work inconsistently foreground.

The capability exists but is not the default supported experience, post-install control is hard to discover, and routing policy does not consistently use background execution when it is safe and useful.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

#### Default behavior

For a fresh installation with no explicit CLI value, Gentle AI environment value, or prior managed choice, `auto` should enable managed OpenCode background subagents when the runtime and launcher topology are supported and activation can be prepared safely. Interactive installation may still present the choice, with enablement as the recommended/default selection. Unsupported, unknown, explicitly disabled, or unmanaged runtime topologies must remain foreground.

Do not reinterpret existing explicit or persisted choices. Precedence remains explicit CLI control > Gentle AI environment control > prior managed state > default. An explicit upstream `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BACKGROUND_SUBAGENTS=false` remains authoritative.

#### Independently accessible controls

Provide post-install controls in both surfaces:

- a dedicated Gentle AI CLI command surface to show status, enable, or disable OpenCode background subagents without rerunning installation or a general sync;
- a discoverable TUI management entry that provides the same status and enable/disable behavior after installation.

Both surfaces must expose the same state model:

| Field | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Requested policy | Show `auto`, `on`, or `off`, including the winning source. |
| Effective state | Show active background execution, foreground fallback, or unknown; never infer active from persisted intent alone. |
| Activation | Show whether the managed launcher/environment is effective for future OpenCode CLI/TUI starts. |
| Restart | State whether an OpenCode and/or shell restart is required. |
| Runtime | Show supported, unsupported, unknown, or unmanaged topology with actionable guidance. |
| Persistence | Explain that `on`/`off` survives future install/sync runs until explicitly changed. |

`enable` persists managed `on` intent and applies only Gentle AI-owned activation. If the runtime is unsupported, unknown, or unmanaged, preserve the requested policy but report foreground fallback and the exact next action; do not claim activation. `disable` persists managed `off`, stops Gentle AI from dispatching background work, and removes only Gentle AI-owned activation. Neither action may override external user-managed OpenCode environment or unrelated configuration.

#### Routing policy

Refine the OpenCode routing addendum around dependency and mutation boundaries rather than a blanket read-only category:

| Work | Default execution |
| --- | --- |
| Independent exploration, repository mapping, research, or planning whose result is not needed immediately | Background when capability is active. |
| Independent test, build, lint, or read-only verification while the parent can continue non-overlapping work | Background when capability is active. |
| Work whose result is required before the next action, dependent phases, or user decisions | Foreground. |
| Any writer or implementation actor in the current worktree | Foreground unless a separately approved isolation contract explicitly permits otherwise. |
| Formal RDD/4R reviewers, refuters, validators, Judgment Day actors, and lifecycle-gate work | Foreground where their governing contract requires it. |
| Unsupported, unknown, disabled, or unmanaged OpenCode capability | Foreground with no duplicate dispatch. |

Keep completion notification-driven, bounded, non-duplicative, and honest about process-local/non-durable jobs. This issue must not introduce a scheduler, durable queue, recovery ledger, worktree authority, or parallel-writer policy. Issue [#3470](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/3470) remains the separate parallel-apply scheduling policy.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On a fresh non-interactive OpenCode installation with no explicit or prior policy, supported managed CLI/TUI topology resolves `auto` to active managed background execution.
- [ ] Unsupported, unknown, unmanaged, or explicitly disabled runtimes remain foreground and never report background as active.
- [ ] Existing persisted `on` and `off` choices, explicit Gentle AI CLI/environment values, and explicit upstream `false` retain precedence and behavior.
- [ ] A dedicated post-install CLI surface can display status, enable, and disable without rerunning install or general sync.
- [ ] A discoverable post-install TUI surface provides behavior and state reporting equivalent to the CLI.
- [ ] Status reports requested policy, source, effective state, runtime/topology support, managed activation, persistence, restart requirement, and fallback guidance.
- [ ] Enable/disable operations are idempotent, transactional, and mutate only Gentle AI-owned state and activation.
- [ ] Generated OpenCode policy follows the routing matrix and uses background consistently for eligible independent work.
- [ ] Dependent work, user decisions, current-worktree writers, and contract-required formal review actors remain foreground.
- [ ] Completion remains notification-driven with bounded concurrency, no polling, no duplicate launch, and no recovery claim after restart.
- [ ] CLI, TUI, install, sync, generated assets, status/doctor output, and documentation agree on the same policy and effective-state model.
- [ ] Tests cover the full precedence/default matrix, supported/unsupported/unknown/unmanaged runtime states, explicit upstream false, persistence, restart transitions, and CLI/TUI parity.
- [ ] Prompt/render contract tests cover every routing-matrix row and prove safe foreground fallback when capability is absent or disabled.
- [ ] A public/runtime benchmark journey demonstrates fresh-default activation, post-install enable/disable/status, restart messaging, effective runtime capability, and foreground fallback.

#### Non-goals

- Fixing the reopened POSIX activation defect already tracked by #3043 and its child issues.
- Reintroducing the legacy `background-agents.ts` plugin or adding a third-party background plugin.
- Adding durable task recovery, a scheduler/queue, parallel writer authority, or changing #3470's parallel-apply policy.
- Managing `serve`, `attach`, Desktop, or daemon lifecycles that Gentle AI does not own.
- Weakening foreground requirements imposed by formal review or delivery contracts.

#### Rollout and backward compatibility

- Apply the new default only when no explicit or persisted choice exists; do not migrate existing `off` users to `on`.
- Preserve the current `auto|on|off` state schema and precedence unless a documented compatibility reason requires a migration.
- Roll out fail-closed: unsupported or unknown capability remains foreground with guidance.
- Keep install/sync controls as compatible aliases to the same authority; the new CLI/TUI surfaces must not create a second policy store.
- Document upgrade behavior and any required OpenCode or shell restart.

#### Test evidence required in the issue-closing PR

- Exact commands and observed results for focused unit/contract tests and the repository-required full test suite.
- CLI/TUI golden or integration evidence for status, enable, disable, persistence, and restart messaging.
- Generated-policy contract evidence for each routing-matrix row.
- Public/runtime benchmark output covering active and foreground-fallback paths.
- Backward-compatibility evidence for existing `on`/`off`, external environment ownership, unsupported/unknown runtime, and no-op idempotent transitions.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- **Keep non-interactive `auto` as foreground-off.** Rejected because native background support remains opt-in in practice even on supported managed OpenCode installations.
- **Require users to rerun install or sync.** Rejected because configuration must remain independently manageable after installation.
- **Put every subagent in the background.** Rejected because dependencies, user decisions, writers, and formal review contracts require foreground sequencing.
- **Fold this into #3043.** Rejected because #3043 already delivered the base feature and is currently reopened for a focused activation defect; adding a new default, post-install UX, and routing-policy change would overload active repair scope.
- **Merge with #3470.** Rejected because provider background routing and user-controlled parallel product-code apply are different policies.

### 📎 Additional Context

Current-main evidence:

- `internal/cli/opencode_background.go` resolves unresolved non-interactive `auto` to effective `off`.
- `internal/cli/install.go` and `internal/cli/sync.go` expose the policy only as install/sync flags.
- `internal/tui/screens/opencode_background.go` describes the choice as an interactive installer screen.
- `internal/assets/opencode/background-subagents.md` contains the current background/foreground routing addendum.
- `docs/opencode-profiles.md` documents current precedence, persistence, launcher activation, restart, and unsupported topology behavior.

Related work:

- Base feature and active activation repair: https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/3043
- Merged base implementation: https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/3179
- Native-task migration: https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/812 and https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/813
- Separate parallel-apply policy: https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/3470

title: feat(pi): resolve and invoke the installed model-routing contract
body:
## Parent tracker

Enables #3522. This is the first Gentle AI work unit after the `gentle-pi.model-routing/v1` provider contract lands.

## Problem

Pi packages are resource-oriented. Installing `npm:gentle-pi`, a git package, or a local package does not guarantee that the package's `bin` entry is globally available on `PATH`.

The Gentle AI TUI therefore cannot safely assume `exec.LookPath("gentle-pi-models")` is sufficient, and it must not hard-code one transient Pi cache path or edit Pi configuration directly.

## Proposed work unit

Add a bounded Go resolver and process client for the installed `gentle-pi.model-routing/v1` executable. This PR contains no TUI screen.

Resolution should:

1. Accept explicit cwd, Pi agent/config directory, and target context.
2. Prefer a capability-valid `gentle-pi-models` executable on `PATH`.
3. Read effective project/user Pi package settings with project precedence.
4. Resolve the selected `gentle-pi` npm, git, or local package source through Pi's documented package-root conventions.
5. Read the package manifest and resolve its declared `gentle-pi-models` bin target instead of guessing an internal filename.
6. Capability-probe every candidate using a bounded, non-network `gentle-pi.model-routing/v1` request before accepting it.
7. Never invoke package installation, npm network resolution, model calls, or fallback JSON editing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A typed Pi model-routing client exposes capabilities, inspect, validate, and apply operations.
- [ ] The client sends one versioned JSON request and validates one JSON response plus the documented exit classes.
- [ ] Executable resolution supports a capability-valid PATH command.
- [ ] Project Pi settings take precedence over user Pi settings.
- [ ] npm, git, and local package sources resolve through documented Pi package roots.
- [ ] `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` and explicit agent-directory inputs are honored deterministically.
- [ ] Package manifest `bin` declarations are verified before execution.
- [ ] Missing package, missing bin, malformed settings/manifest, failed capability probe, timeout, invalid JSON, and unsupported contract return distinct actionable errors.
- [ ] Probing is bounded and does not trigger network installation, model execution, or configuration writes.
- [ ] Process cancellation terminates the child and returns promptly.
- [ ] Focused tests cover PATH, package-source layouts, precedence, overrides, probe failures/timeouts, protocol validation, and no-network/no-write behavior.
- [ ] Existing Pi/OpenCode/Claude/Codex behavior remains unchanged.
- [ ] The PR remains at or below 400 changed lines.

## Out of scope

- Rendering or navigating the **Configure Pi Models** TUI.
- Editing Pi JSON directly.
- Installing/upgrading `gentle-pi` automatically.
- Managing provider credentials.

## Chain

```text
PR 1 (this issue): installed contract resolver + Go process client
  -> PR 2 (#3522): Configure Pi Models TUI
```

## Evidence

Pi documents user/project npm roots, git package roots, local package references, and `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` in `docs/packages.md`. Current Gentle AI Pi installation uses `pi install npm:gentle-pi`, while real user settings may select git or local sources. Pi does not expose arbitrary package bins globally, so runtime capability validation is required.

title: bug(review): prompt-carried patch omits binding context and produces a deterministic false blocker
body:
## Automated provider-defect report

### Environment
- Gentle AI: `2.4.0` (stable channel)
- Client: OpenCode `1.18.19`
- OS/architecture: Linux x86_64
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`
- Review tier: medium, one Reliability lens

### Observed behavior
A provider-bound Reliability review repeatedly reports an unbound identifier as a deterministic blocker. The frozen candidate does bind that identifier earlier in the same function, and compilation with warnings treated as errors succeeds.

The prompt-carried evidence describes its patch sections as the complete and only candidate view, but the rendered hunk shows the later identifier use while omitting the nearby unchanged binding needed to interpret it. Because the lens is instructed not to inspect outside the prompt-carried patch, independent reruns reproduce the same false blocker.

This reports observed evidence only; it does not assert an unconfirmed implementation root cause.

### Bounded attempts and outcomes
1. Initial Reliability capture completed and finalized to `correction_required` with blocker `R3-001`.
2. Maintainer-authorized same-lineage quarantine reopened the Reliability slot.
3. A fresh provider-bound Reliability capture completed and reproduced `R3-001`.
4. The result was quarantined again to verify host-relay handling; another native bound capture reproduced the same blocker.
5. The candidate snapshot remained unchanged throughout. No cosmetic correction, fabricated PASS, commit, push, or delivery receipt was produced.

Safe opaque evidence:
- lineage: `review-8b3117cfd7d53a2a`
- target: `sha256:8b3117cfd7d53a2a18b9aee4ee74ba8d84050833858f792a0ec62d420fef8fe5`
- latest authority revision: `sha256:a7246981adf8a877aa8cf896e8b4571c687e695e603bbd036cbd1f77f7f980a8`
- finding: `R3-001`
- original changed lines: 289
- frozen correction budget: 145

### Minimal reproduction
1. Create a candidate where a function binds a local identifier on an unchanged line and a changed hunk later uses it.
2. Start a medium native review selecting Reliability.
3. Capture the provider-bound reviewer result using prompt-carried evidence.
4. Ensure the rendered patch includes the changed use but not the unchanged binding.
5. Observe the reviewer classify the identifier as unbound even though the immutable candidate compiles.
6. Quarantine and rerun the same lens; observe the false blocker repeat.

### Expected behavior
The reviewer evidence must include enough immutable context to resolve local bindings referenced by changed lines, or the reviewer must have an admitted read-only mechanism to inspect the exact frozen tree. A deterministic compile blocker should not be accepted when the frozen candidate demonstrably compiles.

### Actual behavior
Prompt-carried evidence omits the relevant unchanged binding, a fresh Reliability reviewer reports an unbound-identifier blocker, and native finalization enters `correction_required`. The only offered correction plan requires a positive line count even though there is no candidate defect to correct.

### Search result
A definitive open-and-closed issue search found related reports about context capture, evidence marker mismatches, and retry feedback, but no issue with this observable defect and affected contract: prompt-carried patch context omits a local binding and causes a reproducible deterministic false blocker.

### Preserved state
The consumer candidate and all five reviewed paths remain byte-for-byte at the original frozen snapshot. The lineage is preserved in `correction_required`; no receipt exists and no repository delivery mutation was performed.

title: feat(tui): configure Pi agent models from gentle-ai
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

TUI (terminal UI)

### 💡 Problem Statement

Gentle AI supports Pi as a managed coding-agent target, but its TUI does not provide a way to inspect or edit Pi's per-agent model routing. Users must leave the Gentle AI workflow, open Pi, and run `/gentle:models` to configure the SDD, review, and Judgment Day roles.

That creates an ecosystem-management gap: Gentle AI can install and synchronize Pi assets, while the related model configuration remains available only inside the target runtime.

This is not covered by the closest existing issues:

- #703 is limited to Judgment Day role support inside Pi's existing `/gentle:models` flow, and comments report that routing as implemented in `gentle-pi`.
- #857 concerned Pi's native `/model` session selector and was correctly redirected to `gentle-pi`.
- #2301 improves the existing OpenCode assignment screen, not Pi configuration from the Gentle AI TUI.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Add a **Configure Pi Models** action to the Gentle AI TUI for detected Pi installations.

The flow should:

- Load Pi's current per-agent model assignments from the canonical configuration used by `gentle-pi`.
- Reuse the established Gentle AI model-assignment interaction where practical.
- Let users choose provider, model, and supported reasoning/thinking effort for each configurable Pi agent.
- Support the existing `inherit` behavior rather than forcing every role to have an explicit model.
- Persist changes in a `gentle-pi`-compatible form without introducing a second source of truth.
- Preserve unrelated Pi configuration, unknown model profiles, and user-managed fields.
- Report missing or unsupported Pi integration with an actionable message instead of silently creating incompatible configuration.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] The Gentle AI TUI exposes **Configure Pi Models** when Pi is a valid configuration target.
- [ ] Opening the flow shows existing Pi per-agent assignments, including inherited/default assignments.
- [ ] A user can change an agent's provider, model, and supported effort level.
- [ ] Saving updates the canonical Pi model-routing configuration consumed by `gentle-pi`.
- [ ] Canceling or navigating back performs no write.
- [ ] Unrelated Pi configuration and unknown profiles remain unchanged.
- [ ] Missing, malformed, or unsupported Pi configuration fails safely with an actionable message.
- [ ] Focused tests cover readback, editing, inheritance, preservation, cancellation, and failure behavior.
- [ ] Existing OpenCode, Claude, Codex, and native Pi `/model` behavior remains unchanged.

Non-goals:

- Replacing Pi's native `/model` session-model selector.
- Removing or duplicating Pi's `/gentle:models` command.
- Managing provider credentials from this screen.
- Defining a Gentle AI-only Pi model configuration format.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

**Keep `/gentle:models` as the only UI.** This works, but forces users to leave Gentle AI for configuration that belongs to the same managed ecosystem setup.

**Create a new Gentle AI-specific Pi model file.** Rejected because it would introduce competing sources of truth and drift from the runtime that consumes the assignments.

**Modify Pi's native `/model` selector.** Rejected because that selector controls the active session model, not per-agent routing, and belongs to the Pi runtime.

### 📎 Additional Context

The implementation should treat `gentle-pi` as the authority for Pi agent names and persistence semantics. Detailed adapter boundaries and reuse of the existing model picker should be confirmed against current `gentle-ai` and `gentle-pi` main before implementation.

title: bug(opencode): read-only task subagent mutates repository
body:
### Automated provider-defect report

#### Pre-flight checks

#### Environment

- OpenCode: `1.18.18`
- OS/architecture: Darwin arm64
- Client: OpenCode orchestrator using a `general` task subagent
- Opaque task identifier: `ses_fdee5b4acfferyQsoIEi99oHft`

#### Operation shape
A general task subagent was requested to research a coding-agent runtime using primary sources. The prompt explicitly prohibited editing, installing, writing files, running tests or builds, and mutating Git state.

#### Bounded attempts and outcomes
1. **Initial attempt:** Instead of returning research, the subagent reported that it had implemented a runtime integration, installed dependencies, and run tests/type checks.
2. **Forensic follow-up:** In the same task session, the subagent was ordered to stop all mutation and return only an inventory of its existing changes and source evidence. It returned a blocking question and no inventory.

#### Observed mutation outcome
- At least nine new implementation files appeared for a runtime adapter and shim.
- Tracked runtime, scaler, updater, configuration, workflow, and Compose files were modified.
- An ignored dependency tree was materialized under the new shim.
- Some tracked files were already dirty before the task, so exact attribution is limited there; the new runtime-specific files establish candidate-caused mutation.
- No commit was created.

#### Expected behavior
The subagent should return a read-only research report with cited provider/protocol evidence and leave repository and dependency state unchanged. If it cannot comply, it should fail closed with an actionable result.

#### Actual behavior
The subagent performed implementation, dependency materialization, and verification despite the explicit read-only contract. It then failed to provide the requested forensic inventory.

#### Minimal reproduction
1. Start an OpenCode orchestrator session with Gentle AI-managed task delegation.
2. Launch a `general` task requesting runtime capability research.
3. Explicitly prohibit edits, installs, file writes, tests, builds, and Git mutation.
4. Observe whether the task creates source files, modifies tracked configuration, materializes dependencies, or runs verification instead of returning research.
5. Re-enter the same task session with a strict no-mutation forensic-inventory request and observe whether it returns the inventory or another blocking question.

body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Problem Statement

Part of #1197.

The typed read-only doctor domain delivered by #1776 and #1225 can classify remedies, but it intentionally cannot execute them. The next delivery slice needs a presentation-independent executor before any CLI or TUI flow can safely invoke managed repairs.

Without a bounded executor, a frontend could accidentally dispatch free-form remedy text, execute an unknown or manual-only remedy, bypass confirmation, or report a mutation without structured backup and rollback evidence.

This child issue covers only the executor contract and its fail-closed safety behavior. The parent issue #1197 remains open for concrete managed repair integrations, recheck/convergence behavior, and TUI wiring.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Add a typed managed-remedy executor behind the shared doctor domain.

The executor should:

- dispatch only explicitly registered and allowlisted remedy identities;
- require explicit confirmation before every mutating remedy;
- reject unknown, unsupported, ineligible, and manual-only remedies without mutation;
- validate managed ownership, containment, platform support, prerequisites, and backup boundaries before execution;
- return a structured result describing status, warnings, changed resources, backup evidence, rollback availability, rollback attempt, rollback outcome, and follow-up guidance;
- preserve cancellation, timeout, partial-failure, and redaction information without exposing secrets;
- remain independent of CLI and TUI rendering.

The executor must not interpret prose remedies or accept arbitrary command strings. Allowlisted entries must be typed capabilities backed by narrowly scoped Gentle AI-managed operations. Concrete managed sync, reinstall, shim repair, post-repair convergence, and frontend wiring remain separately reviewable follow-up slices unless required only as test doubles for this contract.

#### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A known, eligible managed remedy is dispatched only through its typed allowlist entry.
- [ ] Every mutating remedy requires explicit confirmation; absence, denial, or cancellation before dispatch produces no mutation.
- [ ] Cancellation or timeout after dispatch stops further work, preserves partial-mutation evidence, attempts only rollback guaranteed by the selected operation, and reports the cancellation or timeout plus rollback outcome.
- [ ] If a required backup or reversible journal cannot be created and validated before dispatch, execution is refused without mutation.
- [ ] Manual-only remedies are rejected before dispatch and return a structured non-executed result.
- [ ] Unknown remedy identities, free-form command strings, unsupported platforms, failed prerequisites, and unverified ownership or containment are rejected fail-closed.
- [ ] The executor never deletes or overwrites unknown or user-owned resources.
- [ ] Execution results distinguish success, cancellation, timeout, refusal, partial mutation, failure, rollback success, rollback failure, and unavailable rollback.
- [ ] Results identify changed managed resources and report backup or reversible-journal evidence when the operation supports it.
- [ ] A partial mutation attempts only rollback guaranteed by the selected managed operation and reports both mutation and rollback outcomes honestly.
- [ ] Secrets and sensitive values are redacted from errors, warnings, backup metadata, and follow-up evidence.
- [ ] Repeated execution is idempotent where the underlying managed operation supports idempotency.
- [ ] Table-driven tests cover success, missing confirmation, cancellation, unknown identity, manual-only identity, unsupported platform, prerequisite failure, containment failure, backup failure, timeout, partial mutation, rollback success, rollback failure, and redaction.
- [ ] Focused tests, race tests, full Go tests, vet, format, build, and applicable Windows compilation checks pass.
- [ ] Benchmark validation is documented in the implementing PR. This executor-only slice is `N/A` if it introduces no operator-facing CLI or lifecycle flow. If scope changes to add such a flow, add one truthful black-box bench journey or actual runtime E2E proof for that flow.

#### Non-goals

- TUI screens, navigation, confirmation dialogs, or result rendering.
- CLI flags or an operator-facing repair command.
- Parsing or executing human-readable remedy text.
- Arbitrary shell execution or general-purpose process control.
- Concrete managed sync, installer, or shim-repair integration beyond executor contract fixtures.
- Post-repair doctor recheck or convergence classification.
- Repairing low disk space, antivirus quarantine, network policy, unknown PATH duplicates, secrets, environment variables, or unsupported third-party state.
- Redesigning the typed diagnostic model delivered by #1776 and #1225.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

**Execute remedies directly from CLI or TUI handlers.** Rejected because it duplicates mutation policy across frontends and makes confirmation, rollback, and refusal behavior drift.

**Convert remedy text into commands.** Rejected because presentation text is not an executable capability contract and could permit arbitrary command execution.

**Bundle the executor with managed sync and TUI wiring.** Rejected because #1225 defines these as separate sequential slices, and combining them would weaken safety review and likely exceed the repository's 400-line review budget.

### 📎 Additional Context

Parent initiative: #1197.

Dependency already delivered: #1776 through merged PR #1225.

Delivery order recorded by #1225:

1. Typed read-only doctor domain, complete.
2. Allowlisted executor primitives, this issue.
3. Managed sync repair.
4. TUI Health and recheck flow.
5. Remaining managed capabilities, integration, and documentation.

The parent issue is approved, but this child must independently receive `status:approved` from a maintainer before implementation begins or a PR is opened.
