title: feat(skills): a capability that decides whether a verified observation should change a future authority
body:
## Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. The nearest prior art is #839 (verification of stale Engram observations), #1703 (capture of `Key Learnings` into Engram), and #2415 / #3471 (the refusal ratchet itself). None decides whether a verified observation should change a future authority. The full search list is under Additional Context.
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`.

## 🔍 Affected Area

Catalog/Steps: the skill set.

## 💡 Problem Statement

Three incidents from my own work on this repository share one shape: a verified observation existed, was written down, and nothing decided whether it should change a future authority. The note stayed narrative and the procedure kept making the same decision implicitly.

**1. A stale local `origin/main` anchored a candidate to a past reality. This one is publicly verifiable here.**

I opened #3474 on 2026-08-19 asserting that `a245f260` was the current `main` tip. #3472 had merged as `35deba32` at `09:44:54Z`, 76 minutes before the issue was published at `11:01:12Z`. Candidate, gate and tree were internally consistent, and all of them measured the same wrong tree, so no check disagreed with any other. I published a self-correction on that issue withdrawing the clause (comment `5346401489`, `2026-08-19T18:32:40Z`).

```bash
gh api repos/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/3474 --jq '{created_at, body}'
gh pr view 3472 --repo Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai --json mergedAt,mergeCommit
gh api repos/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/3474/comments \
  --jq '.[] | select(.id == 5346401489) | {id, created_at, author: .user.login, body}'
```

In my clone, `origin/main` stayed at `a245f260` for 25h13m before the next fetch. **From here on, this incident is no longer publicly verifiable:** the reflog figure, the note and the script are local, and I state them as reported facts. The note "re-read the network tip before publishing a commit-bound figure" already existed before that issue was written, and nothing had turned it into a check. Afterwards it became a script that queries the network tip and fails explicitly when the object is absent locally, which is exactly the promotion this issue is about, done by hand, once, after the cost.

**Incidents 2 and 3 come from my own working record and cannot be checked from outside.** I state them as reported facts, not as evidence:

- A burn-in log recorded that three runs had failed on a gate *name*, not on a decision. Four days later the operating procedure still pinned the wrong gate.
- A `grep` with a `^` anchor silently dropped four indented `--- SKIP` lines and produced a false "all green" claim that was handed downstream as measured fact. The rule covering exactly this, that a filtered read is not a read, already existed in another document. The procedure that took the measurement had never absorbed it.

**This repository already values what that promotion produces.** Three frozen baselines are enforced today: `.deadcode-baseline.txt` (249 lines, `scripts/deadcode-ratchet.sh`, run inside the required `Unit Tests` job), `.refusal-ratchet-baseline.txt` (1533 lines, `internal/cli/refusal_resolution_ratchet_test.go`) and `.guard-population-baseline.txt` (10 declarations, `internal/cli/guard_population_test.go`). The CI comment above the first names the observation that produced it, at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:150-152`:

> It exists because InstallCommandsForDep survived with no callers while the install docs described the dependency remediation it would have performed.

That is the move. It happened because someone recognised the right note at the right moment.

**What exists today, and the edge each one stops at.** Checked against `35deba3` and the installed skill set:

| Capability | What it does | Where it stops |
|---|---|---|
| Engram | Captures decisions, bugfixes and discoveries; SDD phases close with `Key Learnings` for passive capture (`internal/assets/skills/_shared/sdd-phase-common.md:117`) | Storage and recall. `internal/assets/engram/protocol.md:67` already requires verifying a `needs_review` memory against current evidence; it says nothing about what is owed to one that survives that check |
| RDD | Binds evidence, receipts and review authority to an existing candidate (`skills/rdd-defect-workflow/SKILL.md`) | The cited workflow does not define how a selected observation becomes a proposed future authority |
| Delivery gates | Validate an existing receipt or authorization at a delivery boundary | They do not decide that a new safeguard is owed |
| `gentle-ai-bench` | Proves driven journey execution rather than accepting ordinary `go test` as equivalent | It does not decide whether an observation should become a journey |
| `skill-improver` | Audits and refactors an existing `SKILL.md` against `docs/skill-style-guide.md` | Takes the target skill as given; does not select which authority an observation belongs to |
| `systemic-issue-triage` | Classifies issues by root class and closes them against named tests | Its input is an issue, not an observation produced during work |

The gap is the step between capture and enforcement: deciding, on the record, whether a verified observation is owed a change to a future authority, and to which one.

## 📦 Proposed Solution

One on-demand skill. No CLI, no manager, no inventory, no cross-client surface. It is invoked explicitly with one selected and already verified observation, then emits a decision with its proof. It does not scan Engram or automatically close the capture-to-enforcement loop.

Its defining constraint, and what makes it falsifiable: **no observation is promoted unless the proposed change is shown to have caught or prevented the original incident.** For incident 1 that check is concrete: the anchoring script must fail against the stale local ref that existed at publication time. An observation whose proposed change cannot be shown to catch its own incident is not promoted.

Proof is specific to the destination:

| Destination | Required counterfactual proof |
|---|---|
| Deterministic test or ratchet | A negative control fails without the safeguard and passes with it, or an equivalent controlled mutation |
| Bench journey | A pinned journey reproduces the incident and passes only under driven execution |
| Skill or procedure | A fresh-context replay of the pinned input is evaluated without and with the canonical rule |
| Duplicate-authority deletion | A consumer and reference sweep proves the surviving authority is the one actually used |

Documentation alone is not promoted unless it is paired with a consumer check.

The output is one auditable chain: `observation → evidence → decision → authority → proof`.

The decision resolves to one of six dispositions: correct an existing authority, add a deterministic ratchet or test, add a bench journey, delete a duplicate authority, keep the observation unpromoted, or block on insufficient evidence. "Keep unpromoted" is a final reviewed decision that no authority change is warranted. "Block" is provisional and must name the missing evidence, its owner and the retry condition. Two of the six recommend no authority change. All six are advisory: the skill does not mutate authority by itself.

Bounds: it does not modify code, skills or procedures on its own; it does not create a new rule when a canonical authority can absorb it; memory is a hypothesis and never an authority; it does not replace `skill-improver`, `systemic-issue-triage`, RDD or bench, it decides which of them an observation is routed to, if any.

Where the file would live is not part of this request. #3490 asks you to settle `skills/` versus `internal/assets/skills/` for contributed skills, and this proposal takes whatever you decide there. No `SKILL.md` is attached: this issue asks only whether the capability is wanted, and implementation follows approval.

## 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- **Keep it manual.** This is the status quo, and it is what produced the three incidents above. It works whenever someone remembers the right note at the right moment.
- **Extend `skill-improver`.** It improves a skill that has already been chosen. The choosing is the missing step, and folding a routing decision into it would widen a skill that currently has a clean scope.
- **Extend `systemic-issue-triage`.** Its input is an issue and its output is a fix cluster. Most of these observations never become issues.
- **Write it as documentation.** A written convention is precisely what already existed in incidents 2 and 3: correct in both cases, and inert in both cases.

## 📎 Additional Context

Prior public step: discussion #3488 (written in Spanish), opened by me on 2026-08-19 in Ideas, which closes with an offer to open this scoped request. As checked on 2026-08-19, it shows 1 upvote, which is my own, and has 0 comments and 0 reactions, so it records the idea and establishes nothing about demand from anyone else.

| Prior art | Boundary |
|---|---|
| #839 | Verifies whether a stale Engram observation may be relied on; it does not route a surviving observation to a future authority |
| #1703 | Captures `Key Learnings` into Engram |
| #2415 / #3471 | Enforce refusal ratchets that already exist |
| #3490 | Asks where contributed skills should live; it does not define this capability |

`counterfactual` appears in four files at `35deba3`, all under `openspec/`, and in a different sense (process ordering, `openspec/specs/rdd-transport-capability/spec.md:27`). It appears zero times under `skills/`, `internal/assets/skills/` and `docs/`.

Duplicate search run through `gh search issues --repo Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai`: `ratchet in:title`, `observation in:title`, `learning in:title`, and free text for `observation ratchet`, `promote learning skill`, `lesson learned skill`, `engram observation rule` and `counterfactual`.

### Triage

This was opened through the API, so the form's labels were not applied. It needs `enhancement` and `status:needs-review` to enter the normal review path.

title: docs(contributing): add a "Contributing a Skill" section built from decisions already made in closures
body:
## Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

## 🔍 Affected Area

Documentation

## 💡 Problem Statement

`CONTRIBUTING.md` at `35deba3` contains **zero** occurrences of "skill", case-insensitive.

The channel is not idle. Eight community pull requests have proposed a new named skill:

| PR | Author | Result |
|---|---|---|
| [#234](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/234) | @jorgehara | closed by the author, replaced by #238 |
| [#238](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/238) | @jorgehara | closed: too broad without a product decision |
| [#313](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/313) | @watsonctl | closed: no approved issue, and no concrete integration point |
| [#601](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/601) | @rortizs | closed: no linked issue carrying `status:approved` |
| [#714](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/714) | @orisepu | closed: no approved issue to review scope against |
| [#719](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/719) | @D4rkGh057 | closed: this importer belongs outside core |
| [#1171](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/1171) | @ardelperal | **merged** |
| [#2042](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/2042) | @Velkez | open; `type:feature` only, no `status:*` label yet |

Three closed skill *issues* carry stated reasons that this section reuses: [#451](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/451), [#764](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/764) and [#965](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/965).

All 59 pull requests the title search below returns were adjudicated by file list rather than by hand: twelve add at least one new `*/SKILL.md`, and the eight above are the community proposals among them. Of the remaining four, three are maintainer-side additions and one ([#1016](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/1016)) is a fork's pull request that its own author closed as opened against the wrong repository. That search reads titles only, so treat the table as a floor rather than a census. The merged side is exact: across the full history of `main`, every `*/SKILL.md` addition traces to the maintainer side except `internal/assets/skills/_shared/SKILL.md` (added inside the Kiro PR #283) and `skills/gentle-ai-collab-perfect/SKILL.md` from #1171. The census command below lists every such addition under its commit's author; five distinct names appear, and the `Claude` one is commit `4e0448c5`, which landed directly on `main` with no associated pull request and mirrored four skills already present under `skills/` into `internal/assets/skills/`. One community-authored named skill has landed.

**The criteria that decided all of this already exist, and they are sound.** They are just written one at a time, inside the closure comment of the individual pull request or issue that already closed, where finding them means already knowing which thread to open.

`docs/skill-style-guide.md` covers the other half of the problem well: structure, frontmatter, token budget, quality gates. It says nothing about whether a skill belongs in core. `git grep -l skill-style-guide 35deba3` returns 13 paths; excluding test files and goldens, seven remain, and all seven point inward: two bundled skills that name it as normative, `internal/assets/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md:22` ("as the normative source") and `internal/assets/skills/skill-improver/SKILL.md:16` ("the normative style contract"); a third, `internal/assets/skills/skill-registry/SKILL.md:50`, which lists it once as a reference ("how skills should be authored before indexing") and nothing stronger; `docs/skill-registry.md:102` inside a "Skill Improvement Flow" text diagram describing what `skill-improver` audits against; and three OpenSpec change records. `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `README.md`, `docs/community-roadmap.md` and `AGENTS.md` carry zero references to it.

## 📦 Proposed Solution

Add a short `## Contributing a Skill` section to `CONTRIBUTING.md`. **No new policy, with one marked exception.** Every line traces to a decision already written, or to the one merged case — except item 3, which asks you for a decision that does not exist yet and is labelled as such.

**1. The issue comes first, and waiting is normal.**
#601 states the rule most plainly and names its authority: *"Per CONTRIBUTING.md, every PR needs an issue linked with `status:approved` before it can be reviewed — and this PR doesn't satisfy that gate (the linked issue doesn't exist, is closed, or isn't approved)."* It then gives the way back in three steps: *"1. Open (or find) an issue describing the change 2. Wait for a maintainer to apply `status:approved` 3. Reopen this PR or open a new one with `Closes #<issue>` in the body"*. That citation is accurate — `status:approved` appears four times in `CONTRIBUTING.md` at `35deba3` — which is also why the skill-specific half of the answer is expected there, and is not there yet.

#1171 is the working example, and its timing is the useful part:

| Event | Timestamp (UTC) |
|---|---|
| Issue #1170 opened | `2026-07-12T09:00:57Z` |
| PR #1171 opened | `2026-07-12T09:01:33Z` |
| `status:approved` applied to #1170 | `2026-07-19T18:33:40Z` |
| PR #1171 merged | `2026-07-19T18:34:18Z` |

Approval arrived seven days after the PR, and the merge followed it by 38 seconds. The PR body states "Issue-first workflow honoured". A contributor reading this knows an unlabelled PR is a queue position, not a verdict.

What that issue has to carry is also already written. #313 gives it in three parts: *"a focused issue that explains the user problem, the exact Gentle AI surface it changes, and the smallest useful slice."* Two of the three closed issues named above add the evidence bar. #965: *"This is a convention-as-skill proposal with no demonstrated demand or failure case. Re-open with concrete evidence."* #451: *"they earn their place by being curated, not scanned"*, and if the gap is in an existing component, *"open a focused issue against `sdd-init` and we'll look at it there."*

**2. What reads as too broad, and the stated alternative.** From #238: *"too broad for the current repo without a product decision on whether this belongs in Gentle AI core"*, and *"the next step should be a design issue that explains the supported workflow, ownership, security expectations, and the smallest skill-only slice."* #313 applies the same test to a skill and names what was missing: *"a broad enterprise/RAG workflow without an approved issue or a concrete integration point in the current product."* The same shape appears on the skills-adjacent feature #20 (a discovery TUI, not a skill file): *"the scope is too large for what it solves, and it has integration conflicts with the current welcome menu that would take significant work to resolve."* The alternative offered there was equally concrete: a standalone command instead of a TUI screen.

Scale is measurable on its own: #601 is the largest of the eight at 65 files and ten new skills. Its stated closure reason is the missing approved issue, not its size. On the issue side, #764 proposed seven skills at once, and its closure states the test and the alternative together: *"A bundle of seven imported skills is scope-breaking as one issue and overlaps existing skills and CodeGraph. If one specific skill has real demand, file it individually with the problem it solves."* The alternative is one skill per issue, filed with the problem it solves.

**3. Where the file goes.** This is the one point the section cannot fill in without you. Two locations exist on `main`: `skills/` (14 files) and `internal/assets/skills/` (44 files). The merged community skill went to `skills/gentle-ai-collab-perfect/SKILL.md` and is still there; #313 targeted `skills/`, #714 targeted `internal/assets/skills/`, and #601 wrote every one of its ten skills into both. This report asserts nothing about which is canonical for an incoming contribution. It is your call, and one sentence from you closes it permanently.

The section would also link `docs/skill-style-guide.md`, which none of the four contributor-facing documents named above currently reference.

## 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- **Leave it in the closure comments.** They are already accurate. The cost is that each one is read by exactly one person, after the work is done.
- **Put it in `docs/skill-style-guide.md` instead.** That file is about how a skill is written, not whether it is accepted, and none of those four documents link to it. Scope criteria there would be equally unfindable.
- **Add a skill or tooling that enforces this.** Explicitly rejected as a proposal here. The gap is that decisions already made are not written down in one place, not that anything needs automating.

## 📎 Additional Context

Adjacent, not duplicate: [#3447](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/3447) (`docs: add Hermes knowledge-layer section in CONTRIBUTING.md`, @ardelperal, open) adds a different section to `CONTRIBUTING.md`, plus a one-line edit to one README table row, closing #966. This proposal follows its shape deliberately: issue first, one narrow section, every claim traceable to a source. If both land, the two sections do not overlap.

Commands behind the figures. The six `git` lines are pinned to `35deba3`; the two `gh` entries are live and returned these counts on 2026-08-19:

```
git show 35deba3:CONTRIBUTING.md | grep -ic skill                      # 0
git show 35deba3:CONTRIBUTING.md | grep -c status:approved             # 4
git ls-tree -r --name-only 35deba3 skills/ | wc -l                     # 14
git ls-tree -r --name-only 35deba3 internal/assets/skills/ | wc -l     # 44
git grep -l skill-style-guide 35deba3 | wc -l                          # 13
git log 35deba3 --diff-filter=A --format='%an' --name-only -- '*/SKILL.md'  # every addition, by author
gh search prs --repo Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai "skill in:title" --limit 100   # 59

# every PR in that search that adds at least one new SKILL.md          # 12 PRs
gh search prs --repo Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai "skill in:title" --limit 100 \
  --json number --jq '.[].number' | while read n; do
  c=$(gh api "repos/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pulls/$n/files?per_page=100" --paginate \
    --jq '.[]|select(.status=="added")|.filename' | grep -c 'SKILL\.md$')
  [ "$c" != "0" ] && echo "$n $c"
done
```

**Triage request:** this issue was created through the API, so `feature_request.yml` did not apply its labels. It needs `enhancement` and `status:needs-review`, plus `status:approved` if the section is worth writing. I am happy to open the PR once it is approved, or to leave it for someone else.

title: feat(review): add immutable receipt-review transport adapter for Antigravity
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 💡 Feature / Proposal Summary

Add support for Google Antigravity (`agy` / Antigravity IDE) as an eligible runtime for immutable receipt-review (RDD) transport in Gentle-AI (`gentle-ai review start`, `capture-result`, `finalize`, `validate`).

### 📌 Context & Motivation

Issue #2209 established a strict capability boundary narrowing native immutable RDD receipt review to `claude-code`, `opencode`, and `codex` (#2208), while gating all other built-in runtimes with `immutable_review_transport_unsupported` (#2207).

With recent releases of Google Antigravity (v1.1.15+ / Antigravity 2.0), the runtime has matured significantly:
1. Native dynamic subagent definitions and invocations (`define_subagent`, `invoke_subagent`, `manage_subagents`) are supported.
2. Bounded, non-interactive execution modes (`agy --print` with directory scoping) are available.
3. Skill discovery, structured prompts, and deterministic execution allow Antigravity to coordinate complex review and verification flows.

Adding an Antigravity immutable review transport adapter would enable developers and workspaces leveraging Antigravity to fully participate in the Receipt-Driven Development lifecycle.

### 📐 Proposed Design

1. **Review Transport Adapter (`internal/agents/` and `internal/cli/review_next_transition.go`):**
   - Implement an immutable review transport strategy for Antigravity matching the evidence-binding contract used by Claude Code and OpenCode.
   - Map Antigravity runtime identity to allow negotiated `gentle-ai review status` calls.
2. **Reviewer & Lens Execution:**
   - Coordinate lens reviews using dynamically defined subagents or non-interactive passes.
   - Capture immutable results and verification evidence bound to the candidate snapshot.
3. **Receipt Validation:**
   - Support Antigravity in `gentle-ai review validate --gate=pre-commit` and delivery gates.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- Keeping Antigravity as a TierFull / SDD-only runtime without RDD support.
- Relying on external provider models or switching to Claude Code / Codex for all review and delivery verification.

### 📋 Affected Area

Review Lifecycle / RDD (`internal/cli/`, `internal/agents/`)

title: fix(antigravity): align global MCP configuration path with ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

Gentle-AI currently synchronizes custom MCP configurations for Antigravity into `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/mcp_config.json`. 

However, according to the official Google Antigravity documentation ([Antigravity MCP Docs](https://antigravity.google/docs/mcp/) and [Antigravity CLI MCP Docs](https://antigravity.google/docs/cli/mcp/)), Antigravity CLI and IDE discover global MCP server definitions from `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json` (and workspace-local server definitions from `.agents/mcp_config.json`).

Because of this path mismatch, the Antigravity runtime never loads or discovers MCP servers managed by Gentle-AI (such as `engram` and `context7`), resulting in runtime errors when attempting to call memory or documentation tools (`invalid tool call error (invalid_args) tool mem_search is not enabled for server engram`).

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Install/sync Gentle-AI with the Antigravity agent and Engram enabled (`gentle-ai install --agent antigravity --component engram` or `gentle-ai sync`).
2. Run `gentle-ai doctor` — notice that it passes the initialize handshake against `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/mcp_config.json`.
3. Launch an Antigravity CLI session (`agy`) or Antigravity IDE and inspect available MCP tools.
4. Observe that only MCP servers configured in `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json` (e.g. `codegraph`) are loaded. `engram` and `context7` are missing.
5. Manually creating or copying the configuration into `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json` or workspace `.agents/mcp_config.json` immediately makes Antigravity recognize and attempt connections to `engram`.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Gentle-AI's installation and sync adapters (`internal/agents/`) should write/merge global MCP server definitions into `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json` (the official global MCP path for Antigravity) so that the runtime discovers and loads them automatically.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Configuration is written to `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/mcp_config.json`, which is ignored by the Antigravity runtime. `gentle-ai doctor` checks this unused path and falsely reports healthy reachability, while the agent in runtime cannot access any MCP tools.

### Gentle AI Version

gentle-ai 2.4.0

### Operating System

macOS (Apple Silicon) / Linux / Windows

### AI Agent / Client

Antigravity (`agy` 1.1.15+ / Antigravity IDE 2.0+)

### 📋 Affected Area

Agent Adapters (`internal/agents/`), MCP Component (`internal/components/`)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```
invalid tool call error (invalid_args) tool mem_search is not enabled for server engram
```

### Additional Context

Official documentation excerpt from [https://antigravity.google/docs/mcp/](https://antigravity.google/docs/mcp/):
> *The configuration file is located globally at `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json` (or locally in your workspace under `.agents/mcp_config.json`).*

title: bug(upgrade): source builds can never self-update — self-upgrade routing checks the platform but not whether the running build has a trust anchor
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I searched open and closed issues for this specific routing behavior. The closest reports are #2903 (trust-anchor failure leaving a *partial* managed-plugin update), #3141 (GGA `vdev` binary unmanageable by upgrade), #2087 (beta-channel `go install` target malformed on Windows) and #724 (decoupled auto-update pipeline for Windows). None of them describe the routing rule below, so this is filed as a distinct report.
- [x] I understand that PRs require maintainer approval before implementation.

### Bug Description

A Gentle AI installed with the documented `go install` method can never self-update. `gentle-ai update` fails on every attempt with `authenticate release: release trust anchor unavailable`, and there is no recovery route in the message.

This is not an intermittent failure. It is deterministic and permanent for the affected installation, because the check that fails can never succeed for a build produced this way.

This report records observed behavior plus the source references that appear to explain it. It does not assert a confirmed root cause.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Gentle AI from source on Linux, e.g. `install.sh --method go`, `install.sh --channel beta` (which supports only `go`), or `go install github.com/gentleman-programming/gentle-ai/v2/cmd/gentle-ai@latest`.
2. Wait for any newer stable release to be published.
3. Run `gentle-ai update`.
4. Observe the failure. Repeat — the result never changes.

### Expected Behavior

One of the following:

- **Preferred:** when the running build carries no trust anchor, Go is on PATH, and the tool declares a `GoImportPath`, route the self-upgrade to `go install <importPath>@<version>` — exactly the routing Windows already uses. The trust anchor moves to the Go checksum database rather than being absent, which is the same reasoning already documented for the Windows path.
- **Minimum:** fail with an actionable, privacy-safe message that names the supported upgrade command for a source build (`go install …@latest`) instead of reporting a missing trust anchor with no exit.

### Actual Behavior

- `gentle-ai update` fails with `authenticate release: release trust anchor unavailable`.
- The binary is never upgraded.
- The message suggests a missing trust anchor, which reads as a recoverable or restorable condition. For a source build it is not: no user action can restore it.
- Users following the error toward a signed release find none for Windows, since Windows binary distribution and Scoop are on hold pending Authenticode signing.

### Source References

These are the two pieces that appear to combine into the behavior.

`internal/update/upgrade/download.go` — the trust anchor is injected only at release build time, and source builds deliberately fail closed:

> `releaseMinisignPublicKeys` is the production trust-anchor injection point. GoReleaser sets it with `-X …upgrade.releaseMinisignPublicKeys=${MINISIGN_PUBLIC_KEYS}` … Source and test builds deliberately retain UNSET and fail closed if their binary updater is invoked.

`internal/update/upgrade/executor.go` — `gentleAISelfUpgradeMethod` decides the method from the platform only, never from whether the running build actually has an anchor:

```go
func gentleAISelfUpgradeMethod(tool update.ToolInfo, profile system.PlatformProfile) update.InstallMethod {
	if profile.OS == "windows" && profile.GoAvailable && tool.GoImportPath != "" {
		return update.InstallGoInstall
	}
	return update.InstallBinary
}
```

A source build on Linux or macOS therefore always routes to `InstallBinary`, and `InstallBinary` can never authenticate for that build. The two behaviors are individually intentional; the gap appears to be that neither side checks the other.

### Who This Affects

- Linux/macOS users who installed with `--method go`, which `install.sh --help` documents as a supported method.
- Anyone on `--channel beta`, which supports only `go`.
- Every Windows user, because `install.ps1` currently refuses the binary method entirely and directs users to `go install` while Windows distribution is on hold. Windows self-upgrade is routed to go-install and works; the failure appears when such a build runs on Linux, e.g. under WSL.

### Environment

- Gentle AI: 2.3.0 and 2.4.0, both built with `go install`
- Go: 1.26.5
- OS: Windows 11 with WSL2 (Ubuntu 24.04), linux/amd64 build
- Client: Claude Code

### Logs / Error Output

```text
✗  gentle-ai
   authenticate release: release trust anchor unavailable
```

### Bounded Outcome and Preserved State

- Upgrade attempts: repeated across 2.3.0 and 2.4.0; identical result each time.
- Binary outcome: unchanged in every attempt.
- Workaround used: running `go install …@latest` directly, which upgrades correctly and is still verified against the Go checksum database.
- No project files or source contents were modified while diagnosing this.

### Duplicate Search

Open and closed issues were searched for `trust anchor`, `minisign`, `source build update`, `go install self-update`, `releaseMinisignPublicKeys UNSET`, and `gentleAISelfUpgradeMethod`. #2903 reports the same error string but describes a partial managed-plugin update and asks for atomic rollback; it does not cover source-build routing, though this may be its underlying cause. No equivalent report was found.

title: ci(policy): required product-behaviour checks never revalidate against the branch tip, so two green PRs can land a red main
body:
## Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I searched open and closed issues for merge queue, `merge_group`, strict
  required status checks, stale bases, and "branch up to date". The phenomenon
  itself is already diagnosed in #3063 and #3420. The adjacent open work is
  #3353, #1853, and #2203. This report is about the merge-policy composition
  that allows the recurrence, which none of those covers; the adjacency is
  spelled out under Additional Context.
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have
  `status:approved`.

## 📝 Bug Description

The required status checks that exercise product behaviour are computed against
the pull request head in isolation and are never revalidated against the branch
tip before the merge lands. Two pull requests that are each green can therefore
produce a red `main` when both merge. This has now happened at least twice.

Two independent facts compose into the gap.

**1. No required check ever exercises the merged product behaviour.**

Every `actions/checkout` step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` pins the checkout to
the pull request head:

```yaml
- name: Checkout exact event candidate
  uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd  # v5.0.1
  with:
    repository: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name || github.repository }}
    ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
```

There are 7 such steps, at lines 23, 47, 162, 212, 282, 326, 431, all named
`Checkout exact event candidate` and all carrying that identical `with:` block.
The step name states its intent. The pattern arrived with `09e4b14c` (#1801);
`93e0e42d` (#2191) added the seventh occurrence for the Claude network-none job.

Without an explicit `ref`, `actions/checkout` uses the ref of the triggering
event, which on a `pull_request` event is `refs/pull/N/merge`: the head merged
into the base tip, recomputed by GitHub. That ref exists and is observable, here
on #3465, which is open, so its refs advance on every push and these two values
are a snapshot rather than a stable identifier:

```
$ git ls-remote origin 'refs/pull/3465/*'
17f40c31897ade88d3a837283b1af06a18de4009  refs/pull/3465/head
1e9ef011564ece32c3d8d4cee83d4b332abb22a2  refs/pull/3465/merge

$ git log -1 --format='%H parents=%P' <fetched 1e9ef011>
1e9ef011... parents=a245f260... 17f40c31...
```

`a245f260` is the current `main` tip and `17f40c31` is the current head of
#3465, so the merge ref is exactly those two composed. The override replaces
that merge result with the head commit alone. A merged pull request cannot
stand in for this observation: GitHub keeps `refs/pull/N/head` after a merge but
drops `refs/pull/N/merge`, so the merge ref is only observable while the pull
request is open.

The four required contexts that exercise product behaviour (`Unit Tests`,
`E2E Tests (ubuntu)`, `E2E Tests (arch)`, `E2E Tests (fedora)`) all live in
`ci.yml` and all use that checkout. `ci.yml` contains no `git merge`, no
`git rebase`, no `origin/main` reference and no `fetch-depth`, so nothing
re-integrates the base later in the job. The remaining three required contexts
(`Check Issue Reference`, `Check Issue Has status:approved`,
`Check PR Has type:* Label`) are metadata jobs in `pr-check.yml` that exercise
no product behaviour. `check-issue-approved` and `check-type-label` have no
checkout step and run only inline `github-script`;
`check-issue-reference` does check out, and `require`s
`.github/scripts/parse-linked-issues.cjs` from the workspace, to parse the PR
body. Its `actions/checkout` carries no `with:` block, so it takes the default
ref, the `refs/pull/N/merge` the `ci.yml` steps override; step 4 shows both refs
checked out for the same head, in the two workflow runs that head triggers.

**2. Nothing downstream revalidates before the merge lands.**

Ruleset `13932547`, the ruleset that governs `main` (its condition is
`ref_name.include: ["~ALL"]`), sets `strict_required_status_checks_policy: false`,
contains no `merge_queue` rule and no `pull_request` rule. Its rule types are
exactly `deletion`, `non_fast_forward`, `copilot_code_review`,
`required_status_checks`, `commit_message_pattern`, `branch_name_pattern`.
`GET /repos/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/rules/branches/main` returns those
six rules and nothing else, all sourced from repository ruleset `13932547`, so
no organization ruleset is inherited. Classic branch protection on `main`
reports `enabled: false` with `enforcement_level: off`. `merge_group` appears
nowhere in the repository at `a245f260`, and no workflow declares a
`merge_group:` trigger.

Neither fact is a defect on its own. Together they mean the merged product
behaviour is never exercised by anything that can block a merge.

**This is not a narrow race window.** In the 2026-08-17 instance the required
checks started *after* the conflicting pull request had already merged, and
were green anyway, because the checkout is head-only. Timing was never the
protection.

**Prevalence.** Of the last 200 pull requests merged into `main` ordered by
merge time (2026-08-06 to 2026-08-18), 77 (38.5%) had a base behind the tip at
merge time, measured as the first-parent distance between `baseRefOid` and the
merge commit's first parent. Distribution:

```
1 commit behind : 29
2               : 11
3               :  9
4-8             : 15
16-17           :  3
18-27           :  3
29-33           :  5
54              :  1   (#2927)
197             :  1   (#2193)
```

Every one of those 77 merges landed content whose merged product behaviour no
required check had exercised.

## 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Confirm `ci.yml` never re-integrates the base:

   ```bash
   git show 'origin/main:.github/workflows/ci.yml' | grep -n 'actions/checkout'
   git show 'origin/main:.github/workflows/ci.yml' | grep -c 'pull_request.head.sha'
   git show 'origin/main:.github/workflows/ci.yml' | grep -nE 'git merge|git rebase|origin/main|fetch-depth'
   ```

   Seven checkouts, seven head pins, zero re-integration.

2. Confirm nothing revalidates before merge:

   ```bash
   gh api repos/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/rulesets/13932547
   gh api repos/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/rules/branches/main
   gh api repos/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/branches/main --jq '.protection'
   git grep -I -i merge_group origin/main
   ```

3. Observe the 2026-08-17 instance. #3410 merged at `15:01:26Z` as `fcbbcd6e`,
   adding `TestReviewAbandonOfAPristineLineageIgnoresAnUnrelatedUnloadableApprovedLineage`
   and `TestUnrelatedReceiptDenialNamesTheCandidateSituationNotOtherLineages`.
   #3413 merged at `15:52:37Z` as `0a33077d`. Both share base `a5f238b4`;
   `0a33077d`'s first parent is `9f906881`, two first-parent merges ahead of
   that base (`fcbbcd6e` from #3410 and `9f906881` from #3415):

   ```bash
   gh pr view 3410 --json mergedAt,mergeCommit,baseRefOid
   gh pr view 3413 --json mergedAt,mergeCommit,baseRefOid
   git rev-list --count --first-parent a5f238b4..9f906881   # 2
   ```

4. Observe that #3413's required checks ran after #3410 was already on `main`
   and passed anyway:

   ```bash
   gh api repos/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/commits/672fb7c2/check-runs \
     --jq '["Check Issue Reference","Check PR Has type:* Label","Check Issue Has status:approved",
            "Unit Tests","E2E Tests (ubuntu)","E2E Tests (arch)","E2E Tests (fedora)"] as $required
           | [.check_runs[] | select(.name as $n | $required | index($n))]
           | sort_by(.started_at, .name)[]
           | [.conclusion, .name, .started_at] | @tsv'
   ```

   ```
   success  Check Issue Reference            2026-08-17T15:40:10Z
   success  Check PR Has type:* Label        2026-08-17T15:40:11Z
   success  Check Issue Has status:approved  2026-08-17T15:40:35Z
   success  E2E Tests (arch)                 2026-08-17T15:40:38Z
   success  E2E Tests (ubuntu)               2026-08-17T15:40:38Z
   success  E2E Tests (fedora)               2026-08-17T15:40:39Z
   success  Unit Tests                       2026-08-17T15:40:39Z
   ```

   The `--jq` filter narrows to the seven required contexts; without it the
   endpoint returns 16 check runs, and the nine it drops are not required
   contexts (one of them, `copilot-pull-request-reviewer`, is a `failure`).

   Those seven contexts do not come from one workflow run. The same head
   triggers two `pull_request` runs, both with `run_started_at`
   `2026-08-17T15:40:07Z`: run `32043009048`, workflow `CI`
   (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`), carries `Unit Tests` and the three
   `E2E Tests`; run `32043009099`, workflow `PR Validation`
   (`.github/workflows/pr-check.yml`), carries the three metadata contexts. The
   job logs of each confirm what it checked out:

   ```bash
   gh api repos/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/actions/jobs/95425604457/logs \
   | grep -o 'git checkout --progress --force .*'   # Unit Tests, run 32043009048
   gh api repos/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/actions/jobs/95425545710/logs \
   | grep -o 'git checkout --progress --force .*'   # Check Issue Reference, run 32043009099
   ```

   ```
   git checkout --progress --force 672fb7c22ff34cd64109f8b08ade11e2dd4543d6
   git checkout --progress --force refs/remotes/pull/3413/merge
   ```

   `Unit Tests` took the head; `Check Issue Reference`, whose checkout carries
   no `with:` block, took the merge ref.

5. Observe the result on `main`. Two `push` runs for `0a33077d` were created at
   `15:52:39Z`, two seconds after the merge, and both failed: `32043649778`
   (`CI`) and `32043649821` (`Windows Full Suite`, which is not a required
   context). In run `32043649778`, `Unit Tests` failed on exactly those two
   tests and nothing else.

6. Reproduce locally:

   ```bash
   go test ./internal/cli \
     -run '^(TestReviewAbandonOfAPristineLineageIgnoresAnUnrelatedUnloadableApprovedLineage|TestUnrelatedReceiptDenialNamesTheCandidateSituationNotOtherLineages)$' \
     -count=1 -v
   ```

   At `fcbbcd6e`: both PASS. At `0a33077d`: both FAIL.

7. Measure the prevalence figure, from a full clone after `git fetch origin`:

   ```bash
   gh pr list --repo Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai --state merged --base main \
     --limit 3000 --json number,baseRefOid,mergeCommit,mergedAt \
     --jq 'sort_by(.mergedAt) | reverse | .[:200][]
           | [.number, .baseRefOid, .mergeCommit.oid] | @tsv' \
   | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n base mc; do
       fp=$(git log -1 --format=%P "$mc" | awk '{print $1}')
       printf '%s #%s\n' "$(git rev-list --count --first-parent "$base..$fp")" "$n"
     done | sort -rn
   ```

   200 rows, 77 of them with a non-zero count. `--limit 3000` covers all 680
   pull requests ever merged into `main`, so the sort by `mergedAt` sees every
   candidate rather than a creation-ordered slice.

## ✅ Expected Behavior

Before a pull request lands on `main`, the content that will exist on `main`
should have been exercised by something that can block the merge. Today nothing
does: the required checks that exercise product behaviour measure the head in
isolation, and no downstream rule re-measures the integration.

Which lever provides that is a maintainer decision, not something this report
prescribes. The fork, with its costs, is under Additional Context.

Two properties should survive whatever is chosen:

- The head-only checkout keeps working for what it was built for. Its step
  name, `Checkout exact event candidate`, states the intent, and this report
  does not ask for it to change.
- A required check keeps meaning what its name implies. #2466 already stated
  the principle: "the failure mode to eliminate is a required check whose name
  implies more coverage than it delivers." A green `Unit Tests` on a pull
  request currently implies coverage of a state that was never compiled.

## ❌ Actual Behavior

The required checks that exercise product behaviour pass against the head. The
merge is admitted. `main` breaks. The earliest signal is the push run on
`main`, which by construction starts only after the breakage is already on the
branch.

The phenomenon is already documented twice in this repository, in the
maintainer's own words:

- #3063 (CLOSED, 2026-08-11): "#3037 (j98, #2696) and #3038 (j99, #2906) each
  added one bench journey and each bumped the baseline 93 -> 94 against a `main`
  where the other had not landed. Both were green on their own. Merging both
  left 95 journeys registered under a baseline of 94. […] The guard did exactly
  what it exists for: it caught a count change that no individual PR suite could
  see."

- #3420 (CLOSED, 2026-08-17): "Neither PR was wrong. #3410 merged before #3413,
  so its branch never saw the new default, and #3413's own sweep could not see
  tests that were not yet in `main`."

Both reports are accurate and both were fixed. Both fixes repaired the instance.
Neither changed the merge policy that admits the next one, which is what this
issue is about.

## Gentle AI Version

Repository CI and merge policy inspected on `main` at
`a245f2605841fbaf68c140b584f5fb4b9a5aa4aa`, after stable `v2.4.0`. The defect is
in merge-policy composition relative to `ci.yml` and ruleset `13932547`, not in
the released binary payload.

Every GitHub API figure in this report .. the ruleset state, the check runs, the
`refs/pull/3465/*` values, the CI wall-clock sample, the total for pull requests
merged into `main`, and the counts of open pull requests overall and by base ..
was measured on 2026-08-19.
All of it is live state that moves.

## Operating System

Windows for the local `go test` bisect. Policy and run data read through the
GitHub REST API. The failing jobs ran on GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest`.

## AI Agent / Client

Not agent-specific. Reproduced through read-only GitHub API inspection and a
local `go test` bisect across two merge commits.

## 📋 Affected Area

Other: GitHub repository merge policy and CI required-check composition.

## 💡 Logs / Error Output

Local bisect, two detached worktrees, real `$HOME`:

```
# at fcbbcd6e (#3410 merged, #3413 not yet)
=== RUN   TestReviewAbandonOfAPristineLineageIgnoresAnUnrelatedUnloadableApprovedLineage
--- PASS: TestReviewAbandonOfAPristineLineageIgnoresAnUnrelatedUnloadableApprovedLineage (2.00s)
=== RUN   TestUnrelatedReceiptDenialNamesTheCandidateSituationNotOtherLineages
--- PASS: TestUnrelatedReceiptDenialNamesTheCandidateSituationNotOtherLineages (8.68s)
PASS
ok  	github.com/gentleman-programming/gentle-ai/v2/internal/cli	12.077s

# at 0a33077d (both merged)
=== RUN   TestReviewAbandonOfAPristineLineageIgnoresAnUnrelatedUnloadableApprovedLineage
    review_receipt_discovery_test.go:1544: receipt-driven development is disabled: advancing an existing review is rejected because the default mode source keeps it off; the review is frozen, not discarded; turn reviews on with gentle-ai review mode enable --scope=global to continue it from where it stopped
--- FAIL: TestReviewAbandonOfAPristineLineageIgnoresAnUnrelatedUnloadableApprovedLineage (0.92s)
=== RUN   TestUnrelatedReceiptDenialNamesTheCandidateSituationNotOtherLineages
    review_receipt_discovery_test.go:1544: receipt-driven development is disabled: advancing an existing review is rejected because the default mode source keeps it off; the review is frozen, not discarded; turn reviews on with gentle-ai review mode enable --scope=global to continue it from where it stopped
--- FAIL: TestUnrelatedReceiptDenialNamesTheCandidateSituationNotOtherLineages (0.91s)
FAIL
FAIL	github.com/gentleman-programming/gentle-ai/v2/internal/cli	3.249s
FAIL
```

Same two names, same message, as the CI job on `main`, verbatim from the job log
of run `32043649778`, job `95427377674`:

```
2026-08-17T15:59:40.9041153Z --- FAIL: TestReviewAbandonOfAPristineLineageIgnoresAnUnrelatedUnloadableApprovedLineage (0.28s)
2026-08-17T15:59:40.9095460Z --- FAIL: TestUnrelatedReceiptDenialNamesTheCandidateSituationNotOtherLineages (0.09s)
```

For completeness on that same `main` run: `E2E Tests (arch)` and
`E2E Tests (fedora)` also failed, but on action-download `429`/`502` while
fetching `docker/setup-buildx-action`, not on candidate content. `Unit Tests`
was the only candidate-caused required-check failure.

## Additional Context

### The fork

Two workable directions, with their real costs. Presented as a choice, not a
recommendation.

**A. Adopt a merge queue.** GitHub builds the merged result and runs the
required checks against it before it lands, which closes the gap directly
rather than shortening the time to notice. The decision is already pending
inside #3353, whose work unit 2 is "Design and implement merge-queue
reevaluation using real `merge_group` semantics, not `ready_for_review`" and
whose dependency list already records "Maintainer decision required for the
exact `merge_group` counting and reevaluation contract." Cost: the ruleset needs
a `merge_group` rule and the workflows need a `merge_group:` trigger, neither of
which exists today; queued builds add CI time and a second failure surface to
learn.

**B. Accept the exposure and shorten the time to notice.** Leave the policy as
it is and improve detection after the merge, since `main` currently reveals
breakage only on the post-merge push run and nothing raises it beyond that run's
status. Cost: `main` still goes red; only the interval between breaking and
knowing shrinks, and the work of unpicking which of two innocent PRs to amend
remains.

### Why `strict: true` is the wrong third option here

Flipping `strict_required_status_checks_policy` to `true` would close the same
gap, and at this repository's rate it should not be used. Every merge into
`main` would invalidate the up-to-date state of the other open pull requests
whose base is `main`, of which there are currently 166 of 170 open overall,
forcing each to update and re-run before it could merge. Over the last 500 pull
requests merged into `main` (2026-07-08 to 2026-08-18, 37 active days) the rate
is mean 13.5 merges/day, median 12, peak 44.

CI wall clock over the last 40 qualifying runs is median 11.2 minutes, p90 11.8
minutes:

```bash
gh api 'repos/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?event=pull_request&status=success&per_page=100' \
  --jq '.workflow_runs[]
        | select(.event == "pull_request" and .conclusion == "success")
        | ((.updated_at | fromdate) - (.run_started_at | fromdate))' \
| awk 'NR<=40' | sort -n \
| awk '{a[NR]=$1} END{printf "median %.2f  p90 %.2f\n", (a[20]+a[21])/120, a[36]/60}'
```

The command encodes the choices this figure is sensitive to, because the number
moves with each of them: only `ci.yml`; only `pull_request` runs, so `push` and
`schedule` runs are excluded; only `conclusion == "success"`, so `failure` and
`action_required` runs are excluded, since a run that terminates early is not a
full required-check cycle and would pull the median down; duration taken from
`run_started_at` rather than `created_at`, though for all 40 in this sample the
two were equal; and p90 by nearest rank, the 36th of 40.

`awk 'NR<=40'` selects the same 40 values as `head -40`; what it avoids is
`head` closing the pipe under `gh`, which makes `gh` exit non-zero. The figure
itself is unchanged by the substitution. Forty consecutive runs of the command
above returned `median 11.16  p90 11.82`.

The window slides: it covered `2026-08-17T10:32:44Z` to `2026-08-19T05:57:09Z`
when measured, and it moves with every new run. The endpoint also occasionally
returns a different 40-run window than the one above; the cause is unknown and
it did not reproduce on demand. Re-measure rather than assume this figure.

Serialising the peak day through one full required-check cycle per merge is
8.2 hours at the median duration and 8.7 hours at p90, before any re-run
failure. Keeping `strict` off is a defensible call at this rate. The gap this
issue reports is the composition, not that setting.

### Adjacency, so this is not read as a duplicate

- **#3353** (OPEN, `status:approved`, parent epic #3154) presupposes that a
  merge queue will exist: work unit 2 and the acceptance criterion "Reopen,
  sync, base/head change, stack update, and merge-queue admission reevaluate the
  gate." Its Outcome is scoped entirely to enforcing
  `additions + deletions <= 400`, so adopting a merge queue would be a
  precondition it inherits, not a result it delivers. It would not close this
  gap as a side effect.

- **#1853** (OPEN, `status:approved`, `priority:high`) concerns the same ruleset
  `13932547` and asks for a source-controlled manifest of declared merge-blocker
  contexts compared against the live ruleset. It reports a different property,
  the absence of `Darwin Runtime` from the required set. It is adjacent rather
  than duplicate: a freshness signal for the required set would ride the same
  manifest, but the missing-context defect and the never-revalidated defect are
  independent.

- **#2203** (OPEN) is the same head-only checkout observed from the opposite
  side: a legacy head that predates a fixture the newer base workflow requires.
  Same underlying property, inverse symptom, different fix surface.

### One small correction, for whoever reproduces next

#3420's Prevention section says the failure "reproduces with `HOME` and
`USERPROFILE` pointed at an empty directory" and will not show on a machine
whose real `$HOME` carries install state. Both tests failed for me at
`0a33077d` on a real, populated `$HOME` that contains `.gentle-ai`. The reason
is visible in the fixture: `reviewModeHome(t)` in
`internal/cli/review_mode_test.go:827` calls `t.Setenv` on both `HOME` and
`USERPROFILE` unconditionally, so the ambient profile cannot influence these two
tests either way. The plain `go test` command in Steps to Reproduce is enough;
no environment preparation is needed.

### Triage

This was opened through the API, so the bug report form's `bug` and
`status:needs-review` labels were not applied. It needs those two labels to
enter the normal review path, plus `status:approved` before any PR references
it.

title: bug(sync): rollback aborts for manifest path outside allowed roots
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing open and closed issues and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I understand that PRs require maintainer approval via `status:approved`.

### 📝 Bug Description

After updating Gentle AI, an existing frozen review reported that managed reviewer assets were outdated and required `gentle-ai sync`. The sync operation aborted during rollback because a managed manifest entry had an `OriginalPath` outside the currently allowed roots.

This leaves the review authority preserved but unable to advance.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Install or update to the affected Gentle AI build on Windows x64.
2. Have an existing managed-assets manifest entry whose `OriginalPath` resolves outside the current user-home and project roots, for example `<outside-allowed-root>\agent\mcp.json`.
3. Start or resume a review that reports managed reviewer assets are outdated.
4. Run `gentle-ai sync`.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

`gentle-ai sync` should safely handle a stale or out-of-scope manifest entry, or return a supported recovery path that preserves the frozen review and allows synchronization to complete.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The sync operation fails during rollback because the manifest `OriginalPath` is outside the allowed roots. The review remains in `reviewing` with its receipt missing, so it cannot advance.

### 🖥️ Environment

- **Gentle AI version:** `2.4.1-0.20260818103739-a245f2605841`
- **Operating system:** Windows x64
- **AI agent/client:** Codex
- **Affected area:** Installation Pipeline / CLI
- **Attempts:** One sync attempt after the update; failure was deterministic.
- **Authority outcome:** Frozen review preserved, no receipt created.

### 💡 Sanitized Error Output

```text
managed reviewer assets are outdated; run `gentle-ai sync`

gentle-ai sync
sync failed during rollback: manifest OriginalPath <outside-allowed-root>\agent\mcp.json is outside allowed roots (<user-home>, <project-root>)
```

The preceding lifecycle operation reported `operation_outcome_unknown`, and a subsequent native status check confirmed that the existing review authority remained preserved.
