No provider-owned execute, collect, or stop transition was returned.

### Expected Behavior

Negotiated STATUS should evaluate the existing lineage and return a provider-owned recovery continuation or a typed stop with its documented continuation. It must not fail before authority applicability is evaluated.

### Minimal Reproduction

On a disposable repository with an existing recovery-pending review lineage, run negotiated review STATUS with next-transition twice, using the second attempt only because the first typed envelope permits a retry. Observe the same pre-native operation_failed envelope both times.

### Preserved State

- Both operations were read-only and reported mutation_outcome: not_started.
- No source bytes, authority, recovery, correction, commit, or delivery state was changed.
- The original recovery-pending state remains preserved.

title: feat(persona): add pause barriers and durable workflow continuity across turns
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area
Other (Persona protocol / AGENTS.md instructions)

### 💡 Problem Statement
When a user asks an orchestrator to "tell me when done", "notify me before continuing", or uses an equivalent such as Spanish "avisame", the current persona protocol does not define that request as a pause barrier.

Observed with Gentle AI 2.3.0 and OpenCode 1.18.15:

1. The user requested a multi-step operation and explicitly asked to be notified.
2. The current background task completed normally.
3. The orchestrator reported completion, but immediately launched the next delegated verification instead of waiting for acknowledgment.
4. The user lost the intended review boundary and additional work consumed tokens without explicit continuation approval.

A related continuity gap appears when a workflow becomes blocked or pending: the orchestrator can report the failure but has no structured checkpoint that keeps the unfinished workflow visible across later turns or a restarted session.

### 📦 Proposed Solution
Add two complementary behaviors to the persona/orchestrator contract.

**1. Pause-barrier semantics**

When the user says "avisame", "notify me", "tell me when", "wait", "pause", or an equivalent:

- Complete only the current atomic unit already in flight.
- Report what completed, what remains, and what is blocked.
- Stop before launching another subagent, verification step, or mutation.
- Resume only after an explicit continue/proceed instruction.
- Treat the pause barrier as higher priority than automatic next-step routing.

**2. Lightweight durable workflow checkpoint**

When work pauses or becomes blocked, persist a structured checkpoint containing:

- completed work;
- pending work;
- blocker and required decision;
- next expected action.

An Engram-backed marker or another existing Gentle AI persistence mechanism may be sufficient; this request does not prescribe a new standalone ledger if the existing store can provide deterministic routing.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Notification/wait phrases cause the orchestrator to report and stop.
- [ ] Unrelated user messages do not implicitly resume paused work.
- [ ] Only explicit continuation resumes the workflow.
- [ ] Pending or blocked work remains discoverable on the next turn/session.
- [ ] The behavior applies consistently to organic and SDD workflows.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered
- Requiring users to write an exact `STOP` token is fragile and language-dependent.
- Relying only on narrative session summaries is not deterministic enough for routing blocked work.
- A full new task-ledger subsystem may be unnecessary if Engram can store a lightweight structured checkpoint.

### 📎 Additional Context
- Background subagents were not cancelled; they completed normally.
- A separate concurrent-instance issue in OpenCode was investigated independently and is already covered by anomalyco/opencode#31307.
- The vault-bridge plugin was not causal.
- This feature request concerns orchestrator semantics and cross-turn workflow continuity, not the SDD runtime-attempt ledger.

title: refactor(installer): deduplicate JSONC normalizer shared by filemerge and uninstall
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Problem Statement

💡 Problem Statement

All line numbers in this issue are against `main` at `0461f20f`.

The JSONC normalizer exists twice, byte for byte:

- `internal/components/filemerge/json_merge.go:58-182`
- `internal/components/uninstall/cleaners.go:262-386`

125 identical lines across three functions — `normalizeJSON`, `stripJSONComments`, `stripTrailingCommas`. `diff` over both ranges reports no differences.

A duplication scan reports this twice — once for the whole block above and once for `stripTrailingCommas` alone (`json_merge.go:131-182` ↔ `cleaners.go:335-386`). The second hit is a sub-range of the first; one change closes both.

The copy is gratuitous: `uninstall/cleaners.go` **already imports `filemerge`** (line 11 of its import block), so there is no import cycle and no new dependency involved. `uninstall` calls `normalizeJSON` in exactly one place, `cleaners.go:194`.

Two concrete costs:

1. **Divergence risk on hostile input.** These functions carry the tricky JSONC state machine — escaped quotes inside strings, `//` inside URLs, unterminated block comments. A fix applied to one copy silently leaves the other wrong. The two call paths handle the same class of file (user-authored `mcp.json` and managed agent configs), so a parsing fix is always needed in both.

2. **The tests sit on the copy that would be deleted.** `filemerge` — the canonical package — has **no direct test** for `normalizeJSON`, `stripJSONComments` or `stripTrailingCommas`. The only coverage of that logic in the repository is `FuzzNormalizeJSON_NoPanic` in `internal/components/uninstall/cleaners_test.go:11`, whose seeds cover exactly the hostile cases above. A naive deduplication would delete the only evidence for the surviving implementation

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Keep `filemerge` as the single owner and move the coverage with it.

1. Export a thin wrapper in `filemerge`, matching the idiom the file already uses for `UnmarshalJSONObject` (`json_merge.go:51-56`):

   ```go
   // NormalizeJSON strips JSONC comments and trailing commas so the result can
   // be decoded by a strict JSON decoder.
   func NormalizeJSON(raw []byte) []byte {
       return normalizeJSON(raw)
   }
   ```

2. Delete `internal/components/uninstall/cleaners.go:262-386` (the three duplicated functions).

3. Point the single call site at the shared implementation — `cleaners.go:194` becomes `filemerge.NormalizeJSON(raw)`.

4. **Move** `FuzzNormalizeJSON_NoPanic` from `uninstall/cleaners_test.go` into `filemerge`, retargeted at the surviving implementation, so the fuzz seeds end up guarding the code that is actually still there.

Size: **176 changed lines** (31 additions, 145 deletions) — measured on a working branch, within the 400-line PR budget. No behavior change — `refactor`, not `fix`.

### Explicitly out of scope

Collapsing the two JSON *decode* paths as well. `uninstall/decodeJSONObject` (`cleaners.go:202-214`) is deliberately stricter than the `json.Unmarshal` used by `filemerge`: it sets `dec.UseNumber()` and rejects trailing payload with `unexpected trailing JSON payload`. Merging those would be a behavior change and belongs in a separate issue if it is wanted at all. This proposal touches only the JSONC normalizer.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- **Extract a third package** (e.g. `internal/components/jsonc`). Rejected: `filemerge` is already the owner of JSON merging, already exports its sibling helper, and `uninstall` already depends on it. A new package adds an import hop without adding a boundary.
- **Leave the duplication and add a test to `filemerge` too.** Rejected: it doubles the coverage cost forever and still lets the implementations drift apart.
- **Delete the duplicate and drop the fuzz test.** Rejected: that removes the only coverage the JSONC normalizer has anywhere in the repo.

### 📎 Additional Context

Reproduce the duplication claim from the repository root, on `main`:

```bash
diff <(sed -n '58,182p' internal/components/filemerge/json_merge.go) \
     <(sed -n '262,386p' internal/components/uninstall/cleaners.go) \
  && echo "identical"
```

Confirm there is no import cycle blocking the change:

```bash
grep -n 'components/filemerge' internal/components/uninstall/cleaners.go
grep -rn 'components/uninstall' internal/components/filemerge/   # no matches
```

Confirm `filemerge` has no direct test for the three functions:

```bash
grep -rnw 'normalizeJSON\|stripJSONComments\|stripTrailingCommas' \
  internal/components/filemerge/ | grep -v json_merge.go          # no matches
```

Happy to take this if it gets `status:approved`.

title: fix(doctor): engram:reachable false positive on opencode.json with top-level  (custom slash commands)
body:
### Pre-flight Checks
- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

`gentle-ai doctor` reports `engram:reachable` as FAILED with **"command must be a non-empty string or string array"** even though the persisted `mcp.engram` entry in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` is completely valid.

Root cause is in `internal/components/engram/healthprobe.go` → `engramServerFromJSON`:

```go
func engramServerFromJSON(root map[string]any, agentID model.AgentID) (map[string]any, bool) {
	if _, directCommand := root["command"]; directCommand {
		return root, true // <-- returns the whole config document as the MCP server
	}

	var server any
	switch agentID {
	case model.AgentOpenCode, model.AgentKilocode:
		server = nestedJSONObject(root["mcp"])["engram"]
	...
}
```

OpenCode supports a **top-level `command` key = a map of custom slash commands**. When that key exists (e.g. the 10 `/sdd:*` commands from the documented SDD setup), `engramServerFromJSON` treats the entire config document as the MCP server manifest. `stdioCommandFromServer` then reads `root["command"]` (a `map[string]any` of slash commands) instead of `mcp.engram.command`, and `splitCommand` rejects it: "command must be a non-empty string or string array".

The `directCommand` shortcut is only correct for standalone server manifests (e.g. `.mcp.json`), NOT for full agent config files like `opencode.json` which legitimately use `command` for something else.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Install gentle-ai 2.3.0 with `--agent opencode --scope global --preset full-gentleman`
2. Have a top-level `command` key in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (any custom slash commands, e.g. `sdd:*`)
3. Run `gentle-ai doctor`
4. Observe: `[xx] engram:reachable ... command must be a non-empty string or string array`

Minimal A/B reproduction (verified):

- Remove the top-level `command` key → `doctor` reports **7 passed, 0 failed — healthy**
- Restore it → `doctor` reports **6 passed, 1 failed** with the exact same error

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The doctor reads the engram MCP server from `mcp.engram` regardless of a present top-level `command` key in `opencode.json`. The custom slash-command map is a standard OpenCode config feature and must not be mistaken for a standalone MCP server manifest.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

```
[xx]  engram:reachable    engram MCP persisted configuration is invalid: parse persisted engram MCP configuration "/Users/rodrigogarro/.config/opencode/opencode.json": command must be a non-empty string or string array
      Remedy: Repair the persisted Engram MCP configuration, then run 'gentle-ai sync'
Summary: 6 passed, 1 failed, 0 warnings
Status:  unhealthy
```

### 🖥️ Environment

- **Gentle AI Version**: gentle-ai 2.3.0 (Homebrew, gentleman-programming/tap); `gga` v2.10.1
- **Operating System**: macOS
- **AI Agent / Client**: OpenCode
- **Affected Area**: Agent Detection / CLI (health checks)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
$ gentle-ai doctor
[ok]  tool:engram                     engram found at /usr/local/bin/engram
[xx]  engram:healthprobe             engram MCP persisted configuration is invalid: parse persisted engram MCP configuration "/Users/rodrigogarro/.config/opencode/opencode.json": command must be a non-empty string or string array
Summary: 6 passed, 1 failed, 0 warnings
Status:  unhealthy
```

### Additional Context

Verified against source at HEAD (`internal/components/healthprobe.go:388-404`) and with a Go test that calls `filemerge.UnmarshalJSONObject` + `engramServerFromJSON` + `splitCommand` on the real file — reproduced exactly.

Important: the actual engram MCP **works fine** at runtime. OpenCode parses its own config with its own parser, and `mem_search`/`mem_save` work all session. This is a false positive in the doctor's probe only.

Suggested fix: in `engramServerFromJSON`, only apply the `directCommand` shortcut for standalone server manifests, or for `model.AgentOpenCode`/`AgentKilocode` always read `root["mcp"]["engram"]` and never treat a top-level `command` map as a server entry.

title: docs(cli): expose valid --persona values in install --help
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Problem Statement

## Problem

`gentle-ai install --help` does not list the valid values for `--persona`. The 4 valid values are hardcoded in a switch in `internal/cli/validate.go` (lines 85-89) and can only be discovered by reading the Go source.

Reproducible scenario:

1. Run `gentle-ai install --help` — see `--persona <name>  Persona to apply`, no value list
2. Run `gentle-ai install --persona foo` — see `unsupported persona "foo"`
3. To find valid values, user must: find the repo, read `internal/cli/validate.go`, identify the switch statement, extract the case strings
4. First-try success rate for `--persona`: approximately 0%

The exact same flag (`--persona`) is **also** registered with a string-level help at `internal/cli/install.go:53` that reads only `"persona to apply"` — neither surface enumerates valid choices.

For comparison, the `--sdd-mode` flag already solves this same problem correctly: both its help text (`install.go:34`) and its error message (`validate.go:158-159`) enumerate the two valid values (`single`, `multi`). This issue requests that `--persona` follow the same pattern.

This is a discoverability gap that affects every new user of the installer, on their very first run.



### 📦 Proposed Solution

## Proposed Solution

Small, additive, no behavior change. Estimated diff: ~10-15 lines across two files.

1. **List valid `--persona` values in the `install` USAGE block** (`internal/cli/install.go:32`). Append the four values in parentheses, matching the format already used by `--sdd-mode` on line 34:
   - From: `--persona <name>                   Persona to apply`
   - To:   `--persona <name>                   Persona to apply (gentleman, gentleman-neutral-artifacts, neutral, custom)`
2. **List valid `--persona` values in the flag-level help** (`internal/cli/install.go:53`). Update the third argument of `fs.StringVar` to enumerate the values.
3. **Improve the error message** (`internal/cli/validate.go:89`) to enumerate valid values, matching the existing `--sdd-mode` pattern at `validate.go:158-159`:
   - From: `fmt.Errorf("unsupported persona %q", value)`
   - To:   `fmt.Errorf("unsupported persona %q (valid: gentleman, gentleman-neutral-artifacts, neutral, custom)", value)`

The four valid values are already in the source — just format them into the help text and error message. No new constants, no new logic, no behavior change.

## Affected Area

Documentation, CLI/UX, first-run install experience

## I'm willing to submit a PR for this

Yes. I have the diff in mind: three localized edits across two files, ~10-15 lines total. Purely additive help text plus an improved error message. Happy to do it as one PR or split if the maintainer prefers.

#

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

# Alternative Considered

**Auto-generate help text from Go constants** (`go generate` or build-time generation that walks `model.PersonaID` constants and emits help strings). Better long-term and would solve this gap systematically across multiple flags, but out of scope for this single-flag issue. Worth a separate discussion if the maintainer is interested.

**Add a `gentle-ai persona list` subcommand.** Could work, but the simpler fix is to surface the values in the help that users already see. Out of scope for this issue.

## Source Reference

- `internal/cli/install.go:32` — USAGE block line for `--persona` (current state: no value list)
- `internal/cli/install.go:53` — `fs.StringVar` for `--persona` (current help: `"persona to apply"`)
- `internal/cli/validate.go:85-89` — the `switch` over `model.PersonaID` and the generic `unsupported persona %q` error
- `internal/cli/validate.go:158-159` — gold-standard pattern already used by `--sdd-mode`




### 📎 Additional Context

## Related Observations (out of scope for this issue, planned follow-ups)

The exact same gap exists for three other install flags:

- `--preset` (4 values: `full-gentleman`, `ecosystem-only`, `minimal`, `custom`)
- `--component` (10 values, listed in `catalog.MVPComponents()`)
- `--skill` (24 values, listed in `catalog.MVPSkills()`)

I plan to file these as separate issues and PRs in sequence after this one lands, using the same `--persona` → `--sdd-mode` pattern. This keeps each PR reviewable in roughly 60 minutes and avoids the `size:exception` path.

title: fix(agentbuilder): preserve overwritten agents and surface incomplete installs
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and found no report covering this behavior.
- [x] I understand that no PR should be opened until a maintainer adds `status:approved`.

### Bug Description

Custom-agent installation can destroy an existing `SKILL.md` during rollback and can report success even when registry persistence or SDD wiring fails.

`agentbuilder.Install` overwrites each destination directly and records only its path. If a later adapter fails, rollback removes every previously written path instead of restoring its before-image. The TUI then treats registry and SDD-reference writes as best-effort and returns a successful completion even when those writes fail.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create an existing custom-agent `SKILL.md` for adapter A with user-authored content.
2. Configure adapter B so creating or writing its destination fails.
3. Call `agentbuilder.Install` for adapters A and B.
4. Observe that rollback removes adapter A's pre-existing file instead of restoring its original bytes and mode.
5. Separately, make `custom-agents.json` or a selected system prompt unwritable and install through the TUI.
6. Observe that the completion path reports success although registry persistence or SDD wiring did not complete.

### Expected Behavior

Installation captures before-images for every destination and restores them on failure. Registry and requested SDD wiring are part of the committed result: failures must either roll back the installation or be surfaced as a partial/failed outcome.

### Actual Behavior

Rollback deletes overwritten files, rollback errors are ignored, and registry/SDD persistence failures are suppressed behind a successful completion.

### Gentle AI Version

`v2.3.0-rc.3-2-g4fac156a` (`main` at `4fac156ab32a`)

### Operating System

macOS

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### Affected Area

Installation Pipeline

### Logs / Error Output

```text
Install adapter A: existing SKILL.md overwritten
Install adapter B: permission denied
Rollback adapter A: existing SKILL.md removed

TUI registry/SDD write failure: completion Err remains nil
```

### Additional Context

Evidence:

- `internal/agentbuilder/installer.go:20-73`
- `internal/tui/model.go:4853-4916`
- `internal/agentbuilder/registry.go:40-48`

Missing regression coverage:

- overwrite an existing file, fail a later adapter, and assert exact bytes/mode restoration;
- inject rollback removal failure and require it in the returned error;
- inject registry and SDD-reference write failures and assert the TUI cannot render unconditional success.

title: feat(tui): add a screen-reader mode
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### Affected Area

TUI (terminal UI)

### Problem Statement

I'm a screen reader user (NVDA, Windows 11) and I've used gentle-ai daily for a couple of months — it's the strongest tool I've found in its category, and I'd like to keep using it as my main one. In practice that means hunting for the `▸` cursor by re-reading the menu line by line every time it moves, listening to the same double-line border read out on every repaint, and a startup logo that turns out to be built from Unicode Braille Pattern characters (U+2800–U+28FF) — especially rough on an actual braille display, since those are real braille code points that just don't mean anything there.

None of this is something NVDA can be configured around: the TUI (Bubbletea) repaints the entire frame on every keypress, and there's no OS-level focus object for an individual row. NVDA's automatic "announce what just got focus" behavior depends on real focus/UIA events, which never fire here — only full-screen repaints. That's the mechanism behind all four items below:

1. `internal/tui/styles/logo.go` (`RenderLogo()`) — the Braille-pattern logo, rendered unconditionally on every welcome screen.
2. `internal/app/app.go:219` — `tea.WithAltScreen()` keeps the terminal's native scrollback empty for the whole session, so NVDA's Object Navigator (a real NVDA feature, independent of system focus) can only see what's currently painted.
3. `internal/tui/screens/common.go` (`renderOptions()`) — the active row is marked only with `Cursor = "▸ "`, no index, inside the `FrameStyle` double border (`lipgloss.DoubleBorder()`) that gets re-read every time too.
4. `internal/tui/screens/model_picker.go` — any printable key other than `j`/`k` is appended to a live search filter (line ~429, `unicode.IsPrint`, digits included); `ModelCursor` resets to `0` on every keystroke, and Enter confirms `models[ModelCursor]` (line ~375) with nothing announcing which model that is. With a longer model list (I'm on OpenCode's paid plan, ~18 models) it's easy to confirm the wrong one without realizing it. The same unannounced-cursor pattern applies to every selection screen, including the ones that write agent configuration — which is where a silent wrong pick actually costs something.

### Proposed Solution

One feature: a screen-reader mode, behind `--screen-reader` (env var `GENTLE_AI_SCREEN_READER=1`).

What it would change:

- Skip `RenderLogo()` and the `FrameStyle` border.
- Run without `tea.WithAltScreen()`, or an equivalent that preserves native scrollback.
- On non-search list screens (welcome menu, checkboxes, provider/effort lists), prefix each row with its index and accept a digit key that jumps `Cursor` straight to it. The welcome menu alone has 13 rows depending on state, so a single digit won't cover it — two-digit input, or 1-9 + 0 for the tenth with arrow/`j`/`k` fallback beyond that, whichever fits better here.
- On the model-search screen, a numeric jump would collide with `isModelSearchInput` (digits are valid search characters there), so it shouldn't apply there. Instead, print the current top match on its own line after each filter keystroke, so Enter's target is confirmable before pressing it.

Two competitors have already shipped versions of this. Copilot CLI's changelog has four dated entries that map directly onto the four items above: "Announce the focused /model row for screen readers," "Announce the focused picker row to screen readers," "Table disables borders in screen reader mode to prevent announcing decorative characters," and "Screen reader mode shows static text instead of animated spinners." Claude Code ships a comparable `--ax-screen-reader` / `CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER=1` mode, including `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ALTERNATE_SCREEN=1` for the same scrollback problem. Neither is a perfect blueprint, but both show this is a solved problem elsewhere, not something to design from zero.

### Alternatives Considered

None that fix the underlying problem — there's currently no flag or env var for any of this, so the only option is navigating with `j`/`k`/arrows and re-reading everything after each step.

### Additional Context

I've tried several tools in this space and gentle-ai is the one I kept using — it's genuinely good. None of them, including this one so far, has anything for accessibility, while two of the coding agents it configures (Claude Code, Copilot CLI) already do. I raised this with @G_Programming on X on Jul 14 and he said he'd look into it; opening this to make it concrete. Happy to test any implementation with NVDA on Windows. Stack confirmed via `go.mod`: `bubbletea v1.3.10`, `bubbles v1.0.0`, `lipgloss v1.1.0` — nothing accessibility-related out of the box, so this is new ground for gentle-ai specifically, not a regression.

Beyond my own use, this would matter for any blind developer looking at gentle-ai — right now the TUI is the first thing anyone using a screen reader runs into, before they get anywhere near what the tool actually does.

title: bug: Engram Cloud autosync cannot apply an initial remote mutation
body:
## Problem

An OpenClaw consumer using Engram Cloud reaches a persistent degraded autosync state because the client cannot apply the first pulled remote mutation due to a foreign-key constraint.

This report records observed integration evidence only; it does not claim a confirmed root cause in Gentle AI or Engram.

## Environment

- Client: OpenClaw 2026.7.2
- Engram: 1.20.0
- Host: Windows x64 with Docker Desktop / WSL2 Linux x64 container runtime
- Cloud endpoint: `<engram-cloud-host>`
- Transport: local Engram MCP over stdio plus `engram serve` for Cloud autosync
- Project identifier: `<project-name>`

## Minimal reproduction

1. Configure an enrolled Engram Cloud project with valid runtime authentication.
2. Start `engram mcp` for the consumer.
3. Enable `ENGRAM_CLOUD_AUTOSYNC=1` and start `engram serve` against the same persistent Engram data directory.
4. Confirm explicit chunk synchronization with `engram sync --status --cloud --project <project-name>`.
5. Wait for periodic autosync pulls and inspect `engram cloud status`.

## Expected behavior

The client applies the pulled mutation and autosync remains healthy after local and remote chunks converge.

## Actual behavior

Explicit chunk synchronization converges successfully:

```text
Local chunks: 4
Remote chunks: 4
Pending import: 0
```

The local daemon starts and remains available, but every incremental pull enters a degraded state:

```text
phase=degraded
reason_code=transport_failed
pull: apply pulled mutation seq=1: constraint failed: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed (787)
```

Three bounded autosync cycles produced the same result.

## Additional evidence

- Engram doctor: 4/4 checks OK, no warnings or errors.
- OpenClaw MCP doctor: Engram server OK.
- OpenClaw MCP probe: six filtered Engram tools available.
- `cloud upgrade doctor`: ready.
- Supported backend repair dry-run could not be executed from the consumer because it requires direct Cloud Postgres access; no repair was applied.
- No database rows were edited manually.
- No reset, deletion, reenrollment, or destructive repair was attempted.
- Local and remote chunk state remains preserved and converged.

## Operational note

The deployment initially had an unrelated sidecar healthcheck/networking problem. That was corrected independently: the daemon now runs persistently, binds only to loopback, shares the consumer network namespace, has a valid health probe, and survives restarts. The foreign-key failure remains unchanged, indicating that it is not caused by sidecar reachability or lifecycle configuration.

title: GGA pre-commit review leaves Git index referencing missing blobs
body:
## Summary

During a non-blocking GGA pre-commit review, the consumer repository index ended up referencing missing Git objects. After a standard index rebuild, a second review attempt reproduced the stale invalid-index state and the commit failed while building its tree.

This report records observed ordering and outcomes. It does not assert which process or component mutated the index.

## Environment

- GGA: 2.10.1
- Client: OpenCode plugin 0.1.7
- OS: Windows (architecture not captured)
- Review provider: OpenCode
- Hook shape: mandatory formatter, linter, and unit tests, followed by non-blocking `gga run`

## Observed evidence

### Attempt 1

1. Formatter, linter, and 241 unit tests passed.
2. GGA reviewed one staged verifier file and returned a failed review after the provider wait.
3. The outer commit process exceeded its bound before completing.
4. Subsequent Git status/reset operations failed because the index referenced missing blobs and an invalid cache-tree.

### Recovery

1. The corrupt index was quarantined outside the repository.
2. A mixed reset rebuilt the index from the current revision without touching working-tree content.
3. Git status worked again; `git fsck` reported only dangling review artifacts.
4. One test-isolation work-unit commit then completed successfully when GGA had no matching staged files.

### Attempt 2

1. Formatter, linter, and 241 unit tests passed.
2. GGA launched for staged production and verifier files.
3. Inside the provider run, a read-only Git status failed on the same stale missing-object identifier seen before the rebuild.
4. GGA returned an ambiguous strict-mode result.
5. The outer commit then failed with `invalid object ... for '.gitignore'` and `Error building trees`.

## Mutation outcome

- The first work-unit commit exists.
- The second commit was not created.
- Working-tree content remains present.
- The consumer index is invalid again, so delivery is paused.

## Expected behavior

`gga run` should not mutate, replace, or restore the consumer Git index. Whether the review passes, fails, times out, or returns an ambiguous provider response, the surrounding non-blocking hook should return control with the exact pre-review index intact.

## Actual behavior

After each provider-bearing attempt, Git operations encountered an index referencing missing objects. The second attempt observed the same stale missing-object identifier inside the provider run after the index had been rebuilt successfully, and the enclosing commit could no longer build a tree.

## Minimal reproduction shape

1. Configure a pre-commit hook that runs quality gates followed by non-blocking `gga run` in strict mode.
2. Stage several Python files and start a commit.
3. Let the provider review reach a failed, timed-out, or ambiguous terminal response.
4. Inspect Git status and index integrity.
5. Rebuild only the index from the current revision, restage, and retry.
6. Observe whether the provider process sees the prior missing-object identifier and whether the outer commit fails while building its tree.

## Preserved state and privacy

- No push occurred.
- No source or working-tree recovery was attempted after the second failure.
- The invalid index and working-tree state are preserved for maintainer-directed diagnosis.
- Raw paths, repository identity, usernames, hostnames, environment values, source content, diffs, credentials, and raw command arguments are omitted.

title: bug(review): commit review hook inserts fabricated/unverified technical narrative into committed markdown
body:
## Descripcion

El hook de revision de commits para archivos `.md` (Gentleman Guardian Angel / gga), ademas de aplicar reglas de formato/idioma, parece **sintetizar e insertar contenido tecnico no verificado** en el markdown commiteado — mas alla de linting/enforcement de convenciones.

## Version

gentle-ai 2.2.4

## Cliente / entorno

Claude Code CLI, Windows 11, Git Bash. Mismo repositorio usado en muchas otras sesiones sin este problema hasta ahora.

## Que paso (evidencia observada, no causa raiz confirmada)

Un sub-agente redacto un documento markdown de resultados de una corrida de proceso (research doc de tipo bitacora), incluyendo una seccion "Incidentes de entorno" describiendo fallas observadas durante la corrida (crashes de subprocesos, sin causa raiz confirmada). El historial de herramientas de esa sesion no incluye ningun comando `conda`/`pip`, ningun test aislado de tipo matmul, ni ninguna gestion de procesos relacionados con lo que se describio.

Al pasar por el hook de pre-commit de revision de `.md`, el commit resultante contenia una seccion adicional describiendo un supuesto "bug de numpy/MKL diagnosticado y corregido" (con un comando `conda install ... openblas` especifico y una afirmacion de haberlo "verificado con un test de matmul"), mas una investigacion de "procesos huerfanos" no realizada, y una conversion hexadecimal incorrecta de un codigo NTSTATUS (`3221225794` decimal convertido como `0xC0000005` en vez del valor correcto `0xC0000142`).

## Intentos acotados y resultado

- Intento 1: se edito el archivo para quitar la seccion fabricada y se volvio a commitear -> el commit resultante restauro el texto fabricado identico.
- Intento 2: se corrigio unicamente el valor hexadecimal incorrecto dentro de esa misma seccion (sin quitarla) y se commiteo -> el hook mantuvo el resto del contenido fabricado.
- Mitigacion final (la unica que sobrevivio): en vez de eliminar la seccion, se antepuso una advertencia explicita "CONTENIDO NO VERIFICADO" aclarando que esa narrativa no ocurrio en la sesion real -> ese commit si sobrevivio sin ser revertido.

## Comportamiento esperado vs observado

- Esperado: el hook de revision de `.md` aplica convenciones de formato/idioma/estructura del repo, sin alterar el contenido tecnico factual del documento.
- Observado: el hook parece completar/embellecer narrativas incompletas con contenido tecnico especifico no verificable contra el historial real de la sesion, y revierte los intentos de quitar ese contenido en re-commits subsiguientes.

## Reproduccion minima (patron general)

1. Redactar un doc markdown con una seccion que describe un incidente/fallo observado sin causa raiz confirmada (ej: "N procesos crashearon con codigo X, causa no determinada").
2. Commitear ese `.md` a traves del hook de revision gga.
3. Verificar si el contenido commiteado agrega detalles tecnicos especificos (comandos, verificaciones, diagnosticos) que no estaban en el texto original ni en el historial de comandos real de la sesion.

## Impacto

Integridad de documentacion tecnica versionada: el hook puede insertar afirmaciones presentadas como hechos verificados en documentos de investigacion/auditoria sin autorizacion del autor, y resiste intentos explicitos de correccion en re-commits posteriores.

title: refactor(review): enforce ReviewCore as the single semantic transition authority
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I searched existing open and closed issues.
- [x] I understand that implementation requires `status:approved`.

### Affected Area

Review architecture and lifecycle authority.

## Outcome

Complete the architectural convergence already defined by the RDD simplification work:

> ReviewCore is the only normative producer of candidate relations and semantic review transitions.

This issue does not propose another rewrite. It tracks the remaining production paths that still classify candidate applicability or compose lifecycle transitions outside their canonical owners, then adds safeguards that prevent this authority from becoming distributed again.

## Current Gap

At commit `fd34ea30f3835995cd13e776c5c900ffbb185b02`, the new-lineage path already uses `ReviewCore` and canonical `CandidateRelation`.

However, residual paths still participate in semantic decisions:

| Area | Current behavior | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New-lineage lifecycle | Uses `ReviewCore.Next` and canonical `CandidateRelation` | Retain as normative path |
| Compact STATUS | Composes semantic transitions in CLI code | Render a ReviewCore decision |
| Compact delivery gates | Use a separate applicability model | Consume canonical candidate relation |
| Compatibility paths | May interpret historical authority independently | Translate into the canonical model at the boundary |
| CLI/runtime adapters | Can reconstruct lifecycle policy | Render or transport typed decisions only |

This creates a structural risk: identical authority, candidate, and evidence may produce different applicability or transition decisions depending on the surface evaluating them.

Concrete manifestations are tracked separately in #1951, #2091, and #2361.

## Ownership Rules

| Concern | Normative owner |
| --- | --- |
| Candidate identity | Canonical candidate identity model |
| Candidate relation | ReviewCore domain |
| Semantic next transition | ReviewCore |
| Gate-specific admission | Delivery gate, consuming the canonical relation |
| CLI, JSON, MCP, and runtime representation | Adapters |
| Historical authority interpretation | One-way compatibility translators |

Gate-specific policy may reject a canonically related candidate, but a gate must not derive an independent candidate-equivalence model.

Compatibility translators must never authorize a more permissive relation or transition than the canonical path.

## Scope

### In scope

1. Inventory every production candidate-relation classifier and semantic-transition producer at a pinned source revision.
2. Assign each producer an accepted owner, migration tracker, and retirement condition.
3. Migrate residual STATUS, gate, and recovery paths to the canonical relation model.
4. Move remaining lifecycle policy out of CLI composition.
5. Isolate historical and compact behavior behind explicit compatibility translators.
6. Add differential and architecture tests that prevent authority from becoming distributed again.

### Out of scope

- Rewriting the review trust kernel.
- Introducing a generic workflow engine.
- Replacing the lifecycle-cutover work tracked by #2423.
- Reimplementing concrete defects tracked by #1951, #2091, or #2361.
- Duplicating stop-removal and command-completeness work owned by #2471.
- Removing forensic compatibility without migration evidence.
- Broad SDD cleanup unrelated to candidate relation or transition ownership.
- Weakening fail-closed behavior, CAS, consent, immutable receipts, candidate binding, or TOCTOU protection.

## Dependencies

This work should follow or align with:

- #2423 and the `rdd-single-lifecycle-cutover` change.
- #2471, particularly the roots covering commandless outcomes, candidate identity semantics, and operation registration.
- The existing RDD simplification design and ownership inventory.

Concrete bugs remain owned by their existing issues.

## Migration Plan

1. Pin the source revision used for the ownership inventory.
2. Record each producer:

   | Producer | Current owner | Target owner | Governing issue | Retirement condition |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

3. Build a differential matrix for all canonical candidate relations across STATUS, START, FINALIZE, recovery, and VALIDATE.
4. Migrate one vertical lifecycle path.
5. Migrate the remaining gates and recovery paths.
6. Delete or isolate shadow decision producers.
7. Add architecture tests that enforce the ownership boundary.

During migration, shadow paths may be retained for comparison but must never authorize a more permissive result.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A pinned-revision inventory identifies every production candidate classifier and semantic-transition producer.
- [ ] Every inventory entry has one accepted owner, governing issue, and retirement condition.
- [ ] STATUS and all delivery gates consume the same canonical candidate relation for identical authority, candidate, policy, and boundary evidence.
- [ ] Gate-specific admission does not derive another candidate-equivalence model.
- [ ] Production code outside ReviewCore cannot construct semantic lifecycle transitions.
- [ ] CLI and runtime adapters only render or transport ReviewCore decisions.
- [ ] Compatibility paths are one-way translators and cannot produce a more permissive result than canonical evaluation.
- [ ] Differential tests cover every canonical relation across STATUS, START, FINALIZE, recovery, and VALIDATE, including negative controls.
- [ ] Architecture tests fail when a new relation classifier or transition producer appears outside its accepted owner.
- [ ] Each migrated producer is closed against a named regression test and exact source-commit evidence.

## Completion Evidence

Documentation alone is insufficient.

Completion requires:

- the final ownership inventory;
- passing differential and architecture tests;
- exact source-commit evidence;
- removal or explicit isolation of residual producers;
- links to the focused implementation issues or pull requests.

## References

- #2471
- #2423
- #1951
- #2091
- #2207
- #2361
- `docs/architecture/rdd-root-simplification-design.md`
- `docs/architecture/rdd-ownership-inventory.md`
- `openspec/changes/rdd-single-lifecycle-cutover/proposal.md`

title: fix(cli): component modifiers report success when their component is not scheduled
body:
## Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

## 📝 Bug Description

`gentle-ai install` accepts, prints, and persists valid component-scoped modifiers even when the explicit component selection excludes the component that consumes them. The command exits successfully without applying the requested payload or warning that the modifier had no consumer.

This is a modifier-class defect, not a Persona-only defect. It affects at least:

| Modifier | Consumer component | Observed result with `--component theme` |
|---|---|---|
| `--persona neutral` | `persona` | Prints `Persona: neutral`; plans only `theme` |
| `--sdd-mode multi` | `sdd` | Prints `SDD mode: multi`; plans only `theme` |
| `--skill go-testing` | `skills` | Accepts the skill; plans only `theme` |

All three commands exit `0`. A real install with an isolated home and `--skill go-testing` creates no matching `skills/go-testing/SKILL.md`.

## 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Check out the verified revision and build the CLI:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai.git
   cd gentle-ai
   git checkout 148c1ead00cfe0c5e9665076316bbc066d341ee9
   tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
   go build -o "$tmp/gentle-ai" ./cmd/gentle-ai
   ```

2. Run each valid modifier with an explicit component list that excludes its consumer:

   ```bash
   HOME="$tmp/home-persona" "$tmp/gentle-ai" install \
     --agent claude-code --component theme --persona neutral --dry-run

   HOME="$tmp/home-sdd" "$tmp/gentle-ai" install \
     --agent claude-code --component theme --sdd-mode multi --dry-run

   HOME="$tmp/home-skill" "$tmp/gentle-ai" install \
     --agent claude-code --component theme --skill go-testing --dry-run
   ```

3. Observe that every command exits `0`, displays the supplied modifier where applicable, and reports `Components order: theme`.

4. Confirm the missing skill payload with a real isolated-home install:

   ```bash
   HOME="$tmp/home-real" "$tmp/gentle-ai" install \
     --agent claude-code --component theme --skill go-testing

   find "$tmp/home-real" -path '*/skills/go-testing/SKILL.md' -print
   ```

5. Observe that `find` prints nothing even though the install reports success.

## ✅ Expected Behavior

The CLI should not report that an explicit component-scoped modifier was accepted and successfully processed when the selected plan cannot consume it. The outcome of every explicit modifier should be truthful and visible to the user.

## ❌ Actual Behavior

The CLI accepts the valid modifier, prints and persists its value, schedules only `theme`, applies none of the modifier's payload, emits no diagnostic, and exits `0`.

## Gentle AI Version

`gentle-ai 2.2.5-0.20260803170031-943fdea3ad39`

## Operating System

macOS

## AI Agent / Client

Claude Code

## 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

## 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
$ gentle-ai install --agent claude-code --component theme --persona neutral --dry-run
Persona: neutral
Components order: theme
exit=0

$ gentle-ai install --agent claude-code --component theme --sdd-mode multi --dry-run
SDD mode: multi
Components order: theme
exit=0

$ gentle-ai install --agent claude-code --component theme --skill go-testing --dry-run
Components order: theme
exit=0
```

## Additional Context

### Root cause

`NormalizeInstallFlags` resolves component-scoped modifiers independently in `internal/cli/validate.go:20-77`. When an explicit component list is present, `normalizeComponents` returns that list verbatim at `internal/cli/validate.go:106-125`; no rule cross-checks resolved modifiers against the components that would consume them.

The CLI already rejects invalid values such as an unsupported Persona, component, skill, SDD mode, or agent. Commit `09e4b14cbceb8ce75db5b78546e566031f702df9` specifically changed unknown agents from being silently dropped to being rejected. The missing case is a valid modifier whose work disappears because its consumer component is absent.

### Maintainer decision required

This report intentionally does not prescribe a remedy:

- Rejecting orphaned modifiers would preserve the existing fail-loudly principle, but it would change currently accepted CLI behavior and therefore requires breaking-change treatment under `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- Warning about orphaned modifiers would preserve compatibility, but the command would still exit `0` without applying the explicit payload.

The maintainers should choose that compatibility contract. The rule should cover the modifier class consistently rather than making Persona the only special case.

### Related issue

Issue #1702 includes the narrower symptom that `--persona` can be ignored when `persona` is excluded. It does not cover the shared `--persona` / `--sdd-mode` / `--skill` orphan-modifier class, so this report separates the systemic CLI defect from that issue's broader Persona and language-contract scope.

A design proposal for the validation rule follows in a comment on this issue. It is kept separate from this report on purpose, so the proposal can be rejected without invalidating the defect.

### Labels owed by a maintainer

Reported from a fork, so no triage rights here. This issue was filed through the API rather than the web form, so the `bug` and `status:needs-review` labels that `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml` normally applies are missing. Owed by a maintainer:

- `bug` and `status:needs-review`, which the template would have applied.
- `status:approved` before any PR against this issue can pass the `Check Issue Has status:approved` gate.
- A priority label.
- If the chosen remedy is to reject orphaned modifiers, `type:breaking-change` on the eventual PR.

title: bug(suite-wt): timeout leaves prunable worktree metadata and blocks retry
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and found no equivalent report.
- [x] I understand that a linked implementation requires maintainer approval.

### Bug Description

A timed-out `suite-wt` environment creation partially registered a Git worktree but did not leave an active environment or accessible worktree directory. The operation shape was one persistent worktree from a selected submodule with one required localization dependency, identified only as `rate-guard-slice-1`.

The health check passed before creation. The first provider call returned `MCP error -32001: Request timed out`, while native environment status did not list the requested environment. A retry then failed because the branch was reported as assigned to a worktree. After native status reconciliation, one further bounded attempt timed out again.

Final inspection found no active environment, directory, or runtime, but Git retained a prunable worktree registration whose gitdir referenced a nonexistent location. No consumer source code changed. Planning artifacts and tasks remained persisted, and implementation never started. These are observed outcomes only; no root cause is confirmed.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Confirm the read-only `suite-wt` health check passes.
2. Request one persistent worktree from a selected submodule and initialize one required dependency.
3. Let the provider operation exceed the client timeout.
4. Query native environment status.
5. If the environment is absent, retry the same logical request once.
6. Inspect the final environment list, expected directory, and Git worktree metadata.

### Expected Behavior

Creation should either return a complete active environment with its directory and runtime, or fail atomically without leaving branch assignment, worktree registration, directory, or runtime residue. A retry should be deterministic.

### Actual Behavior

The provider timed out after partially mutating Git worktree state. The environment, directory, and runtime were absent, but an orphaned prunable registration remained and blocked a clean retry.

### Environment

- Gentle AI: 2.2.4
- suite-wt build: CLI does not expose a version flag
- OS/architecture: macOS arm64
- Client: OpenCode
- Health check: passed, including Docker daemon/image and required local templates/repositories

### Bounded Attempt Outcomes

- Attempt 1: provider timeout; requested environment absent from native status.
- Attempt 2: retry rejected because the branch was already assigned to a worktree.
- Attempt 3: provider timeout after status reconciliation.
- Final mutation state: prunable Git worktree registration referencing a nonexistent location; no directory/runtime/source mutation.

### Additional Context

A regression test should inject timeout or cancellation at each creation phase and prove the operation either completes fully or removes every registration and runtime artifact needed for a clean retry.

title: bug(gga): claude provider times out silently on pre-commit review (v2.10.1)
body:
## Summary

The Gentleman Guardian Angel (GGA) pre-commit hook's AI code review step times out with no response from the provider, blocking `git commit` entirely.

## Environment

- GGA version: v2.10.1
- Provider: `claude`
- Rules file: `AGENTS.md`
- Trigger: pre-commit git hook (AI code review gate before allowing the commit)

## Observed behavior

The pre-commit hook sent a review request for a moderate batch of staged files (8 files, mix of `.js` source and `.test.js` files) to the configured `claude` provider.

- Attempt 1: hook printed progress at 30s intervals up to 300s, then presumably was interrupted externally before its own timeout fired (no terminal output/exit observed for that attempt).
- Attempt 2 (immediate retry, same staged files, same hook invocation): ran to completion of its own wait loop — progress logged every 30s up to 270s, then:

```
TIMEOUT: Provider did not respond within 300 seconds.
❌ Provider timed out after 300s
```

  Hook exited non-zero and the commit did not happen (no commit object created).

Both attempts: no response at all from the provider (not a rejection, not a partial result, not an error message from the provider itself) — just silence until the hook's own 300s watchdog fired.

## Expected behavior

Either:
1. The `claude` provider responds within the configured `TIMEOUT` window for a review of this size (8 files), or
2. If the provider call itself is going to exceed the timeout, the hook surfaces a more actionable diagnostic (e.g. whether the outbound request was ever sent/acknowledged, vs. hanging on the wire) instead of a bare "did not respond."

## Impact

Commit is fully blocked when this happens — there is no partial/degraded path, only the suggested workarounds (increase `TIMEOUT` in `.gga` config, review fewer files, or bypass the hook with `--no-verify`, which we deliberately did not do).

## Minimal repro shape

1. Configure GGA pre-commit hook with `provider: claude`, default `TIMEOUT` (300s).
2. Stage a batch of ~8 JS files matching the hook's include patterns (mix of implementation + test files), none unusually large.
3. Run `git commit`.
4. Observe the provider call hang with periodic "still waiting" progress logs until the 300s watchdog fires, with no response ever received from the provider.

## Notes

- Reproduced twice in a row (back-to-back attempts), same outcome both times — not a one-off blip.
- No `--no-verify` or other bypass was used; commit is currently still pending on our end.

title: bug(opencode): general worker completes with empty task result
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and found no tracker for this general-worker case.
- [x] I understand that PRs require maintainer approval on the linked issue.

### 📝 Bug Description

A general-purpose read-only worker launched through OpenCode can report `completed` while returning an empty `<task_result>`. Resuming the same worker once to request the missing report can again report `completed` with an empty result.

This is the same observable boundary as the SDD reports in #2117, but maintainers explicitly scoped that issue to SDD phases and requested a separate tracker for general workers.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch a `general` worker through OpenCode for read-only verification of a disposable local prototype, with an explicit structured textual return contract.
2. Let the worker reach the completed state.
3. Observe an empty `<task_result>` with no report or typed failure.
4. Resume the same worker once and explicitly request the missing report.
5. Observe another completed wrapper with an empty `<task_result>`.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

A completed general worker returns the requested non-empty verification report, or a typed incomplete/failure envelope describing why it could not report.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Both bounded attempts completed with empty results. No verification status, command evidence, findings, mutation evidence, or typed failure reached the parent workflow.

### Gentle AI Version

2.2.4

### Operating System

Linux (Other), x86_64

### AI Agent / Client

OpenCode 1.18.13

### 📋 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```text
Attempt 1: state=completed, task_result=<empty>
Attempt 2 (same resumed worker): state=completed, task_result=<empty>
```

### Additional Context

**Operation shape**

The delegated actor was a read-only independent verifier for a disposable prototype. It was instructed not to edit the prototype or consumer repository and to return a structured PASS/FAIL report with command evidence. The second attempt reused the same worker context and requested only the missing report.

**Mutation and preserved-state outcome**

- The consumer repository remained clean before and after both attempts.
- No source mutation, staging, commit, push, pull request, review, or downstream workflow was attributed to the silent worker.
- The disposable prototype remains preserved.
- The consumer stopped fail-closed at the independent-verification boundary and did not infer PASS.

**Minimal reproduction**

1. Create any disposable local artifact that can be inspected read-only.
2. Launch a `general` worker with a structured textual result contract.
3. Observe `completed` with an empty result.
4. Resume that exact worker once to request the report.
5. Observe a second empty completed result.

**Related reports**

- #2117 tracks SDD-phase empty results. A maintainer clarified that general workers need a separate tracker: https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/2117#issuecomment-5187449936
- #387 covered a historical last-tool-call response-loss mechanism. The root cause of this occurrence is not confirmed.

Safe reason identifier: `GENERAL_WORKER_EMPTY_RESULT`.

This report contains observed evidence only. It intentionally excludes raw arguments, absolute paths, private project names, usernames, hostnames, credentials, environment values, source contents, and diffs.

body:

## Bug Description

Native-Windows tests invoke POSIX commands and shells that are not guaranteed in a supported PowerShell environment. The suite therefore fails before testing the intended behavior.

`TestRunStrategyUsesCaskOwnershipAndMigrationGuidance` fails because `printf` is absent from `PATH`. The local root full suite also fails `TestSDDEditAuthorityConsentGrantLoop` because `sh` is absent, and several `internal/update` release-script tests require WSL or `bash`.

main @ c18e51282b665d4dd94eef606bdab9bca985e010

title: .claude/CLAUDE.md mandates tools unavailable on Windows and prescribes brew
body:
## Summary

The generated `.claude/CLAUDE.md` mandates a toolchain that does not exist on Windows, and points at an installer that does not run there either. Because the file is managed by `gentle-ai`, a local fix is reverted on the next sync.

## Environment

- gentle-ai 1.46.0
- Windows 11 Pro (26200), Git Bash
- Agent: Claude Code

## The rule

`.claude/CLAUDE.md`, under `## Rules`:

> Never use cat/grep/find/sed/ls. Use bat/rg/fd/sd/eza instead. Install via brew if missing.

## What is actually available

```
$ for t in bat rg fd eza sd brew; do command -v $t >/dev/null && echo "OK   $t" || echo "MISS $t"; done
MISS bat
OK   rg
MISS fd
MISS eza
MISS sd
MISS brew
```

Only `rg` is present. `brew` is not a Windows package manager, so the stated remedy cannot be followed.

## Impact

1. `.claude/CLAUDE.md` loads on every session, in every project, so the cost is paid on every task.
2. The agent either violates the rule or burns turns discovering the tools are absent — I hit exit code 127 twice in one session before checking.
3. The file is in gentle-ai's managed set (it appears in the install/sync backup manifest alongside `.claude/settings.json`), so editing it locally is not a durable fix.

## Suggested direction

Two options, not mutually exclusive:

- **State the outcome instead of the toolchain.** Something like "prefer the agent's native file-read and search tools over shelling out to `cat`/`grep`/`find`" is shorter, needs no install, and stays correct on every platform. The current phrasing is a blanket prohibition whose remedy is unavailable.
- **Make the install hint platform-aware** — `scoop`/`winget` on Windows, `brew` on macOS — if the toolchain requirement is intentional.

Happy to send a PR if you tell me which direction you prefer.

title: bug(opencode): plugin installation fails when tui.json already contains sub-agent-statusline
body:
## Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`.

## Bug Description

Gentle AI's OpenCode plugin installation fails when the existing OpenCode TUI configuration already contains the `opencode-subagent-statusline` plugin. The failure affects both community plugins selected by the installer, even though one of them is already present in `tui.json`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Gentle AI and launch its interactive installer.
2. Select the OpenCode agent.
3. Select the OpenCode community plugins:
   - Sub-agent Statusline
   - SDD Engram Manager
4. Have an existing `~/.config/opencode/tui.json` containing the `opencode-subagent-statusline` plugin, for example:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/tui.json",
  "plugin": [
    "opencode-subagent-statusline"
  ]
}
```

5. Run the Gentle AI installation.

## Expected Behavior

The installer should parse the existing `tui.json`, preserve existing plugins, and add any missing selected plugins. If the existing file is unsupported or invalid, it should report the exact validation problem before attempting the plugin pipeline.

## Actual Behavior

The installation pipeline fails while processing both OpenCode plugins:

```text
FAILED: opencode-plugin:sub-agent-statusline — parse OpenCode TUI config "/home/antryx/.config/opencode/tui.json": invalid character ']' looking for beginning of value
FATLED: opencode-plugin: sdd-engram-plugin — parse OpenCode TUI config "/home/antryx/.config/opencode/tui.json"

pipeline completed with errors

invalid character ']' looking for beginning of value
```

The installation does not reach 100% completion.

Removing the existing plugin entry and leaving the file with an empty plugin list allowed the installation to complete successfully:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/tui.json",
  "plugin": []
}
```

## Environment

- Gentle AI: `gentle-ai 2.2.4`
- Operating System: CachyOS Linux, x86_64 (`Linux 7.1.5-1-cachyos`)
- OpenCode: `1.18.13`
- Affected area: TUI / OpenCode community plugin installation

## Logs / Error Output

See the exact output under **Actual Behavior**. A screenshot is available from the reproduction and can be attached if needed.

## Additional Context

The relevant configuration path is:

```text
$HOME/.config/opencode/tui.json
```

The implementation appears intended to preserve existing TUI plugins and append missing plugins, so this may be related to parsing or handling an existing plugin list rather than an expected conflict.

title: Engram can persist an ambient-project session summary despite explicit project targeting
body:
## Observed behavior
A planning-only artifact operation that explicitly selects one project can also create a session summary under the ambient project context.

## Expected behavior
Only the explicitly selected project receives persistence. Ambient context must not receive an additional summary.

## Actual behavior
The explicit artifact save reported success, while an additional session-summary record was reported under the ambient project. This creates cross-scope attribution ambiguity and blocks the consumer workflow.

## Minimal reproduction
1. Start from an ambient context for project A.
2. Run a planning-only persistence operation with an explicit target project B and an artifact topic.
3. Observe the explicit save result and inspect returned project attribution.
4. An additional session summary may be recorded for project A.

## Environment
- Gentle AI: 2.3.0-rc.1.0.20260804224658-d8c770829e70
- OS: Windows x64
- Client: OpenCode
- Operation shape: planning-only artifact persistence with explicit project targeting

## Bounded evidence
Observed during one planning-only attempt. No source, service, or external-state mutation was performed. The consumer workflow was halted rather than accepting or moving the ambiguous artifact.

## Scope note
This report describes observed attribution outcomes only; it does not assert a root cause.

title: feat(system): Android/Termux support aligned with core-termux migration (umbrella #2501+#2502+#2142)
body:
## Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

## 📝 Description

Child umbrella of the Android/Termux support goal. The maintainer's official decomposition in #2501 (GOOS=android routes through the existing linux package-manager probe loop instead of a hardcoded `"pkg"` case) and #2502 (installcmd: no `sudo` + npm-prefix writability) supersede my earlier monolithic branch `fix/2143`. This issue tracks implementation **aligned with core-termux v4.18+**, which is the migration tool the user runs to port gentle-ai + CodeGraph + termux-api to a fresh Android device.

**Goal:** a fresh Android/Termux device receives the same patched/stabilized state as the current device, with NO personal paths leaked and NO hardcoded sudo/pkg/npm assumptions.

### Strategic scope: core-termux is an AI-agent platform, not just gentle-ai
`core list ai` reveals core-termux is a platform managing **25 AI agents**, not merely the gentle-ai suite.

**Installed:** OpenCode (default), Engram, CodeGraph, Pi Coding Agent, Gentle AI, Gentleman Guardian Angel, Context7, OpenSpec.

**Available (not yet installed):** Qwen Code (`--qwen-code`), Gemini CLI (`--gemini-cli`), Claude Code (`--claude-code`), Mistral Vibe (`--mistral-vibe`), OpenClaude (`--openclaude`), OpenClaw (`--openclaw`), Ollama (`--ollama`), Codex CLI (`--codex`), Qoder CLI (`--qoder`), KiloCode CLI (`--kilocode-cli`), Cursor CLI (`--cursor-cli`), Kimchi (`--kimchi`), MiMoCode (`--mimocode`), Oh-My-Pi (`--oh-my-pi`), Antigravity CLI (`--antigravity-cli`), Minimax CLI (`--minimax-cli`), Hermes Agent (`--hermes-agent`), Kimi Code (`--kimi-code`), Command Code (`--command-code`), Freebuff (`--freebuff`), SuperCode CLI (`--supercode`), Cline CLI (`--cline`), AMP Code CLI (`--ampcode`).

Because each of these can be installed with `core install ai --<flag>` and shares the same Termux/sudo/npm-prefix/probe-loop surface, the fixes in #2501 (no hardcoded `pkg`; route android through the linux probe loop) and #2502 (no `sudo` on android; `detectNpmWritable` reports real `$PREFIX` prefix writability instead of the `$HOME` heuristic) are **platform-level**: they reduce maintenance load for the maintainer across all 25 agents, not only gentle-ai, on every Android/Termux device.

### Dependency chain (official)
#2533 (this umbrella) → #2501 (android detection via probe loop) → #2502 (installcmd: no sudo + npm-prefix writability) → #2141 (Engram asset mapping) → #2142 (termux-open-url).

### Device evidence (SM-G965F, aarch64, Termux, core-termux-managed)
- `GOOS=android`, `GOARCH=arm64`.
- `apt` lives at `$PREFIX/bin/apt` (`pkg` is an `apt` wrapper; route android through the linux probe loop, distro=debian → apt, no `"pkg"` hardcode).
- `npm prefix -g` returns `$PREFIX` (data/data/com.termux/files/usr), NOT under `$HOME`. The home-prefix heuristic in `detectNpmWritable` must be replaced by real writability, otherwise Termux forces `sudo npm` (which fails — no sudo).
- CodeGraph: installed by core-termux as a **node wrapper** (data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin/codegraph execs `node $HOME/.local/share/core-termux-data/codegraph-linux-arm64/lib/dist/bin/codegraph.js`). Resolve via `exec.LookPath("codegraph")`, never `npm install`, never bundle.
- `termux-open-url` present in `$PREFIX/bin` (requires `termux-api`).

## ✅ Expected Behavior
- `android` is accepted by `IsSupportedOS` and resolves `PackageManager` via the SAME probe loop as linux (apt, not a hardcoded `"pkg"` case).
- `installcmd` never `sudo`-prefixed on android; `NpmWritable` reflects real `$PREFIX` writability.
- CodeGraph resolved via `exec.LookPath("codegraph")` with a clear setup hint when absent.
- Fresh Android device migrates to the same working state using core-termux.

## 🧪 Verification
- CI: `GOOS=android GOARCH=arm64` cross-build + unit tests for `IsSupportedOS(android)=true`, npm prefix writability, and `codegraph` LookPath.
- On-device: boot probe on Termux (bionic), real `$PREFIX`, codegraph.js execution.

Refs: #2501, #2502, #2141, #2142, #1291.

title: fix(cli): restore --yes=false and --list=false exit 0 without restoring, listing, or reporting
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

`gentle-ai restore --yes=false` and `gentle-ai restore --list=false` exit 0 having done nothing at all. No restore, no listing, no error, no output.

The value-bearing form of these boolean flags parses successfully but bypasses the pre-scan variables that decide what the command actually does, so `parseCommandFlags` returns success and the command falls through silently.

A silent success is the worst available outcome here. A caller scripting `gentle-ai restore --yes=false` reads exit 0 as "the restore happened", and nothing in the output contradicts that.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `gentle-ai restore --yes=false` and observe no output and exit code 0.
2. Run `gentle-ai restore --list=false` and observe no output and exit code 0.
3. Run `gentle-ai restore --list` and observe it correctly prints the available backups, confirming the command works in its normal form.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

One of two, and the choice is a maintainer call:

- **Honor the value.** `--list=false` behaves as if `--list` were absent, `--yes=false` behaves as if `--yes` were absent, and the command proceeds down its normal path for the remaining arguments.
- **Refuse the form.** Reject `--yes=<value>` and `--list=<value>` as unsupported with a nonzero exit and a message naming the accepted form.

Either is defensible. What is not defensible is exiting 0 without acting, because that is indistinguishable from success.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Both invocations exit 0 and do nothing. The pre-scan that decides whether to list or to restore never sees the flag, and no branch reports that the requested operation did not run.

### Gentle AI Version

v2.3.0-rc.1 and current `main` (`7aa971d7`)

### Operating System

Linux (Arch/Manjaro)

### AI Agent / Client

Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```
$ gentle-ai restore --yes=false
$ echo $?
0

$ gentle-ai restore --list=false
$ echo $?
0

$ gentle-ai restore --list
Available backups (5):
  [1] <timestamp>  sync — <date> (124 files)  [<version>]
  ...
$ echo $?
0
```

### Additional Context

Surfaced by CodeRabbit while reviewing #2154, which touches `parseCommandFlags` in `internal/cli/restore.go`.

**This is pre-existing, not a regression from that PR.** I verified it by building current `main` (`7aa971d7`) with the PR not applied and reproducing both invocations identically there. Filing it separately so #2154 stays scoped to the `--help` work and does not grow its diff further.

Deliberately filed without an implementation, since the expected behavior above is a genuine choice between two reasonable contracts rather than a single obvious fix.

title: feat(installcmd): android privilege shape, no sudo on Termux and real npm-prefix writability (slice 4 of #2143)
body:
## Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

## 📝 Description

Child of #2143, slice 4, found during design: the series' biggest unlisted breaker on Termux is privilege shape, not detection.

1. Termux has no `sudo`. `internal/installcmd/resolver.go` and the codex/gemini/qwen agent adapters emit `sudo apt-get install -y ...` and `sudo npm install -g ...`; on Termux the exec fails with command-not-found even though unprivileged `apt`/`npm` would succeed.
2. Compounding it, `detectNpmWritable` (internal/system/detect.go) uses a home-prefix heuristic ("npm prefix under $HOME"); on Termux the npm prefix is `$PREFIX`, not under home, so `NpmWritable=false` guarantees the sudo prefix on every npm command. Fixing the heuristic to test actual writability of the npm prefix also helps non-Termux setups with nonstandard prefixes.

## ✅ Expected Behavior

On android, install commands are never sudo-prefixed. `NpmWritable` reflects real writability of the npm prefix rather than its path shape.

## 🧪 Verification

Fully testable in CI: the resolver takes a profile, and the writability check is injectable. Genuine RED first for both parts.

## 🖥️ Environment

`main` at `ba95a709`. Refs #2143 (parent). Sequencing note: `internal/installcmd/resolver.go` is currently being changed by the PR for #2499; whichever lands second rebases.
