title: feat(cli): choose a single source of truth for the command inventory and its drift-proofing contract
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Problem Statement

`internal/app/app.go` dispatches first-level commands through a large `switch`, while `internal/app/help.go` documents them as hand-written prose. The two lists have no mechanical relationship.

Adding a `case` without adding a help line produces a working but undocumented command, and nothing detects it. The reverse is equally possible: a documented command that does not exist.

#2155 is one instance of this, where `codegraph` is dispatched but absent from the help. That one line is being fixed there and needs no decision. This issue is the structural question #2155 was asked to stop short of, per @dnlrsls's review on it: which source of truth the command inventory should have, and what contract prevents the two lists from drifting again.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

The outcome to reach, stated before the mechanism: a command cannot be dispatched without also being documented, and a documented command cannot fail to exist, because both come from the same declaration. A test can then assert the two sets are equal, which is not expressible today.

Deliberately filed without a chosen mechanism. Requesting a maintainer decision on which of the alternatives below to pursue before any PR is opened, so the work does not arrive pre-committed to an architecture that was never selected.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

1. **Full command table replacing the `switch`.** Entries carry name, one-line description, and handler. `gentle-ai --help` renders from the table instead of restating it. Strongest guarantee, because agreement holds by construction. Largest diff, and it touches a heavily exercised dispatcher.
2. **Keep the `switch`, add a declarative registry used only for rendering help, plus a test asserting the registry and the `switch` agree.** Much smaller and lower risk to the dispatcher. The agreement is enforced by a test rather than by construction.
3. **Keep both hand-written and add only the equality test.** Smallest change. Catches drift at CI time instead of preventing it, and leaves the duplication in place.

I lean toward option 2, since it buys most of the guarantee at a fraction of the risk to the dispatcher. That is a stated preference, not an assumed decision.

### 📎 Additional Context

Split out of #2155 at @dnlrsls's request, so the immediate help correction there can proceed independently of this design.

Related: #2155 (the immediate `codegraph` help entry), #2153 (per-command `--help` behavior).

title: meta: the 20 roots behind ~250 open issues, and what done means
body:
All 438 open issues were read in full on 2026-08-04 against `main` at `9b2cf201`, partitioned by number so coverage is complete rather than keyword-filtered. Every root below was verified by reading the code, not inferred from the threads.

This issue exists to answer one question: **when are we actually done?**

## The measurement

| | Count |
|---|---|
| Open issues | 438 |
| Explained by the 20 roots below | ~250 |
| Features and design requests, no defect | ~110 |
| Genuine standalones | ~50 |
| Already fixed on main, nobody closed them | ~10 |

**Roughly 250 reports come from 20 causes.** Fixing them one at a time is why the backlog grows: 262 filed against 151 closed in the last seven days.

## Definition of done

This list is finished when every root in Tier 1 and Tier 2 is closed with a named test, and every issue attached to it is closed against that test. Tier 3 needs a maintainer decision before any code is written, and does not block the others.

That is the finish line. Not zero open issues, which is not a real target for a widely used tool.

---

## Tier 1: blocking the release candidate

These make the current build unusable for most users. Nothing else matters until they land.

| # | Root | Issues | Fix shape | State |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Transport gate shipped without its key.** OpenCode and Codex are declared eligible and then refused, so they cannot start a review at all. ~45 of the newest reports come from those runtimes and are currently unreproducible on their own runtime. | ~9 direct, ~45 blocked | merge #2448, then decide Codex | in flight |
| 2 | **The documented invocation fails.** The negotiated form our own contract documents returns a non-retryable stop on a fresh repository. | all consumers | relax the identity gate | in flight |
| 3 | **Our protocol tells orchestrators to refuse this prerelease.** "Resume only after an installed released fix" reads as stable-only. | community testing | wording, 12 assets | fixed, pending PR |
| 4 | **Hardcoded `claude-code` identity.** In the shared contract asset and in the refusal the binary prints, so a Codex or OpenCode user who copies the printed command impersonates Claude Code and walks through the transport gate. | #2440 | name the caller's runtime | in flight |
| 5 | **Credential disclosure.** Untracked credential files swept into the candidate and their contents delivered to the reviewer. | #2394, #2293 | scope stops being implicit | in flight |
| 6 | **`review-ledger-contract.md` is never deployed.** The only file in embedded `_shared/` that does not ship. #2462 rewrote its contents but not its deployment, so the continuation table reaches nobody. | #2038 | deploy it | not started |

## Tier 2: the roots that explain the flood

Ordered by issues explained.

| # | Root | Issues | Fix shape |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7 | **A terminal is defined to carry no runnable exit.** `stop` "intentionally contains no command-shaped data", and 25 call sites route 16 reason codes into it. Highest severity class in this project. | ~34 | **delete the `stop` kind.** Every terminal is `execute` or `collect`; anything that cannot name one is a missing operation, not a state |
| 8 | **One message, many causes.** The typed error is discarded at the boundary and replaced with a constant. `GitCommandError` already carries args, exit code and output; the envelope throws all three away, and the branch beside it does not | ~32 | project the typed cause instead of constructing strings |
| 9 | **Prose contracts nothing enforces.** The product declares an obligation in rendered instruction text and accepts a self-report as proof | ~25 | mostly Tier 3, some are one concrete identifier written into the asset |
| 10 | **Hand-maintained lists mirroring a truth computed elsewhere.** `_shared/` ships 8 files; three independent lists say 7, 6 and 6 | ~24 | `walkEmbeddedFiles` already exists. **Delete the copies** |
| 11 | **Environment capability assumed rather than probed.** No `cmd.Dir`, hardcoded localhost ports, no android case | ~22 | probe then degrade |
| 12 | **Partial mutation, success reported from the attempt rather than a read-back.** Seven separate reports, seven reporters, one invariant | ~22 | have the writer report whether replacement occurred, deleting the inference at every call site |
| 13 | **Two authorities disagree.** `sdd-status` computes readiness independently of what `acquire` would return; every review verb re-derives validity | ~19 | one predicate, delete the second derivation |
| 14 | **Repository-global authority validation.** One unreadable entry fails the whole per-repository inventory closed, across every worktree sharing the common dir | ~16 | scope to the lineage under operation |
| 15 | **Closed compile-time enums.** Every new agent is a Go change across 6 files; every unlisted Linux distro is a dead end | ~15 | the brew probe at `detect.go:135` already bypasses the distro enum. Generalize it and **delete** `detectLinuxDistro` and its three helpers |
| 16 | **Update advertises one version and installs another; the swap is neither durable nor verified.** No `Sync`, bare rename, digest taken from the in-memory stream | ~13 | the post-condition check already exists in the Homebrew path. Hoist it, delete the per-strategy assumptions |
| 17 | **Windows shipped without a green lane.** The job declared a 30-minute timeout around a 35-minute step, so it was always cancelled and 19 to 27 failures shipped unseen | ~9 | one CI fix, then the defects it reveals |
| 18 | **Gates demand exact identity equality with the receipt.** Commit shape, path-set equality in both directions, tracked/untracked representation | ~7 | Tier 3 |
| 19 | **Install and uninstall have no per-step commit boundary** and no record of what they own | ~5 | per-agent commit plus an owned-key manifest |
| 20 | **A transition names an operation with no invocation.** `review.recover` and five others are absent from the operation registry, so `kind: execute` ships with an empty command | 3 | six registry rows |

## The verification hole that let this happen

Worth stating plainly, because it answers "how did three days of validation miss this".

**`bench/classify.go:291` accepts any non-empty `execute.operation` and never requires `execute.command`.** We had journeys asserting the user receives a runnable exit, and the classifier never checked whether the exit carried a command. Root 20's output scored as `in_band`.

**No test runs the commands we document.** The journeys build invocations by reading the code, so the documented form was never executed once. That is roots 2 and 4.

**The shell E2E runs Tier 1 only on pull requests** (#2466), and a `set -e` leak truncates the suite at the first unguarded assertion, so a failing run under-reports what it found.

Three separate ways for a green check to mean less than its name. All three are being closed.

## Tier 3: needs a maintainer decision before code

No work starts on these until the decision is made.

1. ~~Does a receipt bind to **content identity** or to a Git representation?~~ **DECIDED 2026-08-08: content identity.** Decided and substantially applied: the 5-value candidate-relation classifier and compatible-base-advance already ship across `gate.go`, `receipt.go`, `prepr.go` and `compact_recovery_binding.go`, and `PathsDigest` makes the reviewed path-set part of the receipt's own content identity. Root 18's remaining scope is a pattern sweep for surviving representation constraints, not a design question.
2. ~~Does Codex stay `Eligible: true` with `unsupported` transport?~~ **DECIDED 2026-08-08: dissolved by the shared advisory transport.** Claude Code, OpenCode and Codex ride one solution (`internal/advisoryreview/contract.go:31-33`) and eligibility is computed from the compiled capability (`review_transport_capability.go:62-64`), never declared by hand. Kilo stays dormant rather than eligible-but-refused, which is the principle this question was really asking for.
3. ~~Does `sdd-status` stop computing readiness and start reporting what `acquire` would return?~~ **RESOLVED BY IMPLEMENTATION, better than asked.** Not a delegation: one predicate, `runtimeReadiness` (`runtime_compact.go:137`), consumed by ten call sites across `runtime_compact.go` and `status.go`. Neither surface asks the other; both ask the same function. Building the delegation now would reintroduce the round trip this deleted.
4. ~~Is the orchestrator/executor distinction enforced at runtime, or does it stay prose?~~ **DECIDED 2026-08-08: neither, per invariant.** An obligation moves from prose to runtime when its violation produces reports, and it is enforced as a concrete invariant (a gate, a binding, an authorized root, like the reviewer's no-tools admission or `blocked(edit_authority_missing)`), never as a general role system. Workflow guidance whose violation costs quality rather than authority stays prose. This turns the decision into a triage criterion instead of a project.
5. ~~Does Pi's asset contract move in-repo, or does the boundary become visible so those reports route to `gentle-pi`?~~ **DECIDED 2026-08-08: gentle-ai is the generator, the boundary becomes visible.** The assets themselves are generated in gentle-ai and gentle-pi consumes them, so the source of truth already lives here; what crosses the boundary gets a version handshake and a mismatch error that names `gentle-pi` and the expected version, so those reports route there instead of arriving here mute. The v2.2.0 pin bump that broke every negotiated START is the scar this prevents.

## Bias applied throughout

Every fix shape above was checked against one rule: **the correct fix usually deletes or relaxes something.** Where a proposal adds a state, a flag, a config option, or a parallel representation of existing truth, it is marked as a smell and the removal is named instead. Roots 7, 10, 12, 13, 15 and 16 are all net deletions.

## Progress, 2026-08-04

Updated live as work lands. A box is checked only when the fix is merged into `main` with a named test.

### Tier 1

- [x] **2. The documented invocation fails** — merged, #2472 closes #2473. Verified on the main binary: the un-flagged form now answers instead of returning a non-retryable stop.
- [x] **3. Our protocol tells orchestrators to refuse this prerelease** — merged, #2475 closes #2474. One clause across 12 assets.
- [x] **1. Transport gate shipped without its key** — merged #2479 at `fbd08500`. Verified by `TestReviewPluginInjectsProviderOwnedLensContext`, `TestReviewPluginRefusesLensContextBoundToAnotherCandidate`, and `TestReviewPluginRefusesUnterminatedLensContext`; fresh CI run `30953888210` passed.
- [x] **4. Hardcoded `claude-code` identity** — merged #2484 at `d8c77082`. Verified by `TestGoldenSDD_OpenCode_Multi`, `TestAllRuntimeAssetsDeclareTheirRuntimeIdentity`, and `TestDocumentedInvocationsRunAsDocumented`; fresh CI run `30956861677` passed.
- [x] **5. Credential disclosure** — merged #2491 at `52adc258`. Verified by `TestNegotiatedStartKeepsUndeclaredUntrackedFileOutOfCandidate`, `TestNegotiatedStartKeepsDeclaredUntrackedFileInCandidate`, and `TestReviewerLensContextOmitsUndeclaredUntrackedBytes`; fresh CI run `30959490647` passed.
- [x] **6. `review-ledger-contract.md` is never deployed** — done. Shipped in embedded `skills/_shared/` and consumed by `internal/components/sdd/boundedreview.go:12`.

### Tier 2

- [ ] **7. A terminal carries no runnable exit** — phase 1 complete, see findings below. Slices sequenced, the wedge first.
- [ ] **8. One message, many causes** — not started. Blocked behind root 20's file.
- [x] **10. Hand-maintained lists** — done. `SharedSkillFileNames()` walks the embedded directory (`internal/assets/shared_skill_files.go`) and its contract forbids any deployment path from keeping a literal list; the three disagreeing copies are gone.
- [ ] **11. Environment assumed rather than probed** — not started.
- [ ] **12. Partial mutation, success from the attempt** — in flight, scoped to the durability core.
- [x] **13. Two authorities disagree** — #2515 unifies `sdd-status` with `acquire`, and #2488 makes the artifact map store-derived. `TestEveryArtifactMapBuilderSatisfiesTheV1Projection`; fresh CI run `30952693620` passed.
- [x] **14. Repository-global authority validation** — CLOSED 2026-08-08 on its third round. #2495 fixed the reported sites; #2743/#2741 (`428471d9`) fixed four more walks; #2796 fixed the repair surface (D5). Verified by pattern grep: `EntryDiagnostics) > 0` returns zero across non-test sources, and `compact_scoped_walks_test.go` pins the unreadable-is-absent behavior. Three rounds, each with passing tests, is this root's whole lesson.
- [x] **15. Closed compile-time enums** — VERIFIED DONE 2026-08-08, was never started because it was already fixed. `detectLinuxDistro` does not exist; `resolvePlatformProfile` (`internal/system/detect.go:150`) probes `linuxPackageManagers` for what is installed and states "the distro is reported, never gated on".
- [ ] **16. Update advertises one version and installs another** — partly covered by root 12's slice.
- [ ] **17. Windows shipped without a green lane** — in flight. The lane is sharded and reporting for the first time.
- [ ] **19. Install and uninstall have no commit boundary** — not started.
- [x] **20. A transition names an operation with no invocation** — merged 2026-08-04, #2477 closed #1864 and #1865. Root 8's "blocked behind root 20" note is therefore stale; root 8 is startable.

### What phase 1 of root 7 corrected

Three assumptions in this issue were wrong and are corrected here rather than quietly edited above.

**`review abandon` and `review invalidate` are not the honest terminal exit.** Their preconditions accept only pristine states, and that set is disjoint from every state that reaches `stop`. #1996, #1925, #2168 and #2014 are people discovering that. A state whose only honest content is a code is a missing operation wearing a state's clothes.

**#2422's two anomaly classes are not stop reason codes.** They are recovery-edge classes surfaced through `review inspect-authority`. Same root, different envelope. A fix touching one surface closes half the cluster.

**The batch-reconcile-journal wedge blocks its own escape hatches.** A single stale file wedges an entire Git common-dir, and both `inspect-authority` and `abandon` refuse with the same error. The negotiated envelope, the only surface agents may route from, never mentions the file exists. Pulled forward ahead of everything else in root 7.

**Deleting the `stop` kind is viable.** The schema enum is permissive and there are zero fixtures containing `"kind": "stop"`, so ceasing to emit it validates unchanged. Of the 16 codes, 8 already have a runnable exit the provider can assemble and simply does not route.

### The verification holes, closing

- [x] **The corpus accepted an execute with no command** — PR #2477. The deeper leak was worse than stated: a journey titled "the printed transition executes exactly as printed" never read the printed command, it rebuilt one by splitting the operation name. The fix adds a guard that fails the run on any dead execute transition, blocking or not, so no future commit can teach a call site to accept the broken shape.
- [ ] **No test runs the commands we document** — open. This is what let roots 2 and 4 ship.
- [ ] **The shell E2E runs Tier 1 only on pull requests, and truncates on failure** — #2466, open.

### Also found while working, not in the original 20

- [x] **#2346** — merged #2488 at `36052a91`; the store-derived artifact map is pinned by `TestEveryArtifactMapBuilderSatisfiesTheV1Projection`.
- [ ] **#2451 rollback gap** — merged. Reachable on the released binary, and `resolveOpenClawWorkspaceDir` ignores `--scope` entirely, so it was never limited to workspace scope.
- [ ] **#1770** — the PR template ships `Closes #42` inside an HTML comment and both PR gates read the raw body without stripping comments. Confirmed by walking into it: applying labels from a PR's linked issues wrongly labelled a closed Debian install report.
- [ ] **563 workflow runs await manual approval**, so fork contributors' PRs have never had CI run. Their required checks read as green because nothing ever reported. Left as-is by maintainer decision.

title: Delegated documentation tasks may remove pre-existing untracked directories
body:
### Bug description

A delegated direct documentation workflow appears to have removed a pre-existing, untracked source directory despite explicit instructions not to modify it. The exact mutation actor is unknown; this report describes the observed outcome rather than a confirmed root cause.

### Expected behavior

Delegated tasks must preserve unrelated tracked and untracked workspace content. A read-only or scoped documentation task must not delete a pre-existing untracked directory.

### Actual behavior

A pre-existing untracked directory containing Markdown source material was observed before delegation. After two bounded delegated documentation tasks, the directory was absent. A later task result also claimed that the source directory did not exist, contradicting the earlier inspection. No deletion was requested. The content was not recoverable through Git because it was untracked.

### Minimal reproduction

1. In a Git worktree, create an untracked directory containing a Markdown file.
2. Ask the orchestrator to audit that directory against existing documentation, then delegate a scoped documentation update with an explicit instruction not to modify unrelated files.
3. Inspect the working tree after each delegated task.
4. Observe whether the untracked directory remains present and unchanged.

### Environment

- Gentle AI: 2.2.4
- OS: macOS on Apple architecture
- Client: OpenCode
- Operation shape: two sequential delegated direct documentation tasks; no parallel writers, no requested deletion, no commits.

### Bounded evidence

- Initial inspection: the untracked directory was present and its Markdown files were successfully audited.
- After the delegated tasks: the directory was no longer present; Git status no longer listed it.
- The task results otherwise reported successful documentation updates and successful static/build validation.
- Consumer state was preserved after discovery: no further implementation work was launched, and the remaining working-tree changes were left untouched.

### Impact

This can silently destroy user-authored, untracked source material. The mutation outcome should be visible and prevented or require explicit authorization.

title: fix(review): judge and refuter agents can read live state while adjudicating a frozen candidate
body:
## Problem

Adversarial verification of #2417 surfaced two pre-existing gaps adjacent to the review lenses, both untouched by that work and both on the same review surface.

**The refuter holds `read: true` with no permission block** (`internal/components/sdd/inject.go:972`, byte-identical before and after #2417). It is also absent from `reviewerRoles`, so `internal/assets/claude/agents/review-refuter.md` ships with no immutable-transport clause at all. The refuter's whole job is adjudicating whether a claim about a frozen candidate holds, and it can currently read the live worktree while doing so.

**The judges hold read plus MCP tools.** `internal/assets/claude/agents/jd-judge-a.md` and `jd-judge-b.md` declare `Read, Glob, Grep` plus engram `mem_search` and `mem_get_observation`. The OpenCode judges hold only `read`.

## Why it matters

After #2417 the OpenCode lens holds no shell, no read tool, no MCP tool and cannot spawn a nested agent. A review whose lenses are structurally confined but whose refuter and judges are not has a guarantee only as strong as its weakest adjudicator. A refuter that reads live state can refute a genuine finding using bytes the lens was never allowed to see.

## Work

Bring both roles under the same shape the lenses now use: evidence materialized by the provider, no live-state access. The refuter additionally needs its immutable-transport clause, which means adding it to `reviewerRoles` so its asset is rendered rather than shipped raw.

## Related

#2417 (the lens shape this should match), #2419 (Claude Code lens hardening, same class), #2209.

title: refactor(review): delete orphaned review authority after the SDD clean break
body:
## Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] The full #3417 and #3564 cleanup cluster was audited against current main.
- [x] Existing issues and pull requests were searched before reusing this approved tracker.
- [x] This issue is the non-SDD follow-up. #3564 owns the SDD clean break.

## Outcome

Delete every review/RDD production surface outside SDD that becomes orphaned after #3564 removes its final consumer. Retain only code with a named live path in the current atomic compact-v2 lifecycle.

This is deletion, not migration. Historical formats, versions, bindings, receipts, recovery shells, switches, and compatibility readers carry no lifecycle authority and are not recognized by the replacement implementation.

## Dependency

This work begins after #3564 lands its complete SDD cleanup. The post-#3564 source tree is the only valid reachability baseline. Pre-#3564 references do not justify retaining a provider whose final consumer is scheduled for deletion.

## Maintainer Decisions

### D1. No backward compatibility

Old review formats and authority representations are unsupported. A replaced version fails closed with one actionable instruction to start a fresh atomic review. There is no dual reader, compatibility translator, migration, record rewrite, or legacy fallback.

### D2. Preserve only the live atomic lifecycle

The retained review lifecycle is:

```text
candidate consent → freeze → admitted lenses → at most one bounded correction → targeted validation → approval and burn
```

Fresh STATUS/FINALIZE routing, exact consent, immutable candidate binding, reviewer admission, bounded correction, validator evidence, and terminal burn remain only when they are reachable from this lifecycle.

Approval leaves no terminal receipt, lineage, witness, tombstone, mirror, gate authority, or durable review history. Git remains the durable project history.

### D3. Delete by causal closure

When a consumer is deleted, delete its newly unreachable providers, direct tests, fixtures, schemas, help text, refusal continuations, ratchet entries, manifests, docs, and compile references in the same causal work unit. Do not baseline newly dead code and do not preserve a helper solely because a test calls it.

### D4. Evidence required for retention

Every retained review symbol must have all three:

1. a non-test production caller;
2. a named current compact-v2 scenario;
3. a focused test proving that scenario.

Anything missing one of these is deletion scope unless a separate approved issue owns a concrete current use.

## Scope

After #3564 merges, inventory and delete orphaned review/RDD code outside `internal/sddstatus`, including as applicable:

- retired review contract versions, schema fields, stores, receipts, bindings, lineage relations, selectors, projections, and compatibility translators;
- obsolete lifecycle switches, shadow observers, mirrors, gate evaluators, delivery interceptors, recovery shells, quarantine/repair paths, and maintenance verbs with no live compact-v2 transition;
- CLI/runtime adapter code that reconstructs retired review semantics instead of transporting the current native decision;
- tests, journeys, fixtures, assets, docs, prompts, help, refusals, ratchets, and OpenSpec assertions that preserve removed behavior;
- open issue and pull-request roots whose failure mechanism disappears with the deleted surface.

## Out of Scope

- The SDD cleanup owned by #3564.
- Deleting a compact-v2 operation that still has a reachable current transition and named test.
- Adding a replacement state, verb, flag, gate, mirror, or parallel authority representation.
- Release or publication work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A pinned post-#3564 inventory maps every non-test review/RDD symbol outside SDD to a current compact-v2 scenario or deletion.
- [ ] Every deleted surface includes its callers, tests, fixtures, schemas, help, refusal text, ratchet entries, and docs.
- [ ] No production code recognizes retired review formats or authority versions.
- [ ] No terminal review artifact survives approval and burn.
- [ ] Ordinary commit, push, pull request, release, and archive remain outside review authority.
- [ ] A universal architecture guard rejects reintroduction of retired versions, compatibility readers, terminal artifacts, and delivery gates.
- [ ] Guard decoys prove that mode, receipt, binding, witness, legacy, gate, recovery, and successor variants are detected.
- [ ] `go test ./...` passes at repository root, along with vet, format, refusal/dead-code ratchets, platform builds, and CI-equivalent driven review journeys.
- [ ] Remaining related issues and pull requests receive evidence-backed dispositions.

## Delivery Strategy

Use stacked-to-main, deletion-first slices by causal boundary. Each slice must be independently buildable and reviewable, and tests stay with the behavior they prove. If one causal deletion exceeds 400 changed lines, record the exact reason before applying `size:exception`; do not split a consumer from the providers that become dead because of its removal.

## References

- #3417
- #3564
- #3377
- #2471
- PR #3536
- PR #3567

title: test(review): extend the refusal ratchet to prompts, envelopes and asset prose
body:
## Why

The refusal-resolution ratchet enumerates roughly 2500 Go error-constructor sites and holds them to the blocking-budget rule: every stop names its reason and its executable exit. It structurally cannot see three other surfaces that terminate a consumer flow, and an audit found 113 dead-end sites across them.

| Surface | Covered today | Dead-ends found |
|---|---|---|
| Go error constructors | yes | ratchet-managed |
| Envelope reason codes | no | 76 |
| Embedded asset and skill prose | no | 31 (7 locations, 24 duplicated across runtimes) |
| Agent-facing terminal prompts | no | 6 |

## Proposal

`TestEveryTerminalDirectiveNamesItsExit`, three collectors sharing the existing by-design annotation grammar and closed vocabulary, with an HTML-comment marker form for markdown. Plus one new rule the current ratchet does not have: a named verb must resolve against real dispatch, so a printed command the CLI itself refuses counts as a dead end rather than an exit.

Estimated baseline around 120 sites (prompts ~14, envelopes ~76, assets ~30), against the existing ratchet's 1692. Unlike that one this baseline is unusually cheap to burn down rather than freeze: one constructor edit clears 21, embedding the stop table clears 16, and a single canonical sentence clears 24 duplicated across runtimes.

Land the envelope collector first. It is pure AST with no natural-language judgment and all 76 sites were hand-verified during the audit.

## Not in scope

Rewriting the 1754 disclosed Go-side violations. This is about closing the blind spots, not re-litigating managed debt.

title: bug(subagents): blocking interaction envelope is hidden from orchestrator
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and found no equivalent report.
- [x] I understand that a linked PR requires maintainer approval.

### Bug Description

A delegated operations agent returned a blocking interaction request, but the parent orchestrator received only a placeholder instead of the user-facing choice envelope. Because the prompt, choices, selection mode, and allowed answer domain were absent, the orchestrator could not relay or answer it safely.

This report describes observed behavior only; it does not claim a root cause.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch a project-local delegated operations agent for a bounded local integration task.
2. Let the agent encounter a condition that requires parent or user input.
3. Wait for the delegated task to complete and inspect its final response.
4. Observe that the parent receives only the sanitized envelope shown below, with no actionable prompt or choices.

### Expected Behavior

The parent should receive the complete blocking choice envelope: why input is required, every question and option in order, selection mode, exact allowed-answer domain, and any safe continuation binding needed to return the answer once.

If the envelope cannot be represented safely, the provider should return a typed failure that identifies the transport limitation without pretending an actionable interaction was delivered.

### Actual Behavior

The complete final response was:

```text
[interaction request hidden]
```

No question, options, answer tokens, or continuation binding were available. The parent therefore stopped the integration flow rather than guessing. No dependent work was launched from the ambiguous result. Existing consumer state was preserved, but the mutation outcome of the delegated task could not be established from the final response alone.

### Gentle AI Version

2.2.4

### Operating System

macOS arm64

### AI Agent / Client

Other — Pi coding agent with project-local subagents

### Shell

zsh

### Bounded Attempts and Outcomes

- Attempts: 1 delegated integration attempt.
- Provider outcome: task completed with a hidden interaction placeholder.
- Consumer outcome: fail-closed stop; no answer inferred and no dependent action launched.
- Safe reason identifier: `interaction_request_hidden`.

### Minimal Reproduction

Delegate a bounded task whose worker requests interaction, then inspect only the worker's final response at the parent boundary. The defect is reproduced when the parent sees the placeholder above rather than the complete prompt envelope.

### Additional Context

- The worker had an explicit task scope and skill binding.
- The parent was instructed to consume only the final response, so reopening execution history was intentionally avoided.
- No raw command arguments, repository paths, project names, usernames, hostnames, credentials, diffs, source contents, or environment values are included in this report.
- Consumer staging and unrelated background work remained preserved.

### Acceptance Criteria

- Blocking interaction requests survive the subagent-to-parent boundary with their complete user-facing envelope.
- The envelope includes exact answer semantics and a safe one-time continuation mechanism.
- Privacy redaction removes sensitive values without removing the decision itself.
- Tests cover a delegated worker returning an interaction request when the parent is restricted to reading only the final response.

title: bug(engram): cloud autosync pushes mutations with empty project name (HTTP 400) and never retries visibly
body:

### 📝 Bug Description

## Affected Area

Engram cloud autosync (local daemon `engram serve` with `ENGRAM_CLOUD_AUTOSYNC=1`).

## Problem Statement

With autosync enabled, the local daemon is expected to push newly saved observations to the configured cloud endpoint automatically. Instead, autosync leaves mutations pending: the push fails with HTTP 400 **"mutation entries must specify a project"** because the autosync path emits mutations with an empty project name. The daemon does not surface the failure in its logs (nothing after startup), so the only way to detect it is `engram cloud status` / `engram doctor`.


### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure cloud endpoint + token and enable autosync (`ENGRAM_CLOUD_AUTOSYNC=1`), then start `engram serve`.
2. Save a memory for a project (e.g. `mem_save` with an explicit project).
3. Wait for an autosync cycle. The observation never reaches the cloud.
4. `engram cloud status` reports:

Sync diagnostic: pending
reason_code: transport_failed
reason_message: push: transport push project "": cloud: mutation push: status 400: mutation entries must specify a project

5. Running the explicit `engram sync --cloud --project <name>` succeeds immediately and pushes the same pending mutations (observed: chunk created, mutations synced).



### ✅ Expected Behavior

Autosync pushes each project's mutations with its project name (same behavior as the explicit `--project` path), or at minimum logs the failed push attempts so the operator can act.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Autosync attempts the push with an empty project name → HTTP 400 → mutations remain pending; `engram doctor` shows a growing `pending_mutations_evaluated`; no log lines after daemon startup.

gentle-ai 2.2.4

title: feat(review): support explicit full-4R start intent
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### Problem Statement

Gentle AI intentionally classifies review risk from semantic evidence rather than change volume. That keeps neutral large changes at medium risk, but there is no separate review-start intent for an operator or an SDD task that explicitly requires the canonical full 4R lens set.

An SDD task can require full 4R, yet `review start` exposes no intent/flag for that requirement. START therefore freezes only the lenses selected from classified risk, and an active lineage correctly cannot widen its frozen lens set afterward. The only unsafe workarounds are to falsify risk, modify authority, or allocate an unrelated review lifecycle.

Concrete nomina reproduction:

- Base: `23bbe82f...`
- Candidate HEAD: `1b519198...`
- Scope: 89 paths and 7,484 authored additions plus deletions
- SDD task 5.2 explicitly requires full 4R
- Current semantic classification: medium (size intentionally does not alter risk)
- Native result: only the reliability lens was selected in lineage `review-0b7a74d4168811d0`
- Once that authority existed, there was no supported way to widen it to the canonical four lenses

This is a missing explicit intent at the review-start seam, not a risk-classification defect.

#### Related work, not duplicates

- #1385 covers the broader extraordinary Judgment Day transaction lifecycle. A comment proposes `--full-4r`, but that issue must also decide two-blind-judge authority, bounded re-judgment, final verification, and import/recovery semantics; it is `status:needs-design`. This issue extracts only ordinary review START intent for the existing canonical 4R lifecycle.
- #1380 covers adaptive evidence-driven execution, adjudication, and delta re-review. This issue does not change automatic risk classification, evidence adjudication, correction strategy, or provider scheduling; it adds an explicit escalation-only input at START.
- #1331 is the closed historical size-routing correction. This issue does not restore line count as risk evidence or change the intentional rule that size no longer affects risk.

Exact searches for `ReviewStartIntent`, `explicit full-4R start intent`, `start intent`, `--full-4r`, and open PRs combining full 4R with `review start` found no dedicated issue or open implementation PR.

### Proposed Solution

Add a small closed interface at the review-start seam:

```text
ReviewStartIntent = classified | full-4r
```

- Default omitted intent to `classified`, preserving current behavior.
- Add `gentle-ai review start --start-intent=full-4r`.
- Treat the explicit flag as operator consent to increase review coverage; never infer it from line count or silently apply it.
- Allow `review status` for a fresh target to accept/propagate the requested intent into its exact executable START transition.
- For `full-4r`, select exactly the canonical four lenses using the existing canonical selector/order. Do not expose arbitrary lens lists.
- Preserve classified risk as classified. A medium-risk target remains medium; the effective lens set is explained by start intent, not falsified high risk.
- Freeze the intent with the selected lens set in authority, authority revision/hash inputs, receipt, STATUS, support/inspection output, and recovery bindings.
- Advertise supported start intents through the negotiated capabilities contract so orchestrators can fail closed.
- Validate the frozen intent at capture/finalize, delivery gates, receipt validation, recovery, replay, and status-to-transition execution. Unknown, omitted-where-bound, or mismatched intent must fail closed.
- Read historical authority/receipt records that predate this field as `classified`; do not rewrite their bytes or hashes.
- Do not support in-place widening in the first version. A conflicting request against an active lineage returns a typed refusal. A pristine lineage may use the existing audited abandonment path and then create a fresh lineage; consumed slots/results remain immutable.

This keeps a deep module: callers choose one closed intent, while canonical lens selection, persistence, validation, historical decoding, and lifecycle enforcement remain local to review authority.

#### Expected behavior

For the nomina reproduction, a fresh target started with `--start-intent=full-4r` remains semantically medium risk but freezes the canonical four lenses and carries that explicit reason through STATUS, receipt, recovery, and every delivery gate. Starting without the flag behaves exactly as today.

#### Operator flows

1. **Default direct START:** omit the option; persist/evaluate `classified` and retain current 0/1/4 risk-based selection.
2. **Explicit direct START:** pass `--start-intent=full-4r`; freeze exactly four canonical lenses without changing classified risk.
3. **Negotiated fresh-target flow:** request STATUS with `full-4r`; STATUS advertises and emits an exact START transition containing the same intent; executing it produces matching authority.
4. **Resume/recovery:** report the frozen intent and require an exact match; no caller may reinterpret or widen it.
5. **Historical authority:** decode a record with no intent as `classified`, preserving its original hash and behavior.
6. **Existing active lineage:** reject a conflicting `full-4r` request with a typed next action. Only the existing pristine-lineage abandonment flow may precede a fresh START.

#### Safety invariants

- Start intent is closed, explicit, immutable, target-bound, and content-addressed with authority.
- `full-4r` is escalation-only: it cannot reduce a classifier-selected lens set.
- Intent does not change target identity, candidate bytes/modes, classified risk, or evidence.
- The full profile means exactly the canonical four lenses; no custom subset, duplicates, aliases, or provider-specific order.
- STATUS, START, recovery, finalize, receipts, and gates agree on one frozen intent and lens set.
- Existing active authority is never rewritten or widened in place.
- Historical records remain readable and byte/hash compatible.
- RDD kill-switch and issue/approval gates remain authoritative; this flag cannot bypass them.

#### Negative controls

- Unknown values such as `--start-intent=all` are rejected before mutation.
- Repeating START with the same target and same intent is idempotent; repeating it with a conflicting intent is rejected without a new budget.
- A stale STATUS transition whose bound intent differs from current/requested intent is rejected without authority mutation.
- Omitting intent on a new request preserves `classified`; omission cannot inherit an unrelated prior `full-4r` choice.
- A receipt or recovered authority with intent/lens mismatch is rejected at finalize and every delivery gate.
- A medium target under `full-4r` must not be serialized or reported as high risk.
- An active one-lens lineage cannot be widened by START, recovery, repair, or direct authority edits.
- With RDD disabled, START remains rejected regardless of requested intent.

#### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A versioned closed `ReviewStartIntent` supports exactly `classified` and `full-4r`.
- [ ] Omitted intent is backward-compatible and preserves current classified lens selection.
- [ ] `review start --start-intent=full-4r` freezes exactly the canonical four lenses while preserving classified risk.
- [ ] Fresh-target STATUS accepts/propagates the intent into an exact executable START transition.
- [ ] Capabilities advertise the option and allowed values provider-neutrally.
- [ ] Authority, revision/content hash inputs, receipt, inspection, STATUS, recovery, replay, and gate validation bind the intent.
- [ ] Historical records without the field decode as `classified` without rewrite or hash drift.
- [ ] Same-intent retry is idempotent; conflicting retry or active-lineage widening fails closed without consuming budget.
- [ ] Pristine abandonment followed by fresh full-4R START is supported through existing audited operations; no new in-place widening operation is added.
- [ ] The nomina-sized neutral reproduction can explicitly obtain canonical full 4R without changing risk classification.
- [ ] Default, explicit, historical, stale-transition, mismatch, disabled-mode, and active-lineage negative controls are covered.
- [ ] Help, capabilities, integration contracts, embedded skill/docs, and support output use the same terminology and values.

#### Test and journey requirements

- Add behavior-first unit/contract tests for defaulting, closed-value validation, canonical selection, serialization/hash binding, historical decoding, and mismatch rejection.
- Add one truthful black-box CLI journey for each direct START mode and the negotiated `STATUS -> exact START -> capture/finalize -> validate` full-4R lifecycle.
- Add black-box negative journeys for stale/mismatched intent, disabled RDD, retry conflict, and active-lineage widening refusal; assert no authority, slot, receipt, or budget mutation.
- Exercise recovery/resume and all delivery gates against the exact frozen intent.
- Prove Linux, macOS, and Windows contract/restart behavior remains deterministic. If the core bench cannot represent a lifecycle flow, use actual runtime E2E evidence rather than a synthetic proxy.

#### Size and authority decision required before implementation

Forecast: approximately **450-650 authored additions plus deletions** across the transaction model/store, CLI/status/capabilities contracts, gate/recovery validation, tests/journeys, embedded docs, and generated/distribution surfaces.

This exceeds the RDD 400-line hard limit. Before edits begin, please either:

- approve an explicit size exception for one causal authority invariant and rollback boundary; or
- require an approved chain and define its independent review/rollback slices (for example, persisted contract and historical compatibility first, then CLI/lifecycle propagation and journeys).

Implementation is blocked until this issue receives `status:approved` **and** a maintainer records the size-exception or chain decision. Filing this issue does not claim either approval.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Restore size-based high risk.** Rejected: volume is not semantic risk and current behavior is intentional.
- **Treat explicit full 4R as high risk.** Rejected: it falsifies classification and makes policy/evidence reporting untrustworthy.
- **Expose arbitrary lens overrides.** Rejected: it creates a shallow, unsafe interface and permits accidental downgrade or non-canonical receipts.
- **Widen an active lineage in place.** Rejected initially: selected lenses and budget are already frozen authority. Use typed refusal plus existing pristine abandonment/fresh START.
- **Use Judgment Day (#1385).** Rejected for this need: Judgment Day is a replacement lifecycle with two blind judges and different authority semantics; canonical ordinary 4R already exists.
- **Rely on SDD prose alone.** Rejected: prose cannot alter native frozen authority or satisfy receipt/gate validation.

### Additional Context

```yaml
skill_resolution:
  primary: issue-creation
  supporting:
    - rdd-defect-workflow
    - codebase-design
  artifact: public feature request only
  rdd_mode: on (decided by default)
  authority: no maintainer approval, label mutation, review transaction, or implementation claimed
```

Current diagnosis branch: `fix/explicit-full-4r-review-intent` at `943fdea3ad39a585dbc500f721da6dd7518838aa`. The working tree was clean when this issue was filed. No implementation, commit, push, PR, review-authority mutation, or nomina mutation is part of this issue work.

title: fix(opencode): install custom theme asset and activate it through tui.json
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

Gentle AI does not install the Gentleman color theme for OpenCode.

The problem affects both installation paths:

1. The Full Gentleman preset excludes the generic theme component, so an OpenCode installation receives the logo plugin but not the Gentleman color theme.
2. A Custom installation exposes an “OpenCode Theme” component, but selecting it only writes `"theme": "gentleman"` to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`.

Neither path installs the required theme asset:

`~/.config/opencode/themes/gentleman.json`

Additionally, current OpenCode versions select TUI themes through `~/.config/opencode/tui.json`. The `theme` property in `opencode.json` is deprecated.

As a result, Gentle AI cannot reproduce the complete Gentleman visual configuration for OpenCode through either Full Gentleman or Custom installation.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

### Full Gentleman installation

1. Open Gentle AI.
2. Select OpenCode.
3. Choose the Full Gentleman preset.
4. Complete the installation.
5. Check `~/.config/opencode/themes/`.
6. Check `~/.config/opencode/tui.json`.

The `gentleman.json` theme file is not installed and the theme is not selected.

### Custom installation

1. Open Gentle AI.
2. Select OpenCode.
3. Choose Custom installation.
4. Select the “OpenCode Theme” component.
5. Complete the installation.
6. Check `~/.config/opencode/themes/`.
7. Check `~/.config/opencode/tui.json`.
8. Check `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`.

The theme asset is not installed. The installer writes `"theme": "gentleman"` to the deprecated `opencode.json` location instead of selecting it through `tui.json`.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

When OpenCode is selected:

- The Full Gentleman preset installs the Gentleman OpenCode theme by default.
- Custom installation allows the user to select the Gentleman OpenCode theme.
- The installer copies a valid theme definition to `~/.config/opencode/themes/gentleman.json`.
- The installer merges `"theme": "gentleman"` into `~/.config/opencode/tui.json`.
- Existing unrelated OpenCode configuration is preserved.
- The theme component is only offered when it applies to a selected client.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

- Full Gentleman excludes the theme component for OpenCode.
- Custom installation exposes the component but does not install a theme JSON asset.
- Custom installation writes `"theme": "gentleman"` to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`.
- No installation path creates `~/.config/opencode/themes/gentleman.json`.
- OpenCode therefore cannot load or select the Gentleman theme installed by Gentle AI.

### Gentle AI Version

gentle-ai 2.2.4

### Operating System

Linux (Arch/Manjaro)

### AI Agent / Client

OpenCode

### 📋 Affected Area

Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
N/A. The installation completes without reporting an error, but the required theme asset is not created.
```

### Additional Context

Environment:

- Gentle AI: 2.2.4
- OpenCode: 1.18.10
- OS: Arch Linux, kernel 7.1.4-arch1-1, x86_64

Relevant implementation evidence:

- `internal/model/presets.go` excludes the generic theme component from the Full Gentleman preset.
- `internal/catalog/components.go` exposes an “OpenCode Theme” component for Custom installation.
- `internal/components/theme/inject.go` only merges `"theme": "gentleman"` into the selected adapter settings.
- `internal/agents/opencode/adapter.go` resolves those settings to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`.
- No OpenCode theme asset is bundled or copied to `~/.config/opencode/themes/gentleman.json`.
- Existing tests currently expect the theme property in `opencode.json`.

A valid Gentleman OpenCode theme definition already exists at:

https://github.com/joaquinvesapa/joaquinvesapa-dots/blob/main/themes/gentleman.json

Relevant previous issues:

- #459 added the Claude theme and OpenCode logo, but did not add an OpenCode color theme.
- #497 addressed the invalid top-level OpenCode theme configuration, but did not add the missing theme asset or fix the Custom installation path.

This report is therefore follow-up scope rather than a duplicate.

Transparency: the installation behavior was confirmed from the current source and tests. The local theme asset was installed manually as a workaround.

title: bug(orchestrator): Provider Defect Handoff has no classification test, so ordinary review denials deadlock the agent
body:
## Summary

The **Gentle AI Provider Defect Handoff (MANDATORY)** section injected into the orchestrator system prompt triggers on a workflow that *"appears blocked by a Gentle AI provider or tool defect"*, but the section never defines "appears". It supplies no classification test.

An agent that meets any ordinary review denial can satisfy that phrasing, enter the handoff, and land on its terminal instruction — *"Resume only after an installed released fix, then re-enter through native status"*. When the installed version already equals the latest published release, that instruction is unreachable and the agent deadlocks permanently.

Observed on **gentle-ai 2.2.4** with OpenCode. The same class of false verdict was seen on a different repository five days earlier.

## What the agent actually did

Asked to make a small UI change (rename a label, update two dictionary entries), the orchestrator refused:

> La implementación queda pendiente porque el repositorio conserva el candidato anterior bloqueado por el defecto de revisión de Gentle AI. No modificaré esos archivos hasta contar con una corrección oficial instalada y revalidar el estado nativo.

Told to try again, it verified there was no newer release and refused again:

```
$ gentle-ai --version
gentle-ai 2.2.4
$ gh release view --repo Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai --json tagName
{"tagName":"v2.2.4"}
```

> No existe una corrección oficial posterior instalada. El candidato permanece preservado. Reintentar ahora repetiría el mismo proveedor defectuoso; solo puedo continuar cuando haya una versión oficial corregida instalada.

Told explicitly by the user that nothing was defective, it refused a third time.

## Both of its premises were false

**1. There was no blocked candidate.**

```
$ gentle-ai review status --cwd <repo>
lineages: approved=4          # zero in `reviewing`
```

**2. The denial was an ordinary `scope-changed`, and it named its own fix on its own last line.**

```
$ gentle-ai review validate --gate pre-commit --cwd <repo>
Error: review lifecycle gate denied: scope-changed: 3 paths in this candidate
that no terminal receipt covers: recover via gentle-ai review recover
(requires: predecessor_lineage_id, expected_predecessor_revision,
successor_lineage_id, disposition)
```

A `scope-changed` verdict against healthy `approved` lineages is normal: it means the working candidate moved past what the receipt covers. It is the gate working, not failing.

## Two aggravating factors

**A `pre-commit` gate was treated as blocking source edits.** The gate governs delivery. Nothing in it speaks to modifying files, and no git hook or `core.hooksPath` was installed in that repository. The agent refused to write code because a *commit* gate was unsatisfied — a category error the handoff section does nothing to prevent, because it never scopes what "blocked" means.

**The counter-guidance cannot win on precedence.** Machine-owner guidance saying a denial is never by itself evidence of a defect lives in `AGENTS.md`. The Defect Handoff section lives inside the agent's own system prompt (~52k characters, generated and not intended for hand-editing) and is marked MANDATORY. A generic "supersedes any injected prompt" clause in `AGENTS.md` did not bind against it.

## Why this is a design gap rather than a misconfiguration

The handoff section is well-intentioned — it exists to stop agents from wandering into the gentle-ai repository to "fix" things. But as written it is a one-way door:

1. Its entry condition is subjective (`appears blocked`) with no test.
2. Its exit condition is objective and often unsatisfiable (`an installed released fix`).

Any agent that classifies conservatively — which is the behaviour the section encourages — will over-trigger, and once triggered has no path back. The failure mode is silent: from the user's side the agent simply stops doing work and cites an upstream defect that does not exist.

## Suggested fix

Give the section the classification test it currently assumes. Concretely, require all of the following before it may be entered:

1. `gentle-ai review status` shows a lineage in a **non-terminal** state that the denial actually references. `approved` lineages plus a `scope-changed` verdict are normal and are not a defect.
2. The last line of `gentle-ai review validate --gate <gate>` names **no** recovery operation. If it names `review recover`, `review abandon`, `review invalidate`, or reports `action: explicit-maintainer-action`, the tool has stated the fix and there is no defect.
3. That named operation has been **run** and failed with an error unrelated to the caller's inputs. A refusal such as `healthy approved authority cannot be invalidated: ... a changed candidate is recovered into a successor, not invalidated` is the tool working correctly.

Two additions would also help:

- **Scope the word "blocked".** State that delivery gates (`post-apply`, `pre-commit`, `pre-push`, `pre-pr`, `release`) govern delivery only, and never justify refusing to edit source.
- **Close the unreachable exit.** When the installed version already equals the latest published release, "wait for an official fix" is not an available answer; the section should say what to do in that case rather than leaving the agent parked.

Happy to supply the full anonymised transcript of the three refusals, or the exact `review status` / `validate` payloads, if useful.

title: fix(installer): report state and offer recovery on step failure
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

When a step in the install pipeline fails, the run ends with `pipeline completed with errors` and nothing else. The output never states:

- whether the failed step was rolled back, left half-applied, or never mutated anything
- whether the steps that already succeeded were kept or reverted
- what state the system is now in, and whether re-running is safe and idempotent

There is also no decision point at the moment of failure. As a user I would want to choose: retry the step, skip it and continue with the remaining steps, or abort and revert the whole run. Instead the pipeline decides silently and exits.

The result is a grey state: nothing tells me whether to re-run, undo by hand, or reinstall from scratch.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Make any pipeline step fail. In my case it was the CodeGraph community tool (#2355).
2. Read the final output of the run.
3. Try to determine, from that output alone, what was applied and what was undone.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

On step failure:

1. In interactive/TUI runs, prompt with the available choices — retry / skip and continue / abort and revert.
2. Whatever path is taken, print a state summary at the end: which steps applied, which were rolled back, which were skipped, and which paths were touched or backed up.
3. State explicitly whether re-running `gentle-ai install` / `gentle-ai sync` is safe from the resulting state.

Non-interactive runs should skip the prompt but still emit the state summary, since that is where it matters most.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The run prints the failing step and `pipeline completed with errors`, then exits. No prompt, no rollback statement, no summary of what survived. The failure contract of the pipeline is invisible to the user.

### Gentle AI Version

2.2.4

### Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client

Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area

Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
Logs
  FAILED: community-tool:codegraph — install community tool "codegraph": run "codegraph install --target antigravity,claude,cursor,gemini --location global
  output:
  ┌  CodeGraph v0.9.3
  ✗ Unknown --target id(s): antigravity, gemini. Known: claude, cursor, codex, opencode, hermes, plus 'auto' / 'all' / 'none'.
  pipeline completed with errors
```

That is the complete tail of the run. Nothing after it describes the resulting state.

### Additional Context

**Why this is not a duplicate.** These three touch adjacent ground but all are about the correctness of one specific path, not about the pipeline's failure contract being unobservable:

- **#1725** — roll back applied assets when *state persistence* fails. One specific failure mode, and about performing the rollback rather than reporting it.
- **#2306** — the *uninstall* path aborts on first failure, leaving partial mutations and a stale `state.json`.
- **#1809** — `InstallState` serialized without a lock, risking concurrent-write clobber.

**Scope note for triage:** this could reasonably be split — the missing state summary reads as a bug (the pipeline knows what it did and does not say so), while the retry/skip/revert prompt is closer to a feature request. Filing as one bug because from the user's side it is a single problem: a failed run whose outcome cannot be determined. Happy to split it if maintainers prefer.

title: feat(state): add a locked read-modify-write primitive for install state
body:
## Parent initiative

Part of #1809.

Slice 2 of 3. The parent issue #1809 remains open until the call-site migration lands,
which is the slice that actually fixes the reported bug.

---

### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Problem Statement

`internal/state` offers no way to mutate persisted install state safely. `state.Write` marshals a whole `InstallState` and atomically replaces `state.json`, with no lock, no revision, and no compare-and-swap. Callers therefore read, modify in memory, and write back, with an unguarded window between the read and the write, and the last writer wins with whatever snapshot it held.

That window is what #1809 reports. Fixing #1809 means migrating every persistence call site off read-then-`Write`, and there is nothing for them to migrate *onto*.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Add `state.Update(homeDir, mutate)`:

- takes the exclusive advisory lock from the platform primitive slice,
- re-reads persisted state **inside** the lock,
- applies the caller's mutation to that fresh copy,
- writes while still holding the lock.

`state.Write` stays available so nothing breaks while call sites migrate.

Acceptance criteria for this issue, separate from #1809:

- `Update` serializes concurrent mutations across processes, verified under `-race`.
- The lost-update sequence from #1809 fails before the change and passes after: actor A reads state, actor B writes `rdd_mode=off`, actor A writes `persona` from its stale snapshot and silently restores `rdd_mode=on`.
- The lock contract is documented, including that it is **not** reentrant. Acquisition opens a new descriptor per call and both `flock` and `LockFileEx` are per-handle, so a `mutate` closure that calls back into `Update` would deadlock.
- `Write` and `Update` interacting on the same state file is covered by a test.

**Behaviour change to call out.** `state.Write` ends up taking the same lock and can return a lock-timeout error it never returned before. That is a change to an existing exported function, not just new surface, so callers that ignore its error or assume it cannot block deserve a second look during review.

This issue does **not** cover the platform lock helpers, which are their own slice, nor migrating any call site, which stays on #1809.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

**Make `Write` itself locking instead of adding `Update`.** Rejected, and this is the load-bearing one: a write-only lock does not close the race. The stale snapshot is captured at read time, so serializing only the write still lets a stale full-object write land. That is exactly the failure mode #1809 reports, and it is why the primitive has to own the read as well.

**Lock at each call site instead of adding a primitive.** Rejected: eight independent lock implementations is the shape that produced the three disagreeing `_shared` file lists tracked in #1806.

**Bundle this with the platform lock helpers and the call-site migration in one PR under `size:exception`.** Rejected: combined it is roughly 660 changed lines, and the reviewer asked for the incremental slices to stay inside the budget rather than for an exception.

### 📎 Additional Context

Slice 2 of 3 under #1809. Implementation is ready and verified: 389 changed lines against the platform-lock slice, with `go build`, `go vet`, `gofmtcheck`, `go test -race` and a Windows build all passing.

Following the pattern already merged here, where each slice closes its own approved child issue and the parent stays open. See #1225, which closes #1776 while remaining "Part of #1197", and the #2046 / #2061 pair.

The chain: platform lock primitive, then this, then #1809 for the call-site migration, which is the slice that actually closes the bug.

I have no triage rights on this repository. Maintainer-owed: `status:approved` before PR #2299 can pass its CI gates. It is currently the direct cause of that PR's failing `Check Issue Has status:approved` run.

title: bug(opencode): delegated general executor expands bounded task contract and self-blocks
body:
### Preflight confirmations

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and found no equivalent report.
- [x] I understand that maintainer approval is required before opening a pull request.

### Bug Description

A bounded OpenCode `general` executor repeatedly expanded an exact delegated task contract and then blocked on the checks it had added. The task followed an operator-authorized preflight and explicitly prohibited inferred checks, traversal of protected children, and enumeration outside a supplied metadata table.

This report describes observed behavior only. It does not assume whether the cause is Gentle AI prompt generation, OpenCode task transport, provider behavior, or model instruction compliance.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run Gentle AI through OpenCode and delegate a direct bounded task to a `general` executor.
2. Provide an exact metadata allowlist for a synthetic remote staging tree. Include one protected child that the unprivileged actor cannot traverse, plus a previously completed operator attestation for that child.
3. Explicitly instruct the executor not to infer additional metadata rules, not to traverse or enumerate the protected child, and to treat the supplied attestation as authoritative.
4. Require fail-closed behavior before mutation and no retry after a contract mismatch.
5. Observe successive attempts add checks outside the contract and block before the intended transaction.

Minimal synthetic shape:

- `<remote-root>`: accessible to the delegated actor.
- `<protected-child>`: intentionally inaccessible to that actor and already verified by an operator attestation.
- `<uid-owned-leaf>`: metadata is supplied in the exact allowlist; enumeration is explicitly prohibited.

### Expected Behavior

The executor should follow the supplied allowlist and exclusions exactly. If the runtime cannot enforce that contract, it should return one precise typed inability before constructing or running the transaction.

### Actual Behavior

Four bounded occurrences produced different out-of-contract blockers:

- `GA-20260803-A`: a remote-only home token was expanded in the caller environment.
- `GA-20260803-B`: the executor invented a metadata allowlist and rejected an approved parent mode.
- `GA-20260803-C`: the executor attempted to traverse a protected child that the prompt explicitly excluded.
- `GA-20260803-D`: after being told to trust the operator attestation, the executor enumerated another UID-owned leaf outside the supplied table.

Each occurrence stopped before the intended transaction and requested renewed consent despite no mutation.

### Gentle AI Version

`2.2.4`

### Operating System

macOS, arm64

### AI Agent / Client

OpenCode `1.18.10`, delegated `general` executor

### Affected Area

Other: delegated direct execution and bounded task-contract enforcement.

### Logs / Error Output

Sanitized failure envelopes are summarized above. Raw prompts, commands, paths, host identifiers, account information, environment values, source contents, and consumer artifacts are intentionally omitted.

### Additional Context

The operation was bounded and fail-closed. Across all delegated occurrences, the preserved outcome was:

- remote transfers: 0
- remote writes: 0
- secrets created: 0
- container or image-store actions: 0
- services started: 0
- external API actions: 0

Only a separate operator-authorized filesystem bootstrap existed before these occurrences, and it remained unchanged. The repeated blockers increased consent churn without adding safety evidence.

title: feat(cli): add backup listing and disk space inspection (gentle-ai backup list)
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand this issue needs `status:approved` before a PR can be opened

### 📝 Feature Description

Add a CLI inspection subcommand (`gentle-ai backup list`) and optional retention helper (`gentle-ai backup clean`) to view stored safety snapshots and measure their total disk space footprint in `~/.gentle-ai/backups/`.

### 💡 Problem Statement

`gentle-ai` automatically creates safety backups before state migrations, upgrades, and component syncs under `~/.gentle-ai/backups/` (e.g. `pre-migration-gemini-antigravity/`, `upgrade-20260802T051038Z/`).

However, there is currently no CLI subcommand or TUI tool to:
1. Query existing backups and their creation timestamps or origins.
2. Measure the total disk space footprint consumed by `~/.gentle-ai/backups/`.
3. Safely purge stale backup snapshots without manual file deletion (`rm -rf`).

Over time, multiple upgrade and sync operations accumulate backup directories silently on disk without user visibility or health diagnostics.

### 📋 Proposed Solution & Architecture

#### 1. CLI Inspection Subcommand: `gentle-ai backup list` (`gentle-ai backup ls`)

Add a read-only subcommand `gentle-ai backup list` that inspects `~/.gentle-ai/backups/` and renders a clean, human-readable table:

```text
TIMESTAMP             NAME / REASON                        FILES    SIZE       AGE
2026-08-02 05:10:38   upgrade-20260802T051038Z              42       12.4 MB    22h ago
2026-07-29 16:04:59   pre-migration-gemini-antigravity      15       3.1 MB     5d ago

Total: 2 backups occupying 15.5 MB in /home/user/.gentle-ai/backups
```

#### 2. Machine-Readable JSON Output (`--json`)

Support `--json` to output structured metadata for agent and tooling integration:

```json
{
  "backup_root": "/home/user/.gentle-ai/backups",
  "total_count": 2,
  "total_bytes": 16252928,
  "backups": [
    {
      "name": "upgrade-20260802T051038Z",
      "timestamp": "2026-08-02T05:10:38Z",
      "file_count": 42,
      "size_bytes": 13002342,
      "size_human": "12.4 MB"
    }
  ]
}
```

#### 3. Safe Retention Cleanup: `gentle-ai backup clean`

Add a retention helper `gentle-ai backup clean --keep <N>` (e.g. `--keep 5`) that retains the `N` most recent backups and safely removes older snapshots:
- Prompts for confirmation unless `--force` / `-y` is passed.
- Performs atomic directory deletion using validated sub-paths within `~/.gentle-ai/backups/` (guarding against path traversal as established in issue #220).

#### 4. Diagnostic Integration: `gentle-ai doctor`

Incorporate a backup disk footprint check into `gentle-ai doctor`:
- Reports total backup count and disk space.
- Emits a non-fatal warning if `~/.gentle-ai/backups/` exceeds 500 MB, suggesting `gentle-ai backup clean`.

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI / Backup Subsystem / Diagnostics

### ✅ Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `gentle-ai backup list` (and `gentle-ai backup ls`) inspects `~/.gentle-ai/backups/` and outputs a human-readable table with timestamps, file counts, and human-formatted sizes.
- [ ] `gentle-ai backup list --json` outputs valid, structured JSON metadata.
- [ ] `gentle-ai backup clean --keep <N>` safely purges backups older than the `N` most recent entries.
- [ ] Directory traversal and root validation guard against purging paths outside `~/.gentle-ai/backups/`.
- [ ] `gentle-ai doctor` reports backup count and disk usage with a threshold advisory when exceeding 500 MB.
- [ ] Unit tests cover backup size calculation, list formatting, JSON output, retention filtering, and error handling for missing backup directories.

title: feat(tui): make model assignment lists adaptive and add role guidance
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

TUI (terminal UI)

### 💡 Problem Statement

## Summary

Improve the OpenCode model-assignment experience in two related ways:

1. Use the available terminal dimensions to display as many model and agent assignments as possible instead of always hiding entries behind fixed `more` limits.
2. Provide contextual guidance that helps users understand which model capabilities, reasoning levels, and speed/cost tradeoffs are appropriate for each SDD, Judgment Day, and review role.

The goal is to let users compare the complete assignment matrix when their terminal can display it, while also helping them make informed model-selection decisions.

## Current behavior

### Fixed list limits

The `Assign Models to SDD, JD & Review Agents` screen always renders at most 16 assignment rows. Provider, model, and reasoning-effort selectors are limited to 10 visible entries.

These limits are fixed constants:

- `maxVisiblePhaseRows = 16`
- `maxVisibleItems = 10`

The complete assignment matrix contains more rows than the fixed viewport permits. The review-agent section is therefore hidden behind `↓ more assignments` even when the terminal has enough unused vertical space to display it.

The hidden entries remain reachable with keyboard navigation, so this is not data loss. However, it reduces discoverability and prevents users from comparing the complete configuration at a glance. The indicator currently reflects an implementation limit rather than actual terminal overflow.

### Limited model-selection guidance

The screen displays the provider, model, and reasoning effort assigned to each role, but it does not explain:

- What the selected agent is responsible for.
- What type of work the agent performs.
- Whether the role benefits more from reasoning quality, coding ability, tool use, review ability, speed, or lower cost.
- Which reasoning-effort range may be appropriate.
- Whether Fast mode affects model capability or only processing speed and pricing.
- What tradeoffs apply to coordinators, implementation agents, verifiers, judges, and reviewers.

Users therefore need prior knowledge of every internal role before they can configure the assignment matrix confidently.

## Expected behavior

### Adaptive list height

The assignment screen should:

- Use the current terminal height to calculate how many rows fit.
- Show all assignment rows when they fit together with the title, actions, warnings, and keyboard help.
- Expand provider, model, and reasoning-effort lists beyond 10 entries when space is available.
- Use bounded cursor-following scrolling only when content genuinely exceeds the viewport.
- Show `↑ more`, `↓ more`, and `↓ more assignments` only when entries exist outside the calculated viewport.
- Preserve the selected item after resize.
- Clamp cursor and scroll offsets safely after resize or search filtering.
- Keep search, keyboard navigation, warnings, Continue, Back, and help text usable.

### Contextual role guidance

When an assignment row is selected, the TUI should offer contextual help describing:

- The agent's purpose and type of work.
- The capabilities to prioritize when selecting a model.
- A suggested reasoning range, when appropriate.
- Relevant quality, speed, cost, context, and tool-use tradeoffs.
- Whether the role primarily coordinates, implements, verifies, or performs adversarial review.

The guidance should help users make informed decisions without prescribing one model vendor or hard-coding model IDs that may become outdated. Fast/service-tier guidance must remain separate from reasoning-effort guidance.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

## Viewport-aware rendering

Pass the current terminal dimensions into the model-picker rendering path and derive the visible-row budget from the space remaining after fixed screen chrome.

Use separate calculations for:

- Assignment list mode.
- Provider selection.
- Model selection and search.
- Reasoning-effort selection.
- Warnings and errors.
- Continue and Back actions.
- Keyboard help.
- Optional contextual guidance.

The root Bubble Tea model already receives terminal dimensions through `tea.WindowSizeMsg`. The model-picker renderer should consume that information instead of relying exclusively on fixed 16-row and 10-item limits.

Preserve a minimum usable viewport for small terminals, cap the calculated budget at the number of entries, and reuse the existing cursor-following scrolling. Render overflow indicators only when entries exist outside the calculated window.

## Capability-based role guidance

Associate each configurable agent role with small, stable guidance metadata, for example:

```go
type ModelSelectionGuidance struct {
    Purpose            string
    Priorities         []string
    SuggestedReasoning string
    ToolUse            string
    Tradeoffs          []string
}
```

The guidance should describe capabilities rather than hard-coded model names. Useful guidance may cover:

- Coding and tool-use reliability.
- Reasoning depth for architecture or adversarial evaluation.
- Balanced latency and reasoning for orchestration.
- Cost efficiency for mechanical or low-risk tasks.
- Context capacity for specs, designs, and implementation tasks.
- Fast mode when reduced latency justifies the additional cost.

Where runtime metadata is available, the help can also explain supported reasoning efforts, tool-call support, context limits, Fast/service-tier availability, and provider availability.

## Example guidance

For `sdd-apply`:

```text
Role: sdd-apply
Purpose: Implements approved tasks and modifies project files.

Consider:
• Strong coding and tool-use reliability
• Medium or high reasoning for non-trivial changes
• Sufficient context for specs, design, and tasks
• Fast mode when lower latency justifies the additional cost

Fast changes processing speed and pricing.
It does not replace the selected reasoning effort.
```

For `jd-judge-a`:

```text
Role: jd-judge-a
Purpose: Performs an independent adversarial review.

Consider:
• Strong reasoning and defect detection
• High reasoning effort
• Reliable evidence analysis
• Independence from the implementation model

Prefer review quality over generation speed.
```

For `gentle-orchestrator`:

```text
Role: gentle-orchestrator
Purpose: Coordinates agents, routes work, and maintains workflow state.

Consider:
• Reliable instruction following
• Strong tool and workflow coordination
• Balanced latency and reasoning
• Medium reasoning for normal orchestration
```

## Responsive presentation
