Possible presentations include a compact help line, a collapsible section opened with `?` or `i`, a side panel when width allows, or a lower panel in narrow terminals. Users should be able to hide detailed guidance to maximize list space.

The guidance must adapt to terminal dimensions and must not recreate the viewport problem by unnecessarily hiding assignments.

## Acceptance criteria

### Adaptive viewport

- [ ] A tall terminal displays all current assignment rows without `more assignments` when the complete screen fits.
- [ ] A short terminal keeps the list bounded and allows every row to be reached with keyboard navigation.
- [ ] Provider, model, and effort lists can display more than 10 entries when terminal height allows.
- [ ] Overflow indicators appear only when entries exist outside the calculated viewport.
- [ ] Continue, Back, warnings, search, and keyboard help remain visible at supported terminal sizes.
- [ ] Resizing preserves the selected assignment and safely clamps the visible window.
- [ ] Search filtering safely clamps cursor and scroll state.
- [ ] Profile creation and editing continue to render correctly.

### Role guidance

- [ ] Selecting an assignment provides a concise explanation of that agent's purpose.
- [ ] Guidance identifies the capabilities that matter for the selected role.
- [ ] Guidance distinguishes reasoning effort from Fast/service-tier selection.
- [ ] Guidance explains relevant quality, speed, cost, context, and tool-use tradeoffs.
- [ ] Guidance does not depend on hard-coded model brands or transient model IDs.
- [ ] Detailed guidance can be expanded or hidden without disrupting keyboard navigation.
- [ ] Small terminals retain a usable assignment viewport when guidance is enabled.
- [ ] The selected model, provider, reasoning effort, and assignment remain clearly visible.
- [ ] The number of matching results is shown where lists can be filtered.
- [ ] Existing assignment persistence and keyboard behavior remain unchanged.
- [ ] Focused tests cover tall, short, resized, filtered, guidance-expanded, and guidance-collapsed states.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

## Keep the fixed 16/10 row limits

This prevents uncontrolled growth, but wastes available space and displays overflow indicators when there is no real viewport overflow.

## Render every row unconditionally

This removes unnecessary hiding in tall terminals but can push actions and help text outside smaller terminals.

## Add a manual list expansion action

This introduces additional state and another interaction even though Bubble Tea already provides terminal dimensions.

## Display model guidance permanently

A permanently expanded panel could reduce the viewport and create clutter. Responsive or collapsible guidance preserves discoverability without consuming space when unnecessary.

## Hard-code recommended models

Model catalogs, aliases, pricing, and provider capabilities change over time. Guidance should describe required capabilities and tradeoffs rather than permanently recommending one model ID.

### 📎 Additional Context

## Screenshot evidence

The supplied screenshot shows `↓ more assignments` after the Judgment Day agents while unused vertical space remains below the assignment list. The review-agent assignments remain hidden.

It also demonstrates the decision complexity: the interface displays provider, model, and reasoning effort, but does not explain each role or which model characteristics should be prioritized.

The unrelated `LM Studio discovery failed` warning visible in the screenshot is not part of this request.

> Screenshot attachment pending.

## Source evidence

- [Fixed viewport limits](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/d5f13afc7190083bd8b96d9390e918f98faa319c/internal/tui/screens/model_picker.go#L29-L31)
- [Assignment window and overflow rendering](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/d5f13afc7190083bd8b96d9390e918f98faa319c/internal/tui/screens/model_picker.go#L783-L848)
- [Provider, model, and effort rendering](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/d5f13afc7190083bd8b96d9390e918f98faa319c/internal/tui/screens/model_picker.go#L686-L724)
- [Additional selector rendering](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/d5f13afc7190083bd8b96d9390e918f98faa319c/internal/tui/screens/model_picker.go#L863-L966)
- [Terminal dimensions captured by the root model](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/d5f13afc7190083bd8b96d9390e918f98faa319c/internal/tui/model.go#L786-L792)
- [Model-picker rendering path](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/d5f13afc7190083bd8b96d9390e918f98faa319c/internal/tui/model.go#L1184-L1189)
- [Profile creation reuses the renderer](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/d5f13afc7190083bd8b96d9390e918f98faa319c/internal/tui/screens/profile_create.go#L92-L117)

## Related issues

- #2218 covers runtime model capabilities, OpenCode Fast aliases, service-tier persistence, and the distinction between Fast and reasoning effort.
- #1009 covers general terminal clipping and measured layout.
- #1140 implemented terminal-aware bounded scrolling for welcome advisories.
- #2098 and #2197 concern which agents are included in the picker, not how existing rows use the available terminal height.

This issue is limited to the user experience of displaying and configuring model capabilities. It should consume capability information resolved through #2218 without duplicating that issue's backend discovery or persistence scope.

title: feat(triage): report read-only evidence for needs-review issues
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Problem Statement

Maintainers currently lack a bounded, repeatable way to summarize version and reproduction evidence for issues awaiting review.

Manual triage must distinguish current regressions from reports involving older releases, unknown versions, environment or configuration drift, managed-asset mismatches, agent/provider behavior, related fixes, and insufficient evidence.

A bug report is an observation, not proof of product causality. Issue age, an old reported version, or “upgrading fixed it” must not be treated as sufficient evidence to close an issue or assign responsibility.

`gentle-report` provides consent-based reporting for newly detected internal defects, but it does not analyze the historical issue backlog or help maintainers evaluate existing `status:needs-review` issues consistently.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Add a maintainer-facing, manually triggered GitHub Actions workflow that produces a bounded, read-only evidence report for issues awaiting review.

The pilot should:

- Analyze a configurable, bounded set of open `status:needs-review` issues plus a bounded set of unlabeled issues when lifecycle labels are absent.
- Treat `bug` and `type:bug` as equivalent input signals without modifying labels.
- Extract reported version, release channel, environment, and reproduction evidence.
- Keep stable releases, prereleases, unreleased `main`, and unknown versions distinct.
- Search for a bounded number of related issues, pull requests, releases, and known changes.
- Emit only a workflow artifact and job summary.
- Associate every conclusion with supporting URLs or mark the evidence as unavailable.

Use provisional, evidence-oriented outcomes:

- `current-evidence`
- `retest-requested`
- `related-change-found`
- `insufficient-evidence`

These outcomes are report data, not GitHub labels or root-cause conclusions.

The initial implementation must:

- Use read-only `issues` and `contents` permissions.
- Never comment, label, close, reopen, edit, or create issues.
- Never execute or interpolate issue content into shell commands, expressions, paths, environment variables, or workflow control.
- Escape untrusted text before rendering Markdown.
- Use bounded pagination, API calls, related candidates, runtime, output size, and artifact retention.
- Avoid external LLM calls and repository secrets.
- Produce deterministic results for unchanged evidence.
- Keep classification logic testable outside workflow YAML.

`gentle-report` should remain responsible for consent-based reporting of newly detected internal defects. This workflow would only assist maintainers with existing backlog evidence.

Binary and managed-asset identity from #1884 may be consumed when available, but this proposal must not introduce a competing identity model.


### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

### Close or mark issues stale by age

Rejected. Age measures inactivity, not resolution. Older issues can still reproduce on current releases.

### Automatically request retesting or change labels

Deferred. Automated comments and mutations may create noise, bot loops, incorrect classifications, and additional maintainer cleanup. They should only be considered after the read-only pilot demonstrates acceptable precision.

### Require every reporter to upgrade before submitting

Rejected. Updating may be unsafe, impossible, or may hide evidence needed to understand migration and compatibility failures.

### Use an external LLM to classify issue bodies

Rejected for the initial scope due to privacy, prompt-injection, determinism, cost, and false-causality risks.

### Extend `gentle-report`

Not sufficient. `gentle-report` handles newly detected internal incidents with user consent; it does not analyze historical backlog or general issue evidence.

### Perform triage manually

This remains the final decision path, but maintainers currently have to reconstruct the same version, reproduction, release, and relationship evidence repeatedly.


### 📎 Additional Context

This proposal intentionally treats bug reports as observations rather than confirmed attribution.

A reported problem may originate from Gentle AI, an older release, configuration drift, managed assets, PATH shadowing, migration state, an agent/provider, an external component, or an interaction between them. Reporters should not be required to determine root cause before submitting useful evidence.

The repository already has complementary mechanisms:

- #2060 / #2062: consent-based reporting for newly detected provider defects.
- #2211 / #2217: `gentle-report` labeling and idempotent report recovery.
- #1884: authoritative binary and managed-asset identity work.

None of these provides read-only, version-aware backlog evidence reporting.

The pilot should start with manual dispatch and a representative sample. Scheduled execution, contributor-policy changes, Issue Form hardening, automated comments, label changes, and issue closure should require separate follow-up approval based on measured precision.

Suggested pilot metrics:

- outcome precision after maintainer review;
- percentage of insufficient evidence;
- precision of related-change candidates;
- maintainer triage time saved;
- API usage, duration, and output size;
- incorrect closure or mutation risk avoided.

Out of scope:

- stale automation;
- automatic comments, labels, closure, reopening, or issue creation;
- automatic execution of user reproductions;
- comprehensive release compatibility certification;
- a new support-bundle format;
- root-cause attribution without reproduced evidence.

### Runtime provenance and attribution

When available, consume binary and managed-asset identity from #1884 rather than defining a second identity model.

Evidence from a custom build, dirty source checkout, modified binary, modified managed asset, or unofficial installation must not be classified automatically as either an upstream defect or a downstream-only defect. Report the observed provenance, abstain from product attribution, and request reproduction on an unmodified official release when that is safe and relevant.

A clean official-release reproduction increases attribution confidence; failure to reproduce there does not by itself disprove an upstream defect.

### Minimum evaluation fixtures

Validate the pilot offline with human-ground-truth synthetic fixtures covering:

- a defect reproduced on an unmodified official release;
- evidence available only from a custom build or dirty checkout;
- the same defect reproduced on both custom and official builds;
- unknown runtime provenance.

Measure at minimum:

- false-confirmation rate;
- false-attribution rate;
- abstention rate.

These fixtures must produce no GitHub mutations.

### AI-assisted issue provenance

AI-assisted tooling can produce and publish convincing issue reports with very low friction. Formatting quality and confident causal language must therefore not be treated as evidence that a defect is reproduced or correctly attributed.

When explicit provenance is available, the report should distinguish manual, AI-assisted, `gentle-report`, and unknown origins without treating any origin as inherently valid or invalid. Classification must remain grounded in reproducible evidence and linked repository history.

### Evidence from unlabeled issue intake

Repository Issue Forms disable blank issues in the web interface and apply lifecycle labels automatically. However, the current backlog can still contain issues without lifecycle labels.

Issues #2234 and #2235 are current examples. Their timelines contain no label removal events, but GitHub metadata does not establish the exact publication path. They therefore demonstrate missing lifecycle signals, not a confirmed API or `gentle-report` origin.

The pilot should therefore:

- treat labels as useful but incomplete selection evidence;
- include bounded unlabeled issues as a distinct input cohort;
- recognize `gentle-report` identity only when explicit evidence is available;
- report missing lifecycle labels without applying them;
- avoid interpreting absent labels as proof that an issue is invalid or out of scope.

title: fix(uninstall): Claude adapter removes user-owned keys and leaves orphaned CLAUDE.md content
body:
### Pre-flight Checks
- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand this issue needs status:approved before a PR can be opened

### Bug Description

The Claude Code uninstaller has two related issues caused by the lack of a granular pre/post diff for user files:

1. **Removes keys that may not belong to gentle-ai.** `rewriteJSONFile` in `internal/components/uninstall/cleaners.go` deletes hardcoded JSON paths (`permissions`, `outputStyle`, `theme`, `mcpServers.context7`) without checking whether those keys existed before installation. If the user had a pre-existing `permissions` or `theme` key, it gets deleted.

2. **Leaves orphaned content in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`.** Section cleanup relies on `<!-- gentle-ai:X -->` markers. If a prior installation version wrote content without markers, or if markers were corrupted/partially edited by the user, `removeMarkdownSections` silently skips the content. The preamble removal fingerprint (`## Personality` + `Senior Architect` + `## Rules`) also fails if the user customized any of those headings.

### Root Cause

The uninstaller uses a **declarative code-as-manifest** approach (hardcoded keys/sections to remove) but does NOT store a per-file diff of what was actually written during install. `~/.gentle-ai/state.json` tracks installed agents/components, and `~/.gentle-ai/backups/` snapshots files before uninstall — but there is no record of the file state *before* install to compare against.

### Steps to Reproduce

**Bug 1 — settings.json:**
1. Configure `~/.claude/settings.json` with a custom `permissions` block
2. Install gentle-ai with Claude agent
3. Uninstall gentle-ai
4. Observe: the user's `permissions` block is gone

**Bug 2 — CLAUDE.md:**
1. Install an older version of gentle-ai that writes CLAUDE.md without full markers
2. Upgrade gentle-ai (new version uses markers, but old content stays unmarked)
3. Uninstall
4. Observe: old unmarked content remains as orphaned text

### Expected Behavior

- Uninstall should only remove JSON values that it added (or restore the pre-install state from the install-time snapshot)
- CLAUDE.md should be fully clean after uninstall, or at minimum warn the user about unmanaged content

### Actual Behavior

- User-owned keys in settings.json get deleted
- Orphaned gentle-ai content persists in CLAUDE.md

### Proposed Fix Direction

Consider one of:
- **Install-time snapshot**: store a hash or copy of managed keys/sections at install time; on uninstall, only remove values that match what was injected
- **Merge-aware restore**: use the pre-uninstall backup combined with install-time state to reconstruct the user's original values
- **Warn on ambiguity**: if a key exists but doesn't match the expected installed value, warn instead of deleting

### Operating System

Linux (also reported on macOS)

### Agent / Client

Claude Code

### Shell

zsh

### Additional Context

Related issues: #1078 (symlink cleanup), #306 (sync/uninstall with symlinks), #1828 (kimi settings rewrite assumes JSON). The backup mechanism already captures pre-uninstall state — the gap is at install time.

title: bug(sdd-persistence): hybrid mode can persist incomplete or truncated Engram mirrors
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

Reported occurrences indicate that an SDD phase can explicitly select and forward Hybrid/Both (OpenSpec + Engram) persistence, yet leave an Engram tasks or apply-progress mirror condensed, stale, incomplete, or truncated relative to its OpenSpec artifact. This is separate from #2004's cross-session `artifact_store.mode` drift claim: these reports do not show a missing or changed mode at phase launch.

This is not a maintainer clean-room reproduction and does not attribute a root cause. Ownership is currently unknown among Gentle AI's defensive persistence/validation contract, OpenCode or tool transport, MCP, and Engram.

Relevant reported occurrences:

- [2.2.3 explicit-Hybrid incomplete cumulative mirror](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/2004#issuecomment-5145929971): a long cumulative apply-progress artifact was reported as abbreviated in Engram, and fresh gatekeepers rejected it after the phase reported success.
- [2.2.4 reported 50,000-character read-back](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/2004#issuecomment-5150617105): an update of about 67,072 characters reportedly read back as exactly 50,000 characters, omitting newer evidence.
- [2.2.4 below-50k incomplete mirrors](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/2004#issuecomment-5151515537): reported OpenSpec bodies of about 13,858 and 17,569 Unicode characters remained condensed or stale in Engram, with no raw provider or Engram error envelope. This does not prove a global 50,000-character boundary.

Current Gentle AI contracts require Hybrid writes, cumulative apply-progress, and read-back, but do not explicitly define byte/character parity, artifact-size limits, chunking, or typed partial-write behavior.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

The following is a proposed minimal reproduction, not a claim that maintainers have reproduced the behavior:

1. Start a new OpenCode session and use the native SDD Session Preflight to explicitly choose Both (OpenSpec + Engram).
2. Launch `sdd-apply` in that same session and retain the phase-launch evidence showing Hybrid/Both and the target OpenSpec and Engram artifact locations.
3. Persist a cumulative `apply-progress` artifact, then perform a fresh Engram read-back and compare its full body, terminal section, count, and hash against the OpenSpec artifact.
4. Repeat with bodies below and above 50,000 characters, preserving the request and response envelopes and proof that the complete body was sent.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

For an explicit Hybrid/Both launch, required cumulative artifacts should be recoverable from both selected stores in the form required by a fresh validation gate. If a body cannot be stored completely, the operation should fail before mutation with a typed, actionable oversized or partial-write result, or use a supported chunking/indexing mechanism.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The reported phase launches explicitly forwarded Hybrid/Both, but fresh gatekeepers found Engram mirrors condensed, stale, incomplete, or truncated after successful persistence was reported. One reported update read back as exactly 50,000 characters from an approximately 67,072-character input. Other reported incomplete mirrors were well below that size, so the available evidence does not establish a universal threshold or responsible layer.

### Gentle AI Version

Reported on `2.2.3` and `2.2.4`.

### Operating System

Linux (Other)

### AI Agent / Client

OpenCode

### 📋 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

No raw provider, MCP, or Engram error envelope was retained in the reported occurrences. The 2.2.4 50,000-character occurrence reported a successful update followed by a 50,000-character read-back.

### Additional Context

Exact known versions, only where reported:

- Gentle AI: `2.2.3` and `2.2.4`
- OpenCode: `1.18.10`
- Engram: `1.20.0` only in the [2.2.4 report](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/2004#issuecomment-5151515537)

To triage ownership, please provide or reproduce with:

1. The complete client request and response envelope for `mem_save` or `mem_update`, including any transport or provider errors.
2. Source and read-back byte/character counts and SHA-256 hashes, including whether newline normalization was applied.
3. Proof that the full body was handed to the client/tool before the call, such as an input length and hash captured immediately before dispatch.
4. A direct Engram and MCP reproduction independent of an SDD actor, using the same body and topic semantics.
5. Matched below- and above-50,000-character tests with complete read-back comparisons.
6. The SDD preflight decision and phase launch showing explicit Hybrid/Both forwarding, plus the associated OpenSpec and Engram paths or topic keys with private data redacted.

No source, test, repository, commit, PR, or release change is proposed by this report.

title: fix(tui): preserve Codex capabilities and OpenCode fast variants
body:
## Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`.

## 📝 Bug Description

Gentle AI's model-assignment flow does not preserve the full capability metadata advertised by the installed runtimes.

Codex CLI exposes model-specific reasoning levels, speed tiers, and service tiers, but the Codex Custom picker cannot reliably present all valid choices. OpenCode may expose an OpenAI `-fast` variant while the canonical catalog contains only the base model, causing the variant to be missing from the picker or configuration path.

This is a capability propagation bug. `fast` is a speed/service selection, not a reasoning effort. Pi is out of scope because it owns its runtime model selector.

## 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `codex debug models` using Codex CLI 0.146.0.
2. Note that `gpt-5.6-sol` and `gpt-5.6-terra` advertise `ultra`, `fast`, and service-tier metadata, while `gpt-5.6-luna` advertises `max`, `fast`, and service-tier metadata but not `ultra`.
3. Open Gentle AI and navigate to **Configure Models → Configure Codex models → Custom**.
4. Select the GPT-5.6 models and compare the available choices with the runtime metadata.
5. Configure an OpenAI model through OpenCode and compare the canonical model ID with its available `-fast` variant.
6. Observe that model-specific capabilities, service tiers, or the `-fast` variant are missing or not persisted separately.

## ✅ Expected Behavior

The Custom picker should:

- Use runtime-discovered selectable model IDs while retaining a curated fallback.
- Show reasoning choices per model.
- Show `max` and `ultra` only when the runtime advertises them.
- Treat `fast` as a separate speed/service selection, not as a reasoning effort.
- Persist the selected Codex `service_tier`.
- Materialize an OpenCode `-fast` alias only when an explicit same-provider canonical model exists.
- Preserve existing configuration behavior when no service tier is selected.

## ❌ Actual Behavior

The picker and configuration flow use incomplete or static capability information.

Model-specific reasoning levels such as `max` and `ultra` are not reliably exposed according to the installed runtime metadata. The `fast` capability is not represented as a separate speed/service selection, and an OpenCode `-fast` variant may be unavailable when only the canonical model exists.

As a result, users cannot select or persist the complete set of capabilities advertised by Codex CLI and OpenCode.

## 🖥️ Environment

- **Gentle AI:** `gga v2.10.1`; installed `gentle-ai` binary reports `2.2.4`
- **Operating System:** CachyOS Linux, x86_64, kernel 7.1.5-1-cachyos
- **AI Agent / Client:** Codex CLI 0.146.0 + OpenCode 1.18.8
- **Affected Area:** TUI (terminal UI)

## 💡 Logs / Error Output

Sanitized runtime capability evidence:

```
codex-cli 0.146.0
OpenCode 1.18.8

gpt-5.6-sol:
  multi_agent_version: v2
  reasoning: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra
  additional_speed_tiers: ["fast"]
  service_tiers: ["priority"]

gpt-5.6-terra:
  multi_agent_version: v2
  reasoning: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra
  additional_speed_tiers: ["fast"]
  service_tiers: ["priority"]

gpt-5.6-luna:
  multi_agent_version: v1
  reasoning: low, medium, high, xhigh, max
  additional_speed_tiers: ["fast"]
  service_tiers: ["priority"]
```

## Additional Context

Related work:

- [#1087](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/1087) covers runtime Codex model-ID discovery.
- [#2080](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/2080) covers Codex model discovery, visibility, and API support.
- [#2134](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/2134) covers asynchronous Codex discovery in the TUI.
- [#1648](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/1648) and [#1695](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/1695) cover OpenCode provider-ID fallback for variants.
- [#1066](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/1066) and [#1067](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/1067) introduced the GPT-5.6 defaults but explicitly deferred `max`/`ultra`.

A local candidate was implemented with bounded runtime discovery, model-specific effort choices, separate speed/service-tier persistence, safe same-provider OpenCode fast aliases, and asynchronous TUI discovery.

Focused tests, `go vet`, `gofmt`, `git diff --check`, and `go build ./cmd/gentle-ai` pass. The full repository suite has one unrelated environment-sensitive failure in `internal/cli:TestEngramPathGuidanceDefault`, which expects a `go/bin` path fragment while the active Go installation uses a mise-managed path.

No PR will be opened until this issue receives `status:approved`.

title: feat(cli): add explicit workspace MCP manifest reconciliation
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues and pull requests and found no generic workspace MCP manifest consumer.
- [x] I understand implementation must wait for `status:approved`.

### Affected Area

CLI / Installation Pipeline / MCP components.

### Problem Statement

Gentle-AI already owns agent-specific MCP paths, render strategies, atomic file merging, backups, sync behavior, and removal for built-in integrations. However, `internal/components/mcp.Inject` still hard-codes Context7 and accepts no provider-neutral server definition.

Projects therefore cannot keep durable MCP intent in reviewed workspace manifests and ask Gentle-AI to reconcile that intent across supported harnesses. Their current alternatives are manual edits to generated agent configuration, tool-specific injectors, or automatic consumption of repository content. The first two create competing owners; the last lets an untrusted repository activate tools merely by being opened.

### Proposed Solution

Add an explicit, fail-closed workspace MCP reconciliation surface:

```text
gentle-ai mcp sync --cwd <project-root> --agent codex --agent claude-code --dry-run --json
gentle-ai mcp sync --cwd <project-root> --agent codex --agent claude-code --confirm-plan sha256:<digest> --json
gentle-ai mcp status --cwd <project-root> --agent codex --agent claude-code --json
gentle-ai mcp remove --cwd <project-root> --agent codex --agent claude-code --dry-run --json
gentle-ai mcp remove --cwd <project-root> --agent codex --agent claude-code --confirm-plan sha256:<digest> --json
```

The dry-run derives a digest bound to the canonical Git root, explicit agents, exact manifest bytes, current destination-file digests, and planned mutations. Apply/remove must rederive the same plan before mutation. There should be no unbound `--yes` path.

Initial scope:

- discover regular, non-symlink `mcps/*.yaml` declarations only after the explicit command;
- require a strict schema and reject duplicate keys, unknown fields, multiple YAML documents, unsafe IDs, root escapes, and malformed targets;
- support workspace-scoped streamable HTTP declarations first;
- render through optional workspace MCP capabilities on the Claude Code and Codex adapters rather than switching on agent IDs;
- write Claude project entries to root `.mcp.json` and Codex project entries to `.codex/config.toml`;
- preserve unrelated user entries and fail on identity collisions;
- keep host-local ownership state under `~/.gentle-ai/workspaces/<root-digest>/` so repository content cannot claim ownership;
- remove only exact, still-owned entries and preserve drift with an explicit manual action;
- use the existing backup/mutation/rollback primitives for config plus ownership state;
- never auto-consume manifests from ordinary `install` or `sync`.

`status` should expose the evidence progression from #1873: `declared`, `rendered`, `written`, `loaded`, and `operational`, plus `pending_approval`, `unverified`, or `degraded`. File existence must never be reported as native runtime success.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Automatically consume `mcps/` during normal sync.** Rejected: repository content would become executable configuration without a separately confirmed plan.
- **Add a WriterAgent- or vendor-specific component.** Rejected: it duplicates the existing adapter architecture and does not generalize.
- **Let each project write `.mcp.json` and `.codex/config.toml` directly.** Rejected: generated files become competing durable authorities and drift across harnesses.
- **Extend global `uninstall --all` to scan repositories.** Rejected: global uninstall must not discover and mutate arbitrary workspace roots; explicit `mcp remove --cwd` is the safe boundary.

### Additional Context

- Blocked by #2213, which corrects Claude Code workspace MCP projection before this feature builds on that adapter path.
- `internal/components/mcp/` already provides the renderer seam but currently hard-codes Context7.
- `internal/agents/` already owns per-agent paths and strategies.
- #1873 is approved for native-runtime capability certification and should govern loaded/operational claims.

title: fix(ci): make Claude network-none proof not applicable for legacy PR heads
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing open and closed issues and confirmed this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`.

### 📝 Bug Description

[Main commit `93e0e42d62949946c635938ad36cf20546dccb2c`](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/commit/93e0e42d62949946c635938ad36cf20546dccb2c) adds the required `Claude Network-None Runtime (Required)` job and `e2e/Dockerfile.claude-network-none`. The job checks out the exact pull request candidate and then unconditionally builds that fixture. A valid legacy candidate can predate the fixture, so this is a base-workflow applicability regression, not a candidate-caused failure.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Inspect [the CI workflow at `93e0e42d62949946c635938ad36cf20546dccb2c`](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/93e0e42d62949946c635938ad36cf20546dccb2c/.github/workflows/ci.yml), which checks out `github.event.pull_request.head.sha` and builds `e2e/Dockerfile.claude-network-none` without an applicability guard.
2. Use the valid legacy head [`15460dd387e285bc777f340d62bbd470147c39f8`](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/commit/15460dd387e285bc777f340d62bbd470147c39f8) from [PR #2126](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/2126). That head does not contain `e2e/Dockerfile.claude-network-none`.
3. Inspect [run 30715340413](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/actions/runs/30715340413) and its [Claude Network-None job](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/actions/runs/30715340413/job/91409859283).
4. Observe that checkout succeeds, the image build fails because the Dockerfile is absent, and the runtime proof is skipped.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

A legacy pull request head that does not contain the newly introduced fixture is handled by an explicit safe preflight as not applicable. It must not be reported as a successful runtime proof or silently waived. Main, merge-queue, and current integrated candidates for which the fixture is present must retain the mandatory, fail-closed image build and network-none runtime proof.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The required job runs unconditionally against the legacy head. Its build step fails with `failed to read dockerfile: open Dockerfile.claude-network-none: no such file or directory`, and the transport proof never runs. The resulting required-check failure is caused by the newer base workflow referencing a fixture absent from the candidate.

### Gentle AI Version

`main` at `93e0e42d62949946c635938ad36cf20546dccb2c`

### Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client

Claude Code

### 📋 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
ERROR: failed to build: failed to solve: failed to read dockerfile: open Dockerfile.claude-network-none: no such file or directory
```

### Additional Context

#### Impact

This creates a false-red mandatory check for valid legacy pull requests and attributes a workflow applicability defect to the candidate. It blocks review and integration without exercising the runtime proof.

#### Public Evidence

- [Workflow and fixture introduction in main](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/commit/93e0e42d62949946c635938ad36cf20546dccb2c)
- [Exact workflow source](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/blob/93e0e42d62949946c635938ad36cf20546dccb2c/.github/workflows/ci.yml)
- [Legacy PR #2126](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/2126)
- [Failing run 30715340413](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/actions/runs/30715340413)
- [Failing job 91409859283](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/actions/runs/30715340413/job/91409859283)

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The workflow determines fixture applicability before attempting the Claude image build.
- [ ] A legacy candidate without `e2e/Dockerfile.claude-network-none` produces an explicit not-applicable result rather than a runtime success, waiver, or failure attributed to candidate code.
- [ ] A current integrated candidate with the fixture still executes the required image build and network-none runtime proof.
- [ ] A present but invalid fixture, image-build failure, or runtime-proof failure remains fail-closed.
- [ ] Regression coverage proves both the legacy not-applicable path and the current mandatory proof path.

title: feat(tui): expose OpenCode native fallback agents (general/explore) in TUI model picker
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

### 🔍 Affected Area

OpenCode Agent Configuration & TUI Model Picker

### 💡 Problem Statement

OpenCode includes two native built-in fallback agents:
- `general` (the default primary assistant for un-delegated tasks)
- `explore` (the default read-only research assistant for codebase and web exploration)

Currently, Gentle AI's TUI Model Picker allows configuring models for SDD phases, Judgment Day agents, and native review lenses, but does not expose `general` and `explore` as configurable roles in the TUI model picker. As a result, users cannot assign custom models specifically to OpenCode's native fallback agents from the Gentle AI interface.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

1. Add `general` and `explore` to `NativeFallbackPhases()` in `internal/opencode/models.go` (or expose them as configurable agent roles).
2. Update `OpenCodeModelAssignments` and the TUI Model Picker screen so users can independently select providers/models for `general` and `explore`.
3. In `internal/components/sdd/profiles.go`, respect user-configured TUI model assignments for `general` and `explore`, falling back to `sdd-mid` when unassigned.
4. Add unit tests for TUI model picker rendering and `opencode.json` generation.

title: bug(review): fresh candidate rejected before native START
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues), including open and closed issues, and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

On Gentle AI 2.2.4 through the Pi negotiated review integration, read-only STATUS reports a fresh workspace candidate as ready and returns `review.start`. Executing START is then rejected by the provider integration before native START with `candidate-view-invalid`.

The same rejection occurs for two distinct immutable candidate identities: first with four intended-untracked paths, then after staging those same four paths. Both failures explicitly report that no lineage was created and no mutation was performed. A valid candidate therefore cannot enter the review lifecycle, and the consumer has no provider-owned recovery transition beyond resolving the native-operation failure.

This report records the observed boundary only; it does not claim a root cause.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. On Linux under WSL2, use Pi with Gentle AI 2.2.4 in a normal Git worktree.
2. Prepare a workspace candidate containing four intended-untracked paths and no other visible changes.
3. Call negotiated review STATUS with contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`.
4. Observe `reason_code: fresh_target_ready`, `action: start`, and an exact provider-owned `review.start` transition for opaque candidate A (`sha256:8ed8f9639ba2bffaaedaa872ecc0234e44670adf960e86ebf83b9f4cd9657f64`).
5. Execute START through the Pi integration using ordinary mode.
6. Observe the pre-native `candidate-view-invalid` failure and confirm `lineage_created: false` and `mutation_performed: false`.
7. Stage exactly the same four candidate paths, producing opaque candidate B (`sha256:8f4104173083336ca1dc4a2bd230f4f683fae58483c67d30a1feca9e170c5cb8`).
8. Call STATUS again and observe another fresh exact START transition for candidate B.
9. Execute START once for candidate B and observe the same pre-native rejection with no lineage or mutation.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

A candidate accepted by negotiated STATUS as `fresh_target_ready` should either enter native START successfully or receive a typed provider-owned stop/recovery transition that explains which candidate-view invariant failed.

If provider preflight can reject the candidate view, STATUS and START should apply the same validation so STATUS does not advertise an operation that cannot begin.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

STATUS advertises `review.start` for both candidate identities, but START rejects each before native execution:

- `status: blocked`
- `outcome: native-operation-failed`
- `code: candidate-view-invalid`
- `message: candidate view rejected before native START`
- `lineage_created: false`
- `mutation_performed: false`
- `mutation_outcome: none`
- `next_action: resolve-native-operation-failure`

The candidate bytes remain unchanged. After the second attempt, exactly four intended paths remain staged; no review lineage, commit, push, or publication was created.

### Gentle AI Version

2.2.4

### Operating System

Windows (WSL)

### AI Agent / Client

Other (Pi 0.83.0)

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
Attempt A:
status reason: fresh_target_ready
projection: workspace
candidate shape: 4 intended-untracked paths
START code: candidate-view-invalid
lineage_created: false
mutation_performed: false
mutation_outcome: none

Attempt B:
status reason: fresh_target_ready
projection: workspace
candidate shape: the same 4 paths staged
START code: candidate-view-invalid
lineage_created: false
mutation_performed: false
mutation_outcome: none
```

### Additional Context

Client: Pi 0.83.0. Shell: bash. Architecture: x86_64. Kernel family: Linux under WSL2.

The operation shape was `review.status` followed by the exact provider-returned `review.start`, using contract v2 and workspace projection. No raw command line, repository path, private project name, username, hostname, credentials, environment values, source content, or diff is included.

Related but not duplicates:

- #1807 concerned unsupported START flags on 2.1.11 and was closed after invalid requests became typed as not started.
- #1856 concerned a post-commit candidate-context failure with unknown mutation outcome; this occurrence is rejected before native START and explicitly creates no lineage.

title: feat(grok): add verified full native Grok Build support
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues). This is an implementation follow-up to #1739 that records the verified full native scope rather than the bounded first slice proposed there.
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`.

### 🔍 Affected Area

Installation Pipeline

Secondary areas: CLI, TUI, Agent Detection, Catalog/Steps, SDD, MCP, permissions, sync, doctor, uninstall, and documentation.

### 💡 Problem Statement

Gentle AI does not currently manage Grok Build as a first-class native agent. Grok users cannot receive the same safe install, configuration, SDD, persistent memory, skills, project scope, diagnostics, sync, and uninstall lifecycle available for the other supported agents without relying on Claude compatibility or maintaining `.grok` files manually.

The integration also has correctness and safety constraints that a minimal path-only adapter does not cover:

- Grok uses native commands, agents, skills, hooks, permissions, and TOML MCP configuration at both user and project scope.
- Global and workspace files must not leak into OpenClaw or another adapter's workspace.
- Generated files and named TOML tables need ownership semantics so install, sync, and uninstall preserve user edits and collisions.
- Grok subagents use native frontmatter, tool names, MCP inheritance, and `spawn_subagent`; Claude-specific model routing and prompt vocabulary cannot be copied verbatim.
- A partial uninstall must not leave global files, external workspace files, or Gentle AI state in a mixed transaction state.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Add complete native Grok Build support with the following behavior.

#### Native adapter and product integration

- Register Grok Build as a full-tier agent.
- Detect an existing `grok` binary and `~/.grok` configuration.
- Add Grok to the catalog, TUI, installer, validation, doctor, state, sync, upgrade, and uninstall surfaces.
- Configure Grok without executing its remote bootstrap installer.

#### Global and workspace layouts

- Write global instructions to `~/.grok/AGENTS.md`.
- Write workspace instructions to `<repo>/.grok/rules/gentle-ai.md`.
- Project native `commands/`, `agents/`, `skills/`, `hooks/`, and `config.toml` assets at the correct scope.
- Reject workspace paths whose symlink ancestry escapes the repository.
- Keep Grok and OpenClaw workspace destinations isolated.

#### SDD, Judgment Day, agents, and skills

- Project 18 named agents into Grok-native frontmatter.
- Install 10 native SDD commands.
- Expose 11 public skills while keeping internal SDD executor documents out of Grok's public skill registry.
- Use native tools and `spawn_subagent` with capability-specific permission modes.
- Inherit the active Grok session model instead of emitting unsupported per-phase model or reasoning overrides.
- Restrict MCP inheritance to the named Engram server where required.

#### MCP, permissions, hooks, and ownership

- Configure Context7 and Engram through Grok-native TOML.
- Preserve user TOML, comments, multiline strings, structural boundaries, and file modes.
- Add native permission rules and the skill-registry startup hook.
- Discover semantic Engram operations through Grok's native `search_tool` / `use_tool` bridge.
- Use ownership digests for generated Markdown and managed TOML.
- Preserve edited or unowned collisions instead of overwriting or deleting them.

#### Transactional uninstall

- Snapshot global files, external workspace files, and Gentle AI state before uninstall.
- Roll back Pi cleanup, late operation, state-read, and state-write failures.
- Restore every snapshot entry best-effort and join restoration errors.
- Preserve backup material and manual recovery instructions if rollback itself fails.

#### Deliberate boundaries

- Users install the Grok CLI themselves; Gentle AI configures an existing runtime.
- GGA and CodeGraph remain excluded because neither exposes a compatible Grok provider contract.
- Grok inherits the active session model; no unsupported per-agent model overrides are invented.
- `gentle-ai sync --agent grok` refreshes global managed configuration. Project-local configuration is refreshed by rerunning workspace install from that repository.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- **Bounded adapter-only slice from #1739.** Easier to review, but it leaves native SDD projection, project scope, permissions, hooks, ownership, and safe uninstall unresolved. The complete implementation is already built and verified as one coherent lifecycle.
- **Rely only on Grok's Claude compatibility.** Useful for discovery, but it does not provide first-class Gentle AI ownership, native paths, project isolation, permissions, or deterministic uninstall behavior.
- **Reuse the generic Codex TOML strategy unchanged.** The base format is similar, but Grok needs destination-specific table ownership, permission handling, multiline-string-safe scanning, and native MCP execution semantics.
- **Run Grok's remote bootstrap installer automatically.** More convenient, but it makes Gentle AI execute a separate remote trust step. Manual CLI installation keeps that decision with the user.

### 📎 Additional Context

#### Published implementation

- Branch: [`rechedev9:agent/grok-native-support`](https://github.com/rechedev9/gentle-ai/tree/agent/grok-native-support)
- Full comparison: [`main...rechedev9:agent/grok-native-support`](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/compare/main...rechedev9:gentle-ai:agent/grok-native-support)
- [`f781f6bc`](https://github.com/rechedev9/gentle-ai/commit/f781f6bc0b6d57d39ea34485806e82a4440f03e3) — `feat(grok): add native Grok Build support`
- [`ae739747`](https://github.com/rechedev9/gentle-ai/commit/ae739747b6e7c3852777cdae085e8041da7e2cde) — `docs(grok): document native Grok integration`

#### Verification

- `git diff --check`, formatting checks, and `go vet ./...` completed successfully.
- Candidate package, focused CLI, race-enabled backup, and race-enabled uninstall suites completed successfully.
- Late-operation and post-state-write rollback cases passed 20 repeated runs.
- Linux and Windows builds completed successfully.
- Real Grok Build 0.2.118 global and workspace installations completed successfully.
- `grok inspect --json` discovered the generated agents, commands, skills, instructions, permissions, hooks, and MCP configuration.
- `grok mcp doctor` reported two healthy servers and zero failures.
- Full uninstall removed 137 managed files and 69 managed directories without removing neighboring user content.
- Mixed OpenClaw/Grok workspace, Judgment Day lifecycle, TOML preservation, idempotence, and ownership smokes completed successfully.
- A four-lens native RDD reviewed the exact 103-path candidate with no CRITICAL or WARNING findings.
- RDD lineage: `review-ac926c99173a59ff`.
- RDD `post-apply` gate: `allow`.
- Approved candidate tree: `4c727741b72775061469d8bc83a0e9f87a39ecbc`.

Two unrelated host-baseline failures were reproduced outside the candidate: Git 2.34.1 on the verification server lacks `git merge-tree --write-tree` for `internal/reviewtransaction`, and one existing CLI reconciliation test reports `receipt_scope_changed`. No `internal/reviewtransaction` path is changed by this implementation.

title: feat(release): declare the provider surface as a signed release artifact
body:
## Problem

Keeping `gentle-pi` at parity with `gentle-ai` is currently a manual transcription ritual, repeated every release.

The consumer hand-maintains a per-version capability table, ground-truthed by booting each released binary by hand; a hand-written contract-hash map; and the pinned version duplicated across several literals. That last one already failed in production: the installer once reported installing one version while writing a different one to disk, because two hardcoded copies survived a pin bump.

The irony is that the distribution channel already exists and its payload is discarded. `.goreleaser.yaml` ships `docs/review-integration.md` and `contracts/review-integration/v1/{schemas,fixtures}` inside all four platform archives, and the consumer's installer walks the extracted tree and keeps only the executable. Meanwhile `contracts/review-integration/v2/` is never packaged at all, even though the consumer runs the v2 lane exclusively.

`gentle-ai` also already knows how to describe itself: `review capabilities` emits operations, gates, projections, schemas and features. That output is simply never captured into a shipped file.

## Requested outcome

`gentle-ai` declares its surface as a signed release artifact, so consumers verify and consume a declaration instead of transcribing it.

Scope, provider side only:

1. **A versioned, self-describing release-artifact contract** under `contracts/`, versioned independently from `review-integration`. A contract-major change becomes an explicit compatibility event; a consumer meeting an unsupported major must fail closed with an actionable error rather than infer a layout.
2. **A deterministic semantic capability snapshot** that excludes executable, build and host identity so the same bytes apply on every platform. Today `review capabilities` injects the running binary's digest plus Go build and VCS identity, so its live output cannot ship as-is in a common archive.
3. **A signed, platform-independent assets archive** carrying that manifest, its schema, the contract files and the snapshot, inside the existing checksum and minisign envelope so it is covered by the same signature that binds repository and tag.
4. **Post-publish, post-verification downstream notification**, visible and retryable on failure, and structurally unable to invalidate a release that already published and verified.

Unknown mandatory features keep being rejected, matching the advertised `compatibility.unknown_mandatory: "reject"`. Nothing consumer-specific is published from here.

## Why the release shape must be extended carefully

The release plan is enforced in three layers, and one of them is easy to miss: besides the artifact counts and the per-archive platform matrix, `internal/releasepolicy/policy.go` reads the live `.goreleaser.yaml` and `.github/workflows/release.yml` from disk and diffs their YAML AST against embedded Go constants. Any edit to either file needs its constant updated in the same commit or CI fails closed before GoReleaser runs.

That file exists to make the release shape assertable rather than guessable. The amendment must admit exactly one additional archive and add strictly new assertions (no platform axis, no binaries), never relax the existing four-platform matrix, the per-platform-archive binary requirement, or the Windows/Scoop prohibition.

Two related safety notes:

- `brews:` has no `ids:` filter today. That has never mattered with a single archive, but the Homebrew formula is user-facing, so the additional archive needs an explicit archive id and an explicit `ids:` on `brews:`, proven by comparing the formula GoReleaser produces in snapshot mode.
- The self-updater resolves exactly one asset filename by format and reads one manifest line, so it never enumerates archives. An additive assets archive cannot break existing installs.

## Scope of work

Four repository-local units, delivered as a chained set:

- **A1a** — contract namespace, canonical encoder, entry/path/mode rules, tree digest, manifest schema and fixtures, contract doc.
- **A1b** — semantic snapshot projection, generator command, byte-stable golden.
- **A2** — archive assembly, release-policy amendment, verify-assets update, Homebrew safety, docs. Its first task is empirical rather than implementation: inspect the real snapshot artifacts and tarball member paths before committing to an assembly approach.
- **A3** — downstream notification, credential-gated so it ships inert until the receiver exists on the consumer's default branch.

## Out of scope

- Generated client code for new provider operations. The mechanism can detect and report drift; it cannot write a consumer's decoder.
- Anything consumer-specific published from this repository.
- Any relaxation of existing release-shape exactness.
- A prerelease publication path. The release workflow deliberately excludes prerelease tags, and that stays.

title: fix(community-tool): treat MCP initialize EOF during Pi CodeGraph sync as non-fatal pending action
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand this issue needs `status:approved` before a PR can be opened

### 📝 Bug Description

During `gentle-ai sync` (or the TUI `Upgrade + Sync` workflow), if the Pi CodeGraph MCP stdio process closes unexpectedly during capability probing, the sync pipeline fails hard with:

```text
Sync failed: execute sync pipeline: sync Pi CodeGraph: Pi CodeGraph MCP capability probe failed: MCP initialize: EOF
```

This occurs because `probePiCodeGraphMCPCapability` in `internal/components/communitytool/pi_codegraph.go` wraps stdio transport initialization failures directly as fatal sync pipeline errors.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Pi CodeGraph community tool integration.
2. Cause the configured MCP transport binary (`codegraph mcp`) to exit immediately upon launch (e.g. uninitialized binary or broken stdio pipe returning `EOF`).
3. Run `gentle-ai sync` or invoke `Upgrade + Sync` from the TUI.
4. Observe that the entire sync pipeline halts with an unhandled `MCP initialize: EOF` error.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

If the MCP transport returns `EOF` during the capability probe step of `sync`, Gentle AI should record a non-fatal pending manual action (e.g., `Pi CodeGraph integration remains pending: MCP server exited with EOF during initialization probe`) and allow the rest of the sync pipeline to complete successfully.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The sync pipeline fails completely:
```text
Sync failed: execute sync pipeline: sync Pi CodeGraph: Pi CodeGraph MCP capability probe failed: MCP initialize: EOF
```

### 📋 Affected Area

Community tools / Pi CodeGraph / CLI sync pipeline

### 💡 Proposed Fix

In `internal/components/communitytool/pi_codegraph.go`, inspect errors returned by `probePiCodeGraphMCPCapability`. If the error indicates a transport or initialization failure such as `EOF`, record a pending integration status and manual action instead of aborting the sync pipeline.

title: feat(system): Android/Termux first-class platform detection + external CodeGraph support
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand this issue needs status:approved before a PR can be opened
- [x] This is part of the Android/Termux support series:
  - #1291 (EACCES external storage — active, needs approval)
  - #2141 (Engram binary paths)
  - #2142 (termux-open-url)

### Affected Area
System Detection, Tool Installation Pipeline

### Problem
gentle-ai assumes Linux/macOS/Windows only. On Android/Termux (`GOOS=android`, `GOARCH=arm64`):

1. **Platform detection**: `IsSupportedOS` rejects `android`, `resolvePlatformProfile` has no Android case, `EnsureSupportedOS` error message doesn't mention Android. This is the root cause that blocks everything downstream.

2. **CodeGraph install**: `tool.go:93` defines CodeGraph with `npm install -g @colbymchenry/codegraph@latest`. On Android ARM64, npm downloads x64 binary → fails. The ARM64 binary IS available — [core-termux](https://github.com/DevCoreXOfficial/core-termux) (v4.18.0+) provides it via `core install ai --codegraph`. But gentle-ai never checks `exec.LookPath("codegraph")` before npm install.

3. **OpenCode CodeGraph guidance**: `codegraph_guidance.go` writes `codegraph install` into agent prompts. The ARM64 binary uses `codegraph serve --mcp` (no `install` subcommand). Without Android awareness, guidance is broken.

4. **Pi MCP probe**: `pi_codegraph.go` hardcodes user-specific paths instead of using `exec.LookPath`. On Android, `~/.local/bin` may not be correct.

### Proposed Solution

#### File: `internal/system/detect.go` (lines 43-44, 104-106, 117-163)

**`IsSupportedOS`**: Add `|| goos == "android"`:
```go
func IsSupportedOS(goos string) bool {
    return goos == "darwin" || goos == "linux" || goos == "windows" || goos == "android"
}
```

**`osReleaseContent`**: Add android block before linux guard:
```go
func osReleaseContent(goos string) (string, error) {
    if goos == "android" {
        prefix := os.Getenv("PREFIX")
        if prefix != "" {
            if data, err := os.ReadFile(prefix + "/etc/os-release"); err == nil {
                return string(data), nil
            }
        }
        return "", nil
    }
    if goos != "linux" {
        return "", nil
    }
    // ...existing linux code...
```

**`resolvePlatformProfile`**: Add `case "android"` before `default`:
```go
case "android":
    profile.PackageManager = "pkg"
    profile.Supported = true
    distro := detectLinuxDistro(linuxOSRelease)
    if distro != LinuxDistroUnknown {
        profile.LinuxDistro = distro
    }
    return profile
```

#### File: `internal/system/guard.go` (line 21)

Update error message:
```go
return fmt.Errorf("%w: only macOS, Linux, Windows, and Android are supported (detected %s)", ErrUnsupportedOS, goos)
```

#### File: `internal/components/communitytool/tool.go` (lines 91-127)

Gate npm CodeGraph install behind `runtime.GOOS != "android"`. On Android, use LookPath strategy:
```go
// In CodeGraph CommunityToolDef or equivalent resolution logic
if runtime.GOOS == "android" {
    // Verify codegraph via LookPath instead of npm install
    if _, err := exec.LookPath("codegraph"); err != nil {
        // Show actionable message: "CodeGraph not found. Install via: core install ai --codegraph"
        // But do NOT block — CodeGraph is optional
    }
}
```

#### File: `internal/components/communitytool/codegraph_guidance.go` (lines 170-182)

On Android, write `serve --mcp` guidance instead of `codegraph install`:
```go
if runtime.GOOS == "android" {
    // ARM64 codegraph binary uses serve --mcp, no install subcommand
    // Write: mcpServers.codegraph = {"command": "codegraph", "args": ["serve", "--mcp"]}
}
```

#### File: `internal/components/communitytool/pi_codegraph.go`

Replace hardcoded path checks with `exec.LookPath("codegraph")`:
```go
// Instead of checking ~/.local/bin/codegraph:
codegraphPath, err := exec.LookPath("codegraph")
```

### Migration and Coexistence

| Scenario | Behavior | Conflicts |
|---|---|---|
| Clean install, no CodeGraph in PATH | Shows guidance to install | None |
| CodeGraph from core-termux ($PREFIX/bin) | LookPath finds it | None |
| CodeGraph manually installed | LookPath finds it (PATH) | None |
| npm CodeGraph present (old) | LookPath picks it | None |
| OpenCode guidance on Android | Writes `serve --mcp` | No config overwrite |
| Pi probe on Android | Uses LookPath, not hardcoded dir | Compatible |

### User Data Guarantee
- No config files modified or deleted.
- Existing OpenCode MCP configs NOT overwritten.
- Pi's CodeGraph database untouched.
- Rollback: revert code + rebuild = original behavior.

### AI-Agent Implementation Notes

1. **Order of changes**: detect.go + guard.go FIRST (platform detection). Then tool.go (CodeGraph install). Then codegraph_guidance.go (OpenCode guidance). Then pi_codegraph.go (MCP probe). Each depends on the previous being in place, but they don't share mutable state.

2. **Constants to preserve**: `PackageName: "@colbymchenry/codegraph@latest"` should remain defined (version comparison on non-Android), but gated behind `runtime.GOOS != "android"`.

3. **PATH resolution**: On Termux, `$PREFIX/bin` is in PATH. `exec.LookPath("codegraph")` suffices. Do NOT add Termux-specific path hacks.

4. **Cross-platform safety**: ALL changes must be gated by `runtime.GOOS == "android"` so Linux/macOS/Windows behavior is 100% unchanged. Use normal if-blocks, not build tags.

5. **`$PREFIX`**: Set on Termux to `/data/data/com.termux/files/usr`. The `detect.go` changes use `os.Getenv("PREFIX")` — safe because only Termux sets it.

### Verification
```bash
# Platform detection
go test ./internal/system/... -run "TestIsSupportedOS|TestDetect|TestGuard"
# CodeGraph
go test ./internal/components/communitytool/... -run "TestCodeGraph"
# Pi probe
go test ./internal/components/communitytool/... -run "TestPiCodeGraph"
# Manual smoke on Android ARM64 Termux:
go build -o /tmp/gentle-ai ./cmd/gentle-ai/
/tmp/gentle-ai doctor | grep codegraph
/tmp/gentle-ai install --agent pi  # Should not attempt npm install
```

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `IsSupportedOS("android")` returns `true`
- [ ] `resolvePlatformProfile("android", ...)` returns `{PackageManager: "pkg", Supported: true}`
- [ ] `gentle-ai doctor` shows `[ok] tool:codegraph` when codegraph is in PATH on Android
- [ ] `gentle-ai install --agent pi` on Android does NOT attempt npm install for CodeGraph
- [ ] `gentle-ai sync --agent pi` on Android writes `serve --mcp` MCP config
- [ ] Pi MCP probe uses `exec.LookPath("codegraph")`
- [ ] All existing tests pass on Linux/macOS/Windows (no regression)
- [ ] Existing OpenCode MCP configs preserved (non-Android unaffected)

title: feat(tui): Android/Termux support — termux-open-url for browser commands
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand this issue needs status:approved before a PR can be opened
- [x] Part of the Android/Termux support series. Related: #2141 (Engram paths)

### Affected Area
TUI — browser URL opening

### Problem
gentle-ai's `openBrowserCmd` dispatches URL opening per platform:
- macOS: `open <url>`
- Windows: `rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler <url>`
- Default: `xdg-open <url>`

On Android/Termux, `xdg-open` does not exist. The correct command is `termux-open-url` (from `termux-api` package). Currently, calling `xdg-open` on Android either fails silently or shows "command not found" in the TUI.

[core-termux v4.18.0+](https://github.com/DevCoreXOfficial/core-termux) applies this same fix in its termux-patches.go patcher. This issue makes it official upstream so the patcher becomes a no-op.

### Proposed Solution

**File: `internal/tui/model.go` (lines 4088-4102)**

Add `case "android"` to `openBrowserCmd`:
```go
func openBrowserCmd(url string) tea.Cmd {
    return func() tea.Msg {
        var cmd *exec.Cmd
        switch runtime.GOOS {
        case "darwin":
            cmd = execCommandFn("open", url)
        case "windows":
            cmd = execCommandFn("rundll32", "url.dll,FileProtocolHandler", url)
        case "android":
            cmd = execCommandFn("termux-open-url", url)
        default:
            cmd = execCommandFn("xdg-open", url)
        }
        _ = cmd.Start()
        return nil
    }
}
```

`termux-open-url` opens URLs in the Android system browser via `termux-api`. It supports HTTP/HTTPS, geo:, tel:, and mailto: URIs.

### Migration and Coexistence

| Scenario | Behavior | Conflicts |
|---|---|---|
| Android + termux-api installed | Opens browser correctly | None |
| Android + no termux-api | Falls through to xdg-open (fails, no crash) | None — cmd.Start() returns error silently |
| Linux/macOS/Windows | Unchanged | Zero |
| core-termux patcher | After merge, patcher becomes no-op | Idempotent — harmless |

### AI-Agent Implementation Notes
1. **Single switch case addition** — do NOT modify existing cases.
2. **No new dependencies** — `exec.Command` already imported.
3. **termux-open-url** is installed via `pkg install termux-api`.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `openBrowserCmd` on `GOOS=android` calls `termux-open-url`
- [ ] macOS, Windows, Linux behavior unchanged
- [ ] Graceful fallback if termux-open-url missing (no crash)
- [ ] `go test ./internal/tui/...` passes
- [ ] core-termux patcher becomes no-op for model.go after this PR

title: feat(engram): Android/Termux install paths and upgrade mapping
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand this issue needs status:approved before a PR can be opened
- [x] Part of the Android/Termux support series.

### Affected Area
Engram auto-installation and upgrade pipeline

### Problem
gentle-ai downloads and installs the Engram binary for persistent memory. On Android/Termux (`GOOS=android`, `GOARCH=arm64`):

1. **Asset lookup fails**: `DownloadLatestBinary` uses `profile.OS` to determine the GitHub release asset URL. Since there is no `android` asset on Engram's releases, the download URL returns 404. The correct asset is the `linux` one — Go cross-compiles Engram for `linux/arm64`, which runs on Android via Termux glibc.

2. **Install directory is wrong**: `engramInstallDir` returns `/usr/local/bin` on Linux-like systems. On Termux, this path is not writable. The correct path is `$PREFIX/bin` (typically `/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin`).

3. **Self-upgrade fails the same way**: `internal/update/upgrade/download.go` uses `profile.OS` to resolve archive names. With no `android` mapping, the upgrade produces invalid URLs.

4. **core-termux alternative**: [core-termux v4.18.0+](https://github.com/DevCoreXOfficial/core-termux) compiles Engram from source and installs to `$PREFIX/bin/engram`. gentle-ai should detect it there via LookPath before attempting download.

### Proposed Solution

#### File: `internal/components/engram/download.go`

**`DownloadLatestBinary` (line 164):** Map android → linux for asset URLs:
```go
goos := profile.OS
if goos == "android" {
    goos = "linux"
}
```

**`engramInstallDir` (line 654):** Add Android branch:
```go
func engramInstallDir(goos string) string {
    if goos == "android" {
        prefix := os.Getenv("PREFIX")
        if prefix != "" {
            return filepath.Join(prefix, "bin")
        }
        return "/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin"
    }
    // ... existing windows/linux checks unchanged ...
```

**Pre-download LookPath check:** Before download, check if Engram is already in PATH:
```go
if engramPath, err := exec.LookPath("engram"); err == nil {
    return engramPath, nil  // Skip download
}
```

#### File: `internal/update/upgrade/download.go`

**`Download` function (line 86):** Add android → linux mapping:
```go
func Download(ctx context.Context, r update.UpdateResult, profile system.PlatformProfile) error {
    if profile.OS == "android" {
        profile.OS = "linux"
    }
    // ... existing windows check unchanged ...
```

### Migration and Coexistence

| Scenario | Behavior | Conflicts |
|---|---|---|
| Clean Android, no Engram | Downloads linux/arm64 asset, installs to $PREFIX/bin | None |
| Engram from core-termux | LookPath detects it, skips download | None |
| Engram manually compiled | LookPath finds it | None |
| Upgrade gentle-ai on Android | Maps android→linux, downloads correct asset | None |

### AI-Agent Implementation Notes
1. **Order**: download.go first (LookPath + asset + install dir), then upgrade/download.go.
2. **`exec.LookPath("engram")`** is the single check — no extra path scanning needed.
3. **`os.Getenv("PREFIX")`** is only set on Termux. Fallback: `/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin`.
4. **Cross-platform**: ALL android-specific code gated by `if goos == "android"`.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `DownloadLatestBinary` on Android uses `linux` asset URL
- [ ] `engramInstallDir("android")` returns `$PREFIX/bin`
- [ ] LookPath check runs before download on Android
- [ ] `upgrade.Download` on Android maps `android` → `linux`
- [ ] Existing Engram in PATH is detected and not re-downloaded
- [ ] Non-Android platforms 100% unaffected
- [ ] go test ./internal/components/engram/... and ./internal/update/upgrade/... pass

title: feat(sync): preserve user customizations in managed agent instruction files during sync
body:
## Summary

When `gentle-ai sync` (or re-install) rewrites managed agent instruction files (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.claude/agents/*.md`, `~/.cursor/rules/gentle-ai.mdc`, `~/.cursor/agents/`, etc.), every managed block delimited by the existing `<!-- gentle-ai:<id> -->` / `<!-- /gentle-ai:<id> -->` markers is **replaced wholesale** with the new canonical content. Any line the user customized *inside* a managed block (e.g. tweaking their persona section or the Engram protocol) is silently lost on the next sync.

This issue proposes a preservation system: detect user modifications in agent instruction files **before** syncing, diff the old vs. new managed block line-by-line, and ask the user whether to overwrite everything, keep their customized lines, or skip the file.

## Problem

- `filemerge.InjectMarkdownSection` replaces the whole managed block between the markers with the canonical content from embedded assets. User edits inside that range are destroyed.
- `internal/cli/sync.go` already snapshots bytes (`snapshotSyncFiles`, `changedSyncFiles`, `restoreSyncFiles`) but only to detect *that something changed* and to roll back on failure — it cannot distinguish a managed update from a user customization, and it does not preserve customized lines when re-injecting.
- Agent prompt strategies vary per provider (`StrategyMarkdownSections`, `StrategyFileReplace`, `StrategyAppendToFile`, `StrategyInstructionsFile`, `StrategySteeringFile`, `StrategyJinjaModules`), so file-replace agents (e.g. Cursor's `gentle-ai.mdc`) need the same protection with a different merge approach.

## Proposed Design — three phases

### Phase 1: Pre-sync detection (text-marker pattern)

Before any managed write:

1. Read the current file on disk and extract every managed block using the existing marker pattern `<!-- gentle-ai:<id> -->` ... `<!-- /gentle-ai:<id> -->` (already produced by the SDD, persona, engram, permissions, strict-tdd and codegraph-guidance components, and by the agent builder's `custom-agent:<name>` markers in `internal/agentbuilder/sdd.go`).
2. If the marker is absent → clean injection, nothing to preserve.
3. If present → compare the on-disk block against the canonical block the new version would write.
4. Also detect user content in file-replace/append files (e.g. Cursor `.mdc`) where gentle-ai owns the whole file.

### Phase 2: Classification and line diff

- Compute a line-level diff between the on-disk block (user's version) and the previous canonical block (base).
- Classify: user-added lines, user-modified lines, user-deleted lines, reordering, or removed marker.
- Produce a per-file summary: "N customized lines in block `<id>` at lines X–Y".

### Phase 3: Blocking prompt before overwrite

Only when user changes exist, present a lossless blocking prompt per affected file/block before writing:

1. **Overwrite everything** — current behavior; customized lines are lost (explicit consent).
2. **Keep custom lines** — three-way merge line-by-line: base = previous canonical block (persisted), theirs = new canonical block, ours = on-disk block; re-apply user lines onto the new canonical content.
3. **Skip this file** for this sync run.

Support "apply to all" for multi-file runs, plus non-interactive flags for automation/CI: `--yes` (current behavior) and `--preserve-user-changes` (auto three-way merge).

## Supporting evidence in the codebase

- `internal/agents/claude/adapter.go` — `SystemPromptFile` → `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`; `SubAgentsDir` → `~/.claude/agents/*.md` (frontmatter + prompt body).
- `internal/agents/cursor/adapter.go` — `SystemPromptFile` → `~/.cursor/rules/gentle-ai.mdc` (`StrategyFileReplace`); `SubAgentsDir` → `~/.cursor/agents/`.
- `internal/cli/sync.go` — `snapshotSyncFiles` / `changedSyncFiles` / `restoreSyncFiles` (byte-level snapshot, rollback only); `RunSyncWithSelection` pipeline.
- `internal/components/*/inject.go` — marker-based section injection (`<!-- gentle-ai:persona -->`, `engram-protocol`, `sdd-orchestrator`, `strict-tdd-mode`, `codegraph-guidance`, ...).
- `internal/agentbuilder/sdd.go` — `markerFormat = "<!-- gentle-ai:custom-agent:%s -->"` for user-installed sub-agents.
- `internal/components/uninstall/cleaners.go` — already removes managed blocks by marker (the inverse operation).

## Requirements

- Persist the previous canonical version of each managed block (e.g. in the gentle-ai state/ledger) so the three-way merge has a real base.
- Cover system prompts, sub-agents (`*.md` under `agents/`), skills installed by the agent builder, and file-replace agents (Cursor).
- Never ask when there is nothing to preserve (no user diff) — the prompt appears only when a real customization exists.

## Alternatives considered

- **(a) Move all managed content to separate include files** — cleaner isolation, but breaks the current block model, every adapter, and existing installs; too invasive.
- **(b) Backup + manual restore** — partially addressed by #1724; still does not preserve changes automatically and depends on the user noticing.
- **(c) Only rewrite when bytes differ** — insufficient: a canonical block replacement still erases customizations even when the file changed "for a good reason".

## Scope

- This is a feature proposal; no PR yet. Needs design review (`status:needs-design`) before implementation per the project's issue-first workflow.
