En el prerelease `gentle-ai 2.2.0-rc.1` Refresh 4, `review capture-evidence` rechaza correctamente una evidencia de verificación final que supera por un byte el máximo publicado, pero pierde o clasifica mal la causa nativa del tamaño. Un archivo de **4.194.305 bytes**, frente al `maxLength` de **4.194.304**, devuelve exactamente el mismo error que una entrada vacía:

```text
Error: final verification evidence is required
```

El comportamiento fail-closed es correcto: ambos rechazos son atómicos, la autoridad conserva estado y revisión, y una captura válida posterior funciona. El defecto es exclusivamente diagnóstico: una entrada presente pero sobredimensionada se informa como si faltara.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Crear en un repositorio temporal un review nativo de riesgo medio y llevar su autoridad a `validating`, sin receipt y con evidencia final pendiente.
2. Consultar `gentle-ai review schema verification-evidence` y comprobar que `maxLength` es `4194304`.
3. Crear un archivo vacío y otro de exactamente `4194305` bytes, por ejemplo:
   ```shell
   : > evidence-empty.txt
   dd if=/dev/zero bs=1 count=4194305 status=none | tr '\0' x > evidence-over-limit.txt
   ```
4. Ejecutar `gentle-ai review capture-evidence` contra la misma `lineage`, `target` y `expected-revision`, primero con el archivo vacío y luego con el archivo sobredimensionado.
5. Consultar `review status --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v1 --lineage <lineage> --next-transition` y verificar que el estado sigue en `validating` y la revisión no cambió.
6. Repetir la captura con un archivo de texto válido y pequeño.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

La evidencia vacía debe rechazarse como ausente. La evidencia de 4.194.305 bytes debe rechazarse con una causa de tamaño específica que preserve el límite publicado y permita distinguirla de una entrada vacía. Ambos rechazos deben seguir siendo atómicos, sin alterar autoridad, revisión ni receipt, y una captura válida posterior debe continuar funcionando.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

La entrada vacía y la entrada presente de 4.194.305 bytes terminan con exit code `1` y el mismo mensaje:

```text
Error: final verification evidence is required
```

Después de ambos rechazos, la autoridad continúa sin mutación:

```text
state: validating
revision: sha256:bb3b4d4d2366ff5f8e9e55ab6b69b11a1516eca6bda7916a94c2cd0e2dcb4842
receipt.status: expected_missing
next_transition.reason_code: verification_evidence_required
```

Una evidencia válida posterior se acepta con exit code `0` y publica un manifiesto `gentle-ai.review-verification-evidence/v1`. Por lo tanto, no se reporta una falla del rechazo fail-closed, sino la pérdida o clasificación incorrecta de la causa nativa de tamaño.

### Gentle AI Version

`gentle-ai 2.2.0-rc.1` Refresh 4

Commit fuente: `c2b91ac966ca3a625d29ef27fd66320608f07ced`

SHA-256 Linux AMD64: `ffd9f94b0d5cc5379b09218e62bd3fb79ddbc55f1cfd637788001aaaa85586a2`

### Operating System

Linux (Other)

### AI Agent / Client

OpenCode

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
$ gentle-ai review schema verification-evidence
# schema maxLength: 4194304

$ gentle-ai review capture-evidence ... --input evidence-empty.txt
Error: final verification evidence is required
# exit 1

$ wc -c evidence-over-limit.txt
4194305 evidence-over-limit.txt

$ gentle-ai review capture-evidence ... --input evidence-over-limit.txt
Error: final verification evidence is required
# exit 1

# STATUS después de ambos rechazos
state: validating
revision: sha256:bb3b4d4d2366ff5f8e9e55ab6b69b11a1516eca6bda7916a94c2cd0e2dcb4842
receipt.status: expected_missing

$ gentle-ai review capture-evidence ... --input evidence-valid.txt
# exit 0; schema gentle-ai.review-verification-evidence/v1
```

### Additional Context

Entorno de reproducción: Linux, OpenCode y zsh, en fixtures temporales aislados. La evidencia completa del contribuidor se conserva localmente bajo `/tmp/opencode/gentle-ai-2.2.0-rc.1-refresh4-expanded-20260726T004523Z-18585`; todos los datos esenciales están incluidos arriba porque esa ruta no es accesible desde GitHub.

Se revisaron búsquedas abiertas y cerradas por el mensaje exacto, `capture-evidence`, `maxLength`, `4194304`, evidencia sobredimensionada y errores de verificación final. `#1775` trata la indisponibilidad del schema en 2.1.11, `#1663` la reanudación de FINALIZE desde evidencia capturada, y `#1802` el resultado derivado de evidencia canónica. Ninguno cubre la pérdida de la causa de tamaño durante un rechazo atómico.

Este resultado está limitado a Linux/OpenCode. No constituye certificación multiplataforma y el E2E orgánico de Windows continúa sin resolverse.

title: fix(theme): theme injection would overwrite TOML/YAML settings files with JSON
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

`theme.Inject` merges `{"theme":"gentleman-kanagawa"}` into the agent settings file via `MergeJSONObjects`. For agents whose settings are not JSON (kimi uses TOML `config.toml`, hermes uses YAML), an unparseable base is treated as `{}`, so the file would be silently replaced with JSON, destroying the existing config.

This is not triggered today because no preset selects `ComponentTheme` for those agents, but it is one preset wiring away from silent config loss.

Suggested fix: gate theme injection to JSON-settings agents, the same class of guard as the uninstall settings-rewrite issue (#1828).

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Wire a preset that selects `ComponentTheme` for an agent with TOML or YAML settings (for example kimi with `~/.kimi/config.toml`)
2. Run the install for that agent
3. Inspect the settings file afterwards

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Theme injection is skipped (or handled natively) for agents whose settings file is not JSON, and the existing config is preserved.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The TOML/YAML settings file would be silently overwritten with `{"theme":"gentleman-kanagawa"}` JSON, discarding the original config.

### 🖥️ Environment

**Gentle AI Version:** build from main (e01b1149)

**Operating System:** Linux (Other)

**AI Agent / Client:** Other (Kimi Code CLI)

**📋 Affected Area:** Installation Pipeline

### Additional Context

Latent issue found while testing the kimi install path in a fake-HOME sandbox. Related: #1828 (same root class, JSON assumed for non-JSON settings files, in the uninstall path).

title: fix(agent): uninstall fails for kimi because settings rewrite assumes JSON
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

`gga uninstall --agent kimi` crashes and exits 1 because the uninstall service unconditionally rewrites the agent settings file as JSON, but kimi's settings file is TOML (`~/.kimi/config.toml`).

Root cause: `internal/components/uninstall/service.go` plans an unconditional `rewriteJSONFile(adapter.SettingsPath(homeDir), ...)` for the persona component (~line 500) and the theme component (~line 545). For kimi, `SettingsPath` returns `config.toml`, which is TOML, so the JSON unmarshal fails on the first character.

Because the operation aborts on the first rewrite, uninstall leaves everything behind: zero cleanup happens.

This is reproducible on current main with the legacy `~/.kimi` layout. It predates PR #840 and is independent of it (that PR inherits the same crash for `~/.kimi-code`).

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Set up a HOME with the legacy kimi layout (`~/.kimi/config.toml` present, TOML content) and gentle-ai persona/theme installed
2. Run `gga uninstall --agent kimi`
3. Observe exit code 1 and that no files were removed

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Uninstall completes, removing the injected persona/theme content (or safely skipping the settings rewrite for non-JSON settings files).

### ❌ Actual Behavior

```
Error: clean json file "~/.kimi/config.toml": unmarshal json object: invalid character 'd' looking for beginning of value
```

Exit code 1, nothing is cleaned up.

### 🖥️ Environment

**Gentle AI Version:** build from main (e01b1149)

**Operating System:** Linux (Other)

**AI Agent / Client:** Other (Kimi Code CLI)

**📋 Affected Area:** CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
$ gga uninstall --agent kimi
Error: clean json file "~/.kimi/config.toml": unmarshal json object: invalid character 'd' looking for beginning of value
```

### Additional Context

Verified with a fake-HOME sandbox on a main-based build. Suggested fix class: gate the JSON rewrite on the settings file actually being JSON (per-agent), or add a TOML-aware rewrite path for kimi.

title: feat(codex): establish dedicated sdd-spec profile and move sdd-tasks to sdd-mid
body:
### Pre-flight Checks
- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand this issue needs status:approved before a PR can be opened

### Problem Description
Currently, Codex per-phase model configurations assign `sdd-spec` and `sdd-tasks` to the `sdd-cheap` carril (`gpt-5.6-luna` / `low` effort).

This creates two architectural design defects:
1. **Under-specified Requirement Contracts**: `sdd-spec` defines the formally verifiable contracts, edge cases, and threat matrix. Running it under `luna:low` leads to weak specifications that fail downstream verification.
2. **Inaccurate Workload Forecasts**: `sdd-tasks` performs the Review Workload Forecast and 400-line budget estimation. Running it under `luna:low` leads to inaccurate diff estimates and missing TDD RED-test tasks.

### Proposed Solution
1. Introduce a dedicated `sdd-spec` carril in `codexPresetMatrix` and `codexTierGroups`:
   - `Low-Cost`: `gpt-5.6-terra` / `medium`
   - `Recommended`: `gpt-5.6-terra` / `high`
   - `Powerful`: `gpt-5.6-sol` / `high`
2. Move `sdd-tasks` from `sdd-cheap` to `sdd-mid` (`gpt-5.6-terra`) across all presets:
   - `Low-Cost`: `gpt-5.6-terra` / `medium`
   - `Recommended`: `gpt-5.6-terra` / `medium`
   - `Powerful`: `gpt-5.6-terra` / `high`
3. Keep `sdd-cheap` (`gpt-5.6-luna` / `low`) strictly for passive/read-only phases (`sdd-explore`, `sdd-archive`, `sdd-onboard`).
4. Update model definitions, rendering functions, asset templates (`sdd-orchestrator.md`), TUI pickers, and test goldens.

### Affected Area
Other (Agent presets & CLI profiles)

### Alternatives Considered
Keep `sdd-spec` and `sdd-tasks` in `sdd-cheap`, which risks weak specifications and inaccurate PR budget forecasts.

title: fix(review): preserve staged target selectors and support atomic scope replacement
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues), including open and closed results, and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

On installed/upstream Gentle AI v2.1.11 (`51a5d9e20706b05718b1f2b7fcafda45bab21802`), the negotiated review integration cannot safely launch or retarget a staged review.

The START schema omits the candidate diff and path manifest that the generated OpenCode consumer contract requires before launching each lens. Independently, `next_transition` emits a fresh `review.start` with empty arguments, so an already selected staged projection/selector is lost. If a pristine review was accidentally started against the wrong workspace target, no native atomic operation can invalidate it and stage the intended successor without allocating a fresh review/correction budget.

This is a combined contract and native-transition defect, not a packaging mismatch:

- **Orchestrator-contract defect:** the consumer requires canonical candidate material that START does not represent.
- **Native transition defect:** executable START transitions omit exact selectors/bindings.
- **Unsupported budget-preserving retarget:** the wrong workspace target cannot become the predecessor of a staged successor atomically under the original budget.

No workaround is safe under authority-first routing. Consumers may not infer omitted flags, select a target by guesswork, or reconstruct a canonical diff from mutable Git state.

Related issues cover narrower slices but not this full correction path:

- #1454 covers immutable candidate material from START/restart.
- #1601 covers selected target/contract preservation in START transitions.
- #1683 covers authorized staged scope expansion from an already approved base-diff predecessor.

None provides atomic replacement of an initially wrong pristine workspace target with the intended staged target while preserving one budget and predecessor/successor provenance.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Inspect the released v2.1.11 START schema without invoking any review lifecycle command:

   ```bash
   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/v2.1.11/contracts/review-integration/v1/schemas/start.schema.json | jq -e '.properties | has("candidate_diff") and has("paths")'
   ```

2. Observe that the command returns `false` and exits with status 1.
3. Compare that schema with the generated OpenCode review consumer contract, which requires the exact immutable candidate diff and changed-path manifest before lens launch.
4. Inspect a negotiated fresh-target `next_transition`: `newReviewNextTransition` emits `review.start` with empty arguments, so exact execution cannot preserve a selected staged projection or its bindings.
5. Consider a pristine lineage created for the wrong workspace target. Native invalidation/recovery/start operations do not offer one atomic predecessor-to-staged-successor correction that preserves the original review/correction budget.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The provider should support the following approved design:

1. **Atomic scope replacement:** atomically invalidate the wrong predecessor and create a staged successor, preserving one review/correction budget and recording predecessor/successor provenance. Failure must leave both authority and budget unchanged.
2. **Provider-owned candidate materialization:** expose an API that persists and returns a signed or hash-bound artifact containing the exact candidate diff, canonical path manifest, file modes, and base/candidate tree identities, all bound to `target_identity`.
3. **Complete executable transitions:** `next_transition` must carry every exact argument, selector, and binding needed to reproduce the assessed target. Any omission must invalidate the transition rather than inviting consumer inference.
4. **Existing-lineage migration:** after support lands, an already blocked lineage should be migratable as the invalidated predecessor of its intended staged successor without opening another budget.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

- `contracts/review-integration/v1/schemas/start.schema.json` has no `candidate_diff` or `paths` properties.
- START therefore cannot satisfy the generated OpenCode consumer contract with canonical provider-owned candidate inputs.
- `newReviewNextTransition` can emit `review.start` with empty arguments, dropping staged projection/selector state on exact execution.
- A wrongly targeted pristine workspace lineage cannot be atomically replaced by the intended staged lineage while retaining the original budget and auditable provenance.
- Retrying START risks a second authority/budget; inferring flags or rebuilding a diff would violate authority-first routing.

### Gentle AI Version

v2.1.11, commit `51a5d9e20706b05718b1f2b7fcafda45bab21802`, installed via Homebrew

### Operating System

macOS

### AI Agent / Client

OpenCode

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
$ curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/v2.1.11/contracts/review-integration/v1/schemas/start.schema.json | jq -e '.properties | has("candidate_diff") and has("paths")'
false
# exit status: 1
```

### Additional Context

Shell: zsh.

Exact affected files and symbols identified by read-only diagnosis:

- `contracts/review-integration/v1/schemas/start.schema.json`
- `contracts/review-integration/v1/schemas/status.schema.json`
- `internal/cli/review_start_contract.go`: `ReviewIntegrationStartResult`, `newReviewIntegrationStartResult`
- `internal/cli/review_status_contract.go`
- `internal/cli/review_next_transition.go`: `newReviewNextTransition`, `reviewExecuteTransition`
- `internal/cli/review_facade.go`: `RunReviewFacadeStart`, `RunReviewInvalidate`, `RunReviewRecover`

Required regression coverage:

- Staged selector and binding preservation through STATUS → START.
- Wrong-workspace → staged atomic replacement without allocating a second review/correction budget.
- Candidate materialization, readback, signature/hash verification, and binding to `target_identity`.
- Generated OpenCode prompt/schema conformance, proving every required lens input is provider-owned and available after restart.
- Migration of an existing blocked lineage as predecessor after replacement support lands.

This report contains no local usernames, credentials, private paths, unrelated file contents, or project domain data. Generic staged paths are sufficient for fixtures.

title: fix(review): status cannot recover multi-lineage compact-v2 authority
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

A repository with four simultaneous compact-v2 lineages in `reviewing` state cannot obtain a valid negotiated `review.status` result or reach any supported maintenance transition.

The unqualified status path emits `invalid negotiated review failure message`. An explicit-lineage status initially exposed a separate Windows Git obstruction and, after that obstruction was removed, now terminates with the negotiated `operation_timeout` failure before authority applicability is evaluated. `review abandon` is intentionally refused for a lineage containing authoritative `reviewer-results`, but there is no supported compact-v2 repair/disposition for that non-pristine reviewing state or its stale lock.

This leaves the repository unable to create or validate a receipt without manually changing Git-common-dir authority, which would violate provenance and CAS guarantees.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. On Windows, use native Gentle AI v2.1.11 through gentle-pi v1.2.0.
2. Have a Git common-dir containing multiple compact-v2 `reviewing` entries under `.git/gentle-ai/review-transactions/v2/`; at least one entry contains `reviewer-results` while state still has no admitted `lens_results`.
3. Leave a well-formed store `LOCK` whose recorded PID no longer exists.
4. Run:
   `gentle-ai review status --cwd <repo> --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v1 --next-transition`
5. Observe `Error: validate negotiated review failure: invalid negotiated review failure message`.
6. Attempt the documented, explicitly authorized `review abandon` operation for a non-pristine lineage.
7. Observe native refusal because `reviewer-results` exists; the integration wrapper receives empty stdout and classifies mutation outcome as unknown.
8. Run explicit-lineage read-only status as required by the returned action.
9. Observe a negotiated `operation_timeout` with `authority_applicability: not_evaluated` and `next_action: stop`.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

`review.status` should always emit a schema-valid, bounded failure/status envelope. For this authority class, it should either:

- return deterministic `select_lineage` / per-lineage status without timing out; or
- expose a provider-owned, CAS-bound compact-v2 repair/disposition for non-pristine `reviewing` lineages and stale locks.

Underlying process-control error text should never make the negotiated failure envelope itself invalid.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

- Unqualified status emits an invalid negotiated failure message.
- `abandon` correctly refuses authoritative `reviewer-results`, but no supported alternative maintenance route exists.
- Explicit-lineage status times out before authority applicability is evaluated.
- `review repair` on current main only handles the legacy historical-alias repair class, not this compact-v2 state.
- The only apparent local workaround would be manual authority/lock deletion, which is unsafe and intentionally not performed.

### Gentle AI Version

Native facade: v2.1.11 / module revision `51a5d9e20706b05718b1f2b7fcafda45bab21802`

gentle-pi: v1.2.0

Current upstream main inspected: `0d95c399c79edb341e3d874032eba4654b2b3f17`

### Operating System

Windows

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
$ gentle-ai review status --cwd <repo> --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v1 --next-transition
Error: validate negotiated review failure: invalid negotiated review failure message

$ gentle-ai review abandon ...
Error: review abandon refused: store entry "review-14c0b4236b87742c" holds authoritative artifact "reviewer-results" beyond its pristine state

# Wrapper result after the refused mutation produced empty stdout:
outcome: native-operation-failed
mutation_outcome: unknown
replayability: status_required
next_action: review.status

# Required explicit-lineage status after removing an unrelated Windows `NUL` path obstruction:
code: operation_timeout
message: The negotiated review operation exceeded its aggregate time budget.
mutation_outcome: not_started
authority_applicability: not_evaluated
retry_safe: false
replayability: manual_action_required
next_action: stop
```

### Additional Context

- Native executable SHA256: `1c92cdcaf826d4bec6a6560770e5a0edefc09997364a664a5033abc6ab932b2b`, matching its reported/published build.
- Reinstalling latest reproduces the same native revision; installing current main does not appear to fix the core state.
- Current main still concatenates underlying process-control error text before validating the 240-byte/single-line negotiated message contract (`internal/cli/review_operation_contract.go`).
- Current main intentionally refuses `abandon` when `reviewer-results` exists (`internal/reviewtransaction/compact_abandon.go`) and the generic repair classifier does not support this compact-v2 state.
- The repository authority bytes were left intact. No lock, reviewer-result, state, or lineage directory was manually deleted or edited.
- No private dataset content or medical data is involved.

title: fix(review): classify upgraded lineages without preserved reviewer output
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues), including open and closed results, and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### Bug Description
An upgraded legacy review lineage can remain `reviewing` after its selected reviewer invocation completed under the pre-preservation workflow, but result adaptation/capture failed before any durable preserved-result artifact existed. The immutable candidate and compact-v2 authority are recovered correctly, yet native repair classifies this target as unsupported and negotiated status asks for a fresh reviewer result for the same reliability lens.

That collection request is not actionable under the external exactly-once orchestration contract: the original reviewer invocation was already consumed. This is not the earlier lens-name/CWD capture defect from #1411, which was released in v2.1.8; the remaining compatibility gap is the upgraded legacy no-artifact state.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a review lineage with the older workflow and launch its selected reliability reviewer once.
2. Let the reviewer invocation complete, then have result adaptation/capture fail before preservation support is available.
3. Upgrade to a current Gentle AI build and leave the candidate unchanged.
4. Run the target-scoped command:
   ```powershell
   gentle-ai review status --cwd <repo> --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v1 --next-transition --base-ref <base>
   ```
5. Observe compact-v2 authority in `reviewing`, the exact immutable target, a six-path manifest, 271 changed lines, and the missing expected receipt.
6. Observe repair assessment `status: unsupported`, `eligible_candidates: 0`, and `candidates: []`; the displayed supported repair operations are only `review/complete-fix` and `review/validate-fix`.
7. Observe `next_transition.kind: collect` with `reason_code: reviewer_results_required`, requesting a new `reviewer_result` for the same reliability lens.

### Expected Behavior
Classify this legacy no-artifact state explicitly and return a safe native transition that preserves the original budget and provenance. Maintainer-defined outcomes may include a narrowly authorized retriable transition, or an explicit terminal invalidate/abandon transition. The transition must not require reconstructing or attaching unavailable reviewer output, manually editing authority, or silently opening a new review budget.

### Actual Behavior
Repair advertises supported operations generally, but this target is `unsupported` with zero eligible candidates. At the same time, `next_transition` asks to collect a fresh reviewer result without explaining the legacy exactly-once or budget semantics for an invocation that already completed before result preservation existed.

```text
repair:

  kind: collect

```

### Additional Context
- Shell: PowerShell/pwsh.
- The candidate remains immutable and clean; `git diff --check` passes.
- The current negotiated status recovers the expected compact-v2 authority and immutable manifest, so this is not an authority-discovery failure.
- No durable preserved-result artifact exists because the incident predates preservation support.

title: feat(review): require concrete defects for language-style findings
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

---

## 📋 How this works

1. **Submit** this feature request → it gets the `status:needs-review` label automatically
2. A **maintainer reviews** it and adds `status:approved` (or closes it as out-of-scope/duplicate)
3. **Only then** should you (or anyone) open a PR to implement it

PRs that implement features without `status:approved` on the linked issue will be automatically rejected.

---
## 💡 Problem Statement

The `review-readability` lens sub-agent (4R set) produces false-positive WARNING findings against Go code whose names follow Go's official convention but violate an invented "all type names must be PascalCase regardless of export status" rule. The lens has no guard against the established package-level naming precedent, so every package with a substantive number of unexported types generates an advisory warning on the first NEW unexported type the lens encounters — even when that name matches 50+ existing precedents in the same package.

Concrete observed incident (this matters because the same surface is reused across PRs and the false positive compounds):

- PR #1696 on `Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai`: `internal/reviewtransaction/compact_decision_transitions.go:22` flagged `type allowedDecisionEdge struct {...}` as a convention violation.
- Effective Go (https://go.dev/doc/effective_go#names) and the Go language spec mandate `camelCase` for unexported names (first letter lowercase) and `PascalCase` for exported names (first letter uppercase). The codebase establishes the convention unambiguously: 53+ unexported types in `internal/reviewtransaction/` already use camelCase (`compactStateEqual`, `compactPrePRChainMember`, `CompactDecideOperation` (exported) vs `compactStateEqual` (unexported), etc.).
- The finding's reasoning was "Go convention requires PascalCase for all type names regardless of export status" — a claim that is factually incorrect. The lens's pre-verified context (no precedent list, no Go visibility convention summary) made the false positive unavoidable for any reviewer who trusted the canonical sources.
- Severity at the receipt verdict was `WARNING` (advisory, not merge-blocking). The PR proceeded via `gentle-ai review finalize` with receipt approved, and `validate --gate post-apply` returned `allow`. So this is not a gate-breaking defect, but it IS a recurring noise pattern that will appear on any Go PR whose lens sub-agent encounters a new unexported type.

## 📦 Proposed Solution

Add a precedent-aware guard to the `review-readability` lens's correctness contract for the Go convention specifically (and analogous guards for other languages):

**Minimum remediation**

Before flagging a Go identifier as a naming-convention violation, the lens MUST verify both:

1. **Visibility match**: the symbol's first letter matches the convention for its visibility class:
   - If exported (CapitalFirstLetter): flag `lowercase_first_letter` violations only.
   - If unexported (lowercaseFirstLetter): flag `CapitalFirstLetter` violations only.
2. **Precedent check**: cross-reference the package-local type population via `grep -E '^type [A-Za-z_]+ (struct|interface)' <package_dir>/*.go`. If 50%+ of existing precedents in the package already follow a non-standard convention for that visibility class, suppress the warning to a SUGGESTION/INFO or skip it entirely.

**Robust remediation**

1. Bake the Go visibility convention into the sub-agent's contract prompt as explicit normative content (not as something the lens must reason out each time):
   > "Per the Go language specification and Effective Go, exported identifiers use `PascalCase` (CapitalFirstLetter) and unexported identifiers use `camelCase` (lowercaseFirstLetter). A name's first letter is determined by its visibility — do not flag this pattern. If you believe a specific name violates a different rule, only do so after pre-loading the package-local precedent via `grep -E '^type [A-Za-z_]+ (struct|interface)' <package_dir>/*.go` and confirming the majority divergence."
2. Add a regression test under `internal/reviewtransaction/`'s bounded review test suite that asserts the lens does NOT flag `allowedDecisionEdge` (camelCase unexported type) at line 22 of `compact_decision_transitions.go` — the canonical example cited above.
3. Add a correspondence guard for JavaScript/TypeScript (`camelCase` for variables/functions, `PascalCase` for classes/components), Python (`snake_case` for functions/variables, `PascalCase` for classes), Rust (`snake_case` for functions/variables, `PascalCase` for types/traits), and any other language routinely shipped in 4R review sub-agents.
4. Surface the suppressed warnings in a separate INFO bucket in the receipt so the contributor sees the precedent-based suppression happened (transparent de-noising, not silent dropping).

## 🔄 Alternatives Considered

1. **Promote the precedent grep to a pre-apply step in the apply/review-bound workflow itself, before the lens runs**: this shifts the cost to apply phase and may slow down the 4R cycle; rejected for the user's PR cycle time but appropriate as a follow-up for projects with multi-language surfaces.
2. **Have the orchestrator inject a `package_conventions.json` snapshot into the lens prompt when Go is detected in the diff**: this requires orchestrator-side language detection and JSON assembly; defensible but more code than is strictly needed.
3. **Document and live with the false positive**: rejected because it repeats on every Go PR.

## 📎 Additional Context

**Severity**: WARNING (advisory, not merge-blocking).

**Reproducibility**: observed during PR #1696 review with `gentle-ai 2.1.11`, OpenCode on Windows. The orchestrator's pre-verified context included `gentle-ai review start`, `go test ./...` results, docstring coverage, focused test command evidence, etc. — but did NOT include the package precedent list. The lens returned the false positive because it had no way to validate against the codebase's established convention.

**Related but not duplicate**:

- #1579 (CLOSED): addresses reviewer output formatting (prose prefix before JSON), distinct from this naming-convention false positive.
- #1372 (CLOSED): addresses MCP permission leakage in read-only reviewers, distinct from this naming-knowledge gap.
- #1331 (CLOSED): large-doc-documentation routing, unrelated.

**Project-specific precedent** (snapshot at this issue's filing time): 53+ unexported type definitions in `internal/reviewtransaction/` all use camelCase, including the false-positive target `allowedDecisionEdge`. The pattern is the codebase's established convention.

**Affected area**: sub-agent prompt and contract (not CLI/TUI/installer/etc.); pick `Other` from the bug-report dropdown if you wish to file under a bug template. I have chosen `feature_request` because the fix is an enhancement (precedent-aware guard) rather than a hard correctness defect.


---

**Re-verified on main @ ec3b1db7aa6d (gentle-ai 2.4.1-0.20260821223000) on 2026-08-22.** Feature request still applies — review-readability lens behavior unchanged in recent commits (no Go exported/unexported guard added).

title: feat(cli): add `gentle-ai account link` to connect a machine to an existing Engram Cloud account
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Problem Statement

Memory captured by Engram today is local to each machine (`~/.engram/engram.db`, per `docs/engram.md` / `docs/codebase/memory-core.md`). A user running Gentle AI on a second PC gets an empty, unrelated memory store — there is no way to see the same agent conversations/decisions across machines through Gentle AI itself.

This isn't a missing backend problem: Engram already ships a self-hosted "Engram Cloud" server (`engram cloud serve`, Postgres-backed) with a real account/token/project-grant model (`cloud_principals`, `cloud_human_users`, `cloud_principal_tokens`, `cloud_project_grants` — implemented and archived in the Engram repo under `openspec/specs/cloud-user-token-management/spec.md`, 2026-07-03). The gap is that **Gentle AI never surfaces or wires up any of it**: `internal/components/engram/inject.go` only ever configures the local `engram mcp --tools=agent` server and never touches `~/.engram/cloud.json` or invokes any `engram cloud ...` / `engram sync --cloud ...` subcommand.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Add a new top-level command, `gentle-ai account link`, that links the current machine to an existing Engram Cloud account/project by shelling out to the already-installed `engram` binary — reusing Engram Cloud's existing account system as-is, with **no new backend, database, or authentication** introduced by Gentle AI.

Example usage:
```
export ENGRAM_CLOUD_TOKEN=<token issued via engram cloud bootstrap admin>
gentle-ai account link --server https://engram.example.com --project my-repo
```

Expected behavior:
1. Probe that the installed `engram` binary supports `cloud` subcommands (version gate); fail clearly if not.
2. Shell out, in order: `engram cloud config --server <url>`, `engram cloud enroll <project>`, `engram sync --cloud --project <project>` — token passed only via the `ENGRAM_CLOUD_TOKEN` subprocess environment, never as a CLI flag, never persisted by Gentle AI.
3. Persist only non-secret metadata (`EngramCloudLinked`, `EngramCloudServerURL`, `EngramCloudProject`) in `~/.gentle-ai/state.json` — never the token, never touching `~/.engram/cloud.json` directly (that file stays exclusively Engram-owned, per the existing documented boundary in `docs/codebase/memory-core.md`).
4. `gentle-ai doctor` gains a check reporting link status and server reachability.
5. `gentle-ai sync --engram-cloud-resync` re-triggers a cloud pull using the persisted server/project.

Per-agent MCP wiring is unchanged — every agent still points at the local `engram mcp --tools=agent` server. Cross-machine memory sharing happens entirely inside Engram's own local↔cloud replication, transparent to every agent Gentle AI configures.

I already have a full OpenSpec-style design drafted locally (`proposal.md`, `design.md` with architecture-decision tables and exact file/function touch points, `specs/engram-cloud-account-linking/spec.md` with RFC 2119 + Given/When/Then scenarios, and a phased `tasks.md`), ready to attach to the PR once this issue is approved.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- **Build a brand-new cloud/account backend for Gentle AI** — rejected: would duplicate Engram Cloud's already-implemented and audited `cloud_principals`/`cloud_principal_tokens`/`cloud_project_grants` system instead of reusing it.
- **Overload `gentle-ai sync` instead of a new `account` verb** — rejected: `docs/codebase/sync-and-cloud.md` already documents two distinct existing meanings of "sync" (`gentle-ai sync` = config refresh; `engram sync` = memory export/import); a third meaning under the same verb would worsen an already-flagged ambiguity.
- **Reimplement the Engram Cloud HTTP client in Go instead of shelling out to `engram`** — rejected: duplicates logic Engram already owns/maintains and would need to track Engram Cloud's auth/versioning independently, inconsistent with how Gentle AI treats Engram everywhere else in this repo (install/verify/setup — always via subprocess, never reimplemented).

### 📎 Additional Context

- Confirmed via code inspection, not assumption: `internal/components/engram/inject.go`, `internal/state/state.go`, `internal/cli/run.go`, `internal/cli/doctor.go` — no existing account/device/cloud-sync concept anywhere in Gentle AI's Go source.
- Related prior issue: #422 ("Engram Cloud | Command to sync mutations", closed, moved to `Gentleman-Programming/engram#327`) confirms that manual `engram sync --cloud` pulls chunks but not `cloud_mutations` reliably — only `engram serve`/autosync does. This is exactly why the proposed design treats the sync step as a **non-fatal** step after a successful `cloud config`/`cloud enroll` (the account link itself still succeeds and is retryable via `--engram-cloud-resync`), rather than assuming sync is always fully reliable.
- Related: #1021 (docs for optional Engram cloud sync setup, approved) and #921 (cloud-aware data-directory migration contract) — both adjacent but distinct: neither adds an account-linking command or doctor visibility.

title: fix(sdd): detect pure Engram artifact stores without hidden signals
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

Native SDD status can resolve Engram artifacts, but it attempts Engram only when one of three hidden signals exists:

- `GENTLE_AI_SDD_STATUS_ENGRAM` is set.
- A workspace `.engram/` directory exists.
- `openspec/config.yaml` or `openspec/config.yml` declares Engram or hybrid storage.

A pure, fileless Engram workflow does not necessarily create any of these signals. Consequently, `sdd-status` and `sdd-continue` report an OpenSpec-only state even when the requested change has valid Engram observations.

First-party assets work around this by telling orchestrators not to invoke the native dispatcher for Engram, contradicting the native Engram implementation and forcing weaker manual status reconstruction.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Check out the frozen `main` snapshot at `942a3957a9954f5646f8edd97b6b1f32a17bfb33` on Linux.
2. Create an isolated Git repository named `engram-project`.
3. Do not create `openspec/`, `.engram/`, or any artifact-store configuration.
4. Ensure `GENTLE_AI_SDD_STATUS_ENGRAM` is unset.
5. Put a deterministic `engram` stub on `PATH` that records invocation and implements `engram export <path>`.
6. Have the stub export valid observations for `sdd/pure/proposal`, `sdd/pure/spec`, `sdd/pure/design`, and `sdd/pure/tasks`, with project `engram-project`.
7. Run `gentle-ai sdd-status pure --cwd <repo> --json`.
8. Observe that the Engram stub is not invoked and the command reports an absent OpenSpec change.
9. Add only an empty `<repo>/.engram/` directory and repeat the same command.
10. Observe that the identical Engram observations are now resolved and routing advances to `apply`.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

A selected pure Engram store should be discoverable without an undocumented environment variable, marker directory, or OpenSpec configuration.

The native status engine should return `artifactStore: engram` and route from the exported Engram artifacts. First-party assets should describe the actual native behavior.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Without a hidden signal, Engram is never queried and the command returns `artifactStore: openspec`, `nextRecommended: sdd-new`, and `Active OpenSpec change not found`.

Adding only `.engram/` changes the same fixture to `artifactStore: engram` and `nextRecommended: apply`.

### Gentle AI Version

`main` snapshot at `942a3957a9954f5646f8edd97b6b1f32a17bfb33`  
Git descriptor: `v2.1.11-105-g942a3957`  
Plain local source build: `gentle-ai dev`

### Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client

OpenCode

### 📋 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
# No .engram/, OpenSpec config, or environment override
engram invoked: false
"artifactStore": "openspec"
"nextRecommended": "sdd-new"
"blockedReasons": [
  "Active OpenSpec change not found: pure."
]

# Identical fixture after adding only .engram/
engram invoked: true
"artifactStore": "engram"
"nextRecommended": "apply"
"blockedReasons": []
```

### Additional Context

Exact locations:

- `internal/sddstatus/status.go:256-275` calls the Engram fallback when OpenSpec cannot resolve the change.
- `internal/sddstatus/status.go:585-610` exits before export when `shouldTryEngram` rejects the workspace.
- `internal/sddstatus/status.go:806-829` defines the three hidden eligibility signals.
- `internal/assets/skills/_shared/sdd-status-contract.md:18-19` incorrectly describes the native dispatcher as OpenSpec-only.
- `internal/assets/opencode/commands/sdd-status.md:20` and `sdd-continue.md:13` prohibit native Engram dispatch.

Duplicate boundary:

- [#929](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/929) and [#948](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/948) reported the original absence of native Engram support and are closed as completed.
- [#957](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/957) added Engram resolution but left it behind the eligibility gate.
- This issue covers only the residual pure-Engram detection gap and alignment of generated assets with the implemented native behavior.
- Final duplicate triage for the frozen snapshot retained this draft as `create`.

Acceptance criteria:

- A pure Engram change resolves without requiring `.engram/`, an OpenSpec configuration, or an undocumented environment variable.
- A documented explicit artifact-store selection is acceptable if first-party orchestrators pass it consistently.
- `sdd-status` and `sdd-continue` produce Engram-backed routing for the unmarked fixture.
- Workspaces with neither OpenSpec nor Engram changes retain the normal `sdd-new` result.
- Existing OpenSpec and hybrid behavior remains unchanged.
- Generated status contracts and commands no longer claim the native engine cannot observe Engram.
- Regression tests cover unmarked pure Engram, marked Engram, OpenSpec, and no-store cases.

title: fix(backup): make restore atomic and conflict-aware
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description
`RestoreService` applies manifest entries sequentially. If a later entry fails, earlier targets remain restored while later targets retain their post-install state.

Restore also has no expected-current-state check. A user edit made after apply can be overwritten silently by an older snapshot.

This can leave a mixed configuration or destroy concurrent user changes.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce
1. Set the test home to `/tmp/gentle-ai-audit/home` and the backup root to `/tmp/gentle-ai-audit/home/backups`.
2. Create two live targets containing `after-one` and `after-two`.
3. Create a valid snapshot containing `before-one` for the first target.
4. Construct a plain manifest whose second entry references a missing snapshot.
5. Call `RestoreService{}.Restore(manifest)`.
6. Observe that the first target changed to `before-one` before the second entry failed.
7. In a separate fixture, snapshot `before`, set the live target to expected post-apply bytes, then simulate a user edit to `user-change`.
8. Restore the snapshot and inspect the target.

### ✅ Expected Behavior
A restore either completes as one operation or leaves every target unchanged. If any target differs from its expected current state, restore reports a conflict and does not overwrite it.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
The first case leaves mixed before/after state. The second succeeds and silently replaces `user-change` with `before`.

### Gentle AI Version
`main` snapshot at `942a3957a9954f5646f8edd97b6b1f32a17bfb33`  
Git descriptor: `v2.1.11-105-g942a3957`

### Operating System
Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client
Other

### 📋 Affected Area
Other

### 💡 Logs / Error Output
```text
Restore() error:
read snapshot file "/tmp/gentle-ai-audit/home/backups/files/missing":
no such file or directory

first target:  "before-one"
second target: "after-two"

conflict case:
Restore() error: <nil>
target after restore: "before"
user-change was lost
```

### Additional Context
**Template classification**

The defect affects all agents and belongs to Backup / Restore. The form uses `Other` because neither cross-client impact nor Backup / Restore is available as a dropdown option.

**Snapshot source locations**

- `internal/backup/restore.go:71-97` mutates compressed entries sequentially.
- `internal/backup/restore.go:105-119` does the same for legacy plain backups.
- `internal/backup/restore.go:129-155` writes each target immediately without an expected-state comparison.
- `internal/backup/manifest.go:97-102` contains no expected-current fingerprint or revision.
- `internal/cli/run.go:671-690` invokes this service for pipeline rollback.
- `docs/rollback.md:55-60` promises atomic file restoration with no partial restores.

**Duplicate boundaries**

- `#1676` covers the post-rename ambiguity in `mutationjournal`.
- This issue covers operation-wide atomicity and conflict detection inside `backup.RestoreService`.
- `mutationjournal` changes are explicitly outside this issue.
- Final duplicate triage for the frozen snapshot retained this draft as `create`.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Restore validates and materializes every required source before mutating live targets.
- [ ] A failure after mutation begins compensates every already-mutated target.
- [ ] Any entry conflict aborts the operation without modifying other targets.
- [ ] The restore contract carries or receives an expected-current fingerprint for conflict checks.
- [ ] Conflict errors identify the affected path without overwriting user changes.
- [ ] Tests cover later-entry failure, deletion entries, concurrent edits, compressed backups, and legacy backups.

title: fix(review): anchor authority parent creation and state publication
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description
The final Unix lock open uses descriptor-anchored, no-follow traversal, but surrounding authority operations remain pathname-based.

Two residual behaviors are reproducible:

1. `acquireLocalStoreLock` calls `os.MkdirAll` before the secure open. A symlinked authority root therefore causes an external `v2/` directory to be created before lock acquisition correctly fails.
2. After safely locking `v2/LOCK`, compact publication calls pathname-based `writeAtomic` for the lineage state. If the lineage path is a symlink, the operation succeeds and writes `review-state.json` outside the authority tree.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce
1. Check out the frozen `main` snapshot at `942a3957a9954f5646f8edd97b6b1f32a17bfb33` on Linux.
2. Derive a compact store, replace its authority root with a symlink to a temporary external directory, and invoke `Replace`.
3. Observe that secure lock opening fails but an external `v2/` directory has already been created.
4. Restore a real authority and `v2` directory.
5. Replace the requested lineage directory with a symlink to another external directory.
6. Invoke `Replace("", "review/start", state)`.
7. Observe that the call succeeds and publishes a valid compact record through the symlink.

### ✅ Expected Behavior
Authority parent creation and state publication should remain anchored beneath the validated repository authority root. Encountering a symlinked authority component should fail without creating or publishing anything outside that root.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
Pre-lock directory creation produces an external side effect, and later state publication can succeed through a symlinked lineage despite the safe `v2` lock.

### Gentle AI Version
`main` snapshot at `942a3957a9954f5646f8edd97b6b1f32a17bfb33`  
Git descriptor: `v2.1.11-105-g942a3957`

### Operating System
Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client
OpenCode

### 📋 Affected Area
Other

### 💡 Logs / Error Output
```text
secure lock open refused the symlink, but pre-open MkdirAll created external .../v2; error=not a directory
secure v2 lock succeeded while writeAtomic published 1855 bytes at external .../review-state.json
```

### Additional Context
**Source evidence**

- `internal/reviewtransaction/store_lock.go:139-144` performs `MkdirAll` before `secureOpenLocalStoreLock`.
- `internal/reviewtransaction/compact_store.go:1198-1275` locks `v2/LOCK` and later publishes the lineage state.
- `internal/reviewtransaction/store.go:940-971` creates and replaces files using pathname-based operations.
- `internal/reviewtransaction/repository_locator.go:388-431` binds repository and Git directory identity before authority-root derivation; it does not anchor later descendant operations.
- The final lock-parent traversal in `internal/reviewtransaction/secure_open_unix.go:14-62` correctly uses `O_NOFOLLOW`; that fixed boundary is not part of this report.

Independent reproduction at `1f3fda46311030abb351ff81971d905b78d40cac` confirmed both residuals and confirmed that the final secure lock open refused the symlink. The source delta through the frozen `942a3957a9954f5646f8edd97b6b1f32a17bfb33` snapshot changes authority-root identity derivation only; the vulnerable parent creation and state-publication operations are unchanged.

**Duplicate analysis**

Issue #1567 with PR #1571 and issue #1572 with PR #1573 harden the final lock open. PR #1706 hardens Git directory parsing and canonicalization, while PR #1714 binds the selected Git common-directory identity. Neither anchors descendant `MkdirAll` or `writeAtomic` operations after root derivation. Final duplicate triage for the frozen snapshot retained this draft as `create`.

**Threat-model scope**

This is narrowly an operational pathname-integrity issue. It does not claim resistance to a malicious same-user actor; it requires normal authority operations to avoid following stale or misconfigured path aliases outside their derived root.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Authority parent creation uses anchored no-follow traversal or rejects unsafe existing components before mutation.
- [ ] Compact temporary-file creation, replacement, and directory synchronization are anchored to the validated lineage directory.
- [ ] A symlinked authority root fails without creating external directories.
- [ ] A symlinked lineage fails without writing external state.
- [ ] Existing secure final-lock tests continue to pass.

title: fix(review): contain Unix descendants that escape the Git process group
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description
Unix Git cleanup controls only the process group initially created for the Git subprocess.

A descendant can call `setsid`, move into a new session and process group, and escape `syscall.Kill(-command.Process.Pid, SIGKILL)`. Focused probes confirmed that such descendants survive both normal Git completion and context timeout.

This can leak background processes after a review command has completed or failed.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce
1. Check out the frozen `main` snapshot at `942a3957a9954f5646f8edd97b6b1f32a17bfb33` on Linux.
2. Use a temporary package-local helper as `gitCommandContext`.
3. Have the helper start a child process that calls `setsid`, records its PID, and sleeps.
4. Let the original helper exit normally, then check the recorded PID.
5. Repeat while forcing `runGit` to time out.
6. Observe that the escaped descendant remains alive in both cases.

### ✅ Expected Behavior
Git cleanup should terminate or otherwise contain every descendant started for that invocation, including descendants that create a new process group or session.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
The original process group is killed, but the `setsid` descendant remains running after both normal return and timeout.

### Gentle AI Version
`main` snapshot at `942a3957a9954f5646f8edd97b6b1f32a17bfb33`  
Git descriptor: `v2.1.11-105-g942a3957`

### Operating System
Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

### AI Agent / Client
OpenCode

### 📋 Affected Area
Other

### 💡 Logs / Error Output
```text
mode=return escaped_pid=<pid> running_after_return=true
mode=timeout escaped_pid=<pid> running_after_return=true
```

### Additional Context
**Source evidence**

- `internal/reviewtransaction/git_process_unix.go:10-15` enables `Setpgid` and releases only `-command.Process.Pid`.
- `internal/reviewtransaction/snapshot.go:1163-1180` invokes that release path after completion or cancellation.

**Duplicate analysis**

PR #1338 introduced process-group cleanup, but does not cover descendants that escape into another session. Final duplicate triage for the frozen snapshot found no exact active or fixed-on-snapshot duplicate and retained this draft as `create`.

**Threat-model scope**

This is subprocess lifecycle and resource containment, not protection against a malicious same-user actor.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Supported Unix execution contains descendants that call `setsid` or otherwise leave the original process group.
- [ ] Cleanup applies after normal completion, timeout, and process-control failure.
- [ ] No descendant remains alive after `runGit` returns.
- [ ] Regression tests verify both normal-return and timeout paths and clean up all probe processes.

title: fix(sync): fail closed when persisted persona state is invalid
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

Persona synchronization fails open when persisted installation state cannot be read or contains an unknown/empty persona. The sync path discards `state.Read` errors and normalizes invalid persona state to Neutral, then rewrites an existing valid persona block. A corrupted or unreadable state file can therefore become destructive configuration input instead of stopping before mutation.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Pi with a valid Gentleman persona block.
2. Corrupt `~/.gentle-ai/state.json`, make it unreadable, or set its persisted persona to an unknown value while keeping Pi discoverable.
3. Run `gentle-ai sync` without an explicit persona override.
4. Inspect the existing Pi persona block after sync.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Sync should fail closed before persona mutation when persisted state is unreadable or contains an unsupported persona. A missing legacy persona field may use a deliberately documented compatibility default, but malformed/unknown state must not silently replace valid existing configuration.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The state read error is discarded and invalid/empty persona input falls back to Neutral. Sync succeeds and replaces the existing Pi persona with Neutral. The existing test `TestRunSyncWithSelection_UnknownPersistedPersonaFallsBackToNeutral` codifies the destructive fallback rather than rejecting it.

### Gentle AI Version

`gentle-ai 1.49.1-0.20260722122850-8881b60b01c7` (commit `8881b60b01c7cbf80da072d95579fe66b3e3a63b`)

Other

CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
go test ./internal/cli -run TestRunSyncWithSelection_UnknownPersistedPersonaFallsBackToNeutral -count=1
# PASS: unknown persisted persona is normalized to Neutral

before: Pi persona = gentleman
state:  malformed, unreadable, or unknown persona
after:  Pi persona = neutral
```

### Additional Context

Affected symbols:

- `internal/cli/sync.go`: persisted state read, persona normalization, `RunSyncWithSelection`
- `internal/components/persona/inject.go`: persona replacement

Related but not duplicate:

- #610 and PR #611 only synchronize the selected persona into Pi's `.pi/gentle-ai/persona.json`; they do not define malformed global-state handling or protect an existing persona from a fail-open fallback.

title: fix(filemerge): preserve large JSON integers during managed merges
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

Managed JSON merges decode user configuration into `map[string]any` with `json.Unmarshal`. JSON numbers therefore become `float64`, and integers above JavaScript's safe-integer boundary lose precision when Gentle AI re-encodes an otherwise unrelated configuration update.

A deterministic input value of `9007199254740993` is persisted as `9007199254740992` after a Pi settings or generic managed JSON merge.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a managed Pi or OpenCode JSON file containing an unrelated integer field with value `9007199254740993`.
2. Run an install or sync operation that calls `mergePiJSONFile` or `filemerge.MergeJSONObjects` with an unrelated overlay.
3. Re-open the JSON file and inspect the integer field.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Unrelated JSON numeric values should survive managed merges exactly. Decoding should preserve number tokens, for example with `json.Decoder.UseNumber()`, before re-encoding.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The integer is decoded through `float64`, rounded, and written back as `9007199254740992`. The managed overlay does not need to touch that field for corruption to occur.

### Gentle AI Version

`gentle-ai 1.49.1-0.20260722122850-8881b60b01c7` (commit `8881b60b01c7cbf80da072d95579fe66b3e3a63b`)

Installation Pipeline

- `internal/components/filemerge/json_merge.go`: `unmarshalJSONObject`, `MergeJSONObjects`
