title: feat(skills): add verifiable skill loading and compliance validation
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

Other — skill resolution and orchestrator validation

### 💡 Problem Statement

Gentle AI currently treats `skill_resolution: paths-injected` as “all good”, although this value is a self-report from the subagent and has no independent runtime evidence. It does not prove that the skill was actually read, understood, or followed.

This creates a false assurance path:

1. A delegator injects an exact `SKILL.md` path.
2. The subagent reports `skill_resolution: paths-injected`.
3. The orchestrator accepts that report as successful skill resolution.
4. The result can still violate explicit rules from the skill, with no compliance gate detecting it.

A real incident occurred with a copywriting skill: the agent reported `paths-injected`, but the generated copy used vague claims, failed to state a concrete differentiator, did not translate features into benefits, and produced a weak hero promise—contrary to the skill contract.

In v2.1.4:

- `internal/assets/skills/_shared/skill-resolver.md` defines `paths-injected` as receiving exact paths and loading them, but the value is returned by the same model being evaluated.
- `internal/skillregistry/registry.go` indexes only skill name, description, and path.
- `internal/assets/opencode/sdd-orchestrator.md` treats `paths-injected` as “all good”.
- The automatic gatekeeper validates result shape, artifact existence, hallucinated references, input drift, routing, and risks, but not compliance with loaded skills.
- Existing tests verify prompt anchors and fields, not actual skill reads or behavioral compliance.

This is related to #435, where behavioral verification was explicitly left out of scope. No equivalent open or closed issue was found. The relevant behavior is unchanged between tag v2.1.4 (`6b7474ae3166f2dae73bd8a21c4af411ad509cab`) and current `main` at the time of verification (`1b5a5f59f74d3f6dab7de01c1603d5ce1b77af17`).

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Separate skill delivery, loading evidence, and compliance into distinct signals instead of treating `paths-injected` as sufficient:

1. **Delivery evidence**
   - Record the exact skill path and content hash supplied to the subagent.
   - Distinguish `paths-provided` from `content-loaded`.
   - When the client supports it, bind `content-loaded` to an observable read/tool event rather than model self-report.

2. **Compliance evidence**
   - Require the result to map applicable skill rules to concrete output evidence.
   - For tasks with objective output rules, run a fresh validator against the produced result and the loaded `SKILL.md`.
   - Do not treat skill compliance as proven merely because the Result Contract contains `skill_resolution`.

3. **Orchestrator behavior**
   - Replace the unconditional “all good” interpretation with explicit confidence/verification states.
   - Surface unverifiable loading as telemetry, not as a verified fact.
   - Fail or warn when mandatory skill rules are observably violated.

4. **Regression coverage**
   - Test that injected paths alone cannot produce a verified-compliance state.
   - Test that a result violating deterministic skill rules is rejected or flagged.

This should preserve lightweight contextual loading while removing the false implication that path injection proves skill application or output quality.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- Rely exclusively on stronger prompt wording. This improves intent but remains model self-report without evidence.
- Require every skill to perform its own self-critique. This helps quality, but the same model still judges its own compliance.
- Treat the incident only as a weak copywriting skill. That cannot explain why the orchestrator accepts `paths-injected` without checking any rule from the skill.

### 📎 Additional Context

The requested guarantee is not that every subjective result must be excellent. The narrower requirement is that Gentle AI must not present skill loading or compliance as verified when it only has an uncorroborated model assertion. Subjective quality can remain advisory; deterministic skill rules should be independently checkable.

title: Engram protocol is injected three times per session (~4,950 tokens of duplication) on claude-code
body:
## Summary

On `claude-code`, the Engram protocol is delivered to the model **three times in every session**, from three independent sources. Together they cost **~4,950 tokens of always-on context** for a protocol that only needs to be stated once.

This is especially visible because the v2 release is framed around cutting prompt size (86–89% smaller review prompts, measured). That win is real — but it is a *per-review* saving. Meanwhile the *always-on* injection quietly went up, because `gentle-ai install` writes a full copy of the Engram protocol into `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, which is loaded on **every** session, including ones that never touch SDD or memory.

## Evidence

| # | Source | Bytes | ~Tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `engram` plugin `SessionStart` hook → `scripts/session-start.sh` | 12,244 | ~3,061 |
| 2 | `<!-- gentle-ai:engram-protocol -->` block written into `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` by `gentle-ai install` | 6,759 | ~1,689 |
| 3 | Engram MCP server `instructions` (lands in the system prompt) | ~800 | ~200 |
| | **Total** | **~19,800** | **~4,950** |

All three carry the same content — the `## Engram Persistent Memory` heading, the `PROACTIVE SAVE` trigger list, the `mem_save` format, and the search flow. Sources (1) and (2) share top-level headings verbatim.

## Reproduce

```bash
gentle-ai install --agents claude-code --components skills

# (2) — the block gentle-ai adds to the always-loaded global rules file
awk '/<!-- gentle-ai:engram-protocol -->/,/<!-- \/gentle-ai:engram-protocol -->/' ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md | wc -c
# 6759

# (1) — what the plugin hook already injects every session anyway
~/.claude/plugins/cache/engram/engram/0.1.1/scripts/session-start.sh | wc -c
# 12244
```

Both then appear in the same context window, saying the same thing.

## Why (2) looks like the redundant one

`docs/intended-usage.md` states:

> "CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md serve as **project-level convention registries, not always-on rule containers**. They work on-demand... This keeps context focused rather than loading everything globally."

But the installer writes ~289 lines of always-on rules into `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (engram-protocol + sdd-orchestrator + trigger-rules + persona). The doc and the installer disagree.

Since the `engram` plugin already delivers the protocol via its `SessionStart` hook **and** its MCP `instructions`, copy (2) appears to add nothing the model would not already have.

## Suggested fix

Skip the `gentle-ai:engram-protocol` block in `CLAUDE.md` when the `engram` plugin is installed (detectable via `~/.claude/plugins/`), or reduce it to a short pointer. Ideally (1) and (3) would also be deduped against each other — the MCP `instructions` and the `SessionStart` hook currently overlap heavily too.

Happy to test a patch.

## Environment

- gentle-ai `2.1.0`
- engram plugin `0.1.1`
- agent: `claude-code` (registered in `~/.gentle-ai/state.json`)
- macOS (darwin), Homebrew install

---

Unrelated but adjacent, in case it's useful: `gentle-ai sync` (bare, no `--components`) runs the `persona` component and **overwrites the top of `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`**, destroying user-authored global rules above the gentle-ai markers. `gentle-ai install --agents codex --components skills` correctly appends below them instead. Happy to open that separately if you'd prefer.

title: fix(pi): prevent Judgment Day judge-budget overflow from detached retries
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

The Pi Judgment Day orchestration path can exceed its mandatory two-judge budget when detached judge execution is not observable or controllable.

A graph-v1 Judgment Day transaction starts with exactly two blind judges. The runtime may return neither stable child run IDs nor a capability preflight result. If an operator retries a judge because its execution cannot be observed, the runtime can dispatch a third detached judge. That makes the transaction unusable: the contract permits exactly two judges, while the extra actor cannot be safely incorporated into discovery.

In the observed failure mode, detached judges also lacked filesystem-read capability. This was discovered only after the review transaction had already started and budget slots were consumed.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. In Pi, start an explicit graph-v1 Judgment Day transaction with its two-judge budget.
2. Dispatch the two blind judges through the detached runtime.
3. Observe that the runtime does not expose stable judge run IDs or a capability preflight result to the controller.
4. Retry one unobservable judge.
5. Observe that a third detached judge can be dispatched; some detached judges may report no filesystem-read tools after dispatch.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

- Judgment Day should preflight each judge's required read capabilities before START consumes the two-judge budget.
- The controller should receive stable run IDs/status for both allocated judges.
- A retry after allocation must be rejected or bound to the original judge, never create a third judge.
- If orchestration fails before usable discovery, the transaction should expose a documented, non-destructive terminal invalidation/recovery path.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

- Detached judge execution did not expose usable run IDs to the controller.
- Retrying an unobservable judge dispatched a third actor, exceeding the exact two-judge contract.
- Detached judge sessions reported no filesystem-read capability after the transaction had started.
- The safe response was to halt before discovery reduction, finalize, receipt, gate, or publication, leaving the attempted transaction irrecoverable without an explicit recovery procedure.

### Gentle AI Version

gentle-ai 2.0.2; issue also affects the Pi Judgment Day orchestration contract packaged with gentle-pi 1.0.2.

### Operating System

macOS

### AI Agent / Client

Other (Pi)

### 📋 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```text
Judgment Day budget: 2 judges / 0 refuters
Detached judge runs: no stable run IDs visible to the controller
Retry outcome: a third detached judge was dispatched
Detached judge capability: no filesystem-read tools available
Safety action: halted before discovery reduction/finalize/gate/publication
```

### Additional Context

This report intentionally omits application/repository details. The issue is about preserving the bounded Judgment Day contract when the runtime cannot prove actor identity, status, and required read capability.

title: feat(tui): add doctor diagnostics with safe managed repairs
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### Affected Area

TUI (terminal UI)

### Problem Statement

`gentle-ai doctor` provides useful read-only CLI diagnostics, but users who start from the TUI cannot discover system health, understand which findings are safely repairable, apply a bounded repair, or verify that it worked without leaving the application and translating prose remedies into commands.

The current doctor result is also presentation-oriented: each check returns a status, detail string, and free-form remedy string. Adding repair behavior directly to either renderer would risk duplicated logic, inconsistent CLI/TUI results, and unsafe command-like remedies.

The desired user outcome is a guided **Health / Doctor** workflow where users can:

- inspect the same diagnostics from CLI or TUI;
- distinguish automatic, confirmation-required, and manual-only remedies before acting;
- apply only explicitly supported Gentle AI repairs with clear impact and recovery information;
- re-run diagnostics after each action and see whether the system converged to healthy, improved but still degraded, or unchanged/failed;
- leave with actionable manual guidance when Gentle AI cannot safely repair a finding.

### Proposed Solution

Add a **Health / Doctor** entry to the TUI, preferably near other maintenance actions on the welcome screen. It should run diagnostics, present a navigable summary and per-finding details, expose only eligible actions, show progress/results, and offer **Run checks again**.

#### Shared diagnostic and remedy contract

Evolve doctor toward a structured, typed model consumed by both CLI and TUI. The design should represent concepts such as:

- stable diagnostic identity, status/severity, summary, detail, and relevant evidence;
- an optional typed remedy identity with eligibility, action category, impact summary, and platform support;
- execution result, warnings, changed resources, backup/rollback information, and follow-up guidance;
- recheck results that can be correlated with the original finding.

CLI text and TUI views should render this shared model rather than independently detecting problems or parsing remedy strings. Exact package boundaries and interfaces should be decided during design; this issue does not prescribe brittle internals.

#### Action categories

| Category | Expected behavior |
|---|---|
| Automatic | Low-risk, idempotent action confined to known Gentle AI-managed resources. The UI still explains what will happen and reports the result. |
| Confirmation required | A supported mutation with meaningful filesystem, download, overwrite, restart-guidance, or rollback implications. Require explicit confirmation and show affected managed resources. |
| Manual only | No executable repair. Show precise guidance because ownership, secrets, external processes, permissions, disk cleanup, or unknown state prevents safe automation. |

Classification should be capability-based and auditable, not inferred from human-readable text.

#### Initial safe MVP actions

The first increment should support only repairs that can reuse established managed operations and ownership boundaries:

- sync managed configuration when doctor detects missing or drifted managed config;
- reinstall a missing Gentle AI-managed component or tool through the existing supported install path;
- repair or recreate a Gentle AI-managed shim where the platform and component explicitly support it;
- for Engram reachability, provide bounded restart/recheck guidance and then recheck health; do **not** introduce arbitrary process discovery, termination, or process control;
- rerun doctor after a repair or on explicit user request.

Findings such as low disk space, unknown PATH duplicates, malformed user-owned content without a safe recovery source, unavailable permissions, or unsupported platforms should remain manual-only until a separately reviewed safe capability exists.

#### Safety, confirmation, backup, and rollback

- Show the action, reason, scope, managed paths/components, expected side effects, and whether backup/rollback is available before confirmation.
- Reuse existing backup, mutation-journal, install, sync, and rollback capabilities where suitable rather than creating a parallel mutation system.
- Create a backup or reversible journal before overwriting/removing managed data when the underlying operation supports it.
- On failure, attempt only the rollback guaranteed by that operation, report partial changes and rollback outcome, and preserve logs/evidence for troubleshooting.
- Never present rollback as guaranteed when external installers, permissions, security software, network failures, or process state make it best-effort.
- Disable or downgrade a remedy to manual-only when ownership, containment, platform support, prerequisites, or a safe backup boundary cannot be established.
- Confirmation must be explicit, keyboard-accessible, default to cancel, and must not be bypassed by navigation or retry.

#### Destructive boundaries and explicit non-goals

This feature must not:

- execute arbitrary shell commands or free-form command strings from diagnostics;
- delete unknown, duplicate, shadowing, or user-installed binaries;
- silently mutate secrets, credentials, environment variables, or unrecognized/user-owned configuration;
- provide general-purpose process termination or restart control;
- claim to repair low disk space, antivirus quarantine, network policy, or unsupported third-party state;
- turn every prose remedy into an executable action;
- redesign all doctor checks or settle final internal APIs before an approved design.

#### Post-repair recheck and convergence

After an attempted repair, rerun the relevant checks and preferably the full doctor suite. The result must distinguish:

- **resolved**: the original finding now passes;
- **improved**: severity decreased but the finding remains;
- **unchanged**: no diagnostic change;
- **new/regressed**: another finding appeared or worsened;
- **recheck failed**: diagnostics could not complete.

Repeated repair should be idempotent where practical. If the same supported action does not converge, stop offering blind retries and surface evidence plus manual guidance.

#### Cross-platform, accessibility, and error handling

- Model platform support explicitly for Windows, macOS, Linux, and WSL; unsupported actions remain visible as manual guidance rather than disappearing.
- Preserve platform-specific executable/shim semantics and avoid assuming POSIX paths or shells.
- Support keyboard-only navigation, clear focus, non-color status labels/icons, readable narrow-terminal wrapping, and screen-reader-friendly text ordering.
- Do not rely on animation alone; expose progress and final status in text.
- Handle cancellation, resize, timeout, permission denial, offline downloads, partial install/sync, backup failure, rollback conflict/failure, and diagnostic failure without crashing or losing the prior report.
- Keep actionable error details while redacting secrets and sensitive values.

#### Acceptance criteria and scenarios

- [ ] **Given** a user opens the TUI, **when** they select Health / Doctor, **then** they receive a navigable report produced from the same structured diagnostic model used by `gentle-ai doctor`.
- [ ] **Given** a passing or manual-only finding, **when** it is selected, **then** the TUI does not expose an executable repair and provides an explanation or manual guidance.
- [ ] **Given** a missing managed config that existing sync can safely restore, **when** the user confirms repair, **then** the scoped managed sync runs, reports changed resources, and doctor rechecks the result.
- [ ] **Given** a missing managed component/tool, **when** prerequisites and platform support are satisfied and the user confirms, **then** the existing supported install path is used and the result is rechecked.
- [ ] **Given** a broken managed shim on a supported platform, **when** ownership and containment are verified, **then** only that managed shim is repaired/recreated; unknown binaries are not removed.
- [ ] **Given** Engram is unreachable, **when** the finding is opened, **then** the user receives restart/recheck guidance and can rerun the check without Gentle AI arbitrarily controlling processes.
- [ ] **Given** an action can overwrite managed data, **when** confirmation is shown, **then** affected scope, backup/rollback availability, and destructive boundaries are visible and cancel is the safe default.
- [ ] **Given** repair fails after a partial mutation, **when** rollback is supported, **then** rollback is attempted and both mutation and rollback outcomes are reported; unsupported recovery is stated honestly.
- [ ] **Given** a repair succeeds but recheck remains degraded, **then** the TUI reports improved/unchanged state and does not claim success solely because the action exited successfully.
- [ ] **Given** repeated repair does not converge, **then** blind retry is stopped and manual guidance/evidence is shown.
- [ ] **Given** an unsupported OS/action, **then** diagnostics remain available and the remedy is manual-only with platform-specific guidance.
- [ ] **Given** a narrow or non-color terminal, **then** all findings, confirmations, progress, errors, and outcomes remain understandable and operable by keyboard.
- [ ] Existing CLI doctor output remains supported, and CLI/TUI classification cannot drift because detection and remedy metadata are shared.
- [ ] Tests prove that no remedy path accepts arbitrary command strings, deletes unknown binaries, or silently mutates secrets/unrecognized config.

#### Architecture considerations

- Keep diagnosis, remedy eligibility, execution, and rendering separate so checks remain testable and frontends remain thin.
- Treat remedies as an allowlisted capability registry or equivalent typed dispatch, never as shell text embedded in a finding.
- Preserve a read-only diagnostic path; running doctor must not mutate state merely because a remedy exists.
- Reuse current sync/install/backup/rollback primitives only where their contracts meet the narrower doctor safety requirements.
- Make cancellation/timeouts and structured execution results first-class so CLI and TUI can report consistently.
- Define ownership and containment checks for every mutating remedy, including symlink/path traversal and concurrent-change behavior.
- Keep future headless/JSON output possible, without making it an MVP requirement.

#### Test strategy

- Unit-test diagnostic status, remedy category/eligibility, platform capability, typed dispatch, redaction, and convergence classification.
- Table-test every MVP remedy across success, cancellation, unsupported platform, prerequisite failure, timeout, partial mutation, backup failure, rollback success/failure, and recheck failure.
- Add filesystem tests for managed-path containment, symlink escape, unknown binaries, concurrent changes, idempotency, and preservation of user-owned config/secrets.
- Add TUI model/screen tests for navigation, confirmation default, keyboard-only operation, resize/narrow layout, non-color labels, progress, retry suppression, and error recovery.
- Add CLI regression tests proving existing doctor rendering is derived from the shared report and remains read-only.
- Include Windows executable/PATHEXT/shim coverage plus macOS/Linux/WSL behavior where capabilities differ.
- Run the repository's standard Go test, vet, build, and cross-platform build checks; use focused integration tests with fake installers/services rather than mutating a developer machine.

#### Suggested staged implementation

This feature is likely to exceed the 400 changed-line review budget. Prefer reviewable, non-cumulative stages after maintainer approval, for example:

1. Introduce the shared typed diagnostic/remedy model and preserve CLI behavior with no repair execution.
2. Add the read-only Health / Doctor TUI report and recheck flow.
3. Add the allowlisted repair executor and one narrow managed repair with backup/rollback tests.
4. Add remaining MVP actions in small capability-focused PRs, with platform and safety tests beside each action.

The exact split should follow the approved design and keep tests with each behavior; request `size:exception` only if splitting would weaken safety review.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Keep doctor CLI-only and show command hints in the TUI:** lower effort, but users still leave the workflow and free-form commands cannot safely express eligibility, confirmation, rollback, or convergence.
- **Have the TUI parse current doctor text:** rejected because presentation text is not a stable API and would duplicate classification logic.
- **Automatically run every remedy:** rejected because many findings concern user-owned resources, external tools, secrets, disk, permissions, or processes that Gentle AI cannot safely mutate.
- **Build a general repair shell:** rejected because arbitrary command execution is outside the product's managed ownership and safety boundaries.

### Additional Context

Related work that this feature should build on without duplicating:

- PR #690 introduced the read-only `gentle-ai doctor` checks and remedy text.
- PR #952 fixed Windows PATHEXT/shim-aware duplicate detection; repair design must preserve those platform semantics.
- PR #973 demonstrates a focused TUI welcome shortcut and targeted managed sync flow.
- PR #1059 adds version-aware managed community-tool reconcile/upgrade behavior that may inform eligible reinstall capabilities.
- PR #1193 provides precedent for confirmation, managed ownership boundaries, reversible mutations, rollback reporting, and TUI result screens.
- Issue #709 tracks state-aware doctor tool checks and false-positive PATH diagnostics.
- Issue #850 shows missing prerequisites and Engram install/process-state failures that require honest guidance rather than unsafe automation.
- Issue #932 tracks a Windows managed `gga.ps1` shim resolution failure and is a candidate class for a narrowly supported shim repair.
- Issue #914 shows why antivirus/security-software deletion must remain outside silent or arbitrary repair behavior.

The duplicate search covered open and closed issues/PRs for doctor, diagnostics, health, repair, remedies, and TUI integration. These references overlap individual checks or safe mutation primitives, but none requests this shared CLI/TUI diagnostic model and bounded repair workflow.

title: feat(agent): add Oh My Pi support
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that `status:approved` is required before implementation begins

### Affected Area
Agent Detection

### Problem Statement
Oh My Pi is a separate terminal coding agent and does not currently have
first-class support in Gentle AI.

OMP provides native capabilities for agent resources, commands, context rules,
MCP, plugins, extensions, and discovery. An integration should work with those
native mechanisms instead of treating OMP as Pi or duplicating capabilities
already available in the OMP ecosystem.

### Proposed Solution
Add Oh My Pi as a supported Gentle AI agent.

The integration should use Gentle AI's standard agent lifecycle while respecting
OMP's native configuration, profiles, resource discovery, plugins, extensions,
and MCP support.

It should preserve existing OMP behavior and configuration, avoid modifying
OMP itself, and avoid creating a separate OMP-specific workflow when the
standard Gentle AI flow can be used.

### Alternatives Considered
- Manual setup outside Gentle AI.
- Reusing the Pi integration directly, despite OMP having a different runtime,
  configuration model, and extension ecosystem.

### Additional Context
The goal is a maintainable integration where Gentle AI adds its own value
without replacing or duplicating OMP-native tooling.

title: feat(uninstall): add symlink cleanup policy
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

TUI (terminal UI), CLI (commands, flags)

### 💡 Problem Statement

Issue #306 covers the immediate bug where sync/uninstall failed when managed config files were symlinks, which is common for GNU Stow, chezmoi, and dotfiles repositories.

PR #1077 intentionally keeps the bugfix small and conservative:

- sync writes through existing symlinks and preserves the link;
- uninstall can read symlinked managed files;
- when uninstall removes a symlinked file path, it removes the symlink path rather than deleting the dotfiles target.

That default is safe, but it does not let users choose a more destructive cleanup mode when they explicitly want uninstall to remove the original file inside their dotfiles repo too.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Add an explicit symlink handling policy for uninstall when symlinked managed files are detected before the final confirmation step.

Suggested TUI flow:

1. User selects an uninstall mode/components as today.
2. Before the final confirm screen, Gentle AI detects symlinked managed file paths in the uninstall plan.
3. If no symlinks are present, the flow stays unchanged.
4. If symlinks are present, show a policy selection screen:

   - Remove only the symlink
     - Deletes the managed path such as `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`.
     - Keeps the original file in the dotfiles repository.
     - Safe default.

   - Remove the symlink target too
     - Deletes or cleans the resolved target in the dotfiles repository.
     - More complete uninstall, but destructive.
     - Should be clearly warned and backed up.

The selected policy should be passed into the uninstall service, not implemented only in the TUI. The CLI should also get an equivalent flag, for example:

```bash
gga uninstall --symlink-policy=remove-link
gga uninstall --symlink-policy=remove-target
```

Default should remain safe: `remove-link`.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- Always delete only the symlink: safest, but users who want complete dotfiles cleanup must do manual cleanup.
- Always delete the resolved target: too destructive for an uninstall command, especially with dotfiles repos.
- Add no TUI choice and only document manual cleanup: lower implementation cost, but worse UX for users who intentionally want target cleanup.

### 📎 Additional Context

Related work:

- Original bug: #306
- Conservative bugfix PR: #1077

Implementation notes:

- Keep this as a separate PR from #1077 to stay under the 400-line review budget.
- Model the behavior as a service-level policy so TUI and CLI share semantics.
- Add tests for both policies: preserving/removing only the symlink and removing/cleaning the target when explicitly selected.
- Be careful with backups and messaging. If the target is in a dotfiles repo, deleting it is user data destruction unless clearly requested.

Maintainer note: this issue was created via `gh issue create`, which cannot combine issue-form templates with explicit body content. The body follows the feature request template fields manually.

title: feat(context-pruning): integrate dynamic context pruning for OpenCode
body:
### Pre-flight Checks
- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand this issue needs status:approved before a PR can be opened

### Problem Description
LLM coding sessions accumulate redundant tool calls, duplicate file reads, and stale error outputs that bloat the context window. This increases token costs and degrades response quality. OpenCode has a mature plugin ecosystem for context management, but Gentle AI doesn't integrate any context pruning tool.

The OpenCode DCP plugin (`opencode-dynamic-context-pruning`) provides:
- Zero-cost automatic strategies (deduplication, write superseding, error purging)
- LLM-driven pruning tools (discard, extract)
- Real-time token statistics (/dcp stats, /dcp context)
- Configurable protection (turn protection, protected tools, file patterns)

### Proposed Solution
Integrate DCP as an OpenCode plugin (not a community tool — it's a harness-specific plugin, not a CLI):

1. Add DCP npm package as a dependency in the OpenCode plugin config
2. Generate `opencode.json` plugin entry during component apply
3. Add configuration options to the Gentle AI TUI (enable/disable, notification style, manual mode)
4. Ensure DCP doesn't conflict with Gentle AI's built-in compaction (DCP replaces it)
5. Add tests for plugin injection and config generation

**Architecture consideration:** DCP is OpenCode-specific. For other harnesses:
- Pi: `pi-context-prune` exists (separate maintainer)
- Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf: no equivalent plugin exists
- `@cortexkit/magic-context` supports OpenCode + Pi but is a different project

This PR focuses on OpenCode DCP only. Multi-harness context pruning can be explored separately.

### Affected Area
Other

### Alternatives Considered
- `magic-context` (cortexkit) — supports OpenCode + Pi but is a different, newer project
- Built-in compaction only — doesn't provide granular control or statistics
- No integration — users install DCP manually

### Additional Context
- DCP GitHub: https://github.com/Opencode-DCP/opencode-dynamic-context-pruning
- DCP is the most popular OpenCode plugin (3.1.14, AUR package exists)
- Config schema: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Opencode-DCP/opencode-dynamic-context-pruning/master/dcp.schema.json
- Conflicts with built-in compaction — must be mutually exclusive

title: fix(antigravity): enforce dynamic subagent runtime parity
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

Antigravity CLI (`agy`) is documented by the platform as supporting runtime custom subagents via `define_subagent` and `invoke_subagent`, but Gentle AI's Antigravity integration still behaves closer to a solo-agent flow in key places. This means Antigravity does not reliably match the Pi/OpenCode behavior for SDD phase isolation, 4R/Judgment Day review delegation, CodeGraph-first exploration, and Engram-backed artifact continuity.

This is especially visible compared with Pi/OpenCode: Pi gets package-managed subagents and CodeGraph/Engram harness behavior, OpenCode gets static subagent overlays, while Antigravity has to use runtime dynamic subagents. The current Antigravity contract should explicitly require that dynamic runtime path and fail closed when required subagent tools are unavailable.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Install/sync Gentle AI for Antigravity CLI (`agy`).
2. Start a non-trivial SDD request that requires exploration/apply/verify or 4R/Judgment Day review.
3. Compare behavior with Pi or OpenCode.
4. Observe that Antigravity lacks the same enforced phase boundary and fresh-context reviewer behavior unless the prompt manually follows dynamic subagent delegation.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Antigravity CLI should use its native runtime subagent primitives to approximate Pi/OpenCode behavior:

- SDD phase work should be delegated through `define_subagent` + `invoke_subagent` instead of running heavy work inline.
- Required 4R/Judgment Day reviews should use dynamic fresh-context agents.
- The orchestrator should fail closed when dynamic subagent tools are unavailable for required phase/review work.
- CodeGraph should be used before broad codebase exploration.
- Engram should be treated as the default artifact backend when MCP/memory tools are available, without pretending persistence exists when they are unavailable.
- Both `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli` and `~/.gemini/antigravity-desktop` skill/config surfaces should be documented and respected.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The Antigravity integration is not as strongly aligned with Pi/OpenCode behavior:

- The public docs still describe Antigravity as solo-agent / Mission Control in places.
- The Antigravity SDD prompt needs a stronger dynamic delegation contract for `define_subagent` / `invoke_subagent`.
- Review/Judgment Day behavior is not explicitly modeled as dynamic runtime agents.
- CodeGraph and Engram expectations are not explicit enough for Antigravity CLI sessions.
- Legacy `~/.gemini/antigravity` wording can conflict with the current `antigravity-cli` / `antigravity-desktop` surfaces.

### Gentle AI Version

gga v2.10.1

### Operating System

Windows (WSL)

### AI Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Affected Area

Documentation

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```shell
N/A — behavior/contract mismatch in Antigravity CLI integration.
```

### Additional Context

Official Antigravity docs describe asynchronous subagents and runtime custom subagents using `define_subagent` and `invoke_subagent`. Gentle AI should not copy Pi/OpenCode implementation details directly, but should provide equivalent behavior using Antigravity's runtime primitives.

title: bug(claude-code): Engram MCP connection gets SIGINT'd seconds after connecting and never reconnects
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 📝 Bug Description

The Engram MCP server (registered by gentle-ai as the built-in plugin `engram@engram` in `~/.claude/settings.json` → `enabledPlugins`) fails to stay connected in Claude Code. On every session start, Claude Code's MCP client connects to the `engram` server successfully (handshake completes, `hasTools:true`), but within 2-5 seconds Claude Code itself sends `SIGINT` to the server process, clears its connection cache "for reconnection", and then **never reconnects** for the rest of the session. As a result, none of the `mem_*` tools (`mem_save`, `mem_search`, `mem_context`, etc.) are ever available to the model — not as directly-loaded tools, not as ToolSearch-discoverable deferred tools.

`claude mcp list` / the `/mcp` panel initially shows `engram` as "Connected", but since no tools ever got registered, the memory protocol injected by the SessionStart hook is dead on arrival. After repeated reconnection attempts the `/mcp` panel eventually shows `plugin:engram:engram ✗ failed`.

This reproduces across multiple projects on the same machine (confirmed in at least 2 separate project directories), and persists across a **full process restart** of Claude Code (not just `/clear` — closing the terminal entirely and relaunching `claude` in a new terminal reproduces the exact same failure).

The `engram` binary itself is healthy: querying it manually over stdio with a raw `initialize` + `tools/list` JSON-RPC request returns a complete, valid tool list (18 tools) in under 200ms, with no errors on stderr. So the defect is in the connection lifecycle management between Claude Code and this specific plugin-registered MCP server, not in the Engram binary.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce
1. Have `engram@engram` enabled as a Claude Code plugin (`enabledPlugins` in `~/.claude/settings.json`, installed via the `gentle-ai`/Engram marketplace, binary via Linuxbrew: `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/engram`, engram v1.17.0).
2. Start a new Claude Code session in any project (`claude` in a fresh terminal).
3. Immediately after the SessionStart hook fires (memory protocol gets injected into context), check `~/.cache/claude-cli-nodejs/<project>/mcp-logs-plugin-engram-engram/<latest>.jsonl`.
4. Try calling any `mem_*` tool, or search for it via `ToolSearch` with query `select:mem_save` / `mcp__plugin_engram_engram`.

### ✅ Expected Behavior
The `engram` MCP connection stays alive for the duration of the session (as it does for other plugins/MCP servers, and as it used to for `engram` itself in older sessions — see below), and the `mem_*` tools declared by the server (`mem_save`, `mem_search`, `mem_context`, `mem_session_summary`, `mem_get_observation`, `mem_save_prompt` as always-loaded; the rest as ToolSearch-deferred) are actually reachable by the model.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
Every session start produces this exact log pattern in `mcp-logs-plugin-engram-engram/*.jsonl`:

```
{"debug":"Starting connection with timeout of 30000ms", ...}
{"debug":"Successfully connected (transport: stdio) in ~190ms", ...}
{"debug":"Server instructions truncated from 2539 to 2048 chars", ...}
{"debug":"Connection established with capabilities: {\"hasTools\":true,...}", ...}
{"debug":"Sending SIGINT to MCP server process", ...}          ← 2-5s later, no tool ever called
{"debug":"UNKNOWN connection closed after Ns (cleanly)", ...}
{"debug":"Cleared connection cache for reconnection", ...}
{"debug":"MCP server process exited cleanly", ...}
```
— and no further connection attempt is logged for the rest of the session. `ToolSearch` with queries like `select:mem_save` or `mcp__plugin_engram_engram` returns "No matching deferred tools found".

For comparison, logs from other projects on the same machine, from before ~2026-07-03, show the server connecting once and staying alive for the full session (hours, dozens of successful `mem_save`/`mem_search`/`mem_update` calls), with `SIGINT` only appearing once at genuine session end — no "Cleared connection cache for reconnection" line at all in those healthy logs. That line only appears in the broken pattern.

### 🖥️ Environment

**Gentle AI Version:** v2.8.1 (`gga version`)

**Operating System:** Linux (Arch/Manjaro) — specifically CachyOS

**AI Agent / Client:** Claude Code (CLI v2.1.201, up to date)

**📋 Affected Area:** Other (MCP plugin lifecycle / Engram integration)

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

```
{"debug":"Starting connection with timeout of 30000ms","timestamp":"2026-07-05T10:02:44.340Z","sessionId":"4f3f9430-...","cwd":"/home/ginopc/Desarrollo/Billetera"}
{"debug":"Successfully connected (transport: stdio) in 191ms","timestamp":"2026-07-05T10:02:44.528Z", ...}
{"debug":"Server instructions truncated from 2539 to 2048 chars","timestamp":"2026-07-05T10:02:44.529Z", ...}
{"debug":"Connection established with capabilities: {\"hasTools\":true,\"hasPrompts\":false,\"hasResources\":false,\"hasResourceSubscribe\":false,\"serverVersion\":{\"name\":\"engram\",\"version\":\"0.1.0\"}}","timestamp":"2026-07-05T10:02:44.529Z", ...}
{"debug":"Sending SIGINT to MCP server process","timestamp":"2026-07-05T10:02:48.884Z", ...}
{"debug":"UNKNOWN connection closed after 4s (cleanly)","timestamp":"2026-07-05T10:02:48.890Z", ...}
{"debug":"Cleared connection cache for reconnection","timestamp":"2026-07-05T10:02:48.896Z", ...}
{"debug":"MCP server process exited cleanly","timestamp":"2026-07-05T10:02:48.938Z", ...}
```

Manual verification that the binary itself is healthy (run outside Claude Code):
```
$ printf '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize",...}\n{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}\n' | engram mcp --tools=agent
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{...,"serverInfo":{"name":"engram","version":"0.1.0"},...}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"tools":[... 18 valid tool definitions ...]}}
```

### Additional Context

- `claude mcp list` shows `plugin:engram:engram - ✔ Connected` right after this broken cycle (misleading — it reflects the transport handshake, not tool availability), and later the `/mcp` panel shows `plugin:engram:engram ✗ failed`.
- Ruled out as causes: outdated Claude Code CLI (already on latest 2.1.201), duplicate MCP registration (no `engram` entry exists in the project's `.mcp.json`, in `~/.claude.json` `mcpServers`, or in `~/.claude/settings.json` `mcpServers` — it's only registered via the plugin's own `.mcp.json` with `enabledPlugins["engram@engram"] = true`), and a corrupt/misbehaving binary (manual JSON-RPC test above proves it responds correctly).
- Reproduces across at least 2 different project directories on the same machine, so it is not specific to one project's `CLAUDE.md`/settings.
- Related but distinct existing issues I found while searching before filing this: #797 (double MCP registration, but explicitly scoped to the Antigravity/Gemini CLI integration, not Claude Code) and #727 (brew upgrade missing `--cask` flag — different symptom, upgrade path, not connection lifecycle).
- Happy to provide the full `mcp-logs-plugin-engram-engram/*.jsonl` files or test further changes if it helps narrow this down.

title: feat(cli): add managed-block footprint diagnostic to gentle-ai doctor
body:
## Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

## 🔍 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

## 💡 Problem Statement

`gentle-ai doctor` currently checks only binary/environment health: tool binaries resolvable on PATH (+ duplicate-copy detection), `~/.gentle-ai/state.json` validity, Engram HTTP health, and free disk space. It has no visibility into the size/token footprint of the managed `gentle-ai:*` blocks (persona, engram-protocol, sdd-orchestrator, strict-tdd-mode, codegraph-guidance, etc.) that `install`/`sync` inject into each agent's instruction file (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, etc.).

This makes footprint-reduction work (see #801, #259) hard to measure objectively. Confirming and sizing the engram-protocol duplication discussed in #259 required manually running `wc -c` across multiple files and manually cross-referencing plugin hook scripts and MCP server instructions by hand — there's no built-in way to answer "how many tokens is gentle-ai injecting into my agent right now, broken down by block?"

## 📦 Proposed Solution

Add a "Managed block footprint" check to `gentle-ai doctor` (or a `gentle-ai doctor --footprint` flag) that, per configured agent:
- Parses each `<!-- gentle-ai:X -->...<!-- /gentle-ai:X -->` tagged block in the agent's instruction file(s)
- Reports character count, line count, and a rough token estimate per block
- Optionally sums a total "static floor" per agent

This gives maintainers and contributors an objective before/after metric for footprint-reduction issues like #801 and #259, replacing manual archaeology with a read-only diagnostic that fits doctor's existing "health check" mandate (per the README: "read-only health check of your ecosystem").

## 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- **Manual measurement (status quo)**: error-prone, not repeatable, not discoverable by other contributors.
- **A standalone script**: less discoverable than `doctor`, which is already the documented entry point for ecosystem diagnostics.

## 📎 Additional Context

Directly supports the ongoing discussion in #259 and #801 about which managed blocks to trim/lazy-load — this issue is about measurement tooling, not about deciding what to cut, so it shouldn't conflict with either.

title: feat(community-tool): add version-aware upgrade/reconcile for CodeGraph
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate of #586 or #846
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

Installation Pipeline

### 💡 Problem Statement

Gentle AI installs CodeGraph via `npm install -g @colbymchenry/codegraph@latest` during the first install/sync. The `@latest` tag is only evaluated on the initial installation; once CodeGraph is present and reconciled, subsequent `gentle-ai install` / `gentle-ai sync` runs skip the community-tool step entirely.

This means users stay on whatever version was current at first install, even when newer releases fix bugs or add features. For example, `@colbymchenry/codegraph@latest` is now `1.1.2`, but a user who installed when `1.1.1` was current will not be upgraded by Gentle AI unless they manually run `npm install -g @colbymchenry/codegraph@latest`.

There is currently no `--force` or dedicated upgrade path for community tools in the CLI/TUI.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Add a version-aware upgrade/reconcile mechanism for community tools:

1. **Detect installed vs. latest version**
   - Read the installed CodeGraph version (`codegraph --version` or `npm list -g @colbymchenry/codegraph --json`).
   - Compare against the desired target version (`latest` from npm, or a pinned version in Gentle AI).

2. **Re-run install when outdated**
   - During `gentle-ai install` / `gentle-ai sync`, if the installed version is older than the target, re-execute `npm install -g @colbymchenry/codegraph@<target>` before reconciling agent wiring.

3. **Add `--force-community-tools` flag (or similar)**
   - Allow users to force a fresh install/reconcile of community tools without uninstalling everything.

4. **Surface available updates in the TUI**
   - In `Upgrade tools ★` or `Community Tools/Plugins`, show when a community tool has an update available and offer to apply it.

Example usage:

```bash
gentle-ai sync --agent opencode
# Detects CodeGraph 1.1.1 vs latest 1.1.2 and upgrades automatically
```

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- **Manual upgrade**: Users run `npm install -g @colbymchenry/codegraph@latest` themselves. This works but bypasses Gentle AI's managed-install UX and leaves agent wiring potentially out of sync.
- **Pin version and use `npx` in MCP config**: As suggested in #846, pin a specific version and invoke CodeGraph via `npx -y --package=@colbymchenry/codegraph@<VERSION> codegraph serve --mcp`. This guarantees the agent always uses the pinned version, but still requires Gentle AI to bump the pinned version and refresh configs on sync.
- **Leave it opt-in**: Do nothing and document that users must upgrade CodeGraph manually. This contradicts Gentle AI's goal of managing the agent ecosystem consistently.

### 📎 Additional Context

**Environment:**
- **Gentle AI version:** 1.43.2
- **CodeGraph version installed by Gentle AI:** 1.1.1
- **Latest CodeGraph version available on npm:** 1.1.2

**Current behavior observed:**

```bash
# Gentle AI installed CodeGraph via the TUI/CLI
codegraph --version
# 1.1.1

# npm already has 1.1.2
npm view @colbymchenry/codegraph dist-tags --json
# { "latest": "1.1.2" }

# Running gentle-ai sync --agent opencode does not upgrade CodeGraph
```

**Relevant source:**
- `internal/components/communitytool/tool.go` defines `CodeGraphCommands()` and `CodeGraphReconcileSatisfied()`.
- `internal/cli/run.go` calls `communitytool.Install()` during install/sync.
- Once reconciled, the install step is skipped, so `@latest` is never re-evaluated.

**Related issues:**
- #586 — optional CodeGraph helper
- #846 — mandatory CodeGraph ecosystem component

title: feat(agents): add native Crush adapter support
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

Agent Detection

### 💡 Problem Statement

Gentle AI currently supports 16 AI coding agents, but **Crush** is not among them. Users of the Crush CLI agent cannot benefit from the ecosystem configuration Gentle AI provides: persistent memory (Engram), Spec-Driven Development workflows, curated skills, MCP servers, persona injection, and per-phase model assignment.

There is no mention of Crush anywhere in the repository (no adapter, no catalog entry, no assets). Every other comparable CLI agent (Codex, Hermes, Pi) has an adapter, so the absence of Crush is a gap in agent coverage.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Add Crush as a supported agent following the established adapter pattern documented in `docs/codebase/repository-map.md` and exemplified by `internal/agents/hermes/adapter.go` (the most recent solo-agent adapter).

### Implementation plan

1. **Agent ID** — add `AgentCrush AgentID = "crush"` to `internal/model/types.go`
2. **Catalog entry** — add Crush to `allAgents` in `internal/catalog/agents.go` with `ConfigPath: "~/.crush"` (or the config root Crush actually uses — needs confirmation from maintainers)
3. **Adapter** — implement `agents.Adapter` in `internal/agents/crush/adapter.go`:
   - Detection via `crush` binary on `PATH` + config dir existence
   - Config paths (`GlobalConfigDir`, `SystemPromptFile`, `SkillsDir`, `SettingsPath`)
   - Strategies (`SystemPromptStrategy`, `MCPStrategy`) matching how Crush reads its config
   - Capability flags (`SupportsSkills`, `SupportsMCP`, `SupportsSubAgents`, etc.)
4. **Factory registration** — wire `case model.AgentCrush` in `internal/agents/factory.go` `NewAdapter()` and add to `defaultAgentIDs`
5. **Auto-install** (if applicable) — add a case in `internal/installcmd/resolver.go` `ResolveAgentInstall`, or return `AgentNotInstallableError` if Crush is manual-install only
6. **Embedded assets** — create `internal/assets/crush/sdd-orchestrator.md` (and persona files if applicable)
7. **Tests** — table-driven adapter tests with swappable `lookPath`/`statPath` (pattern from `internal/agents/claude/adapter_test.go`); golden files in `testdata/golden/` regenerated with `go test -update`
8. **Docs** — update `docs/agents.md` (agent matrix), `README.md` (supported agents table), and `docs/codebase/integrations.md` if needed

### Open questions for maintainers

- What is Crush's config root path? (`~/.crush` is the assumption — needs confirmation)
- Does Crush support MCP servers natively, and in what format (JSON, YAML, TOML)?
- Does Crush support native sub-agents/delegation, or is it a solo-agent?
- Is there an auto-install path (npm/brew/go install), or is it manual-install only?
- What is the system prompt file convention? (e.g. `AGENTS.md`, `CRUSH.md`, `CLAUDE.md`-style markdown sections)


### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- **Generic/manual configuration**: Users could manually copy skills and prompts into Crush's config dir. Rejected — this defeats the purpose of Gentle AI's idempotent sync, backup/rollback, and managed-asset injection.
- **Detect-only support (like Hermes initially)**: Add a minimal adapter that detects Crush but requires manual setup. This could be a pragmatic first step if some capabilities are still unknown, matching how Hermes was introduced before full support.

### 📎 Additional Context

- The adapter pattern is well-documented in `internal/agents/interface.go:17-19`: "Components use adapter methods instead of switch statements on AgentID, making it trivial to add new agents without modifying component code."
- The golden placement rule (`docs/codebase/repository-map.md`) puts per-agent code in `internal/agents/<agent>/` and shared behavior in `internal/components/`.
- All invariants apply: backups before mutation, sync idempotency, adapters own paths.
- Reference adapters by complexity: `internal/agents/hermes/adapter.go` (minimal solo-agent, no auto-install), `internal/agents/codex/adapter.go` (TOML config), `internal/agents/claude/adapter.go` (full capabilities).

## Summary

MiniMax Code (https://agent.minimax.io) is a desktop AI coding agent built on OpenCode. It shares the same config structure as OpenCode but runs as a native Electron application. Adding support for MiniMax Code would bring the Gentle-AI ecosystem to MiniMax's growing user base.

## Motivation

MiniMax Code is an OpenCode variant with:

- **Same config structure as OpenCode**: `~/.minimax/` follows the OpenCode directory layout
- **Multi-agent delegation**: 4 built-in agents (coder, general, mavis, verifier)
- **Full MCP support**: cu, engram, matrix, playwright, trash servers active
- **Native model integration**: Built-in MiniMax models (M2.7, M2.7-highspeed, M3) with reasoning
- **Electron desktop app**: Alternative to CLI-based agents

## Discovery Details

Config root: `~/.minimax/`

```
~/.minimax/
├── agents/          # coder, general, mavis, verifier (built-in agents)
├── harnesses/       # SDD harness support
├── mcp/             # MCP config (manifest.json + mcp.json)
├── skills/          # Generated from MCP tools
├── .builtin-skills/ # Built-in skills (mcp-cli, pdf, xlsx, etc.)
├── config.yaml      # Model provider config (@ai-sdk/minimax)
└── .electron-installed
```

**Agent capabilities:**
- Skills: Yes (MCP-generated)
- MCP: Yes
- Delegation: Full (multi-agent with sub-agents)
- Slash Commands: Yes
- Config Path: `~/.minimax/`

## Scope

The implementation would follow the existing agent adapter pattern:

1. **Detection**: Check for `~/.minimax/` directory and `MiniMax Code` binary
2. **Agent adapter**: New `internal/agents/minimax/` package following OpenCode patterns
3. **Catalog entry**: Add to `internal/catalog/agents.go`
4. **Model integration**: Leverage existing MiniMax model support
5. **Documentation**: Update `docs/agents.md`

- Brings Gentle-AI ecosystem to MiniMax Code users
- Shares infrastructure with OpenCode (similar adapter patterns)

- Same `agents/` structure with built-in agent stubs

title: feat(engram): add cloud-aware data-directory migration contract
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs require an issue with status:approved

### Affected Area

TUI (terminal UI), Installation Pipeline, Documentation

### Problem Statement

#346 was completed by the initial Engram data-directory storage/disk-space infrastructure, but the remaining migration behavior still needs an approved contract before implementation continues.

The missing behavior is the safe setup/TUI contract for changing Engram's active data directory when existing data is present.

This matters because Engram's runtime treats the data directory as more than only SQLite files:

- ENGRAM_DATA_DIR controls the active data directory.
- SQLite artifacts live there: ^[ngram.db, ^[ngram.db-wal, ^[ngram.db-shm.
- Engram cloud config is stored under the active data dir as cloud.json.
- Autosync can be enabled through ENGRAM_CLOUD_AUTOSYNC=1 plus cloud token/server configuration.

A Gentle-AI migration flow must not silently drop cloud state, silently copy credential-bearing cloud config, or partially update MCP config/state if migration fails.

![Cloud-aware Engram data-dir migration contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tonyblu331/gentle-ai/adr/engram-data-dir-migration-contract/docs/adr/assets/engram-data-dir-migration-contract-v2.png)

### Proposed Contract

Gentle-AI should own:

- setup/TUI UX for choosing the data directory
- ENGRAM_DATA_DIR propagation into existing Engram MCP configs
- destination validation
- backup orchestration
- filesystem operation orchestration
- rollback of Gentle-AI-managed state and MCP config

Engram should continue to own:

- SQLite runtime semantics
- cloud.json meaning
- cloud enrollment
- autosync behavior
- any future real lock/quiesce/migrate API

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Preflight detects DB artifacts, cloud.json, and cloud/autosync env.
- [ ] User must choose preserve cloud config, local-data-only, or cancel when cloud state is detected.
- [ ] Destination validation rejects same, nested, non-empty, and insufficient-space destinations.
- [ ] Copy/move/delete/start-fresh snapshot before mutation.
- [ ] Copy/move checks source stability and fails if Engram data changes during copy.
- [ ] MCP config updates preserve existing Engram command paths and unrelated env keys.
- [ ] ENGRAM_DATA_DIR is added/removed only in existing Engram MCP configs.
- [ ] State write and MCP config update failures roll back together where possible.
- [ ] TUI review screen displays source, destination, backup scope, cloud status, selected cloud handling, and stop-Engram requirement.
- [ ] Docs keep the boundary clear: Gentle-AI configures setup; Engram owns runtime/cloud semantics.

### Out of Scope

- Implementing Engram cloud sync inside Gentle-AI
- Changing the MCP protocol
- Running ^[ngram sync --cloud or cloud enrollment from Gentle-AI
- Merging into non-empty destination directories
- Claiming a real lock before Engram exposes one

### Design Notes

Detailed ADR and PR-chain plan are preserved on the personal tracking branch: https://github.com/tonyblu331/gentle-ai/tree/adr/engram-data-dir-migration-contract

Companion issues:

- TUI/setup-flow proposal: #922
- PR-chain implementation plan: #923

title: feat: decouple persona (style) from language/region in install and sync
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

`TUI (terminal UI)` — single-select; the change also touches CLI and the installation pipeline / también afecta CLI y el pipeline de instalación.

### 💡 Problem Statement

**🇬🇧 English**

Today the persona is a **single coupled axis**: the options `gentleman`, `gentleman-neutral-artifacts`, `neutral` and `custom` mix TWO distinct decisions into one — **WHO** the assistant is (personality/style) and **HOW** it speaks (language/region). This causes:

- You can't use the "Gentleman" style (teach before solving) while speaking another regional Spanish or another language: the Rioplatense voice is glued to the style.
- The `gentleman-neutral-artifacts` variant exists only to force English artifacts, inflating the option set with what is really just a toggle.
- Language/region isn't persisted as its own data, so it can't be versioned or re-synced independently from the style.

**🇪🇸 Español**

Hoy la persona es un **único eje acoplado**: las opciones `gentleman`, `gentleman-neutral-artifacts`, `neutral` y `custom` mezclan DOS decisiones distintas en una sola — **QUIÉN** es el asistente (personalidad/estilo) y **CÓMO** habla (idioma/región). Esto genera:

- No se puede usar el estilo "Gentleman" (enseñar antes de resolver) hablando en otro español regional o en otro idioma: la voz rioplatense viene pegada al estilo.
- La variante `gentleman-neutral-artifacts` existe solo para forzar artefactos en inglés, inflando el set de opciones con algo que en realidad es un simple toggle.
- El idioma/región no se persiste como dato propio, así que no puede versionarse ni re-sincronizarse de forma independiente del estilo.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

**🇬🇧 English**

Split the persona into **TWO independent axes** that converge at a single Go composition point:

1. **Style:** `gentle | neutral | custom`
2. **Language/Region:** 5 curated regions (Argentine Rioplatense/voseo, Mexican, Colombian, Spain Spanish, Chilean) + "User's language" + free-text "Other…"
3. **"Artifacts in English" checkbox** (default ON, opt-out)

Behavior:
- Regional voice is injected as **ONE composed directive** at build time from a Go region map (no per-region files).
- `custom` injects nothing and skips the language screen.
- **Back-compat migration:** `gentleman` and `gentleman-neutral-artifacts` → `gentle` + region `argentina` + `artifactsInEnglish: true` (the hybrid is proven to be a no-op).
- `region` and `artifactsInEnglish` are persisted in `state.json`; a second sync reads the migrated fields directly, without re-migrating, and produces byte-identical output.

TUI flow: persona (style) screen → language/region screen (for gentle/neutral) → review shows region + flag.

**🇪🇸 Español**

Separar la persona en **DOS ejes independientes** que convergen en un único punto de composición en Go:

1. **Estilo:** `gentle | neutral | custom`
2. **Idioma/Región:** 5 regiones curadas (Argentino rioplatense/voseo, Mexicano, Colombiano, Español de España, Chileno) + "Idioma del usuario" + texto libre "Otro…"
3. **Checkbox "Artefactos en inglés"** (default ON, opt-out)

Comportamiento:
- La voz regional se inyecta como **UNA sola directiva compuesta** en build-time desde un mapa de regiones en Go (sin archivos por región).
- `custom` no inyecta nada y saltea la pantalla de idioma.
- **Migración back-compat:** `gentleman` y `gentleman-neutral-artifacts` → `gentle` + región `argentina` + `artifactsInEnglish: true` (la híbrida queda probada como no-op).
- `region` y `artifactsInEnglish` se persisten en `state.json`; un segundo sync lee los campos migrados directo, sin re-migrar, y produce salida byte-idéntica.

Flujo TUI: pantalla de persona (estilo) → pantalla de idioma/región (para gentle/neutral) → review muestra región + flag.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

**🇬🇧 English**

- **Keep the single coupled axis and add combined variants** (`gentleman-es-mx`, `gentleman-en`, …): explodes combinatorially, doesn't scale.
- **Per-region asset files:** rejected; multiplies files. A composed Go directive is preferred.

**🇪🇸 Español**

- **Mantener el eje único y sumar variantes combinadas** (`gentleman-es-mx`, `gentleman-en`, …): explota combinatoriamente, no escala.
- **Archivos de asset por región:** descartado; multiplica archivos. Se prefiere la directiva compuesta en Go.

### 📎 Additional Context

**🇬🇧 English**

- Full design and deltas in SDD: `openspec/changes/decouple-persona-language/` (proposal, spec, design, tasks).
- Motor-first slice already implemented locally as stacked commits on `feat/decouple-persona-language` (WU-1..11), pending this issue before opening PRs.
- Deferred adapters (OpenCode/Kilocode, Kimi, Kiro, Hermes) and TUI e2e are left for follow-up PRs.

**🇪🇸 Español**

- Diseño completo y deltas en SDD: `openspec/changes/decouple-persona-language/` (proposal, spec, design, tasks).
- Slice motor-first ya implementado localmente como commits stacked en `feat/decouple-persona-language` (WU-1..11), pendiente de este issue para abrir PRs.
- Adapters diferidos (OpenCode/Kilocode, Kimi, Kiro, Hermes) y e2e TUI quedan para PRs siguientes.

title: feat(tui): add StrictWorkflow mode — sequential PR gate and atomic commit enforcement
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area

Other

### 💡 Problem Statement

Teams using gentle-ai on multi-developer projects frequently hit merge conflicts and review fatigue from two root causes:

1. **Parallel branch sprawl** — developers start new branches before previous ones are reviewed and merged, producing overlapping diffs and compounding conflicts in later PRs.
2. **Non-atomic commits** — commits bundle unrelated changes (model + service + test as separate commits), making individual commits non-revertable and reviews harder to scope.

The `work-unit-commits` and `branch-pr` skills document the right approach, but there is no installation-time opt-in that makes these constraints active and enforceable at the skill layer for every task in a project.

### 📦 Proposed Solution

Add a **StrictWorkflow** opt-in mode that follows the same pattern as the existing `StrictTDD` mode:

**TUI addition** — a new screen after `ScreenStrictTDD` in the installation flow:

```
STRICT WORKFLOW MODE

Should agents enforce sequential PR gates and atomic commits?
When enabled:
  • New branches require all previous task PRs to be merged first.
  • Commits must be atomic work units (code + tests + docs together).
  • All SDD phases are mandatory — no skipping.

  ○ Enable
  ● Disable   ← default
```

**New embedded skill** — `skills/sequential-branches/SKILL.md` that activates when `strict_workflow: true` is set in `openspec/config.yaml`. The skill gates branch creation on zero open PRs from the current feature set, enforces the work-unit commit contract, and blocks phase-skipping by requiring explicit sign-off between SDD phases.

**`Selection` model change** — `StrictWorkflow bool` field, mirroring `StrictTDD bool`.

**`openspec/config.yaml` injection** — when enabled, writes `strict_workflow: true` so every SDD phase downstream reads the constraint automatically.

### Why this belongs in the installer (not just docs)

`work-unit-commits` and `branch-pr` already document these rules. The gap is activation: teams need a one-time opt-in at project setup that writes the constraint into `openspec/config.yaml` and injects the enforcement skill — so the agent checks the gate on every task, not only when a developer remembers to apply the skill manually.

Making it opt-in (default: Disable) means zero impact on existing users or solo workflows.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Manual `openspec/config.yaml` editing per project** — works but requires each team member to know the config schema. No guarantee of consistency across the team.
- **Extending `branch-pr` skill directly** — the gate logic is conditional on a project-level flag, so it belongs in a separate skill activated by that flag rather than hardcoded into `branch-pr` for all users.

### Additional Context

Implementation follows the `StrictTDD` pattern exactly:

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `internal/model/selection.go` | Add `StrictWorkflow bool` |
| `internal/model/types.go` | Add `SkillSequentialBranches SkillID` + screen constant |
| `internal/catalog/skills.go` | Register new skill |
| `internal/tui/screens/strict_workflow.go` | New render function + test |
| `internal/tui/router.go` | Route: `ScreenStrictTDD → ScreenStrictWorkflow → ScreenDependencyTree` |
| `internal/components/sdd/inject.go` | Inject skill + write flag when enabled |
| `skills/sequential-branches/SKILL.md` | New skill file |

Estimated diff: ~270 lines — fits within the 400-line review budget in a single PR.

title: feat(tui): add compact OpenAI quota indicator
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist
- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### 🔍 Affected Area
TUI (terminal UI)

### 💡 Problem Statement
Gentle AI/OpenCode users authenticated with OpenAI currently have no compact in-terminal visibility into their ChatGPT/Codex plan quota while working.

This matters because OpenAI usage is managed through rolling quota windows such as the short 5-hour window and the weekly window. When users are working inside OpenCode, they can only see that information by leaving the terminal and checking the ChatGPT/Codex UI manually.

The result is a small but repeated workflow break:

- the user is actively coding in OpenCode
- the current model is visible in the sidebar/prompt
- subagent/context/MCP status is visible
- but remaining OpenAI quota and reset timing are not visible

This is especially useful for users running GPT-5.x/Codex models from a ChatGPT Plus/Pro account, where the quota is account-wide and may be consumed from multiple surfaces, not only OpenCode.

### 📦 Proposed Solution
Add a compact native OpenAI quota indicator to the Gentle AI/OpenCode TUI sidebar when OpenAI OAuth is available.

Suggested UX:

```text
OpenAI quota
5h     68% reset 3h55m
Week   30% reset 5d
```

Behavior:

- Reuse OpenCode's existing OpenAI OAuth session.
- Do not require Codex CLI.
- Do not require a new API key.
- Do not require extra user configuration.
- Hide the quota block completely when OpenAI auth is unavailable.
- Show only sanitized values: quota percentage remaining and reset time.
- Refresh periodically, e.g. every 60 seconds.
- Avoid overlapping refresh requests.
- Fail closed with actionable messages if the quota contract changes:
  - `OpenAI auth expired`
  - `quota endpoint changed`
  - `quota format changed`
  - `quota check rate-limited`
  - `OpenAI quota API down`
  - `quota timeout`

Implementation shape proven in a local MVP:

1. Read OpenCode's native OpenAI OAuth entry from `auth.json`.
2. Accept only OpenAI-looking OAuth tokens, validated by OpenAI JWT namespaces such as:
   - `https://api.openai.com/auth`
   - `https://api.openai.com/profile`
3. Call the ChatGPT quota endpoint:
   - `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage`
4. Parse only explicit known fields:
   - `rate_limit.primary_window` → short window, displayed as `5h`
   - `rate_limit.secondary_window` → weekly window, displayed as `Week`
   - `code_review_rate_limit.primary_window` → optional `Review` row
5. If `primary_window` is absent, display `quota format changed` instead of guessing from unrelated fields.

The MVP was validated locally against OpenCode `1.17.4` and matched the quota shown in the Codex/ChatGPT UI.

Recommended placement:

- Prefer integrating this into the existing OpenAI/GPT-5.x model/provider/TUI status support if Gentle AI already has a provider-specific UI layer.
- If that coupling is not desired, the same behavior can live as a small dedicated TUI sidebar plugin.

I would recommend the integrated native approach first because the feature is only valuable when OpenAI is already configured, and it should feel zero-config rather than another optional plugin users need to discover.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered
1. Install a third-party quota plugin such as `@slkiser/opencode-quota`.
   - Pros: already supports multiple providers and rich displays.
   - Cons: larger dependency surface, broader scope, more behavior than the MVP needs.

2. Create a separate Gentle AI quota plugin.
   - Pros: clean isolation and easier iteration.
   - Cons: users may need to discover/install/configure it separately unless bundled.

3. Keep quota visibility outside OpenCode and rely on the ChatGPT/Codex UI.
   - Pros: no implementation required.
   - Cons: breaks terminal workflow and hides quota context exactly when users need it.

The proposed native MVP is intentionally OpenAI-only. Other providers can be added later through the same adapter pattern, but they should not be part of the first slice.

### 📎 Additional Context
Local MVP properties:

- No external npm dependencies.
- No token logging.
- No token rendering.
- No token persistence.
- Hidden when OpenAI auth is missing.
- Uses compact color thresholds:
  - green: quota remaining >= 50%
  - yellow: quota remaining >= 20%
  - red: quota remaining < 20%
- Refreshes immediately on mount and then every 60 seconds.
- Uses an 8-second timeout.

Security/reliability notes from an adversarial review:

- Token source must be narrowed to OpenAI-related auth entries only.
- Do not send generic OAuth tokens to ChatGPT.
- Validate OpenAI JWT namespaces before using an access token.
- Do not recursively guess quota fields from the whole response body.
- Parse explicit quota fields and fail closed if the format changes.
- A native implementation should include deterministic tests for:
  - missing auth hides the block
  - expired auth shows a compact auth message
  - timeout handling
  - endpoint changed handling
  - response format changed handling
  - parser behavior for primary/secondary/review windows

This is a small quality-of-life feature, but it makes the OpenAI/GPT-5.x experience feel more complete and transparent inside Gentle AI.

title: feat(skills): code-comment discipline — orchestrator templates and commit/PR skills never enforce minimal comments
body:
### Pre-flight Checks
- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand this issue needs status:approved before a PR can be opened

### Problem Description
LLMs have a strong training prior toward over-commented code (tutorial-style narration: `// increment the counter`, `// now we handle X`). A user-level rule like "keep comments minimal" in CLAUDE.md reduces this but cannot eliminate it, because:

1. A prompt rule is **probabilistic** — it competes against the prior on every generated token, and in long diffs some narration comments slip through.
2. **Sub-agents are the worst offenders**: their fresh context is dominated by the task prompt the orchestrator writes, so the user's global comment rule gets diluted. Gentle AI's own Sub-Agent Launch Pattern tells the orchestrator to pass skill paths and model aliases — but says nothing about comment discipline, so every delegated writer reverts to the prior.

Today gentle-ai has **no comment-discipline rule anywhere**:
- `internal/assets/*/sdd-orchestrator.md` (all 12 agent variants) — Delegation Rules / Sub-Agent Launch Pattern never mention comments.
- `skills/work-unit-commits/SKILL.md` — has commit-hygiene checklist and pre-commit diff review commands, but no comment scan.
- `skills/branch-pr/SKILL.md` — pre-PR checklist covers Conventional Commits and no Co-Authored-By trailers, but not comment bloat.

The result: users who adopt gentle-ai's orchestration get PRs padded with narration comments, and review budgets (the 400-line rule this repo itself enforces) get wasted on noise.

### Proposed Solution
Bake the discipline into the three layers where code gets written or shipped:

1. **Orchestrator templates** (`internal/assets/<agent>/sdd-orchestrator.md`, all variants): add a rule to the Sub-Agent Launch Pattern — every delegated prompt that writes code MUST include an explicit instruction: default is NO new code comments; only keep a comment that states a non-obvious WHY (hidden constraint, subtle invariant, bug workaround). Comments narrating WHAT the code does, the task, or the PR context are forbidden.

2. **`work-unit-commits` skill** (source + embedded twin): add a checklist item + a concrete pre-commit scan:
   `git diff --cached | grep -E '^\+\s*(//|#|/\*)'`
   Any hit must be justified as a non-obvious WHY or deleted before committing.

3. **`branch-pr` skill** (source + embedded twin): add a pre-PR checklist item — the full branch diff has been scanned for added comments and none narrate the obvious.

Rationale for the design: prompt rules lower the probability of comment bloat, a diff scan at the commit/PR chokepoint catches the rest deterministically. Both layers are needed.

### Affected Area
Skills

### Alternatives Considered
- Relying on each user's CLAUDE.md comment rule — already proven insufficient, especially for sub-agents (fresh context).
- Shipping a PreToolUse hook that blocks `git commit` when the diff adds comment lines (deterministic enforcement, model reviews flagged lines and re-commits with a bypass marker). I have this working locally and it composes well with the doc changes — could be a follow-up issue if there is interest, since it touches Go install/uninstall code rather than markdown assets.

### Additional Context
I can submit the PR for the three doc layers once approved (estimated ~160 added lines across 12 orchestrator variants + 4 skill files, within the 400-line budget).
