- Implemented and verified on branch `feat/cloud-project-api` (36 files including Go handlers, store transactions, unit/integration tests, Docker Compose, docs, and Bruno specs).
- Complete test coverage in `internal/cloud/cloudserver/admin_handlers_test.go` (`TestAdminCreateProject*`) and `internal/cloud/cloudstore/identity_storage_test.go` (`TestCreateProjectWithGrantAndAuditLifecycle`).

title: question(policy): define HTTP caller authority and MCP administrative-delete policy
body:
### Question

What should establish caller authority for observation mutations across local HTTP and native MCP, independently of a caller-supplied owner assertion?

Please define the supported trust model for each transport, the source of any project-level grants, and whether administrative `mem_delete` may intentionally target an explicitly asserted owner independently of cwd/process context. This is a policy decision request, not a proposal to treat `expected_project` or a detected cwd as an authenticated tenant identity.

### Why does this need issue tracking?

Review of #1575 raised two related authority/policy questions. Comparing baseline `58d7029d1b1a50716c397ed49a377444c1f68add` with reviewed head `4467678a0d94b6080f68c9f8dc113c58f3238ca4` confirms both boundaries predate that PR:

- Local HTTP has an optional instance-wide bearer token and a loopback/Unix-socket listener, not authenticated project grants. PATCH is unwrapped by the token check; DELETE uses it. Loopback does not imply isolation from every local client.
- MCP update already checks current/process project and session directory, while ID-based administrative deletion does not perform the same contextual checks. Those process-context checks are not authenticated tenant principals.

A durable maintainer decision is needed before adding authorization machinery or changing administrative deletion semantics. The decision should specify supported callers/exposure, authority provenance and error precedence per transport, intentional cross-project maintenance behavior, compatibility/migration requirements, and named regression tests. Prefer one coherent authority policy with explicit transport boundaries, not parallel representations of ownership.

No authority model, implementation or approval is selected by opening this issue. The ownership-consistency guard in #1575 remains separate from tenant isolation.

### Affected Area

Project workflow or policy

### Additional Context

- Origin: #1569 and #1575. `expected_project` is an explicit intended-owner consistency assertion, not authentication or tenant isolation.
- HTTP review: https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1575#discussion_r4141210797
- Outside-diff MCP review: https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/pull/1575#pullrequestreview-5361982429
- Baseline HTTP route policy: https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/blob/58d7029d1b1a50716c397ed49a377444c1f68add/internal/server/server.go#L438-L439
- Baseline MCP administrative deletion: https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/blob/58d7029d1b1a50716c397ed49a377444c1f68add/internal/mcp/mcp.go#L1852-L1869
- Specific baseline delete contract: https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/blob/58d7029d1b1a50716c397ed49a377444c1f68add/DOCS.md#L1074-L1083
- Related but distinct work: #200 (global HTTP token), #1111 (project-merge HTTP authentication parity), #1348 (agent/admin tool profiles), #1347 (MCP/Pi contract parity), #1532 (remote MCP transport).

Existing focused store/server owner-assertion tests and MCP update-context tests pass. They do not prove malicious-client isolation or a delete-context denial policy. No source changes, new security fixtures or exploit reproduction are included in this tracking request.

title: perf(mcp): mem_save latency grows with database size (FindCandidates scans the whole FTS index by title words)
body:
### 📋 Pre-flight Checks

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/issues) and this is not a duplicate. The closest one is #881, which measures the `mem_judge` step *after* `mem_save`; this one is about `mem_save` itself.
- [x] I understand this issue needs `status:approved` before a PR can be opened

### 📝 Bug Description

`mem_save` latency grew from ~0.2 s (May) to ~10 s median (September) on a database of ~14,700 observations. On Sep 26 there were 15 calls over 60 s, the worst 903 s. `mem_session_summary` never went over 5 s. The observation is stored anyway: the slow part comes after the write.

What we measured (client-side timing, 885 calls since Sep 20, Claude Code and Codex):

- It does not depend on content length. With no other MCP calls in flight the median is still 8.5 s.
- It depends on **title length**: 0–3 words 2.5 s, 4–6 words 5.4 s, 7–9 words 7.6 s, 10–13 words 8.6 s (p90 110 s).
- The WAL is small (229 pending frames), so it does not look like that.
- On a copy of the database, an FTS5 `optimize` brought a search from 589 ms to 339 ms. It helps but does not explain ~10 s.

Likely cause, from reading the v2.2.1 source (not profiled): `handleSave` (`mcp.go:1587`) calls `FindCandidates` (`relations.go:358`), which builds an OR query from the title words and runs it against the whole FTS index (trigram since Sep 2). That cost grows with the database. `mem_session_summary` skips it since Sep 5, which matches it not being affected. It gets worse with one connection per process (a long search queues every other call), a 5 s `busy_timeout` with retries, and no WAL checkpoint.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a database with ~10k+ observations, engram 2.2.1, Windows.
2. Call `mem_save` through MCP with a 10+ word title and time it.
3. Repeat with a 2–3 word title, and with `mem_session_summary` on the same database.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

`mem_save` latency should not grow with database size or title length: the candidate search bounded (per project, by date, or an early LIMIT), limited to the rarest title words, or moved off the critical path (after the response).

### ❌ Actual Behavior

~10 s median, 2.5 s for very short titles, a tail up to 903 s, on a database of ~14,700 observations.

### 🖥️ Environment

- OS: Windows
- Engram version: 2.2.1
- Agent / Client: Claude Code (also Codex)

### 💡 Additional Context

Our workaround for now: a guard that refuses titles over 5 words, and a 3-minute MCP tool timeout. A flag or env var to disable the candidate search would also be enough for us. Happy to run a benchmark or test a branch. Related: #881.

title: test(sessions): verify host identity across model changes and lifecycle transitions
body:
### 🔍 Problem Description

#1270 now has real HTTP/SQLite evidence for concurrent host-owned writes on Pi native and Codex, plus a local Claude candidate pending exact-candidate review. Those tests do not run an operator's model switch, compaction, or resume in the host and then prove the *same* two authoritative session owners still receive their own writes. Simulated callbacks and seeded rows must not be described as that proof. Without an explicit runtime journey, a later host update could lose the binding while adapter unit tests stay green.

### 💡 Proposed Solution

Add bounded host/runtime conformance journeys for supported integrations, using isolated configuration and a temporary Engram server/database, without touching the operator's Engram data or agent configuration:

- Register two host sessions with the same project and directory; persist distinguishable writes before and after a real host model change and available compaction/resume event.
- Verify the stored rows preserve each original host ID and never cross-attribute; failed or ended ownership must refuse an attributed write rather than retry without an ID as if it were a manual MCP save.
- Clearly label which steps ran through an actual host/client and which use synthetic callbacks, intercepted HTTP, or a simulated external MCP dispatcher. If an operator event cannot be invoked deterministically offline, document the missing executable test route instead of replacing it with a green imitation.
- Keep tests and code in reviewable ≤400-changed-line work units. Preserve independent direct/manual MCP semantics and existing session rows/leases; no new identity registry.

### 📦 Affected Area

MCP Server (tools, transport)

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

A seeded-session unit test that changes a fake `model` field is useful for adapter regression, but does not prove real operator model-switch continuity. Broadening #1270 indefinitely makes the accepted host-owned binding work impossible to close honestly.

### 📎 Additional Context

Follow-up to #1270's formally narrowed acceptance. OpenCode V2 adapter/runtime support is tracked by #1220; its restart with an ended root is a distinct reproduced bug in #1522, so do not duplicate that fix here. Pi legacy adapter configuration is addressed separately from native Pi host binding (related #1507). Claude's local conformance commit `fab6aa5c` is not yet review-approved or published. Pi 0.1.17 npm publication and the Go installer version pin are separate release decisions.

title: Pi plugin: memory protocol is lost on turns started without before_agent_start (breaks pi-claude-bridge)
body:
### 📝 Bug Description

The Pi plugin injects `MEMORY_INSTRUCTIONS` (and the post-compaction recovery notice) by returning `{ systemPrompt }` from `before_agent_start` (`plugin/pi/index.ts`, still present on `main`, around L1961–1982).

Pi (0.87.1) turns a handler-returned `systemPrompt` into a **run-scoped** `forceSystemPrompt` (`extensions/runner.js`) and clears it when the run ends (`agent-session.js`, `_runSystemPromptOptions = undefined`). A turn started by `pi.sendMessage(..., { triggerTurn: true })` while Pi is idle — for example a background subagent result — runs **without** `before_agent_start`, so that turn's system prompt reaches the provider without the Engram memory protocol.

- With most providers this is **silent**: the model just runs without the memory protocol.
- With `pi-claude-bridge` the turn **fails**, because the bridge recorded the prompt including Engram's text and receives one that is an exact prefix of it.

The missing tail is exactly `"\n\n" + MEMORY_INSTRUCTIONS` (2673 chars), observed on two different prompts.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Pi 0.87.1 with the Engram Pi plugin and `pi-claude-bridge`, using a `claude-bridge/*` model.
2. Launch any subagent in **background** mode (for example gentle-pi's `subagent_run` with `mode: "background"`) and let the parent turn end.
3. When the result is delivered (`sendMessage` with `triggerTurn: true`), the new turn fails.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The memory protocol is present on every turn, including turns started by `triggerTurn` messages. No provider error.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

```
Error: prompt-capture: no capture for this 62770-char system prompt, and it embeds none of the 12 known.
Closest known match diverges at offset 62770 (65443-char key, last recorded at turn_start).
```

65443 − 62770 = 2673 = `"\n\n" + MEMORY_INSTRUCTIONS`.

### Operating System

Linux (Arch/Manjaro)

### Engram Version

2.2.1 (Pi plugin from a source checkout; the same code is on `main`)

### Agent / Client

Other

### 📋 Relevant Logs

_No response_

### 💡 Additional Context

- Client detail: Pi coding agent 0.87.1 + pi-claude-bridge.
- **Proposed fix** (same pattern as gentle-shell#1485 / #1497): append the protocol idempotently to `event.systemPromptOptions.appendSystemPrompt` instead of returning a replacement `systemPrompt`; keep the current return only as a fallback when `systemPromptOptions` is absent (older Pi).
- Verified locally: 4 new tests (RED 3/4 → GREEN 4/4), full plugin suite 131/131, and the real repro (background subagent result arriving while Pi is idle) no longer fails.
- **Related, same symptom from other layers:** Gentleman-Programming/gentle-shell#1528, elidickinson/pi-claude-bridge#144. Neither identifies Engram as the source of the missing tail.

title: feat(mcp): streamable HTTP transport for hosts that cannot install the engram binary
body:
### 🔍 Problem Description

Engram's MCP server only speaks stdio, so every machine that uses it must install the `engram` binary. Some team machines cannot install binaries at all (locked-down corporate laptops, ephemeral dev containers, shared hosts), which leaves those users without Engram memory even though their MCP clients (VS Code, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode) already support remote MCP servers over Streamable HTTP.

This is a different case from #112. That issue was resolved by fixing the binary path for OpenCode headless mode: stdio was still viable because the binary was installed. Here there is no binary on the client host, so stdio cannot work.


### 💡 Proposed Solution

An opt-in Streamable HTTP transport (MCP spec 2025-03-26) that a user can run in a container, on their own machine or on a personal server, and consume with a standard remote-MCP config:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "engram-remote": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "${env:ENGRAM_REMOTE_URL}",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ${env:ENGRAM_REMOTE_TOKEN}",
        "X-Engram-Subproject": "${env:ENGRAM_SUBPROJECT}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```
Scope (personal / single-user deployments, not a multi-tenant hosted MCP):

- `engram mcp --transport=http` serves `/mcp` (Streamable HTTP via mark3labs/mcp-go, already a dependency) and `/health`. stdio stays the default and is unchanged.
- The project comes from the `X-Engram-Subproject` header on every request; HTTP mode never falls back to the server's cwd.
- Local-only mode: optional `ENGRAM_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN` bearer guard, Origin/Host validation against DNS rebinding, loopback bind by default.
- Local-only mode: optional `ENGRAM_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN` bearer guard, Origin/Host validation against DNS rebinding, loopback bind by default.
- Optional Engram Cloud sync: the request bearer is the user's Engram Cloud token. It is validated through a new authenticated `GET /auth/whoami` route and bound to the owner account; a token from another account is rejected. `ENGRAM_CLOUD_TOKEN` is optional (bearer-only mode). Cloud traffic stays HTTPS-only, reusing the existing rule that bearers never travel over plaintext HTTP.
- Deployment: `docker/http/Dockerfile` + `docker-compose.http.yml`, env-file driven (`docker/http/env.example`), plus an optional Caddy `tls` profile for `docker-compose.cloud.yml` so local and server setups both use HTTPS. Existing `docker-compose.cloud.yml` defaults and the published cloud image are unchanged.
- An existing engram data dir can be mounted as the container's data volume to continue from local memories.

I have a working implementation on a branch (tests, docs, and an end-to-end run: VS Code → engram-http → container SQLite → HTTPS sync → Engram Cloud dashboard). Happy to split it into chained PRs once this is approved.


### 📦 Affected Area

MCP Server (tools, transport)

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- Installing the binary everywhere: not possible on the target machines.
- Exposing the existing REST API (`engram serve`): it is not MCP, so MCP clients cannot use it.
 - Implementing MCP tools directly on the cloud server (Postgres): the cloud only stores sync chunks/mutations, so it would need a second search/store implementation with different semantics than FTS5.
- The deprecated HTTP+SSE transport (2024-11-05): superseded by Streamable HTTP.


### 📎 Additional Context

- Related precedent: #112 (closed; stdio remained viable in that scenario).
- Security notes: loopback by default; bearer bound to the cloud principal via `/auth/whoami`; fail-closed on cloud errors; startup refuses an `http://` cloud URL in cloud mode; warnings when the endpoint can be reached without a secret.

title: feat(ci): recognize cross-repository issue references in PR validation
body:
### 🔍 Problem Description

The PR validation gates only recognize same-repository closing keywords. The pattern in `.github/workflows/pr-check.yml` (`/(?:closes|fixes|resolves)\s+#(\d+)/gi`) does not match the cross-repository form `Closes OWNER/REPO#N`, so a PR whose approved issue lives in a sibling repository fails `Check Issue Reference` with "no closing issue reference found" even though it links an approved issue.

Today this forced opening a mirror tracking issue in engram (PR #1500 ↔ #1499) for work that was already approved and claimed in Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai#1019. The org already tracks twin issues across repos (for example #648 and gentle-ai#1019 describe the same defect), so cross-repo delivery is a recurring pattern, and every occurrence pays the mirror-issue cost: duplicated tracking, split discussion, and extra triage.

### 💡 Proposed Solution

Extend the recognized reference grammar to the cross-repository form (`Closes/Fixes/Resolves OWNER/REPO#N`) and have the approval check resolve the referenced issue through the REST API in its own repository before testing `status:approved`. A bare `#N` remains equivalent to `OWNER/REPO#N` for this repository. PRs could then link the repository where the work is actually approved, and mirror tracking issues become optional instead of structurally required.

### 📦 Affected Area

Other

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

The current workaround is the mirror tracking issue (what PR #1500 does today): it keeps the gates green but duplicates tracking and discussion, and it only works after the mirror issue itself gets triaged and approved.

### 📎 Additional Context

Observed while opening #1500: `Check Issue Reference` passed only after adding a bare `Closes #1499`, while the cross-repository reference to gentle-ai#1019 (approved, priority:high) was not recognized. Prior art in the same check family: gentle-ai#1770 fixed a different parsing defect (HTML comments), so the reference parser has an established maintenance history.

title: feat(mcplogs): surviving-witness classifier for Claude Code MCP logs
body:
### 🔍 Problem Description

The connect/close/never-reconnect failure class tracked in Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai#1019 (Engram's MCP connection gets SIGINT'd 2-5 seconds after connecting under Claude Code and never reconnects) has no client-free diagnostic. Today the only way to tell a real defect from ordinary session teardown is manual inspection of Claude Code's `mcp-logs-<server>/*.jsonl` cache fragments: reporters publish raw logs and every reader re-derives the judgment by hand, thread after thread.

### 💡 Proposed Solution

Add a Go package `internal/mcplogs` that scans a Claude Code cache fragment, groups log lines by (server, sessionId), and classifies each connection lifecycle under the surviving-witness standard proposed in the gentle-ai#1019 thread: a 4-clause candidate (declared close of 2-5s, cache-clear, zero completed tool calls, no later reconnection) is only a `defect-suspect` when a peer MCP server in the same session demonstrably outlived the close (a tool call completed after our close, or a declared close beyond a 10s window). Peers that closed within the window mean ordinary session `teardown`; a candidate with no possible witness either way is `indeterminate`; everything else is `healthy`.

Delivery is planned as a chained pair: the parse layer (`ScanLifecycles`, session lifecycle extraction) first, then the classification layer plus fixtures transcribed from the thread evidence. Client-free by design: no Claude Code invocation anywhere, including tests.

### 📦 Affected Area

MCP Server (tools, transport)

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

Manual log reading (the status quo, which does not scale across reporters). A detector running inside Claude Code itself was considered and rejected: acceptance would be client-bound, while fixture-based validation over reporter-published logs keeps every assertion deterministic.

### 📎 Additional Context

Cross-references: Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai#1019 (approved; the surviving-witness standard and the negative control come from its thread) and #648, the closed engram-side twin of the connection bug. The fixture set includes jjeg1979's unauthenticated short-session runs as the load-bearing negative control (strict 4-clause matches on multiple servers, zero defect-suspects) and a labeled synthetic defect-positive, since no confirmed defect-positive log exists in the wild yet.

title: feat(governance): accept non-closing approved issue references for partial PRs
body:
### 🔍 Problem Description
The PR validation requires `Closes/Fixes/Resolves #N` for every PR. When an approved umbrella issue is delivered in reviewable partial PRs (e.g. #1270), merging the first slice to `main` closes that issue before its remaining work is complete. The current check rejects `Refs #N` even though the referenced issue is approved.

### 💡 Proposed Solution
Accept `Refs #N` as a non-closing reference in both ordinary-PR and merge-group issue-reference checks. Validate `status:approved` for *every* accepted reference, including closing and non-closing forms; still reject missing or unapproved references. Document when to use `Refs` versus `Closes`, and cover both paths with deterministic tests. After this policy is active on `main`, replace partial #1270 PRs’ closing references with `Refs #1270` and only close the umbrella on the final completing PR.

### 📦 Affected Area
Other — contributor governance and PR validation workflow.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered
Reopen #1270 after each merge, which causes transient closures and can trigger external automation; or create a separate issue per slice, adding avoidable tracker noise. Neither is as honest as a non-closing approved reference.

### 📎 Additional Context
This issue is scoped to the policy only. Keep existing issue-first approval and type-label requirements intact; no #1270 behavior slice or merge is authorized as part of this change.

title: feat(cli): move sessions, prompts and observations between projects
body:
### 🔍 Problem Description

Engram sometimes stores information in the wrong project and there is no way to move a session, prompt or individual observation that already has a project assigned to another project, neither via CLI, MCP nor TUI.

Verified today on v2.2.1:

- `engram projects rescue-ownership --project <name> --session/--observation/--prompt <id>` only rescues rows with NULL/empty project and reports already-owned rows as Blocked.
- `engram doctor repair --project P --check ... --apply` (from #286) only reclassifies contaminated sessions when there is trustworthy evidence (`git_remote`/`git_root` or `manual-save-{known-project}` name), with SQLite backup under `<ENGRAM_DATA_DIR>/backups/`.
- MCP `mem_update` exposes no `project` field and the store rejects project changes with `ErrObservationProjectImmutable` (`internal/store/store.go`).
- `engram projects consolidate` and MCP `mem_merge_projects {from,to}` (admin profile) only merge name variants equivalent under normalization and reject arbitrary pairs like `acmeapi` → `acme-api`.
- `engram projects merge --from/--to` requested in #1296 does not exist in v2.2.1 and its building block (#1451, `MergeProjectsByName` + `CountProjectRecords`) is still OPEN.

### 💡 Proposed Solution

New `engram move --to <project> [--session <id>]... [--observation <id>]... [--prompt <id>]... [--dry-run|--apply]`, reusing the transaction/journaling of `RescueNullProjectOwnership` but WITHOUT requiring empty project, with prior backup like `doctor --apply`, recalculated `ownership_mode`, and rejection when an observation would be split from its session (same anti-split guard as rescue).

MCP counterpart `mem_move_records` under admin profile with identical parameters.

In parallel, `engram projects merge --from A --to B --dry-run|--apply` on top of #1451.

### 📦 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

Evaluated existing paths, none of which move already-owned records: `rescue-ownership` (NULL/empty rows only), `doctor repair` (evidence-based reclassification only), `projects consolidate` / `mem_merge_projects` (normalization-equivalent name variants only), `mem_update` (project immutable by design).

### 📎 Additional Context

References:

- #286 (closest existing, CLI/MCP repair with backup)
- #179 (`mem_update` never persisted project change)
- #1296 (`merge --from/--to`, CLOSED without the subcommand)
- #1451 (OPEN, pending seam)
- #94 (TUI delete sessions, delete not move)
- #107 (selective export TUI, not move)

Acceptance criteria:

- Move one already-assigned session to another project via CLI with dry-run first and backup on apply.
- Move one already-assigned observation to another project via CLI with dry-run first and backup on apply.
- Move one already-assigned prompt to another project via CLI with dry-run first and backup on apply.
- MCP admin equivalent (`mem_move_records`).
- Docs updated.
- Existing `rescue-ownership` and `doctor` behavior unchanged.

title: feat(cli): run engram serve in the background as a daemon (--daemon, --status, --stop)
body:
### 🔍 Problem Description

Running `engram serve` as a persistent background daemon currently requires hand-authoring OS-specific supervisor units from the docs (launchd plist on macOS, systemd unit on Linux, Task Scheduler on Windows). Three concrete pain points, all reproduced today on a real macOS setup:

1. **Silent staleness of manual units.** The launchd template needs literal absolute paths (launchd does not expand `$HOME`). After the install method changed (Homebrew `/opt/homebrew/bin/engram` → a plain `~/.local/bin/engram` install), the previously installed plist kept pointing at the old binary path. The service was disabled and unloaded — the daemon silently stopped surviving reboots, with no diagnostic pointing at the cause.

2. **No CLI verbs for daemon control.** Start/stop/status means remembering `launchctl`/`systemctl` incantations and plist paths. There is no `engram serve --status`, no `--stop`, no way to ask engram itself whether a daemon is running.

3. **Bind failure exits 0.** When the port is already taken, `serve` logs `HTTP server did not bind on 127.0.0.1:7437: an existing instance owns the port` and exits with code 0. Under a `KeepAlive` supervisor this produces a silent restart loop every throttle interval — the stderr log fills with bind failures while the supervisor's run counter just climbs. A supervisor cannot distinguish healthy from crash-looping, and users see nothing.

A related collision: MCP clients (e.g. the Pi adapter) spawn their own transient `engram serve` per session, so a supervised daemon and a session-owned instance race for the port with no defined ownership or reuse contract.

### 💡 Proposed Solution

CLI-native daemon support that works regardless of how the binary was installed:

```bash
engram serve --daemon        # fork to background, write pidfile, print PID/port, exit 0
engram serve --status        # running (pid N) / not running / unreachable
engram serve --stop          # stop the daemon instance tracked by the pidfile
# or, as a superset:
engram service install       # render + install the platform unit (launchd/systemd/schtasks) with the CURRENT binary path
```

Expected behavior:

- `--daemon` backgrounds the process (double-fork or equivalent), records a pidfile under the data dir (e.g. `~/.engram/serve.pid`), prints the PID and port, exits 0.
- A second `serve` against a live instance detects it (pidfile + port probe) and reports `already running (pid N)` with a non-zero exit code by default, so callers can decide to reuse or replace.
- **Port-in-use returns a non-zero exit code** (today it is 0), keeping the clear message. Any supervisor (launchd KeepAlive, systemd Restart) can then react correctly instead of hot-looping.
- `service install` renders the existing docs templates with the real binary path and home directory, removing the literal-path fragility that made manual units go stale.

### 📦 Affected Area

CLI (commands, flags)

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- **Manual docs templates (added via #279):** they work, but are copy-paste-heavy, go silently stale when the binary path changes (hit today: a launchd agent pointing at a removed Homebrew path), and every control verb is OS-specific shell knowledge.
- **Homebrew `service` stanza (#1357):** right direction for brew installs, but does not cover other install methods (e.g. a binary at `~/.local/bin`), and the CLI itself still has no daemon verbs.
- **`nohup engram serve &`:** no supervision, no restart on crash or reboot, dies with the session.

### 📎 Additional Context

Repro notes from today (macOS, arm64):

- A launchd agent with `KeepAlive=true` running the current `serve`: while another process held port 7437, `engram serve` exited 0 every ~10 seconds; stderr showed only repeated `HTTP server did not bind on 127.0.0.1:7437: an existing instance owns the port` lines. `launchctl` kept respawning — an invisible crash-loop.
- The stale-unit case: plist referencing `/opt/homebrew/bin/engram` after migrating to `~/.local/bin/engram` — service disabled and unloaded, nothing surfaces the mismatch.

Related: #279 (closed — docs templates + `Local daemon:` status line), #1357 (open — Homebrew formula `service` integration). This request is complementary: CLI-level and install-agnostic, and it also gives programmatic clients a defined attach/reuse contract instead of racing the port.

title: Allow omitted or empty session directory metadata in cloud sync
body:
### 🔍 Problem Description

Legacy sessions can retain valid session identities and useful linked observations/prompts while lacking filesystem directory metadata. Cloud sync currently rejects such sessions. The exporter includes parent sessions needed by dependent records, so excluding an explicit session journal entry alone does not remove that dependency.

The local-import changes in #1287/#1298 intentionally retain strict cloud validation. This is a request to extend compatibility, not a report that their local-only fix regressed.

### 💡 Proposed Solution

Support omitted or string-valued session `directory` metadata consistently across cloud client canonicalization, server validation, and cloud import.

Acceptance criteria:
- Accept omitted `directory`, empty strings, whitespace-only strings, and concrete string paths.
- Reject explicit `null`, numbers, arrays, objects, and other non-string values.
- Preserve session identity/entity-key consistency, project authorization, referential closure, and atomic import guarantees.
- Preserve existing concrete directory metadata when later incoming metadata is empty; allow later concrete metadata to complete a legacy session.
- Include regression tests for push validation and cloud import of a legacy session with linked observations/prompts, plus invalid-type and authorization/reference rejection tests.
- Document server-first then client rollout; old strict servers/clients remain incompatible with these payloads.

Do not invent directory paths, delete memories, or weaken identity and authorization checks to obtain compatibility.

### 📦 Affected Area

Sync (multi-instance)

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

Retaining strict validation leaves historical sessions without directory evidence unable to synchronize. Fabricating a directory introduces misleading metadata. Omitting parent sessions risks breaking dependency closure; quarantining only session journal entries does not prevent observation export from including their source parent sessions. Deleting dependent memories sacrifices otherwise useful content.

### 📎 Additional Context

Related work: #1287 and #1298. The local-import fix is included in inspected commit `3692e1aff0f70a1ef41f0ce3ca7b9f54aad2dc68`; comparison with `3eb2832a8e21ae2d97f1a7e2ace0cc86de7d958a` showed no changes to the relevant cloud session validation.

Evidence is source inspection and local diagnostics, not a newly executed public cloud reproduction. Relevant implementation areas are `internal/cloud/chunkcodec`, `internal/cloud/cloudserver`, `internal/store`, and the dependency-preserving exporter in `internal/sync`. This request does not claim to resolve unrelated malformed observation data or enrollment/target configuration.

title: bug(codex/windows): Norton behavioral detection during hook execution; HTTP unavailable while MCP remains usable
body:
### 📝 Bug Description

On a native Windows host using the official Engram Codex integration, Norton reports `IDP.HELU.PSE91` (command-line behavioral detection) and lists Windows PowerShell and Engram processes as terminated during Codex use.

Engram MCP memory operations remain usable, but the managed HTTP server used by lifecycle hooks is unavailable during subsequent inspection. This report describes observed behavior; it does **not** establish the exact detection trigger or attribute every server exit to Norton.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

**Observed workflow on the affected host; not independently reproduced on a clean machine:**

1. Install the official Engram 2.2.1 Windows amd64 release.
2. Run `engram setup codex` with the official Codex plugin enabled.
3. Restart Codex and resume a session while Norton protection is enabled.
4. Inspect Norton history, Engram's HTTP startup log, and the availability of the default local HTTP port.

These steps were performed before this report. The latest investigation was passive: no hooks were manually executed, no processes were stopped, and no configuration was changed, to avoid disrupting ongoing Codex work.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

The supported integration should provide its HTTP-backed lifecycle functionality. Startup/backend failures should produce actionable diagnostics. A healthy MCP connection should not be mistaken for evidence that lifecycle hooks are healthy.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

- Norton reports termination of `powershell.exe` and `engram.exe`.
- MCP memory reads and writes succeed. Three `engram.exe mcp --tools=agent` processes were active during inspection; their multiplicity is **not** being reported as a bug.
- The HTTP startup log records listening events, but subsequent inspection finds no TCP listener on port 7437 and no persistent `engram serve` process.
- Previously collected `engram doctor --json` reports 9/9 checks OK. Those store checks do not establish HTTP or lifecycle-hook health.
- An Engram-executable-only behavioral exclusion did not restore HTTP availability and was removed. No broad antivirus exclusions are requested.

### Operating System

Windows

Native Windows 11 Pro, x64, version 10.0.26200 (build 26200).

### Engram Version

`engram 2.2.1`

Codex plugin version: `0.1.5`.
Plugin marketplace checkout: `3692e1aff0f70a1ef41f0ce3ca7b9f54aad2dc68`.

### Agent / Client

Other

- Codex desktop package: `26.924.2738.0`.
- App-server version reported earlier that day: `0.158.0-alpha.2.1`.
- Windows PowerShell engine recorded in hook events: `5.1.26100.9549`.
- NortonUI executable file/product version: `26.8.11125.1056` (not independently established as the detection-engine version).

### 📋 Relevant Logs

All times below are local, **2026-09-26, UTC-3**.

```text
08:11:25.251 — Windows PowerShell event 400 records the SessionStart launcher.
08:11        — Norton history reports IDP.HELU.PSE91.
               Activity lists powershell.exe and engram.exe as terminated.

2026/09/26 08:20:55 [engram] HTTP server listening on 127.0.0.1:7437
2026/09/26 08:25:12 [engram] HTTP server listening on 127.0.0.1:7437

Later passive inspection:
- Engram MCP processes remain active.
- No TCP listener on port 7437.
```

The Windows event exposes the official encoded PowerShell bootstrap dispatching `run-bash-hook.ps1` with `session-start.sh`. The timing is correlated with the Norton incident at minute resolution; Norton's supplied activity report does not identify the exact blocked invocation or its PID.

### 💡 Additional Context

#### Artifact verification

- The downloaded `engram_2.2.1_windows_amd64.zip` SHA-256 matches the official release asset digest:
  `c66947b2468d27104296fedb1bb8416f45fd880262606759217193a4bab9be0f`.
- The installed executable matches the executable extracted from that verified release.
- Inspected hook definitions and dispatch/startup/helper scripts match the identified marketplace checkout after line-ending normalization.

These checks establish artifact provenance, **not** that the behavioral detection is necessarily a false positive.

#### Related work reviewed

Issue searches covered open and closed reports using Norton, the exact detection name, antivirus, GLOBALROOT, ownership mismatch, and Codex/Windows/server terms. No equivalent report was found in those searches.

- #45 and #93 concern older Windows antivirus/download detections.
- #1271 concerns a Windows UserPromptSubmit timeout.
- #1255 and #1269 concern Pi server identity/health behavior.
- PR #1377 contains the encoded Windows launchers present in this checkout. This report does not establish that it introduced the Norton detection.

#### Investigation targets, not a proposed verified fix

Please investigate the Windows hook/server lifecycle and compatibility with Norton. Static inspection also identifies diagnostic limitations worth considering:

- The Windows wrappers can suppress exceptions with `exit 0`.
- The SessionStart health helper maps unreachable endpoints and instance mismatches to failure; the caller reports a generic ownership-mismatch message. **That message was not captured as an observed runtime error in this incident.**
- The real-session-context regression in `codex_windows_hook_dispatcher_test.go` uses an external HTTP fixture via `ENGRAM_URL`; it does not validate managed local server survival after the hook finishes.

The precise Norton-detected invocation and the cause of each HTTP server exit remain unknown. No clean-host reproduction, tested fix, or recommendation to disable antivirus protection is claimed. Any further reproduction should be isolated from ongoing user workloads.


**Triage note:** This report follows the current Bug Report fields. The submitting account cannot assign repository labels; please apply `type:bug` and `status:needs-review`. No implementation approval is assumed.

title: feat(store): explicit by-name project merge entry and record counts
body:
### 🔍 Problem Description

The approved #1296 asks the CLI to merge two explicitly named projects (for example `acmeapi` into `acme-api`). Today no store entry can serve that pair: `MergeProjects` requires the names to be normalization-equivalent, and the explicit admission merged in #1415 only accepts same-length `-`/`_` separator swaps for the admin MCP tool. `CanonicalizeProjectName` preserves separators, so `acmeapi` and `acme-api` stay deliberately distinct under normalization and every existing merge path rejects them.

This is the store-side slice of the #1296 chain, split out because the full change (store seam + CLI + docs) exceeds the 400-line review budget.

### 💡 Proposed Solution

Add `MergeProjectsByName(from, to)`:

- Migrates every record of the exact source spelling onto the normalized target in a single transaction (observations, sessions, user prompts, sync journal/enrollment), reusing the #1415 migration core.
- Refuses the pair when both names normalize to the same project (that case belongs to `consolidate`), and when either name is empty.
- Does not loosen the existing admission contracts of `MergeProjects` or `MergeExplicitProjectVariants`; regression tests pin both.

Plus `CountProjectRecords(name)`: read-only exact-spelling observation/session/prompt counts that mirror the merge UPDATE predicate, so a CLI dry-run preview can neither overstate nor understate what an applied merge would move.

The CLI subcommand (`engram projects merge --from/--to`) that consumes this seam lands in the follow-up slice closing #1296.

### 📦 Affected Area

Store (database, queries)

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- Broadening `MergeExplicitProjectVariants` admission: rejected — #1415 deliberately narrowed the admin MCP tool to separator variants; unrelated names are rejected there by design.
- Hand-written SQL by the CLI: off-contract and easy to get wrong across observations, sessions, prompts, and the sync journal.

### 📎 Additional Context

Chain split of #1296: this issue covers slice 1 (store seam, PR1), #1296 keeps tracking the user-facing CLI delivery (slice 2, PR2, closing #1296).

title: feat(pi): canonical topic workflow so agents update existing memories instead of saving duplicates
body:
### 🔍 Problem Description

The memory protocol injected by `gentle-engram` tells agents to call `mem_save` immediately after every bug fix, decision, discovery, and similar event. It gives no instruction to look for an existing observation on the same topic first. In practice, agents keep appending new observations about the same evolving subject instead of updating the existing one, even though `mem_update` and `topic_key` exist for exactly that purpose.

Over months this bloats personal stores with near-duplicate and partially contradictory observations. Cleaning them up afterwards is expensive and risky, because each candidate has to be read in full and judged by hand.

### 💡 Proposed Solution

Replace the "WHEN TO SAVE" section of the Pi memory protocol with a canonical topic workflow, and mirror it briefly in the tool descriptions:

1. `mem_search` the bounded subject in the intended project and scope before writing.
2. Read plausible candidates in full with `mem_get_observation`. Search snippets are not enough to decide identity.
3. Same bounded topic: `mem_update` by ID, keep the existing `topic_key`, preserve still-valid facts, and mark superseded facts as history instead of leaving competing current truths.
4. Genuinely new topic: `mem_save` with a deliberate, distinct `topic_key`. If the learning is already covered, write nothing.
5. Ambiguous identity or failed lookup: no blind overwrite and no duplicate fallback save. A failed read is not evidence of absence.
6. Never merge across projects or scopes. A matching suggested `topic_key` or similar title is a hint, not proof of identity.

I have a working local draft (about 25 changed lines in `plugin/pi/index.ts`, plus README and source-contract test updates) and can open a PR if this is approved.

### 📦 Affected Area

Other

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- Post-hoc cleanup (`conflicts scan`, manual consolidation): works, but it is costly and treats the symptom rather than the write path.
- Automatic server-side dedup on `mem_save`: riskier, because deciding topic identity needs the full content and context the agent has at write time.

### 📎 Additional Context

I ran a small A/B benchmark: 5 scripted cases (new topic, enrichment, correction, already-covered repeat, similar but ambiguous topic), one session per case and arm (10 sessions per run), repeated with two models (gpt-6-astra low and gpt-5.6-sol medium).

| Arm | Passed | Duplicates | Lost facts | Wrong merges |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Current protocol (astra) | 2/5 | 3 | 1 | 0 |
| Canonical workflow (astra) | 3/5 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| Current protocol (sol) | 1/5 | 4 | 2 | 0 |
| Canonical workflow (sol) | 3/5 | 0 | 3 | 0 |

Duplicates went to zero in both models with no wrong merges. Known limitations:

- The harness used synthetic scoped lexical search, not Engram FTS.
- Native lifecycle hooks were not executed.
- Fact loss was checked with literal oracles, without a semantic judge.
- With the sol model, fact loss increased (2 to 3), so the "preserve still-valid facts" wording probably needs tightening before this is ready.

I would treat these results as directional evidence rather than proof.

title: feat(sync): opt-in personal-scope export for `engram sync --project`
body:
### 🔍 Problem Description

I use Engram on my own, on Linux and Windows with a separate store on each, and move memory between them through a private Git repository with local `engram sync --project NAME`, one reviewed project at a time. I keep cross-project preferences and decisions in `scope: personal` so they show up in personal context from any project (#425).

On v1.20.0, `engram sync --project NAME` exports the project's personal-scope observations with the rest, and my repository has v1.20.0 chunks that carry them. Since #784 (the fix for #701), v2.x exports only `scope: project` observations for a named project and skips relations with a personal endpoint ([filter in v2.2.0](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/blob/v2.2.0/internal/sync/sync.go#L2079-L2091)). The run succeeds and nothing reports the skipped observations. I reproduced this on v2.1.0 with a copy of my store: the chunk left out the project's personal-scope observation and its three relations, and only `engram sync --all` exported them. The same code is in v2.2.0.

The docs still describe the v1.20.0 behavior. docs/TEAM-USAGE.md in v2.2.0 says local `engram sync` exports "observations of the target project regardless of their scope" and that changing this "needs a deliberate design decision" ([L104-L116](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/engram/blob/v2.2.0/docs/TEAM-USAGE.md?plain=1#L104-L116)). #784 marked docs as not required and no release note mentions the change, so anyone syncing per project who upgrades from v1.20.0 stops syncing new and edited personal memories without being told. It's the reason I'm still on v1.20.0.

### 💡 Proposed Solution

Keep the 2.x default and add an explicit opt-in that lets a local per-project sync include that project's personal-scope observations and the relations that link them within the project. A flag such as `engram sync --project NAME --include-personal` or a per-project setting would both work for me.

The maintainer asked three contract questions in #474, which requested the opposite (keeping personal observations local for teams). My answers for this case:

- Local or Cloud: local `engram sync` only. Cloud keeps its current behavior.
- Default or opt-in: opt-in and off by default, so nothing changes for anyone who doesn't enable it.
- Existing rows: untouched unless the opt-in is used. When it is, the project's personal-scope observations that earlier 2.x runs skipped should be exported too.

Relations should keep the #701 guarantee: a relation travels only when both of its endpoints reach the receiver as well. Since #1374 (v2.2.0), import already applies same-project relations regardless of endpoint scope, so receivers should need no change.

Whatever you decide, the docs and the code should agree on what local sync does with personal scope.

### 📦 Affected Area

Sync (multi-instance)

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- `engram sync --all` includes personal scope, but it exports every project in one run. I publish one reviewed project at a time and keep some records out of Git on purpose.
- Cloud sync needs an Engram Cloud server, and my memory only moves through a private Git repository.
- Re-scoping these memories to `project` would remove them from cross-project personal search and context (#425).

### 📎 Additional Context

_No response_

title: refactor(setup): share OpenCode JSONC config I/O
body:
### 🔍 Problem Description

Remove duplicated OpenCode setup work without changing configuration behavior. The criterion is justified simplification: eliminate redundant or genuinely unnecessary code, not maximize deleted lines or force superficially similar flows into one abstraction.

Revalidated on `main` at `b08308ad`: `injectOpenCodeTUIPlugin` and `injectOpenCodeMCP` repeat JSONC root loading and serialization/write in `internal/setup/setup.go:599–717`. The MCP injector also constructs the same server entry already produced by `mcpEntry(opencodeObject)` in `internal/setup/registry.go`.

This is a behavior-preserving maintenance proposal, not a reported installation failure.

### 💡 Proposed Solution

#### Bounded design

| Action | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Reuse | Replace the inline MCP entry construction with existing `mcpEntry(opencodeObject)`, after the existing-registration early return. | Removes a second definition of the same payload without adding an abstraction or resolving the command on a no-op path. |
| Consolidate | Share only the duplicated OpenCode JSONC root read/parse and config serialize/write steps through small private functions in the existing setup package. | One implementation of identical I/O policy; no callback pipeline, options framework, or all-agent configuration layer. |
| Keep | Separate `injectOpenCodeTUIPlugin` and `injectOpenCodeMCP`, their section parsing/mutations, and existing test seams. | Plugin-list append and MCP registration are different responsibilities with different errors and no-op checks. |
| Keep | Separate TUI and MCP path entry points and destinations. | `openCodeTUIConfigPath()` targets `tui.json[c]`; `openCodeConfigPath()` targets `opencode.json[c]`. |

The MCP flow remains: resolve path, load root, parse MCP block, return without writing if `engram` already exists, build the missing entry with the existing builder, then persist. The TUI flow remains: resolve its own path, load root, parse plugin list, return without writing if the package already exists, append the missing package, then persist.

#### Private helper contracts

The proposed private boundaries are:

```go
readOpenCodeJSONCConfig(path string) (map[string]json.RawMessage, error)
writeOpenCodeJSONCConfig(path string, config map[string]json.RawMessage) error
```

- Keep the existing `map[string]json.RawMessage` representation and section-specific decoding. Do not round-trip unrelated fields through `map[string]any`, which can change numeric values through float decoding.
- The reader uses existing `readFileFn` and `stripJSONC` behavior. Only a missing file creates an empty map; do not add normalization or validation of decoded null/malformed roots as part of extraction.
- The writer retains `jsonMarshalIndentFn(config, "", "  ")`, `writeFileFn`, and mode `0644`; it does not create directories, append a newline, or introduce atomic-write behavior.
- Each helper owns its I/O-stage error wrapping, exactly once and with `%w`: `read config` / `parse config` in the reader, `marshal config` / `write config` in the writer. Injectors return these errors unchanged, without adding another prefix or collapsing the stages.
- Section errors stay in the injectors: `parse plugin block`, `marshal plugin block`, `parse mcp block`, `marshal engram entry`, and `marshal mcp block`. Both injectors retain their existing early returns before serialization/persistence.

These are two fixed OpenCode I/O functions, not an extensible strategy/options interface. Existing generic JSON helpers and their consumers remain unchanged.

#### Contracts to preserve

- Prefer an existing `.jsonc` file over `.json`; retain XDG/home resolution and Windows behavior.
- Missing config starts as an empty object. Retain current read, parse, marshal, and write error classifications and wrapping, including section-specific errors.
- Preserve unrelated keys, other servers, existing plugin ordering, and existing `engram` registrations, including customized values. Do not turn registration-if-missing into an upsert.
- Keep current JSONC comment/string handling. Successful writes retain existing indentation, mode `0644`, and no newly appended newline. Do not add directory creation to these I/O steps.
- No-op paths must not serialize or write; existing file bytes, including comments, remain untouched on a no-op.

#### Explicitly out of scope

- Replacing the OpenCode injector with generic `injectMCP`: it uses strict JSON and upsert semantics rather than JSONC and preserve-existing semantics.
- Reusing `readJSONConfig`/`writeJSONConfig` unchanged: their strict-JSON/null validation, directory creation, newline, and error policies differ. Do not add option flags just to force reuse.
- Changing Pi, Claude, Gemini, Codex, registry installation policies, or the shipped/mirrored OpenCode TypeScript adapters.
- Rewriting `stripJSONC`, fixing malformed/null config behavior incidentally, broad dead-code cleanup (#973), or merging the path selectors merely to reduce line counts. Path-selection extraction is deferred unless separate evidence shows meaningful simplification.

### 🧪 Verification and Acceptance

Characterize current behavior before changing production code, then run the same checks against the refactor:

- [ ] Retain focused JSONC, path-precedence, resolved-command, existing-entry, idempotence, and non-fatal installation-failure tests in `internal/setup/setup_test.go`.
- [ ] Add assertions for zero serialization/writes and byte-identical files on no-op paths, including an existing customized MCP registration and an already-listed TUI package.
- [ ] Cover missing files, unrelated keys/servers, plugin ordering, read/parse failures, section failures, marshal/write failures, and unchanged file content on failures before persistence.
- [ ] Assert I/O error stage prefixes and wrapped causes (`errors.Is`/`errors.As` as appropriate), with no duplicated wrapping after extraction. Keep section-error assertions separate.
- [ ] Preserve an unrelated integer above JavaScript's exact-number range (2^53) through a real changed-config write, guarding against an accidental `map[string]any` decode/re-encode.
- [ ] Characterize uncovered malformed/null inputs where relevant. If a pre-existing defect is found, record it separately rather than silently changing behavior in this refactor.
- [ ] Confirm TUI/MCP destinations remain distinct and the reused entry builder emits the same payload and resolves the binary only on the missing-registration path.
- [ ] Run focused setup tests and `go test -mod=readonly ./internal/setup`. Follow repository ratchets and applicable PR CI once an implementation candidate exists; report actual outcomes, not assumed coverage.
- [ ] Review the resulting diff for fewer duplicated responsibilities and no unnecessary new layer. Line reduction is supporting evidence, not the goal or a substitute for preserved behavior.

### 📦 Affected Area

CLI setup: `internal/setup/setup.go` and focused `internal/setup/setup_test.go` coverage. Reuse the existing builder from `internal/setup/registry.go`; no registry behavior change is planned.

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

Leave duplication in place, introduce a generic configuration framework, or unify all agents' JSON I/O. None offers the same bounded simplification while preserving their different policies. Start with existing equivalent code reuse, then consolidate only the demonstrably identical OpenCode steps.

### 📎 Additional Context

CodeGraph was synced and used to map setup/registry callers and test dependencies. The local checkout is `dd1261149`, while the design base is remote `main` at `b08308ad`; relevant OpenCode blocks and registry logic were cross-checked against that remote snapshot rather than relying on local graph line numbers alone.

OpenCode V2 support already landed through #1526. Remote main has since moved to module `engram/v3`; comparing `a43183c2` to `b08308ad` changes only module imports in the relevant setup source, not the proposed OpenCode/registry logic.

Second-review baseline: `go test -mod=readonly -count=1 -timeout=90s ./internal/setup` passed on an isolated archive of `b08308ad` on Windows/amd64 with Go 1.26.4 (14.120s). This is evidence for the unchanged baseline only. The added characterization cases above and refactor-equivalence verification have not been implemented or run; their checkboxes remain open.

This update documents proposed scope and verification, not implementation. The issue remains pending maintainer review; documenting or reviewing this design does not approve implementation.

title: refactor(store): isolate semantic scan worker execution
body:
### 🔍 Problem Description

`internal/store/relations.go:1311–1664` implements `scanProject` as one roughly 350-line function. It combines page loading, candidate selection, relation insertion and caps, semantic-pair deduplication, and a concurrent semantic judgment pool. This puts distinct failure and accounting paths into one unit and makes semantic changes hard to review without rechecking structural scan behavior. This is a maintainability proposal, not a claim that the scan currently misbehaves.

### 💡 Proposed Solution

Extract only semantic worker execution and result accounting into a private, focused function after candidate pairs have been selected. Keep page/query logic, pair selection/caps and structural inserts in `scanProject`. Preserve dry-run/apply semantics, worker concurrency, timeouts, panic/error handling, counters and result ordering. Do not combine this with a behavioral performance fix.

Acceptance: existing scan batching/page and semantic tests still pass; focused cases in `internal/store/scan_semantic_test.go` cover dry-run versus apply, valid/invalid verdicts, runner errors/panics, capped pairs, and concurrent accounting. No public API, SQL semantics or response fields change; prefer net simpler code rather than shifting the same complexity to more layers.

### 📦 Affected Area

Store (database, queries)

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

Split the entire scan pipeline at once (larger review and regression surface) or leave all paths together. A bounded semantic execution seam permits one behavior-preserving work unit with existing tests.

### 📎 Additional Context

Source revalidated on `main` at `a43183c2` (the semantic worker pool still lives inside `scanProject`): `internal/store/relations.go:1311–1664`, particularly the semantic worker block `:1562–1663`; tests in `internal/store/scan_semantic_test.go`, `scan_batch_test.go`, and `scan_page_test.go`. The closed #590 and #721 tracked different behavioral bugs; this proposal does not reopen them. No implementation or tests were run for this proposal.

title: refactor(dashboard): consolidate pagination recovery across list handlers
body:
### 🔍 Problem Description

Six dashboard list handlers repeat pagination recovery: re-clamp the requested page against the returned total, re-fetch the clamped page, and, if that fails with no rows, retry page one. On `main` at `a43183c2`, the recovery branches in `internal/cloud/dashboard/dashboard.go` start around lines 444 (observations), 486 (sessions), 528 (prompts), 635 (contributors), 757 (projects), and 1150 (audit log). They maintain nearly identical branches and logging. A future fix to empty-page or refetch behavior can drift across endpoints. This is a maintainability issue, not a reported user-facing defect.

### 💡 Proposed Solution

Consolidate only the post-fetch pagination recovery into a small typed helper or similarly smaller structure. Keep initial store errors, per-endpoint data fetching, partial/full-page rendering, and project controls in their current handlers. Do not introduce a generic dashboard-handler framework or change HTTP responses.

Acceptance: all six lists retain their current page bounds and row ordering; a failed re-fetch retains existing rows; a failed re-fetch with no rows attempts page one once; store errors still use each endpoint's current response, including the audit log's request context, filtering, and 502 initial-store-error response. Extend `internal/cloud/dashboard/dashboard_test.go` with table-driven recovery cases while retaining the existing re-clamp/HTMX tests. Prefer a net reduction in duplicated code.

### 📦 Affected Area

Other

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

Leave the branches duplicated (low immediate risk, but fixes can diverge); unify whole handlers (too broad, obscures endpoint-specific contracts). The shared recovery step is the narrower seam.

### 📎 Additional Context

Revalidated on `main` at `a43183c2`: all six handlers still duplicate post-fetch recovery, including the newer audit log list. Existing tests include browser out-of-range clamping, contributors/projects real-total pagination, HTMX rendering, and audit log coverage in `internal/cloud/dashboard/dashboard_test.go`. Extend focused recovery coverage for each list rather than unifying endpoint-specific response policies. No implementation or functional tests were run for this update.

title: feat(pi): honor mem_save capture_prompt association semantics
body:
### 🔍 Problem Description

The Pi-native `mem_save` advertises `capture_prompt` but its HTTP dispatch never reads the argument. MCP `mem_save` applies this option (default true) when associating an available prompt with a saved observation (#308). Pi independently stores prompt rows from `before_agent_start`, but that does not prove the same observation association or the requested `capture_prompt=false` behavior. Thus the Pi-facing field currently promises behavior the native tool does not implement.

### 💡 Proposed Solution

Define and implement the same observation↔prompt association semantics for Pi, preferably in Go/HTTP core rather than a second TypeScript algorithm. An omitted field should use the documented default; `false` should skip association for that save, without implying it disables Pi lifecycle prompt capture. If no prompt exists the save still succeeds. Cover default, explicit false, missing prompt, same-session/project ownership, and dedupe with cross-transport behavior tests. If exact parity cannot be supported, remove or clearly scope the misleading Pi parameter instead of silently ignoring it.

Acceptance: `capture_prompt` has a documented, observable meaning for Pi mem_save and tests fail if the option is discarded.

### 📦 Affected Area

Other

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

Treating Pi prompt-event capture as equivalent: events store prompts independently, not necessarily the association of a specific observation, and cannot honor a per-save opt-out. Reimplementing prompt matching in the adapter duplicates core policy.

### 📎 Additional Context

Evidence on main e50d697: `plugin/pi/index.ts` tool schema near 1229, mem_save dispatch near 1412, `before_agent_start` near 1697; MCP `internal/mcp/mcp.go` near 1468. Related parity umbrella #1347 and default Pi alignment #1348; this issue isolates the observable `capture_prompt` behavior rather than duplicating the entire contract effort. Static source evidence only; runtime repro has not been run.

title: feat(homebrew): provide a managed service and safe upgrade path
body:
### 🔍 Problem Description

The GoReleaser-generated Homebrew formula for `engram` has no `service do` stanza. An unmanaged `engram serve` can survive a binary upgrade in the old, now-unlinked Cellar path and keep port 7437 occupied indefinitely. I reproduced this after upgrading 1.20.0 to 2.0.0: `lsof` showed the listener still executing `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/engram/1.20.0/bin/engram`, although `engram --version` on PATH reported 2.0.0. The Pi adapter on npm `latest` then refused memory operations with an opaque ownership-mismatch error.

This is distinct from #279 (daemon status plus a *manual* launchd template), #1255 (client diagnostic, fixed on main), and #1346 (that diagnostic not yet published). The formula still provides no standard managed-service path, and plain `brew upgrade engram` does not restart an unmanaged daemon.

### 💡 Proposed Solution

1. Add an opt-in Homebrew `service` definition in the upstream GoReleaser `brews` configuration (the generated tap formula must not be hand-edited). Use `opt_bin/"engram"` with `serve`, `keep_alive true`, and standard log paths. Do **not** auto-start the service at install time or terminate a listener whose ownership cannot be established.
2. Document the one-time transition from an unmanaged daemon (stop the old listener only after verifying it), `brew services start gentleman-programming/tap/engram`, and verification through `/health`/CLI. Document that **plain** `brew upgrade engram` may leave a still-running old process; the supported post-upgrade path should explicitly `brew services restart ...`, or use a Brewfile with `restart_service: :changed` and `brew bundle` to automate restarts. Do not imply that `KeepAlive` replaces a still-running process automatically.
3. Add a deterministic release-config/formula-render regression check, if practical, so future generated formulas retain the service block.

I'd like to prepare a focused PR if the maintainers approve the approach. An alternative would be a dedicated `engram` upgrade command, but that is a much larger and more dangerous change to process ownership.

### 📦 Affected Area

Other (Homebrew release configuration and installation documentation)

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- #279's manual launchd recipe works, but isn't integrated with `brew services` and is easy to miss.
- Killing the listener automatically from Pi or a post-install hook is unsafe: a port occupant without a matching instance ID must be treated as untrusted.
- `KeepAlive` by itself cannot reload a process that stays alive during `brew upgrade`; document an explicit managed restart path instead.

### 📎 Additional Context

The `engram` 2.0.0 formula in `Gentleman-Programming/homebrew-tap/Formula/engram.rb` is GoReleaser-generated and contains no `service do` block. The old server's pre-v2 `/health` response lacks an `instance_id`; its `version` field is hardcoded `0.1.0`, so it is not a reliable running-binary version indicator. Verify the process image path when diagnosing this case. Related: #279, #1255, #1346.

title: feat(store): make session closure replay-safe
body:
### 🔍 Problem Description

PR #1250 is the autonomous core slice of umbrella issue #1192. Linking that PR directly with `Closes #1192` would close the umbrella before its remaining sync and OpenCode archive slices are delivered.

The store also needs deterministic replay behavior: repeated closure, import, or sync operations must not replace the first closure timestamp or the first meaningful summary, while existing guarded session identity updates must continue to work.

### 💡 Proposed Solution

Track the core session-closure work independently from #1192:

- Make session closure idempotent and preserve the first `ended_at` value and first meaningful summary.
- Return explicit errors for unknown sessions and retryable SQLite lock contention.
- Preserve first-closure semantics across import and sync replay.
- Keep the established guarded updates for `project`, `ownership_mode`, `directory`, and `started_at`.
- Add focused regression coverage for conflicting replay values, whitespace-only stored summaries, transaction failure, and HTTP error mapping.

Archive-specific inactivity policy remains owned by #1263, where the caller has archive intent; generic session closure must continue to support an active runtime closing itself.

### 📦 Affected Area

Store (database, queries)

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

Closing #1192 from PR #1250 was rejected because #1192 remains the umbrella for #1259, #1263, #1264, and #1235. A non-closing reference alone would not satisfy the repository's issue-first PR validation, so a dedicated child issue is required.

### 📎 Additional Context

title: feat(protocol): negotiate agent contract compatibility at runtime
body:
### 🔍 Problem Description

A coordinated release and matching version numbers do not guarantee that a running Pi session is connected to the matching Engram server.

`gentle-engram` may launch whichever `engram` binary is available on `PATH`, or connect to an independently managed server through `ENGRAM_URL`. Existing users can therefore combine a newer Pi contract with an older HTTP server, or the reverse, even when official releases were published correctly.

Without runtime capability negotiation, missing endpoints or changed semantics surface as generic tool failures, and the package can imply parity that the active server cannot provide.

### 💡 Proposed Solution

Expose a small Go-owned runtime contract/capability endpoint and make `gentle-engram` validate it.

The endpoint should provide a stable contract identifier and digest plus the supported agent operations needed for compatibility decisions. Pi should compare the server contract with its generated projection before claiming full memory-tool availability.

Required behavior:

- Matching contracts proceed normally.
- Compatible older contracts follow an explicitly tested compatibility policy.
- Missing, malformed, unknown, or incompatible contracts produce a clear actionable diagnostic rather than silent degradation.
- Version-string equality alone is never treated as proof of compatibility.
- Runtime checks preserve current server identity protections and do not accept model-supplied authority.
- Tests cover local auto-start, an existing binary on `PATH`, remote `ENGRAM_URL`, legacy servers, and malformed capability responses.

### 📦 Affected Area

MCP Server (tools, transport)

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- Compare only Engram and npm SemVer: does not prove which binary/server Pi is actually using or whether the semantic contract matches.
- Rely exclusively on release CI: cannot protect manual installs, remote servers, stale processes, or mixed-version environments.
- Dynamically infer capabilities from failed calls: produces poor diagnostics and can discover incompatibility only after a tool is invoked.

### 📎 Additional Context

The HTTP `/health` response already carries Engram version and instance identity, and Pi already verifies server identity during lifecycle management. Contract negotiation should extend that boundary without moving business behavior into the plugin.

title: feat(release): coordinate Engram and gentle-engram releases
body:
### 🔍 Problem Description

Engram core and `gentle-engram` are currently published by independent workflows and version streams. Core tags matching `v*` run GoReleaser, while `pi-v*` tags publish npm. Nothing coordinates the two publications or proves that the released pair implements the same agent contract.

The intended product policy is now a lockstep release train: every official Engram release must also publish `gentle-engram` with the identical SemVer. The current workflows cannot enforce that policy, cannot safely recover from partial publication, and do not handle npm prerelease dist-tags.

Publication spans immutable npm versions, GitHub Releases, GoReleaser artifacts, and Homebrew, so it cannot be truly atomic. Matching version numbers also does not replace semantic contract validation or runtime compatibility negotiation.

### 💡 Proposed Solution

Introduce one coordinated, state-aware release path for Engram and `gentle-engram`.

Release invariants:

- Core tag, `plugin/pi/package.json`, the installer pin, and Pi release metadata use the same strict SemVer.
- The candidate passes Go tests, Pi tests, package/tarball checks, exact `ProfileAgent` parity, and semantic contract checks before publication.
- npm publication uses OIDC trusted publishing and provenance.
- npm artifacts are published under a non-default staging tag first, then GoReleaser publishes core artifacts, and only then is npm promoted to `next` for prereleases or `latest` for stable releases.
- The workflow probes each destination before writing, accepts an existing artifact only when its source commit and expected contract/content match, and safely resumes partial releases without attempting to republish an immutable npm version.
- Per-version concurrency prevents overlapping publication attempts.
- A terminal immutable mismatch requires a corrective version; it must never overwrite or silently reuse the bad version.

Migration work:

- Move `gentle-engram` from the `0.1.x` stream onto the active Engram `2.0.0-*` release train.
- Replace hard-coded historical package-pin lists with a scalable, explicit migration policy for prior managed `gentle-engram` pins.
- Remove or generate hard-coded version examples in documentation so every release does not introduce documentation drift.
- Update the npm trusted-publisher configuration if the publishing workflow identity changes.
- Document partial-release recovery, dist-tag behavior, rollback/compensation, and the fact that identical SemVer is a product pairing policy rather than proof of runtime compatibility.

### 📦 Affected Area

Other

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- Independent Core and Pi SemVer plus a compatibility matrix: technically reduces coupling and avoids no-op npm releases, but does not provide the selected single release-train product experience.
- Keep two manually triggered tag workflows: preserves race conditions and allows version divergence.
- Publish npm directly to `latest` before core succeeds: can expose a package whose matching core release is unavailable.
- Publish core first: can ship a binary whose exact installer pin is missing from npm.

### 📎 Additional Context

Current release surfaces include `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `.github/workflows/publish-pi.yml`, `release_config_test.go`, `plugin/pi/test/release-contract.mjs`, `plugin/pi/package.json`, `internal/setup/setup.go`, and `docs/RELEASE-POLICY.md`.

npm trusted publishing validates configured workflow identity, and `npm publish` uses `latest` unless another dist-tag is supplied. Those external settings and defaults must be included in the migration plan.

title: feat(plugin): align Pi default tools with ProfileAgent
body:
### 🔍 Problem Description

The Pi-native tool surface does not currently match MCP `ProfileAgent` and duplicates behavior that already belongs to Go.

MCP exposes 19 default agent tools and classifies `mem_delete`, `mem_stats`, `mem_timeline`, and `mem_merge_projects` outside that profile. Pi registers the 19 agent tools plus `mem_delete`, `mem_stats`, and `mem_timeline` as model-callable native tools. This exposes destructive `mem_delete`, including permanent deletion, in Pi's default model surface.

Pi also implements `mem_suggest_topic_key` with local JavaScript slug logic while MCP and the HTTP server use `store.SuggestTopicKey`, allowing equivalent calls to produce different keys. Other per-tool input differences have not yet been classified as intentional runtime projections or accidental capability loss.

### 💡 Proposed Solution

Align the Pi default native tool surface with the canonical MCP `ProfileAgent` contract.

- Register exactly the 19 agent tools by default.
- Remove administrative tools from the default model-callable Pi profile. Keep administrative access in explicit MCP/CLI or a separately designed opt-in profile with server-side authorization.
- Route `mem_suggest_topic_key` through the existing Go-owned HTTP endpoint instead of computing it in TypeScript.
- Audit every tool field and classify each difference as semantic, transport-specific, runtime-injected, or accidental loss.
- Add behavior-first regressions for the corrected divergences and preserve Pi's opaque runtime session ownership.
- Keep chrome labels/status rendering as presentation metadata rather than contract authority.

Acceptance criteria:

- Pi default inventory exactly matches `ProfileAgent`.
- No destructive administrative capability is silently model-callable by default.
- Topic-key suggestions are identical across MCP and Pi for shared inputs.
- Every remaining schema difference has a documented projection reason.
- Existing project, session, privacy, timeout, and error behavior remains covered.

### 📦 Affected Area

Other

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- Add all administrative tools to MCP `ProfileAgent`: increases default risk and weakens the profile boundary.
- Preserve Pi as an undocumented superset: prevents strict parity and leaves destructive capabilities exposed by default.
- Reimplement Go algorithms in TypeScript: keeps behavior duplicated and allows future drift.

### 📎 Additional Context

The default Pi inventory is declared in `plugin/pi/index.ts` and duplicated for presentation in `plugin/pi/memory-tool-chrome.js`. The Go profiles and topic-key implementation live in `internal/mcp/mcp.go`, `internal/server/server.go`, and `internal/store/store.go`.

title: feat(protocol): define MCP-Pi agent parity contract
body:
### 🔍 Problem Description

Engram exposes the same memory system through two independently maintained agent adapters: the Go MCP server and the Pi-native `gentle-engram` package. Their model-visible contracts can drift because tool inventories, schemas, descriptions, and transport mappings are declared separately.

The current MCP `ProfileAgent` contains 19 tools, while Pi registers 22 native tools and includes three tools classified as administrative by MCP. Existing MCP contract fixtures protect backward compatibility, but they do not provide an exact current MCP-to-Pi parity gate.

Without a canonical semantic contract, an MCP capability can be added or changed without an equivalent Pi projection, and the repository can still pass its component-local tests.

### 💡 Proposed Solution

Define a versioned, Go-owned semantic agent contract, initially `engram.agent-contract/v1`, with `ProfileAgent` as the parity baseline.

The contract should describe stable tool names, profile membership, risk/effect classification, canonical model-visible inputs, runtime-owned fields, project/session semantics, and stable response/error guarantees. Generate a checked-in language-neutral artifact from that authority.

Verify both transport projections against it:

- MCP registration must expose the exact current `ProfileAgent` inventory and a compatible MCP schema.
- Pi must expose the exact same default agent inventory through a generated or verified TypeBox projection.
- Intentional transport differences, such as Pi injecting its opaque runtime session ID, must be declared explicitly rather than hidden in allowlists.
- Administrative capabilities must remain outside the default agent contract.
- Shared semantic test vectors must exercise representative behavior through MCP and HTTP/Pi without requiring byte-identical transport envelopes.

The implementation should replace duplicated authority rather than introduce a third manually maintained list.

Acceptance criteria:

- One exact 19-tool agent inventory is authoritative.
- MCP and Pi default inventory drift fails CI.
- Schema projection exceptions are explicit and justified.
- Contract changes are deterministic and release-detectable.
- Semantic behavior tests cover project/session ownership, defaults, validation, errors, and state effects.

### 📦 Affected Area

MCP Server (tools, transport)

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- Comparing tool counts or names only: misses schema and behavioral drift.
- Requiring raw MCP and Pi schemas to be identical: incorrectly exposes transport-owned fields such as Pi runtime session identity.
- Keeping manually synchronized Go and TypeScript registries: preserves the source of the current drift.
- Treating the historical MCP compatibility fixture as the exact current inventory: mixes backward-compatibility guarantees with present-state parity.

### 📎 Additional Context

Relevant surfaces include `internal/mcp/mcp.go`, `internal/mcp/tool_contract_test.go`, `internal/mcp/testdata/tool-contract-v1.json`, `plugin/pi/index.ts`, `plugin/pi/memory-tool-chrome.js`, and Pi native contract tests.

title: ci(governance): enforce root-cause-first designed and assigned PR lifecycle
body:
## Problem

Engram enforces issue linkage and `status:approved` for pull requests, but the current contract does not prove that an issue was reproduced against current `main`, investigated to a repository-owned root cause, given an approved design, or assigned to an owner before implementation. Duplicate reports can also fragment evidence across symptom-level trackers.

## Current-state evidence

Audited against remote `main` at `f74102fa34219fb9740d451dd007ee9648ce81d2`.
