title: bug(vim): the >=0.99.2 Pi bump leaves the host gate pinned to 0.99.1 — verify is red on main with 114 failing tests
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

`main` is currently red in the CI `verify` job, and a fresh `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm test` fails 114 distinct tests locally.

The whole Vim editor surface rejects the host pair it is actually built against. `lib/vim-editor-adapter.ts` gates on `SUPPORTED_VERSIONS = new Set(["0.99.1"])`, but the dependency bump that landed in `408ac8e4` (PR #1624, issue #1623) moved the Pi devDependencies to `>=0.99.2`, so the committed lockfile resolves `@earendil-works/pi-tui@0.99.2` and `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.99.2`. Every identity check then fails closed with `Error: Unsupported Pi editor layout/version`, which cascades into vim tests, `tests/gentle-shell.test.ts`, and the manifest assertions.

### Steps to reproduce

Deterministic, from a clean clone of `408ac8e4`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-shell
cd gentle-shell
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
node -e "console.log(require('./node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-tui/package.json').version)"  # -> 0.99.2
pnpm test
```

The same run on `408ac8e4`'s parent `1162ce90` is green, so the regression is introduced by that commit and not by the environment.

### Expected and actual behavior

**Expected:** with the frozen lockfile installed, `pnpm test` is green, and the adapter accepts the Pi/TUI pair the lockfile actually pins.

**Actual:** `pnpm test` fails the `unit-tests` stage. 114 distinct tests fail; 39 failure sites report `Error: Unsupported Pi editor layout/version` thrown from `lib/vim-editor-adapter.ts:166`, and the remainder are downstream Vim-mode assertion failures (`NORMAL`, `INSERT`, `VISUAL` frames, `p must not insert its key`).

```
=== test suite summary ===
FAIL  unit-tests
PASS  provider-contract
PASS  runtime-harness
```

The manifest assertions show the mismatch directly:

```
tests/package-manifest.test.ts:131 - technical reference declares the tested Pi minimum required for agent_settled
  + actual  '>=0.99.2'
  - expected '0.99.1'

tests/package-manifest.test.ts:143 - packed runtime uses optional Pi host peers with exact development pins
  + actual  '>=0.99.2'
  - expected '0.99.1'
```

### Root cause

Three places still assert `0.99.1` while the manifest and lockfile moved to `>=0.99.2`:

| Location | Current value |
| --- | --- |
| `lib/vim-editor-adapter.ts:40` | `const SUPPORTED_VERSIONS = new Set(["0.99.1"]);` |
| `tests/vim-editor-adapter.test.ts` | 61 hardcoded `0.99.1` literals (e.g. `assert.equal(bundledAgent.VERSION, "0.99.1")`, `assertInstalledPiPairBehavior(version: "0.99.1", ...)`) |
| `tests/package-manifest.test.ts:134,148` | expects `0.99.1` for `@earendil-works/pi-ai` / Pi minimum |

With `IMPORTED_TUI_VERSION === "0.99.2"`, `hasEditorIdentity` compares the caller's `0.99.1` against it and returns `false`, so `createVimEditorAdapter` throws.

### CI evidence

| Commit | CI | `verify` job |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `1162ce90` (parent) | success | success |
| `408ac8e4` (head) | **failure** | **failure** — failing step: `Run tests` |

`test (ubuntu-24.04)` and `test (windows-latest)` are green because they do not run the full suite; `verify` is the job that runs `pnpm test`.

### Suggested fix

Either direction closes it, but they should be applied together so the gate and its expectations can never drift again:

1. **Certify 0.99.2** — add `"0.99.2"` to `SUPPORTED_VERSIONS` and update the hardcoded expectations in `tests/vim-editor-adapter.test.ts` and `tests/package-manifest.test.ts`. The version should ideally be derived from the installed pair / `package.json` range rather than repeated as 61 literals.
2. **Revert the bump** — restore the `0.99.1` pin in `package.json` and the lockfile, and revisit the adoption once the vim fixtures are version-agnostic.

Option 1 matches the stated intent of the open-range policy (#1623), and #1597 ("make `SUPPORTED_VERSIONS` the single source of truth for the host gate") looks like the right home for removing the literal duplication.

### Related

- #1623 / #1624 — open-range Pi dependency policy that introduced the bump
- #1597 — refactor of the `SUPPORTED_VERSIONS` host gate
- #1430 — Vim fixtures assume one Pi TUI `Editor` constructor

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```
test at tests/vim-editor-adapter.test.ts:686:1
✖ empty logical line accepts cursor column zero (0.597488ms)
  Error: Unsupported Pi editor layout/version
      at createVimEditorAdapter (lib/vim-editor-adapter.ts:166:79)

test at tests/vim-editor-adapter.test.ts:693:1
✖ visual highlight spans wraps and treats collapsed paste as one selection unit (0.551547ms)
  Error: Unsupported Pi editor layout/version
      at createVimEditorAdapter (lib/vim-editor-adapter.ts:166:79)
```

```
=== test suite summary ===
FAIL  unit-tests
PASS  provider-contract
PASS  runtime-harness
1 stage(s) failed: unit-tests
```

title: feat(agents): publish the ODD phase (with its source) in the session presence record
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

The ODD phase is the most decision-dense signal the harness has, and it is the only one that never leaves the process that computed it.

`lib/odd-phase.ts` keeps the current phase in `processState` (`OddPhaseRegistry`), from two sources: an explicit report through the `gentle_odd_phase` tool, and the deterministic inference in `lib/odd-phase-inference.ts` (tool-to-phase map, deliberately conservative: an unknown tool or ambiguous shell command yields `undefined` and the label is left unchanged). The eight phases are `authorizing`, `exploring`, `researching`, `deciding`, `planning`, `implementing`, `checking`, `closing`.

`lib/orchestrator-presence.ts` already publishes, per live session, `<profile>/gentle-agents/presence/<sessionHash>.<incarnation>.header.json`, carrying `label`, `counts{running,queued,waiting,finished}`, `heartbeat`, `generation` and a sha256 `digest`, alongside the matching `.activity.json`. The phase is not among those fields, and no other channel carries it either (it is absent from the `gentle-agents.activity/v1` RPC payload too).

Consequence: no consumer other than the primary session's own input can show the phase. A reader that wants "which ODD step is the orchestrator on" has exactly one option today -- infer it -- which is precisely what #1438 refused to do: *"Pi exposes a binary agent-working lifecycle, not an authoritative ODD phase event, so guessing the phase from tool calls or assistant prose would be misleading."*

Measured evidence, not inference: 6 presence headers on one machine, one of them live (heartbeat < 1 s, `digest` verified against the activity bytes). All 6 carry `label` and `counts`; none carries a phase. The phase reported in that same live session applied correctly and is invisible in its own published record -- the same process publishes both, and only one of the two facts survives.

Who benefits: multi-session and desktop hosts, which already consume this record for cross-session discovery; and ODD's own premise, that the phase is a bounded, honest signal rather than a guess rendered as fact.

### Proposed outcome

Add an optional, provenance-carrying phase to the presence header.

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `phase` | One of the eight phase literals, or the field is absent. |
| `phase_source` | `explicit` or `inferred`, mirroring `OddPhaseSource` in `lib/odd-phase.ts`. Present only with `phase`. |

The source is load-bearing, not decoration: an explicit report is the orchestrator's own claim, an inference is best-effort from a tool name. A consumer that renders both identically is overstating what it knows, which is why `OddPhaseSource` already exists in the registry.

Constraints I believe are part of the change, not follow-up polish:

- **The exact-key contract moves in one commit.** `validHeader` in `lib/orchestrator-presence.ts` validates the envelope with an exact key-set check (`keys(h, [...])`). Adding a field changes producer and reader together, or a current reader classifies every record as `malformed` and rejects it. This is the only non-trivial part of the change.
- **Absent means not reported, never a carried-over value.** Per #1438 the label is cleared between turns and sessions, so a consumer must render "not reported" rather than reuse the previous phase.
- **No new I/O and no new timer.** A phase literal is <= 10 bytes; the 400 ms coalescing and 5 s heartbeat are unaffected.
- **Read-only metadata.** The phase is an observation about the session, and grants no review, delivery or authority state.

One open decision for maintainers: #432 defines `gentle-pi.agent-activity/v1` as a Gentle-owned projection, and its frozen entry contract already carries `model_id`, `model_provider` and `effort`. If that is the intended canonical seam, the phase belongs in that contract rather than in the presence header. I am happy to do either; the header is simply the narrower change that fixes the gap today, since the header is already the per-session, replayable, integrity-checked envelope that cross-session consumers read.

### Alternatives considered

- **Infer the phase on the consumer side from the activity or thread.** Rejected: that is the exact thing #1438 refused, and it re-derives outside the process a mapping (`lib/odd-phase-inference.ts`) that already exists inside it, so the two can drift.
- **Publish it on the `activity/v1` RPC summary only.** Rejected as the sole route: that path is gated on `GENTLE_SHELL_INTERACTIVE_HOST=1` and is in-process, so it does not address cross-session visibility, which is where the gap actually hurts.
- **A separate sidecar file.** Rejected: a second record to keep in sync with the header's `generation`/`digest`, for one short field.
- **Keep showing `working...`.** That is today's behavior, and is the reason the gap exists.

### Additional context

Environment: macOS 26.6.2 (build 25G83), arm64; Pi 0.99.2; gentle-pi 3.7.0 at commit 1162ce90 (branch `main`); gentle-ai 3.7.0; Node v22.15.1; TERM=xterm-256color.

Observed header, exactly as published by a live session (session hash shortened; personal paths and project labels removed):

```json
{"schema":1,
 "sessionHash":"b2c975a9<...>","incarnation":"b89e07c3<...>",
 "label":"<project>","heartbeat":1790824683514,"generation":1,
 "counts":{"running":0,"queued":0,"waiting":0,"finished":0},

```

In the same session, `gentle_odd_phase` reported `researching` and the registry accepted it. Nothing in that record, or in the matching activity document, reflects it.

Relevant source: `lib/odd-phase.ts`, `lib/odd-phase-inference.ts`, `lib/orchestrator-presence.ts` (`validHeader`, `PresencePublisher`), `docs/gentle-agents-activity.md`.

This is filed under the repository's issue-first policy. Related: #1438 (the delivered in-prompt half), #432 (projection design), #430 (status-bar consumer), #1262 (presence polling cost).

title: fix(quiet-tools): re-rendering an expanded read-with-image result crashes Pi (text.setText is not a function)
body:
### Before submitting
- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem
Pi exits with an uncaught `TypeError: text.setText is not a function` when `quiet-tools` re-renders an expanded `read` result that contains an image.

In `extensions/quiet-tools.ts`, the expanded read-with-image branch (lines 747-748 on `main` @ 1162ce90) delegates to Pi's official `read` `renderResult` and passes `sanitizedRenderContext(renderContext)`. `sanitizedRenderContext` (lines 653-660) spreads `...context`, which also forwards `context.lastComponent`.

Pi 0.99.2's `read` `renderResult` reuses that component:
```js
renderResult(result, options, theme, context) {
  let text = context.lastComponent ?? new Text("", 0, 0);
  return text.setText(formatReadResult(...)), text;
}
```
On the first render `lastComponent` is undefined, so it works. On any re-render, `lastComponent` is the `ToolCardBody` that quiet-tools returned the previous time (the `carded(...)` wrapper), not a Pi `Text`. `setText` does not exist on it, and the exception escapes the TUI render loop and terminates Pi.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Install Gentle Shell from `main` as a Pi package (`pi install git:github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-shell@main`) with Pi 0.99.2.
2. In a session, let the agent `read` an image file so the tool result contains image content.
3. Expand that tool result.
4. Trigger a re-render while it is expanded (resize or redraw the terminal, or any later repaint).

Observed path: the terminal (Warp, with herdr) stopped responding for a while; when it recovered and repainted, Pi exited with the error below.

### Expected and actual behavior
**Expected:** the expanded read result re-renders normally, as it does with the official Pi renderer.
**Actual:** Pi crashes with `pi exiting due to uncaughtException: TypeError: text.setText is not a function`, and the session must be resumed with `pi -r`.

**Suggested fix:** do not forward `lastComponent` to the official renderer (e.g. `{ ...sanitizedRenderContext(renderContext), lastComponent: undefined }`). Alternatively, keep a dedicated inner Pi `Text` per card and pass that as `lastComponent`.

### gentle-pi version
3.7.0 (installed from git `main` @ 1162ce90)

### Pi version
0.99.2

### Operating system
Windows

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)
```
pi exiting due to uncaughtException:
TypeError: text.setText is not a function
    at renderResult (<pi-coding-agent 0.99.2>/dist/bundle/chunks/chunk-3YAHQSW6.js:1027:574)
    at ToolCardBody.inner (<gentle-shell>/extensions/quiet-tools.ts:748:29)
    at <gentle-shell>/extensions/quiet-tools.ts:620:18
    at <gentle-shell>/lib/shell-card.ts:295:68
    at withChrome (<gentle-shell>/lib/shell-card.ts:107:12)
    at floatRows (<gentle-shell>/lib/shell-card.ts:294:16)
    at ToolCardBody.render (<gentle-shell>/extensions/quiet-tools.ts:619:37)
    at MouseRegion.render (<pi-coding-agent 0.99.2>/dist/bundle/chunks/chunk-7QSPBJKW.js:105:6834)
    at Container.render (<pi-coding-agent 0.99.2>/dist/bundle/chunks/chunk-7QSPBJKW.js:71:20190)
    at ToolExecutionComponent.render (<pi-coding-agent 0.99.2>/dist/bundle/chunks/chunk-3YAHQSW6.js:1154:1937)

A stack frame came from loaded extension `git:github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-shell@main`, which may be involved.
```
The terminal freeze before the crash is reported as observed context only; I have not verified that quiet-tools caused it.

title: review: START deterministically fails in candidate-view phase - git checkout-index fails although manual invocation succeeds
body:
# review: START deterministically fails in candidate-view phase — `git checkout-index` fails (exit≠0) although manual invocation succeeds

**Environment:** gentle-pi 3.7.0, contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, Windows 11 (NTFS, git 2.x via Git for Windows), repo with ~1.1k tracked files, ordinary review through the Pi compact facade.

## Failure

`review start` (committed range, ordinary mode) fails 3× in a row during the **candidate-view** phase:

```json
{"phase":"candidate-view","category":"git-failure","git_subcommand":"checkout-index",
 "timeout_ms":10000,"max_buffer_bytes":67108864,
 "message":"candidate-view Git command checkout-index failed; inspect the candidate state before any new START"}
```

- `lineage_created: false`, `mutation_outcome: none` — no authority created, retry-safe.
- The exact same `git checkout-index -f --prefix=<tmp>/ --all` run manually in the repo: **exit 0 in 0.25s** (pack is 5.4 MiB, ~1.1k objects) — so it is NOT the 10s timeout and NOT a slow tree.
- Fresh idempotency keys per attempt; `git status` clean; no `index.lock`.

## Suspects (for maintainers)

1. The native invocation likely targets a prefix inside `.git/gentle-ai/candidate-views/<uuid>/` — possibly the Windows absolute-path/UNC handling of that prefix, or an output-buffer capture issue (`max_buffer_bytes` exceeded path?) rather than the command itself failing.
2. Possibly related to the earlier-session stale `candidate-views` directories with `.owner.json` files (three views from previous sessions exist).
3. Reproducible on every START for this candidate; earlier candidates (same session, earlier commits) started fine minutes before — so something in the current tree/index state trips it.

## Context

This is the second native review-engine defect we hit today (see #741/#1154 for the capture-route rejection and #1513 for the generated-code budget). The candidate in question: 7 files / 243 insertions, base-diff projection, committed range. Happy to run any diagnostic command or capture more native output if pointed to where the stderr/stdout of the failing `checkout-index` lands.

## Workaround status

Candidate remains unreviewed natively; coverage was provided by an independent read-only security audit + full E2E smoke + 115 unit tests (documented in-repo).

title: bug(history): prompt history store and transcript bootstrap ignore the active agent home and always use ~/.pi/agent
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

The prompt history extension resolves every path from `homedir()` and ignores the agent home that gentle-shell actually runs with (`GENTLE_SHELL_HOME`, `--home`, `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`):

```ts
// extensions/history/index.ts:127-133
const AGENT_DIR = join(homedir(), ".pi", "agent");
const PI_HISTORY_ROOT = join(AGENT_DIR, "history");
const SESSIONS_ROOT = join(AGENT_DIR, "sessions");
```

This has two effects under gentle-shell's default isolated home (`~/.gentle-shell/agent`) or any custom home:

1. **Capture writes outside the active home.** With capture enabled, prompts typed in a gentle-shell session go to the vanilla Pi store `~/.pi/agent/history/`. This breaks the isolation of the gentle-shell home, and every home on the machine silently shares one store.
2. **Transcript bootstrap reads the wrong sessions.** The one-time bootstrap from project session transcripts (docs/prompt-history.md, "Legacy migration and seeding are opt-in") scans `~/.pi/agent/sessions`. gentle-shell's own transcripts live in `<agent home>/sessions`, so they are never imported; only vanilla-Pi transcripts are.

This is the same class of bug that `39c8d870 fix(banner): count MCP servers from the active agent dir` and `1393db7c fix(banner): read every startup count from the active agent dir` fixed for the startup banner.

### Steps to reproduce

Controlled reproduction (nothing real is touched):

1. `export GENTLE_SHELL_HOME=/tmp/gs/agent GENTLE_PI_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/gs/config HOME=/tmp/gs/home` (HOME is redirected only so the hardcoded path can be observed safely).
2. In a git repo under `/tmp`, run `gentle-shell` and enable `/gentle:customize` → History → `Prompt history capture: enable`.
3. Submit three prompts, then list the store: `find /tmp/gs/home/.pi/agent/history /tmp/gs/agent -path '*history*' -name '*.jsonl'`.
4. Leave gentle-shell. Run more sessions in the same repo so `/tmp/gs/agent/sessions/<project>/` holds transcripts. Start again and open `ctrl+shift+r`: only the prompts captured live are listed, and no `seed.jsonl` exists.
5. Copy the same session directory into `/tmp/gs/home/.pi/agent/sessions/` and restart: `seed.jsonl` now appears and the older prompts show up in the selector.

Observed in normal use as well: with capture enabled globally and every session running with `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=<home>/.gentle-shell/agent` (default isolated home), new files appeared under `<home>/.pi/agent/history/` (registry entries for two different projects) while `<home>/.gentle-shell/agent/history/` was never created.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: the history root and sessions root follow the active agent dir (`getAgentDir()`, the same source Pi and the banner use), so `<agent home>/history/` and `<agent home>/sessions/` are used.

Actual: `$HOME/.pi/agent/history/projects/<hash>/<instance>.jsonl` is written while `GENTLE_SHELL_HOME` points elsewhere, and transcript bootstrap creates `seed.jsonl` only from `$HOME/.pi/agent/sessions`, never from `<agent home>/sessions`.

### gentle-pi version

main @ cc36bd8d (package.json 3.7.0); the same lines are unchanged at main @ 1162ce90

### Pi version

0.99.1

### Operating system

Windows (WSL)

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
# capture enabled, GENTLE_SHELL_HOME=/tmp/gs/agent, HOME=/tmp/gs/home
/tmp/gs/home/.pi/agent/history/projects/<hash>/<instance>.jsonl   (3 lines)
/tmp/gs/home/.pi/agent/history/registry.json
# nothing history-related under /tmp/gs/agent
# after copying <agent home>/sessions/<project> into $HOME/.pi/agent/sessions and restarting:
/tmp/gs/home/.pi/agent/history/projects/<hash>/seed.jsonl  (2.8K)
```

title: bug(review): committing a candidate's untracked path strands its open lineage — preflight rejects the changed untracked inventory and abandon can no longer derive its inputs
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

A workspace review whose candidate includes an **untracked** path becomes unreachable if that path is committed while the lineage is still open. Committing the file takes it out of the untracked inventory, the negotiated request of the open lineage keeps expecting the old inventory digest, and every later lineage-bound `status` fails at preflight:

```text
code: invalid_request
message: The negotiated review request is invalid.
cause: untracked inventory changed; rerun `gentle-ai review status --cwd <repo> --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --agent <runtime> --next-transition` before selecting paths
retry_safe: true
mutation_outcome: not_started
```

The lineage is then stranded: it cannot be approved, corrected, or even queried. Refreshing the untracked declaration through bound `inspect` (`untrackedScope: "exclude"`, which reports the new inventory digest with `untracked_selection: not-required`) does **not** repair it — the lineage still expects its original digest.

The stranding then collapses into #1159: audited `abandon` needs `expectedRevision`, `snapshotIdentity`, `capturedLensResults` and `findingsPresent`, and those four were only obtainable from the lineage-bound `status` that now fails. Renegotiation is a dead end because the facade exposes no permitted read-only inventory operation, and inferring the values from admitted results or persisted state is exactly what the mirrored contract forbids. So the lineage is not merely blocked from moving forward; it also cannot be discarded.

How this differs from related reports:

- #1159 describes the abandon-side gap generically: the facade cannot expose the discarded-work inputs. This report adds the cause that turns that gap into a dead end, because the `status` read that would have supplied them stops working first.
- #1596 concerns a **committed-range** lineage that dead-ends after the refuter, where STATUS demands an untracked selection and then stops as `corrupted_or_unverifiable_authority`. Here the lineage is a workspace review, and the failure is a preflight rejection of a changed untracked inventory.
- #1324 refreshes the untracked declaration through bound STATUS on a workspace review. This report shows that refresh is insufficient when a path leaves the untracked inventory entirely.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Leave one candidate path untracked and start an ordinary review on the workspace, selecting it as intended untracked (`inspect` with `untrackedScope: "select"`, then START). The frozen projection records `intended_untracked: ["<path>"]` and an inventory digest.
2. Take the lineage through the lens and the refuter until it reaches `correction_required`. (Any non-terminal state reached through a capture works.)
3. Apply the correction and **commit** the candidate, including the previously untracked `<path>`. This is the ordinary "close the work unit" step.
4. Call `gentle_review` `status` with only `lineageId`.
5. Observe the preflight failure quoted above.
6. Call `gentle_review` `inspect` with `untrackedScope: "exclude"` to refresh the declaration (new inventory digest, `untracked_selection: not-required`), then call `status` with the lineage again.
7. Observe the same preflight failure. The lineage is unreachable.
8. Call `gentle_review` `abandon` with only `lineage`, `actor` and `reason`.
9. Observe `native-input-required` for exactly `expectedRevision`, `snapshotIdentity`, `capturedLensResults`, `findingsPresent` — the four fields whose only facade source was the `status` that now fails.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: either the preflight tolerates a path dropping out of the untracked inventory (the review froze specific candidate trees; committing the same bytes does not change them), or the failure names a facade route that re-binds the lineage to the current inventory, or `abandon` derives its discarded-work inputs natively as #1159 requests.

Actual: the lineage is stranded in a non-terminal state with no facade route forward and no facade route to discard it.

### Impact

Any workspace review that selects an untracked path and later commits it strands the lineage. With RDD enabled, committing a reviewed work unit is the normal end of a task, so the sequence is easy to walk into: the work looks finished and the review lifecycle is silently dead behind it. The store accumulates unreachable non-terminal lineages that no facade operation can clear. Two lineages were left in that state in a single session.

### Environment

- gentle-pi 3.7.0
- Pi coding agent with the mirrored provider bundle 1.2.0
- Linux

### Relevant logs or error output

```text
operation: status
status: blocked
native_failure:
  phase: preflight
  code: invalid_request
  message: The negotiated review request is invalid.
  cause: untracked inventory changed; rerun `gentle-ai review status --cwd <repo> --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --agent <runtime> --next-transition` before selecting paths
  retry_safe: true
  mutation_outcome: not_started
mutation_performed: false
```

```text
operation: abandon
status: blocked
outcome: native-input-required
native_operation: review abandon
missing_input:
  - expectedRevision
  - snapshotIdentity
  - capturedLensResults
  - findingsPresent
mutation_performed: false
mutation_outcome: none
next_action: resubmit-with-exact-native-maintenance-input
```

title: review-host-relay: reviewer at thinking:high exhausts the shared output budget and returns empty output (stopReason: length)
body:
## Summary

The in-process reviewer completion sets no `maxTokens`, so the routing entry's `thinking` label shares the model's entire output ceiling with the JSON answer. A reasoning model at `thinking: high` can spend the whole budget on reasoning and return zero text, which the host relay reports as `reviewer-empty-output` with `stopReason: length`.

This failure wears the costume of a candidate-size problem (and, later, of a host-session-context problem). Neither was the cause, and both sent operators to shrink scope for no reason: a 46 KB candidate failed exactly like a 1.24 MB one.

## Environment

- `gentle-ai` 3.7.0 (Go), `gentle-pi` 3.7.0
- Reviewer routing entry `review-reliability` → `nan/deepseek-v4-flash`, `thinking: high`
- Model declaration: `reasoning: true`, `maxTokens: 32768`, `api: openai-completions`
- Host relay transport: `pi_host_relay`

## Where it happens

- `lib/inprocess-reviewer.ts` — the `SimpleStreamOptions` built for the completion carries `reasoning` but no `maxTokens`, so pi applies the model ceiling and reasoning tokens are drawn from the same pool as the answer:

  ```ts
  const options: SimpleStreamOptions = {
    signal: combinedSignal,
    timeoutMs: request.timeoutMs,
    ...,
    ...(reasoning.reasoning === undefined ? {} : { reasoning: reasoning.reasoning }),
  };
  ```

- `resolveReasoning` (~L134) forwards the routing label verbatim.
- The empty-text refusal (~L325) reports only `stopReason`, with no sign of the budget or the reasoning label that consumed it.

## Evidence

Seven `reviewer-empty-output` failures across four transactions, in two different Pi host sessions — one of them freshly started for this purpose — on candidates from 46 KB to 1.24 MB:

| Candidate                          | `stopReason` | elapsed |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------ | ------- |
| 89 files / 23 841 lines / 1.24 MB  | `length`     | 180 s   |
| same                               | `stop`       | 1.5 s   |
| same                               | `length`     | 162 s   |
| 7 files / 11 573 lines / 623 KB    | `length`     | 139 s   |
| same                               | `length`     | 1 s     |
| 30 files / 767 lines / 46 KB       | `length`     | 181 s   |
| 89 files / 23 890 lines / 1.24 MB  | `length`     | 194 s   |

- The relay's own bound was ~17.6 min (`timeout_ms: 1058643`), so none of these were timeouts.
- Every attempt followed the documented route (fresh bound STATUS, which reoffered the identical one-slot binding, then the forecast and its acknowledgement). Nothing was admitted, no acknowledgement was issued, and **no authority was burned**; the collect slot stays open.
- A fresh host session produced the identical failure, which rules out host-session context as the explanation.

## Counter-evidence, unresolved

One earlier review in the same repository closed `approved` over a 1.10 MB candidate with the same single lens and the same routing profile. The mechanism above does not explain that success, and I am not going to invent an explanation for it. Either the provider's accounting of reasoning tokens against the output ceiling is variable, or something else also contributes.

## Suggested directions

1. Reserve an answer budget instead of letting reasoning consume the whole ceiling.
2. Derive `maxTokens` from the model minus a reasoning allowance for the selected label.
3. Refuse typed when the ceiling cannot hold both, before launching the completion.
4. At minimum, make the empty-output refusal surface the output ceiling and the reasoning label. Today it reads as a candidate defect and sends operators to narrow scope — a costly wrong turn that this report had to disprove twice.

title: bug(skill-registry): unhandled async EMFILE from directory watcher crashes pi on startup
body:
### Problem

`pi` exits on startup with an uncaught exception coming from the skill-registry extension's directory watchers:

```
pi exiting due to uncaughtException:
Error: EMFILE: too many open files, watch
    at FSWatcher._handle.onchange (node:internal/fs/watchers:269:21) {
  errno: -24, syscall: 'watch', code: 'EMFILE', filename: null
}
```

`startSkillRegistryWatcher` (`extensions/skill-registry.ts`) calls `watch(dir, { recursive: true }, refresh)` for each skill directory. `watch()` returns synchronously and reports failures later as an `'error'` event on the `FSWatcher`. The extension only wraps the synchronous call in `try/catch` and attaches no `'error'` listener, so an asynchronous failure becomes an `uncaughtException` and takes down the whole host process.

The EMFILE here is not real fd exhaustion (few open fds, `RLIMIT_NOFILE` ~1M). On macOS 26.5 with Node 26.7, `fs.watch` on any directory (even an empty temp dir) is created successfully and then emits EMFILE asynchronously, while `fs.watch` on a file and `fs.watchFile` work. Whatever the environment cause, a best-effort watcher should never crash pi.

### Steps to reproduce

1. macOS 26.5 + Node 26.7, run `pi` with gentle-pi installed from source.
2. Start with at least one existing skill directory (project or user).
3. Quick check outside pi: `node -e "require('fs').watch(require('os').tmpdir()).on('error',console.log)"` and observe EMFILE.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: a watcher failure degrades gracefully (automatic registry refresh is disabled; startup and manual refresh still work).
Actual: pi crashes with `uncaughtException`.

### Environment

- gentle-pi: main @ ab60cb45
- Pi: 0.99.2
- OS: macOS

### Proposed fix

Attach an `'error'` listener to each `FSWatcher` that closes it and drops it from `activeWatchers`. PR to follow.

title: feat(explore): allow read-only web research and MCP queries
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

These operational checks were completed while preparing this request.

### Problem or opportunity

`gentle-ai-explore` currently allows only `read`, `grep`, `find`, and `codegraph`. This prevents it from performing web searches, fetching external documentation, or querying read-only MCP resources, even when those integrations are available in the parent session.

The desired workflow is for the explorer itself to conduct authorized remote research and return supporting sources and findings, rather than handing that work back to the orchestrator.

This request concerns generic exploration, independently of SDD. It proposes a new capability, not unrestricted inheritance of the parent's tools.

### Proposed outcome

Support explicitly selected read-only web and MCP operations in `gentle-ai-explore`, while preserving its read-only role.

Acceptance criteria:

- Approved search, documentation-fetching, and resource-query tools can be made available and usable in the child session.
- Permissions are enforced per tool or remote method. Allowing a generic MCP gateway must not expose unrestricted remote operations.
- Write, update, and delete operations remain blocked, as do installation, authentication changes, and configuration changes.
- Unknown or unclassified remote operations are denied by default. Tool descriptions or MCP read-only annotations alone do not grant permission.
- Missing or unavailable capabilities are reported clearly before remote research begins.
- Tests demonstrate successful approved queries and rejection of mutation attempts, including through generic gateways where applicable.

The exact configuration and enforcement mechanism is open for maintainer design. The goal is safe delegated research, not bypassing existing permission boundaries.

### Alternatives considered

- Parent-only research: works around the limitation, but defeats delegation of the external research itself.
- Unrestricted MCP access: exceeds the explorer's read-only responsibilities.
- Manually extending the agent's tool list: may expose tools but does not establish a safe method-level permission boundary for generic gateways.

### Additional context

Observed with `gentle-pi` 3.7.0. The packaged and installed global explorer definitions both contain the same four-tool allowlist. The installed launcher applies the agent's tools through `--tools`.

Relevant implementation:

- `assets/agents/gentle-ai-explore.md`
- `lib/agents-runner.ts`, `childArguments`

Related, but distinct:

- #1269 addresses capability-aware delegation. This proposal adds safe remote-query capabilities to the explorer instead of merely routing incompatible tasks elsewhere.
- #1276 proposes declarative MCP discovery and on-demand loading. This request is narrower: the generic explorer's read-only permissions and ability to perform remote research.

No MCP connection or authentication failure is claimed here. The verified limitation is the explorer's effective tool allowlist.

title: refactor(vim): make SUPPORTED_VERSIONS the single source of truth for the host gate
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-shell/issues) and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand that PRs will be rejected if the linked issue does not have `status:approved`

### Problem or opportunity

The set of verified Pi hosts is currently known in three places and nothing keeps them in sync:

- `lib/vim-editor-adapter.ts` holds it privately for the identity gate (`SUPPORTED_VERSIONS`);
- `extensions/gentle-shell.ts` repeats it inside `resolveVimRuntime()` in the bundled-graph branch;
- and repeats it again in the installed-pair branch.

After #1582 narrowed the list to `{"0.99.1"}`, an edit that touches only one or two of those sites changes behaviour silently: a host can be admitted by the gate while one resolver path refuses to certify it, or the reverse. The failure mode is quiet — the adapter is designed to fail closed, so a mismatch degrades Vim to ordinary editing instead of reporting the inconsistency.

@dnlrsls suggested this as a smaller follow-up on the superseded #1572 ("the single-source-of-truth refactor for `SUPPORTED_VERSIONS`, which could go in a smaller follow-up").

### Proposed outcome

Export the verified-host list from `lib/vim-editor-adapter.ts` as the single source of truth, and have both `resolveVimRuntime()` branches read it instead of restating the versions. No behaviour change: the admitted set stays `{"0.99.1"}` and every identity proof is untouched (host package name, matching `CustomEditor`/`Editor` classes, prototype chain, bundled `VERSION`).

A unit assertion that the gate and both resolver branches consult the same list would keep the invariant enforced rather than merely documented.

### Alternatives considered

- Leaving the three sites duplicated and relying on review. That is the current state, and the drift is silent by design (fail-closed), which is why the inconsistency is worth removing rather than documenting.
- Moving `resolveVimRuntime()` into the adapter module. Bigger than needed: the resolver depends on the extension's `CustomEditor` subclass identity, so it belongs where it is.

### Additional context

The change shipped as one part of #1572, which was closed as superseded by #1582 and #1594; this refactor is the piece the maintainer flagged as still worth carrying, and it is independent of the peer-dependency work. Happy to open the small PR once the issue is approved.

title: bug(review): committed-range lineage in correction_required dead-ends — STATUS demands an untracked selection, then stops as corrupted_or_unverifiable_authority
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

These checks attest to the reporting agent's completed actions (a duplicate search across open and closed issues, and a privacy scan of this body), not actions attributed to the user. Related reports are distinguished below.

### Problem

A native ordinary review of a **committed range** (START with an explicit `baseRef` and `committedOnly: true`) reached `correction_required` when the refuter capture closed the lineage. From there, no Pi facade route reaches the provider-owned correction route. Every path either reports an unrelated target, asks for an untracked-path selection that a committed-only lineage should not need, or stops terminally with `corrupted_or_unverifiable_authority`. The lineage is stranded in `correction_required`.

How this differs from related reports:

- #433 (closed) fixed the committed base selector on STATUS. That part now works: STATUS accepts `{"baseRef":…,"committedOnly":true}` and reports `applicability: current_target` and `state: correction_required`. The failure happens after that.
- #1324 refreshes the untracked declaration through bound STATUS on a workspace review. Here the same refresh on a committed-range lineage produces a terminal `corrupted_or_unverifiable_authority` stop.
- #871 and #941 concern pre-lineage `select-intended-untracked` before START. Here that operation is not a valid route at all. In `extensions/gentle-ai.ts` (around line 8309), the operation ends in `executeReviewControllerOperation({operation: START, …})`, so on a bound lineage it would create a new lineage rather than continue this one. It was rejected with `intended-untracked-selection-binding-rejected`.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed session sequence. It is not yet reduced to a synthetic fixture.

1. Commit a multi-file candidate on a feature branch; here it was 19 tracked paths and 1525 changed lines. The repository has a large unrelated untracked inventory (screenshots, scratch notes). The candidate itself has no untracked paths.
2. Start an ordinary review with `{"mode":"ordinary","baseRef":"<base>","committedOnly":true}`. This gives a medium tier with the `review-reliability` lens. The frozen snapshot has `kind: base-diff`, `intended_untracked: []`, and `initial_atomic_start.selector: {kind: base-diff, base_ref: <base>, intended_untracked: null}`.
3. Capture the reviewer. It reports one inferential CRITICAL finding, so the next transition is `provider_refuter_required`.
4. Capture the refuter. The response is `outcome: native-last-event-closure`, `state: correction_required`. Its `status_continuation` names `gentle-ai review status … --lineage=<lineage> --base-ref=<base> --committed-only=true`.
5. Call `gentle_review` `status` with only `lineageId`. It reports `applicability: unrelated`, `action: start` and `projection.kind: current-changes`. This STATUS projected the uncommitted, unrelated workspace edits instead of the lineage.
6. Call `gentle_review` `status` with `lineageId` and `input: {"baseRef":"<base>","committedOnly":true}`. It reports `applicability: current_target`, `state: correction_required`, `next_transition: {kind: collect, reason_code: intended_untracked_selection_required}`, plus a `selectionBinding`.
7. Call `gentle_review` `select-intended-untracked` with that exact `selectionBinding` and `intendedUntracked: []`. The outcome is `intended-untracked-selection-binding-rejected`, with no mutation.
8. Call `gentle_review` `status` with `lineageId` and `input: {"baseRef":"<base>","committedOnly":true,"untrackedScope":"exclude","expectedUntrackedInventory":"<digest from step 6>","intendedUntracked":[]}`.
   - The first attempt used a stale digest and failed with `invalid_request`, cause `untracked inventory changed`.
   - Retried with the fresh `eligible_untracked_inventory` from an immediately preceding STATUS, it returns `applicability: current_target`, `state: correction_required`, `action: stop`, `next_transition: {kind: stop, reason_code: corrupted_or_unverifiable_authority}`, `forecast.horizon: terminal`.
9. The review state file did not change across steps 5–8: same `revision`, still `correction_required`. Only the transaction lock files were touched.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: for a lineage started with `baseRef` and `committedOnly: true`, bound STATUS in `correction_required` offers the provider-owned correction route (correction plan / correction-candidate collection). It should not ask for an untracked-path selection, because a committed-range candidate cannot contain untracked paths. If a selection is required, declaring `untrackedScope: "exclude"` with the current inventory digest should lead to that correction route.

Actual:
- Without the committed selector, STATUS reports an unrelated `current-changes` target.
- With the selector, STATUS demands `intended_untracked_selection_required`.
- The only selection operation in the facade (`select-intended-untracked`) is a pre-lineage START path and rejects the binding.
- Declaring the selection through bound STATUS stops terminally with `corrupted_or_unverifiable_authority`.

The lineage cannot be corrected, approved or acknowledged. The only exits left are abandoning it or disabling the review switch.

### gentle-pi version

3.7.0 (from source, commit 290c0dc1)

### Pi version

0.99.1

### Operating system

Linux

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
# step 4 — refuter capture
{"tool":"gentle_review_capture","status":"closed","outcome":"native-last-event-closure","closure":{"schema":"gentle-ai.review-last-event-closure/v1","operation":"review.capture-refuter","state":"correction_required","action":"candidate-caused severe findings require one bounded correction","status_continuation":{"operation":"review.status","command":"gentle-ai review status --cwd=<repo> --contract=gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --next-transition=true --lineage=<lineage> --agent=pi --base-ref=<base> --committed-only=true", ...}}}

# step 5 — bare bound STATUS
"applicability":"unrelated","action":"start","projection":{"kind":"current-changes","projection":"workspace", ...},"next_transition":{"kind":"collect","reason_code":"intended_untracked_selection_required"}

# step 6 — STATUS with {"baseRef":"<base>","committedOnly":true}
"applicability":"current_target","authority":{"state":"correction_required", ...},"action":"collect","next_transition":{"kind":"collect","reason_code":"intended_untracked_selection_required"}

# step 7 — select-intended-untracked with the exact selectionBinding from step 6
{"operation":"select-intended-untracked","status":"blocked","outcome":"intended-untracked-selection-binding-rejected","mutation_performed":false,"mutation_outcome":"none"}

# step 8a — STATUS with the selection and a stale inventory digest
"native_failure":{"phase":"preflight","code":"invalid_request","cause":"untracked inventory changed; rerun `gentle-ai review status --cwd <repo> --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --agent <runtime> --next-transition` before selecting paths"}

# step 8b — STATUS with the selection and the fresh inventory digest
"applicability":"current_target","state":"correction_required","action":"stop","next_transition":{"kind":"stop","reason_code":"corrupted_or_unverifiable_authority"},"forecast":{"horizon":"terminal","steps":[{"step":1,"kind":"stop","reason_code":"corrupted_or_unverifiable_authority","description":"Review authority is corrupted or unverifiable"}]}
```

title: feat(profiles): directory-based profile rules so unpinned clones stop silently falling back to the global profile
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Profile pins live in `<git-common-dir>/gentle-ai/profile-pin.json`, so each pin covers exactly one clone. Any clone without a pin — a fresh clone, or a sibling repository that belongs to the same project — routes with the global active profile, and nothing in the session says so.

Concrete case: one project is split across two clones (automation + content). The first was pinned to a GPT/GLM profile; the second had no pin, so its subagents ran on the global profile's models for days. I only found out by reading the subagent session files.

A second, sharper problem: in a pinned repository, `/gentle:models` shows `Current profile: <pinned> (pinned)` in the header, but its rows are the **global** routing, not the pinned profile's. Worse, the `u` key is labelled `capture session in "<pinned> (pinned)"`, yet `updateCurrentProfileFromSavedRouting` snapshots `readGlobalEffectiveModelConfig()` and writes it into the pinned profile. One keypress silently overwrites the pinned profile with the global routing, and the repository then runs on global models while still showing "pinned".

### Proposed outcome

1. Directory-scoped profile rules in the global config, for example `path-profiles.json`:
   ```json
   { "rules": [
     { "path": "~/work/university/**", "profile": "drain" },
     { "path": "~/work/apps/project-x-*", "profile": "drain" }
   ] }
   ```
   First match wins; `~`, `*` and `**` are supported; symlinks are resolved on both sides. Resolved at launch as a layer below the local pin and the repo declaration, and above the global profile.
2. A matching rule also sets the orchestrator on new sessions (not on resume or fork), so one rule covers the whole session.
3. A startup notice that names the effective profile and its source (`local pin`, `repo`, `path rule`, `global`), so a fallback to global is never silent.
4. In a pinned repository, `/gentle:models` either shows the pinned profile's rows or clearly labels the rows as global; and `u` captures the routing actually in effect for this repository (the pinned one), or is disabled there.

### Alternatives considered

Pinning every clone by hand plus a project `.pi/settings.json` for the orchestrator works, but it is per-clone bookkeeping that fails silently.

I'm running a local extension that implements 1–3 on `session_start`: it writes the repo declaration `.pi/gentle-ai/profile.json` (only when that path is Git-ignored and untracked), calls `setModel` / `setThinkingLevel` with the profile's orchestrator, and skips `--mode rpc` children and explicit `--model` launches. Verified: the orchestrator switches, and a real subagent child runs on the profile's model without being switched. Happy to share it or open a PR if the direction fits.

### Additional context

Related: #1064 (session-bound profiles), #1478 (orchestrator selection), #1074 (repository pin), #1176 (Status showed the global profile).

title: feat(shell): per-session statistics module — cost, tokens, time and a billable report
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

#1545 is the visible half: Gentle Shell renders exactly one session-level cost number, and it is the orchestrator's own spend, so as soon as a subagent runs the number under-reports what the session actually spent. The same gap runs deeper:

- **No breakdown exists anywhere.** There is no per-subagent, per-model or per-agent-class cost or token aggregate; `TaskStore.summary()` carries counts only, and the delegated cost never crosses the RPC wire (`gentle-agents.activity/v1` has no `cost` or `tokens`).
- **No time exists.** There is no per-turn model latency, no per-tool duration, and no honest split between measured and derived time.
- **No report exists.** A human billing hours at a rate cannot turn any of this into an hours report.
- **The one number that does exist is recomputed per frame.** `sessionCost()` iterates every session entry, and it runs on every render because `buildShellBarModel` calls it. That is the exact shape of the render-cost regressions this repository has already paid for (#1142, #1254, #1011).

Who benefits: an operator billing hours at an hourly rate, who needs the same panel to produce the hours report and its cost, and anyone who wants to know where a long session's time and money actually went.

### Proposed outcome

A self-contained per-session statistics module, layered so each part is independently reviewable and useful on its own:

1. **Canonical record, no coercion.** A `SessionUsageRecord` whose cost distinguishes a provider-reported `0` from an unreported cost, so a partial total can be shown honestly. (Removes the `?? 0` / `|| 0` at both ingestion sites.)
2. **Session cost total in the bar and header** — orchestrator plus every subagent, with an opt-in `+` marker when the total is partial, and the scan moved off the render path onto events. This is the visible fix for #1545.
3. **Transcript reader and replay** for parent and child sessions. The transcripts, not the live event stream, are the backbone: both carry model, the six token counters, the full cost breakdown and a timestamp per assistant message, and one normalizer serves both.
4. **Pure aggregation engine** — session, subagent, model, agent class and project totals, with provenance on every monetary, token and count figure.
5. **Timeline** — per-turn model latency and per-tool duration by timestamp pairing, reported as median and p90 with the sample size (never a mean), the parallel-batch artifact flagged, and the harness's `cd <cwd> &&` prefix normalized.
6. **Local opt-in JSONL store** with bounded retention, following the #1302 shape: local, silent, `DO_NOT_TRACK`/`CI` opt-out, nothing ever transmitted, and never the telemetry path.
7. **Versioned RPC transport and exporters** — `gentle-shell.statistics/v1` on its own widget key, plus markdown/CSV/JSON from the same aggregate so the export and any UI cannot diverge.
8. **Overlay view and command** — `ctx.ui.custom(..., { overlay: true })` plus a `/` command, and one additive `alt+k` palette row.
9. **Billable-hours report** — hourly rate, currency, a rounding policy and a date range, exported through the same renderers. Opt-in, because not everyone bills hours.

Every figure states measured / derived / partial, and an unavailable value renders as unavailable, never as `0`.

### Configuration (environment variables)

The module adds no settings UI and no config file: the whole surface is environment variables, so it stays out of the repo's persisted-settings path and out of `/gentle:usage`. This is the part I would most like your opinion on — env vs a config file vs a `/` command.

| Variable | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `GENTLE_BILLABLE` | unset | Opt-in for the billable report. `1` enables it (hours only); `0` disables it and wins over the rate. |
| `GENTLE_BILLABLE_RATE` | `0` | Amount per hour. Setting it enables the feature. `0` reports the hours without an amount. |
| `GENTLE_BILLABLE_CURRENCY` | `USD` | Currency label, upper-cased. |
| `GENTLE_BILLABLE_ROUNDING` | `none` | `none`, `nearest-6`, `nearest:15`, `up-15` … A malformed or non-positive policy fails closed to `none`, so a typo cannot inflate an invoice. |
| `GENTLE_STATISTICS_STORE` | unset | `0` / `false` / `off` disables the local JSONL store. |
| `DO_NOT_TRACK`, `CI`, `GITHUB_ACTIONS` | unset | Any truthy value disables the store (the #1302 opt-out convention). |

The agent home is read from the existing `GENTLE_PI_AGENT_HOME` / `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` (falling back to `~/.pi/agent`), so the module follows the profile the session already uses.

Env is read once at extension activation, so a change needs a restart. A config file under the agent home, or a `/` command that writes one, is the alternative; I am happy to switch if that fits the repository better. Nothing here is network-bound: the store is a local artifact and the only optional network access is the deferred pricing catalog.

### Alternatives considered

- **A sidebar rail.** Not reachable from an extension today — the painted section list is hardcoded and the header/Status slots are singletons — so the panel is an overlay. The rail extension point is #1063, and this proposal deliberately does not duplicate it.
- **A fully separate plugin.** Partial, and measured rather than assumed. A plugin can carry the read/aggregate/report half (3–9), but not (1), which is a producer-side edit inside `gentle-pi`, nor (2), which needs the single-owner footer. A plugin's only additive hook is a separate `setStatus` line, which is a different feature from what #1545 asked for. The measured boundary is recorded in the epic.
- **Reusing the telemetry path.** Refused: `docs/telemetry.md` forbids metrics disk storage and session reconstruction, so the store is a separate local artifact.
- **Estimating a price when the provider reports none.** Not done. There is no pricing catalog in the repository; the module says so instead of inventing a number.

### Additional context

**The panel.** The statistics overlay, in a real session (this screenshot predates the last layout tweak, which drops the blank lines and the Efficiency section on a short terminal):

![Statistics panel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/efirvida/gentle-shell/statistics-panel-asset/docs/assets/statistics-panel.png)

**The epic.** The architecture, the data catalog, the measured/derived/unavailable split and the settled decisions live in a fork epic: efirvida/gentle-shell#1.

**Related upstream issues.** Directly resolved: #1545, #975, #1263. Partially (reporting half only): #636, #731. Consumer / enabler: #1081. Dependency avoided by design: #1063. Prior art adopted: #1302. Precedent for the RPC discipline: `gentle-agents.activity/v1`. Related and already closed: #1547.

**Non-blocking (hard).** No filesystem or network I/O in a render path; the bar and the panel read a cached value that events update; transcript reads are streamed and bounded; publishing uses one fire-and-forget attempt slot and discards while busy; failures are silent and never enter the shared event bus; shutdown never waits on a report or a store write; the only optional network access is a deferred pricing catalog, and the subscription-quota refresh is explicitly not part of this module.

**Core-change footprint.** The producer fix (1) and the bar/header total (2), plus one additive `alt+k` palette row for the command. That row is safe to merge with the feature absent because `buildCommandPaletteGroups` drops a catalog entry whose command is not registered.

**Evidence.** A complete implementation with focused and full-suite tests exists in a maintained fork (nine dependency-ordered work units, each with its own tests; the full serialized unit stage is green). I can open it here as a PR against `main` if you want to carry it, or keep it as a plugin if ownership of (1) and (2) is declined. The epic that drives it records the architecture, the data catalog, the measured/derived/unavailable split, the non-blocking rules and the settled decisions.

**Out of scope.** The subscription-quota path (`/gentle:usage`), telemetry emission to any collector, the startup HUD stats panel, and any behavioural change to make agents consume less context — only the reporting half of #636 is in scope.

title: feat(usage): support the new OpenAI ChatGPT plan login
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Pi now supports signing in with a ChatGPT plan through the `openai` provider, separately from the older `openai-codex` (legacy) provider. Gentle Shell's subscription-usage integration currently fetches usage for `openai-codex`, but not for `openai`. As a result, after signing in through the new OpenAI/ChatGPT flow, `/gentle:usage` does not show the ChatGPT plan usage. The screenshot shows `OpenAI` stored while `OpenAI Codex (legacy)` is unconfigured.

### Proposed outcome

Support the new OpenAI/ChatGPT plan OAuth flow in the Gentle Shell status bar and `/gentle:usage` panel, using an appropriate usage source for that flow. Distinguish subscription OAuth from ordinary OpenAI API-key usage so API usage is not presented as ChatGPT-plan quota.

### Alternatives considered

Use the older `OpenAI Codex (legacy)` login, but it is a separate legacy provider and does not solve the missing usage display for users signed in through the new `openai` flow.

### Additional context

Pi introduced the new ChatGPT-plan login through `/login openai` in v0.99.0: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/releases/tag/v0.99.0

The existing Gentle Shell issues #1041 and #1155 concern legacy Codex account-switch staleness and percentage presentation, respectively; neither addresses usage support for the new OpenAI provider.

title: feat(harness): let agents fill repo issue templates with the form's labels applied
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Agents that submit issue reports through the CLI or the API cannot apply the labels a repository's issue form declares: the REST API silently drops payload labels for users without push access ("Only users with push access can set labels for new issues. Labels are silently dropped otherwise."), while the web form handler applies the form's declared labels for any submitter (verified empirically: this repository's #751 and vitest-dev/vitest #11380/#11383 - authors with no write access applied their own form's labels at creation, as their own actor). The gap is specific to forms that declare labels; label-less forms lose nothing through the CLI.

Today an agent (or any terminal user) has two incomplete paths: `gh issue create -T` uses the template as body text with no form rendering and no form labels, and the web path applies labels but takes the user out of the terminal. Repositories lose fast, correctly-labeled reports, and agents either ship unlabeled issues (needing maintainer triage) or interrupt the user with a browser.

### Proposed outcome

Agents and terminal users should be able to fill a repository's issue templates from the terminal with the form's labels applied, degrading gracefully by permission:

1. Read the YAML form schema (field `id`s are the canonical identifiers for URL query parameter prefills).
2. Fill the fields and open the pre-filled new-issue URL (`template` + per-field params) for a one-click human submit - the form path applies its labels for anyone, and the human Submit click keeps the label gate honest.
3. Fall back to the CLI path (`-T` or a form-shaped body) only when the form declares no labels or the actor has triage access, with an explicit warning when payload labels will be dropped silently.

This could land as a gh extension or as agent guidance in an issue-creation workflow. `gh issue create --web` already opens the template chooser, but its preview URL does not pass the template, so prefills land on the blank issue rather than the form.

### Alternatives considered

- `gh issue create -T`: uses the template as starting body text only; no form-field rendering; labels come only from `--label` and are silently dropped without triage.
- GitHub MCP `issue_write` (create): same REST API gate for labels; no template/form support.
- URL `labels` query parameter: permission-gated - the docs state the URL returns 404 without label permission.
- `gh issue create --web`: opens the chooser (good door), but the preview URL does not include the template, so prefills land on the blank issue.
- yudai-nkt/gh-form: previews a form as HTML; does not fill or submit it.

### Additional context

Verified evidence: this repository's #751 (author with no special access created the issue via the web Feature Request form; the form's labels were applied by the author's own account one second after creation) vs #1573 (same repository, created via gh CLI; labels silently dropped until a maintainer triaged about 50 minutes later). vitest-dev/vitest #11380 and #11383 show the same pattern: authors with author_association NONE applied their own form's pending-triage label at creation. The 2022 community discussion #22510 describing template labels as write-only is outdated.

title: Warning del extension loader: @earendil-works/pi-tui debe ir en peerDependencies
body:
## Warning del extension loader

Al iniciar Pi aparece este warning:

```
Warning: Extension package "/Users/<user>/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/gentle-pi/package.json":
Host-provided extension packages must be declared in peerDependencies with a "*" range, not
dependencies: @earendil-works/pi-tui. Installed copies can bypass the extension loader and
create duplicate runtime modules.
```

## Causa

En `package.json`, `@earendil-works/pi-tui` está declarado en `dependencies` (fijado a `0.85.1`):

```json
"dependencies": {
  "@earendil-works/pi-tui": "0.85.1",
  "@heyhuynhgiabuu/pi-pretty": "0.6.27"
}
```

Según la documentación de Pi (docs/packages.md), los paquetes provistos por el host —`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, `@earendil-works/pi-tui`, `typebox`— deben declararse en `peerDependencies` con rango `"*"` y no incluirse como copia física, porque esa copia puede esquivar el mapeo de módulos de la extensión y crear módulos/registros duplicados en runtime.

## Fix propuesto

Mover `@earendil-works/pi-tui` de `dependencies` a `peerDependencies` con rango `"*"`:

```json
"dependencies": {
  "@heyhuynhgiabuu/pi-pretty": "0.6.27"
},
"peerDependencies": {
  "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent": ">=0.85.1",
  "@earendil-works/pi-tui": "*",
  "typebox": "*"
}
```

(`typebox` ya está correctamente en `peerDependencies`; solo falta mover `pi-tui`.)

## Entorno

- gentle-pi 3.7.0
- Pi coding agent 0.85.x

title: bug(review): gentle_review START fails with "input: must be string" — escaped-string contract has no object→string coercion
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

With Receipt-driven development enabled, `gentle_review` START (and every other facade call that takes a JSON-string parameter: `collectBinding`, `collectBindings`, and the ASSESS `input`) repeatedly fails tool validation with:

```
Validation failed for tool "gentle_review":
  - input: must be string
```

`gentle_review` declares `input` as `{ "type": "string" }` — a JSON-serialized object string, not a nested object (`extensions/gentle-ai.ts`). Models orchestrating the review reflexively emit the JSON as an object literal or as bare JSON text instead of a quoted, escaped JSON string, so the call fails before it executes.

Impact: the review lifecycle stalls at START. Validation is fail-closed (no lineage is created, no authority is burned), so the cost is workflow friction — the orchestrator tends to retry with the same emission style and then abandons the review route, leaving the candidate unreviewed.

Root cause, two layers:

1. The tool-call layer JSON-parses parameter content: the bare form `{"mode": "ordinary"}` arrives as an object; only the quoted+escaped form `"{\"mode\": \"ordinary\"}"` arrives as a string.
2. Pi's `validateToolArguments` runs TypeBox `Value.Convert` plus `validator.Check`, which never coerces object→string (it only coerces primitives), so there is no safety net.

Related but distinct: #1550 (Gemini injects extra parameters into zero-param tools) — same family of model-emission quirks versus strict validation, different tool and failure.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable Receipt-driven development and run an orchestrator model that emits tool parameters as JSON object literals.
2. Trigger review inspect: `gentle_review({ operation: "inspect" })` returns `status: "ready"`, action `start`.
3. Call START passing the input as bare JSON text (not the escaped string):

   `gentle_review({ operation: "start", input: {"mode": "ordinary"}, ... })`

4. Observe `Validation failed for tool "gentle_review": - input: must be string`; the `Received arguments` block shows `input` as an object.

Minimal live proof of the parsing layer (same harness, harmless tool):

- `read` with parameter content `{"x": 1}` (bare JSON text) → `Validation failed for tool "read": - path: must be string` (arrived as an object).
- `read` with parameter content `"{\"x\": 1}"` (quoted+escaped) → `ENOENT: no such file or directory, access '~/proyectos/gentle-pi/{"x": 1}'` (arrived as a string).

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: either the model emits the escaped-string form and START validates, or the facade (or pi's coercion layer) converts an unambiguous JSON object passed to a string-typed parameter into its JSON-serialized string. TypeBox `Value.Convert` handles primitive coercions only today.

title: bug(shell): prompt select-all consumes Alt+A before the Gentle Agents shortcut
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

The checks above were completed by the reporting assistant: searches covered `"alt+a"` and `"selection" "shortcut"` across all issue states. #804 describes selection integration, and #934 concerns delegation visibility with an overlay that opens normally; neither reports this shortcut interception bug.

### Problem

With the Gentle Shell prompt editor in ordinary editing mode (Vim off), Alt+A does not open the Gentle Agents overlay. The package assigns the same chord to both the agents view and the prompt's select-all operation. Selection consumes it before Pi can dispatch the registered extension shortcut. With an empty prompt, this can appear to do nothing.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Load gentle-pi with both Gentle Shell and Gentle Agents enabled in interactive Pi.
2. Keep prompt Vim editing disabled (the default), with no `GENTLE_PI_AGENTS_VIEW_KEY` override.
3. Focus the main prompt and press Alt+A. The reported symptom is that the agents overlay does not open.
4. As a diagnostic variation, type a non-empty draft and press Alt+A: the code path selects the draft instead of dispatching the agents shortcut. This variation is derived from source inspection, not a separately captured interactive test.
5. Compare with `/gentle:agents`, whose registered handler calls the same `openOverlay` directly and bypasses the key interception. This is a source-supported workaround; no separate interactive result was captured during this investigation.

Reported environment: Linux, fullscreen Pi, inside Herdr 0.9.1, `TERM=xterm-256color`. The internal collision is sufficient to explain the behavior; this report does not claim a separately reproduced terminal transport defect.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: The advertised Alt+A agents shortcut opens the Gentle Agents overlay when the main prompt is focused.

Actual: In ordinary editing mode, the prompt selection engine consumes Alt+A for select-all and never forwards it to Pi's extension-shortcut dispatcher. An empty draft makes the interception visually silent.

Source evidence at installed commit `f1226423daa78cf3bf9904e646a510ef789cf443`:

- `lib/agents-keys.ts:8-15` defaults `agentsViewKey()` to `alt+a`.
- `extensions/gentle-agents.ts:1393-1402` registers `/gentle:agents` and the view shortcut with handlers that both call `openOverlay(ctx)`.
- `extensions/gentle-shell.ts:530-540` routes input through `selectionEngine.handleInput(...)` before the native chain when Vim is off.
- `lib/selection-engine.ts:331-334` matches `alt+a`, calls `selectAll()`, and returns without invoking `native(data)`.
- Pi 0.99.1's `CustomEditor.handleInput()` checks `onExtensionShortcut` first, but that base handler is never reached for this key.

The installed Pi parser was checked directly: `matchesKey(data, "alt+a")` returns true for legacy ESC+a, Kitty CSI `97;3u`, and CSI `97;3:1u`. This establishes parser compatibility, not a capture of the user's physical keypress.

Suggested resolution: preserve extension-shortcut precedence and resolve the overlapping default bindings deliberately. Add an integration regression test with the real GentlePromptEditor and an extension shortcut callback, for both empty and non-empty drafts in ordinary editing mode. The existing isolated selection and agents-registration tests do not establish that this composed dispatch path works.

No fix has been implemented or validated as part of this report.

### gentle-pi version

3.7.0, Git-installed package at commit f1226423daa78cf3bf9904e646a510ef789cf443 (local source inspection; package-lock.json is untracked)

### Pi version

0.99.1 (@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent)

Linux

_No response_

title: bug(install): gentle-pi hard-depends on host-provided @earendil-works/pi-tui (and pi-ai on main), tripping the extension-loader warning and hoisting a stale duplicate
body:
### Problem

Pi's extension loader warns about `gentle-pi/package.json` on every startup:

```
Warning: Extension package "…/node_modules/gentle-pi/package.json":
 Host-provided extension packages must be declared in peerDependencies with a "*" range, not dependencies:
 @earendil-works/pi-tui. Installed copies can bypass the extension loader and create duplicate runtime modules.
```

`@earendil-works/pi-tui` is in the host's own allowlist of host-provided extension packages (the `HOST_PROVIDED_EXTENSION_PACKAGES` set in the Pi coding agent's resource loader), together with `@earendil-works/pi-ai`, `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, `typebox`, `@sinclair/typebox`, and the `@mariozechner/*` equivalents. Pi already supplies every one of them to extensions.

Published `gentle-pi@3.7.0` (current latest) declares:

```json
"dependencies": {
  "@earendil-works/pi-tui": "0.85.1",
  "@heyhuynhgiabuu/pi-pretty": "0.6.27"
},
"peerDependencies": {
  "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent": ">=0.85.1",
  "typebox": "*"
}
```

`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` and `typebox` are already declared correctly as peers, so the remaining hard dependency on a host-provided module reads as an oversight rather than intent. `@heyhuynhgiabuu/pi-pretty` is genuinely third-party and correctly stays a regular dependency.

`package.json` on `main` has the same problem and is worse: it also hard-depends on `@earendil-works/pi-ai`, which is in the same host-provided allowlist, so the same warning and the same hoisting will ship with the next release.

### Why this matters beyond the warning

Declaring a host-provided package as a dependency gives npm a reason to hoist the extension-local copy into the shared tree root, where it is resolved instead of the host's. Observed in a `~/.pi/agent/npm` tree, same session:

| module | tree copy | host copy (pi-coding-agent 0.99.1) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@earendil-works/pi-tui` | 0.85.1 | 0.99.1 |

`require.resolve("@earendil-works/pi-tui")` executed from the tree root returns the tree copy, not the host's, so the tree copy is the one on the resolution path for anything inside that tree. `gentle-pi` imports `@earendil-works/pi-tui` from 61 sites, which is what turns a 14-minor version skew into a live divergence rather than a theoretical one; the loader's own warning wording ("bypass the extension loader and create duplicate runtime modules") is describing exactly this.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install `gentle-pi@3.7.0` into a Pi agent npm tree managed by npm (`~/.pi/agent/npm`), e.g. as a dependency of that tree's root `package.json`.
2. Start `pi`.
3. Observe the loader warning naming `@earendil-works/pi-tui`.
4. Compare the hoisted copy against the host's:
   - from the tree root: `node -p "require('./node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-tui/package.json').version"`
   - from the `pi-coding-agent` install tree: `node -p "require('./node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-tui/package.json').version"`

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: no loader warning, and `gentle-pi` resolving the host's single `@earendil-works/pi-tui` and `@earendil-works/pi-ai` instances, with no extension-local copy hoisted into the shared tree.

Actual: the loader warns on every startup, and the tree root holds a `@earendil-works/pi-tui` copy at 0.85.1 while the host runs 0.99.1.

### gentle-pi version

3.7.0 (published, current latest)

### Pi version

0.99.1 (host ships `@earendil-works/pi-tui` 0.99.1)

### Operating system

macOS

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```
Warning: Extension package "…/node_modules/gentle-pi/package.json":
 Host-provided extension packages must be declared in peerDependencies with a "*" range, not dependencies:
 @earendil-works/pi-tui. Installed copies can bypass the extension loader and create duplicate runtime modules.
```

```json
{
  "dependencies": { "@earendil-works/pi-tui": "0.85.1", "@heyhuynhgiabuu/pi-pretty": "0.6.27" },
  "peerDependencies": { "typebox": "*", "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent": ">=0.85.1" }
}
```

### Suggested fix

Move `@earendil-works/pi-tui` — and `@earendil-works/pi-ai` on `main` — from `dependencies` to `peerDependencies`, mirroring how `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` and `typebox` are already declared here. Add `peerDependenciesMeta.optional` for both if `gentle-pi` should stay installable outside a Pi host.

This is the same defect class as Gentleman-Programming/engram#853, which was fixed for `gentle-engram`'s `@earendil-works/pi-tui`; the identical remaining entry for `gentle-engram`'s `typebox` is noted there.
