- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

title: feat(agents): account for streamed tool-call arguments as bounded watchdog progress
body:
### Before submitting

The reporting agent completed these operational checks.

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

Search evidence: completed all-state searches for watchdog, toolcall_delta, long tool, idle timeout, argument streaming, and tool arguments. Related but distinct: #1070 covers an already-running foreground command; #1034 covers irrelevant RPC traffic indefinitely renewing the watchdog; #1251 covers zero-turn startup stalls; #1323 requests semantic progress check-ins. This request covers meaningful argument-generation progress before tool execution.

### Problem or opportunity

Repeated attempts at the same substantial single-file landing-page implementation showed no visible progress after completed preliminary tools. A minimal worker instructed to write a one-word file completed successfully. This is not evidence of a general worker or filesystem failure.

Earlier retained investigations recorded four-minute inactivity-watchdog terminations after completed tools. In the latest attempt, the parent manually cancelled the worker after repeated unchanged status snapshots: running, 3 turns, 3 calls, last tool bash. The exact child session contains three successful direct tool pairs (read, read, bash), followed by a write tool call retained in an aborted assistant message at cancellation, with no paired tool result. Execution of that write is unconfirmed.

The child log contains no codemode invocation. The parent used codemode to launch the worker, and that wrapper completed successfully. There is no evidence that child codemode or an unresolved bash caused this incident.

Hypothesis, not established root cause: generating a large write argument can leave the status projection and inactivity watchdog without recognized progress while the provider is still streaming tool-call arguments. A previous parser inspection suggested toolcall_delta events may not count as progress; raw provider/RPC streaming traces were unavailable, so continuous streaming during these specific quiet intervals has not been proven. The manually cancelled attempt must not be presented as a proven watchdog timeout.

### Proposed outcome

Account for meaningful streamed tool-call argument progress separately from announced/executing tools and genuine silence.

- Investigate the Pi event contract for tool-call argument deltas, including direct write calls and codemode calls with large script arguments; use the supported event names rather than assuming a version-independent spelling.
- Refresh the generation inactivity budget on validated nonempty argument progress for the active child generation. Do not renew it for unrelated UI/RPC traffic or empty/replayed events.
- Keep a bounded overall generation/run ceiling so continuous traffic cannot extend execution indefinitely.
- Project a privacy-safe state such as generating tool arguments, distinct from executing a tool and waiting for parent input. Do not increment executed-tool counters before execution.
- Retain event-type/timestamp/progress-count diagnostics, without raw prompts, script contents, tool arguments, environment values, credentials, or source bytes.
- Distinguish no generation progress, tool execution timeout, and overall ceiling in terminal diagnostics.

Acceptance tests should cover streamed arguments lasting longer than the idle threshold, genuinely silent generation, empty/replayed deltas, unrelated RPC traffic, an overall ceiling, cancellation during partial arguments, normal tool start/completion, and unsupported/missing delta events. No partial tool call should execute after cancellation. This is a requested investigation and bounded improvement, not a claim that the existing incident has a confirmed mechanism.

### Alternatives considered

- Raising the idle timeout globally masks genuine hangs and does not explain the state.
- Splitting the landing into smaller writes may be a workaround and a useful controlled experiment, but it has not yet been run and does not repair progress accounting.
- Relaunching the same full request repeatedly has already failed to provide diagnostic evidence.
- Counting all RPC traffic repeats the failure class described in #1034.
- Semantic progress reminders from #1323 cannot run while the model is still generating a tool argument and do not substitute for transport progress accounting.

### Additional context

Observed checkout package metadata: gentle-pi 3.7.0. Loaded runner-byte equivalence at historical failure time is not verified. The latest exact child metadata recorded medium effort. No provider fault is established.

Privacy-safe child chronology from the latest manually cancelled attempt, all UTC on the same date:

```text
21:46:21.087 -> 21:46:21.099  read: paired success
21:46:24.500 -> 21:46:24.509  read: paired success
21:46:28.894 -> 21:46:28.921  bash: paired success, direct
21:47:13 through 21:48:41      repeated unchanged status: 3 turns / 3 calls
21:48:01                     parent steering queued; consumption not acknowledged
21:49:43.688                 write present in aborted assistant message; no tool result
21:49:43                     manual cancellation acknowledged
```

These are retained session events, not raw streaming timestamps. The final aborted message does not establish when argument generation began or whether it progressed continuously.

title: feat(review): persistent user-owned opt-in to run RDD reviews without the consent envelope (parent and delegated children)
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Users who have decided that *every* RDD candidate should be reviewed still get the consent envelope over and over in long autonomous work:

- The standing permission from #642 is memory-only and scoped to one live session (by design: "never restore from files or process restart"). Every restart, `/resume`, compaction-driven rebuild or new session asks again.
- Delegated children (`gentle-ai-worker`, etc.) only get the grant through the parent's in-memory permission. When the parent has not answered the envelope in *this* session, a worker's medium/high-risk candidate relays the consent question to the human mid-run, even though the human's standing answer is always "review it".
- With several orchestrators running in parallel (one per repository/worktree), the human becomes the bottleneck for a question whose answer never changes.

The answer only authorizes *running* reviews; it never approves verdicts. For that level of authority gentle-ai already has a persistent, user-owned control: the RDD mode switch (`gentle-ai review mode`), which is stored on disk and survives restarts.

### Proposed outcome

A persistent, user-owned opt-in with the same semantics as the #642 standing permission ("run reviews without asking"), kept outside provider schemas:

- Scope: global or per repository (clone-local), mirroring how `review mode` is scoped.
- When set, a fresh validated envelope is answered `granted` automatically for the parent **and** for delegated children in that repository.
- It authorizes execution only: no verdict approval, no RDD enablement, no delivery-policy change. `declined`/kill-switch semantics stay as they are.
- Visible status and revocation, e.g. `/gentle:review-session-permission status` showing "persistent (user opt-in)" and a command to revoke.
- Off by default.

### Alternatives considered

- Answering the envelope once per session (#642): works, but is lost on every restart/resume and does not reach children whose parent has not answered yet.
- Turning RDD off (`/gentle:review-mode disable`): removes the prompt by removing the reviews, which is the opposite of the intent.
- A local patch that reads a user config flag in the consent path (parent `permissionAlreadyActive` and the child `requestAuthorization` branch). This works in practice today but is unsupported and has to be re-applied after every update.

### Additional context

Observed with gentle-pi 3.7.0 and Pi 0.87.1 on Linux (WSL2), running four long refactor sessions in parallel; one prompt came from a `gentle-ai-worker` candidate (one file, ~880 changed lines, medium risk) while the human's standing intent was to review everything. Related: #642 (session-scoped permission), #1212 (re-prompts per candidate in throwaway clones).

title: bug(install): gentle-pi ships host-provided @earendil-works/pi-tui as a dependency, hoisting a duplicate 0.85.1 copy over the host 0.99.0
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

`gentle-pi@3.7.0` declares `@earendil-works/pi-tui` in `dependencies`:

```json
"dependencies": {
  "@earendil-works/pi-tui": "0.85.1",
  "@heyhuynhgiabuu/pi-pretty": "0.6.27"
},
"peerDependencies": {
  "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent": ">=0.85.1",
  "typebox": "*"
}
```

`pi-tui` is a host-provided module: the Pi installation always supplies it, and this package already peer-declares `pi-coding-agent` for exactly the same reason. Declaring it as a hard dependency gives npm a legal reason to install a second copy into the extension tree, and Pi's extension loader reports it on every startup:

```text
Warning: Extension package "<npm-root>/node_modules/gentle-pi/package.json":
Host-provided extension packages must be declared in peerDependencies with a "*"
range, not dependencies: @earendil-works/pi-tui. Installed copies can bypass the
extension loader and create duplicate runtime modules.
```

The duplicate is not inert — it shadows the host's copy at import time, and the two copies are different versions:

| module | resolved from `gentle-pi` | host copy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@earendil-works/pi-tui` | 0.85.1 | 0.99.0 |

The package imports pi-tui directly in roughly 20 modules (`extensions/gentle-ai.ts:33`, the other extensions under `extensions/`, and `lib/agents-view.ts`, `lib/shell-bar.ts`, `lib/native-choice-list.ts`, `lib/questionnaire/questionnaire-view.ts`, `lib/review-consent-component.ts`). Symbols crossing that boundary — `Key` constants, `matchesKey`, `KeybindingsManager`, `truncateToWidth` — come from a different module instance than the one rendering the UI, which is precisely the duplicate-runtime-module failure the warning describes.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install `gentle-pi@3.7.0` into a Pi npm extension tree (`~/.pi/agent/npm`).
2. Start Pi.
3. Observe the `Host-provided extension packages ... @earendil-works/pi-tui` warning on stderr.
4. Confirm that bare imports resolve the duplicate, not the host copy:

```console
$ cd ~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/gentle-pi
$ node -e "console.log(require.resolve('@earendil-works/pi-tui'))"
<npm-root>/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-tui/dist/index.js
$ node -e "console.log(require(require.resolve('@earendil-works/pi-tui/package.json')).version)"
0.85.1
$ node -e "console.log(require('<pi-install-root>/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-tui/package.json').version)"
0.99.0
```

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: `@earendil-works/pi-tui` is declared in `peerDependencies` with a `"*"` range and never in `dependencies` — exactly how this package already declares `typebox`. npm installs no second copy, the host's `pi-tui` is the only one in the module graph, and the loader emits no warning.

Actual: npm installs `@earendil-works/pi-tui@0.85.1` into the extension tree, it shadows the host's 0.99.0 copy for every bare import in the package, and the extension loader emits the duplicate-runtime-module warning on every startup.

### gentle-pi version

3.7.0 (`npm view gentle-pi version` -> 3.7.0)

### Pi version

0.99.0

### Operating system

Windows

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
Warning: Extension package "<npm-root>/node_modules/gentle-pi/package.json": Host-provided extension packages must be declared in peerDependencies with a "*" range, not dependencies:
 @earendil-works/pi-tui. Installed copies can bypass the extension loader and create duplicate runtime modules.
```

The 5-hour and weekly subscription usage gauges remain stale while a parent agent or orchestrator is still running multiple tasks or subagents. The usage snapshot should be invalidated or refreshed whenever confirmed provider usage becomes available, at least after each completed task or subagent, so the 5-hour and weekly gauges remain useful during long-running workflows.

title: Windows: postinstall fails deterministically with EPERM renaming .gentle-ai staging bundle (blocks pi update --extensions)
body:
- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

## Problem

On Windows, `pi update --extensions` (and any npm lifecycle install of gentle-pi) fails **deterministically** at the postinstall, so the whole update aborts:

```
gentle-pi could not install its package-local Gentle AI v3.7.0 binary:
EPERM: operation not permitted, rename '~/.pi/agent/git/github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-pi/.gentle-ai/.v3.7.0.staging-<nonce>' -> '~/.pi/agent/git/github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-pi/.gentle-ai/v3.7.0'
npm error code 1
```

This blocks Windows users from updating gentle-pi through the pi extension manager; the extension git pull succeeds but the native binary is left missing.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Windows 11 (10.0.26200), Node 24.11.1, npm 11.11.1 — gentle-pi 3.7.0 via `pi update --extensions`.
2. Run `pi update --extensions`.
3. The postinstall (`node scripts/install-gentle-ai.mjs`) compiles `gentle-ai.exe` from source (Windows Go SumDB path), executes it to assert the pinned version, then atomically renames the staging directory to `.gentle-ai/v3.7.0`.
4. The rename fails with `EPERM` on the first attempt — reproduced 3/3 times across independent runs, including a plain manual `node scripts/install-gentle-ai.mjs`.

## Expected and actual behavior

- **Expected:** the postinstall publishes `.gentle-ai/v3.7.0` and the update completes.
- **Actual:** the single no-retry `fs.rename` in `publishBundle` hits a transient lock on the freshly built/executed binary. Instrumented runs consistently show attempt 1 → `EPERM`, attempt 2 (~250 ms later) → success — so the lock is short-lived but the lack of retry fails the install every time.

**Root cause:** Windows refuses to rename a directory while any process holds an open handle on it or on a file inside it; here a real-time scanner/OS component briefly holds the freshly compiled unsigned `gentle-ai.exe` right after it was executed for the version check.

**Fix proposed:** PR #1552 adds a short backoff retry to the publish rename (`EPERM`/`EBUSY` only, win32) — validated end-to-end on the affected machine (attempt 1 `EPERM`, retry → `Gentle AI v3.7.0 installed`), and the installer test suite matches baseline exactly (no new failures; the 4 pre-existing Windows-environment failures are unrelated).

## gentle-pi version

3.7.0 (package-local), extension commit `0d66123d`

## Pi version

0.87.1

## Operating system

Windows

## Relevant logs or error output (optional)

Full postinstall excerpt (private paths masked):

```
> gentle-pi@3.7.0 postinstall
> node scripts/install-gentle-ai.mjs

gentle-pi could not install its package-local Gentle AI v3.7.0 binary: EPERM: operation not permitted, rename '~/.pi/agent/git/github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-pi/.gentle-ai/.v3.7.0.staging-Qz0yuI' -> '~/.pi/agent/git/github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-pi/.gentle-ai/v3.7.0'
npm error code 1
```

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem


During an ordinary RDD correction cycle, `gentle_review` became indefinitely stuck on:

`{"operation":"status"}`

The STATUS call remained pending for about 30 minutes even though native review STATUS is configured with a 30,000 ms timeout.

While the tool call was stuck, the corresponding package-local `gentle-ai` process was visible as a direct zombie (`Z`, `<defunct>`) child of the long-lived Pi process. Pi itself remained blocked waiting for the tool result.

Pressing Ctrl+C caused the pending tool call to return immediately as:

```json
{
  "operation": "status",
  "status": "blocked",
  "outcome": "native-operation-failed",
  "diagnostics": {
    "operation": "review/status",
    "error_code": "cancelled",
    "timed_out": false,
    "output_limit_exceeded": false
  },
  "mutation_performed": false,
  "mutation_outcome": "none",
  "next_action": "resolve-native-operation-failure"
}
```

I then retried the exact same `gentle_review status` operation on the same lineage. It completed in roughly 280 ms, the lineage was healthy, and the review subsequently completed successfully and was acknowledged as approved.

So this does not appear to have been a legitimately long-running review or a corrupted lineage. The native STATUS subprocess/tool-call settlement appears to have wedged.

I also observed another older `gentle-ai` zombie under the same long-lived Pi process, so this may not be an isolated subprocess-reaping incident.

`NativeReviewCliV216` appears to configure non-mutating native review operations with a 30,000 ms timeout, so a STATUS call remaining pending for ~30 minutes also suggests that the timeout did not settle the tool operation as intended.

Related but apparently not duplicate:
- #1139 concerns reviewer-child signal termination being collapsed into `pi-failed`.
- #1187 concerns reviewer relay timeout calibration.
- #1137 concerns a deterministic reviewer slot failure being reoffered indefinitely.

This report concerns the native `gentle_review status` subprocess itself becoming stuck after its `gentle-ai` child has already become a zombie.

### Steps to reproduce

I do not yet have a deterministic minimal reproduction. This is the sequence from the observed production session:

1. Run Gentle Shell with RDD enabled and start an ordinary native review.
2. Let the review produce a `correction_required` result.
3. Apply and independently verify the bounded correction.
4. Commit the correction.
5. Call `gentle_review` with:

   ```json
   {
     "operation": "status",
     "lineageId": "<existing-lineage>"
   }
   ```

6. In the observed run, this STATUS call never returned.

7. While it was pending, inspect the Pi process tree. The `gentle-ai` process spawned at the time of the STATUS call was:

   ```text
   State: Z (zombie)
   Parent: the active Pi process
   Command: [gentle-ai] <defunct>
   ```

8. Wait beyond the native STATUS timeout. In my case the tool remained pending for about 30 minutes despite the configured ~30 s timeout.

9. Press Ctrl+C once.

10. The tool immediately returns `native-operation-failed` with:

    ```text
    error_code: cancelled
    timed_out: false
    mutation_outcome: none
    ```

11. Send another message and retry the exact same `gentle_review status` on the same lineage.

12. The retry completes almost immediately (~280 ms). The review can continue normally and reach `approved`.

Observed timing in this run:

```text
13:06:41  gentle_review status invoked
           corresponding gentle-ai child later observed as zombie

13:37:29  Ctrl+C
           pending STATUS returns cancelled

13:37:38  same STATUS retried
13:37:39  STATUS returns successfully (~280 ms)
```

No repository or review-state repair was necessary between the cancelled call and the successful retry.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected:

`gentle_review status` should either:

1. complete normally, or
2. return a typed timeout/failure within its configured native timeout.

If the direct `gentle-ai` child exits, the parent should reap it and the tool Promise should settle. A dead/zombie child must not leave Pi waiting indefinitely.

Actual:

The STATUS tool call remained pending for about 30 minutes, far beyond the configured 30,000 ms native timeout.

During the hang, the corresponding `gentle-ai` child was already in zombie (`Z`, `<defunct>`) state while Pi continued waiting.

Ctrl+C was required to settle the tool call. It then returned `error_code: cancelled`, not `timed_out`.

Retrying the exact same STATUS against the same lineage completed in ~280 ms and allowed the review to finish successfully.

### gentle-pi version

3.7.0

### Pi version

0.87.1

### Operating system

Linux

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
Before the hang:

gentle_review
  operation: status
  lineage: <redacted>

# No tool result for ~30 minutes.

During the hang:

gentle-ai child:
  State: Z (zombie)
  Parent: active Pi process
  Command: [gentle-ai] <defunct>

After Ctrl+C:

{
  "operation": "status",
  "status": "blocked",
  "outcome": "native-operation-failed",
  "diagnostics": {
    "operation": "review/status",
    "error_code": "cancelled",
    "timed_out": false,
    "output_limit_exceeded": false
  },
  "mutation_performed": false,
  "mutation_outcome": "none",
  "next_action": "resolve-native-operation-failure"
}

Retry, same lineage:

gentle_review
  operation: status

# Returned successfully in ~280 ms.
# The lineage then proceeded through targeted validation and ended approved.
```

title: fix(gentle-agents): allow optional reason in zero-param tools to prevent Gemini delegation aborts
body:
### Before submitting
- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem
When Google Gemini models (e.g. `antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash-tiered`, `gemini-3.1-pro-high`) are used as the orchestrator, they fail to delegate organically to subagents (`gentle-ai-verify`, `gentle-ai-explore`, etc.).

Investigation revealed that Gemini's function calling behavior frequently injects an explanatory parameter (e.g., `{"reason": "Check available subagents for testing"}`) when invoking tools that take no arguments.

In `gentle-pi/extensions/gentle-agents.ts`:
```typescript
tool("list_agents", "List the subagents defined for this project and user, with their descriptions.", { properties: {} }, async (_params, ctx) => { ... })
tool("list_tasks", "List the subagent tasks of this session, newest first.", { properties: {} }, async (_params, ctx) => { ... })
```

Because `properties` is empty, Pi's tool validator enforces strict schema matching (`additionalProperties: false`) and rejects Gemini's call with:
```
Validation failed for tool "subagent_list_agents":
  - reason: schema is false
  - root: must not have additional properties
```

Upon receiving this validation failure on turn 1, Gemini assumes the subagent subsystem is broken or unavailable, abandons the delegation route, and falls back to executing commands inline via `bash` or `read`, violating ODD Mandatory Delegation Triggers.

In contrast, models like `gpt-6-sol` and `deepseek-v4.1-flash` pass `{}` cleanly, so they do not hit this wall.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Run Pi with Gemini as the orchestrator model:
   `pi -p --mode json --model omniroute/antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash-tiered "Ejecutá una verificación de la suite de tests en tests/ con pytest y reportá si pasan."`
   (This fires Mandatory Delegation Trigger 5: Verification rule).
2. Inspect the turn 1 tool calls:
   Gemini attempts: `subagent_list_agents {"reason": "Checking available subagents for test verification"}`.
3. Observe tool execution:
   Pi validator rejects with `must not have additional properties`.
4. Observe subsequent turns:
   Gemini aborts `subagent_run` and falls back to executing `bash: pytest ...` inline.

### Expected and actual behavior
**Expected:**
`subagent_list_agents` and `subagent_list_tasks` gracefully tolerate an optional `reason` parameter. The tool call succeeds, returns the subagent list, and Gemini proceeds to invoke `subagent_run` (`gentle-ai-verify` / `gentle-ai-explore`) organically according to ODD rules.

**Actual:**
Validation failure on `subagent_list_agents` causes Gemini to abandon subagent delegation and execute commands inline.

### gentle-pi version
3.7.0

### Pi version
0.87.1

### Operating system
Linux

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)
```text
-> TOOL START: subagent_list_agents args: {"reason": "Check available verification subagents"}
<- TOOL END: subagent_list_agents isError: true
   Error text: Validation failed for tool "subagent_list_agents":
     - reason: schema is false
     - root: must not have additional properties

-> TOOL START: bash args: {"command": "cd ... && pytest ..."}
```

Proposed fix in `extensions/gentle-agents.ts`:
```typescript
tool(
  "list_agents",
  "List the subagents defined for this project and user, with their descriptions.",
  {
    properties: {
      reason: { type: "string", description: "Optional explanation or reasoning for listing subagents." }
    }
  },
  async (_params, ctx) => { ... }
);

tool(
  "list_tasks",
  "List the subagent tasks of this session, newest first.",
  {
    properties: {
      reason: { type: "string", description: "Optional explanation or reasoning for listing tasks." }
    }
  },
  async (_params, ctx) => { ... }
);
```

title: feat(shell): expose a session cost total that includes delegated subagent cost
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Gentle Shell renders exactly one session-level cost number, and that number is the orchestrator's own spend. Delegated subagent cost is accumulated per task and is never folded into it, so as soon as any subagent runs, the displayed cost under-reports what the session actually spent.

The parent figure comes from `sessionCost()`, which sums `usage.cost.total` over the parent session's own entries:

```ts
// extensions/gentle-shell.ts:244-252
function sessionCost(ctx: ExtensionContext): number {
	let total = 0;
	for (const entry of ctx.sessionManager.getEntries() as AssistantUsageEntry[]) {
		if (entry.type !== "message" || entry.message?.role !== "assistant") continue;
		total += entry.message.usage?.cost?.total ?? 0;
	}
	return total;
}
```

That value becomes `costTotal: sessionCost(ctx)` (`extensions/gentle-shell.ts:275`) and is painted by `costSegment()` through the shared `formatCost()` (`lib/shell-bar.ts:113`, `:145-146`), used identically by the fullscreen header (`:153`) and the compact bar (`:296`).

Subagent cost never reaches those entries. Every child is its own process with its own session directory:

- `lib/agents-runner.ts:10` — "Every subagent is its own `pi --mode rpc` process".
- `lib/agents-runner.ts:241` — `const args = ["--mode", "rpc", "--session-dir", request.sessionDir];`

Child usage arrives only as an RPC event and lands on that task's record:

```ts
// lib/agents-protocol.ts:258 — child message_end becomes a usage delta
events.push({ type: TASK_EVENT.USAGE, tokens: Number(usage.totalTokens ?? 0) || 0, cost: Number(cost?.total ?? 0) || 0 });

// lib/agents-protocol.ts:379-380 — the only cost summation in the repository
case TASK_EVENT.USAGE:
	return { ...resumed, tokens: task.tokens + event.tokens, cost: task.cost + event.cost };
```

Consequences, each verifiable by reading the sources listed under Additional context:

1. **No cross-agent cost aggregate exists anywhere.** `costTotal` is produced at a single site and read only by the bar surfaces. `TaskStore.summary()` (`lib/agents-protocol.ts:438`) returns `TaskSummary`, which carries counts only — `running`, `queued`, `waiting`, `finished` (`lib/agents-protocol.ts:141-146`) — no cost and no tokens.
2. **Bucketing is per task only.** Delegated cost is rendered per task in the card (`lib/agents-widget.ts:188`, `:213`) and in the `alt+a` view header (`lib/agents-view.ts:146`). There is no per-session or per-group total to read.
3. **The number is unlabeled.** No code comment, doc, or UI string states that it excludes delegated work, so a reader reasonably takes it as the session total.
4. **Delegated cost does not even cross the RPC wire.** The desktop projection `gentle-agents.activity/v1` (`lib/agents-rpc-publisher.ts:14`, `:110`) publishes id, agent, label, prompt, status, timestamps, `lastStep`, `turns`, `toolCalls` and `error`; it has no `cost` or `tokens` field, so a desktop client cannot see cost at all.

Worked example. Three subagents that each spent $0.05 render `$0.050` three times in the Agents card, while the bar header shows the orchestrator's own `$0.090`. Both numbers are visible at the same time and disagree about the same session; the session's real spend is `$0.240`.

Relationship to #1434 / PR #1465: that change unified the *formatting* of cost across the card, the view and the bar (`$${task.cost.toFixed(2)}` → the shared `formatCost()`). It did not unify the *fact*. The surfaces still describe different scopes, so the drift #1434 fixed is only half closed.

### Proposed outcome

- A session-level cost total that includes delegated subagent cost, so the compact bar, the fullscreen header and the Status sidebar report what the session actually spent. If the orchestrator-only figure is deliberately kept, it should be labeled as orchestrator spend with the delegated delta shown next to it — an explicit, honest number rather than an unlabeled partial one.
- A delegated-cost aggregate over all known tasks, sourced from the task store rather than from the rendered rows. `TaskSummary` (`lib/agents-protocol.ts:141-146`) is the natural seam and already has a change path (`summaryListeners`, `TaskStore.summary()` at `:438`), but it is also a published wire shape, so widening it is a compatibility decision rather than a local edit.
- The total must survive row expiry. The card drops finished rows after `FINISHED_TTL_MS = 60_000` (`lib/agents-widget.ts:65`, filter at `:112`), so aggregating over the *visible* rows would make the total shrink a minute after an agent finishes. `TaskStore` retains finished tasks and `TaskRecord.cost` is persisted and restored, so an aggregate over `store.list()` can be both correct and stable.
- Whichever number ships should say what it covers. That is the cheapest half of this request and does not depend on the aggregation.

### Alternatives considered

1. **Document the limitation only.** Cheapest, and it removes the ambiguity, but the session number stays incomplete for anyone doing cost-sensitive work — which is the case that motivated this report.
2. **Sum the cost of the currently rendered rows.** Rejected: row TTL (`FINISHED_TTL_MS`) would make the total shrink after 60 seconds and under-report, which is worse than the current honest-but-narrow number.
3. **Extend the summary delivered for #997** ("Sidebar: add a dedicated subagent status summary section", closed COMPLETED). The delivered summary counts statuses; its token/cost totals were explicitly optional and were not part of it, and its concern was sidebar visibility, not what the header number means. Reopening it would mix two different problems.
4. **Read the children's session directories from disk and sum usage there.** Heavier, duplicates the runtime's own accounting, and would still have to reconcile against the live RPC stream.
5. **Rely on #975** ("show read/write/output token usage breakdown"). Adjacent, but tokens do not answer cost: price differs per model, and the orchestrator and a subagent can run different models.

### Additional context

Evidence table (all paths are repository-relative; read at commit `4d2c3f5c`):

| Location | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| `extensions/gentle-shell.ts:244-252` | `sessionCost()` sums only parent session entries |
| `extensions/gentle-shell.ts:275` | `costTotal: sessionCost(ctx)` — the single bar/header model field |
| `lib/shell-bar.ts:113,145-146,153,296` | `formatCost()` / `costSegment()` paint that one value in header and compact bar |
| `lib/agents-protocol.ts:258` | child `message_end` becomes a `TASK_EVENT.USAGE` delta |
| `lib/agents-protocol.ts:379-380` | the only cost addition in the repository: per task |
| `lib/agents-protocol.ts:141-146` | `TaskSummary` is counts only — no cost, no tokens |
| `lib/agents-protocol.ts:438` | `TaskStore.summary()` — the seam an aggregate would use |
| `lib/agents-widget.ts:65,112,188,213` | per-task cost render, and the 60s finished-row TTL |
| `lib/agents-view.ts:146` | per-task cost in the `alt+a` view header |
| `lib/agents-runner.ts:10,241` | each child is its own process with its own session dir |
| `lib/agents-rpc-publisher.ts:14,110` | the RPC activity projection omits cost and tokens |

Environment where the code was read: gentle-pi 3.7.0, Pi 0.87.1, Linux.

How these findings were produced: by reading the sources above, not from a live runtime trace. Traceability of the widget row column widths and the cost cell is from the module's own layout code and its tests.

Remaining uncertainty: whether the Pi runtime itself folds child process usage back into the parent's persisted entries through some mechanism outside this repository. Based on `lib/agents-runner.ts:241` (separate `--session-dir`) the parent `getEntries()` should not contain child usage, but that is inferred rather than traced. If it does fold them in, the header number would be correct and only the labeling part of this request would remain.

One caveat worth deciding while implementing: the aggregate can only be as complete as the runner's observed usage events. A child killed or detached mid-run may have an incomplete recorded cost. That is a bounded caveat, not a blocker.

title: feat(pi): expose supported AgentSession tool dispatch
body:
### Before submitting
- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity
Pi extensions can register model-facing tools, but an external programmatic orchestrator cannot invoke an already registered tool through the same supported dispatch path used by the model. The SDK and RPC surface support session prompting and events, but do not provide deterministic registered-tool invocation.

This blocks contract-preserving workflows that must carry opaque tool results in memory without passing them through model generation. One example is a native review flow where STATUS returns an ordered array of opaque bindings and a subsequent registered capture-group tool must receive those exact strings unchanged.

### Proposed outcome
Provide a supported AgentSession-level API for invoking an active registered tool through the same wrapped registry and dispatch path as a model tool call. The API design should be evaluated before acceptance; a candidate shape is:

```ts
session.executeTool(name, args, options?): Promise<AgentToolResult>
```

The supported path must preserve the live ExtensionContext, registered-tool lookup, tool hooks, lifecycle events, permission and policy enforcement, executionMode, cancellation, errors, session/workspace isolation, and the standard tool result shape. It must reject unknown tools and invalid arguments without creating an alternate path around existing controls.

### Alternatives considered
- Prompting a model to call the tool: cannot guarantee byte-for-byte propagation of opaque values.
- Calling extension-internal functions directly: unsupported and bypasses normal dispatch context.
- Adding a review-specific wrapper or temporary binding handle: changes the review-facing API and duplicates review authority logic.
- Tool-to-tool composition in Gentle Shell: no public dispatcher is exposed.

### Additional context
This is a platform composition concern, not a request to change the native review contract or weaken opaque bindings. The desired implementation should include unit and integration coverage, including an extension-registered status-to-group workflow that retains opaque strings in memory and verifies they reach the second tool unchanged.

title: bug(agents): shell-centric CodeGraph guidance block injected into bash-less agents causes retry loops
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

`gentle-ai sync` injects the `<!-- gentle-ai:pi-codegraph-guidance -->` CodeGraph block verbatim into every installed Pi agent definition under `~/.pi/agent/agents/`, including agents whose declared tool list has **no shell access**. The block's "Required order" demands shell commands those agents cannot execute, while explicitly forbidding fallback — a combination that sends the subagent into a tool-call retry loop (observed: the same call repeated indefinitely; the agent tried to satisfy the `git rev-parse` step).

Affected installed agents carrying the block **without** `bash` in their tool list (11 of 23):

- `gentle-ai-explore`
- `review-readability`, `review-reliability`, `review-resilience`, `review-risk`
- `sdd-design`, `sdd-explore`, `sdd-proposal`, `sdd-research`, `sdd-spec`, `sdd-tasks`

The block's conflicting instructions for a bash-less agent:

1. Step 1: "Resolve the project root with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel || pwd`" — impossible without bash.
2. Step 4: "immediately run `gentle-ai codegraph init --cwd <project-root>` once" — impossible without bash.
3. "CodeGraph intelligence surface": "invoke the upstream CLI directly: `codegraph status`, `codegraph query`, ..." — impossible without bash.
4. Steps 5 and 8: "Do not fall back just because `.codegraph/` is missing" / "Only fall back to normal filesystem tools after CodeGraph initialization or use fails" — the model is forbidden from abandoning a checklist it cannot execute.

A model that follows the checklist literally cannot complete step 1, is told not to fall back, and retries indefinitely. The behavior is intermittent because it only triggers when the model takes the checklist literally; a model that ignores the block and goes straight to `grep` completes normally.

The block is embedded in the `gentle-ai` Go binary (verified: the marker string `pi-codegraph-guidance` appears in the binary, zero times in the gentle-pi npm TypeScript sources), so rendering happens at sync time and is not tool-aware.

Related but distinct: #372 (the integrated `codegraph` tool hanging when the model picks `init` over `query`) is a tool-level timeout/dispatch issue; this report is about the prompt-level guidance injected into bash-less agents.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install gentle-pi 3.7.0 and run `gentle-ai sync` so agent files are installed under the Pi agents directory.
2. Confirm `gentle-ai-explore.md` (or any of the 10 other listed agents) contains the `pi-codegraph-guidance` block while its frontmatter tool list lacks `bash`.
3. From a parent Pi session, delegate a structural/codebase question (e.g. "how does X work", repo map, call flow) to `gentle-ai-explore`.
4. With a model that follows the injected "Required order" literally, observe the child repeat the same tool call indefinitely, attempting to satisfy the shell-command steps it cannot run.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected:

- The sync-time injection renders a tool-aware variant of the CodeGraph block: when the target agent's tool list lacks bash, the block references only the Pi-native `codegraph` tool (`operation: "init"` when `.codegraph/` is absent, then `query`/`explore`), states that any shell-named step is satisfied by the equivalent tool operation, and keeps the fallback rule.

Actual:

- All 23 agents receive the identical shell-centric block; 11 of them cannot execute its required steps and are told not to fall back, producing intermittent infinite retry loops.

Local workaround I applied: patched the 11 installed files with a bash-less variant of the block (same outer HTML markers). A probe launch of the patched `gentle-ai-explore` followed the corrected checklist (`find` for `.codegraph/` → `codegraph query` → `codegraph explore` → justified `grep` fallback) and completed normally. The patch is overwritten by the next `gentle-ai sync`, hence this report.

### gentle-pi version

3.7.0

### Pi version

0.87.1

### Operating system

Linux

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

_No response_

title: bug(review): terminal unachievable lens slot lacks a facade withdrawal route
body:
### Before submitting
- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this specific problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem
A small committed-only ordinary review with one `review-reliability` lens timed out in the Pi host relay. `gentle_review_capture` recorded `unachievable-lens-slot-declared`; subsequent bound `gentle_review status` returned a terminal `unachievable_lens_slot` STOP with a provider-issued native `review.capture-unachievable ... --withdraw=true` command. The installed `gentle_review` operation set has no withdrawal operation, while `gentle_review_capture` accepts only offered collect slots. The compact Pi review route therefore cannot reoffer this exact reviewer after the timeout without stepping outside its facade. Increasing the relay timeout in a new Pi process does not clear the already-recorded STOP.

This is narrower than #1238 (forecast visibility and survivable/partial review) and distinct from closed #638 (native declaration of an unachievable slot). The native withdraw command itself is not claimed to be broken; the missing piece is its safe Pi facade continuation.

### Steps to reproduce
1. In a disposable repository, use `gentle_review inspect` and ordinary `start` for a small committed-only candidate that selects one materialized reviewer lens; grant consent when requested. To shorten a test run, set a small positive `GENTLE_PI_REVIEW_RELAY_PI_TIMEOUT_MS` in the Pi host environment before launch so the reviewer exceeds the bound.
2. Call bound `gentle_review status`, then submit the returned reviewer collect binding through `gentle_review_capture` (forecast, followed by the same binding with `reviewerRunAcknowledged: true`).
3. Observe `unachievable-lens-slot-declared` with `failure.kind: pi-timed-out` and a committed `unachievable_lens_slot` STOP. A fresh bound `gentle_review status` returns `hint: run gentle-ai review capture-unachievable ... --withdraw=true`.
4. Inspect the registered `gentle_review` operations: there is no corresponding withdrawal route. Merely starting a new Pi process with a larger timeout leaves that lineage at the same STOP.

### Expected and actual behavior
Expected: Expose a narrowly bound facade continuation for the provider-issued withdrawal, validating its exact current lineage/revision/target/context/request binding before mutation, then let bound STATUS reoffer only that reviewer slot. An equivalent documented facade-safe continuation would also work; do not infer new tokens, reset authority, or start a replacement lineage.

Actual: The provider supplies only a native CLI withdrawal command. Under the compact facade-only lifecycle, the review remains stopped with no reviewer verdict or acknowledgement, even though the source candidate is small and unchanged.

### gentle-pi version
3.7.0

### Pi version
0.87.1

### Operating system
Linux

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)
```text
outcome: unachievable-lens-slot-declared
failure.kind: pi-timed-out
elapsed_ms: 912772
timeout_ms: 912766
next_transition: stop / unachievable_lens_slot
mutation_outcome: committed
```

title: feat(odd): package a Pi Sec-TDD subagent with security routing and model profiles
body:
### Before submitting

### Problem or opportunity

Pi runtime agents belong to Gentle Shell. The local, user-authored security prototype is neither a packaged asset nor proof of discovery, permissions or model routing. Current ODD guidance names security-sensitive delegation, but the package does not own a verified Sec-TDD test-authoring agent.

Package a Pi-native `gentle-ai-security` definition with explicit owner and safe upgrade/retirement behavior. Route bounded security-sensitive ODD tasks to it; keep production fixes with the implementation worker. Verify negative-test-only edit scope, synthetic fixtures, no active attacks, and the difference between tool policy and OS isolation. Add focused tests proving installation, preservation of user modifications, dispatch, and model selection through both `/gentle:models` and `/gentle:profiles` under `--link` and isolated homes. Record RED/GREEN from actual tests; do not infer success from instructions.

### Alternatives considered

Use the local prototype directly (unmanaged), replace `review-risk` (read-only reviewer), or rely on Pi package contents alone (Pi package documentation does not promise subagent discovery).

### Additional context

Coordinate with the Gentle AI client-integration issue. Do not claim package uninstall cleans agents: HEAD currently shows retirement during installation, but no independently proven package-uninstall cleanup contract.

- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Motivation

The `gentle-pi` npm package's postinstall pins the bundled `gentle-ai` binary to a fixed release tag. `scripts/gentle-ai-installer.mjs` declares `export const INSTALLER_VERSION = "3.7.0"`, derives `GENTLE_AI_WINDOWS_SOURCE_TAG = "v3.7.0"`, and ships a hard-coded `GENTLE_AI_WINDOWS_SOURCE_MODULE_CHECKSUM = "h1:MQbzHlLdPklUQn0rVE9Mz94UygHsN2OPe7xMfPn9aGw="`. On Darwin/Linux the installer downloads the signed `gentle-ai_3.7.0_<platform>_<arch>.tar.gz` archive with SHA-256 pinned per platform; on Windows it source-builds from Go SumDB at the `v3.7.0` tag and verifies the pinned module checksum.

That is the right default for stability and reproducibility, but there is no opt-out for operators who explicitly want the bundled `gentle-ai` to track upstream main HEAD (or any other tag/commit). The existing `GENTLE_PI_GENTLE_AI_DEV_BINARY` escape hatch redirects `gentle-ai` invocations at runtime, but the on-disk binary inside `gentle-pi/.gentle-ai/v3.7.0/gentle-ai.exe` is still the pinned v3.7.0 build, which is what `gentle-ai doctor`, freshness probes, RDD review checks, and any tool that introspects the package-local runtime see as authoritative.

The bundled `gentle-engram` package (npm) presumably has the same shape against the Engram Go binary; a parallel audit is needed but the contract should be identical.

A complementary concern is raised in #1524, which documents that the README's `pi install npm:gentle-pi@<release>` form silently freezes users on that exact release. This proposal addresses the bundled-binary side of the same drift problem.

### Proposed behavior

Honor a new environment variable in `scripts/gentle-ai-installer.mjs` (and, by parallel construction, a sibling installer for `gentle-engram`) that overrides `INSTALLER_VERSION`:

| Env var | Value | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `GENTLE_PI_GENTLE_AI_INSTALL_VERSION` | unset (default) | Current behavior; pinned to `INSTALLER_VERSION`. |
| same | `main` | Resolve the latest commit on `https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai.git` `refs/heads/main`, then install that exact commit (signed release if one exists for the resolved version, else Go SumDB source-build with the corresponding module checksum). |
| same | `vX.Y.Z`, `X.Y.Z`, a 40-char commit SHA, or `github.com/.../gentle-ai@vX.Y.Z` | Install the requested pin via the same code path the default uses after version resolution. |

When the env var selects a non-default version the installer must:

1. Recompute `GENTLE_AI_WINDOWS_SOURCE_TAG`, `GENTLE_AI_WINDOWS_SOURCE_MODULE_CHECKSUM`, and (where applicable) the per-platform `GENTLE_AI_RELEASE_ASSETS` SHA-256 pair against the requested pin, instead of repeating the hard-coded literals. The current `GENTLE_AI_PENDING_DIGEST = "PENDING-GENTLE-AI-RELEASE-DIGEST"` sentinel already enforces fail-closed on a missing digest; that discipline must apply to the override path too.
2. Refuse to fall back to the hard-coded `INSTALLER_VERSION` checksum on mismatch. The current checksum verification already fails closed; the override path preserves that.
3. Refuse to proceed if the env var names a target that cannot be verified (no signed archive for that platform, no matching SumDB checksum). The default behavior is "pinned to a value with a known good digest"; the override should fail loudly rather than silently installing from a stale cache.

A companion `GENTLE_PI_ENGRAM_INSTALL_VERSION` would mirror the same contract for the Engram binary that `gentle-engram` bundles.

### Alternatives considered

- **Document the workaround only.** `GENTLE_PI_SKIP_GENTLE_AI_INSTALL=1` plus a separately managed binary registered via `~/.pi/gentle-ai/dev-binary.json` already exists, but it requires every operator to maintain a Go toolchain and a side `go install` workflow. The proposed env var keeps the npm-only install path viable for main-tracking operators.
- **Always pull main HEAD.** Would break the stability guarantee that signed release archives and pinned SumDB checksums provide. Not appropriate as a default; suitable as opt-in via the new env var.
- **Introduce a separate package (e.g. `gentle-pi@main`).** Heavyweight; doubles the publish surface for one extra env var.

### Compatibility

The env var is opt-in. The default branch keeps `INSTALLER_VERSION = "3.7.0"` and the current signed-archive / source-build checksum verification. No existing install path changes. Operators who already manage their own dev-binary through `GENTLE_PI_GENTLE_AI_DEV_BINARY` continue to work unchanged.

### Related

- #1524 — open: documented update path for the pinned `pi install npm:gentle-pi` command (complementary, addresses the install-pinned side of the same drift).
- #474 — closed: `dev-binary override not honored by agent-executed review lifecycle commands — bare gentle-ai still resolves the pinned 2.4.0 install` (complementary, addresses a different layer of the same family).
- #578 — open: document review relay configuration including `GENTLE_PI_GENTLE_AI_DEV_BINARY` (complementary; the new env var would belong in the same documentation surface).
- #1207 — open: facade rejects gentle-ai main's negotiated schema under the dev-binary override (further motivation for letting operators pin the package-local runtime to the same commit the dev-binary override uses).

title: bug(update): no post-upgrade gentle-ai sync notice or deferred sync when gentle-pi is bumped via Pi
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

Bumping `gentle-pi` through Pi's own extension update (`pi update --extensions`) leaves the pinned Gentle AI managed assets
 stale, with no in-product signal at any point.

   `gentle-ai` documents that after any upgrade the user must run `gentle-ai sync`, because its managed reviewer/runtime
 assets are version-bound to the binary and review lifecycle operations fail closed until sync succeeds. For its own update
 path, `gentle-ai` enforces this with a deferred-sync mechanism: `markPendingSyncAfterSelfUpdate` writes `PendingSync: true`
 to the install-state file before exiting, and the next launch under the new binary completes the deferred sync. It also
 prints a non-blocking advisory (`Run 'gentle-ai doctor' ... after upgrade`).

   That mechanism is never triggered in Pi. When gentle-pi is bumped, the new package-local binary is installed by gentle-pi's
 own postinstall (`scripts/install-gentle-ai.mjs`), which never sets `PendingSync` and never writes the install-state file. Pi
 CLI owns the package update and is generic by design, so it cannot know gentle-ai exists (correctly so). The bridging step
 belongs to gentle-pi, and it is missing.

   This is an asymmetry with every other managed agent. For OpenCode, Kilo, Claude Code, etc., `gentle-ai` owns the whole
 install -> upgrade -> sync cycle, so `PendingSync` covers it end to end. In Pi the package layer was taken over by Pi CLI's
 generic updater, so nothing bridges the two layers.

   Consequence, compounded by a hardcoded canonicalization in the pinned gentle-ai binary:
   - The v3.7.0 binary contains the literal `^2.6.0` as its canonical `pi-mcp-adapter` range.
   - `gentle-ai sync` writes that range into the Pi extension `package.json`.
   - With `pi-mcp-adapter` 3.x actually installed, the rewritten `^2.6.0` does not satisfy it, so the next `pi update
 --extensions` can silently downgrade the adapter 3.x -> 2.x.
   - Adapter 3.0.0 changed the config schema (requires `mcp-adapter.json`), so that downgrade can break MCP wiring.

   Because nothing surfaces the sync step, a user has no in-product pointer to the cause.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install gentle-pi into a Pi agent home with the package-local pinned gentle-ai binary provisioned.
   2. Start from a gentle-pi pinned to an older gentle-ai, then run `pi update --extensions` (or `pi install
 npm:gentle-pi@<newer>`).
   3. Restart Pi.
   4. Observe: no notice anywhere that `gentle-ai sync` is now required. The startup banner, `/gentle:doctor`, and the
 postinstall all stay silent.
   5. Run a review that needs the managed reviewer assets: it stops with `managed_assets_outdated`, which is the first and
 only place the sync command is ever surfaced.

   Evidence from the installed 3.7.0 package:
   - `extensions/startup-banner.ts` -> no managed-asset/digest awareness (every `sync` occurrence is `async`).
   - `scripts/install-gentle-ai.mjs` -> no `PendingSync` or install-state write.
   - `extensions/gentle-ai.ts:5611` and `:6258` (plus `lib/review-integration-v2.ts:580,1812`) -> the only code paths that
 render `gentle-ai sync`, all inside the review lifecycle.
   - `/gentle:doctor` audits only gentle-pi's own package assets (`delegation`/`review`/`sdd`) and points at
 `/gentle:install-<owner> --force`, not `gentle-ai sync`.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected:
   After a gentle-pi bump that changes the pinned gentle-ai version, Pi surfaces the required `gentle-ai sync` -- either by
 completing it automatically on the next launch (mirroring gentle-ai's own `PendingSync` deferred sync), or by an explicit,
 unmissable notice in the startup banner and `/gentle:doctor`.

   Proposed solution (either, or both):
   1. Set an equivalent pending-sync marker in gentle-pi's postinstall when the pinned gentle-ai version changes, and have the
 startup path complete or offer `gentle-ai sync` on the next launch.
   2. Extend `/gentle:doctor` -- which already audits assets via `packageAssetDiagnosticLines` -- to detect a
 `managed_asset_digest` mismatch between the pinned gentle-ai binary and the managed state file, and surface the exact
 `gentle-ai sync` command.
   3. Related: make the canonical `pi-mcp-adapter` range in the pinned gentle-ai version-aware, or at least never a floor
 below what the Pi package stack declares.

   Actual:
   Nothing is surfaced anywhere. The required sync is only revealed lazily, after a review already fails closed, and the
 canonicalization can then silently change the next update outcome.

### gentle-pi version

3.7.0

### Pi version

0.87.1

### Operating system

macOS

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
Deferred-sync mechanism (gentle-ai, internal/app/selfupdate.go, app.go):
   - `markPendingSyncAfterSelfUpdate` sets `PendingSync: true` under the canonical install-state lock.
   - Next launch with `PendingSync=true` runs the deferred sync and clears the flag; failures leave it set to retry.
   - `printPostUpgradeDoctorAdvisory` prints `[info]    Run 'gentle-ai doctor' to verify ecosystem health after upgrade`
 (app.go:252-255 next-launch path, app.go:588 CLI upgrade path).

   Absence in the Pi path:
   - `scripts/install-gentle-ai.mjs` -> zero occurrences of `PendingSync` / install-state write.
   - The managed state file -> no `PendingSync` field after a gentle-pi bump.
```

title: bug(docs): README's exact-version install pin freezes users on that release; no documented update path
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

`README.md` section "Path B: inside an existing pi" instructs an exact-version install:

```bash
# Published stable release: v3.5.1
pi install npm:gentle-pi@3.5.1
```

Pi treats versioned npm specifications as pinned, and its documented update command never moves them:

> Versioned npm specifications are pinned. Git tags and commits are also pinned; package updates reconcile the checkout but do not move a configured ref. — Pi `docs/packages.md`

So a user who follows the README's primary install command is frozen on that exact release for as long as the declaration stands, while `pi update --extensions` (documented as "Update all installed packages") keeps reporting success. The README never says the install is permanent, and no user-facing upgrade procedure exists anywhere in the docs.

`docs/readme-reference.md` section "Install -> Path B" says the opposite:

```bash
pi install npm:gentle-pi
```

> "This installs the current npm release; select an explicit version if you need a reproducible pin."

The two documents disagree on the recommended default, and the visible one (README) is the pinning one. It is also stale: the published `gentle-pi@3.7.0` tarball ships a README that instructs installing `3.5.1`, a release older than the package carrying the instruction.

The impact is not cosmetic. In the reported case the frozen package (2.6.0) bundled its own `gentle-ai` 2.8.0, while a separate `gentle-ai` on `PATH` (installed from the Go module and updated with `gentle-ai upgrade`) reported 3.7.0. `gentle-ai --version` therefore looked current while Pi's native review still ran the bundled 2.8.0 and blocked with `managed_assets_outdated`, with no signal pointing at the stale pin.

### Steps to reproduce

Environment: Windows 11, Pi 0.87.1.

1. Follow the README: `pi install npm:gentle-pi@<release>` and confirm the settings declaration is pinned (`npm:gentle-pi@<release>`).
2. Wait for newer releases, then run `pi update --extensions`.
3. Observe the command prints only `Updated packages` (exit 0), the installed version is unchanged, and nothing reports that newer releases exist.

Minimal pin reproduction with any npm Pi package, in an isolated agent home so no user state is touched:

```bash
export PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=/tmp/pi-pin-test/agent
pi install npm:pi-btw@0.5.0
pi update --extensions
node -p "require('/tmp/pi-pin-test/agent/npm/node_modules/pi-btw/package.json').version"
npm view pi-btw version
```

Observed: settings keep `"npm:pi-btw@0.5.0"`, the update prints `Updated packages`, the installed version stays `0.5.0`, and npm's latest is `0.6.1`. Installing without a version keeps the declaration floating (`npm:pi-btw`), so the freeze is created by the documented pin, not by Pi.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: following the README produces an install that `pi update --extensions` can advance, or the README states that the pin is permanent and gives the exact bump command (`pi install npm:gentle-pi@<new>`).

Actual: silent, indefinite freeze with a misleading success line, and two documents recommending opposite installs.

### gentle-pi version

2.6.0, frozen from 2026-09-14 (installed per the README's release-day pin). 3.7.0 was published 2026-09-23 and the drift was found on 2026-09-28, after roughly 20 `pi update --extensions` invocations in that window.

### Pi version

0.87.1

### Operating system

Windows

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
$ pi update --extensions
Updated packages
$ echo $?
0
```

No hint of the pin, and no notice of available newer releases. `gentle-pi` contains no update check today (no "newer version available" path), and `gentle-ai doctor` validates coherence against the installed binary rather than npm freshness.

Related: #299 (stale install version text, distinct from this pin/update-path defect). The Pi-side counterpart is reported separately in earendil-works/pi.

### Proposed fix

1. Make README Path B match the reference: default to `pi install npm:gentle-pi`, keeping pins as an explicit reproducibility choice.
2. Document the upgrade path for pinned installs (`pi install npm:gentle-pi@<new>`) and state that `pi update --extensions` does not move a pin.
3. Optionally surface version drift (startup banner, `/gentle:status`, or `gentle-ai doctor`) so a stale install is visible without reading Pi's documentation.

title: bug(release): the claude-bridge harness fix (#1497) is merged but unreleased; gentle-pi 3.7.0 still drops ODD on claude-bridge
body:
### Before submitting

### Problem

The fix for #1485 (#1497, "deliver the harness through appendSystemPrompt so bridge providers receive it") was merged to `main` on 2026-09-27. It is not in any published release:

2. Ask "Tell me about ODD".
