title: bug(editor): an abandoned bracketed-paste frame makes the prompt unresponsive for the rest of the session
body:
### Before submitting
- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem
Both prompt-editing paths buffer a bracketed-paste frame until they see the terminator, and **neither offers any way out once a frame has been abandoned**. In Vim mode the prompt stops accepting every subsequent keystroke for the rest of the session.

In `extensions/gentle-shell.ts:921-957`, `handleVimPasteFrame` returns `true` as soon as a `PASTE_START` marker is seen and the frame is not yet terminated. The caller at `:544` does `return` on that result, so the input never reaches `super.handleInput`. `pasteFrame` is cleared in exactly two places: a completed frame (`:948`) and `setVimPolicy` (`:430`). The 1 MiB overflow branch at `:937-939` only sets `pasteOverflow = true` and keeps swallowing input — it is explicitly not an escape.

So after an abandoned frame, Esc, Enter, printable keys, and `app.interrupt` are all consumed and dropped. Recovery requires `/reload` or a session switch.

The same pattern exists in the non-Vim selection path at `lib/selection-engine.ts:284`, but there a bound was added: `MAX_INCOMPLETE_PASTE_BYTES` (16 MiB, `:192`, `:293`) eventually abandons the frame. That is the correct mitigation and it already exists in this codebase — it was simply never applied to the Vim path, which uses a character bound with no exit at all.

### Steps to reproduce
Derived from source review of `main`, not from an observed runtime failure, so treat these as a proposed validation.

1. Check out `main` at `b27bd328b95e83967ffc23f62b76e77901b91130` with Pi `0.87.1` installed.
2. Enable Vim prompt mode with `/gentle:vim` and set the policy to `on`.
3. Send `ESC [ 200 ~` without the matching `ESC [ 201 ~`, so a paste frame is opened and never terminated. A truncated paste, an interrupted terminal client, or a synthetic `pi.sendInput` is enough.
4. Type any key, for example `x`, then press Esc, then press Enter.
5. Observe that nothing appears in the prompt and no command runs. The editor is inert.
6. Run `/reload`. The prompt returns to normal, confirming the state is per-instance and that no other path clears it.

For the non-Vim variant, step 2 is unnecessary: with the policy `off`, the selection engine buffers at `lib/selection-engine.ts:284` and only recovers once 16 MiB have accumulated, so the same abandoned frame is survivable but not escapable.

### Expected and actual behavior
Expected: an abandoned bracketed-paste frame is abandoned rather than left open. Either the buffer resets after a bounded idle period, or Esc while no terminator has arrived cancels the frame and returns the editor to a usable state, and the buffered bytes are discarded instead of forwarded to the host editor.

Actual: the frame stays open indefinitely. Every subsequent keystroke is consumed by the paste handler and dropped, including Esc and the abort key. The prompt is unresponsive until `/reload` or a session switch discards the editor instance.

### gentle-pi version
Unreleased `main` at commit `b27bd328b95e83967ffc23f62b76e77901b91130` (the most recent tag is `v3.7.0`, `59257bff`).

Vim path introduced in `8e0e859` (`feat(shell): wire opt-in Vim prompt mode with docs and tests`). Selection path bound in `177988b` (`fix(editor): bound incomplete selection paste frames`), which fixed the same class of problem for the selection engine only.

### Pi version
0.87.1

### Operating system
Other

Source was reviewed on Android/Termux (aarch64). The finding is in platform-neutral TypeScript and is not believed to be OS-specific; it is reached through the normal key-event path, so it should reproduce on any terminal that delivers the paste markers.

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)
```text
extensions/gentle-shell.ts:544
        if ((this.vimPolicy === "on" || this.vimRejected) && this.handleVimPasteFrame(data)) return;

extensions/gentle-shell.ts:936
        if (!this.pasteOverflow) {
            if (this.pasteFrame.length + content.length > MAX_BRACKETED_PASTE_CHARS) {
                this.pasteFrame = "";
                this.pasteOverflow = true;
            } else this.pasteFrame += content;
        }

lib/selection-engine.ts:192
const MAX_INCOMPLETE_PASTE_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
```

Related: #1413 (opt-in Vim prompt editing, closed) is the feature this regresses. It documents paste as a supported capability but does not specify abandonment semantics.

title: bug(agents): receiver-side session message enters the model context with triggerTurn and no consent or sender authentication
body:
### Before submitting
- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem
`orchestrator_send_message` gates outbound messages behind a human decision (#1364), but the **receiving** session applies no gate at all, and the sender identity is self-declared. Together these mean the consent control is not a boundary: it only constrains cooperating callers.

Two independent gaps in the same path:

1. **No receiver-side gate.** The transport listener in `extensions/gentle-agents.ts:438-442` validates staleness only, then calls `pi.sendMessage(..., { deliverAs: "followUp", triggerTurn: true })`. There is no prompt, no allowlist, and no `SessionMessagingGrants` consultation on the receive side. Any inbound message is inserted into the model context and **forces a turn**, interrupting the receiving user's session.

2. **No sender authentication.** `senderSessionId` is validated in `lib/agents-session-transport.ts` against a regex (`/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,127}$/`) and against the `SESSION` frame kind, but nothing binds it to the connecting process or to a presence record. Any same-uid process able to read the presence directory or reach the endpoint can advertise any session id.

The consent grant is additionally **per-peer rather than per-disclosure**: `lib/session-messaging-grants.ts:84` short-circuits on `this.grants.get(id)?.has(recipient)`, so a single "Allow for this session" decision authorizes every later payload to that same recipient for the life of the session. This is consistent with the three documented decisions in #1364, but it means a one-time benign exchange silently authorizes an unrestricted channel afterwards.

`docs/gentle-shell.md:183` documents consent as outbound-only, so the asymmetry is intentional in the docs. The defect is that the documented scope leaves the receiver unprotected against an unauthenticated sender.

### Steps to reproduce
This was derived from source review of `main`, not from an observed runtime failure, so treat the steps below as a proposed validation rather than an observed session.

1. Check out `main` at `b27bd328b95e83967ffc23f62b76e77901b91130` with Pi `0.87.1` installed.
2. Open two sessions on the same machine and profile, so both appear as advertised peers.
3. In session A, call `orchestrator_send_message` once and answer **Allow for this session**.
4. Call `orchestrator_send_message` again to the same recipient with unrelated full task context. Note that no prompt is shown — the grant at `lib/session-messaging-grants.ts:84` returns before any UI interaction.
5. In session B, observe that the arriving message enters the model context and starts a turn with no prompt and no visible authorization step in B.
6. For the authentication gap: construct a transport frame whose `senderSessionId` names a session that is not the connecting process, and observe that the receiver's admission check at `extensions/gentle-agents.ts:439` passes, because it compares generation/session identity, not sender provenance.

### Expected and actual behavior
Expected: the receiving session authorizes inbound orchestrator messages before they enter the model context, and the sender identity is established by something other than a self-declared field — or, at minimum, an unauthenticated inbound message is surfaced for the user to accept instead of forcing a turn.

Actual: any same-uid process can inject a message that is inserted into the model context with `triggerTurn: true` and no receiver-side decision. The sender-side consent gate does not prevent this, because it lives in the process that calls the tool, not in the transport.

### gentle-pi version
Unreleased `main` at commit `b27bd328b95e83967ffc23f62b76e77901b91130` (the most recent tag is `v3.7.0`, `59257bff`).

### Pi version
`0.87.1`

### Operating system
Other

Source was reviewed on Android/Termux (aarch64). The finding is in platform-neutral TypeScript and is not believed to be OS-specific.

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)
```text
extensions/gentle-agents.ts:438
                listener = sessionTransport.createListener(registry, sessionId, async (notification) => {
                    const active = activeSessionTransport;
                    if (!active || active.generation !== generation || active.sessionManager !== sessionManager || active.sessionId !== sessionId || sessions !== sessionManager || activeSessionId() !== sessionId) throw new Error("stale session transport");
                    pi.sendMessage({ customType: AGENTS_ORCHESTRATOR_MESSAGE_TYPE, content: `Session message from ${notification.senderSessionId} (correlation ${notification.id}): ${notification.message}`, display: true, details: { gentleAgents: { senderSessionId: notification.senderSessionId, recipientSessionId: sessionId, correlationId: notification.id, direction: "incoming" } } }, { deliverAs: "followUp", triggerTurn: true });
                });

lib/session-messaging-grants.ts:84
        if (this.grants.get(id)?.has(recipient)) return;
```

Related: #1364 (sender-side consent, closed) and #798 (notification transport, closed). Neither covers receiver-side authorization or sender provenance.

title: bug(agents): background subagent completion never reaches a working parent lane; steering stays queued until Pi is relaunched
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

**Summary.** In an interactive Pi session running as an orchestrator lane under Herdr, background subagents launched with `subagent_run` (`mode: "background"`) finish, but the parent session never processes their completion. The parent stays in `working` indefinitely, and any new user message is shown as `Steering … queued` and is never processed. The only way out is to kill Pi and relaunch it with `pi --session <id>`.

The completion itself is not lost on disk: the task record under the Gentle Agents task store (`gentle-agents/tasks/<task-id>.json`) contains the subagent's final message, with a modification time 30 to 60 minutes before the moment the parent was observed still waiting.

This looks different from #1092: there the parent becomes idle after the completion is downgraded to a transcript-only stale entry. Here the parent never leaves `working` and stops processing steering messages, so it cannot be recovered from inside the session. It may share a root with #1092 (both involve completion delivery while the parent is busy), but the observable symptom differs, so I am filing it separately. I am not asserting a root cause.

### Steps to reproduce

No deterministic reproduction yet. Conditions under which it was observed:

1. Run gentle-shell (`gentle-shell --link`) inside a Herdr pane as an orchestrator lane, with the claude-bridge provider.
2. Launch one or more subagents with `subagent_run` in background mode (several were often running in parallel: verifiers, Judgment Day judges, workers).
3. Wait for them to finish.
4. Observe that the parent keeps showing `working`, and that a new message typed into the lane is shown as `Steering … queued` and is never processed.
5. Check the task record: its final message is present and its mtime is well before the current time.

Context that may matter (not verified as causal): several subagents ran in parallel, and during the same day there were machine reboots and provider session-limit cutoffs in between.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: when a background subagent settles, the parent receives the completion (or at least a wake request) and returns to processing; queued steering messages are processed.

Actual: the parent stays in `working` for 30+ minutes after the subagent settled; steering messages stay queued; only killing Pi and resuming the session with `pi --session <id>` recovers the lane.

**Workaround:** kill Pi and relaunch with `pi --session <id>`; then read the result with `subagent_result`.

**Frequency:** at least 4 occurrences on a single day, in 4 different lanes (e.g. a verifier that finished and the lane was still waiting ~35 minutes later; Judgment Day judges; workers finishing while the lane kept waiting).

**Not verified:** the root cause; whether the parent was inside a long tool call when the completion settled (the #1092 branch); whether reboots or provider cutoffs were involved in each case; raw RPC event timestamps were not captured; not reproduced on a clean single-subagent session.

**Versions:** gentle-pi package 3.7.0, prerelease build `main-06c9915c`; gentle-ai binary `main-3a19dbf8` (prerelease); Pi 0.87.1; Linux 7.0 x86_64; runtime Pi with the claude-bridge provider, inside Herdr.

### gentle-pi version

3.7.0 (prerelease build main-06c9915c)

### Pi version

0.87.1

### Operating system

Linux

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
Steering … queued
(new user messages stay queued; the lane keeps showing "working" while the
subagent task record already holds its final assistant message)
```

title: test(history): mtime fallback tests in history-session-scan-extract fail intermittently
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

Two tests in `tests/history-session-scan-extract.test.ts` fail intermittently and pass on retry:

- `ts precedence: message ms beats entry ISO; ISO alone; header ts; file mtime; NaN hops tolerated (AC-S1-4)` (line 197)
- `a header with NO timestamp field (parseHeader NaN branch) plus timestamp-less messages falls back to the file mtime` (line 567)

Both check that the timestamp falls back to the file mtime using the same window:

```ts
const before = Date.now() - 5;
// write the session file
const after = Date.now() + 5000;
assert.ok(ts >= before && ts <= after);
```

**Cause.** The 5 ms lower margin is smaller than the granularity of file timestamps. On Linux the kernel stamps mtime from a coarse clock that advances per tick (every 4 ms with `CONFIG_HZ=250`), so the mtime can land behind the `Date.now()` taken *before* the write. When that lag exceeds 5 ms, `ts >= before` fails.

I measured it by writing and statting a file 5000 times on the same machine (WSL2, ext4, `CONFIG_HZ=250`):

```text
{ n: 5000, below_before_minus_5ms: 942, max_lag_ms: '7.366' }
```

So in ~19% of writes the mtime landed more than 5 ms before `before`, with a maximum lag of 7.4 ms. In the full suite, with many more files and load, the test hits that case now and then.

**Possible fix.** Make the lower bound independent of the file clock resolution:
- widen the margin (for example `Date.now() - 1000`, still precise enough for what is checked), or
- compare directly against `statSync(file).mtimeMs`, which is exactly the value the timestamp should come from.

The second option is exact and needs no margin.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Linux (or WSL2), run `pnpm test` several times, or just `node --experimental-strip-types --test tests/history-session-scan-extract.test.ts` in a loop.
2. Sooner or later one of the two tests fails on `assert.ok(ts >= before && ts <= after)`.

To see the cause directly:

```bash
node -e '
const fs=require("fs");let worse=0,maxLag=0,n=5000;
for(let i=0;i<n;i++){const before=Date.now();fs.writeFileSync("/tmp/mt.txt","x"+i);const m=fs.statSync("/tmp/mt.txt").mtimeMs;const lag=before-m;if(lag>maxLag)maxLag=lag;if(m<before-5)worse++;}
console.log({n,below_before_minus_5ms:worse,max_lag_ms:maxLag.toFixed(3)});'
```

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: the tests always pass, whatever the file clock resolution.

Actual: they fail intermittently with:

```text
AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: The expression evaluated to a falsy value:
  assert.ok(ts >= before && ts <= after)
    at tests/history-session-scan-extract.test.ts:244:10
```

### gentle-pi version

`main` at b27bd328 (3.7.0)

### Pi version

0.87.1

### Operating system

Windows (WSL)

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
✖ ts precedence: message ms beats entry ISO; ISO alone; header ts; file mtime; NaN hops tolerated (AC-S1-4) (19.479844ms)
  AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: The expression evaluated to a falsy value:

    assert.ok(ts >= before && ts <= after)

      at TestContext.<anonymous> (tests/history-session-scan-extract.test.ts:244:10)
  actual: false,
  expected: true,
```

title: review: candidates touching src/generated/** reliably exceed lens_context_budget_exceeded - need path-exclusion mechanism
body:
# review: candidates touching `src/generated/**` reliably exceed `lens_context_budget_exceeded` — need a path-exclusion mechanism

**Environment:** gentle-pi 3.7.0, contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, Windows, ordinary reviews via the Pi compact facade.

## Problem

Any feature commit that includes changes to generated code (in our case the tracked Prisma client output `web/src/generated/prisma/**`, regenerated on every migration) produces reviewer-evidence so large that `review.start` dies in preflight:

```
code: lens_context_budget_exceeded
"The candidate's complete reviewer evidence exceeds the native context budget…
 immutable candidate evidence is never truncated and retrying this exact
 candidate cannot succeed, so split it into a chained sequence of smaller
 reviewable commits…"
```

Three START attempts today failed this way across two single commits and one chained range (13–18 files, 3644 insertions dominated by generated output). The remediation the stop message suggests ("split into smaller reviewable commits") is **not applicable**: the generated diff lives inside a single commit, and splitting it would require rewriting history, which is exactly what a review tool must never force a user to do.

## What we did instead (suboptimal)

- Reviewed the pre-generated-code and post-generated-code slices; the generated-heavy commits went without native review (documented, code covered by manual audit + smoke).
- Untracked `web/src/generated/**` entirely (hygiene commit) — helps all *future* commits, but historical commits remain permanently unreviewable by the engine.

## Request

One of:

1. **Path-exclusion hint at inspect/START time** — e.g. `--exclude-path web/src/generated/**`, producing a target whose changed-path manifest ignores generated paths (and lists them as inert). The reviewer never needs generated boilerplate to judge a feature commit.
2. **Treat generated-looking paths as inert evidence** — e.g. `.gitattributes`-style declaration (`gentle-ai: generated`), or convention-based (`*generated*`), excluded from the lens context budget automatically.
3. **Budget scoping for deletions/context lines** — if the budget currently counts context+removals, reviewing only the *reviewable* portion of the diff (additions in non-generated paths) may already fit most feature commits.

## Related

#1154 / #741 — separate capture-route defect (same candidate series reproduced it today, comment added).

title: bug(assets): published gentle-pi@3.7.0 still ships the pre-retirement SDD surfaces
body:
## Summary

The repository tree is post-retirement (`#1408`, tracked in `#1456`), but the **published npm artifact** `gentle-pi@3.7.0` still ships the pre-retirement SDD surfaces and the pre-retirement prompt vocabulary.

## Evidence

```
$ npm pack gentle-pi@3.7.0 --pack-destination /tmp
$ tar -tzf /tmp/gentle-pi-3.7.0.tgz | grep -ci sdd
43
```

Those 43 paths include:

- 13 `package/assets/agents/sdd-*.md` (apply, archive, design, explore, init, onboard, proposal, remediate, research, spec, status, tasks, verify)
- 3 `package/assets/chains/sdd-{full,plan,verify}.chain.md`
- `package/assets/sdd-orchestrator-workflow.md`
- `package/assets/support/sdd-status-contract.md`

The same tarball's `package/assets/agents/gentle-ai-worker.md` reads:

> `description: Scoped package-owned implementation writer for bounded non-SDD work.`

while the post-retirement tree (`fe61793e`) reads `bounded ODD work`, and `find assets -iname '*sdd*' | wc -l` there returns `0`.

Both the published tarball and the tree declare `"version": "3.7.0"` — same version, different content.

## Impact

Any install from the registry receives the retired asset set and the older prompt vocabulary. On the machine where this was found, the retirement guard in `installPackageAssets` prevented the `sdd-*` files from being materialized (0 in the active home), so the reachable damage was limited to the **prompt vocabulary**: 3 of 10 active agent prompts differed from the tree (`gentle-ai-explore` 6 lines, `gentle-ai-verify` 8 lines, `gentle-ai-worker` 16 lines), with `non-SDD` wording plus `sdd-init` / Strict TDD references.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- `#1456` sweeps the backlog against **main**, which is verifiably clean ("0 files of OpenSpec parsing code, `sdd-preflight`, `sdd-init`, and `sdd-profiles` assets"). This report is about the gap between **main and what the registry publishes**, which no tracker covers.
- `#608` is about *installed* SDD agents becoming orphaned and never refreshing (manifest/hash drift). This report is about the **published artifact** shipping pre-retirement surfaces — including for an agent that is not SDD at all (`gentle-ai-worker.md`).

## Suggested fix

Republish a version whose `assets/` match the post-retirement tree, so a registry install cannot reintroduce the retired surfaces or the retired vocabulary.

title: Gentle Agents: optional per-subagent context guard and CodeGraph-first hint
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Gentle Agents replaces the third-party `pi-subagents-j0k3r` package. I still run a local build of that package because it has two features I rely on that Gentle Agents (3.7.0) does not have:

1. **A per-subagent context guard.** A child is stopped with a clear error before it runs past its model's context window. The limit is the smallest of a hard token cap, `window × ratio`, and `window − reserve`, configured in `subagents.json`. There is also an optional preflight check on the parent before a run starts. Without it, a runaway exploration child spends tokens until the provider rejects the request.
2. **An opt-in "CodeGraph first" hint.** When the child session has CodeGraph tools, a short note is appended to its system prompt telling it to use them before broad file reads. This noticeably cuts tokens for exploration agents.

Because Gentle Agents stays unregistered while the old package is installed, I keep that package and get the startup warning in every session.

### Proposed outcome

Add both as optional settings for Gentle Agents in `subagents.json`, off by default. For example:

```json
{
  "resource_guard": {
    "enabled": true,
    "context_hard_limit_tokens": 180000,
    "context_limit_ratio": 0.8,
    "context_reserve_tokens": 16384,
    "parent_context_preflight": true
  },
  "codegraph_first_advisory": true
}
```

When the guard trips, the task ends with a typed, visible error, such as `resource_limit`, that includes the observed usage and the limit. It should not look like a silent stall.

### Alternatives considered

- **Keep the old package.** That leaves Gentle Agents disabled and shows a warning on every start.
- **Rely on the stall watchdog.** It catches silence, not a child that is busy but growing its context without bound.
- **A heap guard.** The old in-process runner needed one. Gentle Agents runs each child in its own `pi --mode rpc` process, so it is probably not needed.

### Additional context

The implementation lives in a local, unpublished branch of `pi-subagents-j0k3r` (`resource-guard`, about 120 lines plus tests). I can share it if it helps.

title: bug(issue-creation): agent asks user to affirm its own checks again after #875
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

These are evidence-backed checks performed by the submitting agent, not actions attributed to the user. The earlier report #875 describes the original defect; this is a recurrence with the fix already shipped.

### Problem

Gentle AI v3.7.0's issue-creation skill can still interpret operational issue-form checkboxes as declarations that *the user* must repeat in first person, even after the agent itself has searched for duplicates and reviewed the draft for sensitive information. A user explicitly asked the agent to publish a prepared issue, repeatedly authorized publication, and asked the agent to do these checks; publication was nevertheless blocked for multiple turns until the user repeated the exact first-person phrasing.

This is the behavior #875 was closed as fixing. Reproduction was added to #875 as a comment, but a new issue is needed to track the regression while the previous one remains closed as completed.

### Steps to reproduce

1. With gentle-pi 3.7.0 and the bundled `gentle-ai-issue-creation` skill v1.3, ask the agent to publish a reviewed bug report using the repository's Bug Report YAML form.
2. Have the agent search open and closed issues and inspect the exact publication body for sensitive data. In the observed session it did both, retaining the search and scan results.
3. Authorize publication and, if asked, instruct the agent to perform the checks itself.
4. Observe that the agent insists on the user personally saying "I searched" and "I reviewed" before it will mark the required checkboxes, despite those being checks the agent performed.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: The agent may attest to its own evidence-backed operational checks, making clear that it performed them rather than attributing them to the user. Personal facts, legal declarations and consent still require human affirmation. Keep the duplicate search, privacy review, form structure, and publication authorization.

Actual: The agent treated the first-person wording as requiring an exact personal declaration from the user, refused to publish despite repeated authorization, and falsely described the operational checks as user-only requirements. This caused several unnecessary back-and-forth turns and user frustration.

Related: #875 (closed as completed), its recurrence comment, and the eventual publication #1494. Consider a regression example that distinguishes agent-owned operational checks from genuinely human-only assertions and accepts natural-language publication authorization without treating it as consent to *human-only* declarations.

### gentle-pi version

3.7.0 (`gentle-ai-issue-creation` skill v1.3)

### Pi version

0.87.1

### Operating system

Windows (WSL)

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
Agent after completing duplicate and privacy checks:
Agent required the user to repeat first-person checkbox statements despite having completed both checks.
User asked agent to check, authorized publication again, and was prompted again for a first-person statement.
```

title: bug(orchestrator): small fixes trigger disproportionate ODD, memory and review overhead
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

On a trivial, fully specified task, the primary-session gentle-ai prompt makes an OpenAI model do about **5x the work of the same model without gentle-pi**. Both runs produce the same correct result. The extra cost is orchestration, not problem solving.

In a controlled A/B test, same model, same task, and same repository, gentle-pi's rules were each applied literally:

- one `gentle-ai-verify` subagent **per unit test**, plus a baseline and a final verify;
- an ODD task file in the target repo;
- 10 Engram operations for a 3-line fix;
- 3 native review calls that could not complete unattended.

To users this looks like a "dumber" or "nerfed" model. The model is fine: without the harness it solves the same task in under a minute. This is the problem class of #463 (verification command presence forces subagent delegation) and #1342 (closed by its author, no linked fix). This report adds a controlled, reproducible measurement on the latest release (v3.7.0). It also shows that the overhead is not limited to verification: ODD, memory, and review all trigger for work that is small and already understood.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a throwaway git repo with this fixture (3 independent one-line bugs, 3 failing `unittest` tests):

   `inventory.py`
   ```python
   def total_stock(items):
       total = 0
       for item in items[1:]:
           total += item["qty"]
       return total

   def parse_price(text):
       return float(text.replace("$", ""))

   def low_stock(items, threshold):
       return [i["name"] for i in items if i["qty"] < threshold]
   ```

   `tests/test_inventory.py` expects `total_stock(ITEMS) == 16`, `parse_price("$1,234.50") == 1234.50`, and `low_stock(ITEMS, 5) == ["apple", "pear"]` for `ITEMS = [pear:5, apple:2, fig:9]`.

2. Copy it into two directories, `A` and `B`, and use this prompt in both:

   > The test suite in this repo fails (run it with `python3 -m unittest`). Fix the three bugs in inventory.py so every test passes, without changing the tests. Track the three fixes as a task list and keep it accurate as you go. You are running unattended: do not ask me any questions, make reasonable decisions yourself, and do not commit. When finished, reply with a short summary.

3. Run both arms with the same model:

   ```bash
   # A: full gentle-pi install
   (cd A && pi -p --mode json --model openai-codex/gpt-6-sol --session-dir ../sess-A "$PROMPT")
   # B: no extensions, only gentle-pi's todo tool so task tracking stays comparable
   (cd B && pi -p --mode json --model openai-codex/gpt-6-sol --no-extensions \
      -e <gentle-pi>/extensions/gentle-todo.ts --session-dir ../sess-B "$PROMPT")
   ```

4. Compare tool calls and usage in both session files.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: for a small, fully specified task, gentle-pi takes a bounded fast path (edit, run the test command once inline, update the task list, report), with overhead in the same range as the bare model. Subagent verification, ODD artifacts, memory sync, and native review should scale with task size and risk, not trigger on every task.

Actual (n=1 per arm):

| | A: full gentle-pi | B: no extensions + todo |
|---|---|---|
| Tests pass | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| Wall time | **245 s** | **46 s** |
| Tool calls | 40 | 10 |
| `subagent_run` | 5 (`gentle-ai-verify`: baseline, **one per test**, final) | 0 |
| Engram ops | 10 (`mem_search`×2, `mem_save`, `mem_update`×4, `mem_get_observation`, `mem_review`, `mem_session_summary`) | 0 |
| `gentle_review` | 3 (ended "unapproved: could not answer consent prompt") | 0 |
| Files created by the model in target repo | `odd/tasks/…md` | none |
| Total tokens (parent session) | ~1.30M (1.20M cache read) | ~113k |
| Final todo state | all `done` | all `done` |

Both gentle-pi runs also got a `.gitignore` with `.atl/`, written by the extension runtime rather than the model. Token totals are for the parent session only and exclude the 5 verifier subagents, so A's real cost is higher.

Notes:
- The fixed code was functionally identical in both arms.
- In real sessions, the same literal reading also shows up as task lists that never move to `done`, because `orchestrator-memory.md` requires checking off only observed outcomes and any pending human or commit step keeps an implemented, verified task `pending`. That makes the task list hard to use as a progress signal.
- Limitations: one run per arm, one task, one model. I have not measured whether other providers follow these rules less literally. The OpenAI models tested appear to execute every MUST/mandatory rule as written, which makes proportionality in the prompt especially important for them.

### gentle-pi version

3.7.0

### Pi version

0.87.1

### Operating system

Windows (WSL)

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
A subagent tasks (truncated):
- "Read-only baseline verification ... Run exactly `python3 -m unittest`, report exit status..."
- "Run exactly `python3 -m unittest tests.test_inventory.InventoryTest.test_total_stock` to verify first..."
- "Run exactly `python3 -m unittest tests.test_inventory.InventoryTest.test_parse_price_with_thousands`..."
- "Run exactly `python3 -m unittest tests.test_inventory.InventoryTest.test_low_stock_inclusive_and_sor..."
- "Read-only final verification ... Run exactly `python3 -m unittest`; report command result/count..."

A final reply: "... Native review remains unapproved because this unattended run could not answer its consent prompt."
```

title: feat(review): surface in-flight reviewer lens progress during capture (wire the discarded onUpdate)
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

A high-tier native review runs four reviewer lenses through the Pi host relay, and each lens run is a minutes-long one-shot completion (`runInProcessReviewer`, `lib/inprocess-reviewer.ts`). While a capture runs, the session shows only the amber in-flight capture card naming the lens:

- the capture tools discard the streaming `onUpdate` channel they receive (`execute(_toolCallId, parameters, signal, _onUpdate, ctx)` for `gentle_review_capture` / `gentle_review_capture_group`, `extensions/gentle-ai.ts`)
- the reviewer's model stream is consumed by `.result()` and never forwarded (`lib/inprocess-reviewer.ts`)
- per-slot progress is computed only after slots settle and exists solely in the tool's return value (`reviewHostRelayGroupProgress`, `extensions/gentle-ai.ts`)

So a single-lens capture can block for several minutes with zero feedback, and a four-lens tier-high review multiplies that. From the user's seat it looks like a hung tool call: no way to tell the materialize/review/prepare phases apart, and no visibility into group concurrency (`runReviewHostRelayReviewerGroup` starts all reviewers via `Promise.allSettled`, `lib/review-host-relay.ts`).

### Proposed outcome

Surface per-slot reviewer progress while a capture runs, without changing the review lifecycle or the provider contract:

- Wire the currently discarded `onUpdate` of the capture tools to a compact per-slot projection emitted from the relay choke points (`prepareReviewHostRelaySlot` / `runReviewHostRelayReviewerGroup`, `lib/review-host-relay.ts`): `selected -> materialized -> reviewing -> prepared -> submitted`, plus elapsed time.
- Render it in the existing in-flight lifecycle card (`renderGentleAiLifecycleCall` already renders lens names for captures), so a running capture shows live lens state instead of a static label.
- Keep it read-only presentation with no cancel affordance. Reviewer lifecycle authority stays with the native controller; a UI-side abort is exactly the reviewer-aborted failure class, not a feature.

### Alternatives considered

- Showing reviewer runs as rows in the `gentle:agents` overlay: rejected. That overlay is the subagent task surface (its palette label is literally "Subagents"); every row promises task interactions (open transcript, stop) that reviewer runs cannot support, and reviewers are deliberately tool-less single completions, not delegable agents. Mixing them there would misrepresent the reviewer/agent boundary that keeps adjudication off live state.
- #1306 covers the cross-turn compact lifecycle summary in the Status sidebar and explicitly excludes individual reviewer rows; this request is the in-flight counterpart inside the running tool call, not a replacement.
- #544 (reviewer roles as native Pi subagents) would give visibility for free if adopted, since real subagent rows already appear in the agents surface. This request is the smaller step for today's in-process relay and becomes moot for any slot #544 migrates.

### Additional context

- Related: #1238 surfaces per-lens prompt size and relay bounds before capture; this covers the during-run half. #1463 covers the idle-at-collect case (controller waiting for manual submission); this covers the opposite state (submission running, nothing visible).
- Evidence anchors: `extensions/gentle-ai.ts` (capture tool execute signatures discarding onUpdate; `GENTLE_TIMED_TOOLS` timing ledger; `renderGentleAiLifecycleCall` lens rendering), `lib/review-host-relay.ts` (slot preparation, group runner), `lib/inprocess-reviewer.ts` (one-shot completion, tool-call refusal).
- Observed while delivering a tier-high four-lens review end to end: single-slot reviewer runs of roughly one to five minutes each, a group capture aborted mid-run with no interim signal, and post-hoc recovery through fresh STATUS reoffering the same slot.

title: bug(launcher): --package-root warning is wrong when a path declaration plus a different requested root forces the take-over
bug(installer): Windows global pnpm paths exceed staging path limit
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

On Windows, the `gentle-pi` postinstall can fail before Go starts when pnpm's global package layout makes the package-local Gentle AI staging prefix exceed the classic Windows path limit. In the reproduced layout, the package root was 233 characters and the `.gentle-ai\\.v3.7.0.staging-*` prefix reached 261 characters, causing `mkdtemp` to fail with `ENOENT`. The package update then cannot publish the package-local runtime.

This is independent of #946. That issue covers a later `EPERM` while renaming a populated staging directory. This report covers the earlier path-length failure during staging-directory creation.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use Windows with a deep pnpm global package layout for `gentle-pi`.
2. Install or update `gentle-pi` through pnpm's global package flow.
3. Observe that the postinstall fails before the Go source-build step with an `ENOENT` from `mkdtemp` for the package-local `.gentle-ai` staging path.
4. Repeat with a shorter package-root path and observe that staging succeeds.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: the installer keeps its temporary staging path usable for deep global package layouts, without requiring users to change Windows long-path policy, and publishes a verified package-local runtime.

Actual: `mkdtemp` rejects the staging prefix once the resolved path exceeds the classic Windows limit. No package-local runtime is published, and installation fails before Go starts.

### gentle-pi version

3.7.0

### Pi version

Not applicable, reproduced in the package postinstall path.

### Operating system

Windows

```text
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, mkdtemp '<package-root>\\.gentle-ai\\.v3.7.0.staging-XXXX'
```

title: bug(review): readability/reliability lenses deterministically exhaust the relay output bound (stopReason length) on any model — review uncompletable
body:
### Before submitting
- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem
On a committed-range native review of a large documentation-heavy diff (26 paths, +858/-137, risk tier `high`), two of the four reviewer lenses — `review-readability` and `review-reliability` — **deterministically fail with `reviewer-empty-output` (`stopReason: length`)** while the other two (`review-risk`, `review-resilience`) complete normally on the same ~190 KB materialized prompt. The lineage can therefore never reach 4/4 lenses, so the review can never complete, on any model the host has available.

Observations across 10 capture attempts (single-slot captures, fresh STATUS before each):

| lens | attempts | stopReasons | model / effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| review-readability | 4 | length ×3, stop ×1 | nan/deepseek-v4-flash, effort high |
| review-readability | 2 | length ×2 | nan/glm5.3-flash, effort high |
| review-readability | 1 | length | nan/glm5.3-flash, effort medium |
| review-readability | 1 | length | openai-codex/gpt-6-astra, effort medium |
| review-reliability | 1 | length | nan/deepseek-v4-flash, effort high |
| review-reliability | 1 | length | nan/glm5.3-flash, effort high |

Every failing run lasts ~55–60 s and then reports `stopReason: length` with **no text at all** — the fixed output budget is consumed entirely (apparently by reasoning) before any artifact text is emitted. `review-risk` and `review-resilience` on the identical prompt size complete in one to three attempts with 2–4 KB results.

Related but distinct reports: #1167 (default thinking level can end a review — ours fails even at `medium` effort), #1083 (deterministic zero bytes — ours is truncation via `length`, not a silent child), #1259 (empty-output refusal discards model/token evidence — agreed, that made the diagnosis slower).

Two secondary observations from the same investigation:
- The lens model routing is user-owned through `subagents.json` `model_profiles`, but the `agents/review-*.md` files carry a `model:` frontmatter that managed-asset sync reverts on every capture — editing them looks like a supported knob but silently has no durable effect. A doc pointer to the real knob would save users a long detour.
- The failure envelope does not report the output bound that was hit, so users cannot tell truncation from a model bug (echoes #1259).

### Steps to reproduce
1. Repo with a reviewable committed range of ~25–30 mostly-Markdown/Shell paths (~1000 changed lines), mostly normative prose.
2. `gentle-ai review start` committed-range (full base ref, `committedOnly`), high risk tier, four lenses, in-process host relay (`--materialize=true` slots).
3. Capture `review-risk` and `review-resilience` — they admit normally.
4. Capture `review-readability` (order 2): observe `reviewer-empty-output`, `stopReason: length`, ~55–60 s elapsed, no text produced.
5. Repeat with any enabled model/effort routed via `subagents.json` `model_profiles` — same result. `review-reliability` (order 3) behaves the same.

### Expected and actual behavior
Expected: every lens slot can eventually produce its reviewer artifact on a reasonable model, or the failure envelope names the binding constraint (output bound reached, prompt size, lens) so the operator can act.

Actual: `review-readability` and `review-reliability` never produce text on any of three model families and two effort levels; the envelope only says `stopReason: length`, and the review is permanently uncompletable — it had to be abandoned with the audited `operator_disposition` flow.

### gentle-pi version
3.7.0 (provider binary: dev-main build `3a19dbf8961bea9771b4e867cf3872e47ebe2699`)

### Pi version
0.87.1

### Operating system
Windows (WSL)

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)
```text
{"tool":"gentle_review_capture","status":"blocked","outcome":"pi-host-relay-transport-failure",
 "failure":{"kind":"reviewer-empty-output","stage":"pi","exit_code":null,"timed_out":false,
 "elapsed_ms":58598,"timeout_ms":1062764,"reviewer":{"stopReason":"length"}},
 "reason":"Reviewer produced no text for review-readability (stopReason: length).",
 "mutation_performed":false,"mutation_outcome":"none"}
```
(Representative of all 10 attempts; only `lens`, `stopReason` and model/effort routing varied.)

title: feat(models): explicit orchestrator model/effort selection in /gentle-models so profiles stop silently overwriting the live session
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Applying a profile has a silent side effect on the live session. The flow is: I'm working with `/model` set to one orchestrator, I open `/gentle-models` or `/gentle:profiles` just to change **subagent** routing, I apply a profile, and without any warning my live orchestrator model is replaced by the one stored in the profile. I only notice much later, when the orchestrator already answers with a different model.

Root causes found in code:

- The profile snapshot (`profileSnapshotFrom`) reads the orchestrator from Pi's global `settings.json` (`readOrchestratorSettings`), never from the live session. A `/model` switch that isn't persisted there is invisible to the snapshot, so `u` (in `/gentle-models`) and `s` (in `/gentle:profiles`) capture a stale value into the profile's `orchestrator` key without telling the user.
- Applying a profile with that key writes `settings.json` **and** switches the live session (`switchLiveOrchestrator`). Skipping only happens when the profile has no `orchestrator` key at all, but no panel shows whether the profile carries it.
- There is no UI to set the orchestrator explicitly. The only way to get the desired value into a profile today is hand-editing `settings.json` first and snapshotting afterwards.

Who benefits: anyone combining `/model` with named profiles, which is the normal way to work with workload-dependent routing.

### Proposed outcome

Add an explicit orchestrator row in `/gentle-models` (model + thinking effort, plus a "leave untouched" option), so that:

- Saving (`ctrl+s` / `u`) snapshots the **chosen** value into the profile's `orchestrator` key instead of inferring it silently from `settings.json`.
- The profile detail shows whether it carries an orchestrator entry and which one, so applying it never surprises.
- Choosing "leave untouched" stores no `orchestrator` key, and applying such a profile preserves the live `/model` (the skip path that already exists).

### Alternatives considered

- Hand-editing `settings.json` before snapshotting: works but fragile and undiscoverable; no regular user should need it.
- Removing the orchestrator from profiles: rejected, it would undo the full-snapshot intent behind #916 and the live-switch fix behind #1220.
- Relying on `/gentle:profiles` alone: doesn't solve it, it snapshots from the same `settings.json` source.

### Additional context

- Code: `lib/profiles-orchestrator.ts` (`readOrchestratorSettings` / `applyOrchestratorSettings`), `lib/agent-profiles.ts` (`PROFILE_ORCHESTRATOR_KEY`, `readProfileOrchestrator`), `extensions/gentle-ai.ts` (`profileSnapshotFrom`, `updateCurrentProfileFromSavedRouting`, apply path with `switchLiveOrchestrator`).
- Related: #900 (profiles initially excluded the orchestrator), #916 (profiles became full snapshots including it), #1220 (apply also switches the live session), #1099 (the `u` shortcut that snapshots from `settings.json`). No open issue requests an explicit orchestrator field; searched open and closed issues for "profile orchestrator model" and "gentle-models orchestrator".

title: review.capture-validation slot is always rejected under contract v2 (singular `value` wire shape gated on v5)
body:
## Summary

`gentle_review_capture` can never submit the `review.capture-validation` slot. It rejects the
provider-issued binding with:

```
collectBinding is unknown, expired, or belongs to a different session route
```

Because of that, a review that reaches `correction_required` and has its correction plan
accepted cannot be validated, and the lineage cannot close. Reviewer and refuter slots on the
same lineage capture fine.

## Environment

- `gentle-pi` 3.7.0 (Pi extension `extensions/gentle-ai.ts`)
- `gentle-ai` 3.7.0 (provider, `/home/gaston/.local/bin/gentle-ai`)
- contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, `--agent=pi`
- host: Pi coding agent, Linux

## Steps to reproduce

1. Take a candidate to `correction_required` (a reviewer or refuter finding classified as
   candidate-caused and severe). Submit the correction plan through
   `gentle_review_capture` with `correctionLines`; it is accepted.
2. Call STATUS. It returns `next_transition.reason_code: targeted_validation_required` plus a
   `collectBinding` for `captureOperation: review.capture-validation`.
3. Submit exactly that binding with `gentle_review_capture` (`lineageId` + the binding, and
   also tried with an explicit `workspaceRoot`).

## Expected

The validator runs, as the reviewer and refuter slots do.

## Observed

Immediate rejection, both with and without `workspaceRoot`:

```json
{"tool":"gentle_review_capture","status":"blocked","outcome":"capture-binding-rejected",
 "reason":"collectBinding is unknown, expired, or belongs to a different session route",
 "mutation_performed":false,"mutation_outcome":"none"}
```

- 5 occurrences across 3 different lineages.
- Always with a binding just returned by STATUS, with no delay between STATUS and the capture.
- Reviewer and refuter captures succeed on the same lineages, with the same call shape.

## Root cause (as far as I could take it)

The provider renders the validator input in a **different wire shape** than the other slots.
Raw `gentle-ai review status --next-transition=true ... --agent=pi --projection=workspace`
output for the validator slot:

```json
{"next_transition":{"kind":"collect","reason_code":"targeted_validation_required",
  "collect":{"inputs":[{
    "arguments":[...],
    "capture_operation":"...",            // note: snake_case
    "name":"provider_targeted_validator",
    "schema":"https://gentle-ai.dev/schema/review/validator/v1",
    "submission":{
      "operation_token":"capture-validation",
      "argument_tokens":[...],
      "value":{"slot":"provider_targeted_validator","domain":"artifact_path_or_stdin",...}
    }                                     // note: `value` singular, snake_case
  }]}}}
```

The reviewer/refuter inputs use camelCase (`captureOperation`) and `submission.values`
(plural, an array).

In `lib/review-integration-v2.ts`, the branch that decodes this singular shape is gated on
`v5`:

```ts
if (v5 && typeof value === "object" && value !== null && "value" in value && !("values" in value)) {
```

and the comment directly above it states that gentle-ai's v9 contract renders that same
singular-value shape for the two host-mediated role operations (`capture-refuter`,
`capture-validation`). Under `--contract=gentle-ai.review-integration/v2` that gate is false,
so this shape is not decoded into the form the route registry keys on:

- `extensions/gentle-ai.ts` publishes the binding for the model (normalized: camelCase,
  `submission.values` as an array),
- while `retainNativeCaptureRoutes` registers keys derived from
  `status.nextTransition.collect.inputs`,
- and `readRetainedNativeCaptureRoute` runs **before** the internal STATUS re-fetch
  (`extensions/gentle-ai.ts:7409`), so a key mismatch rejects immediately instead of
  surfacing an "unsupported capture operation" error.

The rejection message says "unknown, expired, or belongs to a different session route", which
reads like a stale binding, but the binding is freshly issued; the mismatch is in the
canonical key.

## What I could not determine

Which side should change. The client's own comment suggests it intends to support the singular
shape (but only under `v5`), while the provider may be emitting the wrong shape under `v2`.
I have no access to the Go side to check which contract version should render which shape.

## Workaround that works

After applying a correction, the corrected candidate is offered as a **new unreviewed target**.
A fresh review of it runs end to end (reviewer + refuter) and can approve. That is how the
reviews in that project have been closing.

## Authorship

This report was produced by an AI coding agent — `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, provider
`opencode-go`, running in the Pi coding agent — while working on a private Django project. The
human maintainer of that project does not work in this area and asked for the report to be
filed on their behalf. The finding comes from reading this package's code plus a controlled
reproduction (including the `workspaceRoot` experiment that ruled out the obvious
caller-side mistake), so please treat the root-cause section as a hypothesis to confirm rather
than as a proposed fix.

title: orchestrator_send_message: parallel sends show only one consent prompt; the other blocks indefinitely with no visible prompt
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

If an agent issues **two `orchestrator_send_message` calls in parallel** (in the same assistant turn), and both recipients need consent, only **one** consent prompt is shown. The other call waits forever on a consent `select` that never appears. The agent turn stays open, the user's messages only queue as steering, and nothing indicates that the session is waiting for input. The call only ends when the user cancels or interrupts the turn, which returns `Cross-orchestrator communication was cancelled.`

This happened first in real use: a coordinator session sent two parallel notifications to two peer sessions. One was accepted, and the other blocked the session for ~16 minutes. We then reproduced it locally in a controlled test (below).

A related usability issue makes this worse. The consent prompt preselects **"Allow once"**, so any Enter press while the user is typing elsewhere approves the send without them noticing. In real use the user never knowingly saw a consent prompt. Some sends went through only after 1.5–7 minute delays, which is consistent with accidental approval.

Relevant code: `SessionMessagingGrants.authorize()` in `lib/session-messaging-grants.ts` awaits `ctx.ui.select(...)` with no timeout; it is called from `orchestrator_send_message` in `extensions/gentle-agents.ts`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start two idle Pi sessions with gentle-pi in the same trusted local profile (peers A and B), e.g. `pi` in two tmux sessions under a temp directory.
2. In a third interactive Pi session S, make sure no "Allow for this session" grant exists for A or B.
3. **Single send (control):** have S's agent call `orchestrator_send_message` once to A. The consent prompt appears inline in S ("Authorize cross-orchestrator message to <id>?" with Reason, Message, and Allow once / Allow for this session / Deny), with "Allow once" preselected. Choosing Deny returns `denied by user`. This works as expected.
4. **Parallel sends:** have S's agent call `orchestrator_send_message` twice in the **same assistant turn**, once to A and once to B.
5. Observe: only one consent prompt is displayed. Choose Deny. That call returns `denied by user`, but the other call stays pending with no prompt visible. The session remains blocked until the user interrupts it.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: each parallel send shows its own consent prompt, either one after the other or together. Or the pending consent times out or fails with an error the agent can report. The session should never block indefinitely on an invisible prompt.

Actual: only one of the two prompts is ever shown. The second `orchestrator_send_message` call hangs with no visible prompt and no timeout (~7 minutes in the local test, ~16 minutes in real use) until the user interrupts, then returns `Cross-orchestrator communication was cancelled.`

### gentle-pi version

3.7.0 (git checkout 5456811)

### Pi version

0.87.1

### Operating system

Linux

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
Local reproduction (UTC):
14:31:13  assistant  -> orchestrator_send_message (to A)                       [single]
14:32:51  toolResult    "Error: Cross-orchestrator communication denied by user."   (prompt shown, user chose Deny)
14:32:58  assistant  -> orchestrator_send_message (to A), orchestrator_send_message (to B)   [parallel]
          (only ONE consent prompt shown; user chose Deny; session then blocked with no visible prompt)
14:39:56  toolResult (A) "Cross-orchestrator communication was cancelled."            (after user interrupted)
14:39:56  toolResult (B) "Error: Cross-orchestrator communication denied by user."

Original occurrence:
05:23:57  assistant  -> orchestrator_send_message (to A), orchestrator_send_message (to B)   [parallel]
05:40:12  toolResult (A) "Cross-orchestrator communication was cancelled."
05:40:12  toolResult (B) "Message <id> from <S> to <B> accepted for delivery; it is not a delivery or read receipt."
```

Possible mitigations: queue consent prompts so they are shown one at a time across parallel tool calls, add a timeout to the consent `select`, show a persistent status indicator while consent is pending, and/or default the selection to "Deny" instead of "Allow once".

title: fix(rdd): surface and advance manual reviewer collection
body:
## Before submitting
- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

## Problem
A high-risk native review can enter `action=collect` with `replayability=manual_action_required` and remain indefinitely idle. The controller returns complete materializable reviewer bindings, but neither launches them nor prominently reports that no background work is running and that the parent orchestrator must submit the whole group. This makes a user reasonably believe review is progressing when it is not.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Start an ordinary committed-range review for a high-risk candidate.
2. Call review status after start.
3. Observe `action=collect`, `reason_code=reviewer_results_required`, and complete materialize bindings.
4. Do not manually invoke the complete capture group.
5. Observe that the review remains in `reviewing` with no progress or explicit idle indication.

## Expected and actual behavior
Expected:
- The harness either launches the complete provider-issued reviewer group automatically, or prominently reports that collection is idle and requires one group-capture action.
- Status distinguishes waiting for review execution from review execution in progress.

Actual:
- The review remains in `reviewing`/`collect` with no background activity.
- Progress resumes only after the parent explicitly invokes the provider-issued complete capture group.

## gentle-pi version
3.7.0

## Pi version
0.87.1

## Operating system
Linux

## Relevant logs or error output (optional)
```text
state=reviewing
action=collect
replayability=manual_action_required
reason_code=reviewer_results_required
```

title: feat(communication): configurable clarity layer for user-facing replies, plans, and docs
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Cuando el agente explica un problema, una decisión, un plan o un resultado, su respuesta está calibrada para otro desarrollador que ya comparte su modelo mental y su vocabulario interno. Entiendo cada palabra por separado, pero no construyo una comprensión clara de lo que está diciendo: tengo que traducir mentalmente cada respuesta antes de poder usarla.

No es un problema de tono, ni de personalidad, ni de "inglés vs. español", y no pido que el agente sea menos técnico ni que elimine profundidad. Lo que falta es una capa que ordene la explicación para la persona que supervisa.

#### Qué es y qué no es este problema

| Dimensión | ¿Está regulada hoy? | ¿Es el problema reportado? |
|---|---|---|
| Personalidad / tono (rioplatense vs. neutral) | Sí — prompt de persona | No |
| Estilo de comunicación (registro, voseo, calidez) | Sí — prompt de persona | No |
| Claridad pedagógica (qué pasó → por qué → impacto → opciones) | No | **Sí** |
| Jerga técnica sin explicación previa | No | **Sí** |
| Estructura y densidad de la información | Solo "síntesis corta" | **Sí** |
| Distinción estado interno del workflow vs. información para decidir | No | **Sí** |

Probé las dos Personas disponibles (Gentleman y Neutral): el problema de comprensión persiste con ambas, porque ninguna de las dos regula los cuatro ejes marcados. No tengo paquetes de terceros que transformen el output del agente (Caveman, I Have ADHD, Ponytail, u otros no están instalados), así que el comportamiento no se explica por una interacción con otra extensión de personalización.

#### Evidencia: una sesión exportada (2026-09-26)

Setup: `gentle-pi` 3.7.0 (subió de 2.7.0 durante la sesión), Pi 0.87.1, Linux, sin paquetes de terceros que alteren el output. 49 respuestas del agente, sin code blocks en el conteo:

| Métrica | Valor |
|---|---|
| Respuestas que narran vocabulario interno del review (`lineage`, `lens`, `forecast`, `acknowledgement`, `authority`, `slot`, `closure`, `controller-only`) | 15 / 49 |
| `lens` / `lineage` / `acknowledgement` | 15 / 6 / 3 |
| `shim` / `lockfile` / `host` / `store` / `override` | 15 / 14 / 13 / 12 / 12 |
| Chequeos de comprensión ("¿se entiende?", "¿te queda claro?") | 0 |
| Respuestas que contienen siquiera una pregunta al usuario | 2 |

Ejemplos representativos (citas textuales, paths abreviados):

1. **Internals antes que la situación.** Pregunto "que es esto?" por un warning al arrancar. La respuesta arranca con el path del archivo y el código fuente de la extensión; el significado para el usuario recién aparece en la cuarta sección, "Consecuencia real":
   > La lógica está en: `~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/.pnpm/pi-web-access@0.31.0.../tool-activation.ts`
   > Si el gate falla, printea el warning y cae al modo **eager**.

2. **Jerga sin explicación previa.** Un mismo párrafo encadena `peer dependency`, `host`, `lockfile`, `peer` y `gate` sin aclarar qué es cada uno ni qué consecuencia tiene para mí:
   > … declaran el host como **peer dependency** con rango `'*'`: pnpm auto-instaló ese peer **una vez**, cuando el lockfile se creó, y lo resolvió a **0.86.0**. Ese es el valor congelado que lee el gate.

3. **Demasiada información por oración.** Varias relaciones causales, calificadores y conceptos en dos oraciones que tengo que descomponer a mano:
   > Los "referenciados" son symlinks **dentro** de otros huérfanos (viejos `gentle-engram@0.1.14` y una variante stale de `0.1.15` resuelta contra 0.86.0), no desde el árbol vivo. No los toco: borrarlos exige calcular el cierre transitivo y si me equivoco te rompo el pi entero.

4. **Contexto implícito.** El agente referencia su propio razonamiento anterior como si ya compartiéramos las abstracciones:
   > mi regex de hermanos no baja un nivel en los paquetes con scope (`@aws-sdk/*`, `@ast-grep/*`, `@earendil-works/*`)
   > No voy a GC a mano un árbol del que dependen tus tools.

5. **Estado interno del agente comunicado como si fuera el resultado.** Durante la revisión automática, la narración pública es literalmente el estado del controller:
   > Lineage creado (`review-…`), estado `reviewing`, tier medio, lens `review-reliability`. No vino envelope de consentimiento pendiente — el siguiente paso es status.
   > Forecast del slot (no corrió nada, `mutation_performed: false`) … Un solo model run, sobre el lens `review-reliability`, contra los dos archivos del candidate. Lo autorizo.
   > El acknowledgement es controller-only: rechaza `input`. Reenvío solo el lineage.
   > Authority quemada. No emito más STATUS.

   Y el cierre que se me presenta como resumen del trabajo es un bloque de estado interno:
   ```
   lineage:   review-…
   tier:      medium          lens: review-reliability
   estado:    approved → authority: burned
   evidence:  gentle-ai.review-acknowledged/v1
   ```

6. **Inglés completo dentro de frases en español.** No son nombres de API ni comandos, son cláusulas enteras de la explicación:
   > el receipt lo marca explícitamente como trabajo separado: no reabre el review ni ofrece corrección
   > El closure da la continuación exacta de acknowledgement; la confirmo contra STATUS antes de ejecutarla.

**Contra-ejemplo dentro de la misma sesión:** el agente a veces lo hace bien. Una respuesta posterior usa el orden que necesito — "## Lo que pasó" → "## Verificación" (tabla) → "## Dos cosas que encontré y **no** toqué" → "## Rollback", y otra presenta "## Opciones" en tabla con riesgos y "Yo iría con **A**". La capacidad existe; el problema es que no es el default.

#### Por qué afecta la supervisión humana del agente

- No puedo aprobar un plan que no puedo parafrasear en mis propias palabras. Si la intención del cambio no queda clara, la aprobación es un acto de fe, no una revisión.
- La información que necesito para decidir (qué pasó, por qué, qué impacto tiene, qué opciones hay, qué se recomienda) sí está en la respuesta, pero dispersa entre detalle de mecanismo, así que el esfuerzo cognitivo va a armar el relato en vez de evaluar la decisión.
- Me falta la separación entre **estado interno del workflow** (útil para depurar el harness) e **información útil para la persona que supervisa** (la que me deja auditar).
- El mismo registro gobierna los planes y la documentación que escribe el agente. Si la doc sale en este formato, el revisor no puede mantenerla: la documentación tiene que ser comprensible para la persona que la va a cuidar. (Esta sesión no escribió documentación; el punto es estructural, no una cita.)

#### Jerga necesaria vs. innecesaria

| Necesaria (mantener, con glosa de una línea al primer uso) | Innecesaria para decidir (resumir; dejar el detalle opcional) |
|---|---|
| `peer dependency`, `lockfile`, `corepack`, `shim`, `store`, `override`, `runtime` — nombres reales del dominio pnpm/Node | `lineage`, `lens`, `forecast`, `acknowledgement`, `authority burned`, `controller-only`, `slot materializable`, `candidate`, `closure`, `binding` — estado interno del review | 

No se pide eliminar la segunda columna: se pide que la traducción al humano venga primero ("la revisión automática aprobó los 2 archivos; abajo está el detalle del protocolo") y que el detalle siga disponible.

#### Orígenes probables (con evidencia, sin atribuir sin comprobar)

1. **Contenido del prompt de persona (alta confianza).** `GENTLEMAN_PERSONA_PROMPT` y `NEUTRAL_PERSONA_PROMPT` (`extensions/gentle-ai.ts:1232-1249`, gentle-pi 3.7.0) regulan tono, idioma y regionalismo; ambos comparten "Be direct, technical, and concise" y "senior architect and teacher". Ninguno de los dos dice nada sobre orden de la explicación, densidad por oración, glosa de jerga ni audiencia. Explica por qué cambiar de Persona no cambia la comprensión. Además, en el canal de Pi no existe ni el `Response Length Contract` que sí tiene el output style de Claude.
2. **Regla de síntesis del harness (alta confianza).** `assets/orchestrator.md:15`: *"Keep synthesis short by default: decision, outcome, next action."* Optimiza respuestas cortas, no comprensibles; ningún lado del prompt pide orden pedagógico.
3. **Contratos inyectados escritos para la máquina (confianza media-alta).** El prompt de identidad + orchestrator + contrato de review se anexan al system prompt (`extensions/gentle-ai.ts:9259`) en vocabulario de proveedor, sin instrucción de re-codificarlos para el humano. Existen precedentes acotados que muestran que el principio ya se conoce y se aplica en forma puntual: se prohíbe exponer códigos internos en *labels* de envelopes de consentimiento (`assets/orchestrator-delegation.md:24`) y el propio código documenta *"Names the situation before the mechanism"* para un error dirigido al operador (`extensions/gentle-ai.ts:5200`). Cubre las 15 respuestas con vocabulario de review.
4. **Jerga de dominio (alta confianza, ajena a Gentle).** `lockfile`, `shim`, `store`, `corepack`, `gate`, `eager`, `drift` vienen del registro técnico de pnpm/Node y del modelo, no del harness. Es un eje separado: se arregla glosando, no cambiando el workflow.
5. **Capacidad de claridad existe pero es opt-in (alta confianza).** `gentle-pi` ya envía skills que codifican buena redacción: `cognitive-doc-design` (docs orientadas a revisión), `comment-writer` (comentarios de colaboración: "be useful fast", "explain why", fórmula observación → por qué → acción) e `issue-creation`. Todas se activan por trigger, no son el default y no cubren las explicaciones corrientes ni la narración de progreso. La sesión analizada no cargó ninguna: 0 lecturas de `SKILL.md` en 126 llamadas a herramientas.

**Descartado con evidencia:** elección de Persona (probada ambas), paquetes de terceros que transformen output (ninguno instalado) y la hipótesis "el modelo es demasiado técnico" como causa única (la misma sesión explica bien otras partes).

### Proposed outcome

Una forma configurable de priorizar la claridad, el contexto y el lenguaje natural para la persona que supervisa, aplicable a las tres superficies que escribe el agente: respuestas conversacionales, planes/tasks y documentación generada.

Comportamientos observables que debería producir (no son una implementación, son el contrato de salida):

1. Orden por defecto: **qué pasó → por qué pasó → qué impacto tiene → qué opciones existen → qué se recomienda y por qué → detalle técnico opcional**.
2. Cada término nuevo, glosado o definido a la primera aparición; la jerga de dominio se conserva, no se elimina.
3. Estado interno del workflow separado de la información necesaria para decidir; el protocolo va al detalle, el resultado va primero.
4. Una relación causal principal por oración; sin apilar calificadores.
5. Referencias explícitas a lo que ya se compartió ("el lockfile interno de pnpm", no "ese tree" / "la variante stale").
6. Preguntas de verificación de comprensión cuando la explicación es larga (hoy: 0 en 49 respuestas).
7. Profundidad técnica intacta: disponible en la sección de detalle o bajo pedido, nunca recortada por defecto.

Observación adicional: hoy la claridad depende de que el agente cargue una skill por trigger, o de suerte. Si `comment-writer` y `cognitive-doc-design` ya codifican estas reglas, el salto natural es que sus **principios** (no el archivo completo) vivan en la capa always-on — prompt de persona o un contrato de comunicación compartido — para que apliquen a respuestas, planes y docs sin que nadie tenga que pedirlos.

No propongo un mecanismo concreto: el diseño queda en manos de los maintainers. Dejo anotados los canales que ya existen y podrían alojarlo (el prompt de persona de Pi, los output styles, la skill `cognitive-doc-design`) solo como referencia de que no haría falta inventar una superficie nueva.

### Alternatives considered

- **Cambiar de Persona**: probado con Gentleman y Neutral; el problema persiste en ambos.
- **Invocar `cognitive-doc-design` / `comment-writer` a mano en cada request**: son opt-in por trigger, hay que pedirlos en cada turno, y no cubren la narración de progreso de una tarea en curso.
- **Pedir "explícalo más simple" mensaje por mensaje**: funciona puntualmente, no escala y no persiste entre sesiones.
- **Reducir el contenido técnico**: descartado directamente — bajaría la capacidad de auditoría, que es justamente lo que quiero mejorar.

### Additional context

- Versiones observadas: `gentle-pi` 2.7.0 → 3.7.0 (misma sesión), Pi 0.87.1, Ubuntu 24. La sesión exportada está disponible si a los maintainers les sirve como evidencia.
- Relacionadas (otro repo, otro eje): `Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai#333` (gobernanza de longitud de respuesta — verbose ≠ incomprensible) y `Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai#789` (paridad Gentleman/Neutral). Los output styles viven en gentle-ai; el prompt de persona de Pi vive en este repo, por eso el reporte va acá.
- Non-goals: no pedimos tono más suave, menos inglés, menos técnica, ni una personalidad nueva. Pedimos legibilidad y revisabilidad humana como propiedad configurable, sin sacrificar profundidad.
