title: bug(agents): dead sessions with a surviving socket file are advertised as live peers
body:
### Before submitting
- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem
`orchestrator_list` advertises sessions that are no longer alive. With exactly 3 `pi` processes running (verified with `ps`), it returned 4 peers.

`SessionPresenceRegistry.advertises()` decides whether a record is announced with `lstat` alone (`lib/agents-session-transport.ts:207-216`): if the endpoint path exists, is a socket, and is owned by the same user, the record is advertised. Nothing ever connects to it, so a session terminated without cleanup keeps being announced for as long as its socket file survives, in the observed profile for days.

The tool's own text says reachability is unknown, but a caller has no way to separate a live peer from a corpse, and the practical reading of the list is "4 sessions are live". That is what happened here: an agent read the list, concluded there were 4 peer sessions, and recorded it as fact.

Impact: peers that do not exist appear as coordination partners, messages to them fail, and the real session count is hidden. The leaked record also consumes discovery budget, which is the separate failure reported in #1422; that report assumes endpoints are *missing*, so this surviving-endpoint case is not covered there.

### Steps to reproduce
1. On Linux, in one agent profile, start session A. It publishes a presence record and binds its endpoint (`SessionPresenceRegistry.record()` then `publish()` in `lib/agents-session-transport.ts`).
2. Terminate A abnormally, for example `kill -9`. Node unlinks a UNIX socket path on a graceful `server.close()` but leaves it on abnormal termination (measured with a minimal script: the path exists after `listen()`, is gone after `close()`, and survives `SIGKILL`). `registry.removeOwn()` never runs, so **both** the record and the endpoint file leak together.
3. In session B, call `orchestrator_list`. A is advertised.
4. `orchestrator_send_message` to A fails with `Error: session message was not accepted.` The failed connect then makes B delete A's *record* (`registry.removeOwn(record)` applied to the peer's file, `lib/agents-session-transport.ts:659-664`), so A stops being advertised while its `.sock` file stays behind permanently.

Observed before the failed sends: 3 live `pi` processes, 4 advertised peers, and the 3 extras carrying `.sock` files dated 2026-09-21 and 2026-09-23 (days earlier), with no listener in `ss -lx` and no `/proc/<pid>/fd` reference in any running process.

### Expected and actual behavior
Expected: an announced peer should be reachable, or the announcement should distinguish "cannot be confirmed" from "reachable". A bounded connect attempt during discovery would demote an endpoint with no listener, and reclamation should not depend on some session happening to message the corpse. The leaked endpoint file should be reclaimed too, since nothing removes it once the owner terminates abnormally.

Actual: liveness is inferred from the existence of the socket file, so any abnormally terminated session stays advertised indefinitely. Reclamation happens only as a side effect of a failed send, and the endpoint file is never reclaimed at all.

### gentle-pi version
3.7.0

### Pi version
0.87.1

### Operating system
Linux

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)
```text
Advertised sessions (reachability is unknown):
- <session-a>   # live
- <session-b>   # live
- <session-c>   # leaked endpoint, dated 2026-09-23
- <session-d>   # leaked endpoint, dated 2026-09-21

$ ss -lx | grep <runtime-tmp>/<profile-hash>
(no listener for <session-c> or <session-d>)

$ ls -l <runtime-tmp>/<profile-hash>
srw------- 2026-09-23 12:01 <session-c>.sock
srw------- 2026-09-21 20:24 <session-d>.sock

Error: session message was not accepted.   # for the 3 leaked peers
Message <id> from <session-b> to <session-a> accepted for delivery; it is not a delivery or read receipt.
```

title: feat(shell): acknowledge accepted third-party usage sources
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Since #1299, extensions register usage sources on `gentle-pi:usage-source/v1` and gentle-shell meters them like built-ins. But event delivery is fire-and-forget: the owning extension cannot tell "the shell accepted my registration and meters this provider natively" from "nobody consumed my source". Extensions that also ship their own fallback segment (so they work without gentle-shell) must therefore always paint it, which duplicates the native usage next to it and ignores the user's `/gentle:customize` settings — e.g. `visibility.usageCost=false` or `statusPlacement=hidden` hide the native meter while the third-party segment keeps showing. This affects any third-party meter built on the hook (e.g. the Z.ai GLM Coding Plan meter for #687, xAI in #800).

### Proposed outcome

gentle-shell emits an acknowledgement on the same bus for every registration it accepts: `gentle-pi:usage-source-ack/v1` with `{ schema: "gentle-pi.usage-source-ack/v1", provider }` on `pi.events`, replacements included (so re-emitting at every `session_start` renews it). Malformed payloads — which never register anything — are never acknowledged. Consumers can then retire their fallback UI when the shell meters natively and keep it otherwise (older shell, no shell, rejected payload). ~15 lines in `lib/shell-usage.ts` plus the emit in the existing `USAGE_SOURCE_EVENT` handler; contract documented in `docs/gentle-shell.md` next to the registration example.

### Alternatives considered

- Extensions reading gentle-shell's `visual-customization.json` directly (rejected: couples a third-party package to an internal settings file, and still cannot tell whether the shell actually consumed the registration).
- A presence/global-symbol probe (rejected: undocumented internals, same load-order fragility the event was designed to avoid).

### Additional context

Working implementation with tests and docs ready on a local branch (`feat/usage-source-ack`, commit `36637079`), plus a consumer that already retires its standalone segment on the ack (Z.ai GLM Coding Plan meter, danielgap/pi-zai-usage). Happy to open the PR when this gets `status:approved`.

title: bug(orchestrator): parent session can execute work outside delegated worktrees
body:
### Before submitting
- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem
During multi-agent work, the parent Pi session can lose its orchestrator role and execute substantive implementation work inline instead of delegating it to the agent assigned to the relevant branch and Git worktree. This can make the parent write in `main`, the coordinator worktree, or another agent's worktree, even when independent Herdr worktrees already exist.

This is a coordination-safety bug: the system allows the parent to cross from coordination into implementation without an enforceable ownership boundary.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Start a Pi session as the parent coordinator in a repository with multiple Herdr workspaces or delegated agents.
2. Create or select an independent branch/worktree for a substantive task and delegate that task to a child agent.
3. Leave the child agent working or make its status/output temporarily unavailable.
4. Continue the parent session with a follow-up implementation request related to the delegated task.
5. Observe that the parent can edit files directly from its current working directory instead of routing the work to the delegated branch/worktree.
6. Repeat with more than one active worktree or session to observe ownership ambiguity and possible cross-worktree writes.

### Expected and actual behavior
**Expected:**

- The parent remains a coordinator after delegation.
- Every substantive task is bound to one owner, branch, and canonical worktree before implementation.
- Parent writes are limited to coordination artifacts or explicitly parent-owned work.
- The system warns or blocks when a parent attempts to write in `main` or in a worktree owned by another agent.
- Cross-worktree path resolution and duplicate writers are detected before changes are made.

**Actual:**

- The parent can continue with inline implementation after delegation should have occurred.
- This can duplicate work, create changes on the wrong branch, produce concurrent writers, and lose change provenance.
- The failure is especially easy to trigger when several Herdr workspaces are active and the parent has enough context to perform the task directly.

### gentle-pi version
3.7.0

### Pi version
0.87.1

### Operating system
macOS

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)
Runtime context observed during investigation:

- Herdr 0.9.0, gentle-shell 3.1.0.
- Multiple Herdr workspaces were active with Pi agents in `idle`, `working`, `done`, and `unknown` states.
- Related BC3-Suite history records duplicate sessions and overlapping ownership, cross-worktree autofix behavior, and an explicit requirement that the parent remain coordinator-only.
- The intended lifecycle is: `ticket -> branch -> worktree -> delegated implementation -> work-unit commit -> verification -> PR -> cleanup`.

Suggested acceptance criteria:

- Require an explicit delegation record before substantive parent implementation.
- Bind each task to an owner, branch, and canonical worktree.
- Detect and report parent writes outside the assigned worktree.
- Surface duplicate or overlapping writers before changes are made.
- Add regression coverage for parent-versus-delegated worktree ownership, multiple delegated worktrees, stale agent status, and wrong-current-directory resolution.

### Problem

When starting Gentle Shell in standalone mode, Pi reports prompt and theme collisions where both the selected resource and the skipped resource point to the exact same physical file.

The installation otherwise appears healthy and fully functional. Gentle AI, Engram, MCP, skills, extensions, model routing, and subagents all load correctly.

The collisions affect:

- `skill-creation` prompt
- `Gentle` theme
- `Gentleman-Cute` theme
- `Gentleman-Sexy` theme

In every case, the selected and skipped entries resolve to the same resource inside the globally installed `gentle-pi` package.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install Gentle Shell globally:

2. Install the Pi runtime:

title: bug(agents): orphaned session advertisements exhaust discovery
body:
### Before submitting
- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

These checks were performed by the automated reporter, not attributed to the repository owner.

### Problem
Session-to-session discovery becomes unavailable after enough orphaned presence advertisements accumulate. Each orphan is a valid record for a session whose Unix socket no longer exists. An observed profile had 73 records, 71 with missing sockets; `orchestrator_list` failed until the stale records were moved to a private, reversible quarantine. The reason those sessions left records behind was not established. This report concerns the discovery behavior when such records exist, not a claim about the cause of abnormal termination.

### Steps to reproduce
1. On Linux/WSL, create a disposable, private agent profile and a `SessionPresenceRegistry` in it. Do not use a real user's profile.
2. Create/publish 65 otherwise valid presence records with distinct IDs using `record()` and `publish()`, but do not bind their socket endpoints (simulating orphaned announcements).
3. Call `registry.list()` or `registry.resolve(<one of the IDs>)`. The scan counts directory entries before filtering missing endpoints and returns `SessionPresenceError` with code `busy` on entry 65. The extension maps a failed list to `Error: session discovery is unavailable.`
4. With fewer than 65 such records, listing filters the missing endpoints. Removing the simulated orphan records also restores discovery.

The same 64-entry cap without orphan reclamation is present in the latest stable `gentle-pi` 3.7.0 and upstream `gentle-shell` main at `6a4dae2` (`lib/agents-session-transport.ts`, `listActivations()` and `resolve()`). Existing tests expect `busy` after overflow.

### Expected and actual behavior
Expected: Bounded, identity-checked discovery should tolerate and safely reclaim validated records whose endpoints are conclusively absent, while retaining live, malformed, unsafe, or inconclusive entries and failing closed on hostile input.

Actual: The 65th directory entry produces `busy` before stale records can be filtered or removed. A new pair of sessions can therefore fail to discover each other even when only those two have live sockets.

### gentle-pi version
3.7.0 (locally configured source checkout; same transport behavior in stable tag and upstream main referenced above)

### Pi version
0.87.1

### Operating system
Windows (WSL)

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)
```text
Error: session discovery is unavailable.
SessionPresenceError: presence registry is busy
```

No credentials, raw session IDs, hostnames, or local filesystem paths are included.

title: bug(memory): session-bound memory writes fail permanently with "session has already ended" until pi is restarted
body:
### Before submitting - [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem. - [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data. ### Problem In a normal pi session using the gentle-engram provider with a local Engram server (engram 2.1.0, `engram serve`), every session-bound memory write suddenly starts failing with `session has already ended`. From that point the failure is permanent for the rest of the pi session: - `mem_save` returns `session has already ended`. - `mem_session_start` returns the same error, both with a brand-new session id and with the original host session id (an ended session cannot be reopened). - Restarting the Engram daemon does NOT help: the ended state is persisted in the local store, not in process memory. After a daemon restart (new PID listening on the same port), `mem_save` still fails with the same error. We verified the store itself is healthy: `engram save "t" "m" --project

` via the CLI succeeds and the observation is created. Only the pi-session binding is burned. The only recovery we found is restarting pi, so the host gets a fresh session id; after that, memory works normally again. Impact: memory persistence silently stops working for the rest of the session — saves are lost unless the agent notices the tool errors. Disclaimer: we are not deep technical users of the internals; we are reporting the observed behavior with the evidence we could gather locally, and we are happy to run more diagnostics on request. ### Steps to reproduce We could not pin down the exact trigger — the session had been running for a long time (many hours, hundreds of tool calls, at least one compaction). What we can consistently observe once it happens: 1. Run pi with the gentle-engram provider against a local Engram server (`engram serve`, Windows, default port 7437). 2. After extended session lifetime, `mem_save` starts returning `session has already ended`. 3. `mem_session_start` with a brand-new session id → same error. With the original host session id → same error. 4. Kill the `engram.exe` daemon and start `engram serve` again (new PID, port 7437 listening) → `mem_save` still returns `session has already ended`. 5. `engram save ... --project

` via CLI → succeeds, proving the store accepts writes. 6. Restart pi → fresh host session id → memory writes work again. ### Expected and actual behavior Expected: - Session-bound memory writes should recover instead of failing permanently — e.g. transparently re-binding to a replacement session, or allowing `mem_session_start` to reopen/recover the binding for a live pi session. Actual: - Every session-bound write fails with `session has already ended` until pi is restarted. Daemon restart does not clear the state. ### gentle-pi version 3.7.0 ### Pi version 0.87.0 ### Operating system Windows ### Relevant logs or error output (optional) ```text mem_save -> error: session has already ended mem_session_start (brand-new session id) -> error: session has already ended mem_session_start (host session id) -> error: session has already ended [daemon restart: engram.exe killed, restarted, listening on 127.0.0.1:7437] mem_save -> error: session has already ended (still fails) engram save "t" "m" --project

-> Memory saved: # (CLI works) [pi restart: fresh host session id] mem_save -> success (recovered) ```

title: feat(shell): show claude-bridge subscription usage (5h/7d windows) in the bar and /gentle:usage panel
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

With Pi on the `claude-bridge` provider (Claude Code through the Agent SDK, the way a Claude Max/Pro subscription is used from Gentle Shell), the bar shows `$0.000` and `/gentle:usage` (`alt+u`) reports:

```
✿ claude-bridge · no subscription usage for this provider
```

The 5-hour and 7-day plan windows that Claude Code shows with `/usage` are invisible in Pi, so the user only learns about the window when the bridge returns a `five_hour` rejection.

The numbers are already delivered to the bridge on every turn. From one morning of bridge log (156 events):

```
consumeQuery: rate_limit_event {"status":"allowed","rateLimitType":"five_hour","unifiedWindows":{"five_hour":{"utilization":0.63,"resetsAt":1790245200},"seven_day":{"utilization":...}}}
```

What is missing is the connection:

- Gentle Shell has adapters for `openai-codex`, `anthropic` (`anthropic-ratelimit-unified-*` headers) and `nan` (#1177 / #1180), plus the generic `gentle-pi:usage-source/v1` hook in `lib/shell-usage.ts`. Neither `pi-claude-bridge` nor the `@schuettc/pi-claude-bridge` fork emits that hook.
- The `@schuettc/pi-claude-bridge` fork (the build that carries the unreleased upstream fixes, including Opus 5.5 at 1M) already normalizes the SDK events into a process-wide bus: `globalThis[Symbol.for("pi.provider-usage.bus.v1")]` exposing `register / adapters / subscribe / publish`, with windows `five_hour`, `seven_day`, `seven_day_opus`, `seven_day_sonnet`, `seven_day_oauth_apps`, each carrying `usedPercent` and `resetsAt` (`src/usage-bus.ts`). Gentle Shell does not read it.

### Proposed outcome

Show claude-bridge subscription usage in the bar and in `/gentle:usage`, following the NaN precedent (#1180):

1. When the active model's provider is `claude-bridge`, resolve `globalThis[Symbol.for("pi.provider-usage.bus.v1")]`; if present, subscribe and map the latest `claude` snapshot to `ProviderUsage`: `five_hour` and `seven_day` as the main limits, `seven_day_opus` / `seven_day_sonnet` / `seven_day_oauth_apps` as additional limits, each with used percent and reset time.
2. Render it where Codex shows its percentage in the bar, and as a provider block in the panel.
3. When the bus is absent (upstream `pi-claude-bridge` without the fork), replace the generic unsupported note with a pending note that says the bridge build does not publish usage, so the user knows why.

I can contribute the implementation once this is approved.

### Alternatives considered

- Asking upstream `pi-claude-bridge` to emit `gentle-pi:usage-source/v1`: upstream is provider-agnostic and should not learn Gentle Shell's event name; consuming the neutral bus symbol keeps that boundary.
- Reading Claude Code's on-disk usage cache: brittle and undocumented; the SDK already streams the values per turn.
- Leaving `$0.000`: correct for a subscription but hides that the real budget is the plan window.

### Additional context

Windows 11, pi 0.87.1, gentle-pi 3.7.0, gentle-ai 3.7.0, `@schuettc/pi-claude-bridge` 0.8.0-schuettc.5, Claude Max, model `claude-opus-5-5`. Originally filed in the wrong repository as Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai#4945; that one will be closed in favour of this issue. Sibling requests for other providers: #1047, #872, #800, #687, #1261.

title: bug(launcher): gentle-shell cannot find the bundled pi runtime (ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED)
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

On a machine without a separate `pi` install, `npm i -g gentle-pi` followed by `gentle-shell` fails with "No pi runtime could be found", even though `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` is installed next to gentle-pi (`node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/bundle/cli.js` exists).

This breaks README "Path A: standalone `gentle-shell` (recommended, no pi changes)". It only works today when another `pi` is already on `PATH`, which hides the bug for most users.

Root cause: `resolveBundledCli()` in `bin/gentle-shell.mjs` calls

```js
require.resolve("@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/package.json")
```

but `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` declares an `exports` map that does not expose `./package.json` (checked 0.85.1, 0.86.0 and 0.87.1). Node throws `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`, the `catch` swallows it, and resolution falls through to `PATH`. The `.` export also only has an `import` condition, so `require.resolve("@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent")` fails the same way.

### Steps to reproduce

Clean container, no pi installed:

```bash
docker run --rm node:24 bash -c '
  npm i -g gentle-pi@3.7.0 >/dev/null 2>&1
  which pi || echo "no pi on PATH"
  gentle-shell --version; echo "EXIT=$?"'
```

Isolating the resolver, from the installed gentle-pi directory:

```bash
node -e 'try { require.resolve("@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/package.json") } catch (e) { console.log(e.code) }'
# ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED
```

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: `gentle-shell` uses the bundled pi runtime (resolution step 2 in `docs/readme-reference.md`) and starts.

Actual:

```
no pi on PATH
No pi runtime could be found. Pick one of:
  - Set GENTLE_SHELL_PI to the path of a pi executable.
  - Install @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent next to gentle-pi (it ships as an optional peer dependency).
  - Install pi and make sure it is on your PATH.
EXIT=1
```

Workaround: `export GENTLE_SHELL_PI="<npm root -g>/gentle-pi/node_modules/.bin/pi"`.

Possible fix (verified locally, finds `dist/bundle/cli.js`): resolve through the `import` condition instead of `package.json`:

```js
const entry = fileURLToPath(import.meta.resolve("@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent")); // .../dist/index.js
const cliPath = join(dirname(entry), "bundle", "cli.js");
```

The launcher tests stub `resolveBundledCli` (for example `resolveBundledCli: () => "/bundled/cli.js"` in `tests/gentle-shell-launcher.test.ts`), so the real resolution against an installed pi-coding-agent is never exercised. A test that runs it against the real package would catch this.

### gentle-pi version

3.7.0 (resolver unchanged on `main` at 4d702a4)

### Pi version

@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 0.87.1 (bundled peer); none on PATH

### Operating system

Linux

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

Reproduced on Linux (Node 24.14.1, npm 11.11.0) and in the `node:24` Docker image (Node 24.21.0, npm 11.19.0).

title: feat(shell): add a versioned Project Map definition with draft and human approval
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Gentle Shell shows the active session, captured changes, agents, and task-level TODOs. Those surfaces explain current execution, but they cannot answer project-level questions: which user-facing capabilities make up the product, which foundations and dependencies enable them, what is done, active, ready, blocked, or merely planned, and which technical surfaces each capability requires.

That gap rewards local optimization. An orchestrator can make sustained backend progress while frontend, UX, operations, deployment, and end-to-end readiness drop out of sight until integration breaks. Nothing in the repository states what the product is supposed to be, so "the project is 70% done" is not answerable from the project itself.

### Proposed outcome

A versioned, repository-owned Project Map artifact (`openspec/project-map.json`) recording capabilities, their foundations, dependencies, required coverage surfaces, lifecycle state, and feature-document references, without embedding mutable runtime state.

On top of it, two capabilities that make the map obtainable and trustworthy rather than aspirational:

1. A deterministic draft generator that reads only what the repository already declares (package manifest, OpenSpec configuration, ODD work units) and reports everything it could not determine as an explicit omission instead of inventing coverage.
2. An explicit human approval transition. A map stays a draft until a person approves it with an auditable actor and timestamp, and approval grants plan authority only: it starts no writer, mutates no source, and authorizes no commit, push, merge, or release.

This request covers the definition, the draft, and the approval transition. Rendering the map in the shell, a capability inspector, and cross-worktree coordination are out of scope here.

### Alternatives considered

- A companion approval file instead of a field inside the map: rejected because two artifacts drift, and the map is the thing being approved.
- Inferring coverage surfaces from repository structure so a draft is always complete: rejected because it manufactures coverage, the exact failure the map exists to prevent. A draft may be incomplete; an approved map may not.
- A model-generated draft: rejected for the first slice because it cannot be pinned by tests and would make the artifact non-reproducible.
- Markdown with frontmatter instead of JSON: rejected because deterministic validation is weaker than a contract with stable diagnostic codes.

### Additional context

- Issue #1257 requests only the session-only visual preview of the map and does not authorize this work.
- Implemented so far: a schema and validator with a frozen v1 vocabulary, stable diagnostic codes, canonical serialization, a deterministic draft generator, and the approval contract, each with focused test coverage.
- The change exceeds the 400-line review budget several times over, so it is planned as chained, independently reviewable slices rather than one pull request.
- No pull request exists yet; this issue is the prerequisite for opening one.

title: bug(launcher): auto-provision setup fails on CodeGraph "path escapes allowed roots" — infinite first-run loop
body:
## Bug description

Running `gentle-shell` on a fresh or un-provisioned home enters an infinite first-run loop. The auto-provisioning setup (introduced in #1351) installs all companion packages successfully but then fails at the CodeGraph capture step with:

```
Error: execute install pipeline: capture Pi CodeGraph child "/home/cleceta/.pi/agent/agents/gentle-ai-verify.md": Pi CodeGraph path "/home/cleceta/.pi/agent/agents/gentle-ai-verify.md" escapes allowed roots
```

Because the setup exits non-zero, the provisioning marker in `~/.gentle-shell/config.json` is never written, so every subsequent `gentle-shell` launch retries the same failing setup.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have no `~/.gentle-shell/config.json` (or delete it).
2. Run `gentle-shell` (or `gentle-shell setup`).
3. Observe the full package install succeeds, then the CodeGraph capture step fails.
4. Run `gentle-shell` again — same output, same failure.

## Expected behavior

Setup completes, writes the provisioning marker to `~/.gentle-shell/config.json`, and subsequent launches skip the auto-provision step.

## Actual behavior

Setup fails at CodeGraph capture because `--scope global` writes agents into `~/.pi/agent/agents/` (Pi's own default agent dir) while CodeGraph's allowed roots are scoped to `~/.gentle-shell/agent/` (the `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` the launcher sets). The path mismatch triggers the "escapes allowed roots" guard.

## Root cause analysis

The auto-provision flow in `runSetupFlow` spawns:

```
gentle-ai install --agent pi --scope global
```

with `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=~/.gentle-shell/agent`. The `--scope global` flag causes gentle-ai to write managed agents into the user's real `~/.pi/agent/agents/` directory instead of the `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` target. The subsequent CodeGraph capture step then tries to index those files but rejects them because `~/.pi/agent/` is outside the allowed root (`~/.gentle-shell/agent/`).

PR #587 fixed a similar `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` alignment for subagent asset installation and model routing, but the CodeGraph capture pipeline step was not covered by that fix.

## Environment

| Component | Version |
|-----------|---------|
| gentle-pi | 3.7.0 |
| gentle-ai (pinned) | v3.7.0 |
| Pi | 0.87.1 |
| Node | v24.19.0 |
| OS | WSL2 (Linux 6.6.87.2, x86_64) |

## Workaround

Until this is fixed, either:

1. **Create the provisioning marker manually** — write `~/.gentle-shell/config.json` with:
   ```json
   {
     "provisioned": {
       "/home/<user>/.gentle-shell/agent": {
         "gentleAi": "3.7.0",
         "gentlePi": "3.7.0",
         "at": "2026-09-24T00:00:00.000Z"
       }
     }
   }
   ```
   (Replace paths/versions with your actual values.)

2. **Disable auto-setup** — set `GENTLE_SHELL_NO_AUTO_SETUP=1` in your shell environment.

## Related

- #1351 — `feat(launcher): provision Gentle Shell's own home automatically on first run` (introduced the auto-provision flow)
- #587 — `fix(subagents): honor PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR for assets` (fixed the same mismatch for subagent assets, but not for CodeGraph capture)

title: bug(review): review-reliability lens fails Bedrock reviewer completion with "InvalidSignatureException: Credential should be scoped to a valid region"
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

During an ordinary RDD review lineage started through the `gentle_review`/`gentle_review_capture` MCP tools (agent `pi`, provider `amazon-bedrock`, model configured as an application inference profile ARN with an embedded non-`us-east-1` region), the reviewer relay deterministically fails to complete the `review-reliability` lens with a `pi-host-relay-transport-failure`, reason: `InvalidSignatureException: Credential should be scoped to a valid region.`

The shell/repo AWS configuration is correct (`~/.aws/config` `[default]` has the same region as the model ARN; `AWS_PROFILE`/`AWS_REGION`/`AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` are unset in the shell), and the interactive Pi session itself completes turns against the same model/ARN without any region or credential error — only the reviewer relay's completion path fails.

This looks structurally related to #1304 (`No API provider registered for api: claude-bridge`): both are `pi-host-relay-transport-failure` failures at the `collect` step of an RDD lineage, originating in the reviewer relay's own model resolution/completion path (`lib/inprocess-reviewer.ts` / `lib/review-host-relay.ts`, `completeSimple` from `@earendil-works/pi-ai/compat` or the composed `getProvider` path) rather than in the session's live `ModelRegistry`. However, the concrete defect here is different: the failing provider (`amazon-bedrock`) *is* resolved and reached — the reviewer relay actually calls Bedrock — but with a region that does not match the region embedded in the model's ARN, producing a SigV4 signature mismatch instead of a "provider not found" error.

I confirmed the upstream `@earendil-works/pi-ai` region-resolution fix for exactly this class of bug (extracting the region from an inference-profile ARN instead of falling back to `AWS_REGION`/SDK default, `earendil-works/pi` PR #5527 / issue #4860, shipped since Pi v0.79.1) **is present** in the bundled `@earendil-works/pi-ai` version used here (`dist/api/bedrock-converse-stream.js`, `arnRegionMatch` check). That logic keys off `model.id` being the literal ARN string. My working hypothesis is that the `modelId` the reviewer relay resolves/passes for the `review-reliability` lens completion is **not** the same ARN string the interactive session uses (e.g. a different reviewer-model selection, an alias, or a re-derived identifier that loses the `arn:aws:bedrock:<region>:...` prefix), so `arnRegionMatch` never matches and region resolution falls through to the `AWS_REGION`/SDK-default branch, which resolves to `us-east-1` while the credentials are signed/scoped for the model's actual region — hence the `InvalidSignatureException`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure Pi with `PI_PROVIDER=amazon-bedrock` and `PI_MODEL` set to an application inference profile ARN whose embedded region is **not** `us-east-1` (e.g. `arn:aws:bedrock:eu-west-1:<account>:application-inference-profile/<id>`), inside a git repository with RDD enabled.
2. Have an ordinary uncommitted/committed change eligible for review.
3. Trigger `gentle_review {"operation":"inspect"}`; follow the returned `next_transition` through `review.start` (`mode: ordinary`) until the lineage reaches `state: reviewing` with `selected_lenses: ["review-reliability"]`.
4. Call bound `gentle_review {"operation":"status","lineageId":"<lineageId>"}`; observe `next_transition.kind: collect` with one `collectBindings[0]` entry for `review-reliability` (agent `pi`, `materialize: true`).
5. Call `gentle_review_capture` with that exact `collectBinding`; observe the expected one-time `reviewer-model-run-forecast` (`mutation_performed: false`).
6. Resubmit the identical `collectBinding` with `reviewerRunAcknowledged: true`.
7. Observe the failure below. Re-fetching fresh `status` and resubmitting the freshly reoffered binding reproduces the identical failure again (fails fast, ~900–950 ms — not a timeout, and not a transient network blip).

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: The `review-reliability` lens completion runs against the session's configured Bedrock model/region (matching the ARN's embedded region) and the reviewer result is admitted, advancing the lineage past `collect`.

Actual: The capture fails before any reviewer result is admitted:

```json
{"tool":"gentle_review_capture","status":"blocked",
 "outcome":"pi-host-relay-transport-failure",
 "failure":{"kind":"pi-failed","stage":"pi","exit_code":null,"timed_out":false,
            "elapsed_ms":900},
 "reason":"Reviewer completion failed for review-reliability: InvalidSignatureException:
           Credential should be scoped to a valid region. ",
 "mutation_performed":false,"mutation_outcome":"none",
 "next_action":"Call fresh STATUS and submit only an exact reoffered one-slot binding;
               never replay this capture from transcript inference."}
```

`mutation_performed: false`, so the lineage stays in `reviewing` and unusable — no lens can complete, `correction_budget` is never reached, and the human-approved review can never close for this candidate. Retried twice with a freshly reoffered binding each time; identical failure both times. The interactive Pi session in the same process/environment completes normal turns against the same `amazon-bedrock` model/ARN without any region or credential error, which points at the reviewer relay's own model resolution rather than at ambient AWS configuration.

### gentle-pi version

3.6.0

### Pi version

0.87.1

### Operating system

macOS

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```
{"tool":"gentle_review_capture","status":"blocked","outcome":"pi-host-relay-transport-failure","failure":{"kind":"pi-failed","stage":"pi","exit_code":null,"timed_out":false},"reason":"Reviewer completion failed for review-reliability: InvalidSignatureException: Credential should be scoped to a valid region. ","mutation_performed":false,"mutation_outcome":"none","next_action":"Call fresh STATUS and submit only an exact reoffered one-slot binding; never replay this capture from transcript inference."}
```

### Suggested investigation pointers (not a fix proposal)

- Compare the exact `model.id`/ARN string reaching `amazon-bedrock`'s `bedrock-converse-stream` region-resolution logic (`arnRegionMatch` in `@earendil-works/pi-ai`) when invoked from the interactive session vs. from the reviewer relay (`lib/inprocess-reviewer.ts` / `lib/review-host-relay.ts`) for the same configured model — likely candidate: a reviewer-specific model selection or alias resolution step that strips or replaces the ARN before it reaches the region-resolution code.
- Related: #1304 (same failure class — `pi-host-relay-transport-failure` at `collect`, reviewer-relay model resolution diverging from the live `ModelRegistry`), different concrete provider (`claude-bridge` vs `amazon-bedrock`) and different concrete defect (missing provider vs. mis-scoped region).

title: bug(review): approved closure envelope offers acknowledgement input the facade refuses, with no lineage-only hint
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

The approved last-event closure envelope republishes the provider's raw acknowledgement continuation, whose closed positional argument list (`cwd`, `lineage`, `target`, `expected-revision`, `token`) invites a literal machine caller to pass those values back through the facade. The `acknowledge-approved` facade operation refuses all of them (`controller-only-input`) and re-derives the exact invocation itself from a fresh selector-free STATUS. Nothing in the envelope states that the facade route is lineage-only, so the only usage hint arrives after the refusal. The approved bound STATUS mapping has the same shape: it returns `result.raw` carrying the identical `review.acknowledge-approved` execute transition with the one-time token.

This is a discoverability defect for machine callers, not a correctness defect: no authority is mutated on the refused call, and the burn itself works when only the lineage is supplied.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start an ordinary review with a full commit `baseRef` and `committedOnly: true` (observed on gentle-ai 3.6.1 / gentle-pi 3.4.0; re-verified against gentle-shell `main`).
2. Complete reviewer capture until native last-event closure returns `approved`.
3. Read the closure envelope: `closure.acknowledgement` carries the raw continuation with the explicit argument list, including the one-time `token`.
4. Pass those values back through the facade, as the envelope presents them: `gentle_review {"operation":"acknowledge-approved","lineageId":...,"input":{...envelope arguments...}}`.
5. Observe the refusal below; the lineage-only guidance (`resubmit-the-exact-lineage-without-controller-only-input`) appears only at this point.

Source evidence on `main`: verbatim republication in `mapLastEventClosure` (`extensions/gentle-ai.ts:6685`), the provider's closed argument list `REVIEW_APPROVED_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT_ARGUMENTS` (`lib/review-integration-v2.ts`), the lineage-only refusal (`extensions/gentle-ai.ts:8016`), and the re-derivation through `assertReviewApprovedAcknowledgementExecuteV1` (`extensions/gentle-ai.ts:8077`).

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: the closure envelope (and the approved STATUS mapping) carries an additive `next_action` naming the exact facade invocation, `gentle_review {"operation":"acknowledge-approved","lineageId":...}`, alongside the untouched raw continuation. The raw continuation must stay verbatim: it is runnable as-is by the native CLI (the documented escape hatch for blocked consumers) and the facade never rewrites provider-issued envelopes.

Actual: a literal caller is invited to handle an opaque one-time token it is required to ignore, burns one round trip on a refused call, and only learns the correct shape from the post-refusal `next_action`.

### gentle-pi version

3.4.0 (observed); re-verified against `main` (`ef55af79`)

### Pi version

0.87.1

### Operating system

Linux

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
{"outcome":"native-approved-acknowledgement-input-invalid","reason":"controller-only-input","field":"input",
 "next_action":"resubmit-the-exact-lineage-without-controller-only-input"}
```

Reported by @dasafo in #654 after re-testing the original committed-only selector loss as fixed; split into its own issue because it is a different defect class with different acceptance criteria.

title: review: session report — 25-commit Next.js MVP through 13 lineages, a 353-line committed-range unit, and 5 reproduced lifecycle defects
body:
## What this session was

Delivering an MVP web app (a Spanish-language extras tracker for construction SMEs; private repository) from a 10-branch feature chain onto the default branch, with native bounded review gating every unit. This is a session-level report: which lifecycle defects were re-encountered, two observations not yet covered by an individual issue, and what the discipline actually bought.

**Environment** — `pi` 0.87.1 · `gentle-pi` 3.4.0 · `gentle-ai` 3.6.1 (build `sha256:67f6b54f...`) · Linux x86_64.

## Shape of the work

- **13 lineages** across the project, each gating one work unit; twelve approved before their commit.
- Every unit was sliced so a single lens covered it. Tiers came out `medium` throughout, which in practice meant one lens per unit and no consent stop.
- Verification behind the review: 394 unit tests in 49 files, 29 runtime smoke checks against a real server, 9 real-browser layout checks at 390px, and a container run against the standalone production server.

## The final unit

A **committed range**: 14 files / **353 changed lines**, tier `medium`, one lens (`review-reliability`), correction budget 177. Started with `{"mode":"ordinary","baseRef":"<full commit sha>","committedOnly":true}`.

**Approved on the first capture, zero corrections**, with 4 advisory findings (`R3-001` WARNING `src/app/globals.css:1` · `R3-002` WARNING `src/domain/seed-datos.ts:31` · `R3-003` WARNING `src/lib/estilos.ts:15` · `R3-004` SUGGESTION `src/components/ui/table.tsx:41`).

The lens capture behaved exactly as documented: `status` → `collect`, the first call returned only the materialize forecast, and resubmitting the identical binding with `reviewerRunAcknowledged: true` ran one model run and closed `approved`. Worth stating plainly next to the defect list below: **a correctly scoped candidate is cheap, fast, and the forecast/acknowledgement handshake never got in the way.**

## Defects re-encountered (all still live on 3.6.1)

| issue | what happened |
|---|---|
| #992 | `start` with `baseRef` + `committedOnly` but without `mode` → `Judgment Day graph-v1 START requires lineageId`. Adding `"mode":"ordinary"` to the same object worked immediately. A new detail added there: the pre-lineage `inspect` offers an `external.select_base_ref` collect slot with no facade route to satisfy it. |
| #1154 | Validator-slot capture refused with `capture-binding-rejected`; **the lens capture worked normally in the same session**, which narrows this to the validator role. Three refusals across three work units, always with the binding straight from `status`. |
| #654 | The original symptom did **not** recur — acknowledgement by lineage alone succeeded and burned authority. A new adjacency did appear: the closure envelope hands over a token-bearing `arguments` list that the facade then rejects as `controller-only-input`. |
| #1159 | `abandon` through the facade returned `missing_input:["lineage","capturedLensResults"]` — naming a field that was already supplied and one that is not a native flag. The working route is the eight-line `--maintainer-authorization` binding built from `review status` `entries[].discarded_work`; five lineages abandoned cleanly that way. |
| #1277 | Tool-name collision; still reproduces, and `pi remove` does not hold because the colliding package remains declared at `^2.11.0` in `~/.pi/agent/npm/package.json`. |

## Two observations not yet covered by an issue

**1. A `reviewing` lineage can be arbitrarily older than the work in hand, and nothing says so.**

This repository had a lineage sitting in state `reviewing` whose frozen candidate was **31 paths / 5,902 lines** — the project's *oldest* work unit, already delivered and already approved under a different lineage. Its manifest did not even cover the current delta: it **omitted 8 of the 14 files** that had actually changed, and included roughly 25 files the delta never touched.

`status` presented it as `applicability: current_target`, `action: collect`, `reason_code: reviewer_results_required` — indistinguishable from a legitimate live slot. Resuming it would have burned a model run reviewing the wrong code while leaving the real change unreviewed. The only thing that exposed it was comparing `candidate_paths` against the delta I actually wanted reviewed.

Suggested direction: surface a staleness signal on the collect transition (for example, that the frozen candidate tree is not the current delta), or state explicitly in the contract that an open `reviewing` slot may refer to an arbitrary earlier candidate. As written, the standing rule — "resume the bound slot" — actively leads a caller into it.

**2. The pre-lineage `select_base_ref` collect slot has no satisfying route.**

`inspect` on an empty candidate returns `next_transition.reason_code = "empty_candidate_base_ref_required"` with a binding whose `captureOperation` is `external.select_base_ref` (`schema: gentle-ai.review-base-ref-selection/v1`). No facade operation submits it: `gentle_review_capture` requires a `lineageId` that does not exist pre-lineage. The only way through is the `baseRef` field of the START input — where, per #992, `mode` is also required.

## What the discipline bought

Across the project the adversarial passes caught **2 CRITICALs and 5 real defects that 300+ passing tests did not see** — among them a route guard that returned a total 500, a config parser that silently turned `1e5` into `1`, and a duplicate-reference classifier that named the wrong rule. The advisory tail is real and asymptotic (a lens will always find something on new code, including on newly written tests), but the blocking signal was genuine every time.

One process note for anyone running this at scale: the review lifecycle is per-candidate and knows nothing about stacked PRs. Merging a chain bottom-up rewrote the ancestry of the default branch and made every remaining PR unmergeable; the chain had to be delivered by replaying its commits onto the default branch. That is a repository-shape hazard rather than a review defect, but it is easy to warn about and it cost a detour.

title: bug(todo): dynamic stale-turn counter in system prompt invalidates prompt cache every turn
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

Gentle Todo injects the todo block into the system prompt on every before_agent_start.

In extensions/gentle-todo.ts, the per-session turn counter is incremented on every agent start:

current.turn += 1;

and the prompt block is rebuilt with:

const block = todoPromptBlock(
  current.state,
  staleTurns(current.state, current.turn)
);

return {
  systemPrompt: `${event.systemPrompt}\n\n${block}`
};

In lib/shell-todo.ts, once the todo list is stale, todoPromptBlock() appends:

(stale: ${stale} turns without an update — bring the list up to date now)

This means an unchanged todo list still changes the system prompt every turn:

(stale: 7 turns without an update ...)
→
(stale: 8 turns without an update ...)
→
(stale: 9 turns without an update ...)

For providers/backends using prefix/prompt caching, this is particularly expensive because this mutation occurs before the conversation history. A one-character change in the system prompt invalidates the reusable prefix from that point onward, forcing a large existing conversation to be re-prefilled/re-cached.

I reproduced this on a long session with ~300K tokens.

A request-level probe showed, before the fix:

REQUEST=1
SYSTEM len=75922 sha=b8b4253651dbaab5
TOOLS count=56 sha=b0b3e0a4f49e357f
MESSAGES count=456

REQUEST=2
SYSTEM len=75922 sha=2eaf5afc5f7355f2
TOOLS count=56 sha=b0b3e0a4f49e357f
MESSAGES count=458

SYSTEM_COMPARE same=false
common_prefix_chars=73191

SYSTEM_PREV_AROUND=...(stale: 7 turns without an update ...)...
SYSTEM_CURR_AROUND=...(stale: 8 turns without an update ...)...

TOOLS_COMPARE same=true

So the tools were unchanged; the relevant system-prompt difference was the stale-turn counter.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run gentle-pi with Gentle Todo enabled.
2. Create a todo list containing at least one open task.
3. Leave the todo list unchanged for enough turns to trigger the stale warning.
4. Compare the effective system prompt immediately before two consecutive provider requests.
5. Observe that the stale counter changes from N turns to N+1 turns, even though the todo state itself did not change.
6. With a provider/backend that exposes prompt-cache or prefix-cache statistics, observe the resulting cache miss / large context reprocessing.

In my test, SGLang with radix/prefix caching repeatedly performed a very large prefill because the prefix changed.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected:

The todo list may legitimately alter the system prompt when the actual task state changes, but simply advancing from stale turn N to stale turn N+1 should not mutate the cached system-prompt prefix.

The visual stale indicator can continue counting turns in the UI without putting that volatile counter into the model's system prompt.

Actual:

Every stale turn changes the system prompt:

stale: 7 turns
stale: 8 turns
stale: 9 turns
...

This invalidates prompt-prefix reuse even when the actual todo list and the rest of the conversation are unchanged.
Validated workaround / suggested fix

I tested a minimal local patch:

export function todoPromptBlock(
  state: TodoState,
  _stale: number
): string | undefined {
  if (todoSummary(state).open === 0) return undefined;

  const lines = state.tasks.map(
    (task, index) =>
      `${index + 1}. [${task.status}] ${task.title}${
        task.note ? ` — ${task.note}` : ""
      }`
  );

  return [
    "## Todo list",
    "Keep it current with the `todo` tool: mark a task in_progress before starting it, done right after finishing it, and rewrite the whole list with `write` whenever the plan changes. Update it before you end the turn.",
    ...lines,
  ].join("\n");
}

The existing UI-side staleness logic remains unchanged:

const stale =
  options.staleTurns >= STALE_AFTER_TURNS;

const body = stale
  ? [
      theme.fg(
        NOTE_ROLE,
        `stale · ${options.staleTurns} turns`
      ),
      ...rows,
    ]
  : rows;

So the human still sees the live stale-turn counter, while the model's system prompt remains stable until the actual todo state changes.

After this patch, consecutive requests showed:

SYSTEM_COMPARE same=true
TOOLS_COMPARE same=true
MESSAGE_COMPARE common_messages=472/472 append_only=true

And the backend immediately reused the long context instead of recomputing it:

Prefill batch:
#new-token: 1024
#cached-token: 308864
#pending-token: 167

followed by only the small remaining delta.

This changed the behavior from effectively re-prefilling the long session to reusing ~309K cached tokens.

A possible alternative would be a non-numeric, stable stale reminder, but that would still change the prefix once when crossing the stale threshold. Keeping volatile staleness entirely in the UI avoids this class of cache invalidation.
Related issues
#67 — prompt-cache ordering of the stable Gentleman harness vs runtime system prompt.
#1029 — volatile RDD/SDD status embedded in the rebuilt system prompt defeating prompt caching.
#922 — todo staleness semantics and the (stale: N turns...) reminder, but focused on reminder effectiveness rather than prefix-cache invalidation.
#603 — original Gentle Todo design.

This issue is specifically about the numeric stale-turn counter making an otherwise unchanged system prompt different on every turn.

### gentle-pi version

3.3.0

### Pi version

0.87.0

### Operating system

Windows

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
Before workaround: SYSTEM_COMPARE same=false common_prefix_chars=73191 SYSTEM_PREV_AROUND=...(stale: 7 turns without an update ...)... SYSTEM_CURR_AROUND=...(stale: 8 turns without an update ...)... TOOLS_COMPARE same=true After workaround: SYSTEM_COMPARE same=true TOOLS_COMPARE same=true MESSAGE_COMPARE common_messages=472/472 append_only=true Backend after workaround: #new-token: 1024 #cached-token: 308864 #pending-token: 167
```

title: feat(i18n): añadir soporte configurable de idioma para la interfaz
body:
### Antes de enviar

- [x] He buscado entre las issues abiertas y no he encontrado una propuesta equivalente para añadir localización configurable a la interfaz de Gentle.
- [x] He revisado el alcance para mantener el idioma únicamente como una preferencia de presentación.
- [x] He validado una implementación de referencia contra el último `main` de upstream.
- [x] La implementación de referencia dispone de tests unitarios, de contrato y E2E, además de validación multiplataforma mediante CI.

### Problema u oportunidad

Actualmente, gran parte de la interfaz visible de Gentle se presenta únicamente en inglés.

Esto incluye elementos como:

- Command Palette
- nombres visibles de grupos y opciones
- descripciones de comandos
- selectores
- notificaciones
- mensajes de estado
- otros textos propios de la interfaz

Para usuarios que no hablan inglés, esto dificulta entender qué está haciendo Gentle, aunque el modelo pueda comunicarse perfectamente en su idioma.

La propuesta consiste en introducir una pequeña capa de internacionalización (`i18n`) determinista para los textos de interfaz propiedad de Gentle.

El idioma debe afectar únicamente a la presentación y no modificar el comportamiento interno del sistema.

### Resultado propuesto

Añadir soporte nativo para configurar el idioma de la interfaz.

Como primera versión:

- `auto`
- `en`
- `es`

La configuración estaría disponible mediante:

`/gentle:language`

Ejemplos:

`/gentle:language auto`

`/gentle:language en`

`/gentle:language es`

Si se ejecuta `/gentle:language` sin argumentos, debería mostrarse un selector interactivo.

La preferencia seleccionada debería persistir entre sesiones.

### Comportamiento de `auto`

`auto` debería intentar determinar el idioma utilizando la configuración regional del entorno.

Inicialmente:

- locale inglés → `en`
- locale español → `es`
- locale desconocido/no soportado → inglés

Una configuración explícita `en` o `es` siempre debería tener prioridad sobre la detección automática.

Para entornos compatibles se puede respetar la prioridad:

`LC_ALL` → `LC_MESSAGES` → `LANG`

con inglés como fallback seguro.

### Separación entre idioma y comportamiento

El idioma debe ser exclusivamente estado de presentación.

No debería modificar:

- identificadores de comandos como `/gentle:status`
- argumentos como `status`, `enable`, `disable` o `--edit`
- persona
- routing de modelos/proveedores
- comportamiento de agentes
- políticas de review
- comportamiento SDD/TDD/ODD
- referencias Git
- rutas
- variables de entorno
- identificadores de modelos/proveedores
- contratos JSON/schema/tools
- prompts de agentes
- tokens de protocolo
- semántica persistida de las sesiones

Por ejemplo, la interfaz podría mostrar:

`Configuration` → `Configuración`

`Session` → `Sesión`

`Diagnostics` → `Diagnóstico`

pero el comando seguiría siendo exactamente:

`gentle:status`

La traducción nunca debería modificar la parte ejecutable.

### Command Palette como primera superficie

Propongo utilizar el Command Palette como primera superficie delimitada para introducir i18n.

Se podrían traducir:

- títulos de grupos
- labels visibles
- descripciones de comandos propiedad de Gentle

Manteniendo sin cambios:

- identificadores de comandos
- shortcuts
- argumentos
- orden y comportamiento de ejecución

El propio comando de idioma también debería aparecer en el Command Palette.

Por ejemplo:

`Idioma de la interfaz`

manteniendo internamente:

`gentle:language`

### Persistencia

La preferencia podría almacenarse mediante una política pequeña y versionada:

`$GENTLE_PI_CONFIG_HOME/language.json`

Ejemplo:

~~~json
{
  "schema": "gentle-pi.language/v1",
  "language": "es"
}
~~~

La escritura debería seguir las mismas garantías utilizadas por otras configuraciones de Gentle:

- sustitución atómica
- permisos privados cuando el sistema lo permita
- recuperación segura ante configuración inválida
- inglés como fallback de compatibilidad

### Catálogo de traducciones

El catálogo inglés debería permanecer como referencia canónica.

Los demás idiomas deberían garantizar:

- paridad exacta de claves
- paridad de placeholders
- interpolación determinista
- fallback determinista a inglés
- ausencia de llamadas al modelo para textos fijos de interfaz

Esto permite que la internacionalización sea totalmente testeable.

### Tests / criterios de aceptación

La implementación debería cubrir como mínimo:

- [ ] schema versionado y estricto para la política de idioma
- [ ] soporte para `auto | en | es`
- [ ] prioridad del idioma explícito sobre el locale
- [ ] prioridad `LC_ALL` → `LC_MESSAGES` → `LANG`
- [ ] fallback a inglés para locales no soportados
- [ ] recuperación segura ante configuración persistida inválida
- [ ] persistencia mediante sustitución atómica
- [ ] ausencia de archivos temporales huérfanos tras una escritura correcta
- [ ] paridad exacta de claves entre EN y ES
- [ ] paridad de placeholders
- [ ] interpolación determinista
- [ ] persistencia de `/gentle:language es`
- [ ] selector interactivo de idioma
- [ ] aplicación inmediata del idioma seleccionado
- [ ] rechazo de idiomas inválidos sin modificar la configuración
- [ ] grupos, labels y descripciones del Command Palette en español
- [ ] identificadores `/gentle:*` exactamente iguales independientemente del idioma
- [ ] compatibilidad exacta del comportamiento existente en inglés
- [ ] validación del paquete/runtime

### Implementación de referencia

Para comprobar la viabilidad de la propuesta antes de solicitar su integración en upstream, he preparado una implementación de referencia en mi fork.

Rama:

`asenbanskaliev/gentle-shell:feat/i18n-language`

PR de desarrollo:

https://github.com/asenbanskaliev/gentle-shell/pull/5

La rama se ha sincronizado y probado contra el último `main` utilizado para la validación:

`5df9590e55b68717ea0cf8760eb9771c1dc9ed2b`

El HEAD validado de la rama es:

`2c16fe1e40875867246de530eb644a89ba604111`

### Evidencia de validación

La implementación de referencia ha pasado correctamente el CI completo después de sincronizarse con `main`.

**CI #25: PASS**

Se han validado correctamente:

- suite completa de tests
- TypeScript typecheck
- generated runtime modules
- package contents
- packed installation
- regresiones de review/Git en Windows
- session transport en macOS
- hidden-process contract tests en Windows
- hidden-process contract tests en Ubuntu

Además, la funcionalidad i18n dispone de tests específicos para:

- política y resolución del idioma
- persistencia
- configuración inválida
- prioridad de locales
- paridad de catálogos
- placeholders
- Command Palette
- preservación de identificadores técnicos
- `/gentle:language`

También se han añadido tests E2E que ejecutan el handler real de `/gentle:language`, no únicamente funciones auxiliares aisladas.

Estos E2E comprueban:

1. selección explícita de español;
2. persistencia real en `language.json`;
3. selector interactivo localizado;
4. cambio inmediato del idioma;
5. cambio posterior a inglés;
6. rechazo de valores no soportados;
7. ausencia de escritura de configuración cuando la entrada es inválida.

### Alcance propuesto para el primer PR

Para mantener el cambio pequeño y revisable, propongo que la primera integración se limite a:

1. política y resolución del idioma;
2. persistencia de la preferencia;
3. catálogo tipado EN/ES;
4. `/gentle:language`;
5. localización del Command Palette;
6. tests unitarios, de contrato y E2E.

El resto de superficies de Gentle podrían migrarse progresivamente en cambios posteriores.

Esto evita convertir la introducción de i18n en una modificación transversal demasiado grande.

### Alternativas consideradas

#### Traducir dinámicamente la interfaz mediante el modelo

No parece apropiado para textos fijos.

Introduciría:

- comportamiento no determinista
- latencia
- dependencia del proveedor/modelo
- mayor dificultad para realizar tests

Los textos fijos de interfaz deberían resolverse mediante un catálogo determinista.

#### Utilizar automáticamente el idioma de la conversación

El idioma de la conversación y el idioma de la aplicación son preferencias diferentes.

Por ejemplo, un usuario puede querer:

- interfaz de Gentle en español;
- código y documentación generados en inglés.

Por ello ambas configuraciones deberían permanecer independientes.

#### Traducir los comandos `/gentle:*`

No sería conveniente.

Los comandos y argumentos forman parte del contrato estable de interacción.

Por ejemplo:

`/gentle:status`

debería continuar siendo exactamente el mismo comando independientemente del idioma.

Solo debería traducirse su representación visible y su descripción.

### Evolución futura

Si esta base resulta aceptable, otros elementos de interfaz podrían migrarse progresivamente al mismo sistema sin modificar la arquitectura.

Esto permitiría añadir posteriormente más idiomas reutilizando:

- resolución de idioma
- persistencia
- catálogo tipado
- validaciones de paridad
- infraestructura de tests

sin introducir lógica condicional de idiomas dispersa por el código.

### Asistencia mediante IA

Se ha utilizado asistencia de IA de forma material para el análisis, exploración de la implementación, generación de tests y auditoría de la implementación de referencia.

El resultado ha sido revisado mediante tests deterministas y CI del repositorio, y asumo la responsabilidad sobre la propuesta y los cambios que eventualmente se presenten.

title: feat(orchestrator): automatic non-blocking delegation reminders that keep inline-vs-delegate decision with the model
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Less capable models — including some with a high Intelligence Index that still are not good orchestrators — silently skip the delegation contract in `assets/orchestrator-delegation.md`. They keep working inline past the mapping / multi-file-write / long-session thresholds until a human reminds them of the rule. Prompt-only wording loses to momentum in long turns. Verified live in-session: after 3 distinct inline `read` calls the parent kept going with no self-correction until the reminder fired.

Related problem statement: #1117 (mechanical delegation-pressure guard — the long-session rule is prompt-only).

### Proposed outcome

A runtime **automatic reminder that does not block**: count parent tool calls per session since the last successful `subagent_run` dispatch, and when a threshold is crossed inject a short reminder naming the crossed rule and the expected delegation route (`gentle-ai-explore` / `gentle-ai-worker` / `gentle-ai-verify`). The decision stays with the model — trivial work can stay inline, non-trivial work should delegate.

Concrete thresholds: 3 distinct files read, 5 exploration calls (`read`/`grep`/`find`/`codegraph_codegraph_explore`), 20 tool calls in the session, 2 distinct files written. One notice per threshold per delegation interval; a successful delegation resets the counters, a failed one does not. Harness bookkeeping (`odd/tasks/**`) and skill reads are exempt. Delivery is post-tool via `tool_result` → `sendMessage` (`display: false`, steer, `triggerTurn: true`): it informs the next model decision, never refuses a tool, never wakes an idle session, never mutates a result.

### Alternatives considered

- **Hard block / refusal at the tool boundary**: rejected — it removes the model's judgment for genuinely trivial inline work and adds failure modes at the hook layer.
- **Prompt-only strengthening (softer/harder wording)**: the status quo; soft rules lose to momentum in long turns (see the evidence in #1117).

### Additional context

Implemented on branch `feat/orchestrator-delegation-reminders`: a pure state module (`lib/orchestrator-delegation-reminders.ts`) plus wiring in `extensions/gentle-ai.ts`, with focused unit coverage (`tests/orchestrator-delegation-reminders.test.ts`) and a real-hook runtime-harness scenario. Verified live: the "3 files read" reminder fired exactly at the third distinct inline read, and exploration continued correctly through delegation afterwards. This proposal does not cover the status-bar counter or bash-output counting suggested in #1117 — those remain open scope there.

title: feat(ask): add per-question notes to ask_user_question with the n key
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

The `ask_user_question` questionnaire supports structured single- and multi-select decisions, but users cannot attach additional context to an individual question without replacing the structured answer with the generic `Type something.` response.

This becomes limiting when the listed option is correct but needs a qualification, constraint, or short explanation. The user must either lose the structured selection or provide the context later in a separate message, making it harder for the agent to associate the note with the corresponding question.

The questionnaire already has an internal representation for notes. However, issue #833 deliberately excluded question-note and global-note controls from the initial first-party TUI delivery. This request proposes exposing only the per-question capability through a compact, optional interaction.

### Proposed outcome

Allow users to add an optional note to the currently active question by pressing `n`.

Expected behavior:

- Pressing `n` while a question is active opens a text editor for that question's note.
- The note belongs to the question, not to an individual option.
- Adding a note does not replace or modify the selected answer.
- Notes work with both single-select and multi-select questions.
- Pressing `n` again allows the note to be reviewed, edited, or removed.
- Questions with a note show a small visible indicator.
- The footer includes the `n` shortcut so the capability is discoverable.
- Submitted results preserve the structured answer and its note as separate fields.
- Notes remain optional and do not prevent submission.
- Cancellation and partial-answer behavior remain unchanged.
- Notes are informational only. They must not grant permissions, alter opaque answer tokens, or become an authority mechanism for consent or maintenance workflows.
- The separate `ask_user_choice` authority-bearing path remains unchanged.

Example:

```text
Deployment target
> Production

Note:
Deploy after the scheduled database backup completes.
```

The resulting answer should retain `Production` as the selected option and return the note as supplementary context for that question.

### Alternatives considered

- **Use `Type something.` instead:** this replaces the structured selection rather than supplementing it.
- **Send a follow-up chat message:** the agent must infer which question the note belongs to, especially when several questions were asked together.
- **Add notes to individual options:** unnecessarily complicates the interaction. A single note associated with the question is sufficient.
- **Add a global questionnaire note:** useful for general context, but it does not preserve the relationship between a note and a specific question.
- **Expose every internal note control:** broader than necessary. This request intentionally proposes only an optional per-question note opened with `n`.

### Additional context

Related issues:

- #833 introduced the first-party TUI questionnaire and explicitly kept question-note and global-note controls hidden in its initial scope.
- #1282 mentions questionnaire notes while discussing multi-select support for `ask_user_choice`, but it does not request this interaction.

This request is therefore a deliberate extension of #833 rather than a duplicate.

The note should remain structurally separate from the selected option so downstream agents can distinguish the user's decision from supplementary context.

title: fix(openspec): preserve internal markdown dividers in requirement content
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

In `lib/openspec-deltas.ts`, `cleanRequirementContent` strips trailing boundary delimiters using:
```ts
return content.trimEnd().replace(/\n\s*---\s*$/m, "").trimEnd();
```
Because the regular expression uses the multiline flag `/m` without `/g` and is not anchored to the end of the entire string, `replace()` matches the **first** line ending with `---`. 

If a requirement body contains an internal divider (such as a markdown thematic break, horizontal rule, or table/code block containing `---`), `replace()` strips that internal divider instead of the trailing delimiter at the bottom of the section, corrupting the requirement body and leaving the trailing delimiter intact.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Parse a requirement section whose body text contains an internal markdown horizontal rule (e.g. `Some text\n\n---\n\nMore text\n\n---`).
2. Run `cleanRequirementContent(content)`.
3. Observe which `---` gets removed.

### Expected and actual behavior

**Expected:**
The internal `---` is preserved, and only the trailing section delimiter at the end of the string is removed.

**Actual:**
The first internal `---` line is stripped, and the trailing `---` delimiter remains at the end of the requirement body.

main

### Pi version

latest

### Operating system

Linux
