title: bug(startup): text logo missing below 122 columns and 5s animation cap freezes last letters on slow devices
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

On narrow terminals (phones, phones-in-tmux, any session with fewer than 122 columns), the startup banner's "Gentle Shell" text logo never renders: `render()` only draws the ASCII wordmark when `width >= logoBase.width + 2` (120 + 2), and there is no fallback, so narrow sessions show only the rose and the stats table with no branding at all.

Additionally, the letter-writing animation has a hard 5-second wall-clock cap (`Date.now() - animStart > 5000`). On slower devices the Pi startup workload starves the 25 ms interval, so ticks lag far behind wall-clock time. Because the script letters are drawn left to right, the final letters of "SHELL" are drawn last; when the 5 s cap kills the interval, the frozen frame permanently misses those last letters. This reproduces regardless of terminal width.

A related papercut: the end-of-writing sparkle replaces the last logo cell with `✦` for a few ticks. If the final repaint is dropped or coalesced by the terminal, the glyph stays frozen mid-effect, replacing a letter with a star.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install gentle-pi 3.3.0 on a phone-sized terminal (80 columns, 24-30 rows; e.g. Termux on Android, default font size).
2. Run `pi` and watch the startup banner.
3. Observe: no text logo at all (only the rose and stats).
4. For the frozen-letters case: run on a slow device (or throttle the event loop during startup) with the terminal at 122+ columns so the full art renders, and let the animation run. The last letters of "SHELL" never appear; the frame freezes mid-writing when the 5 s cap is reached.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected:
- The startup branding degrades gracefully on narrow terminals (some form of text logo still visible).
- The letterwriting animation always reaches its final frame, even when the event loop is busy.

Actual:
- Below 122 columns, no text logo is rendered at all.
- On slower devices the 5 s wall-clock cap stops the animation mid-writing, permanently freezing a frame without the last letters of "SHELL".

### gentle-pi version

3.3.0

### Pi version

0.86.0

### Operating system

Other

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text

N/A - visual/rendering issue. Reproduced and root-caused by inspecting
extensions/startup-banner.ts (width gate at logoBase.width + 2; hard cap
`Date.now() - animStart > 5000` in the animation interval).

```

title: Measured: where a delegated child's wall-clock actually goes (12 children, 471 turns) — and the four things that are guardable
body:
I measured the wall-clock profile of delegated children from their own session transcripts, because "the workers feel slow" is not actionable and the guess was wrong. **It is not the model.**

Method: one interactive session, Pi 0.85.1, gentle-pi 3.3.0, macOS. **12 children** (`gentle-ai-worker`, `gentle-ai-verify`, `gentle-ai-explore`), **97 minutes** of child wall-clock in total, read from `~/.pi/agent/gentle-agents/sessions/*.jsonl` by pairing each message gap to exactly one cause: `assistant → toolResult` is tool execution, `toolResult → assistant` is model latency.

## The profile

| | time | share |
|---|---|---|
| model thinking | 59.3 min over **471 turns** | **61%** |
| tools executing | 36.3 min over 720 calls | 37% |
| startup/teardown | 1.1 min | 1% |

**Per-turn latency, by resolved model** — the only apples-to-apples number here:

| model | children | turns | median | range |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deepseek-v4.1-flash` (workers) | 9 | 430 | **5.3 s** | 3.3 – 11.3 s |
| `glm-5.3-flash` (verifiers) | 3 | 41 | **17.3 s** | 13.1 – 29.1 s |

So the harness is not slow per step: it is **1.5 tool calls per turn**, and 471 turns at ~5 s each is what the hour is made of. Full tool distribution, with medians rather than means (the means are poisoned by outliers — see finding 1):

| category | n | median | total |
|---|---|---|---|
| reads (`cat`/`sed`/`ls`/`find`) | 120 | **0.1 s** | 12.7 min |
| `rg`/`grep` | 53 | **0.1 s** | 2.9 min |
| focused test run | 49 | 4.4 s | 4.8 min |
| `pnpm typecheck` | 11 | 5.4 s | 2.5 min |
| full test suite | 16 | 21.1 s | 5.2 min |
| **`pnpm lint`** | 15 | **35.1 s** (p90 39.8) | **9.1 min** |

**83% of all bash time sits in 39 of 319 calls** (every one over 20 s).

## Four things that are guardable

**1. Unguarded filesystem scans — the single worst offender, and the cheapest fix.** Two calls, **10.4 minutes = 11% of everything**:

- **470 s**: `find / -path /proc -prune -o -name "*.yml" -path "*lens*" -print` — a worker hunting for a rule file, starting at the filesystem root.
- **154 s**: `ls <project dir>; find ~ -name "STRINGS-phase1.md" -not -path "*/node_modules/*"` — the same pattern over the home directory.

The prompt-side fix is a line in the shipped worker/orchestrator assets ("never scan above the repository root"). The harness-side fix is the only *guaranteed* one, and it is unusually cheap here because gentle-pi already rewrites every bash call: a rule that flags (or asks before running) a recursive scan whose root is `/` or `$HOME` would have paid for itself in this one session by 11%.

**2. The repeatable gate cost is `lint`, not the tests.** 15 runs × 35 s = 9.1 min, and every worker re-ran it inside the loop. Note what the workers *did* do well: only 49 focused test runs against 16 full ones, so the test strategy is fine. (This one is arguably ours to fix in the target repo with an eslint cache — flagging it because the harness's own gate guidance is what drives the repetition.)

**3. Model routing is the verifier's problem, not the worker's.** 17.3 s/turn versus 5.3 s is a 3.3× difference on the same task shapes. If the verification step is on the critical path — and in an ODD/RDD flow it always is — the routing choice there dominates the routing choice for the worker.

**4. Nothing ran in parallel.** Those 97 child-minutes were strictly sequential. 61% of them are model latency, which is exactly the share two independent children could overlap. There is no policy blocker for it (§ #479 asks for the parallel-execution knob), but a session-shaped nudge would help: the "long-session rule" that exists is about delegation pressure, not about whether two tasks that share no files could go out together.

## Tried and ruled out, so nobody repeats it

- **`rtk` is not adding latency**: `rtk cat` measures 0.01–0.03 s against `cat`'s 0.00 s.
- **Reads and greps are already fast** (median 0.1 s), and so are focused test runs (4.4 s). There is no general slowness to optimize.

## Caveats, stated because they bound the claims

- **One session, 12 children.** Enough to decide where to look, not a benchmark.
- **Attribution artifact**: when a turn emits parallel tool calls, the first result's gap absorbs the whole batch. Two of the "slow" numbers above (a 154 s single-file `rg`) are artifacts of that, not real command times — I checked the full command text before reporting, which is how the two real outliers surfaced.
- **No cost data**: the child transcripts carry no `usage`, so this is wall-clock only (reported separately on #975).
- The `cd <cwd> &&` prefix the harness prepends to every bash call defeats naive grouping by command; it has to be normalized first.

title: perf(agents): avoid re-reading unchanged remote activity files on every presence poll
body:
# perf(agents): avoid re-reading unchanged remote activity files on every presence poll

## Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues and PRs for this problem.
- [x] I reviewed related presence-poll work, especially #1011 and PR #1123.
- [x] This is complementary to #1123: that PR avoids unnecessary renders after a quiet poll; this proposal avoids the expensive activity-file read/parse/hash work before that decision.

## Problem

`AgentsView` refreshes remote presence approximately once per second.

For every recent remote session, the current flow calls `readActivity(...)` again even when that session's activity has not changed.

That means an unchanged peer repeatedly pays for:

- opening and reading the activity file;
- validating the file;
- parsing the JSON;
- computing/verifying its SHA-256 digest;
- reconstructing the remote tasks and threads.

This happens even though the lightweight presence header already exposes enough information to know whether the activity changed:

- `generation`
- `digest`
- `unavailable`

A quiet remote session therefore has its full activity payload re-read every poll.

## Current flow

~~~text
every ~1 second
    ↓
read remote header
    ↓
read full activity file
    ↓
parse + validate + hash
    ↓
build remote tasks/threads
    ↓
repeat next second even if unchanged
~~~

## Proposed direction

Keep the last valid remote activity snapshot keyed by the session activation and the header version:

~~~text
generation + digest + unavailable
~~~

Then:

~~~text
every ~1 second
    ↓
read lightweight header
    ↓
did its version change?
    ├─ no  → reuse the existing activity snapshot
    └─ yes → read and rebuild the activity
~~~

Transient read failures should not be cached, so the following poll can retry normally.

Cached entries should also be removed when a remote session disappears and cleared when the Agents view is disposed.

## A/B measurements

I implemented a proof of concept in my fork:

~~~text
asenbanskaliev/gentle-shell
branch: perf/presence-activity-cache-validation
~~~

The benchmark uses the existing presence/activity format and compares repeated unchanged polling with and without the activity cache.

Environment: Node.js 22.16.0, local filesystem, same process/machine for both paths.

| Activity per remote session | Sessions | Current per poll | Cached per poll | Saved per poll |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 100 KB | 1 | 0.137 ms | 0.001 ms | 0.136 ms |
| 100 KB | 5 | 0.646 ms | 0.004 ms | 0.642 ms |
| 100 KB | 10 | 1.279 ms | 0.007 ms | 1.272 ms |
| 1 MB | 1 | 1.645 ms | 0.031 ms | 1.614 ms |
| 1 MB | 5 | 8.560 ms | 0.169 ms | 8.391 ms |
| 1 MB | 10 | 17.094 ms | 0.342 ms | 16.752 ms |
| 5 MB | 1 | 8.210 ms | 0.410 ms | 7.800 ms |
| 5 MB | 5 | 41.585 ms | 2.017 ms | 39.568 ms |

The improvement grows with both the number of open sessions and the size of their retained activity.

For example:

~~~text
5 remote sessions × ~5 MB activity

current: ~41.6 ms / poll
cached:   ~2.0 ms / poll
~~~

That is roughly a **20× reduction** in this specific hot path.

## Why this is different from PR #1123

PR #1123 optimizes the end of the presence polling flow:

~~~text
read activity
→ build state
→ compare display signature
→ unchanged
→ skip render
~~~

This proposal optimizes the earlier part:

~~~text
read lightweight header
→ version unchanged
→ skip full activity read/parse/hash
~~~

The two optimizations are complementary.

Combined, a quiet peer could do:

~~~text
read small header
→ unchanged
→ no large activity read
→ no activity parsing/hash
→ no state rebuild
→ no render
~~~

## Correctness constraints tested in the proof of concept

The experimental implementation preserves these behaviors:

- a changed `generation` / `digest` invalidates the cached snapshot;
- changed remote activity is read and displayed normally;
- transient `readActivity()` failures are not cached;
- a failed read is retried on the next poll;
- disappeared remote sessions are removed from the cache;
- the cache is cleared when the view is disposed.

## Relevant code

Main areas:

~~~text
lib/agents-view.ts
lib/orchestrator-presence.ts
~~~

Current expensive call:

~~~ts
readActivity(source.profile, header)
~~~

The header already carries the version information required to decide whether that call is necessary.

## Expected outcome

Unchanged remote sessions should not require re-reading their full activity files every second.

The presence polling cadence and freshness semantics can stay unchanged; this only avoids repeating expensive work for an activity version that has already been successfully loaded.

title: Support opencode-go subscription usage in /gentle:usage
body:
### Problem or opportunity

`/gentle:usage` cannot show anything for the `opencode-go` provider. It renders "no subscription usage for this provider" because the provider list is closed:

- `lib/shell-usage.ts` → `SUPPORTED_USAGE_PROVIDERS = [openai-codex, anthropic, nan]`
- `extensions/gentle-shell.ts` → the automatic refresh returns early for any other provider

The data does exist. OpenCode Go exposes the same rolling / weekly / monthly windows the web dashboard draws, at a fixed API-key authenticated endpoint:

```
GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/usage
Authorization: Bearer <key>
-> 200
{"usage":{
  "rolling":{"status":"ok","percent":3, "resetsAt":"2026-09-20T05:35:53.613Z"},
  "weekly": {"status":"ok","percent":36,"resetsAt":"2026-09-21T00:00:00.000Z"},
  "monthly":{"status":"ok","percent":0, "resetsAt":"2026-10-20T00:50:21.000Z"}}}
```

Verified with a Go subscription key. The sibling paths (`/usage/limits`, `/usage/tokens`, `/subscription`, `/plan`) return 404, and `/zen/go/v1/models` carries only `id` / `object` / `created` / `owned_by`, so this endpoint is the whole surface.

### Proposed outcome

`opencode-go` joins the supported usage providers, so the shell-bar segment and the `/gentle:usage` panel render the three windows the same way Codex, Claude and NaN already do: limit name, meter, percentage, and the reset when the window reports one. The documented plan limits are dollar-based and per model (5-hour 20%, weekly 50%, monthly 100% of a per-model monthly allowance), so a token or dollar figure should not be invented from a rounded integer percentage — percentage plus reset is what the endpoint actually reports.

The insertion points are small and mirror how NaN was added: a `fetchOpencodeGoUsage` plus a defensive parser in `lib/shell-usage.ts`, the provider added to `SUPPORTED_USAGE_PROVIDERS` and `PENDING_NOTE`, and the early return in `extensions/gentle-shell.ts` relaxed for it. The existing 5-minute refresh floor, the fixed-origin fetch with redirects refused, and the keep-the-last-valid-snapshot rule all apply unchanged.

### Alternatives considered

- **Scraping the console dashboard.** Rejected: the API endpoint above is the supported surface, and it needs only the key Pi already holds.
- **Showing a token or dollar allowance.** Rejected: the payload reports no tokens, and the documented allowances are per-model monthly dollar amounts that the payload does not identify, so any figure would be derived from a rounded percentage and could mislead.
- **Credit balance / spend.** Out of scope: the Zen wallet is not exposed to API keys.
- **Keeping it out of the package.** What I do today: a local Pi extension outside gentle-pi. It works, but it cannot feed the bar segment or the panel, which are owned by this extension, so the data lives in a second place instead of where the user already looks.

### Additional context

I already implemented and verified this as an external Pi extension against a live Go subscription: the three windows parse correctly, a malformed or empty payload is treated as a failure rather than a zeroed subscription, and the fetch refuses redirects so the bearer cannot be replayed to another origin. Happy to send it as a PR in this repository's shape, with tests, once the approach is agreed.

title: Native review cannot complete on OpenCode-hosted providers: the in-process completion omits x-opencode-session
body:
### Problem

Native review cannot complete when the reviewer model is served by an OpenCode-hosted provider. Every lens capture fails at the `pi` stage with:

```
Reviewer completion failed for review-reliability: 400: {"type":"MissingSessionID","message":"Request is missing x-opencode-session and cannot be routed efficiently. Please see https://opencode.ai/docs/go/#where-can-i-use-it"}
```

The capture is refused before it can be acknowledged, so the lineage stays in `reviewing` and nothing is admitted. No lens can succeed, and `correction_budget` is never reached because no reviewer result exists.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have `opencode-go` as the only configured provider (auth through `/login`).
2. Assign a model to any lens in the agent model routing config, e.g. `review-reliability` in `~/.pi/gentle-ai/models.json` (the same entry shape `review-refuter` and `review-validator` already use).
3. Start a native review over any non-trivial committed candidate.
4. Capture the materialize slot and acknowledge the forecast.

### Expected and actual behavior

**Expected:** the lens completion runs and the reviewer result is admitted.

**Actual:** the launch fails with `pi-host-relay-transport-failure`, `failure.kind: pi-failed`, and the provider's `400 MissingSessionID`. `mutation_performed: false`, so the lineage is untouched but unusable.

### Root cause

The in-process reviewer completion runs outside Pi's agent loop:

- `lib/inprocess-reviewer.ts` resolves credentials through the injected registry (`deps.registry.getApiKeyAndHeaders(model)`) and then calls pi-ai's `completeSimple` directly.
- Pi adds `x-opencode-session` and `x-opencode-client` inside its own agent loop, through `transformHeaders` / `mergeProviderAttributionHeaders`. That path is not used here.
- The registry that gentle-pi passes is Pi's own `ctx.modelRegistry`, which returns provider-config headers but not the OpenCode session attribution.
- The completion already forwards whatever headers the registry resolved (`options.headers = auth.headers`), so the gap is exactly the registry seam.

This is the same class of problem already documented and worked around in `pi-web-access/opencode-session-headers.ts`: "Pi adds OpenCode attribution headers inside the main agent loop. Extension side-calls dispatch directly, so they must add the same session attribution."

Note that **no configuration can work around it**: provider-level `headers` (both through `pi.registerProvider` and in `models.json`), `modelOverrides` with a wildcard, and full per-model definitions each leave the resolved `Model` without headers, because config headers are applied in Pi's request layer — the layer this completion bypasses.

### Proposed fix

A small registry wrapper that adds the two headers for exactly the models Pi itself would attribute (the `opencode` and `opencode-go` providers, or any model whose base URL is the OpenCode host), applied at both capture call sites. Every other model passes through untouched, and a header the provider already resolved keeps its own value.

Prepared and verified on a fork: branch `fix/opencode-session-attribution`. Tests: 10 new cases, including one that drives `runInProcessReviewer` with the wrapped registry and asserts both headers reach the completion. Full suite on that branch: 2898 tests, 2850 pass, 1 fail — that failure ("a missing review-refuter routing model is refused typed") reproduces on a pristine `main` here, so it is pre-existing and unrelated to this report.

### gentle-pi version

3.3.0

### Pi version

0.86.0

### Operating system

macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), Node v26.8.2

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```
{"tool":"gentle_review_capture","status":"blocked",
 "outcome":"pi-host-relay-transport-failure",
 "failure":{"kind":"pi-failed","stage":"pi","exit_code":null,"timed_out":false},
 "reason":"Reviewer completion failed for review-reliability: 400: {\"type\":\"MissingSessionID\",...}",
 "mutation_performed":false,"mutation_outcome":"none"}
```

A minimal probe against the same endpoint shows the request is otherwise accepted: `GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/usage` returns 200 with the same credentials, and a `POST` to `/zen/go/v1/chat/completions` returns 200 when the session header is present.

title: bug(review): an empty-output refusal discards the reviewer model and its token usage — the evidence that separates truncation from an empty answer
body:
## Summary

When a lens capture returns no text, the refusal carries `stopReason` but neither the reviewer model nor the completion's token usage. Both are in scope at the refusal site, and the relay already forwards whatever the refusal puts in `evidence` (`review-host-relay.ts:542` → `reviewerEvidence`). The success path returns `reviewerModel`; the failure path drops it.

That asymmetry is what turned a one-run diagnosis into a nine-run one.

## Where

`lib/inprocess-reviewer.ts`.

Success path (line 259):

```ts
return { kind: "text", text, reviewerModel: `${model.provider}/${model.id}` };
```

Empty-output refusal (lines 243-250):

```ts
const text = assistant.content.filter(isTextContent).map((part) => part.text).join("");
if (text.length === 0) {
	return refuse(
		INPROCESS_REVIEWER_FAILURE.EMPTY_OUTPUT,
		`Reviewer produced no text for ${request.routingKey} (stopReason: ${assistant.stopReason}).`,
		{ stopReason: assistant.stopReason, ...(assistant.errorMessage === undefined ? {} : { errorMessage: assistant.errorMessage }) },
	);
}
```

`assistant.usage` is in scope and is discarded. So is `model.provider` / `model.id`.

## Why it matters — a real case

Nine consecutive captures of a single candidate, every one refused with `reviewer-empty-output` and `stopReason: length` at 59-70 s. The reviewer model was recorded nowhere: the refusal evidence carried `stopReason` only, and the lineage's `review-state.json` records neither the model nor any usage. The only signal of which model had run was the wall-clock time — a routing change that moved the same capture from 59 s to 201 s was the single clue that a different model was involved.

The underlying cause turned out to be a **provider** defect (an OpenAI-compatible provider whose streaming endpoint truncates long completions with `finish_reason: "length"` and emits zero content, while the identical request without streaming completes normally). That part is not this project's. What *is* this project's is that the envelope could not say it:

- with `usage` in the evidence, the first refusal would have read *"32,768 output tokens, all of them reasoning, `stopReason: length`"* — the truncation diagnosis, in one run instead of ten;
- with the model id, "which model ran" stops being an inference from elapsed time;
- with the requested `max_tokens`, it closes completely, because a truncation is only interpretable next to the ceiling that was asked for.

## Proposed change (small, and the plumbing already exists)

1. **Add the fields to the refusal `evidence`** at the empty-output site — and anywhere else a completion succeeded but the result was refused: `reviewerModel`, `usage` (input / output / reasoning / total) and the requested max tokens. The relay already propagates `evidence`, so nothing downstream needs to change for these to reach the operator.
2. **Consider a distinct code** for "the completion ended with `stopReason: "length"` and produced no text", so truncation is not collapsed into the same `EMPTY_OUTPUT` as a model that simply answered nothing. Listed second on purpose: the failure codes are a stable contract and appear to be mapped on the Go side, so this one may be more expensive. If it is, `stopReason` plus `usage` in the evidence is already enough for a human to tell the two apart.
3. **Related, same incident:** the lineage does not record attempts. A lineage left in `reviewing` with the lens slot open is indistinguishable from one nobody has run yet. An attempt counter (or last-failure summary) in `STATUS` would make "it failed nine times" visible without reading the tool transcript.

## Repro

Any provider or model that answers with `stopReason: "length"` and no text content. `tests/inprocess-reviewer.test.ts` already exercises the empty-output refusal against a stub model, so the assertion can be extended to require `usage` and `reviewerModel` in the evidence with no network involved.

Version: gentle-pi 3.3.0.

Add a session-only Project Map preview below Status
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Gentle Shell shows the current session, captured changes, and task-level TODOs, but it does not keep the whole product visible. On broad greenfield projects, planning can concentrate on the first technical surface—often API or database work—while frontend, UX, operations, security, and testing remain invisible.

The user can see what the current agent is doing, but not:

- which product capabilities exist;
- which are complete, active, ready, blocked, or planned;
- which technical surfaces each capability spans;
- whether the project is becoming unbalanced toward backend work;
- which capability is ready to start next.

### Proposed outcome

Approve a bounded **visual-only Project Map preview** directly below the unified Status card in Gentle Shell fullscreen mode.

The requested first slice is deliberately small:

- static `Example Shop` demonstration data;
- same informational-card style as the existing sidebar;
- disabled by default in every session;
- `/gentle:project-map` toggles it for the current session only;
- no persistence, project discovery, worktrees, terminal launching, coordination, or clickable actions.

The real fullscreen order is:

```text
Status → Project Map (when enabled) → Agents → TODO
```

`Changes` remains a group inside the unified Status card; it is not a separate rail card.

#### Primary visual experience

```text
PROJECT MAP · Example Shop                    6/12

Foundations
✓ Repository and environments
✓ Authentication and merchant authority
◉ Deployment and observability        review

Product capabilities
✓ Merchant invitations       Web · API · DB
◉ Merchant catalog           Web · API · DB    session-42
○ Shopping cart              Web               ready     [Open Pi]
○ Checkout and orders        Web · API · DB    blocked
○ Payments                   Web · API · DB    planned
○ Admin dashboard            Web · API         ready     [Open Pi]

Coverage
Product/UX  45%   Web 35%   API 70%   Data 75%   Ops 25%
```

The map is intended to become the user's persistent project-navigation surface. In this first slice, however, every displayed state, session marker, percentage, and `[Open Pi]` label is inert presentation used only to validate hierarchy, readability, and placement.

#### Requested decision

Approve only this visual preview as the first bounded change. Approval does not authorize the larger orchestration system described under “Future direction,” and it grants no automatic source-write, delivery, worktree, terminal, or merge authority.

### Alternatives considered

- **Continue using TODOs:** insufficient because TODOs describe the active work unit, not the whole product.
- **Put the map inside Status:** rejected for the prototype because the map needs its own scan-friendly hierarchy and may grow independently from session metadata.
- **Organize work as frontend/backend/database streams:** rejected because horizontal streams hide incomplete user journeys and increase coupling.
- **Implement live data immediately:** rejected because visual comprehension and sidebar fit should be validated before introducing persistence or coordination state.
- **Enable the preview globally:** rejected for the first slice; session-only, default-off behavior makes evaluation reversible and low-risk.

### Additional context

#### Local proof of concept

A local, unpublished proof of concept was used to validate feasibility. It implements only the requested visual slice and has no functional Project Map behavior.

Observed checks:

- focused Project Map/layout tests: **21 passed**;
- related Gentle Shell suite: **93 passed**;
- package suite: **2,626 passed, 38 skipped**;
- provider-contract check: passed;
- runtime harness: passed;
- typecheck: no regressions against the recorded baseline;
- independent verification: passed;
- native reliability review: approved.

The proof of concept is not being presented as pre-approved or merge-ready implementation. Its purpose is to reduce uncertainty about rendering, width safety, session isolation, and sidebar placement before maintainers decide whether the first slice belongs in the product.

#### First-slice success criteria

- A new session does not display the Project Map until the user enables it.
- `/gentle:project-map` shows and hides the preview only for the current session.
- The enabled fullscreen rail renders Status, then Project Map, then Agents and TODO.
- Narrow and regular layouts remain unchanged.
- The card uses existing Gentle Shell visual language and remains within sidebar width.
- The mockup clearly distinguishes foundations, product capabilities, lifecycle state, surface coverage, and project imbalance.
- `[Open Pi]` and all other labels remain inert.
- A second session never inherits the first session's enabled state.

#### Explicit non-goals for this issue

- Reading or generating a real project map.
- Persisting capabilities or user preferences.
- Creating branches or Git worktrees.
- Opening terminals or launching Pi sessions.
- Clicking `[Open Pi]` or any capability row.
- Lead/satellite orchestrator coordination.
- Claims, leases, heartbeats, contracts, blockers, or offline synchronization.
- Integration queues, automatic commits, push, PR creation, or merge.

#### Future direction — separate approval required

If the visual preview proves useful, follow-up issues can independently propose:

1. a human-reviewed, versioned capability-map schema;
2. live status overlay from cross-worktree coordination state;
3. lead/satellite ownership and contract negotiation;
4. safe branch/worktree provisioning and an explicit `Open Pi` action;
5. integration-readiness sequencing without automatic delivery authority.

Each item should receive its own design review, issue approval, implementation boundary, and rollback plan. None is required to accept or evaluate this first visual slice.

#### Risks and mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| The preview creates expectations of working actions | Label it explicitly as visual-only; keep all rows and `[Open Pi]` inert. |
| The sidebar becomes crowded | Default off; render only in fullscreen; validate wrapping and width bounds. |
| Session state leaks across sessions | Key state by Pi session ID and remove it on shutdown. |
| The prototype is mistaken for the final data model | Keep demonstration data static and defer schemas to a separately approved issue. |

title: bug(orchestrator): writer pre-check rejects valid task surfaces with non-specific reason (regression-class of #484)
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this exact failure mode.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

After the fix for #484 (commit `514f9e57`, version 3.3.0), `gentle-ai-worker` continues to reject some otherwise-valid task specs that contain a canonical `## Allowed edit surfaces` block. The rejection message is the generic `WRITER_EDIT_SURFACE_REJECTION` constant in `extensions/gentle-ai.ts`, which does not tell the parent why the section was rejected — only that the parent must "derive or map" it.

Reproduction shows the rejection correlates with:

- Task string size (small tasks ~10 lines accepted; ~200-line tasks rejected)
- `mode: background` (default) vs `mode: "task"` (the latter succeeds for short tasks)
- Code-block escaping in the task body (the parser may interpret backtick fences inside the task body as headings)

But the parent cannot distinguish these failure modes from "heading missing" or "invalid path" because the rejection message is generic. The fix for #484 addressed a different parser bug (heading detection didn't stop at deeper headings); this is a different failure mode that the parser still has.

Related (read for context):

- #484 (closed, parser fix for a different shape of the same bug)
- #1174 (open, mode handling; related to the `mode: background` angle)
- #598 (closed, backtick parsing for SDD; similar class)

### Steps to reproduce

All from the same session, dispatched to `gentle-ai-worker`, `workspace_root: /home/javi/Dev/webdev`.

#### Task A — ACCEPTED (3 surfaces, ~10-line body, `mode: "task"`)

```text
## Allowed edit surfaces

.pi/skills/problem-based-srs/SKILL.md
.pi/skills/epic-decomposition/SKILL.md
.pi/skills/backlog/SKILL.md

## Boundaries

Minimal test. Verify you can see the 3 surfaces. Return a one-line confirmation. Do not write anything.

## Key Learnings closing

After your normal result, close with a `## Key Learnings` block (1-5 numbered factual sentences, ≥20 chars, ≥4 words each).
```

Result: `status: completed`. The worker read the 3 SKILL.md files and returned a one-line confirmation. No rejection.

#### Task B — REJECTED (1 surface, ~200-line body with escaped code blocks, `mode: default`)

Same surface shape as Task A's first entry, with a task body that contains the full text of a new SKILL.md to create (including escaped code fences like ```` ``` ````). The body has the canonical `## File content` heading after `## Boundaries`. The task body is structurally identical to Task A inside the surfaces block.

Result: rejection with `WRITER_EDIT_SURFACE_REJECTION`. No subagent launched. No files modified.

#### Task C — REJECTED (1 surface, ~200-line body, `mode: default`, explicit `workspace_root`)

Same as Task B with `workspace_root: /home/javi/Dev/webdev` and `mode: default` (background).

Result: same rejection as Task B.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: per the contract in `orchestrator-delegation.md` lines 225–235 and the regression tests in `tests/writer-edit-surface-scope.test.ts` lines 199–224, all three tasks have a canonical `## Allowed edit surfaces` block with valid repo-relative paths and prose under the next heading. All three should be accepted (or rejected with a specific reason).

Actual:

- Task A accepted.
- Tasks B and C rejected with the generic `WRITER_EDIT_SURFACE_REJECTION`.
- The parent has no way to distinguish "task exceeds a size limit" from "code blocks confused the parser" from "background mode is stricter" from "your surfaces section is actually broken".

### gentle-pi version

3.3.0

### Pi version

unknown (not captured in repro; user environment)

### Operating system

Linux (Ubuntu 24.04)

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

The rejection payload returned to the parent:

```
Writer tasks must include the exact Markdown heading `## Allowed edit surfaces`
with narrow repository-relative paths or narrow globs, one per line. Every
non-empty line belongs to the section until the next canonical Markdown
heading and must be a valid surface entry. Paths containing whitespace
require whole-entry backticks; begin explanatory prose under the next
Markdown heading. The parent must derive or map that canonical block from
the delegated task and relaunch the writer; do not accept aliases, and
do not ask the human to author paths or globs.
```

This message is identical for "heading missing", "invalid path", and the silent failures observed in Tasks B and C.

title: Provider review.start transition unresolvable from headless/relay session (no consent envelope; native START rejects target)
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

Provider `review.start` transition (`--consent=relay`) is unresolvable from a headless/relay session: no consent envelope is surfaced, and native START rejects the provider target.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In a headless session (no eligible interactive host UI), hold an unreviewed candidate.
2. Call `gentle_review` with `{"operation":"inspect"}` (or `status`).
3. Observe `next_transition.execute`: `gentle-ai review start ... --contract=gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --target=sha256:57d30f... --consent=relay`.
4. No three-action host UI is available, and no `gentle-ai.review-integration.consent/v3` envelope with `consentBinding` is returned, so `answer-consent` has nothing to consume.
5. Calling `gentle_review(start)` fails: missing input → requires input → requires idempotencyKey → `native-operation-failed / candidate-view-invalid` (native START only accepts `{mode, projection, policyHash, evidenceHash, budget}`).

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: either surface the consent envelope so the agent can relay the two provider choices to the human (then `answer-consent` once), or return a typed outcome such as "provider start not executable in this session" instead of an unexecutable transition.

Actual: unexecutable transition plus failed start attempts. Fails closed (no lineage created, no mutation) — safe direction, poor diagnosability.

Evidence: `extensions/gentle-ai.ts:8878` (only the interactive host third UI action runs the provider grant; extension never runs START itself); `:5176` (native START supports only ordinary/judgment-day); `:6357` (candidate view rejected before native START); fails closed headless ("requires fresh explicit authorization through the interactive Pi UI; headless execution fails closed").

### gentle-pi version

3.1.1

### Pi version

0.85.1

### Operating system

Linux

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```json
{"operation":"start","status":"blocked","outcome":"native-operation-failed","lineage_created":false,"mutation_performed":false,"mutation_outcome":"none","reset_eligible":false,"diagnostics":{"code":"candidate-view-invalid","message":"candidate view rejected before native START"},"next_action":"resolve-native-operation-failure"}
```

title: bug(subagents): sdd-init stalls with zero turns on phase-shaped prompts while trivial prompts complete (controlled A/B, servable model)
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

A `sdd-init` subagent launch stalls for the full stall timeout with `0 turns`, `0 tool calls` and `0 tokens` — but **only when the prompt asks for real SDD phase work**. The same agent, same model, same session and same workspace completes normally when given a trivial prompt. No error, no partial output, and no session file is ever produced, so the caller cannot distinguish "child never started" from "child started and produced nothing".

This is a different cause class from the two reports I found, and I think it supplies the two things they lacked:

- #1005 (`sdd-apply` stalls with zero activity) was closed with "Root cause and deterministic reproducibility are not established". This report is a deterministic, controlled reproduction.
- #1068 (unservable pinned model to zero-turn stall) states in its own honesty paragraph: "the correlation is across **different** phase prompts, not a controlled A/B of one prompt across models". This is that controlled A/B, and the model here is provably servable — it completed four other launches in the same session, including `sdd-init` itself.

The distinguishing factor is the prompt's **content class**, not its size, and not model availability.

### Steps to reproduce

Environment: gentle-pi 2.6.0, Pi 0.85.1, Linux, one authenticated OpenAI-compatible provider. Stall watchdog at its 4-minute default.

Controlled matrix, all launches in one Pi session, same workspace, same provider, same model, same stall limit:

| agent | prompt | size | turns | tokens | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gentle-ai-explore` | `Reply with exactly the word OK and nothing else.` | 96 chars | 1 | 15505 | completed |
| `gentle-ai-explore` | same instruction behind ~5.3 KB of inert padding | ~5.3 KB | 1 | 17570 | completed |
| `sdd-status` | `Reply with exactly the word OK and nothing else.` | 96 chars | 1 | 12581 | completed |
| `sdd-init` | `Reply with exactly the word OK and nothing else.` | 96 chars | 1 | 13523 | completed |
| `sdd-init` | `Run the sdd-init phase for the project <project>. Report status only - do not read files, do not run commands, do not save anything.` | ~150 chars | 0 | 0 | timed_out |
| `sdd-init` | full phase prompt (skill paths, preflight, deliverables) | 5425 chars | 0 | 0 | timed_out (x3) |

Two hypotheses this rules out:

1. **Prompt size is not the trigger.** ~5.3 KB of inert padding completed on another agent (+2065 tokens), while a ~150-char phase-shaped prompt stalls on `sdd-init`.
2. **Model availability is not the trigger.** Every failing launch records `model = deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` — the same model that completed the trivial `sdd-init` run.

Minimal deterministic reproduction, two launches:

```text
# 1. completes in seconds
subagent_run(agent: "sdd-init", mode: "background",
  task: "Reply with exactly the word OK and nothing else.")

# 2. stalls for the full stall timeout, 0 turns / 0 tokens
subagent_run(agent: "sdd-init", mode: "background",
  task: "Run the sdd-init phase for the project <project>.")
```

Inspect the failing task record — the model resolved fine:

```bash
python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('<agent-home>/gentle-agents/tasks/<id>.json'))['task'];print(d['model'],d['thinking'],d['turns'],d['tokens'],d['status'])"
# -> deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash high 0 0 timed_out
```

The prompt class that triggers it is the one that asks for phase work. The agent's instructions require consuming a `## SDD Session Preflight` block from parent-provided context, and `sdd-init` is not a member of the native phase enum (`apply|verify|sync|archive|remediate`), so no native attempt binding is ever supplied. The child appears to block on that path, which would also explain why the watchdog sees no traffic.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: either the phase runs, or the launch fails with an actionable diagnostic naming the last completed startup stage (model resolution, child spawn, RPC handshake, first provider response). A prompt-content difference must not silently turn "completes in seconds" into "produces nothing for four minutes".

Actual: `timed_out: stalled for 4 min`, `0 turns`, `0 tool calls`, `0 tokens`. The session JSONL reported by `get_state` is never created on disk, while the runner's sessions directory does receive one for the trivial launcher in the same session. The returned diagnostic is identical to the generic inactivity timeout, so it cannot be told apart from an unservable model, a dead child, or a transport failure.

Workaround in use: run the phase inline, or send a trivial non-phase prompt (which proves the agent definition itself is healthy).

### gentle-pi version

2.6.0

### Pi version

0.85.1

### Operating system

Linux

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
subagent_run: Subagent sdd-init timed_out: stalled for 4 min
subagent_status: sdd-init . timed_out . background . 0 turns . 0 tool calls . last: stalled for 4 min
task record: model=deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash thinking=high turns=0 toolCalls=0 tokens=0 cost=0
sessionPath from get_state = <agent-home>/gentle-agents/sessions/<ts>_<uuid>.jsonl   (file never created)
```

Runner evidence for the stall semantics (`lib/agents-runner.ts`): `receive()` re-arms the watchdog on every child message, so an entire stall interval with zero messages means the child emitted nothing at all after the prompt was accepted.

One adjacent friction worth noting: `subagents.json` is read at extension startup, not live, so creating or editing `stall_timeout_ms` mid-session has no effect until Pi restarts — the emitted message kept reporting the 4-minute default. That made this harder to characterise.

### Not the problem reported here

This version's `sdd-init` definition also pins `model: openai-codex/gpt-5.3-codex`. That separate defect is already tracked as #216. With the pin removed the agent still stalls on phase-shaped prompts, which is why this is filed separately.

title: Native review selection fails schema decoding with a registered dev binary
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

Native ordinary review can inspect a valid workspace candidate and request intended-untracked selection, but the exact selection continuation fails as `schema-incompatible` before creating a lineage. The read-only assessment path also fails to decode the native result and reports `native command returned empty output`.

This prevents receipt-driven review from producing a native receipt even though the candidate is otherwise valid. The fallback path correctly fails closed and permits independent verification, but the diagnostic does not identify the actual contract/version mismatch or a supported recovery.

The session used a registered development binary. The package is pinned to Gentle AI 2.7.0, while the registered binary reports `gentle-ai dev-main-01e6fac15df1`. If that combination is unsupported, gentle-pi should reject it before review execution with a precise `version-incompatible` or capability diagnostic rather than reaching `schema-incompatible`/empty output.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run gentle-pi 2.5.0 with Pi 0.85.1 on Linux and register the development binary listed below.
2. Prepare a workspace candidate containing tracked changes and intended untracked source/test files.
3. Call review `inspect` for the workspace.
4. Confirm that inspect returns `intended_untracked_selection_required`, a selection binding, and the eligible untracked paths.
5. Submit the exact selection binding with the exact eligible paths through `select-intended-untracked`.
6. Observe that the native operation fails before lineage creation.
7. Run the read-only review assessment for the same candidate.
8. Observe that assessment is unavailable because the native command returned empty output.

The failure reproduced on more than one valid candidate.

### Expected and actual behavior

**Expected:**

- The exact intended-untracked continuation should freeze the selected candidate and proceed to review consent/start; or
- an incompatible registered binary should be rejected before mutation with an actionable, typed version/capability error.
- Read-only assessment should return its documented assessment schema.

**Actual:**

The selection continuation returns:

```text
status: blocked
outcome: native-operation-failed
lineage_created: false
mutation_performed: false
diagnostics.operation: review/start
diagnostics.error_code: schema-incompatible
next_action: resolve-native-operation-failure
```

Assessment returns:

```text
risk: unassessable
reason: native-assess-unavailable
native review assess failed: native command returned empty output
```

No lineage or native receipt is created.

### gentle-pi version

2.5.0 (`6e4478c04615`); package Gentle AI pin: 2.7.0; registered development binary: `gentle-ai dev-main-01e6fac15df1`.

### Pi version

0.85.1

### Operating system

Linux

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
select-intended-untracked:
  native-operation-failed
  operation=review/start
  error_code=schema-incompatible
  lineage_created=false

assess:
  native-assess-unavailable
  native command returned empty output
```

title: feat(sdd): add a documented way to remove gentle-pi-owned SDD assets
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

gentle-pi owns a set of global SDD assets and documents how to install or refresh them, but documents no way to remove them:

- `/gentle:install-sdd` — "Installs missing global SDD agents, chains, and support only, without overwriting files" (`docs/readme-reference.md`).
- `/gentle:install-sdd --force` — "Refreshes only managed global SDD assets, preserving user edits and project overrides."

There is no `/gentle:uninstall-sdd`, no removal flag, and no removal section in the docs. The `sdd`-owner assets are registered in `~/.pi/agent/gentle-ai/managed-assets.json` and mapped in `ASSET_OWNER_BY_KEY` (`lib/sdd-preflight.ts`):

- `agents/sdd-*.md` (14 files)
- `chains/sdd-*.chain.md` (3 files)
- `gentle-ai/support/{sdd-status-contract,strict-tdd,strict-tdd-verify}.md` (3 files)

`installPackageAssets`/`installSddAssets` only create and refresh; the only removal-like logic, `RETIRED_MANAGED_ASSETS`, targets retired assets rather than the live `sdd` owner set. `extensions/gentle-ai.ts` registers `gentle:install-${owner}` and nothing for the inverse operation.

The consequence is that a user who wants ODD and/or RDD without SDD has to hand-delete files under `~/.pi/agent/`, which is exactly the fragile territory described in #608: deleting files decouples them from the managed-assets manifest, while the install path treats drifted or unknown content as user edits forever.

The removal story is also split across two owners, and only one half is documented:

- Native `gentle-ai` owns the `sdd-*` SKILL.md files under `~/.agents/skills/` and does document removal: `gentle-ai uninstall --agent pi --component sdd`.
- gentle-pi owns the Pi-side agents, chains, and support files listed above, and documents only the install direction.

So `gentle-ai uninstall --component sdd` leaves the gentle-pi-owned half untouched, and nothing in gentle-pi tells the user how to remove it.

Who benefits: users configuring an RDD-only or ODD-only harness (see #965), and anyone who tried SDD and wants to back it out cleanly instead of uninstalling the whole package.

### Proposed outcome

Add a supported, documented removal path for gentle-pi-owned SDD assets that mirrors the existing install command:

- `/gentle:uninstall-sdd` (or an explicit removal flag on the existing command) that removes exactly the manifest-owned `sdd`-owner assets, updates `managed-assets.json` accordingly, and reports — without silently rewriting — any drifted or user-modified copies it declined to remove.
- Document the command and its scope in `docs/readme-reference.md`, including the ownership boundary: this removes Pi-side `agents/sdd-*.md`, `chains/sdd-*.chain.md`, and `gentle-ai/support/*`, and is separate from the native `gentle-ai uninstall --agent pi --component sdd` that removes the `sdd-*` SKILL.md files under `~/.agents/skills/`.
- State what "removed" means for re-entry: after removal, `/gentle:status` should report the SDD assets as absent rather than as drift, `/gentle:install-sdd` should reinstall cleanly, and ODD/RDD must keep working unchanged.

Acceptance criteria:

- No `sdd`-owner file listed above remains under `~/.pi/agent/agents`, `~/.pi/agent/chains`, or `~/.pi/agent/gentle-ai/support`.
- `managed-assets.json` no longer carries the removed `sdd` entries and carries no dangling ones.
- Drifted or user-edited files are preserved and reported, never overwritten or silently deleted.
- Reinstalling with `/gentle:install-sdd` restores a healthy state and `/gentle:status` reports no drift.

### Alternatives considered

- **Document hand deletion as the recovery**, the route #608 currently names. This is the fragile path the manifest exists to avoid: it couples file and manifest by hand and leaves no drift signal if it goes wrong.
- **Uninstall the entire package.** Removes review and RDD assets too, which the SDD-only user still wants.
- **Point users only at the native `gentle-ai uninstall --component sdd`.** Correct for the skills, but it does not touch the gentle-pi-owned agents, chains, or support files, so it cannot be the whole answer.
- **A full SDD on/off switch (#965).** Complementary but larger in scope. An explicit removal command is the smaller, orthogonal piece and does not depend on that design landing first.

### Additional context

Related issues:

- #965 — make SDD user-owned and support an RDD-only Gentle Pi configuration (broader; asks for an SDD switch).
- #608 — orphaned global SDD agents never refresh and are invisible to drift; manual deletion is named as the only recovery.
- #1042 — native selected-only skill resolution and loading.

Repository evidence:

- `lib/sdd-preflight.ts` — `ASSET_OWNER_BY_KEY` maps `agents/sdd-*.md`, `chains/sdd-*.chain.md`, and `gentle-ai/support/*` to owner `sdd`; `installPackageAssets` / `installSddAssets` expose only install/refresh; `RETIRED_MANAGED_ASSETS` covers retired keys only.
- `extensions/gentle-ai.ts` — registers `gentle:install-${owner}` via `pi.registerCommand`, with no removal counterpart.
- `docs/readme-reference.md` — documents `/gentle:install-sdd` and `/gentle:install-sdd --force` only.

title: feat(startup): allow disabling the runtime info panel (stats table) entirely
body:
## Problem

The startup banner currently shows a runtime info panel (GIT, PATH, MCP, PLUGINS, AGENTS, SKILLS, EXTENSIONS, VER, TOOLS) **unconditionally** when the banner renders in full/minimal mode. Even when both the rose and text logo are disabled via config, the stats table still appears.

Users who want to keep the banner (logo + rose) but hide the stats table have no option today.

## Expected behavior

Add a `showStats` option to the banner config that, when `false`:
- Shows the banner (logo and/or rose per existing config)
- Hides only the stats table

And add a command `gentle:toggle-stats` to toggle the stats panel on/off.

## Proposed config

```json
// ~/.pi/gentle-ai/banner.json
{
  "showRose": true,
  "showTextLogo": true,
  "showStats": false,
  "color": "pink"
}
```

## Proposed commands

- `gentle:toggle-stats` — toggle `showStats` on/off (persists)
- Keep existing: `gentle:toggle-rose`, `gentle:toggle-text-logo`, `gentle:banner-color`, `gentle:banner`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New `showStats: false` config option hides the stats table while preserving logo/rose rendering
- [ ] `gentle:toggle-stats` flips `showStats` and persists to config
- [ ] Existing behavior unchanged when `showStats: true` (default)
- [ ] Tests cover config loading and command behavior
- [ ] README documents the new option and command

## Local validation

Implemented and tested locally as a patch to `extensions/startup-banner.ts`:
- Added `showStats` to `BannerConfig` interface and `DEFAULT_BANNER_CONFIG`
- Updated `normalizeBannerConfig` to read the new field
- Wrapped the stats table render block with `if (bannerConfig.showStats && ...)`
- Added `registerToggleCommand("gentle:toggle-stats", "showStats", "stats panel")`

Works as expected: banner (logo + rose) displays, stats table is hidden.

title: feat(profiles): two concurrent sessions in the same clone cannot hold different profiles — session-bound selection required
body:
### Before submitting

- [ ] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature. — **Not applicable as written: a related request exists and I declare the relationship explicitly under "Additional context" below rather than claiming novelty.**
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Two concurrent Pi sessions **in the same clone** cannot use different gentle profiles. Changing the active profile in one session rewrites the routing that the other session's later subagent launches will use, so parallel work has to be serialized: finish the work in session A, and only then switch profiles for session B.

The chain is reproducible and specific:

1. The profile store is global and carries a single active marker.
2. Applying a profile writes the routing authority (`<config home>/models.json`) and then materializes routing.
3. Materialization targets Pi's agent home (`<agent home>/subagents.json` plus the agent frontmatter), which is a second, different home from the config home.
4. Subagent launches re-resolve routing on every launch from the materialized stores, with no session-lifetime cache, so the other running session adopts the change mid-work — with the documented one-launch reconciliation lag.
5. Review lens captures read the routing authority directly at capture time, so lens routing moves at the next capture.

The result: a second session's delegated agents silently change model, with no way for that session to hold its own choice. This is a per-session configuration boundary, not a host-specific concern.

### Proposed outcome

An explicit, opt-in active-profile binding at the parent Pi session boundary, leaving today's global mechanism intact as the default. The invariants that matter for this report:

- Concurrent parent sessions in the **same clone** can select different profiles without rewriting each other's routing.
- A profile switch inside one session affects only that session's binding; running and already-queued children keep the routing resolved at launch.
- New child launches inherit the parent session's current binding.
- The binding survives session resume.
- The effective profile, its scope, and its configuration source are visible in the UI.
- Sessions without a binding behave exactly as today, and existing profile files need no migration.
- **The review lens read path is covered too**, not only subagent launches: lens routing is read from the routing authority at capture time, so a session binding must govern that read as well.

### Alternatives considered

Both existing mechanisms were audited against those invariants. Neither satisfies them.

**Per-repository pin.** This does solve parallel *repositories*, which is what the docs advertise it for. It does not solve parallel sessions:

- The pin is a **per-clone** artifact with a **single value**, so two sessions in the same clone cannot hold different pins — the second selection overwrites the first.
- It only governs **subagent launches**; the review lens capture path reads the routing authority directly and is unaffected by the pin.
- It also does not isolate the global active marker or the materialized stores, so anything reading those still sees the shared state.

**`GENTLE_PI_CONFIG_HOME`.** This relocates the profile store and the routing authority, but not the materialization target, because the two homes are resolved independently:

- config home = `GENTLE_PI_CONFIG_HOME` (profiles, routing authority, persona, guardrails, background policy, dev binary)
- agent home = `GENTLE_PI_AGENT_HOME` / `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` (materialized `subagents.json` and agent frontmatter)

Relocating both would isolate the **entire** Pi agent home — agents, skills, authentication, and session history — which is a parallel installation rather than profile selection, and it is not discoverable as a profile feature. So even the most aggressive existing workaround leaves the invariant unmet.

### Additional context

**Relationship to an existing request.** #1064 requests session-bound active profiles without global routing mutation and states the same central invariant. This report is not presented as independent novelty: it exists to supply what that request does not contain — a user-visible reproduction with the exact read and write paths, an audit showing that the two mechanisms currently offered do **not** meet the invariant (per-clone pin; config home without the agent home), and the same-clone concurrent-session case. Maintainers may prefer to fold this in as supporting evidence for #1064, and closing it as a duplicate is an acceptable outcome if that is the call.

**Feasibility signal.** Session-scoped machinery already ships in this codebase: the review-integration consent grants are bound to a live SessionManager, a non-empty session id, and the canonical Git common-directory identity, and the profile pin module already imports the session worktree registry. A session-bound profile binding is therefore consistent with the existing architecture rather than a new concept.

**Environment.** gentle-pi 3.3.0 (Pi client, macOS arm64), review contract v2, repository without a `.pi/` directory, so only the global stores apply.

**Note on the first checkbox.** It cannot be answered affirmatively here: the search did find the related request above. It is reported rather than silently skipped.

title: feat(review): surface per-lens prompt size + active relay bound before capture; survivable route for unachievable lens slots
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Reviewing one mid-size candidate (15 files, 2,917 changed lines, tier `high`, 4 lenses) consumed ~60% of a provider quota in a single review run, most of it wasted:

- Each lens materializes its own full-diff prompt (~150,800 bytes each, i.e. the diff is effectively sent 4 times).
- The capture forecast showed only `model_runs: 1` per slot. It did not surface the materialized prompt size, the timeout bound that would apply, or its source (derived vs. `GENTLE_PI_REVIEW_RELAY_PI_TIMEOUT_MS` override). The session had a 3600000 ms override from earlier debugging, silently replacing the derived bound (~1.03M ms for this prompt size) with a full hour.
- The one lens routed to a slower provider model never finished. It was killed at the 1h override bound with zero output. By design relaunching the identical slot reaches the same wall, so the only paths are raising the override toward the 2h ceiling (re-spending quota for the same wall) or abandoning the lineage and re-reviewing smaller candidates, which re-spends the already-admitted lens.
- The provider stop left the review with one lens admitted and three uncollected; there is no skip-lens / partial-approve route to salvage the admitted evidence.

### Proposed outcome

1. Capture forecast surfaces, per slot: materialized prompt bytes, the active relay bound (and whether it is derived or overridden, naming the env value), and the resolved reviewer model/effort. Cost stops being discovered after the spend.
2. START warns when candidate size implies expensive lens prompts (e.g. materialized prompt per lens above a threshold) and recommends per-work-unit-commit candidates.
3. A survivable route for unachievable slots: skip-lens with an explicit recorded downgrade, or partial approval that keeps admitted lens evidence, instead of stop + full re-review.
4. The timeout message states the bound source (derived formula vs. env override), so operators can tell "your override made this expensive" from "the derived bound was too tight".

### Alternatives considered

- Unsetting `GENTLE_PI_REVIEW_RELAY_PI_TIMEOUT_MS` to restore the derived bound: correct for future runs (fail-fast at ~17 min for this prompt class instead of 60 min), and we will do it, but it does not recover the spent quota nor fix the missing visibility.
- Rerouting the slow lens's profile to the faster provider (user-owned `review-<lens>` routing): works, but is invisible until a lens already failed, for the same reason as (1).
- Reviewing per work-unit commit (the documented candidate discipline): what we will adopt going forward; still leaves the oversized-candidate failure mode unguarded for the next user.

### Additional context

- One review run, 4 lenses, tier `high`: risk lens (fast provider) prompt 150,815 B / result 3,234 B, completed; resilience lens (slow provider) prompt 150,829 B, killed at 3,600,003 ms against a 3,600,000 ms override; derived bound for that size would have been ~1,029,437 ms.
- The overridden bound came from an exported env var left over from earlier relay debugging; nothing in the flow exposed that the derived bound had been replaced, so the failure looked like "the tool runs reviews for an hour" rather than "my override did this".
- Related: #1077 (usage exhaustion discovered only after START freezes the candidate), #573 (~40 min per lens round on large corpora), #1187 (derived-bound margin).
- gentle-pi 3.3.0, gentle-ai 3.4.0, Pi 0.85.1.
