n/a (content contradiction between two shipped texts; no runtime log involved)

title: feat(skills): single-source the skills shipped by both gentle-ai and gentle-pi
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

`skills/` in gentle-pi vendors copies of skills that also ship from `internal/assets/skills/` in gentle-ai. Both distributions reach the same Pi session (npm package skills plus installer-placed skills), and the copies have drifted apart while their `metadata.version` fields stayed equal:

- `judgment-day`: 123 diff lines and opposite lifecycle semantics. The gentle-ai copy still says "It replaces ordinary 4R as the adversarial method for that target; never run both"; the gentle-pi copy says "Judgment Day is independent: it neither enables nor replaces ordinary review". Both copies have overlapping triggers, so a single judgment-day request can load two contradictory contracts.
- `work-unit-commits`: bidirectional drift. The gentle-pi copy adds the "Budget is not code-golf" decision row and the bounded one-pass slicing rule; the gentle-ai copy adds the evidence checklist (focused test command, runtime harness, rollback boundary) and the generated-goldens counting rule. Neither side is a superset.
- `issue-creation`: 202 diff lines. `skill-creator`: 135. `go-testing`: 52. `systemic-issue-triage`: 53. `comment-writer` and `rdd-defect-workflow`: smaller but real semantic differences.
- Inside gentle-ai itself, `skills/` duplicates `internal/assets/skills/` (for example `branch-pr` diverges by 424 lines between the two in-repo locations).

There is no sync mechanism, checksum pinning, or CI parity check anywhere in the chain, and the same drift class has already produced gentle-ai#4520 and gentle-ai#4104.

### Proposed outcome

- Declare `internal/assets/skills/` in gentle-ai the single canonical source for shared skills.
- Either generate the vendored copies in gentle-pi from that source, or pin them with content hashes and add a CI check that fails when the copies drift.
- Version bumps for shared skills happen once, at the source, and propagate mechanically.
- Document the vendor contract: which skills are shared and who owns edits.

This generalizes the byte-identical mirror plus integrity-test pattern accepted in gentle-ai#1863 across the repository boundary.

### Alternatives considered

- Move all shared skills into one repository only: bigger migration, breaks per-repo packaging.
- Split ownership per skill with explicit lists: still needs a drift check to be enforceable.

### Additional context

- #365 fixed the name collisions by prefixing, but content drift between the distributions remained.
- A companion issue in gentle-ai proposes installed-copy verification so end users can detect stale local copies of distributed skills.

title: bug(review): reviewer relay child emits zero bytes deterministically — native review uncompletable across independent sessions
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

The reviewer host relay repeatedly launches child reviewer processes that produce **zero output bytes** and die, deterministically, across independent sessions and worktrees of the same repository on the same day. Retrying with a fresh bound STATUS re-offering the exact slot reproduces the failure. The lineage is left open and unburned every time, so nothing is corrupted — but the review can never complete through the relay.

Observed during a single day of parallel feature work (4-7 concurrent writer sessions in linked git worktrees of one repository):

- **7+ distinct relay failures** across at least 4 different sessions (different candidates: a 3-file test change, a 14-file service change, a 16-file UI change, and a 23-page docs batch).
- Candidate size is NOT the trigger: it reproduced on a **14-file / +1124-line diff** (small) after also failing on 518-file freezes (the base-resolution issue tracked in #992).
- Symptom every time: the relay spawns the child reviewer (PI_MODEL set, relay contract env present), the child writes **0 bytes**, the relay reports a transport failure. `mutation_performed: false`, lineage `reviewing`, no capture admitted — recoverable but never completable by retry.
- One session hit the failure **5 times in a row** on the same candidate with fresh STATUS + exact bound slot re-offered each time.

Per the relay contract the writers behaved correctly (STATUS once after failure, relaunch only on exact slot re-offer, stop after repeated deterministic failure, never fabricate captures). The only workaround that unblocked delivery was the maintainer disabling receipt-driven development globally and switching to an external verifier subagent — which defeats the purpose of the relay.

Suspicion (from the writers' reports, not verified): the child process environment/flags — the child dies before writing anything, suggesting an env, flag, or provider-session inheritance problem in the relay spawn, not a model refusal (no bytes at all, not even an error payload).

Related but distinct: #863 (intermittent upstream refusal reported as terminal transport), #367 (600s timeout strands large candidates), #992 (base resolution freezes default-branch base).

### Reproduction

1. Repository with linked git worktrees; RDD enabled globally.
2. From a feature session whose candidate is committed and clean, run the native review START (ordinary mode; base resolves per #992 or correctly depending on context).
3. Accept the materialize reviewer forecast (single R3/reliability lens run).
4. The relay spawns the reviewer child; the child emits zero bytes; the capture fails with a transport error.
5. Fresh STATUS re-offers the same bound slot; relaunching repeats the identical failure deterministically.
6. Reproduced on multiple machines-sessions the same day with different candidates and different model traffic; persisted across hours.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: the relay child runs the reviewer model and emits a lens result (or a model/provider error payload the relay can classify).

Actual: the child emits zero bytes and the relay reports a transport failure; retrying the exact bound slot fails identically every time, making native review uncompletable for the session until RDD is disabled globally.

### gentle-pi version

2.6.2

### pi version

0.85.1

### Operating system

Linux

title: Queued orphan subagent task cannot be terminalized and blocks SDD lifecycle
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

A managed subagent task can remain queued after its runner is no longer active. The parent session cannot formally terminalize the retained task: cancel, continue, and reconciliation paths do not produce a terminal state. An SDD change that references the failed evidence revision then remains on `remediate`, while `verify` and `archive` stay blocked.

This leaves the user with no supported recovery path other than editing or deleting retained runtime state manually, which should not be required.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start an SDD flow that delegates a managed phase task.
2. Interrupt or lose the runner after the task record is retained but before the task reaches a terminal state.
3. Observe that task status remains `queued` while no runner is active.
4. Attempt the supported cancellation, continuation, and reconciliation operations.
5. Query the SDD change status and attempt `verify` or `archive`.

Observed sanitized state:

- task status: `queued`
- active runner: none
- cancel: does not terminalize the retained task
- continue: unavailable
- reconcile: does not recover the task
- SDD status: `remediate`
- verify/archive: blocked by the retained failed-evidence revision

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected:

A queued task with no active runner can be formally cancelled, reconciled, or recovered through a supported audited operation. The operation should produce a durable terminal state and allow the SDD lifecycle to continue without manual retained-state edits.

Actual:

The task remains queued indefinitely. Cancel, continue, and reconciliation do not terminalize it, and the retained failed evidence keeps the SDD change blocked on remediation.

### gentle-pi version

2.7.0

### Pi version

0.85.1

### Operating system

macOS

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
task status: queued
active runner: none
cancel: no terminal transition
continue: unavailable
reconcile: recovery unsuccessful
sdd next action: remediate
verify/archive: blocked by retained failed evidence
```

title: feat(shell): make status telemetry configurable
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Gentle Shell provides a native status bar and a richer fullscreen Status sidebar, but the telemetry shown in the compact bar is currently fixed.

`pi-powerline-footer` demonstrates the value of configuring status information through Pi's `settings.json`: users can adapt the information they see to their workflow, including its order and relevant display preferences.

The opportunity is to make the same categories of session information available through Gentle Shell's native status experience, including the fullscreen Status sidebar, for users who prefer that integrated presentation.

### Proposed outcome

Provide a `settings.json` configuration surface for Gentle Shell status telemetry.

The configuration should allow users to select and arrange the available status fields, and provide display options appropriate to each field. It should make the following information available where applicable:

- model and reasoning level;
- path and Git branch;
- staged, unstaged, and untracked Git counts;
- session identity and elapsed time;
- local time;
- input, output, total, and cache token usage;
- context usage;
- cost, currency, and subscription display;
- extension statuses.

Gentle-specific information, including captured session changes and provider quota usage, should remain available and clearly distinct from Git working-tree state.

Existing users should retain the current default status experience unless they enable additional configuration.

### Alternatives considered

Continue using `pi-powerline-footer` alongside Gentle Shell.

This remains a valid and capable option. Pi renders one footer at a time, while Gentle Shell also provides a native fullscreen Status sidebar. Configurable status telemetry in Gentle Shell would let users who prefer that interface keep their relevant session information within the same presentation.

`pi-powerline-footer` is useful reference material for the requested user-facing configuration:

https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-powerline-footer

This request focuses on status information rather than Powerline's separate shell and queue workflows.

### Additional context

`pi-powerline-footer` exposes configurable layouts, segment selection, separators, placement, and per-segment display options through Pi's `settings.json`.

Its `full` preset includes model, thinking level, path, Git state, token usage, cache usage, cost, context usage, elapsed time, clock, and extension statuses. Its `nerd` preset additionally includes session identity, cache-write usage, context totals, and presentation differences.

title: bug(review): a live candidate view inside .git is read as source by repository scans and produces phantom findings
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

A candidate view is a **full copy of the working tree** materialized at `<git-common-dir>/gentle-ai/candidate-views/<uuid>/`. Being inside `.git` hides it from most tooling, but not from any repository tool that globs with dot-directories enabled — and such a tool then reads the copy as first-class source.

In my repository this broke an architecture test that enforces a security invariant. The scan globs `**/*.ts` with `dot: true` (so that generated hidden directories can be excluded by name rather than by being hidden) and excludes `node_modules`, `build`, `tests`, and two generated dot-directories — but not `.git`, because nothing is supposed to live there. With one open review lineage, the scan read:

```
.git/gentle-ai/candidate-views/<uuid>/app/.../probe_page_controller.ts
.git/gentle-ai/candidate-views/<uuid>/tests/bootstrap.ts
...
```

and reported the copied, correctly gated controller as a **second, ungated route registration**. The whole architecture suite failed, and the reported location was a path no deployment ships.

Two properties make this worse than an ordinary false positive:

- **It is invisible in review.** The failure appears while a review is open and disappears when the view is swept, so it reads as a flaky or unrelated regression. I only established the cause by stashing my own changes and watching the suite fail identically on a clean tree.
- **`.gitignore` cannot help.** The path is inside `.git`, so the usual repository-level exclusion mechanism does not apply. Every affected project has to learn this and hard-code an exclusion.

This is not #343 (leaked views never swept, closed) nor #826/#707/#596 (candidate-view permissions). Those are about views that are stale or unusable. This one happens with a perfectly healthy, live, correctly created view.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In a repository, add a scan that globs the tree including dot-directories. Minimal shape:

   ```ts
   import fg from "fast-glob";
   const files = await fg(["**/*.ts"], { cwd: repoRoot, dot: true, onlyFiles: true,
     ignore: ["node_modules/**", "build/**"] });
   ```

2. Start any RDD review in that repository so a candidate view is materialized under `<git-common-dir>/gentle-ai/candidate-views/<uuid>/`.
3. Run the scan.
4. Observe that every source file appears twice: once at its real path and once under the candidate view.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: a materialized candidate view is not discoverable as source by repository tooling operating on the working tree. Either materialize it outside the repository (for example under the user-level gentle-ai cache), or document the requirement prominently enough that projects exclude it before a review surfaces it as a phantom finding.

Actual: the view sits inside the repository's own `.git`, is a byte-for-byte copy of the tree, and any dot-inclusive scan treats it as source. A correctly gated file is reported as an ungated duplicate of itself, at a path that does not exist in any deployment.

My local fix was to add `.git/**` to that one scan's exclusion list, which is fine for one project but is a rule every consumer has to rediscover the hard way.

### gentle-pi version

2.7.0

### Pi version

0.85.1

### Operating system

macOS

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
AssertionError: A /probe path outside `if (probePageIsExposed(app.inProduction))`
exists in production.

  .git/gentle-ai/candidate-views/<uuid>/app/<redacted>/probe_page_controller.ts:300
  .git/gentle-ai/candidate-views/<uuid>/tests/bootstrap.ts:104
  .git/gentle-ai/candidate-views/<uuid>/tests/bootstrap.ts:114
  .git/gentle-ai/candidate-views/<uuid>/tests/functional/probe_page.spec.ts:28

Control: the same suite fails identically with all local changes stashed,
and passes once `.git/**` is excluded from the scan.
```

title: bug(review): provider usage exhaustion is discovered only after START freezes the candidate and the human authorizes the forecast
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

When the provider account cannot serve the reviewer runs, the RDD lifecycle only finds out **after** it has already frozen a lineage and **after** the human has authorized the cost.

The order observed twice today on the same machine:

1. `gentle_review {"operation":"inspect"}` → `action: start`.
2. `START` → lineage created, `state: reviewing`, risk tier and lenses frozen.
3. `STATUS` → `action: collect` with the materialize bindings.
4. `gentle_review_capture_group` → `outcome: reviewer-model-run-forecast`, `model_runs: 4`. I relayed that forecast and the human authorized it.
5. Re-submitted with `reviewerRunAcknowledged: true` → `outcome: pi-host-relay-transport-failure`, `kind: pi-failed`, `exit_code: 1`, **`elapsed_ms: 847`**.

The child never got past the first request. The cost the human approved was never spendable, and the approval was collected for work that could not start.

Two consequences:

- **Two lineages are left open** (`reviewing`, zero reviewers captured, no authority burned). They are recoverable, but every future candidate in that clone now sits behind stale open authority that the user has to reason about.
- **The failure class is wrong for the cause.** `pi-host-relay-transport-failure` reads as "the transport broke". An account that cannot serve any request is not a transport fault and is not fixed by re-querying STATUS and relaunching the same bound slot, which is what `next_action` instructs. #863 makes the same distinction for intermittent upstream refusals; this is the deterministic sibling of it.

### Steps to reproduce

Setup: `pi` authenticated against a provider account whose usage allowance is exhausted for programmatic runs. RDD enabled globally.

1. Produce any reviewable candidate in a repository.
2. `gentle_review {"operation":"inspect"}`, then `start`, then `status`.
3. Call `gentle_review_capture_group` with the complete collect set, acknowledge the forecast, and re-submit.
4. Observe the relay failure, and observe that the lineage remains in `reviewing`.

Minimal check that the relay path itself is the affected one, without any review state, using the adapter's own argv (`lib/opaque-pi-reviewer-adapter.ts`, `OPAQUE_PI_REVIEWER_ARGV`):

```
pi --print --mode text --no-session --no-tools --no-extensions --no-skills \
   --no-prompt-templates --no-themes --no-context-files --no-approve <<< "say ok"
```

If that returns the provider's refusal, every reviewer launch will fail identically — and it can be known before freezing anything.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: a cheap transport probe before `START` freezes a candidate, or at the latest before the forecast is presented for authorization, so the user is told "reviewers cannot run on this account right now" instead of being asked to approve four model runs that cannot happen. And when it does fail mid-lifecycle, a stop reason of its own with a continuation that matches the cause, rather than a generic transport failure whose documented continuation is to relaunch the same slot.

Actual: the lifecycle freezes the candidate, classifies risk, selects lenses, renders the forecast, collects human authorization, and only then discovers that no reviewer can run. The lineage stays open and the returned guidance points at a retry that cannot succeed while the cause persists.

### gentle-pi version

2.7.0

### Pi version

0.85.1

### Operating system

macOS

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
{"tool":"gentle_review_capture_group","status":"blocked",
 "outcome":"pi-host-relay-transport-failure","reason":"pi subprocess failed",
 "failure":{"kind":"pi-failed","stage":"pi","exit_code":1,"timed_out":false,
            "elapsed_ms":847,"timeout_ms":976956,
            "stderr":"400 {\"type\":\"error\",\"error\":{\"type\":\"invalid_request_error\",
                      \"message\":\"<provider usage-exhausted message>\"}}"},
 "prepared_reviewers":0,"submitted_reviewers":0,
 "host_relay":{"transport":"pi_host_relay","reviewers":[]},
 "mutation_performed":false,"mutation_outcome":"none",
 "next_action":"Call fresh STATUS and submit only an exact reoffered one-slot binding; ..."}

Frozen at that point: tier high, 4 lenses, 9 files, 1321 changed lines,
correction budget 200. Earlier failure the same day: tier medium, 1 lens,
2 files, 47 lines, elapsed_ms 619.
```

Observation offered as evidence, not as a diagnosis: while every spawned `pi --print ...` child was refused, the **interactive Pi session in the same terminal, on the same account and the same credentials file, kept working normally** — including calls to the same model. I could not explain that asymmetry and am not claiming a mechanism for it; I mention it only because it is what made the failure look like a gentle-pi defect rather than an account state, and because a preflight probe run through the relay's own argv would have distinguished the two immediately.

title: sdd-research cannot consume Markdown exploration artifacts generated by sdd-explore
body:
### Before submitting
- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem
On Windows, Gentle Pi 2.7.0's standard SDD exploration output cannot be consumed by its bounded research flow. The current `sdd-explore` contract persists `openspec/changes/<change>/exploration.md` as Markdown. The current `sdd-research` controller reads that same locator as complete JSON bytes, requires a positive `revision`, and rejects the artifact when JSON parsing fails. No supported migration or regeneration path was found; rerunning exploration writes Markdown again.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Use Gentle Pi 2.7.0 with Pi coding agent 0.85.1 on Windows in a normal Git worktree.
2. Run the supported SDD exploration flow for a change using the OpenSpec store.
3. Observe that it creates `openspec/changes/<change>/exploration.md` as Markdown, without a JSON envelope or revision.
4. Select the SDD research lane and provide the required bounded `explore` locator.
5. The research controller requires a digest-matching readback whose bytes parse as JSON and whose `revision` matches the locator. The Markdown exploration cannot satisfy that contract.

A separate Windows guard also requires `research_artifact.worktree` to equal both literal `cwd` and `realpath(cwd)`. Equivalent slash spelling can fail before the artifact readback, but canonical paths only expose the Markdown-versus-JSON incompatibility.

### Expected and actual behavior
Expected: artifacts emitted by `sdd-explore` should be accepted by `sdd-research`, or the runtime should provide a documented migration/compatibility path.

Actual: `sdd-explore` emits Markdown while the research readback requires versioned JSON. The research phase cannot safely start from a supported exploration artifact. The observed pre-launch error for a path-spelling mismatch is `Research artifact worktree/store scope mismatch.`

title: feat(profiles): support session-bound active profiles without global routing mutation
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Concurrent Pi processes may need different active profiles while sharing the same machine or project. Today, `/gentle:profiles` updates shared configuration and materialized routing by default. Running work remains unchanged, but later subagent launches can observe another process's profile changes.

This affects ordinary terminals, terminal multiplexers, IDE panes, CI, and other environments. It is a Pi process/session configuration boundary rather than a host-specific integration concern.

### Proposed outcome

Preserve the existing global profile mechanism and add an explicit, opt-in active-profile binding at the parent Pi session boundary.

The profile UI should distinguish actions conceptually equivalent to:

- **Use in this session** — resolve and store a session-local profile binding and effective routing snapshot without mutating shared routing files.
- **Reload in this session** — explicitly refresh that session's snapshot from the saved profile definition.
- **Set as global default** — retain the existing global persistence and materialization behavior for future or unbound sessions.

Session-bound behavior should satisfy these invariants:

- Concurrent parent sessions can select different profiles without rewriting each other's shared defaults or routing.
- Switching profiles within one parent session updates only that session's binding.
- New child launches inherit the parent's current effective snapshot.
- Running and already-queued children retain the routing resolved when they were launched or queued.
- Resuming a parent session restores its last session-bound profile and snapshot.
- Editing a saved profile definition does not silently alter an already-bound session; refreshing it requires an explicit reload or re-selection.
- Display the effective profile, scope, and configuration source.
- Existing behavior remains unchanged when no session binding is selected.
- Existing profile files require no migration.

A possible precedence model is:

```text
explicit launch-local route
→ parent session-bound profile snapshot
→ project routing
→ global active profile
→ existing defaults
```

The exact command names and persistence mechanism can follow the maintainers' preferred configuration authority. The central invariant is that session-scoped selection must not mutate routing observed by unrelated concurrent parent sessions.

Suggested regression coverage:

- two concurrent parent sessions using different profiles;
- concurrent sessions in the same project;
- switching one session while the other remains unchanged;
- queued and running child stability;
- future child inheritance after switching;
- session resume;
- explicit session reload after editing a saved profile;
- unchanged behavior for sessions without a binding;
- existing profile files loading without migration.

### Relationship to the existing per-repository pins

The per-repository pin shipped in #1074 solves a narrower configuration boundary:

- `p` writes a clone-local selection to `<git-common-dir>/gentle-ai/profile-pin.json`. It is isolated from other clones, but every worktree and every Pi session in that clone shares it.
- `P` writes a repository declaration to `<worktree-root>/.pi/gentle-ai/profile.json`. It is intended as a shared repository or team default, so it is also shared by concurrent sessions using that worktree.
- Both layers affect subagent routing at launch without rewriting the globally active routing. The clone-local `p` layer takes precedence over `P`, then routing falls back to the globally active profile.

Those pins solve parallel work across different repositories or clones. They do not allow two parent sessions in the same clone to select different profiles. If session A changes `p`, future child launches from session B observe the same clone-local selection. `P` is likewise a repository default, not a session override.

This request adds an independent layer above those defaults. A parent session should hold its own effective profile snapshot, children should inherit the snapshot of the parent that launched or queued them, and another session should remain unchanged. Because it is a snapshot rather than a shared profile-name lookup on every launch, later edits to the saved profile definition should require explicit reload or re-selection before affecting that bound session.

The resulting conceptual precedence is:

```text
explicit launch-local route
→ parent session-bound profile snapshot
→ clone-local pin (`p`)
→ repository declaration (`P`)
→ global active profile
→ existing defaults
```

The existing `p` and `P` behavior should remain unchanged. They become defaults for sessions that have no explicit session binding.

### Alternatives considered

Separate `GENTLE_PI_CONFIG_HOME` and `GENTLE_PI_AGENT_HOME` / `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` roots provide supported path isolation, but require external environment setup and duplicated configuration rather than a native session binding.

Project-local routing helps separate projects but does not solve concurrent sessions in the same project. Switching the shared active profile is not session isolation.

### Additional context

Related: #1025 proposes authorized routing classes selected for individual child launches. This request concerns a human-selected active profile bound to the parent Pi session and inherited as its default routing context. The two features can coexist if launch-local routes have explicit higher precedence.

Coordinate precedence with #600 and preserve the path-isolation support established by #575 and #633.

title: feat(shell): extension point for external sidebar parts (top/bottom placement)
body:
## Problem

The fullscreen sidebar rail renders a hardcoded section list (`footer`, `changes`, `agents`, `todo`) plus the branding banner. There is no supported way for an external extension (user-level or third-party) to contribute a rail section without forking gentle-shell — so personal UI like an identity portrait must live as commits inside this repo and disappears on every branch switch.

## Proposal

Generalize the rail layout with an explicit, minimal contract:

- `SidebarRail` gains optional `placement?: "top" | "bottom"`.
- Parts outside the built-in set render **before the branding banner** with `placement: "top" (identity art, portraits) and after the known sections otherwise, in registration order.
- Top-placed parts keep blank rows so animated parts (reveal frames that are blank at elapsed 0) hold stable geometry instead of flapping the rail.
- Only parts with `handleMouse` own a click region (read-only art never captures clicks).

External extensions reach the rail through the existing terminal-owned state (`Symbol.for("gentle-pi.experimental-sidebar.state")`) and invalidate through the existing cache symbol, so they need no imports from gentle-pi and degrade invisibly on older layouts that ignore unknown parts.

## Evidence

- Reference consumer: a user-level animated ASCII portrait extension living in `~/.pi/agent/extensions`, verified end-to-end against the real `installSidebar` (order portrait → branding → Status).
- Full suite passes: 2259 tests, plus 2 new layout tests covering placement order and click-region ownership.

title: bug(sdd): a change-name argument flips artifactStore from engram to openspec, blocking every named SDD phase in Engram-only repositories
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

In a repository whose artifact store is Engram (no `openspec/` directory), `sdd-status` and `sdd-continue` resolve the artifact store **differently depending on whether a change name is passed**. With no positional argument they correctly report `store: engram`. With a change name — any change name — they silently switch to `store: openspec` and point `planning_home` at an `openspec/` directory that does not exist.

The repository's own declared configuration is ignored on that path. `.pi/gentle-ai/sdd-preflight.json` contains `"artifactStore": "engram"`, which the no-argument invocation honors and the named invocation does not.

The consequence is that **no SDD phase that needs a change name can complete in an Engram-only repository**. Both routes dead-end:

- without a name, the change resolves to the bare project name and blocks on `tasks.md has no markdown task checkboxes` — expected for an Engram-mode planning snapshot, which apply never rewrites into checked boxes;
- with a name, it blocks on `Active OpenSpec change not found: <change>`.

There is no input that satisfies the engine without fabricating an `openspec/changes/` tree, and `sdd-status` accepts no flag to force the store.

This is worse for `sdd-continue`, because it does not merely report the wrong store — it injects the wrong instruction into the dispatched child's prompt: `"Artifact store: openspec; read the file at that path."` A phase executor launched this way is told to read a filesystem path that does not exist, for artifacts that live in Engram.

Observed impact: the `sdd-archive` executor for a completed, merged change was blocked twice and correctly refused to fabricate a report. The archive record had to be written by the orchestrator instead, from artifacts it read and verified directly. Three earlier archives in the same repository completed under the same Engram-only condition, so this is a regression rather than an unsupported configuration.

### Steps to reproduce

Setup: any repository with **no** `openspec/` directory and `.pi/gentle-ai/sdd-preflight.json` containing `"artifactStore": "engram"`.

```
cd <repo>
gentle-ai sdd-status                              # store: engram
gentle-ai sdd-status <any-change-name>            # store: openspec
```

The flip is caused by the positional argument alone. `--cwd` is not involved — the full 2x2 rules it out:

```
sdd-status --cwd .                       -> store: engram   planning_home: engram:sdd
sdd-status                               -> store: engram   planning_home: engram:sdd
sdd-status <change> --cwd .              -> store: openspec planning_home: <repo>/openspec
sdd-status <change>                      -> store: openspec planning_home: <repo>/openspec
```

It is not a lookup miss either: a name that exists as an Engram change and a name that exists nowhere both produce `store: openspec`. The store is chosen before the change is resolved.

```
gentle-ai sdd-status zzz-does-not-exist           # store: openspec
```

Same behavior on the dispatcher:

```
gentle-ai sdd-continue                            # "artifactStore": "engram"
gentle-ai sdd-continue <any-change-name>          # "artifactStore": "openspec"
```

No escape hatch exists:

```
gentle-ai sdd-status <change> --store engram      # Error: unknown sdd-status argument "--store"
gentle-ai sdd-status --help                       # Error: unknown sdd-status argument "--help"
```

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: the artifact store is a property of the repository, not of the invocation. Passing a change name narrows WHICH change is reported; it must not change WHERE artifacts are believed to live. With `"artifactStore": "engram"` declared in `.pi/gentle-ai/sdd-preflight.json` and no `openspec/` directory present, `gentle-ai sdd-status <change>` should report `store: engram` and resolve the change against the Engram store — and `sdd-continue` should inject the Engram instruction into the child.

Actual: the positional argument flips the store to `openspec` and sets `planning_home` to a nonexistent `<repo>/openspec`, so every phase requiring a change name reports `blocked`, and `sdd-continue` instructs the dispatched executor to read artifacts from the filesystem instead of Engram.

Secondary, and lower confidence: a flag to force the store would be a useful fallback, but the defect is the inconsistency, not the missing flag. Fixing the flag alone would leave the default path wrong.

### gentle-pi version

2.7.0 (npm package). The `gentle-ai` CLI binary that produces the output above reports 2.9.1. First observed on 2.4.0-rc.3 and still reproducing on 2.9.1.

### Pi version

0.85.1

### Operating system

macOS

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
$ gentle-ai sdd-status
## SDD Status: <project>
schema: gentle-ai.sdd-status@2
store: engram
planning_home: engram:sdd
next: resolve-blockers
### Blocked Reasons
- tasks.md has no markdown task checkboxes.

$ gentle-ai sdd-status <change>
## SDD Status: <change>
schema: gentle-ai.sdd-status@2
store: openspec
planning_home: <repo>/openspec
next: sdd-new
### Blocked Reasons
- Active OpenSpec change not found: <change>.

$ cat .pi/gentle-ai/sdd-preflight.json
{
  "executionMode": "auto",
  "artifactStore": "engram",
  "chainedPrStrategy": "auto-chain",
  "reviewBudgetLines": 800,
  "engramAvailable": true,
  "prompted": true
}
```

title: bug(sdd): failed verification does not select remediation
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

After an SDD verification fails with correctable critical findings, native status remains on `verify` instead of selecting `remediate`.

This prevents the SDD workflow from progressing: a source correction is needed, but the remediation phase is not authorized by native status.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run an SDD change through apply and independent verification.
2. Let verification fail with concrete, source-correctable findings.
3. Settle the verification attempt as `failed` with a fresh evidence revision.
4. Query native status:

   ```sh
   gentle-ai sdd-status --contract gentle-ai.sdd-status/v2
   ```

5. Observe that status returns:

   ```text
   nextRecommended: verify
   remediationState.required: false
   ```

6. Attempting remediation is refused because `remediate` was not selected; rerunning verification without source changes repeats the failure.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: a failed verification with correctable findings selects `remediate`, or returns an explicit supported transition that authorizes a bounded correction.

Actual: native status continues to select `verify` with a blocker stating that verification evidence is incomplete. The workflow cannot reach source remediation.

### gentle-pi version

2.7.0

### Pi version

0.85.1

### Operating system

Linux

```text
Verifier result:
- verdict: FAIL
- critical findings: 3
- recommended next action: remediate

Native status after the failed settlement:
- nextRecommended: verify
- remediationState.required: false
- blocked reason: failed verification evidence is incomplete; rerun SDD verification
```

### SDD configuration

- Native status schema: `gentle-ai.sdd-status@2`

title: bug(sdd): selected sync injects local v1 status despite native v2 readiness
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

A selected `sdd-sync` phase receives the Pi-local `gentle-pi.sdd-status` v1 projection even when a fresh native `gentle-ai.sdd-status` v2 projection reports the same OpenSpec change as fully applied, fully verified, and ready for archive.

A contract-following sync worker must stop because the injected projection disagrees with the native authority. This prevents a verified change from being synchronized and archived without bypassing the status contract.

The behavior is still present in the published v2.7.0 source: `resolveSelectedNativeSddChangeStartup()` explicitly routes `selection.phase === "sync"` through `localResolver(...)`, while other selected execution phases use `native.sddStatus(...)`.

Related issue #821 fixed native status authority for archive through #862, but #862 intentionally retained the local resolver branch for sync. Therefore this is not the already-fixed archive path.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use an OpenSpec change whose native v2 status reports all implementation tasks complete, apply and verify complete, archive ready, and no blockers.
2. Run `gentle-ai sdd-status --contract gentle-ai.sdd-status/v2` and retain that fresh projection.
3. Dispatch the selected change to the installed `sdd-sync` Pi agent.
4. Observe that the child prompt receives `gentle-pi.sdd-status` v1 from the local resolver instead of the fresh native v2 projection.
5. Observe that the sync worker stops without writes when the local projection reports sync/archive blocked.

The reproduction was bounded to one selected sync dispatch. The existing evidence and repository state were preserved; no retry loop or manual readiness reconstruction was used.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected:

Selected `sdd-sync` should receive the same authoritative native v2 status identity and readiness facts used by the parent gate, or the runtime should provide one explicit, documented reconciliation contract. The child must not receive a contradictory local authority projection.

Actual:

Selected sync is special-cased to inject Pi-local `gentle-pi.sdd-status` v1. The local projection can disagree with native v2 readiness and block sync/archive. Updating managed SDD Markdown assets cannot correct this because the branch is extension code.

### gentle-pi version

2.6.0 installed. The same sync-specific local resolver branch was verified in the published v2.7.0 tag.

### Pi version

0.85.1

### Operating system

Linux

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
parent native projection:
  schema: gentle-ai.sdd-status v2
  tasks: complete
  apply: all_done
  verify: all_done
  archive: ready
  blockers: none

selected sdd-sync child projection:
  schema: gentle-pi.sdd-status v1
  sync/archive: blocked

result:
  sync stopped before reading or writing artifacts
  repository state preserved
```

title: Persist failed managed-remediation tasks after uncertain acquire
body:
### Before submitting
- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem
When managed remediation acquisition returns an ambiguous outcome twice, the prepared task is marked `failed` only in the in-memory `TaskStore`. Its persisted record remains `queued` with `acquireUncertain: true`, even though no runner or actor exists.

The retained task cannot be cancelled because runner ownership is absent, cannot be continued because `queued` is non-terminal, and appears as a zombie task until its exact native mutation can be reconciled. Evidence task `mu2p98f7-32-zk2l` exhibited this state with zero turns and zero tool calls; its persisted record was not manually modified.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Prepare an `sdd-remediate` task.
2. Make `sddAttemptAcquire` throw an ambiguous error on both the initial attempt and the single exact retry.
3. Observe that no child process or remediation actor starts.
4. Reload the persisted task history.
5. Observe `status: queued` together with `sddRemediation.acquireUncertain: true` and no runner ownership.
6. Attempt cancellation or continuation; neither operation can make progress.
7. Reconcile the exact retained acquire request from its owning clone and observe that legacy queued records must remain safely terminalizable without actor replay.

### Expected and actual behavior
Expected:
- Before the admission error returns, the prepared task's local `failed` transition is persisted durably.
- Exact `acquireUncertain` history remains available for `subagent_reconcile`.
- No actor starts and no native authority is invented or discarded.
- Legacy persisted `queued + acquireUncertain` records can still reconcile to `failed/reconciled` without actor replay or token disclosure.

Actual:
- Only the in-memory task becomes `failed`.
- The durable record remains `queued` with no runner.
- Cancellation reports that the task is not running, continuation rejects the non-terminal status, and the task remains operationally stranded until reconciliation is performed in an eligible owning-clone session.

### gentle-pi version
2.6.4 from source at commit `7df2f2fb702124e50a79ecfbad6516024136c58f`

### Pi version
0.85.1

### Operating system
macOS

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)
```text
mu2p98f7-32-zk2l · sdd-remediate · queued · 0 turns · 0 tool calls · last: queued

subagent_cancel: task is not running
subagent_continue: task cannot be continued yet (queued)
```

Proposed invariant and regression coverage:
- Persist the prepared task after applying the `FAILED` transition in the admission/dispatch catch.
- Preserve the exact uncertain acquire payload.
- Cover ambiguous acquire with zero actor spawn.
- Cover terminal reconciliation of legacy queued records.
- Keep `actorClaimed`, token-consistency, settlement, and same-clone guards unchanged.

title: bug(provider): kimi-k3 tool calls fail with 400 'tool_call_id is not found' after compaction or parallel batches
body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report for this bug.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, session IDs, file paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

## Describe the bug

Selecting `kimi-coding/k3` (or `kimi-coding/k3-256k`) as the active model and triggering a turn that includes tool calls fails with:

```
Error: 400 {"error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"tool_call_id  is not found"},"type":"error"}
```

Note the empty value between the two spaces — `tool_call_id` is being serialized as an empty string. The error originates from the Kimi API (`api.kimi.com/coding`), not from pi.

The same session workflow with `kimi-coding/kimi-for-coding` (K2.7 Code) does not reproduce.

## Reproduction

1. Sign in to Kimi Code: `/login` → "Sign in with Kimi Code".
2. Switch model: `/model kimi-coding/k3`.
3. Run any prompt that triggers tool calls (e.g. read a file with `read`, then write with `write`).
4. The first tool round may succeed. After auto-compaction or a parallel batch, the next assistant turn that follows a tool result fails with the 400 above.
5. Switching to `/model kimi-coding/kimi-for-coding` in the same workflow succeeds.

## Suspected trigger

Two confirmed triggers from the upstream MoonshotAI report (kimi-code#1053, same symptom):

- Auto-compaction on long sessions.
- Parallel tool-call batches that Kimi API groups server-side.

Either path leaves the client with a `toolMsg.toolCallId` that the server does not recognize on the next turn.

## Root cause (best guess, no private data shared)

`pi-ai/dist/bundle/chunks/openai-completions-EKZT2IH2.js:7` serializes tool results without validating the id:

```js
toolResultMsg = { role: "tool", content: ..., tool_call_id: toolMsg.toolCallId };
```

When `toolMsg.toolCallId` is `undefined` or `""`, the payload that reaches Kimi contains `"tool_call_id": ""`, which the server rejects with 400.

## Cross-references

- MoonshotAI/kimi-code#1053 — same 400, session permanently bricked, triggered by compaction splitting a parallel tool-call batch.
- openai/codex#43515 — same 400 with Kimi provider on the Codex desktop client.

## Suggested fix (upstream, pi-ai)

Two non-mutually-exclusive options:

1. **Skip + warn** when the id is missing. Cheap, drops one tool result silently but keeps the session alive.
2. **Re-id locally**: assign a fresh `crypto.randomUUID()` to any tool result with an empty id, keep a `clientToolCallId → newId` map, and remap on subsequent turns. Heavier, but preserves the tool result semantics.

Either fix needs a small `pi-ai` change in the openai-completions chunk (and an analogous one for the Anthropic-Messages chunk if it serializes the same way). Out of reach for downstream packages like `gentle-pi` because pi-coding-agent does not expose a `before_provider_request` hook for extensions to rewrite the outgoing payload.

## Environment

- pi-coding-agent: 0.85.1
- pi: 0.85.1
- model: `kimi-coding/k3` (also reproduces on `kimi-coding/k3-256k`)
- working model: `kimi-coding/kimi-for-coding`
- subscription: Kimi Code (OAuth, device flow)

## Workaround for users today

Use `kimi-coding/kimi-for-coding` (K2.7 Code) instead of K3 for any session that drives tool calls. K3 is otherwise fine for chat-only or research tasks that do not trigger tool roundtrips.

## Contributor checklist

- [x] Linked an approved issue — N/A (this IS the issue)
- [x] Added exactly one `type:*` label requested — `type:bug`
- [x] All checks pass locally — N/A (no code changes)
- [x] Conventional commit format — N/A
- [x] No `Co-Authored-By` trailers
- [x] Sensitive data scrubbed — no session IDs, no tokens, no file paths

title: feat(sdd): coordinate classical workflow parity across Pi runtime and assets
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Gentle Pi users explicitly choosing SDD need the same practical workflow as Gentle AI. Pi owns shipped SDD instructions and runtime consumers; a provider update or prompt-only edit cannot deliver full parity.

At inspected Pi commit `51636dc32b0d2fc06ba9be364e43246127b2b1fa`, the default chain mandates verification and sync, sync separately computes local readiness, managed remediation acquires/settles attempts, and research requires proposal admission plus pre-existing artifact revisions/digests and durable session checkpoints. These are not substitutes for real user permissions.

The maintainer selected a new coordinating owner after the overlapping reports were explained. This issue coordinates the full behavior without rewriting those reports, claiming all their symptoms fixed, or authorizing their closure.

### Proposed outcome

#### User flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
 A[Explicitly select SDD] --> B[Explore and clarify product questions]
 B --> C{Research useful or requested?}
 C -->|Yes| D[Requested depth and authorized external sources]
 D --> E[Useful findings and honest limitations]
 E --> F[Proposal, specs, design and tasks]
 C -->|No| F
 F --> G[Authorized implementation with configured TDD]
 G --> H[Applicable functional checks and truthful progress]
 H --> I{Independent verification selected?}
 I -->|Yes| J[Verify and report observed results]
 I -->|No| K[Archive readiness]
 J --> K
 K --> L[Applicable spec sync and archive report]
 L --> M[Selected-store locators and recovery]
```

Real unresolved product decisions and absent edit grants still stop dependent work. Optional verification does not skip applicable implementation checks or hide actual failures. No post-SDD RDD phase is introduced.

#### Coherent implementation units

| Unit | Outcome and exact mapped consumers | Required regression surfaces |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Optional verify and archive | Permit completed apply to archive without a mandatory verify report, retaining explicit verify and applicable canonical spec sync. Simplify typed report attestation/pre-persistence admission, preserve real failure/task truth and archive reports. Update `assets/sdd-orchestrator-workflow.md`, `assets/chains/sdd-full.chain.md`, `assets/chains/sdd-verify.chain.md`, `assets/agents/sdd-apply.md`, `assets/agents/sdd-verify.md`, `assets/agents/sdd-sync.md`, `assets/agents/sdd-archive.md`, `assets/support/sdd-status-contract.md`. | `tests/sdd-agent-tools.test.ts`, `tests/sdd-selection-transport.test.ts`, `tests/sdd-status.test.ts`: actual direct archive without a verify report; explicit verify; incomplete work and real failures remain honest. |
| One status owner, no ordinary attempt governance | Remove selected sync startup's local status fork in `extensions/gentle-ai.ts:1820-1825` and competing readiness in `lib/sdd-status.ts:593-610`. Align `lib/native-review-cli.ts:1461-1498` with the final provider contract. Retire ordinary governed-remediation admission/settlement in `extensions/gentle-agents.ts:224-290,1198-1209` and affected `lib/agents-runner.ts` transport, retaining actual edit grants, workspace identity and safe handling of existing uncertain effects. | `tests/native-review-cli.test.ts`, `tests/sdd-native-managed-uptake.test.ts`, `tests/native-sdd-attempt-authority.test.ts`, `tests/sdd-managed-runtime-settlement.test.ts`: real dispatch has no ordinary acquire/settle; denied edits remain denied; sync cannot reinstate another status authority. |
| Optional useful research | Preserve product questions, requested depth, source attribution and actual authorized tool provenance. Remove mandatory completion/proposal-ready admission and pre-existing revision/session gates in `assets/sdd-orchestrator-workflow.md:138-150,193-211`, `assets/agents/sdd-research.md:31-68`, `lib/sdd-research-capabilities.ts:24-87,125-228`, `extensions/gentle-agents.ts:538-651,1142-1168`, and research transport in `lib/agents-runner.ts:544`. Useful partial research can continue with explicit limitations; persistence failures cannot become a generic success blockade. | `tests/sdd-research-capabilities.test.ts`, `tests/sdd-research-live.test.ts`: first artifact creation, partial research, missing/denied tools, exact extension provenance, failed persistence, actual readback and safe resume. |
| Minimal planning and recovery parity | Align actual installed planning/result consumers with the upstream five-root simplification: remove arbitrary planning caps and duplicated state authority while retaining useful planning artifacts, selected-store/locator identity, recovery and archive reports. Preserve TDD configuration and forwarding. Distribution remains owned by `lib/sdd-preflight.ts`; affected SDD agents/chains/support files change with their behavior, not through a new framework. | `tests/sdd-preflight.test.ts`, `tests/sdd-execution-routing-contract.test.ts`, `tests/sdd-planning-routing-contract.test.ts`: installed assets reflect the new workflow; TDD, recovery, workload decisions and chaining are retained. |

Dependencies: settle the final provider wire shape first. Optional archive and single-owner status must agree before delivery. Research simplification must retain host permissions and tool provenance; it does not authorize installing providers or widening scope. Coordinate overlapping reports in one owner/migration map before implementation; keep tests and docs with each coherent behavior unit.

The approximately 400-line task heuristic is advisory, not a hard cap or reason to minify, delete comments/tests, perform cosmetic shrinking, or repeatedly split a cohesive task. Preserve existing repository PR gates, workload decisions, exceptions and chained-PR conventions rather than silently replacing them with the task heuristic.

Required proof includes the existing runtime/child-startup branches against an explicitly identified build of the completed Gentle AI changes, with exact build identity and results. Distinguish scripted integration proof from actual model-driven observations; prompt assertions alone do not prove parity. No new framework, agent, command harness or parallel state store.

Rollback follows coherent behavior units and matching provider compatibility; preserve actual artifacts and recovery facts, never delete historical state or replay uncertain mutations as rollback.

### Alternatives considered

Provider-only or prompt-only updates leave Pi-owned runtime gates intact. Fixing each symptom separately risks growing the same admission machinery. Silently expanding one narrow report into the whole feature obscures its original scope; instead this coordinator links the reports and requires separate proof before any closure.

### Additional context

Upstream: [Gentle AI #4612](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/issues/4612) and its implementation chain through [#4625](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/4625). These are dependency references, not proof of a compatible published release.

Related reports:
- [Pi #965](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-pi/issues/965): SDD/RDD configuration ownership, not a promise to satisfy unrelated configuration requests.
- [Pi #1022](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-pi/issues/1022): local verification-result parsing; overlaps removal of competing sync readiness.
- [Pi #1032](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-pi/issues/1032): actual research extension provenance; removing gates alone does not prove tool reachability fixed.
- [Pi #1033](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-pi/issues/1033) and [Pi #1046](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-pi/issues/1046): locator and first-run research persistence; require separate observable regressions before proposing closure.

The prior open/closed SDD lookup returned 144 unsaturated results. The informed maintainer decision selects a new coordinated owner for this combined feature. It does not claim an exhaustive model reading of every candidate body or treat existing reports as fixed.

Pi currently pins Gentle AI 2.9.1. Compatibility tests may identify a built upstream candidate; a production pin must wait for a verified compatible published release. No unpublished version pin is authorized.

Excluded: separate ODD TDD forwarding, unrelated RDD redesign, model/provider changes, new lifecycle machinery, and unrelated pre-existing dirty checkout edits. Issue creation itself grants neither implementation authority nor an approval label.

title: feat(shell): show kimi-coding subscription usage in the bar and /gentle:usage panel
body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

## Problem or opportunity

Kimi Code (`kimi-coding`) is the Kimi Code subscription OAuth provider available in pi-coding-agent. Pi exposes it through the device-flow login flow at `https://auth.kimi.com` and answers requests at `https://api.kimi.com/coding` using a `Bearer` access token.

Gentle Shell's status bar / sidebar already surfaces subscription usage for `openai-codex`, `claude-bridge`, `antigravity`, and `minimax`, but kimi-coding has no path into `UsageStore`, so the bar never reflects quota for Kimi Code users.

## Proposed outcome

Show kimi-coding quota in the same places as the other subscription providers:

- `parseKimiUsage(payload, now)` for `GET https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1/usages`. The endpoint answers the weekly plan quota in `usage` plus per-window caps in `limits[]` (e.g. 5h rolling). Numeric fields are string-encoded; `timeUnit` is one of `TIME_UNIT_MINUTE/HOUR/DAY/WEEK`; `resetTime` is RFC3339 with nanosecond precision in UTC.
- `fetchKimiUsage(token, fetch, now)` reuses the OAuth bearer pi already holds for the subscription.
- `SUPPORTED_USAGE_PROVIDERS` and `PENDING_NOTE` updated so the sidebar explains itself when no snapshot is in memory yet.
- Display name "kimi" (consistent with "gemini", "claude", "minimax"); internal provider remains `kimi-coding` for pi-coding-agent compatibility.

## Alternatives considered

- Could fold into the generic Moonshot/Kimi Open Platform path, but that uses api.moonshot.ai with a pay-as-you-go balance (not subscription quota). kimi-coding is a distinct OAuth subscription, so it deserves its own branch in `refreshUsage`.

## Additional context

The smoke test in `tests/gentle-shell.test.ts` mirrors the minimax test: fake `fetch` asserts the exact URL, the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, the 5-min throttle, and the no-token no-fetch path. The parser is covered for weekly-only, limits-only, exhausted windows, and unknown `timeUnit` values.

title: sdd-research cannot persist on a first run: the scope guard requires pre-existing carried artifact locators
body:
## Summary

A **first** `sdd-research` run can never persist its own artifact. The scope guard requires `research_artifact` to carry pre-existing locators, and it requires every carried locator to have a *matching initial readback* before any mutation is allowed. Since on a first run neither `research.md` nor `preproposal.md` exists, there is no valid locator set to carry — so every local and memory tool in the child is blocked, and the phase returns its artifact inline instead of persisting it.

The child still does the research correctly. The problem is that the orchestrator then has to recover the artifact bytes out of band (in our case, by parsing the child's own session JSONL for the refused `write` / `mem_save` payloads) and persist them itself.

## Environment

- gentle-pi 2.7.0
- pi 0.85.1
- Artifact store: `hybrid`
- Launched via the `subagent_run` tool

## Reproduction

1. `subagent_run` an `sdd-research` task with a valid `research_selection`, and **without** `research_artifact`.

   `research_artifact` is optional in the tool schema (it is not in `required`), so omitting it looks legitimate.

2. Observe every local/store tool call in the child being refused:

```
Research scope refused: Research artifact worktree/store scope mismatch.
Retain intent and uncertainty; no replacement store.
```

Affected tools: `read`, `find`, `grep`, `write`, `edit`, `mem_search`, `mem_get_observation`, `mem_save`. The four web tools keep working, so the child completes collection with an empty local scope and returns the artifact inline with `proposal_ready: false`.

## Root cause

`extensions/gentle-agents.ts`:

```ts
const artifactScope = (cwd: string) => parseResearchArtifactIntent(JSON.parse(env[RESEARCH_ARTIFACT_ENV] ?? "null"), cwd);
```

With no `research_artifact`, `JSON.parse("null")` yields `null`, and `parseResearchArtifactIntent` rejects it (`ARTIFACT_STORES.includes(undefined)` is false) by throwing `"Research artifact worktree/store scope mismatch."` — the same exception raised for a genuine out-of-scope path, which makes the failure read as a scope violation rather than "no scope was supplied".

Even when locators ARE supplied, writing is only authorized for paths that are themselves carried locators (`researchArtifactCall`), and the mutation precondition requires every carried locator to have had a matching initial readback:

```ts
if (!scope.locators.every((_, i) => tools.every(tool => initialReads.has(`${i}:${tool}`))))
  throw new Error("Every selected artifact requires matching initial readback before mutation.");
```

Because `researchArtifactCall` also refuses write/edit/mem_save for `explore` locators, the only writable paths are `research` and `preproposal`. Both must therefore **already exist with bytes matching the carried revision and digest** before the child may advance them to a newer revision. There is no first-run bootstrap path, and nothing tells the orchestrator that it is expected to pre-create revision-1 stubs.

## Impact

- The agent that produced the artifact is not the agent that persists it. In our run the orchestrator had to recover the exact bytes from the child's session log to keep the phase output.
- `proposal_ready` stays `false`, and the persisted record says persistence never happened even after the orchestrator persists it — the record and reality disagree.
- The child cannot perform any local readback at all, so the terrain-mapping half of its job (reading the local config surfaces it is asked to map) is impossible. In our run it had to rely on web sources plus parent-supplied observations.
- A side observation: the child serialized the two `hybrid` legs with different formatting (28,314 bytes for the file vs 28,258 for the Engram save, 56 bytes apart) while believing it was writing identical bytes. The "identical bytes in both stores" contract is not enforced anywhere the child can see, so a divergence is easy to introduce and hard to notice. In our case it was caught only because the orchestrator compared digests after recovering the payloads.

## Suggested fix

Either, or both:

1. Give the first run a bounded creation path — e.g. accept `store` with zero locators as "this child may create its artifacts under `openspec/changes/{change}/`", keeping the exact-path bound while removing the pre-existence requirement.
2. If pre-created stubs really are the intended contract, document it and surface it to the caller: make `research_artifact` clearly required for a research launch, and fail the launch with an actionable message rather than letting the child run with no local scope and silently degrade to web-only evidence.
3. Consider distinguishing "no scope supplied" from "scope violation" in the guard message.
4. Consider validating the hybrid identical-bytes invariant before accepting a mutation, so a divergent serialization cannot be recorded as an identical-bytes write.

## Evidence

The full guarded-tool refusal and the recovered payloads are available in the child session log (`~/.pi/agent/gentle-agents/sessions/`), including four refused persistence calls: two `write` and two `mem_save`.
