title: feat(shell): unify responsive status across footer and sidebar
body:
### Before submitting

These first-person statements remain unchecked until the user explicitly affirms them.

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other
      sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Gentle Pi presents related runtime information in the responsive shell footer and the fullscreen
Status sidebar, but each surface currently handles width constraints and visual hierarchy as a
separate concern.

On narrow terminals, the footer can drop execution metadata or integration status. In fullscreen
mode, the Status card can consume more vertical space than necessary. The effective RDD state must
also remain visible without being inferred from opaque integration strings.

Users would benefit from one coherent shell-status experience for project, model, context, usage,
review, and integrations across terminal widths and TUI modes.

### Proposed outcome

Deliver the unified experience as three independent, reviewable work units:

1. Preserve execution metadata and integration status in responsive footer layouts, including safe
   truncation for Unicode branch names.
2. Expose effective structured RDD state as `ON`, `OFF`, or unknown.
3. Compact the fullscreen Status sidebar:
   - show the project basename instead of its complete path;
   - keep branch and dirty count on the same logical line;
   - preserve the session name;
   - render Model before Review in responsive columns;
   - render Context before Usage in responsive columns;
   - omit only the provider name from sidebar usage;
   - preserve all windows from the first usage limit;
   - keep Integrations full-width and opaque;
   - stack column groups when the available width is insufficient.

The traditional bottom bar must preserve its semantics. Every rendered line must fit the supplied
visible width, including ANSI sequences and Unicode characters.

The work should be delivered through three separate PRs in this order:

```text
responsive shell footer
  -> structured RDD status
  -> compact Status sidebar
```

The integration branch demonstrates compatibility only and should not become a monolithic PR.

### Alternatives considered

### One combined PR

Rejected because the integrated comparison contains 1,260 changed lines across 11 files. That review
load would obscure the boundaries between behaviors and make regressions harder to isolate.

### Completely independent changes

Keeping the branches independent protects review size, but without shared validation it does not
show that their overlapping shell and Status changes work together.

### Infer RDD from integrations

Rejected because integration statuses are opaque strings. RDD must come from its structured source.

The recommended approach keeps three work units and uses an integrated branch only for end-to-end
validation.

### Additional context

Related issues:

- [#715](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-pi/issues/715) covers responsive footer
  metadata and Unicode width. It is related but does not cover the umbrella outcome.
- [#938](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-pi/issues/938) covers effective structured
  RDD state. It is related but does not cover the umbrella outcome.

A refreshed open-and-closed issue search found no equivalent umbrella request. It found #715; #938
was also read directly to confirm its narrower scope.

Implementation branches:

| Work unit | Branch | Tip | Diff against `main` |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| Responsive footer | `fix/responsive-shell-footer` | `579a025e` | 5 files, +638/-89 |
| Structured RDD | `feat/shell-rdd-status` | `fd704bd0` | 9 files, +342/-24 |
| Compact sidebar | `feat/compact-status-sidebar` | `ebdcec3b` | 2 files, +150/-49 |
| Integration evidence | `feat/unified-shell-status` | `2c57d6f` | 11 files, +1111/-149 |

The integration commit preserves both the original integration history and the reconstruction on the
updated `main`. Its tree is byte-identical to the validated reconstructed tree at `8fca04f`.

Recorded validation for that identical tree:

```text
pnpm test
2378 passed
11 skipped
0 failed

pnpm typecheck
passed

pnpm run check:runtime-modules
passed

git diff --check
passed
```

Interactive validation was also performed with the integrated runtime installed locally.

#### Acceptance criteria

- The three work units remain independently reviewable.
- The footer preserves semantic metadata at narrow widths.
- RDD comes from structured data.
- The Status sidebar reduces height without changing data sources.
- Model appears before Review.
- Context appears before Usage.
- Narrow fallback preserves the same semantic order.
- Integrations remain sanitized opaque text.
- The bottom bar preserves its behavior.
- No line exceeds the supplied visible width.
- Focused tests, typecheck, runtime-module checks, and the complete suite pass.

title: perf: gentle-shell render pulse drives high CPU in long regular-mode sessions
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

`gentle-shell` continuously requests a full TUI render every 160 ms while an agent is running. With a long Pi session, the render cost becomes significant. The pulse is not the sole cause—the core renderer also becomes expensive with long history—but it amplifies the cost by forcing repeated renders even when no meaningful UI state changed.

This is a residual case related to #832. PRs #840 and #876 improved fullscreen sidebar caching, but the regular-mode path still retains the 160 ms petal pulse and repeatedly recomputes session-derived information such as `sessionCost()`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run Pi 0.85.1 on Linux with a long session history (the measured session was approximately 1.21 MB).
2. Compare idle CPU over repeated 30-second windows with no active Git watcher:
   - Pi core, idle.
   - Pi with `gentle-shell`, idle.
   - Pi core with a synthetic extension calling `requestRender()` every 160 ms during `agent_start`.
   - Pi with `gentle-shell` while its 160 ms pulse is active.
3. Observe CPU during a real active turn in the same long session.
4. Confirm that Git status is not the bottleneck and background Git-related threads are sleeping.

Measured ranges across three controlled repetitions:

| Configuration | Average CPU |
| --- | ---: |
| Pi core idle | 0% |
| `gentle-shell` idle | 0.27–0.53% |
| Pi core + `requestRender()` every 160 ms | 3.85–4.93% |
| `gentle-shell` + 160 ms pulse | 4.89–6.04% |

The production session measured 40.9%, 53.25%, and 101.3% CPU in active 10-second windows. Earlier observations reached a 158% average with peaks around 215%.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: cosmetic agent-running animation should have bounded CPU cost and should not force full-history work on every animation frame. Long sessions should remain responsive in both regular and fullscreen modes.

Actual: the 160 ms pulse calls `requestRender()` repeatedly. Render work scales with session history, so active long sessions can saturate one or more CPU cores. Existing fullscreen sidebar caching reduces one path but does not cover this regular-mode residual behavior.

Potential direction:

- decouple the petal animation from full TUI renders, or make the pulse adaptive/static;
- stop the timer when its visual state is not visible or cannot change meaningfully;
- cache or incrementally maintain `sessionCost` instead of traversing all entries per render;
- add a long-session performance regression covering regular and fullscreen modes.

### gentle-pi version

2.6.2 (the current `main` implementation was also inspected and retains `PETAL_PULSE_MS = 160`)

### Pi version

0.85.1

### Operating system

Linux

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
No error log is emitted. This is a reproducible CPU/performance regression measured through process CPU sampling.
```

title: bug(review): committed-range START unreachable (3 contradictory prerequisite errors → native schema-incompatible) and inspect bases the range on the default branch
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

Two independent defects in the review integration make it impossible to review a **committed range** (the normal PR shape: everything committed, clean working tree) with the compact facade. A third, related defect makes `assess` mis-scope its candidate and its risk reasons.

**A. Committed-range START is unreachable.** `gentle_review` START with an explicit `baseRef` walks a contradictory prerequisite chain and finally fails natively, creating no lineage:

1. `idempotencyKey` + `input '{"baseRef":"<base branch>","committedOnly":true}'` → `Judgment Day graph-v1 START requires lineageId`
2. add the provider-issued `lineageId` returned by `inspect` → `Review controller START supports only "ordinary" or "judgment-day" mode; use "ordinary" unless Judgment Day was explicitly selected. Pass input as a JSON string encoding the START object. START failed before authority access, so no lineage was created; do not call STATUS or ADVANCE for this attempted lineage.`
3. add `mode` to the input → `{"status":"blocked","outcome":"native-operation-failed","lineage_created":false,"mutation_performed":false,"mutation_outcome":"none","reset_eligible":false,"diagnostics":{"operation":"review/start","error_code":"schema-incompatible"},"next_action":"resolve-native-operation-failure"}`

Every attempt reports `lineage_created: false`, and a subsequent `inspect` still shows `lineages: 0` and the same `fresh_target_ready` route — so nothing was mutated, and nothing is recoverable either.

**Impact:** already-committed work cannot be reviewed at all. The `workspace` projection is not a workaround: with a clean tree, `inspect` reports `paths: []` and an empty candidate, so the lenses have nothing to read. A PR is exactly "committed work with a clean tree", which is the shape the compact review path is most needed for.

**B. `inspect` bases the review range on the remote default branch, not on the change's base branch.** In a repository where PRs target `develop` while `origin/HEAD` points at `main`, the offered START route carried `--base-ref` equal to a merge commit from the default branch, and a `target-evidence` whose base tree was the default branch's tree. The range it would review was ~240 commits / 486 files / ~34,860 changed lines, versus the change's actual 29 files / 4,817 lines — it would have reviewed months of unrelated, already-merged work. Because `target-evidence` is opaque and signed against that base, a caller cannot repair the route by editing only `--base-ref`, so the offered route is unusable as offered.

**C. `assess` scopes its candidate with a two-dot diff.** With `input '{"baseRef":"<base branch>","committedOnly":true}'`, `assess` reported `changedPaths: 100`, `changedLines: 8035` and a single risk reason `hot_path` for a file the change never touches. The base branch had advanced past the branch's fork point, so its extra commits were counted as part of this change (`100 = 29 ours + 71 from the base branch`; `8035 = 5311 + 2724`). If two-dot is the intended semantics, the risk reason is still mis-scoped: it named a file modified by the base branch, not by the candidate.

### Steps to reproduce

Any Git repository works; no special contents are needed beyond a fully committed change.

Setup:
- a feature branch whose fork point is older than the PR base (the base branch advanced afterwards), clean working tree;
- `gentle_review {operation:"inspect"}` and note the offered route.

Defect A:
1. `gentle_review {operation:"start", idempotencyKey:"<fresh>", input:'{"baseRef":"origin/develop","committedOnly":true}'}` → error 1.
2. the same call plus `lineageId:"<the lineageId inspect returned>"` → error 2.
3. the same call with `input:'{"mode":"ordinary","baseRef":"origin/develop","committedOnly":true}'` → envelope 3.
4. `gentle_review {operation:"inspect"}` again → `lineages: 0` and the same `fresh_target_ready` route, unchanged.

Defect B:
5. from step 4's offered route, compare `--base-ref` with (a) the PR base branch and (b) `origin/HEAD`; it matches the default branch.
6. compare `git diff --shortstat <offered base-ref> HEAD` with `git diff --shortstat <merge-base of the PR base and HEAD> HEAD`.

Defect C:
7. `gentle_review {operation:"assess", input:'{"baseRef":"origin/develop","committedOnly":true}'}` and compare `changedPaths`, `changedLines` and `reasons[].path` against the two `--shortstat` numbers, and against whether the named file appears in the change at all.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected:
- A START with an explicit `baseRef` + `committedOnly: true` either starts (and asks for consent) or fails with one actionable error naming the missing input — not three mutually contradictory ones.
- The reviewed range is the change between the given base and HEAD.
- `inspect` derives its base from the branch under review / the PR base, not from `origin/HEAD`.
- `assess` scopes its candidate and risk reasons to that same range.

Actual:
- START cannot be completed: the native operation fails with `schema-incompatible` and no lineage is created, and no route is offered to review committed work.
- The route `inspect` offers is based on the default branch, so following it would have reviewed several hundred unrelated commits.
- `assess` reports an inflated candidate and a risk reason for a file the change never touches.

### gentle-pi version

gentle-pi 2.6.1 (CLI `gentle-ai 2.8.2`)

### Pi version

0.85.1

### Operating system

Linux

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
A1  gentle_review start (idempotencyKey + input baseRef/committedOnly)
Judgment Day graph-v1 START requires lineageId

A2  same call + lineageId
Review controller START supports only "ordinary" or "judgment-day" mode; use "ordinary" unless Judgment Day was explicitly selected. Pass input as a JSON string encoding the START object. START failed before authority access, so no lineage was created; do not call STATUS or ADVANCE for this attempted lineage.

A3  same call + input mode: ordinary
{"operation":"start","status":"blocked","outcome":"native-operation-failed","lineage_created":false,"mutation_performed":false,"mutation_outcome":"none","reset_eligible":false,"diagnostics":{"operation":"review/start","error_code":"schema-incompatible","timed_out":false,"output_limit_exceeded":false},"next_action":"resolve-native-operation-failure"}

A4  inspect after the three failures
{"repair":{"counts":{"lineages":0,"compact_lineages":0,"legacy_lineages":0,"events":0,"bytes":0}},"candidates":[],"next_transition":{"kind":"execute","reason_code":"fresh_target_ready"}}

B   offered route, excerpt (values replaced by placeholders)
gentle-ai review start ... --target=<digest> --target-evidence=v1:base-diff:workspace:<default-branch-tree>:<head-tree>:sha256:<digest> --projection=workspace --base-ref=<default-branch-merge-commit> --committed-only=true --lineage=<id> --agent=pi --consent=relay

C   assess
{"risk":"high","reasons":[{"code":"hot_path","path":"<file not part of the change>","detail":"signal: update"}],"changedPaths":100,"changedLines":8035,"candidate":{"kind":"base-diff","baseRef":"<base branch>"},"plan":{"writerSelfVerification":true,"independentVerifier":true}}
```

Related, not duplicates: #983 (STATUS `schema-incompatible` on an escalated lineage), #919 (correction-representation gap on committed ranges), #857 (START reconciles to unknown mutation outcome), #599 (`inspect` without `workspaceRoot` swallows the native cause for nested foreign Git repos).

title: bug(installer): package-local-binary-missing recurs on upgrade under ignore-scripts=true; recovery names only GENTLE_PI_SKIP_GENTLE_AI_INSTALL
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

gentle-pi ships its native review CLI as a package-local pinned binary at
`<packageRoot>/.gentle-ai/v<INSTALLER_VERSION>/gentle-ai` (+ `integrity.json`), provisioned only by
the package `postinstall` (`scripts/install-gentle-ai.mjs`). On hosts whose npm config sets
`ignore-scripts=true`, npm skips `postinstall`, so the runtime is never created. Every native
operation then fails with `package-local-binary-missing` — including the `/gentle-sdd-status`
command and the RDD status line.

This is distinct from #764 (closed). #764's complaint was that the remediation recommended
reinstalling, which re-skips postinstall in a loop; that remediation now points at the correct
command. Two gaps remain, both hit on a normal gentle-pi upgrade:

1. The recovery message names only the `GENTLE_PI_SKIP_GENTLE_AI_INSTALL` env var as a cause. Here
   that variable was NOT set; the actual cause was `ignore-scripts=true` in a user-level `.npmrc`. A
   user without the env var gets a conditional instruction ("If GENTLE_PI_SKIP_GENTLE_AI_INSTALL is
   set...") that does not apply, plus "does not prove install lifecycle scripts were disabled", with
   no mention of `ignore-scripts`.
2. `INSTALLER_VERSION` (in `scripts/gentle-ai-installer.mjs`) is independent of the package.json
   version and bumps on upgrades. Observed: package.json 2.6.2 pins gentle-ai v2.8.2. Each upgrade
   therefore targets a fresh `.gentle-ai/v<new>` directory that postinstall never created under
   `ignore-scripts=true`, so the same breakage silently recurs after every upgrade.

There is also no lazy self-heal: when the pinned binary is missing, resolution throws instead of
(optionally) running the already-pinned, SHA-256-verified `scripts/install-gentle-ai.mjs` once.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set `ignore-scripts=true` in a user- or prefix-scoped `.npmrc` (leave `GENTLE_PI_SKIP_GENTLE_AI_INSTALL` unset).
2. Install or upgrade gentle-pi through Pi. npm skips `postinstall`; `.gentle-ai/` is never created.
3. Confirm `.gentle-ai/` is absent under the installed `node_modules/gentle-pi`.
4. Run `/gentle-sdd-status` (or any native review operation / RDD status read).
5. Observe `package-local-binary-missing` for the pinned version, with recovery text that only references `GENTLE_PI_SKIP_GENTLE_AI_INSTALL`.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected:
- Recovery guidance identifies `ignore-scripts=true` / skipped npm lifecycle scripts as a first-class
  cause and states that the package-owned command succeeds:
  `cd <installed gentle-pi> && node scripts/install-gentle-ai.mjs`.
- Optionally self-heal on `package-local-binary-missing` by running the pinned, digest-verified
  installer once (or offering it as a bound next-action), so upgrades under `ignore-scripts=true` do
  not silently break the command and native review.

Actual:
- `/gentle-sdd-status` and native review fail with `package-local-binary-missing`. The recovery text
  keys only on `GENTLE_PI_SKIP_GENTLE_AI_INSTALL`, which was not set, so the real `ignore-scripts=true`
  cause is not surfaced. Running the installer manually is the only fix and must be repeated after
  every upgrade.

Manual workaround that worked: `cd <installed gentle-pi> && node scripts/install-gentle-ai.mjs`
(downloads the signed release asset, verifies archive+binary SHA-256 against pinned digests, writes
`.gentle-ai/v<X>/{gentle-ai,integrity.json}`). Verified: `resolveGentleAiBinary()` resolves and
`gentle-ai --version` reports 2.8.2. A session restart is needed because the RDD-status
prompt/commands are memoized per process.

### gentle-pi version

2.6.2 (package.json), pinning gentle-ai INSTALLER_VERSION 2.8.2

### Pi version

0.85.1

### Operating system

Windows (WSL)

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
Extension "command:gentle-sdd-status" error: package-local-binary-missing: Gentle AI v2.8.2 is not installed at <home>/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/gentle-pi/.gentle-ai/v2.8.2/gentle-ai. If GENTLE_PI_SKIP_GENTLE_AI_INSTALL is set, remove or unset it before changing to the installed gentle-pi package directory and running `node scripts/install-gentle-ai.mjs`. A missing binary can result from skipped lifecycle scripts, but does not prove install lifecycle scripts were disabled.
```

title: ci(windows): candidate owner preparation fails when a PowerShell spawn exceeds its 5 s timeout
body:
## Problem

The `review-repository-windows` job intermittently fails in `tests/review-candidate-view.test.ts` ("candidate ownership is private and durable before worktree add") with:

```
CandidateViewError: candidate view owner preparation failed
    candidateViewParent (lib/review-candidate-view.ts:649)
```

The wrapped cause is not printed, but the timing is diagnostic: on the failing attempts the test ended after ~5.7 s, while on a green run of the same job on `main` minutes earlier the same test took ~25 s. `prepareCandidateOwnerParent` on Windows runs `whoami.exe`, `powershell.exe` (owner SID and DACL enforcement) and `icacls.exe` through `execFileSync` with `timeout: 5000` each (`lib/review-candidate-view-owner.ts:39,48,58,154,178`). A cold Windows PowerShell 5.1 start on a slow hosted runner can exceed 5 s, so the first spawn is killed and the whole preparation is reported as failed.

## Evidence

- PR #989 (pin bump, does not touch candidate view code; the job skips the Gentle AI install via `GENTLE_PI_SKIP_GENTLE_AI_INSTALL=1`): failed twice in a row, run 34783464943.
- `main` run 34781588474: the Windows job re-run at the same time succeeded; the test took 25097 ms.

## Expected

- Surface the wrapped cause in `CandidateViewError` so the TAP output names the killed executable and the timeout.
- Give the Windows owner-resolution spawns a timeout that tolerates a cold PowerShell start on hosted runners (or reuse one PowerShell process for the boundary walk), so a slow runner does not turn a correct ACL state into a red job.

Maintainer-approved for a follow-up fix.

title: bug(pi-pretty): FFF fff-bg threads busy-loop on small workspaces — Pi frozen at 100%+ CPU after session_start
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

Starting Pi leaves the process stuck at ~100-133% CPU almost immediately after the TUI renders, with the UI frozen/unresponsive for minutes. Two independent busy-loops were found and diagnosed; both are described below along with the mitigation applied locally.

**Loop 1 — FFF native threads.** pi-pretty's `session_start` handler calls `ensureFinder(ctx.cwd)`, which creates a `@ff-labs/fff-node` `FileFinder` on the workspace. On this machine the finder's background threads (`fff-bg-0` … `fff-bg-5`) spin in a busy loop and never settle, so the whole Pi process sits at ~113% CPU (main thread included at `do_epoll_wait` / `RNl+`) with 0 bytes/s of disk I/O — pure CPU burn, not indexing I/O.

**Loop 2 — gentle-pi changes-tracker over a home-rooted repository.** Independently of FFF, gentle-pi's session changes-tracker scans the session worktree and hangs the main thread on very large repositories — see the "Residual finding" section below.

This is the second time a fresh install reproduced it. It is not tied to a huge workspace: the reported workspace is small (<64 MB, ~3.7k files, ~280 dirs).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Linux (CachyOS, kernel 6.x), Pi 0.85.1 + gentle-pi from npm.
2. Open a terminal in a normal project directory (small workspace, ~3.7k files).
3. Run `pi`.
4. Watch the process: within seconds the TUI freezes, and `ps` shows the process at ~100-133% CPU sustained.

Observed thread distribution on the stuck process (loop 1):

```text
main  (pi)          do_epoll_wait | RNl+   ~18% CPU
fff-bg-0 / -1       RNl+                 ~55% / ~48% CPU
(further fff-bg-*)  present, sleeping
disk I/O            0 bytes/s (busy loop, not indexing)
```

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected:
- FFF indexes the workspace once, then the finder goes idle; the TUI stays responsive. If FFF cannot index, pi-pretty's documented fallback keeps SDK-backed file tools available.
- gentle-pi tracks changes only for repositories that are real project roots, and never blocks the TUI on a scan.

Actual:
- The `fff-bg-*` native threads busy-loop (loop 1), and/or gentle-pi's changes-tracker pins the main thread scanning a giant repository (loop 2). Only killing the process recovers. Both patterns reproduced across multiple fresh Pi instances/processes.

### Follow-up 1 (resolved): root cause and library update — FFF busy-loop

Loop 1 was identified. Version chain: `gentle-pi@2.6.1` pins `@heyhuynhgiabuu/pi-pretty@0.6.14` (exact, no caret), which depends on `@ff-labs/fff-node@^0.9.6`. On `session_start`, pi-pretty's `ensureFinder(ctx.cwd)` creates the native `FileFinder` and calls `waitForScan(15_000)`; when the scan does not finish inside that window, `partialIndex` stays set and the native `fff-bg-*` threads keep spinning.

Upgrading locally via npm `overrides` to `pi-pretty@0.6.28` + `fff-node@0.10.6` **eliminated the `fff-bg` busy-loop**. The relevant fix is in fff core: PR dmtrKovalenko/fff#751 "Reduce amount of rescans in giant $HOME like folders" (closes dmtrKovalenko/fff#743), plus #780, #644, #645. Since `fff-node@0.10.6` no longer satisfies pi-pretty 0.6.14's `^0.9.6` range, I recommend bumping `@heyhuynhgiabuu/pi-pretty` off the exact `0.6.14` pin so consumers can pick up the fixed core.

### Follow-up 2 (resolved): residual busy-loop — gentle-pi changes-tracker on a home-rooted repository

After loop 1 was fixed, a *second* loop remained in the `pi` main thread. This one is gentle-pi, not pi-pretty/fff: the session changes-tracker. `SessionWorktreeRegistry` resolves the session worktree with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and registers that root. When `pi` is launched inside a directory that belongs to a repository rooted at the user's home directory — e.g. an accidental `git init` in `$HOME`, common with dotfiles setups — the resolved root is the ENTIRE home directory.

`WorktreeChangesTracker.capture()` then runs `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all -z` on that root and, the expensive part, opens and line-counts **every untracked file** (`lineCounter` in `gentle-shell.ts`). On the reporter's machine the home repo held on the order of a million untracked files:

- `git status --untracked-files=all` expanded to ~100 MB of output and took ~6 s per invocation;
- the watcher tick (default 5 s) chained behind each run (`queued`), so the loop never drained;
- main thread pinned at ~100% CPU, dominated by buffer `write`/`string_decoder` plus the line-counter `readFile` per untracked file (verified with a V8 CPU profile).

**Mitigation (applied locally):** in `SessionWorktreeRegistry`, when the resolved repository root equals the user's home directory (or its parent), the session worktree is not registered and changes tracking is skipped for that session. Repositories that live below the home and carry their own `.git` (e.g. a normal project under a `projects/` folder) still resolve to their own toplevel and remain tracked, so no real project loses its changes widget.

**Suggested upstream change:** skip changes tracking when `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` equals `os.homedir()` (or an ancestor such as the parent of the home), and/or avoid expanding `--untracked-files=all` plus opening every untracked file when counting lines — a repository rooted at the home directory is almost never a real project root.

### gentle-pi version

2.6.1 (npm) — reported chain: pi-pretty 0.6.14 / fff-node 0.9.6; fixed locally with pi-pretty 0.6.28 / fff-node 0.10.6

### Pi version

0.85.1

### Operating system

Linux

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
# ps during the freeze (reported run)
PID STAT %CPU %MEM ELAPSED WCHAN
100807 RNl+ 113 5.0 06:11 do_epoll_wait

# V8 CPU profile after loop 1 was fixed (loop 2, gentle-pi changes-tracker)
# main thread in buffer write / string_decoder (48%) + lineCounter (20%) over
# hundreds of thousands of untracked files in a home-rooted repository.
```

title: review: session report — cross-unit dependency scoping escalates false CRITICALs; STATUS schema-incompatible on escalated lineage; partial_unknown group outcomes
body:
### Problem

Session report following #573 and #919 (same candidate family: a ~37k-line working tree split into work-unit commits, reviewed per unit through the compact facade). Numbered findings; re-confirmations from the prior reports are marked.

1. NEW — **Cross-unit dependency scoping artifacts make per-unit review unable to complete honestly.** Unit k consumes APIs implemented in unit j<k; the frozen candidate tree hides the implementation, so the reviewer cannot verify the contract and policy escalates or demands correction even when the combined branch is provably correct (typecheck + 820 tests green):
   - U9: reliability CRITICAL claimed the RPC model-override path was broken because `model-resolver.ts` (unit 1) was outside the changed-path manifest; in-candidate witnesses (a removed `typeof resolved === "string"` branch and a stale in-file comment) described the obsolete contract. Unknown causality → escalated (`native_stop_required`, terminal). HEAD verification: the typed `ResolvedModel` union exists exactly as consumed; the only real defect was the stale comment (fixed in a follow-up commit).
   - U10: refuter-corroborated CRITICAL claimed call sites might mismatch the manager signature because `agent-manager.ts` (unit 5) was outside the tree and in-candidate tests mock the manager → `correction_required`. HEAD: both `spawn`/`spawnAndWait` take the options object; typecheck compiles every call site against the real signature.
   Suggested: let a transaction declare "context commits" (read-only reviewer context from dependency units), or first-class committed-range candidates (overlaps the gentle-ai committed-range request).

2. NEW — Facade STATUS fails with `schema-incompatible` on an **escalated** lineage (twice, deterministic). Diagnosis required a read-only native CLI status, which rendered the escalated state fine (`unknown_causality`, finding id). The facade should render every state the documented stop table names.

3. NEW — `capture_group` ended `partial_unknown` (3 of 4 reviewers reported submitted; reconciliation via STATUS showed all four admitted and the lineage already advanced). There is no resume-once outcome; recovery only through STATUS slot reoffers.

4. NEW — Relay variants: one reviewer received no `GENTLE_AI_REVIEW_PATCH` sections (declared "inspection unavailable"; slot correctly not consumed; re-run admitted); another emitted an invalid severity enum (admission refused; re-run admitted).

5. Re-confirmed #919 — consent: `answer-consent` → `consent-binding-unknown` with the exact workspaceRoot (twice; `restart-for-fresh-consent` recovery worked: fresh START applied the host-recorded grant). Additionally one candidate was machine-declined (`consent-declined-this-candidate`) without any envelope ever being presented to the human; fresh inspect + START created the lineage directly.

6. NEW — Facade inspect ignores `{"baseRef":"HEAD~1","committedOnly":true}` and still binds the whole workspace projection, so committed-range candidates had to be simulated: detached worktree at the unit's parent + `git checkout <sha> -- .` + explicit `git rm` for deletions (checkout of a tree does not apply deletions — without the explicit rm, deletion hunks silently vanish from the reviewed candidate).

7. Re-confirmed #919 — the only working completion path for a stuck lineage was a fresh lineage on a changed candidate (the escalated lineage itself stays as a permanent audit record).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Split a ~37k-line working tree into 11 thematic work-unit commits; full tree green (typecheck, tests, lint).
2. Review each unit through the facade using a simulated committed-range candidate: detached worktree at the unit's parent commit, `checkout <unit-sha> -- .`, explicit `git rm` for paths the unit deletes.
3. For a unit whose dependencies were committed in earlier units, observe the reviewer flag a CRITICAL against an API contract it cannot see (units 9 and 10), reaching `escalated` / `correction_required`.
4. Attempt bound facade STATUS on the escalated lineage; attempt `capture_group` on a 4-lens lineage with one reviewer transport failure; attempt `answer-consent` with a provider-issued binding.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected:
- Facade STATUS renders every documented state, including `escalated`.
- Group captures reconcile once and return the exact remaining slots instead of `partial_unknown`.
- Consent bindings are held by the relaying session; no candidate is declined without an envelope being presented.
- Per-unit review of a split can complete: dependency units are available as context, or committed-range candidates are first-class.

Actual:
- STATUS `schema-incompatible` on the escalated lineage; raw CLI status needed.
- `partial_unknown` with no resume semantics.
- `consent-binding-unknown` despite the correct workspaceRoot; one phantom decline.
- Two false CRITICALs reached severe states purely from scoping; both disproven at HEAD.

2.5.0 (source build)

### Pi version

0.85.1

macOS

U10 lineage review-a3341db19d4b9ad7: state=correction_required (R3-01, inferential)

title: Startup banner MCP stat counts configured servers, not enabled ones
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

The startup banner stats (the side status bar shown at session start, with rows like `GIT:`, `PATH:`, `MCP:`) reports `MCP: N server(s)` where N counts every server **configured** in the global `~/.pi/agent/mcp.json` — including servers that are **disabled** and therefore never connect or register any tools.

`extensions/startup-banner.ts` reads the raw config file and counts keys (session_start handler, around lines 656–664):

```ts
const raw = await readFile(
  join(os.homedir(), ".pi", "agent", "mcp.json"),
  "utf8",
);
const cfg = JSON.parse(raw);
mcpServersCount = Object.keys(cfg.mcpServers || {}).length;
```

That count is rendered as `MCP: ${mcpServersCount} server(s)` in all three stat layouts (wide row, narrow rows, and the `narrowRows` array — lines ~863, ~890–891, ~911).

With pi-mcp-adapter, a server can be disabled (`"disabled": true` in any MCP config, or `/mcp disable <server>`, which persists the flag in the project-local `.pi/mcp.json`); disabled servers make no connections, no authentication, and register no tools — they only stay visible in config and status. The banner still counts them, so the panel overstates the MCP surface the session actually has available. Layered config also escapes the count: servers defined only in a project-layer MCP config are invisible to the global-file parse.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure two MCP servers in `~/.pi/agent/mcp.json` and add `"disabled": true` to one of them (or run `/mcp disable <server>` in a project).
2. Start a new pi session with gentle-pi loaded.
3. The stats panel shows `MCP: 2 server(s)`, while the `/mcp` panel reports 1 enabled server (1 disabled).

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected:

`MCP:` reflects the **enabled** servers the session actually loads. pi-mcp-adapter already publishes a read-only, machine-readable status snapshot (`MCP_STATUS_EVENT` / `McpStatusSnapshot`) with per-server `status`/`disabled` plus `connectedCount` and `disabledCount`; the banner could consume that instead of parsing the raw config file.

Actual:

`MCP:` reports every key configured in the global `~/.pi/agent/mcp.json`, including disabled servers and ignoring project-layer MCP config.

### gentle-pi version

2.5.0 (running from source, commit 6e4478c0)

### Pi version

0.85.1

### Operating system

macOS

_No response_

title: Review preflight re-offers the whole approved candidate after a post-approval edit (expected: atomic delta scope)
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

The review preflight re-offers a full review over an already-approved candidate after any post-approval edit. Concretely: an RDD review over a 5-file candidate completes approved and its authority is burned; afterwards ONE of those files is modified (same uncommitted worktree); the next `gentle_review` inspect offers a brand-new full review over the SAME 5 files. There is no atomic per-file scoping: approved-and-unchanged files are re-frozen and re-reviewed, so every small post-review edit triggers a full multi-lens review round (full reviewer group cost) over mostly byte-identical content.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run an RDD review over a candidate of 5 changed files; it completes approved and the acknowledgement burns the authority.
2. Modify one of those 5 files (still uncommitted, same worktree).
3. Run the review preflight again (the `gentle_review` tool, operation `inspect`, or the agent-end preflight reminder).
4. Observe the offered `review.start`: the frozen projection contains all 5 paths again, and all lenses re-run over them.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected:

- Review units should be atomic per file. A post-approval modification should scope the next review offer to ONLY the file(s) changed since the last approved revision.
- Files already covered by an approved, acknowledged (burned) lineage and unchanged since the burn should not re-freeze into a new candidate.

Actual:

- The next inspect offers `review.start` over the full 5-file projection; all paths re-freeze and every lens re-runs over all of them, even though 4 of the 5 files are byte-identical to the approved revision.

2.5.0 (source @ 6e4478c0)

title: feat(subagents): show read/write/output token usage breakdown
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Gentle Agents currently show token usage primarily as a single accumulated total.

For long-running or context-heavy agents, this can be confusing. For example, seeing something like 1.1M tokens can make it look like the agent generated 1.1M output tokens, when most of that usage may actually come from input/context reads, cache reads, or cache writes.

This makes it difficult to understand how much content the model actually generated versus how much context it consumed during the run.
Users who regularly use Gentle Agents/subagents, especially on large repositories or long-running tasks, would benefit from a clearer token usage breakdown.

### Proposed outcome

Show separate token usage values for Gentle Agents, ideally including:

- Read/Input tokens
- Write/Cache tokens
- Output tokens
- Total tokens

For example:
``` bash
Tokens
Read:    980K
Write:    85K
Output:   35K
Total:   1.1M
```
A more compact TUI representation would also work as long as the different token categories remain distinguishable.

Ideally, this breakdown should be visible:

- While a Gentle Agent is running.
- In the completed agent summary.

The existing total can remain, but it should be clear that it represents aggregate usage rather than output tokens alone.

### Alternatives considered

Another option would be to show the detailed breakdown only in an expanded/details view. That would reduce visual noise, but having at least a compact read/write/output breakdown directly visible would make token usage much easier to understand.

### Additional context

This is especially noticeable when working with long-running subagents or large repositories.

For example, an agent may display around 1.1M tokens, while its actual generated output is only a small portion of that total. Most of the usage may come from repeatedly reading context or other cache/input activity.

The goal is not to remove the total token count, but to make that number easier to interpret by exposing its components.

title: Support documentary evidence in SDD verification
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Documentation-only SDD changes can explicitly permit acceptance without live execution, while the current verification contract recognizes a scenario as compliant only when a covering runtime test passes. The report schema has no documentary/manual evidence status, so a statically complete and independently reviewed documentation change can only produce an admitted FAIL and can never reach archive.

Running unrelated application suites does not cover documentary scenarios. Adding string-matching tests solely to satisfy the gate would create misleading coverage and conflict with behavior-focused testing.

### Proposed outcome

Add a fail-closed, explicit documentary verification path across the report schema, validator, status projection, archive readiness, and `sdd-verify` agent.

Suggested safeguards:

- Require the specification to explicitly permit acceptance without execution.
- Require an explicit project policy enabling documentary evidence.
- Require the implementation diff to contain no executable, schema, migration, authorization, or runtime configuration changes.
- Represent documentary evidence distinctly from runtime-tested compliance.
- Require structured static evidence and independent review for every documentary scenario.
- Forbid documentary evidence for runtime, security, authorization, database, migration, deployment, or hosted-state claims.
- Fail closed on mixed changes, missing evidence, unknown fields, contradictory counts, or unsupported scenario types.
- Add validator and status/archive tests proving both acceptance and bypass resistance.

### Alternatives considered

- Running unrelated ETL, web, build, or E2E suites: rejected because green commands would not cover the scenarios.
- Adding tests that search Markdown strings: rejected because they would verify implementation text rather than behavior.
- Removing or renaming scenarios after implementation: rejected because it would game the verification count.
- A project-local configuration workaround: insufficient because the current validator and report status domain do not represent documentary compliance.

### Additional context

The current verifier can correctly admit a canonical FAIL with every documentary scenario marked UNTESTED, but native status then blocks archive. A first-class evidence type would preserve that fail-closed behavior while allowing genuinely documentation-only changes to close without inventing runtime claims.

title: bug(sdd): fresh managed remediation selection is rejected as stale
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

The Gentle Pi managed SDD remediation path rejects a fresh, provider-current remediation selection before launching the remediation agent:

```text
Stale remediation selection; refresh native status
```

This occurred after an SDD apply attempt failed independent verification and native settlement recorded the failed evidence. The candidate needed a bounded correction for two concrete verifier findings, but managed remediation could not start. The candidate remained preserved, with no correction edit, remediation token, or settlement produced.

A fresh remediation launch and one bounded corrective retry both failed before edits even though each used the exact current native generation, objective, revision, failed-evidence revision, and selected paths supplied for that launch.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In a consumer worktree, run an SDD apply phase through the managed `pi-contributor/main` integration.
2. Let independent verification fail with concrete findings and settle the apply attempt as failed, producing a native failed-evidence revision.
3. Request remediation for the preserved candidate and obtain fresh native status.
4. Launch the managed `sdd-remediate` agent using the current change name, canonical worktree, failed-evidence revision, remediation attempt metadata, and exact current selected paths/inventory.
5. Observe that pre-launch admission rejects the request with `Stale remediation selection; refresh native status` before the agent can edit.
6. Refresh native state and repeat once with the newly returned exact current generation, objective, revision, failed evidence, and selection.
7. Observe the same pre-edit rejection.

No private repository contents or infrastructure access are required. A synthetic failed candidate with two selected correction paths should be sufficient to exercise the admission boundary.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: a remediation launch bound to the exact current native status and failed-evidence revision is admitted, and the remediation agent receives the bounded correction scope.

Actual: managed pre-launch admission reports the current selection as stale on both the initial launch and one fresh corrective retry. No remediation agent runs, no correction token is issued, and the valid failed candidate remains blocked from correction.

### gentle-pi version

2.5.0 (`pi-contributor/main`, commit `8ec0f98b`)

title: feat: make SDD user-owned and support an RDD-only Gentle Pi configuration
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Gentle Pi is becoming increasingly attractive as an RDD provider for Pi, especially now that Organic RDD keeps review after implementation and makes review explicitly user-owned.

However, users who primarily want RDD still inherit a broader behavioral surface that includes SDD/OpenSpec assets and other orchestration concerns.

There is a useful middle ground:

- let the model/user own the implementation strategy;
- use RDD only as a post-candidate verification layer;
- keep SDD available, but only when explicitly enabled or requested;
- avoid requiring unrelated workflow policy just to obtain RDD.

This seems especially relevant now that Gentle AI itself treats SDD as optional, while RDD is deliberately opt-in and independently controlled.

A user should be able to build a minimal Pi harness such as:

model → Pi/tools → candidate → freeze → RDD → receipt/evidence

without also adopting SDD as an implicit routing option.

### Proposed outcome

Make SDD explicitly user-owned and allow RDD to be used independently from the rest of the Gentle Pi behavioral stack.

Ideally, this could be achieved through one or more of these approaches:

### 1. Explicit SDD switch

For example:

/gentle:sdd-mode status
/gentle:sdd-mode enable
/gentle:sdd-mode disable

When disabled:

- natural-language routing must not autonomously select SDD;
- task size or risk must not override the user's decision;
- SDD assets/instructions should not be injected into the active context;
- RDD must continue to work normally;
- only the user should be able to change the setting.

### 2. RDD-focused minimal profile

For example, a profile equivalent to:

- RDD: ON
- SDD: OFF
- Strict TDD: OFF
- Persona: neutral/off where possible
- Background subagents: OFF
- Automatic model routing: inherit/default
- Skills: optional
- Engram: optional

### 3. Optional standalone RDD extension/provider

If the architecture allows it, exposing the Pi RDD integration as an independent package would be even more composable.

Conceptually:

Pi
└── RDD provider
    ├── candidate freeze
    ├── 4R review
    └── receipt/evidence

The goal is not to remove SDD.

The goal is to make the separation explicit:

- implementation strategy → model/user owned
- specification workflow → optional SDD
- post-candidate verification → optional RDD
- delivery authority → repository/human owned

This would preserve the full Gentle Pi workflow for users who want it, while also making RDD reusable as a standalone verification capability.

### Alternatives considered

A few alternatives were considered:

1. Keep the current setup and simply avoid using SDD.
   - This is not equivalent to disabling it, because SDD can still remain part of the behavioral/routing surface.

2. Install Gentle Pi and rely on neutral persona + disabled background subagents.
   - This reduces orchestration, but still does not provide a clear user-owned "SDD = off" policy.

3. Reimplement RDD independently outside Gentle Pi.
   - This would provide the desired minimalism, but would duplicate logic that already exists in Gentle AI and fragment the ecosystem.

4. Remove SDD entirely.
   - This is not the goal of this request. SDD can still be useful for users who explicitly want specification-driven workflows.

The preferred direction is therefore composability: keep SDD available, but make it explicitly optional, while allowing RDD to be consumed independently.

### Additional context

This request is motivated by the recent direction of Gentle AI toward Organic RDD and optional SDD.

It also seems related to the ongoing work separating SDD-owned and non-SDD assets in Gentle Pi.

The core idea is:

- implementation strategy should remain model/user owned;
- SDD should be optional and explicitly enabled;
- RDD should remain a post-candidate verification layer;
- users should be able to adopt RDD without adopting unrelated workflow policy.

This would also make RDD more reusable for custom Pi setups and multimodel harnesses.

title: feat(models): add ordered fallback chains per agent role on provider quota exhaustion
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Gentle Pi can assign a model and thinking level to each agent role, but it does not provide a role-scoped fallback when that model's provider exhausts its credits or quota.

The existing #882 request covers opt-in fallback for the primary orchestrator. It does not cover subagent roles such as exploration, implementation, or verification. A single global fallback would be too broad because these roles have different cost, capability, and reasoning requirements.

### Proposed outcome

Allow each configured agent role/profile to define a primary model plus one or more ordered fallback models.

When the primary provider explicitly reports credit or quota exhaustion, Gentle Pi should retry the same work unit with the next configured fallback for that role, preserving the role-specific thinking level and task context.

Example configuration shape:

```json
{
  "sdd-apply": {
    "model": "provider-a/primary-model",
    "thinking": "high",
    "fallbacks": [
      "provider-b/fallback-model"
    ]
  }
}
```

The runtime should expose the fallback reason and the model that completed the work in its status/result evidence. If every fallback is exhausted, it should stop with an actionable failure rather than silently changing routing.

### Alternatives considered

- Manual model switching and rerunning the task: interrupts long workflows and loses automatic role routing.
- One global fallback chain: does not preserve the distinct requirements of exploration, implementation, and verification roles.
- The primary-orchestrator fallback proposed in #882: useful, but insufficient for subagent roles.

### Additional context

This feature would complement #882 rather than duplicate it. The requested scope is per-role fallback routing for provider credit or quota exhaustion.

title: bug(skill-registry): recursive skill watcher crashes Pi with uncaughtException ENOENT when a watched skill subdirectory is removed
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

Pi exits with an `uncaughtException` while a command regenerates a skill subdirectory. The skill-registry extension (`extensions/skill-registry.ts`) opens recursive `fs.watch` handles on every user skill root, and Node's recursive watch can emit an `'error'` event (ENOENT scandir) when a watched subdirectory is removed mid-rescan. The extension never attaches an `'error'` listener, and Node's EventEmitter rethrows an `'error'` event with no listener as an `uncaughtException` that kills the whole process, taking any running command/session with it.

Observed crash:

```
pi exiting due to uncaughtException:
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, scandir '<home>/.agents/skills/<skill>/storage'
    at readdirSync (node:fs:1590:26)
    at #watchFolder (node:internal/fs/recursive_watch:111:21)
    at FSWatcher.<anonymous> (node:internal/fs/recursive_watch:191:26)
    at FSWatcher.emit (node:events:519:28)
    at FSWatcher._handle.onchange (node:internal/fs/watchers:222:12)
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install gentle-pi 2.5.0 with Pi 0.85.1.
2. Start Pi in the TUI — `session_start` starts the skill-registry watcher over the user skill roots (for example `<home>/.agents/skills`).
3. While Pi is running, run a command that removes and recreates a subdirectory of a skill (observed with a skill that regenerates generated docs into `<skill>/storage/`).
4. Pi exits with the `uncaughtException` above.

Deterministic variant: the failure is an `'error'` event emitted on a recursive `FSWatcher` with zero listeners. Emitting any `'error'` on such a watcher reproduces the process kill; Node rethrows unhandled `'error'` events.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: a transient recursive-watch error must not kill Pi; the watcher stays best-effort, matching the extension's existing `catch` blocks.

Actual: Pi dies with `pi exiting due to uncaughtException`; any command in progress is lost and the session must be restarted.

### gentle-pi version

2.5.0

### Pi version

0.85.1

### Operating system

Linux

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
pi exiting due to uncaughtException:
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, scandir '<home>/.agents/skills/<skill>/storage'
    at readdirSync (node:fs:1590:26)
    at #watchFolder (node:internal/fs/recursive_watch:111:21)
    at FSWatcher.<anonymous> (node:internal/fs/recursive_watch:191:26)
    at FSWatcher.emit (node:events:519:28)
    at FSWatcher._handle.onchange (node:internal/fs/watchers:222:12) {
  errno: -2,
  code: 'ENOENT',
  syscall: 'scandir',
  path: '<home>/.agents/skills/<skill>/storage'
}
```

title: review: an acknowledged capture reports native-operation-failed while the native state is approved
body:
## What happens

The first acknowledged capture (`gentle_review_capture`, or `gentle_review_capture_group`, with `reviewerRunAcknowledged: true`) returns:

```json
{"outcome":"native-operation-failed","mutation_performed":false,"mutation_outcome":"partial_unknown","next_action":"resolve-native-operation-failure"}
```

while the native review state is already final: one fresh STATUS call on the same lineage reports `state: "approved"` and offers `review.acknowledge-approved`. The same envelope reports `prepared_reviewers: 4, submitted_reviewers: 3`.

Observed on all four reviews run today — four different lineages, tiers medium and high, on both the single-slot and the four-slot path.

## Why it matters

The envelope asks the operator to resolve a native failure that does not exist, and acting on it invites replaying a capture that already landed.

## Evidence

- `extensions/gentle-ai.ts:4730-4759` — emits `native-operation-failed`; a non-`unknown` mutation outcome gets `next_action: "resolve-native-operation-failure"`.
- `extensions/gentle-ai.ts:4762-4773` — reconciliation runs only when `mutationOutcome === "unknown"` exactly, or when the error explicitly asks for `review.status`. `partial_unknown` does not match.
- `extensions/gentle-ai.ts:5898-5904` — group progress maps partial submission plus uncertainty to `mutation_outcome: "partial_unknown"`.
- `extensions/gentle-ai.ts:5118-5149` — `reconcileUnknownReviewCaptureFailure` performs one target-scoped STATUS call and returns `reconciled`; `lib/review-last-event-controller.ts:15-31` makes reconciliation a single probe that never retries the capture.
- `lib/review-host-relay.ts:86-103` and `651-661` — a launched submission failure defaults to mutation outcome `unknown`; only a typed admission refusal is classified as `none`.

## Hypothesis (not proven from source)

`partial_unknown` falls outside the reconciliation predicate at `4762-4773`, so a partially admitted group skips the single STATUS probe and reports a failure that the native state contradicts. The runtime sequence "3 of 4 admitted then a false failure" is consistent with this and is not proven by reading alone.

## Expected

`partial_unknown` reconciles like `unknown`: one target-scoped STATUS probe, and when that STATUS reports a final state, return its continuation instead of the failure envelope.

title: review: a queued consent binding is returned as the next START result
body:
## What happens

`gentle_review` with operation `start` and `input {"mode":"ordinary"}` does not always create the lineage. It returns an envelope whose `operation` is `answer-consent` with a binding id that was never shown to the human, and no lineage is created. Retrying `start` with a fresh `idempotencyKey` succeeds — and each retry appears to consume one queued entry, so a backed-up session can need several attempts before one is accepted.

Observed four times today in one repository, twice in a row for a single candidate.

## Why it looks like queued state

A fresh idempotency key with identical content behaved differently from the previous key on the same candidate, which points at pending consent state keyed per candidate view rather than at the input itself.

## Evidence

- `extensions/gentle-ai.ts:4603-4614` — emits `outcome: "consent-binding-stale"` with `native_invocation_attempted: false`.
- `extensions/gentle-ai.ts:4374-4379` — pending bindings live in the session map plus a `byBinding` index.
- `extensions/gentle-ai.ts:4390-4396` and `4405-4414` — `consume`/`expire` remove the entry and record its stale disposition.
- `extensions/gentle-ai.ts:6729-6743` — a new consent-required START mints a fresh UUID binding.
- `extensions/gentle-ai.ts:6737-6740` — discards prior pending entries sharing the candidate-view token.

## Expected

A START that returns a consent envelope returns the binding the human will answer. A stale queued binding is never the answer to a fresh START: if the candidate already has a pending consent, the new START should reuse it or replace it atomically.

## Honest limit

I could not confirm from source that one retry drains exactly one entry. The per-retry behaviour is field observation, not a traced mechanism.

title: feat(guardrails): own Moshi approval mirroring for guarded commands
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

gentle-pi owns guarded-command confirmation, the request ID, and the Pi event that describes a waiting or resolved permission. The official Moshi Pi extension has PermissionRequest envelope builders but does not subscribe to that event.

piQuota currently adds this missing bridge. That puts approval behavior in a quota monitor, which is the wrong ownership boundary.

### Proposed outcome

Move the Moshi approval adapter into gentle-pi. It should mirror the existing permission lifecycle without changing approval authority: no auto-approval, no synthetic terminal input, no secret expansion, and the terminal remains the fallback.

When Pi exposes a scoped working-visibility lease, gentle-pi should acquire it synchronously before its native confirmation dialog and release it in finally. This keeps the prompt visually stable without letting an observer extension overwrite global UI state.

piQuota can then return to quota and Usage reporting only.

### Alternatives considered

Keep the adapter in piQuota: works structurally but couples quota reporting to permission policy.

Hide the indicator from `ui_prompt_start`/`ui_prompt_end`: rejected because those events are best-effort observers and current Pi APIs cannot restore an unobservable prior state safely.

Inject terminal keys or use undocumented daemon endpoints: rejected because they bypass or weaken the human-confirmation boundary.

### Additional context

Live diagnosis found the phone action reaches the daemon but screen verification is unreliable while Pi redraws. The proposed change only fixes ownership and prepares the correct pre-confirm integration point; it does not claim to bypass daemon verification.

AI-assisted draft, reviewed by @J3pf.

title: bug(agents): model routing breaks block scalar descriptions and empties them
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

On every session start, gentle-pi rewrites agent model routing into the wrong position inside an agent definition whose `description` is a YAML block scalar. The `model:` key lands between the `description: >` header and its indented continuation lines, so the description parses as an empty string and its text is folded into the model value.

Observed on a real run against a project whose `.agents/agents/` set declares `description: >` in 18 of 18 files:

```yaml
description: >
model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash
  Adversarial review lens evaluating security risks, data exposure, and permission flaws.
```

which parses as:

```
description: ''
model: 'deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash Adversarial review lens evaluating security risks, data exposure, and permission flaws.'
```

Every discovered agent definition using a block scalar description is silently left with an empty description and a garbage model id.

This is not limited to one adapter. The packaged agent sets use `description: >` as follows: antigravity 18/18, claude 13/19, cursor 10/16, kimi 10/16, kiro 13/19.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Define an agent whose frontmatter uses a block scalar description:

```yaml
---
name: review-risk
description: >
  Adversarial review lens evaluating security risks.
subagent: true
---
```

2. Give it a routing entry, e.g. through `/gentle:models` or a `model_profiles` entry in `.pi/subagents.json`.
3. Start a Pi session in that project.

Actual result: the definition is rewritten at the next session start into the broken frontmatter above.

Root cause in `extensions/gentle-ai.ts` (`main` @ `db788aef`):

```ts
const descriptionIndex = lines.findIndex((line) => line.startsWith("description:"));
const insertIndex = descriptionIndex >= 0 ? descriptionIndex + 1 : Math.min(1, lines.length);
lines.splice(insertIndex, 0, ...toInsert);
```

`descriptionIndex + 1` is the first line of the block scalar, not the first key after it. The same logic existed a second time in `lib/sdd-preflight.ts` as `updateAgentFrontmatterRouting`.

The trigger is `pi.on("session_start")` -> `applySavedModelConfig` -> `applyModelConfig`. It does not require a model change.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected:

Routing keys are inserted after the block scalar's continuation lines, and a definition that already carries correct routing is left untouched.

Actual:

Routing keys are inserted inside the block scalar, so the description becomes empty and its text is folded into the model value on every session start.

### gentle-pi version

2.5.0 (main @ db788aef)

### Pi version

0.85.1

### Operating system

Other

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
$ git diff .agents/agents/sdd-init.md
@@ -2,8 +2,8 @@
 name: sdd-init
 role: "SDD Stack Initializer"
 description: >
-  Initialize SDD context, detect project stack, testing capabilities, and bootstrap persistence backend.
 model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash
+  Initialize SDD context, detect project stack, testing capabilities, and bootstrap persistence backend.
 subagent: true
```

Parsed with PyYAML:

```text
description repr: ''
model       repr: 'deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash Initialize SDD context, detect project stack, testing capabilities, and bootstrap persistence backend.'
```

Against the current implementation, a 12-case regression suite fails 5 cases. A local fix on branch `fix/agent-frontmatter-block-scalar` consolidates both writers into `lib/agent-frontmatter.ts` and inserts routing keys after the block scalar continuation lines.

title: bug(review): orphaned candidate-view registration strands active lineage
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.

### Problem

During a high-risk native review, grouped reviewer materialization failed because an active candidate view lost its Git worktree registration. The ownership sidecar remained, while the candidate root's `.git` pointer and `.git/worktrees/<candidate-id>` registration were absent. The lineage remained in `reviewing`, and both capture and bound status returned only a generic `ls-files` failure with no provider-owned recovery or terminal route.

This correctly fails closed, but strands the active lineage and leaves the operator without a safe executable continuation. Manual `git worktree prune/remove/repair` or deleting the sidecar is unsafe because it bypasses ownership proof.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On macOS, enable RDD and create a high-risk current-changes candidate in a temporary linked Git worktree.
2. Start an ordinary review and reach grouped reviewer materialization.
3. Observe or simulate, in an isolated fixture, loss of the candidate view's `.git` pointer and shared `.git/worktrees/<candidate-id>` registration while preserving its owner sidecar and active lineage.
4. Run grouped capture, then one bound status reconciliation.
5. Observe that both fail with the generic candidate-view Git error and no recovery/terminal transition.

The production incident was observed once; the exact external remover is unknown. Another candidate view in the same repository remained healthy.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: Candidate-view ownership artifacts remain consistent. If registration is missing, the facade emits an actionable missing-registration diagnostic and offers a provider-owned recovery or terminal route while retaining conservative ownership evidence.

Actual: The owner sidecar remained, the Git registration disappeared, grouped capture failed, bound status returned the same generic error, and the lineage remained `reviewing` without a safe continuation.

macOS

title: bug(installer): Windows EPERM renaming the staging bundle leaves .gentle-ai empty
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

On Windows, `publishBundle` in `scripts/gentle-ai-installer.mjs` renames the staging bundle to `.gentle-ai/v<pin>` exactly once, with no retry. When that rename fails, the `finally` block removes the staging directory, so the install ends with `.gentle-ai/` completely empty: the package source is updated and `node_modules` is complete, but the pinned package-local Gentle AI binary is gone and every native review call is unavailable.

The rename fails with `EPERM` because the installer executes the freshly built binary immediately before publishing it (`assertExactGentleAiVersion` runs `<staging>/gentle-ai.exe --version`), and on Windows a directory rename returns `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` while any file inside still has an open handle (the image handle of the just-executed exe, plus real-time scanner activity on a brand-new unsigned binary). Node maps that to `EPERM`.

This is a different step from #360, which reports `EBUSY` inside `safeRemoveDirectory` during staging cleanup. Same root class (transient Windows handle locks in the publish path, tolerated nowhere), different function and different errno. #360 does not mention `publishBundle`, `rename`, or `EPERM`.

Impact: a package install or update reports failure after it already moved the checkout, leaving a half-updated package with no native CLI. There is no supported fallback on Windows: `GENTLE_AI_RELEASE_ASSETS` publishes darwin and linux assets only, and `isWindowsGoSumdbSourceTarget` forces win32 x64/arm64 through the Go source build, so the failing path is the only path.

### Steps to reproduce

Setup: Windows 11 x64, Pi 0.85.1, Node v24.18.0, Go 1.26.4, gentle-pi installed from `git:github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-pi@main`, real-time antivirus enabled, `.gentle-ai/` absent or stale.

1. Run `pi update --extension "git:github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-pi@main"`.
2. Pi resets the clone to `origin/main` and runs `npm install`, whose `postinstall` is `node scripts/install-gentle-ai.mjs`.
3. Observe: the installer reports that it could not install the package-local Gentle AI v2.7.0 binary, with `EPERM: operation not permitted, rename '<pi-packages>/gentle-pi/.gentle-ai/.v2.7.0.staging-XXXX' -> '<pi-packages>/gentle-pi/.gentle-ai/v2.7.0'`, then npm exits with code 1 and Pi reports that its working-tree clean step failed with code 1.
4. Inspect `<pi-packages>/gentle-pi/.gentle-ai/` — it is empty.
5. Re-run `node scripts/install-gentle-ai.mjs` unchanged: same `EPERM` (reproduced twice consecutively, each after a full cold source build).
6. Call `installGentleAi({ rename })` with an injected `rename` that retries the same operation after a short delay: attempt 1 fails with `EPERM`, attempt 2 succeeds, and the bundle publishes with a valid `integrity.json`.

Step 6 is the evidence that the lock is transient and that only the missing retry makes this fatal.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: publishing the built bundle tolerates a transient Windows handle lock — a bounded retry with backoff around `renameFile(stagingDirectory, versionDirectory)` — or the installer avoids renaming a directory that contains a binary it just executed. A failed publish should never leave `.gentle-ai/` with no runtime at all after the checkout was already moved.

Actual: one rename attempt, `EPERM`, staging deleted by the `finally`, `.gentle-ai/` empty, postinstall exits non-zero, and the package update reports failure while the clone is already on the new commit. Recovery requires a manual workaround (injecting a retrying `rename`), because re-running the installer reproduces the same failure.

Suggested direction: wrap the two `renameFile` calls in `publishBundle` in a small bounded retry (for example five attempts with an increasing delay) on win32, and keep failing closed once the budget is exhausted. #360 already asks for retry tolerance on the cleanup side, so one shared helper could cover both steps.

### gentle-pi version

package 2.5.0 at commit `6e4478c04615b0c013a017178dcfefa51579982d` (`main`); pinned runtime `INSTALLER_VERSION = "2.7.0"`

### Pi version

0.85.1

### Operating system

Windows

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
gentle-pi could not install its package-local Gentle AI v2.7.0 binary: EPERM: operation not permitted,
rename '<pi-packages>\gentle-pi\.gentle-ai\.v2.7.0.staging-4S7Kyk' -> '<pi-packages>\gentle-pi\.gentle-ai\v2.7.0'
npm error code 1
npm error path <pi-packages>\gentle-pi
npm error command failed
npm error command C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe /d /s /c node scripts/install-gentle-ai.mjs
Error: working-tree clean step failed with code 1

# Same failure re-running the installer directly, then with an injected retrying rename:
[rename] attempt 1 EPERM: <staging> -> <pi-packages>\gentle-pi\.gentle-ai\v2.7.0
[rename]   staging entries: ["gentle-ai.exe","integrity.json"]
[rename] ok on attempt 2: <staging> -> <pi-packages>\gentle-pi\.gentle-ai\v2.7.0
{"installed":true,"method":"go-sumdb-source-build","seconds":58,"renameAttempts":3}

# Non-fatal and unrelated to the rename, from the same update run (native DLLs held by the running Pi process):
npm warn cleanup [Error: EPERM: operation not permitted, unlink '<pi-packages>\gentle-pi\node_modules\@yuuang\ffi-rs-win32-x64-msvc-y0DsQ1Gh\ffi-rs.win32-x64-msvc.node']
npm warn cleanup [Error: EPERM: operation not permitted, unlink '<pi-packages>\gentle-pi\node_modules\@ff-labs\fff-bin-win32-x64-EVa6YoCa\fff_c.dll']
```

title: feat(ui): add a compact transcript mode for tool activity
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Gentle Pi already includes `quiet-tools` and `pi-pretty`, but completed agent sessions can still be visually dense. Command invocations, tool-result previews, diffs, and code snippets across built-in and package-defined tools can occupy many transcript rows and make the actual agent narrative difficult to scan.

OpenCode presents comparable activity more compactly, which makes long sessions easier to follow. This is a transcript-presentation problem, distinct from reducing the model-visible token count.

### Proposed outcome

Provide a coherent compact transcript mode for Gentle Pi that:

- summarizes completed successful tool activity in a small, scannable representation;
- keeps failures and their bounded diagnostics clearly visible;
- lets the user expand the complete sanitized command, output, diff, or code preview through the existing tool-expansion interaction;
- behaves consistently across built-in tools and Gentle Pi-defined tools without duplicate tool registrations;
- allows users to return to the existing verbose presentation; and
- changes presentation only, without altering the tool data supplied to the model.

The design should reuse the existing `quiet-tools` and `pi-pretty` foundations where possible and identify any transcript surfaces that require upstream Pi support.

### Alternatives considered

- Continue relying only on the existing `quiet-tools` behavior. This improves selected tool results but does not provide one consistent transcript-density policy.
- Integrate RTK. RTK can reduce model-visible command output, but it does not control how Gentle Pi renders commands, tool cards, diffs, or snippets.
- Implement the behavior only in Pi core. Some transcript surfaces may require upstream support, but Gentle Pi can still own its package-specific presentation and define the desired contract.

### Additional context

This request is intentionally separate from Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai#111, which concerns RTK as an optional Gentle AI ecosystem component.

Related prior work: #392 introduced compact rendering for routine Gentle AI command output. This request covers the remaining need for a coherent, user-selectable transcript mode rather than reopening that narrower completed slice.

title: feat(review): opt-in standing auto-grant for RDD consent (global + per-repo)
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

When RDD is already enabled globally, every new review candidate still stops for per-candidate host consent. The session standing permission from #642 is memory-only: it ends on new/resume/fork/quit/process restart, is bound to one session plus one repository identity, and cannot cover unattended or background runs. Users who want RDD always-on in every repository must babysit the consent dialog, otherwise verification stalls and the session blocks until a human returns.

### Proposed outcome

An explicit opt-in standing auto-grant policy for review consent, configured globally with a per-repository override and defaulting to off, mirroring the existing `runtime-guardrails.json` autonomousMode design. When enabled, each fresh validated provider consent envelope is answered `granted` exactly once through the existing answer-consent path, with a visible audit notice per candidate. The provider envelope and its two candidate responses stay intact; the standing grant must never approve verdicts, acknowledge forecasts, authorize maintenance, change delivery policy, or cross repository identities. It must coexist as the mirror of the opt-in always-confirm policy proposed in #925 (the two policies are mutually exclusive).

### Alternatives considered

- Session standing permission (#642): kept as-is for interactive use, but it does not survive session replacement and does not help unattended runs.
- Disabling RDD per clone or globally: removes the independent check entirely; the goal here is always-RDD, not no-RDD.
- Environment variable override: less discoverable and harder to scope per repository than a config-file pair.

### Additional context

Related work: #642 implemented the session-scoped permission (closed); #925 proposes opt-in always-confirm (open) and this request is its mirror. Request prepared against upstream/main around the #933 merge era; observed with gentle-pi package 2.5.0 (source), gentle-ai binary 2.7.1, Pi coding agent 0.85.1, on Linux.
