title: bug(review): select-intended-untracked rejects provider-issued selection binding, blocking START for fully-tracked candidates
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

Native ordinary review cannot START when the candidate has zero untracked files but the repo has a large unrelated untracked inventory (here: 426 files - QA screenshots plus MCP-server logs; candidate = 3 tracked modified files, 352 changed lines). `gentle_review {operation: select-intended-untracked}` with the provider-issued `selectionBinding` and the only honest value (`intendedUntracked: []`, matching the provider's own projection `intended_untracked: []` + precomputed proof) is rejected every time. Effect: the RDD gate blocks delivery with no valid forward route; the ledger/apply side is complete and green (73/73 self-tests).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Repo with committed SDD change artifacts + large unrelated untracked inventory (inventory digest `sha256:a4ea…`, stable across calls - no filesystem churn).
2. Apply a slice touching only tracked files (candidate target `sha256:540a…`).
3. `gentle_review {operation: inspect}` -> `action: start`, `next_transition: {kind: collect, reason_code: intended_untracked_selection_required}`, projection paths = 3 tracked files, `intended_untracked: []`.
4. `gentle_review {operation: select-intended-untracked, selectionBinding: <exact provider-issued bytes>, intendedUntracked: []}` -> rejected (see logs). Retried across fresh inspects with machine-verified bytes (canonical CLI oracle: eligible list byte-identical to `git status` untracked sorted list, 426 entries; escape level and short fields cross-checked).

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: the pre-lineage selection is accepted (empty selection is consistent with the provider's own projection), unblocking START - as the non-empty selection did for a prior lineage whose candidate genuinely contained untracked files.
Actual: deterministic rejection. No lineage is created, no authority burned, no mutation performed in any attempt.

### gentle-pi version

2.5.0

### Pi version

0.85.1

### Operating system

Linux

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
attempts 1-4: {"operation":"select-intended-untracked","status":"blocked",
  "outcome":"intended-untracked-selection-binding-rejected",
  "mutation_performed":false,"mutation_outcome":"none"}
attempt 5 (machine-built bytes, round-trip verified):
  {"operation":"select-intended-untracked","status":"blocked",
  "outcome":"Review capture collectBinding must encode exactly one collect input object",
  ...}
```

Facade-side notes (locally installed gentle-pi source, for triage): the second error is raised by `parseCanonicalReviewCaptureBinding` (`extensions/gentle-ai.ts:5132`); the select handler (`~l5975-5989`) re-negotiates fresh STATUS and byte-compares canonical forms, so a ~22KB/426-entry opaque binding must be echoed byte-perfect through the agent's own tool-call emission - demonstrated slip rate makes this unreliable, and the validator returns no diff-level feedback. Related (different slot/stage): #926. Subagents in this session run on local GLM-5.3 flash (model routing, informational).

title: bug(review): admission reads a reviewer's statement of contract compliance as an inspection failure and refuses a valid result
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

Reviewer artifact admission rejected a lens result because it read the reviewer's **correct description of its own method** as a confession that inspection had failed:

```
reviewer artifact admission incomplete: reviewer evidence reports the candidate could not
be inspected even though inspection.status is "completed"; declare inspection.status:
"unavailable" with a non-empty inspection.reason instead of describing the failure only
in evidence
```

The payload was not degraded. `inspection.status` was `completed` and `inspection.paths` listed all four manifest paths. The reviewer had produced five substantive findings with locations and line numbers. The sentence that appears to have triggered the rejection is the first evidence entry:

> "Inspected all four manifest paths in full from the supplied patch sections only; no working-tree or command access was used."

That is not an inspection failure. It is the reviewer **stating compliance with the contract**, which requires that reviewers inspect only the provider-bound immutable trees and never substitute the live worktree, index or `HEAD`. The admission check appears to pattern-match phrases such as "no working-tree ... access was used" as evidence of non-inspection, so a reviewer is penalised precisely for declaring that it followed the rules.

**It resolved on retry, which localises the cause.** The slot was correctly not consumed. I took a fresh `STATUS`, resubmitted the identical reoffered binding, and the same lens was admitted immediately — the second run simply phrased its evidence differently. So the check is sensitive to reviewer wording rather than to any structured field, which also means it will keep firing at random and is not reproducible on demand.

**Why it is worth fixing rather than tolerating.** The retry costs a full model run, and the guidance in the error is actively wrong for this case: it tells the operator to declare `inspection.status: "unavailable"`, which would discard five valid findings and mark a completed inspection as failed. An operator who follows the message literally degrades a good review.

Neighbouring but distinct: the decoder-strictness family in #820, and the genuine no-shell inspection failure where `inspection.status` really should be `unavailable`. This report is the inverse of that one — a successful inspection misclassified as a failed one.

### Steps to reproduce

Not reliably reproducible on demand, since it depends on reviewer wording. Observed sequence:

1. Start an ordinary review on a four-file candidate (`risk_tier: high`).
2. Capture the lens slots one at a time.
3. One lens returns a well-formed result whose evidence opens by stating that only the supplied patch sections were inspected and that no working-tree or command access was used.
4. Admission refuses it with the message above; the slot is not consumed and the payload is preserved under `.git/gentle-ai/rejected-results/<lineage>/<lens>-<attempt>-<sha>.json`.
5. Fresh `STATUS`, resubmit the identical reoffered binding. The lens is admitted.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: admission decides whether inspection succeeded from the structured `inspection` object — `status`, `paths`, and `reason` — and not from prose in `evidence`. A reviewer that reports `completed` with a full path list and substantive findings is admitted regardless of how it describes its method, and a statement of contract compliance is never read as a failure signal.

Actual: a contract-compliant sentence in `evidence` overrides `inspection.status: "completed"`, the result is refused, a model run is wasted, and the remediation the message suggests would destroy five valid findings.

### gentle-pi version

2.5.0

### Pi version

0.85.1

### Operating system

Linux

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
Error: reviewer artifact admission incomplete: reviewer evidence reports the candidate
could not be inspected even though inspection.status is "completed"; declare
inspection.status: "unavailable" with a non-empty inspection.reason instead of describing
the failure only in evidence: the rejected admission did not consume the lens slot, so
re-run the lens and invoke gentle-ai review capture-result again on the same lineage with
a result that echoes the binding's top-level subject_hash [invalid_request]

inspection: {"status":"completed","paths":[ ...four manifest paths... ]}
evidence[0]: "Inspected all four manifest paths in full from the supplied patch sections
              only; no working-tree or command access was used."
```

title: feat(agents): show task labels in the Agents overlay
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

The `/gentle:agents` overlay shows the agent name and elapsed time but omits the existing task label. When multiple tasks use the same agent, users cannot distinguish their purpose at a glance without opening their threads.

`TaskRecord.label` already describes the delegated work, and the legacy agent card already displays it. Showing it in the overlay would improve visibility of delegated work without introducing new commands or runtime behavior.

### Proposed outcome

Append the existing nonempty task label to the subagent row:

```text
Subagent explore · Map modules
Subagent explore · Review tests
```

- Preserve the existing `Subagent <agent-name>` prefix and row-based task selection.
- Omit the separator when the label is empty.
- Retain existing width clipping, including long Unicode labels.
- Do not change task execution, permissions, persistence, or review behavior.

### Alternatives considered

Opening each task thread reveals its purpose but interrupts scanning. Giving each task a different agent name would confuse the agent role with the task description. Reusing the existing label avoids adding new metadata or commands.

### Additional context

A small implementation has been prepared separately in `lib/agents-view.ts` with focused coverage in `tests/agents-view.test.ts`: 40 additions and 1 deletion across two files.

Validation:
- 30 focused Agents view tests passed, including distinct labels, label clicks, empty labels, and Unicode clipping.
- Typecheck ratchet passed with no regressions against 205 recorded diagnostics.
- Independent verification found no blocking findings; native review was approved.

Known limitation: existing whole-row clipping can hide elapsed time sooner when a label is long. No interactive terminal test or full-suite run is claimed.

This request is limited to displaying existing labels; it does not propose a new status dashboard or agent runtime.

title: feat(shell): show effective RDD ON/OFF state in Status
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Gentle Shell provides an at-a-glance Status area, but users would benefit from an explicit indication of whether Receipt-Driven Development (RDD) is enabled for their current context. Without this, it is difficult to tell whether RDD is active without consulting configuration or requesting a separate status check.

### Proposed outcome

Add a compact RDD indicator to the fullscreen right-hand Status panel and to the regular/narrow-terminal status presentation:

- `RDD: ON` when RDD is effectively enabled for the current context.
- `RDD: OFF` when it is explicitly disabled.
- `RDD: ?` (or `Unknown`) when the effective state cannot be determined. Do not present unavailable information as OFF.

The indicator should reflect the authoritative effective runtime state, including applicable configuration overrides, rather than merely detecting that a skill or package is installed. Refresh it when that state or the active context changes.

This is a read-only visibility feature: displaying the indicator must not enable or disable RDD, start a review, request review consent, or mutate project state. ON should mean enabled, not imply that a review is currently running, approved, or that a delivery gate has passed.

Use a readable text label, with optional theme-aware color, so the distinction is not conveyed by color alone.

### Alternatives considered

Manually inspecting configuration or asking for RDD status each time: possible, but less convenient than an always-visible indicator alongside the other session status information.

A dedicated status command alone would not provide the requested at-a-glance visibility.

### Additional context

The request is specifically for the Gentle Shell UI maintained in gentle-pi, regardless of whether authoritative RDD state is provided by the underlying Gentle AI runtime.

Related but different: #715 concerns extension-status visibility on narrow terminals. This proposal asks for the RDD state itself to be exposed, while retaining a usable representation in both sidebar and bottom-status layouts.

No implementation is attached; this is a feature proposal.

title: bug(review): Anthropic-backed reviewer models are refused by a provider policy filter; the refusal is reported as a generic transport failure
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

The `review-readability` lens fails **reproducibly** with an upstream policy refusal:

```
This request was blocked as it seems to violate Anthropic's Terms of Service
restrictions on reverse engineering or duplicating model outputs
```

Two attempts, with a fresh `STATUS` between them, identical outcome. The lineage cannot reach a terminal receipt, because one of its four required lenses can never be captured.

**The candidate is not the cause, and I can show it rather than assert it.** In the same lineage, over the same frozen candidate, the risk and resilience lenses were captured successfully. Only readability is refused. Whatever trips the upstream policy filter therefore lives in the readability lens prompt, not in the reviewed code. For the record the candidate is mundane: a test file asserting that a CI workflow declares a typecheck step, plus that workflow. No prompts, no model outputs, no reverse-engineering content of any kind.

**Why this is not #863.** That issue describes an *intermittent* upstream refusal that is mapped to `pi-host-relay-transport-failure`, where resubmitting the identical binding later succeeds. This one is different on both axes: the message is a distinct, explicit policy block rather than a generic transport failure, and it is reproducible rather than transient. They may well share a fix — a reason code that names upstream policy refusals as a category — but they are not the same observation, and #863's "just resubmit" guidance does not help here.

**Consequence, which is the part worth fixing.** There is no known workaround. A four-lens review where one lens is structurally unable to run has no terminal state, and the work is complete and verified but unreceipted. In my case the owner chose to deliver the commit without a receipt rather than leave a verified CI-protection fix unshipped. That is the failure mode I would most want closed: the review system pushing a careful operator toward shipping unreviewed, because the alternative is shipping nothing.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On any ordinary candidate, start a review that provisions the four-lens group.
2. Capture the group, or capture slots individually after a fresh `STATUS`.
3. Observe risk and resilience admit normally.
4. Observe `review-readability` fail with the policy refusal above.
5. Take a fresh `STATUS` and resubmit the verbatim binding for that lens. It fails identically.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: the readability lens prompt does not trip an upstream policy filter. Failing that, the refusal is surfaced under its own reason code, distinct from a transport failure, and the lifecycle offers a documented route — a degraded receipt recording that the lens was unavailable, or an explicit operator acknowledgement — so a lineage is not left permanently unclosable.

Actual: the lens is refused reproducibly, the refusal carries no reason code of its own, and the lineage has no terminal state. The only available choices are to ship without a receipt or not to ship.

2.5.0

### Pi version

0.85.1

Linux

title: bug(review): targeted validator subagent is sometimes spawned without a shell, so it can never inspect the frozen candidate
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

The targeted validator subagent is sometimes spawned **without a shell tool**. Since its whole job is to inspect the immutable frozen trees by running `gentle-ai review inspect-candidate`, it then cannot inspect anything, and returns:

```
targeted validation is inconclusive: original_criteria inspection.status reports the
immutable candidate could not be inspected (No shell was available in this turn, so
'gentle-ai review inspect-candidate' could not be run...)
```

The mirrored contract handles this correctly on the host side — "a validator that cannot inspect the immutable trees produced no verdict: surface one blocked human decision and submit nothing" — and indeed the bounded correction attempt is **not** consumed. So this is not a correctness bug in the guard. It is a provisioning bug: a subagent is being launched without the one capability its task requires, and the failure is only discovered after a model run.

**This is intermittent, not deterministic, and that matters.** On the same repository and the same pairing I have both outcomes:

- lineage with a deterministic finding: targeted validation **ran and returned a verdict** (shell was present).
- lineage with an inferential finding that had already passed a refuter batch: **no shell**, inconclusive.

That second data point is worth stating explicitly because it **refutes a plausible-sounding hypothesis** I held for two sessions and wrote down before testing it: that targeted validation fails for deterministic findings (no refuter batch) and succeeds for inferential ones. It does not. Evidence class is not the discriminator; shell availability in the spawned subagent is. Anyone triaging #924 alongside this may hit the same false lead.

**The pattern is broader than the validator.** In the same runtime I have observed other subagents launched without shell. The most damaging case was an exploration agent that, lacking `git`, produced diff statistics by reading planning documents instead — and reported them as measurements. They were wrong by a wide margin, and the only reason it was caught is that the parent re-measured with `git`. A subagent silently degrading from "measure" to "guess from prose" is worse than one that fails loudly, which is what makes the validator's honest `inconclusive` the better behavior of the two.

### Steps to reproduce

Not reliably reproducible on demand, since it depends on how the subagent is provisioned. Observed sequence:

1. Drive an ordinary review to `correction_required` on any candidate.
2. Declare the correction plan with the working tree intact; apply the bounded edit.
3. Fresh `STATUS` reoffers the targeted-validation slot; submit the verbatim binding.
4. Sometimes the validator returns a verdict. Sometimes it returns the inconclusive result above, naming the absent shell.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: either the targeted validator is always spawned with the shell capability its task requires, or the missing capability is detected **before** the model run and surfaced as a provisioning error, so no run is spent and the operator is told what is missing rather than that validation was "inconclusive".

Actual: the subagent runs without a shell, cannot execute the inspection command it is instructed to run, and returns an inconclusive verdict. The lineage has no forward route; the only escape is to abandon it and open a fresh lineage over the already-corrected tree.

### gentle-pi version

2.5.0

### Pi version

0.85.1

### Operating system

Linux

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
targeted validation is inconclusive: original_criteria inspection.status reports the
immutable candidate could not be inspected (No shell was available in this turn, so
'gentle-ai review inspect-candidate' could not be run)
```

title: bug(review): targeted validator result decoder rejects proof_refs, a field the provider emits in its own validation_request
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

The targeted validator's result decoder rejects `proof_refs` with:

```
decode provider targeted validator result: json: unknown field "proof_refs"
```

This is a **different decoder and a different code path** from #820, which covers `decode reviewer result` for the `reviewer/v1` schema. Filing separately for that reason; the two share a failure mode (strict decoding via `DisallowUnknownFields` against a payload the provider's own prompt permits) but not a fix site.

What makes this one sharper than generic schema drift: `proof_refs` is not an invented field. The provider itself carries it in `validation_request.fix_findings[].proof_refs` when it asks for targeted validation. It also appears as a finding key in reviewer payloads on the same pairing — the artifact attached to #820 has findings whose keys are `id`, `claim`, `severity`, `evidence_class`, `causal_disposition`, `location`, `proof_refs`. So the same field name travels through the provider's own request and through reviewer results, yet the targeted-validator result decoder treats it as unknown.

**Stated limit of that evidence.** Strict decoding stops at the first unknown field, and the reviewer payload above was refused for a different key (`paths_note`). So I cannot prove from that artifact alone that `proof_refs` is accepted by the reviewer decoder. What I can state is that the provider emits `proof_refs` in its own `validation_request`, and that the validator result decoder then refuses it.

The cost is that the correction path cannot close. A targeted validation that cannot return a verdict leaves the lineage in `correction_required` with no forward route, which is the same end state as #926 and #924 but reached through a third cause. In this repository no lineage has ever completed a correction cycle, and this is one of the two reasons why.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Drive an ordinary review to `correction_required` with at least one finding carrying `proof_refs` in the provider's `validation_request.fix_findings[]`.
2. Declare the correction plan with the working tree intact, apply the bounded edit to exactly the corroborated files.
3. Take a fresh `STATUS`; it reoffers the targeted-validation slot.
4. Submit the verbatim collect binding for that slot.
5. Observe the decode failure above. The correction attempt is **not** consumed, so the lineage neither advances nor burns its one bounded correction.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: the targeted validator result decoder accepts `proof_refs`, since the provider emits that field in the corresponding `validation_request`, and returns a verdict that lets the correction cycle close.

Actual: the decoder rejects the field as unknown before any verdict is produced; the lineage stays in `correction_required` with no forward route.

### gentle-pi version

2.5.0

### Pi version

0.85.1

### Operating system

Linux

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
decode provider targeted validator result: json: unknown field "proof_refs"
```

body:
### Before submitting

### Problem

When gentle-pi and pi-taskflow are installed together, Taskflow's delegation instructions can steer the assistant away from Gentle Agents. The Gentle Agents overlay opens with Alt+A or /gentle:agents, but tasks delegated through the other system are not visible there. This makes a working panel look misconfigured.

This report concerns delegation routing and visibility, not a demonstrated general incompatibility between the packages.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use Pi 0.85.1 on Windows with gentle-pi 2.5.0 and pi-taskflow 0.3.0-beta.1.2 installed as separate packages.
2. Ask the assistant to delegate work. Inspect the Taskflow instruction quoted below, which directs all delegation to Taskflow rather than subagent_run.
3. Open Alt+A or /gentle:agents. In our session, both opened but the Gentle task list was empty; agent discovery worked (24 definitions).
4. Remove pi-taskflow from the active package configuration and restart Pi.
5. Launch a read-only background task explicitly through Gentle's subagent_run using gentle-ai-explore.
6. The user confirmed that the task appeared in Alt+A and completed successfully.

The explicit native-agent test succeeded. We did not capture a Taskflow run ID or perform a controlled comparison of the same task through both runners before disabling Taskflow.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: Clear guidance about which runner the panel monitors, and ideally a warning or coexistence guidance when another installed extension instructs the assistant to replace Gentle's delegation tools.

Actual: The panel opens normally but remains empty when no native Gentle tasks have been launched, while Taskflow supplies an instruction to use its own runner for all delegation. This led to unnecessary troubleshooting of agent installation and the shortcut.

Suggested improvement: Document the visibility boundary and competing delegation instructions, or detect this combination and explain it to the user. No claim that the panel should automatically track every third-party runner.

title: feat(review): make the committed-range base-ref path self-describing for RDD
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues. This report overlaps **#874** (unroutable `external.select_base_ref` binding), **#695** (missing committed-range recipe), **#654** (acknowledge loses the committed-only baseRef selector), **#893** (relay rejects its own binding), and **#748** (consent prompt lifetime). I filed it anyway because #874 covers only the mechanical half; dedupe at triage if you prefer one thread.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

Under RDD, the committed-range review path has **no self-describing route**. The agent is told "the candidate needs a base ref" but not which operation resolves it, which value is valid, or in what order to review versus commit. Every dead-end costs a full session, and the only way through today is to reverse-engineer the route from provider output.

This is the friction log from one session that did eventually close a full review (tier `high`, 4 lenses, 141 changed lines) and open PR #930, without local bypasses and without weakening validation. All of it is workflow cost, not review value.

### Steps to reproduce (the actual session, in order)

1. Implement the change in a dirty worktree. Run `gentle_review {"operation":"inspect"}`.
2. Hit `next_transition.kind = "stop"`, `reason_code = "managed_assets_outdated"`. Note: also stops for `inspect` on an unrelated change.
3. Run the emitted `gentle-ai sync --agent pi`. It edits files **outside** the repository (the Pi agent settings, the npm package manifest, a shared SDD skill doc).
4. Follow ordinary delivery order: branch, commit, push, PR. The worktree is now clean.
5. Run `inspect` again. Get `next_transition.kind = "collect"`, `reason_code = "empty_candidate_base_ref_required"`, one binding with `captureOperation = "external.select_base_ref"`, schema `gentle-ai.review-base-ref-selection/v1`, arguments `target_identity`, `projection`, `base_tree`, `candidate_tree` — and no lineage.
6. Try to submit that binding: `gentle_review_capture` / `gentle_review_capture_group` reject it (they accept provider-role runs), and `gentle_review` has no `select-base-ref` operation. The call has no valid continuation.
7. Guess the route: `gentle_review {"operation":"start"}` with a fresh `idempotencyKey` and `input = {"mode":"ordinary","baseRef":"main","committedOnly":true}`. The value `"main"` was derived by hand with `git rev-parse main origin/main` + `git merge-base`, because the provider only echoes tree hashes.
8. The lineage is created and the lifecycle completes: STATUS → 4 materialize lenses → group forecast → acknowledged group run → `approved` → `acknowledge-approved` → `authority: burned`.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected:

- A stop should carry the exact continuation that resolves it: the operation, the accepted input shape, and the accepted value domain.
- A base-ref selection should be routable (like `external.select_intended_untracked`) or derivable by the provider for a clean candidate.
- The mirrored contract and this repo's own PR skill should state the recommended order: implement → review → commit → push → PR, including what to do when the tree is already clean.

Actual:

- The base-ref stop returns a collect binding with no lineage and no `nextStep`/`hint`, so the only way forward is to guess an operation the envelope never names. (Contrast: `managed_assets_outdated` does emit `hint: run gentle-ai sync --agent pi`, and the intended-untracked stop documents its continuation in prose.)
- The binding carries trees only, never a ref name, while every documented route takes a ref name.
- Nothing states that committing first invalidates the working-tree candidate, or how to review a committed range.
- The managed-assets gate blocks the whole lifecycle until a human runs a command that writes outside the repository, and `review mode status` does not surface it.

### Concrete proposals

1. **Route the selection.** Expose a `select-base-ref` operation (mirroring `select-intended-untracked`), or accept an external selection submission through `gentle_review_capture`. Independently, filter **all** `external.*` selections out of `publicReviewCaptureBindings` instead of only `external.select_intended_untracked`, so an unroutable binding can never reach the model as a capture slot.
2. **Make the stop self-describing.** Add `nextStep` to the base-ref stop with the exact START input and a fresh-idempotencyKey note: `{"mode":"ordinary","baseRef":"<ref>","committedOnly":true}`.
3. **Echo a ref name, not only trees.** Include the resolved ref name (and its merge-base) next to `base_tree`/`candidate_tree`, or accept explicit tokens such as `baseRef: "merge-base:origin/main"` for a clean candidate.
4. **Surface the managed-assets gate earlier.** Report it from `review mode status` (or a session-start preflight) with the exact sync command, instead of only from an interactive `inspect`.
5. **State consent resolution explicitly.** A high-risk START returned `operation: "answer-consent"` with `risk_tier: "high"`, `lenses_required: true` and no `gentle-ai.review-integration.consent/v3` envelope, so the caller cannot tell whether consent was host-granted or still required. Return the envelope, or a field such as `consent: "host_granted" | "required"`.
6. **Document the order.** Put the review-versus-commit order in the mirrored contract, the `rdd-defect-workflow` skill, and this repo's PR skill, including the clean-worktree case.

### Evidence (non-sensitive)

```text
inspect (clean worktree):
  next_transition.kind        = collect
  reason_code                 = empty_candidate_base_ref_required
  captureOperation            = external.select_base_ref
  schema                      = gentle-ai.review-base-ref-selection/v1
  arguments                   = target_identity, projection, base_tree, candidate_tree   (no lineage)

start (guessed route, worked):
  input                       = {"mode":"ordinary","baseRef":"main","committedOnly":true}
  result                      = lineage created, state reviewing, risk_tier high,
                                changed_files 6, original_changed_lines 141,
                                correction_budget 71, selected_lenses
                                [review-risk, review-resilience, review-readability, review-reliability]

close:
  group capture               = prepared_reviewers 4, submitted_reviewers 4, state approved
  acknowledge-approved        = authority burned, evidence gentle-ai.review-acknowledged/v1,
                                delivery ordinary-repository-policy
```

### gentle-pi version

2.5.0 (working copy at the PR #930 branch, loaded directly as a Pi package).

### Pi version

0.85.1

- [x] macOS

title: Windows changes watcher leaks orphaned Git processes until RAM is exhausted
body:
### Before submitting
- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem
On Windows, the Gentle Shell working-tree watcher can accumulate orphaned Git for Windows processes until physical memory is exhausted and the operating system becomes unusable.

In one observed session, 193 `git.exe` processes consumed 29.33 GiB of combined working set. Every process used the same Gentle Shell status signature against a large repository rooted at the user profile. Their direct parents had already exited.

### Steps to reproduce
1. On Windows, use a large Git working tree rooted at the user profile or another directory whose status scan exceeds five seconds.
2. Launch Pi from that directory with gentle-pi enabled.
3. Leave the Gentle Shell UI running with its default changes watcher.
4. Inspect Git for Windows processes over several minutes.
5. Observe a new orphaned `mingw64/bin/git.exe` process approximately every five seconds.

The relevant runtime behavior at the reported source commit is:
- `extensions/gentle-shell.ts`: the background watcher runs every 5000 ms.
- `extensions/gentle-shell.ts`: each Git command also has a 5000 ms timeout.
- `lib/shell-changes.ts`: every capture runs `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all -z`.

This timing causes the next poll to begin as the preceding command times out. On Windows, terminating the direct child does not reliably terminate the Git for Windows descendant process tree, so the descendants accumulate.

### Expected and actual behavior
Expected:
A timed-out status scan terminates its complete process tree. Repeated timeouts should trigger bounded backoff or disable the watcher until an explicit refresh.

Actual:
The direct process exits, but a Git for Windows descendant remains alive. Polling continues at the timeout boundary and creates another process every cycle, eventually exhausting RAM.

### gentle-pi version
2.5.0 from source commit `a8e68b0cfcb596a24eeb69e591c94f004a7d831a`

### Pi version
0.85.1

### Operating system
Windows

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)
```text
Observed process count: 193
Combined Git working set: 29.33 GiB
Repeated sanitized command:
git.exe -C <user-home> status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all -z
Direct parent state: exited
Creation cadence: approximately 5 seconds
Executable: <git-install>/mingw64/bin/git.exe
```

title: correction-plan capture rejects provider-issued binding (lineage/target token mismatch)
body:
## Summary
`gentle_review_capture` (correction-plan slot) rejects the exact provider-issued `collectBinding` from a fresh `STATUS`, twice in a row, leaving the lineage stuck in `correction_required` with no valid forward route.

## Repro
1. Ordinary review reaches `correction_required` (2 deterministic BLOCKER/CRITICAL findings, R3-001 + R3-002).
2. Bounded correction applied to exactly the corroborated files; tests green (138 tests, 0 failures).
3. Fresh `STATUS` → reoffers identical `correction_plan_required` slot (`review.capture-correction-plan`, bounds 1..200).
4. Submit the **verbatim** `collectBinding` with `correctionLines: 130` → `capture-binding-rejected`: `collectBinding does not carry one non-empty matching provider lineage and target token`.
5. Repeat 3–4 once more with another fresh `STATUS` → identical rejection.

## Expected vs actual
Expected: the verbatim binding from current `STATUS` is admitted (as reviewer-result bindings are — 4 lineages approved in the same session via the group capture route).
Actual: deterministic rejection; the provider's own emitter and validator disagree, so the lineage has no forward path.

## Evidence
- lineage: `review-44cfd43a4bd9b8c1`
- binding target: `sha256:9e09703758b71edf82ef468021e17c3a51c74594d46799ac781560e15794c6c1`
- expected-revision: `sha256:4a15b7d995be0e88a5d3f11a678c1b45c30cb1b774d7d1e6edc3ba474a3a4bbb`
- request-hash: `sha256:e37cf121b407a7947c4a7bd0935c7f517f3412742af3a08dd000b7d4176b2e6b`
- correctionLines: `130` (bounds min 1 / max 200)
- Note: post-fix `STATUS` reports `target_identity: sha256:a6e8e49e…` with `authority_target_identity: sha256:9e097037…` while the binding still targets the authority identity.

## Hypothesis
The correction-plan slot carries plain `lineage`/`target` arguments while reviewer slots carry `lineageId`/`targetIdentity` artifact subjects; the capture validator appears to look for the reviewer shape and never matches the correction shape. Same session also saw one truncated reviewer payload (transport failure, recovered on retry), so provider-side flakiness is in the area.

## Workaround used
Explicit user-ordered commit documenting non-approved status; lineage left in `correction_required`.

## Env
- gentle-pi 2.5.0 (`Gentleman-Programming/gentle-pi`), Pi coding agent host relay
- Contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, ordinary workspace projection

title: feat(review): add an opt-in always-confirm host authorization policy
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

Users need a persistent policy requiring fresh human authorization before every ordinary review START, including candidates for which the provider does not emit a consent envelope. Existing session standing permission is intentional, but cannot enforce this policy.

### Proposed outcome

- Add an opt-in always-confirm policy.
- Bind host authorization to the current candidate and revalidate it after the human answers.
- Do not reuse session grants while this policy is active.
- Cancellation, unavailable human interaction, or candidate drift must prevent START.
- Preserve provider-issued consent envelopes unchanged; host authorization must not fabricate provider consent.
- Cover consecutive candidates, existing session grants, cancellation, drift, and noninteractive execution with tests.

### Alternatives considered

Revoking session permission does not enforce confirmation for every START. Raw CLI fallback does not enforce the Pi policy. Do not remove the existing optional session-permission feature.

### Additional context

Consent policy and Windows candidate preparation are separate changes. Windows preparation already has issue #775 and merged PR #795.

title: review.capture-validation rejects its own admitted evidence when the corrected finding is deterministic (no refuter batch)
body:
**Package:** gentle-pi, native binary `v2.7.0`
**Runtime:** Pi, contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, projection `workspace`
**Repository:** private (portal-contratos-melilla-v2). All four lineages below are retained and inspectable in `.git/gentle-ai/review-transactions/v2/`.

## Summary

The bounded-review correction route cannot close when the corrected finding's `evidence_class` is `deterministic`. `review.capture-validation` fails at `phase: "preflight"` with `code: "invalid_request"` and `cause: "admitted targeted-validator evidence does not match its request and digests"`, with `mutation_performed: false` and no authority burned.

The same route completes normally when the corrected finding is `inferential`, because an `inferential` finding first runs a refuter batch. The discriminating variable appears to be the presence of an admitted refuter result, not the candidate, the repository, the lens or the correction size.

Net effect: a deterministic BLOCKER/CRITICAL finding can never be closed through the official route. The caller has no available remedy, because the targeted-validator vector is self-contained and executed verbatim.

## Evidence: controlled comparison in one repository, one session, one lens

Lens `review-reliability` in every case, tier `medium`, projection `workspace`, two changed files in each candidate.

| Lineage | Finding | `evidence_class` | Refuter admitted | `capture-validation` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `review-6b96c7491c9e8241` | `R3-guard-unguarded-subscript` | `deterministic` | no | **`invalid_request`** |
| `review-46c6adae44fcb940` | `R3-evidenced-touched-partial-guard` | `inferential` | **yes** | **`approved`** |

Exact failure payload for the deterministic case, received twice, after a fresh bound STATUS, submitting the exact binding STATUS re-offered (byte-identical `request_hash`, `expected_revision` and `target`):

```json
{
  "operation": "gentle_review_capture",
  "status": "blocked",
  "native_failure": {
    "schema": "gentle-ai.review-integration.failure/v2",
    "contract": "gentle-ai.review-integration/v2",
    "operation": "review.capture-validation",
    "phase": "preflight",
    "code": "invalid_request",
    "message": "The negotiated review request is invalid.",
    "mutation_outcome": "not_started",
    "authority_applicability": "not_evaluated",
    "retry_safe": true,
    "replayability": "not_replayable",
    "next_action": "correct_request",
    "cause": "admitted targeted-validator evidence does not match its request and digests"
  },
  "mutation_performed": false
}
```

`next_action: "correct_request"` is not actionable: there is no caller-side field to correct. Per `lib/native-review-cli.ts:2168-2186` Pi executes the provider-rendered argument tokens verbatim, Go materializes its own validator prompt and admits the verdict, and `runtime/review-integration-v2.mjs:1655-1657` forbids `submission` on this vector. A re-serialization or ordering mistake on the Pi side would produce a different, Pi-side error (`gentle-ai.ts:5203-5206`), not this `native_failure`.

Provider-role captures are **not** broken in general: `review.capture-refuter` succeeded first time with the same self-contained vector shape and no `submission`.

## A second, independent finding: the correction plan is only submittable before the fix exists

`gentle_review_capture` with `correctionLines` is accepted while the working tree is untouched, and rejected once the fix is applied:

```json
{
  "status": "blocked",
  "outcome": "capture-binding-rejected",
  "reason": "collectBinding does not carry one non-empty matching provider lineage and target token",
  "mutation_performed": false
}
```

Mechanism: after the edit, STATUS starts publishing `authority_target_identity` separately from the current `target_identity`, and the Pi-side binding matcher requires the `--target` token to match the **current** target, while the provider keeps re-offering a binding bound to the **pre-correction** target. The binding becomes unusable and nothing marks it stale.

Verified in `review-c6ac9eeeef0634c2` (rejected after editing) against `review-6b96c7491c9e8241` and `review-46c6adae44fcb940` (accepted with the tree untouched).

This forces the order *declare the plan first, edit second*. That is fine in itself, but combined with the first finding it means a deterministic finding has no closing path at all.

## What was ruled out

- **Not the `target` asymmetry.** The vector's `--target` carries `correction_target_identity` while `validationRequest.targetIdentity` carries the original target. `extensions/gentle-ai.ts:5211-5213` documents this as intentional. Initially suspected, then discarded.
- **Not caller re-serialization.** The binding is matched by canonical value equality against the provider's own re-offered tokens.
- **Not a transient race.** Two identical submissions after a fresh STATUS produced the identical deterministic rejection.
- **Not `fix_delta_hash`.** It is the SHA-256 of the empty string in every lineage in the store, including pristine `reviewing` ones, so it is an unset default rather than a signal.

## Impact

Before this was isolated, three lineages in this repository died at this step over four days (`review-6f794f717fed955e` on 2026-09-08, `review-6b96c7491c9e8241` and `review-c6ac9eeeef0634c2` on 2026-09-11), with no usable diagnostic. Until the first `inferential` case closed, no correction had ever completed in this clone.

Worth noting: the binary contains `"targeted validator exhausted its three inconclusive attempts"`. Because every rejection reported `mutation_outcome: "not_started"` and did not rewrite the state file, no attempt was consumed — but a caller who retries blindly would make the lineage terminal while believing the retry was free.

## Workaround

Apply the fix, leave the blocked lineage intact, and open a fresh lineage over the corrected tree. The lens then runs on healthy code and approves. Cost: one extra model run per affected unit. Do not abandon the blocked lineage: `review abandon` requires a maintainer authorization binding and destroys the evidence.

## Suggested direction

Either make the targeted validator derive its evidence directly from the corrected candidate when no refuter batch exists, or route a deterministic correction past the validator entirely (consistent with the policy text "a deterministic blocker needs no refuter"). Failing that, the stop should name the real condition instead of `invalid_request` / `correct_request`, which sends the caller looking for a request defect that does not exist.

title: bug(gentle-shell): framePromptLines consumes the last autocomplete row — single-match slash dropdown renders nothing
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

`framePromptLines()` treats the last line it receives as the editor's bottom border and replaces it with the frame's bottom rule. Pi's `Editor.render()` appends the autocomplete dropdown rows *after* that bottom border, so the last dropdown row is consumed on every render.

The slash-command dropdown therefore always renders one row fewer than the provider returned. When exactly one command matches, nothing renders at all, which reads as "autocomplete is broken" even though the command runs normally when submitted.

**Why it usually goes unnoticed:** when the filtered list overflows `autocompleteMaxVisible` (Pi default `5`), the consumed row is `SelectList`'s `  (i/N)` counter line rather than a command row. That line is discarded, not folded into the frame: `SCROLL_INDICATOR` is `/[↑↓] \d+ more/`, which matches the editor's own scroll borders from pi-tui's `createScrollBorder` but never the dropdown's `(i/N)` text. `scrollIndicator(bottom)` returns `undefined` and `bottomRule()` draws a plain rule. Losing a counter is far less noticeable than losing a command, so the bug only becomes obvious once the filtered list fits without scrolling and a real command row is the one being eaten.

#### Where

`lib/shell-prompt.ts` — `framePromptLines()`:

```ts
const top = lines[0];
const bottom = lines[lines.length - 1];   // assumed to be the editor's bottom border
const content = lines.slice(1, -1).map((line) => sideRules(line, innerWidth, options));
return [topRule(width, options, scrollIndicator(top)), ...content, bottomRule(width, options, scrollIndicator(bottom))];
```

`extensions/gentle-shell.ts` — `GentlePromptEditor.render()` passes the editor output straight through:

```ts
const lines = super.render(Math.max(1, width - 2));
...
return framePromptLines(lines, width, { ... });
```

Pi's `Editor.render()` (`@earendil-works/pi-tui`) produces:

```
[ topBorder, ...contentLines, bottomBorder, ...autocompleteLines ]
```

The dropdown rows are pushed *after* `renderBottomBorder()`, and their count is stored in `Editor.renderedAutocompleteHeight`. The two-border assumption in `framePromptLines()` only holds while no dropdown is open.

`tests/shell-prompt.test.ts` encodes the same assumption in its header comment — *"pi's editor output (a top rule, padded content lines, a bottom rule)"* — and every case feeds exactly that shape. `framePromptLines keeps the editor scroll indicators inside the frame` passes three lines with `↑ 2 more` / `↓ 3 more`. No case constructs a dropdown block, which is why the suite stays green.

Still present on `main` at the time of this report.

#### Suggested direction

Split the dropdown block off before framing and render it as framed content, so the bottom rule lands after every row:

1. In `GentlePromptEditor.render()`, split the `super.render()` output into the editor block and the trailing dropdown rows.
2. In `framePromptLines()`, accept the dropdown rows separately, wrap them with `sideRules()` after the editor content, and emit `bottomRule()` last.

Two points worth deciding before implementing:

**1. No public API exposes the dropdown height.** `Editor.renderedAutocompleteHeight` is assigned at runtime but is not declared in `@earendil-works/pi-tui`'s `dist/editor-component.d.ts`, nor in Pi's `dist/modes/interactive/components/custom-editor.d.ts`. Reading it today means casting to an undeclared internal, which can break on any Pi update. Having Pi expose the value upstream (a field declaration or a `getRenderedAutocompleteHeight()`) would make this robust.

**2. The `(i/N)` counter will start appearing once this is fixed.** Today it is silently dropped, so a long list renders five rows and no counter at all. After the fix it becomes an ordinary framed row. That is a restoration rather than a regression, but it is a visible change to the prompt and worth an explicit decision — and worth a test either way.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run Pi with gentle-pi installed and the gentle-shell prompt active (default).
2. Type `/ex` — the dropdown shows `export` and `exit`.
3. Add `p` so the line reads `/exp` — the dropdown disappears entirely.
4. Press Enter — `/export` runs normally.
5. Delete the `p` — the dropdown comes back.

Confirmed by installing a temporary pass-through autocomplete wrapper via `ctx.ui.addAutocompleteProvider` that logs the base provider's result without modifying it. With 67 registered commands, the provider's output is always correct and the loss happens during render.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected: every item the provider returns is rendered; a single match renders one row.

Actual: the last row is always dropped; a single match renders nothing, so the dropdown looks broken.

### gentle-pi version

2.5.0

### Pi version

0.85.1

### Operating system

Windows (WSL)

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
Pass-through autocomplete wrapper (provider output, before render):

  before="/"      ->  67 items  [settings,model,tree,thinking,scoped-models,export]
  before="/e"     ->  53 items  [export,exit,settings,session,new,resume]
  before="/ex"    ->   3 items  [export,exit,gentle:toggle-text-logo]
  before="/exp"   ->   1 items  [export]

Rows actually visible on screen:  5, 5, 2, 0
```

title: todo staleness counts agent runs, not work done: the stale nag loses attention in long tool-chain turns — field evidence + design options (v2.5.0)
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

Field investigation of why the todo list stopped updating while work completed, from a 25-unit orchestration session (work-unit commits each reviewed via the committed-range review loop; each unit cycle = 10-20 tool calls inside one agent run).

**TL;DR: the code works exactly as designed — but the design's staleness clock counts agent runs, not work done, and the stale nag is one small line competing with multi-KB tool results. Across 6 completed unit cycles the model made zero todo calls; the nag fired (stale: 3-4 turns) only after several units had already finished unrecorded.**

#### Mechanism (current implementation)

| Behavior | Anchor |
|---|---|
| Only write path = the model calling the `todo` tool; `applyTodo()` stamps `updatedTurn = turn`. No event anywhere infers task completion. | `extensions/gentle-todo.ts:157-170`, `lib/shell-todo.ts:151,167,179,185` |
| Turn counter increments once per agent run in `before_agent_start` — one turn spans the entire multi-call agent loop | `extensions/gentle-todo.ts:196-199` |
| Staleness = `currentTurn − updatedTurn`, threshold `STALE_AFTER_TURNS = 2`, only while open tasks exist | `lib/shell-todo.ts:91,116-119` |
| System-prompt block re-injected once per agent run; at ≥2 stale turns appends `(stale: N turns without an update …)` | `lib/shell-todo.ts:233-243` |
| `tool_execution_end` re-renders only for the todo tool itself; `agent_end` only clears finished lists | `extensions/gentle-todo.ts:219-233` |

#### What happened in the session

1. Six unit cycles (stage → commit → typecheck → negotiate → consent → capture → acknowledge) completed; every cycle's final steps were git + external-CLI calls. **Zero `todo` tool calls** across those cycles — nothing in the work chain touches the tool, so `updatedTurn` stayed frozen while tasks actually finished.
2. Because a whole unit fits inside one agent run, the next run started at `stale = 1` — under `STALE_AFTER_TURNS = 2`. The nag only surfaced at `stale: 3-4 turns`, after several units were already done unrecorded.
3. When the nag did fire, it was one ~80-byte line appended to the todo block, competing each turn against 8-12KB tool-result documents relayed inline (review STATUS envelopes, capture bindings sent twice per capture, consent envelopes). It fired and was deprioritized — attention competition, not absence.
4. Every explicit `todo` call in the session succeeded (`applyTodo` has no silent-drop path; errors only on invalid params). The tool itself is healthy; the gap is enforcement.

#### Root causes

1. **Model-driven design with no completion signal** — by design ("the task list the model keeps"), but the backstops assume turns are the unit of work.
2. **Turn-granularity staleness clock** — long tool-chain turns make `staleTurns` systematically under-report; a unit can finish inside one turn so staleness resets to 1 at the next run.
3. **Nag placement loses the attention race** — one muted line inside the todo block vs multi-KB tool outputs in the same context.
4. **Reminders only at run start** — `before_agent_start` injects before the tools run; there is no re-injection at tool boundaries, exactly where plan drift happens.

#### Improvement options (from the same investigation)

1. **Tool-boundary re-injection**: on `tool_execution_end` for non-todo tools, when `staleTurns >= STALE_AFTER_TURNS`, append a one-line reminder to the tool result ("todo list is N turns stale — update it").
2. **Secondary staleness signal**: count tool calls since `updatedTurn`; treat the list as stale above K calls even within a single turn (directly fixes the coarse clock).
3. **Escalating placement**: at stale >= 4, append the reminder at the END of the system prompt (recency wins) rather than only inside the todo block.
4. **Drift detection at `agent_end`**: an `in_progress` task whose note is unchanged across N turns gets flagged in the card.

Related but distinct: #749 (end-of-mission final-report vs list desync — atomic-close invariant, different mechanism), #737 (`write` id invalidation/display divergence), #603 (original "stays current as the agent works" design — this session is counter-evidence for the "keeps current" half under long tool-chain turns).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Give the agent multi-step work whose every step is an external tool call (git commits + a CLI lifecycle), sized so several steps complete within one agent run.
2. Observe the agent finish step after step without calling `todo`; the next run's stale counter reads 1 (under threshold) despite a finished task.
3. Only after 2+ further runs does the `(stale: N turns …)` line appear — by then multiple tasks finished unrecorded.

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected:
- Staleness that reflects work done (tool calls), not just agent runs, so the list is flagged within the same turn in which tasks finish.
- A stale reminder that survives competition with large tool results (tool-boundary re-injection and/or end-of-prompt placement).

Actual:
- `staleTurns` under-reports during exactly the long tool-chain turns where drift happens; the nag appears late and is a single muted line; six completed units went unrecorded despite the mechanism functioning to spec.

### gentle-pi version

2.5.0 (source build a3865715)

### Pi version

0.85.1

### Operating system

macOS

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)

```text
session evidence (25-unit orchestration, 6 unit cycles without a todo call):
stale marker observed in injected block: "(stale: 4 turns without an update — bring the list up to date now)"
todo tool calls in the whole session: 6 (all succeeded; 3 during early planning, 3 at compaction/recovery)
units completed before the list was finally rewritten: U01-U06
```

title: review: session report #4 to #577 — correction-representation gap on committed ranges, escalated-lineage dead end, host-relay failures (v2.5.0)
body:
### Before submitting
- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem
Follow-up session report to #577 and #573 (same candidate family: a ~37k-line working tree split into work-unit commits, reviewed per committed range). This session exercised the **correction path for committed-range reviews** for the first time in the series (#577 had zero corrections) and hit a hard gap: the mirrored contract's mandated correction route has **no working implementation** for committed-only candidates. It also adds new host-relay reliability and consent-routing findings. Items already reported in #573 (capture-group route rejection, controller-owned binding requirement for `review-*` dispatch) were hit again and are confirmed at the end, not re-reported.

Scope note: all commits in this session passed `tsc --noEmit`; only tool-attributable findings are listed.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Split a large working tree into work-unit commits on a branch; typecheck green after each.
2. Per unit, drive the committed-range loop: negotiated native STATUS (`--base-ref <full SHA> --committed-only --untracked-scope=exclude --expected-untracked-inventory <digest>`) → execute the emitted `review start --consent=relay` → replay `choices[].invocation` with `--consent granted` → adopt lineage via facade STATUS → `gentle_review_capture` (forecast → acknowledged resubmission) → native `acknowledge-approved`.
3. On the unit where the reviewer returned `correction_required` (CRITICAL, deterministic, introduced): capture the correction plan (`--correction-lines` within budget), apply the bounded edit, then attempt every candidate representation:
   - corrected file in the **working tree** → STATUS stop `corrected_candidate_unavailable`
   - corrected file **staged** → same stop (revision moves, stop persists)
   - negotiated STATUS with `--projection staged --base-ref … --committed-only` → same stop
   - **amend** the unit commit with the fix → STATUS stop `captured_artifacts_unverifiable` (terminal)
4. Attempt recovery of the stuck lineages: facade `recover` (asks for 6 exact inputs → then `native-status-unavailable` / `schema-incompatible`, `inventory_complete:false`), native `recover` (refused: "recovery scope has not changed"), native `abandon` (refused: lineage "holds terminal escalated authority"). `repair --preflight` on the same store classifies it clean (1 compact lineage, 0 conflicts).
5. Only working path found: fresh lineage re-reviewing the amended commit → approved + acknowledged.

### Expected and actual behavior
Expected:
- A sanctioned path from `correction_required` to validation for base-diff/committed-only lineages — or a typed, documented "restart on corrected commit" transition that preserves the audit chain.
- `gentle_review answer-consent` (the contract-mandated continuation) to work for natively-created lineages, or the mirrored contract to document the `choices[].invocation` replay as the canonical alternative.
- Host-relay failures to carry diagnostics (child stderr / log artifact) and a typed transport-vs-admission distinction so retry semantics are clear.
- The facade to preflight managed-asset freshness before relaying a capture, not refuse mid-lifecycle with an outcome-unknown envelope after consent and freeze.

Actual:
- Every correction representation above dead-ends in terminal stops; the correction budget stays unconsumed and the lineage becomes a permanent unreviewed audit record.
- With a native `--consent=relay` envelope there is no `consentBinding`, so the mandated `answer-consent` call is impossible; the provider-named `choices[].invocation` replay worked every time (7/7 consents).
- One acknowledged capture was refused with `submission-refused` ("managed reviewer assets are outdated; run `gentle-ai sync`") after consent and freeze — reconciliation confirmed the slot open; `gentle-ai sync` (user-approved) fixed the skew.
- The next capture attempt failed as `pi subprocess failed` after ~785s (budget 7200s) with no stderr, no log artifact, and `mutation_outcome: none`.
- Minor: `review-*` subagent dispatch rejected the generic `label` parameter ("review subagent dispatch contains an unsupported input field").

Already reported in #573, re-confirmed this session: `gentle_review_capture` rejects the lineage created via direct CLI START ("belongs to a different session route") until facade STATUS adopts it; `review-reliability` dispatch requires a "controller-owned candidate view lineage binding". In practice all reviewer runs executed inside the facade's pi-host-relay; the review personas went unused for the whole session.

### gentle-pi version
2.5.0 (source build a3865715)

### Pi version
0.85.1

### Operating system
macOS

### Relevant logs or error output (optional)
```text
capture #1: {"outcome":"submission-refused","stderr":"Error: managed reviewer assets are outdated; run `gentle-ai sync` [operation_outcome_unknown]"} → reconciled once → same collect slot reoffered
capture #2: {"outcome":"pi-host-relay-transport-failure","failure":{"kind":"pi-failed","stage":"pi","exit_code":null,"timed_out":false,"elapsed_ms":784794,"timeout_ms":7200000},"reason":"pi subprocess failed","mutation_performed":false}
correction stops: corrected_candidate_unavailable → captured_artifacts_unverifiable (terminal)
recover: native-input-required → resubmitted 6 inputs → {"code":"schema-incompatible","inventory_complete":false} ; native recover → "Error: recovery scope has not changed" ; native abandon → "holds terminal escalated authority"
```

title: Windows: telemetry and subagent spawns can flash cmd windows
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a report of this problem.
- [x] I reviewed this report and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem

On Windows, gentle-pi can briefly flash visible `cmd.exe` / console windows when Pi starts an agent turn and when a subagent is launched. The windows appear and disappear quickly, which is distracting and looks like an unexpected external process even though the launched work is background/RPC work.

Current installed package evidence shows at least two remaining package-owned spawn paths that do not pass `windowsHide: true`:

- `lib/telemetry-trigger.ts:128-133` starts the package-local `gentle-ai telemetry trigger --json` child with `detached: true` and `stdio: "ignore"`, but no `windowsHide: true`.
- `extensions/gentle-agents.ts:55` wires the subagent dependency spawn without `windowsHide: true`.
- `lib/agents-runner.ts:274-279` launches `pi --mode rpc` subagent children through that dependency. On Windows, if the command resolves through a `.cmd` wrapper, the missing hide flag can flash a console window.

This looks related to, but not fully covered by, earlier closed reports such as #708 and #828. In the installed `gentle-pi@2.5.0`, the above code paths still omit `windowsHide: true`; telemetry also explains flashes perceived during normal Pi startup/first agent turn.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use Windows with `gentle-pi` installed and enabled as a Pi package.
2. Ensure telemetry is not disabled by environment kill switches such as `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, `GENTLE_AI_TELEMETRY=0`, or `CI=true`.
3. Open Pi and start a primary agent turn.
4. Invoke a subagent, for example through `subagent_run`.
5. Observe that a console / `cmd.exe` window may briefly appear and hide.

Static evidence from the installed package:

```text
lib/telemetry-trigger.ts:128-133 spawns telemetry trigger without windowsHide.
extensions/gentle-agents.ts:55 spawns subagent process without windowsHide.
lib/agents-runner.ts:274-279 launches pi --mode rpc via the dependency spawn.
```

### Expected and actual behavior

Expected:

title: bug(skills): bundled gentle-ai-issue-creation stays at v1.3 and diverges from the canonical gentle-ai v1.4 contract
body:
### Before submitting

### Problem

The bundled `skills/issue-creation/SKILL.md` (`gentle-ai-issue-creation`, frontmatter `version: "1.3"`) is still behind the canonical `gentle-ai` contract (`issue-creation`, `version: "1.4"`, shipped with gentle-ai 2.7.0 for Claude Code and OpenCode). #574 closed the browser-only routing gap, but the remaining divergence still changes what Pi publishes:

- v1.3 keeps three publication paths that v1.4 forbids outright: a Markdown template completed "from known evidence", a "reviewed structured blank fallback" when `isBlankIssuesEnabled` is true, and a `gh issue create --repo "$TARGET" --web` handoff. v1.4 states "YAML Issue Forms are the single format authority. - v1.3 ships no `references/delegated-workflow-actions.md`, so the v1.4 rules for post-publication mutations and protected labels (`status:approved`, `size:exception`, `viewerPermission` `MAINTAIN`/`ADMIN` required, `TRIAGE` never suffices) do not exist in Pi.
- v1.3 has no explicit label expansion contract (v1.4 step 6: zero or one separate `--label` pair per permitted label) and no `DISCOVERY_FILE` / `PRE_READ_FILE` / `POST_READ_FILE` handling for candidate read-back.

In practice, issues created from Pi in a repository that uses YAML Issue Forms have come out as free Markdown bodies with no form headings and no labels, or with sections the selected form does not declare, while the same request from Claude Code or OpenCode (v1.4) produces the form-shaped body and the form-declared labels. Every other bundled skill I compared (`branch-pr` 2.0, `chained-pr` 1.0, `judgment-day` 1.7) matches the gentle-ai copy; only `issue-creation` drifted.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install gentle-ai 2.7.0 (Claude Code or OpenCode) and gentle-pi from `git:github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-pi@main` (commit `a5b772bf`, `main` at `46577c60` shows the same `version: "1.3"`).

   - gentle-pi copy: `skills/issue-creation/SKILL.md`, `version: "1.3"`, no `references/` directory.
3. Observe in the gentle-pi copy the sentences "A blank fallback is allowed only when `isBlankIssuesEnabled` is explicitly true", "A Markdown template may be completed only from known evidence", and the `gh issue create --repo "$TARGET" --web` block. None of them exist in v1.4.
4. In Pi, ask the agent to create an issue in a repository whose `config.yml` sets `blank_issues_enabled: false` but where the GitHub API still reports `isBlankIssuesEnabled: true`. The v1.3 contract permits a blank or Markdown body; the resulting issue carries no form headings and no labels.

Expected:
- The bundled `gentle-ai-issue-creation` skill matches the canonical gentle-ai `issue-creation` v1.4 contract byte for byte apart from the collision-prefixed frontmatter name, including `references/delegated-workflow-actions.md`.
- Issues created from Pi have the same form-shaped body and form-declared labels as issues created from Claude Code or OpenCode.

Actual:
- gentle-pi still ships v1.3 with Markdown, blank, and `--web` fallbacks and without the delegated-workflow-actions reference.
- Issues created from Pi can be published without the selected form's headings and without its declared labels.

2.5.0 (git install from `main`, commit a5b772bf; `main` at 46577c60 is unchanged for this)

0.85.1

macOS

<   version: "1.4"
>   version: "1.3"
< - YAML Issue Forms are the single format authority. Never use Markdown, a blank body, an alternate publisher, or a browser route as a fallback.
> A blank fallback is allowed only when `isBlankIssuesEnabled` is explicitly true.

title: feat(windows): provide safe guidance for container paths passed through Git Bash
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

On Windows, model-authored Docker commands may pass container-only POSIX paths through Git Bash to a native executable. MSYS automatically converts path-like arguments, so a container entrypoint can arrive as a Windows host path. This caused a real container inspection to fail. No incorrect installation directory or Gentle AI native-controller path construction was established.

A harmless native-Python probe reproduced the boundary without Docker, containers or network access:
```sh
python -c 'import sys; print(repr(sys.argv[1]))' /bin/sh
MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL=/bin/sh python -c 'import sys; print(repr(sys.argv[1]))' /bin/sh
```
Observed arguments: `<Git-root>/usr/bin/sh`, then `/bin/sh`. A separate direct native invocation with an argument vector also preserved `/bin/sh`.

Inspected installed Pi 0.85.1 selects Git Bash on Windows and executes the supplied Bash command. Gentle Pi's inspected quiet-tools execution wrapper forwards parameters to the built-in tool; its inspected Bash safety hook confirms the command. We did not find a path-rewriting routine in those inspected branches. This is a compatibility opportunity, not a demonstrated installer or Gentle Pi path-construction bug.

### Proposed outcome

Provide a supported, discoverable way or targeted guidance to preserve container-only arguments when invoking native tools from Windows, while retaining legitimate host-path conversion and existing Linux behavior.

Please assess whether this belongs in Gentle Pi guidance/integration or the upstream Pi execution interface before implementing a wrapper. Prefer structured executable/argument invocation when shell semantics are unnecessary. If Bash is required, scope exclusions to known container-only arguments and that command only.

Acceptance should cover Windows native and Git-Bash invocation, host bind sources versus container destinations, spaces/Unicode, Linux behavior, and existing safety, working-directory, cancellation and exit-code contracts. Do not globally disable MSYS conversion or rewrite every slash-prefixed argument.

### Alternatives considered

Per-command exclusions and direct invocation both worked in the local probe. They depend on the caller understanding the boundary. Changing an installation path would not address the demonstrated cause. Global conversion disabling risks breaking legitimate host-path workflows.

### Additional context

Official behavior: https://www.msys2.org/docs/filesystem-paths/#process-arguments

Only the Windows argument behavior above was executed. No cross-platform fix or Linux validation is claimed. No implementation or PR exists. Material AI assistance: Pi supported the source inspection, probe and drafting; publication is user-authorized. The report excludes private project identifiers, logs and environment values.

title: feat(doctor): detect legacy SDD change artifacts and report remediation
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

When an SDD change carries artifacts that predate the current contracts, the native status engine blocks it correctly but gives the operator no path forward.

Two concrete cases, both present in this repository:

1. **Non-canonical apply artifact name.** An active change ships `apply.md` where the engine reads `apply-progress.md`, so `gentle-ai sdd-status` reports `artifacts.applyProgress: missing` even though the implementation evidence exists on disk.
2. **Verify report without the machine-readable envelope.** The `sdd-verify` contract requires `verify-report.md` to open with a fenced `yaml` block carrying the `gentle-ai.verify-result/v1` payload. Legacy reports open with a `# Verification Report` heading or a bare `status: passed` line instead.

This is not an edge case. Across the active changes in this repository, **6 of the 7 that have a `verify-report.md` carry an invalid or legacy envelope**; only one is valid.

The engine behaves correctly: it keeps `nextRecommended: verify` and blocks archive. The problem is the operator's experience. The only signal is a native `blockedReasons` string:

````text
verification evidence is incomplete: missing valid gentle-ai.verify-result/v1 envelope: the first non-empty line must be ```yaml (```yml and any letter case are admitted; ~~~ fences, untagged fences, and content before the fence are not); check the exact bytes with gentle-ai sdd-verify-validate --input <path|-> --requirements <n> --scenarios <n>
````

That says the artifact is wrong, but not which changes are affected, how many there are, whether the block is expected for a pre-contract change, or what the smallest correct repair is. `/gentle:doctor` currently checks package assets, `openspec/config.yaml`, the skill registry, global model config, the sensitive-path guard, Engram access, and the dev-binary override — nothing about SDD change artifact shape. `remediationState` exists in the status payload but is scoped to review-authority remediation and does not describe artifact-shape repairs.

### Proposed outcome

A read-only diagnostic that enumerates active SDD changes whose artifacts no longer satisfy the current contracts, and states the smallest corrective action per change.

Per active change it should report:

- apply evidence present under a non-canonical name (`apply.md`) where `apply-progress.md` is expected;
- a `verify-report.md` that does not begin with a valid `gentle-ai.verify-result/v1` envelope;
- the resulting route state (`nextRecommended` and the envelope `blockedReasons`), so the operator sees the consequence and not just the symptom.

Each finding should carry a remediation line — renaming the apply artifact, or re-emitting the verify report through `sdd-verify` so the envelope is produced and admitted by `gentle-ai sdd-verify-validate` before the write.

The diagnostic must stay read-only: it must not rewrite, rename, or migrate repository artifacts on its own.

### Alternatives considered

- **Rely on `sdd-status` per change.** Workable, but it requires already knowing which change is broken, surfaces one change at a time, and offers no repository-wide view.
- **Auto-migrate legacy artifacts.** Rejected as a first step: renaming an apply artifact or synthesizing a verify envelope rewrites planning evidence, and the envelope carries hashes and counts that must come from a real verification run rather than a migration script.
- **Treat the block as a bug and accept legacy envelopes.** Rejected: the envelope is the machine-readable contract archive depends on. Relaxing it would let unverified changes reach archive.
- **Document the migration in the SDD docs only.** Helpful but static, and it still leaves the operator to find the affected changes by hand.

### Additional context

Reproduction on the active change that carries the non-canonical artifact name:

```text
$ ls openspec/changes/gentle-models-effort/
apply.md  design.md  proposal.md  spec.md  tasks.md  verify-report.md

$ test -f openspec/changes/gentle-models-effort/apply-progress.md || echo missing
missing

$ head -1 openspec/changes/gentle-models-effort/verify-report.md
status: passed

$ gentle-ai sdd-status gentle-models-effort
next: verify
archive: blocked
artifacts: {"applyProgress": "missing", "verifyReport": "done", ...}
```

Note the two failure shapes differ: `applyProgress` reports `missing` while `verifyReport` reports `done` despite being inadmissible, so a caller cannot distinguish "absent" from "present but rejected" without parsing `blockedReasons`.

The envelope contract and its validator already ship — `gentle-ai sdd-verify-validate --input <path|-> --requirements <n> --scenarios <n>` exists and is documented in the `sdd-verify` executor contract, including the requirement to validate before any persistence attempt. The missing piece is discovery and guidance for artifacts written before that contract.
