title: feat(shell): show z.ai (GLM Coding Plan) subscription usage in the bar and /gentle:usage panel
body:
## Problem

The Gentle Shell bar and the `/gentle:usage` panel show subscription usage windows for Codex (5h + weekly) and Claude Pro/Max, but not for z.ai's GLM Coding Plan. A session running on the z.ai provider has no visibility into its 5-hour and weekly quota consumption, while the same information is visible for the other two subscription providers.

## Proposal

Extend the existing provider-agnostic usage pipeline (`lib/shell-usage.ts` → `UsageStore` → bar + panel) with a z.ai parser and fetcher:

- **Source**: z.ai sends no rate-limit headers on responses, but exposes the same endpoint its own subscription UI reads: `GET https://api.z.ai/api/monitor/usage/quota/limit`. It is undocumented but stable in practice, corroborated by several community tools (openusage, quotai, ai-usagebar, pi-glm-usage).
- **Shape**: the response carries a `limits[]` array. `TOKENS_LIMIT`/`CREDIT_LIMIT` entries are percentage quota windows; `unit:3` → 5h window, `unit:6` → weekly window, and `unit:5` is the monthly web-search count. Reset times come back as `nextResetTime` in epoch milliseconds.
- **Auth**: the z.ai API key pi already stores (auth.json `zai` entry), read via `ctx.modelRegistry.getApiKeyForProvider("zai")`. No new configuration for existing users.
- **Cadence**: poll-only, same cycle Codex already uses — session start, at most every 5 minutes, and `r` in the panel. On failure or shape drift it degrades to the existing "no usage yet · r to fetch" note instead of erroring.

Out of scope for a first cut: monthly web-search quota display and plan-name enrichment via `/api/biz/subscription/list` (both can follow later without rework).

## Size

Small and contained — the render pipeline (`UsageStore`, `renderUsageBar`, `renderUsagePanel`, `UsageView`) is already provider-agnostic and needs zero changes:

| File | Change | Estimate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lib/shell-usage.ts` | `ZAI_PROVIDER`, `ZAI_USAGE_URL`, `parseZaiUsage()` + raw types, `SUPPORTED_USAGE_PROVIDERS`/`PENDING_NOTE` entries | ~60–80 lines |
| `extensions/gentle-shell.ts` | extend `refreshUsage` to fetch when the active provider is `zai` | ~20–30 lines |
| `tests/shell-usage.test.ts` | cases mirroring the existing Codex/Anthropic tests | ~40–60 lines |

Total: **~120–170 lines including tests**. No UI work: the bar already names the provider it shows, and the panel picks up any recorded `ProviderUsage` automatically.

## Evidence

- Provider-agnostic model already in place: `lib/shell-usage.ts` (`ProviderUsage`, `parseCodexUsage`, `parseAnthropicHeaders`) wired in `extensions/gentle-shell.ts` (`fetchCodexUsage`, `refreshUsage`); Anthropic support was added as the same kind of contained change.
- Endpoint semantics corroborated by community tooling: [openusage z.ai provider docs](https://openusage.sh/docs/providers/zai/), [quotai](https://github.com/soakes/quotai), [ai-usagebar wire types](https://docs.rs/ai-usagebar/latest/ai_usagebar/zai/types/index.html), and the community pi package [pi-glm-usage](https://pi.dev/packages/pi-glm-usage).
- GLM Coding Plan quota model (5-hour + weekly limits): [z.ai devpack docs](https://docs.z.ai/devpack/overview.md).

Caveat: the endpoint is undocumented, so the parser must treat unknown shapes as "no data" rather than failure — the same graceful degradation path Codex already has.

title: feat(harness): redirect all tool outputs to a workspace-local tmp/ folder
body: ## Summary Today, keeping bulky tool output out of the model context is achieved only through prompt-level discipline in `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` ("Mandatory User Instructions"). This issue proposes making it a harness-level guarantee in gentle-pi: **all tool outputs are redirected to a `tmp/` folder inside the project workspace**, and the model receives an artifact path plus a bounded preview instead of the full bulk output. ## Current state (prompt-level workaround) The installed `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` (attached below in full; its required location is the `~/.pi/agent/` folder, from where pi loads it into every session) carries a whole rule system whose only purpose is to keep the session context lean by pushing artifacts to `/tmp/`: - `Set up tmp/ inside project workspace and use it as the workspace local temporary folder (create if not exists; NEVER delete or clean existing contents — tmp/ is persistent)` - `write tool must write to a file in tmp. no output to the session context` - `read tool must read from a file in tmp. no output to the session context` - python/node/bun/bash scripts, `rg`/`grep`/`fd`/`find`, and all git tools "must write and read params from a file in tmp. no output to the session context" - `Agent-written scripts (sh tmp/.sh) must not print results to the session context` - `Agents and subagents output MUST be done to the tmp folder in the project workspace and not in a sandbox` Problems with relying on the prompt alone: - **Compliance-based, not enforced**: it depends on the model remembering and obeying; every violation silently pollutes the session context. - **Token-expensive**: the rules are paid on every session, and rule re-explanations around each command add more. - **Not uniform**: subagents, chained scripts, and long sessions drift away from the convention. ## Proposed behavior gentle-pi enforces the redirection natively at the harness level (`extensions/quiet-tools.ts` is the natural prior art to extend): 1. Tool outputs that produce bulk results (bash stdout/stderr, `rg`/`grep`/`fd`/`find` matches, git command output, script output) are written to deterministic artifacts under `/tmp/`. 2. The model-facing result contains: the artifact path, a bounded head/tail preview, and line/byte counts — never the unbounded bulk. 3. `tmp/` is auto-created per workspace at session start if missing, is persistent, and is never auto-cleaned — the same contract the AGENTS.md rule states today. 4. The write→read round-trip through `tmp/` stays symmetric: artifacts are produced to `tmp/` and consumed from `tmp/` by path. 5. Redirection applies uniformly to subagent outputs (workspace `tmp/`, not a sandbox). 6. Small outputs (a status line, an exit code) may remain inline; the harness decides by threshold, with an explicit opt-out for commands whose output must be seen in full. ## Benefits - **Token savings**: bulky tool output is paid once as a short artifact path plus a bounded preview, not as the full text in the conversation; follow-up reads pull only the needed slice from the artifact. - **Session context stops growing with tool output**: redirection keeps the conversation context bounded regardless of how verbose commands, searches, or git tools get, leaving more room for actual work and review. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Tool output redirection to `/tmp/` works with an empty `AGENTS.md` — no prompt-level instructions needed. - [ ] `tmp/` is created automatically and its contents survive across sessions (no auto-cleanup). - [ ] Model-facing tool results carry artifact path + bounded preview instead of full bulk output. - [ ] Subagent outputs land in the workspace `tmp/` as well. - [ ] `AGENTS.md` is reduced to the rules that cannot be enforced mechanically. ## Non-goals - No automatic cleanup or pruning of `tmp/`. - Not proposed upstream (`earendil-works/pi`) yet — gentle-pi-local first. ## Extracted `tmp/`-related rules (evidence) The attached `AGENTS.md` lives at `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` and contains rules for many other topics too — review workload gates, provider-material handling, git lifecycle isolation, `gh` flows, formatting and preflight rules — so the `tmp/` rules extracted below are only the subset relevant to this issue. All of it rides along in every session's context. Every quote below is whitespace-normalized, otherwise verbatim, and machine-verified against the attached file: **From `## General rules` (the core contract):** - Set up tmp/ inside project workspace and use it as the workspace local temporary folder (create if not exists; NEVER delete or clean existing contents — tmp/ is persistent) - write tool must write to a file in tmp. no output to the session context - read tool must read from a file in tmp. no output to the session context - python, node, bun, bash scripts must write to a file in tmp and read as param from there. no output to the session context - rg, grep, fd and find must write and read params from a file in tmp. no output to the session context - all bash tools that supports writing to a file and later read as param must do it this way. no output to the session context - all git tools that supports writing to a file and later read as param must do it this way. no output to the session context - Agents and subagents output MUST be done to the tmp folder in the project workspace and not in a sandbox and every finding anchor pre-verified against the changed-line hunks - Agent-written scripts (`sh tmp/.sh`) must not print results to the session context: no trailing `cat`/`echo`/`tail` of output files. Scripts write artifacts to tmp/ and print at most one short status line (exit code or path). Read artifacts from their tmp/ path with the `read` tool. **From `## Syntax gate before code writes`:** - Generated code and new code blocks: write the draft to `tmp/.` → run the check-only command → only after it passes, write/patch the real target. **From `## Bash preflight gate`:** - `node -e` / `python3 -c` / any inline script code → write `tmp/.mjs|py|sh` with the `write` tool first, then run the file. - Heredocs `<<`, `<<-`, `<<<` (including inside `$(...)`, pipes, or multi-line commands) → content to a tmp/ file; the command receives the path as a parameter. **From `## Shell instructions`:** - If it contains `python3 -c` write the script `tmp/descriptive_file_name.py` and then call `python3 tmp/descriptive_file_name.py` - If it contains `node -e` write the script to `tmp/descriptive_file_name.mjs` and then call `node tmp/descriptive_file_name.mjs` - if it contains any bash script code write to `tmp/descriptive_file_name.sh` and the call `sh ./tmp/descriptive_file_name.sh` **From `## Heredoc usage`:** - Write the heredoc content to `tmp/descriptive_file_name.` with the `write` tool (never with a redirect). - Then call the consuming command passing that tmp/ file path as a parameter. **From `## Provider material fidelity`:** - Transport large blobs (>50 lines) by file, never by inline hand-copy: the producer writes tmp/. once (CLI output redirect or the write tool), and every consumer receives that path as a parameter. Never transcribe a large blob from a read into another tool call's parameters. **From `## Generated scripts and JSON parsing`:** - Do not hide producer or generator diagnostics with `> /dev/null 2>&1`. Redirect output to a `tmp/` file and inspect it before continuing. **From `## JSON writes via jq` (no-file-source exception):** - Transcribe the RAW answer (prose/markdown fence included) verbatim to `tmp/answer-.txt`, then extract the JSON object mechanically — first `{` to last `}` — into `tmp/result-.json`. The extractor must fail unless the slice parses as exactly one JSON object; never edit inside the extracted JSON. **From `## Host-write readback verification`:** - Read the artifact back FROM the target host into a tmp/ file (`gh issue view --json`, `gh api .../comments/`, `git ls-remote`) and verify from that file only: - Body-bearing readback data stays in tmp/ and is compared by diff, never printed to the session. **From `## gh interactive flows`:** - publish with `gh issue create --repo / --title "" --body-file tmp/<descriptive-name>.md` - Write the paste-ready body to `tmp/<descriptive-name>.md`. ## Attachment Full installed `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md`, used as the example of the current prompt-level contract: <details> <summary><code>AGENTS.md</code> — Mandatory User Instructions (current workaround)</summary> ````markdown # Mandatory User Instructions ## General rules - Only use fallow mcp tools when the user includes “fallow” in the prompt - context-mode tools must run only inside the project workspace - Use codegraph for ssd-propose, ssd-design and ssd-apply, refactors and code fixes - Set up tmp/ inside project workspace and use it as the workspace local temporary folder (create if not exists; NEVER delete or clean existing contents — tmp/ is persistent) - write tool must write to a file in tmp. no output to the session context - read tool must read from a file in tmp. no output to the session context - python, node, bun, bash scripts must write to a file in tmp and read as param from there. no output to the session context - rg, grep, fd and find must write and read params from a file in tmp. no output to the session context - all bash tools that supports writing to a file and later read as param must do it this way. no output to the session context - all git tools that supports writing to a file and later read as param must do it this way. no output to the session context - ALWAYS stay strictly inside the project workspace. Only the user can override it. - Spawn agents in parallel whenever possible - ALWAYS use 'fd' and NEVER 'find' if available in path - ALWAYS use 'rg' and NEVER 'grep' if available in path; do not translate flags 1:1 (`grep -E` becomes plain `rg` — rg is regex by default, and `-E` in rg means `--encoding`) - ALWAYS use node instead of python for scripts - NEVER use `mapfile` (bash≥4 builtin — absent from zsh entirely and from macOS's default bash 3.2: it does not exist on macOS at all; use `while IFS= read -r` loops or pass files as parameters), never use `cat -A` (use `cat -et`), and no other GNU-only coreutils flags on macOS (BSD userland) - NEVER start editing without asking consent from the user - NEVER revert any file without asking consent from the user - ALWAYS prioritize fixing code than using disabling rules - NEVER invent content when you can not find evidence - NEVER stage or track files without asking consent from the user - ALWAYS tell the user when creating a branch - Agents and subagents output MUST be done to the tmp folder in the project workspace and not in a sandbox and every finding anchor pre-verified against the changed-line hunks - ALWAYS use `jq` to write json data and files to avoid syntax errors - ALWAYS commit using `git commit -F` - ALWAYS use 2 spaces as indentation and convert from tabs - Agent-written scripts (`sh tmp/<name>.sh`) must not print results to the session context: no trailing `cat`/`echo`/`tail` of output files. Scripts write artifacts to tmp/ and print at most one short status line (exit code or path). Read artifacts from their tmp/ path with the `read` tool. ## Syntax gate before code writes — mandatory preflight Before ANY code write or edit reaches its final target file (any language), validate syntax with the language parser in check-only mode. Never hand the user code that fails a parse check. - Generated code and new code blocks: write the draft to `tmp/<descriptive_name>.<ext>` → run the check-only command → only after it passes, write/patch the real target. - In-place edits of existing code: apply the edit, then IMMEDIATELY run the check-only command on the target file; fix any failure before the next step. - Trivial edits are exempt: single-token fixes, comments, config values, markdown prose. - Never report a code task done with a failing check. If the language has no checker available on this machine, state that explicitly in the summary — never skip silently. - Prefer the project's own checks when configured; here that is `npm run typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`) and `npm run lint` (`biome check`). The table below is the portable fallback for single files and other languages. Single-file `npx tsc --noEmit file.ts` ignores tsconfig (defaults to CommonJS) — expect false ESM/NodeNext errors; treat it as a rough parse check only. Check-only commands (parse/compile without executing, no side effects): | Language | Check command | | --- | --- | | TypeScript (project) | `npm run typecheck` | | JavaScript | `node --check file.js` (`.mjs` works on current Node) | | JSON | `jq empty file.json` | | YAML | `yamllint file.yaml` | | Bash / POSIX sh | `bash -n file.sh` / `sh -n file.sh` | | Python | `python3 -m py_compile file.py` | | Go | `gofmt -e file.go > /dev/null` or `go build ./...` | | Ruby | `ruby -c file.rb` | | Rust | `cargo check` | | C / C++ | `clang -fsyntax-only file.c` | | Markdown | `npx markdownlint-cli2 file.md` (project config) | Rule violations are fix-the-cause, never disable/skip-the-check. ## Subagent turn budgets and failure policy For broad investigations, omit `max_turns` or use a generous budget > 100. If a bounded agent hits its limit, resume that same agent rather than restarting it. Treat `partial` or turn-limit results as incomplete; never report them as successful until the artifact and verification are complete. For lint and test tasks use 300 seconds as maximum value. Subagent failure classes — handle by class, never by blind retry: - Dispatch rejection (e.g. `review subagent dispatch requires mode task`): nothing was consumed. Fix the dispatch envelope exactly as the runtime demands — review-* agents require explicit `mode: "task"` — and relaunch. Do not strip the dispatch contract from the task to make dispatch pass. - Mid-run failure (provider rate limit, transport error, crash): resume the SAME agent with its original task; its context survives a resume, while a cold restart loses paid inspection work. Never silently drop the failed slot from a batch: the batch is complete only when every slot is captured. - Malformed or rejected output (envelope-wrapped JSON, prose around the payload, out-of-scope proof paths): resume the same agent to re-emit in the required shape; never hand-fix its artifact (see the jq exception). - Failed, cancelled, or partial results are never evidence: a subagent result counts only when the resumed run completes and, for reviewer results, native admission accepts the capture. SDD tasks-phase lesson (three consecutive ~2-3x misses): derive test-LOC forecasts from matrix-row counts (rows × ~40 lines) or apply a 2-3x multiplier to prose estimates, so the 400-line budget gate stops firing mid-RED. ## Decision prompts When progress requires a user decision, use the structured `ask_user_question` tool rather than asking in plain chat and wait for the response before continuing. Always mark the recommended option with '(Recommended)' text. ## Structured prompt payload hygiene — mandatory preflight Before EVERY `ask_user_question` or `ask_user_choice` call, inspect the complete payload. - Every `question`, `header`, `label`, `description`, and `preview` string MUST be plain single-line text: no `\r`, `\n`, `\t`, or any escape sequence between words. - Correct: `label: "Run the review now"`. Broken: `label: "Run\r the\r review\r now"` — each stray `\r` renders as a line break and shatters the option vertically. - Re-verify the serialized arguments before submitting: if any value contains `\r` or `\n` inside a sentence, rewrite the payload cleanly and resubmit. Never submit a polluted payload and let the user cope with mangled text. - Completeness check: every required field must be present and every string must terminate cleanly — `question` and `header` present, 2–4 options, each option with both `label` and `description`. A payload whose strings stop mid-sentence or that is missing required fields was truncated in serialization: regenerate the WHOLE payload cleanly; never patch or complete a truncated one in place. The tool's schema rejection is the backstop, not the plan. - Consent-envelope relays are fidelity-critical: provider choice labels, effects, and answer tokens must reach the human byte-exact; escape-sequence pollution distorts the consent gate itself, even when answer tokens survive. ## Todo tool calls — mandatory shape Every `todo` tool call MUST carry a valid top-level `action` field (`create` | `update` | `list` | `get` | `delete` | `clear`). - Creating a task: `action: "create"` plus `subject` (+ optional `description`, `activeForm`). The payload fields alone are NOT enough — omitting `action` fails schema validation before anything executes. - Changing a task: `action: "update"` plus its `id` and the target field (e.g. `status`). - In parallel batches, EACH call needs its own `action`; batching task payloads without per-call `action` produces four validation errors, not four tasks. - Before submitting, verify `action` is present; never re-send a malformed batch unchanged. - Completeness mirrors shape: every call carries `action`, every create carries `subject`, every update carries `id` plus the target field, and every parallel batch carries its own per-call `action` — a batch that stops mid-array was truncated in serialization: regenerate it whole, never patch it. ## Bash preflight gate — one-pass trigger scan (mandatory) Before EVERY Bash tool call, scan the COMPLETE planned command — every `&&`, `;`, newline, pipe, and `$(...)` segment — against this trigger list, and rewrite the plan BEFORE submitting. The detailed sections below (lifecycle isolation, shell instructions, heredoc) stay authoritative; this gate is the single scan that feeds them all: - `node -e` / `python3 -c` / any inline script code → write `tmp/<descriptive_name>.mjs|py|sh` with the `write` tool first, then run the file. - Heredocs `<<`, `<<-`, `<<<` (including inside `$(...)`, pipes, or multi-line commands) → content to a tmp/ file; the command receives the path as a parameter. - Lifecycle ops (`git commit`, `git push`, `gh pr create`, `gh release create`) → sole command in its own tool call; no `&&`, no `| tail/head/sed`, no `;` siblings, nothing before or after. - A single Bash call must not both generate script(s) and execute what it generated. Generation, verification of the generated script (see "Generated scripts and JSON parsing" #1), and execution are separate tool calls: generate → verify → run. `node gen.mjs && sh gen-out.sh` in one call leaves no room to catch a broken generator before it runs. - GNU-only flags fail on macOS BSD userland with "illegal option": never use `cat -A` (use `cat -et`), `readlink -f`, `date -d`, `stat -c`, or `grep -P`. If a command fails with "illegal option", switch to the BSD form (or `od -c` for byte-level inspection) — never retry the same flag. - In-place `sed -i` per platform — same command, different parsing: macOS (BSD sed): the suffix is its OWN argument — `sed -i '' 's/a/b/' file` Linux (GNU sed): the suffix attaches to the flag (optional) — `sed -i 's/a/b/' file` or `sed -i.bak 's/a/b/' file`; `sed -i ''` on Linux is an empty-script error. Cross-platform-safe default: `sed 's/a/b/' file > file.tmp && mv file.tmp file` - Chaining, redirection (`> file`, `2>&1`), or the code being "tiny" do NOT exempt a segment. There is no size threshold: two lines of inline JS is still a violation. - If you catch yourself typing code inside a command string, abort the call and write the tmp/ file first. - Prefer reusing an existing tmp/ helper over a new one-off; the compliant path must be cheaper than going inline. ## Lifecycle command isolation — mandatory preflight Before EVERY Bash tool call, inspect the complete planned command. If it contains a lifecycle operation (`git commit`, `git push`, `gh pr create`, or `gh release create`), the lifecycle operation MUST be submitted as the sole command in its own tool call. Preventively rewrite the plan BEFORE invoking `bash`: - Remove output-only pipeline suffixes such as `| tail`, `| head`, or `| sed`. Pi already captures and bounds command output. - Move independent follow-up commands after `&&`, `;`, or a newline into separate tool calls, executed only after the lifecycle command succeeds. - Never submit the compound form and wait for the gate to reject it. - Never silently execute commands that appeared before the lifecycle command. Example: Planned: `git commit -F tmp/descriptive_file_name.txt | tail -n 50` `git commit -qm "text"` `git commit -m "text"` Execute instead: `git commit -F tmp/descriptive_file_name.txt` Planned: `git commit -F tmp/descriptive_file_name.txt && git status --short` Execute as two sequential tool calls: 1. `git commit -F tmp/descriptive_file_name.txt` 2. `git status --short` — only if step 1 succeeds. ## Shell instructions - mandatory preflight Before EVERY Bash tool call, inspect the complete planned command - If it contains `python3 -c` write the script `tmp/descriptive_file_name.py` and then call `python3 tmp/descriptive_file_name.py` Preventively rewrite the plan BEFORE invoking `python3`: Example: Planned: `pyhon3 -c "import json d = json.load(open('tmp/lens-u1-reliability.json')) for f in d['findings']: print(f.get('severity'), '|', f.get('id'), '|', str(f.get('claim'))[:95])"` Execute instead: `write tmp/descriptive_file_name.py` `python3 tmp/descriptive_file_name.py` - If it contains `node -e` write the script to `tmp/descriptive_file_name.mjs` and then call `node tmp/descriptive_file_name.mjs` Preventively rewrite the plan BEFORE invoking `node`: Example: Planned: `node -e "console.log('Hello from node')"` `node -e "console.log('skip')" 2>/dev/null; echo ok` `cd /Users/admin/Dev/src/gentle-pi-rc && node -e "const p=require('./package.json'); console.log(JSON.stringify({name:p.name,version:p.version,files:p.files,pi:p.pi,scripts:Object.keys(p.scripts||{})},null,1))" 2>/dev/null` Execute instead: `write tmp/descriptive_file_name.mjs` `node tmp/descriptive_file_name.mjs` - if it contains any bash script code write to `tmp/descriptive_file_name.sh` and the call `sh ./tmp/descriptive_file_name.sh` Preventively rewrite the plan BEFORE invoking `bash`: Example: Planned: `#!/bin/bash set -e BINDING="$(printf '%s' "$(cat tmp/recovery-auth-c2.txt)")" gentle-ai review recover \ --cwd /Users/admin/Dev/pi/@tintinweb97/pi-subagents \ --predecessor-lineage=review-13cdb98b74e627b5-c1 \ --expected-predecessor-revision=sha256:296dff0ec0d1255ca1df230191ed4a28c58c77a69003ae3c9f0a60187d531a05 \ --successor-lineage=review-13cdb98b74e627b5-c2 \ --disposition=scope_changed \ --actor=admin \ --reason="bounded correction: R3-001 completed-viewer toggle re-dispatch + toggle contract tests (195 changed lines, budget 200)" \ --maintainer-authorization="$BINDING"` Execute instead: `write tmp/descriptive_file_name.sh` `sh ./tmp/descriptive_file_name.sh` ## Review workload gate (hard rule) Before relaying any review consent envelope — or starting any review — for a candidate exceeding 400 changed lines (additions + deletions), the work-unit split (work-unit-commits / gentle-ai-chained-pr skills) MUST be offered to the user as an explicit, first-class decision option. Mentioning the budget breach in prose is not enough: the split must be a real choice in the decision prompt, before any consent envelope is relayed. ## Heredoc usage — mandatory preflight Before EVERY Bash tool call, inspect the complete planned command. If it contains a heredoc (`<<`, `<<-`, or `<<<`), or would pipe/interpolate one anywhere in the command, NEVER submit it. Preventively rewrite the plan BEFORE invoking `bash`: - Write the heredoc content to `tmp/descriptive_file_name.<ext>` with the `write` tool (never with a redirect). - Then call the consuming command passing that tmp/ file path as a parameter. Example: Planned: `node tmp/script.mjs << 'EOF' {"name":"pi","n":2} EOF` Execute instead: 1. `write` tmp/input-data.json with the exact content `{"name":"pi","n":2}` 2. `node tmp/script.mjs tmp/input-data.json` The same applies to `cat << EOF > file`, `<<-`, `<<<` (here-strings), and heredocs embedded in `$(...)`, pipes, or multi-line commands: the content goes to a file in tmp/ and the command receives that path as a parameter. ## Provider material fidelity — mandatory preflight Before relaying ANY provider-owned material (review bindings, materialized reviewer tasks, collect bindings, consent envelopes, frozen manifests, patches), inspect how it is transported. - Provider material is opaque and byte-exact. Never retype, summarize, collapse, reformat, truncate, or "improve" it. A placeholder like "lines collapsed for transport" inside provider material is a hard error: it silently replaces the reviewer's only evidence with fabrication. - Transport large blobs (>50 lines) by file, never by inline hand-copy: the producer writes tmp/<name>.<ext> once (CLI output redirect or the write tool), and every consumer receives that path as a parameter. Never transcribe a large blob from a read into another tool call's parameters. - After producing a copy of provider material, verify byte-equality against the source. Checksums per platform — macOS: `shasum -a 256 file` Linux: `sha256sum file` (`cmp file1 file2` works on both.) One mismatch = regenerate from the source file; never hand-patch the copy. - Reviewer dispatch: never hand-assemble a reviewer task for subagent_run. Use the provider's materialize/capture route (CLI `--materialize` for the task, file-based `--input` for the result) or the sanctioned MCP relay. Review subagents carry a bounded dispatch contract; manual envelopes are rejected — and a hand-mangled envelope that slipped through would invalidate the review itself. - If a provider route rejects a binding (e.g. "belongs to a different session route"), do NOT retry the same payload through another route with hand edits. Diagnose the route mismatch and run the entire lifecycle through one route. ## Generated scripts and JSON parsing — mandatory preflight Two recurring failure classes when scripts read tool output or generate other scripts. Prevent both BEFORE running: 1. **Generated scripts must NOT interpolate values at generation time.** When a script writes another script, the writer script's own shell variables (`$REPO`, `$T`, `$CMD`, ...) must appear literally in the generated text or be defined inside the generated file — never expanded by the writer's double-quoted strings/heredocs. An empty expansion silently produces `cd "/tmp/verify-wt": No such file or directory` style breakage at RUN time, not at write time. - Prefer generating with node `fs.writeFileSync` and a template that only embeds values read from data files (bindings, shas), while paths/wrappers (`REPO=`, `cd`, `export`) stay as literal text in the generated file. - After generating, run the generator's own verification: `head -n 6` the generated script and check the variable definitions exist before `sh` it. 2. **Generator prerequisites must be present and valid before execution.** A generator that reads `tmp/status-cli.json`, a binding, or any other artifact MUST NOT run until that exact input exists and is non-empty. Use the order: `mkdir → producer → input validation → generator → generated-script verification → consumer`. - Verify each declared input before invoking the generator, for example: `test -s tmp/status-cli.json && jq empty tmp/status-cli.json`. - If a producer fails or an input is missing/invalid, stop immediately. Do not run a generator or consumer with missing, stale, or partially written input. - Dependent shell steps MUST use `set -eu` plus `&&`, not `;`. A semicolon can continue into a generator after its producer failed. - Do not hide producer or generator diagnostics with `> /dev/null 2>&1`. Redirect output to a `tmp/` file and inspect it before continuing. - Do not reuse or adapt a generator from another transaction without checking every input/output path and transaction selector against the current data. 3. **Never `require()`/parse tool output files blindly — strip to the JSON body first.** `gentle-ai` CLI output files may carry non-JSON prefix lines (e.g. `ok <sha>` status lines) before the JSON document. Parsing the raw file with `node -e "require('file.json')"` throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'` and aborts the whole pipeline mid-step. - Before parsing, filter from the first line that starts with `{`: `awk '/^{/{flag=1} flag' in.out > in.json`, then parse `in.json`. - Never assume the parse succeeds inside a larger `&&` chain; extract the parse into its own step and check its output before consuming values (tokens, shas, commands) extracted from it. - Corollary: never hand-copy tokens (shas, revisions, handles) read from JSON into a new script — regenerate the script FROM the binding/data files programmatically so tokens are byte-exact. 4. **Never hand-author native-derived exact values (authorization bindings, tokens, digests).** When a native CLI requires an "exact" value — e.g. `gentle-ai review recover --maintainer-authorization` — do NOT construct it by hand in any format (compact JSON, pretty JSON, key=value): the value is natively derived (schema-header + `key=value` LF lines, actor from git config, CLI-set reason) and hand-built variants are always rejected. Instead: run the command WITHOUT the value so the CLI derives it itself (self-recovery path), or extract it verbatim from native output. Fix all other flags first, then add the derived value last. 5. **Status artifacts are point-in-time state, not stable inputs.** A `gentle-ai` status/capture JSON dump describes the lineage state AT WRITE TIME. When the lineage advances (collect → execute → acknowledged/burned), old paths disappear: re-running an extraction like `.next_transition.collect.inputs[0]...` against a stale dump crashes with `Cannot iterate over null` even though the file still parses fine (the crash point is the `[]` iteration over a path that is now null). Treat a null path as "state moved on": re-read fresh STATUS from the live lineage with the exact provider tokens instead of retrying the stale file. Fail soft when exploring: end the path with `// empty` (e.g. `.next_transition.collect.inputs[0].submission.argument_tokens // empty | .[]`) so a closed lineage yields no output instead of a crash. ## JSON writes via jq — mandatory preflight ALL JSON data files (reviewer results, collect bindings, request payloads, any JSON artifact) MUST be written with `jq`, never hand-typed as raw JSON. - Assemble objects with `jq -n --arg` / `--argjson` / `--slurpfile`, reading machine tokens (subject hashes, lineage ids, lens names) from the provider's token files via `jq -r` instead of transcribing them by hand. - Validate every produced file with `jq empty <file>` before submitting it to any consumer; a parse error means rebuild from fragments, never hand-patch. - Provider-owned hashes are the highest-risk transcription targets: one invented hex tail silently corrupts a binding. If a value came from a file, read it from that file inside the jq invocation. - Exception — provider-role results with no file source: reviewer/refuter results that arrive ONLY as a subagent's final answer (reviewer agents have no `write`/`bash` by design, so no file source exists) may be transported with the `write` tool, but only through this shape: 1. Transcribe the RAW answer (prose/markdown fence included) verbatim to `tmp/answer-<role>.txt`, then extract the JSON object mechanically — first `{` to last `}` — into `tmp/result-<role>.json`. The extractor must fail unless the slice parses as exactly one JSON object; never edit inside the extracted JSON. 2. `jq empty tmp/result-<role>.json` is mandatory before any consumer sees the file (e.g. before `capture-result --input`). 3. If validation or native admission rejects the payload (e.g. `proof_path_out_of_scope`), resume the SAME reviewer agent to re-emit; hand-patching the JSON is forbidden. 4. `proof_refs` and `location` values must be plain repository-relative `path[:line]` tokens exactly as they appear in the changed-path manifest; prefixed forms (`changed-hunk:`, `candidate-created-path:`) reject the entire payload. Everything else (bindings, payloads, any JSON with a file source) keeps the full jq rule unchanged. ## gh interactive flows — non-TTY preflight Every Bash tool call in this harness runs WITHOUT a TTY. `gh` flows that would prompt (`issue create`, `pr create`, `release create`, `--web`, `--editor`) fail with "must provide `--title` and `--body` when not running interactively" or hang on a hidden prompt. Before EVERY `gh` call, inspect the complete planned command: - NEVER use `--web` or `--editor` from an agent shell. There is no TTY to confirm and no browser handoff through gh. - Repo WITHOUT mandatory issue forms (no `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.yml`, or `blank_issues_enabled` not false): publish with `gh issue create --repo <org>/<repo> --title "<title>" --body-file tmp/<descriptive-name>.md` Body always via `--body-file`, never inline, never prompted. - Repo WITH YAML issue forms (`blank_issues_enabled: false`): do NOT attempt `gh issue create`. Instead: 1. Write the paste-ready body to `tmp/<descriptive-name>.md`. 2. Build the deep link with a script (never hand-encode): `https://github.com/<org>/<repo>/issues/new?template=<name>.yml&title=<url-encoded-title>` 3. Open it with `open` (macOS) / `xdg-open` (Linux) and STOP for human completion. Report the body file path for pasting. - If gh errors with a prompt-related message, do NOT retry the same command with more flags — switch once to the non-interactive form or the deep link. The same non-TTY assumption applies to `gh pr create` / `gh release create`: always fully flagged (`--title/--body-file/--notes-file/--draft`), never prompt-dependent. ## Host-write readback verification — mandatory postflight After EVERY mutating call against a remote host (`gh issue create`, `gh issue comment`, `gh pr create`, `gh release create`, any API write, `git push`), the returned URL, ID, or exit code is NOT evidence of success. Before reporting the mutation as done: - Read the artifact back FROM the target host into a tmp/ file (`gh issue view --json`, `gh api .../comments/<id>`, `git ls-remote`) and verify from that file only: right target (owner/repo/number — for comments, the parent `issue_url`), exact title, body diffed after ONLY CRLF-to-LF and trailing-final-newline normalization, and the labels/state actually applied. Report only what the readback shows. - Classify the write as exactly one of `confirmed | no_write | unknown`: `confirmed` requires a stable identity AND matching readback; `no_write` requires an authoritative rejection; timeouts, lost responses, mismatched identity, or a body difference beyond the allowed normalization are `unknown`. - `unknown` stops every later mutation and retry on that target — never blind-retry a possibly-succeeded write; re-read state first and ask if it stays ambiguous. - Body-bearing readback data stays in tmp/ and is compared by diff, never printed to the session. - Correct: `gh issue create ... > out.txt` → `gh issue view <N> --json > readback.json` → diff → report `confirmed` with the readback's labels. Wrong: `gh issue create ...` printed a URL → report "issue created ✅". ## Labels — never at creation time `gh issue create` / `gh pr create` MUST be called with ZERO labels: - An unknown label makes the API reject the entire create — the artifact is never published. Labels are triage metadata owned by maintainers; omitting them loses nothing. - If a label is genuinely load-bearing, add it AFTER creation as a separate `gh issue edit <N> --add-label <label>` call, using only names returned by `gh label list`, each with its own readback. A label failure then costs nothing. ```` </details>

title: bug(gentle-shell): missing visual feedback when entering Bash mode with !
body:
## Problem

When typing `!` in the Gentle Shell input to execute a Bash/shell command, the input and its border remain visually unchanged. There is no clear visual feedback distinguishing command execution mode from a normal AI prompt.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open Pi with gentle-pi and Gentle Shell enabled.
2. Observe the input's normal appearance.
3. Type `!`, then a harmless command such as `!pwd`, without submitting it.
4. Compare the input and border with their normal appearance.

## Actual behavior

The input and border do not change color or otherwise visibly indicate Bash mode.

## Expected behavior

Entering Bash mode should immediately make the input visually distinguishable, for example through a theme-aware border/input color change or a clear mode indicator. Removing the `!` prefix should restore the normal appearance.

The distinction should be visible before submitting the command, not only while it is executing.

## Why this matters

This is important visual feedback: users should be able to tell at a glance whether they are composing an AI prompt or a command that will execute in the shell.

## Context

Reported during interactive use; not independently reproduced for this report. Exact affected versions have not been established.

Searched open and closed issues for related shell, Bash, border, and input-color reports; no matching duplicate was found. #601 introduced Gentle Shell but does not describe this specific behavior.

title: bug(review): opaque Pi reviewer inherits placeholder ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from session env → 401 invalid x-api-key
body:
Every Pi host-relay reviewer run fails with `pi-host-relay-transport-failure`, stderr `401 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"authentication_error","message":"invalid x-api-key"}}` (7/7 attempts, distinct request ids), while the byte-identical `pi --print` invocation with scrubbed env (`PATH`+`HOME` only) succeeds repeatedly.

## Root cause

`runOpaquePiReviewer` spawns with `env: options.environment ?? process.env` (`lib/opaque-pi-reviewer-adapter.ts`). The session env carries a harness-injected placeholder `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=omniroute` (9 chars, plus a dead `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` pointing at an unlistened localhost port). Pi's credential resolution prefers env keys over `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`, so the dummy shadows the valid opencode credential and the provider rejects the call.

## Minimal repro

Same argv (`--print --mode text --no-session --no-tools --no-extensions --no-skills --no-prompt-templates --no-themes --no-context-files --no-approve`), same `HOME`, fresh empty cwd:

- full session env → `401 invalid x-api-key`
- `env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (everything else identical) → works, including a ~60KB prompt

Observed via `/proc` sampling: the relayed reviewer process carries the full parent env (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `OPENCODE_ZEN_*`, … present).

## Suggested direction

Mirror the Go-side hardening (gentle-ai `5a081a0d` "preserve Pi authentication locator", which scrubs to process locators) — or drop implausible placeholder keys before spawn. Note the file's `environment untouched` comment documents the opposite intent (user-owned routing), so this needs a maintainer call: placeholders must never shadow real auth, but legitimate routing env must keep flowing.

## Env

- gentle-pi 2.4.0, gentle-ai 2.6.0 pin, Linux
- Pi `defaultProvider: opencode` with valid `auth.json` credential (`pi auth check --provider opencode` → ready)
- Local workaround (ephemeral, node_modules): strip non-`sk-ant-` `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the adapter; relay went green and a reliability-lens review completed on it

title: feat(vision): add capability-based vision fallback for text-only models
body:
### Pre-flight Checks

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand this issue needs `status:approved` before a PR can be opened

### Problem Description

When the active Pi model does not support image input, images attached to the
conversation (pasted images, `read` on image files) are silently dropped: Pi's
provider layer replaces each image block with `(image omitted: model does not
support images)` via its message transform (`downgradeUnsupportedImages`), and
the read tool emits a non-vision note.

Consequence: a user running a strong text-only model gets no image context at
all, and there is no built-in delegation of vision work to another
authenticated model.

### Proposed Solution

Add a gentle-pi extension implementing a capability-based vision fallback,
activated only when the active model lacks image input:

1. **Capability-based model resolution** (no hard-coded provider): optional
   `@vision` role setting -> default model if image-capable -> active model if
   image-capable -> first image-capable model in `ctx.modelRegistry.getAvailable()`.
   Never resolves to a text-only model.
2. **Describe-and-inject**: on `before_provider_request`, replace each outgoing
   image block with a text block `<image path="...">description</image>`, where
   the description comes from a one-shot call to the resolved vision model via
   pi-ai dispatch (the model's `api` field selects the wire, so any provider
   works).
3. **Persisted image**: save each image content-addressed under the session
   directory so later analysis can re-read it.
4. **Explicit re-analysis tool**: `inspect_image(path, question)` always routed
   to the resolved vision model.
5. **Fail-safe**: a failed description leaves a note; it never breaks the turn.

The session model is never switched - vision is a delegated capability.

### Affected Area

Extensions (new extension; no core Pi changes)

### Implementation Steps

- [ ] Capability-chain vision model resolution (auth-scoped only)
- [ ] `before_provider_request` interception for image blocks + text-only model
- [ ] One-shot describe call through pi-ai provider dispatch
- [ ] Content-addressed image persistence per session
- [ ] `inspect_image(path, question)` tool
- [ ] Optional `@vision` role setting
- [ ] Tests: text-only model + image; vision-capable model (no-op); no vision
      model available (note fallback)

title: Add interactive subagent messaging and active-session notifications
body:
## Problem

Delegated work needs a way to report progress, ask for missing information, and coordinate with other active orchestrator sessions without losing task ownership or blocking the parent indefinitely.

## Proposed behavior

- Let subagents send progress notifications to their parent.
- Support correlated background questions and replies using task and request IDs.
- Yield a foreground task when its child asks a question, retaining the running child so the parent can answer. Tasks without questions retain blocking behavior.
- Expose host-only `orchestrator_session_id` and `orchestrator_send_message` tools for notifications between active sessions sharing the same local transport scope.
- Use local Unix sockets with per-activation presence records, bounded messages and pending work, explicit deadlines, and owned-resource cleanup.
- Define acknowledgement as acceptance for handling, not confirmation that a human or model read the message or completed work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Parent-visible notifications and correlated question/reply flows work through the extension.
- [ ] A foreground query releases the parent without cancelling the child or duplicating its terminal result.
- [ ] Active-session notifications preserve sender/recipient identity and reject stale session ownership.
- [ ] Startup, session replacement, shutdown, and failed delivery preserve bounded cleanup and pending-operation semantics.
- [ ] Supported behavior and acknowledgement limits are documented.
- [ ] Independently developed integration and process-test changes are assembled into one candidate and validated together.
- [ ] The combined candidate is activated and tested in the isolated `pi-lab` profile before PR preparation; the principal profile remains unchanged.

## Evidence so far

Work exists in local, uncommitted candidates; this issue does not imply that the feature is published or activated.

- Notifications, background queries/replies, and foreground yielding have prior live validation.
- Cross-session extension integration passed 14 focused host tests and 56 supporting transport/query/runner tests with its pinned Pi 0.74.0 dependencies.
- A separate two-process transport proof passed 4 tests, with 37 transport regression tests passing.
- An isolated Pi SDK 0.85.1 proof passed all 19 phases, including correlated IDs, acceptance acknowledgement, one real Unix connection/acceptance, recipient observation, and owned-resource cleanup.

The SDK proof used local synthetic responses, one internal extension-factory loader API, and manually invoked extension cleanup. It does not establish installed-CLI end-to-end behavior, SDK-dispatched shutdown, or external-provider behavior. Combined-candidate and `pi-lab` validation remain pending.

## Scope boundaries

- Active sessions only; no offline mailbox, persistence across inactive sessions, automatic delivery retries, or broadcast.
- No direct peer-to-peer subagent messaging or bilateral peer trust; that is separate from this scope and from #442.
- No read receipts or completion guarantees.
- No release or publication implied by the issue.

## Related work and integration dependency

#633 tracks runner settlement, process cleanup, and profile-specific storage. This messaging work is separate, but shares implementation surfaces with #634 and #635. Those PRs currently have merge conflicts; their integration relationship must be resolved before preparing the messaging PR, without merging or modifying them as part of issue creation.

title: Candidate view materialization fails on Windows for repositories with committed symlinks
body:
## Defect

`CandidateViewRegistry.createOrReuse` fails on Windows for any repository whose tree contains committed symlinks (mode `120000`), e.g. eduvic-mastra's `.claude/skills/mastra` and `skills/mastra`. `gentle_review` START surfaces this as an opaque `candidate-view-invalid` / "candidate view rejected before native START".

Real error: `candidate view symlink does not match its frozen tree`.

## Root cause (three Windows layers)

1. `checkoutMaterializedEntries` runs `checkout-index -f` in the private worktree. On Windows the repository default is `core.symlinks=false`, so symlink entries are written as plain text files containing the target.
2. Even with `core.symlinks=true` (host has symlink privilege / Developer Mode), Git for Windows rewrites forward-slash targets to backslashes when creating the link.
3. Node/libuv `readlinkSync` on win32 always reports separators as backslashes, so `entryContentHash` can never compare readlink bytes byte-exactly against a forward-slash blob.

## Proposed fix (prototyped and verified)

In `lib/review-candidate-view.ts`:

- Exclude mode `120000` entries from the `checkout-index` batch and materialize them directly from their blob bytes via `fs.symlinkSync`, validating the blob target lexically with `assertSafeSymlinkTarget` first (authoritative bytes, platform-independent rejection of unsafe targets).
- In `entryContentHash`, normalize win32 readlink separators back to `/` before the safety checks and content hash; every other platform stays byte-exact.

## Verification

- Repro: candidate view creation for eduvic-mastra (2 committed symlinks) fails on `main`, succeeds with the fix.
- `tests/review-candidate-view.test.ts` on Windows: tests 38 (symlink target-byte tampering) and 39 (dangling symlink retention) flip fail → pass; 0 regressions. Test 37's symlink-materialization defect is fixed; its residual assertion failure is the separate autocrlf issue below.

## Follow-up (separate issue)

Global `core.autocrlf=true` on Windows contaminates materialized candidate worktrees with CRLF, which explains most of the remaining ~11 Windows-only test failures (e.g. test 37's `example\r\n` readback, exec-bit tests, unborn worktree tests). Materialization likely needs an invocation-scoped `core.autocrlf=false` for `checkout-index`/`read-tree`.

title: bug(review): acknowledge-approved loses committed-only baseRef selector
body:
## Summary

`acknowledge-approved` loses the committed-only `baseRef` selector for an approved review lineage. It queries native STATUS as an empty workspace target and rejects the exact acknowledgement as `native-approved-acknowledgement-not-current`.

## Environment

- gentle-pi: `2.4.0`
- Gentle AI: `2.6.0`
- Client: Pi
- OS: Linux x86_64
- Review shape: committed-only base diff in an isolated Git worktree

## Reproduction

1. Start an ordinary review with a full commit `baseRef` and `committedOnly: true`.
2. Complete the reviewer capture until native last-event closure returns `approved` and an acknowledgement continuation.
3. Call the supported `acknowledge-approved` facade operation with the exact lineage and workspace root.
4. Observe `native-approved-acknowledgement-not-current`; the attached native STATUS projection is an empty `current-changes` workspace rather than the lineage's committed base diff.
5. Re-enter through START using the same full `baseRef`: STATUS correctly recovers the existing approved lineage and returns `approved_acknowledgement_required`.
6. Call `acknowledge-approved` again: it loses the selector again and fails unchanged.

## Expected

The facade retains and reapplies the lineage's committed-only `baseRef` when validating and executing acknowledgement.

## Actual

The acknowledgement route builds target STATUS without `baseRef` or `committedOnly`, evaluates the clean worktree as an unrelated empty candidate, and refuses to burn approved authority.

## Root cause

`CandidateViewRegistry` and retained lifecycle selectors are in-memory. START re-entry returns before retaining the committed selector, while `readRetainedNativeUntrackedSelection` explicitly discards `baseRef` entries. `acknowledge-approved` forbids controller input and therefore has no path to reconstruct the selector.

## Suggested regression

Exercise START/status re-entry for a committed-only base diff, then call `acknowledge-approved` without controller input and assert that native `targetStatus` receives `{ cwd, lineageId, baseRef, committedOnly: true }`.

## Preserved state

- Approved authority remains unburned.
- No acknowledgement mutation occurred.
- Candidate content remains unchanged.

title: feat(issues): add a YAML bug-report form
body:
## Request

Please consider adding a small `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml` while keeping blank issues enabled. The goal is more consistent, actionable bug reports for maintainers and compatibility with reporting tools that require a YAML schema.

Checked against default-branch commit `bc3821fea872ab8456c505be31fc5b0b3204483b`:
