title: bug(extensions): pi-pretty hard-crashes extension load when @heyhuynhgiabuu/pi-pretty is not installed
body:
### Summary

`extensions/pi-pretty.ts` calls `requireFromRealPackage("@heyhuynhgiabuu/pi-pretty")` at module top level with no error handling. In a source checkout where dependencies were never installed (no `node_modules` at all), this turns a missing cosmetic dependency into a hard extension-load failure on every Pi startup, with a confusing `Cannot find module` error that points at `package.json`.

### Error

```text
Error: Failed to load extension "<local gentle-pi checkout>/extensions/pi-pretty.ts": Failed to load extension: Cannot find module '@heyhuynhgiabuu/pi-pretty'
Require stack:
- <local gentle-pi checkout>/package.json
```

### Root cause

Top-level, unguarded require in `extensions/pi-pretty.ts`:

```ts
const packageJsonPath = realpathSync(
  fileURLToPath(new URL("../package.json", import.meta.url)),
);
const requireFromRealPackage = createRequire(packageJsonPath);
const piPrettyModule = requireFromRealPackage("@heyhuynhgiabuu/pi-pretty");
```

pi-pretty is a purely cosmetic enhancement (syntax highlighting, tool-output formatting). When the package cannot be resolved, the exception propagates out of the module and Pi's loader reports the extension as failed, instead of gentle-pi skipping the enhancement with an actionable message.

Observed state of the checkout where this fired:

- `package.json` declares `"@heyhuynhgiabuu/pi-pretty": "0.6.14"` in `dependencies` — the pin is correct
- `pnpm-lock.yaml` is in sync (lockfile entries present for 0.6.14)
- The npm package and the pinned 0.6.14 tarball are intact on the registry (verified via `npm view`)
- `node_modules/` does not exist at all in the checkout — dependencies were simply never installed there, and neither README nor a CONTRIBUTING file documents an install step for running extensions from source

So this is not a registry or versioning problem: any source checkout used directly as a Pi extension directory without `pnpm install` first will crash the pi-pretty extension load on every startup.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Fresh clone of gentle-pi (no `pnpm install`, so no `node_modules`)
2. Point Pi at the checkout's `extensions/` directory
3. Start Pi
4. The pi-pretty extension fails to load with `Cannot find module '@heyhuynhgiabuu/pi-pretty'`

### Impact

- Noisy hard error on every startup for source checkouts and any environment where the dependency is not resolvable
- The error gives no actionable hint (it names `package.json`, not the missing install step)
- A cosmetic feature's absence should not surface as an extension load failure

### Suggested fix

Guard the top-level require and degrade gracefully, for example:

```ts
let piPrettyModule;
try {
  piPrettyModule = requireFromRealPackage("@heyhuynhgiabuu/pi-pretty");
} catch {
  console.error(
    "[gentle-pi] @heyhuynhgiabuu/pi-pretty is not installed; pi-pretty output formatting disabled. Run `pnpm install` to enable it.",
  );
}
```

and export a no-op default extension when the module is missing. This also composes with the fallback-bundle idea discussed in #238 (Option B).

### Relation to #238

#238 covers pi-pretty failing to load in the compiled Pi binary because jiti intercepts `createRequire` even when the package IS installed. This report is the simpler sibling: the package is genuinely absent (no `node_modules`), so even native filesystem resolution fails. Both stem from the same unguarded top-level `requireFromRealPackage(...)` call, and both would be softened by a try/catch plus graceful skip.

### Environment

- Pi: 0.85.1
- gentle-pi: 2.4.0 (source checkout at 62d5efe3)
- @heyhuynhgiabuu/pi-pretty: pinned 0.6.14 (registry intact; not installed locally)
- OS: macOS
- Package manager: pnpm (packageManager pin: pnpm@11.1.1)

title: Excessive cumulative input-token usage across multiple gentle-* agents
body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [ ] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.
- [ ] I understand that PRs require the linked issue to have `status:approved`.

### 📝 Bug Description

Multiple `gentle-*` agents exhibit excessive cumulative input-token usage during extended tasks with repeated continuations.

In one observed session, `gentle-ai-worker` displayed approximately **888k input tokens**. The orchestrator repeatedly continued the same worker across research, implementation, dependency resolution, and follow-up corrections.

The user reports the same pattern in additional `gentle-*` agents, suggesting this is not isolated to one agent definition. Their individual metrics have not yet been collected.

The reported failure is disproportionate context consumption during orchestration. Its underlying cause—and whether accounting contributes to the displayed total—remains unconfirmed.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

Observed sequence; not yet a controlled reproduction:

1. Start an implementation task that requires repository exploration, external documentation, and tests.
2. Delegate work to a `gentle-*` agent.
3. Continue the same agent repeatedly after research blockers and partial results.
4. Reuse that session for subsequent units of work.
5. Observe the cumulative input-token counter growing substantially, including during rounds with limited progress.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Agents should reuse context proportionately to the work being performed.

Independent tasks should not unnecessarily carry a large accumulated history. When continuing an agent would substantially increase consumption, the orchestrator should renew or compact its context, or surface the trade-off to the user.

Usage reporting should distinguish cumulative input from unique context size and identify cached versus uncached tokens where available.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

- Repeated continuations accumulated instructions, source code, documentation, and previous results.
- The same worker was reused across separate units of work.
- Several blocked rounds led to further continuations and context growth.
- One agent displayed approximately **888k input tokens**.
- The user observed similar behavior in other `gentle-*` agents.
- No clear consumption warning was observed before reaching that figure.

### Gentle AI Version

Not collected. The affected integration is **Gentle Pi**; its installed version and the Pi runtime version should be added.

### Operating System

macOS

### AI Agent / Client

Other — Pi with Gentle Pi

### 📋 Affected Area

Other — subagent orchestration and context management

### 💡 Logs / Error Output

No sanitized usage export is attached yet.

The approximately **888k input-token figure** was reported from the agent’s displayed counter.

### Additional Context

Cached-versus-uncached usage, monetary cost, and metrics for the other affected agents remain unverified.

Repeated session continuation is an observed pattern, not a confirmed root cause. Investigation should distinguish:

- Unnecessary context replay or duplication.
- Inefficient orchestration and session reuse.
- Expected cumulative accounting presented ambiguously.
- A possible usage-accounting defect.

This report concerns **Gentle Pi**. The referenced YAML bug template belongs to Gentle AI and requires repository-specific adaptation.

title: bug(herdr): keep working state while background subagents run
body:
## Summary

When the orchestrator launches a Gentle Agent in background mode and becomes available for input again, Herdr stops showing the session as `working` even though the child agent is still active.

Parent input availability is not the same as aggregate session idleness. The visible status should account for background work owned by the session.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run Gentle Pi with Gentle Agents and Herdr enabled.
2. Launch a subagent with `subagent_run` using `mode: "background"`.
3. Let the parent/orchestrator return control to the prompt while the child keeps running.
4. Observe the Herdr header/status.

## Actual behavior

Herdr no longer shows `working` once the parent agent loop ends, although one or more background subagents remain active.

## Expected behavior

Herdr should keep an aggregate active status while owned background tasks are non-terminal. At minimum, queued/running/stopping child work should keep `working` visible; waiting or blocked work may use a stronger dedicated state if available. The session should become idle only after both the parent and every owned background task have settled.

## Evidence from current `main`

Inspected at `60eb3fb4a97fa98d4dcade90247bd7b689c3fec0`:

- `extensions/gentle-shell.ts` sets its working state on parent `agent_start` and clears it on parent `agent_end`.
- `extensions/gentle-agents.ts` returns immediately for a background launch while the child remains active, but it does not project that task lifecycle into Herdr status.
- `extensions/gentle-ai.ts` publishes `herdr:blocked` only for input blockers; it has no aggregate background-work projection.
- Existing Gentle Agents tests cover background execution and completion, while Herdr tests cover blockers separately. No test covers a parent becoming input-ready while a background child remains active.

This points to a missing aggregate bridge between the authoritative Gentle Agents task store and the Herdr-facing status, rather than a completed child being rendered incorrectly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A running background subagent keeps the Herdr session status active after the parent prompt becomes available.
- [ ] With multiple background tasks, the active status remains until the last relevant task settles.
- [ ] Completion, failure, cancellation, timeout, and session shutdown cannot leave a stale `working` state.
- [ ] Parent activity, background activity, and input-blocked states have deterministic precedence.
- [ ] Status comes from the authoritative Gentle Agents task lifecycle, not polling, process inspection, or timing heuristics.
- [ ] A focused regression test reproduces the parent-idle/child-active transition.

## Related work

- #606 / #609 introduced the Gentle Agents background runtime that makes this state possible.
- #430 concerns an in-terminal agent status bar, not Herdr's aggregate session status.
- #134 concerned launching subagents in separate Herdr panes, not preserving `working` for background work.

title: fix: reconcile parent todos at SDD phase boundaries
body:
## Problem

Parent Pi todos can remain `pending` or `in_progress` after an SDD lifecycle has completed successfully.

Pi session todos and SDD/OpenSpec task artifacts are separate state systems. Phase subagents update OpenSpec and memory artifacts but cannot update the parent session todo tool. The orchestrator workflow currently lacks explicit reconciliation checkpoints.

## Expected behavior

The parent orchestrator should reconcile lifecycle todos from authoritative SDD evidence:

- complete the design todo after the design gate passes;
- complete the implementation todo when native status reports `applyState: all_done`;
- complete the closure todo after verify, sync, and archive;
- list and reconcile lifecycle todos before the final response or session summary.

Todo state must remain a progress projection, not an authority for SDD readiness.

## Reproduction

1. Create high-level session todos for design, implementation, and verification/archive.
2. Run an automatic SDD lifecycle through archive using phase subagents.
3. Observe that OpenSpec reports all tasks complete and the change is archived.
4. List parent session todos.

Actual result: the original design todo may remain active while implementation and closure remain pending.

## Acceptance criteria

- The SDD orchestrator workflow explicitly defines all reconciliation checkpoints.
- It states that OpenSpec and memory do not automatically synchronize Pi todos.
- A regression test protects the contract.

title: bug(assets): orphaned global SDD agents never refresh and are invisible to drift after pre-legacy-manifest upgrades
body:
### Problem

Global SDD agents installed by gentle-pi become permanently orphaned: their files never receive package updates, `/gentle:install` reports them as skipped, and the global drift check (`sddGlobalAssetDriftCount`) `continue`s on `!isPackageManagedSddAsset`, so orphans are not even counted as drift. From the user's perspective the install is healthy while every SDD agent is frozen at an old version. Anything delivered through the asset refresh (allowlist updates, the engram capability stamp from #605) never reaches an orphaned install until the user manually deletes `~/.pi/agent/agents/*.md` and reinstalls, which nothing tells them to do.

Two independent triggers converge on the same irreversible step:

**Trigger A, routing-injection desync (confirmed on a live home; [causal evidence](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-pi/issues/608#issuecomment-5622085285)).** Routing injection mutates agent files in place, and its ownership update is best-effort with a blind fallback in both the sync and async apply paths, `extensions/gentle-ai.ts:2803` and `:2854`:

```ts
if (!updatePackageManagedSddAgentOwnership(agent.filePath, original, next)) {
	writeFileSync(agent.filePath, next);
}
```

`updatePackageManagedSddAgentOwnership` returns `false` when the manifest hash does not match the pre-injection content (lib/sdd-preflight.ts:500). On that branch the file is still written and the manifest keeps the stale hash: file and manifest diverge silently, and nothing reports it. Only `agents/` files reach this path (`chains/` and `gentle-ai/support/` are never rewritten post-install, which is exactly the boundary the surviving manifest entries in the linked evidence fall on). Any prior desync (an interrupted write, a manifest rollback, an earlier version's update path) becomes permanent and self-propagating.

**Trigger B, closed-set reclaim (originally reported as a pre-legacy-manifest hash gap; confirmed structural on 2.7.0).** `installSddAssets`' forced refresh skips any installed file whose content hash does not match the manifest entry (and deletes the entry), and for a manifest-less file (`managedHash === undefined`, lib/sdd-preflight.ts:680) the only adoption route consults a closed inventory of past snapshots, `legacyAssetHashes` at :681, rejecting anything absent from it (:688-693). That inventory has since grown from three manifests to four (`managed-assets-{v0.10.7,v0.13,v0.14,v2.5.0}.json`), which proves the point rather than fixing it: the ladder gains one snapshot per notable version, so the current version's content is unknown to every past snapshot by construction, and the branch never compares installed content against the packaged asset being shipped (`source`) at all. Files installed by any other historical version are treated as user edits forever, and a version whose hashes were never enumerated orphans every asset it installed.

**The irreversible step.** Once either trigger has desynced file and manifest, the forced refresh converts "managed but stale" into "unknown", `lib/sdd-preflight.ts:701`:

```ts
} else if (installedHash !== managedHash) {
	delete manifest.assets[ownershipKey];
	skipped += 1;
	continue;
}
```

The entry is deleted, so the legacy-hash reclaim path is the only remaining route, and it compares against packaged content that injected `model:`/`thinking:` frontmatter no longer matches. Without `--force` the earlier branch never consults the manifest at all, so repeated installs report "already present" and repair nothing.

### Environment

Observed on live agent homes upgraded through the 2.x line:

- `~/.pi/agent/agents/sdd-*.md` carried a pre-2.3 tool list (`glob`, `webfetch` era) while the package assets had moved on (`find`, `codegraph`, `mem_*`).
- One home's `~/.pi/agent/gentle-ai/managed-assets.json` held 7 entries, 0 under `agents/`; another held exactly 5, all under `chains/` and `gentle-ai/support/`, with all `agents/` entries lost (the split that isolates Trigger A).
- A forced `installSddAssets` returned `agents: 0, skipped: 23` and left every file untouched; recovery required manually deleting the 23 package-named agent files and re-running the install. Post-repair, the manifest records the post-injection content hash, proving the ownership-preserving path works when file and manifest are in sync at injection time.
- 2.7.0 reproduction (Pi 0.85.1, macOS; [comment](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-shell/issues/608#issuecomment-5687949751)): with all 14 `agents/sdd-*.md` absent and the manifest holding only `chains/` and `gentle-ai/support/` entries, the files were restored byte-identical from `node_modules/gentle-pi/assets/agents/` (13 of 14 exact; the 14th differed only by the `model:` line removed in #216). `/gentle:install-sdd --force` created zero `agents/` entries and left every mtime unchanged: the closed set rejects even byte-identity with the content the install itself ships. The documented recovery (delete, then reinstall without `--force`) registered all 14, with a full-hash verification of the resulting 21 manifest entries coming back clean.

### Expected

Orphaned package agents are reclaimed when their content matches a known historical package asset or the content the package currently ships, or their existence is surfaced (drift count plus a repair command) so the user can recover without tribal knowledge. Ownership should not depend solely on a hash manifest that post-install writers can silently desync and upgrades can invalidate.

### Suggested directions

Refined after the live-home causal evidence and the 2.7.0 closed-set reproduction; the detection marker and the write-path fix are complementary, not alternatives:

1. Make the routing injection fail loud instead of writing through: a package-managed agent whose ownership update fails is a defect, not a user edit. Either refuse the write or update file and manifest transactionally under the existing managed-assets lock, so the blind fallback cannot create the desync in the first place.
2. Surface file-vs-manifest divergence before the next `--force`, which is the point of no return: count drifted manifest entries and installed `sdd-*` files with no manifest entry in the drift `/gentle:status` already reports, with a repair path.
3. Treat an in-file ownership marker (a frontmatter key or trailing comment written at install time) as the primary ownership signal for detection and recovery, with the manifest hash as an integrity check rather than identity, and/or adopt manifest-less files in place when their comparable content matches the packaged asset (`legacyComparableAssetContent(ownershipKey, installedContent) === source` under the `managedHash === undefined` branch). Extending the reclaim inventory alone cannot close this gap: by construction it never contains the current version's content, which the 2.7.0 reproduction demonstrates on files byte-identical to what the install itself ships.

### Relations

- Gates the reach of #605 (the engram `subagentOnlyExtensions` stamp only touches manifest-matching files): orphaned installs keep the #593 failure mode even after that fix merges.
- Adjacent to but distinct from #354 (that one is local `.pi/agents` overrides shadowing package agents; this is global orphans).

title: feat(models): make project-scoped agent model routing effective (project overrides global)
body:
## Summary

Project-scoped agent model routing (`.pi/gentle-ai/models.json`) is silently ineffective: whenever the global config exists, it always wins, and the saved-routing UI persists to the global file regardless of the working directory. On top of that, the session-start apply rewrites project `.pi/subagents.json` model profiles from the resolved global config, so hand edits to project-level routing are overwritten on the next session.

Net effect: a user who configures "other gentle:models" inside a project keeps getting the global routing, and cannot scope model routing per project at all.

## Current behavior (verified on `main` @ 525812fb, observed on installed 2.3.0)

1. **Global wins whenever it exists** — `lib/model-routing-authority.ts` (`readSavedModelConfig` / `readSavedModelConfigAsync`):

   ```ts
   const globalResult = readModelConfigFile(globalPath);
   if (globalResult.status !== "missing") return globalResult;
   return readModelConfigFile(projectPath);
   ```

   The project path is reached only as a fallback when the global file is missing, and it is named `legacyProjectModelConfigPath` in `extensions/gentle-ai.ts` — so project scope is legacy-fallback-only by construction.

2. **The models panel always writes to the global file** — `extensions/gentle-ai.ts`:

   ```ts
   function modelConfigPath(_cwd: string): string {
       return join(gentleAiConfigHome(), "models.json");
   }
   ```

   The `cwd` parameter is ignored; saving from inside a project mutates global state.

3. **Session-start apply clobbers project-level hand edits** — `applyModelConfigAsync` writes the resolved (global-winning) entries into the project `.pi/subagents.json` `model_profiles` (and agent frontmatter) for every discoverable agent present in the config. Reproduced: after starting a session in the project, project and global `subagents.json` were byte-identical with identical mtimes.

## Reproduction

- Global `~/.pi/gentle-ai/models.json` exists with routing for the standard agents.
- Project has no `.pi/gentle-ai/models.json`; hand-editing project `.pi/subagents.json` model profiles is reverted on next session start.
- Configuring models through the panel while cwd is the project writes the global file.

## Impact

- Per-project model routing is impossible, although a project path exists in the code and is silently read as a fallback (surprising dead configuration surface).
- Panel saves from a project silently change global state (data goes somewhere the user did not aim at).
- Project `.pi/subagents.json` looks like project config but behaves as a derived sync output.

## Relation to existing work

- This is the concrete user-facing gap behind the pending #381 outcome item: *"Explicit project and global targeting and Pi config-root overrides are deterministic."*
- #58 explicitly deferred project-level model profiles ("Another option would be project-level model profiles, but this proposal intentionally keeps profiles...").
- #391 (approved) adds canonical names/target authority but explicitly does not change durable writes or profile materialization.

## Proposal

Make project-scoped routing effective and deterministic:

- **Precedence:** per-entry merge with project winning per agent name — `merge(global, project)` — instead of whole-file fallback. Entries present only in global keep applying; a project entry overrides the global entry for that agent.
- **Panel target scope:** the saved-routing panel offers an explicit **Global / Project** save target (project target available when the cwd is a project with `.pi/`), writing to the chosen scope.
- **Apply contract:** documented rule for what apply writes where (e.g. winning project entries also materialize into project `.pi/subagents.json`; global-only entries continue to materialize for user-scope agents), so project files stop being silently rewritten from global-only state.

## Open questions for maintainers

1. Should the project file keep the legacy name (`.pi/gentle-ai/models.json`) or move to a non-legacy canonical path as part of the #391 target-authority work?
2. Should empty/`{}` entries in project scope *clear* an inherited global entry for that agent (explicit override), or be ignored?
3. Does Pi-core's own project-vs-global `subagents.json` resolution need to stay in sync with whatever precedence is chosen here?

## Environment

- gentle-pi 2.3.0 (installed), code verified against `main` @ 525812fb
- Pi 0.85.0, Linux x86-64

title: bug(review): RENAMED arrow headings are double-counted in native line budgets
body:
## Summary

A native SDD/review line counter counts a single OpenSpec `RENAMED` heading written as `Old → New` twice. This inflates the authored-line or correction-budget value even though the Markdown contains one changed line.

Observed with the current integration surface around `gentle-pi@2.4.0` and the bundled Gentle AI native runtime contract `2.6.0`.

## Minimal reproduction

1. Create a small OpenSpec change with a renamed requirement expressed in the compact form:

   ```markdown
   ## RENAMED Requirements

   ### Requirement: Old → New
   ```

2. Run the native SDD/review status path that reports authored lines or the correction budget.
3. Compare the reported count with the same change written without the arrow-form rename heading.

## Expected behavior

The `Old → New` heading is one authored Markdown line and should contribute once to line/budget accounting. If `RENAMED` deltas are unsupported, the parser should reject the construct explicitly rather than partially interpret it.

## Actual behavior

The native counter accounts for the heading twice, apparently once for each side of the arrow. This can raise the reported workload and consume bounded correction authority faster than the actual diff warrants.

## Impact

- Review workload and correction budgets are overstated.
- Changes near a native line threshold may be routed or blocked incorrectly.
- The behavior is surprising because the JavaScript snapshot path documents diff-line accounting, while OpenSpec delta support currently documents `RENAMED` as unsupported.

## Workaround

Avoid the `Old → New` compact heading form and describe the rename without the arrow syntax.

## Relevant surfaces

- `lib/review-risk.ts` — authored changed-line and correction-budget calculation
- `lib/review-snapshot.ts` — snapshot diff-line derivation
- `lib/openspec-deltas.ts` — supported delta headings
- `assets/agents/sdd-spec.md` — current `RENAMED` support policy

The exact double-count appears to occur across the native boundary; a regression test should pin the provider-reported count for the minimal Markdown above.

title: bug(agents): SDD child sessions lose mem_* tools because the engram extension is never provisioned
body:
## Problem

gentle-pi's SDD agent frontmatters declare `mem_*` tools (the allowlist fix landed as `84577d614` and follow-ups, tracked from Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai#602), but the capability those names reference is registered by the `npm:gentle-engram` Pi extension, and no shipped agent declares that extension for child sessions.

Children only resolve `mem_save` when they inherit global extension loading. Any launch path that pins `extensions` for the child loses Engram while `--tools` still declares `mem_save`, producing two public failure shapes on gentle-ai#602:

- **ccarrenoc (Aug 27, occurrence `sdd-child-tools-2026-08-26-a`)**: OpenSpec-only `sdd-explore`, Engram behind the MCP adapter's aggregate proxy, `pi-subagents 0.52.1`. The child hard-failed at launch with `Agent 'sdd-explore' requested unavailable child tools: mem_save` (strict validation catching declaration-without-capability).
- **wahh-22 (Sep 4, occurrence `pi-engram-explore-2026-09-04-a`)**: Engram artifact-store `sdd-explore` on `gentle-pi 2.3.0`, macOS arm64. The child completed its read-only analysis but returned `status: partial` with the artifact `not_persisted`, because Engram tools were unavailable in the executor runtime (silent capability loss).

## Mechanism (verified against pi-subagents source)

- `src/runs/shared/pi-args.ts`: frontmatter `tools:` entries that contain no `/` and do not end in `.ts`/`.js` are passed as builtin names via `--tools`; only path-like entries become `--extension` arguments.
- `mem_save` and friends are not Pi builtins (`BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES` = `read, bash, edit, write, grep, find, ls, mcp`); they exist only when the gentle-engram extension loads in that session.
- When a child launch supplies an `extensions` value (including an empty list, see `src/agents/agent-management.ts`: `extensions: ""` parses to `[]`), the child starts with `--no-extensions` plus only the explicitly listed extensions. Nothing in gentle-pi's agent assets or install adds gentle-engram to that list.
- Result: the `mem_*` declarations are conditional on ambient global extension inheritance. Environments that inherit globals see working children (why live-install verification on Linux passed on gentle-ai#602, and why #586's machine has working `mem_*`); environments that pin extensions see either a strict-validation launch failure (pi-subagents 0.52.1+) or a silently memory-blind child.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install the Pi stack with Engram available to the parent session (parent `mem_*` tools work).
2. Launch an SDD phase child (`sdd-explore`) through a path where `extensions` is pinned for the child (for example an agent-management config with `extensions: ""`, or a launcher that supplies an explicit extension list).
3. On pi-subagents with strict child-tool validation: the launch fails with `requested unavailable child tools: mem_save`. Without it: the child runs but cannot persist its phase artifact (`not_persisted`, `status: partial` when the artifact store is Engram).

## Expected Behavior

An SDD agent that declares a `mem_*` tool receives a working tool in its child session regardless of how extensions are provisioned for that child, or the launch blocks with an actionable capability mismatch before the phase runs.

## Actual Behavior

Child sessions silently lose Engram (or hard-fail at launch on pi-subagents 0.52.1+) because the `mem_*` frontmatter declaration carries no matching extension provisioning.

## Fix Direction

Make the capability travel with the declaration instead of relying on ambient inheritance:

- declare the engram extension for the agents that reference `mem_*` tools (pi-subagents frontmatter `subagentOnlyExtensions` exists for exactly this child-only capability shape), or
- switch those agents to the documented MCP route (`mcp:engram` direct tools),
- and pin whichever contract is chosen in `tests/sdd-agent-tools.test.ts`.

When a declared-but-unprovisioned tool is rejected, surfacing a clear capability diagnostic instead of a partial phase would also address the diagnostic gap raised in #586 for the adapter path.

## Scope Separation

- Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai#602 tracks the original report; its allowlist half is fixed on gentle-pi `main`. This issue is the runtime capability half.
- #586 is the same child-provisioning family but the inverse case: there `mem_*` works and Context7 via pi-mcp-adapter returns `MCP not initialized`.
- #62 covers the YAML tools-frontmatter parsing shape (pinned by `2a10839d`/`6179710e`); different layer.

title: bug(subagents): Context7 MCP is visible in Windows child agents but returns "MCP not initialized"
body:
## Problem

On a native Windows Pi installation configured through the Gentle Pi stack, child/subagent sessions can use Engram through the `mem_*` bridge, but cannot use Context7 through `pi-mcp-adapter`.

The subagent tool allowlist includes `mcp`, and the orchestrator can use Context7 successfully, but the subagent receives:

```text
MCP not initialized
```

## Environment

- OS: native Windows
- Runtime: Pi with Gentle Pi stack
- Packages involved:
  - `gentle-pi`
  - `gentle-engram`
  - `pi-subagents-j0k3r`
  - `pi-mcp-adapter`
  - Context7 MCP server
- Current install/update state: user reports everything fully updated

## Observed behavior

- Orchestrator:
  - Context7 via MCP works.
- Subagent:
  - Engram works via `mem_*`.
  - It saved an observation successfully.
  - It read that observation back successfully.
  - Tool allowlist includes `mem_*` and `mcp`.
  - Calling Context7 through `mcp` returns `MCP not initialized`.

## Attempted mitigation

We tested:

```json
{
  "session_resources": "full"
}
```

globally, then restarted/reloaded Pi.

Result: no change. Context7 still returns `MCP not initialized` inside the subagent.

The setting was reverted because it made subagent sessions heavier without fixing the issue.

## Expected behavior

If Gentle Pi exposes or depends on MCP-backed tools for subagent workflows, child agents should either:

1. initialize `pi-mcp-adapter` correctly inside the nested session; or
2. fail with a clear capability diagnostic explaining that MCP is unavailable in child agents and that the orchestrator must pass Context7 results down explicitly.

A visible `mcp` tool that only returns `MCP not initialized` is misleading and makes the stack look broken.

## Actual behavior

The subagent sees the `mcp` tool but the adapter runtime state is not initialized in the nested session.

This creates a split-brain result:

```text
Engram bridge: works
MCP/Context7: visible but unusable
```

## Current workaround

The practical workaround is:

```text
Orchestrator queries Context7 → passes the relevant docs/evidence to the subagent in the task context
```

This works, but it means subagents cannot independently consult Context7 even when their allowlist says they can use `mcp`.

## Related prior issues

This may overlap with, but does not appear identical to, prior upstream issues:

- `nicobailon/pi-mcp-adapter#428` — failed initialization latches MCP off for a session.
- `nicobailon/pi-mcp-adapter#222` — permanent `not_initialized` state.
- `nicobailon/pi-mcp-adapter#219` — direct MCP tools in child processes.
- `nicobailon/pi-subagents#1146` — regression with `mcp:context7` direct MCP tool selection.

This report is specifically about the Gentle Pi user experience on native Windows where:

- generic `mcp` is allowlisted and visible in the child;
- `mem_*` works in the same child;
- `session_resources: "full"` does not fix it;
- the orchestrator can use Context7;
- the child receives `MCP not initialized`.

## Requested outcome

Please clarify and/or fix Gentle Pi's supported contract for Context7/MCP in subagents:

- If MCP in child agents is intended to work, ensure the installed Gentle Pi/subagent setup initializes or wires `pi-mcp-adapter` correctly.
- If MCP in child agents is not currently supported, update the installed agents/docs/prompts so the orchestrator performs Context7 lookups and passes the result to children instead of implying the child can call MCP directly.

title: review: follow-up field report — 15-commit sliced series through the Pi host
body:
# Review field report: 15-commit sliced series through the Pi host

## Summary

This is a follow-up session report, not a duplicate of the narrower issues linked below. A TypeScript change originally spanning approximately 181 files and 37k changed lines was split into 12 dependency-ordered units, followed by two bounded correction commits and one documentation/rules commit (15 commits total).

Three selected candidates completed the Pi/native review lifecycle and burned approved authorities. A fourth candidate was intentionally left unreviewed after the human cancelled its consent prompt. The session shows that the native CLI route can complete, while the Pi orchestration surface still imposes substantial manual handling for bindings, subprocess dispatch, context size, and clean-state transitions.

## Session workflow

```text
inspect/status
  -> split work above the review budget
  -> committed-range START
  -> relay candidate-scoped consent
  -> exact native STATUS
  -> materialize one provider task per lens
  -> run constrained reviewer
  -> submit exact result through native capture
  -> refute/correct/validate when the transition requires it
  -> acknowledge-approved
  -> ordinary repository delivery decision
```

Pi did not answer consent, invent lifecycle tokens, or treat approval as commit/push authority. The successful path used file-based CLI output and bounded summaries when MCP responses became too large for the parent context.

## Review rounds and reasons

| Review | Risk/lenses | Outcome | Why this number of rounds |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unit 6 | High, four lenses | One review round, refutation, bounded correction, targeted validation, acknowledgement | High risk required four independent lenses. An inferential severe finding required the native refutation stage; corroborated severe findings opened one bounded correction. |
| Unit 9 | Medium, one reliability lens | One review round, bounded correction, targeted validation, acknowledgement | Medium risk selected one lens. The severe finding was deterministic, so no refuter was needed; one correction was enough. |
| Unit 12 | High candidate | Consent cancelled; no round | The human chose not to review this candidate. Pi correctly did not answer consent or start the lineage. |
| AGENTS.md | Medium, one reliability lens | One review round, non-blocking suggestion, acknowledgement | The candidate was classified as executable policy; the only finding was informational, so no correction or refutation was required. |

There were nine reviewer process runs including provider-failure and malformed-result re-runs. Three authorities burned successfully; one candidate remained unreviewed by explicit human choice.

## Errors, failures, blocks, and rejections observed from the host perspective

- The first direct native STATUS was blocked because the Pi relay contract environment was absent; the required value was not printed by the error and had to be discovered from package source.
- The intended-untracked selection surface rejected an empty selection and did not provide a usable “exclude all” path for the committed-only continuation.
- The controller/MCP route and the direct CLI route did not accept the same provider-issued collect route in all cases; exact bindings were rejected as belonging to another session route.
- Purpose-built `review-*` reviewer dispatch was rejected unless the execution mode and current controller-owned binding were present, so generic constrained reviewers were used as a fallback.
- Native admission rejected malformed proof references, requiring the same lens to be resumed with a corrected result.
- A provider rate limit and malformed reviewer output required bounded re-runs rather than blind new starts.
- A repository-context mismatch required a fresh exact STATUS before targeted validation could proceed.

## Reactive and recovery actions that worked

- Export the relay contract for direct CLI calls.
- Use the provider-issued transition as the only source of lifecycle arguments.
- Resume the same reviewer after a retry-safe failure or malformed result.
- Fall back to the direct CLI/native capture route when the controller route could not consume its binding.
- Keep STATUS and validation inside a clean committed-range window.
- Use native refutation, correction planning, targeted validation, and acknowledgement rather than host-authored verdicts.

## Tool output and context pressure

MCP STATUS responses embedded complete collect bindings and repeated changed-path manifests. A four-lens review could move well over 100 KB of protocol material through the parent session before reviewer output. Materialized tasks for broad candidates were thousands of lines. This caused rapid context growth and made exact retransmission fragile.

The practical mitigation was to write provider output to `tmp/`, validate JSON with `jq empty`, generate commands from those files, and pass only bounded summaries to the parent. A first-class bounded handle or file-backed capture surface would remove this operational burden.

## Source discoverability

The host had to inspect Gentle AI/Gentle Pi source and contracts to learn the relay environment, selection and admission grammars, reviewer result shape, transition rules, and route boundaries. This is understandable for implementation debugging but too expensive for a normal review session; the runtime should expose a concise, executable troubleshooting path.

## Expected improvements

1. Inject or clearly expose the relay contract for Pi shell invocations.
2. Make controller and direct CLI bindings interoperable, or fail with a prominent route-boundary explanation.
3. Allow reviewer personas to execute a self-contained provider task without requiring a controller-owned binding, where safe.
4. Add bounded/file-backed STATUS and capture transport for large collect bindings.
5. Surface actionable admission diagnostics while preserving fail-closed native validation.
6. Add a session-level human deferral for a candidate that was explicitly declined or postponed, without suppressing reminders for a materially new candidate.

## Related issues

- gentle-pi#543 — inline collect-binding/context growth;
- gentle-pi#550 and #578 — relay contract injection and documentation;
- gentle-pi#509 — capture route binding rejection;
- gentle-pi#544 — reviewer personas as Pi subagents;
- gentle-pi#551, #573, and #581 — earlier session reports and route findings;
- gentle-ai#2029, #3922, #4019, #4074, and #4082 — provider-side counterparts.

## Environment

- gentle-pi: `2.3.0`
- Native `gentle-ai`: `main` build string
- Contract: `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`
- Host: Pi on macOS

No private paths, tokens, lineage identifiers, or raw provider payloads are included here.

title: review: session report #4 — 13-unit staged series via direct CLI + mirror route (3 corrections, 1 scope_changed recovery, route gaps)
body:
# Session report #4 — 13-unit staged series via direct CLI + mirror route: 3 corrections, 1 scope_changed recovery, and the route gaps it exposed

Follow-up to #551 / #577 / #573. Full negotiated v2 campaign from Pi (`--agent pi`, host-relay captures, contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`) over a staged 13-unit commit series (~37k changed lines: refactor + features, 24 src + ~120 test files). All runs from a plain bash tool in the pi host shell with `GENTLE_PI_REVIEW_RELAY_CONTRACT` exported manually.

## Route

Mirror worktree checked out at each unit commit; `review start --base-ref <parent> --committed-only --consent relay|granted`; per collect input: `capture-result --materialize=true` prints the binding+brief → host runs the reviewer → resubmit raw result with `--input`. Committed ranges only.

## Results

- 10 completed review cycles: 13 units covered (3 four-lens keystones, 1 four-lens cumulative via recovery successor, 5 single-lens, 2 docs).
- 3 correction rounds (all ≤49/200 lines) + targeted validation: all approved.
- 1 scope_changed recovery (cumulative lineage → successor) — worked once the binding was self-derived.
- ~40 advisory findings (WARNING/SUGGESTION) recorded as non-blocking follow-ups.
- Final gates on the delivered branch: lint clean (after one formatter fix), typecheck 0 errors, full suite green.

## Route gaps exposed (details in prior reports where already filed)

1. Evidence prose scanning (`evidence_path_out_of_scope`): host scratch dir references, `/:389` line-number chains, and leading-slash labels in reviewer evidence/claims trip the repository-path scanner; behavior inconsistent between identical-shaped artifacts; diagnostic does not name the offending token (#2029 adjacent).
2. Strict decode rejects reviewer prose fields (`severity_note`/`claim_note`) — had to fold notes into `claim` text; allowed field set is not discoverable at submit time.
3. Progressive collect rounds on high tier (risk admitted → STATUS then offers the remaining 3 lens slots) — undocumented; orchestrators must re-poll.
4. `gentle_review_capture` (controller route) rejects bindings minted via the direct CLI route ("different session routes") — the two routes do not interoperate (#509 adjacent); we ran the entire campaign pure-CLI.
5. `review recover`: hand-built maintainer-authorization bindings always rejected; omitting the flag self-derives the binding (see #4077 / #1612 / #3401). Also `--base-ref` rejects the tree id the predecessor recorded as its base (needs a commit-ish).
6. `review start` via a session route silently clamped the requested base-ref to the session base and offered a cumulative candidate (67 files vs the requested unit's 9) — only `changed_files/lines` revealed it.
7. Pre-split HEAD calibration: relative gates (no-new-typecheck-errors vs parent, lint 3-run union because Biome is nondeterministic run-to-run) were required; absolute gates only pass at series end.
8. Intermediate-state BLOCKERs are inherent when reviewing mid-series ranges (consumers updated in later units) — the correction that "restores the legacy call shape" at the intermediate state is legitimate and validated, then supersedes via the later units.

## What worked well

Consent relay per candidate; frozen immutable briefs; `retry_safe` rejections; union-of-3 lint sampling; targeted validation of corrections; correction budget honored (largest actual: 36/200).

title: enhancement: upstream portable orchestrator preflight rules (generated scripts, JSON strip-first, native-derived values) as a skill
body:
# [enhancement] Upstream portable orchestrator preflight rules as a gentle-pi skill

A consumer project hit five recurring failure classes while driving the native review relay from
shell tools, and codified the fixes as AGENTS.md rules. They generalize beyond the project and
would fit a gentle-pi skill (e.g. `native-review-orchestration`, or an extension of the gentle-ai
skill):

1. **Todo/task tool shape** — every tool call carries its own discriminator field
   (`action`); batch calls each need their own; payload fields alone fail schema validation.
2. **Generated scripts** — a script that writes another script must keep wrapper variables
   (`REPO=`, `cd`, `export`) as literal text in the generated file (never expanded by the
   writer's quoting); embed only data-file values; verify the generated header before running.
3. **CLI output parsing** — strip non-JSON prefix lines (e.g. `ok <sha>`) via
   `awk '/^{/{flag=1} flag' in.out > in.json` before parsing; isolate parse steps outside `&&`
   chains; never hand-copy tokens read from JSON — regenerate commands from the data files.
4. **Native-derived exact values** — never hand-author bindings/tokens/digests the CLI derives
   (e.g. recovery authorization): run without the value so the CLI derives it, or extract it
   programmatically; attach the derived value last.
5. **JSON authoring via `jq`** — validate/canonicalize generated JSON before submission (with the
   carve-out that raw CLI output must be awk-stripped first, since it is not parseable JSON).

Evidence: each rule was forced by a real failure in a 10-cycle review campaign (schema validation
rejections, run-time empty-expansion breakage, JSON prefix SyntaxError, hand-built binding
rejection). A paired docs issue covers the relay protocol itself.

title: docs: document the native review relay orchestrator protocol (host-relay captures, direct CLI route)
body:
# [documentation] Document the native review relay orchestrator protocol for host-relay captures (direct CLI route)

Driving `gentle-ai review` from shell tools with `--agent pi` (host-relay transport) currently
requires reverse-engineering the sequence across multiple rejections. Proposal: a docs page
(or skill section) covering the orchestrator protocol for the direct CLI route:

1. `GENTLE_PI_REVIEW_RELAY_CONTRACT=gentle-pi.review-relay/v1` must be exported before every
   `gentle-ai review` call (the preflight failure names neither the variable nor the value).
2. START (after consent relay) → execute the returned `review.status` command verbatim → collect
   inputs.
3. Per collect input with `--materialize=true`: the CLI prints the provider task to stdout
   (`GENTLE_AI_REVIEW_BINDING` header + instructions + frozen patch). The host runs the reviewer
   against that brief and produces the reviewer result JSON
   (`subject_hash` echo; `inspection.paths` = complete changed-path manifest; findings with
   `id/location/claim/proof_refs/severity/evidence_class/causal_disposition`).
4. Resubmit with the exact `submission.argument_tokens` (note: these carry `--input={{value}}`
   while the collect `arguments` carry `--materialize=true` — the two arrays are not
   interchangeable).
5. High tier offers collect rounds progressively (first lens, then the remaining lens slots in a
   later STATUS round): re-poll STATUS after each admission batch.
6. Closure paths: `approved` + acknowledgement command, or `correction_required` →
   `capture-correction-plan` → corrected-candidate commit → `capture-validation --execute=true` →
   approved → acknowledge. Scope changes require `review recover` (self-derived authorization —
   run without `--maintainer-authorization`; `--base-ref` must be a commit-ish, not the recorded
   tree id).

Evidence: a 10-cycle campaign (13 units, ~37k lines; 3 corrections + validations, 1 scope_changed
recovery) completed on this route; per-cycle gaps filed separately. Happy to contribute the draft
page.

title: docs: document review relay configuration (relay contract env, dev-binary override, reviewer timeout)
body:
Title: `docs: document review relay configuration (relay contract env, dev-binary override, reviewer timeout)`
Repo: Gentleman-Programming/gentle-pi · Type: `documentation` · Labels: `documentation`

## Problem
Operating the native review loop on a machine whose environment is not the default required discovering three configuration surfaces by trial and error (and source reading). None appear in the README/docs:

1. `GENTLE_PI_REVIEW_RELAY_CONTRACT` — the native CLI refuses review operations with `immutable_review_transport_unsupported` unless the environment declares `gentle-pi.review-relay/v1`; the error says to export it but not its value.
2. Dev-binary override — the relay resolves a package-pinned gentle-ai binary unless `~/.pi/gentle-ai/dev-binary.json` exists with exactly `{"schema":"gentle-pi.dev-binary/v1","path":"<absolute path>"}`; the path must be a regular non-symlink executable (a symlinked `~/.local/bin/gentle-ai` is rejected). Field-testing `main` against a differently-versioned pinned binary produces `managed_assets_outdated` with no hint of the skew.
3. `GENTLE_PI_REVIEW_RELAY_PI_TIMEOUT_MS` — reviewer subprocess wall-time bound (observed default ~1000s; ceiling 7200000). Too low for high-tier lens runs with ~200KB materialized prompts; only settable at pi process launch.

## Suggested docs
- A "Review relay configuration" section: the three variables/registration files above, their defaults, ceilings, and the failure codes they resolve (`immutable_review_transport_unsupported`, `managed_assets_outdated`, `pi-host-relay-timeout`).
- A troubleshooting entry for dual gentle-ai binaries in PATH (doctor already warns; link the two).

title: review: session report #3 to #551 — 7-batch committed-range walk via the direct CLI route: 7/7 approved, zero corrections, and the route gaps it exposed
body:
# Session report #3 — 7-batch committed-range walk over the direct CLI route: end-to-end approval, zero corrections, and the route gaps it exposed

Follow-up to #551 (first full negotiated-v2 session report) and #573 (follow-up: concurrent-4R gating, personas, lens timeouts). This session adds a different shape of evidence: a **success** — the full negotiated v2 lifecycle driven entirely through the **direct gentle-ai CLI** on committed ranges, seven times in a row, with zero escalations and zero corrections — plus the residual gaps that still made it harder than the mirrored contract implies.

## Context

Candidate: a ~37k-line uncommitted change in a Pi extension repo (tintinweb/pi-subagents: monolith decomposition of `index.ts` plus ~40 new modules and ~130 test files). The 400-line review workload gate forced a split first:

1. 32 work-unit commits on a feature branch (baseline green: lint 0, typecheck 0, 820 tests).
2. Seven checkpoint reviews over committed ranges `base-ref → HEAD`, executed by walking existing commits in detached-HEAD states (no history rewrite), since the CLI reviews base→HEAD only.
3. Each batch: selectorless STATUS → START (`--consent=relay`) → lossless consent envelope relayed to the human via ask_user_choice → per-lens `capture-result --materialize` → reviewer result submitted via `--input` → closure → STATUS restart → exact `acknowledge-approved`.

## What worked (counter-evidence for #551 / gentle-ai#4031)

- **7/7 lineages approved + acknowledged, receipts burned and visible.** No escalation rounds, no corrections, no refuters — versus #551's 3 escalation rounds and #4031's report that receipts are invisible after burn. In this session every burn printed the `gentle-ai.review-acknowledged/v1` envelope and a later STATUS read back clean terminal state.
- **Committed-range reviews closed cleanly** (7× base-ref + committed-only START → capture → acknowledge), which is positive evidence for the conditions in #569.
- **The consent envelope's `choices[].invocation` replayed exactly** — using the granted invocation verbatim (with `--consent granted`) worked every time.
- Preflight (`capture-result --preflight --input`, no `--agent`) caught a malformed result once without consuming the lens slot — retry-safe as documented.
- Sequential lens runs through the CLI admission were stable: 19 lens results admitted across 7 lineages, one resubmission (self-inflicted, see below).

## Gaps this session exposed

1. **Route fragmentation blocks concurrent reviewer groups.** `gentle_review_capture` (MCP) rejected the lineage created by direct CLI START with `capture-binding-rejected: "belongs to a different session route"` (relates #509, #573, #544). Result: the mandated concurrent reviewer-group launch was unreachable; all 16 four-lens runs executed sequentially inside the parent session. The parent ended up reviewing its own candidate — no fresh-context isolation per lens.
2. **The direct CLI route is absent from the mirrored contract.** The injected contract (#560) documents the MCP/ask_user_choice route but not: the per-command `GENTLE_PI_REVIEW_RELAY_CONTRACT=gentle-pi.review-relay/v1` export (relates #550), `capture-result --materialize` → author → `--input` submission, `--preflight` slot-checking, or `--consent=relay` envelope flow. I reconstructed the loop from `--help` output, binary `strings`, and the gentle-pi source. One documented CLI fallback loop in the mirrored contract would have removed ~40 minutes of discovery.
3. **Envelope token canonicalization is implicit.** Extracting `lineage`/`target` from envelope top-level fields and re-assembling a granted START yields `negotiated review start lineage is not canonical`; only `choices[].invocation` is canonical. A one-line note in the mirrored contract (or a top-level echo of the tokens) removes this class of failure.
4. **Untracked-inventory digest is mint-then-use fragile.** Two consecutive rejections while a gitignored file was being edited between STATUS calls: first `--untracked-scope exclude` demanded `--expected-untracked-inventory`, then the freshly-minted digest was already stale ("untracked inventory changed"). Self-recovered by re-running the canonical STATUS once the file stabilized. A nonce or a same-call scope+inventory form would make this atomic.
5. **Reviewer subagents are undispatchable with materialized tasks** (bounded dispatch contract rejects hand-assembled envelopes — correctly), so without the MCP route there is no sanctioned way to get a fresh executor per lens (#544 asked for exactly this).

## Session data

| Batch | Scope | Lens runs | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | leaf helpers, 433 ln | 1 (reliability) | approved+ack |
| B2 | runtime core, 8,035 ln | 4 | approved+ack |
| B3 | session/ui/config, 1,822 ln | 1 | approved+ack |
| B4 | setup decomposition, 4,524 ln | 4 | approved+ack |
| B5 | UI stack, 7,566 ln | 1 | approved+ack |
| B6 | backfill+schedule, 8,812 ln | 4 | approved+ack |
| B7 | index capstone, 5,963 ln | 4 | approved+ack |

19 lens runs total; 0 corrections (budget 200 never consumed); 0 refuter rounds; 7 consent rounds (all granted); 1 resubmission (hand-typed subject-hash tail rejected as binding_mismatch — operator error, fixed by jq-assembling results from the provider token files); 11 recoverable errors total, all self-diagnosed.

Advisory findings from the lenses went to the reviewed repo as follow-ups (unvalidated `resumeFromSessionFile` path, unguarded resume-on-running accounting, silent drop of project-local settings after consolidation, plus 7 smaller items).

## Reproduction sketch (the CLI loop that worked)

```text
export GENTLE_PI_REVIEW_RELAY_CONTRACT=gentle-pi.review-relay/v1
git checkout --detach <batch-tip>
gentle-ai review status --cwd <repo> --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 \
  --agent pi --next-transition --base-ref <prev-tip> --committed-only
# → START command → run it verbatim (--consent=relay) → relay envelope → human grants
# → run the envelope's granted invocation verbatim
# per lens: capture-result ... --materialize > task.txt   (read task, author result JSON)
#           jq -n assemble result (tokens injected from the status JSON, never hand-typed)
#           capture-result ... --preflight --input result.json   (no --agent)
#           capture-result ... --agent pi --input result.json
# → closure envelope → re-run the bound STATUS → run acknowledge-approved verbatim
```

Materialized lens tasks for the larger batches ran 8k–10.6k lines; reading them in ≤50KB chunks consumed most of the session context — the single-file task-corpus concern from #573 applies to the CLI route too.

title: review: follow-up session report to #551 — concurrent-4R route gating, review personas unusable for host-relayed lineages, lens timeouts from single-file task corpus (main @ v2.3.0-10)
body:
### Pre-flight checks
- [x] Searched public `gentle-pi` issues for these findings; closest are #551 (prior session report), #544 (personas as subagents), #96 (reviewers vs snapshot tree) — overlaps marked per finding
- [x] Understand this issue needs `status:approved` before a PR can be opened

## Description

**Follow-up session report to #551.** The candidate shape there (~180 changed
files / ~37k lines, uncommitted workspace) matches this session's branch
before slicing; this session committed the work into three thematic commits,
sliced them into three linked worktrees under the repo's ignored `tmp/`, and
drove the full negotiated v2 lifecycle to **three approved, acknowledged
receipts**:

- `review-199a18226552ddc0` — core, high risk, 4R (118 files / 24,827 lines)
- `review-03c8717d1f806483` — ui, medium risk, 1 lens (39 files / 8,016 lines)
- `review-31cadf3f0d79a045` — setup, high risk, 4R (23 files / 4,107 lines)

Environment: Pi, macOS arm64 (macOS 26.6.2); gentle-pi host **`main` @
`239a312d` = `v2.3.0-10-g239a312d`** (latest release `v2.3.0` = `6c391ad9`;
0 behind / 10 ahead). The delta contains the **#533 concurrent-4R feature**
(#557/#559) and #561/#558 — findings F1–F3 were observed against that
**unreleased** concurrent-group code path, so this doubles as field testing
for #533 before it ships. gentle-ai side: binary `v2.5.0` + 2 commits (built
2026-09-02 09:07 from `main`).

## Findings

### F1 — controller route vs CLI relay route: same store, two incompatible views

A lineage created via the `gentle-ai` CLI (relay env exported by hand,
provider-issued commands executed exactly) is invisible to this package's
own controller surface:

- `gentle_review_capture_group` rejected byte-exact collect bindings taken
  from the current STATUS: "collectBindings are unknown, expired, or belong
  to different session routes".
- `review-risk` / `review-resilience` / `review-readability` /
  `review-reliability` subagent dispatch rejected with "review subagent
  dispatch has no current controller-owned candidate view lineage binding".

Both surfaces speak to the same binary and store; only the route check
differs. The practical effect: an agent that follows the provider's own
"export it in this shell and re-run" guidance — which works for every CLI
step, including admission and acknowledgement — is locked out of the
package's concurrent group executor and reviewer personas, and must hand-roll
the whole pipeline, with the context and pacing costs that come with it.

**Request**: resolve controller tool bindings from store truth (the lineage
and collect set were current and exact), or document the route boundary
prominently in the runtime contract so agents commit to one route from the
start. Related: #255.

### F2 — `review-*` personas cannot execute a self-contained provider task

The materialized reviewer task is fully self-contained (binding, patch
corpus, instruction, result schema). The gated personas are the ideal
executors (constrained tools, per-lens freshness), but they hard-require the
controller-owned binding, so the session fell back to a generic verify agent
per lens.

**Request**: allow the personas to run from a provider task file path without
a controller binding — essentially #544 plus a non-gated fallback mode.
Related: #96.

### F3 — lens timeouts from a single-file task corpus under the page ceiling

Materialized tasks for the 118-file slice were 27,736 lines each. With the
read tool's ~50KB cap (~582 lines of this file per call), one full pass is
~48 sequential reads; with a 20-minute dispatch wall, 3 of 4 first-round
lenses timed out mid-review. Two mitigations worked once made explicit in
the dispatch: "one forward pass, no re-reads, write the result immediately"
— and on the smallest slice (23 paths, ~4.4k lines), all four lenses
completed first-try in parallel.

**Request**: (a) chunked materialization — per-path or per-section patch
artifacts instead of one mega-file (gentle-ai cooperation possible, but the
host relay can also split what it writes); (b) ship the reviewer personas
with a codified playbook: single forward pass, no re-verification, immediate
result write, plus the admission-safe evidence phrasing rule (paired
gentle-ai issue, F2).

### F4 — `sync --agent pi` wrote a project-local untracked file without flagging it

Refreshing reviewer assets changed 3 files, one of them
`.pi/gentle-ai/persona.json` inside the working repository — discovered only
as a surprise untracked file in `git status` after the review preflight.

**Request**: sync output should explicitly call out writes that land inside
a Git worktree, so they never masquerade as candidate changes.

## Field log (one session, compressed)

- Workflow per slice: preflight → consent relay → freeze → materialize per
  lens → parallel reviewer dispatch → local validation (subject hash, path
  set, banned-phrase scan) → submit in provider order → acknowledge.
- Rounds: core needed 4 lens rounds (timeouts ×2, one admission rejection —
  that part filed upstream, its phrasing fix belongs in dispatch guidance);
  ui 1; setup 1. Consent rounds: 3, all granted.
- Blocked/recover actions: transport env recovered from host source; assets
  recovered via `sync --agent pi`; controller-route lockout recovered by
  falling back to generic verify agents; admission rejection recovered by
  reading the preserved rejected payload and re-running one lens.
- Context cost: reading provider payloads (STATUS manifests, materialized
  tasks, ~100KB binding sets) in the parent session dominated context;
  delegated summarization to `tmp/` files fixed it late. Chunked artifacts
  (F3) would remove most of it.

All claims are backed by session artifacts (task files, submissions,
rejection envelope, ack receipts); happy to attach any of them.

title: feat(models): add one-command full-routing plan switch (/subagents-plan gpt|cheap)
body:
### Pre-flight Checks

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand this issue needs `status:approved` before a PR can be opened
- [x] This complements (does not duplicate) #58 — see "Relationship to #58" below

### Problem Statement

Configuring models in gentle-ai / gentle-pi is a **one-time install flow**, not a repeatable switch. But changing the whole agent routing is something you do *repeatedly* (not once), and today every repetition means re-running the full per-agent picker.

Concrete numbers from the installer code (`internal/opencode/models.go`):

- There are **17+ configurable agents per engine**: 10 SDD phases (sdd-init → sdd-onboard), 3 Judgment-Day agents (jd-judge-a/b, jd-fix-agent), 4 review lenses + the refuter.
- The Claude **custom mode** requires ~2 selections *per agent* (Enter on the row → pick model → pick effort → back), so switching the entire stack by hand is **~34+ interactions**.
- The named presets (Balanced / Performance / Economy) exist for Claude, but they are a **one-time install choice**: `Economy` = "sonnet for all phases, haiku for archiving" is exactly the kind of profile users need — yet once installed, there is no command to *switch back to it* (or to a cheaper stack) mid-month.

The real-world driver: **not every user has the $200/mo GPT plan**. A common pattern is running the expensive routing for part of the month and switching the whole stack to cheaper providers (minimax / stepfun / deepseek / sonnet+haiku) when the budget runs out — then switching back. Doing that by hand through the per-agent picker every time is the friction this issue removes.

### Proposed Solution

Add a one-command **full-routing plan switch** for Pi (complementing `/gentle:models`):

- A plan = a named snapshot of the complete per-agent routing table (model + thinking/effort for every configurable agent).
- Two or three plans ship as sensible defaults, e.g. `gpt` (expensive full stack) and `cheap` (minimax/stepfun/deepseek or sonnet+haiku), user-editable and user-extensible.
- Switching is one invocation:

  ```
  /subagents-plan gpt
  /subagents-plan cheap
  /subagents-plan          # shows current plan + available plans
  ```

- Storage is local and user-scoped (e.g. `~/.pi/gentle-ai/profiles/`), no repo/team config — same scope decision #58 already made.
- A plan should include the **orchestrator (parent session) model** too, not only subagents — otherwise switching subagents to cheap still leaves the parent on the expensive model (mixed bill), the exact gap danielgap raised on #58.

### Relationship to #58

#58 proposes *managing* reusable model profiles (save/load/overwrite/delete) inside the `/gentle:models` UX. This issue is the **consumption half**: a fast, repeatable command that flips the whole routing between pre-made snapshots in one step, for the "mid-month budget switch" use case. If #58's storage layer lands first, this command should read from the same storage rather than introducing a parallel format.

Notably, the data model already exists in the gentle-ai installer for OpenCode: `model.Profile{ Name, OrchestratorModel, PhaseAssignments }` with examples literally named "cheap"/"premium" (`internal/model/types.go`). This issue asks to surface that same concept as a usable switch on Pi.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Re-running the installer TUI** each time: works but is the ~34+ interaction flow this issue exists to remove; presets are install-time only.
- **Manual model_profiles editing**: error-prone, no validation, no plan concept.
- **User-side patch extension** (a local `/subagents-plan`): viable stopgap — I run one today — but it lives outside the package, has no tests, and the community gets no benefit from it. A first-class command should supersede it.

### Additional Context

- I have a working local prototype of `/subagents-plan` (snapshot files + one-command switch + reload) proving the UX; happy to adapt it to the repo's storage/validation conventions and the #58 shape.
- A full plan must cover subagents *and* the parent-session model to avoid a mixed bill at mid-month.

title: feat(review): harden RDD trust model — audit trail, executable evidence, anti-loop metrics, self-invalidating captures
body:
## Summary

Gentle AI's RDD system already implements the core thesis of trust-by-receipt: event-sourced ledger, scope fingerprints, fail-closed captures, and separation of duties (author / lens / refuter / validator). This issue proposes four hardening/evangelism improvements that push the system from "internally sound" to "provably sound from the outside":

## Proposals (ordered by value)

### 1. Human-readable audit trail per lineage

The ledger is event-sourced but infrastructure-only. Add `gentle-ai review audit <lineage>` rendering a readable timeline: who raised which finding, who refuted it with what result, which correction was applied, and the hashes at each step. "Why is this approved?" should be answerable in 30 seconds with a machine-derived receipt, not by digging through state files.

### 2. Machine-verifiable evidence records per finding

Today refutation is largely semantic (the refuter reasons about findings). Raise the bar for severe findings: each finding should optionally carry an executable evidence record (a reproducing command, a failing→passing test, diff + hash) so "prove it" is mechanically checkable rather than persuasive prose. Also invalidates the disappearing-finding failure mode.

### 3. Anti-loop metrics, not just budgets

Correction budgets cap cost but don't detect the pathologies we warn about: findings that vanish between rounds, or oscillation. Track per-lineage counters (findings per round, volatility rate) and surface them in status as a weak-refutation alarm.

### 4. Self-invalidating captures on scope drift

Verify whether a capture is automatically invalidated when the working tree / scope fingerprint changes mid-review (diff hash or HEAD SHA drift after freeze). If not enforced, this is the highest-integrity gap; if enforced, document it prominently in the RDD workflow skill.

### Optional: public dogfooding

Run RDD on gentle-pi itself in CI and publish receipts in the README as both proof and adoption template.

## Evidence / context

- RDD flow in `lib/review-*` and the native `gentle-ai review` CLI already covers: ledger, freeze hashes, correction budgets, consent gates, native-admitted lens/refuter/validator verdicts.
- Motivation: external walkthrough of the exact trust model (author/reviewer/judge separation, "demostralo" refuter, verifiable receipts) surfaced these as the remaining gaps between the current design and the fully provable version.

## Alternatives considered

- Treating these as documentation-only hardening — rejected: 2–4 are behavioral, not just docs.
- One issue per item — deferred; kept as one scoped hardening issue with checkable sub-items; can split during triage.

title: review: full negotiated v2 session from Pi — 3 escalation rounds × 4 sequential lenses, ~40 min per round (session report)
body:
## Description

Session report from one full negotiated review lifecycle driven from a Pi session (gentle-ai binary `main`, contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`, gentle-pi main host relay contract, macOS arm64) over a large uncommitted workspace candidate (~180 changed files, ~37k changed lines). The gentle-ai-side defects are reported in Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai#4031; this is the gentle-pi-side account of the same session: what the host runtime made the operator do by hand, and what each stage cost. Narrow defects already have their own issues (#550, #509, #544); this report carries the session workflow, round economics, timing, and context cost that no single issue covers.

## Session workflow actually followed

1. RDD enabled; first route entry from the session shell failed `immutable_review_transport_unsupported` because the shell does not inherit `GENTLE_PI_REVIEW_RELAY_CONTRACT` (#550). Value recovered by reading `runtime/review-relay-contract.mjs`; exported manually; route became usable.
2. `review.start` → `managed_assets_outdated` → recovered via `gentle-ai sync`.
3. Intended-untracked collect: hand-built schema-bound selection JSON; accepted shape learned from gentle-ai Go source (see gentle-ai#4031).
4. START → consent/v3 (high risk) → human granted → 4 lenses selected (risk/resilience/readability/reliability).
5. Reviewer execution — every gentle-pi execution lane failed:
   - dedicated `review-*` agents: dispatcher rejected (`review subagent dispatch requires mode task`, then `no current controller-owned candidate view lineage binding`) (#544);
   - MCP `gentle_review_capture`: rejected the CLI-minted binding (`capture-binding-rejected ... different session route`) (#509);
   - fallback: hand-assembled `GENTLE_AI_REVIEW_BINDING`-prefixed prompts on generic read-only subagents + manual `gentle-ai review capture-result` submissions (12/12 succeeded).
6. Round 1 → escalated (2 CRITICALs) → terminal `native_stop_required` → maintainer chose fix → fixes → new candidate → new selection → new consent → full re-review.
7. Round 2 → escalated again (new BLOCKER in already-reviewed code + residual CRITICAL) → fix → round 3.
8. Round 3 → approved → `acknowledge-approved` (authority burned) → pre-commit gate reports `invalidated/unmanaged/repository-policy` → committed under ordinary policy.

## Review rounds and the reason for each (3 rounds, 12 lens runs, ~40 min per round)

| # | Lineage (opaque) | Outcome | Why another round was needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | review-02a57db6e2b899d6 | escalated | 2 CRITICALs (timer-ceiling storm; worktree SHA-capture loss). Escalation is terminal; no bounded correction offered; fixing changed the candidate, forcing a fresh lineage, fresh selection, fresh consent, full 4-lens re-review. |
| 2 | review-3fc0db519173bfc7 | escalated | Residual CRITICAL `unknown` + a NEW introduced BLOCKER (`dispose()` destroying retained recovery dirs) in code round 1 had already inspected. |
| 3 | review-aa6fca0dcaa74dc5 | approved → acknowledged | Zero severe findings; only WARNING/SUGGESTION follow-ups. |

## Observed friction, by category

**Errors:** `immutable_review_transport_unsupported` (env not injected — #550); `managed_assets_outdated` (clean cause, `gentle-ai sync` recovered); dispatcher rejections for `review-*` agents (#544); MCP `capture-binding-rejected` (#509). (Four admission rejections also occurred; those are gentle-ai-side — see #4031-umbrella.)

**Endless loops / re-run actions:** escalate→fix→full-re-review cycle; three complete rounds; the untracked selection JSON must be rebuilt every round (fresh inventory digest); the consent envelope re-asked every round. Each fix family cost a full 37k-line re-review instead of an incremental one.

**Blocked actions:** escalation offers only maintainer-review or clone-scoped mode disable; the intended gentle-pi execution lanes (capture wrapper, dedicated agents) were unusable, forcing the manual CLI path for all 12 captures.

**Reactive actions (reading the tools' own source to operate them):** the relay contract value came from gentle-pi's `runtime/review-relay-contract.mjs`; the selection JSON schema, admission grammar, reviewer payload shape, and gate semantics came from gentle-ai's Go source. None were stated by tool output.

**Recover actions that worked:** manual env export (#550 workaround); `gentle-ai sync`; direct `review capture-result` submissions after the capture-lane rejection; rebuilt selection per round.

**Failures:** #509 (capture lane), #544 (agent dispatch), #550 (env injection); plus the approved receipt being invisible to the delivery gate after acknowledgement (gentle-ai-side, cf. their #4007/#3929).

**Rejections:** `capture-binding-rejected` on a fresh, byte-exact STATUS-issued binding; two dispatcher rejections; (admission rejections ×4 on gentle-ai's side).

**Review lenses not in parallel:** four independent read-only reviewers over one frozen candidate ran strictly sequentially every round (foreground per-capture contract); ~40 min per round, ×3. #533 tracks host-relay concurrency.

**Review issues fixed one after another:** round 2's BLOCKER lived in code round 1's four lenses had already reviewed; severe findings surfaced one family per round rather than all at once.

**Context gets full quickly:** each hand-assembled lens reviewer consumed ~55k–160k tokens (147k/112k/87k/159k in round 1) on generic agents, largely because every reviewer artifact must echo the full 180+ path manifest in `inspection.paths`.

**Tool big outputs:** each consent envelope prints the full invocation twice (~8KB, 145+ `--intended-untracked` tokens); STATUS prints the complete eligible-paths JSON inline; terminal truncation forced writing envelopes to files and reading them back.

**No subagents:** the purpose-built reviewer roles could not be dispatched (#544), so the host hand-assembled prompts and manually submitted results — exactly the orchestration-by-hand the dedicated agents and capture wrapper exist to remove.

## Expected behavior

- The session environment carries the relay contract so the route works on first invocation (#550).
- The capture wrapper accepts CLI-minted negotiated bindings (#509), and reviewer roles dispatch as fresh constrained subagents (#544) — no hand-assembled prompts.
- Lens captures can run concurrently per candidate (#533).
- Reviewer payloads reference the frozen manifest instead of echoing it, keeping per-lens context bounded.

## Environment

- gentle-ai: `main` (contract `gentle-ai.review-integration/v2`)
- gentle-pi: `main` (relay contract `gentle-pi.review-relay/v1`)
- OS: macOS (arm64)
- Runtime: Pi session driving the gentle-ai CLI through shell tools + MCP gateway

## Context

Umbrella gentle-ai-side report (admission grammar, escalation loop, gate semantics): Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai#4031. Narrow gentle-pi issues: #550 (env injection), #509 (capture lane), #544 (reviewer subagents), #533 (concurrent lenses). All four severe defects the reviews surfaced were real and are fixed test-first in the consumer project; this report is about the host-side workflow cost of getting there.
